## \|\| 1.5.67 \|\|

*bhavetkūlaṃkapā yadvadalpavarṣeṇakannadī \|*  
*khalardhiralpavarṣeṇa tadvatsyātsvakulaṃkapā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Just as a rivulet becomes over-flooded even when there is a slight shower and begins to erode its banks, so also the affluence of a wicked man based on trivial gains, undermines his own family.

## \|\| 1.5.68 \|\|

*avijñāyānya sāmarthyaṃ svasāmarthyaṃ pradarśayeta \|*  
*upahāsamavāpnoti tathaivāyamihācalaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. If a man tries to demonstrate and display his ability, unaware of that of others, he gets only a derisive laughter. So also this Mountain here had it.

## \|\| 1.5.69 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*godāvarītaṭaṃ ramyaṃ vicarannapi vai muniḥ \|*  
*na tatyāja ca taṃ tāpaṃ kāśīvirahajaṃ param \|\| 69 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

69\. Even while roaming about on the charming banks of Godāvarī, the sage could not get rid of the distress due to the separation from Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.5.70 \|\|

*udīcī dikspṛśamapi sa munirmātariśvanam \|*  
*prasārya bāhū saṃśliṣya kāśyāḥ pṛcchedanāmayam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The sage used to stretch out his arms and embrace the wind blowing in his direction from the north and enquire about Kāśī and its welfare.

## \|\| 1.5.71 \|\|

*lopāmudre na sā mudrā kāpīha jagatītale \|*  
*vārāṇasyāḥ pradṛśyeta tatkartā na yato vidhiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. (He used to say:) “O Lopāmudrā, nowhere on the face of this earth can that inexplicable image of Vārāṇasī be seen, because its maker is not Brahmā.”

## \|\| 1.5.72 \|\|

*kvacittiṣṭhankvacijjalpankvaciddhāvankvacitskhalan \|*  
*kvaccicopaviśaṃśceti babhrāmetastato muniḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The sage wandered here and there prattling like this in some places, standing in certain places, running elsewhere, faltering there and sitting here.

## \|\| 1.5.73-75 \|\|

*tato vrajandadarśāgre puṇyarāśistapodhanaḥ \|*  
*caṃcaccaṃdragatābhāsāṃ bhāgyavāniva suśriyam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*vijityabhānu nābhānuṃ divāpi samuditvarām \|*  
*nirvāpayaṃtīmiva tāṃ svacetastāpasaṃtatim \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tatrāgastyo mahālakṣmīṃ dadṛśe suciraṃ sthitām \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-75. Proceeding ahead from there, Agastya, the mass of merit, the storehouse of penance, saw in front of him Goddess Mahālakṣmī (of Kolhapur) like a lucky man, the best of glory. She had the lustre of a hundred rising moons. With her own lustre, she appeared to surpass even the Sun, even during the day time. She was brilliantly dazzling, (yet) she appeared to alleviate the distress of his (Agastya’s) mind.

## \|\| 1.5.76 \|\|

*rātrāvabjeṣu saṃkoco darśeṣvabjaḥ kvacidvrajet \|*  
*kṣīrode maṃdaratrāsāttadatrādhyuṣitāmiva \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Lotuses shrink and close during nights. During New-Moon days the Moon goes away somewhere. There is the fear from the Mandara mountain in the Milk Ocean. Hence, it appears as though she has put up her permanent residence here (Kolhapur).

## \|\| 1.5.77 \|\|

*yadārabhya dadhāraināṃ mādhavo mānataḥ kila \|*  
*tadārabhya sthitāṃ nūnaṃ sapatnīrṣyāvaśādiva \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Ever since Mādhava retained her with great honour, she had certainly stayed here as though out of spiteful rivalry with her co-wife.

## \|\| 1.5.78 \|\|

*trailokyaṃ kolarūpeṇa trāsayaṃtaṃ mahāsuram \|*  
*vinihatya sthitāṃ tatra ramye kolāpure pure \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. A great Asura was frightening the three worlds in the form of a boar. The goddess killed that demon and stayed in the beautiful city of Kolhapur ever since.

## \|\| 1.5.79 \|\|

*saṃprāpyātha mahālakṣmīṃ munivaryaḥ praṇamya ca \|*  
*tuṣṭāva vāgbhiriṣṭābhiriṣṭadāṃ hṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. After reaching the place the excellent sage bowed ḍown to Mahālakṣmī who bestows whatever is desired, through very pleasing words. He was highly delighted in his mind.

## \|\| 1.5.80 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*mātarnamāmi kamale kamalāyatākṣi śrīviṣṇuhṛtkamalavāsini viśvamātaḥ \|*  
*kṣīrodaje kamalakomalagarbha gauri lakṣmi prasīda satataṃ namatāṃ śaraṇye \|\| 80 \|\|*

Agastya said:

(Prayer to Mahālakṣmī)

80\. O mother Kamalā of large eyes resembling lotus, I bow down (to you). O mother of the universe, residing in the lotus-like heart of Śrī Viṣṇu! O Lakṣmī, fair in complexion like the inner kernel of a lotus, be pleased with me. O daughter of the Milk Ocean, you are the sole refuge of those who bow down always.

## \|\| 1.5.81 \|\|

*tvaṃ śrīrupeṃdrasadane madanaikamātarjyotsnāsi caṃdramasi caṃdramanoharāsye \|*  
*sūrye prabhāsi ca jagattritaye prabhāsi lakṣmi prasīda satataṃ namatāṃ śaraṇye \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. You are the glorious lustre in the abode of Upendra (Viṣṇu). O sole mother of Madana, you are the moonlight in the Moon, O goddess with a face captivating the mind like the Moon. You are the splendour in the Sun. You shine with all refulgence in all the three worlds. O Lakṣmī, the sole refuge of those who bow down always, be pleased with me.

## \|\| 1.5.82 \|\|

*tvaṃ jātavedasi sadā dahnātmaśaktirvedhāstvayā jagadidaṃ vividhaṃ vidadhyāt \|*  
*viśvaṃbharopi bibhṛyādakhilaṃ bhavatyā lakṣmi prasīda satataṃ namatāṃ śaraṇye \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. You are the Śakti (the burning power) that always abide in fire; in collaboration with you, Vedhas (Brahmā) creates the different types of worlds. Viśvaṃbhara (Viṣṇu) sustains and supports everything with your (assistance), O Lakṣmī, the sole refuge of these who bow down always; be pleased with me.

## \|\| 1.5.83 \|\|

*tvattyaktametadamale harate haropi tvaṃ pāsi haṃsi vidadhāsi parāvarāsi \|*  
*īḍyo babhūva harirapyamale tvadāptyā lakṣmi prasīda satataṃ namatāṃ śaraṇye \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O deity free from impurities, Hara annihilates only those things forsaken by you; (actually) you create, sustain and annihilate. You are Parā (the greatest) and the Avarā (the smallest). O pure one, Hari became worthy of being adored by securing you (as his consort). O Lakṣmī, the sole refuge of those who always bow down, be pleased with me.

## \|\| 1.5.84 \|\|

*śūraḥ sa eva sa guṇī budhaḥ dhanyo mānyaḥ sa eva kulaśīla kalākalāpaiḥ \|*  
*ekaḥ śuciḥ sa hi pumānsakalepi loke yatrāpatettava śubhe karuṇākaṭākṣaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. O splendid deity, only he on whom your benign glance falls, becomes heroic with good qualities. He alone is a good scholar; he alone is blessed; he alone is worthy of honour through good ancestry, good conduct and artistic qualities. That man is the only clean one in the entire world.

## \|\| 1.5.85 \|\|

*yasminvaseḥ kṣaṇamahopuruṣe gaje'śve straiṇe tṛṇe sarasi devakule gṛhe'nne \|*  
*ratne patattriṇi paśau śayane dharāyāṃ saśrīkameva sakale tadihāstinānyat \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Wherever you happen to stay for even a moment whether in a man, an elephant, a horse, a group of women, grass, lake, temple, house, cooked food, jewel, bird, animal, bed or a plot of land, that alone becomes splendid and glorious, O deity identical with all; none else (can do so).

## \|\| 1.5.86 \|\|

*tvatspṛṣṭameva sakalaṃ śucitāṃ labheta tvattyaktameva sakalaṃ tvaśucīha lakṣmi \|*  
*tvannāma yatra ca sumaṃgalameva tatra śrīviṣṇupatni kamale kamalālaye'pi \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Only the things touched by you get purity. All the things forsaken by you are unclean, O Lakṣmī, O consort of Śrī Viṣṇu. O Kamalā residing in the lotus, wherever your name is (uttered), auspiciousness is there.

## \|\| 1.5.87 \|\|

*lakṣmīṃ śriyaṃ ca kamalāṃ kamalālayāṃ ca padmāṃ ramāṃ nalinayugmakarāṃ ca māṃ ca \|*  
*kṣīrodajāmamṛtakuṃbhakarāmirāṃ ca viṣṇupriyāmiti sadājapatāṃ kva duḥkham \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Where can there be misery unto those who always repeat the names of Lakṣmī, viz., Lakṣmī, Śrī, Kamalā, Kamalālayā, Padmā, Ramā, Nalinayugmakarā, Mā, Kṣīrodajā, Amṛtakuṃbhakarā, Irā and Viṣṇupriyā.

## \|\| 1.5.88 \|\|

*iti stutvā bhagavatīṃ mahālakṣmīṃ haripriyām \|*  
*praṇanāma sapatnīkaḥ sāṣṭāṃgaṃ daṃḍavanmuniḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. After eulogizing Goddess Mahālakṣmī, the beloved of Hari, thus, the sage accompanied by his wife bowed down and lay down like a log of wood with the eight limbs (touching the ground).

## \|\| 1.5.89 \|\|

*śrīruvāca \|*  
*uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhadraṃ te mitrāvaruṇasaṃbhava \|*  
*pativrate tvamuttiṣṭha lopāmudre śubhavrate \|\| 89 \|\|*

Śrī said:

89\. O son of Mitra and Varuṇa, get up, get up. Welfare unto you. O chaste lady Lopāmudrā of auspicious holy vows, get up.

## \|\| 1.5.90 \|\|

*stutyānayā prasannohaṃ vriyatāṃ yaddhṛdīpsitam \|*  
*rājaputri mahābhāge tvamihopaviśāmale \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. I am delighted with this eulogy. Let the cherished desire in you heart, whatever it is, be requested for. O highly fortunate princess free of impurities, sit here.

## \|\| 1.5.91 \|\|

*tvadaṃgalakṣaṇairebhiḥ supavitraiśca te vrataiḥ \|*  
*nirvāpayitumicchāmi daityāstraistāpitāṃ tanum \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. I desire to get my body that was scorched by the weapons and missiles of the demon (Kola) alleviated a bit, by these characteristics of your limbs and your sacred vows.

## \|\| 1.5.92 \|\|

*ityuktvā munipatnīṃ tāṃ samāliṃgya haripriyā \|*  
*alaṃcakāra ca prītyā bahusaubhāgyamaṃḍanaiḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. After saying this, the beloved wife of Hari embraced that wife of the sage. Out of love, she adorned her with many ornaments indicating conjugal bliss.

## \|\| 1.5.93 \|\|

*punarāha mune jāne tava hṛttāpakāraṇam \|*  
*sacetanaṃ dunotyeva kāśīviśleṣajo'nalaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Again she said: “O sage, I know the cause that torments your heart. The fire of grief caused by the separation from Kāśī indeed scorches all sentient beings.

## \|\| 1.5.94 \|\|

*yadā sa devo viśveśo maṃdaraṃ gatavānpurā \|*  
*tadā kāśīviyogena jātā tasyedṛśī daśā \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Formerly when that Lord Viśveśa went to Mandara, a condition similar to this befell him too, due to the separation from Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.5.95 \|\|

*tatpravṛttiṃ punarjñātuṃ brahmāṇaṃ keśavaṃ gaṇān \|*  
*gaṇeśvaraṃ ca devāṃśca preṣayāmāsa śūladhṛk \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. In order to know the full details of that (Kāśī) the Trident-bearing Lord deputed Brahmā, Keśava, his attendants, Gaṇeśvara and the Devas.

## \|\| 1.5.96 \|\|

*te ca kāśīguṇānsarve vicārya ca punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*vrajaṃtyadyāpi na kvāpi tādṛgasti kva vā purī \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Even now all of them are roaming about considering the good qualities of Kāśī. There is no other city like it anywhere. Where is that city?”

## \|\| 1.5.97 \|\|

*iti śrutvātha sa muniḥ pratyuvāca śriyaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya mahābhāgo bhaktigarbhamidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. On hearing this, the highly fortunate sage bowed down and spoke to Goddess Śrī, the following words filled with devotional fervour.

## \|\| 1.5.98 \|\|

*yadi deyo varo mahyaṃ varayogyosmyahaṃ yadi \|*  
*tadā vārāṇasī prāptiḥ punarastveṣa me varaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. “If a boon has to be given to me, if I deserve a boon, let me have an opportunity to return to Vārāṇasī. This is my boon,

## \|\| 1.5.99 \|\|

*ye paṭhiṣyaṃti ca stotraṃ tvadbhaktyā matkṛtaṃ sadā \|*  
*teṣāṃ kadācitsaṃtāpo māstu māstu daridratā \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Never should those people suffer from distress and poverty—the people who always read this prayer composed by me with devotion unto you.

## \|\| 1.5.100 \|\|

*māstu ceṣṭaviyogaśca māstu saṃpatti saṃkṣayaḥ \|*  
*sarvatra vijayaścāstu vicchedo māstu saṃtateḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Let them not be separated from those whom they love. Let there not be destruction of their assets. Let there be success everywhere. Let there not be any break in the line of their progeny.”

## \|\| 1.5.101 \|\|

*śrīruvāca \|*  
*evamastu mune sarvaṃ yattvayā paribhāṣitam \|*  
*etatstotrasya paṭhanaṃ mama sānnidhya kāraṇam \|\| 101 \|\|*

Śrī said:

101\. O sage, let everything be like the way it has been uttered by you. The recitation of this prayer will bring about my presence.

## \|\| 1.5.102 \|\|

*alakṣmīḥ kālakarṇī ca tadgehe na viśetkvacit \|*  
*gajāśvapaśuśāṃtyarthametatstotraṃ sadā japet \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. May not Alakṣmī (ill-luck, misfortune) or Kālakarṇī the Ogress, enter their house. For the purpose of quelling (the distresses) of cows, horses and other animals, one should always repeat this prayer.

## \|\| 1.5.103 \|\|

*bālagrahābhibhūtānāṃ vālānāṃśāṃtikṛtparam \|*  
*bhūrjapatre likhitvā tu badhnīyātkaṃṭhadeśataḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. This prayer should be written on a leaf of Bhūrja tree (or the bark) and tied around the neck. It causes the Śānti (peaceful alleviation) of children attacked by malignant Planets, Bālagraha etc.

## \|\| 1.5.104 \|\|

*idaṃ bījarahasyaṃ me rakṣaṇīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*śraddhāhīne na dātavyaṃ na deyaṃ cāśucau kvacit \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. This is a greater secret than my own Bīja. It should be scrupulously preserved. It should not be imparted to one lacking in faith. It should not be imparted hurriedly.

## \|\| 1.5.105 \|\|

*anyacca śṛṇu vipreṃdra bhaviṣye dvāpare bhavān \|*  
*ekonatriṃśake brahmansatyavyāso bhaviṣyati \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. O eminent Brāhmaṇa, listen further to another thing. In the future Dvāpara, the twenty-ninth one, O Brāhmaṇa, you will become Vyāsa. It is true.

## \|\| 1.5.106 \|\|

*tadā vārāṇasīṃ prāpya siddhiṃ prāpsyasyabhīpsitām \|*  
*vyasya vedānpurāṇāni dharmā nsamupadiśya ca \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. At that time you will classify the Vedas and teach the Purāṇas and pious practices. Then you will reach Vārāṇasī and attain the fulfilment of all your desires.

## \|\| 1.5.107 \|\|

*hitaṃ ca te vadāmyekaṃ sāṃprataṃ tatsamācara \|*  
*paśya kiṃcidito gatvā skaṃdamagre sthitaṃ prabhum \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Now I shall mention something beneficial to you. Act according to it. After proceeding a little ahead, visit Lord Skanda stationed in front.

## \|\| 1.5.108 \|\|

*vārāṇasyā rahasyaṃ ca yathāva cchivabhāṣitam \|*  
*tava tuṣṭikaraṃ brahmankathayiṣyati ṣaṇmukhaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The Six-faced Lord will duly narrate to you the secret of Vārāṇasī in the same manner as has been recounted by Śiva to him. It will cause satisfaction to you, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.5.109 \|\|

*iti labdhvā varaṃ sotha mahālakṣmīṃ praṇamya ca \|*  
*yayāvagastiryatrāsti kumāraśikhivāhanaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. After getting the boon thus, Agastya bowed down to Mahālakṣmī and went to the place where the peacock-vehicled Lord Kuṃāra was present.

## Chapter 6 - Tīrthādhyāya (Sacred Places)

## \|\| 1.6.1 \|\|

*pārāśarya uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu sūta mahābhāga kathāṃ śrutisahodarām \|*  
*yāṃ vai hṛdi nidhāyeha puruṣaḥ puruṣārthabhāk \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pārāśarya said:

1\. O Sūta, O illustrious one, listen to the story comparable (in sanctity) to Śruti which, if retained in the heart, enables a man to attain all his aims in life.

## \|\| 1.6.2 \|\|

*tataḥ śrīdarśa nānaṃda sudhādhārādhunīṃ muniḥ \|*  
*avagāhya sapatnīkaḥ parāṃ mudamavāpa saḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Thereafter, the sage accompanied by his wife took a plunge in the holy river with the current of nectarine bliss arising from the vision of Śrī. He derived the highest joy and bliss.

## \|\| 1.6.3 \|\|

*vahnikuṃḍasamudbhūta sūtanirmalamānasa \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvaikaṃ purā vidbhirbhāṣitaṃ yatsubhā ṣitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Sūta of pure mind, you are born of the sacred pit of sacrificial fire; listen to a saying uttered by those who know the ancient lore.

## \|\| 1.6.4 \|\|

*paropakaraṇaṃ yeṣāṃ jāgarti hṛdaye satām \|*  
*naśyaṃti vipadasteṣāṃ saṃpadaḥ syuḥ padepade \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. If a keen sense of helping others is ever wakeful in the heart of the good, all their adversities perish and riches accrue at every step.

## \|\| 1.6.5 \|\|

*tīrthasnānairna sā śuddhirbahudānairna tatphalam \|*  
*tapobhirugraistannāpyamupakṛtyāya dāpyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. What is obtained by extending help (to others) cannot be derived through severe austerities; that purity cannot be had through the holy ablution and the sacred waters; that benefit cannot be had through plentiful gifts.

## \|\| 1.6.6 \|\|

*paropakṛtyā yo dharmo dharmo dānādisaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*ekatra tulitau dhātrā tatra pūrvo bhavadguruḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The piety resulting from helping others and the piety born of gifts etc., were weighed together in one balance by Brahmā. The former was weightier.

## \|\| 1.6.7 \|\|

*parinirmathya vāgjālaṃ nirṇītamidameva hi \|*  
*nopakārātparo dharmo nāpakārādavaṃ param \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After churning through the network of verbal discussions, this is the conclusion arrived at—there is no piety greater than helping others and no heinous sin greater than injuring others.

## \|\| 1.6.8 \|\|

*upakarturagastyasya jātametannidarśanam \|*  
*kva tādṛkkāśijaṃ duḥkhaṃ kva tādṛkśrīmukhekṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The example is set by Agastya who was keen in helping (the gods). Where is such a misery born (of the separation) from Kāśī? Where is such a benign sight of the face of Śrī?

## \|\| 1.6.9 \|\|

*karikarṇāgracapalaṃ jīvitaṃ vividhaṃ vasu \|*  
*tasmātparopakaraṇaṃ kāryamekaṃ vipaścitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Life and different types of wealth are as fickle as the tips of the ears of an elephant. Hence the only thing to be carried out by a learned man is rendering help to others.

## \|\| 1.6.10 \|\|

*yallakṣmīnāmamātrāptyā naro no māti kutracit \|*  
*sākṣātsamīkṣyatāṃ lakṣmīṃ kṛtakṛtyo bhavanmuniḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The sage felt to have achieved all his objects by directly seeing that Lakṣmī by uttering whose name a man becomes highly boosted so as not to be contained within anything (i.e. becomes greater still).

## \|\| 1.6.11 \|\|

*gacchanyadṛcchayāsotha dūrācchrīśailamaikṣata \|*  
*yatra sākṣānnivasati devaḥ śrītripurāṃtakaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. As he went ahead, he casually espied Śrī Śaila from afar, where Lord Śiva, the slayer of Tripura, was directly present.

## \|\| 1.6.12-14 \|\|

*uvāca vacanaṃ patnīṃ tadā prītamanā muniḥ \|\| \|*  
*ihasthitaiva paśya tvaṃ kāṃte kāṃtataraṃ param \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śrīśaila śikharaṃ śrīmadidaṃtadyadvilokanāt \|*  
*punarbhavo manuṣyāṇāṃ bhavetra nabhavetkvacit \|\| 13 \|\|*

*giri ścaturaśītyāyaṃ yojanānāṃ hi vismṛtaḥ \|*  
*sarvaliṃgamayo yasmādataḥ kuryātpradakṣiṇam \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. The sage spoke to his wife with a delighted mind: “O my beloved, standing here alone, you look at the extremely brilliant peak of Śrī Śaila. It is glorious and by perceiving it, men will not be reborn here in this world. The extent of this mountain is eighty-four Yojanas. Since it is full of Liṅgas all over, one should circumambulate it.”

Lopāmudrā said.

## \|\| 1.6.15 \|\|

*lopāmudrovāca \|*  
*kiṃcidvijñaptumicchāmi yadyājñā svāmino bhavet \|*  
*brūte hi yā'nujñātā patyā sā patitā bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I wish to submit something if it is permitted by my lord and master. A woman who speaks before obtaining the permission of her master becomes fallen.

## \|\| 1.6.16 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ vaktukāmā devi tvaṃ brūhi tattvamaśaṃkitā \|*  
*na tvādṛśīnāṃ vākyaṃ hi patyuḥ khedāya jāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

Agastya said:

16\. O lady, what is it that you are desirous of saying? Say that unhesitatingly. Indeed no statement of women like you can cause grief to the husbands.

## \|\| 1.6.17 \|\|

*tataḥ papraccha sā devī praṇamya munimānatā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ ca hitārthāya svasaṃdehāpanuttaye \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then the pious lady bowed down to the sage and asked for the sake of the welfare of all and for the removal of her own doubts:

## \|\| 1.6.18 \|\|

*lopāmudrovāca \|*  
*śrīśailaśikharaṃ dṛṣṭvā punarjanma na vidyate \|*  
*idameva hi satyaṃ cetkimarthaṃ kāśiriṣyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

Lopāmudrā said:

18\. (You say:) By looking at the peak of Śrī Śaila one has no rebirth. If this is the truth, why is Kāśī sought (by you and others)?

## \|\| 1.6.19 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*ākarṇaya varārohe satyaṃ pṛṣṭaṃ tvayāmale \|*  
*nirṇītamasakṛccaitanmunibhistattvaciṃtakaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Agastya said:

19\. O beautiful lady, listen. O pure lady, what you ask is true. This has been decided on many occasions by sages, the seekers of truth.

## \|\| 1.6.20 \|\|

*muktisthānānyanekāni kṛtastatrāpinirṇayaḥ \|*  
*tāni te kathayāmyatra dattacittā bhava kṣaṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. There are many holy spots bringing about salvation. Decision has been arrived at in regard to that also. I shall enumerate them to you. Listen with attention for a short while.

## \|\| 1.6.21 \|\|

*prathamaṃ tīrtharājaṃ tu prayāgākhyaṃ suviśrutam \|*  
*kāmikaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ dharmakāmārthamokṣadam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The first and the foremost is the well reputed king of Tīrthas (Tīrtharāja) named Prayāga. It is conducive to the realization of the wishes of all the holy spots. (Other holy spots incur the sins of those who resort to them. In order to wipe off those sins, they have to resort to Prayāga.) It accords piety, love, wealth and salvation.

## \|\| 1.6.22-25 \|\|

*naimiṣaṃ ca kurukṣetraṃ gaṃgādvāramavaṃtikā \|*  
*ayodhyā mathurā caiva dvārakāpyamarāvatī \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sarasvatī siṃdhusaṃgo gaṃgāsāgarasaṃgamaḥ \|*  
*kāṃtī ca tryaṃbakaṃ cāpi saptagodāvarītaṭam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kālaṃjaraṃ prabhāsaśca tathā bada rikāśramaḥ \|*  
*mahālayastathoṃkārakṣetraṃ vai pauruṣottamam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*gokarṇo bhṛgukacchaśca bhṛgutuṃgaśca puṣkaram \|*  
*śrīparvatādi tīrthāni dhārātīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. The others are Naimiṣa, Kurukṣetra, Gaṅgādvāra, Avantikā, Ayodhyā, Mathurā, Dvārakā and Amarāvatī, the place where Sarasvatī and Sindhu join the sea, the meeting place of Gaṅgā and the ocean, Kāntī (Kāñcī), Tryambaka and Saptagodāvarī, Kālañjara, Prabhāsa, Badarikāśrama, Mahālaya, Oṃkārakṣetra (Amarakaṇṭaka), Jagannāthapurī which is the most excellent of all the shrines of Viṣṇu, Gokarṇa, Bhṛgukaccha (Broach—Gujarat), Bhṛgutuṅga (in Nepal—De), Puṣkara, Śrīparvata and other holy spots and Dhārātīrtha.

## \|\| 1.6.26 \|\|

*mānasānyapi tīrthāni satyādīni ca vai priye \|*  
*etāni muktidānyeva nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O my beloved, there are mental holy spots sūch as Truth etc. These too are the bestowers of salvation. No doubt need be entertained in this regard.

## \|\| 1.6.27 \|\|

*gayā tīrthaṃ ca yatproktaṃ pitṝṇāṃ hi muktidam \|*  
*pitāmahānāmṛṇato muktāstattanayā api \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The holy spot called Gayātīrtha bestows salvation to the Pitṛs (Manes). Their sons too are liberated from indebtedness to the grandfathers

## \|\| 1.6.28 \|\|

*sadharmiṇyuvāca \|*  
*mānasānyapi tīrthāni yānyuktāni mahāmate \|*  
*kāni kāni ca tānīha hyetadākhyātumarhasi \|\| 28 \|\|*

Sadharmiṇī said:

\[Note: Sadharmiṇī refers to “the partner in pious practices, wife”, i.e., Lopāmudrā\]

28\. O highly intelligent one, what are those holy spots called mental holy spots? It behoves you to narrate them.

## \|\| 1.6.29-32 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tīrthāni gadato mānasāni mamānaghe \|*  
*yeṣu samyaṅnaraḥ snātvā prayāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 29 \|\|*

*satyaṃ tīrthaṃ kṣamā tīrthaṃ tīrthamindriyanigrahaḥ \|*  
*sarvabhūtadayātīrthaṃ tīrthamārjavameva ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dānaṃ tīrthaṃ damastīrthaṃ saṃtoṣastīrthamucyate \|*  
*brahmacaryaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ ca priyavāditā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*jñānaṃ tīrthaṃ dhṛtistīrthaṃ tapastīrthamudāhṛtam \|*  
*tīrthānāmapi tattīrthaṃ viśuddhirmanasaḥ parā \|\| 32 \|\|*

Agastya said:

29-32. O sinless lady, listen even as I enumerate the mental holy spots. By scrupulously taking the holy dips in them a man attains the greatest goal.

Truth is a Tīrtha (holy place); forbearance is a Tīrtha; control of the organs of sense and action is a Tīrtha; compassion for all living beings is a Tīrtha; straightforwardness is a Tīrtha.

Religious gifting is a Tīrtha; self-restraint is a Tīrtha; contentedness is mentioned as a Tīrtha; celibacy is the greatest Tīrtha; speaking pleasing words is a Tīrtha.

Knowledge is a Tīrtha; courage (fortitude) is a Tīrtha; penance is cited as a Tīrtha; the absolute purity of the mind is the holiest of all holy Tīrthas.

SB-35. Holy ablution is not the mere drenching of the body in water. He who has the purificatory bath of mental control, is really the one who has had his holy ablution; he is (really) clean; he has removed all the impurities of the mind.

One who is covetous, slanderous, cruel, a hypocrite and sensualist is sinful and dirty, even if he takes a plunge in all the sacred waters.

A man does not become free from impurities only by doing away with the bodily dirt. If the mental dirt is wiped away, one becomes internally pure.

## \|\| 1.6.36 \|\|

*jāyaṃte ca mriyaṃte ca jaleṣveva jalaukasaḥ \|*  
*na ca gacchaṃti te svargamaviśuddhamanomalāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Aquatic beings are born and die in water. But they do not go to heaven because their mental impurities have not been cleansed.

## \|\| 1.6.37 \|\|

*viṣayeṣvati saṃrāgo mānaso mala ucyate \|*  
*teṣveva hi virāgo sya nairmalyaṃ samudāhṛtam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Too much of attachment to sensual objects is called mental impurity. Non-attachment to them is cited as freedom from impurities.

## \|\| 1.6.38 \|\|

*cittamaṃtargataṃ duṣṭaṃ tīrthasnānānna śuddhyati \|*  
*śataśotha jalairdhautaṃ surābhāṃḍamivāśuci \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If the mind within is defiled, it does not become purified by taking a holy dip in sacred waters. It is impure like a pot of toddy washed hundreds of times in water.

## \|\| 1.6.39 \|\|

*dānamijyātapaḥśaucaṃ tīrthasevā śrutaṃ tathā \|*  
*sarvāṇyetānyatīrthāni yadi bhāvo na nirmalaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If the mental predilection is not pure, all these, viz. liberal gifts, sacrifice, penance, cleanliness, pilgrimage and learning, become non-Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.6.40 \|\|

*nigṛhīteṃdriyagrāmo yatraiva ca vasennaraḥ \|*  
*tatra tasya kurukṣetraṃ naimiṣaṃ puṣkarāṇi ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Wherever a man who has curbed all his organs of sense and action lives, there he has his (holy places like) Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa, Puṣkara etc.

## \|\| 1.6.41 \|\|

*jñānapūte jñānajale rāgadveṣamalāpahe \|*  
*yaḥ snāti mānase tīrthe sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He who takes his holy bath in the mental holy spot that is cleansed with perfect knowledge, that has meditation for its waters and that removes the dirt of attachment and hatred, attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.6.42 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ devi mānasaṃ tīrthalakṣaṇam \|*  
*bhaumānāmapi tīrthānāṃ puṇyatve kāraṇaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. These characteristics of the mental holy places have been recounted to you, O noble lady. Listen to the cause that brings about sanctity to worldly holy spots.

## \|\| 1.6.43 \|\|

*yathā śarīrasyoddeśāḥ kecinmedhyatamāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*tathā pṛthivyāmuddeśāḥ kecitpuṇyatamāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Just as there are certain excellent parts of the body considered very holy and pure, so also some regions of the earth are considered most meritorious.

## \|\| 1.6.44 \|\|

*prabhāvādadbhutādbhūmeḥ salilasya ca tejasaḥ \|*  
*parigrahānmunīnāṃ ca tīrthānāṃ puṇyatā smṛtā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The meritoriousness of holy spots is considered to be a result of the mysterious influence of the ground, of the water and of the fire thereof as well as of the backing and acceptance (as holy) by sages.

## \|\| 1.6.45 \|\|

*tasmādbhaumeṣu tīrtheṣu mānaseṣu ca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*ubhayeṣvapi yaḥ snāti sa yāti paramāṃ gatima \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hence he who takes his holy bath in both the holy spots, i.e., the worldly holy spots and the mental holy spots, attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.6.46 \|\|

*anupoṣya trirātrāṇi tīrthānyanabhigamya ca \|*  
*adattvā kāṃcanaṃ gāśca daridro nāma jāyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. A man becomes poor by not observing fast for three whole nights, by not resorting to the holy spots and by not giving gold and cows.

## \|\| 1.6.47 \|\|

*agniṣṭomādibhiryajñairiṣṭvā vipuladakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*na tatphalamavāpnoti tīrthabhigamanena yat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The benefit that one obtains by undertaking pilgrimages to holy spots is not obtained by performing holy sacrifices including Agniṣṭoma etc., along with liberal monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.6.48 \|\|

*yasya hastau ca pādau ca manaścaiva susaṃyatam \|*  
*vidyā tapaśca kīrtiśca sa tīrthaphalamaśnute \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He whose hands, feet and mind are well-controlled, he who possesses learning, penance and reputation enjoys the benefit of a holy spot.

## \|\| 1.6.49 \|\|

*pratigrahādupāvṛttaḥ saṃtuṣṭo yenakenacit \|*  
*ahaṃkāra vimuktaśca sa tīrthaphalamaśnute \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. One who desists from accepting monetary gifts, one who is contented with whatever accrues to him and one who is devoid of egotistic tendencies enjoys the benefit of pilgrimage to holy spots.

## \|\| 1.6.50 \|\|

*adaṃbhako nirāraṃbho laghvāhāro jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*vimuktasarvasaṃgairyaḥ sa tīrthaphalamaśnute \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. One who is free from religious hypocrisy, one who never undertakes (unholy activities), one who eats but very limited quantities, one who has conquered the organs of sense and action and one who is completely free from affectionate attachments enjoys the benefit of the pilgrimage to holy spots.

## \|\| 1.6.51 \|\|

*akopano'malamatiḥ satyavādī dṛḍhavrataḥ \|*  
*ātmopamaśca bhūteṣu satīrthaphalamaśnute \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. One who is free from anger, one whose intellect is free from impurities, one who is invariably truthful in utterance, one who strictly adheres to holy vows and observances, one who considers all living beings on an equal footing with one’s self, enjoys the benefit of pilgrimage to holy spots.

## \|\| 1.6.52 \|\|

*tīrthānyanusarandhīraḥ śraddadhānaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtapāpo viśuddhyeta kiṃ punaḥ śuddhakarmakṛt \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If one visits holy spots with an understanding of what is righteous and what is not, if one has sincerity, full faith, mental courage and concentration, he becomes pure even if he perpetrates sins, and still more pure becomes one who regularly performs holy rites.

## \|\| 1.6.53 \|\|

*tiryagyoni na vai gacchetkudeśe naiva jāyate \|*  
*na duḥkhī syātsvargabhākca mokṣopāyaṃ ca viṃdati \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He is not reborn as a brute; he does not take birth in dismal godforsaken places; he never becomes miserable; he attains heaven and gets the means of salvation.

## \|\| 1.6.54 \|\|

*aśraddadhānaḥ pāpātmā nāstiko'cchinnasaṃśayaḥ \|*  
*hetuniṣṭhaśca paṃcaite na tīrthaphalabhāginaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. A person who has no faith, a sinful soul, an atheist, one who is constantly in doubt and one who is too much a rationalist—these five never attain the benefit of pilgrimage to holy spots.

## \|\| 1.6.55 \|\|

*tīrthāni ca yathoktena vidhinā saṃcaraṃti ye \|*  
*sarvadvaṃdvasahā dhīrāste narāḥ svargabhāginaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Those men who undertake pilgrimage to holy spots in accordance with the injunctions; those who patiently endure all mutually opposed pairs (of pain, pleasure etc.), attain heaven.

## \|\| 1.6.56-57 \|\|

*tīrthayātrāṃ cikīrṣuḥ prāgvidhāyopoṣaṇaṃ gṛhe \|*  
*gaṇeśaṃ ca pitṝnviprānsādhūñchaktyā prapūjya ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kṛtapāraṇako hṛṣṭo gacchenniyamadhṛkpunaḥ \|*  
*āgatyābhyarcya pitṝnyathoktaphalabhāgbhavet \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. One who is desirous of undertaking a pilgrimage should it the outset observe fast at home. He should then adore and honour Gaṇeśa, the manes, Brāhmaṇas, holy men in accordance with his ability. After taking food by way of concluding the observance of fast, he should joyously follow the regulations. After returning, he should worship the manes. He will then derive the benefits as mentioned.

## \|\| 1.6.58-59 \|\|

*na parīkṣyo dvijastīrtheṣvannārthī bhojya eva ca \|*  
*saktubhiḥ piṃḍadānaṃ ca caruṇā pāyasena ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kartavyamṛṣibhirdṛṣṭaṃ piṇyākena guḍena ca \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ tatra prakartavyamarghyāvāhanavarjitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. In holy spots, Brāhmaṇas should not be subjected to scrutiny; whoever comes seeking food should be fed. The offering of the balls to the manes shall be in the form of Saktu (a preparation from barley flour), Cam (rice, barley and pulse boiled) or milk pudding; Śrāddha should be performed, as observed by the sages, through oil-cake and jaggery. Arghya and Āvāhana (invocation and reception) can be omitted.

## \|\| 1.6.60 \|\|

*akālepyathavā kāle tīrthe śrāddhaṃ ca tarpaṇam \|*  
*avilaṃbena kartavyaṃ naiva vighnaṃ samācaret \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Whether at the proper time or not, Śrāddha and Tarpaṇa should be performed without delay. There should not be hindrance in the middle.

## \|\| 1.6.61 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ prāpya prasaṃgena snānaṃ tīrthe samācaret \|*  
*snānajaṃ phalamāpnoti tīrthayātrāśritaṃ sa ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. If anyone reaches a holy spot casually (when on some other duty or work) and takes the holy bath, he may very well derive the benefit of the bath but not that of pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.6.62 \|\|

*nṛṇāṃ pāpakṛtāṃ tīrthe pāpasya śamanaṃ bhavet \|*  
*yathoktaṃ phaladaṃ tīrthaṃ bhavecchraddhātmanāṃ nṛṇām \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. There will be suppression of the sin of persons committing sins in a holy place. In the case of men having faith, the holy spot shall bestow the benefit as mentioned.

## \|\| 1.6.63 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ sa labhate yaḥ parāthaṃ ca gacchati \|*  
*ardhaṃ tīrthaphalaṃ tasya yaḥ prasaṃgena gacchati \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He who goes to a holy spot on behalf of others derives one-sixteenth of the merit. He who goes there casually gets half of the merit.

## \|\| 1.6.64 \|\|

*kuśa pratikṛtiṃ kṛtvā tīrthavāriṇi majjayet \|*  
*majjayecca yamuddiśya soṣṭamāṃśaṃ labheta vai \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. A pilgrim should make an effigy (of the persons whom he represents) and take the holy dip in the sacred waters. That person on whose behalf this holy bath is undertaken, obtains one-eighth of the merit.

## \|\| 1.6.65 \|\|

*tīrthopavāsaḥ kartavyaḥ śiraso muṃḍanaṃ tathā \|*  
*śirogatāni pāpāni yāṃti muṃḍanato yataḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Holy fast should be undertaken in a holy spot. The hairs on the head should be shaved off because thereby the sins of the head vanish.

## \|\| 1.6.66 \|\|

*yadahni tīrthaprāptiḥ syāttatohnaḥ pūrvavāsare \|*  
*upavāsastu kartavyaḥ prāptāhni śrāddhado bhavet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The fast is to be observed on the day prior to the arrival at the holy spot. On the day of arrival he should perform the rite of Śrāddha.

## \|\| 1.6.67 \|\|

*tīrthaprasaṃgāttīrthāṃgamapyuktaṃ tvatpuromayā \|*  
*svargasādhanamevaitanmokṣopāyaśca vai bhavet \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. While enumerating the holy spots the subsidiary activities too were recounted to you by me. This shall be conducive to the attainment of heaven and a means of salvation too.

## \|\| 1.6.68 \|\|

*kāśīkāṃtī ca māyākhyā tvayodhyādvāravatyapi \|*  
*mathurāvaṃtikā caitāḥ sapta puryotra mokṣadāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. These seven cities are the bestowers of salvation here itself: Kāśī, Kāntī (Kāñcī), Māyā, Ayodhyā, Dvārāvatī, Mathurā and Avantikā.

## \|\| 1.6.69 \|\|

*śrīśailo mokṣadaḥ sarvaḥ kedāropi tato'dhikaḥ \|*  
*śrīśailāccāpi kedārātprayāgaṃ mokṣadaṃ param \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The entire Śrī Śaila (the area extending over 84 Yojanas) bestows salvation. Kedāra is superior to it. Prayāga is a greater bestower of salvation than Śrī Śaila and Kedāra.

## \|\| 1.6.70 \|\|

*prayāgādapi tīrthāgryādavimuktaṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*yathāvimukte nirvāṇaṃ na tathākvāpyasaṃśayam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Avimukta excels Prayāga, the foremost among holy spots. Undoubtedly nowhere else can salvation be acquired as in Avimukta.

## \|\| 1.6.71 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The other holy spots of salvation make Kāśī accessible. If one does not get released (from Saṃsāra) even after reaching Kāśī, he cannot get salvation even if he visits millions of other holy spots.

## \|\| 1.6.72 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. In this context, I shall mention an ancient mythological legend as recounted to a Brāhmaṇa Śivaśarman by the attendants of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.6.73-74 \|\|

*anyāni muktikṣetrāṇi kāśīprāptikarāṇi ca \|*  
*kāśīṃ dhyāyamimaṃ śrutvā naro niyatamānasaḥ \|*  
*śrāvayitvā dvijāṃścāpi śraddhābhaktisamanvitān \|\| 73 \|\|*

*kṣatriyāndharmaniratānvaiśyānsanmārgavartinaḥ \|*  
*śūdrāndvijeṣu bhaktāṃśca niṣpāpo jāyate dvijaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. By listening to this Tīrthādhyāya with a well-controlled mind and by narrating it to Brāhmaṇas endowed with faith and devotion, to Kratriyas engrossed in pious practices, to Vaiśyas following the path of the good and to Śūdras devoted to Brāhmaṇas, a Brāhmaṇa becomes rid of sins.

## Chapter 7 - The Seven Holy Cities

## \|\| 1.7.1 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*mathurāyāṃ dvijaḥ kaścidabhūdbhūdevasattamaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro mahātejāḥ śivaśarmeti viśrutaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Agastya said:

1\. There was a certain Brāhmaṇa, the most excellent of all Brāhmaṇas, in Mathurā. His son of great refulgence is well-known by the name Śivaśarman.

## \|\| 1.7.2-7 \|\|

*adhītyavedānvidhivadarthaṃ vijñāya tattvataḥ \|*  
*paṭhitvā dharmaśāstrāṇi purāṇānyadhigamya ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*aṃgānyabhyasya tarkāṃśca pariloḍya samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*mīmāṃsādvayamālokya dhanurvedaṃ vigāhya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*āyurvedaṃ vicāryāpi nāṭyavede kṛtaśramaḥ \|*  
*arthaśāstrāṇyanekāni prāpyāśvagajaceṣṭitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kalāsu ca kṛtābhyāso mantraśāstravicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhāṣāśca nānā deśānāṃ lipīrjñātvā videśajāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*arthānupārjya dharmeṇa bhuktvā bhogānyadṛcchayā \|*  
*utpādya putrānsuguṇāṃstebhyo hyarthaṃ vibhajya ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yauvanaṃ gatvaraṃ jñātvā jarāṃ dṛṣṭvāśritāṃ śrutim \|*  
*cintāmavāpa mahatī śivaśarmā dvijottamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

2-7. The Brāhmaṇa Śivaśarman duly studied the Vedas and comprehended the meanings of the texts fully. He read Dharmaśāstra texts and understood the Purānas. He learnt the Aṅgas (ancillary subjects), through discussion and pondered over the texts in logic, went through the two (Pūrva and Uttara) Mīmāṃsā systems and mastered Dhanurveda (‘science of archery’). He worked hard in the art of dance; he acquired (mastery) in many texts on political economy; he comprehended the behaviour of horses and elephants; he practised the various types of arts; he became an expert in the Science of Mantras (magical and mystical spells); he learnt the languages of the different countries and the scripts of alien lands. Through pious and legitimate means, he earned wealth. He enjoyed pleasures as much as he liked. He begot sons of good qualities and divided his assets among them. He then realised that youth is of fleeting nature. He found that old age reached his ears (in the form of greying hairs). Then the excellent Brāhmaṇa felt great anxiety.

## \|\| 1.7.8 \|\|

*paṭhato me gataḥ kālastathopārjayato dhanam \|*  
*nārādhito maheśānaḥ karmanirmūlanakṣamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He thought: ‘My time was spent in reading and learning; then in earning wealth. Lord Maheśāna who is capable of eradicating all karmas was not adored and propitiated.

## \|\| 1.7.9 \|\|

*na mayā toṣito viṣṇuḥ sarvapāpaharo hariḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmaprado nṛṇāṃ gaṇeśo nārcito mayā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Viṣṇu, Hari, the destroyer of all sins, was not pleased by me; Gaṇeśa, the bestower of all the desires of men, was not adored by me.

## \|\| 1.7.10 \|\|

*tamastomaharaḥ sūryo nārci to vai mayā kvacit \|*  
*mahāmāyā jagaddhātrī na dhyātā bhavabaṃdhahṛt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Sun-god, the destroyer of masses of darkness, was not worshipped by me anywhere. Mahāmāyā, the creator and sustainer of the universe and the destroyer of worldly bondage, was not meditated upon.

## \|\| 1.7.11 \|\|

*na prīṇitā mayā devā yajñaiḥ sarvaiḥ samṛddhidāḥ \|*  
*tulasīvana śuśrūṣā na kṛtā pāpaśāṃtaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Devas, the bestowers of all prosperity, were not propitiated by all types of Yajñas. Service was not rendered to groves of Tulasī plants for the sake of quelling sins.

## \|\| 1.7.12 \|\|

*na mayā tarpitā viprā mṛṣṭānnairmadhurai rasaiḥ \|*  
*ihāpi ca paratrāpi vipadāmanutārakāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Brāhmaṇas who are the saviours from adversities here and hereafter, have not been rendered satisfied by me through savoury cooked rice and sweet juices.

## \|\| 1.7.13 \|\|

*bahupuṣpaphalopetāḥ succhāyāḥ snigdhapallavāḥ \|*  
*pathi nāropitā vṛkṣā ihāmutraphalapradāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Trees with plenty of blossoms and fruits, smooth glossy sprouts and ample shade have not been planted by me, an act which could have yielded fruit (viz., happiness) here and hereafter.

## \|\| 1.7.14 \|\|

*dukūlaiḥ svānukūlaiśca colaiḥ pratyaṃgabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*nālaṃkṛtāḥ suvāsinya ihāmutrasuvāsadāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Noble married women enjoying conjugal bliss, who are capable of providing excellent places of residence here and hereafter have not been adorned (by me) with ornaments for every limb, silk clothes and bodices befitting them.

## \|\| 1.7.15 \|\|

*dvijāya norvarā dattā yamalokanivāriṇī \|*  
*suvarṇaṃ na suvarṇāya dattaṃ duritahṛtparam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A fertile land (the grant of which) could have warded off (the necessity to go to) Yama’s region has not been gifted to Brāhmaṇas. Gold that utterly removes sins, has not been given to a man of high caste (i.e. Brāhmaṇa)

## \|\| 1.7.16 \|\|

*nālaṃkṛtā savatsā gauḥ pātrāya pratipāditā \|*  
*iha pāpāpahaṃtryāśu saptajanmasukhāvahā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A cow with her calf that removes sins here quickly and accords happiness in the next seven births, has not been bedecked and gifted to a deserving person.

## \|\| 1.7.17 \|\|

*ṛṇāpanuttaye mātuḥ kārito na jalāśayaḥ \|*  
*nātithistoṣitaḥ kvāpi svargamārgapradarśakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. No pond, well or lake has been dug in order to wipe off the indebtedness to our mother. No guest, who could have shown the pathway to heaven, has been pleased (by me).

## \|\| 1.7.18 \|\|

*chatropānatkuṃḍikāśca nādhvagāya samarpitāḥ \|*  
*yāsyataḥ saṃyaminyāṃ hi svargamārgasukhapradāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. No umbrella, pair of sandals, and water pot have been given as gift to a pedestrian, which could have afforded (me) pleasure along the pathway to heaven or while proceeding to Saṃyaminī (i.e. the region of Yama).

## \|\| 1.7.19 \|\|

*na ca kanyāvivāhārthaṃ vasu kvāpi mayārpitam \|*  
*iha saukhyasamṛddhyarthaṃ divyakanyārpakaṃ divi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I have never given monetary help to anyone for celebrating the marriage of (his) daughter, which gift could have increased the happiness here and could have provided one with a celestial virgin (hereafter).

## \|\| 1.7.20 \|\|

*na vājapeyāvabhṛthe snāto lobhavaśādaham \|*  
*iha janmani cānyasminbahumṛṣṭānnapānade \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Out of covetousness, I did not perform the Vājapeya sacrifice which could have accorded plenty of savoury food and sweet beverages in the course of this birth as well as in the next. Nor did I take the holy valedictory ablution therein.

## \|\| 1.7.21 \|\|

*na mayā sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ kṛtvā devālayaṃ śubhama \|*  
*yasminsaṃsthāpite liṃgo viśvaṃ saṃsthāpitaṃ bhavet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I did not build any splendid temple and install a Liṅga (therein). Had that Liṅga been installed the entire universe would have been stabilized.

## \|\| 1.7.22 \|\|

*viṣṇorāyatanaṃ naiva kṛtaṃ sarvasamṛddhidam \|*  
*na ca sūryagaṇeśānāṃ pratimāḥ kāritā mayā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A holy shrine of Viṣṇu that bestows all prosperities has not been built by me; nor have the idols of the Sun and Gaṇeśa been installed by me.

## \|\| 1.7.23 \|\|

*na gaurī na mahālakṣmīścitrepi parilekhite \|*  
*pratimākaraṇe caiṣāṃ na kurūpo na durbhagaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Neither Gaurī nor Mahālakṣmī has been painted even in a picture. If the idols of these are made (the man) never becomes ugly or destitute.

## \|\| 1.7.24 \|\|

*susūkṣmāṇi vicitrāṇi nojjvalānyaṃbarāṇyapi \|*  
*samarpitāni viprebhyo divyāṃbara samṛddhaye \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. For the purpose of obtaining plenty of divine garments, I have not given as gifts fine and glamorous clothes of various colours to Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.7.25 \|\|

*na tilāśca ghṛtenāktāḥ susamiddhe hutāśane \|*  
*hutā vai mantrapūtāśca sarvapāpāpanuttaye \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. For the cleansing of all sins, gingelly seeds soaked in ghee have not been consigned to the well-kindled holy fire after sanctifying them with Mantras.

## \|\| 1.7.26 \|\|

*śrīsūktaṃ pāvamānī ca brāhmaṇo maṃḍalāni ca \|*  
*japtaṃ puruṣasūktaṃ na pāpāri śatarudriyam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I have not performed the Japa of (Vedic hymns like) Śrīsūkta, Pāvamanī Ṛks, Brāhmaṇas, Maṇḍalas, Puruṣasūkta and Śatarudriya, the remover of sins.

## \|\| 1.7.27 \|\|

*aśvattha sevā na kṛtā tyaktvā cārkaṃ trayodaśīm \|*  
*sadyaḥ pāpaharā sā hi na rātrau na bhṛgordine \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Leaving off Sundays and thirteenth lunar days I have not served (attended upon) the holy fig tree. Indeed it promptly removes sins but not during the night or Fridays.

## \|\| 1.7.28 \|\|

*śayanīyaṃ na cotsṛṣṭaṃ mṛdulā ca pratūlikā \|*  
*dīpīdarpaṇasaṃyu्ktaṃ sarvabhogasamṛddhidam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Soft beds with costly cotton have not been gifted along with mirrors and lamps, which are capable of according all prosperities and pleasures.

## \|\| 1.7.29-30 \|\|

*ajāśvamahiṣī meṣī dāsī kṛṣṇājinaṃ tilāḥ \|*  
*sakaraṃbhāstoyakuṃbhā nāsanaṃ mṛdupāduke \|\| 29 \|\|*

*pādābhyaṃgaṃ dīpadānaṃ prapādānaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*vyajanaṃ vastratāṃbūlaṃ tathānyanmukhavāsakṛta \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. None of these things has been given as gifts by me: goat, horse, buffalo, sheep, slave girl, deer’s skin, gingelly seeds, water pots along with curd-soaked wheat flour, seat, soft sandals, massage of the feet, lamp as gift, special arrangement for drinking, water-sheds for pedestrians, fans, garments, betel-leaves etc. together with other things rendering the mouth and breath fragrant.

## \|\| 1.7.31-32 \|\|

*nityaśrāddhaṃ bhūtabaliṃ tathā'tithi samarcanam \|*  
*viśantyanyāni dattvā ca praśasyāni yamālaye \|\| 31 \|\|*

*na yamaṃ yamadūtāṃśca nayāmīrapi yātanāḥ \|*  
*paśyanti te puṇayabhājo naitaccāpi kṛtaṃ mayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. The daily Śrāddha offering, oblations to the spirits or living beings, worship of guests were not performed and other praiseworthy things were not given. If one gives all these, one does not enter the region of Yama, nor does one see Yama, his messengers or the torturers in the region of Yama. They (such persons) are meritorious. But I have not done any of these things.

## \|\| 1.7.33 \|\|

*kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇādīni tathā naktavratāni ca \|*  
*śarīraśuddhikārīṇi na kṛtāni kvacinmayā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Kṛcchra, Cāndrāyaṇa and other expiatory rites, the observance of fast by day and a meal at night etc., cause purity of the body. But these were not at all performed by me.

## \|\| 1.7.34 \|\|

*gavāhnikaṃ ca nodattaṃ kokaṃḍūtirna vai kṛtā \|*  
*noddhṛtā paṃkamagnā gaurgolokasukhadāyinī \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The daily mouthfuls of fodder to the cows were not given; I have not scratched the cows for removing the itching sensation; no cow stuck in the mud has been lifted up by me—an act that would have bestowed happiness on me in the Goloka (Region of Cows).

## \|\| 1.7.35 \|\|

*nārthinaḥ prārthitairarthaiḥ kṛtārthā hi mayā kṛtāḥ \|*  
*dehidehīti jalpāko bhaviṣyāmyanyajanmani \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Suppliants have not been rendered satisfied by me through the objects requested for by them. Surely, in the next birth, I shall have to roam about saying, ‘Give! Give!’

## \|\| 1.7.36 \|\|

*na vedā na ca śāstrāṇi nārdho dārā na no sutaḥ \|*  
*na kṣetraṃ na ca harmyādi māyāṃtamanuyāsyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Neither the Vedas nor the scriptural texts, neither riches nor the wife nor the son, neither the field nor the mansion can take one to the end of Māyā.’

## \|\| 1.7.37-38 \|\|

*śivaśarmeti saṃciṃtya buddhiṃ saṃdhāya sarvataḥ \|*  
*niścikāya manasyevaṃ bhavetkṣemataraṃ mama \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yāvatsvasthosti me deho yāvanneṃdriyaviklavaḥ \|*  
*tāvatsvaśreyasāṃ hetuṃ tīrthayātrāṃ karomyaham \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Śivaśarman thought thus after racking his brains fully. Ultimately he decided thus in his mind: ‘If this is done, it shall be conducive to my welfare. As long as the body is hale and hearty, as long as there is no deficiency in the organs of sense and action, it behoves me to undertake a pilgrimage that can bring about my eternal welfare.’

## \|\| 1.7.39-41 \|\|

*dināni paṃcapāṇyevamativāhya gṛho dvijaḥ \|*  
*śubhe tithau śubhe vāre śubhalagnabale dvijaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ prātaḥ śrāddhaṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*gaṇeśānbrāhmaṇānnatvā bhuktvā prasthitavānsudhīḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*iti niścitya nirvāṇapadaniḥśreṇikāṃ parām \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva jaṃtūnāṃ tatra saṃsthitikāriṇām \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. The Brāhmaṇa spent five or six days in the house thus. On an auspicious lunar day, when the week day was good and when the Lagna was propitious, the Brāhmaṇa observed fast for the night and performed Śrāddha in the morning. He bowed down to the leaders of the attendants (of Śiva) and the Brāhmaṇas. He came to the decision that pilgrimage is the highest ladder leading to the state of liberation and that it retains all the creatures there. Thereafter the wise Brāhmaṇa took his food and started.

## \|\| 1.7.42-43 \|\|

*atha paṃthānamākramya kiyaṃtamapi sa dvijaḥ \|*  
*muhūrtaṃ pathi viśramyāciṃtayatprākkva yāmyaham \|\| 42 \|\|*

*bhuvi tīrthānyanekāni lolamāyuścalaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saptapurīryāyāṃ sarvatīrthāni tatra yat \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. The Brāhmaṇa went some distance along the way. He then rested on the road for a short while and thought: ‘Where shall I go first? There are many holy places on the earth. The span of life is unsteady. The mind is fickle. So I shall go to the seven (holy) cities because all the holy spots and shrines are present there.’

## \|\| 1.7.44-45 \|\|

*ayodhyāṃ ca purīṃ gatvā sarayūmavagāhya ca \|*  
*tattattīrtheṣu saṃtarpya pitṝnpiṃḍapradānataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*paṃcarātramuṣitvā tu brāhmaṇānparibhojya ca \|*  
*prayāgamagamadviprastīrtharājaṃ suhṛṣṭavat \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. He went to the city of Ayodhyā and took his holy bath in Sarayū. He propitiated the manes by offering balls of rice in the different holy spots. There he stayed for five nights and fed Brāhmaṇas. Thereafter the delighted Brāhmaṇa went to Prayāga, the king of holy places.

## \|\| 1.7.46 \|\|

*sitā'site saricchreṣṭhe yatrāstāṃ suradurlabhe \|*  
*yatrāpluto naraḥ pāpaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. That is the place where the two excellent rivers of black and white colours, viz., Yamunā and Gaṅgā are present. They are inaccessible even to Suras. By taking his holy ablution there, (even) a sinner realizes the highest Brahman.

## \|\| 1.7.47 \|\|

*kṣetraṃ prajāpateḥ puṇyaṃ sarveṣāmeva durlabham \|*  
*labhyate puṇyasaṃbhārairnānyathārthasya rāśibhiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. That is the holy place of Prajāpati inaccessible to all. Only through merits accumulated, is it obtained and not otherwise or through heaps of wealth.

## \|\| 1.7.48 \|\|

*damayaṃtīṃ kaliṃ kālaṃ kaliṃdatanayāṃ śubhām \|*  
*āgatya militā yatra puṇyā svargataraṃgiṇī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. It is the place where the sacred celestial river (Gaṅgā) comes and meets the splendid river (Yamunā) having its source in the Kalinḍa Mountain, which suppresses (the evils of) the Kali age and the god of Death.

## \|\| 1.7.49 \|\|

*prakṛṣṭaṃ sarvayāgebhyaḥ prayāgamiti gīyate \|*  
*yajvanāṃ punarāvṛttirna prayāgārdravarṣmaṇām \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The word Prayāga means that which is superior to all Yāgas (sacrifices). Those who perform sacrifices there and get their bodies made wet by the river are not reborn.

## \|\| 1.7.50 \|\|

*yatra sthitaḥ svayaṃ sākṣācchūlaṭaṃko maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatrāplutānāṃ jaṃtūnāṃ mokṣavartmopadeśakaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The trident and axe wielding Maheśvara is directly present there himself. It is he who points out the path of salvation to the living beings who take their holy dip there.

## \|\| 1.7.51 \|\|

*tatrā'kṣayyavaṭo'pyasti saptapātālamūlavān \|*  
*pralayepi yamāruhya mṛkaṃḍatanayo'vasat \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. There is an Akṣayya (‘Never-fading’) eternal holy banyan tree there, with its roots going deep into the seven nether worlds. At the time of the ultimate annihilation, the son of Mṛkaṇḍu (i.e., Mārkaṇḍeya, the sage) climbed it and stayed (free from annihilation).

## \|\| 1.7.52 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbho vijñeyaḥ sa sākṣādvaṭarūpadhṛk \|*  
*tatsamīpe dvijānbhaktyā saṃbhojyākṣaya puṇyabhāk \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. That should be known as Hiraṇyagarbha himself assuming the form of the banyan tree. The devotee, who feeds Brāhmaṇas with faith and devotion near it, attains eternal merit.

## \|\| 1.7.53 \|\|

*yatra lakṣmīpatiḥ sākṣādvaikuṃṭhādetya mānavān \|*  
*śrīmādhavasvarūpeṇa nayedviṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The Consort of Lakṣmī directly comes there and takes men to the great region of Viṣṇu in the form of Śrīmādhava.

## \|\| 1.7.54 \|\|

*śrutibhiḥ paripaṭhyete sitā'sita saridvare \|*  
*tatrāplutāṃ gāhyamṛtaṃ bhavaṃtīti viniścitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The excellent black and white rivers (Yamunā-Gaṅgā) are mentioned in the Vedas. It is certain that those who get their limbs submerged therein attain immortality.

## \|\| 1.7.55-57 \|\|

*śivalokādbrahmalokādumālokavarātpunaḥ \|*  
*kumāralokādvaikuṃṭhātsatyalokātsamaṃtataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|tapojanamaharbhyaśca sarve svarlokavāsinaḥ \|*  
*bhuvolokācca bhūrlokānnāgalokāttathā'khilāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

*acalā himavanmukhyāḥ kalpavṛkṣādayo nagāḥ \|*  
*snātuṃ māghe samāyāṃti prayāgamaruṇodaye \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. Residents from all these worlds, viz., those of Śiva, Brahmā, Umā, Kumāra and Lokas like Vaikuṇṭha, Satyaloka, Tapoloka, Jana, Mahar, Bhuvaḥ, Bhū, all the Nāgalokas, all the heaven-dwellers and the mountains the chief of whom is Himvān as well as the wish-yielding Kalpa and other trees come to Prayāga at dawn in the month of Māgha, in order to take the holy bath.

## \|\| 1.7.58 \|\|

*digaṃganāḥ prārthayaṃti yatprayāgānilānapi \|*  
*tepi naḥ pāvayiṣyaṃti kiṃ kurmaḥ paṃgavo vayam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The female deities of the quarters request the winds blowing from Prayāga saying, “Even they (the winds) will sanctify us. What shall we do? We are lame.”

## \|\| 1.7.59 \|\|

*aśvamedhādiyāgāśca prayāgasya rajaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tulitaṃ brahmaṇā pūrvaṃ na te tadrajasā samāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Formerly horse-sacrifice and other sacrifices were weighed against the dust particles at Prayāga by Brahmā. They (sacrifices) were not equal to the dust particles.

## \|\| 1.7.60 \|\|

*majjāgatāni pāpāni bahujanmārjitānyapi \|*  
*prayāganāmaśravaṇātkṣīyaṃte'tīva vihvalam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The sins embedded in the marrow accumulated over many births become agitated on just hearing the name of Prayāga and get destroyed.

## \|\| 1.7.61 \|\|

*dharmatīrthamidaṃ samyagarthatīrthamidaṃ param \|*  
*kāmikaṃ tīrthametacca mokṣatīrthamidaṃ dhruvam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. This is a perfect Dharmatīrtha. This is a great Arthatīrtha; it is a Kāmikatīrtha; it is certainly a Mokṣatīrtha. (That is, it is conducive to the accomplishment of all the four great human aims.)

## \|\| 1.7.62 \|\|

*brahmahatyādi pāpāni tāvadgarjaṃti dehiṣu \|*  
*yāvanmajjaṃti no māghe prayāge pāpahāriṇi \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Brāhmaṇa-slaughter and other sins of embodied beings roar and boast of their powers only so long as they do not take their bath in the month of Māgha at Prayāga, the annihilator of sins.

## \|\| 1.7.63 \|\|

*tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ \|*  
*etadyatpaṭhyate vede tatprayāgaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “Wise men always see the greatest region of Viṣṇu”: This is frequently referred to in the Vedas. That is Prayāga itself since it is the giver of salvation.

## \|\| 1.7.64 \|\|

*sarasvatī rajo rūpā tamorūpā kaliṃdajā \|*  
*sattvarūpā ca gaṃgātra nayaṃti brahmanirguṇam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The river Sarasvatī is of the nature of Rajas; the river Yamunā is of the nature of Tamas and the river Gaṅgā here is of the nature of Sattva. All the three together lead (the devotees) to Brahman (the Absolute) which is free from attributes (Rajas etc.)

## \|\| 1.7.65 \|\|

*iyaṃ veṇīhi niḥśreṇī brahmaṇo vartmayāsyataḥ \|*  
*jaṃtorviśuddhadehasya śraddhā'śraddhāplutasya ca \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. This confluence (of the three rivers) acts as the ladder to the path of Brahman unto a living being whose body is sanctified, whether he takes the holy dip with faith or otherwise or even when he is forcibly dipped into it, and hence proceeds along the path of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.7.66 \|\|

*kāśīti kācidabalā bhuvaneṣu rūḍhā lolārka keśavavilolavilocanā \|\| \|*  
*taddoryugaṃ ca varaṇāsiriyaṃ tadīyā veṇīti yā'tra gaditā'kṣayaśarmabhūmiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. There is a certain noble lady renowned in the worlds as Kāśī. Eager and enthusiastic Arka (Sun-god) and Keśava constitute her tremulous eyes. Varaṇā and Asi are her two arms. This confluence is her Veṇī (unornamented single braid of hair). This Kāśī is proclaimed as the source of everlasting bliss.

## \|\| 1.7.67 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*sudharmiṇi guṇāṃstasya kotra varṇayituṃ kṣamaḥ \|*  
*tīrtharājaprayāgasya tīrthaiḥ saṃsevitasya ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

Agastya said:

67\. O pious lady, who is competent to describe the good qualities of Prayāga, the king of holy places, served and resorted to by the other holy spots?

## \|\| 1.7.68 \|\|

*pāpināṃ yāni pāpāni prasahya kṣālitānyaho \|*  
*tacchuddhyai sevyate tīrthaiḥ prayāgamadhikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. It is resorted to by the other holy Tīrthas in order to get rid of the accumulated sins of the sinners completely washed of (and left behind in it) by them. Hence Prayāga is superior (to them).

## \|\| 1.7.69 \|\|

*prayāgasya guṇānjñātvā śivaśarmā dvijaḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*tatra māghamuṣtvā'tha prāpa vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Having come to know the good qualities of Prayāga, the wise Brāhmaṇa, Śivaśarman, stayed there for the whole of the month of Māgha and then went to the city of Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 1.7.70-71 \|\|

*praveśa eva saṃvīkṣya sa dehalivināyakam \|*  
*anvaliṃpattato bhaktyā sājyasiṃdūrakardamaiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*nivedyamodakānpaṃca vaṃcayaṃtaṃ nijaṃ janam \|*  
*mahopasargavargebhyastatoṃ'taḥ kṣetramāviśat \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. At the entrance itself he saw Dehalī Vināyaka (Lord Gaṇeśa at the threshold) who protects his people (devotees) from great obstacles. With great devotion, he smeared (the idol) with saffron paste mixed with ghee and offered five Modakas (sweetmeats) as Naivedya. Then he entered the inner shrine.

## \|\| 1.7.72 \|\|

*āgatya dṛṣṭvā maṇikarṇikāyāmudagvahāṃ svargataraṃgiṇīṃ saḥ \|*  
*saṃkṣīṇapuṇyetarapuṇyakarmaṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ gaṇaiḥ sthāṇugaṇairivāvṛtām \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. After entering, he saw the celestial river that flows towards the north at Maṇikarṇikā, the river that was surrounded by groups of men whose merits as well as sins were washed off and who resembled the attendants of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.7.73 \|\|

*sacailamāplutya jale'male'male'vilaṃbamālaṃbita śuddhabuddhiḥ \|*  
*saṃtarpya dervīṣamanuṣyadivyapitṝnpitṝnsvānsahi karmakāṃḍavit \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. That Śivaśarman who knew the details of Karmakāṇḍa (rituals) plunged into the pure waters along with the clothes he wore, O blameless lady, without delay. With his intellect purified he offered libations to gods, sages, human beings, celestial manes and his own manes.

## \|\| 1.7.74 \|\|

*vidhāya ca drāksa hi paṃcatīrthikāṃ viśveśamārādhya tato yathāsvam \|*  
*punaḥpunarvīkṣyapurīṃ purāreridaṃ mayālokinaveti vismitaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. He quickly performed the rite of Pañcatīrthikā (five holy waters at Varaṇā, Asi, Pañcanada, Maṇikarṇikā and Daśāśvamedha), propitiated Viśveśvara in accordance with his financial resources and went round the city. On seeing time and again the city of the Enemy of the Three Puras, he wondered, ‘Is this seen by me or not?’

## \|\| 1.7.75 \|\|

*na svaḥ purī sā tvanayā purāsamaṃ samaṃjasāpi pratisāmyamāvaheta \|*  
*prabaṃdhabhedādvyatiriktapustakapratiryathā sallipibhedabhaṃgataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. If scrupulously examined, even that celestial city (Amarāvatī) cannot be on a par with this city, because of the difference in the creation (of the two cities). The said difference is like the difference of a worthless text and the sacred literature written in excellent characters.

## \|\| 1.7.76 \|\|

*payopi yatratyamaciṃtyavaibhavaṃ divisthitā sādhusudhāpyatomudhā \|*  
*tathā prasūtestu payodhare payo na pīyate pītamidaṃ yadi kvacit \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Even the water here has such divine properties as are incomprehensible. Though the ambrosia in the heavenly city is good, it is worthless in comparison with this. If this is drunk at any time, there shall not be any opportunity to drink the milk from the breasts of one’s mother. (One gets Mokṣa but Nectar-drinkers have to take birth in Saṃsāra.)

## \|\| 1.7.77 \|\|

*anāmayāściṃtanayā na yeśiturjanāmanāgyatra vinā pinākinā \|*  
*na karmasatkarmakṛtopi kurvate'nukurvate śarvagaṇāṃśca sarvataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. By pondering over the Lord of the Vedas, the people here are free from ailments. People performing sacred rites do not do so without referring to Pinākin (i.e. dedicating the fruit thereof to the Lord). They, therefore, imitate the attendants of Śiva in all respects. They attain a status equal to that of the attendants (of Śiva).

## \|\| 1.7.78 \|\|

*na varṇyate kaiḥ kila kāśikeyaṃ jaṃtoḥ sthitasyātra yatoṃtakāle \|*  
*pacelimaiḥ prākkṛtapuṇyabhārairoṃkāramoṃkārayatīṃdumauliḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. By whom is this Kāśī not eulogized? At the time of the death, through the fruition of the many merits performed and earned before, the Moon-crested Lord imparts the instruction in Oṃkāra to the embodied beings staying here.

## \|\| 1.7.79 \|\|

*saṃsāriciṃtāmaṇiratra yasmāttaṃ tārakaṃ sajjanakarṇikāyām \|*  
*śivobhidhatte sahasāṃ'takāle tadgīyatesau maṇi karṇiketi \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The auspicious Lord Śiva, the wish-yielding Cintāmaṇi jewel unto the men of worldly pursuits, whispers the Tāraka Mantra into the (right) ear of good people at the time of death. Hence this holy spot is spoken of as Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 1.7.80 \|\|

*muktilakṣmī mahāpīṭha maṇistaccaraṇābjayoḥ \|*  
*karṇikeyaṃ tataḥ prāhuryāṃ janā maṇikarṇikām \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. This holy spot is a jewel in the great pedestal of Goddess Lakṣmī of salvation, as well as a pericarp of her lotus-like feet. Hence people call this Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 1.7.81 \|\|

*jarāyujāṃḍajodbhijjāḥ svedajāhyatra vāsinaḥ \|*  
*na samā mokṣabhājaste tridaśairmuktidurdaśaiḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The four types of living beings staying here, viz., the womb-born, the egg-born, the germinating ones and the sweat-born ones, are not on the same footing as the gods to whom salvation is unobtainable. They are superior.

## \|\| 1.7.82 \|\|

*mama janma vṛthājātaṃ durvṛttasya jaḍātmanaḥ \|*  
*nādyayāvanmayai kṣiṣṭa kāśikā muktikāśikā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. “My birth was futile till today, because ill-behaved and ignorant (as I was), I did not perceive Kāśikā, the illuminator of liberation.”

## \|\| 1.7.83 \|\|

*punaḥpunaśca tatkṣetramatithīkṛtyanetrayoḥ \|*  
*vicitraṃ ca pavitraṃ ca tṛptiṃ nādhijagāma ha \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Śivaśarman was not fully satisfied even though he frequently made that holy spot the guest of his eyes, the holy spot that is sacred and wonderful.

## \|\| 1.7.84-85 \|\|

*saptānāṃ ca purīṇāṃ hi dhurī ṇāmavayāmyaham \|*  
*vārāṇasīṃ sunirvāṇaviśrāṇanavicakṣaṇām \|\| 84 \|\|*

*tathāpi na catasronyā mayā dṛggocarīkṛtāḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ prabhāvaṃ vijñāyāpyāgamiṣyāmya haṃ punaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. “I know that Kāśī is the chief of all the seven (holy) cities, (since) it is efficient in according excellent salvation. Yet, since the other four cities have not been visited by me, I shall go there and learn their greatness and come back once again.”

## \|\| 1.7.86 \|\|

*tīrthayātrāṃ pratidinaṃ kurvannūnaṃ savatsaram \|*  
*na prāpa sarvatīrthāni tīrthaṃ kāśyāṃ tiletile \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Although he undertook the pilgrimage everyday for a year, he could not visit all the Tīrthas. Indeed, there is a holy spot at every place as small as even a gingelly seed.

## \|\| 1.7.87 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*jānanna pi guṇāndevi kṣetrasyāsya parāndvijaḥ \|*  
*nānā pramāṇaiḥ pravaṇo niragātsa tathāpyaho \|\| 87 \|\|*

Agastya said:

87\. O noble lady, though conscious of all the great qualities of this holy spot, the Brāhmaṇa, well-versed in all the means of valid knowledge, did set out (from Kāśī), alas!

## \|\| 1.7.88 \|\|

*kiṃ kurvaṃti hi śāstrāṇi sapramāṇāni suṃdari \|*  
*mahāmāyāṃ bhavitrī tāṃ ko nivārayituṃ kṣamaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. O fair lady, what can scriptures do though they are authoritative? Who is competent to ward off the inevitable advent of Mahāmāya?

## \|\| 1.7.89 \|\|

*kaḥ samuccalitaṃ cetastoyaṃvā saṃpratīpayet \|*  
*proccathānasthitamapi svabhāvoyaccalastayoḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Who can cause restraint in the mind which wavers though stationed in an exalted place, or the water though stationed in an elevated place but flows down? The nature of both of them is unsteady.

## \|\| 1.7.90 \|\|

*śivaśarmā vrajansotha deśāddeśāṃtaraṃ kramāt \|*  
*mahākāla purīṃ prāpa kalikālavivarjitām \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Proceeding from one land to another duly, that Śivaśarman reached the city of Mahākāla (i.e. Ujjayinī) free from the bad effects of Kali and Kāla.

## \|\| 1.7.91 \|\|

*kalpekalpekhilaṃviśvaṃ kālayedyaḥ svalīlayā \|*  
*taṃ kālaṃ kalayitvā yo mahākālo bhavatkila \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. He who devours the entire universe in every Kalpa sportingly is Kāla. He who swallows Kāla becomes Mahākāla.

## \|\| 1.7.92 \|\|

*pāpādavaṃtī sā viśvamavaṃtīti nigadyate \|*  
*yugeyugenyanāmnī sā kalāvujjayinīti ca \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The city that saves the universe from sin is called Avantī. In every Yuga, it has a different name. In the Kali age it is called Ujjayinī.

## \|\| 1.7.93 \|\|

*vipanno yatra vai jaṃtuḥ prāpyāpi śavatāṃ sphuṭam \|*  
*na pūtigaṃdhamāpno ti samucchrayati na kvacit \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. A creature in adversity there, even after becoming a corpse, does not emit putrefying smell nor does it become swollen.

## \|\| 1.7.94 \|\|

*yamadūtā na yasyāṃ hi praviśaṃti kadācana \|*  
*paraḥkoṭīni liṃgāni tasyāṃ saṃti padepade \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The messengers of Yama never enter it. There are many millions and millions of Liṅgas there at every step.

## \|\| 1.7.95 \|\|

*hāṭakeśo mahākālastārake śastathaiva ca \|*  
*ekaliṃgaṃ tridhā bhūtvā trilokīṃ vyāpya saṃsthitam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. The self-same fiery Liṅga of refulgence becomes three, viz. Hāṭakeśa, Mahākāla and Tārakeśa and remains pervading the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.7.96 \|\|

*jyotiḥ siddhavaṭe jyotiste paśyaṃtīha ye dvijāḥ \|*  
*athavāśrīmahākāladraṣṭāraḥ puṇyarāśayaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The fiery refulgence at Siddhavaṭa is seen by Dvijas (men of the first three castes) or those are the meritorious persons who visit Mahākāla.

## \|\| 1.7.97 \|\|

*mahākālasya talliṃgaṃ yairdṛṣṭaṃ kaṣṭibhiḥ kvacita \|*  
*na spṛṣṭāste mahāpāpairna dṛṣṭāste yamodbhaṭaiḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. If that Liṅga of Mahākāla is seen by those who suffer from worldly sorrows, they will never be sullied by great sins; they will never be seen by the arrogant soldiers of Yama.

## \|\| 1.7.98 \|\|

*mahākālapatākāgraiḥ spṛṣṭapṛṣṭhāsturaṃgamāḥ \|*  
*aruṇasya kaśāghātaṃ kṣaṇaṃ viśramayaṃti khe \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. When their backs are stroked by the tips of the banners (fluttering on the tops of the mansions) in Mahākāla, the horses of the Sun in the sky get rid of the pain resulting from the lashes of the whip of Aruṇa.

## \|\| 1.7.99 \|\|

*mahākālamahākālamahākāletisaṃtatam \|*  
*smarataḥsmarato nityaṃ smarakartṛsmarāṃtakau \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The Father of Smara (Viṣṇu) and the Slayer of Smara (Śiva) always remember those who remember and repeat the name Mahākāla constantly.

## \|\| 1.7.100 \|\|

*evamārādhya bhūteśaṃ mahākālaṃ tato dvijaḥ \|*  
*jagāma nagarīṃ kāṃtīṃ kāṃtāṃ tribhuvanādapi \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. After propitiating thus Mahākāla, the lord of spirits, the Brāhmaṇa went to the city of Kāntī (Kañcī, Tamil Nadu) that is more brilliant than the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.7.101 \|\|

*lakṣmīkāṃtaḥ svayaṃ sākṣājjaṃtūṃstatranivāsinaḥ \|*  
*śrīkāṃtāneva kurute paratreha ca niścitam \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. It is definite that Lakṣmīkānta (Lord Viṣṇu) himself directly makes all the creatures staying here Śrīkāntas (possessors of wealth, identical with Viṣṇu) here and hereafter.

## \|\| 1.7.102 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā kāṃtīṃ kāṃtimatīṃ kāṃtimadbhirniṣevitām \|*  
*kāṃtimānabhavatsopi nākāṃtistatra kasyacit \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. By visiting Kāntī (Kāñcī) which is refulgent and which is resorted to by those who are brilliant, that Brāhmaṇa also became resplendent. There is no fading of splendour of anyone there.

## \|\| 1.7.103 \|\|

*tatra kṛtyaṃ ca yatkṛtyaṃ tatkṛtvā sarvakṛtyavit \|*  
*saptarātramuṣitvā tu yayau dvāravatīṃ purīm \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. The Brāhmaṇa conversant with all duties, performed everything that should be done there and stayed there for seven nights. Then he went to the city of Dvārāvatī.

## \|\| 1.7.104 \|\|

*caturṇāmapi vargāṇāṃ yatra dvārāṇi sarvataḥ \|*  
*ato dvāravatītyuktā vidvadbhistattvavedibhiḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. There are places and opportunities of entries for all the four aims of life in this city. Hence, it is called Dvārāvatī by learned men who know reality.

## \|\| 1.7.105 \|\|

*asthīnyapi ca jaṃtūnāṃ yatra cakrāṃkitānyaho \|*  
*kiṃ citraṃ tatra yatra syuḥ śaṃkhacakrāṃkitaiḥ karaiḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. If the bones of the creatures (dying here) are marked with discus, what wonder is there that they will become Viṣṇus in form, with their hands marked with conch and discus?

## \|\| 1.7.106 \|\|

*aṃtakaḥ śikṣayatyeva nijadūtānmuhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*te tyājyā yairdvāravatyā nāmāpi parigṛhyate \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The god of Death frequently teaches his messengers thus: “They who merely utter the name of Dvārāvatī should be abandoned (by you).

## \|\| 1.7.107 \|\|

*śrīkhaṃḍe kva sa āmodaḥ svarṇe varṇaḥ kva tādṛśaḥ \|*  
*tatpāvitryaṃ kva vai tīrthe tadgopīcaṃdane yathā \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Where is that fragrance in sandalwood, where is such a colour in gold, where is that sanctity in (the other) Tīrthas, as is found in the Gopīcandana of Dvārāvatī?

## \|\| 1.7.108 \|\|

*dūtāḥ śṛṇvaṃtu yadbhālaṃ gopacaṃdanalāṃchitam \|*  
*jvaladiṃgalavatsopi dūre tyājyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. O messengers, may all of you hear: He also whose forehead is marked with Gopīcandana, should be kept at a distance like blazing fire.

## \|\| 1.7.109 \|\|

*tulasyalaṃkṛtā ye ye tulasī nāmajāpakāḥ \|*  
*tulasīvanapālā ye te tyājyā dūrato bhaṭāḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. O soldiers, they also should be kept far off and abandoned, those who are adorned with Tulasī, those who repeat the name of Tulasī and those who grow Tulasī plants.”

## \|\| 1.7.110 \|\|

*yugeyuge dvāravatyā ratnāni parito muṣan \|*  
*abdhīratnākarodyāpi lokeṣu parigīyate \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. For ages together the ocean has been stealing away the jewels of Dvārāvatī all round and so it is being sung about as Ratnākara (‘storehouse of jewels’).

## \|\| 1.7.111 \|\|

*dvāravatyāṃ mriyaṃte ye jaṃtavaḥ kālanoditāḥ \|*  
*caturbhujāḥ syurvaikuṃṭhe te pītāṃbaradhāriṇaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Urged by the god of Death when creatures die at Dvārāvatī, they become Viṣṇu in Vaikuṇṭha endowed with four arms and wearing yellow cloths.

## \|\| 1.7.112 \|\|

*tatrāpi saṃtarpya pitṝnsasadevarṣimānavān \|*  
*tatra teṣu ca tīrtheṣu sasnau sarveṣvataṃdritaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. There also he (Śivaśarman) offered libations to the manes along with the gods, sages and men. Without lethargy, he took the holy bath in all those Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.7.113 \|\|

*tato māyāpurīṃ prāpto duṣprāpāṃ pāpakāribhiḥ \|*  
*yatra sā vaiṣṇavī māyā māyāpāśairnapāśayet \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Then he reached Māyāpurī which is inaccessible to sinners and where the Māyā pertaining to Viṣṇu does not fetter the living beings with the nooses of Māyā (those of ‘I’ and ‘mine’).

## \|\| 1.7.114 \|\|

*kecidūcurharidvāraṃ mokṣadvāraṃ tataḥ pare \|*  
*gaṃgādvāraṃ ca kepyāhuḥ kecinmāyāpuraṃ punaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Some call this holy spot Haridvāra; others call it Mokṣadvāra. Some call it Gaṅgādvāra and some call it Māyāpura.

## \|\| 1.7.115 \|\|

*yato vinirgatā gaṃgā khyātā bhāgīrathī bhuvi \|*  
*yannāmoccāraṇātpuṃsāṃ pāpaṃ yā ti sahasradhā \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. It is from here that Gaṅgā originated and became well-known all over the world as Bhāgīrathī. By the utterance of its name, the sin of men gets shattered into thousand pieces.

## \|\| 1.7.116 \|\|

*vaikuṃṭhasyaikasopānaṃ haridvāraṃ jagurjanāḥ \|*  
*atrāplutā narā yāṃti tadviṣṇoḥparamaṃ padam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. People have called Haridvāra as a single flight of steps to Vaikuṇṭha. Those men who take their holy plunge here go to the greatest region of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.7.117-118 \|\|

*tīrthopavāsakaṃ kṛtvā niśājāgaraṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*prātaḥ snātvā ca gaṃgāyāṃ tarpyānsaṃtarpapya sarvataḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

*yāvatsa pāraṇaṃ kartumiyeṣa dvijasattamaḥ \|*  
*tāvacchītajvarākrāṃtaścakaṃpe'tyarthamāturaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

117-118. He observed the fast customary in a Tīrtha and kept awake at night. In the morning he took his bath in Gaṅgā and offered libations to those who should be offered. When that excellent Brāhmaṇa desired to take food for breaking the fast, he was attacked by cold and fever. Ailing much, he shivered awfully.

## \|\| 1.7.119 \|\|

*vaideśikastathaikākī tathā'tijvarapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*ciṃtāmavāpa mahatī kimetatsamupasthitam \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Alone and a stranger to the place, afflicted with high fever, he was overwhelmed by great anxiety: ‘What is this that has befallen me?’

## \|\| 1.7.120 \|\|

*ciṃtārṇave nimagnobhūttyaktāśo jīvite dhane \|*  
*sāṃyātrika ivāgādhe bhinnapoto mahārṇave \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. He sank in the ocean of anxious thoughts. He abandoned all hopes of life and wealth like a sea-faring merchant whose ship is wrecked in the deep ocean.

## \|\| 1.7.121 \|\|

*kvakṣetraṃ kva kalatraṃ me kva putrāḥ kva ca tadvasu \|*  
*kva tadvicitraṃ vai harmyaṃ kva sā pustakasaṃbhṛtiḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Where is this holy spot? Where is my wife? Where are my sons? Where are those assets? Where is that wonderful mansion? Where is that collection of books (of mine)?

## \|\| 1.7.122 \|\|

*adyāpi nāyuḥ paryāptaṃ pa litaṃ na tathā mayi \|*  
*jvaroyaṃ dāruṇaḥ prāptaḥ kālajñaścātidāruṇaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. My age is not so ripe now. Hairs have not turned grey. This sickness is awful. God of Death who knows when to strike is also terrible.

## \|\| 1.7.123 \|\|

*mṛtyurmūrdhnikṛtāvāso vāso dūre vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*agnau gṛhopari prāpte kūpaṃ tu khanayediha \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Death has settled on my head. My residence is far off. When the house is on fire shall one begin to dig a well?

## \|\| 1.7.124 \|\|

*kimebhiściṃtanairvyarthairatitāpakarairmama \|*  
*ciṃtayāmi hṛṣīkeśaṃ śivadaṃ śivameva ca \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Of what avail are these futile thoughts? They but increase my distress. I shall think about Hṛṣīkeśa or Śiva, the bestower of auspicious welfare.

## \|\| 1.7.125 \|\|

*athavā muktyupāyo vai mayaikaḥ sadanuṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*muktipuryastu saptaitāḥ svanetraviṣayīkṛtāḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Or one good means of salvation has been performed by me. These seven cities of salvation have been directly visited by me.

## \|\| 1.7.126 \|\|

*svargāpavargayorekaḥ sādhyo hi viduṣā dhruvam \|*  
*tayorasādhane paścātsaṃtāpena ca tapyate \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Either heavenly bliss or salvation, one of these two should be invariably achieved by a learned man. If that has not been acquired, one will surely regret with distress.

## \|\| 1.7.127 \|\|

*athavā ciṃtayā kiṃ me tvanayā duravasthayā \|*  
*raṇe vā maraṇaṃ śreyastīrthevātra yathā mama \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Or, of what avail is this endless series of thoughts? Death is conducive to welfare either in a battle or in a holy spot like mine here.

## \|\| 1.7.128 \|\|

*kimahaṃ maṃdabhāgīva rathyāṃ kvāpi mriyedhunā \|*  
*bhāgīrathyāṃ mriye cādya kā ciṃtā mama mūḍhavat \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. Am I to die somewhere in the street now like an unlucky fellow? I shall die in the river Bhāgīrathī. Why should I worry like a foolish fellow?

## \|\| 1.7.129 \|\|

*carmāsthi saṃcayenāhamanena vapuṣā dhruvam \|*  
*prāpsyāmi nidhanādatra siddhiṃ naiḥśreyasīṃ dhruvam \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. I shall certainly achieve salvation by dying with this body, a conglomeration of bones and skin.’

## \|\| 1.7.130 \|\|

*evaṃ ciṃtayatastasya pīḍāsīdatidāruṇā \|*  
*koṭi vṛścikadaṣṭasya yāvasthā tāmavāpa saḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. While he was thinking thus, he experienced a terrible pain. He fell into that condition which one stung by ten million scorpions falls into.

## \|\| 1.7.131 \|\|

*smartavyaṃ vismṛtaṃ sarvaṃ kvāhaṃ kohaṃ na vetti ca \|*  
*dināni saptasapteti sthitvā paṃcatvamāgataḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Everything that should have been remembered was forgotten. He did not even know who he was and where he was. After remaining in this condition for fourteen days, he died.

## \|\| 1.7.132 \|\|

*tāvadvaikuṭhabhuvanād vimānaṃ samupasthitam \|*  
*tārkṣyopalakṣito yatra dhvajaścātisamucchritaḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. By that time, an aerial chariot came there from the region of Vaikuṇṭha. There was a lofty flagstaff therein marked with (the images of) Tārkṣya (Garuḍa).

## \|\| 1.7.133 \|\|

*adhiṣṭhitaṃ sukanyānāṃ svarṇakauśeyavāsasām \|*  
*cāmaravyagrahastānāṃ sahasreṇātivistṛtam \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. It was very spacious and occupied by a thousand excellent girls with chowries in their hands, wearing golden-coloured silken cloths.

## \|\| 1.7.134 \|\|

*puṇyaśīlasuśīlābhyāṃ gaṇābhyāṃ ca virājitam \|*  
*caturbhujābhyāṃ svāsyābhyāṃ kiṃkiṇījālamālitam \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. It was rendered brilliant by the two attendants Puṇyaśīla (‘of meritorious habits’) and Suśīla (‘of excellent behaviour’) endowed with four arms and excellent countenances. The aerial chariot had garlands of tinkling ornaments.

## \|\| 1.7.135 \|\|

*tadvimānamathāruhya pītavāsāścaturbhujaḥ \|*  
*alaṃcakre nabhovartma sa dvijo divyabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Endowed with four arms and clad in yellow garments, he got into that aerial chariot and adorned the path of the firmament.

## Chapter 8 - The World of Yama

## \|\| 1.8.1 \|\|

*lopāmudrovāca \|*  
*jīviteśa kathāmetāṃ puṇyāṃ puṇyapurīśritām \|*  
*na tṛptimadhigacchāmi śrutvā tvacchrīmukheritām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Lopāmudrā said:

1\. O lord of my life, I have not been fully contented by listening to the meritorious story of the holy cities as narrated by your glorious tongue.

## \|\| 1.8.2 \|\|

*māyāpuryāṃ muktipuryāṃ śivaśarmā dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*mṛtopi mokṣaṃ naivāpa brūhi tatkāraṇaṃ vibho \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. ŚiVaśarman, the excellent Brāhmaṇa, died in Māyāpurī, the city of salvation. Still he did not get salvation. O lord, kindly tell the reason thereof.

## \|\| 1.8.3-4 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*sākṣanmokṣo na caitāsu purīṣu priyabhāṣiṇi \|*  
*puroddiśyāmumevārthamitihāso mayāśrutaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śṛṇu kāṃte vicitrārthāṃ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*puṇyaśīlasuśīlābhyāṃ kathitāṃ śivaśarmaṇe \|\| 4 \|\|*

Agastya said:

3-4. O pleasant voiced lady, in these cities one does not attain liberation directly. Formerly an old legend pertaining to this matter was heard by me. O my beloved wife, listen to this story of wonderful implication, destructive of sins, which was narrated by Puṇyaśīla and Suśīla to Śivaśarman.

## \|\| 1.8.5 \|\|

*śivaśarmovāca \|*  
*ayi viṣṇugaṇau puṇyau puṃḍarīkadalekṣaṇau \|*  
*kiṃcidvijñaptukāmohaṃ pravṛddhakarasaṃpuṭaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Śivaśarman said:

5\. O meritorious attendants of Viṣṇu, with eyes like the petals of lotus! With palms joined together (in reverence) I wish to submit something.

## \|\| 1.8.6 \|\|

*na nāma yuvayorvedmi vedmyākṛtyā ca kiṃcana \|*  
*puṇyaśīlasuśīlākhyau yuvāṃ bhavitumarhathaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*
