6\. I do not know your names. I have understood something from your features. You are sure to be Puṇyaśīla and Suśīla.

## \|\| 1.8.7 \|\|

*gaṇā vūcatuḥ \|*  
*bhagavadbhaktiyuktānāṃ kimajñātaṃ bhavādṛśām \|*  
*etadeva hi nau nāma yaduktaṃ śrīmatā tvayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

The two attendants said:

7\. What is unknown to people like you endowed with devotion to the Lord? These alone are our names as spoken by you, the glorious one.

## \|\| 1.8.8 \|\|

*yadanyadapi te citte praṣṭavyaṃ tadaśaṃkitam \|*  
*saṃpṛcchasva mahāprājña prītyā tatprabravāvahe \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. If there is anything else in your mind to be asked, out with it unhesitatingly, O highly intelligent one. With great delight, we shall reply.

## \|\| 1.8.9 \|\|

*iti śrutvā sa vacanaṃ bhagavadgaṇabhāṣitam \|*  
*atiprītikaraṃ hṛdyaṃ tatastau pratyuvāca ha \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On hearing these sincere and highly pleasing words uttered by the attendants of the Lord, he replied thereafter:

## \|\| 1.8.10 \|\|

*divya dvija uvāca \|*  
*ka eṣa loko 'lpaśrīkaḥ svalpapuṇyajanākṛtiḥ \|*  
*ka ime vikṛtākārā brūtametanmamāgrataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

The divine Brāhmaṇa said:

10\. What is this world of very little glory and splendour? It contains the figures of people with very little merit. Who are these persons of ugly features? Speak it to me.

The attendants told:

## \|\| 1.8.11-12 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ piśācalokotra vasaṃti piśitāśanāḥ \|*  
*dattvānutāpabhājo ye nono kṛtvā dadatyapi \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śivaṃ prasaṃgatobhyarcya sakṛttvaśucicetasaḥ \|*  
*alpapuṇyālpalakṣmī kāḥ piśācāsta ime sakhe \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. This is the world of the Piśācas (ghosts). Flesh-eaters live here. Those who give some gifts and then repent, those who say “nay, nay” and then ultimately give something, those who worship Śiva once incidentally and then become impure in mind, those persons of very little merit and much less of prosperity, O friend, they have become these ghosts.

## \|\| 1.8.13-14 \|\|

*tato gacchandadarśāgre hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtam \|*  
*picaṃḍilaiḥ sthūlavaktrairmeghagaṃbhīraniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*lokairapyuṣitaṃ lokaṃ śyāmalāṃgaiśca lomaśaiḥ \|*  
*gaṇau kathayatāṃ kemī ko lokaḥ puṇyataḥ kutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Proceeding ahead from that place, he saw a world occupied by delighted and well-nourished people. The people residing there had huge bellies, thick mouths (lips) and dark hairy limbs. Their voice is stentorian like that of a thundering cloud. “O attendants, say who are these? What is this world? Is it (acquired) through merit?”

## \|\| 1.8.15-19 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*guhyakānāmayaṃ lokastvete vai guhyakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*nyāyenopārjya vittāni gūhayaṃti ca ye bhuvi \|\| 15 \|\|*

*svamārgagādhanāḍhyāśca śūdraprāyāḥ kuṭuṃbinaḥ \|*  
*saṃvibhajya ca bhoktāraḥ krodhāsūyāvivarjitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*na tithiṃ naiva vāraṃ ca saṃkrātyādi na parva ca \|*  
*nādharmaṃ na ca dharmaṃ ca vidaṃtyete sadā sukhāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ekameva hi jānaṃti kulapūjyo hi yo dvijaḥ \|*  
*tasmai gāḥ saṃprayacchaṃti manyaṃte tadvacaḥsphuṭam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*samṛddhibhājohyatrāpi tena puṇyena guhyakāḥ \|*  
*bhuṃjate svargasaukhyāni devavaccākutobhayāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

The attendants said:

15-19. This is the world of Guhyakas (Hoarders). These people are remembered as Guhyakas. In the earth (they dig big cavities) and hoard their wealth (of course) earned legitimately. They go their own way. They are rich householders behaving mostly like Śūdras. They share with others what they eat. They are devoid of anger and jealousy. They are easygoing, always fond of happiness and pleasure. They don’t observe the different lunar days, the days of the week, the festival days, days of the transit of the Sun, etc. They understand neither impiety nor righteousness. One thing they know perfectly well. They give cows as gifts to that Brāhmaṇa who is regarded worthy of the veneration of the whole family. They clearly abide by his words. Due to these meritorious activities, Guhyakas are prosperous here too. Like Devas, these Guhyakas enjoy heavenly pleasures. They have nothing to fear from anywhere.

## \|\| 1.8.20 \|\|

*tato vilokayāmāsa lokaṃ locanaśarmadam \|*  
*ke'mī janāstvasau lokaḥ kiṃnāmā vadatāṃ gaṇau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereafter, he espied a world that bestowed happiness unto the eyes. (He asked:) “Who are these people? What is the name of this world? O attendants, please tell (me).”

## \|\| 1.8.21 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*gāṃdharvastveṣaloko'mī gaṃdharvāśca śubhavratāḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ gāyanādyete cāraṇāḥ stutipāṭhakāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

The attendants said:

21\. This world is that of Gandharvas. These persons are the Gandharvas of splendid holy observances, because they sing the praise of the Devas. Those who were Cāraṇas and singers of praises (have now become Gandharvas).

## \|\| 1.8.22 \|\|

*gītajñā atigītena toṣayaṃti narādhipān \|*  
*stuvaṃti ca dhanāḍhyāṃśca dhanalobhena mohitā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Conversant with the science of music, they give much delight to kings and praise wealthy people, because they are fascinated by greed for money.

## \|\| 1.8.23-24 \|\|

*rājñāṃ prasādalabdhāni suvāsāṃsi dhanānyapi \|*  
*dravyāṇyapi sugaṃdhīni karpūrādīnyanekaśaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchaṃti gītaṃ gāyaṃtyaharniśam \|*  
*śrutāveva manasteṣāṃ nāṭyaśāstrakṛtaśramāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. They hand over to Brāhmaṇas the excellent garments, wealth, fragrant things like camphor and many other things obtained by them with the favour of the kings. They sing songs day and night. Their mind always dwells on the (Gāndharva) Veda. They persevere in their practice and study of the art of dance.

## \|\| 1.8.25 \|\|

*tena puṇyena gāṃdharvo lokastveṣāṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*brāhmaṇāstoṣitā yadvai gītavidyārjitairdhanaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Since Brāhmaṇas were propitiated through the wealth earned by them by means of music, they have become meritorious. Hence their world, the Gandharva world, has special significance.

## \|\| 1.8.26 \|\|

*gītavidyāprabhāvena devarṣirnārado mahān \|*  
*mānyo vaiṣṇavaloke vai śrīśaṃbhoścātivallabhaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is due to the power of the science of music, that the great celestial sage Nārada has become worthy of honour in the region of Viṣṇu. He is a great favourite of Śrīśaṃbhu too.

## \|\| 1.8.27 \|\|

*tuṃbururnā radaścobhau devānāmatidurlabhau \|*  
*nādarūpī śivaḥ sākṣānnādatattvavidau hi tau \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Tuṃburu and Nārada both of them are rare (venerable musicians) inaccessible even to the Devas. Śiva is Nāda (sound, melody) personified and both of them are conversant with the principles of melody.

## \|\| 1.8.28 \|\|

*yadi gītaṃ kvacidgītaṃ śrīmaddhariharāṃtike \|*  
*mokṣastu tatphalaṃ prāhuḥ sā nnidhyamathavā tayoḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If a song is sung near the glorious Hari or Hara, the benefit thereof is salvation or a direct visit by them or their presence.

## \|\| 1.8.29 \|\|

*gītajño yadi gītena nāpnoti paramaṃ padam \|*  
*rudrasyānucaro bhūtvā tenaiva saha modate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If an expert musician does not attain the greatest region (salvation) through his music, he (at least) becomes an attendant of Rudra and rejoices with him.

## \|\| 1.8.30 \|\|

*asmiṃlloke sadā kālaṃ smṛtire ṣā pragīyate \|*  
*tadgītamālayā pūjyau devau hariharau sadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In this world the following Smṛti is always sung about: “Lord Hari and Hara should always be worshipped through the series of their own songs.”

## \|\| 1.8.31 \|\|

*iti śṛṇvankṣaṇātprāpa punaranyanmanoharam \|*  
*śivaśarmātha papraccha kiṃ saṃjñaṃ nagaraṃ tvidam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Even as he heard this, Śivaśarman reached another charming city instantly. He asked, “What is the name of this city?”

## \|\| 1.8.32-35 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*asau vaidyādharo loko nānā vidyā viśāradāḥ \|*  
*ete vidyārthināmannamupānadvastrakaṃbalam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*auṣadhānyapi yacchaṃ ti tatpīḍāśamanāni hi \|*  
*nānākalāḥ śikṣayaṃti vidyāgarvavivarjitāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śiṣyaṃ putreṇa paśyaṃti vastra tāṃbūla bhojanaiḥ \|*  
*alaṃkṛtāśca satkanyā dharmā dudvāhayaṃti ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*abhilāṣadhiyā nityaṃ pūjayaṃtīṣṭadevatāḥ \|*  
*etaḥ puṇyairvasaṃtīha vidyādhara varā ime \|\| 35 \|\|*

The attendants said:

32-35. This is the world of Vidyādharas. They are all experts in various lores. They teach the students different kinds of arts. They are devoid of undue pride and arrogance in their learning. They give the pupil food, sandals, clothes, blankets and medicines for quelling their ailments. They consider the disciples as their own sons. Following pious practices, they give good girls in marriage to them along with clothes, betel leaves and food. They worship the deities of their choice with a keen desire for benefit. These Vidyādharas stay here due to those merits.

## \|\| 1.8.36-37 \|\|

*yāvaditthaṃ kathāṃ cakrustāvatsaṃyaminīpatiḥ \|*  
*dharmarājobhisaṃprāpto devaduṃdubhi niḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*somyamūrtirvimānastho dharmajñaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*sevākarmasu caturairbhṛtyaistricaturaiḥ saha \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. While they were talking thus, Dharmarāja, the lord of Saṃyaminī, came there amidst the sounds of Dundubhis (drums). He had assumed a gentle form. He was seated in an aerial chariot and was surrounded by persons knowing Dharma (pious practices) as well as three or four servants clever in the performance of their services.

## \|\| 1.8.38-40 \|\|

*dharmarāja uvāca \|*  
*sādhusādhu mahābuddhe śivaśarmandvijottama \|*  
*kulocitaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ bhavatā pratipāditam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vedābhyāsaḥ kṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ guravaścāpi toṣitāḥ \|*  
*dharmaśāstrapurāṇe ṣu dṛṣṭo dharmastvayā'dṛtaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kṣālitaṃ muktipuryadbhirāśugaṃtṛśarīrakam \|*  
*kovido'sti bhavāneva jīvite jīvitetare \|\| 40 \|\|*

Dharmarāja said:

38-40. Well done! Well done, O highly intelligent excellent Brāhmaṇa Śivaśarman! Everything befitting the families of Brāhmaṇas has been adopted by you. The Vedas were studied at the outset; the preceptors were delighted. Pious practices laid down and found in Dharmaśāstras were duly honoured by you. The fleeting body was washed and purified with the waters of the Muktipurīs (‘Cities of salvation’). You are an expert in matters concerning life and death.

## \|\| 1.8.41 \|\|

*kalevaraṃ pūtigaṃdhi sadaivāśucibhājanam \|*  
*sutīrthapuṇya paṇyena samyagvinimitaṃ tvayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The body with putrid odour that is always unclean has been exchanged for the merit accruing from excellent holy spots.

## \|\| 1.8.42 \|\|

*ataevāhi pāṃḍityamādriṃyate vicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*ahaḥkṣepaṃ na kṣipaṃti kṣaṇamekaṃ hi te budhāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It is for this reason that learned people honour and respect learning combined with a sense of discrimination between good and evil. Those scholars do not waste even a single moment of the day.

## \|\| 1.8.43 \|\|

*nimeṣānpaṃcapānmartye prāṇaṃti prāṇino dhruvam \|*  
*tatrāpi na pravarteyuraghakarmaṇi garhite \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Living beings live for a brief span of five or six moments in their mortal life. There, they should not indulge in vicious and sinful activities.

## \|\| 1.8.44 \|\|

*sthirāpāyaḥ sadā kāyo na dhanaṃ nidhane'vati \|*  
*tanmūḍhaḥ prauḍhakārye kiṃ na yateta bhavāniva \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The body is always sure to be destroyed. Monetary assets do not protect at the time of death. Therefore why does a foolish man not exert himself in noble activities like you?

## \|\| 1.8.45 \|\|

*satvaraṃ gatvaraṃ cāyurlokaḥ śokasamākulaḥ \|*  
*tasmāddharme matiḥ kāryā bhavateva sudhārmikaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Life is fleeting; people of the world are agitated by grief. Hence mind should be directed towards pious practices by righteous men like you.

## \|\| 1.8.46 \|\|

*satkarmaṇo vipāko'yaṃ tava vaṃdyau mamāpyaho \|*  
*yadetau bhagavadbhaktau sakhitvaṃ bhavato gatau \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. It is due to fruition of your virtuous actions that these two devotees of the Lord, who are worthy of my respect too, have become your friends.

## \|\| 1.8.47 \|\|

*mamājñā dīyatāṃ tasmātsāhāyyaṃ karavāṇi kim \|*  
*yatkartavyaṃ mādṛśaiste tatkṛtaṃ bhavataivahi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Hence let me be commanded. What help can I render? What should have been done by people like me has already been done by you.

## \|\| 1.8.48 \|\|

*adya dhanyatarosmīha yaddṛṣṭau bhagavadgaṇau \|*  
*sevā sadaiva me jñāpyā śrīmaccaraṇasannidhau \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Today I have become extremely blessed, for the attendants of the Lord have been seen. My readiness to serve always should be conveyed to the divine presence of the Lord.

## \|\| 1.8.49 \|\|

*tataḥ prasthāpitastābhyāṃ prāviśatsvapurīṃ yamaḥ \|*  
*aprākṣīcca tato viprastau gaṇau prasthite yame \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Sent off by those two, Yama entered his city. After Yama had returned, the Brāhmaṇa asked those two attendants:

## \|\| 1.8.50 \|\|

*śivaśarmovāca \|*  
*sākṣādayaṃ dharmarājo nanu saumyatarākṛtiḥ \|*  
*dharmyāṇyeva vacāṃsyasya manaḥ prītikarāṇi ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

Śivaśarman said:

50\. Directly viewed, this Dharmarāja is indeed of very gentle features. His words are conducive to righteousness and pleasant to the mind.

## \|\| 1.8.51 \|\|

*purī saṃyamanī seyamatīva śubhalakṣaṇā \|*  
*ākarṇya yasya nāmāpi pāpino'tīva bibhyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. This city of Saṃyaminī is really extremely splendid in its characteristic features. (But) the mere name thereof, when heard, terrifies the sinners too much.

## \|\| 1.8.52 \|\|

*yamarūpaṃ varṇa yaṃti martyaloke'nyathā janāḥ \|*  
*anyathā'yaṃ mayā dṛṣṭo brūtaṃ tatkāraṇaṃ gaṇau \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In the mortal world, the people describe the form of Yama otherwise. But what has been seen by me is contrary, just the opposite. O attendants, kindly tell the reason why.

## \|\| 1.8.53 \|\|

*kena paśyaṃtyamuṃ lokaṃ nivasaṃti tathātra ke \|*  
*idamevāsya kiṃ rūpaṃ kiṃ cānyacca nivedyatām \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Wherefore do people see this world? Who stays here? Is this alone his form, or something else? Let it be narrated.

## \|\| 1.8.54 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*śṛṇu saumya susaumyo'sau dṛśyatetra bhavādṛśaiḥ \|*  
*dharmamūrtiḥ prakṛtyaiva niḥśaṃkaiḥ puṇyarāśibhiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

The attendants said:

54\. Listen, O gentle Sir, he is seen very gentle by people like you who are not apprehensive and are meritorious. Naturally, he is the personification of piety.

## \|\| 1.8.55-56 \|\|

*ayameva hi piṃgākṣaḥ krodharaktāṃtalocanaḥ \|*  
*daṃṣṭrākarālavadano vidyullalanabhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*ūrdhvakeśo'tikṛṣṇāṃgaḥ pralayāṃbudaniḥsvanaḥ \|*  
*kāladaṃḍodyatakaro bhukuṭī kuṭilānanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. This (gentle) Yama is described otherwise in the following manner. He is tawny-eyed. The extremities of his eyes are red due to anger. His mouth is terrible with curved teeth. He looks awful with the tongue lolling like lightning. The hairs on his head stand erect. His limbs are excessively dark in complexion. His voice is loud like that of the thundering cloud at the time of ultimate annihilation. His Kāladaṇḍa (fierce staff) is lifted up by his hand. His brows are crooked making the face terrible.

## \|\| 1.8.57 \|\|

*ānayainaṃ pātayainaṃ badhānāmuṃca durdama \|*  
*ghātayainaṃ sudurvṛttaṃ mūrdhni tīvramayoghanaiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. (What he is supposed to be ordering is described in the following verses:) “O Durdama, bring him (here); cause him to fall; bind him; beat him soundly. Strike this man of excessive misdeeds with hammers on his head.

## \|\| 1.8.58 \|\|

*ātāḍayainaṃ durvṛttaṃ dhṛtvā pādau śilātale \|*  
*utpāṭayāsya netre tvaṃ nidhāya caraṇaṃ gale \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Hold this wicked man by his feet and dash him against the rocky ground. Place your foot on his neck and pluck out his eyes.

## \|\| 1.8.59 \|\|

*etasya gallāvutphullau kṣureṇāśuvi pāṭaya \|*  
*pāśena kaṃṭhaṃ baddhāsya samullaṃbaya bhūruhe \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Slit open this man’s swollen cheeks with the razor quickly. Tie this man’s neck with a rope and hang him on a tree.

## \|\| 1.8.60 \|\|

*vidārayāsya mūrdhānaṃ karapatreṇa dāruvat \|*  
*pārṣṇighātairghnatāsyāsyaṃ samuccūrṇaya dāruṇaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Sever this man’s head with a saw as if it were a piece of wood. Kick his face mercilessly and crush it into powder.

## \|\| 1.8.61 \|\|

*paradāraprasṛmaraṃ karaṃ chiṃdhyasya pāpinaḥ \|*  
*paradāragṛhaṃ yātuḥ pādau cāsya vikhaṃḍaya \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Chop off this sinner’s hand that used to assault and rape other men’s wives. Cut off the feet of this man who used to go to the houses of other men’s wives.

## \|\| 1.8.62 \|\|

*sūcībhī romakūpeṣu tanuṃ vyadhihi sarvataḥ \|*  
*dātuḥ parakalatrāṃge nakhapaṃktī durātmanaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. With needles pierce through the pores of the hairs of the body of this wicked man who used to make nail-marks on the limbs of other men’s wives.

## \|\| 1.8.63 \|\|

*paradāramukhāghrāturmukhe niṣṭhīvayāsya hi \|*  
*vaktuḥ parāpavādasya kīlaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ mukhe kṣipa \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Spit phlegm into the mouth of this sinner who used to sniff up the scent of the mouths of other men’s wives. Thrust a stiff peg into the mouth of this sinner, who used to speak slanderously of other people.

## \|\| 1.8.64 \|\|

*bharjayainaṃ caṇakavattaptavāluka karparaiḥ \|*  
*bhrāṣṭre vikaṭavaktratvaṃ parasaṃtāpakāriṇam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O Vikaṭavaktra, roast this man like Bengal gram in a frying pan, along with sand and gravel. He used to harass others.

## \|\| 1.8.65 \|\|

*doṣāropaṃ sadākarturadoṣe krūralocana \|*  
*nimajjayāsya vadanaṃ pūyaśoṇitakardame \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Krūralocana, immerse the face of this man in the slushy putrid pool of blood. He always used to find fault with blameless persons.

## \|\| 1.8.66 \|\|

*adattaparavastūnāṃ gṛhṇataḥ karapallavam \|*  
*āplutyāplutya tailena taptāṃgāre pacotkaṭa \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O Utkaṭa, this man used to take away other men’s articles, not given to him. Catch hold of his palms, sprinkle them with oil and roast them on hot charcoal fire.

## \|\| 1.8.67 \|\|

*apavādaṃ gurorvakturniṃdākartuḥ suparvaṇām \|*  
*taptalohaśalākāśca mukhe bhīṣaṇa nikṣipa \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O Bhīsaṇa, introduce hot iron rods and bars into the mouths of those who had made scandalous remarks about their preceptors and censured Devas.

## \|\| 1.8.68 \|\|

*paramarma spṛśaścāsya paracchidraprakāśituḥ \|*  
*sutaptāyomayāñcchaṃkūnsarvasaṃdhiṣu ropaya \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Fix red-hot iron pegs into all the joints of this sinner who used to pierce the vital parts of other people and to reveal their secrets and frailties.

## \|\| 1.8.69 \|\|

*anye na dīyamāne sve niṣeddhuḥpāpakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*ācchettuḥ paravṛttīnāṃ jihvāṃ chiṃdhyasya durmukha \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O Durmukha, cut off the tongue of this sinner who denies having received the money given by others and who robs others of their means of sustenance.

## \|\| 1.8.70 \|\|

*devasvabhoktuḥ kroḍāsya brāhmaṇasvasyabhojinaḥ \|*  
*vidāryodaramasyāśu viṭkīṭaiḥ paripūraya \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. O Kroḍāsya, quickly cut open the belly of this sinner and fill it with faecal worms. He used illegitimately to enjoy temple properties and assets of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.8.71 \|\|

*na devārthe na viprārthe nātithyarthe pacetkvacit \|*  
*tamamuṃ svārthapaktāraṃ kuṃbhīpāke pacāṃdhaka \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. O Andhaka, cook this sinner in the vessels of the hell Kuṃbhīpāka. He was utterly selfish cooking for himself and not (sharing them with) the deities, Brāhmaṇas and guests.

## \|\| 1.8.72 \|\|

*ugrāsya śiśuhaṃtāramamuṃ viśraṃbhaghātinam \|*  
*kṛtaghnaṃ naya vegena mahāraurava rauravam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O Ugrāsya, hurry up and take this sinner to the hell of Mahāraurava or Raurava. He was ungrateful. He used to kill infants. He was guilty of breach of trust.

## \|\| 1.8.73-75 \|\|

*brahmaghnaṃ cāṃdhatāmisre surāpaṃ pūyaśoṇite \|*  
*kālasūtre hemacauramavīcau gurutalpagam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tatsaṃsargiṇamāvarṣamasipatravane tathā \|*  
*etānmahāpātakinastaptatailakaṭāhake \|\| 74 \|\|*

*āplutyāplutya durdaṃṣṭrakākolairlohatuṃḍakaiḥ \|*  
*saṃtodyamānānpāpiṣṭhānnityaṃ kalpaṃ nivāsaya \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-75. O Durdaṃṣṭra, take this Brāhmaṇa-slayer to Andhatāmisra, this alcohol-addict to Pūyaśoṇita, this gold stealer to Kālasūtra, this defiler of the preceptor’s bed to Avīci. This sinner is in intimate contact with them. Take him to the hell Asipatra-Vana till the year is over. Put all these great sinners into the cauldrons filled with hot oil. Let them be constantly afflicted by ferocious ravens with steel-like beaks. Make these sinners stay there permanently till the end of the Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.8.76 \|\|

*strīghnaṃ goghnaṃ ca mitraghnaṃ kūṭaśālmalipādape \|*  
*ullaṃbaya ciraṃkālamūrdhvapādamadhomukham \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Hang up for a long time on the Kūṭaśālmali tree the sinners who had killed women, cows and friends, with their feet above and the head down.

## \|\| 1.8.77 \|\|

*tvacamasya ca saṃdaṃśaistroṭaya tvaṃ mahābhuja \|*  
*āśleṣiturmitrapatnyā bhujāvutpāṭayā śuca \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. O Mahābhuja, with a pair of tongs tear off the skin of this sinner who had embraced the wife of his friend. Very soon cut off his hands too.

## \|\| 1.8.78 \|\|

*jvālākīle mahāghore narake'muṃ ni pātaya \|*  
*yo vahninā dāhayati parakṣetraṃ parālayam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Cause this sinner to fall into the great hell Jvālākīla. He had set fire to and burned other men’s fields and houses.

## \|\| 1.8.79 \|\|

*kālakūṭe ca garadaṃ kūṭasākṣyābhivādinam \|*  
*mānakūṭaṃ tulākūṭaṃ kaṃṭhamoṭe nipātaya \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Cast the sinner who had administered poison to others and who is guilty of perjury into the hell Kālakūṭa. Throw the sinner who used to cheat others through false measures and weights into the hell Kaṇṭhamoṭa (or push him down after wringing his neck).

## \|\| 1.8.80 \|\|

*lālāpibeca duṣprekṣya tīrthāsuṣṭhīvinaṃ naya \|*  
*āmapāke ca garbhaghnaṃ śūlapāke'nyatāpinam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. O Duṣprekṣya, take the sinner who spits into the sacred waters to the hell Lālāpiba, the sinner who destroys foetus to the hell Āmapāka and that man who distresses others to Śūlapāka hell.

## \|\| 1.8.81 \|\|

*rasavikrayiṇaṃ vipramikṣuyaṃtre prapīḍaya \|*  
*prajāpīḍākaraṃ bhūpamaṃdhakūpe nipātaya \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Torture in the sugarcane-crushing machine that Brāhmaṇa who used to sell juices and beverages (Ikṣuyantra may be the name of a hell also). Throw the king harassing his subjects into the hell Andhakūpa.

## \|\| 1.8.82-84 \|\|

*gotilāṃśca turaṃgāṃśca vikretāraṃ dvijādhamam \|*  
*mātulānyāḥ surāyāśca vikretāraṃ halāyudha \|\| 82 \|\|*

*musalolūkhale vaiśyaṃ kaṃḍayainaṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*śūdraṃ dvijāvamaṃtāraṃ dvijāgre maṃcasevinam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*adhomukhe ca narake dīrghagrīvaprapīḍya \|\| 84 \|\|*

82-84. O Halāyudha, with mortar and pestle thrash constantly the Vaiśya who sells hemp and alcohol, as well as the base Brāhmaṇa who sells cows, gingelly seeds and horses.

O Dīrghagrīva, torture in the hell Adhomukha the Śūdra who insults Brāhmaṇas and occupies a cot in the presence of a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.8.85-87 \|\|

*śūdraṃ brāhmaṇajetāraṃ vaiśyaṃ bāhmaṇamāninam \|*  
*kṣatriyaṃ yājakaṃ cāpi vipraṃ vedavivarjitam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*lākṣālavaṇamāṃsānāṃ satailaviṣasarpiṣām \|*  
*āyudhekṣuvikārāṇāṃ vikretāraṃ dvijādhamam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*pāśapāṇekaśāpāṇe baddhvaitāṃścaraṇedṛḍham \|*  
*ghātayaṃtau kaśāghātairnayataṃ taptakardame \|\| 87 \|\|*

85-87. O Pāśapāṇi, O Kaśāpāṇi, bind the feet of these sinners: the Śūdra who competes with a Brāhmaṇa, the Vaiśya professing to be a Brāhmaṇa, the Kṣatriya who performs Yajñas on behalf of others, the Brāhmaṇa who is bereft of the Vedas, and the base Brāhmaṇa who regularly sells red lac, salt, meat, oil, poison, ghee, weapons and sugarcane products. Hit them hard with whips and take them to Taptakardama.

## \|\| 1.8.88 \|\|

*imāṃ striyaṃ śleṣayāśu puṃścalīṃ kulakalmaṣām \|*  
*tenopapatinā sārdhaṃ taptāyasamayena ca \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Make this woman who had been an unchaste harlot, a stigma on the family, embrace the red hot iron image of her paramour.

## \|\| 1.8.89 \|\|

*svayaṃ gṛhītvā niyamaṃ yastyajedajiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*taṃ prāpaya durādharṣaṃ bahubhramaradaṃśake \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. O Durādharṣa, take into the hell named Bahubhramaradaṃśaka (‘where there are many black bees and wasps’) the sinner who having taken up vows and observances forsakes them, because he could not restrain his sense-organs.”

## \|\| 1.8.90 \|\|

*ityādijalpandurvṛttaiḥ śrūyate dūrato yamaḥ \|*  
*svakarmaśaṃkitaiḥ pāpai rdṛśyateti bhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Yama is heard uttering these words from far off by men of evil deeds. He is seen as extremely terrible by the sinners who are suspicious of their own activities.

## \|\| 1.8.91 \|\|

*ye prajāḥ pālayaṃtīha putrāneva nijaurasān \|*  
*daṃḍayaṃti ca dharmeṇa bhūpāste'sya sabhāsadaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Those kings who protect the subjects like their own bosom-born children and punish them as demanded by justice are the members of his assembly.

## \|\| 1.8.92 \|\|

*varṇāśramāśca yadrāṣṭre 'nutiṣṭhaṃti nijāṃ kriyām \|*  
*kālenāpannanidhanā bhūpāste'sya sabhāsadaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Those kings in whose kingdom the persons belonging to different castes and stages of life invariably perform their respective duties and those who die at the proper time are the members of his assembly.

## \|\| 1.8.93 \|\|

*naiva dīno na durvṛtto nāpadgrasto na śokabhāk \|*  
*yeṣāṃ rāṣṭre pradṛśyaṃte bhūpāste'sya sabhāsadaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Those kings in whose kingdom neither the impoverished nor the evil-behaved, neither the persons overwhelmed with calamities nor those who are grief-stricken are to be found, are the members of his assembly.

## \|\| 1.8.94 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ svadharma niratāḥ sadā \|*  
*anyepi ye saṃyaminaḥ saṃyaminyāṃ vasaṃti te \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The Brāhmaṇas, the Kṣatriyas and the Vaiśyas who are steadfast in their own duties and others who have perfect self-control live in the city Saṃyaminī.

## \|\| 1.8.95-97 \|\|

*uśīnaraḥ sudhanvā ca vṛṣaparvā jayadrathaḥ \|*  
*rajiḥ sahasrajitkukṣirdṛḍhadhanvā ripuṃjayaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*yuvanāśvo daṃtavaktro nābhāgo ripumaṃgalaḥ \|*  
*karaṃdhamo dharmasenaḥ paramardaḥ parāṃtakaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*ete cānye ca bahavo rājāno nītivartinaḥ \|*  
*dharmādharmavicārajñāḥ sudharmāyāṃ samāsate \|\| 97 \|\|*

95-97. Uśīnara, Sudhanvan, Vṛṣaparvan, Jayadratha, Rāji, Sahasrajit, Kukṣi, Dṛḍhadhanvan, Ripuñjaya, Yuvanāśva, Dantavaktra, Nābhāga, Ripumaṅgala, Karandhama, Dharmasena, Paramardaka, Parāntaka—these and many other kings abiding by good policies and conversant with the discussion on what is pious and what is not, stay in Sudharmā.

## \|\| 1.8.98 \|\|

*anyacca te pravakṣyāvo yena paśyaṃti bhāskarim \|*  
*daṃḍapāśodyatakarāndūtānugrānanānkvacit \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. We shall mention another thing also to you as to who do not see the son of the Sun (i.e., Yama) or his messengers of fierce faces, wielding staffs and nooses in their raised hands.

## \|\| 1.8.99 \|\|

*goviṃdamādhavamukuṃda haremurāre śaṃbho śiveśa śaśiśekhara śūlapāṇe \|*  
*dāmodarācyuta janārdana vāsudeva tyājyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanaṃti \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O Bhaṭas (Yama’s officers), those who always repeat the following names are to be let off. (Yama instructs his soldiers thus:) O Govinda, Mādhava, Mukunda, Hari, Murāri, Dāmodara, Acyuta, Janārdana, Vāsudeva (Viṣṇu’s names), O Śaṃbhu, Śiva, Īśa, Śaśiśekhara, Śūlapāṇi (Śiva’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.100 \|\|

*gaṃgādharāṃdhakaripo haranīlakaṃṭha vaikuṃṭha kaiṭabharipo kamaṭhābjapāṇe \|*  
*bhūteśakhaṃḍaparaśomṛḍacaṃḍikeśa tyājyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanaṃti \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. O Gaṅgādhara, Andhakaripu, Hara, Nīlakaṇṭha, Bhūteśa, Khaṇḍaparaśu, Mṛḍa, Caṇḍikeśa (Śiva’s name)! O Vaikuṇṭha! O Kaiṭabharipu! O Kamaṭha (Divine tortoise)! O Abjapāṇi (lotus-handed) (Viṣṇu’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.101 \|\|

*viṣṇonṛsiṃhamadhusūdanacakrapāṇe gaurīpate giriśa śaṃkara caṃdracūḍa \|*  
*nārāyaṇāsuranibarhaṇaśārṅgapāṇe tyājyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanaṃti \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. O Viṣṇu, Nṛsiṃha, Madhusūdana, Cakrapāṇi, Nārāyaṇa, Asuranibarhaṇa, Śārṅgapāṇi (Viṣṇu’s names)! O Gaurīpati, Girīśa, Śaṅkara, Candracūḍa (Śiva’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.102 \|\|

*mṛtyuṃjayograviṣamekṣaṇakāmaśatro śrīkāṃtapītavasanāṃbuda nīlaśaure \|*  
*īśānakṛttivasanatridaśaikanātha tyājyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanaṃti \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. O Mṛtyuñjaya, Ugra, Viṣamekṣaṇa, Kāmaśatru, Īśāna, Kṛttivasana, Tridaśaikanātha (Śiva’s names)! O Śrīkānta, Pītavasana, Aṃbudanīla, Śauri (Viṣṇu’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.103 \|\|

*lakṣmīpate madhuripo puruṣottamādyaśrīkaṃṭhadigvasana śāṃtapinākapāṇe \|*  
*ānaṃdakaṃda dharaṇīdhara padmanābha tyājyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanati \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. O Lakṣmīpati, Madhuripu, Puruṣottama, Ādya, Ānandakanda, Dharaṇīdhara, Padmanābha (Viṣṇu’s names)! O Śrīkaṇṭha, Digvasana, Śānta, Pinākapāṇi (Śiva’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.104 \|\|

*sarveśvara tripurasūdana devadeva brahmaṇyadevagaruḍadhvaja śaṃkhapāṇe \|*  
*tryakṣoragābharaṇabālamṛgāṃkamaule tyajyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanaṃti \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. O Sarveśvara, Tripurasūdana, Devadeva, Tryakṣa, Uragābharaṇa, Bālamṛgāṅkamauli (Śiva’s names)! Brahmaṇya Deva, Garuḍadhvaja, Śaṅkhapāṇi (Viṣṇu’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.105 \|\|

*śrīrāmarāghavarameśvararāvaṇāre bhūteśamanmatharipo pramathādhinātha \|*  
*cāṇūramardanahṛṣīkapatemurāre tyājyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanati \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. O Śrīrāma, Rāghava, Rāmeśvara, Rāvaṇāri, Cāṇūramardana, Hṛṣīkapati, Murāri (Viṣṇu’s names)! O Bhūteśa, Manmatharipu, Pramathādhinātha (Śiva’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.106 \|\|

*śūlingirīśa rajanīśa kalāvataṃ sakaṃsapraṇāśana sanātanakeśināśa \|*  
*bhargatrinetrabhavabhūtapate purāre tyājyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanaṃti \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. O Śūlin, Giriśa, Rajanīśakalāvataṃsa, Bharga, Trinetra, Bhava, Bhūtapati, Purāri (Śiva’s names)! O Kaṃsaprāṇāśana, Sanātana, Keśināśa (Viṣṇu’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.107 \|\|

*gopīpate yadupate vasudevasūno karpūragauravṛṣabhadhvajabhālanetra \|*  
*govardhanoddharaṇadharmadhurīṇagopa tyājyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanaṃti \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. O Gopīpati, Yadupati, Vasudevasūnu! O Govardhanoddharaṇa, Dharmadhurīṇa, Gopa (Viṣṇu’s names)! O Karpūragaura, Vṛṣabhadhvaja, Bhālanetra (Śiva’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.108 \|\|

*sthāṇo trilocana pinākadharasmarāre kṛṣṇāniruddhakamalākarakalmaṣāre \|*  
*viśveśvara tripathagārdrajaṭākalāpa tyājyā bhaṭāya iti saṃtatamāmanaṃti \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. O Sthāṇu, Trilocana, Pinākadhara, Smarāri, Viśveśvara, Tripathagārdrajaṭā-kalāpa (Śiva’s names)! O Kṛṣṇa, Aniruddha, Kamalākara, Kalmaṣāri (Viṣṇu’s names)!

## \|\| 1.8.109 \|\|

*aṣṭottarādhikaśatenasucārunāmnāṃ saṃdarbhitāṃ lalitaratnakadaṃbakena \|*  
*sannāyakāṃ dṛḍhaguṇāṃ ddhijakaṃṭhagāṃ yaḥ kuryādimāṃ srajamaho sa yamaṃ na paśyet \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. O Brāhmaṇas, this series of one hundred and eight excellent names has been wreathed into a garland as though with clusters of excellent jewels. The heroes of these names are exquisite ones (Gods Viṣṇu and Śiva). The string is strong. (It is full of good qualities.) He who wears (commits to memory) this garland will not see Yama.

## \|\| 1.8.110 \|\|

*itthaṃ dvijeṃdra nijabhṛtyagaṇānsadaiva saṃśikṣayedavanigānsa hi dharmarājaḥ \|*  
*anyepi ye hariharāṃkadharā dharāyāṃ te dūrataḥ punaraho parivarjanīyāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Thus, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that Dharmarāja always instructs the groups of his servants going to the earth. Others too on the earth, who may be having the marks and characteristics of Hari or Hara, are to be avoided from afar.

## \|\| 1.8.111-112 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*yo dharmarājaracitāṃ lalitaprabaṃdhāṃ nāmāvaliṃ sakalakalmaṣabījahaṃtrīm \|*  
*dhīrotra kaustubhabhṛtaḥ śaśibhūṣaṇasya nityaṃ japetstanarasaṃ sa pibenna mātuḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

*iti śṛṇvankathāṃ ramyāṃ śivaśarmāpriye'naghāma \|*  
*prahṛṣṭavaktraḥ purato dadarśāpsarasāpurīm \|\| 112 \|\|*

Agastya said:

111-112. A bold and intelligent man who always repeats this series of names of the Kaustubha-wearing Viṣṇu and the Moon-adorned Śiva wreathed into a lucid composition by Dharmarāja will never drink the secretion from the breasts of any mother. It destroys the seeds of all sins. Even as he heard this fascinating story that is faultless, O beloved one, Śivaśarman became delighted with a beaming face. He saw in front of him the city of the celestial damsels.

## Chapter 9 - The Regions of Celestial Damsels and of the Sun

## \|\| 1.9.1 \|\|

*śivaśarmovāca \|*  
*kā imā rūpalāvaṇya saubhāgyanidhayaḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*divyālaṃkāradhāriṇyo divyabhogasamanvitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śivaśarman said:

1\. Who are these ladies, the storehouse of beauty, radiance and conjugal bliss, wearing divine ornaments and enjoying divine pleasures?

## \|\| 1.9.2 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*etā vāravilāsinyo yajñabhājāṃ priyaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*gītajñā nṛtyakuśalā vādyavidyā vicakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The attendants said:

2\. These are the glamorous courtesans, the beloved ones of the Devas. They are conversant with music, experts in dance and very efficient in the art of playing musical instruments.

## \|\| 1.9.3 \|\|

*kāmakelikalābhijñā dyūtavidyāviśāradāḥ \|*  
*rasajñā bhāvavedinyaścaturāścocitoktiṣu \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. They are adepts in the art of love making; very clever at the game of dice. They appreciate the beauty of things. They understand the innermost feelings of others. They are very clever in suitable repartees.

## \|\| 1.9.4 \|\|

*nānādeśa viśeṣajñā nānābhāṣā sukovidāḥ \|*  
*saṃketodaṃtanipuṇā naikāsvairacarā mudā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They are experts in knowing the specialities of different countries and have mastery over the languages spoken in different lands. They are skilful in probing secret news. They move about delightfully at their sweet will in groups, and not alone.

## \|\| 1.9.5 \|\|

*līlānarmasusābhijñāḥ supralāpeṣu paṃḍitāḥ \|*  
*yūnāṃ manāṃsi satataṃ svairhāvai ramayaṃtyamūḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. They are experts in coquettish gestures exciting amorous feelings and expressions of love and amorous sports. They are adept in continuous light talk. They always delight the minds of the youths through their coquettish gestures and seductive charms.

## \|\| 1.9.6 \|\|

*nirmathyamānātkṣīrodātpūrvamapsarasastvamūḥ \|*  
*niḥsṛtāstrijagajjeturmohanāstramanobhuvaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Formerly these celestial ladies emerged from the Milk-Ocean while it was being churned. They are the fascinating weapons of the mind-born god of Love, the conqueror of the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.9.7-12 \|\|

*urvaśī menakā raṃbhā caṃdralekhā tilottamā \|*  
*vapuṣmatīkāṃtimatī līlāvatyutpalāvatī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*alaṃbuṣā guṇavatī sthūlakeśī kalāvatī \|*  
*kalānidhirguṇanidhiḥ karpūratilakorvarā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*anaṃgalatikā cāpi tathā madanamohinī \|*  
*cakorākṣī caṃdrakalā tathā munimanoharā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*grāvadrāvā tapodveṣṭī cārunāsā sukarṇikā \|*  
*dārusaṃjīvinī suśrīḥ kratuśulkā śubhānanā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tapaḥśulkā tīrthaśulkā dānaśulkā himāvatī \|*  
*paṃcāśvamedhikā caiva rājasūyārthinī tathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*aṣṭāgnihomikā tadvadvājapeyaśatodbhavā \|*  
*ityādyapsarasāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sahasraṃ ṣaṣṭisaṃmitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

7-12. They are: Urvaśī, Menakā, Raṃbhā, Candralekhā, Tilottamā, Vapuṣmatī, Kāntimatī, Lilāvatī, Utpalavatī, Alaṃbuṣā, Guṇavatī, Sthūlakeśī, Kalāvatī, Kalānidhi, Guṇanidhi, Karpūratilakā, Urvarā, Anaṅgalatikā, Madanamohinī, Cakorākṣī, Candrakalā, Munimanoharā, Grāvadrāvā, Tapodveṣṭrī, Cārunāsā, Sukarṇikā, Dārusañjīvinī, Suśrī, Kratuśulkā of splendid countenance, Tapaḥśulkā, Tīrthamedhikā, Rājasūyārthinī, Aṣṭāgnihomikā, Vājapeyaśatodbhavā.

These celestial damsels number sixty thousand.

## \|\| 1.9.13 \|\|

*etasminnapsaroloke vasaṃtyanyā apistriyaḥ \|*  
*sadā skhalitalāvaṇyāḥ sadāskhalitayauvanāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In this world of celestial damsels other women too live. Their radiance never fades and dims. Their youth never diminishes.

## \|\| 1.9.14 \|\|

*divyāṃbarā divyamālyā divyagaṃdhānulepanāḥ \|*  
*divyabhogaiḥ susaṃpannāḥ svecchāvidhṛtavigrahāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Their garments are divine; their garlands are celestial; their scents and unguents are divine; they are richly endowed with heavenly means of enjoyments; they can assume any form they like.

## \|\| 1.9.15-16 \|\|

*kṛtvā māsopavāsāni skhalaṃti brahmacaryataḥ \|*  
*sakṛdeva dvikṛtvo vā triḥkṛtvo daivayogataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tā imā divyabhoginyo rūpalāvaṇyasaṃpadaḥ \|*  
*nivasaṃtyapsaroloke sarvakāmasamanvitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. (Some women in the world) observe the monthly fasts but violate the vow of celibacy once, twice or thrice as

ill-luck would have it. It is such women who come to Apsarāloka and stay there enjoying divine pleasures and possessing the rich beauty and refulgence. They realize all their desires.

## \|\| 1.9.17 \|\|

*kṛtvā vratāni sāṃgāni kāmikāni vidhānataḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃti svairacāriṇyo devabhogyā ihāgatāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After following the holy vows and observances in accordance with the injunctions along with their ancillaries with a view to obtain their desires, some ladies become adulteresses. Such women come to this world as the objects of enjoyment of the Devas.

## \|\| 1.9.18 \|\|

*pativratadhṛtā nāryo balena balinā dhṛtāḥ \|*  
*bhartabuddhyāramaṃtetaṃ kadācittā imā dvija \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. There are some women of great fidelity but some powerful man might have raped them and they might have enjoyed sexual dalliance with him, wrongly taking him to be their husband. Such women are these, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.9.19 \|\|

*bhartari proṣite yāśca brahmacaryavratāḥ sadā \|*  
*viplavaṃ te sakṛddaivāttā etā vāmalocanāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When the husbands were away from the homes, some women who had always been observing celibacy, may by chance or due to cruel fate err and fall. These are such ladies of beautiful eyes.

## \|\| 1.9.20-25 \|\|

*kusumāni sugaṃdhīni suvāsaṃ caṃdanaṃ tathā \|*  
*sugauraṃ cāpi karpūraṃ susūkṣmāṇyaṃbarāṇi ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*parṇāni ṛjutārāṇi jīrṇāni kaṭhināni ca \|*  
*sāgrāṇi svarṇavarṇāni sthūlanīlaśirāṇi ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*suvāsopaskarāḍhyāni nāgavallyā dvijottama \|*  
*śayyāvicitrābharaṇā ratiśālocitāni ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bahukautukavastūni samarcyadvijadaṃpatī \|*  
*bhogadānamidaṃ kāmyaṃ pratisaṃkramaṇaṃ raveḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kiṃvā prativyatīpātamekasaṃvatsarāvadhi \|*  
*kodāditi ca maṃtreṇa yā dadyādvaravarṇinī \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kāmarūpadharo devaḥ prīyatāmiti vādinī \|*  
*sā śreṣṭhā'psarasāṃ madhye vasetkalpamihāṃganā \|\| 25 \|\|*

20-25. There are various things to be given as gifts such as sweet-smelling flowers; fragrant sandal-paste; exquisitely white camphor; garments of very fine texture; betel leaves that are symmetrical and long, that are ripe and firm, that have golden hue at the tips, that have thick and blue nerve-like lines running through and that are accompanied by sweet-smelling nuts and other ingredients; beds with various kinds of ornaments; all fanciful objects befitting the chamber of love-play and other things too. A lady of excellent complexion should honour a Brāhmaṇa couple and give them the gifts mentioned above. This gift of objects of pleasure is something to be desired. At the time of the monthly transit of the Sun or on the days of Vyatīpāta (New Moon in combination with Sunday), these gifts should be made and continued for a year. The lady should repeat the Mantra (“ko’ dāt, kasmā adāt, kāmāyādāt kāmo dātā, kāmaḥ pratigrahītā, kāma etatte”) (of the Vedas) (or any other similar Mantra) and say “May the Lord in the form of god of Love be pleased” and give the things to the Brāhmaṇa couple. She will become the most excellent one among the celestial damsels and stay there for a Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.9.26-27 \|\|

*kanyārūpadharākācidyābhuktā kenacitkvacit \|*  
*devarūpeṇa taṃ kālamārabhya brahmacāriṇī \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tadeva vṛttaṃ dhyāyaṃtī nidhanaṃ yāti kālataḥ \|*  
*divyarūpadharā seha jāyate divya bhogabhāk \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. A beautiful virgin was carnally enjoyed somewhere by someone in the form of a Deva. Ever since then that girl continued to be celibate meditating upon the same incident (and not marrying anyone else). That girl attains a divine form and is born here sharing divine pleasures.

## \|\| 1.9.28-32 \|\|

*nidānamapsarolokasyetiśṛṇvandvijāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*sauraṃ lokamatha prāpya kṣaṇena sa vimānagaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yathā kadaṃbakusumaṃ kiṃjalkaiḥ sarvatovṛtam \|*  
*dedīpyamānaṃ hi tathā samaṃtādbhānubhānubhiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dūrādraviṃ sa vijñāya dhṛtatāmarasadvayam \|*  
*navabhiryojanānāṃ ca sahasraiḥ saṃmitena ha \|\| 30 \|\|*

*vicitreṇaikacakreṇa saptasaptiyutena ca \|*  
*anūruṇādhiṣṭhitena puratodhṛtaraśminā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*apsaromunigaṃdharva sarpagrāmaṇi nairṛtaiḥ \|*  
*syaṃdanenātijavinā praṇanāma kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

28-32. Hearing the origin of the Apsarāloka (the region of Apsarās) in this manner the eminent Brāhmaṇa reached the Solar World in a moment, travelling in an aerial chariot.

Due to the rays of the Sun, the world was shining brilliantly all round like a Kadaṃba flower surrounded by its filaments.

From a distance he saw the Sun sporting two lotuses. He could know that it was the Sun through the wonderful fast chariot of a single wheel drawn by seven horses. It was nine thousand Yojanas in size. It was driven by Anūru who held the reins in front. The celestial damsels, sages, Gandharvas, serpents, Yakṣas and Rākṣasas were there. Then he joined his palms in reverence and bowed down.

## \|\| 1.9.33 \|\|

*tasya praṇāmaṃdevopi bhrūbhaṃgenānumanya ca \|*  
*atidūraṃ nabhovartma vyaticakrāma sakṣaṇāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Lord Sun acknowledged his obeisance with a slight knitting of the eyebrows and traversed a great distance along the path of the sky in a moment.

## \|\| 1.9.34-35 \|\|

*prakrāṃte dyumaṇau dūraṃ śivaśarmātiśarmavān \|*  
*provāca bhagavadbhaktau kathaṃ labhyaṃ raveḥ padam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotumācakṣāthāṃ mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*satāṃ sāptapadī maitrī tanme maitryā praṇoditau \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. When the Sun had gone afar, Śivaśarman joyously spoke to the devotees of the Lord: “How is the region of the Sun to be attained? I wish to hear this. Kindly recount it to me. Friendship among good people is created by a mere exchange of seven words. Urged by friendship for me, you should narrate the same to me.”

## \|\| 1.9.36 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*śṛṇu dvija mahāprājña tvayyakathyaṃ na kiṃcana \|*  
*satsaṃgādeva sādhūnāṃ satkathā saṃpravartate \|\| 36 \|\|*

The attendants said:

36\. Listen, O Brāhmaṇa of great intellect. There is nothing that should not be spoken to you. It is through the contact of the good people that a good discourse takes place.

## \|\| 1.9.37-39 \|\|

*niyaṃtā sarvabhūtānāṃ ya ekaḥkāraṇaṃ param \|*  
*anāmā gotrarahito rūpādi parivarjitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*āvirbhāva tirobhāvau yadbhūnartanavartinau \|*  
*sa eva vakti satataṃ sarvātmā vedapūruṣaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yosāvādityapuruṣaḥ sosāvahamiti sphuṭam \|*  
*aṃdhatamaḥ praviśaṃti ye caivānyamupāsate \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. The Absolute Being is the controller of all living beings. It is the ultimate cause. It is nameless and devoid of a family. It has no form or anything like that. The manifestation and the disappearance (of the universe) takes place when his brows move. That absolute source or originator of the Vedas, the immanent soul of all says thus: “It is clear that I am identical with the Puruṣa (Person, Being) who is in the Āditya (Sun). Those who worship another being (deity) enter blinding darkness.”

## \|\| 1.9.40-41 \|\|

*niścitārthāṃ śrutimimāṃ brāhmaṇāso dvijottama \|*  
*tamekamupatiṣṭhaṃte niścityeti punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*upalabhya ca sāvitrīṃ nopatiṣṭheta yaḥ parām \|*  
*kāle trikālaṃ saptāhātsa patennātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, Brāhmaṇas comprehend the meaning of this irrefutable Vedic passage and worship that single Being. He who, having acquired the great deity in the form of the Sun, does not worship it thrice a day, undoubtedly falls in seven days.

## \|\| 1.9.42 \|\|

*tāvatprātarjapaṃstiṣṭhedyāvadardhodayo raveḥ \|*  
*āsanastho japenmaunī pratyagātārakodayāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The devotee should continue (to stand) repeating the Japa while facing the Sun in the morning as long as the disk of the Sun rises up half. In the evening he should perform the Japa silently sitting down till the stars appear (in the sky).

## \|\| 1.9.43 \|\|

*sādityāṃ madhyamāṃ saṃdhyāṃ japedādityasaṃmukhaḥ \|*  
*kālalopo na kartavyastataḥ kālaṃ pratīkṣayet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The devotee should continue the Japa even as the setting Sun is present in the sky. During midday he should repeat the Japa facing the Sun. The time should not be missed. It should rather be waited for.

## \|\| 1.9.44 \|\|

*kāle phalaṃtyoṣadhayaḥ kāle puṣpaṃti pādapāḥ \|*  
*varṣaṃti toyadāḥ kāle tasmātkālaṃ na laṃghayet \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Plants bear fruit at the proper time. Trees bloom at the proper time. Clouds shower at the proper time. Hence one should not transgress the proper time (of performing Sandhyā prayer).

## \|\| 1.9.45 \|\|

*maṃdehadehanāśārthamudayāstamaye raviḥ \|*  
*samīhate dvijotsṛṣṭaṃ maṃtratoyāṃjalitrayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. At the time of his rise and setting, the Sun wishes for three handfuls of water inspired by the Mantra and offered by the Brāhmaṇas, for the purpose of the destruction of the demons named Mandehas.

## \|\| 1.9.46 \|\|

*gāyatrīmaṃtratoyāḍhyaṃ dattaṃ yenāṃjalitrayam \|*  
*kāle savitre kiṃ na syāttena dattaṃ jagattrayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Is it not equivalent to the gift of three worlds if three handfuls of water sanctified by the Gāyatrī Mantra are offered to the Sun at the stipulated time?

## \|\| 1.9.47-48 \|\|

*kiṃ kiṃ na savitā sūte kāle samyagupāsitaḥ \|*  
*āyurārogyamaiśvaryaṃ vasūni sapaśūni ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

*mitraputra kalatrāṇi kṣetrāṇi vividhāni ca \|*  
*bhogānaṣṭavidhāṃścāpi svargaṃ cāpyapavargakam \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Worshipped duly at the proper time, what is it that the Sun does not yield? He bestows long life, good health, prosperity, wealth with cattle, friends, sons, wives, different kinds of fields, the eight types of pleasurable things (viz. sweet scents, women, garments, music, betel-chewing, foodstuff, vehicles and mansions, heavenly pleasures and salvation).

## \|\| 1.9.49-50 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśa suvidyāsu mīmāṃsātigarīyasī \|*  
*tatopi tarkaśāstrāṇi purāṇaṃ tebhya eva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tatopi dharmaśāstrāṇi tebhyo gurvī śrutirdvija \|*  
*tatopyupaniṣacchreṣṭhā gāyatrī ca tatodhikā \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Among the eighteen esteemed lores, Mīmāṃsā is the greatest; the system of logic is still greater; Purāṇa is greater than it; Dharmaśāstras are still greater, O Brāhmaṇa. The Śruti is greater than they; the Upaniṣad is still greater and Gāyatrī is superior to it.

## \|\| 1.9.51 \|\|

*durlabhā sarvamaṃtreṣu gāyatrī praṇavānvitā \|*  
*na gāyatryādhikaṃ kiṃcittrayīṣu parigīyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Among all the Mantras, Gāyatrī with Praṇava is the most rare and hence worthy of respect. No Mantra greater than Gāyatrī is sung in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.9.52 \|\|

*na gāyatrī samo maṃtro na kāśī sadṛśī purī \|*  
*na viśveśa samaṃ liṃgaṃ satyaṃsatyaṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. It is true. It is true again and again that there is no Mantra on a par with Gāyatrī. There is no city equal to Kāśī. There is no Liṅga on a par with Viśveśa.

## \|\| 1.9.53 \|\|

*gāyatrī vedajananī gāyatrī brāhmaṇaprasūḥ \|*  
*gātāraṃ trāyate yasmādgāyatrī tena gīyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Gāyatrī is the mother of the Vedas. Gāyatrī gives births to Brāhmaṇas. Since it saves him who sings (performs Japa of) it, it is described as Gāyatrī.

## \|\| 1.9.54 \|\|

*vācyavācakasaṃbaṃdho gāyatryāḥ saviturdvayoḥ \|*  
*vācyosau savitā sākṣādgāyatrīvācikāparā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The relationship between the two, the Sun and Gāyatrī is that of the word and the object signified by it. Gāyatrī is the great expression and the Sun is the expressed object.

## \|\| 1.9.55 \|\|

*prabhāveṇaiva gāyatryāḥ kṣatriyaḥ kauśiko vaśī \|*  
*rājarṣitvaṃ parityajya brahmarṣipadamīyivān \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. It is through the power of Gāyatrī that Kauśika (Viśvāmitra), the Kṣatriya of good control over his sense-organs, discarded his status as a royal sage and attained the status of a Brāhmaṇa sage.

## \|\| 1.9.56 \|\|

*sāmarthyaṃ prāpa cātyuccairanyadbhuvanasarjane \|*  
*kiṃ kiṃ na dadyādgāyatrī samyagevamupāsitā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He attained another miraculous power of high order, i.e. that of creating a new world. What is it that Gāyatrī served and resorted to very well in this manner, does not bestow?

## \|\| 1.9.57 \|\|

*na brāhmaṇo vedapāṭhānna śāstrapaṭhanādapi \|*  
*devyāstrikālamabhyāsādbāhmaṇaḥ syāddhi nānyathā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A man becomes a Brāhmaṇa neither by reciting the Vedas nor by learning philosophical texts. One becomes a Brāhmaṇa by repeated utterance of the goddess (i.e., Gāyatrī). Indeed not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.9.58 \|\|

*gāyatryeva paraṃ viṣṇurgāyatryeva paraḥśivaḥ \|*  
*gāyatryeva parobrahmā gāyatryeva trayī tataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Gāyatrī alone is the great Viṣṇu; Gāyatrī alone is the great Śiva; Gāyatrī alone is the great Brahmā. Therefore, Gāyatrī alone is the triad of Vedas (which are identical with Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva).

## \|\| 1.9.59 \|\|

*devatrayaṃ sa bhagavānaṃśumālī divākaraḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ mahasāṃ rāśiḥ kālakālapravartakaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. That Lord, the creater of the day (i.e. Sun) with rays as a garland, is identical with the triad of the Devas. He is the mass of all lustres. He is Time, the prime mover of time.

## \|\| 1.9.60 \|\|

*arkamuddiśya satatamasmallokanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*śrutiṃ hyudāharaṃtīmāṃ sārāsāravivekinaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Residents of our world (i.e., Vaikuṇṭha) who can discriminate between what is essential and what is non-essential, always cite this Śruti with the Sun in view.

## \|\| 1.9.61 \|\|

*eṣo ha devaḥ pradiśonu sarvāḥ pūrvo ha jātaḥ sa u garbhe aṃtaḥ \|*  
*sa eva jātaḥ sa janiṣyamāṇaḥ pratyaṅjānāstiṣṭhati sarvatomukhaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. This refulgent one penetrates all quarters and interior of quarters (sideways, above and below). He is without beginning or end. He is within the womb of the mother. He is the born. He will be the born. O people, he stands pervading every object with faces everywhere (like the Puruṣa of the Puruṣa Sūkta—Com.)

## \|\| 1.9.62 \|\|

*sadaivamupatiṣṭheransaurasūktairataṃdritāḥ \|*  
*ye namaṃtyatra te viprā viprā bhāskarasannibhāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Those who are active and alert and worship the Sun with the hymns pertaining to the Sun (Saura hymns) constantly and those who bow down, are the real Brāhmaṇas and those Brāhmaṇas are on a par with the Sun.

## \|\| 1.9.63 \|\|

*puṣyārkepyatha hastārke mūlārkepyathavā dvija \|*  
*uttarārke'tha yatkāryaṃ tatphalatyeva nānyathā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Whatever task is undertaken on a Sunday in conjunction with the constellation of Puṣya, Hasta, Mūla or Uttarā does become fruitful and not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.9.64-65 \|\|

*pauṣe māsyarkadivase yaḥ snātvā bhāskarodaye \|*  
*dānahomaṃjapaṃkuryādarcāmarkasya suvrata \|\| 64 \|\|*

*śraddhāvānekabhaktaśca kāmakrodhavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*sahāpsarobhirdyutimānsa vasedatra bhogavān \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. The devotee observing holy vows should take his holy bath at sunrise on a Sunday in the month of Pauṣa, and perform the rites of Dana (gift), Homa and Japa. He should adore the Sun with faith and devotion. He should be free from lust and anger. He shall thereby become brilliant and live here along with the celestial damsels enjoying all pleasures.

## \|\| 1.9.66-69 \|\|

*ayane viṣuve cāpi ṣaḍaśītimukheṣu vā \|*  
*viṣṇupadyāṃ ca ye dadyurmahādānāni suvratāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*tilāñjuhvati sājyāṃśca brāhmaṇānbhojayaṃti ca \|*  
*pitṝnuddiśya ca śrāddhaṃ ye kurvaṃti vipaścitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*mahāpūjāṃ ca ye kuryurmahāmaṃtrāñjapaṃti ca \|*  
*te'tra vaikartane loke vikartanasamaprabhā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*na daridrā na ca duḥkhārtā na vyādhi paripīḍitāḥ \|*  
*saṃkrameṣvarkabhaktā ye na virūpā na durbhagāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

66-69. Liberal gifts should be made at the time of the Ayana (i.e. during the transit of the Sun to the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn). Viṣuva days (equinoxes of Meṣa and Tulā), Ṣaḍaśīti etc. (during the transit of the Sun in Dhanus, Mithuna, Kanyā and Mīna Zodiacs) and Viṣṇupadī (i.e. during the transit to Vṛścika, Vṛṣa, Siṃha and Kuṃbha Zodiacs).

Gingelly seeds soaked in ghee should be used for Homa. Brāhmaṇas should be fed. Śrāddha should be performed with the manes in view.

Great Pūjās should be performed and great Mantras should be repeated. Those scholars who do like this attain the world of the Sun and get a lustre on a par with that of the Sun.

Those who perform devotional rites during the transit of the Sun to the various Zodiacs, never become poor, distressed, afflicted with ailments, ugly or unfortunate.

## \|\| 1.9.70-71 \|\|

*saṃkrameṣu na yairdattaṃ na snātaṃ tīrthavāriṣu \|*  
*viśeṣahomo na kṛtaḥ kapilājyāplutaistilaiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*te dṛśyaṃte pratidvāraṃ vihīna nayanānanāḥ \|*  
*dehidehīti jalpaṃto dehinaḥ sapaṭaccarāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. If gifts are not made, holy bath is not taken in the sacred waters, special Homa is not performed with gingelly seeds soaked in ghee from the milk of a tawny-coloured cow, the men guilty thereof, shall become blind and very poor and will be uttering piteously beseeching “Give, give” at every door wearing rags.

## \|\| 1.9.72 \|\|

*samaṃ kṛṣṇalakenāpi yo dadyātkāṃcanaṃ kṛtī \|*  
*sūryagrahe kurukṣetre sa vasedatra puṇyabhāk \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. A blessed man who makes a gift of a gold piece even as small as a Guñjā berry at the time of solar eclipse in Kurukṣetra shall become meritorious and stay here.

## \|\| 1.9.73 \|\|

*sarvaṃ gaṃgāsamaṃ toyaṃ sarve brahmasamā dvijāḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ deyaṃ svarṇasamaṃ rāhugraste divākare \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. When the Sun is swallowed by Rāhu (i.e., during solar eclipse) all waters are on a par with Gaṅgā, all Brāhmaṇas are on a par with Brahmā and everything gifted equal with gold.

## \|\| 1.9.74 \|\|

*dattaṃ japtaṃ hutaṃ snātaṃ yatkiṃcitsadanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*bhānūparāge śrāddhādi taddheturbradhna saṃnidhe \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Whatever holy thing is performed by way of gifts, Japas, Hoṃas, holy baths, Śrāddha etc., at the time of solar eclipse shall be the cause of the presence of the Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.9.75 \|\|

*ravivāre saṃkramaśceduparāgo'thavābhavet \|*  
*tadā yadarjitaṃ puṇyaṃ tadihākṣayamāpyate \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. If the transit of the Sun falls on a Sunday or if there is a solar eclipse then, the merit acquired at that time becomes never-ending.

## \|\| 1.9.76 \|\|

*bhānuvāro yadā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ saptamyāmatha jāyate \|*  
*tadā yatsukṛtaṃ karma kṛtaṃ tadiha bhujyate \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. If the Sunday coincides with sixth or seventh lunar day and a meritorious holy rite is performed, then that will be enjoyed here itself.

\[Seventy names of the Sun god\]

## \|\| 1.9.92 \|\|

*ityekadeśaḥ kathito bhānulokasya sattama \|*  
*mahātejonidherasya koviśeṣamavaityaho \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Thus, O excellent one, an aspect of the Solar world has been recounted. Who can comprehend the special characteristics of this (god), the storehouse of great refulgence.

## \|\| 1.9.93 \|\|

*svakarṇaviṣayīkurvannitipuṇyakathāmimām \|*  
*kṣaṇādālokayāṃcakre maheṃdrasya mahāpurīm \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Having attentively listened to this meritorious story, (the Brāhmaṇa) espied the great city of Mahendra soon.

## \|\| 1.9.94 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*śrutvā saurīṃ kathametāmapsarolokasaṃyutām \|*  
*na daridro bhavetkvāpi nādharmeṣu pravartate \|\| 94 \|\|*

Agastya said:

94\. By listening to this story pertaining to the Sun along with that of the world of Apsarās, the devotee will never be afflicted with poverty. He will never engage himself in unrighteous activities.

## \|\| 1.9.95-96 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaiḥ satataṃ śrāvyamidamākhyānamuttamam \|*  
*vedapāṭhena yatpuṇyaṃ tatpuṇyaphaladāyakam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śṛṇvaṃto'dhyāyamuttamam \|*  
*pātakāni visṛjyeha gatiṃ yāsyaṃtyanuttamām \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. This excellent narrative should always be listened to by Brāhmaṇas. It accords the merit that accrues from Vedic study and recitation.

Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas listening to this excellent chapter abandon all their sins here, and attain the excellent goal.

## Chapter 9 - Seventy names of the Sun God

## \|\| 1.9.77 \|\|

*haṃso bhānuḥ sahasrāṃśustapanastāpano ravi \|*  
*vikartano vivasvāṃśca viśvakarmā vibhāvasuḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

\[Note: The seventy names of the Sun god are to be Repeated and Arghya offered; The commentary gives interpretations of each name. See previous chapter for context.\]

77\. (1) Haṃsa (the pure Sattva), (2) Bhānu (the refulgent), (3) Sahasrāṃśu (thousand-rayed), (4) Tapana (blazing), (5) Tāpana (scorching), (6) Ravi (protector of the worlds), (7) Vikartana (whetted for more brilliance), (8) Vivasvān (having special refulgence), (9) Viśvakarman (of universal activity), (10) Vibhāvasu (of fiery nature),

## \|\| 1.9.78 \|\|

*viśvarūpo viśvakartā mārtaṃḍo mihiroṃ'śumān \|*  
*ādityaścoṣṇaguḥ sūryo'ryamā bradhno divākaraḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. (11) Viśvarūpa (of universal form), (12) Viśvakartā (the procreator of the universe), (13) Mārtaṇḍa (present in the insentient Cosmic Egg in the form of Vairāja), (14) Mihira (destroyer of mist), (15) Aṃśumān (having rays), (16) Āditya (Aditi’s son), (19) Aryamān (Triad of Vedas personified), (20) Bradhna (making the universe flourish), (21) Divākara (maker of the day),

## \|\| 1.9.79 \|\|

*dvādaśātmā saptahayo bhāskaro haskaraḥ khagaḥ \|*  
*suraḥ prabhākaraḥ śrīmāṃllokacakṣurgraheśvaraḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. (22) Dvādaśātmā (having twelve forms), (23) Saptahaya (seven-horsed), (24) Bhāskara (creator of brilliance), (25) Ahaskara (usherer of the day), (26) Khaga (going forth in the firmament), (27) Sūra (one that gives birth to the universe), (28) Prabhākara (illuminator), (29) Śrīmān Lokacakṣuḥ (the glorious one brightening the worlds, the eye of the worlds), (30) Graheśvara (Lord of the Planets),

## \|\| 1.9.80 \|\|

*trilokeśo lokasākṣītamoriḥ śāśvataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*gabhastihastastīvrāṃśustaraṇiḥ sumahoraṇiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. (31) Trilokeśa (the controller of the three worlds), (32) Lokasākṣī (the immanent soul of the world), (33) Tamori (enemy of darkness), (34) Śāśvata (the eternal one), (35) Śuci (sacred), (36) Gabhastihasta (having rays for hands), (37) Tīvrāṃśu (hot-rayed), (38) Taraṇi (redeemer of devotees like a raft across the ocean), (39) Sumahaḥ (of splendid brilliance), (40) Araṇi (the place of maifestation of everything),

## \|\| 1.9.81 \|\|

*dyumaṇirharidaśvorko bhānumānbhayanāśanaḥ \|*  
*chandośvo vedavedyaśca bhāsvānpūṣā vṛṣākapiḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. (41) Dyumaṇi (jewel of the firmament), (42) Haridaśva (green-horsed), (43) Arka (of swift movement, worthy of respect), (44) Bhānumān (possessor of rays), (45) Bhayanāśana (destroyer of fear), (46) Chandośva (having the Metres of the Vedas for horses), (47) Vedavedya (to be realized through the Vedas), (48) Bhāsvān (luminous), (49) Pūṣan (one who nourishes), (50) Vṛṣākapi (showering merit and shaking off sin),

## \|\| 1.9.82 \|\|

*ekacakraratho mitro maṃdehāristamisrahā \|*  
*daityahā pāpahartā ca dharmodharma prakāśakaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. (51) Ekacakraratha (having a single-wheeled chariot), (52) Mitra (friendly), (53) Mandehāri (enemy of the demons Mandehas), (54) Tamisrahā (destroyer of pitch darkness), (55) Daityahā (slayer of demons), (56) Pāpahartā (remover of sins), (57) Dharma (sustained, righteousness personified), (58) Dharmaprakāśaka (illuminator of piety),

## \|\| 1.9.83 \|\|

*helikaścitrabhānuśca kalighnastārkṣyavāhanaḥ \|*  
*dikpatiḥ padminīnāthaḥ kuśeśayakaro hariḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. (59) Helika (moving about in the firmament), (60) Citrabhānu (having variegated rays), (61) Kalighna (destroyer of kali, strife), (62) Tārkṣyavāhana (having Tṛkṣa’s i.e., Kaśyapa’s son i.e., Anūru as charioteer), (63) Dikpati (lord of the quarters), (64) Padmininātha (lord of the lotus pond), (65) Kuśeśayakara (having a lotus in the hand), (66) Hari (remover of darkness and sin),

## \|\| 1.9.84-89 \|\|

*gharmaraśmirdurnirīkṣyaścaṃḍāṃśuḥ kaśyapātmajaḥ \|*  
*ebhiḥ saptatisaṃkhyākaiḥ puṇyaiḥ sūryasya nāmabhiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*praṇavādi caturthyaṃtairnamaskāra samanvitaiḥ \|*  
*pratyekamuccarannāma dṛṣṭvādṛṣṭvā divākaram \|\| 85 \|\|*

*vigṛhya pāṇiyugmena tāmrapātraṃ sunirmalam \|*  
*jānubhyāmavaniṃ gatvā paripūrya jalena ca \|\| 86 \|\|*

*karavīrādi kusumai raktacaṃdanamiśritaiḥ \|*  
*dūrvāṃkurairakṣataiśca nikṣiptaiḥ pātramadhyataḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*dadyādarghyamanarghyāya savitre dhyānapūrvakam \|*  
*upamauli samānīya tatpātraṃ nānyadṛṅmanāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*pratimaṃtraṃ namaskuryādudayāstamaye ravim \|*  
*anayā nāmasaptatyā mahāmaṃtrarahasyayā \|\| 89 \|\|*

84-89. (67) Gharmaraśmi (hot-rayed), (68) Durnirīkṣya (very painful to look at), (69) Caṇḍāṃśu (hot-rayed), (70) Kaśyapātmaja (son of Kaśyapa).

These seventy names of the Sun-god are meritorious. They are to be used in the dative case with Om in the beginning and namaḥ (obeisance) added afterwards. (For example ‘om mitrāya namaḥ’). Looking every time at the Sun directly, these names should be uttered holding a copper vessel (free from impurities with both the hands). (The vessel is to be filled with water.) The devotee kneels on the ground and fills the waterpot with Karavīra and other flowers mixed with red sandal-paste. Dūrvā grass and raw rice grains should be put into the waterpot. Meditating on him, the devotee offers Arghya to the most esteemed Savitṛ (Sun) god taking the pot up to the head. The eyes and the mind should not be directed elsewhere.

These seventy names are on a par with great esoteric Mantras. At the end of each name, Mantra, the devotee should bow to the Sun-god. This has to be done both at sunrise and at sunset.

## \|\| 1.9.90 \|\|

*evaṃ kurvannaro jātu na daridro na duḥkhabhāk \|*  
*vyādhibhirmucyate ghorairapijanmāṃtarārjitaiḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Performing the holy rite thus, no man shall ever be poor or miserable. He will be rid of all terrible ailments and (even sins) though acquired in the course of many births.

## \|\| 1.9.91 \|\|

*vinauṣadhairvinā vaidyairvināpathyaparigrahaiḥ \|*  
*kālena nidhanaṃ prāptaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Without medicines, without doctors, without following strict regimen (he will be cured). When he dies in due course, he is honoured in the world of the Sun-god.

## Chapter 10 - The Worlds Of Indra And Agni

## \|\| 1.10.1 \|\|

*śivaśarmovāca \|*  
*ramayaṃtī manotīva keyaṃ kasyeyamīśituḥ \|*  
*nayanānaṃdasaṃdohadāyinīpūranuttamā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śivaśarman said:

1\. What is this excellent city that accords much delight to the eyes and a great deal of pleasure to the mind? Who is the Lord thereof?

## \|\| 1.10.2 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*śivaśarmanmahābhāgasutīrthaphalitadruma \|*  
*loko'tra ramate vipra sahasākṣapurī tviyam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The attendants said:

2\. O glorious Śivaśarman whose pilgrimage to sacred places (v.l., people whose pilgrimage to holy places) has become a fruitful tree sport about in this world. O Brāhmaṇa, this is the city of the thousand-eyed Indra.

## \|\| 1.10.3 \|\|

*tapobalena mahatā vihitā viśvakamarṇā \|*  
*divāpi kaumudī yasyāḥ saudhaśreṇīśriyaṃ śrayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It has been built by Viśvakarman through the great power of penance. The places hereof have the splendour of the moonlight even during the day.

## \|\| 1.10.4 \|\|

*yadākalānidhiḥ kvāpi darśe 'dṛśyatvamāvahet \|*  
*tadā svapreyasīṃ jyotsnāṃ saudheṣveṣu nigūhayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Whenever during the New-Moon day (and other occasions) the moon becomes invisible, he sends (secretly) his wife Jyotsnā (Moonlight) to move about among these mansions.

## \|\| 1.10.5 \|\|

*yadacchabhittau vīkṣya svamanyayopidviśaṃkitā \|*  
*mugdhānāśuviśeccitramapisvāṃcitraśālikām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It is surprising indeed that an immature lady among the celestial women sees her own reflection in the excellent walls of (her house) and begins to suspect that another lady has already come in, and therefore (feeling jealous) she does not enter her own apartment.

## \|\| 1.10.6 \|\|

*harmyeṣu nīlamaṇibhirnirmiteṣvatranirbhayam \|*  
*svanīlimānamādhāya tamohaḥsvapi tiṣṭhati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Even during the day time, darkness stays in this city without fear, after transferring its own blackness on the mansions built of sapphire.

## \|\| 1.10.7 \|\|

*caṃdrakāṃtaśilājālasrutamātrāmalaṃjalam \|*  
*tatra cādāya kalaśairnecchaṃtyanyajjalaṃ janāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. People here in this city, collect in their pots the pure water oozing out of the Candrakānta Crystals (moonstones) and never desire any other type of water.

## \|\| 1.10.8 \|\|

*kuviṃdā na ca saṃtyatra na ca te paśyato harāḥ \|*  
*cailānyalaṃkṛtīratra yataḥ kalpadrumorpayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There are neither weavers nor goldsmiths here, because the wish-yielding Kalpa-tree supplies clothes and ornaments.

## \|\| 1.10.9 \|\|

*gaṇakā nātra vidyaṃte ciṃtāvidyāviśāradāḥ \|*  
*yataściketi sarveṣāṃ ciṃtā ciṃtāmaṇirdrutam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Astrologers clever in the art of calculation are not present here, because the fabulous philosopher’s stone (Cintāmaṇi) calculates and understands quickly the innermost thoughts and desires of everyone.

## \|\| 1.10.10 \|\|

*sūpakārā na saṃtyatra rasakarma vicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*dugdhe sarvarasānekā kāmadhenuratoyataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There are no cooks here efficient in the art of preparation of beverages and juices, because the cow Kāmadhenu alone yields all types of juices by way of milk.

## \|\| 1.10.11 \|\|

*kīrtiruccaiḥśravā yasya sarvato vājirājiṣu \|*  
*ratnamuccaiḥśravāḥ sotra hayānāṃ pauruṣādhikaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Uccaiśśravas, the jewel among horses, possessing superior power (or which is the Vibhūti of Viṣṇu), whose reputation is sung about loudly everywhere in the midst of groups of horses (stays here).

## \|\| 1.10.12 \|\|

*airāvato daṃtivaraścaturdaṃtotra rājate \|*  
*dvitīya iva kailāso jaṃgamasphaṭikojjvalaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Airāvata, the four-tusked excellent elephant, shines here as the second mobile Kailāsa mountain. It is as brilliant as crystal.

## \|\| 1.10.13 \|\|

*taruratnaṃpārijātaḥ strīratnaṃ sorvaśī tviha \|*  
*naṃdanaṃ vanaratnaṃ ca ratnaṃ maṃdākinī hyapām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Pārijāta, the most excellent tree, Urvaśī the jewel among women, Nandana, the most excellent park and Mandākinī (Gaṅgā), the most excellent river (waterway), are here.

## \|\| 1.10.14 \|\|

*trayastriṃśatsurāṇāṃ yā koṭiḥ śruti samīritā \|*  
*pratīkṣate sā'vasaraṃ sevāyai pratyahaṃtviha \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thirty-three crores of Suras as mentioned in the Vedas await their turn everyday here for service (unto their Lord).

## \|\| 1.10.15 \|\|

*svargeṣviṃdrapadādanyanna viśiṣyeta kiṃcana \|*  
*yadyattrilokyāmaiśvaryaṃ na tattulyamanena hi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Nothing is more excellent than the status of Indra in the heavenly worlds. Whatever glory and prosperity is in the three worlds, cannot be on a par with his (Indra’s) prosperity.

## \|\| 1.10.16 \|\|

*aśvamedhasahasrasya labhyaṃ vinimayena yat \|*  
*kiṃ tena tulyamanyatsyātpavitramathavā mahata \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. What else can be as holy and as great as that which is acquired in exchange for a thousand horse sacrifices?

## \|\| 1.10.17 \|\|

*arciṣmatī saṃyaminī puṇyavatyamalāvatī \|*  
*gaṃdhavatyalakeśī ca naitattulyā mahardhibhiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. None (of the seven cities of Fire-god and other Guardians of Quarters) viz. Arciṣmatī, Saṃyaminī, Puṇyavatī, Amalavatī, Gandhavatī, Alakā or Aiśī is equal to this in glory and prosperity.

## \|\| 1.10.18 \|\|

*ayameva sahasrākṣastvayameva divaspatiḥ \|*  
*śatamanyurayaṃ devo nāmānyetāni nāmataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He alone is called Sahasrākṣa (‘Thousand-eyed’); he alone is Divaspati (‘Lord of Heaven’); this lord alone is Śatamanyu (‘one with hundred sacrifices’); these are his very famous names.

## \|\| 1.10.19 \|\|

*saptāpi lokapālā ye ta enaṃ samupāsate \|*  
*nāradādyairmunivarairayamāśīrbhirīḍyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The seven (other) Guardians of the world serve and adore him. He is honoured with blessings by the excellent sages, Nārada and others.

## \|\| 1.10.20 \|\|

*etatsthairyeṇa sarveṣāṃ lokānāṃ sthairyamiṣyate \|*  
*parājayānmaheṃdrasya trailokyaṃ syātparājitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The stability of all the worlds is wished for through the stability of this (lord). All the three worlds will be defeated at the defeat of Mahendra.

## \|\| 1.10.21 \|\|

*danujā manujā daityāstapasyaṃtyugrasaṃyamāḥ \|*  
*gaṃdharva yakṣarakṣāṃsi maheṃdrapadalipsavaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Dānavas, human beings, Daityas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas etc. desirous of Amarāvatī, the city of Mahendra, perform penances with strict self-control.

## \|\| 1.10.22 \|\|

*sagarādyā mahīpālā vājimedhavidhāyakāḥ \|*  
*kṛtavaṃto mahāyatnaṃ śakraiśvaryajighṛkṣavaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Desirous of seizing the glory and prosperity of Śakra, kings like Sagara, and others, made great effort such as the performance of horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.10.23 \|\|

*niṣpratyūhaṃ kratuśataṃ yaḥ kaścitkurute'vanau \|*  
*jiteṃdriyomarāvatyāṃ sa prāpnoti pulomajām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Whoever keeps all his senses under control and performs a hundred sacrifices without any hindrance on the earth, gets Pulomajā (Śacī) in the city of Amarāvatī.

## \|\| 1.10.24 \|\|

*asamāptakratuśatā vasaṃtyatra mahībhujaḥ \|*  
*jyotiṣṭomādibhiryāgairye yajaṃtyapi te dvijāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Kings who could not complete a hundred sacrifices reside here; so also do the Brāhmaṇas who perform Jyotiṣṭoma and other sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.10.25 \|\|

*tulāpuruṣadānādi mahādānāni ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*ye yacchaṃtyamalātmānaste labhaṃte'marāvatīm \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Those who offer the sixteen great gifts such as Tulā-Puruṣadāna (‘offering things equal in weight to the donor’) become purified souls and they attain Amarāvatī.

## \|\| 1.10.26 \|\|

*aklībavādino dhīrāḥ saṃgrāmeṣvaparāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*vikrāṃtā vīraśayane te'tra tiṣṭhaṃti bhūbhujaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Bold men never uttering timid words, those who never turn back in battles and those who lie down in the battlefield (lit. hero’s bed)—those kings stay here.

## \|\| 1.10.27 \|\|

*ityuddeśātsamākhyātā maheṃdranagarī sthitiḥ \|*  
*yāyajūkā vasaṃtyatra yajñavidyāviśāradāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus, in general, the situation of the city of Mahendra has been recounted. Those who invariably perform sacrifices, are experts in the science and technique of sacrifices reside here.

## \|\| 1.10.28 \|\|

*imāmarciṣmatīṃ paśya vītihotrapurīṃ śubhām \|*  
*jātavedasi ye bhaktāste vasaṃtyatra suvratāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. See this splendid Arciṣmatī, the city of the Fire-god. Those who are devotees of Fire-god and observe excellent vows, reside here.

## \|\| 1.10.29 \|\|

*agnipraveśaṃ ye kuryurdṛḍhasattvā jiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*striyo vā sattvasaṃpannāste sarve agnitejasaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Persons with steadfast Sattva quality and with control over the organs of sense and action entering the blazing fire (for self-immolation), women richly endowed with Sattva quality—all these possess fiery splendour.

## \|\| 1.10.30 \|\|

*agnihotraratā viprāstathāgnibrahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*paṃcāgnivratino ye vai te'gnilokegnitejasaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Brāhmaṇas engaged in Agnihotra, men observing the vow of celibacy, keeping the sacred fire blazing, those who observe the holy vow of Pañcāgni—all these attain the region of Fire and possess fiery splendour.

## \|\| 1.10.31 \|\|

*śīte śītāpanutyai yastvidhmabhārānprayacchati \|*  
*kuryādagniṣṭikāṃ vā'tha sa vasedagnisannidhau \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He who makes a gift of bundles of fuel in winter season for the purpose of warding off cold as well as of ovens of fire, shall reside near Fire-god.

## \|\| 1.10.32 \|\|

*anāthasyāgnisaṃskāraṃ yaḥ kuryācchraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*aśaktaḥ prerayedanyaṃ sogniloke mahīyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He who, with great faith, performs cremation and consecration with fire of a helpless person or, if he is incapable himself, urges others to do so, is honoured in the world of Fire-god.

## \|\| 1.10.33 \|\|

*jaṭharāgnivivṛddhyai yo dadyādāgneyamauṣadham \|*  
*maṃdāgnaye sa puṇyātmā vahniloke vasecciram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A man of meritorious soul who gives a person of chronic indigestion, medicines kindling the gastric fire, shall live in the world of Agni for a long time.

## \|\| 1.10.34 \|\|

*yajñopaskara vastūni yajñārthaṃ draviṇaṃ tu vā \|*  
*yathāśakti pradadyādyo hyarciṣmatyāṃvasetsa vai \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He who offers in accordance with his capacity, articles essential for a sacrifice or money for the sake of sacrifice, shall reside in Arciṣmatī.

## \|\| 1.10.35 \|\|

*agnireko dvijātīnāṃ niḥśreyasakaraḥ paraḥ \|*  
*gururdevo vrataṃ tīrthaṃ sarvamagnirviniścitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Agni alone is the greatest god bringing about salvation to Brāhmaṇas; he is the preceptor, God, religious vow, holy spot. Nay, Agni is decisively everything.

## \|\| 1.10.36 \|\|

*apāvanāni sarvāṇi vahnisaṃsargataḥ kṣaṇāt \|*  
*pāvanāni bhavaṃtyeva tasmādyaḥ pāvakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. All unholy and unclean things become purified in a moment due to contact with fire. Hence Agni is spoken as Pāvaka (‘purifier’).

## \|\| 1.10.37 \|\|

*api vedaṃ viditvā yastyaktvā vai jātavedasam \|*  
*anyatra badhnāti ratiṃ brāhmaṇo na sa vedavit \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Even after studying the Vedas, if one abandons sacrificial fire and cultivates interest elsewhere, he is not a genuine Brāhmaṇa knowing the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.10.38 \|\|

*aṃtarātmā hyayaṃ sākṣānniścito hyāśuśukṣaṇiḥ \|*  
*māṃsagrāsānpacetkukṣau strīṇāṃ no māṃsapeśikām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Certainly Fire-god is the immanent soul. It may very well burn (reduce) the external flesh in the belly of women but not the foetus in the womb.

## \|\| 1.10.39 \|\|

*taijasī śāṃbhavī mūrtiḥ pratyakṣā dahanātmikā \|*  
*kartrī haṃtrī pālayitrī vinaināṃ kiṃ vilokyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The fiery form of Śaṃbhu is of scorching feature. It is the creative, destructive and sustaining force. What is there to be seen without it?

## \|\| 1.10.40 \|\|

*citrabhānurayaṃ sākṣānnetraṃ tribhuvaneśituḥ \|*  
*aṃdhaṃ tamomaye loke vinainaṃ kaḥ prakāśakaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. This Citrabhānu (Fire) is the eye of the Lord of the three worlds himself. In the world of blinding darkness who else is the illuminator excepting him (Fire)?

## \|\| 1.10.41 \|\|

*dhūpapradīpanaivedya payo dadhi ghṛtaikṣavam \|*  
*etadbhuktaṃ niṣevaṃte sarve divi divaukasaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Incense, lamp, Naivedya (food offerings), milk, curd, ghee and sugarcane juice taken in by this Fire is resorted to by all the heaven-dwellers in the heaven.

Śivaśarman asked:

## \|\| 1.10.42 \|\|

*śivaśarmovāca \|*  
*koyaṃ kṛśānuḥ kasyāyaṃ sūnuḥ kathamidaṃ padam \|*  
*āgneyaṃ labdhametena brūtametanmamāgrataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Who is this Kṛśānu (Fire)? Whose son is he? How is this fiery region obtained by him? Recount this to me.

The attendants replied:

## \|\| 1.10.43 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*ākarṇaya mahāprājña varṇayāvo yathātatham \|*  
*yoyaṃ yasya yathā'nena prāpi jyotiṣmatīpurī \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Listen, O highly intelligent one. We shall describe duly who he is, whose son he is and how the city of Jyotiṣmatī was obtained by him.

## \|\| 1.10.44 \|\|

*narmadāyāstaṭe ramye pure narmapure purā \|*  
*purāribhaktaḥ puṇyātmā'bhavadviśvānaro muniḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On the beautiful banks of Narmadā, in the city of Narmapura, formerly there was a sage named Viśvānara, a devotee of Śiva and a meritorious soul.

## \|\| 1.10.45 \|\|

*brahmacaryāśrame niṣṭho brahmayajñarataḥsadā \|*  
*śāṃḍilyagotraḥ śucimānbrahmatejo nidhirvaśī \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He was in the Brahmacarya (celibate) stage of life firmly established therein. He was always engaged in Brahmayajña \[the holy Yajña (adoration) of the study of Vedas\]. He belonged to Śāṇḍilya Gotra. He was pure, a storehouse of Brāhmaṇical splendour, a man of great self-control.

## \|\| 1.10.46 \|\|

*vijñātākhilaśāstrārtho laukikācāracaṃcuraḥ \|*  
*kadācicciṃtayāmāsa hṛdi dhyātvā maheśvaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He had understood the meanings of all scriptural texts. He was an expert in social conventions and pious practices. Once he meditated on Maheśvara and thought in his heart thus:

## \|\| 1.10.47 \|\|

*caturṇāmapyāśramāṇāṃ kotīva śreyase satām \|*  
*yasminprāpnoti saṃkṣuṇṇe paratreha ca vā sukham \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. ‘Which among the four stages of life, is more conducive to the welfare of good people, by properly practising which a man attains happiness here and hereafter?’

## \|\| 1.10.48 \|\|

*idaṃ śreyastvidaṃ śreyastvidaṃ tu sukaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*itthaṃ sarvaṃ samāloḍya gārhasthyaṃ praśaśaṃsa ha \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He pondered over everything carefully and from several points of view: ‘This is beneficial’, ‘This also is beneficial’, ‘This may be easy to do’, and ultimately praised the stage of a householder.

## \|\| 1.10.49 \|\|

*brahmacārī gṛhastho vā vānaprastho'tha bhikṣukaḥ \|*  
*eṣāmādhārabhūtosau gṛhastho nānyatheti ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. To the religious student, the householder, the forest-dweller or the recluse, it is the householder who acts as the supporter and no one else.

## \|\| 1.10.50 \|\|

*devairmanuṣyaiḥ pitṛbhistiryagbhiścopajīvyate \|*  
*gṛhasthaḥ pratyahaṃ yasmāttasmācchreṣṭho gṛhāśramī \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Devas, human beings, manes and lower animals—all depend upon the householder everyday. Hence the householder is the most excellent one.

## \|\| 1.10.51 \|\|

*asnātvā cāpyahutvā vā'dattvā vāśnāti yo gṛhī \|*  
*devādīnāmṛṇī bhūtvā narakaṃ pratipadyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The householder who partakes of food without bathing, without performing Homo or without making any gift becomes indebted to Devas and others and falls into hell.

## \|\| 1.10.52 \|\|

*asnātāśī malaṃ bhuṃkte tvajapī pūyaśoṇitam \|*  
*ahutāśī kṛmīnbhuṃktepyadattvāviḍvibhojanaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. One who eats without bathing, eats dirt; one who takes in without performing Japa, drinks putrid blood; one who eats without performing Homa, eats worms; and one who eats without making a gift eats special diet of faeces.

## \|\| 1.10.53 \|\|

*brahmacaryaṃ hi gārhasthye yādṛkkalpanayojjhitam \|*  
*svabhāvacapale citte kva tādṛgbrahmacāriṇi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Celibacy in the course of a householder’s life is free from self-deception. How can such a celibacy be found in a bachelor whose mind is naturally fickle?

## \|\| 1.10.54 \|\|

*haṭhādvā lokabhītyā vā svārthādvā brahmacaryabhāk \|*  
*saṃkalpayati citte cetkṛtamapyakṛtaṃ tadā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. A bachelor adopts celibacy out of circumstantial compulsion or fear of the public or for some selfish ends. If he indulges in thinking (about wedded bliss), the celibacy adopted by him is no better than non-existent.

## \|\| 1.10.55 \|\|

*paradāraparityāgātsvadāraparituṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*ṛtukālābhigāmitvādbrahmacārī gṛhīritaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. A householder is considered to be a celibate if he avoids (contact with) other men’s wives, is fully satisfied with his wife, carnally enjoying her only on stipulated days after the menstrual bath.

## \|\| 1.10.56 \|\|

*vimuktarāgadveṣo yaḥ kāmakrodhavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*sāgniḥ sadāraḥ sa gṛhī vānaprasthādviśiṣyate \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A householder who is without undue attachment and hatred, who is devoid of lust and anger, who has a wife and who maintains sacrificial fire, is far better than a forest-dweller.

## \|\| 1.10.57 \|\|

*vairāgyādgṛhamutsṛjya gṛhadharmānhṛdi smaret \|*
