*hṛṣīkeśa iti khyāto yaḥ sa sarvatrasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The supreme lord has all-powerful control over all the sense-organs. Hence he is well known as Hṛṣīkeśa. He is present everywhere.

## \|\| 1.20.10 \|\|

*na cyavaṃtepi yadbhaktā mahati pralaye sati \|*  
*ato'cyuto'khile loke sa ekaḥ sarvago'vyayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Even in the great Pralaya (ultimate annihilation) his devotees never perish. Hence he is Acyuta. He alone is all-pervasive in the entire world. He is immutable.

## \|\| 1.20.11 \|\|

*idaṃ carācaraṃ viśvaṃ yo babhāra svalīlayā \|*  
*bhṛtyāsvarūpasaṃpattyā so'tra viśvaṃbharo'khilam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He bears and sustains sportingly the entire universe including the mobile and immobile beings, by direct administration as well as by richly endowing the devotee with his own identity (salvation). Hence, he is Viśvaṃbhara.

## \|\| 1.20.12 \|\|

*tasyekṣaṇe samīkṣete nānyadvipṇupadādṛte \|*  
*nirīkṣyaḥ puṃḍarīkākṣo nānyo niyamato hyataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. His (Dhruva’s) eyes never saw anything other than the feet of Viṣṇu, because invariably Puṇḍarīkākṣa and no one else is worthy of being seen.

## \|\| 1.20.13 \|\|

*nānya śabdagrahau tasya jātau śabdagrahāvapi \|*  
*vinā mukuṃda goviṃda dāmodara caturbhuja \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. His ears never heard any other words except Mukunda, Govinda, Dāmodara, Caturbhuja (and other names of Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 1.20.14 \|\|

*goviṃdacaraṇārthārcāṃ tatpriyaṃkarmavai vinā \|*  
*śaṃkhacakrāṃkitau tasya nānyakarmakaraukarau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. His hands marked by the lines of conch and discus did no other work, except the adoration seeking the feet of Govinda and such work as is loved and approved by him.

## \|\| 1.20.15 \|\|

*nirdvaṃdvacaraṇadvaṃdvaṃ tanmano manute hareḥ \|*  
*hitvānyanmananaṃ sarvaṃ niścalatvamavāpa ha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. His mind dwelt upon the pair of feet of Hari free from the pairs of opposites afflicting the world. Eschewing the thought of everything else, it became perfectly steady.

## \|\| 1.20.16 \|\|

*caraṇau viṣṇuśaraṇau hitvā nārāyaṇāṃgaṇam \|*  
*tasya no caratonyatra carato vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. As he performed the elaborate penance, his feet taking refuge only in Viṣṇu, never stirred out anywhere leaving the precincts of Nārāyaṇa’s abode.

## \|\| 1.20.17 \|\|

*vāṇīpramāṇī kriyate goviṃdaguṇavarṇane \|*  
*joṣaṃ samāsatā tena mahāsāraṃ tapasyatā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The organ of speech was authorised solely in the extolling of the good qualities of Govinda by him, taking delight therein and performing the penance with a lofty purpose.

## \|\| 1.20.18 \|\|

*nitāṃtakamalākāṃta nāmadheyasudhārasam \|*  
*rasayaṃtī na rasanā tasyānyarasaspṛhā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Tasting solely the nectarine juice of the names of the Consort of Kamalā, his tongue was not desirous of any other juice.

## \|\| 1.20.19 \|\|

*śrīmukuṃda padadvaṃdva padmāmodapramoditam \|*  
*gaṃdhāṃtaraṃ na tadghrāṇaṃ parijighratyaśīghragam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Delighted and rendered fragrant by the sweet scent of the lotus-like feet of Śrīmukunda, his organ of smell steadfastly avoided other scents.

## \|\| 1.20.20 \|\|

*tvagiṃdriyaṃ madhuripoḥ parispṛśya padadvayam \|*  
*sarvasparśasukhaṃ prāpa tasya bhūjānijanmanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After touching the pair of feet of the Enemy of Madhu, the organ of touch of that prince attained the pleasure of all types of tactile pleasures.

## \|\| 1.20.21 \|\|

*śabdādiviṣayādhāraṃ sāraṃ dāmodaraṃ param \|*  
*dhruveṃdriyāṇi saṃprāpya kṛtārthānyabhavaṃstadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After having attained the greatest Lord Dāmodara, the essential basis of all sorts of objects of sense, the sense-organs of Dhruva became perfectly contented.

## \|\| 1.20.22 \|\|

*luptāni sarvatejāṃsi tattapastapanodaye \|*  
*caṃdrasūryānalarkṣāṇāṃ pradīpita jagattraye \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. At the rise of the Sun of his penance that illuminated (scorched) the three worlds all the splendour of the Moon, Sun, fire and the stars became extinguished.

## \|\| 1.20.23 \|\|

*iṃdra caṃdrāgni varuṇa samīraṇa dhanādhipāḥ \|*  
*yama nairṛtamukhyāśca jātāḥ svapadaśaṃkitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. (Due to Dhruva’s penance) Indra, Candra, Agni, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera, Yama, Nairṛta and other important (heavenly beings) became doubtful of their positions.

## \|\| 1.20.24 \|\|

*vaimānikāstathā'nyepi vasumukhyā divaukasaḥ \|*  
*tato dhuvātsamuttresuḥ svādhikāraidhitādhayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The other heaven-dwellers too, who move about in aerial chariots and the chief of whom were the Vasus, became afraid of Dhruva, feeling increasing anxiety about their official rights.

## \|\| 1.20.25 \|\|

*yatra yatra dhruvaḥ pādaṃ minoti pṛthivītale \|*  
*dharā tasya bharākrāṃtā vinamettatra tatra vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Wherever Dhruva set his feet on the ground, the earth bent down overwhelmed by his weight.

## \|\| 1.20.26 \|\|

*aho tadaṃgasaṃgīni tyaktvā jāḍyaṃ jalānyapi \|*  
*rasavaṃti padasthāni sphuraṃtyanyatra tadbhayāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is wonderful that the waters that come into contact with his limbs eschew their sluggishness (liquidity) due to their fear for him and retain their position even elsewhere and remain tasty.

## \|\| 1.20.27 \|\|

*yāvaṃti viṣvaktejāṃsi siddharūpaguṇāni ca \|*  
*netrātithīni tāvaṃti tattapastejasā'bhavan \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Due to the splendour of his penance, all the radiant refulgences present everywhere with the forms and qualities of Siddhas displayed, came within his vision.

## \|\| 1.20.28 \|\|

*aho nijaguṇasparśaḥ satataṃ mātariśvanā \|*  
*dūradeśāṃtarasthopi tattvaco viṣayīkṛtaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. His own quality of touch though stationed elsewhere in a far-off place was brought as the object of his (Dhruva’s) organ of touch by the wind for ever.

## \|\| 1.20.29 \|\|

*vyomnāpi śabdaguṇinā dhruvārādhanabuddhinā \|*  
*śabdajātastvaśeṣopi tatkarṇa śaraṇīkṛtaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The entire range of sounds (words) was placed under the disposal of his (Dhruva’s) ears by the firmament too, the quality whereof is sound, because he was bent upon propitiating Dhruva.

## \|\| 1.20.30 \|\|

*ārādhito'nudivasaṃ sabhūtairapi paṃcabhiḥ \|*  
*tapa eva paraṃ mene goviṃdārpita mānasaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Propitiated day by day by the five elements too, he considered penance alone greater than everything else with his mind dedicated unto Govinda.

## \|\| 1.20.31 \|\|

*kaustubhodbhāsitahṛdaḥ pītakauśeyavāsasaḥ \|*  
*dhyānāttejomayaṃ viśvaṃ tenaikṣi nṛpasūnunā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Due to the meditation on (Lord Viṣṇu) having the chest embellished with the jewel Kaustubha and clad in yellow silk garments, the universe was seen by the prince fully radiant and resplendent.

## \|\| 1.20.32-36 \|\|

*marutvatātimahatī ciṃtā'ptā tattapobhayāt \|*  
*matpadaṃ cedakāṃkṣiṣyadahariṣyaddhruvaṃ dhuvaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*samarthastvapsarovargo niyaṃtuṃ yamināṃ yamān \|*  
*sa tu yūni prabhavati nātra bāle karomi kim \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tapasvināṃ tapo haṃtuṃ dvau matsāhāyyakāriṇau \|*  
*kāmakraudhau na tāvasminprabhavetāṃ śiśau dhruve \|\| 34 \|\|*

*eka eva kilopāyo bāle me prabhaviṣyati \|*  
*bhūtāliṃ bhīṣaṇākārāṃ prahiṇomīha tadbhiye \|\| 35 \|\|*

*bālatvādbhīṣito bhūtaistapastyakṣyatyasau dhruvam \|*  
*iti niścitya bhūtāliṃ preṣayāmāsa vāsavaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

32-36. Afraid of his penance, Indra became excessively worried. ‘If Dhruva were to desire my position, he would have certainly seized it. The group of the celestial damsels is capable of nullifying the practice of restraint by (grown up) recluses. They are not powerful in regard to a boy, though they are so in regard to youth. What shall I do? There are two assistants of mine in destroying the austerities of saints, viz., lust and anger. They are not powerful in regard to the child Dhruva. Only one means of mine will be effective on this child. I shall send terrible hosts of evil spirits to frighten him. In his childish weakness, he will be frightened by the evil spirits and will abandon austerities surely.’

Deciding thus, Vāsava sent the host of evil spirits.

## \|\| 1.20.37 \|\|

*bhallūkākārasarvāṃga uṣṭralaṃbaśirodharaḥ \|*  
*kaściddurdarśadaśanastvabhyadhāvattamarbhakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A certain evil spirit of awful teeth resembling a bear in every limb, with a long neck like that of a camel rushed at that child.

## \|\| 1.20.38 \|\|

*taṃ vyāghravadanaḥ kaścidvyādāya vikaṭānanam \|*  
*dvipocca dehasaṃsthāno muhurgarjansamabhyagāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A certain evil spirit with the face of a tiger perched itself on the lofty body of an elephant. It opened its gruesome mouth widely and rushed at him roaring frequently.

## \|\| 1.20.39 \|\|

*rayāttu māṃsakaṃ bhuṃjankaścidvikaṭadaṃṣṭrakaḥ \|*  
*roṣāttamabhidudrāva dṛṣṭvā saṃtarjayanniva \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Hurriedly chewing a piece of flesh, a certain spirit of hideous fangs, angrily rushed at him as though looking at him and threatening him.

## \|\| 1.20.40 \|\|

*atitīkṣṇairviṣāṇāgraistaṭānuccānvidārayan \|*  
*khurāgrairdalayanbhūmiṃ mahokṣo'bhijagarjatam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Tearing up the high banks with the sharp tips of his horns and rending the ground with his hoofs, a great bull bellowed at him.

## \|\| 1.20.41 \|\|

*kaściddhi pannagī bhūya phaṭāṭopabhayānakaḥ \|*  
*atiloladvirasanaḥ pusphūrjanikaṣācitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Assuming the form of a serpent, a certain spirit of terrible hood spreading out, and dangling and rolling a pair of tongues hissed very near him.

## \|\| 1.20.42 \|\|

*kaścicca mahiṣākāraḥ kṣipañśṛṃgāgrato giron \|*  
*lāṃgūlatāḍitadharaḥ śvasanvegāttamāptavān \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A certain spirit in the form of a buffalo hurled boulders with the tips of his horns and lashed the ground with his tail. Breathing furiously, he approached Dhruva.

## \|\| 1.20.43 \|\|

*kaściddāvānalālīḍha kharjūradrumasannibham \|*  
*bibhradūrudvayaṃbhūto vyāttāsyastamabhīṣayat \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Having a pair of thighs resembling palm trees partially burned by forest fire, a certain spirit tried to frighten him opening his mouth widely.

## \|\| 1.20.44 \|\|

*maulijairabhrasaṃgharṣaṃ kurvandīrghakṛśodaraḥ \|*  
*nimagnapiṃganayanaḥ kaścidbhīṣayati sma tam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. With his hairs struggling against the clouds, a spirit with a long, lean belly and sunken tawny eyes theatened him.

## \|\| 1.20.45 \|\|

*kṛpāṇapāṇirbhagnāsyo vāmahastakapāladhṛt \|*  
*pracaṃḍaṃ kṣveḍayankaścidabhyadhāvattamarbhakam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Holding a dagger in his (right hand) and a skull in his left, a certain spirit with his face cut, rushed at the child, roaring and whistling fiercely.

## \|\| 1.20.46 \|\|

*viśāla sālamādāya kurvankila kilāravam \|*  
*kaścittamabhito yāti kālo daṃḍadharo yathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Holding a huge Sāla tree and making hideous din, a certain spirit rushed at him like the god of Death holding a stout staff.

## \|\| 1.20.47 \|\|

*tamaḥ saṃketasadanaṃ vyāghraṃ vai vadanaṃ mahat \|*  
*kṛtāṃtakaṃ darākāraṃ bibhratkaścittamabhyagāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Possessing the huge mouth of a tiger, a place of meeting of pitch darkness, resembling the cave of the god of Death, a certain spirit rushed at him.

## \|\| 1.20.48 \|\|

*ulūkākāratāṃ dhṛtvā phūtkārairatidāruṇaiḥ \|*  
*hṛdayākaṃpanaiḥ kaścidbhīṣayāmāsa taṃ dhruvam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Assuming the form of an owl, a spirit tried to frighten Dhruva with awful hissing noises making the heart quiver.

## \|\| 1.20.49 \|\|

*yakṣiṇī kācidānīya rudaṃtaṃ kasyacicchiśum \|*  
*apibadrudhiraṃ koṣṭhāccakhādāsthi mṛṇālavat \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A female ogress brought someone’s crying child and drank the blood from its bowels and chewed the bone, as though it was a lotus stalk.

## \|\| 1.20.50 \|\|

*pipāsitādya rudhiraṃ tepi pāsyāmyahaṃ dhuva \|*  
*yathāsya bālasya tathā carvitvāsthīni vādinī \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. She continued the chewing saying “O Dhruva, I am thirsty. I will drink your blood too after chewing your bones like those of this boy.”

## \|\| 1.20.51 \|\|

*anīya tṛṇadārūṇi paristīrya samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*dāvāgniṃ jvālayāmāsa kācidvātyāvivardhitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. A certain female evil spirit brought grass and wood and scattered them all around; she then kindled a forest fire rendered more fierce by a violent gust of wind.

## \|\| 1.20.52 \|\|

*vetālī rūpamāsthāya bhaṃktvā kācittarūngirīn \|*  
*rurodha gaganādhvānaṃ kaṃpayaṃtī ca taṃ bhṛśam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Assuming the form of a vampire, a certain ogress split trees and rocks and blocked the path of the firmament causing it to quake very much.

## \|\| 1.20.53 \|\|

*anyā sunītirūpeṇa tamabhiprekṣya dūrataḥ \|*  
*rurodātīvaduḥkhārtā vakṣoghātaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Another one took the form of Sunīti. Glancing in the direction of the boy from far off, she lamented a lot in great misery beating her breasts frequently.

## \|\| 1.20.54 \|\|

*uvāca ca vacaścāṭu bahumāyā vinirmitam \|*  
*kāruṇyapūrṇa vātsalyamatīvātanvatī satī \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Deceitfully she expressed cajoling words of sympathy and affection.

## \|\| 1.20.55 \|\|

*tvadekaśaraṇāṃ vatsa bata mṛtyurjighāṃsati \|*  
*rakṣarakṣa gatāsuṃ māṃ śaraṇāgatavatsala \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. “O dear one, you are my sole refuge. But the god of Death wants to kill me. Oḥ, you are indeed endearing to those who seek refuge in you! My life is almost gone. Save me. Save me.

## \|\| 1.20.56 \|\|

*pratigrāmaṃ pratipuraṃ pratyadhvaṃ pratikānanam \|*  
*pratyāśramaṃ pratigiriṃ śrāṃtā tvadvīkṣaṇāturā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. I am tired wandering over every village, every city, every pathway in every forest and mountain, in every hermitage eager to see you.

## \|\| 1.20.57 \|\|

*yadā prabhṛti re bāla niragāttapase bhavān \|*  
*tadeva dinamārabhya nirgatā'haṃ tvadīkṣaṇe \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O boy, ever since you set out for the sake of the penance, from that very day I too have come out in your quest.

## \|\| 1.20.58 \|\|

*taistaiḥ sapatnīdurvākyairdunopi tvaṃ yathārbhaka \|*  
*tathā'hamapi dūnāsmi nitarāṃ tadvaco'gninā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O my child, I am also distressed in the same way as you were at the mischievous words of my co-wife. Her words scorch me like a fire.

## \|\| 1.20.59 \|\|

*na nidrāmi na jāgarmi nāśnāmi na pibāmyaham \|*  
*dhyāyāmi kevalaṃ tvā'haṃ yoginīva viyoginī \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. I never sleep nor keep alert and awake. I never eat or drink. I simply meditate upon you like a Yoginī in my grief of separation from you.

## \|\| 1.20.60 \|\|

*nidrādaridranayanā svapnepi na tavānanam \|*  
*ānaṃdi sarvathā yanme maṃdabhāgyā vilokaye \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. With my eyes bereft of sleep, I, the most unfortunate one, do not see even in dream your face that is delightful to me in every respect.

## \|\| 1.20.61 \|\|

*tvadānanapratinidhirvidhurvidhurayā mayā \|*  
*uditvaropināloki tāpaṃ vai tyaktukāmayā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. I am too eager to dispel the distress in my separation, yet I do not even see the rising moon, the representative of your face.

## \|\| 1.20.62 \|\|

*tvadālāpasamālāpaṃ kalayankilakākalīm \|*  
*kokilopi mayākarṇi nālakākīrṇakarṇayā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The unarranged forelocks of my hairs have spread over my ears. Hence the cuckoo chirping sweetly like your lisping words has not been heard by me.

## \|\| 1.20.63 \|\|

*tvadaṃgasaṃgamadhuro dhruvadhūpitayāmayā \|*  
*nānilopi mayāliṃgi kvacidviśrāṃtayā bhṛśam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Nor has the wind, exquisitely sweet, due to the contact with your body, been embraced by me with ciḍequate rest, O Dhruva, as I am excessively agitated (due to motherly affection).

## \|\| 1.20.64 \|\|

*ke deśāḥ kāśca saritaḥ ke śailāstvatkṛte dhruva \|*  
*mayā caraṇacāriṇyā rājapatnyā na laṃghitāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. What countries, what rivers, what mountains, O Dhruva, have not been traversed by me walking all the way, despite the fact that I am the wife of a king?

## \|\| 1.20.65 \|\|

*adhruvaṃ sarvamevaitatpaśyaṃtyaṃdhīkṛtāsmyaham \|*  
*dhātrīṃ trāyasva māṃ putra prāpya tvaṃmeṃ'dhayaṣṭitām \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Seeing all these without Dhruva I have been rendered blind. Dear son, assume the status of the supporting staff of a blind one and save me, your nursing mother.

## \|\| 1.20.66 \|\|

*mṛdulāni tavāṃgāni kvemāni kva tapastvidam \|*  
*paruṣaṃ puruṣaiḥ sādhyaṃ paruṣāṃgairnararṣabha \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O dear one, foremost among human beings, where are those tender limbs of yours? Where is this austere penance that can be achieved only by hardy men?

## \|\| 1.20.67 \|\|

*anena tapasā vatsa tvayā'pyaṃ kimanenasā \|*  
*dharādhīśatanūjatvādadhikaṃ tadvadādhunā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O dear one, you are free from sins. What else, more than the status of the prince of an emperor, is sought to be achieved through this penance?

## \|\| 1.20.68 \|\|

*anena vayasā bāla khelanīyaṃ tvayā'niśam \|*  
*bālakrīḍanakairanyaiḥ savayaḥ śiśubhiḥ samam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O boy, at this age of yours, you ought to play with toys befitting young children along with the other children of your own age.

## \|\| 1.20.69 \|\|

*tataḥ kaumāramāsādya vayo'bhidhyānaśīlinā \|*  
*bhavatā sarvavidyānāṃ bhāvyaṃ vai pāradṛśvanā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Having reached youth thereafter you ought to be contemplative and become the master of all lores.

## \|\| 1.20.70 \|\|

*vayotha caturaṃ prāpya yoṣāsrakcaṃdanādikān \|*  
*nirvekṣyasi bahūnbhogāniṃdriyārthānkṛtārthayan \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Thereafter, attaining the maturity of youth, you will enjoy many pleasures through women, garlands, sanḍalpaste etc. fulfilling the obligations of the senses and sensual objects.

## \|\| 1.20.71 \|\|

*utpādyātha bahūnputrānguṇino dharmavatsalān \|*  
*parisaṃkrāmitaśrīkasteṣvatho tvaṃ tapaścara \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Beget many virtuous sons of very excellent conduct, transfer your royal glory and assets to them and then you do carry on your austerities and penance.

## \|\| 1.20.72 \|\|

*idānīmeva tapasi bālye vayasi kaḥ śramaḥ \|*  
*pādāṃguṣṭhakarīṣāgniḥ kadā maulimavāpsyati \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Why this extraordinary effort in respect of penance now itself in your boyhood? When can the fire on the dry cow-dung sticking to the toe reach the top of the head?

## \|\| 1.20.73 \|\|

*vipakṣaparibhūtena hṛtamānena kenacit \|*  
*paribhraṣṭaśriyā vāpi taptavyaṃ teṣu ko bhavān \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Distress of austerity should be undergone by one assailed by an enemy, or by one whose honour has been slighted by someone or by one who has lost all prosperity. Are you one of these? If so, which?”

## \|\| 1.20.74 \|\|

*hṛtamānena taptavyaṃ niśamyeti vaco dhruvaḥ \|*  
*dīrghamuṣṇaṃ hi niḥśvasya punardadhyau hariṃ hṛdi \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. On hearing the words “Distress of austerity should be undergone by one whose honour has been slighted,” Dhruva heaved a deep sigh breathing hot air out and then meditated on Hari in his heart.

## \|\| 1.20.75 \|\|

*janayitrīmanābhāṣya bhūtabhītiṃ vihāya ca \|*  
*dhruvo'cyutadhyānaparaḥ punareva babhūva ha \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. He did not speak to his mother. He did not have any fear from the evil spirits. Once again Dhruva engaged himself in meditating on Acyuta.

## \|\| 1.20.76 \|\|

*sāpi bhūtāvalī bhītiṃbahubhīṣaṇabhūṣaṇā \|*  
*darśayaṃtī tamabhito'drākṣīccakraṃ sudarśanam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The host of other evil spirits with many hideous things worn as ornaments showed many gestures to terrify him but saw the discus Sudarśana all round.

## \|\| 1.20.77 \|\|

*paritaḥ pariveṣābhaṃ sūryasyoccaiḥ sphuratprabham \|*  
*rakṣaṇāya ca rakṣobhyastasyādhokṣaja nirmitam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. (Evidently) it had been sent there for protecting him from the demons and ogresses. It had the refulgence of a halo all round. Its lustre was exalted like that of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.20.78-80 \|\|

*bhūtāvalī tamālokya sphuraccakrasudarśanam \|*  
*jvālāmālākulaṃ tīvraṃ rakṣaṃtaṃ parito dhruvam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*atīva niṣkaṃpahṛdaṃ govidārpitacetasam \|*  
*tapoṃkuramivodbhidya medinīṃ samuditvaram \|\| 79 \|\|*

*sāpi pratyutabhītātaṃ dhruvaṃ dhruvaviniścayam \|*  
*namaskṛtya yathāyātaṃ yātāvyarthamanorathā \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-80. The host of evil spirits saw the dazzling discus Sudarśana, excessively brilliant, according protection to Dhruva from all sides even as he sat there with a steady heart with his mind dedicated to Govinda. He appeared to be like the seedling of austerities that burst open the ground and grew up. The host of evil spirits themselves became frightened. They were disappointed in their evil intentions. They bowed down to Dhruva of fixed resolution and went away along the path they had come.

## \|\| 1.20.81 \|\|

*garjatkādaṃbinījālaṃ vyomni vai vyākulaṃ yathā \|*  
*vṛthā bhavati saṃprāpya manāganilalolatām \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Just as a thundering cloud becomes scattered and ineffective after being shaken by wind (so also the host of evil spirits dispersed).

## \|\| 1.20.82 \|\|

*atha jaṃbhāriṇā sārdhaṃ bhītāḥ sarve divaukasaḥ \|*  
*saṃmaṃtrya tvaritā jagmurbrahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ dvija \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Then, O Brāhmaṇa, all the terrified heaven-dwellers held discussion with Indra and hurriedly sought refuge in Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.20.83 \|\|

*natvā vijñāpayāmāsuḥ pariṣṭutyā pitāmaham \|*  
*vacro'vasaramālokya pṛṣṭāgamanakāraṇāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. They bowed down to and eulogized him, the Grandfather (of the worlds). On being asked for the reason of their visit and finding a suitable opportunity for their submission they did so.

## \|\| 1.20.84 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*dhātaruttānapādasya tanayena suvarcasā \|*  
*tapatā tāpitāḥ sarve trilokī talavāsinaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

The Devas said:

84\. O Dhātṛ (Creator), all the residents of the three worlds have been distressed by the extremely brilliant son of Uttanāpāda, who is performing a penance.

## \|\| 1.20.85 \|\|

*samyaksaṃvidmahe tāta dhuvasya na manīṣitam \|*  
*padaṃ parijihīrṣuḥ sa kasyāsmāsu mahātapāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. O dear one, we do not perfectly comprehend the intention and desire of Dhruva. From among us whose office he is eager to capture by performing the great penance. (We have not understood.)

## \|\| 1.20.86 \|\|

*iti vijñāpito devairvihasya caturānanaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvācātha tānsarvāndhruvato bhītamānasān \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. On being informed thus by the Devas, the Four-faced Lord laughed and replied to them who were gripped with fear in their minds from Dhruva.

## \|\| 1.20.87 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*na bhetavyaṃ surāstasmāddhruvāddhruvapadaiṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*vrajaṃtu vijvarāḥ sarve na sa vaḥ padamicchati \|\| 87 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

87\. O Suras, there is no need to fear Dhruva who is desirous of a firm and fixed position. All of you may go without needless excitement and mental anguish. He is not desirous of your offices.

## \|\| 1.20.88 \|\|

*na tasmādbhagavadbhaktādbhetavyaṃ kenacitkvacit \|*  
*niścitaṃ viṣṇubhaktā ye na te syuḥ paratāpinaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. No one need be afraid of that devotee of the Supreme Lord. Those who are the devotees of the Supreme Lord will not certainly be the tormentors of others.

## \|\| 1.20.89 \|\|

*ārādhya viṣṇuṃ deveśaṃ labdhvā tasmātsvakāṃkṣitam \|*  
*bhavatāmapi sarveṣāṃ padāni sthirayiṣyati \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. After propitiating Viṣṇu, the Lord of Devas, and obtaining his cherished desire he will make your own positions still more secure.

## \|\| 1.20.90 \|\|

*niśamyeti ca gīrvāṇāḥ praṇītaṃ brahmaṇo vacaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya svadhiṣṇyāni prahṛṣṭāḥ parivavrajuḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. On hearing these words uttered by Brahmā, the Devas bowed down to him and departed in great delight.

## \|\| 1.20.91 \|\|

*atha nārāyaṇo devastaṃ dṛṣṭvā dṛḍhamānasam \|*  
*ananyaśaraṇaṃ bālaṃ gatvā tārkṣyaratho'bravīt \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Seeing him to be fully resolved in his mind and realizing that the boy had no other refuge, Lord Nārāyaṇa approached him seated on his vehicle Tārkṣya (Garuḍa) and said:

## \|\| 1.20.92 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*prasannosmi mahābhāga varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*tapaso'smānnivartasva ciraṃ khinnosi bālaka \|\| 92 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

92\. O boy of great dignity and fortune, I am delighted. O child of good holy vows, choose your boons. Desist from proceeding ahead in this penance. You are already distressed with a long drawn (austerity).

## \|\| 1.20.93 \|\|

*vaco'mṛtaṃ samākarṇya paryunmīlya vilocane \|*  
*iṃdranīlamaṇijyotiḥ paṭalīṃ paryalokayat \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. On hearing the nectarlike words, he opened his eyes and saw a massive column of the brilliant splendour of sapphire gems.

## \|\| 1.20.94 \|\|

*pratyagravikasannīlotpalānāṃ nikuraṃbakaiḥ \|*  
*protphullitāṃ samaṃtācca rodasī sarasīmiva \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. It appeared like a lake expanding over heaven and earth with full-blown clusters of blue lotuses.

## \|\| 1.20.95 \|\|

*lakṣmīdevīkaṭākṣoghaiḥ kaṭākṣitamivākhilam \|*  
*dhuvastadāniraikṣiṣṭa dyāvābhūmyoryadaṃtaram \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Dhruva then saw the entire space between heaven and earth blessed with the benign glances of Goddess Lakṣmī.

## \|\| 1.20.96 \|\|

*prodyatkādaṃbinīmadhya vidyuddāmasamānaruk \|*  
*puraḥ pītāṃbaraḥ kṛṣṇastena netrātithīkṛtaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. There in front of him, Lord Kṛṣṇa clad in yellow garments was visualized by him; he had the splendour of the lightning streak in the midst of rising clouds.

## \|\| 1.20.97 \|\|

*nabho nikaṣa pāṣāṇo merukāṃcana rekhitaḥ \|*  
*yathātathā dhruveṇaikṣi tadā garuḍavāhanaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The Garuḍa-vehicled Lord was seen by Dhruva like the sky resembling a whet-stone having the golden Meru for the testing.

## \|\| 1.20.98 \|\|

*sunīlagaganaṃ yadvadbhūṣitaṃ tu kalāvatā \|*  
*pītena vāsasā yuktaṃ sa dadarśa hariṃ tadā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. He saw Hari clad in yellow garments like the dark blue sky embellished with the moon.

## \|\| 1.20.99 \|\|

*daṃḍavatpraṇipatyātha paritaḥ pariluṭhya ca \|*  
*ruroda dṛṣṭveva ciraṃ pitaraṃ duḥkhitaḥ śiśuḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. He prostrated before the Lord stretching himself like a long staff. He rolled and cried like a sad child seeing its father after a long time.

## \|\| 1.20.100-102 \|\|

*nāradena sanaṃdena sanakena susaṃstutaḥ \|*  
*anyaiḥ sanatkumārādyairyogibhiryogināṃ varaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*kāruṇyavāṣpanīrārdra puṃḍarīkavilocanaḥ \|*  
*dhruvamutthāpayāṃcakre cakrī dhṛtvā kareṇa tam \|\| 101 \|\|*

*haristu paripasparśa tadaṃgaṃ dhūlidhūsaram \|*  
*karābhyāṃ sukaṭhorābhyāṃ nityaṃ śāstraparigrahāt \|\| 102 \|\|*

100-102. The Lord who had been continuously eulogized by Nārada, Sananda, Sanaka, Sanatkumāra and other Yogins, who is the most excellent one among Yogins and whose eyes resembled a wet lotus, being full of tears of kindness, raised Dhruva with his hand. The discus-bearing Hari touched his soiled limbs with his hands rendered firm by wielding the arms incessantly.

## \|\| 1.20.103 \|\|

*sparśanāddevadevasya susaṃskṛtamayī śubhā \|*  
*vāṇī pravṛttā tasyāsyāttuṣṭāvātha dhruvo harim \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. At the touch of the Lord of Devas, splendid flow of words issued from his mouth. Dhruva eulogized Hari thus:

## Chapter 21 - The Story of Dhruva: Dhruva’s Eulogy of Viṣṇu

## \|\| 1.21.1 \|\|

*dhruva uvāca \|*  
*namo hiraṇyagarbhāya sarvasṛṣṭividhāyine \|*  
*hiraṇyaretase tubhyaṃ suhiraṇyapradāyine \|\| 1 \|\|*

Dhruva said:

1\. Hail to you, O Hiraṇyagarbha (‘the support of the Golden Egg’—Comm.), the performer of the function of all (sorts, e.g. ādhyātmika, ādhibhautika) creation, one who has gold as his semen virile, the bestower of gold!

## \|\| 1.21.2 \|\|

*namo harasvarūpāya bhūtasaṃhārakāriṇe \|*  
*mahābhūtātmabhūtāya bhūtānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Obeisance to you, the Lord in the form of Hara, the cause of the annihilation of all living beings. Obeisance to the controller of all living beings, the soul of all great living beings.

## \|\| 1.21.3 \|\|

*namaḥ sthitikṛte tubhyaṃ viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave \|*  
*tṛṣṇāharāya kṛṣṇāya mahābhāra sahiṣṇave \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Obeisance to you, the cause of sustenance, Viṣṇu (the all-pervader), the powerful one. Obeisance to Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of thirst (for worldly affairs), the endurer of the great burden (of the earth as the Divine Boar),

## \|\| 1.21.4 \|\|

*namo daityamahāraṇya dāvavahnisvarūpiṇe \|*  
*daityadrumakuṭhārāya namaste śārṅgapāṇaye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Obeisance to you in the form of the forest conflagration for the great forest of Daityas, the axe that fells down the trees in the form of Daityas. Obeisance to you holding the Śārṅga bow in your hand.

## \|\| 1.21.5 \|\|

*namaḥ kaumodakīvyagra karāgrāya gadādhara \|*  
*mahādanujanāśāya namo naṃdakadhāriṇe \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O holder of the mace, obeisance to you whose fingers are firmly engrossed in holding the Kaumodakī mace; obeisance to the holder of (the sword) Nanḍaka, for the destruction of the great Danujas.

## \|\| 1.21.6 \|\|

*namaḥ śrīpataye tubhyaṃ namaścakradharāya ca \|*  
*dharādharāya vārāha rūpiṇe paramātmane \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Obeisance to you, the Consort of Śrī (Goddess of Fortune); obeisance to the wielder of the discus. Obeisance to the great soul in the form of the Divine Boar supporting the Earth.

## \|\| 1.21.7 \|\|

*namaḥ kamalahastāya kamalāvallabhāya te \|*  
*namo matsyādirūpāya namaḥ kaustubhavakṣase \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Obeisance to you, to the holder of the lotus in the hand, the lover of Goddess Lakṣmī; obeisance to the Lord in the form of Fish etc. Hail to you wearing the gem Kaustubha on the chest!

## \|\| 1.21.8 \|\|

*namo vedāṃtavedyāya namaḥ śrīvatsadhāriṇe \|*  
*namo guṇasvarūpāya guṇine guṇavarjite \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Obeisance to the Lord who can be comprehended only through the Vedānta; obeisance to the Lord having Śrīvatsa; obeisance to the Lord in the form of the G-uṇas; to one who is with and without attributes.

## \|\| 1.21.9 \|\|

*namaste padmanābhāya pāṃcajanyadharāya ca \|*  
*vāsudeva namastubhyaṃ devakīnaṃdanāya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Obeisance to you having the lotus in the navel; obeisance to the holder of Pāñcajanya conch. O Vāsudeva, obeisance to you, the delighter of Devakī.

## \|\| 1.21.10 \|\|

*pradyumnāya namastubhyamaniruddhāya te namaḥ \|*  
*namaḥ kaṃsavināśāya namaścāṇūramardine \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Obeisance to Pradyumna, to you Aniruddha; obeisance to the killer of Cāṇūra.

## \|\| 1.21.11 \|\|

*dāmodarahṛṣīkeśa gorvidācyutamādhava \|*  
*upeṃdrakaiṭabhā'rāte madhuhaṃtaradhokṣaja \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Dāmodara, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Govinda, Acyuta, Mādhava, Upendra, O enemy of Kaiṭabha, O slayer of Maḍhu, O Adhokṣaja!

## \|\| 1.21.12 \|\|

*nārāyaṇāya narakahāriṇe pāpahāriṇe \|*  
*vāmanāya namastubhyaṃ haraye śauraye namaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Obeisance to you, Nārāyaṇa, the destroyer of (the demon) Naraka, the destroyer of sins; obeisance to you, Vāmana; bow to Hari, Śauri.

## \|\| 1.21.13 \|\|

*anaṃtāya namastubhyamanaṃtaśayanāya ca \|*  
*rukmiṇīpataye tubhyaṃ rukmipramathanāya ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Obeisance to you, the infinite one; obeisance to the Lord with Ananta (Serpent Śeṣa) for your couch; obeisance to you the Consort of Rukmiṇī, to the suppressor of Rukmi.

## \|\| 1.21.14 \|\|

*caidyahaṃtre namastubhyaṃ dānavāresurāraye \|*  
*mukuṃdaparamānaṃda naṃdagopapriyāya ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Obeisance to you, the slayer of Caidya (Śiśupāla); obeisance to the enemy of Asuras, the enemy of the enemies of Suras, O Mukunda of great bliss; obeisance to the favourite darling of the cowherd Nanda.

## \|\| 1.21.15 \|\|

*namaste puṃḍarīkākṣa danujeṃdra niṣūdine \|*  
*namo gopālarūpāya veṇuvādanakāriṇe \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Obeisance to you the lotus-eyed one, the destroyer of leading Danujas. Bow to the Lord in the form of the cowherd, to the player on the flute.

## \|\| 1.21.16 \|\|

*gopīpriyāya keśighne govardhanadharāya ca \|*  
*rāmāya raghunāthāya rāghavāya namonamaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Repeated obeisance to the lover of the cowherdesses. Obeisance to Rāma Rāghava, the leading member of the family of Raghu, to the slayer of Keśin.

## \|\| 1.21.17 \|\|

*rāvaṇāre namastubhyaṃ vibhīṣaṇaśaraṇyada \|*  
*ajāya jayarūpāya raṇāṃgaṇavicakṣaṇa \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Bow to you, the enemy of Rāvaṇa, to the bestower of refuge to Bibhīṣaṇa, to the unborn one, to the victory incarnate, the expert in fighting.

## \|\| 1.21.18 \|\|

*kṣaṇādi kālarūpāya nānārūpāya śārṅgiṇe \|*  
*gadine cakriṇe tubhyaṃ daityacakravimardine \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Obeisance to the form of Kāla (Time) such as Kṣaṇa (moment) etc., the assumer of various forms, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, the mace and the discus, the suppressor of multitudes of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.21.19 \|\|

*balāya balabhadrāya balārātipriyāya ca \|*  
*baliyajñapramathana namo bhaktavaraprada \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Obeisance to the powerful one, to Balabhadra, to the Lord dear to the enemy of the demon Bala. O destroyer of the sacrifice of Bali, obeisance to you, the bestower of boons on your devotees.

## \|\| 1.21.20 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśiporvakṣo vidāraṇa raṇapriya \|*  
*namo brahmaṇyadevāya gobrāhmaṇahitāya ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Lord who tore the chest of Hiraṇyakaśipu; O Lord fond of battles; O Lord benevolent to Brāhmaṇas; O Lord causing the welfare of cows and Brāhmaṇas!

## \|\| 1.21.21 \|\|

*namaste dharmarūpāya namaḥ sattvaguṇāya ca \|*  
*namaḥ sahasraśirase puruṣāya parāya ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Obeisance to you, righteousness personified. Bow to one possessing the Sattva quality. Obeisance to the thousandheaded one, to the Supreme Puruṣa.

## \|\| 1.21.22 \|\|

*sahasrākṣa sahasrāṃghre sahasrakiraṇāya ca \|*  
*sahasramūrte śrīkāṃta namaste yajñapūruṣa \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O thousand (i.e., innumerable)-eyed one; O thousandfooted one, obeisance to the thousand rayed one. O thousand-formed one, O Consort of Śrī, O deity of sacrifice, obeisance to you.

## \|\| 1.21.23 \|\|

*vedavedyasvarūpāya namo vedapriyāya ca \|*  
*vedāya vedagadine sadācārādhvagāmine \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Lord whose form can be comprehended only through the Vedas, O lord to whom Vedas are dear, O lord of the form of knowledge (and consciousness), obeisance to you, the propounder of the Vedas, to the Lord treading the path of those of good conduct.

## \|\| 1.21.24 \|\|

*vaikuṃṭhāya namastubhyaṃ namo vaikuṃṭhavāsine \|*  
*viṣṭaraśravase tubhyaṃ namo garuḍagāmine \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Obeisance to you, the son of Vikuṇṭhā; obeisance to the Lord residing in Vaikuṇṭha; obeisance to the Lord moving about on Garuḍa; obeisance to the Lord heard (and sung about) in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.21.25 \|\|

*viṣvaksena namastubhyaṃ jaganmaya janārdana \|*  
*trivikramāya satyāya namaḥ satyapriyāya ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Obeisance to you, O Viṣvaksena, O Janārdana, identified with the universe; obeisance to Trivikrama, to the truthful one, to the Lord fond of truth.

## \|\| 1.21.26 \|\|

*keśavāya namastubhyaṃ māyine brahmāgāyine \|*  
*taporūpāya tapasāṃ namaste phaladāyine \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Obeisance to Keśava; obeisance to you, to the controller of Māyā, to the singer of the Vedas. Obeisance to you, austerity personified, to the bestower of the benefit of austerity.

## \|\| 1.21.27 \|\|

*stutyāya stutirūpāya bhaktastutiratāya ca \|*  
*namaste śrutirūpāya śrutyācāra priyāya ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Obeisance to the Lord worthy of eulogy, eulogy personified; to the Lord interested in the eulogy of devotees. Obeisance to you in the form of the Vedas, to the Lord pleased with the conduct of life in accordance with the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.21.28 \|\|

*aṃḍajāya namastubhyaṃ svedajāya namostu te \|*  
*jarāyuja svarūpāya nama udbhijjarūpiṇe \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Obeisance to you, identified with the egg-born beings (birds); obeisance to you born of the sweat (lice etc.); obeisance to you in the form of the uterus-born; obeisance to you in the form of the Udbhijja (germinating plants).

## \|\| 1.21.29 \|\|

*devānāmiṃdrarūposi grahāṇāmasi bhānumān \|*  
*lokānāṃ satyaloko'si siṃdhūnāṃ kṣīrasāgaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Among the Devas you are in the form of Indra; among the Planets you are the Sun; among the worlds you are Satyaloka; among the oceans you are the Milky Ocean.

## \|\| 1.21.30 \|\|

*surāpagā'si saritāṃ sarasāṃ mānasaṃ saraḥ \|*  
*himavānasi śailānāṃ dhenūnāṃ kāmadhugbhavān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Among rivers you are the heavenly Gaṅgā; among lakes you are the Mānasa lake; among mountains you are Himavān; among cows you are the wish-yielding divine cow.

## \|\| 1.21.31 \|\|

*dhātūnāṃ hāṭakamasi sphaṭikaścopaleṣvasi \|*  
*nīlotpalaṃ prasūneṣu vṛkṣeṣu tulasī bhavān \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Among metals you are gold; among precious stones you are crystal; among flowers you are blue lotus; among trees and plants you are Tulasī (Basil) Plant.

## \|\| 1.21.32 \|\|

*sarvapūjyaśilānāṃ vai śālagrāma śilā bhavān \|*  
*muktikṣetreṣu kāśī tvaṃ prayāgastīrthapaṃktiṣu \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Among the stones worthy of the worship of everyone, you are the Sālagrāma stone; among the holy salvation-giving places you are Kāśī and among the sacred regions you are Prayāga.

## \|\| 1.21.33 \|\|

*varṇeṣu śvetavarṇo'si dvipadāṃ brāhmaṇo bhavān \|*  
*garuḍosyaṃḍajeṣvīśa vyavahāreṣu vāgbhavān \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Among colours you are the white; among bipeds you are the Brāhmaṇa; O Lord, you are Garuḍa among birds; of all activities you are speech.

## \|\| 1.21.34 \|\|

*vedeṣūpaniṣadrūpā maṃtrāṇāṃ praṇavohyasi \|*  
*akṣarāṇāmakārosi yajvanāṃ somarūpadhṛk \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Among the Vedas you are of the form of the Upaniṣaḍs; among Mantras you are Praṇava (Om); among the letters you are the letter A and among sacrificial beings you are one of the form of Soma.

## \|\| 1.21.35 \|\|

*pratāpināmagnirasi kṣamā'si tvaṃ kṣamāvatām \|*  
*dātṝṇāmasi parjanyaḥ pavitrāṇāṃ parohyasi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Among the blazing ones you are fire; you are forgiveness (of Earth) among those who have forbearance; among donors you are the presiding deity of Parjanya (rain-bearing cloud); among the sacred ones you are the greatest.

## \|\| 1.21.36 \|\|

*cāposi sarvaśastrāṇāṃ vāto vegavatāmasi \|*  
*manosīṃdriyavargeṣu nirbhayāṇāṃ karohyasi \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Among all weapons you are the bow; you are wind among those moving with velocity; among sense-organs you are the mind; among the fearless ones you are hand (since at the time of physical danger, all raise their hands in resistance).

## \|\| 1.21.37 \|\|

*vyomavyāptimatāṃ tvaṃ vai paramātmā'si cātmanām \|*  
*saṃdhyopāstirbhavāndeva sarvanityeṣu karmasu \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Among those who pervade you are the firmament; among the souls, you are the Supreme Soul. O Lord, among all daily rites you are the Sandhyā Prayer (performed at dawn and dusk).

## \|\| 1.21.38 \|\|

*kratūnāmaśvamedhosi dānānāmabhayaṃ bhavān \|*  
*lābhānāṃ putralābhosi vasaṃtastvamṛtuṣvaho \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Among holy sacrifices you are the horse sacrifice; among gifts you are the gift of freedom from fear; among acquisitions you are the birth of a son; O Lord, among seasons you are the spring.

## \|\| 1.21.39 \|\|

*yugānāṃ prathamosi tvaṃ tithīnāṃ tvaṃ kuhūrhyasi \|*  
*puṣyosi nakṣatragaṇe saṃkramaḥ sarvaparvasu \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Amog the Ages you are the first one (Kṛta); among the lunar days you are the New Moon (Kuhū); among constellations you are Puṣya and among all holy days you are the transit of the Planets (from one zodiac to another).

## \|\| 1.21.40 \|\|

*yogeṣu vyatipātastvaṃ tṛṇeṣu hi kuśo bhavān \|*  
*udyamānāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ nirvāṇaṃ tvamasi prabho \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Among Yogas (combinations of Planets, stars etc.) you are Vyatīpāta; among the grasses you are the Kuśa grass; among all the efforts or human interests (Puruṣārthas) you are salvation, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.21.41 \|\|

*sarvāsāmiha buddhīnāṃ dharmabuddhirbhavānaja \|*  
*aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣeṣu somavallī latāsu ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O unborn Lord, among all purposeful activities you are the intention to be righteous; among all trees you are Aśvattha and among the creepers you are the Soma creeper.

## \|\| 1.21.42 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmosi sarvepu sādhaneṣu śuciṣvaho \|*  
*sarvadaḥ sarvaliṃgeṣu śrīmānviśveśvaro bhavān \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Among all purifying expedients you are Prāṇāyāma; among all Liṅgas you are the glorious Viśveśvara Liṅga, the bestower of everything.

## \|\| 1.21.43 \|\|

*mitrāṇāṃ hi kalatraṃ tvaṃ dharmastvaṃ sarvabaṃdhuṣu \|*  
*tvatto nānyajjagatyasminnārāyaṇa carācare \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Among all friendly ones you are the spouse; among all kinsmen you are Dharma (pious activity). O Nārāyaṇa, there is nothing other than you in the whole world including the mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 1.21.44 \|\|

*tvameva mātā tvaṃ tātastvaṃ sutastvaṃ mahādhanam \|*  
*tvameva saukhyasaṃpattistvamāyurjīvaneśvaraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. You alone are the mother; you are the father; you are the son; you are a great asset; you alone are the achievement of all happiness; you are the life span; you are the lord of life.

## \|\| 1.21.45 \|\|

*sā kathā yatra te nāma tanmano yattvadarpitam \|*  
*tatkarma yattvadarthaṃ vai tattapo yadbhavatsmṛtiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. That is the holy discourse where your name (is sung); that is the genuine mind which is dedicated to you; that is the real activity which is offered unto you; that is the penance wherein you are remembered.

## \|\| 1.21.46 \|\|

*taddhanaṃ dhanināṃ śuddhaṃ yattvadarthe vyayīkṛtam \|*  
*sa eva sakalaḥ kālo yasmiñjiṣṇo tvamarcyase \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. That wealth of the rich which is spent for your sake is the pure one; that alone is the time fruitfully spent when you are adored, O Jiṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.21.47 \|\|

*tāvacca jīvitaṃ śreyo yāvattvaṃ hṛdi vartase \|*  
*rogāḥ praśamamāyāṃti tvatpādodaka sevanāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Life is beneficial as long as you are present in the heart; illnesses perish by taking in the holy water (of the worship) of your feet.

## \|\| 1.21.48 \|\|

*mahāpāpāni goviṃda bahujanmārjitānyapi \|*  
*sadyo vilayamāyāṃti vāsudeveti kīrtanāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O Govinda, all great sins (such as Brāhmaṇa killing) incurred in the course of many births become annihilated immediately by uttering (your name) Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.21.49 \|\|

*aho puṃsāṃ mahāmohastvaho puṃsāṃ pramādatā \|*  
*vāsudevamanādṛtya yadanyatra kṛtaśramāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Alas, the great delusion of men! Ah! Pity! The blunder of men whereby they slight Vāsudeva and put in effort elsewhere!

## \|\| 1.21.50 \|\|

*idameva hi māṃgalyamidameva dhanārjanam \|*  
*jīvitasya phalaṃ caitadyaddāmodarakīrtanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This alone is conducive to happiness and auspiciousness; this alone is acquisition of wealth; this is the fruit of life viz. the glorification of Dāmodara.

## \|\| 1.21.51 \|\|

*adhokṣajātparodharmo nārtho nārāyaṇātparaḥ \|*  
*na kāmaḥ keśavādanyo nāpavargo hariṃ vinā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. There is no greater pious activity apart from Adhokṣaja; there is no wealth greater than Nārāyaṇa; there is no (true) desire apart from Keśava; there is no salvation without Hari.

## \|\| 1.21.52 \|\|

*iyameva parā hānirupasargo yamevahi \|*  
*abhāgyaṃ paramaṃ caitadvāsudevaṃ na yatsmaret \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. This is the greatest loss, this alone is the greatest harassment, this is the height of bad luck, whereby one does not remember Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.21.53 \|\|

*harerārādhanaṃ puṃsāṃ kiṃ kiṃ na kurute bata \|*  
*putramitrakalatrārtha rājyasvargāpavargadam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. What is it that the propitiation of Hari does not achieve? It accords sons, friends, spouses, riches, kingdom, heavenly pleasures and ultimate salvation.

## \|\| 1.21.54 \|\|

*haratyaghaṃ dhvaṃsayati vyādhīnādhīnniyacchati \|*  
*dharmaṃ vivardhayetkṣipraṃ prayacchati manoratham \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. It dispels sin, destroys ailments, and controls mental anguishes. It quickly increases piety and accords what is desired.

## \|\| 1.21.55 \|\|

*bhagavaccaraṇadvaṃdvaṃ nirddvaṃdva dhyānamuttamam \|*  
*pāpināpi prasaṃgena vihitaṃ svahitaṃ param \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The unwavering meditation on the pair of feet of the Lord is the most excellent thing. Even if it is performed by a sinner and that too casually, it accords the greatest benefit to oneself.

## \|\| 1.21.56 \|\|

*pāpināṃ yāni pāpāni mahopapadabhāṃjyapi \|*  
*sulīnadhyānasaṃpanno nāmoccāro harerharet \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The utterance of the name of Hari during very deep meditation will remove even the sins designated as the greatest ones of sinners.

## \|\| 1.21.57 \|\|

*pramādādapi saṃspṛṣṭo yathā'nalakaṇo dahet \|*  
*tathauṣṭhapuṭasaṃspṛṣṭa harināma haredagham \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Just as a particle of fire when touched even by mistake, causes a burn, so also the name of Hari that slightly touches the lips, dispels sin.

## \|\| 1.21.58 \|\|

*nitāṃtaṃ kamalākāṃte śāṃtacittaṃ vidhāya yaḥ \|*  
*saṃśīlayetkṣaṇaṃ nūnaṃ kamalā tatra niścalā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. If anyone makes his mind quiescent and directs it steadily towards the Consort of Kamalā and practises (meditation) even for a moment, indeed the Goddess of Wealth is steady and firm there (with him).

## \|\| 1.21.59 \|\|

*ayameva parodharmastvidameva paraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*idameva paraṃ tīrthaṃ viṣṇupādāṃbu yatpibeta \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. This is the greatest pious practice; this is the greatest austerity; this is the most excellent of all holy spots whereby one imbibes the water that washes Viṣṇu’s feet.

## \|\| 1.21.60 \|\|

*tavopahāraṃ bhaktyāya sevate yajapūruṣa \|*  
*sevitastena niyataṃ puroḍāśo mahādhiyā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O Yajñapuruṣa, he who devoutly takes in the Naivedya offered to you, has become a man of great intellect. It is as good as Puroḍāśa has been regularly taken in by him.

## \|\| 1.21.61 \|\|

*sa caivāvabhṛthasnātaḥ sa ca gaṃgājalāplutaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇupādodakaṃ kṛtvā śaṃkhe yaḥ snāti mānavaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. If a man takes the water with which the feet of Viṣṇu have been washed in a conch-shell and performs the holy ablution with that (it is as good as) he has actually performed the Avabhṛthasnāna (valedictory bath after a holy sacrifice) and he has taken the holy bath in the waters of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.21.62 \|\|

*śālagrāma śilā yena pūjitā tulasī dalaiḥ \|*  
*sa pārijātamālābhiḥ pūjyate surasadmani \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He, by whom a Śālagrāma stone has been worshipped with Tulasī leaves, will be worshipped in the heavenly world with the garlands of divine Pārijāta flowers.

## \|\| 1.21.63 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdro vā yadi vetaraḥ \|*  
*viṣṇubhakti samāyukto jñeyaḥ sarvottamaśca saḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Whether he is a Brāhmaṇa, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, a Śūdra or anyone else, one endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu, should be known as the most excellent one among all.

## \|\| 1.21.64 \|\|

*śaṃkhacakrāṃkitatanuḥ śirasāṃ maṃjarīdharaḥ \|*  
*gopīcaṃdanaliptāṃgo dṛṣṭaścettadaghaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If a man sees a devotee with sandal-paste marks of conchshell and discus, wearing a bunch of Tulasī flowers on the head and having marks of Gopīcanḍana paste over the body, he will be free from all sins. No other sin shall defile him.

## \|\| 1.21.65 \|\|

*pratyahaṃ dvādaśaśilāḥ śālagrāmasya yo'rcayet \|*  
*dvāravatyāḥ śilāyuktaḥ sa vaikuṃṭhe mahīyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He who worships everyday twelve stones of Śālagrāma and Dvārāvatīcakra stones(?) is honoured in Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 1.21.66 \|\|

*tulasī yasya bhavane pratyahaṃ paripūjyate \|*  
*tadgṛhaṃ nopasarpaṃti kadācidyamakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The servants of Yama never approach that house where Tulasī is worshipped everyday.

## \|\| 1.21.67 \|\|

*harināmākṣaramukhaṃ bhāle gopīmṛdāṃkitam \|*  
*tulasīmālitoraskaṃ spṛśeyurnayamānugāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The followers of Yama will never touch one in whose mouth the letters constituting the name of Hari (dwell for ever), whose forehead is marked with Gopīcandana and whose chest is garlanded with Tulasī leaves.

## \|\| 1.21.68 \|\|

*gopīmṛttulasī śaṃkhaḥ śālagrāmaḥ sacakrakaḥ \|*  
*gṛhepi yasya paṃcaite tasya pāpabhayaṃ kuta \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. If these five things: Gopīcanḍana clay, Tulasī leaf (plant), conchshell, Śālagrāma and Cakra (discus) are present in any one’s house, whence need he be afraid of sins?

## \|\| 1.21.69 \|\|

*ye muhūrtāḥ kṣaṇā ye ca yā kāṣṭhā ye nimeṣakāḥ \|*  
*ṛte viṣṇusmṛteryātāsteṣu muṣṭo yamena saḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. A person is plundered by Yama in all those Muhūrtas, Kṣaṇas, Kāṣṭhās and Nimeṣas that have been spent without remembering Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.21.70 \|\|

*kva dvayakṣaraṃ harernāma sphuliṃgasadṛśaṃ jvaleta \|*  
*mahatī pātakānāṃ ca rāśistūlopamā kva ca \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. What a great disparity there is between the name of Hari consisting of two syllables and blazing like sparks of fire and the great mass of sins comparable to a heap of cotton!

## \|\| 1.21.71 \|\|

*goviṃda paramānaṃdaṃ mukuṃdaṃ madhusūdanama \|*  
*tyaktvānyaṃ naiva jānāmi na bhajāmi smarāmi na \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. I neither know, nor resort to, nor even remember anyone else leaving Govinda, the highest bliss, Mukunda, the slayer of Madhu.

## \|\| 1.21.72 \|\|

*na namāmi na ca staumi na paśyāmīha cakṣuṣā \|*  
*na spṛśāmi na vāyāmi gāyāmi na na hariṃ vinā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. I never bow down to, neither eulogize nor even see with my eyes, neither touch nor approach nor sing about anyone except Hari.

## \|\| 1.21.73-74 \|\|

*jale sthale ca pātālepyanile cānale'cale \|*  
*vidyādharāsurasure kiṃ nare vānare nare \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tṛṇestraiṇe ca pāṣāṇe tarugulmalatāsu ca \|*  
*sarvatra śyāmalatanuṃ vīkṣe śrīvatsavakṣasam \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. I see everywhere the dark-complexioned Lord with Śrīvatsa mark on the chest, in waters, on the earth, in nether regions, in wind, in fire and on mountains, among Vidyādharas, Asuras, Suras, Kinnaras, monkeys, human beings, in grass, groups of women, stones, trees, and creepers.

## \|\| 1.21.75 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ hṛdayāvāsaḥ sākṣātsākṣī tvameva hi \|*  
*bahiraṃtarvinā tvāṃ tu nahyanyaṃ vedmi sarvagam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. You have your residence in the heart of everyone. You alone are the direct witness. Whether without or within, I do not know any other omnipresent being except you.

## \|\| 1.21.76 \|\|

*ityuktvā virarāmāsau śivaśarmandhruvastadā \|*  
*devopi bhagavānviṣṇustamuvāca prasannadṛk \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. After saying this, O Śivaśarman. Dhruva stopped. With delight evident in his eyes, Lord Viṣṇu spoke to him:

## \|\| 1.21.77 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*api bāla viśālākṣa dhruva dhruvamate'nagha \|*  
*parijñāto mayā samyaktavahṛtstho manorathaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

The Lord said:

77\. O child Dhruva of wide large eyes, free from sins and having fixed resolve, the desire cherished in your heart has been clearly understood by me.

## \|\| 1.21.78 \|\|

*annādbhavaṃti bhūtāni vṛṣṭerannasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*tadvṛṣṭeḥ kāraṇaṃ sūryaḥ sūryādhāro dhruvaidhi bhoḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The living beings originate from food; food grows through rain; the Sun is the cause of that rain. O Dhruva, you be the support of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.21.79 \|\|

*jyotiścakrasya sarvasya graharkṣādeḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*gagane bhramato nityaṃ tvamādhāro bhaviṣyasi \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. You will become the pivot of the entire group of Planets, Stars etc., of the system of luminaries that moves about in the firmament for ever.

## \|\| 1.21.80 \|\|

*meḍhībhūtastu vai sarvānvāyupāśairniyaṃtritān \|*  
*ākalpaṃ tatpadaṃ tiṣṭha bhrāmayañjyotiṣāṃgaṇān \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Like a pivotal pillar unto them, controlling them by holding them together with aerial strings, you stay there till the end of the Kalpa and make the luminaries revolve.

## \|\| 1.21.81 \|\|

*ārādhya śrī mahādevaṃ purāpadamidaṃ mayā \|*  
*āsādiyattadetatte tapasā pratipāditam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. By propitiating Lord Mahādeva formerly this position was acquired by me. Due to your penance it (the position of Dhruva) has now been given over to you.

## \|\| 1.21.82 \|\|

*keciccaturyugaṃ yāvatkecinmanvaṃtaraṃ dhruva \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃti tvaṃ tu vai kalpaṃ padametatpraśāsyasi \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Some of them remain for a period of four Yugas, O Dhruva, and some for a period of a Manvantara. You will be holding this position for a Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.21.83 \|\|

*manunāpi na yatprāpi kimanyairmānavairdhruva \|*  
*tatpadaṃ vihitaṃ tvatsācchakrādyairapi durlabham \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O Dhruva, can what was not obtained by even Manu, be obtained by other men? That position which is inaccessible to Śakra and others, has been entrusted to you.

## \|\| 1.21.84 \|\|

*anyānvarānprayacchāmi stavenānena toṣitaḥ \|*  
*sunītirapi te mātā tvatsamīpe cariṣyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. I have been rendered delighted by this prayer. I shall grant you other boons too; your mother Sunīti too will be near you.

## \|\| 1.21.85 \|\|

*idaṃ stotravaraṃ yastu paṭhiṣyati samāhitaḥ \|*  
*trisaṃdhyaṃ manujastasya pāpaṃ yāsyati saṃkṣayam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. If a man recites this excellent prayer with concentration and mental purity during the three Sandhyās, his sin will perish.

## \|\| 1.21.86 \|\|

*na tasya sadanaṃ lakṣmīḥ parityakṣyatyasaṃśayam \|*  
*na jananyā viyogaśca na baṃdhukalahodayaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Undoubtedly Lakṣmī will never leave his house. He will never be separated from his mother, nor will he have any quarrel with any of his kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.21.87 \|\|

*dhruvastutiriyaṃ puṇyā mahāpātakanāśinī \|*  
*brahmahāpi viśuddhyeta kā kathetara pāpinām \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. This prayer of Dhruva is meritorious and destructive of great sins. Even a Brāhmaṇa-slayer will be freed therefrom. What to speak of other sinners?

## \|\| 1.21.88 \|\|

*mahāpuṇyasya jananī mahāsaṃpattidāyinī \|*  
*mahopasargaśamanī mahāvyādhivināśinī \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. It will produce great merit. It will accord great riches. It suppresses all harassments and tortures. It destroys great ailments.

## \|\| 1.21.89 \|\|

*yasyā'stiparamā bhaktirmayi nirmalacetasaḥ \|*  
*dhruvastutiriyaṃ tena japyā matprītikāriṇī \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. He who is pure in mind and has great devotion to me, should perform the Japa of this Dhruva prayer which delights me much.

## \|\| 1.21.90 \|\|

*samasta tīrthasnānena yatphalaṃ labhate naraḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samyagāpnoti japanstutyānayā mudā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. He who joyously repeats this prayer attains that benefit which a man usually gets by taking the holy dip in all holy rivers.

## \|\| 1.21.91 \|\|

*saṃti stotrāṇyanekāni mama prītikarāṇi ca \|*  
*dhruvastuterna caitasyāḥ kalāmarhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. There are many other eulogies and they do delight me. But they do not merit even a fraction of a sixteenth part of Dhruva’s prayer.

## \|\| 1.21.92 \|\|

*śrutvāpīmāṃ stutiṃ martyaḥ śraddhayā parayā mudā \|*  
*pātakairmucyate sadyo mahatpuṇyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. By listening to this prayer with great faith and joy, a man gets liberated from sins immediately and he shall attain great merit.

## \|\| 1.21.93 \|\|

*aputraḥ putramāpnoti nirdhano dhanamāpnuyāt \|*  
*abhakto bhaktimāpnoti kīrtanācca dhruvastuteḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. By reciting Dhruva’s prayer a sonless man acquires (begets) a son, a poor man gets wealth and a man without devotion shall become devout.

## \|\| 1.21.94 \|\|

*dattvā dānānyanekāni kṛtvā nānā vratāni ca \|*  
*yathālābhānavāpnoti tathā stutyā'nayā naraḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Through this prayer, a man get those benefits which one gets by making many religious gifts and by observing different holy vows.

## \|\| 1.21.95 \|\|

*tyaktvā sarvāṇi kāryāṇi tyaktvā japyānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*dhruvastutiriyaṃ japyā sarvakāmapradāyinī \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Abandoning all activites, setting aside many of the other Japas, this Dhruva-prayer which accords all desires should be repeated regularly.

## \|\| 1.21.96 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*dhruvāvadhehi vakṣyāmi hitaṃ tava mahāmate \|*  
*yena te niścalaṃ samyakpadametadbhaviṣyati \|\| 96 \|\|*

Śrībhagavān said:

96\. O Dhruva, be attentive. O highly intelligent one, I shall mention what is beneficial to you and whereby this position of yours will become unchangeable.

## \|\| 1.21.97 \|\|

*ahaṃ jigamiṣustvāsaṃ purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ śubhām \|*  
*sākṣādviśveśvaro yatra tiṣṭhate mokṣakāraṇam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Formerly, I was desirous of going to the splendid Vārāṇasī where Viśveśvara himself, the cause of salvation, is ever present.

## \|\| 1.21.98 \|\|

*vipannānāṃ ca jaṃtūnāṃ yatra viśveśvaraḥ svayam \|*  
*karṇe jāpaṃ prakurute karmanirmūlana kṣamam \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. It is there that Viśveśvara whispers into the ears of dying beings that Mantra which is capable of uprooting all (binding) Karmas.

## \|\| 1.21.99 \|\|

*asya saṃsāraduḥkhasya sarvopadravadāyinaḥ \|*  
*upāya eka evāsti kāśikānaṃdabhūmikā \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. There is only one means of remedy for the misery of the mundane world that accords all sorts of troubles and that is Kāśikā, the Ānandabhūmikā (‘the blissful holy spot’).

## \|\| 1.21.100 \|\|

*idaṃ ramyamidaṃ neti bījaṃ duḥkhamahātaroḥ \|*  
*tasminkāśyagninā dagdhe duḥkhasyāvasaraḥ kutaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The (discriminatory) feeling “this is beautiful, this is not”, is the seed of the great tree of misery. When that is burnt down by means of the fire of Kāśī, where is the occasion for misery?

## \|\| 1.21.101 \|\|

*prāpya saṃprāpyate yena na bhūyo yena śocyate \|*  
*parāyānirvṛteḥ sthānaṃ yattadānaṃdakānanam \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. That Ānandakānana (Kāśī) is the spot of the greatest bliss; it is through it that everything worth attaining is attained and there remains no cause of regret thereafter.

## \|\| 1.21.102 \|\|

*amṛtāyanamutsṛjya puruṣonyatra yo vaset \|*  
*ānaṃdakānanaṃ śaṃbhoḥ kutastasya sukhodayaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. If a man resides elseswhere after forsaking the Ānandakānana of Śaṃbhu, the site of divine nectar, whence can he hope to have the rise (outcome) of happiness?

## \|\| 1.21.103 \|\|

*varaṃ śarāvahastasya cāṃḍālāgāravīthiṣu \|*  
*bhikṣārthamaṭanaṃ kāśyāṃ rājyaṃ nānyatra nīriṣu \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. It is better to go a-begging in Kāśī in the streets abounding in Cāṇḍāla houses with a bowl in the hands, rather than reign over a kingdom elsewhere without any enemy.

## \|\| 1.21.104 \|\|

*vaikuṃṭhanagarātkāśīṃ nityaṃ viśveśamarcitum \|*  
*ahamāyāmi niyamājjagadarcyaṃ tadarcitām \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. From the city of Vaikuṇṭha, I regularly go to Kāśī worshipped by the entire universe, in order to adore Viśveśa worthy of being worshipped by the universe.

## \|\| 1.21.105 \|\|

*mayi yā paramā śaktistrilokyā rakṣaṇakṣamā \|*  
*tatra heturmaheśānaḥ sa sudarśanacakradaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. That supreme Maheśāna who gave (me) Discus Sudarśana is the cause of the great power in me, capable of protecting the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.21.106 \|\|

*purā jālaṃdharaṃ daityaṃ mamāpi parikaṃpanam \|*  
*pādāṃguṣṭhāgrarekhotthaṃ cakraṃ sṛṣṭvā haro'harat \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Formerly, Hara created a Cakra arising out of the lines at the tip of the big toe and slew the Daitya Jālandhara who made even me tremble.

## \|\| 1.21.107 \|\|

*tacca cakraṃ mayā labdhaṃ netrapadmārcanādvibhoḥ \|*  
*etatsudarśanākhyaṃ vai daityacakrapramardanam \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. That Cakra has been obtained by me by adoring the Lord with the lotus-like eye. This Cakra named Sudarśana suppresses hosts of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.21.108 \|\|

*tanmayā tava rakṣārthaṃ bhūtavidrāvaṇaṃ param \|*  
*tāvatpraṇunnaṃ puratastataścāhamihāgataḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. In order to protect you by driving away the evil spirits, that Cakra was sent by me ahead and then only have I come here.

## \|\| 1.21.109 \|\|

*kāśīmidānīṃ yāsyāmi viśveśvara vilokane \|*  
*adya yātrā'sti mahatī kārtikyāṃ bahupuṇyadā \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Just now, I will go to Kāśī for visiting Viśveśvara. Today there is a great pilgrimage held in the month of Kārttika. It accords great merit.

## \|\| 1.21.110 \|\|

*kārtikasya caturdaśyāṃ viśveśaṃ yo vilokayet \|*  
*snātvā cottaravāhinyāṃ na tasya punarāgatiḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. If a man takes his holy bath in the north-flowing (Gaṅgā) and visits Viśveśa on the fourteenth day in the month of Kārttika, he never comes back (to the human world of misery).

## \|\| 1.21.111 \|\|

*ityuktvā tārkṣyamāropya dhruvamānaṃdameduram \|*  
*kṣaṇādvārāṇasīṃ prāpa hariḥ smaraharoṣitām \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. After saying this and making the extremely delighted Dhruva ride on Garuḍa, Hari reached immediately Vārāṇasī where Smarahara (Lord Śiva) is present.

## \|\| 1.21.112-113 \|\|

*paṃcakrośyāśca sīmānaṃ prāpya devo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*vainateyādavāruhya kare dhṛtvā dhruvaṃ tataḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*maṇikarṇyāṃ parisnāya viśveśamabhipūjya ca \|*  
*dhruvaṃ babhāṣe bhagavānhitaṃ tasya cikīrṣayan \|\| 113 \|\|*

112-113. After reaching the outskirts of Pañcakrośī (limit of ten miles perimeter), Lord Janārdana got down from Garuḍa. Holding Dhruva by the hand, he had the ablution at Maṇikarṇī and worshipped Viśveśa. Then desirous of doing something beneficial to Dhruva, the Lord said to him:

## \|\| 1.21.114 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ sthāpaya yatnena kṣetre'traivāvimuktake \|*  
*trailokyasthāpanaṃ puṇyaṃ yathā bhavati te'kṣayam \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. “Scrupulously install a Liṅga here itself in the holy-spot of Avimukta, so that you will have the never-ending merit establishing you in the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.21.115 \|\|

*niyutaṃ yatparisthāpya liṃgāni phalamāpyate \|*  
*anyatra tadihaikena liṃgena parilabhyate \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. The benefit that is acquired by installing a million Liṅgas elsewhere, is obtained by installing a single Liṅga here.

## \|\| 1.21.116 \|\|

*kālena bhaṃgamāpannaṃ jīrṇoddhāraṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*iha tasya phalasyāṃtaḥ pralayepi na jāyate \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. If anyone repairs the ruins here due to lapse of time, that benefit does not come to an end even at the time of Pralaya.

## \|\| 1.21.117 \|\|

*vittaśāṭhyaṃ parityajya prāsādaṃ yo'tra kārayet \|*  
*tena datto bhavetsarvo merurniyutayojanaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. He who does not grudge in spending money here and building a palace (to Śiva), has actually made a gift of the entire Meru extending to a million Yojanas.

## \|\| 1.21.118 \|\|

*kūpavāpītaḍāgāni śaktyā yo'tra tu kārayet \|*  
*anyatra karaṇāttasya puṇyaṃ koṭiguṇādhikam \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. If anyone digs wells, tanks or lakes in accordance with his capacity in this holy spot, his merit becomes a hundred million times more than what is obtained by doing it elsewhere.

## \|\| 1.21.119 \|\|

*ijyārthamatra yaḥ kuryātsuramyāṃ puṣpavāṭikām \|*  
*puṣpepuṣpe phalaṃ tasya suvarṇakusumādhikam \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. If a man grows a beautiful flower-garden here for the purpose of worship, the benefit acquired by him for each flower is more than that of a golden flower.

## \|\| 1.21.120 \|\|

*atra brahmapurīṃ kṛtvā yo viprebhyaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*varṣāśanena saṃyuktāṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. If anyone makes a Brahmapurī (a colony of Brāhmaṇas) here and hands it over to Brāhmaṇas along with the arrangement for fooding for a year, listen to the benefit he will get.

## \|\| 1.21.121 \|\|

*kṣīyaṃte salilānyabdherbhaumāśca trasareṇavaḥ \|*  
*kṣayo na tasya puṇyasya śivaloke samāsataḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. The waters of the ocean may be dried up. The Trasareṇus (dust particles) of the earth may perish, but there is no destruction of the merit of that devotee staying in Śivaloka.

## \|\| 1.21.122 \|\|

*maṭhānapi tapasvibhyaḥ kārayitvā'tra yorpayet \|*  
*jīvanopāyasaṃyuktānsopi pūrvaphalāśrayaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. If anyone builds monasteries and hands them over to saints along with sustenance of life, he too will have the benefit said before.

## \|\| 1.21.123 \|\|

*kṛtvā mahāṃti puṇyāni yo'tra viśveśvare'rpayet \|*  
*na tasya punarāvṛratti ghore saṃsārasāgare \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. After performing great and meritorious rites, a man must dedicate the fruit thereof to Viśveśvara. He never returns to the terrible ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.21.124 \|\|

*anaṃta iti vādoyaṃ mayiloke'tra gīyate \|*  
*paraṃ kāśī guṇānāṃ hi mayāpyaṃto na labhyate \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. It is sung about here in this world that I am Ananta, but the end of the good qualities of Kāśī is not obtained even by me.

## \|\| 1.21.125 \|\|

*tasmātprayatnataḥ kāśyāṃ dhuva śreyaḥ samāśrayet \|*  
*kāśī śreyaḥ phalaṃ puṃsāmakṣayā yopajāyate \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Hence, O Dhruva, one should scrupulously resort to permanent weal at Kāśī. The benefit of weal acquired by man from Kāśī is everlasting.

## \|\| 1.21.126-127 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*dhruvamityupadiśyātha jagāma garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*dhruvopi liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya vaidyanāthasamīpataḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

*prāsādaṃ sumahatkrṛtvā kṛtvā kuṃḍaṃ tadagrataḥ \|*  
*viśveśvaraṃ samabhyarcya kṛtakṛtyo gṛhaṃ yayau \|\| 127 \|\|*

The Gaṇas said:

126-127. After advising Dhruva thus, the Garuḍa-emblemed Lord went away. Dhruva then installed a Liṅga near Vaidyanātha. He built a great palace and made a holy pit in front of it. After worshipping Viśveśvara, he became contented and went home.

## \|\| 1.21.128 \|\|

*dhruveśvaraṃ samabhyarcya dhruvakuṃḍe kṛtodakaḥ \|*  
*dhruvalokamavāpnoti naro bhogasamanvitaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. By worshipping Dhruveśvara and offering water libations in Dhruvakuṇḍa, a man attains Dhruva’s world endowed with all pleasures and enjoyments.

## \|\| 1.21.129 \|\|

*dhruvasya paramākhyānaṃ yaḥ paṭhetpāṭhayedapi \|*  
*sa viṣṇulokamāsādya jāyate viṣṇuvallabhaḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. He who reads, narrates and makes others read the great narrative of Dhruva, reaches Viṣṇu’s world and becomes a favourite of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.21.130 \|\|

*naro dhruvasya caritaṃ prasaṃgena smarannapi \|*  
*na pāpairabhibhūyeta mahatpuṇyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Remembering even casually the story of Dhruva, a man shall attain great merit. He will never be assailed by sins.

## Chapter 22 - Brahmā Praises Kāśī

## \|\| 1.22.1 \|\|

*śivaśarmovāca \|*  
*dhruvākhyānamidaṃ ramyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*mahāścaryakaraṃ puṇyaṃ śrutvā tṛptosmi bho gaṇau \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śivaśarmā said:

1\. O Gaṇas, I have become contented and pleased on listening to this story of Dhruva. It is very charming and destructive of great sins. It causes one to wonder and produces merit.

## \|\| 1.22.2 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ yāvaddvijo brūte vimānaṃ vāyuvegagam \|*  
*tāvatprāpa maharlokaṃ svarlokātparamādbhutam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Agastya said:

2\. Even as the Brāhmaṇa said this, the aerial chariot of a speed rivalling that of the wind, reached Maharloka, more miraculous than the heavenly world.

## \|\| 1.22.3 \|\|

*dvijo'tha lokaṃ saṃvīkṣya sarvato mahasā vṛtam \|*  
*tau gaṇau pratyuvācedaṃ koyaṃ loko manoharaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then on seeing that region enveloped in refulgence all round, the Brāhmaṇa said to the Gaṇas again, “What a charming world is this!”

## \|\| 1.22.4-6 \|\|

*tāvūcatustato vipraṃ niśāmaya mahāmate \|*  
*ayaṃ sa hi maharlokaḥ svarlokātparamādbhutaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kalpāyuṣo vasaṃtyatra tapasā dhūtakalmaṣāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇusmaraṇa saṃkṣīṇa samastakleśasaṃcayāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*nirvyājapraṇidhānena dṛṣṭvā tejomayaṃ jagat \|*  
*mahāyogasamāyuktā vasaṃtyatra surottamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. Then they said to the Brāhmaṇa: “O highly intelligent one, listen. This is that Maharloka which is more wonderful and mysterious than the heavenly world. People who have dispelled their sins by their austerities live here for one Kalpa. By meditating on Viṣṇu, all their miseries have subsided. Excellent Suras practising the great Yoga (of the identity of the Supreme Soul with the individual soul) see this region full of refulgence by means of genuine meditation and they stay here.”

## \|\| 1.22.7 \|\|

*itthaṃ kathāṃ kathayatorbhagavadgaṇayoḥ priye \|*  
*kṣaṇārdhena vimānaṃ tajjanalokaṃ nināyatān \|\| 7 \|\|*

Agastya said:

7\. O dear one, even as the attendants of the Lord said this, the aerial chariot took them to Janaloka within half a moment.

## \|\| 1.22.8 \|\|

*nivasaṃtyamalā yatra mānasā bahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*sanaṃdanādyā yogīṃdrāḥ sarve te hyūrdhvaretasaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It is there that the sinless mental sons of Brahmā, leading Yogins (like) Sanandana and others, who have sublimated their sex-instinct (ūrdhvaretasaḥ) dwell.

## \|\| 1.22.9 \|\|

*anye tu yogino ye vai hyaskhaladbrahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*sarvadvaṃdvavinirmuktāste vasaṃtyatinirmalāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There are other Yogins too residing here. They are extremely pure. They never waver from celibacy. They are free from all Dvandvas (opposing pairs) like heat and cold.

## \|\| 1.22.10 \|\|

*janalokāttapolokasteṣāṃ locanagocaraḥ \|*  
*kṛtastena vimānena manovegena gacchatā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Tapoloka which is beyond Janaloka was brought within their view by that aerial chariot that was proceeding at a speed equalling that of the mind.

## \|\| 1.22.11 \|\|

*vairājā yatra te devā vaseyurdāhavarjitāḥ \|*  
*vāsudeve mano yeṣāṃ vāsudevārpitakriyāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Vairajas (created by Hiraṇyagarbha) (a class of Devas) free from thirst (or fire ending the world), reside there. They have their minds directed and their actions dedicated to Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.22.12 \|\|

*tapasā toṣya goviṃdamabhilāṣavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*tapolokamimaṃ prāpya vasaṃti vijiteṃdriyāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Those who have conquered their sense-organs and have propitiated Govinda through their penance, attain this Tapoloka and stay there free from all ambitions and desires.

## \|\| 1.22.13-21 \|\|

*śiloṃcha vṛttayā ye vai daṃtolūkhalikāśca ye \|*  
*aśmakuṭṭāśca munayaḥ śīrṇaparṇāśinaśca ye \|\| 13 \|\|*

*grīṣme paṃcāgnitapaso varṣāsu sthaṃḍileśayāḥ \|*  
*hemaṃtaśiśirārdhe ye kṣapaṃti salile kṣapāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kuśāgranīraviprūṣastṛṣitā yatayo'piban \|*  
*vātāśinotikṣudhitāḥ pādāgrāṃguṣṭha bhūspṛśaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ūrdhvadoṣo ravidṛśastvekāṃghri sthāṇu niścalāḥ \|*  
*ye vai divā nirucchvāsā māsocchvāsāśca ye punaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*māsopavāsavratinaścāturmāsya vratāśca ye \|*  
*ṛtvaṃtatoyapānā ye ṣaṇmāsopavāsakāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ye ca varṣanimeṣā vai varṣadhārāṃbu tarṣakāḥ \|*  
*ye ca sthāṇūpamāṃ prāptā mṛgakaṃḍūti saukhyadāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*jaṭāṭavī koṭarāṃtaḥ kṛtanīḍāṃḍajāśca ye \|*  
*prarūḍhavāmalūrāṃgāḥ snāyunaddhāsthisaṃcayāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*latāpratānaiḥ parito veṣṭitāvayavāśca ye \|*  
*sasyāni ca prarūḍhāni yadaṃgeṣu cirasthiti \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ityādi sutapaḥ kliṣṭavarṣmāṇo ye tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*brahmāyuṣastapoloke te vasaṃtyakutobhayāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

13-21. Those who have pursued the following kinds of austerities in the world, live in Tapoloka and have the same span of life as Brahmā: those who sustain themselves by means of pieces of grains lying scattered on the ground; those who use their teeth alone as the mortar for cleansing husks; sages and devotees using stone for breaking the grains; those who eat only decaying leaves scattered on the ground; those who perfom penance in the midst of five fires during summer; those who lie on bare rough ground during rainy season; those who spend half of Hemanta and Śiśira (i.e., winter) staying in water during the nights; those ascetics who drink only the drops of water from the tips of Kuśa grass when thirsty; those who when very hungry take in only wind; those who touch the ground with the tips of their toes while performing penance; those who keep their hands lifted up; those who keep looking at the Sun; those who stand motionlessly on a single foot; those who never breathe during the day (i.e., practice Kumbhaka type of breath control—Comm.); who exhale (breath) throughout the month (Comm.); those who have taken the vow of fasting for a whole month; those who have similar vows for four months altogether; those who drink water at the end of every season (i.e., two months); those who observe fast for a period of six months; those who wink their eyes once in a year; those who quench their thirst with rain water; those who resemble posts and give the deer the pleasure of scratching when their bodies itch; those who have nests of birds within the forest-like growth of matted hairs; those round whose limbs anthill has grown; those who are mere skeletons with sinews tying the bones together; those whose bodies are entwined all round by spreading creepers; those round whose limbs even plants grow and remain there for a long period. Those ascetics who have subjected their bodies to various sorts of torture stay here without any fear from anywhere.

## \|\| 1.22.22 \|\|

*yāvaditthaṃ sa puṇyātmā śṛṇoti gaṇayormukhāt \|*  
*tāvannetrātithībhūtaḥ satyaloko mahojjvalaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Even as that meritorious soul (i.e., Śivaśarmā) was listening to these words issuing from the mouths of those two attendants, the excessively refulgent Satyaloka came within his view.

## \|\| 1.22.23 \|\|

*tvarāvaṃtau gaṇau tatra vimānādavaruhya tau \|*  
*sraṣṭāraṃ sarvalokānāṃ tena sārdhaṃ praṇematuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Those two attendants then hurriedly got down from the aerial chariot and, along with Śivaśarmā, bowed down to the Creator of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.22.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*gaṇāvasau dvijo dhīmānvedavedāṃgapāragaḥ \|*  
*smṛtyuktācāracaṃcuśca pratīpaḥ pāpakarmasu \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

24\. O attendants, this Brāhmaṇa is intelligent and a master of Vedas and Vedāṅgas. He is proficient in the practice of the code of conduct laid down in Smṛtis. He is averse to sinful activities.

## \|\| 1.22.25 \|\|

*ayi dvija mahāprājña jāne tvāṃ śivaśarmaka \|*  
*sādhūkṛtaṃ tvayā vatsa sutīrthaprāṇamokṣaṇāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Brāhmaṇa of great intellect, I know you, O Śivaśarman, O dear one, you have done well in abandoning your life in a holy spot.

## \|\| 1.22.26 \|\|

*satvaraṃ gatvaraṃ sarvaṃ yaccaitadbhavatekṣitam \|*  
*dainaṃdinapralayataḥ sṛjāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Whatever is seen by you will quickly pass off. I am creating them again and again after Pralaya (annihilation).

## \|\| 1.22.27 \|\|

*ā vairājaṃ pratipadamupasaṃharate haraḥ \|*  
*kā kathā maśakābhānāṃ nṛṇāṃ maraṇadharmiṇām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I am creating everything upto Vairāja and Hara annihilates them at every step. Nothing need be said about men who are insignificant like mosquitos and mortal by nature.

## \|\| 1.22.28 \|\|

*caturṣu bhūtagrāmeṣu hyeka eva guṇo nṛṇām \|*  
*tasminvai bhārate varṣe karmabhūmau mahīyasi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Out of the four categories of living beings (e.g. the egg-born, the sweat-born etc.) for men there is one good advantage in Bhāratavarṣa, a great land of religious rituals (the advantage is mentioned in v 35).

## \|\| 1.22.29-35 \|\|

*capalāni vinirjityeṃdriyāṇi manasā saha \|*  
*vihāya vairiṇaṃ lobhaṃ viṣvagguṇagaṇasya ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dharmavaṃśaharaṃ kāmamarthasaṃcayahāriṇam \|*  
*jarāpalitakartāraṃ viniṣkṛtya vicārataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*jitvā krodharipuṃ dhairyāttapaso yaśasaḥ śriyaḥ \|*  
*śarīrasyāpi hartāraṃ netāraṃ tāmasīṃ gatim \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sadā madaṃ parityajya pramādaikapadapradam \|*  
*pramādaikaśaraṇyaṃ ca saṃpadāṃ vinivartakam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sarvatra laghutā hetumahaṃkāraṃ vihāya ca \|*  
*dūṣaṇāropaṇe yatnaṃ kurvāṇaṃ sajjaneṣvapi \|\| 33 \|\|*

*hitvā mohaṃ mahādroharopaṇaṃ matighātinam \|*  
*atyaṃtamaṃdhīkaraṇamaṃdhatāmisradarśakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śrutismṛtipurāṇoktaṃ parikṣuṇṇaṃ mahājanaiḥ \|*  
*dharmasopānamāruhya yadihāyāṃti helayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

29-35. After conquering the fickle sense-organs along with the mind, after eschewing greed which pervades all inherent qualities; after dispelling thoughtfully lust that destroys the whole of righteousness, that removes collection of wealth and that brings about greying of hairs and old age; after courageously overcoming the enemy in the form of anger that removes power of penance, reputation, glory and even the body and that leads one along the path of darkness; after abandoning forever arrogance that accords the sole basis for erring, that is the sole refuge of all faults and that turns back all riches; after eschewing egotism that causes dishonour everywhere and that makes one endeavour to defame and blame even good persons; after giving up delusion that causes the growth of excessive hatred, that benumbs intellect and renders it powerless, that utterly blinds the people and that guides one to ‘eternal darkness’ (a hell of that name viz., Andhatāmisra) people can climb the steps of Dharma (righteousness) that is laid down by Śrutis, Smṛtis and Purāṇas and that is followed by great men and then they come here with care. (This is the advantage mentioned in v 28 above, that human beings can get.)

## \|\| 1.22.36 \|\|

*karmabhūmiṃ samīhaṃte sarve svargaukaso dvija \|*  
*yattatrārjitabhoktāraḥ padeṣūccāvaceṣvamī \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Brāhmaṇa, all the heaven-dwellers desire and seek the land of pious rites (Kannabhūmi), because therein all these people enjoy what is earned by them at different lower and higher levels.

## \|\| 1.22.37 \|\|

*nāryāvartasumo deśo na kāśī sadṛśī purī \|*  
*na viśveśa samaṃ liṃgaṃ kvāpi bahmāṃḍamaṃḍale \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Nowhere in the entire ‘Cosmic Egg’ is there a land on a par with Āryāvarta, a city similar to Kāśī and a Liṅga equal to Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 1.22.38 \|\|

*saṃti svargā bahuvidhāḥ sukhetara vivarjitā \|*  
*sukṛtaikaphalāḥ sarve yuktāḥ sarvasamṛddhibhiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. There are many types of Svargas free from non-happiness (i.e., are full of happiness). All of them are the sole outcome of merits (achieved). They are endowed with all kinds of riches and prosperities.

## \|\| 1.22.39 \|\|

*svarlokādadhikaṃ ramyaṃ nahi brahmāṃḍagolake \|*  
*sarve yataṃte svargāya tapodānavratādibhiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. (It is the belief) that there is nothing in the entire ‘Cosmic Egg’ more charming than the heavenly world. All people endeavour to attain Svarga through penance, gifts, holy vows and other things.

## \|\| 1.22.40 \|\|

*svarlokādapiramyāṇi pātālānīti nāradaḥ \|*  
*prāha svargasadāṃ madhye pātālebhyaḥ samāgataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “The nether regions are better and more charming than even Svarloka.” So said Nārada in the open assembly of heaven-dwellers, when he returned from Pātālas.

## \|\| 1.22.41 \|\|

*āhlādakāriṇaḥ śubhrā maṇayo yatra suprabhāḥ \|*  
*nāgāṃgābharaṇaprotāḥ pātālaṃ kena tatsamam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. With which can Pātāla be compared, where the jewels set in the ornaments on the limbs of Nāgas are highly refulgent, splendid and very pleasing?

## \|\| 1.22.42 \|\|

*daityadānavakanyābhiritaścetaśca śobhite \|*  
*pātāle kasya na prītirvimuktasyāpi jāyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Pātāla that is resplendent with the damsels of Daityas and Dānavas, delights everyone. Who is not delighted with it, even if he be a man devoid of attachment?

## \|\| 1.22.43 \|\|

*divārkaraśmayastatra prabhāṃ tanvaṃti nātapam \|*  
*śaśinaśca na śītāya niśi dyotāya kevalam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. During day-time rays of the Sun merely spread lustre there and not fierce heat. During night rays of the moon spread only light and do not increase chillness.

## \|\| 1.22.44 \|\|

*yatra na jñāyate kālo gatopi danujādibhiḥ \|*  
*vanāni nadyo ramyāṇi sadaṃbhāṃsi sarāṃsi ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. (Hence) the time that passess off is not known by Danujas and others (i.e., they are not aware of it).

The forests and rivers are very charming, The lakes contain excellent waters.

## \|\| 1.22.45-47 \|\|

*kalāḥ puṃsko kilālāpāḥ sucailāni śucīni ca \|*  
*bhūṣaṇānyatiramyāṇi gaṃdhādyamanulepanam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vīṇāveṇumṛdaṃgādi nisvanāḥ śrutihāriṇaḥ \|*  
*hāṭakeśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ yatra vai sarvakāmadam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*etānyanyāni ramyāṇi bhogyogyāni dānavaiḥ \|*  
*daityoragaiśca bhujyaṃte pātālāṃtaragocaraiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. The following things are enjoyed by the denizens of the nether regions: sweet chirping sounds of the male cuckoo, good garments, clean clothes, very charming ornaments, sweet scents and unguents, the sounds of flute, lute etc. that captivate the ears. These and other excellent things worthy of being enjoyed are duly enjoyed by the Dānavas, Daityas and Serpents residing in the interior of Pātāla.
