The great Liṅga called Hāṭakeśa bestows all cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.22.48 \|\|

*pātālebhyopi vai ramyaṃ dvija varṣamilāvṛtam \|*  
*ratnasānuṃ samāśritya paritaḥ parisaṃsthitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O Brāhmaṇa, the continent called Ilāvṛta that is stationed nestling within the ridges of Meru (surrounded by its peaks) is more charming than Pātāla.

## \|\| 1.22.49 \|\|

*sadā sukṛtino yatra sarvabhogabhujo dvija \|*  
*navayauvanasaṃpannā nityaṃ yatra mṛgīdṛśaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O Brāhmaṇa, there meritorious persons are always enjoying all pleasures. Fawn-eyed damsels are ever youthful there.

## \|\| 1.22.50 \|\|

*bhogabhūmiriyaṃ proktā śreyo vinimayārjitā \|*  
*bhujyate tvadvidhairlokaistīrthābhityakta dehakaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This is called Bhogabhūmi (‘Place of enjoyment’) acquired and enjoyed by people like you by exchanging their merits in view of their having abandoned their bodies in the holy spots on the earth.

## \|\| 1.22.51 \|\|

*aklībabhāṣibhiścāpi putrakṣetrādyahīnakaiḥ \|*  
*paropakārasaṃkṣīṇasukhāyurdhanasaṃcayaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. They are no speakers of falsehood. They are not devoid of sons, wives etc. They used to spend their happiness, span of life and hoarded wealth for the sake of helping others.

## \|\| 1.22.52 \|\|

*saṃti dvīpā hyanekā vai pārāvārāṃtarasthitāḥ \|*  
*jaṃbūdvīpasamo dvīpo na kvāpi jagatītale \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. There are many islands and continents stationed within oceans. But nowhere on the whole surface of the earth is there a continent like Jaṃbūdvīpa.

## \|\| 1.22.53 \|\|

*tatrāpi navavarṣāṇi bhārataṃ tatra cottamam \|*  
*karmabhūmiriyaṃ proktā devānāmapidurlabhā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. There are the nine Varṣas and among them Bhārata is the most excellent This is called Karmabhūmi (‘Land of righteous acts’). It is inaccessible even to Devas.

## \|\| 1.22.54 \|\|

*aṣṭau kiṃpuruṣādīni devabhogyāni tāni tu \|*  
*teṣu svargātsamāgatya ramaṃte tridivaukasaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The eight (Varṣas) including Kiṃpuruṣa and others are the places worthy of being enjoyed by Devas. The heaven-dwellers arrive there from Svargaloka and sport about.

## \|\| 1.22.55 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi navavistāratastvidam \|*  
*bhārataṃ prathamaṃ varṣaṃ merordakṣiṇataḥ sthitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The chief of them, Bhāratavarṣa, is nine thousand Yojanas (Yojan = 12 Kms.) in extent. It is situated to the south of Meru.

## \|\| 1.22.56 \|\|

*tatrāpi himaviṃdhyādreraṃtaraṃ puṇyadaṃ param \|*  
*gaṃgāyamunayormadhye hyaṃtarvedī bhuvaḥ parāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. There too the region between Himālaya and Vindhya is the greatest bestower of merit. The region called Antarvedī between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā is the most excellent of all.

## \|\| 1.22.57 \|\|

*kurukṣetraṃ hi sarveṣāṃ kṣetrāṇāmadhikaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*tatopi naimiṣāraṇyaṃ svargasādhanamuttamam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Kurukṣetra is superior to all the other holy spots. There too the Naimiṣa forest is the most excellent means of achieving heaven.

## \|\| 1.22.58 \|\|

*naimiṣāraṇyatopīha sarvasminkṣitimaṃḍale \|*  
*sarvebhyopi hi tīrthebhyastīrtharājo viśiṣyate \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On the entire earth Tīrtharāja Prāyāga is the most excellent one among all the holy places, even greater than Naimiṣāraṇya.

## \|\| 1.22.59 \|\|

*svargadomokṣadaścaiva sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*prayāgastanmahatkṣetraṃ tīrtharāja iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. It is the bestower of heaven. It is the bestower of salvation. It is the bestower of all the cherished desires. That great holy place Prayāga is called Tīrtharāja.

## \|\| 1.22.60-61 \|\|

*yāgāḥ sarve mayā pūrvaṃ tulayā vidhṛtā dvija \|*  
*tacca tīrthavaraṃ ramyaṃ kāmikaṃ kāmapūraṇāta \|\| 60 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā prakṛṣṭayāgebhyaḥ puṣṭebhyo dakṣiṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*prayāgamiti tannāma kṛtaṃ hariharādibhiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. O Brāhmaṇa, all the Yāgas were held in the balance by me for weighing. That holy place is the most excellent one among all holy places. It is the most charming and desirable because it fulfils all desires. That holy place too is held in the balance. On finding the holy place better and more excellent than all the Yagas well endowed with Dakṣiṇās etc., it was named Prayāga by Hari, Hara and others.

## \|\| 1.22.62 \|\|

*nāmamātrasmṛteryasya prayāgasya trikālataḥ \|*  
*smartuḥ śarīre no jātu pāpaṃ vasati kutracit \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. By remembering merely the name of Prayāga thrice (a day), no sin can stay anywhere in the body of the person remembering.

## \|\| 1.22.63 \|\|

*saṃti tīrthānyanekāni pāpatrāṇakarāṇi ca \|*  
*na śaktānyadhikaṃ dātuṃ kṛtainaḥ pariśuddhitaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. There are many Tīrthas saving people from sins. They are not capable of giving anything more than redemption from the sins committed.

## \|\| 1.22.64 \|\|

*janmāṃtareṣvasaṃkhyeṣu yaḥ kṛtaḥ pāpasaṃcayaḥ \|*  
*duṣpraṇodyo hi nitarāṃ vratairdānaistapojapaiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The heap of sins committed in the course of the numerous previous births cannot be removed adequately by holy vows, Dānas, Japas and penances.

## \|\| 1.22.65 \|\|

*sa tīrtharājagamanodyatasya śubhajanmanaḥ \|*  
*aṃgeṣu vepate'tyaṃtaṃ drumo vātahato yathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Like a tree assailed by wind that mass of sins begins to tremble in the limbs of that man of auspicious nativity, who has intended to go to Tīrtharāja.

## \|\| 1.22.66 \|\|

*tataḥ krāṃtārdhamārgasya prayāga dṛḍhacetasaḥ \|*  
*puṃsaḥ śarīrānniryātumapekṣeta padāṃtaram \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Then it begins to set out and go to another place from the body of the man who has traversed half the distance and who has resolved firmly in the mind to go to Prayāga.

## \|\| 1.22.67 \|\|

*bhāgyānnetrātithībhūte tīrtharāje mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*palāyate drutataraṃ tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. If fortunately the Tīrtharāja comes within the vision of that noble soul, that collection of sins begins to flee like darkness at sunrise.

## \|\| 1.22.68 \|\|

*saptadhātumayī bhūtatanau pāpāni yāni vai \|*  
*keśeṣu tāni tiṣṭhaṃti vapanādyāṃti tānyapi \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. In the body consisting of the seven Dhātus (constituent elements) the sins collect together in the hairs. On being shaved they clear out.

## \|\| 1.22.69 \|\|

*evaṃ niṣkaluṣībhūya tataḥ snāyātsitāsite \|*  
*yaṃyaṃ kāmamabhidhyāyaṃstaṃ tamāpnoti nānyathā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. After becoming free of sins thus, the devotee should take his holy bath in the Sitāsita (i.e. the confluence of the white Gaṅgā and the black Yamunā.) Thus he achieves whatever he desires and not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.22.70 \|\|

*puṇyarāśiṃ ca vipulaṃ puṇyānbhogānyathepsitān \|*  
*svargaṃ prāpnoti tatpuṇyānniṣkāmo mokṣamāpnuyāt \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He attains enorṃous quantity of merits and meritorious enjoyment of pleasures as desired. Due to that merit he attains heaven. If he is devoid of desires, be attains salvation.

## \|\| 1.22.71 \|\|

*snāyādyobhilaṣanmokṣaṃ kāmānanyānvihāya ca \|*  
*sopi mokṣamavāpnoti kāmadāttīrtharājataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. If anyone takes the holy dip eschewing other desires but desiring salvation, he too attains salvation from the Tīrtharāja, the bestower of all desires.

## \|\| 1.22.72 \|\|

*tīrtharājaṃ parityajya yo'nyasmātkāmamicchati \|*  
*bhāratākhye mahāvarṣe sa kāmaṃ nāpnuyātsphuṭam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. It is certain that in the great Varṣa named Bhārata, if anyone leaves off the Tīrtharāja and desires anything from elsewhere, he shall not attain his desire.

## \|\| 1.22.73 \|\|

*satyaloke prayāge ca nāṃtaraṃ vedmyahaṃ dvija \|*  
*tatra ye śubhakarmāṇaste mallokanivāsinaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O Brāhmaṇa, I do not know of any distinction between Satyaloka and Prayāga. Those who perform excellent rites there become the residents of my world.

## \|\| 1.22.74-75 \|\|

*tīrthābhilāṣibhirmartyaissevyaṃ tīrthāṃtaraṃ nahi \|*  
*anyatra bhūmivalaye tīrtharājātprayā gataḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*yathāṃtaraṃ dvijaśreṣṭha bhūpetvitarasevake \|*  
*dṛṣṭāṃtamātraṃ kathitaṃ prayāgetara tīrthayoḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. No other holy place should be resorted to by men desirous of (visiting) holy places.

O excellent Brāhmaṇa, the difference between Prayāga, the Tīrtharāja, and other places in the world is like the difference between a king and a servant of another man. Only an example (of comparison) is cited between Prayāga and other holy spots.

## \|\| 1.22.76 \|\|

*yathākathaṃcittīrthe'sminprāṇatyāgaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*tasyātmaghātadoṣo na prāpnuyādīpsitānyapi \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. If anyone casts off his life here in this holy spot somehow, he does not incur the sin of suicide. He shall achieve everything desired.

## \|\| 1.22.77 \|\|

*yasya bhāgyavataścātra tiṣṭhaṃtyasthīnyapi dvija \|*  
*na tasya duḥkhaleśopi kvāpi janmani jāyate \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. If, O Brāhmaṇa, the bones of any fortunate man remain here, he will never have even an iota of sorrow in any of his births.

## \|\| 1.22.78 \|\|

*brahmahatyādi pāpānāṃ prāyaścittaṃ cikīrṣuṇā \|*  
*prayāgaṃ vidhivatsevyaṃ dvijavākyānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Prayāga should be duly resorted to, certainly in accordance with the injunctions of a Brāhmaṇa, by a person desirous of performing expiatory rites for the sins of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter etc.

## \|\| 1.22.79 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena vipreṃdra mahodayamabhīpsunā \|*  
*sevyaṃ sitāsitaṃ tīrthaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ jagatītale \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. O eminent Brāhmaṇa, why say more? The holy spot Sitāsita (Prayāga), the most excellent one in the entire world, should be resorted to by one desirous of acquiring great rise in prosperity.

## \|\| 1.22.80 \|\|

*prayāgatopi tīrtheśātsarveṣu bhuvaneṣvapi \|*  
*anāyāsena vai muktiḥ kāśyāṃ dehāvasānataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. By terminating the mortal body at Kāśī, one gets salvation without effort more than from even Prayāga, the lord of all Tīrthas, in all the world.

## \|\| 1.22.81 \|\|

*prayāgādapi vai ramyamavimuktaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yatra viśveśvaraḥ sākṣātsvayaṃ samadhitiṣṭhati \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Undoubtedly Avimukta is more charming than even Prayāga, because Viśveśvara is directly presiding over it.

## \|\| 1.22.82 \|\|

*avimuktānmahākṣetrādviśveśa samadhiṣṭhitāt \|*  
*na ca kiṃcitkvacidramyamiha brahmāṃḍagolake \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Nothing anywhere in the entire Cosmic Sphere is more charming than Avimukta, the great holy spot presided over by Viśveśa.

## \|\| 1.22.83 \|\|

*avimuktamidaṃ kṣetramapi brahmāṃḍamadhyagam \|*  
*brahmāṃḍamadhye na bhavetpaṃcakrośapramāṇataḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. This holy spot Avimukta is away from the middle of the Cosmic Egg to the extent of five Krośas (1 Krośa = 3 Kms.), though it is in the centre of the Cosmic Egg.

## \|\| 1.22.84 \|\|

*yathāyathā hi vardheta jalamekārṇavasya ca \|*  
*tathātathonnayedīśastatkṣetraṃ pralayādapi \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. As and when the water of the vast ocean rises up (at the time of Pralaya), the Lord lifts up the holy spot from the Pralaya water-level.

## \|\| 1.22.85 \|\|

*kṣetrametattriśūlāgre śūlinastiṣṭhati dvija \|*  
*aṃtarikṣena bhūmiṣṭhaṃ nekṣaṃte mūḍhabuddhayaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. O Brāhmaṇa, this holy spot rests on the tip of the trident of Lord Śiva in the intermediate region without touching the ground. Men of deluded intellect do not perceive it.

## \|\| 1.22.86 \|\|

*sadā kṛtayugaṃ cātra mahāparvasadā'tra vai \|*  
*na grahā'stodayakṛto doṣo viśveśvarāśrame \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. There is perpetual Kṛtayuga here. There is great festivity here forever. There is no defect or adverse condition in the hermitage of Viśveśvara, caused by the rise or setting of the Planets.

## \|\| 1.22.87 \|\|

*sadā saumyāyanaṃ tatra sadā tatra mahodayaḥ \|*  
*sadaiva maṃgalaṃ tatra yatra viśveśvarasthitiḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. There is perpetual Saumyāyana (the gentle transit i.e. the northern transit of the Sun) there; there is auspiciousness forever, where Viśveśvara is stationed.

## \|\| 1.22.88 \|\|

*yathābhūmitale vipra puryaḥ saṃti sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*tathā kāśī na maṃtavyā kvāpi lokottarātviyam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. O Brāhmaṇa, Kāśī should not be considered on a par with the thousands of cities that exist on the surface of the earth. It is superior to (higher than) the fourteen worlds.

## \|\| 1.22.89 \|\|

*mayā sṛṣṭāni vipreṃdra bhuvanāni caturdaśa \|*  
*asyāḥ puryā vinirmātā svayaṃ viśveśvaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. O eminent Brāhmaṇa, fourteen worlds have been created by me. But the creator of this city is Lord Viśveśvara himself.

## \|\| 1.22.90 \|\|

*purā yamastapastaptvā bahukālaṃ suduṣkaram \|*  
*trailokyādhikṛtiṃ prāptastyaktvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Formerly Yama performed a very severe penance for a long time. He acquired authority over all the three worlds, excepting the city of Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 1.22.91 \|\|

*carācarasya sarvasya yāni karmāṇi tāni vai \|*  
*gocare citraguptasya kāśīvāsikṛtādṛte \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. All the activities of the entire world consisting of mobile and immobile beings are within the ambit of the knowledge (i.e., record) of Citragupta and not so in the case of the residents of Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.22.92 \|\|

*praveśo yamadūtānāṃ na kadāciddvijottama \|*  
*madhye kāśīpurī kvāpi rakṣiṇastatra tadgaṇāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, the messengers of Yama have no right of entry anywhere within the city of Kāśī. The Gaṇas of Rudra stand guard there.

## \|\| 1.22.93 \|\|

*svayaṃ niyaṃtā viśveśastatra kāśyāṃ tanutyajām \|*  
*tatrāpi kṛtapāpānāṃ niyaṃtā kālabhairavaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Viśveśa himself is the controller of those who give up their bodies at Kāśī. Kālabhairava is the chastiser of those who commit sins there.

## \|\| 1.22.94 \|\|

*tatra pāpaṃ na kartavyaṃ dāruṇā rudrayātanā \|*  
*aho rudrapiśācatvaṃ narakebhyopi duḥsaham \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. No sin should be committed there. Torture from Rudras is highly terrible. Oh, the state of being a Rudrapiśāca is extremely unbearable, more than the sufferings in hell.

## \|\| 1.22.95 \|\|

*pāpameva hi kartavyaṃ matirasti yadīdṛśī \|*  
*sukhenānyatra kartavyaṃ mahī hyasti mahīyasī \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. If the mind is bent upon committing a sin, may it be comfortably perpetrated elsewhere. The earth is very vast.

## \|\| 1.22.96 \|\|

*api kāmāturo jaṃturekāṃ rakṣati mātaram \|*  
*api pāpakṛtā kāśī rakṣyā mokṣārthinaikikā \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Even a lustful creature avoids its mother. Kāśī alone is to be avoided by a committer of sin if he seeks salvation.

## \|\| 1.22.97 \|\|

*parāpavādaśīlena paradārābhilāṣiṇā \|*  
*tena kāśī na saṃsevyā kva kāśī nirayaḥ kva saḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Kāśī should not be resorted to by a person habituated to scandalise others, and by one who desires adultery with another man’s wife. Where is Kāśī and where is that hell? (What a great difference between the two!)

## \|\| 1.22.98 \|\|

*abhilaṣyaṃti ye nityaṃ dhanaṃ cātra pratigrahaiḥ \|*  
*parasvaṃ kapaṭairvāpi kāśī sevyā na tairnaraiḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Those who always seek wealth here through Pratigraha (accepting monetary gifts), or others’ wealth through fraudulent means, should keep away from Kāśī. Kāśī should not be resorted to by those men.

## \|\| 1.22.99 \|\|

*parapīḍākaraṃ karma kāśyāṃ nityaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*tadeva cetkimatra syātkāśīvāso durātmanām \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. All activities causing affliction to others should always be avoided at Kāśī. If that is persisted in, of what avail is the residence at Kāśī of the evil-minded one?

## \|\| 1.22.100 \|\|

*tyaktvā vaiśveśvarīṃ bhaktiṃ ye'nyadevaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*sarvathā tairna vastavyā rājadhānī pinākinaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. If the people adore other deities abandoning devotion to Viśveśvara, they should not at all reside here. It is the capital city of the Lord wielding Pināka.

## \|\| 1.22.101 \|\|

*arthārthinastu ye vipra ye ca kāmārthino narāḥ \|*  
*avimuktaṃ na taiḥ sevyaṃ mokṣakṣetramidaṃ yataḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Avimukta should not be resorted to, O Brāhmaṇa, by those men who seek wealth and those who seek sexual enjoyment, because this is the holy spot of salvation.

## \|\| 1.22.102 \|\|

*śivaniṃdāparā ye ca vedaniṃdā parāśca ye \|*  
*vedācārapratīpā ye sevyā vārāṇasī na taiḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Vārāṇasī should not be resorted to by those who are engaged in censuring Śiva, those who ridicule the Vedas and those who are against the conduct of life laid down in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.22.103 \|\|

*paradrohadhiyo ye ca parerṣyākāriṇaśca ye \|*  
*paropatāpino ye vai teṣāṃ kāśī na siddhaye \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Kāśī is not conducive to the spiritual achievement of those who think of harassing others, those who are jealous of others and those who torment others.

## \|\| 1.22.104 \|\|

*manasāpi na ye kāśīmabhinaṃdaṃti durdhiyaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ nirvāṇavārtāpi dūre durvṛttacetasām \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Even the talk of salvation is irrelevant in the case of those of evil action and mentality who do not praise Kāśī (even) in their minds.

## \|\| 1.22.105 \|\|

*jñānena na vinā mokṣaḥ kvacidastīha bhūtale \|*  
*tajjñānaṃ na vratairlabhyamapi cāṃdrāyaṇādibhiḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Without knowledge there is no salvation anywhere in the world, and that knowledge cannot be got through vows and rites including Cāndrāyaṇa.

## \|\| 1.22.106-109 \|\|

*tulāpuruṣamukhyaiśca dānaiśca śraddhayānvitaiḥ \|*  
*deśakāle ca vidhinā pātrebhyaḥ pratipāditaiḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*na yamairbrahmacaryādyairniyamairnārcanādibhi \|*  
*śarīraśoṣaṇairugrairna tapobhirdvijottama \|\| 107 \|\|*

*na mahāmaṃtrajapyaiśca gurubhiḥ pratipāditaiḥ \|*  
*na svādhyāyairyathoktaiśca nāgniśuśrūṣaṇaiḥ paraiḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

*na sevayā gurūṇāṃ ca na śrāddhairdevatārcanaiḥ \|*  
*na nānātīrthayātrābhirjñānaṃ samadhigamyate \|\| 109 \|\|*

106-109. Knowledge is not properly gained by any of these means: through gifts, of which Tulāpuruṣa (that is making gifts of things equal in weight to the donor) is the chief one even if they are done with faith, even if they are made in accordance with the injunctions, even if they are made over to the deserving persons at the proper place and time. (Knowledge is not obtained) through activities of restraint such as vow of celibacy etc., through worships etc., through severe austerities causing emaciation of the body, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

(It cannot be gained) through the Japas of great Mantras imparted by preceptors, through study of the Vedas as laid down, nor through scrupulous maintenance of the holy fire.

Knowledge is not obtained through service done to preceptors, through Śrāddhas or through the adoration of the deities, nor through different kinds of pilgrimages.

## \|\| 1.22.110 \|\|

*na yogena vinā jñānaṃ yogastattvārthaśīlanam \|*  
*gurūpadiṣṭamārgeṇa sadābhyāsavaśena ca \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Without Yoga there is no knowledge and Yoga is meditation on Tattvārtha i.e., the nature of reality, in accordance with the teachings of the preceptor and repeated practice.

## \|\| 1.22.111 \|\|

*tasyāṃtarāyā bahavaḥ sudūraśravaṇādayaḥ \|*  
*ato na prāpyate jñānaṃ yogādekena janmanā \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. There are many obstacles such as Siddhis like Sudūraśravaṇa etc. (ability to hear what is far off—Yogic Siddhis obstruct the ultimate knowledge). Hence knowledge is not acquired in a single birth through Yoga.

## \|\| 1.22.112 \|\|

*vinā tapo japādyaiśca vinā yogena suvrata \|*  
*niḥśreyo labhyate kāśyāmihaikenaiva janmanā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. (But) O righteous one, without penance, Japa and other things, without Yoga, salvation is obtained at Kāśī here itself in a single birth.

## \|\| 1.22.113 \|\|

*tvayā śuddhadhiyā kāśyāṃ yacchreyaḥ samupārjitam \|*  
*tacchreyasopyudarkaste mahānasti dvijottama \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Merit has been acquired by you of pure mind and intellect at Kāśī. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, the ultimate benefit of that merit is indeed very great.

## \|\| 1.22.114 \|\|

*ukteti virarāmājaḥ śṛṇvatorgaṇayostayoḥ \|*  
*sopi pramuditaścābhūcchivaśarmā mahāmanāḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. After saying this Brahmā stopped even as the attendants were listening. That Śivaśarman of a noble mind also became very glad.

## Chapter 23 - Caturbhujābhiṣeka (Caturbhuja-abhiṣeka)

## \|\| 1.23.1 \|\|

*śivaśarmovāca \|*  
*satyalokeśvara vidhe sarveṣāṃ prapitāmaha \|*  
*kiṃcidvijñaptukāmosmi na bhayādvaktumutsahe \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śivaśarman said:

1\. O Vidhi, O Lord of Satyaloka, O grandfather of all, I am desirous of submitting something but I do not dare to speak out due to fear.

## \|\| 1.23.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yattvaṃ praṣṭumanā vipra jñātaṃ te tanmanogatam \|*  
*pipṛcchiṣustvaṃ nirvāṇaṃ gaṇau tatkathayiṣyataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

2\. What you are about to ask, what is lurking in your mind is known to me. You are desirous of asking me about salvation. These two Gaṇas will describe it to you.

## \|\| 1.23.3 \|\|

*netayorviṣṇugaṇayoragocaramihāsti hi \|*  
*sarvametau vijānīto yatkiṃcidbrahmago lake \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There is nothing that is not known to these two attendants. They know everything whatever there is in the Cosmic Sphere.

## \|\| 1.23.4 \|\|

*ityuktvā satkṛtāste vai brahmaṇā bhagavadgaṇāḥ \|*  
*praṇamya lokakartāraṃ te'pi hṛṣṭāḥ pratasthire \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After saying this, Brahmā honoured the attendants (and the Brāhmaṇa). After bowing down to the creator of the world, they too started joyfully.

## \|\| 1.23.5 \|\|

*punaḥ svayānamāruhya vaikuṃṭhamabhito yayuḥ \|*  
*gacchatāpi punastatra dvijenāpṛcchitau gaṇau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Again they got into their vehicle and went towards Vaikuṇṭha. The Gaṇas were asked by that Brāhmaṇa while going ahead:

## \|\| 1.23.6 \|\|

*śivaśarmovāca \|*  
*kiyaddūre vayaṃ prāptā gaṃtavyaṃ ca kiyatpunaḥ \|*  
*pṛcchāmyanyacca vāṃ bhadrau brūtaṃ prītyā tadapyaho \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śivaśarman said:

6\. How far have we come? How much are we yet to go? O fair ones, I am asking another thing too. Be pleased to answer that too.

## \|\| 1.23.7 \|\|

*kāṃcyavaṃtī dvāravatī kāśyayodhyā ca paṃcamī \|*  
*māyāpurī ca mathurā puryaḥ sapta vimuktidāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. There are seven cities granting salvation, viz., Kāñcī, Avantī, Dvārāvatī, Kāśī, Ayodhyā—the fifth one, Māyāpuri and Mathurā.

## \|\| 1.23.8 \|\|

*vihāya ṣaṭpurīścānyāḥ kāśyāmevapratiṣṭhitā \|*  
*muktirviśvasṛjā tatkiṃ mama muktirna saṃprati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Leaving off the other six cities, salvation has been stabilized only in Kāśī by the Creator. Then how is it that I have no salvation as yet?

## \|\| 1.23.9 \|\|

*iti sarvaṃ mama puraḥ prasādādvaktumarhatam \|*  
*iti tadvākyamākarṇya gaṇāvūcaturādarāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. I shall be grateful if you please clarify it to me.

On hearing these words of his, the Gaṇas spoke with due respect:

## \|\| 1.23.10 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*yathārthaṃ kathayāvaste yatpṛṣṭaṃ bhavatānagha \|*  
*viṣṇuprasādājjānīvo bhūtaṃbhāvibhavattathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

The Gaṇas said:

10\. O sinless one, we shall tell you truthfully what you have asked. By Viṣṇu’s grace, we two know the past, the present and the future.

## \|\| 1.23.11 \|\|

*viprāvabhāsate yāvatkiraṇaiḥ puṣpavaṃtayoḥ \|*  
*tāvatībhūḥ samuddiṣṭā sasamudrādri kānanā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Brāhmaṇa, that extent of space which is illuminated by the rays of the Sun and the Moon is called the earth having oceans, mountains and forests.

## \|\| 1.23.12 \|\|

*viyacca tāvadupari vistāraparimaṃḍalam \|*  
*yojanānāṃ ca niyute bhūmerbhānurvyavasthitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Above those is the sky, extensive and circular. The Sun is two hundred thousand Yojanas above the earth.

## \|\| 1.23.13 \|\|

*bhānoḥ sakāśādupari lakṣe lakṣyaḥ kṣapākaraḥ \|*  
*nakṣatradhaṃ ḍalaṃ somāllakṣayojanamucchritam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Moon is seen a hundred thousand (Yojanas) above the Sun. The region of the stars is a hundred thousand Yojanas above the Moon.

## \|\| 1.23.14 \|\|

*uḍumaṃḍalataḥ saumya upariṣṭāddvilakṣataḥ \|*  
*dvilakṣe tu budhācchukraḥ śukrādbhaumo dvilakṣake \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Budha (Mercury) is two hundred thousand (Yojanas) above the stellar region. Śukra (Venus) is two hundred thousand Yojanas away from Budha and Bhauma (Mars) is two hundred thousand (Yojanas) away from Venus.

## \|\| 1.23.15 \|\|

*māheyādupariṣṭācca surejyo niyutadvaye \|*  
*dvilakṣayojanotsedhaḥ saurirdevapurohitāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Bṛhaspati (Jupiter) is two hundred thousand Yojanas above Bhauma (Mars). Śauri (Saturn) is two hundred thousand Yojanas above Brahaspati, the priest of gods.

## \|\| 1.23.16 \|\|

*daśāyutasamucchrāyaṃ saureḥ saptarṣimaṃḍalam \|*  
*saptarṣibhyaḥ sahasrāṇāṃ śatādūrdhvaṃ dhruvasthitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The region of the Seven Sages (Great Bear) is a hundred thousand Yojanas away from Śani. Dhruva (the Pole Star) is stationed a hundred thousand Yojanas away from the Seven Sages.

## \|\| 1.23.17 \|\|

*pādagamyaṃ hi yatkiṃcidvastvasti dharaṇītale \|*  
*tadbhūrloka iti khyātaḥ sābdhidvīpādrikānanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Whatever object there may be which could be reached by walking on foot is known as (included in) Bhūrloka containing oceans, continents, mountains and forests.

## \|\| 1.23.18 \|\|

*bhūrlokācca bhuvarloko bradhnāvadhirudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*ādityādādhruvaṃ vipra svarloka iti gīyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The space extending from Bhūrloka to the Sun is known as Bhuvarloka. The space from the Sun extending up to Dhruva is known as Svarloka, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.23.19 \|\|

*maharlokaḥ kṣiterūrdhvamekakoṭipramāṇataḥ \|*  
*koṭidvaye tu saṃkhyāto jano bhūrlokato janaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Maharloka is ten million Yojanas above the earth. Janaloka is calculated to be twenty million Yojanas above Bhūrloka by the people.

## \|\| 1.23.20 \|\|

*catuṣkoṭipramāṇastu tapoloko'sti bhūtalāt \|*  
*upariṣṭātkṣiteraṣṭau koṭayaḥ satyamīritam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Tapoloka is forty million Yojanas from the earth. Satyaloka is spoken as eighty million Yojanas above the earth.

## \|\| 1.23.21 \|\|

*satyādupari vaikuṃṭho yojanānāṃ pramāṇataḥ \|*  
*bhūrlokātparisaṃkhyātaḥ koṭiṣoḍaśasaṃmitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Vaikuṇṭha is above Satya. It is calculated as one hundred and sixty million Yojanas above the earth.

## \|\| 1.23.22 \|\|

*yatrāste śrīpatiḥ sākṣātsarveṣāmabhayapradaḥ \|*  
*tatastu ṣoḍaśaguṇaḥ kailāso'sti śivālayaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. It is there that Śrīpati dwells in person. He is the bestower of freedom from fear on all. Kailāsa is sixteen times more than that. It is the abode of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.23.23 \|\|

*pārvatyā sahitaḥ śaṃbhurgajāsya skaṃda naṃdibhiḥ \|*  
*yatra tiṣṭhati viśveśaḥ sakalaḥ sa paraḥ smūtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It is there that Śambhu, the Lord of the universe, dwells with Pārvatī, Gajāsya (Ganeśa), Skanda and others. He is regarded as Sakala (accompanied with Kalā i.e., Pārvatī or in his entire form) and the supreme one.

## \|\| 1.23.24 \|\|

*tasya devasya khelo'yaṃ svalīlā mūrtidhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*sa viśveśa iti khyāta stasyājñākṛdidaṃ jagat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He assumes forms sportingly. The entire universe is a sport of that Lord. He is well-known as Viśveśa (Lord of the universe). This universe obeys his command.

## \|\| 1.23.25 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ śāsakaścāsau tasya śāstā na cāparaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ sṛjati bhūtāni svayaṃ pāti tathātti ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He is the controller and chastiser of all. There is no one else to control him. He himself creates living beings. He himself protects them and eats them up (i.e., annihilates them).

## \|\| 1.23.26 \|\|

*sarvajña ekaḥ sa proktaḥ svecchādhīna viceṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*tasya pravatarkaḥ kopi nahi naiva nivartakaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He is spoken as Sarvajña (omniscient) and single. His activities depend upon his will. There is no one to make him act or desist from any activity.

## \|\| 1.23.27 \|\|

*amūrtaṃ yatparaṃ brahma samūrtaṃ śruticoditam \|*  
*sarvavyāpi sadā nityaṃ satyaṃ dvaitavivarjitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He is Amūrta (having no visible form) and the supreme Brahman. He is described by Śrutis as Mūrta (having visible forms). He is omnipresent. He is eternal. He is the truth. He is devoid of Dvaita (duality).

## \|\| 1.23.28 \|\|

*sarvebhyaḥ kāraṇebhyaśca parātparataraṃ param \|*  
*ānaṃdaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ śrutayo yatpracakṣate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He is far beyond Pradhāna which is beyond Mahat and other (causal) categories. As stated by the Śrutis, he is the blissful form of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.23.29 \|\|

*saṃvidaṃ tena yaṃ vedā viṣṇurveda na vai vidhiḥ \|*  
*yato vāco nivartaṃte hyaprāpya manasā saha \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Even the Vedas do not comprehend him; neither Viṣṇu nor Vidhi know him fully. Words recede from him along with the mind after failing to reach him.

## \|\| 1.23.30 \|\|

*svayaṃvedyaḥ paraṃ jyotiḥ sarvasya hṛdi saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*yogigamyastvanākhyeyo yaḥ pramāṇaikagocaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He is self-known. He is the great brilliant splendour stationed in the heart of everyone, comprehended by Yogins. He cannot be narrated and described. Means of valid knowledge do not comprehend him. Vedas alone know him.

## \|\| 1.23.31 \|\|

*nānārūpopyarūpo yaḥ sarvagopi na gocaraḥ \|*  
*anaṃtopyaṃtaka vapuḥ sarvavitkarmavarjitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Though he appears in many forms, he is formless. Though present everywhere, he is imperceptible. Though he is infinite, he has the form of the annihilator. Knower of all, he is devoid of activities.

## \|\| 1.23.32 \|\|

*tasyedamaiśvaraṃ rūpaṃ khaṃḍacaṃdrāvataṃsakam \|*  
*tamālaśyāmalagalaṃ sphuradbhālavilocanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. This is the divine form of that Lord having the crescent moon for embellishment, a throat dark like Tamāla and a sparkling eye in the forehead.

## \|\| 1.23.33 \|\|

*lasadvāmārdhanārīkaṃ kṛtaśeṣaśubhāṃgadam \|*  
*gaṃgātaraṃgasatsaṃga sadādhautajaṭātaṭam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The left half dazzles with the form of a woman, Serpent Śeṣa constitutes his splendid armlet and the matted hairs are perpetually washed by the excellent contact with the waves of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.23.34 \|\|

*smarāṃgarajaḥpuṃja pūjitāvayavojjvalam \|*  
*vicitragātravidhṛtamahāvyālavibhūṣaṇam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He is refulgent with the limbs smeared with the ashes of the body of Smara (god of Love) and great serpents for ornaments worn round the wonderful body.

## \|\| 1.23.35 \|\|

*mahokṣasyaṃdanagamaṃ virutājagavāyudham \|*  
*gajājinottarāsaṃgaṃ daśārdhavadanaṃ śubham \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He moves about in a vehicle in the form of the great Bull; he has the humming and twanging bow Ājagava; he has the upper garment made of elephant hide and five faces.

## \|\| 1.23.36 \|\|

*uttrāsita mahāmṛtyu mahābalagaṇāvṛtam \|*  
*śaraṇārthikṛtatrāṇaṃ nata nirvāṇakāraṇam \|*  
*manorathapathātītaṃ varadānaparāyaṇam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He is surrounded by extremely powerful Gaṇas who can frighten Mahāmṛtyu (the great god of Death); he accords protection to those who seek refuge; he is the cause of salvation unto those who bow down; he is beyond the ken of even mental powers; he is eager to bestow boons.

## \|\| 1.23.37 \|\|

*tasya tattvasvarūpasya rūpātītasya bho dvija \|*  
*parāvare rudrarūpe sarvevyāpyāvatiṣṭhata \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Brāhmaṇa, his greater and lesser Rudra Forms pervade everything. Actually he is of the form of the Truth and is beyond all forms.

## \|\| 1.23.38 \|\|

*nirākāropi sākāraḥ śiva eva hi kāraṇama \|*  
*muktaye bhuktaye vāpi na śivānmokṣado paraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Though without shape and form, he has forms. Śiva alone is the cause of enjoyment of pleasures, and attainment of salvation. There is no one other than Śiva who bestows salvation.

## \|\| 1.23.39-40 \|\|

*yathā tenākhilaṃ hyetatpārvatīpatisātkṛtama \|*  
*idaṃ carācaraṃ sarvaṃ dṛśyādṛśyamarūpiṇā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tathā mṛḍānīkāṃtena viṣṇusādakhilaṃjagata \|*  
*vidhāya krīḍyate vipra nityaṃ svacchaṃda līlayā \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Just as this visible and invisible world consisting of mobile and immobile beings has been handed over to the Consort of Pārvatī by that formless Being, so also the entire universe has been handed over to Viṣṇu by the Consort of Mṛḍānī, O Brāhmaṇa, and he sports about in his unfettered playful activities.

## \|\| 1.23.41 \|\|

*yathāśivastathā viṣṇuryathāviṣṇustathā śivaḥ \|*  
*aṃtaraṃ śivaviṣṇvośca manāgapi na vidyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. What is Śiva, so is Viṣṇu; what as Viṣṇu, so is Śiva; there is no difference at all between Śiva and Viṣṇu.

\[Preparation for the Coronation of Viṣṇu (VV 42-52)\]

## \|\| 1.23.42 \|\|

*āhūya pūrvaṃ brahmādīnsamastāndevatāgaṇān \|*  
*vidyādharoragādīṃśca siddhagaṃdharvacāraṇān \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. At the outset, he summoned all the gods including Brahmā, Vidyādharas, serpents and others, Siddhas, Gandharvas and Cāraṇas.

## \|\| 1.23.43 \|\|

*nijasiṃhāsanasamaṃ kṛtvā siṃhāsanaṃ śubham \|*  
*upaveśya hariṃ tatra cchatraṃ kṛtvā manoharam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He made a splendid throne on a par with his own throne and made Hari sit thereon. Then he made a charming umbrella.

## \|\| 1.23.44 \|\|

*ślakṣṇaṃ koṭiśalākaṃ ca viśvakarmavinirmitam \|*  
*pāṃḍuraṃ ratnadaṃḍaṃ ca sthūlamuktāvalaṃbitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. It was beautiful with ten million ribs and designed by Viśvakarman. It was white in colour. The handle was embellished with jewels. Big pearls were suspended from it.

## \|\| 1.23.45 \|\|

*kalaśena vicitreṇa hyupariṣṭādvirājitam \|*  
*sahasrayojanāyāmaṃ sarvaratnamayaṃ śubham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. A wonderful pot shone above it. It extended to a thousand Yojanas. It was very splendid with all kinds of gems embedded therein.

## \|\| 1.23.46 \|\|

*paṭṭasūtramayairamyaiścāmaraiśca pariṣkṛtam \|*  
*rājābhiṣekayogyaiśca dravyaiḥ sarvauṣadhādibhiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. It was embellished with chowries consisting of silken cords. There were all articles essential for the coronation of a king. There were all medicinal herbs.

## \|\| 1.23.47 \|\|

*pratyakṣatīrthapāthobhiḥ paṃcakuṃbhairmanoharaiḥ \|*  
*siddhārthākṣatadūrvābhirmaṃtraiḥ svayamupasthitaiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. There were five beautiful pots filled with holy waters from all visible holy spots and white mustard, raw rice grains and Dūrvā grass. They had come there themselves with the Mantras which inspired them.

## \|\| 1.23.48 \|\|

*devānāṃ ca tatharṣīṇāṃ siddhānāṃ phaṇināmapi \|*  
*ānīya maṃgalakarāḥ kanyāḥ ṣoḍaśaṣoḍaśa \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Sixteen virgins were brought from each of the families of the Devas, Sages, Siddhas and Serpents. These virgins had auspicious articles in their hands.

## \|\| 1.23.49 \|\|

*vīṇāmṛdaṃgābjabherī maru ḍiṃḍimajharjharaiḥ \|*  
*ānakaiḥ kāṃsyatālādyai rvādyairlalitagāyanaiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. There were musical instruments like Lute, Mṛḍangas \[Mṛḍāṅgas?\], Conches, War-drums (Bherī), Marus, Ḍiṇḍimas, Jharjharas, Ānaka drums, brass cymbals etc. and also light music.

## \|\| 1.23.50 \|\|

*brahmaghoṣamahārāvairāpūritanabhoṃgaṇe \|*  
*śubhe tithau śubhe lagne tārācaṃdrabalānvite \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. With these sounds and chanting of the Vedic Mantras, the entire sky was filled. The lunar day was auspicious, the Lagna was splendid possessing the power of the Moon and the Stars.

## \|\| 1.23.51-53 \|\|

*ābaddhamukuṭaṃ ramyaṃ kṛtakautukamaṃgalam \|*  
*mṛḍānīkṛtaśṛṃgāraṃ suśriyā suśriyāyutam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*abhiṣicya maheśena svayaṃ brahmāṃḍamaṃḍape \|*  
*dattaṃ samastamaiśvaryaṃ yannijaṃ nānyagāmi ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tatastuṣṭāva deveśaḥ pramathaiḥ saha śārṅgiṇam \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ lokakartāramuvāca ca vacastvidam \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. A beautiful crown was placed on the head of Viṣṇu. He shone beautifully with the requisite auspicious threads etc. essential for the solemn ceremony. Mṛḍānī herself did the make-up and embellishment. The glorious goddess Śri accompanied him. Maheśa himself crowned him pouring the auspicious sacred waters. There in the Brahmāṇḍa Pavilion, all his riches and prosperity were passed on to Viṣṇu, everything that was Śiva’s and hitherto not gone to anyone else.

Then the Lord of Devas accompanied by his Pramathas eulogized Śārṅgin. Then he spoke the following words to Brahmā, the creator of the worlds.

## \|\| 1.23.54 \|\|

*mama vaṃdyastvayaṃ viṣṇuḥ praṇamatvamamuṃ harim \|*  
*ityuktvātha svayaṃ rudro nanāma garuḍadhvajam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. “This Viṣṇu is worthy of my adoration. You too bow down to this Hari.” After saying this, Rudra himself bowed down to the Garuḍa-emblemed Lord.

## \|\| 1.23.55-58 \|\|

*tato gaṇeśvaraiḥ sarvaiṃrbrahmaṇā ca marudgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*yogibhiḥ sanakādyaiśca siddhairdevarṣibhistathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*vidyādharaiḥ sagaṃdharvairyakṣarakṣopsarogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*guhyakaiścāraṇairbhūtaiḥ śeṣa vāsuki takṣakaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*patatribhiḥ kiṃnaraiśca sarvaiḥ sthāvarajaṃgamaiḥ \|*  
*tato jayajayetyuktvā namostviti namostviti \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tatoharirmaheśena saṃsadi dyusadāṃ tadā \|*  
*etairmahāravai ramyaiścānarci paramārciṣā \|\| 58 \|\|*

55-58. Thereafter, Lord Viṣṇu, the excessively refulgent one was adored by all the Gaṇeśvaras, Brahmā accompanied by Devas, Sanaka and other Yogins, Siddhas, divine sages, Vidyādharas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, groups of celestial damsels, Guhyakas, Cāraṇas, Bhūtas, Śeṣa, Vāsuki and Takṣaka, birds, all the Kinnaras, and all mobile and immobile beings. They uttered, “Be victorious, be victorious” and “Obeisance to you, obeisance to you.”

Then in the assembly of the heaven-dwellers Hari was adored by Maheśa of great splendour, and all these who made loud sounds.

\[Eulogy of Viṣṇu:\]

## \|\| 1.23.59 \|\|

*tvaṃ kartā sarvabhūtānāṃ pātā hartā tvameva ca \|*  
*tvameva jagatāṃ pūjyastvameva jagadīśvaraḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. “You are the creator of all living beings; you are the protector. You alone are the annihilator; you alone are worthy of being worshipped by all the worlds. You alone are the Lord of the universe.

## \|\| 1.23.60 \|\|

*dātā dharmārthakāmānāṃ śāstā durnayakāriṇām \|*  
*ajeyastvaṃ ca saṃgrāme mamāpi hi bhaviṣyasi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. You will be the giver of Dharma (Virtue), Wealth and Love. You will be the chastiser of persons of evil deeds. You will be invincible in battle even unto me.

## \|\| 1.23.61 \|\|

*icchāśaktiḥ kriyāśaktirjñānaśaktistathottamā \|*  
*śaktitrayamidaṃ viṣṇo gṛhāṇa prāpitaṃ mayā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O Viṣṇu, accept these three Śaktis handed over by me, i.e. Icchāśakti (power of will), Kriyāśakti (power of action) and the excellent Jñānaśakti (power of knowledge).

## \|\| 1.23.62 \|\|

*tvaddveṣṭāro hare nūnaṃ mayā śāsyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tvadbhaktānāṃ mayā viṣṇo deyaṃ nirvāṇamuttamam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Indeed, O Hari, those who hate you should be scrupulously admonished by me. O Viṣṇu, excellent salvation should be granted by me to your devotees.

## \|\| 1.23.63 \|\|

*māyāṃ cāpi gṛhāṇemāṃ duṣpraṇodyāṃ surāsuraiḥ \|*  
*yayā saṃmohitaṃ viśvamakiṃcijjñaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Accept this Māyā too. It cannot be dispelled by Suras and Asuras. Deluded by it, the entire universe will become bereft of knowledge. They will not have the least vestige of knowledge.

## \|\| 1.23.64 \|\|

*vāmabāhurmadīyastvaṃ dakṣiṇosau pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*asyāpi hi vidheḥ pātā janitāpi bhaviṣyasi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. You are my left arm. This Pitāmaha shall be the right arm. You will be the progenitor and protector of this Vidhi too.”

## \|\| 1.23.65 \|\|

*vaikuṃṭhaiśvaryamāsādya hareritthaṃ haraḥ svayam \|*  
*kailāse pramathaiḥ sārdhaṃ svairaṃ krīḍatyumāpatiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Granting thus Vaikuṇṭha and entire Aiśvarya to Hari, Hara, the Consort of Umā, freely sports about in Kailāsa along with Pramathas.

## \|\| 1.23.66 \|\|

*tadā prabhṛti devosau śārṅgadhanvā gadādharaḥ \|*  
*trailokyamakhilaṃ śāsti dānavāṃtakaro hariḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Ever since then, Hari, the destroyer of the Dānavas, administers the three worlds wielding his mace and the bow Śārṅga.

## \|\| 1.23.67 \|\|

*iti te kathitā vipra lokānāṃ ca paristhitiḥ \|*  
*idānīṃ kathayiṣyāvastavanirvāṇa kāraṇam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Thus, O Brāhmaṇa, the situation of all the worlds has been recounted to you. Now we shall tell you the cause of salvation.

## \|\| 1.23.68 \|\|

*idaṃ tu paramākhyānaṃ śṛṇuyādyaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*svarlokamabhigamyātha kāśyāṃ nirvāṇamāpnuyāt \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He who listens attentively to this great narrative, will go to heaven and shall attain salvation in Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.23.69-70 \|\|

*yajñotsave vivāhe ca maṃgaleṣvakhileṣvapi \|*  
*rājyābhiṣeka samaye devasthāpanakarmaṇi \|\| 69 \|\|*

*sarvādhikāradāneṣu navaveśmapraveśane \|*  
*paṭhitavyaṃ prayatnena tatkārya parisiddhaye \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. This narrative should be read scrupulously on the following occasions for the success of those activities: festivals, Yajñas, marriage celebration, all auspicious occasions, at the time of coronation, while installing deities, while relinquishing authority and while entering a new house.

## \|\| 1.23.71 \|\|

*aputro labhate putramadhano dhanavānbhavet \|*  
*vyādhito mucyate rogādbaddho mucyeta baṃdhanāt \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. One without sons shall get a son; one without wealth shall become rich; the sick becomes rid of the ailments and a man in bondage gets release.

## \|\| 1.23.72 \|\|

*japyametatprayatnena satataṃ maṃgalārthinā \|*  
*amaṃgalānāṃ śamanaṃ haranārāyaṇapriyama \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. This is to be used for Japa by those who seek welfare strenuously. It subdues all inauspiciousness. It is liked by Hara and Nārāyaṇa.

## Chapter 24 - Śivaśarman Attains Salvation

## \|\| 1.24.1-4 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*śivaśarmannudarkaṃ te kathayāvo niśāmaya \|*  
*tvamatra vaiṣṇave loke bhuktvā bhogānsupuṣkalān \|\| 1 \|\|*

*brahmaṇo vatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ ramamāṇo'psarogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*sutīrthamaraṇopātta puṇyaśeṣeṇa vai punaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyasi mahīpālo nagare naṃdivardhane \|*  
*rājyaṃ prāpyāsapatnaṃ ca samṛddhabalavāhanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kṛṣṭibhirhṛṣṭapuṣṭaiśca ramyahāṭakabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*saṃjuṣṭamiṣṭāpūrtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nityakartṛbhiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

The Gaṇas said:

1-4. O Śivaśarman, we shall speak what you are destined to have in future. Listen. Here in the world of Viṣṇu you will enjoy all pleasures in plenty. For the period of a year of Brahmā you will be sporting about with groups of celestial damsels. Due to the residue of the merit acquired by dying in an excellent holy place, you will become a king in the city of Nandivardhana. You will acquire a kingdom without any rivals or enemies. You will have plenty of vehicles and divisions of the army. In the kingdom, all the learned men will be hale and hearty. They will be having charming golden ornaments. The people there will perform regularly virtuous rites of Iṣṭa and Pūrta.

## \|\| 1.24.5 \|\|

*sadāsaṃpannasasyaṃ ca sūrvarakṣetrasaṃkulam \|*  
*sudeśaṃ suprajaṃ susthaṃ sutṛṇaṃ bahugodhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There will be perpetual growth of vegetation. The fields will be very fertile. All the region will be excellent, the subjects noble and healthy. There will be plenty of cattle and pasture-lands.

## \|\| 1.24.6 \|\|

*devatāyatanānāṃ ca rājibhiḥ parirājitam \|*  
*suyūpā yatra vai grāmāḥ suvittarddhi virājitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It will have many rows of shining temples for the deities. Excellent sacrificial posts will be found in all the villages, prosperous and remarkable in every way.

## \|\| 1.24.7 \|\|

*supuṣpa kṛtrimodyānāḥ sasadāphalapādapāḥ \|*  
*sapadminīkakāsārā yatra rājaṃti bhūmayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. There will be excellent man-made parks with plenty of flowers and perpetually fruit-bearing trees. All the plots of lands will have lakes and lotus-ponds in plenty.

## \|\| 1.24.8 \|\|

*sadaṃbhā nimnagārājirna yatra janatā kvacit \|*  
*kulānyeva kulīnāni na cānyāyadhanāni ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There the rivers are Sadāmbhāḥ (Sad-ambhaḥ: having excellent, translucent water) but seldom are the people Sadaṃbha (Sa-daṃbha—having hypocrisy). The families (thereof) are of noble descent (Kūlināni) and not possessors of ill-gotten wealth concealed in the earth (Ku-līnāni).

## \|\| 1.24.9 \|\|

*vibhramo yatra nārīṣu navidvatsu ca karhicit \|*  
*nadyaḥ kuṭilagāminyo na yatra viṣaye prajāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There is Vibhrama (coquettishness) in women. There is no Vibhrama (ignorance, delusion) in learned men. Only rivers are Kuṭilagāminyaḥ (going along zigzag paths) and not the subjects in that land.

## \|\| 1.24.10 \|\|

*tamoyuktāḥ kṣapā yatra bahuleṣu na mānavāḥ \|*  
*rajoyujaḥ striyo yatra na dharmabahulā narāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In that land the nights in the dark half of the month are full of darkness. The men are not Tamoyukta (possessed of Tamas quality). Only the women are Rajoyujaḥ (having menstrual flow of blood) and not men full of righteousness (i.e. they do not have the quality of Rajas.)

## \|\| 1.24.11 \|\|

*dhanairanaṃdho yatrāsti mano naiva ca bhojanam \|*  
*anayaḥ syaṃdanaṃ yatra na ca vai rājapūruṣaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The people are Anandha (not blind) due to wealth and not food (not having rice). The chariot is Anayaḥ (an-ayas) (having no iron but gold-plated) but the king’s office is not Anayaḥ (a-nayaḥ: devoid of good policies).

## \|\| 1.24.12 \|\|

*daṃḍaḥ paraśukuddāla vālavya janarājiṣu \|*  
*ātapatreṣu nānyatra kvacitkrodhāparādhajaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There is Daṇḍa (staff, wooden handle) in axes, spades, chowries, umbrellas etc. but there is seldom Daṇḍa (punishment) due to anger or guilt.

## \|\| 1.24.13 \|\|

*anyatrākṣikavṛṃdebhyaḥ kvacinna paridevanam \|*  
*ākṣikā eva dṛśyaṃte yatra pāśakapāṇayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Except in the case of gamesters nowhere else there is Paridevanam (playing with dice; lamenting). Only gamesters are seen Pāśakapāṇis (having dice in the hands/hands bound with ropes).

## \|\| 1.24.14 \|\|

*jāḍyavārtā jaleṣveva strīmadhyā eva durbalāḥ \|*  
*kaṭhorahṛdayā yatra sīmaṃtinyo na mānavāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The talk of Jāḍya (chillness, sluggishness) is only in regard to water; only the middle part of women is Durbala (slender) and not men (weak). There, only the ladies are having hard breasts (Kaṭhorahṛdayāḥ) and not men (cruel in the heart).

## \|\| 1.24.15 \|\|

*auṣadheṣveva yatrāsti kuṣṭhayogo na mānave \|*  
*vedhopyaṃtaḥsuratneṣu śūlaṃ mūrtikareṣu vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. There is Kuṣṭhayoga (medicinal preparation from the drug Kuṣṭha) in medicines alone but (attack of leprosy) not in men. There is Vedha (one hole) in excellent jewels and (Vedha—beating) not elsewhere. There is Śūla (trident) in the hands of idols but no Śūla (pain) in men.

## \|\| 1.24.16 \|\|

*kaṃpaḥsāttvikabhāvottho na bhayātkvāpi kasyacit \|*  
*saṃjvaraḥ kāmajo yatra dāridryaṃ kaluṣasya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There is Kaṃpa (trembling) due to Sāttvika Bhāva (affection and fidelity) and not due to fear in regard to anyone at any place. Saṃjvara (fever) in that city is due to love but Saṃjvara (distress for want of money) is not there. There is poverty but that of sinfulness.

## \|\| 1.24.17 \|\|

*durlabhatvaṃ sadā kasya sukṛtena ca vastunaḥ \|*  
*ibhā eva pramattā vai yuddhaṃ vīcyorjalāśaye \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. There is scarcity of sin and not in regard to merit or commodities. Only elephants are Pramattas (in rut, mad) but not others. There is war only in lakes between waveṣ

## \|\| 1.24.18 \|\|

*dānahānirgajeṣveva drumeṣveva hi kaṃṭakāḥ \|*  
*janeṣveva vihārā hi na kasyaciduraḥsthalī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. There is cessation of the flow of ichor (Dāna) among elephants and not stopping of the flow in religious gifts (Dāna) among the people. There are Kaṇṭakas (thorns) on the trees and no Kaṇṭakas (troublesome persons) among the public. There are Vihāras (sports) among the people but nobody’s chest was without a necklace (Vi-hāra: necklessness).

## \|\| 1.24.19 \|\|

*bāṇeṣu guṇaviśleṣo baṃdhoktiḥ pustake dṛḍhā \|*  
*snehatyāgaḥ sadaivāsti yatra pāśupate jane \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There is Guṇaviśleṣa (separation from the string) only in regard to the arrows. There is a firm mention of binding (Bandhoktiḥ) only in regard to books (which require strong binding). Snehatyāga (eschewing oily and fatty substance, abandoning affection) is only in regard to Pāśupatas (and not in regard to others).

## \|\| 1.24.20 \|\|

*daṃḍavārtā sadā yatra kṛtasaṃnyāsakarmaṇām \|*  
*mārgaṇāścāpakeṣveva bhikṣukā brahmacāriṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The usual talk about Daṇḍa (sacred staff) is among Sannyāsins (and not of Daṇḍa—punishment). Mārgaṇas (arrows) are only on the bows but there was no Mārgaṇa (begging) anywhere else. And only religious students beg as a ritual and hence are beggars (Sannyāsins are cordially invited for meals and need not beg).

## \|\| 1.24.21 \|\|

*yatra kṣapaṇakā eva dṛśyaṃte maladhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*prāyo madhuvratā eva yatra caṃcalavṛttayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. There, only Kṣapaṇakas (Jaina recluses) have the impurities of the body (due to non-bath) and are seen so; generally the bees alone are fickle in their activities (wandering from flower to flower).

## \|\| 1.24.22-27 \|\|

*ityādi guṇavaddeśe tvayirājyaṃ praśāsati \|*  
*dharmeṇa rājadharmajña śauṃḍīryaguṇaśālini \|\| 22 \|\|*

*saubhāgyabhāji rūpāḍhye śauryaudāryaguṇānvite \|*  
*sīmaṃtinīnāṃ ramyāṇāṃ lāvaṇyavarjita suśriyām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*rājñīnāmayutaṃbhāvi kumārāṇāṃ śatatrayam \|*  
*vṛddhakāla iti khyāta ugraḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*vijitānekasamaraḥ śrīsaṃtarpitamārgaṇaḥ \|*  
*anekaguṇasaṃpūrṇaḥ pūrṇacaṃdranibhadyutiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*saṃtatāvabhṛthaklinna mūrdhajaḥ kṣitiṣarṣabhaḥ \|*  
*prajāpālanasaṃpannaḥ kośaprīṇitabhūsuraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*padāraviṃdaṃ gauviṃdaṃ hṛdi dhyāyannataṃdritaḥ \|*  
*vāsudevakathālāpaparikṣipta dinakṣapaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

22-27. You will be ruling a kingdom consisting of all the virtues mentioned before. You will be righteous and conversant with the duties of a king. You will be heroic too.

You will possess all good fortunes and handsome features. You will be endowed with such virtues as heroism, liberalmindedness etc. You will have ten thousand queens, all beautiful women, who will have earned good reputation through their beauty. You will beget three hundred sons.

You will be famous by the name Vṛddhakāla. You will be awe-inspiring and capable of conquering the cities of foes. You will be victorious in many battles. You will propitiate suppliants with your wealth. You will be full of many good qualities. Your lustre will be like that of the full Moon. You will be a leading king with your tresses of hairs kept wet due to the incessant performance of Avabhṛtha Snāna (holy ablution as a valedictory rite after concluding sacrifices). You will be richly endowed with the quality of ably protecting the subjects. You will be making Brāhmaṇas delighted through your treasury. You will be meditating on the lotus-like feet of Govinda in your heart with care. You will be spending days and nights in discoursing on the exploits of Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 1.24.28 \|\|

*kadācidupaviṣṭaḥsanmadhye rājasabhaṃ dvija \|*  
*dūrātkārpaṭikairdṛṣṭo vārāṇasyāḥ samāgataiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Once you are seated in the assembly of the kings, O Brāhmaṇa, you are seen from a distance by Karpaṭikas (saints in red garments) who arrive from Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 1.24.29 \|\|

*tatkarmabhāvisadṛśaistadātvamabhinaṃditaḥ \|*  
*taiḥ sarvai rājaśārdūlasyāśīrvādairanekaśaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then you are congratulated and blessed in a manner befitting your merits by all of them, through their words of benediction addressing you “O tiger among kings.”

## \|\| 1.24.30 \|\|

*śrīmadviśveśvaro devo viśveṣāṃ jagatāṃ guruḥ \|*  
*kāśīnāthastute kuryātkumaterapavarjanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “May the glorious Lord Viśveśvara, the preceptor of all the worlds, Lord of Kāśī, wipe off all your evil intentions and ignorance.

## \|\| 1.24.31 \|\|

*naiḥśreyasīṃ ca saṃpattiṃ yo deyātsmaraṇādapi \|*  
*kāśīnāthaḥ sa te diśyājjñānaṃ malavivarjitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Lord of Kāśī is the bestower of riches in the form of salvation even when you only remember him. May he grant you knowledge free from all impurities.

## \|\| 1.24.32 \|\|

*yena puṇyena te prāptaṃ rājyaṃ prājyamakaṃṭakam \|*  
*tatpuṇyaśeṣatobhūyādviśvanāthe matistava \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The excellent kingdom free from foes has been acquired by you through merit. May the balance of the same merit bring about your inclination towards Viśvanātha.

## \|\| 1.24.33 \|\|

*yasya prasādātsulabhamāyuḥ putrāṃbarāganāḥ \|*  
*samṛddhayaḥ svargamokṣau sa viśveśaḥ prasīdatu \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. May that Viśveśa be pleased with you—Viśveśa with whose favour long life, sons, garments and women, all prosperities, heavenly pleasures and salvation are easily available.

## \|\| 1.24.34 \|\|

*nāmaśravaṇamātreṇa yasya viśveśiturvibhoḥ \|*  
*mahāpātakavicchedaḥ sa viśveśo'stu te hṛdi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. May that Viśveśa be present in your heart—Viśveśa, merely by listening to whose name all great sins will be split and dispelled.”

## \|\| 1.24.35 \|\|

*tvaṃ vṛddhakālo bhūpālaḥ śrutvetyāśīḥ paraṃparām \|*  
*smariṣyasīdaṃ vṛttāṃtaṃ pulakāṃkavapustadā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On hearing this continuous series of benediction you, king Vṛddhakāla, will remember this present incident with hairs standing on their ends.

## \|\| 1.24.36-37 \|\|

*ākāragopanaṃ kṛtvā tebhyo dattvā dhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*sumuhūrtamanuprāpya sute rājyaṃ vidhāya ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*anaṃgalekhayā rājñyā tataḥ kāśīṃ gamiṣyasi \|*  
*dattvā dānāni bhūrīṇi prīṇayitvā'rthino janān \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Concealing your reactions and features, you will be giving them much wealth. At an auspicious hour, you will be entrusting the kingdom to your son. Accompanied by Anaṅgalekhā, the (chief) queen, you will go to Kāśī. You will be making many gifts and propitiating many people seeking various things.

## \|\| 1.24.38 \|\|

*svanāmnā tatra saṃsthāpya liṃgaṃ nirvāṇakāraṇam \|*  
*prāsādaṃ tatra kṛtvoccaistadagre kūpamuttamam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. You will instal a Liṅga named after you. It will be the cause of salvation. You will erect a big palace-like mansion there and dig an excellent well there.

## \|\| 1.24.39-40 \|\|

*vidhāya vidhivattatra kalaśāropaṇādikam \|*  
*maṇimāṇikya cāṃpeya dukūlebhāśvagodhanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*mahādhvajapatākāśca cchatracāmaradarpaṇam \|*  
*devopakaraṇaṃ bhūri viśrāṇya śramavarjitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. You will duly perform the rites of establishing the sacred pot (Kalaśa) etc. and will make gifts of jewels, rubies, yellow silk garments, elephants, horses, cows, money, great banners and flags, umbrellas, chowries, mirrors and many other things essential for the Lord. You will then relax.

## \|\| 1.24.41 \|\|

*vratopavāsaniyamaiḥ parikṣīṇakalevaraḥ \|*  
*madhyāhne nirjane tatra drakṣyasyekaṃ tapodhanam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. With the entire body emaciated and fatigued through holy vows, fasts and other restraints and observances, you will see a sage at midday in an isolated place.

## \|\| 1.24.42-43 \|\|

*atīvajīrṇavapuṣaṃ paripiṃgajaṭānvitam \|*  
*mūrtimaṃtaṃmiva prāṃśuṃ dharmaṃ janamanoharam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*bhāraṃ śarīrayaṣṭeśca dṛḍhayaṣṭyāṃ samarpya ca \|*  
*garbhāgārādviniṣkramyābhyāyāṃtaṃraṃgamaṃḍape \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. His body will be extremely feeble. He may be having tawny matted hairs. He will appear as though the personified form of excellent piety. He will be captivating the minds of the people with the burden of his slender body placed on a firm staff. He will be seen coming out of the sanctum sanctorum and proceeding towards the main pavilion.

## \|\| 1.24.44-45 \|\|

*upaviśya samīpe te prakṣyatyevamanukramāt \|*  
*kosi tvaṃ kimihāsi tvaṃ dvitīya iva kastvayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*prāsādaḥ kāritaḥ kena jānāsyeṣa tato vada \|*  
*asya liṃgasya kiṃ nāma prāyo jāne na vārdhakāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. He will sit near you and will ask thus (questions) one after another: “Who are you? Why are you here? (Referring to Anaṅgalekhā) Who is this like a second person unto you? By whom was this palace (mansion) built? If you know, tell me. What is the name of this Liṅga? I almost do not know anything due to old age.”

## \|\| 1.24.46-48 \|\|

*pṛṣṭastvamiti te nātha tadā vṛddha tapasvinā \|*  
*kathayiṣyasyahaṃ rājā vṛddhakāla iti śrutaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*dākṣiṇātya iha prāptastvetayā saha kāṃtayā \|*  
*dhyāyāmi liṃgametacca prārthayāmi na kiṃcana \|\| 47 \|\|*

*prāsādasyāsya jaṭila svayaṃkārayitā śivaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣato'syaliṃgasya nāma no vedmi niścitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. On being asked thus by that old sage, then, you will say: “I am the well-known king Vṛḍdhakāla. I am a Southerner who have come with this my wife. I meditate on this Liṅga. But I do not pray for anything. O sage with matted hairs, Śiva has caused the erection of this palace. I do not certainly know the special name of this Liṅga.”

## \|\| 1.24.49-51 \|\|

*iti śrutvā narapatervākyaṃprāha jaṭādharaḥ \|*  
*satyamuktaṃ tvayaikaṃ hi liṃganāma na vetsi yat \|\| 49 \|\|*

*paśyeyaṃ tvāmahaṃ nityamupaviṣṭaṃ suniścalam \|*  
*śruto bhaviṣyati tava prāsādo yena kāritaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*mamāgre tatsamācakṣva yadi jānāsi tattvataḥ \|*  
*ākarṇyeti vacastasya punaḥ prāha bhavāniti \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. On hearing these words of the king, the old man with matted hairs said (will say): “Indeed one truthful statement has been made by you that you do not know the name of the Liṅga. I see you everyday sitting motionless. Certainly it must have been heard by you by whom the palace was constructed. Speak that to me, if you do know it for certain.”

On hearing these words you said (will say) thus:

## \|\| 1.24.52 \|\|

*kartā kārayitā śaṃbhuḥ kimatathyaṃ bravīmyaham \|*  
*athavā ciṃtayā kiṃ me tapasvinnanayā vibho \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. “It is Śambhu who does things and makes others do. Do I utter a lie? Or, O sage, what do I gain with thinking like this (as to who built etc.)?”

## \|\| 1.24.53 \|\|

*iti tvayi sthite joṣaṃ sa punarvṛddhatāpasaḥ \|*  
*pipāsurasmi pānīyamānīyāśu prayaccha me \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. After uttering this when you kept (will keep) quiet, that aged sage said (will say): “I am thirsty. Fetch some water quickly and give it to me.”

## \|\| 1.24.54-55 \|\|

*iti tena ca nunnastvaṃ vāryānīya ca kūpataḥ \|*  
*pāyayiṣyasi taṃ vṛddhaṃ tāpasaṃ tatkṣaṇācca saḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tadaṃbupānato bhūyātsupārvaṇa śaśiprabhaḥ \|*  
*taruṇo rūpasaṃpannaḥ kośonmuktorago yathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. On being urged by him, you will bring water from the well and make him drink. Instantly, that aged sage becomes one shining with the lustre of the Full Moon, due to the fact that he drank that water. He turned (will turn) into a young man endowed with comely features like a serpent that has cast off its slough.

## \|\| 1.24.56-57 \|\|

*jātāścaryeṇa bhavatā punarevābhyabhāṣi saḥ \|*  
*kaḥ prabhāvo hi bhagavanneṣa yena bhavānpunaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*parityajyātra jarasaṃ na vo bhrājasi sāṃpratam \|*  
*asti cedavakāśaste tato brūhi tapodhana \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. He was (will be) asked then by you who become surprised: “O honoured Sir, what is that power whereby you cast off your old age and shine now (as a youth)? O sage, if you have time, please tell me.”

The sage said (will say):

## \|\| 1.24.58 \|\|

*tapodhana uvāca \|*  
*vṛddhakālakṣitipate jāne tvāṃ sumahāmate \|*  
*imāmapi ca jāne'haṃ tava patnīṃ pativratām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O king Vṛddhakāla, O highly intelligent one, I know you. I know this chaste wife of yours too.

## \|\| 1.24.59 \|\|

*janmano'smādiyaṃ rājannāsīdviprasya kanyakā \|*  
*turvasorvedavapuṣaḥ śubhācārā śubhānanā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O king, being born of this Turvasu who was the embodied form of the Vedas, she was a Brāhmaṇa’s daughter of excellent countenance and splendid conduct.

## \|\| 1.24.60 \|\|

*tena dattā vivāhārthaṃ naidhruvāya mahātmane \|*  
*sa ca kālavaśaṃ prāpto naidhruvo'prāptayauvanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. She was given in marriage by him to the noble-souled Naidhruva. That Naidhruva passed away even before reaching the age of youth.

## \|\| 1.24.61 \|\|

*vaidhavyaṃ pālayaṃtyeṣā mṛtā'vaṃtyāṃ śubhavratā \|*  
*tena puṇyena saṃjātā pāṃḍyasya nṛpateḥ sutā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Suffering widowhood courageously and observing holy vows, she ultimately died at Avantī. Due to that merit, she was born as the daughter of the Pāṇḍya king.

## \|\| 1.24.62 \|\|

*pariṇītā tvayā rājanpativrataratā sadā \|*  
*tvayā saheha saṃprāptā muktiṃ prāpsyatyanuttamām \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. She was married to you, O king. She is always devoted to her husband. She came here along with you. She will attain the excellent salvation.

## \|\| 1.24.63-64 \|\|

*ayodhyāyāmathāvaṃtyāṃ mathurāyāmathāpi vā \|*  
*dvāravatyāṃ ca kāṃcyāṃ vā māyāpuryāmatho nṛpa \|\| 63 \|\|*

*api pātakino ye ca kālena nidhanaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*te hi svargādihāgatya kāśyāṃ mokṣamavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Even if sinners die in due course at Ayodhyā, Avantī, Mathurā, Dvārāvatī, Kāñcī or Māyāpurī, O king, they will come here at Kāśī and attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.24.65 \|\|

*avaimi tvāmapi nṛpadvijo'bhūḥ pūrvajanmani \|*  
*māthuraḥ śivaśarmākhyo māyāpuryāṃ bhavānmṛtaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. I know you too, O king. You were a Brāhmaṇa in your previous birth. A citizen of Mathurā, named Śivaśarman, you died at Māyāpurī.

## \|\| 1.24.66 \|\|

*tatpuṇyātprāpya vaikuṃṭhaṃ bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān \|*  
*tatpuṇyaśeṣātkṣitipo jātastvaṃ naṃdivardhane \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Due to that merit, you attained Vaikuṇṭha and enjoyed all charming pleasures. Due to the residue of that merit, you became a king at Nandivardhana.

## \|\| 1.24.67 \|\|

*vṛddhakālāvanīpāla tenaiva sukṛtena ca \|*  
*mokṣakṣetramidaṃ prāpto muktiṃ prāpsyasyanuttamām \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O King Vṛddhakāla, due to that very merit, you reached this holy spot of salvation. You will attain excellent salvation.

## \|\| 1.24.68 \|\|

*anyacca śṛṇu rājeṃdra tvayā yatsamudīritam \|*  
*kartā kārayitā śaṃbhuḥ prāsādasyeti tatsphuṭam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Listen to another point, O eminent king. Your statement that “It is Śambhu who does things and causes others do” is clear (and relevant).

## \|\| 1.24.69 \|\|

*sukṛtaṃ naiva satatamākhyātavyaṃ kadācana \|*  
*kṛtaṃ mayeti kathanātpuṇyaṃ kṣayati tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. A meritorious act (performed by oneself) should never be frequently boasted of. By saying “It has been done by me”, merit diminishes instantly.

## \|\| 1.24.70 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena gopanīyaṃ nidhānavat \|*  
*sukṛtaṃ kīrtanādvyarthaṃ bhavedbhasmahutaṃ tathā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Hence with all effort, a meritorious act should be concealed and guarded like a treasure. By boasting about it, it becomes futile like the Homa preformed on Bhasma (ash).

## \|\| 1.24.71 \|\|

*niścitaṃ viśvanāthena preritena tvayā'nagha \|*  
*kṛtaṃ hi kṛtakṛtyena prāsādādiha vedmyaham \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Certainly, O sinless one, you have been directed by Viśvanātha and the palace etc. has been built by you. I know it.

## \|\| 1.24.72 \|\|

*vṛddhakāleśvaraṃ nāma liṃgametanmahīpate \|*  
*jānīhyanādisaṃsiddhaṃ nimittaṃ kiṃtu vai bhavān \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Know that this Liṅga, named Vṛddhakāleśvara, O king, already existed since time immemorial. But you were the instrumental cause.

## \|\| 1.24.73 \|\|

*darśanātsparśanāttasya pūjanācchravaṇānnateḥ \|*  
*vṛddhakāleśaliṃgasya sarvaṃ prāpnoti vāṃchitam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. By seeing, touching, worshipping, hearing about and bowing down to the Liṅga Vṛddhakāleśvara one gets whatever is desired.

## \|\| 1.24.74 \|\|

*kūpaḥ kālodako nāma jarāvyādhivighātakṛt \|*  
*yadīya jalapānena mātuḥstanyamapānavān \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. This well named Kālodaka dispels old age and sickness. By drinking its waters one ceases to drink the breast-milk of a mother (i.e. becomes liberated from Saṃsāra).

## \|\| 1.24.75 \|\|

*kṛtakūpodakasnānaḥ kṛtaitalliṃgapūjanaḥ \|*  
*varṣeṇa siddhimāpnoti manobhilaṣitāṃ naraḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A man who takes his bath with the water of this well and who worships this Liṅga acquires fulfilment of whatever is desired by him in one year.

## \|\| 1.24.76 \|\|

*na kuṣṭhaṃ na ca visphoṭā naraṃghā na vicarcikā \|*  
*pītātspṛṣṭātpratiṣṭhaṃti kaphaḥ kālatamodakāt \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. If Kālatamodaka water is drunk or touched, leprosy, swelling, itch, scab and phlegmatic attack are dispelled.

## \|\| 1.24.77 \|\|

*nāgnimāṃdyaṃ naiva śūlaṃ na meho na pravāhikā \|*  
*na mūtrakṛcchraṃ nā pāmā pānāyasyāsya sevanāt \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. By resorting to it and drinking it many diseases are cured, such as indigestion, colic pain, diabetes, diarrhoea, difficulty in urinating, itches etc.

## \|\| 1.24.78 \|\|

*bhūtajvarāśca ye kecidye kecidviṣamajvarāḥ \|*  
*te kṣipramupaśāmyaṃti hyetatkūpodasevanāt \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Fever due to the attack of evil spirits, recurring fever etc. quickly get subdued by resorting to the water of this well.

## \|\| 1.24.79 \|\|

*tavāgrato mama jarā palitaṃ ca yathāvidhi \|*  
*etatkūpodapānena kṣaṇānnaṣṭaṃ navo'bhavam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Before you, my old age and grey hairs became dispelled in a moment by drinking the water of this well duly. I have become a new man.

## \|\| 1.24.80 \|\|

*vṛddhakāleśvare liṃge sevitena daridratā \|*  
*nopasargā na vā rogā na pāpaṃ nāghajaṃ phalam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. If Vṛddhakāleśvara Liṅga is served, one does not incur poverty; neither calamities nor ailments, no sin and no evil consequences of the sins occur.

## \|\| 1.24.81 \|\|

*uttare kṛttivāsasya vārāṇasyāṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*vṛddhakāleśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ siddhikāmukaiḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. At Vārāṇasī, the Liṅga Vṛddhakāleśvara to the north of Kṛttivāsa should be visited carefully by those who desire emancipation and fulfilment.

## \|\| 1.24.82 \|\|

*ityuktvā taṃ mahīpālaṃ haste dhṛtvā tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*sānaṃgalekhā rājñīkaṃ tasmiṃlliṃge layaṃ yayau \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. After saying this, the sage took that king by the hand along with the queen Anaṅgalekhā and became merged into the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.24.83 \|\|

*mahākāla mahākāla mahākāleti kīrtanāt \|*  
*śatadhā mucyate pāpairnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. By repeating ‘Mahākāla’, ‘Mahākāla’ a hundred times, one gets released from sins. No doubt need be entertained in this connection.

## \|\| 1.24.84 \|\|

*itthaṃ bhavitrī te muktiḥ kaiṭabhārātidarśanāt \|*  
*bhogānbhuktvā bahuvidhānvaikuṃṭha nagare śubhe \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. After enjoying many kinds of pleasures in the splendid city of Vaikuṇṭha, your ultimate liberation shall take place thus by seeing the enemy of Kaiṭabha (i.e. Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 1.24.85 \|\|

*iti saṃhṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ sa vipro bhagavattadgaṇavaktrato niśamya \|*  
*svamudarkamathārkakoṭiramyaṃ harilokaṃ parilokayāṃcakāra \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Thus after hearing his own future from those attendants of the Lord, the Brāhmaṇa experienced horripilation due to exhilaration and saw Hariloka, beautiful and resplendent with ten million Suns.

## \|\| 1.24.86-88 \|\|

*maitrāvaruṇiruvāca \|*  
*lopāmudre sa vipreṃdro bhogānbhuktvā manoramān \|*  
*māyāpuryāṃ kṛtaprāṇatyāga puṇyabalena ca \|\| 86 \|\|*

*vaikuṃṭhalokādāgatya pattane naṃdivardhane \|*  
*bhaumāni bhuktvā saukhyāni putrānutpādya suṃdarān \|\| 87 \|\|*

*teṣu rājyaṃ vinikṣipya prāpya vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*viśveśvaraṃ samārādhya nirvāṇapadamīyivān \|\| 88 \|\|*

Maitrāvaruṇi (Agastya) said:

86-88. O dear Lopāmudrā, that eminent Brāhmaṇa enjoyed charming pleasures. Casting off his life at Māyāpurī, and due to the power of that merit, he returned from Vaikuṇṭha and was born in the city of Nandivardhana. He enjoyed all worldly pleasures, begot handsome sons and entrusted the kingdom to them. He reached the city of Vārāṇasī and propitiated Viśveśvara. He then attained salvation.

## \|\| 1.24.89 \|\|

*etatpuṇyatamākhyānaṃ viprasya śivaśarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*śrutvā pāpavinirmukto jñānaṃ paramamṛcchati \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. By listening to this meritorious narrative of the Brāhmaṇa Śivaśarman one gets rid of one’s sins and attains the highest wisdom.

## Chapter 25 - Agastya visits Skanda

## \|\| 1.25.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu sūta pravakṣyāmi kathāṃ kalaśajanmanaḥ \|*  
*yāmākarṇya naro bhūyādvirajā jñānabhājanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1\. Listen, O Sūta, I shall recount the story of the Pitcher-born Sage (Agastya), on hearing which a man becomes free from Rajoguṇa and possessor of knowledge.

## \|\| 1.25.2 \|\|

*giriṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya śrīsaṃjñaṃ kalaśodbhavaḥ \|*  
*sapatnīko dadarśātha ramyaṃ skaṃdavanaṃ mahat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After circumambulating the Śrīgiri mountain, Agastya, accompanied by his wife, saw the great beautiful forest of Skanda.

## \|\| 1.25.3 \|\|

*sarvartaṃ kusumāḍhyaṃ ca rasavatphalapādapam \|*  
*susevya kaṃdamūlāḍhyaṃ suvalkalamahīruham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It was rich in the flowers of all the seasons. The trees were laden with juicy fruits. It abounded in roots (Mūla), bulbous roots (Kanda) that could be easily had. The trees had excellent barks.

## \|\| 1.25.4 \|\|

*nivītaśvāpadagaṇaṃ sasaritpalvalāvṛtam \|*  
*svaccha gaṃbhīrakāsāraṃ sāraṃ sarvabhuvaḥ param \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The hosts of beasts of prey there were tamed. There were many rivers and puddles all round. There was a deep lake of clear water. It appeared to be the great essence of the entire earth.

## \|\| 1.25.5 \|\|

*nānāpatatrisaṃghuṣṭaṃ nānāmunijanoṣitam \|*  
*tapaḥsaṃketanilayamivaikaṃ saṃpadāṃ padam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It was teeming with different kinds of birds. Many sages stayed there. It appeared to be the secret meeting place of all types of austerities. It was the chief place of riches.

## \|\| 1.25.6 \|\|

*lohito nāma tatrāsti giriḥ svarṇagiriprabhaḥ \|*  
*sukaṃdaraprasravaṇaḥ svasānu śikharaprabhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. There is a mountain named Lohita there. It has the lustre of Meru with excellent caverns and rivulets; it shone well shedding lustre from its peaks and ridges.

## \|\| 1.25.7 \|\|

*kailāsasyaikaśakalaṃ karmabhūmāvihāgatam \|*  
*tapastaptumiva proccairnānāścaryasamanvitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It was as though a bit of Kailāsa had come to the land of holy rites (Bhārata) for performing lofty penance. It was full of mysteries and miracles.

## \|\| 1.25.8-9 \|\|

*tatrādrākṣīnmuniśreṣṭho'gastyaḥ sākṣātṣaḍānanam \|*  
*praṇamya daṃḍavadbhūmau sapatnīko mahātapāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tuṣṭāva girijāsūnuṃ sūktaiḥ śrutisamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*tathā svakṛtayā stutyā prabaddha karasaṃpuṭaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. There the excellent sage Agastya saw the Six-faced God directly. Accompanied by his wife, the sage of great penance prostrated before him like a log of wood. Joining the palms together in reverence, he eulogized the Son of the Daughter of the Mountain with the Sūktas of the Vedas and prayers composed by himself.

## \|\| 1.25.10 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*namostu vṛṃdārakavṛṃdavaṃdya pādāraviṃdāya sudhākarāya \|*  
*ṣaḍānanāyāmitavikramāya gaurīhṛdānaṃdasamudbhavāya \|\| 10 \|\|*

Agastya said:

\[Agastya’s Prayer\]

10\. Obeisance to the Six-faced Lord whose lotus-like feet are worthy of being revered by groups of Devas. You are the sea of nectar (Supreme Bliss), whose exploits are endless and who are the cause of mental delight to Gaurī.

## \|\| 1.25.11 \|\|

*namostu tubhyaṃ praṇatārtihaṃtre kartre samastasya manorathānām \|*  
*dātre rathānāṃ paratārakasya haṃtre pracaṃḍāsura tārakasya \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Salutations to you, the destroyer of the distresses of those who bow down (to you), the bestower of the cherished desires of all, the destoyer of the designs of cheaters of others, the slayer of the fierce Asura (called) Tāraka.

## \|\| 1.25.12 \|\|

*amūrtamūrtāya sahasramūrtaye guṇāya guṇyāya parātparāya \|*  
*apārapārāya parāparāya namostu tubhyaṃ śikhivāhanāya \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Obeisance to you, the peacock-vehicled one, to you who are both unembodied and embodied, thousand-formed, attributeless, greater than the greatest; you who are endowed with good qualities and are virtue (incarnate), one whose expanse cannot be comprehended and the supreme one.

## \|\| 1.25.13 \|\|

*namostu te brahmavidāṃvarāya digaṃbarāyāṃbara saṃsthitāya \|*  
*hiraṇyavarṇāya hiraṇyabāhave namo hiraṇyāya hiraṇyaretase \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Obeisance to you, the most excellent one among those who have realized Brahman, the supreme Being, one with the directions for the garments (Digambara), one who is stationed in the firmament, one with golden complexion, one with golden arms (or firmament-bodied one). Obeisance to the golden one (Sāttvika, in form) and one with gold as semen virile (i.e., Rudra).

## \|\| 1.25.14 \|\|

*tapaḥsvarūpāya tapodhanāya tapaḥphalānāṃ pratipādakāya \|*  
*sadā kumārāya himāramāriṇe taṇīkṛtaiśvarya virāgiṇe namaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Obeisance to the Lord who is austerity incarnate, one who has austerity as asset, to the Lord bestowing the fruits of penance, one who is perpetually child-like in form, to the Lord who has conquered Māra (god of Love), one who has considered all prosperity and riches as (worthless as) grass. Obeisance to the detached one.

## \|\| 1.25.15 \|\|

*namostu tubhyaṃ śarajanmane vibho prabhātasūryāruṇadaṃtapaṃktaye \|*  
*bālāya cābālaparākramāya ṣāṇmāturāyālamanāturāya \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Hail to you, the reed-born Lord, to the Lord with a row of teeth having the colour (brightness) of the morning Sun, to you, a child of great heroism uncommon to children, to the Lord nurtured by six mothers, to the Lord completely unafflicted and unperturbed.

## \|\| 1.25.16 \|\|

*mīḍhuṣṭamāyottaramīḍhuṣe namo namo gaṇānāṃ pataye gaṇāya \|*  
*namostu te janmajarātigāya namo viśākhāya suśaktipāṇaye \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Obeisance to Mīḍhuṣṭama (‘the most excellent one among those who bestow desired fruits’), to Uttaramīḍhus (‘bountiful bestower of future benefits’); obeisance to the Lord of the Gaṇas. Obeisance to the Lord who himself is a Gaṇa (of Rudra); obeisance to you who have transcended birth and old age; obeisance to Viśākha with an excellent Śakti in the hand.

## \|\| 1.25.17 \|\|

*sarvasya nāthasya kumārakāya krauṃcāraye tārakamārakāya \|*  
*svāheya gāṃgeya ca kārtikeya śaiveya tubhyaṃ satataṃ namo'stu \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Permanent obeisance to you, to the son of the Lord of everything, to the enemy of Krauñca mountain, to the slayer of Tāraka. Obeisance to you, O son of Svāhā, Gaṅgā, Kṛttikās and Śiva.

## \|\| 1.25.18 \|\|

*itthaṃ pariṣṭutya sa kārtikeyaṃ namo namastvityabhibhāṣamāṇaḥ \|*  
*dvistriḥparikramya puro viveśa sthito munīśopaviśeti coktaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After eulogizing Kārttikeya thus saying “Obeisance, obeisance to you”, he circumambulated him twice and thrice (i.e. five times) and stood in front of him. Then he was told, “O eminent sage, be seated.”

## \|\| 1.25.19 \|\|

*kārtikeya uvāca \|*  
*kṣemosti kuṃbhaja mune tridaśaikasahāyakṛt \|*  
*jāne tvāmiha saṃprāptaṃ tathā viṃdhyācalonnatim \|\| 19 \|\|*

Kārttikeya said:

19\. O Pitcher-born Sage, the support and assistance to gods, I know that you have come here and also about the increase in the size of the Vindhya mountain.

## \|\| 1.25.20 \|\|

*avimukte mahākṣetre kṣemaṃ tryakṣeṇa rakṣite \|*  
*yatra kṣīṇāyuṣāṃ sākṣādvirūpākṣo'sti mokṣadaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Everything is well in the great holy spot Avimukta protected by the Three-eyed Lord. Virūpākṣa is there bestowing salvation directly to those who die there.

## \|\| 1.25.21 \|\|

*bhūrbhuvaḥ svastale vāpi na pātālatale malam \|*  
*nordhvaloke mayā dṛṣṭaṃ tādṛkkṣetraṃ kvacinmune \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O sage, such a sanctifying holy spot has nowhere been seen by me on the earth, Bhuvarloka, Svarloka, Pātāla region or in the higher worlds.

## \|\| 1.25.22 \|\|

*ahamekacaropyatra tatkṣetraprāptaye mune \|*  
*tapye tapāṃsinādyāpi phaleyurme manorathāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Though I move about alone, O Sage, I perform penace \[penance?\] here to attain that holy spot. Till today, my ambitions have not become fruitful.

## \|\| 1.25.23 \|\|

*na tatpuṇyairna taddānairna tapobhirna tajjapaiḥ \|*  
*na labhyaṃ vividhairyajñairlabhyamaiśādanugrahāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It cannot be attained by merits alone, by making gifts, by performing penance or by means of Japas. It cannot be attained through different kinds of Yajñas. It can be obtained only through the blessings of Īśa.

## \|\| 1.25.24 \|\|

*īśvarānugrahādeva kāśīvāsaḥ sudurlabhaḥ \|*  
*sulabhaḥ syānmune nūnaṃ na vai sukṛtakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Residence in inaccessible Kāśī can become easily achievable, Ö Sage, only through the blessings of Īśvara, certainly not by millions of merits.

## \|\| 1.25.25 \|\|

*anyaiva kācitsā sṛṣṭirvidhāturyā'tirekiṇī \|*  
*na tatkṣetraguṇānvaktumīśvaro'pīśvaro yataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It is a separate creation excelling that of the creator (Brahmā), because even Īśvara is not capable of enumerating the merits of that holy place.

## \|\| 1.25.26 \|\|

*aho mateḥ sudaurbalyamahobhāgyasya daurvidham \|*  
*aho mohasya māhātmyaṃ yatkāśīha na sevyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is the height of the weakness of intellect, Alas! it is the outrageous adverseness of fortune, Alas! it is the grand power of delusion, if Kāśī is not resorted to.

## \|\| 1.25.27 \|\|

*śarīraṃ jīryate nityaṃ saṃjīryaṃtīṃdriyāṇyapi \|*  
*āyurmṛgo mṛgayunā kṛtalakṣyo hi mṛtyunā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The body grows old and emaciated incessantly, the sense-organs continuously become weak. Alas! the god of Death has made life, his target like a deer by a hunter.

## \|\| 1.25.28 \|\|

*sāpadaṃ saṃpadaṃ jñātvā sāpāyaṃ kāyamuccakaiḥ \|*  
*capalā capalaṃ cāyurmatvā kāśīṃ samāśrayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One should resort to Kāśī after realizing that riches are fraught with dangers, that the body is excessively subject to adversity and that life is as fickle as lightning.

## \|\| 1.25.29 \|\|

*yāvannaityāyuṣaścāṃtastāvatkāśī na mucyate \|*  
*kālaḥ kalālavasyāpi saṃkhyātuṃ naiva vismaret \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. As long as the end of the life does not approach, Kāśī is not abandoned. Kāla (Time, god of Death) shall not forget to count even the least bit of a second.

## \|\| 1.25.30 \|\|

*jarānikaṭanikṣiptā bādhaṃte vyādhayo bhṛśam \|*  
*tathāpi deho nāneho nāho kāśīṃ samīhate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Ailments thrown in very near to old age do harass very much. Still the body vexed with different kinds of ambitions and aspirations does not yearn for Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.25.31 \|\|

*tīrthasnānena japyena paropakaraṇoktibhiḥ \|*  
*vinārthaṃ labhyate dharmo dharmādarthaḥ svayaṃ bhavet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Without (spending) money, Dharma (piety) can be achieved through ablutions in holy places, performance of Japas, helping others and utterances (of good words, prayers etc.). From Dharma wealth issues spontaneously.

## \|\| 1.25.32 \|\|

*vinaivārthārjanopāyaṃ dharmādartho bhaveddhruvam \|*  
*ato'rthaciṃtāmutsṛjya dharmamekaṃ samāśrayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Even without a specific means of earning money, wealth certainly comes out of Dharma. Hence, giving up the worry for wealth, one should resort to Dharma alone.

## \|\| 1.25.33 \|\|

*dharmādartho'rthataḥ kāmaḥ kāmātsarvasukhodayaḥ \|*  
*svargopi sulabho dharmātkāśye kā durlabhā param \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Wealth is obtained through Dharma; from wealth Kāma can be obtained; all happiness comes from Kāma. Even heavenly pleasure is easily obtained through Dharma; but Kāśī alone is very difficult to attain.

## \|\| 1.25.34 \|\|

*upāyatrayamevātra sthāṇurnirvāṇakāraṇam \|*  
*śarvāṇyagreva bhāṇāddhā parinirṇīya sarvataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. After clearly scrutinizing everything, Sthāṇu spoke to Śarvāṇī only about three means of salvation.

## \|\| 1.25.35 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ pāśupato yogastatastīrthaṃ sitāsitam \|*  
*tatopyekamanāyāsamavimuktaṃ vimuktidam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. First comes Pāśupatayoga (consisting of use of Bhasma etc.), then Sitāsita (i.e., Prayāga), then the effortless means of salvation namely Avimukta (i.e., Kāśī).

## \|\| 1.25.36-41 \|\|

*śrīśaila himaśailādyā nānānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*tridaṃḍadhāraṇaṃcāpi saṃnyāsaḥ sarvakarmaṇām \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tapāṃsi nānārūpāṇi vratāni niyamā yamāḥ \|*  
*siṃdhūnāmapi saṃbhedā araṇyāni bahūnyapi \|\| 37 \|\|*

*mānasānyapi bhaumāni dhārātīrthādikāni ca \|*  
*ūṣarāścāpi pīṭhāni hyacchinnāmnāyapāṭhanam \|\| 38 \|\|*
