76\. The Pitṛs (manes) of different forms always sing these songs: “Would that someone in our family takes the holy bath in Gaṅgā.”

## \|\| 1.27.77 \|\|

*devarṣīnparisaṃtarpya dīnānāthāṃśca duḥkhitān \|*  
*śraddhayā vidhinā snātvā dāsyate salilāṃjalim \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. After propitiating Devas and Sages as well as indigent ones, helpless ones and miserable ones, he would take his holy dip faithfully in accordance with the injunctions and offer handfuls of water libation.

## \|\| 1.27.78 \|\|

*api naḥ sa kule bhūyācchive viṣṇau ca sāmyadṛk \|*  
*tadālayakaro bhaktyā tasya saṃmārjanādikṛt \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. “Would that he is born in our family, who will impartially look at Śiva and Viṣṇu, who will build temples for both of them and will devoutly clean them and carry out other activities as well.”

## \|\| 1.27.79 \|\|

*akāmo vā sakāmo vā tiryagyonigatopi vā \|*  
*gaṃgāyāṃ yo mṛto martyo narakaṃ sa na paśyati \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. He who dies in Gaṅgā will not see hell whether he cherishes desire or not, even if it is the lower strata of living beings that he belongs to.

## \|\| 1.27.80 \|\|

*tīrthamanyatpraśaṃsaṃti gaṃgātīre sthitāśca ye \|*  
*gaṃgāṃ na bahu manyaṃte te syurnirayagāminaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. If those who are staying on the banks of Gaṅgā were to praise another Tīrtha and do not honour Gaṅgā, they are sure to pass on to a hell.

## \|\| 1.27.81 \|\|

*māṃ ca tvāṃ caiva yo dveṣṭi gaṃgāṃ ca puruṣādhamaḥ \|*  
*svakīyaiḥ puruṣaiḥ sārdhaṃ sa ghoraṃ narakaṃ vrajet \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. A base man who hates me as well as you and Gaṅgā shall go to hell along with members of his family.

## \|\| 1.27.82 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭirgaṇasahasrāṇi gaṃgāṃ rakṣaṃti sarvadā \|*  
*abhaktānāṃ ca pāpānāṃ vāse vighnaṃ prakurvate \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Sixty;four thousands of Gaṇas always protect Gaṅgā and they create obstacles in the stay of sinners who are no devotees.

## \|\| 1.27.83 \|\|

*kāmakrodhamahāmohalobhādi niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*ghnaṃti teṣāṃ manastatra sthitiṃ cāpanayaṃti ca \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. With the sharp arrows of Just, anger, excessive delusion, convetousness etc., they overwhelm their minds and oust them from there (Gaṅgā).

## \|\| 1.27.84 \|\|

*gaṃgāṃ samāśrayedyastu sa muniḥ sa ca paṃḍitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ puruṣārthacatuṣṭaye \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. He who resorts to Gaṅgā is a sage. He is a learned man. He should be known as one blessed with achievement in regard to the four aims of life.

## \|\| 1.27.85 \|\|

*gaṃgāyāṃ ca sakṛtsnāto hayamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*tarpayaṃśca pitṝṃstatra tārayennarakārṇavāt \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. One who, just for once, takes his holy dip in Gaṅgā, shall obtain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice. By offering libations of water to the Pitṛs there, he shall redeem them from the ocean of hell.

## \|\| 1.27.86 \|\|

*nairaṃtaryeṇa gaṃgāyāṃ māsaṃ yaḥ snāti puṇyavān \|*  
*śakraloke sa vasati yāvacchakraḥ sapūrvajaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. A meritorious man who continuously bathes in Gaṅgā for one month, lives in the world of Indra along with his ancestors, as long as Indra (continues to live).

## \|\| 1.27.87 \|\|

*abdaṃ yaḥ snāti gaṃgāyāṃ nairaṃtaryeṇa puṇyabhāk \|*  
*viṣṇorlokaṃ samāsādya sa sukhaṃ saṃvasennaraḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. A meritorious man who continuously bathes in Gaṅgā for one year, shall reach the world of Viṣṇu and stay there happily.

## \|\| 1.27.88 \|\|

*gaṃgāyāṃ snāti yo martyo yāvajjīvaṃ dinedine \|*  
*jīvanmuktaḥ sa vijñeyo dehāṃte mukta eva saḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. A man who takes his holy bath in Gaṅgā everyday throughout his life, should be known as Jīvanmukta (a living-liberated soul), who with the destruction of the body (after death) becomes completely liberated.

## \|\| 1.27.89 \|\|

*tithinakṣatraparvādi nāpekṣyaṃ jāhnavī jale \|*  
*snānamātreṇa gaṃgāyāṃ saṃcitāghaṃ vinaśyati \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Any particular lunar day, asterism or day of special significance need not be taken into consideration in regard to (the holy bath) in the waters of Gaṅgā. Merely through holy dip in Gaṅgā all the hoarded sins perish.

## \|\| 1.27.90 \|\|

*paṃḍitopi sa mūrkhaḥ syācchaktiyuktopyaśaktikaḥ \|*  
*yastu bhāgīrathītīraṃ sukhasevyaṃ na saṃśrayet \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. He who does not resort to the banks of Gaṅgā worthy of being resorted to very easily, is a fool though learned, is powerless though endowed with Śakti (power).

## \|\| 1.27.91 \|\|

*kiṃvāyupāpyarogeṇa vikāsinyātha kiṃ śriyā \|*  
*kiṃ vā buddhyā vimalayā yadi gaṃgāṃ na sevate \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. If one does not resort to Gaṅgā, of what use is his longevity free from sickness, of what avail is his ever growing prosperity, of what avail is his blemishless intellect?

## \|\| 1.27.92 \|\|

*yaḥ kārayedāyatanaṃ gaṃgāpratikṛternaraḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā sa bhogānpretyāpi yāti gaṃgā salokatām \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A man who gets a temple built for an idol of Gaṅgā, enjoys all pleasures. After death he attains the world of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.27.93 \|\|

*śṛṇvaṃti mahimānaṃ ye gaṃgāyā nityamādarāt \|*  
*gaṃgāsnānaphalaṃ teṣāṃ vācakaprīṇanāddhanaiḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Those who listen everyday to the greatness of Gaṅgā with respect shall obtain the benefit of a holy dip in Gaṅgā by propitiating with adequate monetary gifts the scholar who reads the text.

## \|\| 1.27.94 \|\|

*pitṝnuddiśya yo liṃgaṃ snapayedgāṃga vāriṇā \|*  
*tṛptāḥ syustasya pitaro mahānirayagā api \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. With Pitṛs in view, if anyone bathes the Liṅga with the waters of Gaṅgā, his ancestors become pleased although they may be in a great hell.

## \|\| 1.27.95 \|\|

*aṣṭakṛtvo maṃtrajaptairvastrapūtaiḥ sugaṃdhibhiḥ \|*  
*procurgāṃgajalaiḥ snānaṃ ghṛtasnānādhikaṃ budhāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Learned men say that far superior to bathing with ghee is bathing with the waters of Gaṅgā, filtered with a cloth, charged eight times with Mantras (pertaining to Śiva or Gaṅgā—Comm.) and rendered fragrant with scents.

## \|\| 1.27.96-97 \|\|

*aṣṭadravyavimiśreṇa gaṃgātoyena yaḥ sakṛt \|*  
*māgadhaprasthamātreṇa tāmrapātrasthitena ca \|\| 96 \|\|*

*bhānave'rghaṃ pradadyācca svakīya pitṛbhiḥ saha \|*  
*sotitejo vimānena sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 97 \|\|*

96-97. If anyone offers Argha at least once to the Sun with the waters of Gaṅgā mixed with the eight Dravyas measured to a Magadhaprastha (i.e., 12½ Palas) in a copper vessel, he goes to the Solar world in a highly brilliant aerial chariot along with his ancestors and is honoured there.

## \|\| 1.27.98-99 \|\|

*āpaḥ kṣīraṃ kuśāgrāṇi ghṛtaṃ madhugavāṃdadhi \|*  
*raktāni karavīrāṇi raktacaṃdanamityapi \|\| 98 \|\|*

*aṣṭāṃgārgho yamuddiṣṭastvatīva ravitoṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*gāṃgairvārbhiḥ koṭiguṇo jñeyo viṣṇo'nyavāritaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. The eight Dravyas (ingredients) are: water, Kuśa grass, honey, cow’s milk, cow’s ghee, cow’s curd, red sandal-paste and red Karavīra flowers. This Argha with eight ingredients is considered extremely propitiatory to the Sun-god. O Viṣṇu, this Argha with the waters of Gaṅgā should be known to be ten million times more meritorious than Argha with other waters.

## \|\| 1.27.100 \|\|

*gaṃgātīre svaśaktyā yaḥ kuryāddevālayaṃ sudhīḥ \|*  
*anyatīrthapratiṣṭhāto bhavetkoṭiguṇaṃ phalaṃ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. If a sensible man erects a temple on the banks of Gaṅgā according to his capacity, it has a benefit ten million times more than that of the installation at another Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.27.101-103 \|\|

*aśvatthavaṭacūtādi vṛkṣāropeṇa yatphalam \|*  
*kūpavāpītaḍāgādi prapā satrādibhistathā \|\| 101 \|\|*

*anyatra yadbhavetpuṇyaṃ tadgaṃgādarśanādbhavet \|*  
*puṣpavāṭyādibhiścāpi gaṃgāsparśaṃ tato'dhikam \|\| 102 \|\|*

*kanyādānena yatpuṇyaṃ yatpuṇyaṃ go'nnadānataḥ \|*  
*tatpuṇyaṃ syācchataguṇaṃ gaṃgāgaṃḍūṣapānataḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

101-103. Merely by visiting Gaṅgā, one gets that merit which one gets elsewhere by planting Aśvattha, Vaṭa, mango and other trees or by digging wells, tanks and lakes or through watersheds and sacrifices. The very touch of Gaṅgā is superior to the act of making flower gardens etc. By drinking a mouthful of the waters of Gaṅgā, one gets the benefit hundred times more than that of the gift of a virgin in marriage, that of the gift of cows and cooked rice.

## \|\| 1.27.104 \|\|

*cāṃdrāyaṇasahasreṇa yatpuṇyaṃ syājjanārdana \|*  
*tato'dhikaphalaṃ gaṃgā'mṛtapānādavāpnuyāt \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. By drinking the nectar-like waters of Gaṅgā, O Janārdana, one gets more benefit than the benefit derived from a thousand Cāndrāyaṇa observances.

## \|\| 1.27.105 \|\|

*bhaktyā gaṃgāvagāhasya kimanyatphalamucyate \|*  
*akṣayaḥ svargavāsopi nirvāṇamathavā hare \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. What other benefit shall be said as resulting from devout plunge in Gaṅgā, O Hari, than everlasting residence in heaven or ultimate salvation?

## \|\| 1.27.106 \|\|

*gaṃgāyāḥ pādukāyugmaṃ nityamarcati yo naraḥ \|*  
*āyuḥ puṇyaṃ dhanaṃ putrānsvargamokṣau ca viṃdati \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. A man who always worships the pair of sandals of Gaṅgā obtains longevity, merit, wealth, sons, heaven, and salvation.

## \|\| 1.27.107 \|\|

*nāsti gaṃgāsamaṃ tīrthaṃ kalikalmaṣanāśanam \|*  
*nāsti muktipradaṃ kṣetramavimuktasamaṃ hare \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. O Hari, for the destruction of the sins and blemishes of Kali, there is no other Tīrtha on a par with Gaṅgā. There is no holy spot on a par with Avimukta in bestowing salvation.

## \|\| 1.27.108 \|\|

*gaṃgāsnānarataṃ martyaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva yamakikarāḥ \|*  
*diśo daśa palāyaṃte siṃhaṃ dṛṣṭvā yathā mṛgāḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. On seeing a man regularly engaged in the holy bath in Gaṅgā, the servants of Yama flee in ten directions like deer on seeing a lion.

## \|\| 1.27.109 \|\|

*gaṃgābhajanaśīlasya gaṃgātaṭanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*arcāṃ kṛtvā yathānyāyamaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. One shall obtain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice by duly worshipping a person staying on the banks of Gaṅgā and regularly worshipping Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.27.110 \|\|

*gobhūhiraṇyadānena bhaktyā gaṃgātaṭe śubhe \|*  
*naro na jāyate bhūyaḥ saṃsāre duḥkhakaṃṭake \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. By devoutly gifting cows, plots of land and gold on the splendid banks of Gaṅgā, a man has no rebirth in the miserable world.

## \|\| 1.27.111 \|\|

*dīrghāyuṣyaṃ ca vāsobhirjñānaṃ pustakadānataḥ \|*  
*annadānena saṃpattiṃ kīrtiṃ kanyāpradānataḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. (On the bank of Gaṅgā) by making gifts of garments, one attains longevity; by gifting books one gets knowledge; by gifting cooked rice one gets wealth; and by gifting a virgin one gets fame.

## \|\| 1.27.112 \|\|

*anyatra yatkṛtaṃ karma vrataṃ dānaṃ japastapaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgātaṭe tu tatsarvaṃ hare koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Whatever rite is performed on the banks of Gaṅgā, such as holy vows, Dāna, Japa or penance, O Hari, has ten million times more benefit than the ones performed elsewhere.

## \|\| 1.27.113-118 \|\|

*dhenuṃ savatsā yo dadyād gaṃgātīre vidhānataḥ \|*  
*goromasaṃkhyayā viṣṇo yugānsarvasamṛddhimān \|\| 113 \|\|*

*goloke mama loke vā kāmadhenupradānataḥ \|*  
*bhuṃjānaḥ sarvakāmāṃstu divyānnānāvidhānbahūn \|\| 114 \|\|*

*devānāmapyalabhyāṃśca bhuktvā tu saha bāṃdhavaiḥ \|*  
*pitṛbhiśca suhṛdbhiśca sarvaratnavibhūṣitaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*jāyate satkule paścāddhanadhānyasamākule \|*  
*ratnakāṃcanasaṃpanne śīlavidyāsamanvite \|\| 116 \|\|*

*bhuktvā sa vipulānbhogānputrapautrasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*punargaṃgāṃ samāsādya kāśyāmuttaravāhinīm \|\| 117 \|\|*

*viśveśvaraṃ samārādhya prāgjanurvāsanāvaśāt \|*  
*kālāddehāṃtamāsādya brahma saṃpadyate tataḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

113-118. One who makes the gifts of a cow along with her calf in accordance with the injunctions on the banks of Gaṅgā, O Viṣṇu, shall have all types of prosperity. By gifting away a Kāmadhenu he will enjoy all desires and pleasures, either in Goloka or in my world for as many Yugas as there are hairs on the body of the cow. Along with his kinsmen, he will enjoy divine pleasure of may kinds, (some of them) not available to even Devas. He will enjoy them along with his ancestors and friends. He will be embellished with all kinds of jewels. Thereafter, he is born in an excellent family possessing good conduct and learning. After enjoying infinite pleasures in the company of sons and grandsons he will come again to Gaṅgā flowing towards the north at Kāśī. After propitiating Viśveśvara, due to the impressions and experiences of the previous births, in due course he may die after which he attains Brahman (i.e., salvation).

## \|\| 1.27.119 \|\|

*vivartanadvayamapi bhūmerbhāgīrathītaṭe \|*  
*naro dadāti yo bhaktyā tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Listen to the meritorious benefit of the man who devoutly gives away a plot of land on the banks of Gaṅgā extending to two Nivartanas (1 Nivartana = 30 Daṇḍas).

## \|\| 1.27.120-122 \|\|

*tadbhūmitrasareṇūnāṃ saṃkhyayā yugamānayā \|*  
*maheṃdra caṃdralokeṣu bhuktvā bhogānmanaḥpriyān \|\| 120 \|\|*

*saptadvīpapatirbhūtvā mahādharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*narakasthānpitṝnsarvānprāpayettridivaṃ hare \|\| 121 \|\|*

*svargasthāṃśca pitṝnsarvānmocayitvā mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*aṃte jñānāsinā chittvā hyavidyāṃ pāṃcabhautikīm \|\| 122 \|\|*

120-122. After enjoying all delightful pleasures in the worlds of Mahendra and Candra for as many Yugas as there are Traṣareṇus (particles of dust) in that plot of land, he becomes lord of the seven continents. O Hari, he will be very righteous and he will be able to redeem his Pitṛs from hells and take them to heaven. He will liberate the Pitṛs staying in heaven. He will be highly resplendent. In the end he will chop off Avidyā by means of the sword of knowledge—the Avidyā that has converted itself into the five elements.

## \|\| 1.27.123 \|\|

*paravaiṃrāgyamāpanno yuṃjāno yogamuttamam \|*  
*prāpyāthavā vimuktaṃ ca paraṃ brahmādhigacchati \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. He may have the greatest Vairāgya (non-attachment) and will practise the excellent Yoga. Or after reaching Avimukta, he will realize the great Absolute Brahman.

## \|\| 1.27.124-127 \|\|

*suvarṇamātramapi yaḥ suvarṇaṃ saṃprayacchati \|*  
*suvarṇāya suvarṇaṃ ca hare bhāgīrathītaṭe \|\| 124 \|\|*

*sa hemaratnakhacite vimāne sarvage śubhe \|*  
*sarvaiśvaryasamāyuktaḥ sarvalokeṣu pūjitaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

*brahmāṃḍāṃtarasaṃstheṣu bhuṃjanbhogānmanoramān \|*  
*sarvaiḥ saṃpūjito viṣṇo yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 126 \|\|*

*ekarāṭca tato bhūtvā jaṃbūdvīpe pratāpavān \|*  
*tato'vimuktamāsādya padaṃ nirvāṇamṛcchati \|\| 127 \|\|*

124-127. One who, on the banks of Gaṅgā, makes a gift of excellent gold weighing a Suvarṇa (i.e., 80 Rattis) to a man of excellent Varṇa, O Hari, will be endowed with all Aiśvaryas (supernatural powers) and he will move about in a gold and gem-set aerial chariot that can go everywhere. He will be honoured in all the worlds stationed in other Cosmic Eggs and experience all pleasures delighting the mind. O Viṣṇu, he will be adored by all until all the living beings are annihilated. Thereafter, he shall be the sole king in Jaṃbūdvīpa and very powerful and valorous. Then he will come to Avimukta and attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.27.128 \|\|

*janmarkṣe tu kṛte snāne gaṃgāyāṃ bhaktipūrvakam \|*  
*janmaprabhṛtipāpaughātsaṃcitānmucyate kṣaṇāt \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. If anyone takes his holy bath devoutly in Gaṅgā on the day on which the star of his nativity falls, he shall instantly be released from the multitude of sins accumulated in the course of various births.

## \|\| 1.27.129 \|\|

*vaiśākhe kārtike māghe gaṃgāsnānaṃ sudurlabham \|*  
*darśe śataguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ saṃkrātau ca sahasrakam \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. A holy bath in Gaṅgā is very rare (i.e., is of special value) in the months of Vaiśākha, Kārttika and Māgha. The bath is hundred times more beneficial if performed on the new-moon day and a thousand times, on the Saṅkrānti day (transit of the Sun).

## \|\| 1.27.130 \|\|

*caṃdrasūryagrahe lakṣaṃ vyatīpātetvanaṃtakam \|*  
*ayutaṃ viṣuve caiva niyutaṃ tvayanadvaye \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. If the bath is taken on the days of lunar or solar eclipses, it is a hundred thousand times; on the Vyatīpāta day (i.e., if the new-moon day is a Sunday) it is innumerable times; if it is on Viṣuva days (equinox days), it is ten thousand times more beneficial; if it is on the Ayana days, a hundred thousand times.

## \|\| 1.27.131 \|\|

*somagrahaḥ somadine ravivāraravagrahaḥ \|*  
*taccūḍāmaṇiparvākhyaṃ tatrasnānamasaṃkhyakam \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. If the lunar eclipse falls on a Monday or the solar eclipse on a Sunday, it is called Cūḍāmaṇi Parva. The bath on that day has unlimited benefit.

## \|\| 1.27.132 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homo yadyaccūḍāmaṇau kṛtam \|*  
*tadakṣayaṃ sarvamiha viṣṇo bhāgīrathītaṭe \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Bathing, Dānaṇḍapa, and Homa, whatever is performed on the Cūḍāmaṇi day on the banks of Gaṅgā, O Viṣṇu, is of everlasting benefit.

## \|\| 1.27.133 \|\|

*śraddhayā bhaktiyuktastu gaṃgāṃ snātvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*brahmahāpi viśuddhyeta kiṃpunastvanya pātakī \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. If one takes the holy dip in Gaṅgā in accordance with the injunctions with devotion and faith, one shall become purified even if one is a Brāhmaṇa-slayer. What to say of other sinners!

## \|\| 1.27.134 \|\|

*kṛmikīṭapataṃgādyā ye mṛtā jāhnavītaṭe \|*  
*kūlātpataṃti ye vṛkṣāstepi yāṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Worms, insects, locusts etc. that die on the banks of Gaṅgā, the trees that fall into Gaṅgā from the bank—all these attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.27.135-137 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe daśamyāṃ hastasaṃyute \|*  
*gaṃgātīre tu puruṣo nārī vā bhaktibhāvataḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

*niśāyāṃ jāgaraṃ kuyādgaṃgāṃ daśavidhairhare \|*  
*puṣpaiḥ sugaṃdhairnaivedyaiḥ phalairdaśadaśonmitaiḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

*pradīpairdaśabhirdhūpairdaśāṃgairgaruḍadhvaja \|*  
*pūjayecchraddhayā dhīmāndaśakṛtvo vidhānataḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

135-137. In the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha, on the tenth day with asterism Hasta, a man or woman should keep awake at night on the banks of Gaṅgā with great devotional fervour. He (or she) should perform the adoration of Gaṅgā ten times, O Garuḍa-emblemed Hari. There shall be ten kinds of flowers of great fragrance: The Naivedyas shall be of ten fruits on every occasion. There shall be Daśāṅga Dhūpas \[constituents: Kustha, jaggery, lac, Nakha (?), Harītakī, Sarjarasa, Māṃsī, Śailaja, Ghana (camphor) and bdellium\], A wise devotee shall perform the worship ten times in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 1.27.138 \|\|

*sājyāṃstilānkṣipettoye gaṃgāyāḥ prasṛtīrdaśa \|*  
*guḍasaktumayānpiṃḍāndadyācca daśamaṃtrataḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. He should drop gingelly seeds smeared with ghee into the waters of Gaṅgā. He should then offer ten handfuls of water. Uttering the Mantra he should offer ten balls of fried wheat-flour mixed with jaggery.

## \|\| 1.27.139-140 \|\|

*namaḥ śivāyai prathamaṃ nārāyaṇyai padaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*daśaharāyai padamiti gaṃgāyai maṃtra eṣa vai \|\| 139 \|\|*

*svāhāṃtaḥ praṇāvādiśca bhavedviṃśākṣaro manuḥ \|*  
*pūjādānaṃ japo homo 'nenaiva manunā smṛtaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

139-140. The twenty-syllabled Mantra is to be “Om namaḥ śivāyai nārāyaṇyai daśaharāyai gaṅgāyai svāhā” (Om, obeisance to Śivā, Nārāyaṇī, Daśaharā, Gaṅgā). The worship, Dāna, Japa and Homa are to be performed with the same Mantra.

## \|\| 1.27.141-145 \|\|

*hemnā rūpyeṇa vā śaktyā gaṃgāmūrtiṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*vastrācchāditavaktrasya pūrṇakuṃbhasya copari \|\| 141 \|\|*

*pratiṣṭhāpyārcayeddevīṃ paṃcāmṛtaviśodhitām \|*  
*caturbhujāṃ trinetrāṃ ca nadīnadaniṣevitām \|\| 142 \|\|*

*lāvaṇyāmṛtaniṣpaṃda saṃśīladgātrayaṣṭikām \|*  
*pūrṇakuṃbhasitāṃbhoja varadābhayasatkarām \|\| 143 \|\|*

*tato dhyāyetsusaumyā ca caṃdrāyutasamaprabhām \|*  
*cāmarairvījyamānāṃ ca śvetacchatropaśobhitāma \|\| 144 \|\|*

*sudhāplāvitabhūpṛṣṭhāṃ divyagaṃdhānulepanām \|*  
*trailaukyapūjitapadāṃ devarṣibhirabhiṣṭutām \|\| 145 \|\|*

141-145. According to his capacity the devotee should prepare an idol of Gaṅgā with gold or silver. It shall be installed above a Pūrṇakumbha (pot filled with water), the face of which is covered with a cloth. He should then bathe the idol with Pañcāmṛta and adore it.

Thereafter he shall meditate upon Gaṅgā as follows: She is very gentle in form with four arms and three eyes. She is served by Nadīs and Nadas (rivers great and small). She has the frequent application of the nectarine exudation of loveliness all over her physical form. She holds in her four hands a Pūrṇakuṃbha, a white lotus, the gestures of granting boon and freedom from fear. Her lustre is like that of ten thousand moons. She is being fanned with chowries. She shines well with a white umbrella. She has flooded the ground with nectar. She is besmeared with divine scents and unguents. Her feet are adored by all the three worlds. She is eulogized by Devas and the divine sages.

## \|\| 1.27.146-147 \|\|

*dhyātvā samarcya maṃtreṇa dhūpadīpopahārataḥ \|*  
*māṃ ca tvāṃ ca vidhiṃ bradhnaṃ himavaṃtaṃ bhagīratham \|\| 146 \|\|*

*pratimāgre samabhyarcya caṃdanākṣatanirmitān \|*  
*daśaprasthatilāndadyāddaśaviprebhya ādarāt \|\| 147 \|\|*

146-147. After meditating and worshipping with the Mantra, he should offer Dhūpa and Dīpa. In front of the idol of Gaṅgā, he should make small idols of myself, yourself and that of Brahmā, the Sun-god, Himalaya and Bhagīratha with sandal-paste and raw rice-grains and worship them. He should respectfully give ten Prasthas of gingelly seeds to ten Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.27.148 \|\|

*palaṃ ca kuḍavaḥ prastha āḍhako droṇa eva ca \|*  
*dhānyamānena boddhavyāḥ kramaśomī caturguṇāḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. These measures of grain are each four times the previous: Pala, Kuḍava, Prastha, Ādhaka and Droṇa (Pala: a handful of grain).

## \|\| 1.27.149-150 \|\|

*matsya kacchapa maṃḍūka makarādi jalecarān \|*  
*haṃsakāraṃḍava baka cakraṭiṭṭibhasārasān \|\| 149 \|\|*

*yathāśakti svarṇarūpya tāmrapṛṣṭhavinirmitān \|*  
*abhyarcya gaṃdhakusumairgaṃgāyāṃ prakṣipedvratī \|\| 150 \|\|*

149-150. The devotee observing the holy vow should make figures of fish, tortoise, frog, shark and other aquatic beings such as swans, Kāraṇḍavas, Bakas (cranes), Cakra (ruddy geese), Ṭiṭṭibha or Sārasa with pasted flour, copper, silver or gold in accordance with his capacity, worship them with scents and flowers and then cast them into Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.27.151 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānena vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjitaḥ \|*  
*upavāsī vakṣyamāṇairdaśapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. By performing this rite thus in accordance with the injunctions, without showing stinginess in spending money, the devotee will be rid of the ten types of sins as mentioned below:

## \|\| 1.27.152-155 \|\|

*adattānāmupādānaṃ hiṃsācaivāvidhānataḥ \|*  
*paradāropasevā ca kāyikaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam \|\| 152 \|\|*

*pāruṣyamanṛtaṃ caiva paiśunyaṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*asaṃbaddha pralāpaśca vāṅmayaṃsyāccaturvidham \|\| 153 \|\|*

*paradravyeṣvabhidhyānaṃ manasāniṣṭaciṃtanam \|*  
*vitathābhiniveśaśca mānasaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam \|\| 154 \|\|*

*etairdaśavidhaiḥ pāpairdaśajanmasamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*mucyate nātra saṃdehaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ gadādhara \|\| 155 \|\|*

152-155. There are three types of physical sins such as taking away what is not duly offered, indulging in violence without scriptural justification and resorting to other men’s wives. There are four types of verbal sins, viz. harsh utterances, untruthful speech, backbiting, indulging in irrelevant and absurd talks. There are three types of mental sins, viz. reflecting constantly on other people’s assets, evil thoughts in regard to others and earnest desire for insignificant and unreal things.

That devotee should be rid of all these ten types of sins originating in the course of ten births. There is no doubt about it, O Gadādhara. It is true, it is (definitely) true.

## \|\| 1.27.156 \|\|

*uttarennarakātpūrvāndaśaghorāddaśāvarān \|*  
*vakṣyamāṇamidaṃ stotraṃ gaṃgāgre śraddhayā japet \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. He shall redeem from terrible hell ten ancestors and ten successors. He should perform the Japa of the prayer presently being recounted with great faith in front of Gaṅgā:

\[Prayer to Gangā: (157-174)\]

## \|\| 1.27.157 \|\|

*oṃ namaḥ śivāyai gaṃgāyai śivadāyai namonamaḥ \|*  
*namaste viṣṇurūpiṇyai brahmamūrttyai namostu te \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. “Om, Obeisance to Gaṅgā, identical with Śiva and the bestower of happiness. Obeisance, obeisance, obeisance to you in the form of Viṣṇu. Obeisance to you in the form of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.27.158 \|\|

*namaste rudrarūpiṇyai śāṃkaryai te namonamaḥ \|*  
*sarvadevasvarūpiṇyai namo bheṣajamūrttaye \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. Bow to you in the form of Rudra, Śāṅkarī (benefactress); obeisance to you in the form of all gods; obeisance to medicine personified.

## \|\| 1.27.159 \|\|

*sarvasyasarvavyādhīnāṃ bhiṣakśreṣṭhyai namostu te \|*  
*sthāsnujaṃgamasaṃbhūta viṣahaṃtryai namostu te \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. Obeisance to you, the most excellent physician of all ailments of all people. Obeisance to you, the destroyer of the poisons arising from mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 1.27.160 \|\|

*saṃsāraviṣanāśinyai jīvanāyai namostu te \|*  
*tāpatritaya saṃhaṃtryai prāṇeśyai te namonamaḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. Hail to you, the destroyer of the poison of worldly existence; obeisance to the enlivener. Repeated obeisance to you, the destroyer of the three types of distresses, the goddess of the vital breath.

## \|\| 1.27.161 \|\|

*śāṃti saṃtānakāriṇyai namaste śuddhamūrtaye \|*  
*sarvasaṃśuddhikāriṇyai namaḥ pāpārimūrtaye \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. Obeisance to the goddess, the cause of continuous peace; obeisance to you, of pure form; obeisance to the purifier of everything; obeisance to you in the form of the enemy of sins.

## \|\| 1.27.162 \|\|

*bhuktimuktipradāyinyai bhadradāyai namonamaḥ \|*  
*bhogopabhogadāyinyai bhogavatyai namostu te \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. Repeated salutes to the bestower of worldly pleasures and salvation; obeisance to the bestower of welfare; obeisance to the bestower of pleasures here and hereafter; obeisance to you, the river in the nether worlds.

## \|\| 1.27.163 \|\|

*maṃdākinyai namastestu svargadāyai namonamaḥ \|*  
*namastrailokyabhūṣāyai tripathāyai namonamaḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. Obeisance to Mandākinī; obeisance, obeisance to the bestower of heavenly pleasures; obeisance to the ornament of the three worlds; obeisance, obeisance to the triple-streamed one.

## \|\| 1.27.164 \|\|

*namastriśuklasaṃsthāyai kṣamāvatyai namonamaḥ \|*  
*trihutāśanasaṃsthāyai tejovatyai namonamaḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. Obeisance to the holy river abiding in the three white ones (pure ones, viz. its source, Prayāga and confluence with the sea); obeisance, obeisance to the one with forbearance; obeisance to the one abiding in the three types of fire; obeisance to the brilliant one.

## \|\| 1.27.165 \|\|

*naṃdāyai liṃgadhāriṇyai sudhādhārātmane namaḥ \|*  
*namaste viśvamukhyāyai revatyai te namonamaḥ \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. Obeisance to Nanda (Alakanandā); obeisance to one holding the Liṅga; obeisance to the one having nectarine current; obeisance to you, the foremost one in the universe; obeisance, obeisance to Revatī.

## \|\| 1.27.166 \|\|

*bṛhatyai te namastestu lokadhātryai namostu te \|*  
*namaste viśvamitrāyai naṃdinyai te namonamaḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. Obeisance to you, the large one; obeisance to the mother of the worlds; obeisance to the one, the benefactor of the universe; obeisance to the delighter, obeisance.

## \|\| 1.27.167 \|\|

*pṛthvyai śivāmṛtāyai ca suvṛṣāyai namonamaḥ \|*  
*parāparaśatāḍhyāyai tārāyai te namonamaḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. Obeisance to one in the form of the earth; to one with auspicious waters; to the one in the form of the excellent piety; repeated obeisance to you, possessed of hundreds of greater and lesser beings; obeisance, obeisance to you, the redeemer.

## \|\| 1.27.168 \|\|

*pāśajālanikṛṃtinyai abhinnāyai namostu te \|*  
*śāṃtāyai ca variṣṭhāyai varadāyai namonamaḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. Obeisance to you, the breaker of the nooses and nets; obeisance to the one devoid of difference (partiality), obeisance to the quiescent one, to the most excellent one; obeisance to the bestower of boons.

## \|\| 1.27.169 \|\|

*ugrāyai sukhajagdhyai ca saṃjīvinyai namostu te \|*  
*brahmiṣṭhāyai brahmadāyai duritaghnyai namonamaḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. Obeisance to the fierce one; to the enjoyer of pleasures. Obeisance to you, the enlivener; obeisance to one stationed in Brahman; to the one bestowing Brahman (Vedas); obeisance, obeisance to the destroyer of sins.

## \|\| 1.27.170 \|\|

*praṇatārti prabhaṃjinyai jaganmātre namostute \|*  
*sarvāpatpratipakṣāyai maṃgalāyai namonamaḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. Obeisance to you, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow down; obeisance to you, the mother of the universe; obeisance to the one that dispels all adversities; obeisance, obeisance to the auspicious one.

## \|\| 1.27.171 \|\|

*śaraṇāgatadīnārta paritrāṇaparāyaṇe \|*  
*sarvasyārti hare devi nārāyaṇi namostu te \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. O Goddess, well disposed to save the poor and the distressed who seek refuge! O Goddess, O remover of the distress of everyone! Obeisance to the Goddess Nārāyaṇī (the abode of waters).

## \|\| 1.27.172 \|\|

*nirlepāyai durgahaṃtryai dakṣāyai te namonamaḥ \|*  
*parāparaparāyai ca gaṃge nirvāṇadāyini \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. Obeisance, obeisance to the one free from all adhesions and smearings (one without the effects of Avidyā and its products); to the destroyer of the demon Durga; obeisance to you, the efficient one; obeisance to the one beyond the greatest and the least, O Gaṅgā, the bestower of liberation!

## \|\| 1.27.173 \|\|

*gaṃge mamāgrato bhūyā gaṃge me tiṣṭha pṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*gaṃge me pārśvayoredhi gaṃge tvayyastu me sthitiḥ \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. O Gaṅgā, be in front of the; O Gaṅgā, stand behind me; O Gaṅgā, be at my sides; O Gaṅgā, let me be stationed in you.

## \|\| 1.27.174 \|\|

*ādau tvamaṃte madhye ca sarvaṃ tvaṃ gāṃ gate śive \|*  
*tvameva mūlaprakṛtistvaṃ pumānpara eva hi \|*  
*gaṃge tvaṃ paramātmā ca śivasvatubhyaṃ namaḥ śive \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. O auspicious Gaṅgā, you are at the beginning, in the middle and at the end; O auspicious one present in the earth, you are everything; you alone are the original Prakṛti; you are the highest Absolute; O Gaṅgā, you are supreme soul, Śiva; O auspicious one, obeisance to you.”

## \|\| 1.27.175 \|\|

*ya idaṃ paṭhate stotraṃ śṛṇuyācchraddhayāpi yaḥ \|*  
*daśadhā mucyate pāpaiḥ kāyavākcittasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. He who reads (recites) this prayer, he who listens to it with faith becomes rid of the ten types of sins originating from body, speech and mind.

## \|\| 1.27.176 \|\|

*rogastho rogato mucyedvipadbhyaśca vipadyutaḥ \|*  
*mucyate baṃdhanādbaddho bhīto bhītaḥ pramucyate \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. One who is sick becomes rid of ailments; one who is in adversity becomes rid of that adversity; one who is fettered becomes free from bondage; one who is terrified becomes free from that fear.

## \|\| 1.27.177 \|\|

*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti pretya ca tridivaṃ vrajet \|*  
*divyaṃ vimānamāruhya divyastrīparivījitaḥ \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. He will obtain all the desires; after his death, he will go to heaven riding a divine aerial chariot and fanned by celestial women.

## \|\| 1.27.178 \|\|

*gṛhepi likhitaṃ yasya sadā tiṣṭhati dhāritama \|*  
*nāgnicorabhayaṃ tasya na sarpādi bhayaṃ kvacita \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. If this prayer is written and kept in the house always or if it is worn always, he will have no cause to fear, fire or thief nor serpents etc.

## \|\| 1.27.179 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe māse site pakṣe daśamī hastasaṃyutā \|*  
*saṃharettrividhaṃ pāpaṃ budhavāreṇa saṃyutā \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. If the tenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha coincides with the asterism Hasta and Wednesday, it destroys all the three types of sins.

## \|\| 1.27.180-181 \|\|

*tasyāṃ daśamyāmetacca stotraṃ gaṃgājale sthitaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ paṭheddaśakṛtvastu daridro vāpi cākṣamaḥ \|\| 180 \|\|*

*sopi tatphalamāpnoti gaṃgāṃ saṃpūjya yatnataḥ \|*  
*pūrvoktena vidhānena yatphalaṃ saṃprakīrtitama \|\| 181 \|\|*

180-181. On that tenth day, he who stands in the waters of Gaṅgā and recites this prayer ten times, even if he is poor or (physically) incapable, obtains that benefit which has been mentioned before as accruing from worshipping assiduously Gaṅgā in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 1.27.182 \|\|

*yathā gaurī tathā gaṃgā tasmādgauryāstu pūjane \|*  
*yo vidhirvihitaḥ samyaksopi gaṃgāprapūjane \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. Gaṅgā is on a par with Gaurī. Hence the injunctions laid down for the adoration of Gaurī are also applicable to the worship of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.27.183 \|\|

*yathā'haṃ tvaṃ tathā viṣṇo yathā tvaṃ tu tathāhyumā \|*  
*umā yathā tathā gaṃgā catūrūpaṃ na bhidyate \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. Just as I am the same as you, O Viṣṇu, so also you are the same as Umā; Gaṅgā is the same as Umā; the forms of the four are not different.

## \|\| 1.27.184 \|\|

*viṣṇurudrāṃ taraṃ caiva śrīgauryoraṃtaraṃ tathā \|*  
*gaṃgāgauryaṃtaraṃ caiva yo brūte mūḍhadhīstu saḥ \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. He who mentions that there is difference between Viṣṇu and Rudra, between Śrī and Gaurī and between Gaṅgā and Gaurī is silly-minded.

## Chapter 28 - The Greatness of Gaṅgā (continued)

## \|\| 1.28.1 \|\|

*umovāca \|*  
*kiṃcitpraṣṭumanā nātha svasaṃdehāpanuttaye \|*  
*vada khedo yadi na te trikālajñānakovida \|\| 1 \|\|*

Umā said:

1\. O Lord, I am thinking of asking something to get rid of my doubts. O Lord, O knower of the three divisions of time, please tell me if you have no difficulty.

## \|\| 1.28.2 \|\|

*tadā bhagīratho rājā kva kva bhāgīrathī tadā \|*  
*yadā viṣṇustapastepe cakrapuṣkariṇī taṭe \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Where was King Bhagīratha and where was Gaṅgā (Bhāgirathī) then, when Viṣṇu performed austerity on the banks of Cakrapuṣkariṇī?

## \|\| 1.28.3-4 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*saṃdeho'tra na kartavyo viśālākṣi sadāmale \|*  
*śrutau smṛtau purāṇeṣu kālatrayamudīryate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhūtaṃ bhāvi bhavaccāpi saṃśayaṃ mā vṛthā kṛthāḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā punarāheśo gaṃgāmāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Śiva said:

3-4. O possessor of large eyes, O ever pure one, no doubt need be entertained in this respect. Three divisions of time are mentioned in the Vedas, Smṛtis and Purāṇas, viz. past, future and present. Do not have any doubt needlessly.

After saying this, Īśa again narrated the excellent greatness of Gaṅgā.

Agastya requested:

## \|\| 1.28.5 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*pārvatīnaṃdana punardyunadyāḥ parito vada \|*  
*mahimokto harau yadvaddevadevena vai tadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O son and delighter of Pārvatī, narrate again in Full the greatness of the celestial river as was recounted to Hari by the Lord of Devas then.

## \|\| 1.28.6 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*muna'tra maitrāvaruṇe yathā devena bhāṣitam \|*  
*śuṇu tripathagāminyā māhātmyaṃ pātakāpaham \|\| 6 \|\|*

Skanda said:

6\. O son of Mìtra and Varuṇa, listen to the sin-eradicating greatness of the triple-streamed river as recounted by the Lord.

## \|\| 1.28.7 \|\|

*trisrotasaṃ samāsādya sakṛtpiṃḍāndadāti yaḥ \|*  
*uddhṛtāḥ pitarastena bhavāṃbhodhestilodakaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. If on approaching the three-currented river, anyone offers balls of rice, at least once, along with the water libations with gingelly seeds, the Pitṛs are redeemed by him from the ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.28.8 \|\|

*yāvaṃtaśca tilā martyairgṛhītā pitṛkarmaṇi \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi pitaraḥ svargavāsinaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Pitṛs will stay in heaven as many thousands of years as there are gingelly seeds taken by the men in the course of the pious rite of the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.28.9 \|\|

*devāḥ sapitaro yasmādgaṃgāyāṃ sarvadā sthitāḥ \|*  
*āvāhanaṃ visargaṃ ca teṣāṃ tatra tato nahi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Since the Devas are always stationed in Gaṅgā along with the Pitṛs, neither the ritualistic invocation nor the dismissal-rite need be performed unto them there.

The following types of men go to heaven after being offered libations with the waters of Gaṅgā:

## \|\| 1.28.10 \|\|

*pitṛvaṃśe mṛtā ye ca mātṛvaṃśe tathaiva ca \|*  
*guru śvaśura baṃdhūnāṃ ye cānye bāṃdhavā mṛtāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. those who are dead in the family of father, as well as those in the family of mother; the other kinsmen of the preceptor, father-in-law or other relatives who are dead;

## \|\| 1.28.11 \|\|

*ajātadaṃtā ye kecidye ca garbhe prapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*agnividyuccorahatā vyāghradaṃṣṭribhireva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. those who died before cutting the teeth; those who had become afflicted even while in the womb; those who had been killed by fire, lightning or by thieves or by tigers or other fanged animals;

## \|\| 1.28.12 \|\|

*udbaṃdhana mṛtā ye ca patitā ātmaghātakāḥ \|*  
*ātmavikrayiṇaścorā ye tathā'yājyayājakāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. those who had committed suicide by hanging themselves; those fallen ones; those of self-inflicted death; those who sell themselves; thieves; those who perform the sacrificial rites unto those who are not eligible for them;

## \|\| 1.28.13 \|\|

*rasavikrayiṇo ye ca ye cānye pāparogiṇaḥ \|*  
*agnidā garadāścaiva goghnāścaiva svavaṃśajāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. those who sell Rasas (juices); those who suffer from diseases arising from sins (such as leprosy); those who are guilty of arson and administration of poison; those who kill cows; those belonging to one’s own family;

## \|\| 1.28.14 \|\|

*asipatravane ye ca kuṃbhīpāke ca ye gatāḥ \|*  
*rauravepyaṃdhatāmisre kālasūtre ca ye gatāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. those who have gone to the following five hells: Asipatravana, Kuṃbhīpāka, Raurava, Andhatāmisra and Kālasūtra;

## \|\| 1.28.15-16 \|\|

*jātyaṃtarasahasreṣu bhrāmyaṃte ye svakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*ye tu pakṣimṛgādīnāṃ kīṭavṛkṣādi vīrudhām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yoniṃ gatāstvasaṃkhyātāḥ saṃkhyātānāmaśobhanāḥ \|*  
*prāpitā yamalokaṃ tu sughorairyamakiṃkaraiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. those who wander through thousands of other births as a result of their own karmas; those who have been born as birds, animals, worms, trees and creepers of innumerable types; those who are not of very good and auspicious features even among those who can be counted; those who had been taken to the world of Yama by the terrible servants of Yama;

## \|\| 1.28.17 \|\|

*ye'bāṃdhavā bāṃdhavā vā ye'nyajanmani bāṃdhavāḥ \|*  
*yepi cājñātanāmāno ye cāputrāḥ svagotrajāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. those who are not kinsmen; those who are so; those who were kinsmen in the course of other births; those whose names are not known; those of one’s own family but without issues;

## \|\| 1.28.18 \|\|

*viṣeṇa ca mṛtā vai ye ye vai śṛṃgibhirāhatāḥ \|*  
*kṛtaghnāśca gurughnāśca ye ca mitradruhastathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. those who died due to poison; those who were struck by horned animals; ungrateful persons; slayers of preceptors and elders; those who had harassed and betrayed friends;

## \|\| 1.28.19 \|\|

*strī bālaghātakā ye ca ye ca viśvāsaghātakāḥ \|*  
*asatyahiṃsāniratā sadā pāparatāśca ye \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. those who killed women and children; those who are guilty of treachery; those who were violent and untruthful; those who have always been sinful;

## \|\| 1.28.20 \|\|

*aśvavikrayiṇo ye ca paradravyaharāśca ye \|*  
*anāthāḥ kṛpaṇā dīnā mānuṣyaṃ prāptumakṣamāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. those who sell horses; those who take away other people’s wealth; helpless ones; the wretched and miserable; those incapable of being born as human beings.

## \|\| 1.28.21 \|\|

*tarpitā jāhnavītoyairnareṇa vidhinā sakṛt \|*  
*prayāṃti svargatiṃ tepi svargiṇo muktimāpnuyuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If these are offered libations even once with the waters of Gaṅgā in accordance with the injunctions, they go to heaven. After being the dwellers of heaven, they shall attain liberation.

## \|\| 1.28.22 \|\|

*etānmaṃtrānsamuccārya yaḥ kuryātpitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ piṃḍapradānaṃ ca sa vidhijña ihocyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He who utters the Mantras and offers the libations of the Pitṛs unto these people and offers Śrāddha and balls of rice, is called as one who is conversant with the procedure.

## \|\| 1.28.23 \|\|

*kāmapradāni tīrthāni trailokye yāni kānicit \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi sevaṃte kāśyāmuttaravāhinīm \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Whatever holy places are there in the three worlds bestowing cherished desires, they resort to Gaṅgā that flows towards the north at Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.28.24 \|\|

*svaḥsiṃdhuḥ sarvataḥ puṇyā brahmahatyāpahāriṇī \|*  
*kāśyāṃ viśeṣato viṣṇo yatra cottaravāhinī \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O Viṣṇu, the celestial river is sacred everywhere, capable of dispelling the sin of even Brāhmaṇa-slaughter. It is particularly so where its current flows towards the north at Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.28.25-26 \|\|

*gāyaṃti gāthāmetāṃ vai daivarṣipitarogaṇāḥ \|*  
*api dṛggocarā naḥ syātkāśyāmuttaravāhinī \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yatratyāmṛtasaṃtṛptāstāpatritayavarjitāḥ \|*  
*syāma tvamṛtamevāddhā viśvanāthaprasādataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Devas, sages and groups of Pitṛs sing (i.e., wish): “Will Gaṅgā flowing towards the north at Kāśī be ever seen by us? We can be satiated through the Amṛta (nectarine water) there and be free from the three types of distresses. Presently, with the grace of Viśvanātha we shall attain salvation too.”

## \|\| 1.28.27 \|\|

*gaṃgaiva kevalā muktyai nirṇītā parito hare \|*  
*avimukte viśeṣeṇa mamādhiṣṭhānagauravāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O Hari, Gaṅgā alone is surely conducive to liberation, particularly so in Avimukta, due to the added weight of my presence.

## \|\| 1.28.28 \|\|

*jñātvā kaliyugaṃ ghoraṃ gaṃgābhaktiḥ sugopitā \|*  
*na viṃdatiṃ janā gaṃgāṃ muktimāgairkadāyikām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After realising that Kali age is excessively terrible, the devotion to Gaṅgā is well-guarded. Ordinary men do not get (the benefit of that holy river) Gaṅgā, the sole bestower of the path of salvation.

## \|\| 1.28.29 \|\|

*anekajanmaniyutaṃ bhrāmyamāṇastu yoniṣu \|*  
*nirvṛtiṃ prāpnuyātkotra jāhnavībhajanaṃ vinā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Without the worship of Jāhnavī who can expect liberation after wandering through various wombs in the course of many thousands of births?

## \|\| 1.28.30 \|\|

*narāṇāmalpabuddhīnāmeno vikṣiptacetasām \|*  
*gaṃgeva paramaṃ viṣṇo bheṣajaṃ bhavarogiṇām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Viṣṇu, Gaṅgā alone is the greatest antidote to men of meagre intelligence, ailing with the ailment of worldly existence, bewildered and distracted on account of sins.

## \|\| 1.28.31 \|\|

*khaṃḍasphuṭitasaṃskāraṃ gaṃgātīre karoti yaḥ \|*  
*mama loke ciraṃ kālaṃ tasyākṣaya sukhaṃ hare \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. If anyone repairs and rebuilds temples on the banks of Gaṅgā, O Hari, he will have never-reducing (everlasting) happiness for a long time in my world.

## \|\| 1.28.32 \|\|

*gaṃtumuddiśya yo gaṃgāṃ parārthasvārthameva vā \|*  
*na gacchati paraṃ mohātsa patetpitṛbhiḥ saha \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If anyone intends to go to Gaṅgā for his own sake or for other’s sake but does not go due to delusion, he will fall (in hell) along with his ancestors.

## \|\| 1.28.33 \|\|

*sarvāṇi yeṣāṃ gāṃgeyaistoyaiḥ kṛtyāni dehinām \|*  
*bhūmisthā api te martyā amartyā eva vai hare \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Those embodied human beings who carry out all their (holy) rites by means of the waters of Gaṅgā are immortal ones, O Hari, even though they stay on the earth.

## \|\| 1.28.34 \|\|

*caramepi vayobhāge svaḥsiṃdhuṃ yo niṣevate \|*  
*kṛtvāpyenāṃsi bahuśaḥ sopi yāyācchubhāṃ gatim \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He who resorts to Gaṅgā, the celestial river, at least during the last days of his life, shall attain excellent goal even after committing many sins.

## \|\| 1.28.35 \|\|

*yāvadasthi manuṣyāṇāṃ gaṃgātoyeṣu tiṣṭhati \|*  
*tāvadabdasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Men are honoured in the heavenly world for as many thousands of years as their bones rest in the waters of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.28.36-37 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*devadevajagannātha jagatāṃ hitakṛtprabho \|*  
*kīkasaṃ cetpateddaivāddurvṛttasya durātmanaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*jale dyunadyā niṣpāpe kathaṃ tasya parā gatiḥ \|*  
*apamṛtyu vipannasya tadīśa vinivedyatām \|\| 37 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

36-37. O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the universe, O Lord and benefactor of the worlds, if the bone of a wicked, evil-intentioned person were to fall casually in the sinless (sanctifying) waters of the heavenly river, how will he attain the great goal, after his premature accidental death? O Īśa, let this be clearly enunciated.

## \|\| 1.28.38 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*atrārthe kathayiṣyāmi purāvṛttamadhokṣaja \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvaikamanā viṣṇo vāhīkasya dvijanmanaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Maheśvara said:

38\. In this regard I shall recount an old anecdote, O Adhokṣaja (Viṣṇu). O Viṣṇu, listen with concentration of mind to the story of the Brāhmaṇa (Vāhīka).

## \|\| 1.28.39 \|\|

*purā kaliṃgaviṣaye dvijo lavaṇavikrayī \|*  
*saṃdhyāsnānavihīnaśca vedākṣaravivarjitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Formerly in the land of Kaliṅga, there was a Brāhmaṇa who used to sell salt. He was devoid of even a syllable from the Vedas. He avoided regular ablutions during dusks.

## \|\| 1.28.40 \|\|

*vāhīko nāmato yajñasūtramātraparigrahaḥ \|*  
*parigrahaśca tasyāsītkauviṃdī vidhavā navā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. His name was Vāhīka. He had only the Yajñasūtra, the sacred thread (to indicate that he was a Brāhmaṇa). The wife of a weaver who became a widow immediately became his wife.

## \|\| 1.28.41 \|\|

*durbhikṣapīḍitenātha vṛṣalīpatinā vinā \|*  
*prāṇādhāraṃ tadā tena deśāddeśāṃtaraṃ yayau \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Without a means of sustenance of life, the Śūdra woman accompanied by her husband tormented by famine, left the country and went to another country.

## \|\| 1.28.42 \|\|

*madhye'tha daṃḍakāraṇyaṃ kṣutkṣāmaḥ saṃgavarjitaḥ \|*  
*vyāghreṇa ghātitastatra naramāṃsapriyeṇa saḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In the middle of the Daṇḍaka forest that Vāhīka, emaciated with hunger and devoid of associates, was killed by a tiger fond of human flesh.

## \|\| 1.28.43 \|\|

*tasya vāmapadaṃ gṛdhro gṛhītvodapatattataḥ \|*  
*māṃsāśinā'nya gṛdhreṇa tasya yuddhamabhūddivi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A certain vulture seized his left leg and flew up. In the sky it had a fight with another flesh-eating vulture.

## \|\| 1.28.44 \|\|

*gṛdhrayorāmiṣaṃ gṛdhnvoḥ parasparajayaiṣiṇoḥ \|*  
*avāpatatpādagulphaṃ kaṃkacaṃcupuṭāttadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. While the two vultures desirous of the meat were fighting together with a desire to vanquish each other, the ankle of the leg fell down from the beak of the vulture.

## \|\| 1.28.45 \|\|

*tasya vāhīka viprasya vyāghravyāpāditasya ha \|*  
*madhye gaṃgaṃ daivayogādapataddvaṃdvakāriṇoḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. While the vultures were engaged in their duel, the ankle of the Brahmaṇa Vāhīka who had been killed by a tiger, casually fell into Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.28.46 \|\|

*yadaiva hatavāndvīpī taṃ vāhīkamaraṇyagam \|*  
*tasminneva kṣaṇe baddhaḥ sa pāśaiḥ krūrakiṃkaraiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. As soon as the tiger killed that Vāhīka travelling through the forest, the cruel servants (of Yama) bound him with nooses.

## \|\| 1.28.47 \|\|

*kaśābhirghātitotyaṃtamārābhiḥ paritoditaḥ \|*  
*vamanrudhiramāsyena nītastaiḥ sa yamāgrataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He was lashed much with whips; prodded all round with iron rods. He began to shed blood from his mouth. He was thus taken to the presence of Yama.

## \|\| 1.28.48 \|\|

*āpṛcchi dharmarājena citraguptotha māpate \|*  
*dharmādharmaṃ vicāryāsya kathayāśu dvijanmanaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then, O Consort of Lakṣmī, Citragupta was asked by Dharmarāja: “Tell me after due consideration the merits and demerits of this Brāhmaṇa quickly.”

## \|\| 1.28.49-50 \|\|

*vaivasvatena pṛṣṭotha citragupto vicitradhīḥ \|*  
*sarvadā sarvajaṃtūnāṃ veditā sarvakarmaṇām \|\| 49 \|\|*

*jagāda yamunābaṃdhuṃ vāhīkasya dvijanmanaḥ \|*  
*janmakarmadinārabhya durvṛttasya śubhetaram \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. On being asked by the son of Vivasvān (i.e., Yama) Citragupta of wonderful intellect, who knew all the activities of all the creatures always, told Yamuna’s brother (i.e., Yama) all the inauspicious activities of the Brāhmaṇa Vāhīka of foul deeds, ever since the day of his birth.

## \|\| 1.28.51 \|\|

*citragupta uvāca \|*  
*garbhādhānādikaṃ karma prākkṛtaṃ nāsya kenacit \|*  
*jātakarmakṛtaṃ nāsya pitrā'jñānavatā hare \|\| 51 \|\|*

Citragupta said:

51\. The sacred rites of Garbhādhāna etc. have not been performed on his behalf before. O Hari (Yama), Jātakarma (post-natal rite) was not performed by his ignorant father.

## \|\| 1.28.52 \|\|

*garbhainaḥ śamane hetuḥ samastāyuḥ sukhapradam \|*  
*ekādaśehni nāmāsya na kṛtaṃ vidhipūrvakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On the eleventh day, the naming ceremony was not duly performed for him: It is that rite which is the cause for subduing the sins since conception and which bestows happiness throughout the life.

## \|\| 1.28.53-58 \|\|

*khyātaḥ syādyena vidhinā sarvatra vidhipāvanam \|*  
*nākārṣīnnirgamaṃ cāsya caturthe māsi maṃdadhīḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*janakaḥ śubhatithyādau videśagamanāpaham \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhe'nnaprāśanaṃmāsi na kṛtaṃ vidhipūrvakam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sarvadā miṣṭamaśnāti karmaṇā yena bhāskare \|*  
*na cūḍākaraṇaṃ cāsya kṛtamabde yathākulam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*karmaṇā yena keśāḥ syuḥ snigdhāḥ kusumavarṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*nākāri karṇavedhosya janitrā samaye śubhe \|\| 56 \|\|*

*suvarṇagrāhiṇau yena karṇau syātāṃ ca suśrutī \|*  
*mauṃjībaṃdhopyabhūdasya vyatītebde'ṣṭame hare \|*  
*brahmacaryābhivṛddhyai yo brahmagrahaṇahetukaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*mauṃjīmokṣaṇavārtāpi kṛtā nāsya januḥkṛtā \|*  
*gārhasthyaṃ prāpyate yasmātkarmaṇo'naṃtaraṃ varam \|\| 58 \|\|*

53-58. On the fourth month, the slow-witted father did not perform the Nirgama (going out from the lying-in chamber) rite, the most sacred of all rites whereby he (the son) would have become famous. The father did not perform the Nirgama rite on an auspicious lunar day with other auspicious features also. It would have prevented the departure to foreign lands.

On the sixth month, the rite of Annaprāśana (feeding with cooked rice) was not performed duly, O son of Bhāskara (i.e., Yama), whereby he (the son) would have always eaten plenty of wholesome food.

On the completion of a year, the rite of Cūḍākaraṇa (‘making tuft of hair’) was not performed befitting the family, through which rite his hairs would have become smooth and glossy and showering flowers.

The rite of Karṇavedha (boring the ear) was not performed on an auspicious day by his father, by which rite the ears could have borne gold (earrings) and grasped excellent learning.

O Hari (Yama), it was (only) after the eighth year had passed that the rite of Mauñjībandha (binding with the Muñja grass or thread-ceremony) was performed, which rite is intended for learning the Vedas and is conducive to the enhancement of celibacy.

The very mentioning of the rite of Mauñji-Mokṣaṇa (Release from the Mauñjī i.e., Samāvartana ceremony) was not performed by his father, after which rite the excellent performance of the duties of a householder would have taken place.

## \|\| 1.28.59 \|\|

*yathākathaṃcidūḍhā'tha patnī tyaktakulādhvagā \|*  
*vṛṣalīpatinā tena paradārāpahāriṇā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Some wife who had discarded the tradition of the family and had become a harlot, was married by this consort of a Śūdra woman, who abducted another man’s wife.

## \|\| 1.28.60 \|\|

*ārabhya paṃcamādvarṣātparasvasyāpahārakaḥ \|*  
*abhūdeṣa durācāro durodaraparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. This fellow had become a pilferer of other men’s wealth ever since his fifth year. He was addicted to the game of gambling and he always practised misdeeds.

## \|\| 1.28.61 \|\|

*rumāyāṃ vasatā'nena hatāgaurekavārṣikī \|*  
*ekadā dṛḍhadaṃḍena lihaṃtī lavaṇaṃ mṛtā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. While he was staying in a Rumā (salt-producing marsh) a year-old cow was hit by him with a stout stick when it licked salt. And the cow died.

## \|\| 1.28.62 \|\|

*jananīṃ pādapātena bahuśo'sāvatāḍayat \|*  
*kadācidapi no vākyaṃ pituḥ kṛtamanena vai \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He used to kick his mother many times. His father’s words were never heeded to by him.

## \|\| 1.28.63 \|\|

*viṣaṃ bhakṣitavāneṣa bahuśaḥ kalahapriyaḥ \|*  
*janopatāpaśīlosau kṛtodaravidāraṇaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He was fond of quarrels. Many times he even ate poison. He habitually harassed people, tearing up their stomach.

## \|\| 1.28.64 \|\|

*dhattūrakaravīrādi bahudhopaviṣāṇi ca \|*  
*krīḍākalahamātreṇa bhakṣayaccaiṣa durmatiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. This evil-minded fellow used to swallow on many occasions small poisons such as Dhattūra, Karavīra etc., even at the time of a playful quarrel.

## \|\| 1.28.65 \|\|

*dagdhosāvagninā saure śvabhiśca kavalīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*śṛṃgibhiḥ paritaḥ proto viṣāṇāgrairasau bahu \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O son of Sūrya (i.e., Yama), he was burnt with fire; he was bitten by dogs; hit by horned animals with the tips of their horns.

## \|\| 1.28.66 \|\|

*daṃdaśūkairbhṛśaṃ daṣṭo duṣṭaḥ śiṣṭairvigarhitaḥ \|*  
*kāṣṭheṣṭaloṣṭaiḥ pāpiṣṭhaḥ kṛtāniṣṭaḥ sadātmanaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. This wicked fellow, despised by all good people, the committer of sins, has been bitten by venomous reptiles. With wooden pieces and lumps of clay, he inflicted injury on himself frequently.

## \|\| 1.28.67 \|\|

*āsphālitaṃ śironenāsakṛccāpi durātmanā \|*  
*yadarcyate sadā sadbhiruttamāṃgamanekadhā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. His head was struck by himself many times. This evil-minded fellow (violently) shook off his head, the best of all limbs of men which is always revered by good people.

## \|\| 1.28.68 \|\|

*asau hi brāhmaṇo maṃdo gāyatrīmapivedana \|*  
*kāmato matsyamāṃsāni jagdhānyetena durdhiyā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Though he was a Brāhmaṇa, this silly fellow did not know even the Gāyatrī. This evil-minded fellow ate fish and flesh as he pleased.

## \|\| 1.28.69-70 \|\|

*ātmārthaṃ pāyasamasau paryapākṣīdanekadhā \|*  
*lākṣālavaṇamāṃsānāṃ sapayodadhisarpiṣām \|\| 69 \|\|*

*viṣalohāyudhānāṃ ca dāsīgovājināmapi \|*  
*vikretā'sau sadā mūḍhastathā vai keśacarmaṇām \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Many times he got milk pudding cooked for his own sake. This silly fellow used to sell lac, salt, flesh along with milk, ghee and curds, poison, iron (hardware) and weapons, girl-slaves, cows and horses, hair and hides too.

## \|\| 1.28.71 \|\|

*śūdrānna paripuṣṭāṃgaḥ parvaṇyahani maithunī \|*  
*parāṅmukho daivapitryakarmaṇyeṣa durātmavān \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. His limbs became nourished with the cooked food from Śūdras. He used to indulge in sexual intercourse on festival days and even during the day-time. This wicked-souled fellow was averse to the holy rites pertaining to Devas and Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.28.72 \|\|

*pakṣiṇo ghātitānena mṛgāścāpi paraḥ śatam \|*  
*akāraṇa drumacchedī sadā nirdayamānasaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Birds were killed by him and hundreds of animals too. This cruel-minded fellow always cut off trees without any purpose.

## \|\| 1.28.73 \|\|

*udvegajanako nityaṃ nijabaṃdhujaneṣvapi \|*  
*asatyavādī satataṃ sadā hiṃsāparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Untruthful in speech and always engrossed in violence, he caused disgust incessantly even to his kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.28.74 \|\|

*adattadānaḥ piśunaḥ śiśnodaraparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ bahūktena ravija sākṣātpātaka mūrtimān \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. O Ravija (son of the Sun i.e., Yama), of what avail is talking too much? He was a slander-monger deeply indulging in the activities pertaining to the stomach and the organ of generation. He never made any monetary gift. He was a living personified form of sins.

## \|\| 1.28.75-77 \|\|

*rauravepyaṃdhatāmisre kuṃbhīpāke'tiraurave \|*  
*kālasūtre kṛmibhuji pūyaśoṇitakardame \|\| 75 \|\|*

*asipatravane ghore yaṃtrapīḍe sudaṃṣṭrake \|*  
*adhomukhe pūtigaṃdhe viṣṭhāgartteṣvabhojane \|\| 76 \|\|*

*sūcībhedye'tha saṃdaṃśe lālāpe kṣuradhārake \|*  
*pratyekaṃ narake tveṣa pātyatāṃ kalpasaṃkhyayā \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. May he be cast into each of the following hells for the period of a Kalpa: Raurava, Andhatāmisra, Kuṃbhīpāka, Atiraurava, Kālasūtra, Kṛmibhuj, Pūyaśoṇitakardama, Asipatravana, the terrible Yantrapīḍa, Sudaṃṣṭraka, Adhomukha, Pūtigandha, Viṣṭhāgarta, Śvabhojana, Sūcībhedya, Sandaṃśa, Lālāpa and Kṣuradhāraka.

## \|\| 1.28.78-79 \|\|

*dharmarājaḥ samākarṇya citraguptamukhāditi \|*  
*nirbhartsya taṃ durācāraṃ kiṃkarānādideśa ha \|\| 78 \|\|*

*bhrū saṃjñayā hṛtairnītaḥ sa baddhvā nirayālayam \|*  
*ākraṃdarāvo yatroccaiḥ pāpināṃ romaharṣaṇaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. On hearing those words from the mouth of Citragupta, Dharmarāja rebuked the misbehaving Brāhmaṇa and commanded his servants. With a gesture of Yama’s eyebrows he was bound and led to the hell by them. The loud screaming and wailing of the sinners caused horripilation.

## \|\| 1.28.80-81 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*yātanāsvatitīvrāsu vāhīke saṃsthite tadā \|*  
*tatkālapuṇyaphalade gāṅgeyāṃbhasi nirmale \|\| 80 \|\|*

*patitaṃ taddhi gṛdhrāsyādvāhīkasya dvijanmanaḥ \|*  
*hare vimānaṃ tatkālamāpannaṃ surasadmataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

80-81. In the course of the very severe tortures Vāhīka expired. Since (the ankle) had fallen from the mouth of the vulture into the pure waters of Gaṅgā that yielded benefit at once, there came an aerial chariot from heaven at the same time, O Hari, for the Brāhmaṇa Vāhīka.

## \|\| 1.28.82-83 \|\|

*ghaṃṭāvalaṃbitaṃ divyaṃ divyastrīśatasaṃkulam \|*  
*āruhya devayānaṃ sa divyaveṣadharo dvijaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*vījyamāno'psarovṛṃdairdivyagaṃdhānulepanaḥ \|*  
*jagāma svargabhuvanaṃ gaṃgāsthipatanāddhare \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. There were many bells hanging down from the aerial chariot. It was divine and full of hundreds of celestial damsels. The Brāhmaṇa who had assumed a divine form and dress climbed on to the divine vehicle. Divine scents and unguents he had applied (to his body) and he was fanned by groups of Apsarās, O Hari, due to the fact that a bone of his had fallen into Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.28.84 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*vastuśaktivicāroyamadbhutaḥ kopi kuṃbhaja \|*  
*dravarūpeṇa kāpyeṣā śaktiḥ sādāśivī parā \|\| 84 \|\|*

Skanda said:

84\. O Pot-born Sage, the power of certain things is (inexplicably) wonderful. This is a mighty power of Sadāśiva in liquid form.

## \|\| 1.28.85 \|\|

*karuṇāmṛtapūrṇena devadevena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*eṣā pravartitā gaṃgā jagaduddharaṇāya vai \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Indeed, it is for the sake of uplifting the worlds that Gaṅgā is made to flow by Śaṃbhu, the Lord of Devas, full of the nectar of kindness.

## \|\| 1.28.86 \|\|

*yathānyāḥ sarito loke vāripūrṇāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*tathaiṣānānumaṃtavyā sadbhistripathagāminī \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. This triple-steamed (Tripathagāminī) Gaṅgā should not be considered by good people on a par with thousands of other rivers in the world (though) filled with water.

## \|\| 1.28.87 \|\|

*śrutyakṣarāṇi niścitya kāruṇyācchaṃbhunā mune \|*  
*nirmitā taddravaireṣā gaṃgā gaṃgādhareṇa vai \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The syllables of Śruti were squeezed out of mercy, O sage, by Śaṃbhu. This Gaṅgā was created by Gaṅgādhara through the liquids arising therefrom (i.e., the water of Gaṅgā is the Brahma-rasa squeezed out of Upaniṣads—Com.)

## \|\| 1.28.88 \|\|

*yogopaniṣadāmetaṃ sāramākṛṣya śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*kṛpayā sarvajaṃtūnāṃ cakāra saritāṃ varām \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Due to his compassion for all creatures Śaṅkara extracted the essence of Yogic and Upaniṣadic texts and created the most excellent one among rivers.

## \|\| 1.28.89 \|\|

*akalānidhayo rātryo vipuṣpāścaiva pādapāḥ \|*  
*yathā tathaiva te deśā yatra nāstyamarāpagā \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The regions where the celestial river is not present are like nights without the moon and trees bereft of flowers.

## \|\| 1.28.90 \|\|

*anayāḥ saṃpado yadvanmakhā yadvadadakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*tadvaddeśā diśaḥ sarvā hīnā gaṃgāṃbhasā hare \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The regions and quarters devoid of the waters of Gaṅgā are like riches devoid of fairness and sacrifices without monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.28.91 \|\|

*vyomāṃgaṇamanarkaṃ ca nakte'dīpaṃ yathā gṛhama \|*  
*avedā brāhmaṇā yadvadgaṃgāhīnāstathā diśaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The directions devoid of Gaṅgā are like the courtyard of the sky without the Sun, like a house at night without a lamp and like Brāhmaṇas without Vedic study.

## \|\| 1.28.92 \|\|

*cāṃdrāyaṇasahasraṃ tu yaḥ kuryāddehaśodhanam \|*  
*gaṃgāmṛtaṃ pibedyastu tayorgaṃgābupo'dhikaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Of the two, one of them doing the observance of a thousand Cāndrāyaṇas purifying the body and the other drinking the water from Gaṅgā, the one that drinks Gaṅgā water is superior.

## \|\| 1.28.93 \|\|

*pādenaikena yastiṣṭhetsahasraṃ śaradāṃ śatam \|*  
*abdaṃ gaṃgāṃbupo yastu tayorgaṃgāṃbupo'dhikaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Of the two, one of them standing on a single foot for a hundred of thousand years and the other drinking the water of Gaṅgā for a year, the one who drinks the water of Gaṅgā is superior.

## \|\| 1.28.94 \|\|

*avākchirāḥ pralaṃbedyaḥ śatasaṃvatsarānnaraḥ \|*  
*bhīṣmasūvālukātalpaśayastasmādvaro hare \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. O Hari, a man who lies down on the sandy banks of Bhīṣmasū (Gaṅgā, the mother of Bhīṣma) as on a bed is superior to a man who hangs down with the head downwards for a period of a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.28.95 \|\|

*pāpatāpābhitaptānāṃ bhūtānāmiha jāhvavī \|*  
*pāpatāpaharā yadvadgaṃgā nānyattathā kalau \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Since Jāhnavī Gaṅgā is the destroyer of the distress resulting from sins of all the living beings suffering from the distress of sins, so there is nothing else like it in Kali age.

## \|\| 1.28.96 \|\|

*tārkṣyavīkṣaṇamātreṇa phaṇinau nirviṣā yathā \|*  
*niṣprabhāṇi tathenāṃsi bhāgīrathyavalokanāt \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Just as serpents become rid of their venom by the mere sight of Garuḍa, so also sins become devoid of lustre (power) at the sight of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.28.97 \|\|

*gaṃgātaṭodbhavāṃ mṛtsnāṃ yo maulau bibhṛyānnaraḥ \|*  
*bibharti so'rkabiṃbaṃ vai tamonāśāya niścitam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. A man who keeps on his head the clay from the banks of Gaṅgā certainly bears on his head the solar disc for the purpose of destroying darkness.

## \|\| 1.28.98 \|\|

*vyasanairabhibhūtasya dhanahīnasya pāpinaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgaiva kevalaṃ tasya gatiruktā na cānyathā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Gaṅgā alone is spoken as the refuge of that sinner who is devoid of wealth and assailed by many vices. It cannot be otherwise.

## \|\| 1.28.99 \|\|

*śrutābhilaṣitā dṛṣṭā spṛṣṭā pītā'vagāhitā \|*  
*puṃsāṃ vaṃśadvayaṃ gaṃgā tārayennātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. There is no doubt about this that Gaṅgā shall redeem both the families (father’s as well as mother’s) of men, if Gaṅgā is heard about, desired, seen, touched, drunk or plunged into.

## \|\| 1.28.100 \|\|

*kīrtanāddarśanātsparśādgaṃgāpānāvagāhanāt \|*  
*daśottaraguṇā jñeyā puṇyāpuṇyarddhināśayoḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The acts of glorification, seeing, touching, drinking and plunging into with respect to Gaṅgā are successively ten times more effective in increasing merit and destroying demerit.

## \|\| 1.28.101 \|\|

*na sutairna ca vā vittairnānyenāpi sukarmaṇā \|*  
*tatphalaṃ prāpyate martye gaṃgāmāpya yadāpyate \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Neither by sons, nor by riches nor by any other excellent activity is obtained that benefit which is derived by men after resorting to Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.28.102 \|\|

*jātyaṃdhāḥ paṃgavaste vai jīvaṃtopyatha te mṛtāḥ \|*  
*samarthā api ye gaṃgāṃ na snāyurmokṣagarbhiṇīm \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Those who never take the holy bath in Gaṅgā that accords liberation even though they are hale and hearty (capable) are cogenitally blind, lame and dead even if they (breathe and) are alive.

## \|\| 1.28.103 \|\|

*śrutiṃ niśāmaya hare gaṃgāmāhātmyabhāṣiṇīm \|*  
*viniścitārthāṃ yāṃ śrutvā śrayedgaṃgāṃ narottamaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. O Hari, listen to the Śruti that glorifies Gaṅgā. After listening to that Śruti of decisive meaning, an excellent man should resort to Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.28.104 \|\|

*irāvatīṃ madhumatīṃ payasvinīmamṛtarūpāmūrjasvatīm \|*  
*tridivaprasūtāṃ gaṃgāṃ śritāsastridivaṃ vrajaṃti \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Those who resort to the heaven-born Gaṅgā go to heaven. She is identical with these five rivers: Irāvatī, Madhumatī, Payasvinī, Amṛtarūpā and Ūrjasvatī.

## \|\| 1.28.105 \|\|

*ṛṣijuṣṭāṃ viṣṇupadīṃ purāṇāṃ supuṇyadhārāṃ manasā hi loke \|*  
*sarvātmanā jāhnavīṃ ye prapannāste brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ saṃprayāṃti \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Those who have resorted with all their heart to Jāhnavī rising from the foot of Viṣṇu and reaching the world, having meritorious current, being very ancient and resorted to by sages, go to the abode of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.28.106 \|\|

*lokānimānnayati yā jananīva putrānsvargaṃ sadā sarvaguṇopapannā \|*  
*sthānamiṣṭaṃ brāhmamabhīpsamānairgaṃgā sadaivātmavaśairupāsyā \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Gaṅgā should always be devoutly approached by spiritually inclined if they yearn for the covetable position of Brahmā. Like a mother leading her sons, Gaṅgā always takes the worlds (people) to heaven. She is endowed with all good qualities.

## \|\| 1.28.107 \|\|

*usrairjuṣṭāmiṣatīṃ viśvarūpāmirāvatīṃ janayitrīṃ guhasya \|*  
*śiṣṭaiḥ sevyāmamṛtāṃ brahmakāṃtāṃ gaṃgāṃ śrayedātmaviśuddhikāmaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. One who is desirous of the purity of himself should resort to Gaṅgā that is worthy of being served by good people. She is immortal, and is identical with Sāvitrī Mantra. She is the mother of Guha and is fully equipped with splendid rays. She is desirous (of granting boons), and is Cosmic-formed and possessed of Irā (Earth and Speech).

## \|\| 1.28.108 \|\|

*gaṃgāyāṃ tu naraḥ snātvā brahmacārī samāhitaḥ \|*  
*vidhūtapāpo bhavati vājapeyaṃ ca viṃdati \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. A man who takes his holy dip in Gaṅgā, practises celibacy and remains pure with mental concentration, becomes rid of all sins and he obtains (the benefit of) Vājapeya sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.28.109 \|\|

*aśubhaiḥ karmabhirgrastānmajjamānānmahārṇave \|*  
*patato niraye gaṃgā saṃśritānuddharetsadā \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. If they (sinners) resort to her, Gaṅgā shall always redeem those persons who are overwhelmed by inauspicious activities, who sink in the great ocean (of worldly existence) and who are about to fall into hell.

## \|\| 1.28.110 \|\|

*brahmalokastu lokānāṃ sarveṣāmuttamo yathā \|*  
*saritāṃ sarasāṃ vāpi variṣṭhā jāhnavī tathā \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Just as the world of Brahmā is the most excellent one among all the worlds, so also Jāhnavī is the most excellent one among rivers and lakes.

## \|\| 1.28.111 \|\|

*anyatra samyaksaṃkalpya tapaḥ kṛtvā samā trayam \|*  
*yatphalaṃ tadbhavedbhaktyā gaṃgāyāṃ ghaṭikā'rdhataḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Within half a Ghaṭikā (i.e., 12 minutes) one gets the benefit that is obtained elsewhere after performing penances for three years with a firm resolve, if one does the same in Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.28.112 \|\|

*svargasthasya na sā prītirbhuṃjataḥ sukhamakṣayam \|*  
*yā syādgaṃgātaṭe puṃsāṃ rātrau caṃdrodaye sati \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. A man staying in heaven and enjoying everlasting pleasure cannot have as much satisfaction as what people get on the banks of Gaṅgā at night when the moon rises.

## \|\| 1.28.113 \|\|

*jarārogābhipannaṃ tu kuṇapaṃ jāhnavī jale \|*  
*dhairyeṇa tṛṇavattyaktvā praviśedamarāvatīm \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. One can assuredly cast like a piece: of grass into the waters of Gaṅgā, the dead body of an old person afflicted with sickness. It will enter Amarāvatī (heavenly city).

## \|\| 1.28.114 \|\|

*vāryoghaiḥ satataṃ yasyāḥ plāvyate śaśimaṃḍalam \|*  
*bhūyodhikatarāṃ śobhāṃ bibharti tadahaḥ kṣaye \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. The lunar disc is always washed by the flood of waters of Gaṅgā. Hence at the end of the day it has added lustre.

## \|\| 1.28.115 \|\|

*āhutasya jale yasyāḥ sadyo naśyaṃti pātakam \|*  
*mahataḥ śreyasaḥ prāptistatkṣaṇādeva jāyate \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. The sin of a person who plunges into the waters of Gaṅgā perishes immediately. At the same moment, he attains the greatest welfare.

## \|\| 1.28.116 \|\|

*pitṛbhyaḥ śraddhayā yatra dattāstvāpaḥ svavaṃśajaiḥ \|*  
*prayacchaṃti parāṃ tṛptiṃ śaradāṃ trayamacyuta \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. O Acyuta, the waters of Gaṅgā if faithfully offered to the Pitṛs by their descendants, accord them great satisfaction for three years.

## \|\| 1.28.117 \|\|

*tārayetkṣitiyānmartyānadhaḥsthāṃśca sarīsṛpān \|*  
*svarge svargasado viṣṇorgaṃ gā tripathagā tataḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. She redeems people of the earth, reptiles residing beneath and dwellers of heaven. Hence, O Viṣṇu, she is called Tripathagā (‘going along the three paths—in three worlds’).

## \|\| 1.28.118 \|\|

*tīrthānāmuttamaṃ tīrthaṃ saritāmuttamā sarit \|*  
*svargadā sarvajaṃtūnāṃ mahāpātakināmapi \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Gaṅgā is the most excellent Tīrtha of all Tīrthas: she is the most excellent of all rivers. She bestows heavenly goal to all creatures, even to the greatest sinners.

## \|\| 1.28.119 \|\|

*adhyuṣṭāḥ koṭayo viṣṇo saṃti tīrthāni sarvataḥ \|*  
*divi bhuvyaṃtarikṣe ca jāhnavyāṃ tāni kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. O Viṣṇu, in the heaven, on the earth and in the atmosphere there are millions and millions of Tīrthas resorted to by the people everywhere. All of them are present in Jāhnavī entirely.

## \|\| 1.28.120 \|\|

*jñātvājñātvā ca gaṃgāyāṃ yaḥ paṃcatvamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*anātmaghātī svargī syānnarakānsa na paśyati \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. One who regularly takes the holy bath in Gaṅgā and meets with death without committing suicide (i.e., is not a committer of suicide), shall become a heaven-dweller. He never sees hells.

## \|\| 1.28.121 \|\|

*gaṃgaiva sarvatīrthāni gaṃgaiva ca tapovanam \|*  
*gaṃgaiva siddhikṣetraṃ hi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Gaṅgā herself is all the Tīrthas. Gaṅgā herself is a penance-grove. Gaṅgā alone is the holy spot of supernatural powers. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 1.28.122 \|\|

*yatra kāmaphalā vṛkṣā mahī yatra hiraṇmayī \|*  
*jāhnavī snāyinastatra nivasaṃti ghaṭodbhava \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. O Pot-born Sage, people taking the holy baths in Jāhnavī dwell where trees bear all desired fruits, where the ground is golden (i.e., in heaven).

## \|\| 1.28.123-124 \|\|

*dhenuṃ bhāgīrathī tīre suśīlāṃ ca payasvinīm \|*  
*vāsoratnairalaṃkṛtvā brāhmaṇāya dadāti yaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

*yāvaṃti tasyā lomāni mune tatsaṃtaterapi \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi sa svargasukhabhugbhavet \|\| 124 \|\|*

123-124. He who adorns with clothes and ornaments a milch cow of excellent behaviour and gives it to a Brāhmaṇa on the banks of Gaṅgā, enjoys heavenly pleasures for as many thousand years as there are hairs on the body of that cow and her calf.

## Chapter 29 - Gaṅgā-Sahasranāma (A Thousand Names of Gaṅgā)

## \|\| 1.29.1 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*vinā snānena gaṃgāyā nṛṇāṃ janmaniratharkam \|*  
*upāyāṃtaramastyanyadyena snānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: It is since the Vedic times that a list of epithets is used as a hymn of prayer, e.g. Rudrādhyaya in TS iv.5. The number of epithets in such lists went on increasing to include one thousand “Names” called Sahasranāma. They are in honour of various deities, great or small, such as Śiva, Viṣṇu, Pārvatī, Śākaṃbharī and even a godlet Malhārī. These epithets are overlapping as these deities came to be regarded as indentical with Supreme Brahman. Hence this Sahasranāma, though only of a river, contains epithets applicable to Brahman.

Agastya said:

1\. The birth of men is futile without a holy bath in Gaṅgā. Is there any other means whereby one may get the benefit of holy dip?

## \|\| 1.29.2 \|\|

*aśaktānāṃ ca paṃgūnāmālasyopahatātmanām \|*  
*dūradeśāṃtarasthānāṃ gaṃgāsnānaṃ kathaṃ bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. How can the feeble, the lame, those who are overpowered by indolence and those who are in far-off foreign lands, get the benefit of holy bath in Gaṅgā?

## \|\| 1.29.3-4 \|\|

*dānaṃ vā'tha vrataṃvā'tha maṃtraḥstotrajapo'thavā \|*  
*tīrthāṃtarābhiṣeko vā devatopāsanaṃ tu vā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yadyastikiṃcitṣaḍvaktra gaṃgāsnānaphalapradam \|*  
*vidhānāṃtaramātreṇa tadvada praṇatāya me \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. O Six-faced Lord, to me who have bowed down to you, kindly say if there is anything that can yield the benefit of holy ablution in Gaṅgā merely by its performance, be it in the form of monetary gift, Vrata (holy vow), Mantra, Stotra (hymn), Japa, worshipping a deity or holy plunge into another holy river.

## \|\| 1.29.5 \|\|

*tvatto na vedaskaṃdānyo gaṃgāgarbha samudbhava \|*  
*paraṃ svargataraṃgiṇyā mahimānaṃ mahāmate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O Skanda born of the womb of Gaṅgā, O highly intelligent one, none excepting you knows the mighty power of the heavenly river.

## \|\| 1.29.6 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*saṃti puṇyajalānīha sarāṃsi sarito mune \|*  
*sthāne sthāne ca tīrthāni jitātmādhyuṣitāni ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

Skanda said:

6\. O sage, here in different places there are Tīrthas with sacred waters, lakes and rivers occupied by people who have subdued their self.

## \|\| 1.29.7 \|\|

*dṛṣṭapratyayakārīṇi mahāmahima bhāṃjyapi \|*  
*paraṃ svargataraṃgiṇyāḥ koṭyaṃśopi na tatra vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They have mighty power and they give apparent results too. But even a ten-millionth part of the heavenly river is not present there.

## \|\| 1.29.8 \|\|

*anenaivānumānena buddhyasva kalaśodbhava \|*  
*dadhre gaṃgottamāṃgena devadevena śaṃbhunā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Gaṅgā is being held on his head by Śaṃbhu, the Lord of Devas. Know (the greatness of Gaṅgā) solely as an inference therefrom, O Pot-born Sage.

## \|\| 1.29.9 \|\|

*snānakāle'nya tīrtheṣu japyate jāhnavī janaiḥ \|*  
*vinā viṣṇupadīṃ kvānyatsamarthamaghamocane \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. At the time of taking the holy bath in the other Tīrthas, the Japa of Jāhnavī is performed by people. Excepting Viṣṇupadī (Gaṅgā) what else is capable of ridding one of sins?

## \|\| 1.29.10 \|\|

*gaṃgāsnānaphalaṃ brahmangaṃgāyāmeva labhyate \|*  
*yathā drākṣāphalasvādo drākṣāyāmeva nānyataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O holy Brāhmaṇa, the benefit of the holy bath in Gaṅgā is derived only from Gaṅgā, just as the taste of grapes is only in the grapes, not in anything else.

## \|\| 1.29.11 \|\|

*astyupāya iha tvekaḥ syādyenāvikalaṃ phalam \|*  
*snānasya devasarito mahāguhyatamo mune \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. But, O sage, there is one means whereby the entire benefit of the holy bath in the divine river can be obtained. It is a great secret.

## \|\| 1.29.12-13 \|\|

*śivabhaktāya śāṃtāya viṣṇubhaktiparāya ca \|*  
*śraddhālave tvāstikāya garbhavāsamupukṣave \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kathanīyaṃ na cānyasya kasyacitkenacitkvacit \|*  
*idaṃ rahasyaṃ paramaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. It should be disclosed to one who is a devotee of Śiva, who is quiescent, who has devotion to Viṣṇu also, who has faith, who is an Āstika (believer in the existence of God) and who desires release from rebirth. It should not be disclosed to anyone else on any occasion. This is a great secret, destructive of great sins.

## \|\| 1.29.14 \|\|

*mahāśreyaskaraṃ puṇyaṃ manorathakaraṃ param \|*  
*dyunadīprītijanakaṃ śivasaṃtoṣasaṃtati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It is conducive to great welfare and is meritorious. It causes pleasure to the celestial river and continuity of Śiva’s pleasure.

## \|\| 1.29.15 \|\|

*nāmnāṃ sahasragaṃgāyāḥ stavarājeṣuśo bhanam \|*  
*japyānāṃ paramaṃ japyaṃ vedopaniṣadāsamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A Thousand Names of Gaṅgā is the most brilliant of all excellent prayers. It is the greatest Japya (word worthy of being repeated for holy purposes) of all Japyas; it is on a par with the Vedas and Upaniṣads.

## \|\| 1.29.16 \|\|

*japanīyaṃ prayannena mauninā vācakaṃ vinā \|*  
*śucisthāneṣu śucinā suspaṣṭākṣarameva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The japa should be performed carefully by a man who maintains silence. The words are not loudly uttered but the letters should be clearly pronounced. The devotee should be personally pure and sit in a clean place.

## \|\| 1.29.17-168 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*oṃnamo gaṃgādevyai \|*  
*oṃkārarūpiṇyajarā'tulā'namatā'mṛtasravā \|*  
*atyudārā'bhayā'śokā'lakanaṃdā'mṛtā'malā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*anāthavatsalā'moghā'pāṃyoniramṛtapradā \|*  
*avyaktalakṣaṇā'kṣobhyā 'navacchinnā'parājitā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*anāthanāthā'bhīṣṭārthasiddhidā'naṃgavardhinī \|*  
*aṇimādiguṇā'dhārāgragaṇyā'līkahāriṇī \|\| 19 \|\|*

*aciṃtyaśaktiranaghā'dbhutarūpā'ghahāriṇī \|*  
*adrirājasutā'ṣṭāṃgayogasiddhipradā'cyutā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*akṣuṇṇaśaktirasudā'naṃtatīrthā'mṛtodakā \|*  
*anaṃtamahimā'pārā'naṃtasaukhyapradā'nnadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*aśeṣadevatāmūrtiraghorā'mṛtarūpiṇī \|*  
*avidyājālaśamanī hyapratarkyagatipradā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*aśeṣavighnasaṃhartrī tvaśeṣaguṇaguṃphitā \|*  
*ajñānatimirajyotiranugrahaparāyaṇā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*abhirāmā'navadyāṃgyanaṃtasārā'kalaṃkinī \|*  
*ārogyadā'naṃdavallī tvāpannārtivināśinī \|\| 24 \|\|*

*āścaryamūrtirāyuṣyā hyāḍhyā'dyā'prā'ryasevitā \|*  
*āpyāyinyāptavidyā'khyātvānaṃdā'śvāsadāyinī \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ālasyaghnyāpadāṃ haṃtrī hyānaṃdāmṛtavarṣiṇī \|*  
*irāvatīṣṭadātrīṣṭā tviṣṭāpūrtaphalapradā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*itihāsaśrutīḍyārthā tvihāmutraśubhapradā \|*  
*ijyāśīlasamijyeṣṭhā tviṃdrādiparivaṃditā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ilālaṃkāramāleddhā tviṃdirāramyamaṃdirā \|*  
*idiṃdirādisaṃsevyā tvīśvarīśvaravallabhā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ītibhītihareḍyā ca tvīḍanīya caritrabhṛt \|*  
*utkṛṣṭaśaktirutkṛṣṭoḍupamaṃḍalacāriṇī \|\| 29 \|\|*

*uditāṃbaramārgosroragalokavihāriṇī \|*  
*ukṣorvarotpalotkuṃbhā upeṃdracaraṇadravā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*udanvatpūrtihetuścodārotsāhapravardhinī \|*  
*udvegaghnyuṣṇaśamanī uṣṇaraśmisutā priyā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*utpatti sthiti saṃhārakāriṇyuparicāriṇī \|*  
*ūrjaṃ vahaṃtyūrjadharorjāvatī cormimālinī \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ūrdhvaretaḥpriyordhvādhvā hyūrmilordhvagatipradā \|*  
*ṛṣivṛṃdastutarddhiśca ṛṇatrayavināśinī \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ṛtaṃbhararddhidātrī ca ṛksvarūpā ṛjupriyā \|*  
*ṛkṣamārgavaharkṣārcirṛjumārgapradarśinī \|\| 34 \|\|*

*edhitā'khiladharmārthātvekaikāmṛtadāyinī \|*  
*edhanīyasvabhāvaijyā tvejitā śeṣapātakā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*aiśvaryadaiśvaryarūpā hyaitihyaṃ hyaiṃdavī dyutiḥ \|*  
*ojasvinyoṣadhīkṣetramojodaudanadāyinī \|\| 36 \|\|*

*oṣṭhāmṛtaunnatyadātrī tvauṣadhaṃ bhavarogiṇām \|*  
*audāryacaṃcuraupeṃdrī tvaugrīhyaumeyarūpiṇī \|\| 37 \|\|*

*aṃbarādhvavahāṃ'vaṣṭhāṃ varamālāṃbujekṣaṇā \|*  
*aṃbikāṃbumahāyoniraṃdhodāṃdhakahāriṇī \|\| 38 \|\|*

*aṃśumālāhyaṃśumatī tvaṃgīkṛtaṣaḍānanā \|*  
*aṃdhatāmisrahaṃtryaṃdhuraṃ janāhyaṃjanāvatī \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kalyāṇakāriṇī kāmyā kamalotpalagaṃdhinī \|*  
*kumudvatī kamalinī kāṃtiḥ kalpitadāyinī \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kāṃcanākṣī kāmadhenuḥ kīrtikṛtkleśanāśinī \|*  
*kratuśreṣṭhā kratuphalā karmabaṃdhavibhedinī \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kamalākṣī klamaharā kṛśānutapanadyutiḥ \|*  
*karuṇārdrā ca kalyāṇī kalikalmaṣanāśinī \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kāmarūpākriyāśaktiḥ kamalotpalamālinī \|*  
*kūṭasthā karuṇākāṃtā karmayānā kalāvatī \|\| 43 \|\|*

*kamalākalpalatikā kālīkaluṣavairiṇī \|*  
*kamanīyajalākamrā kapardisukapardagā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kālakṛṭapraśamanī kadaṃbakusumapriyā \|*  
*kāliṃdī kelilalitā kalakallolamālikā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*krāṃtalokatrayākaṃḍūḥ kaṃḍūtanayavatsalā \|*  
*khaḍginī khaḍgadhārābhā khagā khaṃḍeṃdudhāriṇī \|\| 46 \|\|*

*khekhelagāminī khasthā khaṃḍeṃdutilakapriyā \|*  
*khecarīkhecarīvaṃdyā khyātiḥ khyātipradāyinī \|\| 47 \|\|*

*khaṃḍitapraṇatāghaughā khalabuddhivināśinī \|*  
*khātainaḥ kaṃdasaṃdohā khaḍgakhaṭvāṃga kheṭinī \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kharasaṃtāpaśamanī khaniḥ pīyūṣapāthasām \|*  
*gaṃgā gaṃdhavatī gaurī gaṃdharvanagarapriyā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*gaṃbhīrāṃgī guṇamayī gatātaṃkā gatipriyā \|*  
*gaṇanāthāṃbikā gītā gadyapadyapariṣṭutā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*gāṃdhārī garbhaśamanī gatibhraṣṭagatipradā \|*  
*gomatī guhyavidyāgaurgoptrī gaganagāminī \|\| 51 \|\|*

*gotrapravardhinī guṇyā guṇātītā guṇāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*guhāṃbikā girisutā goviṃdāṃghrisamudbhavā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*guṇanīyacaritrā ca gāyatrī giriśapriyā \|*  
*gūḍharūpā guṇavatī gurvī gauravavardhinī \|\| 53 \|\|*
