*āśvāsya tau mahādevaḥ prītaḥ praṇatavatsalaḥ \|*  
*prāha svāṃ mūrtimaparāṃ bhairavaṃ taṃ kapardinam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Mahādeva who is pleased with those who bow down to him, became delighted and so consoled them both. He then told Bhairava having matted hairs, who is another form of his own self:

## \|\| 1.31.52-53 \|\|

*mānyo'dhvarosau bhavatā tathā śatadhṛtistvayam \|*  
*kapālaṃ vaidhasaṃ cāpi nīlalohita dhāraya \|\| 52 \|\|*

*brahmahatyāpanodāya vrataṃ lokāya darśayan \|*  
*cara tvaṃ satataṃ bhikṣāṃ kāpālavratamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*ityuktvāṃ'tarhito devastejorūpastadā śivaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. “This Adhvara (i.e., Nārāyaṇa) and Śatadhṛti (Brahmā) are worthy of being respected by you. O Nīlalohita, hold the skull of Brahmā and go abegging as a part of holy observance for the purpose of dispelling the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter and thus you personally demonstrate it to laymen.” After saying this, Śiva of brilliant form vanished.

## \|\| 1.31.54-55 \|\|

*utpādya kanyāmekāṃ tu brahmahatyeti viśrutām \|*  
*raktāṃbaradharāṃ raktāṃ raktasraggaṃdhalepanām \|\| 54 \|\|*

*daṃṣṭākarālavadanāṃ lalajjihvātibhīṣaṇām \|*  
*aṃtarikṣaikapādāgrāṃ pibaṃtīṃ rudhiraṃ bahu \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Further (before vanishing) he had created a feminine form (a girl) well-known as Brahmahatyā. She was clad in red and had red garlands, scents and unguents. She also was red in complexion. Her face was hideous with curved fanglike teeth. The lolling tongue made her terrible in appearance. The extremities of her feet were in the firmament. She was drinking up much of blood.

## \|\| 1.31.56 \|\|

*kartrīṃ karparahastāgrāṃ sphuratpiṃgogratārakām \|*  
*garjayaṃtīṃ mahāvegāṃ bhairavasyāpibhīṣaṇām \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. She had a knife and a broken pot in her hand. Her tawny-coloured ferocious eyeballs were bright. She was roaring with rapidity. She was terrifying even unto Bhairava.

## \|\| 1.31.57-58 \|\|

*yāvadvārāṇasīṃ divyāṃ purīmeṣa gamiṣyati \|*  
*tāvattvaṃ bhīṣaṇe kālamanugacchograrūpiṇi \|\| 57 \|\|*

*sarvatra te praveśosti tyaktvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*niyojyatāmiti śivopyaṃtardhānaṃ gatastataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. “O terrible one, by the time he goes to Vārāṇasī follow Kāla, O lady of hideous form. Excepting the city of Vārāṇasī, you will have easy access everywhere.” Saying thus, Śiva employed her on a special task and vanished.

## \|\| 1.31.59-60 \|\|

*tatsānnidhyādbhairavopi kālobhūtkālakālataḥ \|*  
*sa devadevavākyena bibhratkāpālikaṃ vratam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*kapālapāṇirviśvātmā cacāra bhuvanatrayam \|*  
*nātyākṣīccāpi taṃ devaṃ brahmahatyā sudāruṇā \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Due to her close proximity, though he was himself Kālakāla (‘Kāla unto Kāla’ \[death\]), Bhairava became black in colour. At the behest of the Lord of Devas, he observed the Kāpālikavrata and travelled the three worlds guiding the common people. The highly terrible Brahmahatyā did not leave off that deity (Bhairava).

## \|\| 1.31.61-62 \|\|

*satyalokepi vaikuṃṭhe maheṃdrādi purīṣvapi \|*  
*trijagatpatirugropi vratī trijagatīśvaraḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*pratitīrthaṃ bhramannāpi vimukto brahmahatyayā \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. The lord of the three worlds, Ugra, the sole administrator of the three worlds, despite his terrible observance, was never left alone by Brahmahatyā in the course of his wanderings in Satyaloka, Vaikuṇṭha and the cities of Mahendra and others and in every holy spot.

## \|\| 1.31.63 \|\|

*anenaivānumānena mahimā tvavagamyatām \|*  
*brahmahatyāpanodinyāḥ kāśyāḥ kalaśasaṃbhava \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O Pot-born Sage, from this alone let the greatness of Kāśī as the dispeller of the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter be known.

## \|\| 1.31.64 \|\|

*saṃti tīrthānyanekāni bahūnyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*adhi trilokino kāśyāḥ kalāmarhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. There are many holy places and divine shrines all over the three worlds. But they do not deserve even a sixteenth part of the greatness of Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.31.65 \|\|

*tāvadgarjaṃti pāpāni brahatyādikānyalam \|*  
*yāvannāma na śṛṇvaṃti kāśyāḥ pāpācalāśaneḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The sins of Brahmahatyā etc. may very well roar but only until they hear the name of Kāśī which acts like a thunderbolt in the destruction of the mountains in the form of sins.

## \|\| 1.31.66 \|\|

*pramathaiḥ sevyamāno'yaṃ trilokīṃ vicaranharaḥ \|*  
*kāpāliko yayau devo nārāyaṇaniketanam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Attended upon by his Pramathas, Hara, Kālabhairava with a skull in his hand, walked all over the three worlds. He then stepped into the abode of Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 1.31.67-68 \|\|

*athāyāṃtaṃ mahākālaṃ trinetraṃ sarpakuṃḍalam \|*  
*mahādevāṃśasaṃbhūtaṃ bhairavaṃ bhīṣaṇākṛtim \|\| 67 \|\|*

*papāta daṃḍavadbhūmau dṛṣṭvā taṃ garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*devāśca munayaścaiva devanāryaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. On seeing the Three-eyed Lord, Mahākāla with serpents for earrings, who is part of Mahādeva, but was called Bhairava the terrible, coming, the Garuḍa-emblemed Lord fell down on the ground like a log of wood in prostration. So did the Devas, sages and the celestial damsels all round.

## \|\| 1.31.69-70 \|\|

*nipetuḥ praṇipatyainaṃ praṇataḥ kamalāpatiḥ \|*  
*śirasyaṃjalimāropya stutvā bahuvidhaiḥ stavaiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*kṣīrodamathano tāṃ prāha padmālayāṃ hariḥ \|*  
*priye paśyā'bjanayane dhanyā'si subhagenaghe \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. They fell down by way of prostration. With his joined palms kept over the head and eulogizing by means of different kinds of prayers, the Lord of Kamalā (Goddess Lakṣmī), Hari, spoke to Padmā who emerged at the time of the churning of the Ocean of Milk: “O highly blessed, blameless, dear, lotus-eyed one, you are lucky.

## \|\| 1.31.71 \|\|

*dhanyo'haṃ devi suśroṇi yatpaśyāvo jagatpatim \|*  
*ayaṃ dhātā vidhātā ca lokānāṃ prabhurīśvaraḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. I too am lucky, O lady of excellent buttocks, because we see the Lord of the universe directly. He is the creator and dispenser of the destiny of all the worlds. He is the lord and ruler of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.31.72 \|\|

*anādiḥ śaraṇaḥ śāṃtaḥ paraḥ ṣaḍviṃśasaṃmitaḥ \|*  
*sarvajñaḥ sarvayogīśaḥ sarvabhūtaikanāyakaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He is beginningless. He is the sole refuge. He is quiescent. He is supreme Absolute, the twenty-sixth principle. He is omniscient. He is the lord of all Yogins. He is the sole lord of all Bhūtas (goblins or beings).

## \|\| 1.31.73-78 \|\|

*sarvabhūtāṃtarātmā'yaṃ sarveṣāṃ sarvadaḥ sadā \|*  
*yaṃ vinidrā viniḥśvāsāḥ śāṃtā dhyānaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*dhiyā paśyaṃti hṛdaye soyamadya samīkṣyatām \|*  
*yaṃ vidurvedatattvajñā yogino yatamānasāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*arūpo rūpavānbhūtvā soyamāyāti sarvagaḥ \|*  
*aho vicitraṃ devasya ceṣṭitaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*yasyākhyāṃ bruvatāṃ nityaṃ na dehaḥ sopi dehadhṛk \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā na punarjanma labhyate mānavairbhuvi \|\| 76 \|\|*

*soyamāyāti bhagavāṃstryaṃbakaḥ śaśibhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*puṃḍarīkadalāyāme dhanyeme'dya vilocane \|\| 77 \|\|*

*dhigdhikpadaṃ tu devānāṃ paraṃ dṛṣṭvā'tra śaṃkaram \|*  
*labhyate yanna nirvāṇaṃ sarvaduḥkhāṃtakṛttu yat \|\| 78 \|\|*

73-78. He is the immanent soul within all living beings. He is the perpetual bestower of everything unto all. Let him be seen now, whom those engaged in meditation, those who are calm and tranquil, those who have cast off their sleep, those who have curbed their breaths, see in their heart by means of their intellect. He who is formless, whom only Yogins of perfectly controlled minds and those who know the principle of the Vedas realize, who is omnipresent, comes here in an embodied form. Oh! Wonderful indeed is the activity of Parameṣṭhin (‘Dweller in the Absolute’). He has a body while those who repeat his names become bodiless. Here comes the Lord, the Three-eyed One with the moon as his ornament. On seeing him rebirth on the earth is not got by the men of the world. My eyes large and wide like the petals of a lotus are blessed now. Fie upon the status of Devas, for even after seeing the great Śaṅkara here salvation that puts an end to all miseries, is not obtained!

## \|\| 1.31.79 \|\|

*devatvādaśubhaṃ kiṃciddevaloke na vidyate \|*  
*dṛṣṭvāpi sarvadeveśaṃ yanmuktiṃ na labhāmahe \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. There is nothing more inauspicious in the world of gods than their own god-hood, because even after seeing the Lord of all the Devas, we do not get salvation.”

## \|\| 1.31.80 \|\|

*evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya mahādevamidamāha vṛṣadhvajam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. After saying this with joyous horripilation all over his body Hṛṣīkeśa bowed down to Mahādeva. He thus spoke to the Bull-emblemed Lord:

## \|\| 1.31.81 \|\|

*kimidaṃ devadevena sarvajñena tvayā vibho \|*  
*kriyate jagatāṃ dhātrā sarvapāpaharā'vyaya \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. “O Lord, the remover of all sins, O immutable one, what is this that is being done by you, the omniscient one, the Lord of Devas, the creator of all the worlds?

## \|\| 1.31.82 \|\|

*krīḍeyaṃ tava deveśa trilocana mahāmate \|*  
*kiṃ kāraṇaṃ virūpākṣa ceṣṭitaṃ te smarārdana \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. O Lord of Devas, O three-eyed Lord of great intellect, is this your sport? O odd-eyed (three-eyed) one, O destroyer of Smara, what is the reason of this act of yours?

## \|\| 1.31.83 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ bhagavatrchaṃbho bhikṣāṃ carasi śaktipa \|*  
*saṃśayo me jagannātha natatrailokyarājyada \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O Lord Śaṃbhu, why do you go abegging? This is my doubt, O Lord of Śakti, O Lord of the worlds, you who bestow the kingdom of the three worlds to those who bow down to you.”

## \|\| 1.31.84-88 \|\|

*evamuktastataḥ śaṃbhurviṣṇumetadudāharat \|*  
*brahmaṇastu śiraśchinnamaṃgu्lyagranakhena ha \|\| 84 \|\|*

*tadaghapratighaṃ viṣṇo carāmyetadvrataṃ śubham \|*  
*evamukto maheśena puṃḍarīkavilocanaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*smitvā kiṃcinnataśirāḥ punarevaṃ vyajijñapat \|*  
*yathecchasi tathā krīḍa sarvaviṣṭapanāyaka \|\| 86 \|\|*

*māyayā māṃ mahādeva nacchādayitumarhasi \|*  
*nābhīkamalakośāttu koṭiśaḥ kamalāsanān \|\| 87 \|\|*

*kalpe kalpe sṛjāmīśa tvanniyogabalādvibho \|*  
*tyaja māyāmimāṃ deva dustarāmakṛtātmabhiḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

84-86a. On being addressed thus, Śaṃbhu spoke thus to Viṣṇu: “Brahmā’s head was cut off by me with the nail at the tip of my finger. O Viṣṇu, it is to remove that sin that I am observing this auspicious expiatory holy rite.”

On being told thus by Maheśa, the lotus-eyed Lord smiled a little. With head bent down he then spoke:

86b-88. “O Lord of all worlds, sport about as you please. O Mahādeva, it does not behove you to overwhelm me with your Māyā. O mighty Lord, at your behest, I create in every Kalpa crores of lotus-seated ones (Brahmās) out of the lotus from the navel. O Lord, eschew this Māyā very difficult to wade through by those who have not realized their souls.

## \|\| 1.31.89-91 \|\|

*madādyo mahādeva māyayā tava mohitāḥ \|*  
*yathāvadavagacchāmi ceṣṭitaṃ te śivāpate \|\| 89 \|\|*

*saṃhārakāle saṃprāpte sadevānakhilānmunīn \|*  
*lokānvarṇāśramavato hariṣyasi yadā hara \|\| 90 \|\|*

*tadā kva te mahādeva pāpa brahmavadhādikam \|*  
*pārataṃtryaṃ na te śaṃbho svairaṃ krīḍettato bhavān \|\| 91 \|\|*

89-91. O Mahādeva, persons including me are deluded by your Māyā. Hence, O Lord of Śivā, I understand your act as it truly is.

When the time of annihilation comes, when you destroy all the worlds along with the Devas and sages of all castes and in all stages of life, then O Mahādeva, whence unto you is the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter etc.? O Śaṃbhu, you have no dependence on anyone else. Hence you sport about as you please.

## \|\| 1.31.92 \|\|

*atītabrahmaṇāmasthnāṃ srakkaṃṭhe tava bhāsate \|*  
*tadātadā kvānugatā brahmahatyā tavānagha \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The garland of the bones of all previous Brahmās shines round your neck. O sinless one, where then had the (sins of) Brahmahatyā gone?

## \|\| 1.31.93 \|\|

*kṛtvāpi sumahatpāpaṃ tvāṃ yaḥ smarati bhāvataḥ \|*  
*ādhāraṃ jagatāmīśaṃ tasya pāpaṃ vilīyate \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. If anyone remembers you with emotional fervour, despite the commission of great sins, his sin becomes destroyed (as) you are the support of all the worlds and the mighty lord thereof.

## \|\| 1.31.94 \|\|

*yathā tamo na tiṣṭheta saṃnidhāvaṃśumālinaḥ \|*  
*tathā na bhavabhaktasya pāpaṃ tasya vrajetkṣayam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Just as darkness does not stay in the proximity of the sun, so also does the sin of a devotee of Bhava. His sin duly becomes reduced.

## \|\| 1.31.95 \|\|

*yaściṃtayati puṇyātmā tava pādāṃbujadvayam \|*  
*brahmahatyādikamapi pāpaṃ tasya vrajetkṣayam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. If anyone of meritorious soul meditates upon the pair of your lotus-like feet, even the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter and the like becomes reduced and destroyed.

## \|\| 1.31.96 \|\|

*tava nāmānuraktā vāgyasya puṃso jagatpate \|*  
*apyadrikūṭatulitaṃ nainastamanubādhate \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. O Lord of the universe, if the speech of any man is devoutly attached and engrossed in your names, no sin harasses him, even if it be on a par with the peak of great mountain.

## \|\| 1.31.97 \|\|

*rajasā tamasā vivardhitaṃ kva nu pāpaṃ paritāpadāyakam \|*  
*kva ca te śiva nāma maṃgalaṃ janajīvātu jagadrujāpaham \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Where will stay the sin that causes great distress on being immensely increased by means of Rajas and Tamas Guṇas as against your auspicious name of Śiva, the panacea enlivening all, the cure for the ailments of all the worlds?

## \|\| 1.31.98 \|\|

*yadi jātucidaṃdhakadviṣastavanāmauṣṭhapuṭādviniḥsṛtam \|*  
*śivaśaṃkara caṃdraśekharetyasakṛttasya na saṃsṛtiḥ punaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. If the names Śiva, Śaṅkara, Candraśekhara etc. of the enemy of Andhaka come out of the lips even casually, one will never have worldly existence again.

## \|\| 1.31.99 \|\|

*paramātmanparaṃdhāma svecchā vidhṛta vigraha \|*  
*kutūhalaṃ taveśedaṃ kva parādhīnateśvare \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O supreme soul, O greatest refulgence, O you who have assumed a body out of your own will, this is only a curious whim of yours, O Lord. How can there be dependence on others in the case of a great Lord?

## \|\| 1.31.100 \|\|

*adya dhanyosmi deveśa yaṃ na paśyati yoginaḥ \|*  
*paśyāmi taṃ jaganmūlaṃ parameśvaramakṣayam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Today, I am blessed, O Lord of Devas, for I see that great immutable Lord, the root-cause of the universe whom even the Yogins do not see.

## \|\| 1.31.101 \|\|

*adya me paramo lābhastvadya me maṃgalaṃ param \|*  
*tvaddṛṣṭyamṛtatṛptasya tṛṇaṃ svargāpavargadam \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. I have secured a great acquisition today. I have attained the greatest auspicious achievement. To me who have been satiated by the nectar of your vision, even heavenly pleasures and salvation are like a mere blade of grass.”

## \|\| 1.31.102 \|\|

*itthaṃ vadati goviṃde vimalā padmayā tayā \|*  
*manorathavatī nāma bhikṣāpātre samarpitā \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. While Govinda was saying thus, certain alms of sacred nature called Manorathavatī (‘full of keen desire’) were offered unto his bowl by Padmā (Goddess Lakṣmī).

## \|\| 1.31.103 \|\|

*bhikṣāṭanāya devopi niragātparayā mudā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā'nuyāyinīṃ tāṃ tu samāhūya janārdanaḥ \|*  
*saṃprārthayadbrahmahatyāṃ vimuṃca tvaṃ triśūlinam \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. With great joy, the Lord too set out from there for begging. On seeing Brahmahatyā following him, Janārdana requested her: “Leave off the Trident-bearing One (Śiva).”

## \|\| 1.31.104 \|\|

*brahmahatyovāca \|*  
*anenāpi miṣeṇā'haṃ saṃsevyāmuṃ vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*ātmānaṃ pāvayiṣyāmi kva punarbhavadarśanam \|\| 104 \|\|*

Brahmahatyā said:

104\. Under this pretext, I shall attend upon the Bull-emblemed Lord and sanctify myself. Where can I have the vision of Bhava (Lord Śiva or Saṃsāra, the cosmos) once again?

## \|\| 1.31.105 \|\|

*sā tatyāja na tatpārśvaṃ vyāhṛtāpi murāriṇā \|*  
*tamūce'tha hariṃ śaṃbhuḥ smerāsyo vacanaṃ śubham \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Though addressed (and requested) by Murāri (Viṣṇu), she did not leave his side. Then with his face beaming with smile, Śaṃbhu spoke these excellent words to Hari:

## \|\| 1.31.106 \|\|

*tvadvākpīyūṣapānena tṛptosmi bahumānada \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva goviṃda varado'smi tavānagha \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. “O sinless Govinda, O bestower of honour, I am satisfied by drinking your words resembling nectar. Choose your boon. I am the bestower of boons on you.

## \|\| 1.31.107 \|\|

*na mādyaṃti yathā bhaikṣairbhikṣavopyatisaṃskṛtaiḥ \|*  
*yathāmānasudhāpānairnunna bhikṣāṭanajvarāḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Mendicants do not get so elated with highly consecrated alms as with nectarine drinks of honour, (because thereby) their pain of wandering for alms becomes eradicated.”

## \|\| 1.31.108 \|\|

*mahāviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*eṣa eva varaḥ ślāghyo yadahaṃ devatādhipam \|*  
*paśyāmi tvāṃ devadevaṃ manorathapathātigam \|\| 108 \|\|*

Mahāviṣṇu said:

108\. This itself is the most esteemed boon that I see you, the Lord of Devas who have gone beyond even the ken of wishful thinking.

## \|\| 1.31.109 \|\|

*anabhreyaṃ sudhāvṛṣṭiranāyāso mahotsavaḥ \|*  
*ayatno nidhilābho yadvīkṣaṇaṃ harate satām \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. According to the view of saintly persons, the bliss of seeing you, O Hara, is on a par with a shower of nectar without any cloud, a great festivity without undergoing any strain, the acquisition of a treasure-trove without any effort.

## \|\| 1.31.110 \|\|

*aviyogo'stu me deva tvadaṃghriyugalena vai \|*  
*eṣa eva varaḥ śaṃbho nānyaṃ kaṃcidvaraṃ vṛṇe \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. O Lord, let me not be separated from the pair of your feet. O Śaṃbhu, this is the boon; I do not choose any other boon.

## \|\| 1.31.111 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhavatu te'naṃta yattvayoktaṃ mahāmate \|*  
*sarveṣāmapi devānāṃ varadastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|\| 111 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

111\. O Ananta (the infinite one), let what has been wished by you be so, O highly intelligent one. You will become the bestower of boons to all the Devas.

## \|\| 1.31.112 \|\|

*anugṛhyeti daityāriṃ keṃdrādi bhuvane caran \|*  
*bheje vimuktijananīṃ nāmnā vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Thus blessing the enemy of the Daityas, he wandered through the worlds of Brahmā, Indra and others and resorted to the city named Vārāṇasī, the mother of liberation.

## \|\| 1.31.113 \|\|

*yatra sthitānāṃ jaṃtūnāṃ kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|*  
*api brahmādi devānāṃ padāni vipadāṃ padam \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Even the regions of Brahmā and other Devas are not equal to a sixteenth part of Vārāṇasī as the creatures staying there too are subject to adversities.

## \|\| 1.31.114 \|\|

*varaṃ vārāṇasī vāsī jaṭī muṃḍī digaṃbaraḥ \|*  
*nānyatracchatrasaṃchanna vasudhāmaṃḍaleśvaraḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. A resident of Vārāṇasī is far better, even if he be a mendicant with matted hair, tonsured head and completely nude, than an emperor of the entire earth with a royal umbrella staying elsewhere.

## \|\| 1.31.115 \|\|

*varaṃ vārāṇasī bhikṣā na lakṣādhipatānyataḥ \|*  
*lakṣādhīśo viśedgarbhaṃ tadbhikṣāśī na garbhabhāk \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. The alms received at Vārāṇasī is far better, (but) not the state of possessing a hundred thousand (Niṣkas) elsewhere. The lord of a hundred thousand enters the womb (Saṃsāra), but not he who consumes the alms thereof (of Vārāṇasī).

## \|\| 1.31.116 \|\|

*bhikṣāpi yatra bhikṣubhyo dattāmalakasaṃmitā \|*  
*sumeruṇāpi tulitā vārāṇasyāṃ gururbhavet \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. The alms there at Kāśī offered to mendicants, even if it be of the size of a fruit of Emblic Myrobalan, shall be weightier, if weighed against Sumeru (mountain).

## \|\| 1.31.117 \|\|

*varṣāśanaṃ hi yo dadyātkāśyāṃ sīdatkuṭuṃbine \|*  
*yāvaṃtyabdāni tāvaṃti yugāni sa divījyate \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. A person who gives food for the period of a year to one the members of whose family suffer, is honoured in heaven for as many Yugas.

## \|\| 1.31.118 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ varṣabhojyaṃ yo dadyānnirupāyine \|*  
*sa kadācittṛṭkṣudhā no duḥkhaṃ bhuṃkte nararṣabhaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. The best among men who gives annuity for food to a man without means of sustenance, never becomes miserable due to thirst and hunger.

## \|\| 1.31.119 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ nivasatāṃ yatpuṇyamupajāyate \|*  
*tadeva saṃvāsayituḥ phalaṃ tvavikalaṃ bhavet \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. A person who gives accommodation to others in Vārāṇasī obtains the full merit of those who live in Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 1.31.120 \|\|

*brahmahatyādi pāpāni yasyā nāmnopi kīrtanāt \|*  
*tyajaṃti pāpinaṃ kāśī sā kenehopamīyate \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Brāhmaṇa-slaughter and other sins leave off the sinner even when the name of Kāśī is uttered. With what can that Kāśī be compared?

## \|\| 1.31.121 \|\|

*kṣetre praviṣṭamātre'tha bhairave bhīṣaṇākṛtau \|*  
*hāhetyuktvā brahmahatyā pātālatalamāviśat \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. The moment the holy place (Vārāṇasī) was entered into (by Śiva), at the sight of Bhairava of terrible form, Brahmahatyā screamed “Alas! Alas!” and entered into the lowest of nether worlds.

## \|\| 1.31.122 \|\|

*kapālabrahmaṇo rudraḥ sarveṣāmeva paśyatām \|*  
*hastātpatitamālokya nanarta parayā mudā \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Even as all the people stood watching, the skull of Brahmā fell down from Rudra’s hand. On seeing it fallen, he danced with great joy.

## \|\| 1.31.123 \|\|

*vidheḥ kapālaṃ nāmuṃcatkaramatyaṃtaduḥsaham \|*  
*harasya bhramataḥ kvāpi tatkāśyāṃ kṣaṇato'patat \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. While Hara was wandering, the excessively unbearable skull of Brahmā did not leave off his hand at any other place, but at Kāśī it fell instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.31.124 \|\|

*śūlino brahmaṇo hatyā nāpaiti sma ca yā kvacit \|*  
*sā kāśyāṃ kṣaṇato naṣṭā kathaṃ kāśī na durlabhā \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. The sin of Brahmā-slaughter of the Trident-bearing Lord which was never separated anywhere, became destroyed in a moment at Kāśī. How then is Kāśī not: a rare city to be obtained?

## \|\| 1.31.125-127 \|\|

*ataḥ pradakṣiṇīkāryā pūjanīyā purī tviyam \|\| 125 \|\|*

*vārāṇasīti kāśīti mahāmaṃtramimaṃ japam \|*  
*yāvajjīvaṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ tu jaṃturjātu na jāyate \|\| 126 \|\|*

*avimuktaṃ mahākṣetraṃ smaranprāṇāṃstu yastvajet \|*  
*dūradeśāṃtarasthopi sopi jātu na jāyate \|\| 127 \|\|*

125-127. Hence this city should be circumambulated and adored. A creature that repeats this great Mantra “Vārāṇasī”, “Kāśī” thrice a day, throughout his life, is never born again. He who casts off his life remembering the great holy shrine Avimukta even while he is very far off is never reborn.

## \|\| 1.31.128 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānane yasya cittaṃ saṃsmarate sadā \|*  
*tatkṣetranāmaśravaṇānna sa bhūyo'bhijāyate \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. He whose mind always remembers Ānandakānana (Kāśī) is never reborn, thanks to the (merit of) hearing the name of that holy spot.

## \|\| 1.31.129 \|\|

*rudrāvāse vasennityaṃ naro niyatamānasaḥ \|*  
*enasāmapi saṃbhāraṃ kṛtvā kālādvimucyate \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. A man should always reside in the abode of Rudra with the mind fully controlled. Even after committing a mass of sins, he gets liberated in due course.

## \|\| 1.31.130 \|\|

*mahāśmaśānamāsādya yadi devādvipadyate \|*  
*punaḥ śmaśānaśayanaṃ na kvāpi labhate pumān \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. After reaching Mahāśmaśāna (i.e., Kāśī) if one dies accidentally, one never meets with the eventuality of lying in a cremation ground again.

## \|\| 1.31.131 \|\|

*kapālamocanaṃ kāśyāṃ ye smariṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ vinaṃkṣyati kṣipramihānyatrāpi pātakam \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. If men remember the holy spot of Kapālamocana at Kāśī, their sins committed here or elsewhere perish instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.31.132 \|\|

*āgatya tīrthapravare snānaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*tarpayitvā pitṝndevānmucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. After arriving here and performing ablution in this excellent Tīrtha (called Kapālamocana) and offering libations to the manes and gods, one gets liberated from the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.31.133 \|\|

*aśāśvatamidaṃ jñātvā vārāṇasyāṃ vasaṃti ye \|*  
*dehāṃte tatparaṃ jñānaṃ teṣāṃ dāsyati śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. If people reside in Vārāṇasī after fully realizing that this (worldly existence) is evanescent, Śaṅkara will bestow the supreme knowledge on them at the time of their death.

## \|\| 1.31.134 \|\|

*iyaṃ kāśīpurī vipra sākṣādrudratanuḥ parā \|*  
*anirvācyā parānaṃdā duṣprāpyeśavirodhibhiḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. O Brāhmaṇa, this city of Kāśī is the great physical body of Rudra himself. It is Anirvācya (‘cannot be adequately expressed in words’). It accords the greatest bliss. It is difficult of access for those who are antagonistic to Īśa.

## \|\| 1.31.135 \|\|

*asyāstattvamahaṃ jāne śivabhaktiparopi vā \|*  
*mucyaṃte jaṃtavo'traiva yathā yogena yoginaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. I know the reality of this (city). Or one who is engrossed in devotion to Śiva (also may know it). Creatures get liberated here itself like Yogins by means of Yoga.

## \|\| 1.31.136 \|\|

*paraṃpadamiyaṃ kāśī parānaṃda iyaṃ purī \|*  
*iyameva paraṃ jñānaṃ sevyā'sau mokṣakāṃkṣibhiḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. This Kāśī is the greatest region. This city is the greatest bliss. This itself is the supreme knowledge. This should be resorted to by those who desire salvation.

## \|\| 1.31.137 \|\|

*atroṣitvāpīśabhaktānviruṇaddhi tu yaḥ kudhīḥ \|*  
*puryaidruhyati vā mūḍhastasyānyatrātra no gatiḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. If anyone of crooked intellect stays here and becomes antagonistic to the devotees of Śiva or maliciously and deludedly hates this city, he has no redemption here or elsewhere.

## \|\| 1.31.138 \|\|

*kapālamocanaṃ tīrthaṃ puraskṛtvā tu bhairavaḥ \|*  
*tatraiva tasthau bhaktānāṃ bhakṣayannaghasaṃtatim \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. Honouring the holy spot Kapālamocana, Bhairava stood there itself eating up the heap of sins of his devotees.

## \|\| 1.31.139 \|\|

*pāpabhakṣaṇamāsādya kṛtvāpāpaśatānyapi \|*  
*kuto bibheti pāpebhyaḥ kālabhairavasevakaḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Though he might have committed hundreds of sins, why should a devotee of Kālabhairava be afraid of sins after resorting to Pāpabhakṣaṇa (‘the devourer of sins’).

## \|\| 1.31.140 \|\|

*āmardayati pāpāni duṣṭānāṃ ca manorathān \|*  
*āmardaka iti khyātastato'sau kālabhairavaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. This Kālabhairava became well-known as Āmardaka, because he subdues sins as well as the ambitious desires of the wicked ones.

## \|\| 1.31.141 \|\|

*kalikālaṃ kalayati sadā kāśī nivāsinām \|*  
*ataḥ khyātiṃ parāṃ prāptaḥ kālabhairavasaṃjñitām \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. He always puts an end to the influence of Kali on the residents of Kāśī. Hence he became highly famous with the name Kālabhairava.

## \|\| 1.31.142 \|\|

*sadaiva yasya bhaktebhyo yamadūtāḥ sudāruṇāḥ \|*  
*paramāṃ bhīrutāṃ prāptāstatosau bhairavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. The terrible messengers of Yama are always afraid of his devotees. Hence he is remembered as Bhairava.

## \|\| 1.31.143 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣāsitāṣṭamyāṃ kālabhairavasaṃnidhau \|*  
*upoṣya jāgaraṃ kurvanmahāpāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. On the eighth lunar day of the dark half of Mārgaśīrṣa, one should observe fast and keep awake in the presence of Kālabhairava. He is rid of great sins (committed at Kāśī) as sins committed outside are (already) destroyed while entering Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.31.144 \|\|

*yatkiṃcidaśubhaṃ karma kṛtaṃ mānuṣabuddhitaḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti kālabhairava darśanāt \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. What little inauspicious deed was committed due to human weakness of the mind, becomes dissolved at the sight of Kālabhairava.

## \|\| 1.31.145 \|\|

*anekajanmaniyutairyatkṛtaṃ jaṃtubhistvagham \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vilayatyāśu kālabhairava darśanāt \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. The sin committed by creatures in the course of hundreds of thousands of (previous) birth becomes dissolved quickly on seeing Kālabhairava.

## \|\| 1.31.146 \|\|

*kṛtvā ca vividhāṃ pūjāṃ mahāsaṃbhāravistaraiḥ \|*  
*naro mārgāsitāṣṭamyāṃ vārṣikaṃ vighnamutsṛjet \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. By performing different kinds of adoration elaborately with plenty of provisions on the eighth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, a man gets rid of (all the) hindrances of a year.

## \|\| 1.31.147 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ ravibhūmijavāsare \|*  
*yātrāṃ ca bhairavīṃ kṛtvā kṛtaiḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. By performing the festival of the procession of Bhairava on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days as well as on Sundays and Tuesdays, one gets rid of all the sins committed.

## \|\| 1.31.148 \|\|

*kālabhairava bhaktānāṃ sadā kāśīnivāsinām \|*  
*vighnaṃ yaḥ kurute mūḍhaḥ sa durgatimavāpnuyāt \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. A fool who puts obstacles before the devotees of Kālabhairava, the permanent residents of Kāśī, will meet with wretchedness (i.e., hell).

## \|\| 1.31.149 \|\|

*viśveśvarepi ye bhaktā no bhaktāḥ kālabhairave \|*  
*kāśyāṃ te vighnasaṃghātaṃ labhaṃte tu pade pade \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. Those who are devotees of Viśveśvara but not of Kālabhairava will encounter obstacles at every step at Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.31.150 \|\|

*tīrthe kālodake snātvā kṛtvā tarpaṇamatvaraḥ \|*  
*vilokya kālarājaṃ ca nirayāduddharetpitṝn \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. By taking the holy bath in the sacred waters of Kālodaka and performing the libations without haste, and visiting Kālarāja, one will redeem one’s Manes from the hell.

## \|\| 1.31.151 \|\|

*aṣṭau pradakṣiṇīkṛtya pratyahaṃ pāpabhakṣaṇam \|*  
*naro na pāpairlipyeta manovākkāyasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. By circumambulating Pāpabhakṣaṇa eight times everyday, a man prevents getting smeared with sins mental, verbal and physical.

## \|\| 1.31.152 \|\|

*tasminnāmardake pīṭhe japtvāsvābhīṣṭadevatām \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsaṃ siddhimāpnoti sādhako bhairavājñayā \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. By performing the Japa of any of his desired deities seated near the pedestal of Āmardaka for six months, the aspirant achieves supernatural powers (or desired objects)—that is the command of Bhairava.

## \|\| 1.31.153 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāmuṣitvā yo bhairavaṃ na bhajennaraḥ \|*  
*tasya pāpāni vardhaṃte śuklapakṣe yathā śaśī \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. If after staying in the city of Kāśī, a man does not worship Bhairava, his sins go on increasing like the moon in the bright half.

## \|\| 1.31.154 \|\|

*yaṃ yaṃ saṃcitayetkāmaṃ pāpabhakṣaṇasevayā \|*  
*balipūjopahāraiśca taṃ taṃ sa samavāpnuyāt \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. By resorting to the service of Pāpabhakṣaṇa with oblations, Pūjā and presents, the devotee obtains whatever he desires.

## \|\| 1.31.155 \|\|

*kālarājaṃ na yaḥ kāśyāṃ pratibhūtāṣṭamīkujam \|*  
*bhajettasyakṣayetpuṇyaṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe yathā śaśī \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. If a person does not worship Kālarāja at Kāśī on every eighth and fourteenth lunar days and on Tuesdays, his merit declines like the moon in the dark half.

## \|\| 1.31.156-157 \|\|

*śrutvādhyāyamimaṃ puṇyaṃ brahmahatyāpanodakam \|*  
*bhairavotpattisaṃjñaṃ ca sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 156 \|\|*

*baṃdhanāgārasaṃsthopi prāptopi vipadaṃ parām \|*  
*prādurbhāvaṃ bhairavasya śrutvā mucyeta saṃkaṭāt \|\| 157 \|\|*

156-157. By listening to this meritorious chapter which is named Bhairavotpatti (‘Birth of Bhairava’) and which dispels the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, one is freed from all sins. Even a person kept in prison, one in great danger becomes rid of difficulties by listening to the manifestation of Bhairava.

## Chapter 32 - The Manifestation of Daṇḍapāṇi

## \|\| 1.32.1 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*barhiyāna samācakṣva harikeśasamudbhavam \|*  
*kosau kasya sutaḥ śrīmānkīdṛgasya tapo mahat \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Daṇḍapāni is the Sheriff of Kāśī who expels undesirable people out of Kāśī and protects eligible residents of Kāśī. He has Sambhrama and Vibhrama as his assistants. As an assistant of Goddess Annapūrṇā, he feeds the needy at Kāśī. Today, the small shrine of Daṇḍapāṇi is in the Viśvanātha lane to the west of Jñānavāpī Mosque. His Daṇḍa (club) is a pillar-fragment from the Mahāśmaśāna pillar at Laṭ Bhairava in a small shrine near Kālabhairava.—Like Gaṇeśa and Kālabhairava, Daṇḍapāṇi is a major figure in Banaras Pantheon (BCL 198-201).

Agastya said:

1\. O Lord having peacock as your mount, recount to me the nativity of Harikeśa. Who is he? Whose illustrious son was he? How great is his austerity?

## \|\| 1.32.2 \|\|

*kathaṃ ca devadevasya priyatvaṃ samupeyivān \|*  
*kāśīvāsijanīnobhūtkathaṃ vā daṃḍanāyakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. How did he happen to be a favourite of the Lord of Devas? How did he become the chief of the citizens of Kāśī? How did he become the holder of a staff (i.e., the chief dispenser of punishment)?

## \|\| 1.32.3 \|\|

*etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ prasādaṃ kuru me vibho \|*  
*annadatvaṃ ca saṃprāptaḥ kathameṣa mahāmatiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. How did this highly intelligent one gain the status of the bestower of food? I wish to hear this. O Lord, do me this favour.

## \|\| 1.32.4 \|\|

*saṃbhramo vibhramaścobhau kathaṃ tadanugāminau \|*  
*vibhrāṃtikāriṇau kṣetravairiṇāṃ sarvadā nṛṇām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. How did Sambhrama and Vibhrama become his followers? How did they become persons causing confusion to those inimical to the holy spot?

Skanda replied:

## \|\| 1.32.5 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*samyagāpṛcchi bhavatā kāśīvāsisamāhitam \|*  
*kuṃbhasaṃbhava viprarṣe daṃḍapāṇi kathānakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The question has been put relevantly by you, O Pot-born One, O Brāhmaṇa-sage. The story of Daṇḍapāṇi is conductive to the good of the citizens of Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.32.6 \|\|

*yadākarṇya naraḥ prājña kāśīvāsasya yatphalam \|*  
*niṣpratyūhaṃ tadāpnoti viśvabhartturanugrahāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O wise one, by the grace of Viśvabhartṛ (Siva), a man who hears this story, obtains without hindrance the merit of residing in Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.32.7 \|\|

*ratnabhadra iti khyātaḥ parvate gaṃdhamādane \|*  
*yakṣaḥ sukṛtalakṣaśrīḥ purā parama dhārmikaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On the Gandhamādana mountain formerly there was a Yakṣa. He was highly righteous. His prosperity was always directed to the performance of good rites.

## \|\| 1.32.8-9 \|\|

*pūrṇabhadraṃ sutaṃ prāpya so'bhūtpūrṇamanorathaḥ \|*  
*vayaścaramamāsādya bhuktvā bhogānanekaśaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śāṃbhavenātha yogena dehamutsṛjya pārthivam \|*  
*āsasādāśavaṃ śāṃtaṃ śāṃtasarveṃdriyārthakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Having obtained a son named Pūrṇabhadra, he considered all his desires fulfilled. Attaining the close of his life after the due enjoyment of many pleasures, he renounced his earthly body by means of Śāṃbhava Yoga (practice of Yoga specially consisting of meditation on Śiva) and attained permanent peace with all the sense-organs and their objects having been rendered quiescent.

## \|\| 1.32.10-12 \|\|

*pitaryuparateso'tha pūrṇabhadro mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*sukṛtopāttavibhava bhavasaṃbhogabhuktibhāk \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sarvānmanorathāṃllebhe vinā svargaikasādhanam \|*  
*gārhasthyāśrama nepathyaṃ pathyaṃ paitāmahaṃ mahat \|\| 11 \|\|*

*saṃsāratāpasaṃtaptāvayavāmṛtasīkaram \|*  
*apatyaṃ patatāṃ potaṃ bahukleśamahārṇave \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. After the death of his father Pūrṇabhadra of great renown enjoyed all the worldly pleasures, the extent of which was acquired through merit. He got everything he desired except a son, the sole cause for the attainment of heaven—a son that embellishes the stage of life of a householder, that functions as contributing much to the good of grandfathers, that acts like a spray of nectar to the limbs scorched by the distress of worldly existence and that is akin to a great boat to those who fall into the great ocean of distress.

## \|\| 1.32.13-15 \|\|

*pūrṇabhadro'tha saṃvīkṣya maṃdiraṃ sarvasuṃdaram \|*  
*tadbālakomalālāpa vikalaṃ tyaktamaṃgalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śūnyaṃ daridrahṛdiva jīrṇāraṇyamivāthavā \|*  
*pāṃthavatprāṃtaramiva khinno'tīvānapatyavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

*āhūya gṛhiṇī so'tha yakṣaḥ kanakakuṃḍalām \|*  
*uvāca yakṣiṇīṃ śreṣṭhāṃ pūrṇabhadro ghaṭodbhava \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Pùrṇabhadra (who had everything good in plenty) saw his palace that was beautiful to all others, devoid of auspiciousness in view of the fact that it was denied the sweetness of the lisping talk of a child. Without a child he was extremely distressed and saw (his palace) a void like the heart of an indigent person, or a desolate forest. On seeing a lonely path, a traveller becomes distressed. Like that he was also distressed. O Pot-born One, this Yakṣa called his wife Kanakakuṇḍalā, an excellent Yakṣiṇī, and said to her, O Pot-born Sage:

## \|\| 1.32.16-25 \|\|

*na harmyaṃ sukhadaṃ kāṃte darpaṇodarasuṃdaram \|*  
*muktā gavākṣasubhagaṃ caṃdrakāṃtaśilājiram \|\| 16 \|\|*

*padmarāgeṃdranīlārcirarcitāṭṭālakaṃ kvaṇat \|*  
*vidrumastaṃbhaśobhāḍhyaṃ sphuratsphaṭikakuḍyavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

*preṃkhatpatākānikaraṃ maṇimāṇikyamālitam \|*  
*kṛṣṇāgurumahādhūpa bahulāmodamoditam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*anarghyāsanasaṃyuktaṃ cāruparyaṃkabhūṣitam \|*  
*ramyārgalakapāṭāḍhyaṃ dukūlacchannamaṃḍapam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*suramyaratiśālāḍhyaṃ vājirājivirājitam \|*  
*dāsadāsīśatākīrṇaṃ kiṃkiṇīnādanāditam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*nūpurārāvasotkaṃṭha kekikekāravākulam \|*  
*kūjatpārāvata kulaṃ gurusārīkathāvaram \|\| 21 \|\|*

*khelanmarālayugalaṃ jīvaṃ jīvakakāṃtimat \|*  
*mālyāhūta dvirephāṇāṃ maṃjuguṃjāravāvṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*karpūraiṇa madāmoda sodarānilavījitam \|*  
*krīḍāmarkaṭadaṃṣṭrāgrī kṛtamāṇikyadāḍimam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dāḍimībījasaṃbhrāṃtaśukatuṃḍāttamauktikam \|*  
*dhanadhānyasamṛddhaṃ ca padmālayamivāparam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kamalāmodagarbhaṃ ca garbharūpaṃ vinā priye \|*  
*garbharūpamukhaṃ prekṣye kathaṃ kanakakuḍale \|\| 25 \|\|*

16-25. “O dear wife! I do not consider this palace as pleasing, though it is beautiful with a number of mirror-panels in the interior. The windows are beautifully studded with pearls. The courtyard is paved with lunar crystals. There is pleasing sound all-round. The upper storey is rendered brilliant with the lustres of rubies and sapphires that abound in it. Columns of coral add to its splendour. The walls are covered with shining crystals. A number of fluttering banners adorn it with garlands of jewels and rubies. The fragrance of incense and black agallochum render it very joyous. Very costly seats are placed everywhere. Charming couches embellish it. The doors are fitted with beautiful bolts. The pavilion is covered with silk cloth. There are many beautiful dalliance chambers. The palace shines with a number of horses; it is filled with hundreds of servants and servant-maids; it is resonant with the sound of tinkling bells. The cries of peacocks rendered wistful on account of the sounds of anklets, fill the palace. Many doves chirp. It is lofty and resounds with the cries of Sārikās (Mainās). Pairs of swans sport about. There is the splendour of Cakora birds. The humming sounds of bees attracted by flower garlands are heard everywhere. Winds wafting the sweet scent of camphor and musk blow all-round. Dolls of monkeys kept for sport display jewels and rubies on the top of their curved teeth as though they were seeds of pomegranates. Parrots seize pearls mistaking them to be seeds of pomegranates. It is like another palace of Goddess Lakṣmī and is richly endowed with wealth and food-grains. It has the sweet scent of lotuses within. But in spite of all these things, O my dear, I do not find it pleasing in the absence of a child in the womb. How can I, O Kanakakuṇḍalā, my dear, see the face of a child?

## \|\| 1.32.26 \|\|

*yadyupāyo'sti tadbrūhi dhigaputrasya jīvitam \|*  
*sarvaśūnyamivābhāti gṛhametadanaṃgajam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Tell me if there is any means (of getting a son). Fie upon the life of a sonless person! The whole of this house appears to be a void without a child born of my bosom.

## \|\| 1.32.27 \|\|

*dhigetatsaudhasauṃdaryaṃ dhigetaddhanasaṃcayam \|*  
*vināpatyaṃ priyatame jīvitaṃ ca dhigāvayoḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Fie upon the beauty of this mansion! Fie upon this hoarded wealth! Without a son, my dear beloved, our life too is worthless. Fie upon it!”

## \|\| 1.32.28 \|\|

*pralapaṃtamiva proccaiḥ priyaṃ kanakakuṃḍalā \|*  
*babhāṣeṃ'tarviniḥśvasya yakṣiṇī sā pativratā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The chaste Yakṣiṇī, Kanakakuṇḍalā, heaved a deep sigh within herself and spoke to her husband who was lamenting loudly:

## \|\| 1.32.29 \|\|

*kanakakuṃḍalovāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ khidyase kāṃta jñānavānasi yadbhavān \|*  
*atropāyo'styapatyāptyai visrabdhamavadhāraya \|\| 29 \|\|*

Kanakakuṇḍalā said:

29\. O my dear, why do you feel aggrieved? You are endowed with knowledge. There is a means of getting a child. Listen with faith.

## \|\| 1.32.30 \|\|

*kimudyamavatāṃ puṃsāṃ durlabhaṃ hi carācare \|*  
*īśvarārpitabuddhīnāṃ sphuṃraṃtyagre manorathāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. To persons who endeavour (for a goal) what is there difficult to be achieved in this world consisting of the mobile and immobile beings? (The way to achieve one’s) desires and ambition flash before persons who have dedicated their intelligence (mind) to God.

## \|\| 1.32.31 \|\|

*daivaṃ hetuṃ vadaṃtyevaṃ bhṛśaṃ kāpuruṣāḥ pate \|*  
*svayaṃ purākṛtaṃ karma daivaṃ tacca na hītarat \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O my dear husband, only contemptible fellows speak of fate as the cause of things. That fate is nothing but the Karma that one has done formerly.

## \|\| 1.32.32 \|\|

*tataḥ pauruṣamālaṃbya tatkarma pariśāṃtaye \|*  
*īśvaraṃ śaraṇaṃ yāyātsarvakāraṇakāraṇam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Hence one should resort to manliness and for the sake of subduing the Karma one should seek refuge in Īśvara, the cause of all causes.

## \|\| 1.32.33 \|\|

*apatyaṃ draviṇaṃ dārā hārā harmya hayā gajāḥ \|*  
*sukhāni svargamokṣau ca na dūre śivabhaktitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Acquisition of child, wealth, wife, necklaces (ornaments), mansions, horses, elephants, all pleasures and even heaven and salvation is not far from devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 1.32.34 \|\|

*vidhātuḥ śāṃbhavīṃ bhaktiṃ priya sarve manorathāḥ \|*  
*siddhayoṣṭau gṛhadvāraṃ sevaṃte nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There is no doubt in this that all desires and the eight Siddhis resort to the doorway of that person who performs devotional rites of Śaṃbhu, O my dear husband.

## \|\| 1.32.35 \|\|

*nārāyaṇopi bhagavānaṃtarātmā jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*carācarāṇāmavitā jātaḥ śrīkaṃṭhasevayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even Nārāyaṇa, the lord and immanent soul of the universe, became the protector of mobile and immobile beings due to the service rendered to Śrīkaṇṭha.

## \|\| 1.32.36 \|\|

*brahmaṇaḥ sṛṣṭikarttṛtvaṃ dattaṃ tenaiva śaṃbhunā \|*  
*iṃdrādayo lokapālā jātā śaṃbhoranugrahāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The status of being the creator was given to Brahmā by Śaṃbhu. Indra and others became the guardians of the worlds.

## \|\| 1.32.37 \|\|

*mṛtyuṃjayaṃ sutaṃ lebhe śilādopyanapatyavān \|*  
*śvetaketurapi prāpa jīvitaṃ kālapāśataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Śilāda who had no child got a son who could conquer death. Śvetaketu too regained his life from the noose of the god of Death.

## \|\| 1.32.38 \|\|

*kṣīrārṇavādhipatitāmupamanyuravāptavān \|*  
*aṃdhakopyabhavadbhṛṃgī gāṇapatyapadorjitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Upamanyu acquired mastery over the Ocean of Milk; Andhaka became Bhṛṅgi with the exalted status of the lordship of Gaṇas.

## \|\| 1.32.39 \|\|

*jigāya śārṅgiṇaṃ saṃkhye dadhīciḥ śaṃbhusevayā \|*  
*prājāpatyapadaṃ prāpa dakṣaḥ saṃśīlya śaṃkaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Dadhīci conquered Śārṅgin (Viṣṇu) due to the service unto Śaṃbhu. By meditating upon Śaṅkara Dakṣa obtained the status of a Prajāpati.

## \|\| 1.32.40 \|\|

*manorathapathātītaṃ yacca vācāmagocaram \|*  
*gocaro gocarīkuryāttatpadaṃ kṣaṇato mṛḍaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If seen, Mṛḍa (Śiva) shall make (the devotee) realize that region which is beyond the ken of wishful thinking and which cannot be expressed in words.

## \|\| 1.32.41 \|\|

*anārādhya maheśānaṃ sarvadaṃ sarvadehinām \|*  
*kopi kvāpi kimapyatra na labheteti niścitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. It is certain that no one will get anything anywhere without propitiating Maheśāna, the bestower of everything on all embodied beings.

## \|\| 1.32.42 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja \|*  
*yadicchasi priyaṃ putraṃ priyasarvajanīnakam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence, if you wish for a dear son who is the most excellent of all persons, seek refuge in Śaṅkara by all means, O dear lord.

## \|\| 1.32.43-44 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vacaḥ patnyāḥ pūrṇabhadraḥ sa yakṣarāṭ \|*  
*ārādhya śrīmahādevaṃ gītajño gītavidyayā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*dinaiḥ katipayaireva paripūrṇamanorathaḥ \|*  
*putrakāmamavāpoccaistasyāṃ patnyāṃ dṛḍhavrataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. On hearing these words of his wife, Pūrṇabhadra, the king of Yakṣas, who was well-versed in music, propitiated Śrī Mahādeva by means of his musical art. Within a few days his desire was fulfilled. He, of steady vows and observances, acquired the desired son from that wife.

## \|\| 1.32.45 \|\|

*nādeśvaraṃ samabhyarcya kaiḥ kairnāpi svaciṃtitam \|*  
*tasmātkāśyāṃ prayatnena sevyo nādeśvaro nṛbhiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. By whom have all desired things not obtained by worshipping Nādeśvara (Oṃkāreśvara)? Hence Nādeśvara is to be earnestly served by men at Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.32.46 \|\|

*aṃtarvatnyatha kālane tatpatnī suṣuve sutam \|*  
*tasya nāma pitā cakre harikeśa iti dvija \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In due course, his pregnant wife delivered a son. The father named him Harikeśa, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.32.47 \|\|

*prītidāyaṃ dadau cātha bhūriputrānanekṣaṇāt \|*  
*pūrṇabhadrastathāgastya hṛṣṭā kanakakuṃḍalā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Agastya, extremely delighted by seeing the face of a son, Pūrṇabhadra and Kanakakuṇḍalā distributed many presents out of pleasure.

## \|\| 1.32.48 \|\|

*bālo'pi pūrṇacaṃdrābha vadano madanopamaḥ \|*  
*vṛddhiṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ prāpa śuklapakṣa ivoḍurāṭ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The child whose countenance was beautiful like the full moon and was like the god of Love (in appearance), went on growing every moment like the moon in the bright half of a month.

## \|\| 1.32.49 \|\|

*yadāṣṭavarṣadeśīyo harikeśo'bhavacchiśuḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ tadāprabhṛtyevaṃ śivamekamamanyata \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When the child Harikeśa was about eight years old, he began to love devoutly Śiva alone.

## \|\| 1.32.50 \|\|

*pāṃsukrīḍanasaktopi kuryālliṃgaṃ rajomayam \|*  
*śādvalaiḥ komalatṛṇaiḥ pūjayecca sa kautukam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Even when he played about in dust, he made Liṅgas out of the dust particles. With all enthusiasm he used to worship (it) with green leaves and tender blades of grass.

## \|\| 1.32.51-54 \|\|

*ākārayati mitrāṇi śivanāmnā'khilāni saḥ \|*  
*caṃdraśekharabhūteśa mṛtyuṃjaya mṛḍeśvaraḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dhūrjaṭe khaṃḍaparaśo mṛḍānīśa trilocana \|*  
*bhargaśaṃbhopaśupate pinākinnugraśaṃkara \|\| 52 \|\|*

*śrīkaṃṭhanīlakaṃṭheśa smarāre pārvatīpate \|*  
*kapālinbhālanayana śūlapāṇe maheśvara \|\| 53 \|\|*

*ajināṃbaradigvāsaḥ svardhunī klinnamaulija \|*  
*virūpākṣāhinepathya gṛṇannāmāvalīmimām \|\| 54 \|\|*

51-54. He used to call all his friends by the names of Śiva, such as Candraśekhara, Bhūteśa, Mṛtyuñjaya, Mṛḍa, Īśvara, Dhūrjaṭi, Khaṇḍaparaśu, Mṛḍānīśa, Trilocana, Bharga, Śaṃbhu, Paśupati, Pinākin, Ugra, Śaṅkara, Śrīkaṇṭha, Nīlakaṇṭha, Īśa, Smarāri, Pārvatīpati, Kapālin, Bhālanayana, Śūlapāṇi, Maheśvara, Ajināṃbara, Digvāsas, Svardhunīklinnamaulija, Virūpākṣa, Ahinepathya. Thus he repeated these names.

## \|\| 1.32.55 \|\|

*savayaskāniti muhuḥ samāhvayati lālayan \|*  
*śabdagrahau na gṛhṇītastasyānyākhyāṃ harādṛte \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He lovingly called his friends thus. His ears never caught hold of anything except the name of Hara.

## \|\| 1.32.56 \|\|

*padbhyāṃ na padyate cānyadṛte bhūteśvarājirāt \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ rūpāṃtaraṃ tasya vīkṣaṇena vicakṣaṇe \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Except the courtyard of Bhūteśvara, his feet never went anywhere else. His eyes were not capable of seeing any other form.

## \|\| 1.32.57 \|\|

*rasayettasya rasanā haranāmākṣarāmṛtam \|*  
*śivāṃghrikamalāmodādghrāṇaṃ naiva jighṛkṣati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. His tongue relished only the nectar of the syllables constituting Hara’s name. His nose never desired to smell anything other than the fragrance of the lotus-like feet of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.32.58 \|\|

*karau tatkautukakarau mano manati nāparam \|*  
*śivasātkṛtyapeyāni pīyate tena saddhiyā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. His hands did only what pleased him. His mind never thought of anything else. All drinks were drunk by him after dedicating them to Śiva with excellent heart.

## \|\| 1.32.59 \|\|

*bhakṣyate sarvabhakṣyāṇi tryakṣapratyakṣagānyapi \|*  
*sarvāvasthāsu sarvatra na sa paśyecchivaṃ vinā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. All foodstuffs were eaten by him only after offering them to the Three-eyed Lord. In all conditions everywhere he never saw anything except Śiva.

## \|\| 1.32.60 \|\|

*gacchangāyansvapaṃstiṣṭhañcchayāno'danpibannapi \|*  
*paritastryakṣamaikṣiṣṭa nānyaṃ bhāvaṃ ciketi saḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. (While) going along, singing, sleeping, standing, lying down, eating or drinking, he saw the Three-eyed Lord alone. He never noticed any other object.

## \|\| 1.32.61 \|\|

*kṣaṇadāsu prasuptopi kva yāsīti vadanmuhuḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ tryakṣa pratīkṣasva budhyatīti sa bālakaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. During the nights, when asleep, the boy used to wake up frequently saying, “O Three-eyed One, wait for a moment. Where do you go?”

## \|\| 1.32.62-70 \|\|

*spaṣṭāṃ ceṣṭāṃ vilokyeti harikeśasya tatpitā \|*  
*aśikṣayatsutaṃ so'tha gṛhakarmarato bhava \|\| 62 \|\|*

*ete turaṃgamā vatsa tavaite'śvakiśo rakāḥ \|*  
*citrāṇīmāni vāsāṃsi sudukūlānyamūni ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

*ratnānyākaraśuddhāni nānājātīnyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*kupyaṃ bahuvidhaṃ caitadgodhanāni mahāṃti ca \|\| 64 \|\|*

*amatrāṇi mahārhāṇi raupya kāṃsyamayāni ca \|*  
*paṇanīyāni vastūni nānādeśodbhavānyapi \|\| 65 \|\|*

*cāmarāṇi vicitrāṇi gaṃdhadravyāṇyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*etānyanyāni bahuśastvaneke dhānyarāśayaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*etattvadīyaṃ sakalaṃvastujātaṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*arthopārjanavidyāśca sarvāḥ śikṣasva putraka \|\| 67 \|\|*

*ceṣṭāstyaja daridrāṇāṃ dhūlidhūsariṇāmamūḥ \|*  
*abhyasyavidyāḥ sakalā bhogānnirviśya cottamān \|\| 68 \|\|*

*tāṃ daśāṃ caramāṃ prāpya bhaktiyogaṃ tataścara \|*  
*asakṛcchikṣitaḥ pitretyavamanya gurorgiram \|\| 69 \|\|*

*ruṣṭadṛṣṭiṃ ca janakaṃ kadācidavalokya saḥ \|*  
*nirjagāma gṛhādbhīto harikeśa udāradhīḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

62-70. On seeing thus the clear activities of Harikeśa, his father taught him thus: “Be engaged in domestic activities. O dear child, these horses and colts are yours. These clothes of variegated colours, these silk clothes too are yours. The gems are pure, direct from their very source. They are of diverse kinds. These crystal wares too are yours. (Yours) is the ample wealth of cattle. There are very valuable vessels of silver, brass etc. There are many articles of trade originating from various parts of the land. There are wonderful chowries and many sweet-smelling articles. There are heaps of different kinds of grains. All these articles are your own. O son, learn all the lores helpful in the earning of wealth. Eschew these activities of the indigent people always soiled with dust. Practise all lores and enjoy excellent pleasures. After attaining the closing days of your life, you can adopt this Bhaktiyoga.”

Though advised thus many times by his father, he disregarded the words of his guardian. Once when he saw his father with eyes blazing angrily, Harikeśa of liberal views and ideas became afraid and went out of his house.

## \|\| 1.32.71-73 \|\|

*tataściṃtāmavāpoccairdigbhrāṃtimapi cāptavān \|*  
*aho bāliśabuddhitvātkutastyaktaṃ gṛhaṃ mayā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*kva yāmi kva sthite śaṃbho mama śreyo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*pitrā nirvāsitaścāhaṃ na ca vedmyatha kiṃcana \|\| 72 \|\|*

*iti śrutaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ piturutsaṃgavartinā \|*  
*gadatastātapurataḥ kasyacidvacanaṃ sphuṭam \|\| 73 \|\|*

71-73. He then became confounded as to the direction to be taken and began to reflect, ‘Alas, puerile in intelligence, the house has been left off by me! Where shall I go? O Śaṃbhu, where shall I stay, so that it will be conducive to my weal? I have been banished by my father. I do not know anything. Formerly the following (didactic utterance) was heard by me lying on the lap of my father, clearly spoken by someone to my father.

Recollected Advice (74-83)

## \|\| 1.32.74-75 \|\|

*mātrā pitrā parityaktā ye tyaktā nijabaṃdhubhiḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti teṣāṃ vārāṇasī gatiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*jarayā paribhūtā ye ye vyādhivikalīkṛtāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti teṣāṃ vārāṇasī gatiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. “Vārāṇasī is their ultimate resort. Those who are forsaken by mothers and fathers, those who are forsaken by their own kinsmen, those who have nowhere else to go, those who are afflicted with old age, those who are crippled or disabled by sickness, those who have nowhere else to go, Vārāṇasī is their ultimate resort.

## \|\| 1.32.76 \|\|

*pade pade samākrāṃtā ye vipadbhiraharniśam \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti teṣāṃvārāṇasī gatiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Those who are assailed by adversities day and night, at every step, those who have nowhere else to go, Vārāṇasī is their ultimate resort.

## \|\| 1.32.77 \|\|

*pāparāśibhirākrāṃtā ye dāridrya parājitāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti teṣāṃ vārāṇasī gatiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Those who are overwhelmed by heaps of sins, those who are beaten down by poverty, those who have nowhere else to go, Vārāṇasī is their ultimate resort.

## \|\| 1.32.78 \|\|

*saṃsāra bhayabhītāya ye ye baddhāḥ karmabaṃdhanaiḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti teṣāṃ vārāṇasī gatiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Those who are afraid of the danger of worldly existence, those who are bound by fetters of Karma, those who have nowhere else to go, Vārāṇasī is their ultimate resort.

## \|\| 1.32.79 \|\|

*śrutismṛtivihīnā ye śaucācāravivarjitāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti teṣāṃ vārāṇasī gatiḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Those who are bereft of Śrutis and Smṛtis, those who have forsaken rules of cleanliness and good conduct, those who have nowhere else to go, Vārāṇasī is their ultimate resort.

## \|\| 1.32.80 \|\|

*ye ca yogaparibhraṣṭāstapo dāna vivarjitāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti teṣāṃ vārāṇasī gatiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Those who have slipped down from the practice of Yoga, those who have eschewed austerities and desisted from making monetary gifts, those who have nowhere else to go, Vārāṇasī is their ultimate goal.

## \|\| 1.32.81 \|\|

*madhye baṃdhujane yeṣāmapamānaṃ pade pade \|*  
*teṣāmānaṃdadaṃ caikaṃ śaṃbhorānaṃdakānanam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Those who encounter insult at every step in the midst of their kinsmen, to them the only thing that gives delight is the Ānandakānana of Śaṃbhu.

## \|\| 1.32.82 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānane yeṣāṃ rucirvai vasatāṃ satām \|*  
*viśveśānugṛhītānāṃ teṣāmānaṃdajodayaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Those good people who take delight in residing in Ānandakānana are blessed by Viśveśa and they have special delight.

## \|\| 1.32.83 \|\|

*bharjyate karmabījāni yatra viśveśavahninā \|*  
*ato mahāśmaśānaṃ tadagatīnāṃ parā gatiḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. That Mahāśmaśāna is the greatest resort to those who have nowhere to go, because there the seeds of Karma are roasted by the fire of Viśveśa.”

## \|\| 1.32.84-85 \|\|

*harikeśo vicāryeti yāto vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*yatrāvimukte jaṃtūnāṃ tyajatāṃ pārthivīṃ tanum \|\| 84 \|\|*

*punarno tanusaṃbaṃdhastanudveṣiprasādataḥ \|*  
*ānaṃdavanamāsādya sa tapaḥ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. After reflecting thus, Harikeśa went to the city of Vārāṇasī. In this Avimukta the creatures that eschew their earthly bodies, do not have any further contact with bodies, by the grace of Tanudveṣin (‘Hater of bodies’, Śiva). After reaching Ānandavana he resorted to austerities.

## \|\| 1.32.86 \|\|

*atha kālāṃtare śaṃbhuḥ praviśyānaṃdakānamam \|*  
*pārvatyai darśayāmāsa nijamākrīḍakānanam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. After some time, Śaṃbhu entered Ānandakānana and pointed out to Pārvatī his own pleasure grove of sport.

Description of the Pleasure Grove (87-110)

## \|\| 1.32.87 \|\|

*amaṃdāmodamaṃdāraṃ kovidārapariṣkṛtam \|*  
*cārucaṃpakacūtāḍhyaṃ protphullanavamallikam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. There were Mandāra flowers of excessive fragrance. It was adorned by Kovidāras. It was filled with beautiful Caṃpakas and Cūtas. Fresh Mallikās (jasmine) were in full-bloom.

## \|\| 1.32.88 \|\|

*vikasanmālatījālaṃ karavīravirājitam \|*  
*prasphuṭatketakivanaṃ prodyatkurabakorjitam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Mālatī was blooming there. It was shining with Karavīra. The groves of Ketakī flowers were in full-bloom. There were plenty of full-blown Kurabaka flowers.

## \|\| 1.32.89 \|\|

*jṛṃbhadvicakilāmodaṃ lasatkaṃkelipallavam \|*  
*navamallīparimalākṛṣṭaṣaṭpadanāditam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The fragrance of blooming Vicakila (a kind of jasmine) spread everywhere. The tender sprouts of Kaṅkelī (Aśoka) over-hung the trees. The grove was echoing with the humming of bees, attracted by the fragrance of Navamallī.

## \|\| 1.32.90 \|\|

*puṣpyapunnāganikaraṃ bakulāmodamoditam \|*  
*medasvipāṭalāmoda sadāmodita diṅmukham \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. There were many Punnāgas putting forth flowers. The grove was rendered fragrant by the sweet scent of Bakulas. All the quarters were sweetened by the scent of succulent Pāṭala flowers.

## \|\| 1.32.91 \|\|

*bahuśolaṃbirolaṃba mālāmālitabhūtalam \|*  
*calaccaṃdanaśākhāgra ramamāṇapi kākulam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The whole ground appeared to be garlanded by the swarms of bees hanging down in groups. It was pervaded by groups of cuckoos sporting about on the tips of moving Candana branches.

## \|\| 1.32.92 \|\|

*guruṇā'guruṇāmatta bhadrajātivihaṃgamam \|*  
*nāgakesaraśākhāstha śālabhaṃji vinoditam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. There birds of excellent variety were intoxicated as it were by the black Aguru. It was fancifully pleasant with dolls kept on the branches of Nāgakesara.

## \|\| 1.32.93 \|\|

*merutuṃga namerusthacchāyākrīḍitakiṃnaram \|*  
*kiṃnarīmithunodgītaṃ gānavacchukakiṃśukam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. In the shade of Nameru trees as tall as Meru, Kinnaras were sporting about. Pairs of Kinnarīs were singing loudly. Palāśa trees had a number of parrots of sweet voice.

## \|\| 1.32.94 \|\|

*kadaṃbānāṃ kadaṃbeṣu guṃjadrolaṃbayugmakam \|*  
*jitasauvarṇavarṇocca karṇikāravirājitam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Pairs of bees were humming among the clusters of Kadamba trees. The grove shone with Karṇikāra trees whose colour surpassed even the colour of gold.

## \|\| 1.32.95 \|\|

*śālatālatamālālī hiṃtālī lakucāvṛtam \|*  
*lasatsaptacchadāmodaṃ kharjūrīrājirājitam \|*  
*nārikela tarucchanna nāraṃgīrāgaraṃjitam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. It was covered with Śāla, Tāla, clusters of Tamāla, Hintālī and Lakuca trees. The fragrance of Saptacchada trees spread everywhere. A number of Kharjuri trees made it shine. It was covered with coconut trees. The red colour of Nāraṅgīs gave it a beautiful hue.

## \|\| 1.32.96 \|\|

*phalijaṃbīranikaraṃ madhūkamadhupākulam \|*  
*śālmalī śītalacchāyaṃ picumaṃda mahāvanam \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. There were many fruit-bearing Jambīra trees. Bees hovered round Madhūka flowers and hummed loudly. Śālmalī trees had plenty of cool shade. There were great groves of Picumanda (Neem) trees.

## \|\| 1.32.97 \|\|

*madhurāmoda damanacchannaṃ marubanoditam \|*  
*lavalīlolalīlābhṛnmaṃdamārutalolitam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. It was covered with Damana flowers of very sweet scent. It was brilliant with clusters of Marubaka. Gentle wind blew there gracefully shaking the Lavalī creepers.

## \|\| 1.32.98 \|\|

*bhillī hallīsakaprīti jhillīrāvavirāviṇam \|*  
*kvacitsaraḥ parisarakrīḍatkroḍakadaṃbakam \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The grove reverberated with the sound of Jhillī’s (crickets) that pleasantly accompanied the Hallīsaka dance of the Bhilla (tribal) women. In certain places broods of pigs were playing about in the lakes.

## \|\| 1.32.99 \|\|

*marālīgalanālīstha bisāsaktasitacchadam \|*  
*viśokakokamithunakrīḍākreṃkārasuṃdaram \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Male swans were eagerly attracted by the lotus stalks round the neck of female swans. The pleasure grove appeared beautiful when the grief-free Koka (Cakravāka) pairs sported about producing Kreṅkāra sounds.

## \|\| 1.32.100 \|\|

*bakaśāvakasaṃcāraṃ lakṣmaṇāsakta sārasam \|*  
*mattabarhiṇasaṃghuṣṭaṃ kapiṃjalakulākulam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Young ones of Bakas (cranes) moved here and there. Sārasa birds were attached to their mates, Lakṣmaṇās (female Sārasas). Intoxicated peacocks cried loudly. Kapiñjala made the grove agitated.

## \|\| 1.32.101 \|\|

*jīvaṃjīvalasajjīvaṃ kvaṇatkāraṃḍavotkaṭam \|*  
*dīrghikāvārisaṃcāri śītamāruta vījitam \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The living beings there were happy due to the Jīvañjīva birds; the chirping Karaṇḍava birds spread everywhere. The cool wind blowing over the waters of the lake fanned the entire grove.

## \|\| 1.32.102 \|\|

*madāṃdolitakahlāra parāgaparipiṃgalam \|*  
*ullasatpaṃkajamukhaṃ nīleṃdīvaralocanam \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. It was turned reddish yellow due to the pollen dust from the gently moving Kelhāra flowers. The blooming lotuses were its face. The blue lotuses were its eyes.

## \|\| 1.32.103 \|\|

*tamālakabarībhāraṃ vilasaddāḍimīradam \|*  
*bhramarālīlasadbhrūkaṃ śukanāsāvirājitam \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. The Tamāla trees constituted its tresses. The shining Dāḍimīs were its teeth. The swarms of bees were its brows. The parrots provided it with splendid nose.

## \|\| 1.32.104 \|\|

*mahāṃdhuśravaṇaṃ dūrvā śmaśrubhiḥ pariśobhitam \|*  
*kamalāmodaniḥśvāsaṃ biṃbīphala radacchadam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The great wells were its ears. It was splendid with Dūrvā grass resembling moustache. The sweet scent of the lotus flowers was its breath. The Biṃbī fruit was its lips.

## \|\| 1.32.105 \|\|

*supadmapatravasanaṃ karṇikāravibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*kamrakaṃbu lasatkaṃṭhaṃ śaṃkaraskaṃdha baṃdhuram \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The excellent lotus leaves were its clothe; Karṇikāras were ornaments. The beautiful Kaṃbu tree is its graceful neck. The Śaṅkara tree constitutes the undulating portions of the shoulders.

## \|\| 1.32.106 \|\|

*gaṃdhasārasamāsaktā hīna dordaṃḍamaṃḍitam \|*  
*aśokapallavāṃguṣṭhaṃ ketakīnakharojjvalam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The great serpent ensconced in the sandalwood tree is the staff-like arm, that adorns it. The tender sprouts of Aśoka function as the thumb; and Ketakī is the brilliant nail.

## \|\| 1.32.107 \|\|

*lasatkaṃṭhīravoraskaṃ gaṃḍaśailapṛthūdaram \|*  
*jalāvartalasannābhi tarujaṃghā yugānvitam \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. The graceful lion constitutes its chest and the boulder the big belly. The whirlpool makes its shining navel and the pair of trees, the pair of calves.

## \|\| 1.32.108 \|\|

*sthalabhākpadmacaraṇaṃ mattamātaṃgagāminam \|*  
*lasatkadalikedāradalaccīnāṃśukāvṛtam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The resplendent leaves of the plantain trees function like the Chinese silk-cloth that covers it. The ground lotuses make its feet and the intoxicated elephant accounts for its majestic walk.

## \|\| 1.32.109 \|\|

*nānāsukumamālābhirmālitaṃ ca samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*akaṃṭakitarucchannaṃ mahiṣa śvāpadāvṛtam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Various kinds of flowers make it garlanded as it were. It is completely covered with buffaloes and beasts of prey concealed by trees without thorn.

## \|\| 1.32.110 \|\|

*caṃdrakāṃtaśilāsuptakṛṣṇaiṇaharitoḍupam \|*  
*taruprakīrṇakusuma jitasvarlokatārakam \|*  
*darśayannitthamākrīḍaṃ devyai devoviśadvanam \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. The black antelope that was asleep on the lunar cystals (as if) darkened the moon there. The flowers that were scattered by the trees excelled the stars in the heaven. The Lord entered the grove pointing out the pleasure-garden to the goddess thus.

## \|\| 1.32.111 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*yathāpriyatamā devi mama tvaṃ sarvasuṃdari \|*  
*tathā priyataraṃ caitanme sadānaṃdakānanam \|\| 111 \|\|*

The Lord of Devas said:

111\. O beautiful goddess, (though to a lesser degree than you) just as you are the most beloved of mine, this Ānandakānana is always dear to me.

## \|\| 1.32.112 \|\|

*atrānaṃdavane devi mṛtānāṃ madanugrahāt \|*  
*vapustvamṛtatāṃ prāptamapunarbhavinastu te \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. O goddess, the body of those who die here in the Ānandavana becomes immortal through my grace. They are not reborn.

## \|\| 1.32.113 \|\|

*bhavino ye vipadyaṃte vārāṇasyāṃ mamājñayā \|*  
*teṣāṃ bījāni dagdhāni śmaśānajvaladagninā \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. The seeds of those who are born and who die in Vārāṇasī become burned through my behest by the fire blazing in the cremation ground.

## \|\| 1.32.114 \|\|

*mahāśmaśāne ye prāptā dīrghanidrāṃ girīṃdraje \|*  
*na punargarbhaśayane te svapaṃti kadācana \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. O daughter of the Lord of Mountains, those who sleep the long sleep (i.e. die) in Mahāśmaśāna never again lie and sleep in the womb.

## \|\| 1.32.115 \|\|

*brahmajñānena mucyaṃte nānyathā jaṃtavaḥ kvacit \|*  
*brahmajñānamaye kṣetre prayāge vā tanutyajaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Creatures become liberated through the knowledge of Brahma and not otherwise anywhere. Those who cast off their bodies in Prayāga or in the holy spot according realization of Brahma (also become liberated).

## \|\| 1.32.116 \|\|

*brahmajñānaṃ tadevāhaṃ kāśīsaṃsthitibhāginām \|*  
*diśāmi tārakaṃ prāṃte mucyaṃte te tu tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Towards the end of their life, I give the Tāraka Mantra, which is the knowledge of Brahman, to those who die in Kāśī. They become liberated at the very same moment.

## \|\| 1.32.117 \|\|

*gṛhṇīyuḥ pāpakarmāṇi kāśīmṛtaviniṃdakāḥ \|*  
*sukṛtāni stutikṛto mucyaṃte te'tra jaṃtavaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. The people who ridicule those who die at Kāśī take up their sins. Those who praise take up their merit. Those creatures become liberated here.

## \|\| 1.32.118 \|\|

*brahmajñānaṃ kuto devi kalinopahatātmanām \|*  
*svabhāvacaṃcalākṣāṇāṃ tadbrahmeha diśāmyaham \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Whence, O goddess, is the realization of Brahman to those who have been overwhelmed by Kali and whose sense-organs are naturally fickle? Hence I give them Brahma (knowledge) here.

## \|\| 1.32.119 \|\|

*yogino yogavibhraṣṭāḥ pataṃtyaiśvaryamohitāḥ \|*  
*kāśyāṃ patitvā na punaḥ pataṃtyapi mahālaye \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Yogins who become deluded by their Siddhi-powers fall off from the Yogic exercise. But those who fall (die) in Kāśī do not fall again even in the great annihilation (Mahālaya).

## \|\| 1.32.120 \|\|

*brahmajñānaṃ na viṃdaṃti yogairekena janmanā \|*  
*janmanaikena mucyaṃte kāśyāmaṃtakṛto janāḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Through Yogic practice people do not get the knowledge of Brahman in the course of a single birth; but those people who meet with death in Kāśī become liberated in a single birth.

## \|\| 1.32.121 \|\|

*yatheha mucyate jaṃturgirije madanugrahāt \|*  
*avimukte mahākṣetre na tathānyatra kutracit \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. O Girijā, nowhere else is a creature liberated in the manner as it is liberated in the great holy spot Avimukta with my favour.

## \|\| 1.32.122 \|\|

*bahujanmasamabhyāsādyogī mucyeta vā na vā \|*  
*mṛtamātro vimucyeta kāśyāmekena janmanā \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. After practising properly Yoga for many births, a Yogī may or may not become liberated. But the person who dies in Kāśī becomes immediately liberated in a single birth.

## \|\| 1.32.123 \|\|

*na sidhyati kalau yogo na sidhyati kalau tapaḥ \|*  
*nyāyārjitadhanotsargaḥ sadyaḥ sidhyetkalau naraḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. In Kaliyuga Yoga does not fructify. In Kaliyuga penance does not become effective. But a man gifting away the wealth obtained by legitimate means becomes successful immediately.

## \|\| 1.32.124 \|\|

*na vrataṃ na tapo nejyā na japo na surārcanam \|*  
*dānameva kalau muktyai kāśīdānairavāpyate \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Neither holy rite, nor austerity, neither sacrifice nor Japa nor the worship of the deitites (becomes fruitful). Dāna (relgious gift) alone is conducive to liberation and Kāśī is obtained through Dānas.

## \|\| 1.32.125 \|\|

*kalau viśveśvaro devaḥ kalau vārāṇasī purī \|*  
*kalau bhāgīrathī gaṃgā kalau dānaṃ viśiṣyate \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. In Kaliyuga, Lord Viśveśvara, the city of Vārāṇasī, Gaṅgā Bhāgīrathī and Dāna (religious gift) are of special significance.

## \|\| 1.32.126 \|\|

*gaṃgottaravahākāśyāṃ liṃgaṃ viśveśvaraṃ mama \|*  
*ubhe vimuktide puṃsāṃ prāpye dānabalātkalau \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Gaṅgā flowing towards the North at Kāśī and my Liṅga named Viśveśvara in Kāśī, are the two which bestow salvation on men and they are to be attained in Kaliyuga through the power of Dāna.

## \|\| 1.32.127 \|\|

*puṇyavānitaro vāpi mama kṣetrasya sevayā \|*  
*mukto bhavati deveśi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. A man of meritorious deeds and another even otherwise, becomes liberated, O goddess of Devas, by resorting to my holy spot. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 1.32.128 \|\|

*avimuktasya māhātmyātpuṇyapāpena karmaṇā \|*  
*devi prabhavataḥ puṃsāmapijanmaśatārjite \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. O goddess, due to the greatness of Avimukta neither Puṇya (merit) nor Pāpa (sin) become effective though acquired by persons in the course of a hundred births through Karmas.

## \|\| 1.32.129 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ na moktavyaṃ tasmāddevi mumukṣuṇā \|*  
*hanyamānena bahudhā hyupasargaśatairapi \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Hence, O goddess, Avimukta should not be left off by a person desirous of salvation, though assailed in diverse ways by hundreds of obstacles.

## \|\| 1.32.130 \|\|

*vidhāya kṣetrasaṃnyāsaṃ ye vasaṃtīha mānavāḥ \|*  
*jīvanmuktāstu te devi teṣāṃ vighnaṃ harāmyaham \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. After performing the rite of Kṣetrasannyāsa (permanent residence in a holy place) those men who continue to stay here are Jīvanmuktas (‘living-liberated souls’), O goddess; I remove their obstacles.

## \|\| 1.32.131 \|\|

*na yogināṃ hṛdākāśe na kailāse na maṃdare \|*  
*tathā vāsaratirme'sti yathā kāśyāṃ ratirmama \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. I am not as much interested in staying in the firmament of the heart of Yogins, on Kailāsa or on Mandāra, as I am attached to staying in Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.32.132 \|\|

*kāśīvāsi jano devi mama garbhe vasetsadā \|*  
*atastaṃ mocayāmyaṃte pratijñeyaṃ yato mama \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. O goddess, the citizens of Kāśī always stay in my belly. Hence I release them in the end, because this is my promise.

## \|\| 1.32.133 \|\|

*tāmasīṃ prakṛtiṃ prāpya kālo bhūtvā carācaram \|*  
*grasāmi līlayā devi kāśīṃ rakṣāmi yatnataḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Adopting Tāmasī Prakṛti and becoming Kāla (god of Death), I sportingly swallow the mobile and immobile beings, (but) O goddess, I protect Kāśī scrupulously.

## \|\| 1.32.134 \|\|

*premapātradvayaṃ devi nitarāṃ netaranmama \|*  
*tvaṃ vā tapodhane gauri kāśī vānaṃdabhūmikā \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. O Gaurī, there are two recipients of my intense love, viz. you having austere penance as your asset and Kāśī, the place of delight (Ānanda-bhūmikā) and (none) else.

## \|\| 1.32.135 \|\|

*vinā kāśī na me sthānaṃ vinā kāśī na me ratiḥ \|*  
*vinā kāśī na nirvāṇaṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Excepting Kāśī, I have no abode; excepting Kāśī I have no attachment for anything else. Without Kāśī there is no salvation (This the truth). I am stating the truth.

## \|\| 1.32.136 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍagolake yadvanmuktiḥ kāśyāṃ vyavasthitā \|*  
*aṣṭāṃgayogayuktyā vā na tathā helayā'nyataḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. In this Cosmic Egg, neither through the adoption of Aṣṭāṅga Yoga nor through any other means has liberation been achieved as in a playful way at Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.32.137 \|\|

*iti bruvāṇo deveśo harikeśamavaikṣata \|*  
*madhye vanaṃ tapasyaṃtamaśokatarumūlagam \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. While saying these things, the Lord of Devas saw Harikeśa performing penance seated at the root of an Aśoka tree.

Description of the Sage (138-144):

## \|\| 1.32.138 \|\|

*śuṣkasnāyupinaddhāsthi saṃcayaṃ niścalākṛtim \|*  
*valmīkakīṭakākoṭiśoṣitāsṛgasṛgdharam \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. The collection of his bones was bound together with dried tendons and sinews. He was motionless, while ants, moles and other worms had dried up the blood in his veins.

## \|\| 1.32.139 \|\|

*nirmāṃsakīkasacayaṃ sphaṭikopalaniścalam \|*  
*śaṃkhakuṃdeṃdutuhina mahāśaṃkhalasacchriyam \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. The skeleton of bones that he was, he had no flesh at all. He was steady like a crystal column. The lustre that issued from him was that of a conch, Kunda flower, the moon, snow and a oyster shell.

## \|\| 1.32.140 \|\|

*satvāvalaṃbitaprāṇamāyuḥśeṣeṇarakṣitam \|*  
*niḥśvāsocchāsapavanavṛttisūcitajīvitam \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. His very vital breath appeared to be sustained through his inner strength and he was kept alive only because he was destined to live for some more time. The fact that he was alive was indicated by the continuity of his breath.

## \|\| 1.32.141 \|\|

*nimeṣonmeṣasaṃcāra piśunīkṛtajaṃtukam \|*  
*piṃgatārasphuradraśmi netradīpita diṅmukham \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. The winking of his eyes rendered the animals around aware of his being alive. He had illuminated the quarters through the eyes emitting rays from the tawny eyeballs.

## \|\| 1.32.142 \|\|

*tattapogniśikhādāva cuṃbitamlānakānanam \|*  
*tatsaumyadṛksudhāvarṣa saṃsiktā'khilabhūruham \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. The whole forest became faded as it were on being touched by the flames of the forest-fire of penance. All the trees became sprinkled with the shower of nectar from his gentle eyes.

## \|\| 1.32.143 \|\|

*sākṣāttapasyaṃtamiva tapo dhṛtvā narākṛtim \|*  
*nirākṛtiṃ nirākāṃkṣaṃ kṛtvā bhaktiṃ ca kāṃcana \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. He appeared to be directly the rite of penance incarnate in human form, who had adopted an indescribable form of devotion without any specific motive in view, and had begun to perform penance.

## \|\| 1.32.144 \|\|

*kuraṃgaśāvairgaṇaśo bhramadbhiḥ parivāritam \|*  
*nitāṃtabhīṣaṇāsyaiśca paṃcāsyaiḥ parirakṣitam \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. He was surrounded by fawns of deer wandering in groups. He appeared to be protected by wide-jawed lions of excessively terrible faces.

## \|\| 1.32.145-146 \|\|

*taṃ tathābhūtamālokya devī devaṃ vyajijñapat \|*  
*vareṇacchaṃdayeśāmuṃ nijabhaktaṃ tapasvinam \|\| 145 \|\|*

*tvadekacittaṃ tvadadhīnajīvitaṃ tvadekakarmāṇamamuṃ tvadāśrayam \|*  
*tīvraistapobhiḥ pariśuṣkavigrahaṃ kuruṣva yakṣasya vairaranugraham \|\| 146 \|\|*

145-146. On seeing him in such a plight, the goddess submitted to the Lord: “O Lord, fulfil the desire of this devotee of yours by means of the proper boon. He has concentrated his mind in you alone. His very life is under your power. His activities are for your own sake. He considers you as his support and his body is completely dried through very severe austerities. Do bless him through boons granted to this Yakṣa.”

## \|\| 1.32.147 \|\|

*devo vṛṣeṃdrādavaruhya devyā śailādinā dattakarāvalaṃbaḥ \|*  
*samādhisaṃkocitanetrapatraṃ pasparśa hastena dayārdracetāḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. Accompanied by the goddess, the Lord got down holding the hand proffered by Śailādi (Nandikeśvara). The Lord, with his mind melting with pity, touched the sage who had his eyes closed in the course of his meditation.

## \|\| 1.32.148 \|\|

*tataḥ sa yakṣo vinimīlya cakṣuṣī tryakṣaṃ puro vīkṣya samakṣamātmanaḥ \|*  
*udyatsahasrāṃśu sahasratejasaṃ jagāda harṣākula gadgadākṣaram \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. The Yakṣa opened his eyes and saw in front of him the Three-eyed Lord having the refulgence of a thousand rising suns. He then spoke with the words choked in his excitement due to delight:

## \|\| 1.32.149 \|\|

*jayeśa śaṃbho girijeśa śaṃkara triśūlapāṇe śaśikhaṃḍaśekhara \|*  
*sparśatkṛpālo tava pāṇipaṃkajaṃ prāpyāmṛtībhūtatanūlato'bhavam \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. “Victory unto you, O Īśa, Śaṃbhu, Lord of Girijā, O Śaṅkara, O trident-handed one, O lord with the crescent moon as crest-jewel. O compassionate one, being touched by your lotus-like hand my tender body has become immortal.”

## \|\| 1.32.150 \|\|

*śrutvoditāṃ tasya maheśvaro giraṃ mṛdvīkayā sāmyamupeyuṣīṃ mṛdu \|*  
*bhaktasya dhīrasya mahātaponidhe dadau varāṇāṃ nikara tadā mudā \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. On hearing the soft-spoken utterance of that intelligent devotee, bearing comparison to a grape fruit, O great sage (Agastya), the great Lord joyously granted a number of boons (to him):

## \|\| 1.32.151 \|\|

*kṣetrasya yakṣāsya mama priyasya me bhavādhunā daṃḍadharo varānmama \|*  
*sthirastvamadyādi durātmadaṃḍakaḥ supālakaḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ ca matpriyaḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. “With my blessing, O Yakṣa, be the permanent Daṇḍadhara (‘Wielder of the rod of justice’) of this holy spot that is dear to me. From today onwards you shall be my favourite one, the punisher of the wicked and the good protector of the meritorious.

## \|\| 1.32.152 \|\|

*tvaṃ daṃḍapāṇirbhava nāmato'dhunā sarvāngaṇāñchādhi mamājñayotkaṭān \|*  
*gaṇāvimau tvāmanuyāyinau sadā nāmnā yathārthau nṛṣu saṃbhramodbhramau \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. Now you shall be named Daṇḍapāṇi. At my behest control the ferocious Gaṇas. These two attendants shall always follow you. Their names are true to their meaning, viz. Saṃbhrama and Udbhrama (because they create great and excessive excitement) to men.

## \|\| 1.32.153-154 \|\|

*tvamaṃtyabhūṣāṃ kuru kāśivāsināṃ gale sunīlāṃ bhujageṃdra kaṃkaṇām \|*  
*bhālesu netrāṃ karikṛttivāsasaṃ vāmekṣaṇālakṣita vāmabhāgām \|\| 153 \|\|*

*maulau lasatpiṃgakapardabhāriṇī vibhūtisaṃkṣālita puṇyavigrahām \|*  
*ahohimāṃśoḥ kalayā lasacchriyaṃ vṛṣeṃdralīlā gatimaṃdagāminīm \|\| 154 \|\|*

153-154. You are to give the final embellishment to the residents of Kāśī, consisting of a blue mark in the neck, snakes for bracelets, a fine eye in the forehead, wearing the hide of an elephant and the left side characterised by (the presence of) a beautiful woman. On the head, the tawny matted hairs shall be had; the meritorious body should be smeared with ash and lo, the whole body should have a fine splendour with the digit of the crescent moon and moving in slow gait like that of a graceful bull.

## \|\| 1.32.155 \|\|

*tvamannadaḥ kāśinivāsināṃ sadā tvaṃ prāṇado jñānada eka eva hi \|*  
*tvaṃ mokṣado manmukhasūpadeśatastvaṃ niścalāṃ sadvasatiṃ vidhāsyasi \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. You are always the bestower of cooked food to the residents of Kāśī; you alone infuse them with vital breath; you grant them knowledge; you grant them salvation through the advice from my mouth; you will give them a steady and permanent abode.

## \|\| 1.32.156 \|\|

*tvaṃ vighnapūgaiḥ paripīḍya pāpinaḥ saṃbhrātimutpādya vineṣyase bahiḥ \|*  
*ānīya bhaktānkṣaṇatopidūrato muktiṃ parāṃ dāpayitāsi piṃgala \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. O Pīṅgala (‘tawny-complexioned one through penance’), you will harass sinners completely and creating confusion among them, you will drive them out (of Vārāṇasī). In a moment you will bring devotees from afar. You will be the bestower of salvation (on them).

## \|\| 1.32.157 \|\|

*tvatsātkṛte kṣetravare hi yakṣarāṭkastvāmanārādhya vimuktibhājanam \|*  
*sabhājanaṃ pūrvata eva te carettataḥ samarcāṃ mama bhakta ācaret \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. Since the excellent holy place has been entrusted to you, who can have salvation without worshipping you? My devotee must at first propitiate you and only then adore me.

## \|\| 1.32.158 \|\|

*tvaṃ grāmavāsaprada eva me pure'dhyakṣastvamedhīha ca daṃḍanāyakaḥ \|*  
*duṣṭānsamudghāṭaya kāśivairiṇaḥ kāśīṃ purīṃ rakṣa sadā mudānvitaḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. In my city you will bestow residence (to the devotees). You be the officer-in-charge of justice. Eradicate the evil-minded enemies of Kāśī and guard Kāśī forever joyously.

## \|\| 1.32.159 \|\|

*pūrṇabhadrasutadaṃḍanāyaka tryakṣayakṣaharikeśa piṃgala \|*  
*kāśivāsa vasatāṃ sadānnadajñānamokṣadagaṇāgraṇīrbhava \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. O son of Pūrṇabhadra, O Daṇḍanāyaka, O Yakṣa of the tree-eyed lord, O Harikeśa, O Piṅgala, O bestower of cooked food on all those who stay in Kāśī, be the leader of the Gaṇas, the bestower of knowledge and salvation.

## \|\| 1.32.160 \|\|
