*madbhaktiyuktopi vinā tvadīyāṃ bhaktiṃ na kāśī vasatiṃ labheta \|*  
*gaṇeṣu deveṣu hi mānaveṣu tadagramānyo bhava daṃḍapāṇe \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. Even a person highly devoted to me shall not get an opportunity to stay in Kāśī without devotion to you. Hence, O Daṇḍapāṇi, be the chief recipient of honour among the Gaṇas, Devas and men.

## \|\| 1.32.161 \|\|

*jñānodatīrthe vihitodakakriyo yastvāṃ samārādhayitā gaṇeśam \|*  
*sa eva loke kṛtakṛtyatāmagānmamātulānugrahato'tra puṇyavān \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. Only he who, after performing the rites of libation in the Jñānoda Tīrtha (i.e., Jñānavāpī), propitiates you, the chief of the Gaṇas, shall be fully satisfied as having done his duty. With the unparalleled blessings of mine, he shall be meritorious.

## \|\| 1.32.162 \|\|

*tvaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi daṃḍapāṇe sadaiva me netrasamakṣamatra \|*  
*tvaṃ daṃḍayanprāṇabhṛto durīhānihāsvanṝnsvānabhayaṃ diśanvai \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. O Daṇḍapāṇi, you be here always in the southern direction, just in front of my eyes, punishing living beings of wicked activites and granting freedom from fear to your own men. Stay here.”

## \|\| 1.32.163 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*iti dattvā varānvipra girīśo daṃḍapāṇaye \|*  
*vṛṣeṃdramadhiruhyātha viveśānaṃdakānanam \|\| 163 \|\|*

Skanda said:

163\. O Brāhmaṇa, after granting the boons to Daṇḍapāṇi thus, Giriśa mounted his excellent bull and entered Ānandakānana.

## \|\| 1.32.164 \|\|

*kuṃbhodbhava tadārabhya yakṣarāḍdaṃḍanāyakaḥ \|*  
*purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ samyaganuśāsti nideśataḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. O Pot-born One, since that time, the king of Yakṣas, the Daṇḍanāyaka, controls perfectly the city of Vārāṇasī at the behest (of Lord Śiva).

## \|\| 1.32.165 \|\|

*ahamapyatra vasatiṃ cakre tadanusūyayā \|*  
*vasannapi mayā kāśyāṃ yataḥ saṃbhāvito na saḥ \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. I too had to stay here, as he found fault even in my qualities. Though I was staying at Kāśī, he was not (duly) respected by me.

## \|\| 1.32.166 \|\|

*mune kṣetraṃ yadatyākṣīstvamapyevaṃvidho vaśī \|*  
*śaṃke tatrāhamevāddhā kāmaṃ tasyaiva vikriyām \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. O sage, you are such a sage of perfect sense-control, still you left the holy place. Here I suspect that he has acted against you.

## \|\| 1.32.167 \|\|

*manāgviruddhācaraṇaṃ yadi dvija vilakṣayet \|*  
*harikeśastadā kāśyāṃ kva sthitiḥ kva ca nirvṛtiḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. If, O Brāhmaṇa, Harikeśa were to see even the slightest adverse activity, where is one’s stay in Kāśī? Where is happiness? (You will have neither.)

## \|\| 1.32.168 \|\|

*daṃḍapāṇimanārādhya kaḥ kāśyāṃ sukhamāpnuyāt \|*  
*pravivikṣurahaṃ kāśīṃ dūragopi bhajāmi tam \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. Without propitiating Daṇḍapāṇi who can stay happily in Kāśī? Desirous of entering Kāśī, I worship him even from a far distance:

(Prayer of Daṇḍapāṇi)

## \|\| 1.32.169 \|\|

*ratnabhadrāṃgajodbhūtaṃ pūrṇabhadrasuto ttama \|*  
*nirvighnaṃ kuru me yakṣa kāśīvāsaṃ śivāptaye \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. “O excellent son of Pūrṇabhadra born of the limbs of Ratnabhadrā, O Yakṣa, make my stay in Kāśī free from obstacles, for the purpose of acquiring happiness.

## \|\| 1.32.170 \|\|

*dhanyo yakṣaḥ pūrṇabhadro dhanyā kāṃcanakuṃḍalā \|*  
*yayorjaṭharapīṭhebhūrdaṃḍapāṇe mahāmate \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. Yakṣa Pūrṇabhadra is blessed. Kāñcanakuṇḍalā (i.e., Kanakakuṇḍalā) is blessed whose son you were, O wise Daṇḍapāṇi.

## \|\| 1.32.171 \|\|

*jaya yakṣapate dhīra jaya piṃgalalocana \|*  
*jaya rpigajaṭābhāra jaya daṃḍa mahāyudha \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. Be victorious, O lord of Yakṣas. Be victorious, O tawny-eyed lord. Be victorious, O lord with tawny matted hairs. Be victorious, O lord with the staff as your great weapon.

## \|\| 1.32.172 \|\|

*avimukta mahākṣetra sūtradhārogratāpasa \|*  
*daṃḍanāyaka bhīmāsya jaya viśveśvarapriya \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. O Ugratāpasa, the chief controller of the great holy place Avimukta, O Daṇḍanāyaka of terrible face, be victorious, O beloved one of Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 1.32.173 \|\|

*saumyānāṃ saumyavadana bhīṣaṇānāṃ bhayānaka \|*  
*kṣetrapāpadhiyāṃ kāla mahākālamahāpriya \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. O lord, gentle in face to those who are gentle, O terrible one unto the terrible ones, O lord, you are death unto the sinful-minded ones in the holy place. You are a great favourite of Mahākāla.

## \|\| 1.32.174 \|\|

*jayaprāṇada yakṣeṃdra kāśīvāsānnamokṣada \|*  
*mahāratnasphuradraśmi cayacarcita vigraha \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. Be victorious, O giver of life, O eminent Yakṣa, the bestower of cooked food, salvation and stay at Kāśī, O lord whose body is adorned with the shining rays of great jewels!

## \|\| 1.32.175 \|\|

*mahāsaṃbhrātijanaka mahodbhrāṃti pradāyaka \|*  
*abhaktānāṃ ca bhaktānāṃ saṃbhrātyudbhrāṃti nāśaka \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. O lord, O generator of great confusion, O instigator of utmost excitement to those who are no devotees! O eradicator of great confusion and utmost excitement of the devotees!

## \|\| 1.32.176 \|\|

*prāṃtanepathyacatura jayajñānanidhiprada \|*  
*jayagaurīpadābjāle mokṣekṣaṇavicakṣaṇa \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. O lord, skilful in the final decoration (at the time of death of the devotee)! Be victorious, O bestower of the treasure-trove of knowledge. Be victorious, O lord acting as a bee in the lotus-like feet of Gaurī. O lord clever in finding out and discerning the impending salvation!”

## \|\| 1.32.177 \|\|

*yakṣarājāṣṭakaṃ puṇyamidaṃ nityaṃ trikālataḥ \|*  
*japāmi maitrāvaruṇe vārāṇasyāptikāraṇam \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. O Maitrāvaruṇi, I repeat this meritorious Yakṣarājāṣṭaka (‘octave of verses unto the king of Yakṣas) three times everyday. It is conducive to an access to Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 1.32.178 \|\|

*daṃḍapāṇyaṣṭakaṃ dhīmāñjapanvighnairna jātucit \|*  
*śraddhayā paribhūyeta kāśīvāsaphalaṃ labheta \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. A wise man repeating Daṇḍapāṇyaṣṭaka with faith is never assailed by obstacles. He shall get the benefit of stay in Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.32.179 \|\|

*prādurbhāvaṃ daṃḍapāṇeḥ śṛṇvantotramidaṃ gṛṇan \|*  
*vipattimanyataḥ prāpya kāśīṃ janmāṃtare labhet \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. One who listens to this manifestation of Daṇḍapāṇi and repeats this prayer is reborn in Kāśī after dying elsewhere.

## \|\| 1.32.180 \|\|

*śrutvādhyāyamimaṃ puṇyaṃ daṃḍapāṇisamudbhavam \|*  
*paṭhitvā pāṭhayitvāpi na rvighrairabhibhūyatai \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. By listening to this chapter of the meritorious origin of Daṇḍapāṇi, by reading and causing this to be read, one prevents the attack of obstacles.

## Chapter 33 - Description of Jñānavāpī

## \|\| 1.33.1 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*skaṃdajñānodatīrthasya māhātmyaṃ vada sāṃpratam \|*  
*jñānavāpīṃ praśaṃsaṃti yataḥ svargaukasopyalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Jñānavāpī (“The Wisdom Well”—BCL) is the most famous well in Kāśī, said to be dug by Śiva. It is a deep well, ten feet in diameter and is near the mosque built by Aurangzeb after destroying the grand old temple of Viśveśvara. Now it is set in a spacious columned arcade with iron bars across its top. Pilgrims start their pilgrimages in and about Vārāṇasī after sipping its water (as Saṅkalpa) at the beginning and end of their pilgrimage. Śiva dug this well of ‘Liquid Wisdom’ with his trident long before Gaṅgā came there. (BCL 125-129)

Agastya said:

1\. O Skanda, now narrate to me the greatness of Jñānoda Tīrtha. Wherefore do even the heaven-dwellers praise Jñānavāpī very well?

## \|\| 1.33.2 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ghaṭodbhava mahāprājña śṛṇu pāpapraṇodinīm \|*  
*jñānavāpyāḥ samutpattiṃ kathyamānāṃ mayādhunā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

2\. O Pot-born One of great intellect, listen to the origin of Jñānavāpī that removes all sins. It is being narrated now by me.

## \|\| 1.33.3 \|\|

*anādisiddhe saṃsāre purā devayuge mune \|*  
*prāptaḥ kutaścidīśānaścaransvairamitastataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O sage, formerly in Satya (Kṛta) Yuga in the primordial universe Īśāna (Rudra, the presiding deity of the North-Eastern direction—Comm.) was wandering here and there.

## \|\| 1.33.4-5 \|\|

*na varṣaṃti yadābhrāṇi na prāvartaṃta nimragāḥ \|*  
*jalābhilāṣo na yadā snānapānādi karmaṇi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kṣārasvādūdayoreva yadāsījjaladarśanam \|*  
*prathivyāṃ narasaṃcāre vatarmāne kvacitkvacit \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Then, even clouds did not rain and rivers (consequently) did not flow (were non-existent). None had any desire for water for drinking or bathing; water could be seen in the oceans of salty or sweet waters. People roamed about over the earth in places here and there.

## \|\| 1.33.6-9 \|\|

*nirvāṇakamalākṣetraṃ śrīmadānaṃdakānanam \|*  
*mahāśmaśānaṃ sarveṣāṃ bījānāṃ paramūṣaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mahāśayanasuptānāṃ jaṃtūnāṃ pratibodhakam \|*  
*saṃsārasāgarāvarta patajjaṃtutaraṃḍakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yātāyātātisaṃkhinna jaṃtuviśrāmamaṃḍapama \|*  
*anekajanmaguṇita karmasūtracchidākṣuram \|\| 8 \|\|*

*saccidānaṃdanilayaṃ parabrahmarasāyanam \|*  
*sukhasaṃtānajanakaṃ mokṣasādhanasiddhidam \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. Īśāna reached the glorious Ānandakānana (‘the forest of bliss’), the holy spot of Nirvāṇaśrī (glory of Mokṣa). It is called Mahāśmaśāna (‘the Great Cremation Ground’), a barren spot for all seeds (of worldly existence). It is the place that wakes up creatures lying in deep sleep (of ignorance). It is the boat (that takes out) the people falling into the whirlpool of the ocean of worldly existence. It is a pavilion of rest and recreation for creatures, distressed very much due to the frequent travel (in the course of their transmigration). It functions like a knife cutting off the thread (bonds) of Karmas accumulated in the course of many births. It is the abode of Existence and Bliss; it is the great Elixir of Supreme Brahman; it is the cause of the creation of a series of happiness; it bestows the fruition of all the means of the attainment of salvation.

## \|\| 1.33.10-11 \|\|

*praviśya kṣetrametatsa īśāno jaṭilastadā \|*  
*lasattriśūlavimalaraśmijālasamākulaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*āluloke mahāliṃgaṃ vaikuṃṭhaparameṣṭhinoḥ \|*  
*mahāhamahamikāyāṃ prādurāsa yadāditaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Īśāna with matted hairs (covering his head) entered the holy spot. There was a profuse lustre of pure rays from his blazing trident. He espied the Liṅga that manifested itself earlier when there was an intense rivalry between Viṣṇu and Brahma as to who was the greater of the two.

## \|\| 1.33.12 \|\|

*jyotirmayībhirmālābhiḥ paritaḥ pariveṣṭitam \|*  
*vṛṃdairvṛṃdārakarṣīṇāṃ gaṇānāṃ ca niraṃtaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It was surrounded on all sides by garlands of radiant flowers. It was worshipped by multitudes of gods and sages.

## \|\| 1.33.13 \|\|

*siddhānāṃ yogināṃ stomairarcyamānaṃ niraṃtaram \|*  
*gīyamānaṃ ca gaṃdharvaiḥ stūyamānaṃ ca cāraṇaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It was continuously adored by groups of Siddhas and Yogins; it was sung about by Gandharvas and eulogized by Cāraṇas.

## \|\| 1.33.14 \|\|

*aṃgahārairapsarobhiḥ sevyamānamanekadhā \|*  
*nīrājyamānaṃ satataṃ nāgībhirmaṇidīpakaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It was being served in various ways by celestial damsels through their different types of dances. Nāga females served it with the lamps of their luminous jewels through continuous waving with them ceremoniously.

## \|\| 1.33.15 \|\|

*vidyādharīkinnarībhistrikālaṃ kṛtamaṃḍanam \|*  
*amarīcamarīrāji vījyamānamitastataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It was embellished thrice a day with proper ornaments by Vidyādhara and Kinnara females. Here and there, it was fanned with Chowries by the celestial damsels.

## \|\| 1.33.16 \|\|

*asyeśānasya talliṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvecchetyabhavattadā \|*  
*snapayāmi mahalliṃgaṃ kalaśaiḥ śītalairjalaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On seeing that Liṅga, there arose an idea in the mind of this Īśāna, ‘Let me bathe this great Liṅga with potfuls of cool water.’

## \|\| 1.33.17 \|\|

*cakhāna ca triśūlena dakṣiṇāśopakaṃṭhataḥ \|*  
*kuṃḍaṃ pracaṃḍavegena rudrorudravapurdharaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Īśāna who was identical with Rudra in a terrible physical frame, dug up a deep pit with terrific speed by means of his trident. The place was to the south of Viśveśa and very near him.

## \|\| 1.33.18 \|\|

*pṛthivyāvaraṇāṃbhāṃsi niṣkrāṃtāni tadā mune \|*  
*bhūpramāṇāddaśaguṇairyairiyaṃ vasudhāvṛtā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then, O sage, columns of waters covering the earth and ten times its size, came out whereby the whole of the world was inundated on all sides.

## \|\| 1.33.19 \|\|

*tairjalaiḥ snāpayāṃcakre tvatspṛṣṭairanyadehibhiḥ \|*  
*tuṣārairjāḍyavidhurairjaṃjapūkaughahāribhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. With those waters as cool as snow, but devoid of Jāḍya (i.e. of the nature of knowledge), which removed clusters of sins and which were untouched by other embodied beings, he bathed (the Liṅga).

## \|\| 1.33.20 \|\|

*sanmanobhirivātyacchairanacchairvyomavartmavat \|*  
*jyotsnāvadujjvalacchāyaiḥ pāvanaiḥ śaṃbhunāmavat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The waters were sparkling in colour like the (pure) minds of good people. They had bluish tinge like the path of the sky. Their lustre was brilliant like moonlight; they were holy and pure like the names of Śaṃbhu.

## \|\| 1.33.21 \|\|

*pīyūṣavatsvādutaraiḥ sukhasparśairgavāṃgavat \|*  
*niṣpāpadhīvadgaṃbhīraistaralaiḥ pāpiśarmavat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. They were excessively sweet like the divine nectar; pleasant to the touch like the limbs of a cow; had grandeur like the intellect of a sinless person and were sparklingly moving to and fro (fickle) like the happiness of the sinners.

## \|\| 1.33.22 \|\|

*vijitābjamahāgaṃdhaiḥ pāṭalāmodamodibhiḥ \|*  
*adṛṣṭapūrvalokānāṃ manonayanahāribhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Their scent excelled the sweet smell of lotuses; they were delightful with the fragrance of the Pāṭalā flowers. They attracted the minds and the eyes of the people in an unprecedented way.

## \|\| 1.33.23 \|\|

*ajñānatāpasaṃtapta prāṇiprāṇaikarakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*paṃcāmṛtānāṃ kalaśaiḥ snapanātiphalapradaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. They were, as though, the sole protectors of the vital airs of all living beings, distressed through the heat of ignorance. They were capable of yielding more benefit than bathing with potfuls of Pañcāmṛta (curd, milk, ghee, honey and sugar).

## \|\| 1.33.24 \|\|

*śraddhopasparśi dṛdayaliṃga tritayahetubhiḥ \|*  
*ajñānatimirārkābhairjñānadāna nidāyakaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. They were the producers of three Liṅgas(?) in the hearts of those regularly performing the ceremonious rinsing of the mouth with faith; they functioned like the sun in dispelling the darkness of ignorance; they yielded the benign gifts of wisdom.

## \|\| 1.33.25 \|\|

*viśvabharturumāsparśasukhātisukhakāribhiḥ \|*  
*mahāvabhṛthasusnāna mahāśuddhividhāyibhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. They caused more happiness to Viśvabhartṛ (Lord Śiva) than even the gentle caress of Umā. They caused more purity than even the excellent bath of Mahāvabhṛtha (valedictory bath after the performance of sacrifices).

## \|\| 1.33.26 \|\|

*sahasradhāraiḥ kalaśaiḥ sa īśāno ghaṭodbhava \|*  
*sahasrakṛtvaḥ snapayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Extremely delighted in his mind, O Pot-born Sage, Īśāna bathed the Liṅga thousand times through pitchers with thousand streams.

## \|\| 1.33.27 \|\|

*tataḥ prasanno bhagavānviśvātmā viśvalocanaḥ \|*  
*tamuvāca tadeśānaṃ rudraṃ rudravapurdharam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereby, the holy Lord, the omni-eyed, the omni-souled Śiva, became delighted. He spoke to Īśāna, Rudra of terrible physical frame:

## \|\| 1.33.28 \|\|

*tava prasannosmīśāna karmaṇānena suvrata \|*  
*guruṇānanyapūrveṇa mamātiprītikāriṇā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “O Īśāna of excellent holy rites, I am pleased with this great rite of yours, never before undertaken by others. It has caused me great delight.

## \|\| 1.33.29 \|\|

*tatastvaṃ jaṭileśāna varaṃ brūhi tapodhana \|*  
*adeyaṃ na tavāstyadya mahodyamaparāyaṇa \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Hence, O Īśāna, O great ascetic with matted hairs, engaged in a noble task involving excessive endeavour, tell me what boon (you will have). There is nothing that cannot be given to you today.”

## \|\| 1.33.30 \|\|

*īśāna uvāca \|*  
*yadi prasanno deveśa varayogyosmyahaṃ yadi \|*  
*tadetadatulaṃ tīrthaṃ tava nāmnāstu śaṃkara \|\| 30 \|\|*

Īśāna said:

30\. O Śaṅkara, O Lord of Devas, if you are pleased and if I deserve to receive a boon, let this unrivalled holy Tīrtha be named after you.

## \|\| 1.33.31 \|\|

*viśveśvara uvāca \|*  
*trilokyāṃ yāni tīrthāni bhūrbhuvaḥsvaḥ sthitānyapi \|*  
*tebhyokhilebhyastīrthebhyaḥ śivatīrthamidaṃ param \|\| 31 \|\|*

Viśveśvara said:

31\. This Śiva Tīrtha is greater than all those Tīrthas situated in the three worlds, viz., Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ.

## \|\| 1.33.32-33 \|\|

*śivajñānamiti brūyuḥ śivaśabdārthaciṃtakāḥ \|*  
*tacca jñānaṃ dravībhūtamiha me mahimodayāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ato jñānoda nāmaitattīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*asya darśanamātreṇa sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Those who ponder over the meanings of the word, say that Siva means knowledge (wisdom). Here, due to my greatness, that knowledge is liquified (i.e., has taken a watery form). Hence this Tīrtha has become reputed in all the three worlds by the name Jñānoda. Merely at the sight of this Liṅga, one is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.33.34 \|\|

*jñānodatīrthasaṃsparśādaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*sparśanācamanābhyāṃ ca rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. One shall obtain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice by touching the Jñānoda Tīrtha; and that of a Rājasūya and a horse-sacrifice by touching and rinsing the mouth therewith.

## \|\| 1.33.35 \|\|

*phalgutīrthe naraḥ snātvā saṃtarpya ca pitāmahān \|*  
*yatphalaṃ samavāpnoti tadatra śrāddhakarmaṇā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. By performing Śrāddha rite here, one receives that benefit which is obtained by a man after bathing and offering libations to the grandfathers in Phalgu Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.33.36 \|\|

*gurupuṣyāsitāṣṭamyāṃ vyatīpāto yadā bhavet \|*  
*tadātra śrāddhakaraṇādgayākoṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The performance of Śrāddha here on a day when there is Vyatīpāta Yoga or the coincidence of Thursday, Puṣya star and the eighth lunar day in the dark half, yields ten million times more benefit than that at Gayā.

## \|\| 1.33.37 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ samavāpnoti pitṝnsaṃtarpya puṣkare \|*  
*tatphalaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ jñānatīrthe tilodakaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. By offering libations of water with gingelly seeds in Jñāna Tīrtha, one obtains the benefit ten million times more than that obtained by propitiating the Manes at Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.33.38 \|\|

*sannihatyāṃ kurukṣetre tamograste vivasvati \|*  
*yatphalaṃ piṃḍadānena tajjñānode dine dine \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The benefit that is obtained by offering balls of rice in Sannihatyā (Rāmahrada) in Kurukṣetra, when there is a solar eclipse, is obtained by offering the same everyday in Jñānoda.

## \|\| 1.33.39 \|\|

*piṃḍanirvapaṇaṃ yeṣāṃ jñānatīrthe sutaiḥ kṛtam \|*  
*modaṃte śivaloke te yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Those whose sons perform Piṇḍanirvāpaṇa (‘offering balls of rice’) in Jñāna Tīrtha rejoice in Śivaloka while all the living beings are annihilated (at the end of the Kalpa).

## \|\| 1.33.40 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāmupavāsī narottamaḥ \|*  
*prātaḥ snātvātha pītāṃbhastvaṃtarliṃgamayo bhavet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. An excellent man who takes his holy ablution in the morning and drinks (the holy) water but observes fast otherwise on the eighth and the fourteenth lunar day becomes one full of Liṅgas within.

## \|\| 1.33.41 \|\|

*ekādaśyāmupoṣyātra prāśnāti culukatrayam \|*  
*hṛdaye tasya jāyaṃte trīṇi liṃgānyasaṃśayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If the devotee observes fast on the eleventh day and drinks three handfuls of water here, undoubtedly three Liṅgas will rise up in his heart.

## \|\| 1.33.42-43 \|\|

*īśānatīrthe yaḥ snātvā viśeṣātsomavāsare \|\| \|*  
*saṃtarpya devarṣi pitṝndattvā dānama svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tataḥ samarcya śrīliṃgaṃ mahāsaṃbhāravistaraiḥ \|*  
*atrāpi dattvā nānārthānkṛtakṛtyobhavennaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. The devotee should take his holy ablution in the Īśāna Tīrtha, especially on a Monday, propitiate the gods, the sages and the Manes and make gifts in accordance with his capacity. Thereafter, he would worship Śrī Liṅga elaborately with all the requisites. Here also he should make gifts of various objects. Thereby he shall have accomplished all his duties (or desired objects).

## \|\| 1.33.44 \|\|

*upāsya saṃdhyāṃ jñānode yatpāpaṃ kālalopajam \|*  
*kṣaṇena tadapākṛtya jñānavāñjāyate dvijaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. By performing Sandhyā rites in Jñānoda a Brāhmaṇa shall instantaneously dispel all the sins due to transgression of timely duties. He shall become wise and endowed with knowledge.

## \|\| 1.33.45 \|\|

*śivatīrthamidaṃ proktaṃ jñānatīrthamidaṃ śubham \|*  
*tārakākhyamidaṃ tīrthaṃ mokṣatīrthamidaṃ dhuvam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. This has been described as Śiva Tīrtha; this is the splendid Jñāna Tīrtha; this Tīrtha has been called Tāraka (that which redeems); this is certainly Mokṣa Tīrtha (‘salvation-granting Tīrtha’).

## \|\| 1.33.46 \|\|

*smaraṇādapi pāpaugho jñānodasya kṣayeddhruvam \|*  
*darśanātsparśanātsnānātpānāddharmādisaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Certainly multitudes of sins shall perish by remembering Jñānoda. By visiting it, touching it, bathing in it and drinking its water, piousness is engendered.

## \|\| 1.33.47-48 \|\|

*ḍākinīśākinī bhūtapretavetālarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*grahāḥ kūṣmāṃḍajhoṭiṃgāḥ kālakarṇī śiśugrahāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*jvarāpasmāravisphoṭadvitīyakacaturthakāḥ \|*  
*sarve praśamamāyāṃti śivartārthajalekṣaṇāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Goblins, ghosts, vampires, ogres, Ḍākinīs, Śākinīs, evil Planets, evil spirits, Jhoṭiṅga, Kālakarṇīs etc., spirits attacking infants, epileptic fits, tertian fevers, fevers recurring every fourth day, swellings—all these subside by seeing the waters of Śiva Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.33.49 \|\|

*jñānodatīrthapānīyairliṃgaṃ yaḥ snāpayetsudhīḥ \|*  
*sarvatīrthodakaistena dhruvaṃ saṃsnāpitaṃ bhavet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. If a highly intelligent man bathes the Liṅga with the waters of Jñānodatīrtha, it is certainly on a par with having got it bathed with the waters of all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.33.50 \|\|

*jñānarūpoha mevātra dravamūrtiṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*jāḍyavidhvaṃsanaṃ kuryāṃ kuryāṃ jñānopadeśanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. I myself, in the form of Jñāna, having assumed the liquid form, shall destroy Jāḍya (sluggishness, ignorance) and impart knowledge.

## \|\| 1.33.51 \|\|

*iti dattvā varāñchaṃbhustatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyamivātmānaṃ sopyamaṃstatriśūlabhṛt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. After granting boons thus, Śaṃbhu vanished there itself. The trident-bearing īśāna considered himself one whose desires were fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.33.52 \|\|

*īśāno jaṭilo rudrastatprāśya paramodakam \|*  
*avāptavānparaṃ jñānaṃ yena nirvṛtimāptavān \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Rudra, Īśāna with matted hairs, drank the excellent water and acquired the great knowledge whereby he achieved bliss of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.33.53 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*kalaśodbhava citrārthamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*jñānavāpyāṃ hi yadvṛttaṃ tadākhyāmi niśāmaya \|\| 53 \|\|*

Skanda said:

53\. Listen, O Pot-born One. I shall recount what took place in Jñānavāpī, the ancient mythological legend of wonderful content.

## \|\| 1.33.54 \|\|

*harisvāmīti vikhyātaḥ kāśyāmāsīdvijaḥ purā \|*  
*tasyaikā tanayā jātā rūpeṇā'pratimā bhuvi \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Formerly, in Kāśī, there was a Brāhmaṇa well-known as Harisvāmī. A daughter was born to him. She was unexcelled in beauty in the whole earth.

## \|\| 1.33.55 \|\|

*na samā śīlasaṃpattyā tasyā kācana bhūtale \|*  
*kalākalāpakuśalā svareṇajitakokilā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. She was clever in all kinds of fine arts. With her (sweet) voice, she vanquished even the cuckoo. No other woman on the earth was equal to her in the excellence of good conduct.

## \|\| 1.33.56 \|\|

*na nārī tādṛgastīha nā bharī kinnarī na ca \|*  
*vidyādharī na no nāgī gaṃdharvī nāsurī na ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. There was no other woman like her in this world, either among celestial women or among Kinnara, Vidyādhara, Nāga, Gandharva or Asura women.

## \|\| 1.33.57 \|\|

*sarvasauṃdaryanilayā sarvalakṣaṇasatkhaniḥ \|*  
*adhiśete dhruvaṃ dhvāṃtaṃ tanmauliṃ bradhna sādhvasāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. She was the abode of all beauty; she was an excellent mine (i.e., resort) of all good features. Certainly, out of fear for the Sun, darkness resorts to her tresses of hairs.

## \|\| 1.33.58 \|\|

*tadāsya śaraṇaṃ yāto manye darśabhayācchaśī \|*  
*divāpi na tyajettāṃ tu trastaścaṃḍamarīcitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. I suppose, out of fear of the new-moon day, the moon has sought refuge in her face. Even during the day, it does not abandon her because it is afraid of the sun.

## \|\| 1.33.59 \|\|

*tadbhrūrbhramararājīva gaṃḍapatralatāṃtare \|*  
*udaṃcannyaṃcaduḍḍīna gaterabhyāsabhājinī \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Her eyebrows appeared like a swarm of bees moving up and down in the spaces between the cheeks, the decorative markings thereon that resemble a creeper (thus appearing) thereby frequently practising flights.

## \|\| 1.33.60 \|\|

*taccārulocanakṣetre vicaraṃtau ca khaṃjanau \|*  
*sadaiva śāradīṃ prītiṃ nirviśete nijecchayā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The Khañjana birds always passing through the spheres of her eyes, experience the perpetual autumnal pleasure as they pleased.

## \|\| 1.33.61 \|\|

*sudatyā radanaśreṇī chedeṣu viṣameṣuṇā \|*  
*vihitā kāṃcanī rekhā kveṃdāvetāvatī kalā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. A golden streak of light has been placed by the Lord of Love in the row of teeth of that beautiful girl. Is there such a fine digit in the moon?

## \|\| 1.33.62 \|\|

*prāyo madana bhūpāla harmya ratnāṃtare śubhe \|*  
*jitapravālasucchāye tasyā radanavāsasī \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Her lips that had the lustre far excelling the coral, are the splendid jewel-set interspaces in the mansion of King Madana (Lord of Love).

## \|\| 1.33.63 \|\|

*svarge martye ca pātāle naiṣā rekhā kvacitstriyām \|*  
*tatkaṃṭharekhātritaya vyājena śapate smaraḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Lord Smara appears to aver this solemnly through the three lines in her neck, “Neither in heaven nor in the mortal world, nor in the nether region is there a Rekhā (line) like this in women.”

## \|\| 1.33.64 \|\|

*śaṃke citta bhuvo rājño lasatpaṭakuṭīdvayam \|*  
*anarghyaratnakośāḍhyaṃ tamyā vakṣoruhadvayam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Her two breasts, I believe, constitute the two tent-houses of King Kama, abounding in valuable jewel treasures.

## \|\| 1.33.65 \|\|

*anaṃgabhū niyamato'dṛśye madhye natabhruvaḥ \|*  
*romālīlakṣikāmūrdhvāmiva yaṣṭiṃ vidhirvyadhāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Brahmā made a propped up staff, as it were, as indicated by the line of hairs in the invisible middle of the beautiful girl with arched brows, thanks to the instruction of Anaṅga (Lord of Love).

## \|\| 1.33.66 \|\|

*tasyā nābhīdarīṃ prāpya kaṃdarpo'naṃgatā gataḥ \|*  
*punaḥ prāptumivāṃgāni tapyate paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Reaching deep into the cavity of her navel Kanḍarpa became Anaṅga (bodiless). He performs great penance as if to regain (his) body.

## \|\| 1.33.67 \|\|

*guruṇaitannitaṃbena mahāmanmatha dīkṣayā \|*  
*bhuvi ke ke yuvāno na svādhīnā prāpitādṛśām \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. By her weighty hips, through the initiation of the Lord of Love, many young men on the earth became unable to be independent in (moving) their eyes (All of them got their eyes riveted to her hips).

## \|\| 1.33.68 \|\|

*ūrustaṃbhena caitasyāḥ staṃbhavatkasyano manaḥ \|*  
*tastaṃbhena mune vāpi suvṛttena suvartanam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Whose mind was not arrested and fixed firmly like a pillar by her pillar-like thighs round in shape? Even the minds of sages, despite their disciplined good behaviour, got stuck (like a pillar).

## \|\| 1.33.69 \|\|

*pādāṃguṣṭhanakhajyotiḥ prabhayā kasya na prabhā \|*  
*vivekajanitā'dhvaṃsi mune tasyā mṛgīdṛśaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Whose lustre of discrimination was not destroyed, O sage, by the lustre of the nail of the big toe of the foot of that fawn-eyed girl?

## \|\| 1.33.70 \|\|

*sā pratyahaṃ jñānavāpyāṃ snāyaṃ snāyaṃ śivālaye \|*  
*saṃmārjanādi karmāṇi kurute'nanyamānasā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. She regularly took her bath in Jñānavāpī everyday and attended to the tasks of sweeping the premises of the temple of Śiva with concentrated mind.

## \|\| 1.33.71 \|\|

*tatpādapratibiṃbeṣu rekhā śaṣpāṃkuraṃ caran \|*  
*nānyadvanāṃtaraṃ yāti kāśyāṃ yūnāṃ manomṛgaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The deer-like minds of the youths of Kāśī who grazed, as it were, the grass in the form of the lines (e.g. a lotus, a conch) in the imprints of her soles, did not go to any other place.

## \|\| 1.33.72 \|\|

*tadāsya paṃkajaṃ hitvā yūnāṃ netrālimālayā \|*  
*na latāṃtaramāsevi apyāmodaprasūnayuk \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. No other creeper, although it had fragrant flowers was resorted to by the swarm of bees in the form of the eyes of young men, excepting her lotus-like face.

## \|\| 1.33.73 \|\|

*sulocanāpi sā kanyā prekṣetāsyaṃ na kasyacit \|*  
*suśravā api sā bālā nādatte kasyacidvacaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. That girl though endowed with beautiful eyes, never looked at the face of anyone. That maiden, though endowed with excellent ears, did not listen to anyone’s words.

## \|\| 1.33.74 \|\|

*suśīlā śīlasaṃpannā rahastadvirahāturaiḥ \|*  
*prārthitāpi surūpāḍhyairnābhilāṣaṃ babaṃdha sā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. She, of good conduct, endowed with chaste habits, was secretly requested by love-lorn youths of excellent handsome features, but she did not love them in return.

## \|\| 1.33.75 \|\|

*dhanaistasyājanetāpi yuvabhiḥ prārthito bahu \|*  
*nāśakattāṃ sulīlāṃ sadātuṃ śīlorjitaśriyam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Her father too was approached with wealth and requested many times by young men. But he was unable to hand over (in marriage), because she had powerful glory accompanied by good chaste habit.

## \|\| 1.33.76 \|\|

*jñānodatīrthabhajanātsā suśīlā kumāgkiा \|*  
*bahiraṃtastadā'drākṣītsarvaliṃgamayaṃ jagata \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Due to her close worship of Jñānoda Tīrtha, that girl Suśīlā (apparently the name) saw everything within and without pervaded with Liṅgas,

## \|\| 1.33.77-79 \|\|

*kadācidekadā tāṃ tu prasuptāṃ sadanāṃgaṇe \|*  
*mohito rūpasaṃpattyā kaścidvidyādharo'harat \|\| 77 \|\|*

*vyomavartmanitāṃ rātrau yāvanmalayaparvatam \|*  
*sa ninīṣati tāvacca vidyunmālī samāgataḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*rākṣaso bhīṣaṇavapuḥ kapālakṛtakuṃḍalaḥ \|*  
*vasārudhiraliptāṃgaḥ śmaśrulaḥ piṃgalocanaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

77-79. Once, she was asleep in the courtyard of the house. Enamoured of her excellent beauty, a certain Vidyādhara abducted her then. Along the aerial path he was carrying her off to Malaya mountain. But by that time the demon Vidyunmālī also came there. He had a terrible huge body. Skulls made his ear-rings. His limbs were smeared with suet and blood. He had whiskers and his eyes were tawny.

## \|\| 1.33.80 \|\|

*rākṣasa uvāca \|*  
*mamadṛggocaraṃ yāto vidyādharakumāraka \|*  
*adya tvāmetayā sārdhaṃ preṣayāmi yamālayam \|\| 80 \|\|*

The Rākṣasa said:

80\. O young Vidyādhara, you have come within the range of my vision. I shall despatch you to the abode of Yama along with this woman.

## \|\| 1.33.81 \|\|

*iti śrutvātha sā vākyaṃ vyāghrāghrātā mṛgī yathā \|*  
*cakaṃpe'tīva saṃbhītā kadalīdalavanmuhuḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. On hearing these words, she trembled like a hind attacked by a tiger and like a leaf of a plantain tree again and again in her fright.

## \|\| 1.33.82-83 \|\|

*nijaghāna triśūlena rakṣo vidyādharaṃ ca tam \|*  
*vidyādharakumāropi nitarāṃ madhurākṛtiḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*tadbhīṣaṇatriśūlena bhinnosko mahābalaḥ \|*  
*jaghāna muṣṭighātena vajrapātopamena tam \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. The demon hit that Vidyādhara with his trident. The Vidyādhara youth of sweet form, yet of tremendous power, was attacked and pierced in the chest by his terrible Triśūla. Yet he hit back the demon with his adamantine fist.

## \|\| 1.33.84 \|\|

*naramāṃsavasāmattaṃ vidyunmālinamāhave \|*  
*cūrṇito muṣṭipātena so'patadvasudhātale \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The Vidyādhara, in the course of the battle, hit Vidyunmālī who was intoxicated with human flesh and suet. Shattered by that blow of the fist, he fell down on the ground.

## \|\| 1.33.85 \|\|

*rākṣaso mṛtyuvaśago vajreṇeva mahīdharaḥ \|*  
*vidyādharopi tacchūlaghātena vikalīkṛtaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The demon fell a prey to death (on being hit) like a mountain with thunderbolt. The Vidyādhara became crippled by the trident that struck him.

## \|\| 1.33.86-87 \|\|

*uvāca gadgadaṃ vākyaṃ vighūrṇita vilocanaḥ \|*  
*priye mudhā samānītā suśityardhoktimuccaran \|\| 86 \|\|*

*jahau prāṇānraṇe vīrastāṃ priyāṃ paritaḥ smaran \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87. With rolling eyes, he spoke falteringly, uttering half of her name as Sus: “O dear one, you have been brought here in vain.” Then that heroic youth gave up his life in battle, remembering his beloved.

## \|\| 1.33.88 \|\|

*ananyapūrvasaṃsparśa sukhaṃ samanubhūya sā \|*  
*tameva ca patiṃ matvā cakre śokāgnisāttanum \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Experiencing an unprecedented thrill, thanks to his touch, she considered him alone as her husband and consigned her body to the fire of grief.

## \|\| 1.33.89 \|\|

*liṃgatrayaśarīriṇyāstasyāḥ sānnidhyataḥ sa hi \|*  
*divyaṃ vapuḥ samāsādya rākṣasastridivaṃ yayau \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. By the close proximity to that girl whose body contained three Liṅgas that demon acquired a divine body and went to heaven.

## \|\| 1.33.90 \|\|

*raṇe paṇīkṛtaprāṇo vidyādharasutopi saḥ \|*  
*aṃte priyāṃ smaranprāpa janurmalayaketutaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The Vidyādhara youth who had staked his very life in the battle, remembered his beloved at the last moment (of his life). He was reborn as the son of Malayaketu.

## \|\| 1.33.91 \|\|

*dhyāyaṃtī sāpi taṃ bālā vidyādharakumārakam \|*  
*virahāgnau visṛṣṭāsuḥ karṇāṭe janmabhāgabhūt \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. That girl who forsook her life in the fire of separation meditating on the Vidyādhara youth, was reborn in Karṇāṭa.

## \|\| 1.33.92 \|\|

*suto malayaketostāṃ kālena pariṇītavān \|*  
*mālyaketuranaṃgaśrīḥ pitrā dattāṃ kalāvatīm \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Mālyaketu, the son of Malayaketu, who had the glory and splendour of Anaṅga, god of Love, married in due course that Kalāvatī who was given away in marriage by her father.

## \|\| 1.33.93 \|\|

*sāpi prāgvāsanāyogālliṃgārcanaratā satī \|*  
*hitvā malayajakṣodaṃ vibhūtiṃ bahvamaṃsta vai \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Due to the impression of her experiences in the previous birth, that chaste lady excessively interested in the worship of Liṅgas, set aside sandal powder and honoured Vibhūti (holy ash).

## \|\| 1.33.94 \|\|

*muktā vaidūrya māṇikya puṣparāgebhya eva sā \|*  
*mene rudrākṣanepadhyamanarghyaṃ garbhasuṃdarī \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. That lady of natural beauty considered embellishment with Rudrākṣa beads more esteemable than (ornaments of) pearls, lapis lazuli, rubies and topaz.

## \|\| 1.33.95 \|\|

*kalāvatī mālyaketuṃ patiṃ prāpya pativratā \|*  
*apatyatritayaṃ lebhe divyabhogasamṛddhibhāk \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. After marrying Mālyaketu, Kalāvatī, the chaste lady, enjoyed divine pleasures and prosperity and gave birth to three sons.

## \|\| 1.33.96 \|\|

*ekadā kaścidaudīcyo mālyaketuṃ nareśvaram \|*  
*citrakṛccitrapaṭikāṃ citrāṃ darśitavānatha \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Once a certain man from the north, a painter, showed king Mālyaketu a wonderful picture canvas.

## \|\| 1.33.97-98 \|\|

*tāṃ tu citrapaṭīṃ rājā kalāvatyai samarpayat \|*  
*sātha citrapaṭīṃ ramyāṃ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhā \|\| 97 \|\|*

*muhurmuhuḥ prapaśyaṃtī rahasi prāṇadevatām \|*  
*visasmāra svamapi ca samādhistheva yoginī \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. The king presented Kalāvatī with that picture. She became thrilled on seeing the picture again and again in secret. It contained the picture of her revered god and Lord. On looking at the picture, she forget even herself like a Yoginī engrossed in meditation.

## \|\| 1.33.99 \|\|

*kṣaṇamunmīlya nayane kṛtvā netrātithiṃ paṭīm \|*  
*tarjanyagramathotkṣipya svātmānaṃ samabodhayat \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. For a moment she opened her eyes and looked at the picture canvas. Lifting the tip of her index finger, she spoke to herself:

## \|\| 1.33.100 \|\|

*saṃbhedoyamase ramya upalolārkamagrataḥ \|*  
*upaśrīkeśavapadaṃ varaṇaiṣā saridvarā \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. “This is the charming confluence of Asi in front, very near Lolārka. This is the excellent river Varaṇā near the shrine of Keśava (i.e., Ādi Keśava).

## \|\| 1.33.101 \|\|

*svageṃ prārthitasaṃsparśā saiṣā svargataraṃgiṇī \|*  
*udagvahābhilaṣyaṃti yāṃ divodyusadaḥ sadā \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. This is the north-flowing celestial river whose touch is eagerly sought after in heaven and which the heaven-dwellers always desire.

## \|\| 1.33.102 \|\|

*alakṣyāmokṣalakṣmī ryā vedāṃte paripaṭhyate \|*  
*vimuktaye satāṃ saiṣā śrīmatī maṇikarṇikā \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. This is the glorious Maṇikarṇikā which is conducive to the salvation of good men and is spoken of as the inscrutable Mokṣalakṣmī (glory of salvation).

## \|\| 1.33.103 \|\|

*maraṇaṃ maṃgalaṃ yatra saphalaṃ yatra jīvitam \|*  
*svargastṛṇāyate yatra saiṣā śrīmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. This is the glorious Maṇikarṇikā where death is auspicious and life is fruitful and where heaven is as insignificant as grass.

## \|\| 1.33.104 \|\|

*yatra saṃpattisaṃbhārānviśrāṇya nidhanecchayā \|*  
*yativrataṃ samālaṃbya tiṣṭhate mūlakaṃdabhuk \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. This is Maṇikarṇikā where the meritorious ones desire to die and so giving up their wealth and assets, they stay like ascetics with holy rites, eating only roots and bulbous roots (mūla-kanda-bhuk)

## \|\| 1.33.105 \|\|

*yatra trimārgaṃ gāṃgaṃ gāṃ mārgamāṇomṛtānharaḥ \|*  
*svamaulibālacaṃdreṇa muktimārgaṃ pradarśayan \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. It is the place where Śaṅkara who holds the crescent moon and Gaṅgā of triple path (on his head) shows the path of salvation to those who die here.

## \|\| 1.33.106 \|\|

*saṃsāraṃ yatra durvāraṃ pratārayati śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*mṛtā apyamṛtāyaṃte karṇadhārādyato narāḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. It is the place where Śaṅkara annihilates Saṃsāra (worldly existence) though it is difficult to ward off. With Him as helmsman, men, though dead, become immortal (in Mokṣa).

## \|\| 1.33.107 \|\|

*saṃsārāsārapadavī yatra syādadavīyasī \|*  
*karṇe japānmaheśānātkaruṇā varuṇālayāt \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. It is here where Maheśāna, the ocean of sympathy, whispers (the redeeming Tāraka Mantra) into the (right) ear and hence the steadfast path of salvation in the world does not remain far off.

## \|\| 1.33.108 \|\|

*aneka bhavasaṃbhūta prabhūta sukṛtairnarāḥ \|*  
*karṇe japaṃ bhavaṃ yatra labhaṃte te bhavāpaham \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. It is through much of the merit accumulated in the course of many births, that men obtain Bhava as the whisperer (of the Mantra) and the dispeller of worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.33.109 \|\|

*svīkṛtya kṣetrasaṃnyāsaṃ yadbalena mahādhiyaḥ \|*  
*tṛṇaṃ kṛtātaṃ manyaṃte seyaṃ śrīmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. This is Śrī Maṇikarṇikā where men of great intellect adopt Kṣetrasannyāsa (‘renunciation in the form of going away from a fixed holy spot’) and by the strength thereof consider god of Death as insignificant as a blade of grass.

## \|\| 1.33.110 \|\|

*tṛṇīkṛtya nijaṃ dehaṃ yatra rājarṣisattamaḥ \|*  
*hariścaṃdraḥ sapatnīko vyakrīṇādbhūrayaṃ hi sā \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. This is the place where the excellent saintly king Hariścandra, in the company of his wife, considered his body like a blade of grass and sold it off.

## \|\| 1.33.111 \|\|

*abhilaṣyaṃti yatratyamapi vaikuṇṭhavāsinaḥ \|*  
*saikataṃ mṛdulaṃ talpaṃ saiṣā śrīmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. This is that glorious Maṇikarṇikā, the sandy soft bed whereof even the dwellers of Vaikuṇṭha desire to have.

## \|\| 1.33.112 \|\|

*aneka janma janita karmasūtraniyaṃtraṇam \|*  
*unmucya yatra muktāḥ syuḥ saiṣā śrīmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. This is that glorious Maṇikarṇikā where (devotees) become liberated after disengaging themselves from the bondage of Karmas arising in the course of many births.

## \|\| 1.33.113 \|\|

*satyaloke'pi ye lokāste'rthayaṃti niraṃtaram \|*  
*yāmaho dīrghanidrāyai seyaṃ śrīmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. This is that glorious Maṇikarṇikā which is desired for ever for the sake of long sleep (i.e., salvation) by those people who dwell even in Satyaloka.

## \|\| 1.33.114 \|\|

*ayaṃ hi sa kulastaṃbho yatra śrīkālabhairavaḥ \|*  
*kṣetrapāpakṛtaḥ śāsti darśayaṃstīvrayātanām \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. This is that Kulastaṃbha (steady pillar) where Śrī Kālabhairava chastises sinners residing within the holy spot, inflicting severe torture.

## \|\| 1.33.115 \|\|

*anyatra vihitaṃ pāpaṃ naśyetkāśīnirīkṣaṇāt \|*  
*kāśyāṃ kṛtānāṃ pāpānāṃ dāruṇeyaṃ tu yātanā \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. A sin committed elsewhere may perish on seeing Kāśī. But: for sins committed at Kāśī the torture administered is extremely terrible.

## \|\| 1.33.116 \|\|

*kapālamocanaṃ tīrthametattadapi pāvanam \|*  
*kapālaṃ patitaṃ yatra vidherbhairavapāṇitaḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. This is the Tīrtha called Kapālamocana. It is also very sacred. It is the place where the skull of Brahmā fell down from the hand of Bhairava.

## \|\| 1.33.117 \|\|

*ṛṇatrayādvimucyaṃte yatra snātā narotamāḥ \|*  
*tīrthaṃ viśuddhijanakaṃ tadetadṛṇamocanam \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. This is the Tīrtha Ṛṇamocana which produces sanctity and purity. Excellent men who take their holy ablution here become liberated from the three types of indebtedness to the Devas, to the Sages and to the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.33.118 \|\|

*praṇavākhyaṃ paraṃbrahma yatra nityaṃ prakāśate \|*  
*sapaṃcāyatanopeta oṃkāreśoyamadbhutaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. This is the miraculous Oṃkāreśa with five abodes (Āyatana) wherein the absolute Brahman named Praṇava shines forever.

## \|\| 1.33.119 \|\|

*aśca uśca makāraśca nādobiṃduśca paṃcamaḥ \|*  
*paṃcātmakaṃ paraṃbrahma yatra nityaṃ prakāśate \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. The five Āyatanas are A, U, Ma, Nāda and Bindu the fifth one. This is the place where Brahman consisting of the five shines forever.

## \|\| 1.33.120 \|\|

*eṣā matsyodarī ramyā yatsnāto mānavottamaḥ \|*  
*māturjātūdaradarīṃ na viśedeṣa niścayaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. This is that exquisitely beautiful river Matsyodarī. If any excellent man takes his holy ablution here, he will never enter the cavity of a mother’s belly—this is the conclusive decision.

## \|\| 1.33.121 \|\|

*trilocanoyaṃ bhagavānkuryādeva trilocanam \|*  
*nijabhaktaṃ kṛpāyuktastvapi deśātaṃra sthitam \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. This Three-eyed Lord endowed with compassion converts his devotee, even if he is in another country, into a threeeyed one (gives Sarūpatā Mukti i.e. one having the form similar to that of the Lord).

## \|\| 1.33.122 \|\|

*asau kāmeśvaro devo yaḥ kāmānpūrayetsatām \|*  
*durvāsā api yatrāpa nijakāmamahodayam \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. This is Lord Kāmeśvara who fulfils the desires of good people. Even Duravāsas obtained the fulfilment of his desire here.

## \|\| 1.33.123 \|\|

*svayaṃ līno maheśotra bhaktakāmasamṛddhaye \|*  
*tasmātsvarlīnasaṃjñāsya devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. For the sake of the fulfilment of the desires of devotees, Maheśa himself became merged here. Hence the name Svarlīna of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.33.124 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ mahādevo yaḥ purāṇeṣu paṭhyate \|*  
*kṣetrābhimānī bhagavāṃstatprāsādoyamadbhutaḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. This is that wonderful mansion of the Lord who takes pride in his holy spot and who is cited as Mahādeva in Vārāṇasī In the Purāṇas.

## \|\| 1.33.125 \|\|

*asau skaṃdeśvaro devaḥ śraddhayā yadvilokanāt \|*  
*ājanmabrahmacaryasya phalamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. This is Lord Skandeśvara. If a man visits this Lord with faith, he obtains the benefit of life-long celibacy.

## \|\| 1.33.126 \|\|

*vināyakeśvaraścāyaṃ sarvasiddhi pradāyakaḥ \|*  
*yatsevayā praṇaśyaṃti nṛṇāṃ sarve vināyakāḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. This is Vināyakeśvara who bestows all supernatural powers. By serving him all the causes of obstacles of men perish.

## \|\| 1.33.127 \|\|

*iyaṃ vārāṇasī devī sākṣānmūrttimayī śubhā \|*  
*yasyā vilokanātpuṃsāṃ bhūyo no garbhasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. This is Goddess Vārāṇasī herself, the splendid deity in personified form. By visiting her men are never born again in a womb.

## \|\| 1.33.128 \|\|

*pārvatīśvaraliṃgasya mahadāyatanaṃ tvidam \|*  
*yatra nityaṃ maheśāno gauryā saha vimuktidaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. This is the great shrine of Pārvatīśvara Liṅga where Maheśāna accompanied by Gaurī is present forever as the bestower of salvation.

## \|\| 1.33.129 \|\|

*eṣa bhṛṃgīśvaraḥ śrīmānmahāpātakanāśanaḥ \|*  
*jīvanmukto'bhavadbhṛṃgī yasya liṃgasya sevayā \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. This is the glorious Lord Bhṛṅgīśvara, the destroyer of great sins. By serving the Liṅga, Bhṛṅgī became a liberated living soul.

## \|\| 1.33.130 \|\|

*caturvedeśvaraścaiṣa caturvedadharo vidhiḥ \|*  
*labhedyadvīkṣaṇādvipro vedādhyayanajaṃ phalam \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. This is Caturvedeśvara, the creator of all, who upholds the four Vedas. By visiting this Lord, a Brāhmaṇa obtains the benefit of studying the four Vedas.

## \|\| 1.33.131 \|\|

*yajñaiḥ saṃsthāpitaṃ caitalliṃgaṃ yajñeśvarābhidham \|*  
*yadarcanāllabhenmartyaḥ sarvayāgaphalaṃ mahat \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. This is the Liṅga named Yajñeśvara installed by Yajñas (Sacrifices). By worshipping it, a man obtains the great benefit of the performance of all Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.33.132 \|\|

*purāṇeśvara nāmaitalliṃgamaṣṭādaśāṃgulam \|*  
*aṣṭādaśānāṃ vidyānāṃ syādādhāro yadīkṣaṇāt \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. This Liṅga named Purāṇeśvara is eighteen Aṅgulas in length and breadth. By visiting this a devotee shall become receptacle of eighteen Vidyās (lores).

## \|\| 1.33.133 \|\|

*dharmaśāstreśvaraścāyaṃ smṛtibhiśca pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*smṛtyadhyayanajaṃ puṇyaṃ yadvilokanato bhavet \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. This is Dharmaśāstreśvara installed by the Smṛtis. By visiting it, one derives the benefit and merit of studying the Smṛtis.

## \|\| 1.33.134 \|\|

*sārasvatamidaṃ liṃgaṃ sarvajāḍyavināśakṛt \|*  
*sarvatīrtheśvaraṃ liṃgametatsadyo viśuddhidam \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. This is Sārasvata Liṅga that causes the destruction of all sluggishness and ignorance. This is Sarvatīrtheśvara Liṅga which bestows purity instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.33.135 \|\|

*śaileśvarasya liṃgasya maṃḍapoyaṃ mahādbhutaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ ratnajātānāṃ yo bibharti parāṃ śriyam \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. This is the extremely wonderful pavilion of Śaileśvara Liṅga. It has the great splendour of all kinds of jewels.

## \|\| 1.33.136 \|\|

*saptasāgarasaṃjñaṃ vai liṃgametanmanoharam \|*  
*yadvīkṣaṇāllabhenmartyaḥ saptābdhisnānajaṃ phalam \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. This is the charming Liṅga named Saptasāgara, on visiting which a man obtains the benefit of taking the holy bath in the seven seas.

## \|\| 1.33.137 \|\|

*asau maṃtreśvaraḥ śrīmānmaṃtrajāpyaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*saptakoṭimahāmaṃtraiḥ sthāpito yaḥ purā yuge \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. This is the glorious Mantreśvara who bestows the benefit of reciting Mantras. Formerly in Kṛtayuga this was installed by seven crores of great Mantras.

## \|\| 1.33.138 \|\|

*tripureśasya liṃgasya puraḥ kuṃḍamidaṃ mahat \|*  
*tripuraiḥ khānitaṃ pūrvaṃ tripurāripriyaṃ param \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. This is the great Kuṇḍa in front of Tripureśa Liṅga which was dug by Tripuras formerly. It is a great favourite of Lord Śiva.

## \|\| 1.33.139 \|\|

*idaṃ vāṇeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ sahasrabhujapūjitam \|*  
*dvibhujasyāpi bāṇasya sahasrabhujahetukam \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. This is Bāṇeśvara Liṅga worshipped by Bāṇa who had a thousand arms. It had caused the two-armed Bāṇa to become thousand-armed.

## \|\| 1.33.140 \|\|

*vairocaneśvaraścaiṣa puraḥ prahlādakeśavāt \|*  
*balikeśavanāmāsāveṣa nāradakeśavaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. This is Vairocaneśvara in front of Prahlādakeśava. This (Lord) is named Balikeśava and this is Nāradakeśava.

## \|\| 1.33.141 \|\|

*ādikeśava pūrveṇa tvayamādityakeśavaḥ \|*  
*bhīṣmakeśavanāmāsau dattātreyeśvarastvayam \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. This is Ādityakeśava to the east of Ādikeśava. This is Bhīṣmakeśava and this one is Dattātreyeśvara.

## \|\| 1.33.142 \|\|

*dattātreyeśvarātpūrvameṣa ādi gadādharaḥ \|*  
*bhṛgukeśavanāmāsāveṣa vāmanakeśavaḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. To the east of Dattātreyeśvara, this is Ādigadādhara. This is Bhṛgukeśava and this is Vāmanakeśava.

## \|\| 1.33.143 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇāvetau yajñavārāhakeśavaḥ \|*  
*vidāranārasiṃhoyaṃ gopīgoviṃda eṣa ha \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. These are Nara and Nārāyaṇa. This is Yajñavārāhakeśava. This is Vidāranārasiṃha and this is the famous Gopīgovinda.

## \|\| 1.33.144 \|\|

*eṣa lakṣmīnṛsiṃhasya prāsādo ratnaketanaḥ \|*  
*yasya prasādātprahlādaḥ padamaiṃdramavāptavān \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. This is the palace with a jewel-set flagstaff of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha by whose grace Prahlāda attained the region of Indra.

## \|\| 1.33.145 \|\|

*akharvasiddhidaḥ puṃsāmeṣa kharvavināyakaḥ \|*  
*śeṣamādhavanāmāsau śeṣeṇa sthāpitaḥ purā \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. This is Kharvavināyaka who bestows great spiritual powers on men. This is Śeṣamādhava, formerly installed by Śeṣa.

## \|\| 1.33.146 \|\|

*yasya bhaktā na dahyaṃte tvapi saṃvartavahninā \|*  
*śaṃkhamādhavanāmāsau śaṃkhaṃ hatvātra saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. This is Śaṅkhamādhava who stationed himself here after killing Śaṅkha. His devotees do not get themselves burned even by the Saṃvarta fire (of world annihilation).

## \|\| 1.33.147 \|\|

*idaṃ sārasvataṃ srotaḥ paraṃ brahmarasāyanam \|*  
*sarasvatyā mahānadyāḥ saṃgamo yatra gaṃgayā \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. This is the (stream of Sarasvatī), the elixir of the great Absolute. This is the place where the great river Sarasvatī joins Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.33.148-153 \|\|

*yatrāplutā narā bhūyaḥ saṃbhavaṃti na bhūtale \|*  
*śrībiṃdumādhavastveṣa sākṣāllakṣmīpatiḥ paraḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

*śraddhayā yaṃ namanmartyo na vasedgarbhaveśmani \|*  
*na dāridryamavāpnoti vyādhibhirnābhibhūyate \|\| 149 \|\|*

*biṃdumādhavabhakto yastaṃ yamopi namasyati \|*  
*praṇavātmā ya eko'sti nādabiṃdu svarūpadhṛk \|\| 150 \|\|*

*amūrtaṃ yatparaṃ brahma biṃdumādhava eva saḥ \|*  
*etatpaṃcanadaṃ tīrthaṃ paṃcabrahmātmasaṃjñakam \|\| 151 \|\|*

*yatra snāto na gṛhṇīyāccharīraṃ pāṃcabhautikam \|*  
*eṣā sā maṃgalāgaurī kāśyāṃ paramamaṃgalam \|\| 152 \|\|*

*yatprasādādavāpnoti naro'tra ca paratra ca \|*  
*mayūkhādityasaṃjñoyaṃ raśmimālī tamopahaḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

148-151a. Men who immerse themselves therein are not reborn on the earth.

This is Śrī Bindumādhava himself, the great Lord of Lakṣmī. A man who bows to him with faith, will not stay in the abode of a womb. He never suffers from poverty. He is never assailed by ailments. Even Yama bows down to the devotee of Bindumādhava. He is the sole Ātman of Praṇava assuming the form of Nāda and Bindu. The unembodied great Brahman is this Bindumādhava.

151b-152a. This is the holy Tīrtha named Pañcabrahmātman. He who takes his holy dip therein, does not take up physical body consisting of the five (gross) elements.

152b-153. This is that Maṅgalāgaurī in Kāśī, the producer of great auspiciousness here and hereafter by means of her grace.

This Lord is termed Mayūkhāditya, the Sun that has garlands of rays and is the dispeller of darkness.

## \|\| 1.33.154 \|\|

*gabhastīśo mahāliṃgametaddivyamahaḥpradam \|*  
*mṛkaṃḍusūnunāpyatra tapastaptaṃ purā mahat \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. This is the great Liṅga Gabhastīśa that bestows divine lustre. Formerly great penance was performed here by the son of Mṛkaṇḍu.

## \|\| 1.33.155-156 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya paramaṃ svanāmnāyuḥpradaṃ param \|*  
*kiraṇeśvaranāmaitalliṃgaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|\| 155 \|\|*

*sakṛnna tamidaṃ lokaṃ nayetkiraṇamālinaḥ \|*  
*dhautapāpeśvaraṃ liṃgametatpātakadhāvanam \|\| 156 \|\|*

155-156. (Mārkaṇḍeya) had installed a great Liṅga (before performing penance) named after himself. It is the great bestower of longevity.

This Liṅga named Kiraṇeśvara is well-known in all the three worlds. Even if it is bowed to once, it leads one to the region of Kiraṇamālin (Sun).

This Liṅga Dhautapāpeśvara is the purifier of all sins.

## \|\| 1.33.157-167 \|\|

*nirvāṇanarasiṃhoyaṃ bhaktanirvāṇakāraṇam \|*  
*maṇipradīpanāgoyaṃ mahāmaṇivibhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

*yadarcanānnaro jātu na nāgaiḥ paribhūyate \|*  
*kapileśamidaṃ liṃgaṃ kapilena pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 158 \|\|*

*mucyaṃte kapayopyasya darśanātkimu mānavāḥ \|*  
*priyavrateśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ mahadetatprakāśate \|\| 159 \|\|*

*yasyārcanāllabhejjaṃtuḥ priyatvaṃ sarvajantuṣu \|*  
*idamāyatanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ maṇimāṇikyanirmitam \|\| 160 \|\|*

*śrīmataḥ kālarājasya kalikālārtihāriṇaḥ \|*  
*nijabhaktaṃ janaṃ pāti yaḥ pāpātpāpabhakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*kṣetravighnakarānpāpānyātayanyātanā śataiḥ \|*  
*iyaṃ maṃdākinī ramyā tapastaptumihāgatā \|\| 162 \|\|*

*kāśīvāsasukhaṃ prāpya nādyāpi divamīhate \|*  
*snātvātra saṃtarpya pitṝñchrāddhaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

*naro na narakaṃ paśyedapi duṣkṛtakarmakṛt \|*  
*yāni kāni ca liṃgāni kāśyāṃ saṃti sahasraśaḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

*ratnabhūtamidaṃ teṣu liṃgaṃ ratneśvarābhidham \|*  
*ratneśvaraprasādena bhuktvā ratnānyanekaśaḥ \|\| 165 \|\|*

*puruṣārthamahāratnaṃ nirvāṇaṃ ko na labdhavān \|*  
*kṛttivāseśvarasyaiṣā mahāprāsādanirmitiḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

*yāṃ dṛṣṭvāpi naro dūrātkṛttivāsaḥ padaṃ labhet \|*  
*sarveṣāmapi liṃgānāṃ maulitvaṃ kṛttivāsasaḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

157-159a. This is Nirvāṇanarasiṃha, the giver of Nirvāṇa (liberation) unto the devotees. This is Maṇipradīpanāga with great jewels for ornaments. By worshipping it, a man can prevent an attack by serpents. He is never tormented by them.

This is Kapileśa Liṅga installed by Kapila. By visiting this, even monkeys are liberated. Nothing need be said about human beings.

159b-162a. This great Liṅga Priyavrateśvara shines. By worshipping this a creature attains the love and favour of all creatures.

This excellent abode constructed with jewels and rubies belongs to the glorious Kālarāja, the remover of the distress of the Kali Age. He is Pāpabhakṣaṇa (‘devourer of sins’) who protects his devotees from sins by punishing sinners causing obstacles in the holy spot. He tortures them in hundreds of ways.

162b-166a. This is the beautiful Mandākinī who has come here to perform penance. Having experienced the pleasure of residence in Kāśī, she does not yearn for heaven till today. By taking the holy dip here, propitiating the Pitṛs and performing Śrāddha in accordance with the injuctions, even a man committing evil deeds can avoid seeing hells.

This is the Liṅga named Ratneśvara that has become the crest-jewel of the thousands of Ratnas present in Kāśī. Who has not obtained salvation which is the great crest-jewel of all the aims of human life, after enjoying innumerable Ratnas by the grace of Ratneśvara?

166b-167. This is the loftily erected mansion of Kṛttivāseśvara, on seeing which from afar a man may attain even the status of Kṛttivāsas (Lord Śiva).

The Liṅgātmaka Physical Frame of Viśveśvara (167-172)

Of all the Liṅgas, the status of being the head is that of Kṛttivāsas.

## \|\| 1.33.168 \|\|

*oṃkāreśaḥ śikhā jñeyā locanāni trilocanaḥ \|*  
*gokarṇabhārabhūteśau tatkarṇau parikīrtitau \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. Oṃkāreśa is to be known as the tuft of hair. Trilocana constitutes the three eyes. Gokarṇa and Bhārabhūteśa are glorified as the ears.

## \|\| 1.33.169 \|\|

*viśveśvarāvimuktau ca dvāvetau dakṣiṇau karau \|*  
*dharmeśamaṇikarṇeśau dvau karau dakṣiṇetarau \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. The two, Viśveśvara and Avimukta, are the two right hands. The two, Dharmeśa and Maṇikarṇeśa, are the two left hands.

## \|\| 1.33.170 \|\|

*kāleśvarakapardīśau caraṇāvatinirmalau \|*  
*jyeṣṭheśvaro nitaṃbaśca nābhirvai madhyameśvaraḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. The two spotlessly pure feet are Kāleśvara and Kapardīśa. Jyeṣṭheśvara is the waist and Madhyameśvara is the navel.

## \|\| 1.33.171 \|\|

*kapardosya mahādevaḥ śirobhūṣā śrutīśvaraḥ \|*  
*caṃdreśo hṛdayaṃ tasya ātmā vīreśvaraḥ paraḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. Mahādeva is the Kaparda (matted hairs). Śrutīśvara is the crest-jewel. Candreśa is the heart thereof. The Ātman (Ahamkāra—ego) is the great Vīreśvara.

## \|\| 1.33.172 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ tasya tu kedāraḥ śukraṃ śukreśvaraṃ viduḥ \|*  
*anyāni yāni liṃgāni paraḥ koṭi śatāni ca \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. Kedāra is its penis (Liṅga). They know that Śukreśvara is the semen virile. Millions and billions of the other Liṅgas should be known as the nails, hairs and the ornaments of the body.

## \|\| 1.33.173-175 \|\|

*jñeyāni nakhalomāni vapuṣo bhūṣaṇānyapi \|*  
*yāvetau dakṣiṇau hastau nityanirvāṇadau hi tau \|\| 173 \|\|*

*jaṃtūnāmabhayaṃ dattvā patatāṃ mohasāgare \|*  
*iyaṃ durgā bhagavatī pitṛliṃgamidaṃ param \|\| 174 \|\|*

*iyaṃ hi citraghaṃṭeśī ghaṃṭākarṇa hradastvayam \|*  
*iyaṃ sā lalitā gaurī viśālākṣīyamadbhutā \|\| 175 \|\|*

173-175. These two, the right hands (i.e., Viśveśvara and Avimukta), are indeed the perpetual bestowers of salvation on the creatures that fall into the ocean of delusion, after granting them freedom from fear.

This is Goddess Durgā. This is the great Pitṛ Liṅga.

This is Citraghaṇṭeśī. This is the Hrada (eddy) of Ghaṇṭākarṇa. This is that famous Lalitāgaurī. This is miraculous Viśālākṣī.

## \|\| 1.33.176 \|\|

*āśāvināyakastveṣa dharmakūpoyamadbhutaḥ \|*  
*yatra piṃḍānnaro dattvā pitṝnbrahmapadaṃ nayet \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. This is Āśāvināyaka. This is the wonderful Dharmakūpa. If a man offers balls of rice here, he will lead his ancestors to the region of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.33.177-180 \|\|

*eṣā viśvabhujā devī viśvaikajananī parā \|*  
*asau baṃdī mahādevī nityaṃ trailokyavaṃditā \|\| 177 \|\|*

*nigaḍasthānapi janānpāśānmocayati smṛtā \|*  
*daśāśvamedhikaṃ tīrthametattrailokyavaṃditam \|\| 178 \|\|*

*yatrāhutitrayeṇāpi agnihotraphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*prayāgākhyamidaṃ srotaḥ sarvatīrthottamottamam \|\| 179 \|\|*

*aśokākhyamidaṃ tīrthaṃ gaṃgākeśava eṣa vai \|*  
*mokṣadvāramidaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ svarga dvāramidaṃ viduḥ \|\| 180 \|\|*

177-180. This is Goddess Viśvabhujā (‘Omni-armed’), the great Goddess Bandī, always revered by the three worlds. On being remembered, she frees from bondage even if the persons be in fetters.

This is the Daśāśvamedhika Tīrtha, honoured by the three worlds. Even with three Āhutis here, one shall attain the benefit of keeping Agnihotra.

This is the Tīrtha named Prayāga which is the most excellent of all Tīrthas.

This is the Tīrtha named Aśoka. This is Gaṅgākeśava. This is the most excellent gateway to salvation. They know this as the gateway to heaven. (Mokṣadvāra and Svargadvāra are the names of holy shrines.)

## Chapter 34 - In Praise of Jñānavāpī

## \|\| 1.34.1-2 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*punardadarśa tanvaṃgī citrapaṭyāṃ ghaṭodbhava \|*  
*svargadvārātpurobhāge śrīmatīṃ maṇikarṇikām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*saṃsārasarpadaṣṭānāṃ jaṃtūnāṃ yatra śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*apasavyena hastena brūte brahmaspṛśañchrutim \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1-2. O Pot-born One, again the slim (slender-limbed) lady saw in the painted canvas, in front of Svargadvāra, the glorious Maṇikarṇikā where Śaṅkara touches with his right hand the ear of the creatures bitten by the serpent of worldly existence and instructs Brahma-knowledge to them.

## \|\| 1.34.3 \|\|

*na kāpilena yogena na sāṃkhyena na ca vrataiḥ \|*  
*yā gatiḥ prāpyate puṃbhistāṃ dadyānmokṣabhūriyam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. This holy place of salvation shall grant that goal which cannot be attained by men either by Sāṃkhya imparted by Kapila, or by Yoga or by holy rites and observances.

## \|\| 1.34.4 \|\|

*vaikuṃṭhe viṣṇubhavane viṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*japeyuḥ satataṃ muktyai śrīmatīṃ maṇikarṇikām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Even in Vaikuṇṭha, the abode of Viṣṇu, those engrossed in devotion to Viṣṇu engage themselves in the Japa of the glorious Maṇikarṇikā for the sake of liberation.

## \|\| 1.34.5 \|\|

*hutvāgnihotramapi ca yāvajjīvaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*aṃte śrayaṃte muktyai yāṃ seyaṃ śrīmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. This is that glorious Maṇikarṇikā which excellent Brāhmaṇas ultimately resort to for attaining salvation, even after performing Agnihotra throughout their life.

## \|\| 1.34.6 \|\|

*vedānpaṭhitvā vidhivadbrahmayajñaratā bhuvi \|*  
*yāṃ śrayaṃti dvijā muktyai seyaṃ śrīmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. This is the glorious Maṇikarṇikā which Brāhmaṇas who, after duly reciting the Vedas, engaged themselves in Brahmayajña in this world, resort to for the sake of liberation.

## \|\| 1.34.7 \|\|

*iṣṭvā kratūnapi nṛpā bahūnparyāptadakṣiṇān \|*  
*śrayaṃte śreyase dhanyāḥ prāṃte'dhimaṇikarṇikam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After performing many Kratus with profuse monetary gifts the blessed kings resort to Maṇikarṇikā for the sake of excellence.

## \|\| 1.34.8 \|\|

*sīmaṃtinyopi satataṃ pativrataparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*muktyai patimanuvrajya śrayaṃti maṇikarṇikām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Chaste women too, always devoted to their husbands, resort to Maṇikarṇikā for salvation, by following (in death) their husbands (here).

## \|\| 1.34.9 \|\|

*vaiśyā api ca sevaṃte nyāyopārjitasaṃpadaḥ \|*  
*dhanāni sādhusātkṛtvā prāṃte śrīmaṇikarṇikām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Vaiśyas too who have accumulated wealth through legitimate means, entrust (by Dāna) their riches to holy men in the end and serve the glorious Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 1.34.10 \|\|

*tyaktvā putrakalatrādi sacchūdrā nyāyamārgagāḥ \|*  
*nirvāṇaprāptaye caināṃ bhajeyurmaṇikarṇikām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Excellent Śūdras treading the path of the moral code, leave off their sons, wives etc., and resort to this Maṇikarṇikā for the attainment of salvation.

## \|\| 1.34.11 \|\|

*yāvajjīvaṃ caraṃtopi brahmacarya jiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*niḥśreyase śrayaṃtyenāṃ śrīmatīṃ maṇikārṇakām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Those who have conquered the sense-organs and practised celibacy throughout their life, resort to this glorious Maṇikarṇikā for the sake of salvation.

## \|\| 1.34.12 \|\|

*atithīnapi saṃtarpya paṃcayajñaratā api \|*  
*gṛhasthāśramiṇo nemāṃ tyajeyurmaṇikarṇikām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Even those persons in the householder’s stage of life, who propitiate guests (by due reception) and who are engrossed in the performance of Pañcayajñas do not abandon this Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 1.34.13 \|\|

*vānaprasthāśramayujo jñātvā nirvāṇasādhanam \|*  
*sanniyamyeṃdriyagrāmaṃ maṇikarṇīmupāsate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Those who have adopted the stage of life of the Vānaprastha resort to Maṇikarṇika \[Maṇikarṇikā?\] after controlling all the sense-organs and knowing (it to be) the means of salvation.

## \|\| 1.34.14 \|\|

*ananyasādhanāṃ muktiṃ jñātvā śāstrairanekadhā \|*  
*mumukṣubhistvekadaṃḍaiḥ sevyate maṇikarṇikā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. From the diverse scriptural texts they know that salvation cannot be attained by any other means. Hence Ekadaṇḍa sages who desire salvation resort to Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 1.34.15 \|\|

*daṃḍayitvā manovācaṃ kāyaṃ nityaṃ tridaṃḍinaḥ \|*  
*naiḥśreyasīṃ śriyaṃ prāptuṃ śrayaṃte maṇikarṇikām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Tridaṇḍin sages suppress their mind (by Prāṇāyāma), speech (by silence) and body always and resort to Maṇikarṇikā to attain the glory of salvation.

## \|\| 1.34.16 \|\|

*saṃnyastākhilakarmāṇo daṃḍayitvā calaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*ekadaṃḍavratā muktyai bhajeyurmaṇikarṇikām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Persons observing the holy rite of Ekadaṇḍa, who have forsaken all activites and suppressed the fickle mind, resort to Maṇikarṇikā for attaining salvation.

## \|\| 1.34.17 \|\|

*śikhī muṃḍī jaṭī vāpi kaupīnī vā digaṃbaraḥ \|*  
*mumukṣuḥ ko na seveta muktidāṃ maṇikarṇikām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Whether he be Śikhin (having tuft), or Muṇḍin (shavenheaded), Jaṭin (having matted hairs), Kaupīnin (having a loin cloth) or nude, which holy man desirous of salvation does not serve (resort to) Maṇikarṇikā?

## \|\| 1.34.18 \|\|

*tapaḥkartuṃ na śaktā ye dānaṃ vā dātumakṣamāḥ \|*  
*yogābhyāsa vihīnā ye teṣāmeṣā vimuktidā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Those who are unable to perform penance, or to make holy monetary gifts, those who do not have the practice of Yoga—to all these this Maṇikarṇikā accords salvation.

## \|\| 1.34.19 \|\|

*saṃtyupāyāḥ sahasraṃ tu muktaye na tathā mune \|*  
*helayaiṣā yathā dadyānnirvāṇaṃ maṇikarṇikā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There are a thousand means of salvation, O sage. But none of them bestows salvation as easily as this Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 1.34.20 \|\|

*anaśanavratabhṛte trikālābhyavahāriṇe \|*  
*prāṃte dadyātsamāṃ muktimubhābhyāṃ maṇikarṇikā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Maṇikarṇikā bestows equal salvation in the end on both—on him who has undertaken the vow of fast and on him who takes food thrice a day.

## \|\| 1.34.21-22 \|\|

*yathoktamācaredeko niṣṭhā pāśupataṃvratam \|*  
*niraṃtaraṃ smaredeko hṛdyenāṃ maṇikarṇikām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭātra vapuṣaḥ pāte dvayośca sadṛśī gatiḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvavihāyāśu sevyaiṣā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. A person may practise Pāśupata Vrata with great steadfastness in accordance with injunction as laid down in scriptures. Another person may continuously remember Maṇikarṇikā in his heart. If the body is cast into the river at Maṇikarṇikā, the goal attained by both is the same. Hence Maṇikarṇikā should be resorted to quickly after forsaking everything else.

## \|\| 1.34.23 \|\|

*svargadvāre viśeyurye vigāhya maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*teṣāṃ vidhūtapāpānāṃ kāpi svargo na dūrataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Those who dive into Maṇikarṇikā and enter Svargadvāra become rid of all sins. Heaven is not far from them.

## \|\| 1.34.24 \|\|

*svargadvāḥ svargabhūreṣā mokṣabhūrmaṇikarṇikā \|*  
*svargāpavargāvatraiva nopariṣṭānna cāpyadhaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. This Maṇikarṇikā is the gateway to heaven. It is the ground leading to both heaven and salvation. Heavenly goal as well as salvation is accessible here itself, neither above nor below.

## \|\| 1.34.25 \|\|

*dattvā dānānyanekāni vigāhya maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*svargadvāraṃ praviṣṭā ye na te nirayagāminaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After making many types of gifts and taking a bath in Maṇikarṇikā, people shall enter Svargadvāra. They shall never go to hell.

## \|\| 1.34.26 \|\|

*svargāpavargayorarthaḥ kovidaiśca nirūpitaḥ \|*  
*svargaḥ sukhaṃ samuddiṣṭamapavargo mahāsukham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The meaning of the words Svarga and Apavarga has been settled by learned people: Svarga means happiness and Apavarga, great happiness (i.e., Mokṣa).

## \|\| 1.34.27 \|\|

*maṇikarṇyupaviṣṭasya yatsukhaṃ jāyate sataḥ \|*  
*siṃhāsanopaviṣṭasya tatsukhaṃ kva śatakratoḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Though Indra is seated on a throne, where has he that happiness which one sitting in Maṇikarṇikā attains?

## \|\| 1.34.28 \|\|

*mahāsukhaṃ yaduddiṣṭaṃ samādhau vismṛtātmanām \|*  
*śrīmatyāṃ maṇikarṇyāṃ tatsahajenaiva jāyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In the glorious Maṇikarṇikā, one gets naturally that great happiness which has been indicated in the meditation of those who forget themselves in contemplation.

## \|\| 1.34.29 \|\|

*svargadvārātpurobhāge devanadyāśca paścime \|*  
*saubhāgyabhāgyaikanidhiḥ kācidekā mahāsthalī \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. To the east of Svargadvāra and to the west of the celestial river, there is a great territory, the sole storehouse of blessedness and good fortune.

## \|\| 1.34.30 \|\|

*yāvaṃto bhāsvataḥ sparśādbhāsaṃte saikatāḥ kaṇāḥ \|*  
*tāvaṃto druhiṇā jagmurnaityeṣā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. As many sand particles shining due to the touch of the Sun (light) (are there, so many) Brahmās (the creators of the universe) passed away, but Maṇikarṇikā did not.

## \|\| 1.34.31 \|\|

*saṃti tīrthāni tāvaṃti parito maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*yāvadbhistilamātrāpi na bhūmirviralīkṛtā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Around Maṇikarṇikā there are as many Tīrthas as would leave no space of the size of a gingelly seed vacant.

## \|\| 1.34.32 \|\|

*yadanvaye kopi muktaḥ saṃprāpya maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*tadvaṃśyāstatprabhāveṇa mānyāḥ svargaukasāmapi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If a person in a certain family is liberated by attaining to Maṇikarṇikā, his descendants become worthy of being respected by even the heaven-dwellers due to his power.

## \|\| 1.34.33 \|\|

*tarpitāḥ pitaro yena saṃprāpya maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*saptasapta tathā sapta pūrvajāstena tāritāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Twenty-seven generations of his ancestors are redeemed by a man who offers libations to the Manes after reaching Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 1.34.34 \|\|

*āmadhyāddevasarita ā hariścaṃdramaḍapāt \|*  
*ā gaṃgā keśavādā ca svardvārānmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Maṇikarṇikā lies between the middle of the celestial river and Hariścandramaṇḍapa, between Svargadvāra and Gaṅgākeśava.

## \|\| 1.34.35 \|\|

*etadrajaḥkaṇatulāṃ trilokyapi na gacchati \|*  
*etatprāptyai prayatate trilokastho'khilo bhavī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even the three worlds do not attain equality with even a particle of this Maṇikarṇikā. All the beings stationed in the three worlds endeavour to attain this.

## \|\| 1.34.36 \|\|

*kalāvatī citrapaṭīṃ paśyaṃtītthaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*jñānavāpīṃ dadarśātha śrīviśveśvaradakṣiṇe \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Looking the painted canvas thus frequently, Kalāvatī spotted Jñānavāpī to the south of Śrī Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 1.34.37 \|\|

*yadaṃbusatataṃ rakṣeddurvṛttāddaṃḍanāyakaḥ \|*  
*saṃbhramo vibhramaścāsau dattvā bhrātiṃ garīyasīm \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Daṇḍanāyaka, Saṃbḥrama and Vibhrama make the evil-minded ones extremely confused and protect the waters of Jñānavāpī from them.

## \|\| 1.34.38 \|\|

*yoṣṭamūrtirmahādevaḥ purāṇe paripaṭhyate \|*  
*tasyaiṣāṃbumayī mūrtirjñānadā jñānavāpikā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. This Jñānavāpī, the bestower of knowledge, is the aquatic physical form of the eight-formed Mahādeva cited in the Purāṇas.

## \|\| 1.34.39 \|\|

*netrayoratithīkṛtya jñānavāpī kalāvatī \|*  
*kadaṃbakusumākārāṃ babhāra kṣaṇatastanum \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After viewing Jñānavāpī, Kalāvatī experienced horripilation all over her body like the flowers of a Kadaṃba tree.

## \|\| 1.34.40 \|\|

*aṃgāni vepathuṃ prāpuḥ svinnā bhālasthalī bhṛśam \|*  
*harṣavāṣpāṃbukalile jāte tasyā vilocane \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Her limbs experienced tremor; the region of the forehead was profusely covered with perspiration and her eyes were filled with tears of joy.

## \|\| 1.34.41 \|\|

*tastaṃbha gātralatikā mukhavaivarṇyamāpa ca \|*  
*svarotha gadgado jāto vyabhraṃśattatkarātpaṭī \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Her creeper-like body became rigid; the face lost its colour; the voice became choked and the painted canvas fell down from her hands.

## \|\| 1.34.42 \|\|

*sākṣaṇaṃ svaṃ visasmāra kāhaṃ kvāhaṃ na vetti ca \|*  
*sauṣuptāyāṃ daśāyāṃ ca paramātmeva niścalā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. For a moment she forgot her own self. She did not know “Who am I?” “Where am I?” In that state of deep sleep, she was as motionless as the great soul.

## \|\| 1.34.43 \|\|

*atha tatparicāriṇyastvaramāṇā itastataḥ \|*  
*kiṃ kiṃ kimetadetatkiṃ pṛcchaṃti sma parasparam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Her attendants hurriedly moved about here and there and asked one another, “What, what is the matter? What is this?”

## \|\| 1.34.44 \|\|

*tadavasthāṃ samālokya tāṃ tāścaturacetasaḥ \|*  
*vijñāya sāttvikairbhāvairidamūcūḥ parasparam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On seeing her in that plight, those wise and experienced women understood everything through those psychosomatic emotional expresions, and told one another thus:

## \|\| 1.34.45 \|\|

*bhavāṃtare premapātrametayaikṣitu kiṃcana \|*  
*cirāttena ca saṃgatya sukhamūrcchāmavāpa ha \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “Some object of her love in a former birth has been seen by her. After coming into contact thereof, she has reached an ecstatic state.”

## \|\| 1.34.46-47 \|\|

*athanetthaṃ kathamiyamakāṃḍātparyamūmuhat \|*  
*prekṣamāṇā rahaścitrapaṭīmati paṭīyasīm \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tanmohasya nidānaṃ tāḥsamyageva vicārya ca \|*  
*upacerurmahāśāṃtairupacārairanākulam \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. If it is not so, how did she swoon all of a sudden? While viewing this picture-canvas in secrecy, they carefully pondered over the primary cause of her loss of consciousness and administered pacifying remedies calmly to her.

## \|\| 1.34.48 \|\|

*kācittāṃ vījayāṃcakre kadalītālavṛṃtakaiḥ \|*  
*bisinīvalayairanyā dhanyāṃ tāṃ paryabhūṣayat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. One of them fanned her with plantain leaves. Another one embellished the blessed lady with circular garlands of lotus fibres.

## \|\| 1.34.49 \|\|

*amaṃdaiścaṃdanarasairabhyaṣiṃcadamuṃ parā \|*  
*aśokapallavairasyāḥ kācicchokamanīnaśat \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Another attendant sprinkled her with profuse flow of sandal water. A certain attendant removed her sorrow with tender foliage of Aśoka.

## \|\| 1.34.50 \|\|

*dhārāmaṃḍapadhārāṃbusīkaraistattanūlatām \|*  
*iṣṭārthavirahaglānāṃ siṃcayāmāsa kācana \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. With the sprays of water from the fountain pavilion, a certain attendant sprinkled the creeper-like tender body of that lady emaciated through separation, in order to get the desired effect.

## \|\| 1.34.51 \|\|

*jalārdravāsasā kācidetasyāstanumāvṛṇot \|*  
*karpūrakṣodajālepairanyāstāmanvalepayan \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. A certain attendant covered her body with a wet cloth. Another smeared it with the paste of camphor powder.

## \|\| 1.34.52-59 \|\|

*padminīdalaśayyā ca kācityaracayanmṛdum \|*  
*kācitkuliśanepathyaṃ dūrīkṛtya tadaṃgataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*muktākalāpaṃ racayāṃcakre vakṣojamaṃḍale \|*  
*kācicchaśimukhī tāṃ tu caṃdrakāṃtaśilātale \|\| 53 \|\|*

*svāpayāmāsa tanvaṃgīṃ sravacchītāṃbuśītale \|*  
*dṛṣṭvopacāryamāṇāṃ tāmitthaṃ buddhiśarīriṇī \|\| 54 \|\|*

*atitāpaparītāṃgī tāḥ sakhīḥ pratyabhāṣata \|*  
*etasyāstāpaśāṃtyarthaṃ jānehaṃ paramauṣadham \|\| 55 \|\|*

*upacārānimānsavārndūrī kuruta mā ciram \|*  
*apatāpāṃ karomyenāṃ sadyaḥ paśyata kautukam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā citrapaṭīmeṣā sadyo vihvalatāmagāt \|*  
*atraiva kācidetasyāḥ premabhūrasti niścitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*ataścitrapaṭīsparśātparitāpaṃ vihāsyati \|*  
*vākyādbuddhiśarīriṇyāstatastatparicārikāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*nidhāya tatpuraḥ procuḥ paṭīṃ paśya kalāvati \|*  
*tavānaṃdakarī yatra kācidastīṣṭadevatā \|\| 59 \|\|*

52-58a. A certain attendant arranged a soft bed of lotus petals. Another attendant removed all diamond ornaments from her body and embellished her chest with pearls. Another moon-faced woman made the slim-bodied lady lie down on the ground paved with lunar stone slabs, cool on account of flowing cool water.

A certain attendant named Buddhi-śarīriṇī (‘Intellect-bodied’) saw the queen being served thus. Distressed very much, she told her companions: “I am aware of a great remedy for the suppression of her excessive distress. Do not delay. Set aside all these modes of remedy. I shall make her immediately rid of all distress. Watch the wonderful feat. It was after seeing the painted canvas that she suddenly became excited. Certainly some object of her love is here itself. Hence she will become rid of her distress at the touch of the painted canvas.”

58b-59. At the instance of Buddhiśarīriṇī the other attendants placed that painted canvas in front of Kalāvatī and said: “See here, Kalāvatī. There is your favourite deity here, the cause of your delight.”

## \|\| 1.34.60 \|\|

*sāpīṣṭadevatānāmnā tatpaṭīdarśanena ca \|*  
*sudhāsekamiva prāpya mūrchāṃ hitvotthitā drutam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. On hearing the name “favourite deity” and on seeing the painted canvas, she appeared to have been sprinkled with nectar. She regained her consciousness and got up quickly.

## \|\| 1.34.61 \|\|

*avagrahaparimlānā varṣāsārairivauṣadhīḥ \|*  
*punarālokayāṃcakre jñānadāṃ jñānavāpikām \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. It was like the revival of a herbal plant scorched by drought by means of heavy downpours of shower. Again she began to look at Jñānavāpī, the bestower of knowledge.

## \|\| 1.34.62-66 \|\|

*spṛṣṭvā kalāvatī tāṃ tu vāpīṃ citragatāmapi \|*  
*lebhe bhavāṃtarajñānaṃ yathāsītpūrvarjanmani \|\| 62 \|\|*

*punarvicārayāṃcakre vāpī māhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*aho citragatāpīyaṃ saṃspṛṣṭā jñānavāpikā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*jñānaṃ me janayāmāsa bhavāṃtara samudbhavam \|*  
*atha tāsāṃ puro hṛṣṭā kathayāmāsa suṃdarī \|\| 64 \|\|*

*nijaṃ prāgbhava vṛttāṃtaṃ jñānavāpīprabhāvajam \|*  
*kalāvatyuvāca \|*  
*etasmājjanmanaḥ pūrvamahaṃ brāhmaṇakanyakā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*upaviśveśvaraṃ kāśyāṃ jñānavāpyāṃ rame mudā \|*  
*janako me harisvāmī janayitrī priyaṃvadā \|\| 66 \|\|*

62-66. By touching the Vāpī in the picture, Kalāvatī obtained the knowledge of the previous birth and of everything that happened in the previous birth.

Again she pondered over the excellent greatness of the Vāpī: ‘How wonderful! This Jñānavāpī in the picture when touched by me has produced in me the knowledge of what happened in the previous birth.’ Thereupon, the delighted beautiful lady spoke these words in front of those attendants, regarding the events of her previous life as a result of the power of Jñānavāpī:

## \|\| 1.34.67-68 \|\|

*ākhyā mama suśīleti māṃ ca vidyādharo'harat \|*  
*madhyemārgaṃ niśīthetha tadopa malayācalam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*rakṣasā sahato vīro rākṣasaṃ sa jaghānaha \|*  
*rakṣopi muktaṃ śāpāttu divyavapuravāpa ha \|\| 68 \|\|*

Kalāvatī said:

In my previous birth, I was a Brāhmaṇa girl. I rejoiced and sported about in Jñānavāpī near Viśveśvara in Kāśī. My father was Harisvāmī and mother Priyaṃvadā.

67-68. My name was Suśīlā. A Vidyādhara abducted me. While on his way near Malaya mountain, that heroic person was killed by a demon at mid-night. He also killed the demon. Freed from his curse, the demon attained a divine body.

## \|\| 1.34.69 \|\|

*avāpa janmagaṃdharvastvasau malayaketutaḥ \|*  
*karṇāṭanṛpateḥ kanyā babhūvāhaṃ kalāvatī \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. This Gandharva was born of Malayaketu. I became the daughter Kalāvatī of the king of Karṇāṭa.

## \|\| 1.34.70-71 \|\|

*iti jñānaṃ mamodbhūtaṃ jñānavāpīkṣaṇātkṣaṇāt \|*  
*iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā sāpi buddhiśarīriṇī \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tāśca tatparicāriṇyaḥ prahṛṣṭāsyāstadā'bhavan \|*  
*procustāṃ praṇipatyātha puṇyaśīlāṃ kalāvatīm \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. This knowledge came to me instantaneously on seeing Jñānavāpī.

On hearing these words of hers, the attendant Buddhiśarīriṇī and the other attendants as well, became delighted as was evident from their beaming faces.

## \|\| 1.34.72-75 \|\|

*aho kathaṃ hi sā labhyā yatprabhāvoyamīdṛśaḥ \|*  
*dhigjanma teṣāṃ martye'sminyairnaikṣi jñānavāpikā \|\| 72 \|\|*

*kalāvati namastubhyaṃ kurunopi samīhitam \|*  
*janiṃ saphalayāsmākaṃ naya naḥ prārthya bhūpatim \|\| 73 \|\|*

*ayaṃ ca niyamosmākamadyārabhya kalāvati \|*  
*nirvekṣyāmo mahābhogāndṛṣṭvā tāṃ jñānavāpikām \|\| 74 \|\|*

*avaśyaṃ jñānavāpī sā nāmnā bhavitumarhati \|*  
*citraṃ citragatāpīha yā tava jñānadāyinī \|\| 75 \|\|*

They bowed down to that meritorious Kalāvatī and said:

72-75. “How can it be made possible to attain Jñānavāpī whose power is like this? Fie upon the life of those persons in this mortal world, by whom Jñānavāpī is not seen!

Obeissance to you, O Kalāvatī. Carry out our wish too. Make our birth fruitful by requesting the king to take us there. Beginning today, O Kalāvatī, this shall be our main observance. We will experience the delightful pleasures of great magnitude after visiting Jñānavāpī. Necessarily it must be a Jñānavāpī true to its name. It is wonderful that it bestowed on you the knowledge even when painted on a canvas!”

## \|\| 1.34.76 \|\|

*oṃkṛtya tāsāṃ vākyaṃ sā svākāraṃ parigopya ca \|*  
*priyāṇi kṛtvā bhūbhartuḥ prastāvajñā vyajijñapat \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. She assented to their request. She then got over the excited feelings and controlled them adequately. After carrying out everything pleasing to the king, she, fully conscious of the proposal to make, submitted to the king:

## \|\| 1.34.77 \|\|

*kalāvatyuvāca \|*  
*jīviteśa na me tvattaḥ kiṃcitpriyataraṃ kvacit \|*  
*tvāmāsādya patiṃ rājanprāptāḥ sarve manorathāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

Kalāvatī said:
