*jālapādānkhaṃjarīṭānbuḍitvā matsyabhakṣakān \|*  
*matsyāśī sarvamāṃsāśī tanmatsyānsarvathā tyajet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One should not eat Jālapāda-swans, Khañjariṭas and those birds which sink down into the water and eat fishes. One who eats fish is no better than a flesh-eater. So one should avoid fishes in every respect.

## \|\| 1.40.14 \|\|

*havyakavyaniyuktau tu bhakṣyau pāṭhīnarohitau \|*  
*māṃsāśibhistvamī bhakṣyāḥ śaśa śallaka kacchapāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Fishes like Pāṭhīna and Rohita have been recommended for Havya (food of gods) and Kavya (food of Manes). They can be taken in by regular meat-eaters. They can eat rabbit, porcupine and tortoise.

## \|\| 1.40.15 \|\|

*śvāvidgodhe praśaste ca jñātāśca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*āyuṣkāmaiḥ svargakāmaistyājyaṃ māṃsaṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Śvāvit (porcupine) and Godhā (alligator) are good; so also all well-known animals and birds. Meat should be avoided assiduously by those who wish for longevity and heavenly bliss.

## \|\| 1.40.16 \|\|

*yajñārthaṃ paśuhiṃsā yā sā svargyā netarā kvacit \|*  
*tyajetparyuṣitaṃ sarvamakhaṃḍasneha varjitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Killing of animals for the sake of Yajña is conducive to heavenly bliss. Not the other one. One should abandon all stale things utterly devoid of oiliness or ghee.

## \|\| 1.40.17 \|\|

*prāṇātyaye kratau śrāddhe bhaiṣaje viprakāmyayā \|*  
*alaulyamitthaṃ palalaṃ bhakṣayannaiva doṣabhāk \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. One who eats meat when threatened with danger to life, during Yajña, in Śrāddha, as a medicine, for pleasing a Brāhmaṇa without being over-tempted, cannot be blamed.

## \|\| 1.40.18 \|\|

*na tādṛśaṃ bhavetpāpaṃ mṛgayāvṛttikāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*yādṛśaṃ bhavati pretya laulyānmāṃsopasevinaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. One who desires hunting as a means of sustenance does not incur such a sin after death, as one who eats flesh after being over-tempted.

## \|\| 1.40.19 \|\|

*makhārthaṃ brahmaṇā sṛṣṭāḥ paśu druma mṛgauṣadhīḥ \|*  
*nighnannahiṃsako viprastāsāmapi śubhā gatiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Animals, trees, deer and herbs have been created by Brahmā for the sake of Yajñas. A Brāhmaṇa who kills them is really Ahiṃsaka (non-killer). They too will attain splendid goal (after death).

## \|\| 1.40.20 \|\|

*pitṛdevakratukṛte madhuparkārthameva ca \|*  
*tatra hiṃsāpyahiṃsā syāddhiṃsānyatra sudustarā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Causing injury for the sake of Pitṛs, Devas and Yajñas and also for Madhuparka is no injury. Injury in other cases cannot be overcome (i.e., is a sin without remedy).

## \|\| 1.40.21 \|\|

*yo jaṃtūnātmapuṣṭyarthaṃ hinasti jñānadurbalaḥ \|*  
*durācārasya tasyeha nāmutrāpi sukhaṃ kvacit \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He who kills animals for self-nourishment: is weak in knowledge and of evil conduct. He will never have happiness here or hereafter.

## \|\| 1.40.22 \|\|

*bhoktānumaṃtā saṃskartā krayivikrayi hiṃsakāḥ \|*  
*upahartā ghātayitā hiṃsakāścāṣṭadhā smṛtāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hiṃsakas (perpetrators of violence) are of eight kinds: (1) one who eats flesh, (2) one who permits it, (3) one who prepares it, (4) the buyer, (5) the seller, (6) the actual killer, (7) one who make a present of it, and (8) one who persuades others to kill.

## \|\| 1.40.23 \|\|

*pratyabdamaśvamedhena śataṃ varṣāṇi yo yajet \|*  
*amāṃsabhakṣako yaśca tayoraṃtyo viśiṣyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A person may perform yearly horse-sacrifices for a hundred years. Another person may abstain from eating meat. Of these two, the latter is superior.

## \|\| 1.40.24 \|\|

*yathaivātmā parastadvaddraṣṭavyaḥ sukhamicchatā \|*  
*sukhaduḥkhāni tulyāni yathātmani tathā pare \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Another man should be seen in the same way as oneself by one who wishes for happiness. Happiness and misery are equally present in oneself and in others.

## \|\| 1.40.25 \|\|

*sukhaṃ vā yadi vā cānyadyatkiṃcitkriyate pare \|*  
*tatkṛtaṃ hi punaḥ paścātsarvamātmani saṃbhavet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. If happiness or the other one (to the contrary), is caused unto others, it will recoil on oneself afterwards.

## \|\| 1.40.26 \|\|

*na kleśena vinā dravyamarthahīne kutaḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*kriyāhīne kuto dharmo dharmahīne kutaḥ sukham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Without pains or exertions money cannot be earned. How can one carry out holy rites without money? How can one have piety without holy rites? How can one get happiness without piety?

## \|\| 1.40.27 \|\|

*sukhaṃ hi sarvairākāṃkṣyaṃ tacca dharmasamudbhavam \|*  
*tasmāddharmotra kartavyaścāturvarṇyena yatnataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Happiness is desirable by all. That originates from Dharma. Hence Dharma should be performed assiduously by persons of all the four castes.

## \|\| 1.40.28 \|\|

*nyāyāgatena dravyeṇa kartavyaṃ pāralaukikam \|*  
*dānaṃ ca vidhinā deyaṃ kāle pātre ca bhāvataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. All rites for benefits in the other world should be performed by means of wealth acquired by legitimate means. Religious gifts must be duly made with devotion and faith to deserving persons at the proper time.

## \|\| 1.40.29 \|\|

*vidhihīnaṃ tathā'pātre yo dadāti pratigraham \|*  
*na kevalaṃ hi tadyāti śeṣaṃ tasya ca naśyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If one makes a gift to an undeserving person and does not follow the relevant injunction in this regard, then not only that (merit accruing from the) gift vanishes but also does his remaining Puṇya (merit).

## \|\| 1.40.30 \|\|

*vyasanārthe kuṭuṃbārthe yadṛṇārthe ca dīyate \|*  
*tadakṣayaṃ bhavedatra paratra ca na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. What is given to relieve distress, to sustain the family and to repay debts, becomes Akṣaya (having everlasting benefit) both here and hereafter.

## \|\| 1.40.31 \|\|

*mātāpitṛvihīnaṃ yo mauṃjīpāṇigrahādibhiḥ \|*  
*saṃskārayennijairarthaistasya śreyastvanaṃtakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. If one consecrates an orphan through Mauñjī, Pāṇigraha etc. (investing with sacred thread, celebrating the marriage etc.) by spending one’s own money, his Puṇya is infinite indeed.

## \|\| 1.40.32 \|\|

*agnihotrairna tacchreyo nāgniṣṭomādibhirmakhaiḥ \|*  
*yacchreyaḥ prāpyate martyairdvije caike pratiṣṭhite \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Neither through Agnihotra nor through Agniṣṭoma and other Makhas (sacrifices) can that merit be obtained by men that is acquired when a Brāhmaṇa is honoured.

## \|\| 1.40.33 \|\|

*yo hyanāthasya viprasya pāṇiṃ grāhayate kṛtī \|*  
*iha saukhyamavāpnoti sokṣayaṃ svargamāpnuyāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He who gets the marriage of a helpless Brāhmaṇa celebrated and has accomplished his purpose, enjoys happiness here and he shall attain everlasting heavenly bliss.

## \|\| 1.40.34 \|\|

*pitṛgehe tu yā kanyā rajaḥ paśyedasaṃskṛtā \|*  
*bhrūṇahā tatpitā jñeyo vṛṣalī sāpi kanyakā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If a virgin girl has her first menstruation in her father’s house without her marriage being solemnised, her father should be known as a Bhrūṇahā (‘destroyer of a foetus’) and that girl a Vṛṣalī (Śūdra girl).

## \|\| 1.40.35 \|\|

*yastāṃ pariṇayenmohātsa bhavedvṛṣalīpatiḥ \|*  
*tena saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ tyājyamapāṅkteyena sarvadā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He who, out of delusion, marries her will be the husband of a Śūdra girl. He is an Apāṅkteya (not fit to sit in the same row as the others at the time of meals). The very conversation with him should be abandoned forever.

## \|\| 1.40.36 \|\|

*vijñāya doṣamubhayoḥ kanyāyāśca varasya ca \|*  
*saṃbaṃdhaṃ racayetpaścādanyathā doṣabhākpitā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. After knowing the fault of both, i.e., that of the girl and the groom, the father should perform their marriage (once again) afterwards. Otherwise the father is blameworthy.

## \|\| 1.40.37 \|\|

*striyaḥ pavitrāḥ satataṃ naitā duṣyaṃti kenacit \|*  
*māsimāsi rajastāsāṃ duṣkṛtānyapakarṣati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Women are always pure. They do not get defiled by anything whatsoever. The monthly menstrual flow drives away their sins.

## \|\| 1.40.38 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ striyaḥ surairbhuktāḥ somagaṃdharva vahnibhiḥ \|*  
*bhuṃjate mānuṣāḥ paścānnaitāduṣyaṃ ti kenacit \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Women are enjoyed first by Suras, Soma, Gandharva and Vahni. Men enjoy them afterwards. They are not defiled by anything.

## \|\| 1.40.39 \|\|

*strīṇāṃ śaucaṃ dadau somaḥ pāvakaḥ sarvamedhyatām \|*  
*kalyāṇavāṇīṃ gaṃdharvāstena medhyāḥ sadā striyaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Soma gave women cleanliness; Pāvaka (Fire-god), purity above all. Gandharvas gave them auspicious speech. Therefore, women are always pure.

## \|\| 1.40.40 \|\|

*kanyāṃ bhuṃkte rajaḥkāle'gniḥ śaśī lomadarśane \|*  
*stanodbhedeṣu gaṃdharvāstatprāgeva pradīyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Agni enjoys a virgin at the time of the menstruation, the Moon when the (pubic) hair begin to grow and Gandharvas when the breasts begin to develop. Hence a girl is to be given in marriage before this.

## \|\| 1.40.41 \|\|

*dṛśyaromātvapatyaghnī kulaghnyudgatayauvanā \|*  
*pitṛghnyāviṣkatarajāstatastāḥ parivarjayet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A girl with hairs visible (before marriage is consecrated) kills her children; she with the breasts in developed form destroys the family; she who has menstruated destroys the father. Hence one should avoid all (such girls).

## \|\| 1.40.42 \|\|

*kanyādānaphalaprepsustasmādda dyādanagnikām \|*  
*anyathā na phalaṃ dātuḥ pratigrāhī patedadhaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence one who is desirous of the benefit of gift of a virgin should give her in marriage before Agni and others enjoy her. If not, the giver does not enjoy any benefit; one who receives her in marriage falls down (incurs sin).

## \|\| 1.40.43 \|\|

*kanyāmabhuktāṃ somādyairdadaddānaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*devabhuktāṃ dadaddātā na svargamadhigacchati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. One who gives away a girl not enjoyed by Soma and others, attains the benefit of the religious gift. Giving her who has been enjoyed by Devas, the donor does not attain heavenly pleasures.

## \|\| 1.40.44 \|\|

*śayanāsanayānāni kuṇapaṃ strīmukhaṃ kuśāḥ \|*  
*yajñapātrāṇi sarvāṇi na duṣyaṃti budhāḥ kvacit \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The wise do not condemn (as defiled) beds, seats, vehicles, Kuṇapa (a sword, or a blanket from Nepal—Comm.), the mouth of a woman, Darbha grass, sacrificial utensils.

## \|\| 1.40.45 \|\|

*vatsaḥ prasravaṇe madhye śakuniḥ phalapātane \|*  
*nāryo ratiprayogeṣu śvā mṛga grahaṇe śuciḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. A calf is pure at the time of the discharge of milk from the udder of the cow, a bird at the time when it causes a fruit to fall, women during sexual intercourse, and a dog when it catches a deer.

## \|\| 1.40.46 \|\|

*ajāśvayormukhaṃ medhyaṃ gāvo medhyāstu pṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*pādato brāhmaṇā medhyāḥ striyo medhyāstu sarvataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The mouth of goats and horses is pure; cows are pure at their backs; Brāhmaṇas are pure in their feet; and women are pure (in all parts of their person).

## \|\| 1.40.47 \|\|

*balātkāropabhuktā vā corahastagatāpi vā \|*  
*na tyājyā dayitā nārī nāsyāstyāgo vidhīyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A beloved wife should not be abandoned even if she is raped or if she falls into the clutches of robbers. Abandoning her is not laid down (anywhere).

## \|\| 1.40.48 \|\|

*āmlena tāmraśuddhiḥ syācchuddhiḥ kāṃsyasya bhasmanā \|*  
*saṃśuddhī rajasā nāryāstaṭinyā vegataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Copper becomes pure when sour (acidic) things are applied; brass becomes pure by using Bhasma (ash). A woman becomes pure through her menstruation and a river through the flow (of water).

## \|\| 1.40.49 \|\|

*manasāpi hi yā neha ciṃtayetpuruṣāṃtaram \|*  
*somayā saha saukhyāni bhuṃkte cātrāpi kīrtibhāk \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A woman who does not even mentally think of another men enjoys pleasures with Umā and enjoys renown here in the world too.

## \|\| 1.40.50 \|\|

*pitā pitāmaho bhrātā sakulyo jananī tathā \|*  
*kanyāpradaḥ pūrvanāśe prakṛtisthaḥ paraḥparaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The order of the guardians of a girl is: father, grandfather, brother, a member of the same family, mother, the man who formally gives her in marriage. If the preceding one is not available the succeeding one (is the guardian) naturally.

## \|\| 1.40.51 \|\|

*aprayacchansamāpnoti bhūṇahatyāmṛtāvṛtau \|*  
*svayaṃ tvabhāve dātṝṇāṃ kanyā kuryātsvayaṃ varam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. If the guardian does not give her in marriage, he incurs sin of slaughter of a foetus in every menstural cycle. If there is no one to give her in marriage, a girl should choose her own husband.

## \|\| 1.40.52 \|\|

*hṛtādhikārāṃ malināṃ piṃḍamātropajīvinīm \|*  
*paribhūtāmadhaḥśayyāṃ vāsayedvyabhicāriṇīm \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If a woman strays from the path of sexual purity, she shall be divested of all her rights and kept dirty and discarded from the bed. Of course, she should be given a morsel of food for sustenance.

## \|\| 1.40.53 \|\|

*vyabhicārādṛtau śuddhirgarbhe tyāgo vidhīyate \|*  
*garbhabhartṛvadhādau tu mahatyapi ca kalmaṣe \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. If the lapse in morality is only mental, the woman becomes pure after menstruation. She is abandoned if she conceives, or kills the foetus or the husband or commits any other great sin.

## \|\| 1.40.54 \|\|

*śūdrasya bhāryā śūdraiva sā ca svā ca viśaḥ smṛte \|*  
*te ca svā caiva rājñastu tāśca svācāgrajanmanaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. A Śūdra takes a Śūdra girl for wife; a Vaiśya takes a Śūdra girl as well as a Vaiśya girl for wife; a Kṣatriya takes a Śūdra, a Vaiśya as well as a Kṣatriya girl for wife; and a Brāhmaṇa takes all the other three girls as well as a Brāhmaṇa girl.

## \|\| 1.40.55 \|\|

*āropya śūdrāṃ śayane vipro gacchedadhogatim \|*  
*utpādya putraṃ śūdrāyāṃ brāhmaṇyādeva hīyate \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. By allowing a Śūdra woman to lie on his bed (i.e., marrying a Śūdra woman—Comm.) a Brāhmaṇa incurs downfall; by procreating a son of her, he swerves from the status of a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.40.56 \|\|

*daivapitryātitheyāni tatpradhānāni yasya tu \|*  
*devādyāstanna cāśnaṃti sa ca svargaṃ na gacchati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If the rites performed by him in connection with Yajñas, Śrāddhas or hospitality to guests are presided over by the Śūdra wife, Devas, etc. do not partake of it. He too shall not attain Svarga.

## \|\| 1.40.57 \|\|

*jāmayo yāni gehāni śapaṃtyapratipūjitāḥ \|*  
*kṛtyābhirnihatānīva naśyeyustānyasaṃśayam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Close female relatives curse the household wherein they are not properly honoured (which takes place in such a Brāhmaṇā-Śūdra household). Thereby these households certainly perish as if struck down by Kṛtyās (female deities of destructive powers).

## \|\| 1.40.58 \|\|

*tadabhyarcyāḥ suvāsinyo bhūṣaṇācchādanāśanaiḥ \|*  
*bhūtikāmairnarairnityaṃ satkāreṣūtsaveṣu ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Hence Suvāsinīs (women with husbands living) should be propitiated through jewels, raiments and food by men desirous of prosperity and by welcoming them in the course of festivities.

## \|\| 1.40.59 \|\|

*yatra nāryaḥ pramuditā bhūṣaṇācchādanāśanaiḥ \|*  
*ramaṃte devatāstatra syustatra saphalāḥ kriyāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Where women are happy due to ornaments, clothes and foodstuffs offered to them, deities rejoice there. All the holy rites become fruitful there.

## \|\| 1.40.60 \|\|

*yatra tuṣyati bhartrā strī striyā bhartā ca tuṣyati \|*  
*tatra veśmani kalyāṇaṃ saṃpadyeta pade pade \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. At every step, there shall be prosperity in that household where the wife (woman) is fully satisfied with the husband and the husband is completely satisfied with the wife.

## \|\| 1.40.61 \|\|

*ahutaṃ ca hutaṃ caiva prahutaṃ prāśitaṃ tathā \|*  
*brāhmaṃ hutaṃ paṃcamaṃ ca paṃcayajñā ime śubhāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. These five Yajñas are auspicious and splendid: Āhuta, Huta, Prahuta, Prāśita and Brāhmahuta.

## \|\| 1.40.62 \|\|

*japo'hutohuto homaḥ prahuto bhautiko baliḥ \|*  
*prāśitaṃ pitṛsaṃtṛptirhutaṃ brāhmaṃ dvijārcanam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Japa (Repetition of Mantras) is Āhuta; performance of Homa is Huta; oblations given to the Bhūtas constitute Prahuta; propitiation of Manes is Prāśita, and the adoration of Brāhmaṇas is Brāhmahuta.

## \|\| 1.40.63 \|\|

*paṃcayajñānimānkurvanbrāhmaṇo nāvasīdati \|*  
*eteṣāmananuṣṭhānātpaṃcasūnā avāpnuyāt \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. A Brāhmaṇa regularly performing these five Yajñas is never faced with a disaster. By not performing these, he shall incur the sin of the five Sūnās (murders).

## \|\| 1.40.64 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ kuśalaṃ pṛcchedbāhujātamanāmayam \|*  
*vaiśyaṃ sukhaṃ samāgamya śūdraṃ saṃtoṣameva ca \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On meeting a Brāhmaṇa, one should enquire about his Kuśala (welfare); on meeting a Kṣatriya one should enquire about his Anāmaya (health, freedom from illness); on meeting a Vaiśya one should enquire about his Sukha (happiness); and on meeting a Śūdra one shall enquire about his Santoṣa (satisfaction).

## \|\| 1.40.65 \|\|

*jātamātraḥ śiśustāvadyāvadaṣṭau samāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*bhakṣyābhakṣyeṣu no du्ṣyedyāvannaivopanīyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Till the eighth year is completed a child is no better than a new-born baby. Till the Upanāyana ceremony is performed, the child does not become defiled due to indiscriminate eating (prohibited food).

## \|\| 1.40.66 \|\|

*bharaṇaṃ poṣyavargasya dṛṣṭādṛṣṭaphalodayam \|*  
*pratyavāyo hyabharaṇe bhartavyastatprayatnataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The proper sustenance of those people of the Poṣya group (i.e., worthy of being brought up and nourished) has both visible and invisible benefits. In case they are not maintained there shall be disaster. Hence they are to be assiduously sustained.

## \|\| 1.40.67 \|\|

*mātāpitāgurupatnīḥ tvapatyāni samāśritāḥ \|*  
*abhyāgatotithiścāgniḥ poṣyavargā amī nava \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Poṣyas are nine: mother, father, wife of preceptor, one’s own children, dependents, (preceptor), a casual visitor, regular guests and the sacred fire.

## \|\| 1.40.68 \|\|

*sa jīvati pumānyo'tra bahubhiścopajīvyate \|*  
*jīvanmṛtotha vijñeyaḥ puruṣaḥ svodaraṃbhariḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. A man who is depended upon for subsistence by many people, lives in the real sense (of life). A man who fills his own belly should be regarded as dead though alive.

## \|\| 1.40.69 \|\|

*dīnānāthaviśiṣṭebhyo dātavyaṃ bhūtikāmyayā \|*  
*adattadānā jāyaṃte parabhāgyopajīvinaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. One with a desire for prosperity should make gifts unto the wretched, the helpless and the distinguished (scholars). Those who do not make liberal gifts are born as persons living upon other men’s fortune.

## \|\| 1.40.70 \|\|

*vibhāgaśīlasaṃyukto dayāvāṃśca kṣamāyutaḥ \|*  
*devatātithibhaktastu gṛhastho dhārmikaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. A householder of good conduct, sharing what he has with others, one having kindness and perfect forbearance and a. devotee of deities aṇd guests is said to be pious and righteous.

## \|\| 1.40.71 \|\|

*śarvarīmadhya yāmau yau hutaśeṣaṃ ca yaddhaviḥ \|*  
*tatra svapaṃstadaśnaṃśca brāhmaṇo nāvasīdati \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. A Brāhmaṇa who sleeps in the two middle Yāmas of the night (i.e., between 9.00 a.m. and 3.00 a.m.) and drinks the ghee that remains after Homa has been performed, never faces difficulties.

## \|\| 1.40.72-73 \|\|

*navaitāni gṛhasthasya kāryāṇyabhyāgate sadā \|*  
*sudhā vyayāni yatsaumyaṃ vākyaṃ cakṣurmanomukham \|\| 72 \|\|*

*abhyutthānamihāyāta sasnehaṃ pūrvabhāṣaṇam \|*  
*upāsanamanuvrajyā gṛhasthonnati hetave \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. The following nine should always be practised at the visit of a guest by a householder: Enquiry after welfare (Kuśala) in speech, eyes, mind and face; standing up for wel-coming; greeting affectionately at the outset by words like “Welcome here”; Upāsana (making him sit near oneself or massaging his feet—Comm.), Anuvrajyā (following a few steps behind the guest at the time of departure). These acts which involve no expenditure are conducive to prosperity of a householder.

## \|\| 1.40.74-76 \|\|

*tatheṣadvyayayuktāni kāryāṇyetāni vai nava \|*  
*āsanaṃ pādaśaucaṃ ca yathāśaktyāśanaṃ kṣitiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*śayyātṛṇajalābhyaṃga dīpā gārhasthya siddhidāḥ \|*  
*tathā nava vikarmāṇi tyājyāni gṛhamedhinām \|\| 75 \|\|*

*paiśunyaṃ paradārāśca drohaḥ krodhānṛtāpriyam \|*  
*dveṣo daṃbhaśca māyā ca svargamārgārgalāni hi \|\| 76 \|\|*

74-75a. Similarly the following nine should be practised involving a little expense: offering of seats, water for washing the feet, feeding within one’s capacity, ground as bed (grass underneath the bed—Comm.), water for drinking, oil for bath and lights. These nine give Siddhis (powers) in the life of a householder.

75b-76. Similarly the following nine Vikarmas (ill actions) should be avoided by a householder: Backbiting, approaching other men’s wives, injury, ruthlessness, falsehood, displeasing behaviour, hatred, arrogance and deceitfulness. These nine are obstacles in the path of heaven.

## \|\| 1.40.77-79 \|\|

*navāvaśyakakarmāṇi kāryāṇi prativāsaram \|*  
*snānaṃ saṃdhyā japo homaḥ svādhyāyo devatārcanam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*veśvadevaṃ tathātithyaṃ navamaṃ pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*nava gopyāni yānyatra mune tāni niśāmaya \|\| 78 \|\|*

*janmarkṣaṃ maithunaṃ maṃtro gṛhacchidraṃ ca vaṃcanam \|*  
*āyurdhanāpamānaṃ strī na prakāśyāni sarvathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

77-79. There are nine essential daily duties to be performed. They are: bath, Sandhyā prayers, Japa, Homa, study of the Vedas, worship of deities, Vaiśvadeva (oblation into fire before meal), receiving guests and the ninth one, libations to the Pitṛs.

O sage, listen to the nine things to be kept as secret and guarded: The star of nativity, sexual intercourse, Mantras (spells, secret counsels), interfamily feud, deception, span of life, monetary position, insult to prestige, and wife. These are not to be revealed at all.

## \|\| 1.40.80 \|\|

*navaitāni prakāśyāni rahaḥ pāpamakutsitam \|*  
*prāyogyamṛṇaśuddhiśca sānvayaḥ krayavikrayau \|*  
*kanyādānaṃ guṇotkarṣo nānyatkenāpi kutracit \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. These nine things can be revealed: secret sin, undespised thing or person, everything conducive to practical application, repayment of debts, one with the family, sale, purchase, giving away daughter (in marriage), perfection of good qualities. Nothing else should be revealed by anyone anywhere.

## \|\| 1.40.81 \|\|

*pātra mitra vinīteṣu dīnānāthopakāriṣu \|*  
*mātāpitugurūṣvetannavakaṃ dattamakṣayam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. What is given to the following nine yields inexhaustible benefit: deserving persons, friends, humble ones, poor people, helpless ones, those who help others, mother, father and preceptors.

## \|\| 1.40.82 \|\|

*niṣphalaṃ navasūtsṛṣṭaṃ cāṭacāraṇataskare \|*  
*kuvaidye kitave dhūrte śaṭhe malle ca baṃdini \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Futile indeed are these if given over to these nine: a garrulous one, a flatterer, a thief, a bad physician, a cheat, an outrageous one, a rogue, a wrestler, and a prisoner.

## \|\| 1.40.83-84 \|\|

*āpastvapi na deyāni navavastūni sarvathā \|*  
*anvaye sati sarvasvaṃ dārāṃśca śaraṇāgatān \|\| 83 \|\|*

*nyāsādhīkulavṛttiṃ ca nikṣepaṃ strīdhanaṃ sutam \|*  
*yo dadāti sa mūḍhātmā prāyaścittairviśudhyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. Even during emergency these nine things should never be given away: entire property if one has progeny, wife, those who seek refuge, short-term deposits, long-term deposits, pledged things, traditional avocation, dowry amount and a son. One who gives away these is a deluded soul. He can become pure only through expiatory rites.

## \|\| 1.40.85-86 \|\|

*etannavānāṃ navakaṃ jñātvā priyamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*anyacca navakaṃ vacmi sarveṣāṃ svargamārgadam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*satyaṃ śaucamahiṃsā ca kṣāṃtirdānaṃ dayā damaḥ \|*  
*asteyamiṃdriyākocaḥ sarveṣāṃ dharmasādhanam \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. By realizing these nine sets of nine, one shall achieve what is pleasing. I shall mention another set of nine that accords the pathway to heaven unto everyone: truthfulness, cleanliness, abstention from violence, forbearance, liberal-mindedness, mercy, mental control, non-stealing and control over the sense-organs. All these are means of piety (Dharma).

## \|\| 1.40.87 \|\|

*abhyasya navatiṃ caitāṃ svargamārgapradīpikām \|*  
*satāmabhimatāṃ puṇyāṃ gṛhastho nāvasīdati \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. A householder who adopts these ninety things that illuminate the pathway to heaven and that are approved by good persons and so are holy, is never faced with difficulties.

## \|\| 1.40.88 \|\|

*jihvā bhāryā suto bhrātā mitra dāsa samāśritāḥ \|*  
*yasyaite vinayāḍhyāśca tasya sarvatra gauravam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Everywhere one will get high estimation if he has the following: humility, a wife, a son, a brother, a friend, a servant, dependents and (his) tongue (sweet speech).

## \|\| 1.40.89 \|\|

*pānaṃ durjana saṃsargaḥ patyā ca virahoṭanam \|*  
*svapnonyagṛhavāsaśca nārīṇāṃ dūṣaṇāni ṣaṭ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The following six things defile women: drinking (wine), association with wicked persons, separation from the husband, wandering, over-sleeping and staying in another’s house.

## \|\| 1.40.90 \|\|

*samarghaṃ dhānyamuddhatya maharghaṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*sa hi vārdhuṣiko nāma tasyānnaṃ naiva bhakṣayet \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. He who collects (purchases) food-grains cheap and sells dearly (with high rates), is a usurer. No one should partake of his food.

## \|\| 1.40.91 \|\|

*agre māhiṣikaṃ dṛṣṭvā madhye ca vṛṣalīpatim \|*  
*aṃte vārdhuṣikaṃ caiva nirāśāḥ pitaro gatāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. On seeing a buffalo-keeper (Māhiṣika) in the beginning, husband of a Śūdra woman (Vṛṣalī)1 in the middle and a usurer at the end (at the time of the Śrāddha), Manes are disappointed and they go away.

## \|\| 1.40.92 \|\|

*mahiṣītyucyate nārī yā ca syādvyabhicāriṇī \|*  
*tāṃ duṣṭāṃ kāmayedyastu sa vai māhiṣikaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. (Explanation of the above two words in another way) The woman devoid of chastity is called Mahiṣī. He who loves that wicked woman is called Māhiṣika.

## \|\| 1.40.93 \|\|

*sva vṛṣaṃ yā parityajya paravṛṣe vṛṣāyate \|*  
*vṛṣalī sā hi vijñeyā na śūdrī vṛṣalī bhavet \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. She who casts off her Vṛṣa (husband) and loves another Vṛṣa, should be known as Vṛṣalī and not a Śūdra woman (alone).

## \|\| 1.40.94 \|\|

*yāvaduṣṇaṃ bhavatyannaṃ yāvanmaunena bhujyate \|*  
*tāvadaśnaṃti pitaro yāvannoktā havirguṇāḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The Manes partake of the food offerings as long as the cooked rice is hot, people eat silently and the good qualities of the Havis (food offering) are not (boastfully) described.

## \|\| 1.40.95 \|\|

*vidyāvinayasaṃpanne śrotriye gṛhamāgate \|*  
*krīḍaṃtyauṣadhayaḥ sarvā yāsyāmaḥ paramāṃ gatim \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. When a man well-versed in the Vedas and possessing learning and humility comes to the house (as a guest), all the medicinal herbs sport about (saying) “We will attain the highest state.”

## \|\| 1.40.96 \|\|

*bhraṣṭaśaucavatācāre vipre vedavivarjite \|*  
*rodityannaṃ dīyamānaṃ kiṃ mayā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. If the food is offered to a man who is ignorant of the Vedas, who is unclean, who does not practise good conduct or holy vows and who is fallen, the food begins to lament, “What sin has been committed by me?”

## \|\| 1.40.97 \|\|

*yasya koṣṭhagataṃ cānnaṃ vedābhyāsena jīryati \|*  
*sa tārayati dātāraṃ daśapūrvāndaśāparān \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. If a man (guest) is able to digest the food going into his belly due to the Vedic study and practice, he redeems ten previous generations and ten succeeding generations (of the donor).

## \|\| 1.40.98 \|\|

*na strīṇāṃ vapanaṃ kāryaṃ na ca gāḥ samanuvrajet \|*  
*na ca rātrau vasedgoṣṭhe na kuryādvaidikīṃ śrutim \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Women are not to be shaven completely. One should not follow cows (as an avocation). One should not stay in a cowpen during the night. One should not utter Vedic passages (at night, or in a cowpen).

## \|\| 1.40.99 \|\|

*sarvānkeśānsamuddhṛtya cchedayedaṃguladvayam \|*  
*evameva tu nārīṇāṃ śiraso muṃḍanaṃ bhavet \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Muṇḍana (shaving the head) of women shall be done thus: Lifting up the whole of the tress cut off to a length of two Aṅgalas (an Aṅgula is a little less than two centimeters).

## \|\| 1.40.100 \|\|

*rājā vā rājaputro vā brāhmaṇo vā bahuśrutaḥ \|*  
*akārayitvā vapanaṃ prāyaścittaṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. A king, or a prince or a Brāhmaṇa of much learning should not be subjected to tonsure. Some other expiatory rite should be fixed.

## \|\| 1.40.101 \|\|

*keśānāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya dviguṇaṃ vratamādiśet \|*  
*dviguṇā dakṣiṇā deyā brāhmaṇe vedapārage \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. For the preservation of the hairs, twice the usual Vrata should be prescribed and twice the ordinary Dakṣiṇā should be given to a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.40.102 \|\|

*yo'gṛhītvā vivāhāgniṃ gṛhastha iti manyate \|*  
*annaṃ tasya na bhoktavyaṃ vṛthā pāko hi sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. If a man considers himself a Gṛhastha (householder) without taking up the marital fire, his food should not be eaten. He is called a Vṛthāpāka (‘one with futile cooking’).

## \|\| 1.40.103 \|\|

*dārāgnihotra dīkṣāṃ ca kurute yo'graje sthite \|*  
*parivettā sa vijñeyaḥ parivittistu pūrvajaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. If the younger brother takes up a wife and gets initiated on Agnihotra even as the elder brother is awaiting it, he should be known as Parivettṛ and the elder brother becomes Parivitti.

## \|\| 1.40.104 \|\|

*parivittiḥ parivettā yayā ca parividyate \|*  
*sarve te narakaṃ yāṃti dātṛyājakapaṃcamāḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. In such a case all the five, namely Parivitti, Parivettṛ, the bride acting as instrumental (in this sinful act), the person who gave her in marriage and the priest who presided over the rite shall go to hell.

## \|\| 1.40.105 \|\|

*klībe deśāṃtarasthe ca mūke pratrajite jaḍe \|*  
*kubje kharve ca patite na doṣaḥ parivedane \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. (If the elder brother happens to be) impotent, in exile, dumb, a sluggish one, one who has renounced the world, humpback, dwarf or a fallen one, there is no harm in Parivedana (‘supersession in marriage etc.’).

## \|\| 1.40.106 \|\|

*vedākṣaraṇi yāvaṃti niyuṃjyādarthakāraṇe \|*  
*tāvatīrvai bhrūṇahatyā vedavikrayakṛllabhet \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The Brāhmaṇa who sells the Vedas incurs as many Bhrūṇahatyā (‘killing a foetus’) sins as the Vedic syllables he has utilized for monetary gain.

## \|\| 1.40.107 \|\|

*yastu pravrajito bhūtvā sevate maithunaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭirvarṣasahasrāṇi viṣṭhāyāṃ jāyate kṛmiḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. If a person who has become a recluse has sexual intercourse thereafter, he is born as a worm in faeces for sixty thousand years.

## \|\| 1.40.108 \|\|

*śūdrānnaṃ śūdrasaṃparkaḥ śūdreṇa ca sahāsanam \|*  
*śūdrādvidyāgamaḥ kaścijjvalaṃtamapi pātayet \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The following sins make even the most brilliant one fall: the food of a Śūdra, association with Śūdras, occupying the same seat as a Śūdrar and the acquisition of learning from a Śūdra.

## \|\| 1.40.109 \|\|

*śūdrādāhṛtya nirvāpaṃ ye pacaṃtyabudhā dvijāḥ \|*  
*te yāṃti narakaṃ ghoraṃ brahmatejovivarjitāḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Ignorant Brāhmaṇas who fetch donations from a Śūdra and cook that for Brāhmaṇas, being deprived of the lustre of Brāhmaṇahood, go to a terrible hell.

## \|\| 1.40.110 \|\|

*mākṣikaṃ phāṇitaṃ śākaṃ gorasaṃ lavaṇaṃ ghṛtam \|*  
*hastadattāni bhuktāni dinamekamabhojanam \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. If Honey, Phāṇita (raw sugar), greens, milk products, salt and ghee are offered into the hand and taken in, (the expiatory rite is) fasting for a day.

## \|\| 1.40.111 \|\|

*hastadattāśca ye snehā lavaṇaṃ vyajanāni ca \|*  
*dātāraṃ nopatiṣṭhaṃte bhoktā bhuṃkte tu kilbiṣam \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Hand-to-hand offering of oils, salt, pickles etc. does not benefit the donor and one who eats them incurs sin.

## \|\| 1.40.112 \|\|

*āyasenaiva pātreṇa yadannamupadīyate \|*  
*bhoktā tadviṭsamaṃ bhuṃkte dātā ca narakaṃ vrajet \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. If cooked food is offered in an iron vessel, the giver shall go to hell and the person who eats it eats it like faeces.

## \|\| 1.40.113 \|\|

*aṃgulyā daṃtakāṣṭhaṃ ca pratyakṣalavaṇaṃ ca yat \|*  
*mṛttikābhakṣaṇaṃ yacca samaṃ gomāṃsabhakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Cleaning the teeth with finger (i.e., index finger), (handling) only salt and eating clay are on a par with eating cow’s flesh.

## \|\| 1.40.114 \|\|

*pānīyaṃ pāyasaṃ bhaikṣaṃ ghṛtaṃ lavaṇameva ca \|*  
*hastadattaṃ na gṛhṇīyāttulyagomāṃsabhakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Water, milk pudding, alms, ghee and salt should not be accepted if offered hand-to-hand because it is on a par with eating cow’s flesh.

## \|\| 1.40.115 \|\|

*agrato nivasenmūrkho dūrataśca guṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*guṇānvitāya dātavyaṃ nāsti mūrkhe vyatikramaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. If a foolish one sits in front and the meritorious one sit far off, the gift is to be made to the meritorious one. There is no (harm) due to non-observance of precedence in the case of a fool.

## \|\| 1.40.116 \|\|

*brāhmaṇātikramo nāsti vipre vedavivarjite \|*  
*jvalaṃtamagnimutsṛjya nahi bhasmani hūyate \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. If a Brāhmaṇa is bereft of the study of the Vedas, there is no harm in transgressing the rule of precedence in favour of Brāhmaṇas. An oblation is not offered in ash, leaving off blazing (fire).

## \|\| 1.40.117 \|\|

*sannikṛṣṭamadhīyānaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ yo vyatikramet \|*  
*bhojane caiva dāne ca dahedāsaptamaṃ kulam \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. In the matter of taking food and offering of monetary gifts, if anyone disregards the precedence in favour of a Brāhmaṇa well-versed in the Vedas and seated nearby, it shall burn the family till the seventh generation.

## \|\| 1.40.118 \|\|

*gorakṣakānvāṇijakāṃstathā kārukuśīlavān \|*  
*preṣyānvārdhuṣikāṃścaiva viprāñśūdravadācaret \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. One should treat these Brāhmaṇas on a par with Śūdras: those who tend cows, traders, craftsmen, actors, messengers and usurers.

## \|\| 1.40.119 \|\|

*devadravyavibhāgena brahmasva haraṇena ca \|*  
*kulānyāśu vinaśyaṃti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Families come to ruin quickly by sharing the money of gods (i.e., in a temple), by misappropriating a Brāhmaṇa’s property and by disregarding the precedence in favour of a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.40.120 \|\|

*mā dehīti ca yo brūyādgavāgnibrāhmaṇeṣu ca \|*  
*tiryagyoniśataṃ gatvā cāṃḍāleṣvabhijāyate \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. If anyone says “Do not give”, in regard to cows, fires and Brāhmaṇas, he shall be born in a hundred species of brutes and then is born among Cāṇḍālas.

## \|\| 1.40.121 \|\|

*vācā yacca pratijñātaṃ karmaṇānopapāditam \|*  
*ṛṇaṃ taddharmasaṃyuktamihaloke paratra ca \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. If what (e.g. a gift) is promised orally but is not carried out in practice, it should be deemed a debt whose repayment becomes a duty in this world and in the other world.

## \|\| 1.40.122 \|\|

*vighasāśī bhavennityaṃ nityaṃ cāmṛtabhojanaḥ \|*  
*yajñaśeṣo'mṛtaṃbhuktaśeṣaṃ tu vighasaṃ viduḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. One will be Vighasāśin (‘one who eats leavings of food’) always or Amṛtabhojana (‘having nectar for food’). Remnants of Yajña are Amṛta and remnants of what is eaten is Vighasa.

## \|\| 1.40.123 \|\|

*savyādaṃsātparibhraṣṭe nābhideśe vyavasthite \|*  
*vastre sa ekavāsāstaṃ deve pitrye ca varjayet \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. If the cloth has fallen down from the left shoulder and has come to rest near the navel, the man becomes Ekavāsāḥ (‘wearer of one cloth’). One should exclude him from the rites of gods and Manes.

## \|\| 1.40.124 \|\|

*yadeva tarpayatyadbhiḥ pitṝnsnātvā dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*tenaiva sarvamāpnoti pitṛyajñakriyāphalam \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. If an excellent Brāhmaṇa, after taking bath, performs Tarpaṇa (water libation) with water, he obtains the entire benefit of the rites of Piṭryajña thereby.

## \|\| 1.40.125 \|\|

*hastau prakṣālya gaṃḍūṣaṃ yaḥ pibedbhojanottaram \|*  
*daivaṃ pitryaṃ tathātmānaṃ trayaṃ sa upaghātayet \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. If anyone, after taking food, washes his hands and then swallows the mouthful of water, he injures and destroys all the three, viz. the divine rite, the rite of the Manes and his own soul.

## \|\| 1.40.126 \|\|

*gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca yadannaṃ grāmayājake \|*  
*strīṇāṃ prathamagarbheṣu bhuktvā cāṃdrāyaṇaṃ careta \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. One should perform Cāndrāyaṇa rite by way of expiation, after partaking of food in the following cases: group feeding, food cooked or offered by courtezans, food at the place of village priest and food at the celebration (of Sīmanta) at the time of the first confinement of women.

## \|\| 1.40.127 \|\|

*pakṣe vā yadi vā māse yasya gehetti na dvijaḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā durātmanastasya careccāṃdrāyaṇavratam \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. One should perform the expiatory rite of Cāndrāyaṇa after taking food at the place of a wicked man, where no Brāhmaṇa has taken food in the course of a fortnight or a month.

## \|\| 1.40.128 \|\|

*satriṇāṃ dīkṣitānāṃ ca yatīnāṃ brahmacāriṇām \|*  
*eteṣāṃ sūtakaṃ nāsti ṛtvijāṃ karmakurvatām \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. No Sūtaka (i.e., pollution due to births and deaths of relatives) need be observed in the case of Sattrins (those who take part in long-drawn Yajñas), Dīkṣitas (who have become initiated), ascetics, religious students and those who perform the rites of Ṛtviks.

## \|\| 1.40.129 \|\|

*ajīrṇe'bhyudite vāte śmaśrukarmaṇi maithune \|*  
*duḥsvapne durjanasparśe snānameva vidhīyate \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Bath is prescribed in the case of indigestion, vomiting, getting shaved, indulgence in sexual intercourse, seeing a bad dream and touching a wicked person.

## \|\| 1.40.130 \|\|

*caityavṛkṣaṃ citiṃ yūpaṃ śivanirmālyabhojinam \|*  
*vedavikrayiṇaṃ spṛṣṭvā sacailo jalamāviśet \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. One should take bath along with one’s clothes after touching a Caityavṛkṣa (tree worshipped by villagers), a funeral pyre, a sacrificial post, one who partakes of Śivanirmālya (leavings of the food offerings to Śiva) and one who sells the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.40.131 \|\|

*agnyagāre gavāṃ goṣṭhe deva brāhmaṇasannidhau \|*  
*svādhyāye bhojane pāne pāduke vai visarjayet \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. One should leave footwear out of the chamber of sacrificial fire, cowpens, in the presence of the Devas and Brāhmaṇas, while reciting Vedic Mantras, while drinking and while eating.

## \|\| 1.40.132 \|\|

*khalakṣetragataṃ dhānyaṃ kūpavāpīṣu yajjalam \|*  
*agrāhyādapi tadgrāhyaṃ yacca goṣṭhagataṃ payaḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. The grain on a threshing floor and field, the water in wells and tanks and the water in a cowpen can be accepted from a prohibited one.

## \|\| 1.40.133 \|\|

*yadveṣṭitaśirā bhuṃkte yo bhuṃkte dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ \|*  
*sopānatkaśca yadbhuṃkte tadvai rakṣāṃsi bhuṃjate \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. It is the way of eating of demons, if one covers the head while taking food, if one takes food facing south and if one takes food with shoes on.

## \|\| 1.40.134 \|\|

*yātudhānāḥ piśācāśca rākṣasāḥ krūrakarmiṇaḥ \|*  
*haraṃti rasamannasya maṃḍalena vivarjitam \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Yātudhānas, Piśācas, Rākṣasas and men of ruthless activities take away the essence of the food not encircled by Maṇḍala (mystic drawing).

## \|\| 1.40.135 \|\|

*brahmādyāśca surāḥ sarve vasiṣṭhādyā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*maṃḍalaṃ copajīvaṃti tataḥ kurvīta maṃḍalam \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. All the Suras including Brahmā, all the great sages including Vasiṣṭha, derive livelihood from Maṇḍala. Hence one should make the Maṇḍala.

## \|\| 1.40.136 \|\|

*brāhmaṇe caturasraṃ syāttryasraṃ vai bāhujanmanaḥ \|*  
*vartulaṃ ca viśaḥ proktaṃ śūdrasyābhyukṣaṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. The Maṇḍala to be made by a Brāhmaṇa is square. That by a Kṣatriya is a triangle and that by a Vaiśya is a circle. It is laid down that sprinkling of water should be done in the case of a Śūdra.

## \|\| 1.40.137 \|\|

*notsaṃge bhojanaṃ kṛtvā no pāṇau naiva karpaṭe \|*  
*nāsanena ca śayyāyāṃ bhuṃjīta na malārditaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. One should not take food (placing the plate) on the lap, nor in hand, nor in soiled garment, nor on seat, nor on bed. One should not take food when got muddy.

## \|\| 1.40.138 \|\|

*dharmaśāstra rathārūḍhā vedakhaḍgadharā dvijāḥ \|*  
*krīḍārthamapi yadbrūyuḥ sa dharmaḥ paramaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. The Brāhmaṇas are seated in the chariots of Dharmaśāstras. They hold the sword of the Vedas. Even that which they utter playfully is remembered as the greatest Dharma.

## \|\| 1.40.139 \|\|

*rātrau dhānā dadhiyutaṃ dharmakāmo na bhakṣayet \|*  
*aśnato dharmahāniḥ syādvyādhibhiścopapīḍyate \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. One desirous of piety and virtue should not eat food mixed with parched grain and curds at night. If one eats so, one shall become impious and is also afflicted with ailments.

## \|\| 1.40.140 \|\|

*phāṇitaṃ gorasaṃ toyaṃ lavaṇaṃ madhukāṃjikam \|*  
*hastena brāhmaṇo dattvā kṛcchraṃ cāṃdrāyaṇaṃ caret \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. A Brāhmaṇa should perform Kṛcchra Cāndrāyaṇa (expiatory rite) after giving (in case he gives) with bare hands Phāṇita, milk, water, salt, and gruel.

## \|\| 1.40.141 \|\|

*gaṃdhābharaṇamālyāni yaḥ prayacchati dharmavit \|*  
*sasugaṃdhiḥ sadā hṛṣṭo yatrayatropajāyate \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. A person conversant with Dharma who makes gifts of scents, ornaments and garlands shall always be delighted and fragrant, wherever he happens to be.

## \|\| 1.40.142 \|\|

*nīlīraktaṃ tu yadvastraṃ dūrataḥ parivarjayet \|*  
*strīṇāṃ krīḍārthasaṃyoge śayanīyena duṣyati \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. One should cast away a cloth dyed in indigo. It is not harmful in a bed intended for sexual intercourse with women.

## \|\| 1.40.143 \|\|

*pālanādvikrayāccaiva tadvṛtterupajīvanāt \|*  
*apavitro bhavedviprastribhiḥ kṛcchrairviśudhyati \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. By growing Nīlī plants, by selling them and by sustaining himself thereby, a Brāhmaṇa becomes impure. He shall become pure by observing three Kṛcchra rites.

## \|\| 1.40.144 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ tapo homaḥ svādhyāyaḥ pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*vṛthā tasya mahāyajñā nīlī vāso bibharti yaḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. He who wears a cloth dyed with Nīlī does not attain the benefit of holy ablution, gifts, penance, homas, study of Vedas, libation to the Manes and the great Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.40.145 \|\|

*nīlīraktaṃ yadāvastraṃ vipraḥ svāṃgeṣu dhārayet \|*  
*taṃ tu saṃtatisaṃkhyāke narake sa vaseddhruvam \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. If a Brāhmaṇa wears a cloth dyed in Nīlī, he shall certainly reside in hell for as many (years) as there are threads in the cloth.

## \|\| 1.40.146 \|\|

*ahorātroṣito bhūtvā paṃcagavyena śudhyati \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. After fasting for a day and a night, he becomes pure by taking in Pañcagavya.

## \|\| 1.40.147 \|\|

*nīlīraktena vastreṇa yadannamupakalpayet \|*  
*bhoktā viṣṭhāsamaṃ bhuṃkte dātā ca narakaṃ vrajet \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. If food is offered on a cloth dyed in Nīlī, the person who eats it, eats faeces, as it were, and the person who offers it shall fall into hell.

## \|\| 1.40.148 \|\|

*amṛtaṃ brāhmaṇasyānnaṃ kṣattriyānnaṃ payaḥ smṛtam \|*  
*vaiśyasya cānnamevānnaṃ śūdrasya rudhiraṃ smṛtam \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. The food of a Brāhmaṇa is Amṛta; the food of a Kṣatriya is remembered as milk; the food of a Vaiśya is the real food and that of a Śūdra is remembered as blood.

## \|\| 1.40.149 \|\|

*vaiśvadevena homena devatābhyarcanairjapaiḥ \|*  
*amṛtaṃ tena viprānnamṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃskṛtam \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. The food of a Brāhmaṇa is consecrated through Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, by Vaiśvadeva rite, Homa, adoration of the deities and Japas. Hence it is Amṛta.

## \|\| 1.40.150 \|\|

*vyavahārānurūpeṇa nyāyena tu yadarjanam \|*  
*kṣatriyasya payastena prajāpālanato bhavet \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. The food of a Kṣatriya is acquired through the meting out of justice befitting the cases and the due protection of the subjects. Hence it becomes milk.

## \|\| 1.40.151 \|\|

*praharānaddhavāhādyadannamutpādya yacchati \|*  
*sītāyajñavidhānena vaiśyānnaṃ tena saṃskṛtam \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. The food which a Vaiśya offers is produced by means of bullocks yoked for hours to a plough, and is consecrated by performance of Sītāyajña (a holy sacrifice offered to the plough).

## \|\| 1.40.152 \|\|

*ajñānatimirāṃdhasya madyapānaratasya ca \|*  
*rudhiraṃ tena śūdrānnaṃ vedamaṃtravivarjitam \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. A Śūdra is blind due to the darkness of ignorance and is addicted to liquor. The food of a Śūdra is devoid of Vedic Mantras. Therefore it is blood.

## \|\| 1.40.153 \|\|

*na vṛthā śapathaṃ kuryātsvalpepyarthe narottamaḥ \|*  
*vṛthā hi śapathaṃ kurvanpretya ceha vinaśyati \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. A good man should not make futile affidavit for the sake of small sums of money. One who makes it comes to ruin here and hereafter.

## \|\| 1.40.154 \|\|

*kāminīṣu vivāhe ca gavāṃ bhukte dhanakṣaye \|*  
*brāhmaṇābhyupapattau ca śapathairnāsti pātakam \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. There is no sin in swearing for the sake of beautiful loving women, marriage, fodder for cows, when money has been lost and in protecting a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.40.155 \|\|

*satyena śāpayedvipraṃ kṣatriyaṃ vāhanāyudhaiḥ \|*  
*gobījakāṃcanairvaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ sarvaistu pātakaiḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. A Brāhmaṇa must be made to swear by truth, a Kṣatriya by vehicles and weapons, a Vaiśya by cows, seeds and gold and a Śūdra by all sorts of sins.

## \|\| 1.40.156 \|\|

*agniṃ vā hārayedenamapsu cainaṃ nimajjayet \|*  
*sparśayetputradārāṇāṃ śirāṃsyenaṃ ca vā pṛthak \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. A Śūdra may be asked to carry fire; he may be sunk in water or he may be asked to touch the heads of his sons and wife severally.

## \|\| 1.40.157 \|\|

*na yamaṃ yamamityāhurātmā vai yama ucyata \|*  
*ātmā saṃyamito yena taṃ yamaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. They do not call only Yama by the name Yama, It is the self that is called Yama. If the self is controlled, what can Yama do (to him)?

## \|\| 1.40.158 \|\|

*na nistriṃśastathā tīkṣṇaḥ phaṇī vā duratikramaḥ \|*  
*ripurvā nityasaṃkuddho yathātmā duradhiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. A sword cannot be as sharp, a serpent as intractable or an enemy as perpetually angry, as the self out of control.

## \|\| 1.40.159 \|\|

*ekaḥ kṣamāvatāṃ doṣo na dvitīyaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*yadenaṃ kṣamayā yuktamaśaktaṃ manyate janaḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. There is only one fault in those possessing forbearance; there is nothing else as the second. That is, people may consider a patient man to be weak.

## \|\| 1.40.160 \|\|

*na śabdaśāstrābhiratasya mokṣo na caiva ramyā vasathapriyasya \|*  
*na bhojanācchādana tatparasya na lokavitta grahaṇe ratasya \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. There is no salvation to one engrossed in the science of words (Grammar); nor to one fond of beautiful residence; nor to one who is fond of food and raiment (dress); nor to one engaged in taking away the wealth of the (other) people.

## \|\| 1.40.161 \|\|

*ekāṃtaśīlasya sadaiva tasya sarveṃdriyaprīti nivartakasya \|*  
*svādhyāyayoge gatamānasasya mokṣo dhuvaṃ nityamahiṃsakasya \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. Salvation is certain to one who always habitually remains alone, one who makes all desires for sensual pleasures recede, and one whose mind is directed towards Yoga and Svādhyāya (student of Vedas) and who is always nonviolent.

## \|\| 1.40.162 \|\|

*kvaikāṃtaśīlatvamihāsti puṃsaḥ kva ceṃdriyaprītinivṛttirasti \|*  
*kva yogayuktiḥ kva ca daivatejyā kāśyāṃ vinaibhiḥ sahajena muktiḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. There is salvation in Kāśī naturally even without a man living an isolated life, without ceasing to enjoy sensual pleasures, without practising Yoga and without worshipping deities.

## \|\| 1.40.163 \|\|

*viśveśa saṃśīlanamevayogastapaśca viśveśapurīnivāsaḥ \|*  
*vratāni dānaṃ niyamā yamāśca snānaṃ dyunadyāṃ yadudagvahāyām \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. Meditation on Viśveśa alone is Yoga; residence in the city of Viśveśa alone is penance; the ablution alone in the celestial river that flows north constitutes Vratas, Dānas, Niyamas and Yamas.

## \|\| 1.40.164 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*nyāyāgatadhanastattvajñānaniṣṭhotithipriyaḥ \|*  
*śrāddhakṛtsatyavādī ca gṛhasthopīha mucyate \|\| 164 \|\|*

Skanda said:

164\. A householder who acquires wealth by legitimate means, who is engaged in acquiring the knowledge of reality, who is fond of guests, who performs Śrāddhas and who habitually speaks the truth becomes liberated here itself.

## \|\| 1.40.165 \|\|

*dīnāṃdhakṛpaṇārthibhyo dattvānnāni viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā gārhyāṇi karmāṇi gṛhasthaḥ śreya āpnuyāt \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. By giving food particularly to the poor, the blind and the miserable suppliants and by performing those rites that are praise-worthy, a householder shall obtain welfare (salvation).

## \|\| 1.40.166 \|\|

*itthamācaratāṃ puṃsāṃ kāśīnāthaḥ prasīdati \|*  
*kāśīnāthaprasādena kāśīprāptistu mokṣakṛt \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. The Lord of Kāśī becomes pleased with men who practise these. It is through the favour of the Lord of Kāśī that one attains Kāśī that accords salvation.

## \|\| 1.40.167 \|\|

*sa sarvatīrthasusnātaḥ sa sarvakratudīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*sa dattasarvadānastu kāśī yena niṣevitā \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. One by whom Kāśī is resorted to is one who has taken excellent baths in all the Tīrthas, who is initiated into all the Kratus and who has given all the Dānas.

## Chapter 41 - The Path of Yoga

## \|\| 1.41.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*uṣitvaivaṃ gṛhe vipro dvitīyādāśramātparam \|*  
*valīpalitasaṃyuktastṛtīyāśramamāviśet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. After staying in the house in the second stage of life thus, a Brāhmaṇa should proceed on to the third stage of life, when he becomes grey-haired and wrinkled.

## \|\| 1.41.2 \|\|

*apatyāpatyamālokya grāmyāhārānvisṛjya ca \|*  
*patnīṃ putreṣu saṃtyajya patnyā vā vanamāviśet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After seeing the progeny of his progeny, after eschewing all foodstuffs prepared in his village, the Brāhmaṇa should enter the forest along with his wife (if she is ready to go) or after entrusting her to the care of his sons.

## \|\| 1.41.3 \|\|

*vasānaścarmacīrāṇi sāgnirmunyannavartanaḥ \|*  
*jaṭī sāyaṃprage snāyī śmaśrulonakhalomabhṛt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He should wear bark-garments or leather (e.g. deer-hide) ones. He should maintain the sacrificial fires and sustain himself with the foodstuffs befitting sages. He should grow matted hairs and beard and make the hairs and nails grow long. He should take bath in the morning and evening (and also at midday).

## \|\| 1.41.4 \|\|

*śākamūlaphalairvāpi paṃcayajñanna hāpayet \|*  
*ammūlaphalabhikṣābhirarcayedbhikṣukātithīn \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He should not discontinue the five Yajñas even if he has to make use of greens, roots and fruits. He should propitiate mendicants and guests through the alms consisting of water, roots and fruits.

## \|\| 1.41.5 \|\|

*anādātā ca dātā ca dāṃtaḥ svādhyāyatatparaḥ \|*  
*vaitānikaṃ ca juhuyādagnihotraṃ yathāvidhi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He should not accept anything from anyone. He should give others (whatever he can). He should control his mind and be engaged in the study of the Vedas. He should duly perform Agnihotra in the Vaitānīya fire (i.e., in Āhavanīya and Dakṣiṇāgni eschewing Gārhapatyāgni).

## \|\| 1.41.6 \|\|

*munyannaiḥ svayamānītaiḥ puroḍāśāṃśca nirvapet \|*  
*svayaṃkṛtaṃ ca lavaṇaṃ khādetsnehaṃ phalodravam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He should prepare Puroḍāśa with Munyanna (foodgrains grown without cultivation like Nīvāra rice) brought by himself. He should eat the salt prepared by himself. Only things derived from fruits (are to be used).

## \|\| 1.41.7 \|\|

*varjayeccheluśigrū ca kavakaṃ palalaṃ madhu \|*  
*munyannamāśvinemāsi tyajedyatpūrvasaṃcitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He should eschew the plants of Śelu, Śigru and Kavaka and also honey and meat. In the month of Āśvina, he should avoid using the Nīvāra rice hoarded earlier.

## \|\| 1.41.8 \|\|

*grāmyāṇi phalamūlāni phālajānnaṃ ca saṃtyajet \|*  
*daṃtolūkhalako vā syādaśmakuṭṭotha vā bhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He should forego fruits and roots grown in village or Phālaja-anna (foodgrains grown by ploughing i.e., cultivation, even though the owner of the field neglected to collect it—Comm.). He should use his teeth as mortar and pestle (i.e., chew the paddy with teeth) or he should use two stones to separate the grain from the chaff.

## \|\| 1.41.9 \|\|

*sadyaḥ prakṣālako vā syādathavā māsasaṃcayī \|*  
*triṣaḍdvādaśamāsānnaphalamūlādisaṃgrahī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He may collect grains, fruits, roots etc. required for a single day, or one month, three months, six months or even twelve months.

## \|\| 1.41.10 \|\|

*naktāśye kāṃtarāśī vā ṣaṣṭhakālāśanopi vā \|*  
*cāṃdrāyaṇavratī vā syātpakṣabhugvātha māsabhuk \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He may be (the adopter of any of these Vratas): one who eats only at night; one who takes food on alternate days, or once in three days, or one who follows Cāndrāyaṇa Vrata or takes food once in a fortnight or once in a month.

## \|\| 1.41.11 \|\|

*vaikhānasa matasthastu phalamūlāśanopi vā \|*  
*tapasā śoṣayeddehaṃ pitṝndevāṃśca tarpayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He should follow the Vaikhānasa mode of life or solely live on fruits and roots. He should cause emaciation of the body through austerities. He should perform Tarpaṇas unto Pitṛs and Devas.

## \|\| 1.41.12 \|\|

*agnimātmani cādhāya vicaredaniketanaḥ \|*  
*bhikṣayetprāṇayātrārthaṃ tāpasānvanavāsinaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. (If he is too weak to follow the above mode) he should consign the sacred fire into himself (by drinking in ash dissolved in water) and wander without any permanent abode. To keep his life going, he should resort to begging of alms from ascetics dwelling in forest.

## \|\| 1.41.13 \|\|

*grāmādānīya vāśnīyādaṣṭau grāsānvasanvane \|*  
*itthaṃ vanāśramī vipro brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. (In case this is not available) he may also bring in food from the village and take eight morsels while living in the forest. A Vanāśramī (forest-dweller) Brāhmaṇa practising thus, is honoured in the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.41.14 \|\|

*ativāhyāyuṣobhāgaṃ tṛtīyamiti kānane \|*  
*āyuṣastu turīyāṃśe tyaktvā saṃgānparivrajet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After spending the third stage of his life thus in the forest, one should eschew all contacts in the fourth stage and lead the life of a wandering recluse.

## \|\| 1.41.15 \|\|

*ṛṇatrayamasaṃśodhya tvanutpādya sutānapi \|*  
*tathā yajñānaniṣṭvā ca mokṣamicchanvrajatyadhaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Without repaying the three debts of life, i.e., without studying the Vedas, without procreating sons, and without pe rforming Yajñas, if one wishes for salvation one faces downfall.

## \|\| 1.41.16 \|\|

*manāgapi na bhūtānāṃ yasmādutpadyate bhayam \|*  
*sarvabhūtāni tasyeha prayacchaṃtyabhayaṃ sadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. All the living beings always accord fearlessness to him from whom there is not even an iota of fear to the living beings.

## \|\| 1.41.17 \|\|

*eka eva carennityamanagniraniketanaḥ \|*  
*siddhyarthamasahāyaḥ syādgrāmamannārthamāśrayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He should wander alone forever without any abode and fire. For the purpose of Siddhi (achievement of aim), he should remain aidless. He should resort to a village only for food.

## \|\| 1.41.18 \|\|

*jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ vātha nābhikāṃkṣetkvacidyatiḥ \|*  
*kālameva pratīkṣeta nirdeśaṃ bhṛtako yathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The ascetic should crave neither for life nor for death. He should bide his time like a salaried worker waiting for (further) instruction (from the master).

## \|\| 1.41.19 \|\|

*sarvatra mamatā śūnyaḥ sarvatra samatāyutaḥ \|*  
*vṛkṣamūlaniketaśca mumukṣuriha śasyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A (recluse) desirous of salvation should be devoid of Mamatā (sense of mineness or possession) everywhere; he should have equanimity everywhere. He should stay even at the root of a tree. Such a one is praised here.

## \|\| 1.41.20 \|\|

*dhyānaṃ śaucaṃ tathā bhikṣā nityamekāṃtaśīlatā \|*  
*yateścatvārikarmāṇi paṃcamaṃ nopapadyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. An ascetic has only four activities: meditation, (maintaining internal and external) purity, begging for alms and remaining isolated always. There is no other fifth activity.

## \|\| 1.41.21 \|\|

*vārṣikāṃścaturomāsānviharenna yatiḥ kvacit \|*  
*bījāṃkurāṇāṃ jaṃtūnāṃ hiṃsā tatra yato bhavet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. An ascetic should not move out anywhere for the four rainy months, because thereby he may injure germinating shoots and creatures.

## \|\| 1.41.22 \|\|

*gacchetpariharanjantūnpibetkaṃ vastraśodhitam \|*  
*vācaṃ vadedanudvegāṃ na krudhyetkenacitkvacit \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He should move on avoiding creatures. He should drink water filtered with a cloth. He should speak words without excitement. He should not be angry with anyone anywhere.

## \|\| 1.41.23 \|\|

*caredātmasahāyaśca nirapekṣo nirāśrayaḥ \|*  
*nityamadhyātmanirato nīcakeśa nakho vaśī \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He should move about with his soul alone for aid and support. He should be free from desire and eagerness for support. He should always be engrossed in contemplating the Absolute (Brahman). He should have perfect control over the senses. He should neither trim nor clip the nails and hairs.

## \|\| 1.41.24 \|\|

*kusuṃbhavāsā daṃḍāḍhyo bhikṣāśī khyātivarjitaḥ \|*  
*alābudārumṛdveṇu pātraṃ śastaṃ na paṃcamam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He should wear saffron-coloured cloth, hold a staff and eat what is received as alms. He should not boast of his excellence. A vessel made of any of these four things, namely potgourd, wood, clay or hollow bamboo, is recommended, not a fifth one.

## \|\| 1.41.25-27 \|\|

*na grāhyaṃ taijasaṃ pātraṃ bhikṣukeṇa kadācana \|*  
*varāṭake saṃgṛhīte tatratatra dinedine \|\| 25 \|\|*

*gosahasravadhaṃ pāpaṃ śrutireṣā sanātanī \|*  
*hṛdi sasneha bhāvena ceddrakṣetstriyamekadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*koṭidvayaṃ brahmakalpaṃ kuṃbhīpākī na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ekakālaṃ caredbhaikṣaṃ na kuryāttatra vistaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. No metallic vessel should ever be taken by a mendicant. Even if a Varāṭaka (cowrie) is hoarded everyday the sin incurred is that of killing a thousand cows. (So says) the eternal Śruti. If a recluse looks even for once at any woman with the feeling of love in his heart, he shall certainly remain in Kumbhīpāka hell for two crores of Brahmakalpas.

A recluse should beg for alms only once in a day and should not make it elaborate.

## \|\| 1.41.28 \|\|

*vidhūmesanna musale vyaṃgāre bhuktavajjane \|*  
*vṛtte śarāvasaṃpāte bhikṣāṃ nityaṃ caredyatiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. An ascetic should beg for alms in houses where the smoke (from the kitchen) has subsided, where the threshing pestle has come to a stop, where there is no burning charcoal, where the people have taken their food and where the platters have been kept down.

## \|\| 1.41.29 \|\|

*alpāhāro rahaḥsthāyī ttviṃdriyārtheṣvalolupaḥ \|*  
*rāgadveṣavirnirmukto bhikṣurmokṣāya kalpate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Only that Bhikṣu mendicant is eligible for salvation who takes very little food, who remains isolated, who is not enamoured of sensual objects and who is free from passionate attachment and hatred.

## \|\| 1.41.30 \|\|

*āśrame tu yatiryasya muhūrtamapi viśramet \|*  
*kiṃ tasyānekataṃtreṇa kṛtakṛtyaḥ sa jāyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A person in whose hermitage an ascetic takes rest even for a short while, becomes blessed and has his objectives accomplished having done his duty. Of what avail are to him the injunctions laid down in many religious tracts?

## \|\| 1.41.31 \|\|

*saṃcitaṃ yadgrahasthena pāpamāmaraṇāṃtikam \|*  
*nirdhakṣyati hi tatsarvamekarātroṣito yatiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. An ascetic who spends even a night in the house of a householder completely burns down the sins (of the householder) accumulated by him in the course of his life till death.

## \|\| 1.41.32-35 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā jarābhibhavanamasahyaṃ rogapīḍitam \|*  
*dehatyāgaṃ punargarbhaṃ garbhakleśaṃ ca dāruṇam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*nānāyoni nivāsaṃ ca viyogaṃ ca priyaiḥ saha \|*  
*apriyaiḥ saha saṃyogamadharmādduḥkhasaṃbhavam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*punarnirayasaṃvāsaṃnānānarakayātanāḥ \|*  
*karmadoṣasamudbhūtā nṛṇāṃgatiranekadhā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*deheṣvanityatāṃ dṛṣṭvā nityatā paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*kurvīta muktaye yatnaṃ yatrayatrāśrame rataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. Whatever be the stage of life one may be in, one should endeavour for salvation on having seen or in view of the following: the onslaught of old age, the unendurable affliction of sickness, death, being born once again, the terrible sufferings in the womb, birth in various species of living beings, separation from the beloved ones, contact with undesirable persons, the outcome of misery due to impiety, falling again into hell, the sufferings and tortures in various hells and the diverse forms of human plights originating from defective Karmas, non-permanence of bodies and permanence of the Soul Supreme.

## \|\| 1.41.36 \|\|

*karapātrīti vikhyātā bhikṣāpātravivarjitā \|*  
*teṣāṃ śataguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ bhavatyeva dinedine \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. (There are ascetics) who have no alms-bowl. They are well-known as Karapātrins (‘users of hands as bowl’). Everyday their merit increases hundred times.

## \|\| 1.41.37 \|\|

*āśramāṃścaturastvevaṃ kramādāsevya paṃḍitaḥ \|*  
*nirdvaṃdvastyaktasaṃgaśca brahmabhūyāya kalpate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A wise one who maintains all these four stages of life thus and then frees himself from the pairs of opposites (e.g. pleasure-pain) and eschews attachment, becomes qualified to get merged in the Absolute.

## \|\| 1.41.38 \|\|

*asaṃyataḥ kubuddhīnāmātmā baṃdhāya kalpate \|*  
*dhīmadbhiḥ saṃyataḥ sopi padaṃ dadyādanāmayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The uncontrolled Ātman of those with crooked intellects can only remain in bondage. The same Ātman controlled by the wise accords the status free from ailments.

## \|\| 1.41.39-41 \|\|

*śruti smṛti purāṇaṃ ca vidyopaniṣadastathā \|*  
*ślokāḥ maṃtrāṇi bhāṣyāṇi yaccānyadvāṅmayaṃ kvacit \|\| 39 \|\|*

*vedānuvacanaṃ jñātvā brahmacarya tapo damaḥ \|*  
*śraddhopavāsaḥ svātaṃtryamātmanojñānahetavaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sa hi sarvairvijijñāsya ātmaivāśramavartibhiḥ \|*  
*śrotavyastvatha maṃtavyo draṣṭavyaśca prayatnataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. These are the means of acquiring the knowledge of Self: Śrutis, Srnṛtis, Purāṇas, Vidyās, Upaniṣads, Ślokas, Sūtras, Bhāṣyas and other similar literature. After knowing the Vedic passages (containing instructions) the devotee should practise celibacy, austerities, control of the mind, faith, observance of fasts etc., that are also independent means of the knowledge. That self-same Ātman should be known by persons in all the stages of life. It should be known though the Vedas pondered over and assiduously realized.

## \|\| 1.41.42 \|\|

*ātmajñānena muktiḥ syāttacca yogādṛte nahi \|*  
*sa ca yogaściraṃ kālamabhyāsādeva sidhyati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Liberation is possible through the knowledge of Ātman. That cannot happen without Yoga. That Yoga can be acquired only through a practice extending over a long period.

## \|\| 1.41.43 \|\|

*nāraṇyasaṃśrayādyogo na nānāgraṃtha ciṃtanāt \|*  
*na dānairna vratairvāpi na tapobhirna vā makhaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Yoga cannot be acquired merely by resorting to forest, nor by reflecting on the various texts, neither through Dānas nor through Vratas, neither through austerities nor through sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.41.44 \|\|

*na ca padmāsanādyogo na vā ghrāṇāgravīkṣaṇāt \|*  
*na śauce na na maunena na maṃtrārādhanairapi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Yoga is not acquired through the lotus-posture nor by looking at the tip of the nose; neither by scrupulous cleanliness nor by observing silence nor by repeating Mantras and resorting to other means of adoration.

## \|\| 1.41.45 \|\|

*abhiyogātsadābhyāsāttatraiva ca viniścayāt \|*  
*punaḥpunaranirvedātsidhyedyogo na cānyathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. By perseverance and everlasting practice, by steadfast adherence thereto and by desisting from despondency, Yoga can be accomplished and not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.41.46 \|\|

*ātmakrīḍasya satataṃ sadātmamithunasya ca \|*  
*ātmanyeva su tṛptasya yogasiddhirna dūrataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. To one who always sports with the self, to one who is ever in communication with the Supreme Self, to one who is always contented with the self, perfection in Yoga is not far off.

## \|\| 1.41.47 \|\|

*atrātmavyatirekeṇa dvitīyaṃ yo na paśyati \|*  
*ātmārāmaḥ sa yogīṃdro brahmībhūto bhavediha \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He who does not see anything else as different and distinct from the Ātman is a great (perfect) Yogī. He takes complete delight in his Ātman. He becomes identified with Brahman here itself.

## \|\| 1.41.48 \|\|

*saṃyogastvātmamanasoryoga ityucyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*prāṇāpānasamāyogo yoga ityapi kaiścana \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The union of Ātman (soul) and Manas (mind) is called Yoga by wise men. The union of Prāṇa and Apāna is also called Yoga by some.

## \|\| 1.41.49 \|\|

*viṣayeṃdriya saṃyogo yoga ityapyapaṃḍitaiḥ \|*  
*viṣayāsaktacittānāṃ jñānaṃ mokṣaśca dūrataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The unwise and the not very learned say that the contact of the sense-organs with the objects of pleasure is Yoga. Knowledge and salvation are far away from those whose minds are attached to worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 1.41.50 \|\|

*durnivārā manovṛttiryāvatsā na nivartate \|*  
*kiṃ vadaṃtyapiyogasya tāvannedīyasī kutaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The functioning of the mind is difficult to prevent. As long as it does not stop, how can even the talk about Yoga be possible?

## \|\| 1.41.51 \|\|

*vṛttihīnaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā kṣetrajñe paramātmani \|*  
*ekīkṛtya vimucyeta yogayuktaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The mind should be made free from all functions and the individual soul should be united with the Supreme Soul. He (such a person) gets liberated and is called a Yogayukta (one endowed with Yoga).

## \|\| 1.41.52 \|\|

*bahirmukhāni sarvāṇi kṛtvā khānyaṃtarāṇi vai \|*  
*manasyeveṃdriyagrāmaṃ manaścātmani yojayet \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. All the external and the internal sense-organs should be merged in the mind and then all the senses and mind should be made to remain in communion with the soul.

## \|\| 1.41.53 \|\|

*sarvabhāvavinirmuktaṃ kṣetrajñaṃ brahmaṇi nyaset \|*  
*etaddhyānaṃ ca yogaśca śeṣonyo graṃthavistaraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. One should dissolve the individual soul free from all Bhāvas (inclinations) unto the Supreme Brahman. This is Dhyāna and Yoga. Everything else is mere verbosity.

## \|\| 1.41.54 \|\|

*yannāsti sarvalokeṣu tadastīti virudhyate \|*  
*kathyamānaṃ tadanyasya hṛdayenāvatiṣṭhate \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. That which is not present in all the worlds cannot be said to exist. It is contradictory. On being asserted so (by the philosopher) it does not enter the heart of the other (the layman).

## \|\| 1.41.55 \|\|

*svasaṃvedyaṃ hi tadbrahma kumārī strī sukhaṃ yathā \|*  
*ayogī naiva tadvetti jātyaṃdha iva vartikām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. That Brahman is to be realized by the self. Hence an Ayogī (‘non-yogī’) does not understand Brahman just as a virgin cannot understand the felicity of a married woman or the born-blind cannot see the flame of a burning wick.

## \|\| 1.41.56 \|\|

*nityābhyasanaśīlasya svasaṃvedyaṃ hi tadbhavet \|*  
*tatsūkṣmatvādanirdeśyaṃ paraṃ brahma sanātanam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It can be made an object of direct experience by one who regularly practises (Yoga). Because of its subtlety, the eternal Brahman cannot be pointed out (to others).

## \|\| 1.41.57 \|\|

*kṣaṇamapyekamudakaṃ yathā na sthiratāmiyāt \|*  
*vātāhataṃ yathā cittaṃ tasmāttasya na viśvaset \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Just as water wafted by wind does not remain steady even for a moment, so also (does) the mind (that is shaken by the internal wind Prāṇa). It may not have credence in Brahman.

## \|\| 1.41.58 \|\|

*ato'nilaṃ niruṃdhīta cittasya sthairya hetave \|*  
*marunnirodhanārthāya ṣaḍaṃgaṃ yogamabhyaset \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Hence, in order to steady the mind, the aspirant should control the Prāṇa (wind). For the purpose of controlling the wind he must practise Yoga having six Aṅgas (ancillaries).

## \|\| 1.41.59 \|\|

*āsanaṃ prāṇasaṃrodhaḥ pratyāhāraśca dhāraṇā \|*  
*dhyānaṃ samādhiretāni yogāṃgāni bhavaṃti ṣaṭ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. These are the six Aṅgas: Āsana (posture), Prāṇasaṃrodha (restraint of breath), Pratyāhāra (withdrawal of the senses), Dhāraṇā (retention), Dhyāna (meditation) and Samādhi (absorption).

## \|\| 1.41.60 \|\|

*āsanānīha tāvaṃti yāvaṃtyo jīvayo nayaḥ \|*  
*siddhāsanamidaṃ proktaṃ yogino yogasiddhidam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. There are as many Āsanas as there are living species of creatures. The following is said to be Siddhāsana because it gives success in the practice of Yoga to a Yogī.

## \|\| 1.41.61-63 \|\|

*etadabhyasanānnityaṃ varṣmadārḍhyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 61 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇaṃ caraṇaṃ nyasya vāmorūpari yogavit \|*  
*yāmyorūpari vāmaṃ ca padmāsanamidaṃ viduḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*karābhyāṃ dhārayetpaścādaṃguṣṭhau dṛḍhabaṃdhavit \|*  
*bhavetpadmāsanādasmādabhyāsāddṛḍhavigrahaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

61-63. The right foot is placed over the left thigh and the left one over the right thigh. This they know as Padmāsana. By practising this continuously one shall attain firmness of physical body. Thereafter, the aspirant knowing how to get a firm grasp should hold the big toes with the hands. By repeated practice of this Padmāsana, he attains firmness of physical form.

## \|\| 1.41.64 \|\|

*athavā hyāsane yasminsukhamasyopajāyate \|*  
*svastikādau tadadhyāsya yogaṃ yuṃjīta yogavit \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Or the aspirant can be seated in any other posture such as Svastika etc. wherein he is comfortable. The aspirant conversant with Yoga should be in communion with that Brahman.

## \|\| 1.41.65-66 \|\|

*na toyavahnisāmīpye na jīrṇāraṇyagoṣṭhayoḥ \|*  
*na daṃśamaśakākīrṇe na caitye na ca catvare \|\| 65 \|\|*

*keśabhasmatuṣāṃgāra kīkasādi pradūṣite \|*  
*nābhyasetpūtigaṃdhādau na sthāne janasaṃkule \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. He should not practise Yoga near water and fire, in a dilapidated cowpen, in a forest, in a place infested with flies and mosquitoes, in a Caitya (rustic temple overhung by trees) nor in quadrangle. He should not practise in a place defiled by fallen hair, ash, husk, coals, bones etc., nor in a stinking place with putrefying matter, nor in a crowded spot.

## \|\| 1.41.67 \|\|

*sarvabādhāvirahite sarveṃdriyasukhāvahe \|*  
*manaḥprasādajanane sragdhūpāmodamodite \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Yogic exercises should be practised in a place pleasing to all the sense-organs, where the mind is elated and where there is fragrance of garlands and incense. It must not have any obstacles.

## \|\| 1.41.68 \|\|

*nātitṛptaḥ kṣudhārto na na viṇmūtraprabādhitaḥ \|*  
*nādhvakhinno na ciṃtārto yogaṃ yuṃjīta yogavit \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The aspirant should neither be hungry nor overfed, nor one in a hurry to ease himself of urine and faeces. He should not be exhausted after a walk, nor worried with thoughts when practising Yoga.

## \|\| 1.41.69-71 \|\|

*ūrusthottānacaraṇaḥ savyenyasyottaraṃ karam \|*  
*uttānaṃ kiṃcidunnamya vaktraṃ viṣṭabhya corasā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*nimīlitākṣaḥ sattvastho daṃtairdaṃtānna saṃspṛśet \|*  
*tālusthācalajihvaśca saṃvṛtāsyaḥ suniścalaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*sanniyamyeṃdriyagrāmaṃ nātinīcocchritāsanaḥ \|*  
*madhyamaṃ cottamaṃ cātha prāṇāyāmamupakramet \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-71. Then the aspirant begins his Prāṇāyāma thus. The feet turned up shall be placed on the thighs; the hand is placed on the thigh. The face is slightly turned upwards and pressed with the chest. The eyes are closed and the mind is calm. The teeth should not touch one another. The tongue is kept steady touching the palate and the mouth is kept shut. He should remain motionless. He should control all the sense-organs. He should be seated neither too high nor too low. Thereafter he begins the Madhyama and Uttama Prāṇayāmas (as well as the Laghu or Manda—see 76th verse).

## \|\| 1.41.72 \|\|

*cale'nile calaṃ sarvaṃ niścale tatra niścalam \|*  
*sthāṇutvamāpnuyādyogī tato'nilaniruṃdhanāt \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. When the wind is moving, everything moves. When it is steady, everything is steady. By controlling the wind (breath) a Yogin attains the status of Sthāṇu (Śiva or steadiness).

## \|\| 1.41.73 \|\|

*yāvaddehe sthitaḥ prāṇo jīvitaṃ tāvaducyate \|*  
*nirgate tatra maraṇaṃ tataḥ prāṇaṃ niruṃdhayet \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. As long as Prāṇa is stationed in the body there is life. If that goes out, it is death. Hence one should control Prāṇa (the breath).

## \|\| 1.41.74 \|\|

*yāvadbaddho maruddehe yāvacceto nirāśrayam \|*  
*yāvaddṛṣṭirbhuvormadhye tāvatkālabhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. How can there be any fear from death as long as the wind (vital breath) is restrained within the body and the mind is devoid of (unconcerned with) external objects and the eyesight is fixed in between the eyebrows?

## \|\| 1.41.75 \|\|

*kālasādhvasatobrahmā prāṇāyāmaṃ sadācaret \|*  
*yoginaḥ siddhimāpannāḥ samyakprāṇaniyaṃtraṇāt \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Even Brahmā always practises Prāṇāyāma due to the fear of Kāla (god of Death). Yogis have attained Siddhi (spiritual glory) by perfect control of Prāṇa.

## \|\| 1.41.76 \|\|

*maṃdo dvādaśamātrastu mātrā laghvakṣarā matā \|*  
*madhyamo dviguṇaḥ pūrvāduttamastriguṇastataḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. What is called Mātrā is the time for a Laghu Akṣara (such a, i, u). The Manda (type of Prāṇāyāma) has twelve Mātrās. Madhyama one is twice the previous one and Uttama is twice that.

## \|\| 1.41.77 \|\|

*svedaṃ kaṃpaṃ viṣādaṃ ca janayetkramaśastvasau \|*  
*prathamena jayetsvedaṃ dvitīyena tu vepathum \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. This will generate sweat, tremor and exhaustion in due succession. One should control the sweat by means of the first and the tremor through the second.

## \|\| 1.41.78 \|\|

*viṣādaṃ hi tṛtīyena siddhaḥ prāṇotha yoginaḥ \|*  
*bhavetkramātsanniruddhaḥ siddhaḥ prāṇotha yoginā \|*  
*krameṇa sevyamānosau nayate yatra cecchati \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Exhaustion should be removed by the third. Thus Prāṇa when completely mastered by a Yogī (shall control all these). Duly checked and mastered by the Yogī and duly resorted to, Prāṇa takes him wherever he wishes to go.

## \|\| 1.41.79 \|\|

*haṭhānniruddhaprāṇoyaṃ romakūpeṣu niḥsaret \|*  
*dehaṃvidārayatyeṣa kuṣṭhādijanayatyapi \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. When checked forcibly, Prāṇa escapes through the pores of hairs on the body. It may split the body or produce leprosy etc.

## \|\| 1.41.80 \|\|

*tatpratyāyayitavyosau krameṇāraṇyahastivat \|*  
*vanyo gajo gajārirvā krameṇa mṛdutāmiyāt \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Hence Prāṇa should be tenderly tackled like a wild elephant. A wild elephant and a lion shall become softened and tamed when tackled gradually.

## \|\| 1.41.81 \|\|

*karoti śāstṛnirdeśaṃ na ca taṃ parilaṃghayet \|*  
*tathā prāṇo hadisthoyaṃ yoginākramayogataḥ \|*  
*gṛhītaḥ sevyamānastu viśraṃbhamupagacchati \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. That elephant carries out the directions of the driver. It does not transgress it. Similarly, Prāṇa mastered gradually by a Yogī and resorted to, calms down.

## \|\| 1.41.82 \|\|

*ṣaṭtriṃśadaṃgulo haṃsaḥ prayāṇaṃ kurute bahiḥ \|*  
*savyāpasavyamārgeṇa prayāṇātprāṇa ucyate \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The Prāṇa called Haṃsa is thirty-six Aṅgulas as it goes out. It is called Prāṇa as it (the breath) goes out through the Savya and Apasavya path (or Iḍā and Piṅgalā nāḍīs i.e., through left and right nostrils).

## \|\| 1.41.83 \|\|

*śuddhimeti yadā sarvaṃ nāḍīcakra manākulam \|*  
*tadaiva jāyate yogī kṣamaḥ prāṇanirodhane \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. When the entire Nāḍīcakra (system of tubular organs like veins and arteries) becomes purified without being agitated a Yogī becomes capable of restraining Prāṇa.

## \|\| 1.41.84 \|\|

*dṛḍhāsano yathāśakti prāṇaṃ caṃdreṇa pūrayet \|*  
*recayedatha sūryeṇa prāṇāyāmoyamucyate \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Seated firmly in a posture, the aspirant inhales Prāṇa through Candra (i.e., through the left nostril, tubular vessel called Iḍā, the deity of which is Candra) and exhales through Sūirya (i.e., through the right nostril, the tubular vessel called Piṅgalā, the deity whereof is Sūrya). This is called Prāṇāyāma.

## \|\| 1.41.85 \|\|

*sravatpīyūṣadhāraughaṃ dhyāyaṃścaṃdrasamanvitam \|*  
*prāṇāyāmena yogīṃdraḥ sukhamāpnoti tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Meditating on the flowing currents of nectar accompanied by Candra an eminent Yogī performs Prāṇāyāma and instantly obtains joy thereby.

## \|\| 1.41.86 \|\|

*raviṇā prāṇamākṛṣya pūrayedaudarīṃ darīm \|*  
*kuṃbhayitvā śanaiḥ paścādyogī caṃdreṇa recayet \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The Yogī inhales through Ravi (i.e., Piṅgalā or right nostril) and fills the cavity inside. After Kuṃbhaka (i.e., retaining the breath) he gradually exhales through Candra (i.e., Iḍā, the left nostril).

## \|\| 1.41.87 \|\|

*jvalajvalanapuṃjābhaṃ śīlayannuṣmaguṃ hṛdi \|*  
*anena yāmyāyāmena yogīṃdraḥ śarmabhāgbhavet \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. While performing Prāṇāyāma, the Yogī meditates in his heart on the hot-rayed Sun having the brilliance of a column of blazing Fire. By means of this Yamyāyāma (i.e., Prāṇāyāma) the excellent Yogī attains happiness i.e., the bliss of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.41.88 \|\|

*itthaṃ māsatrayābhyāsādubhayāyāmasevanāt \|*  
*śuddhanāḍīgaṇo yogī siddhaprāṇobhidhīyate \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Practising thus for three months the two types of Prāṇāyāma, the Yogī gets all his Nāḍīs purified. He is then called Siddhaprāṇa (‘one who has mastered Prāṇa’).

## \|\| 1.41.89 \|\|

*yatheṣṭaṃ dhāraṇaṃ vāyoranalasya pradīpanam \|*  
*nādābhivyaktirārogyaṃ bhavennāḍīviśodhanāt \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Due to the purification of Nāḍīs, the following results are achieved: control of breath within as long as one pleases, stimulation of the (gastric) fire, Nādābhivyakti (ability to hear the sound of the Parāvāk in the Ādhāracakra), and freedom from ailments.

## \|\| 1.41.90 \|\|

*prāṇodehagatovāyurāyāmastannibaṃdhanam \|*  
*ekaśvāsamayī mātrā prāṇāyāmo nirucyate \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Prāṇa is the air within the body. Āyāma is the restraining thereof. The time thereof is the Mātrā of one breath. Thus is the word Prāṇāyāma derived.

## \|\| 1.41.91 \|\|

*prāṇāyāme'dhame gharmaḥ kaṃpo bhavati madhyame \|*  
*uttiṣṭheduttame deho baddhapadmāsano muhuḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. In the lowest Prāṇāyāma there will be sweat; tremor takes place in the middle one. In the Uttama (highest) the aspirant seated in Padmāsana often goes up levitating.

## \|\| 1.41.92 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmairdaheddoṣānpratyāhāreṇa pātakam \|*  
*manodhairyaṃ dhāraṇayā dhyāneneśvaradarśanam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. One should burn down one’s faults through Prāṇāyāma, sins through Pratyāhāra, get mental courage through Dhāraṇā and the vision of God through Samādhi.

## \|\| 1.41.93 \|\|

*samādhinā labhenmokṣaṃ tyaktvā dharmaṃ śubhāśubham \|*  
*āsanena vapurdārḍhyaṃ ṣaḍaṃgamiti kīrtitam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. One attains salvation through Samādhi after eschewing both Dharma and Adharma, yielding auspiciousness and otherwise. Firmness of the physical form is attained through Āsana. Thus all the six Aṅgas have been explained.

## \|\| 1.41.94 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmadviṣaṭkena pratyāhāra udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*pratyāhārairdvādaśabhirdhāraṇā parikīrtitā \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Pratyāhāra has been cited (as achieved) through twelve Prāṇāyāmas; Dhāraṇā is proclaimed (to have been achieved) through twelve Pratyāhāras (i.e., one hundred and forty-four Prāṇāyāmas).

## \|\| 1.41.95 \|\|

*bhavedīśvarasaṃgatyai dhyānaṃ dvādaśadhāraṇam \|*  
*dhyānadvādaśakenaiva samādhirabhidhīyate \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Dhyāna is conducive to the attainment of God and it consists of twelve Dhāraṇās (or one thousand seven hundred and twenty-eight Prāṇāyāmas). Samādhi is constituted by twelve Dhyānas (or twenty thousand seven hundred and thirty-six Prāṇāyāmas).

## \|\| 1.41.96 \|\|

*samādheḥ parato jyotiranaṃtaṃ svaprakāśakam \|*  
*tasmindṛṣṭe kriyākāṃḍaṃ yātāyātaṃ nivartate \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. After Samādhi, the endless refulgence, the self-luminous brilliance (comes into view). When it is seen, all the groups of activities, the cycle of death and birth, cease.

## \|\| 1.41.97 \|\|
