*pavane vyomasaṃprāpte dhvanirutpadyate mahān \|*  
*ghaṃṭādīnāṃ pravādyānāṃ tataḥ siddhiradūrataḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. When the wind (Prāṇa) reaches the firmament (i.e., when Prāṇa reaches the cerebral aperture), a loud sound of bells and other excellent musical instruments (is heard). Thereafter the attainment of spiritual power is not far off.

## \|\| 1.41.98 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmena yuktena sarvavyādhikṣayobhavet \|*  
*ayuktābhyāsayogena sarvavyādhisamudbhavaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Prāṇāyāma properly practised brings about destruction of all ailments. If it is improperly performed and repeated, it brings about all sorts of ailments.

## \|\| 1.41.99 \|\|

*hikkā śvāsaśca kāsaśca śiraḥ karṇākṣivedanāḥ \|\|*  
*bhavaṃti vividhā doṣāḥ pavanasya vyatikramāt \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Impropriety in the practice of Prāṇāyāma results in several diseases like hiccups, gasping for breath, coughing and pains in head, ear and eyes.

## \|\| 1.41.100 \|\|

*yuktaṃ yuktaṃ tyajedvāyuṃ yuktaṃyuktaṃ ca pūrayet \|*  
*yuktaṃyuktaṃ ca badhnīyāditthaṃ sidhyati yogavit \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. While exhaling, the wind should be released slowly, little by little; while inhaling the wind shall be taken in slowly; and while retaining it shall be properly and sparingly kept checked. A wise Yogī accomplishes his purpose thus.

## \|\| 1.41.101 \|\|

*iṃdriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ viṣayeṣu yadṛcchayā \|*  
*yatpratyāharaṇaṃ yuktyā pratyāhāraḥ sa ucyate \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The withdrawal of sense-organs that move about among the sense-objects as they please, is called Pratyāhāra. This shall be effected through Yukti (i.e., by realizing the defects in the sense-objects).

## \|\| 1.41.102 \|\|

*pratyāharati yaḥ khāni kūrmoṃgānīva sarvataḥ \|*  
*pratyāhṛti vidhānena sa syādvigatakalmaṣaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Like a tortoise that withdraws all its limbs, he who withdraws the sense-organs through the proper procedure of Pratyāhāra shall become free from sins.

## \|\| 1.41.103 \|\|

*nābhideśe vasedbhānustāludeśe ca caṃdramāḥ \|*  
*varṣatyadhomukhaścaṃdro grasedūrdhvamukho raviḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. The Sun is stationed in the navel region and the Moon in the palatal region. The Moon facing down showers (nectar). The Sun with face lifted up swallows it.

## \|\| 1.41.104 \|\|

*karaṇaṃ tacca kartavyaṃ yena sā prāpyate sudhā \|*  
*ūrdhvanābhiradhastālurūrdhvaṃ bhānuradhaḥśaśī \|*  
*karaṇaṃ viparītākhyamabhyāsādeva jāyate \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The Karaṇa (function) should be carried out whereby that nectar is obtained (by keeping) the navel above and the palate down below (so that) the Sun is placed above and the Moon is placed below. This function or activity called Viparīta is achieved through practice.

## \|\| 1.41.105 \|\|

*kākacaṃcuvadāsyena śītalaṃ śītalaṃ pibet \|*  
*prāṇaṃ prāṇavidhānajño yogī bhavati nirjaraḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. With the mouth resembling the beak of a crow, the Yogī conversant with the arrangement of Prāṇa can drink the extremely cool Prāṇa. He becomes free from old age.

## \|\| 1.41.106 \|\|

*rasanāṃ tāluvivare nidhāyordhvamukho'mṛtam \|*  
*dhayannijarratāṃ gacchedāṣaṇmāsānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The Yogī should place the tongue in the hollow of the palate keeping the face looking up. By drinking the nectar he shall certainly be a Nirjara (‘free from old age’) within a period of six months.

## \|\| 1.41.107 \|\|

*ūrdhvajihvaḥ sthiro bhūtvā somapānaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*māsārdhena na saṃdeho mṛtyuṃ jayati yogavit \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. The aspirant conversant with Yoga, who steadies himself and imbibes (the nectar of) the Moon with the tongue raised conquers death within half a month.

## \|\| 1.41.108 \|\|

*saṃpīḍya rasanāgreṇa rājadaṃtabilaṃ mahat \|*  
*dhyātvā sudhāmayīṃ devīṃ ṣaṇmāsena kavirbhavet \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Prodding the great shining inner cavity (at the root of the tongue) with the tip of his tongue and meditating on the goddess of nectar, he becomes a poet within six months.

## \|\| 1.41.109 \|\|

*amṛtāpūrṇadehasya yogino dvitrivatsarāt \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ pravartate reto hyaṇimādiguṇodayam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Within two or three years, the body of the Yogī is filled with Amṛta (nectar). His semen virile has upward flow. It gives rise to spiritual powers like Aṇimā and others.

## \|\| 1.41.110 \|\|

*nityaṃ somakalāpūrṇaṃ śarīraṃ yasya yoginaḥ \|*  
*takṣakeṇāpi daṣṭasya viṣaṃ tasya na sarpati \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. If the Yogī gets his body filled with Somakalā (nectar) forever, no poison has any affect on him even if he were to be bitten by Takṣaka.

## \|\| 1.41.111 \|\|

*āsanena samāyuktaḥ prāṇāyāmena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*pratyāhāreṇa saṃpanno dhāraṇāmatha cābhyaset \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. After practising and mastering Āsana, Prāṇāyāma and Pratyāhāra he should begin to practise Dhāraṇā.

## \|\| 1.41.112 \|\|

*hṛdaye paṃcabhūtānāṃ dhāraṇāṃ yaḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*manaso niścalatvena dhāraṇā sābhidhīyate \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Keeping the mind motionless and retaining severally the five Bhūtas in the heart is called Dhāraṇā.

## \|\| 1.41.113 \|\|

*haritālanibhāṃ bhūmiṃ sa lakārāṃ savedhasam \|*  
*catuṣkoṇāṃ hṛdi dhyāyedeṣā syātkṣitidhāraṇā \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. The aspirant meditates and retains in his heart the element called earth. It resembles Haritāla (Yellow orpiment) in colour and has four corners (rectangular?). It has God Brahmā as its deity and the letter LA as its Bīja. This is called Kṣitidhāraṇā.

## \|\| 1.41.114 \|\|

*kaṃṭheṃ'butattvamardheṃdunibhaṃ viṣṇusamanvitam \|*  
*vakārabījaṃ kuṃdābhaṃ dhyāyannaṃbujayediti \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. In the neck, Aṃbu (water) principle which resembles (in whiteness) the crescent moon and a Kunda flower is meditated upon along with Viṣṇu as its deity and VA-kāra as its Bīja. Thus he should win over the water element.

## \|\| 1.41.115 \|\|

*tālusthamiṃdragopābhaṃ trikoṇaṃ rephasaṃyutam \|*  
*rudreṇādhiṣṭhitaṃ tejo dhyātvā vahniṃ jayediti \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Tejas (fire) element which is stationed in the palate, is triangular in shape and resembles a glowworm and is presided over by Rudra, should be meditated along with Repha (RA) and thus he should conquer the fire-element.

## \|\| 1.41.116 \|\|

*vāyutattvaṃ bhruvormadhye vṛttamaṃjanasannibham \|*  
*yaṃbījamīśadaivatyaṃ dhyāyanvāyuṃ jayediti \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. The Vāyu principle should be meditated upon in the middle of the eyebrows. It is circular in form and resembles collyrium. The Bīja is YA and the deity is Īśa. Thus he should win over the element wind.

## \|\| 1.41.117 \|\|

*ākāśaṃ ca marīcivārisadṛśaṃ yadbrahmaraṃdhrasthitaṃ yannāthena sadāśivena sahitaṃ śāṃtaṃ hakārākṣaram \|*  
*prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya paṃcaghaṭikaṃ ciṃtānvitaṃ dhārayedeṣā mokṣakapāṭapāṭanapaṭuḥ proktā nabhodhāraṇā \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. The Ākāśa element resembles mirage-water (the sun—Comm.). It is stationed in the cerebral aperture. It should be meditated upon along with Lord Sadāśiva and letter HA (as the Bīja). It is calm. In that Ākāśa, Prāṇa of fivefold form should be retained for five Ghaṭikās along with the mind in the contemplation of the Ātman. This is called Nabhodhāraṇā (Dhāraṇā of the firmament). It is capable of opening the portals of salvation.

## \|\| 1.41.118 \|\|

*staṃbhanīplāvanīcaiva dahanībhrāmaṇī tathā \|*  
*śamanī ca bhavaṃtyetā bhūtānāṃ paṃca dhāraṇāḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. These Dhāraṇās of the five Bhūtas are to be (called) Staṃbhanī (Paralysing), Plāvanī (flowing), Dahanī (burning), Bhrāmaṇī (whirling) and Śamanī (subduing).

## \|\| 1.41.119 \|\|

*dhyai ciṃtāyāṃ smṛto dhātuściṃtā tattve suniścalā \|*  
*etaddhyānamiha proktaṃ saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ dvidhā \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. The root Dhyai means ‘to think’ (Cintā). Thinking connotes steadiness on a particular object. This is called Dhyāna. It is of two types Saguṇa and Nirguṇa (with and without object).

## \|\| 1.41.120 \|\|

*saguṇaṃ vaṇarbhedena nirguṇaṃ kevalaṃ matam \|*  
*samaṃtraṃ saguṇaṃ viddhi nirguṇaṃ maṃtravarjitam \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Saguṇa (type of contemplation) is when there are different forms (or objects). The objectless one is considered Nirguṇa. Know that Saguṇa is attended with Mantras and the Nirguṇa is without Mantras.

## \|\| 1.41.121 \|\|

*aṃtaśceto bahiścakṣuravasthāpya sukhāsanam \|*  
*samatvaṃ ca śarīrasya dhyānamudrātisiddhidā \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. The aspirant is resting in a comfortable sitting (posture) with the mind turned inwards and the eyes kept outside. There is calmness in the bodily position. This Dhyānamudrā bestows excellent Siddhis.

## \|\| 1.41.122 \|\|

*nāśvamedhena tatpuṇyaṃ na ca vai rājasūyataḥ \|*  
*yatpuṇyamekadhyānena labhedyogī sthirāsanaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. That Puṇya (merit) which a Yogi of steady posture obtains with a single Dhyāna is not attained either through a horse-sacrifice or through a Rājasūya.

## \|\| 1.41.123 \|\|

*śabdādīnāṃ ca tanmātrā yāvatkarṇādiṣu sthitā \|*  
*tāvadeva smṛtaṃ dhyānaṃ syātsamādhirataḥ param \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Dhyāna is limited to that state where the Tanmātras of Śabda (sound) etc. remain in the ear etc. Thereafter it is (the state of) Samādhi (absorption).

## \|\| 1.41.124 \|\|

*dhāraṇā paṃcanāḍīkā dhyānaṃ syātṣaṣṭināḍikam \|*  
*dinadvāśakena syātsamādhiriha bhaṇyate \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Dhāraṇā has the duration of five Ghaṭis (i.e., about 2 hours); Dhyāna, of sixty Ghaṭis (i.e., 24 hours). It is called Samādhi when its duration is twelve days.

## \|\| 1.41.125 \|\|

*jalasaiṃdhavayoḥ sāmyaṃ yathā bhavati yogataḥ \|*  
*tathātmamanasoraikyaṃ samādhiriha bhaṇyate \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Just as there is identity after the mixing together of water and salt, so also the identity (merger) of the Atman and the mind is called Samādhi in this Yoga Śāstra.

## \|\| 1.41.126 \|\|

*yadā saṃkṣīyate prāṇo mānasaṃ ca pralīyate \|*  
*tadā samarasatvaṃ yatsa samādhirihocyate \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. When the vital breath becomes extinct and the mind is dissolved, there comes an excellent bliss. This is called Samādhi.

## \|\| 1.41.127 \|\|

*yatsamatvaṃ dvayoratra jīvātmaparamātmanoḥ \|*  
*sanaṣṭasarvasaṃkalpaḥ samādhirabhidhīyate \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. The identity of the two, the Jīva (individual soul) and the Supreme Soul, when all Saṃkalpas (thought processes) become lost, is called Samādhi.

## \|\| 1.41.128 \|\|

*nātmānaṃ na paraṃ vetti na śītaṃ noṣmameva ca \|*  
*samādhiyukto yogīṃdro na sukhaṃ na sukhetarat \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. The excellent Yogī in the Samādhi state of Yoga does not know himself nor others, neither cold nor heat, neither happiness nor its opposite (misery).

## \|\| 1.41.129 \|\|

*kālyate naiva kālena lipyate naiva karmaṇā \|*  
*bhidyate na ca śastrāstrai yogī yuktaḥ samādhinā \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. The Yogī in the state of Samādhi is not carried away (or influenced) by Kāla (death or time), is not affected by formas, nor is he pierced by missiles and weapons.

## \|\| 1.41.130 \|\|

*yuktāhāravihāraśca yuktaceṣṭo hi karmasu \|*  
*yuktanidrāvabodhaśca yogī tattvaṃ prapaśyati \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. The Yogī sees (realizes) the Tattva (Reality) with moderation in food and recreation and limited activity in Karmas, and also limited (properly controlled) sleep and wakeful state.

## \|\| 1.41.131 \|\|

*tattvavijñānamānaṃdaṃ brahma brahmavido viduḥ \|*  
*hetudṛṣṭāṃta rahitaṃ vāṅmanobhyāmagocaram \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. The Tattva referred to is called Brahma by the knowers of Brahma, which is of the nature of Vijñāna (perfect knowledge) and bliss. It has neither reason nor an example (i.e., it can’t be known by inference). It is beyond the ken of speech and mind.

## \|\| 1.41.132 \|\|

*tatra yogī nirālaṃbe nirātaṃke nirāmaye \|*  
*ṣaḍaṃgayogavidhinā parebrahmaṇi līyate \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Through the practice of the Ṣaḍaṅga (having six ancillaries) Yoga, the Yogī becomes merged into the Supreme Brahma which is free from fear and ailments and does not require any support.

## \|\| 1.41.133 \|\|

*yathā ghṛte ghṛtaṃ kṣiptaṃ ghṛtameva hi tadbhavet \|*  
*kṣīrekṣīraṃ tathā yogī tatra tanmayatāṃ vrajet \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. When clarified butter is put into clarified butter it too becomes clarified butter; if milk is poured into milk, it becomes milk; so also the Yogī merging into Brahman becomes identical with Brahman.

## \|\| 1.41.134 \|\|

*anasaṃjātapānīyairvidadhyādaṃgamardanam \|*  
*tyajetkaduṣṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ kṣīrabhojī sadā bhavet \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. The Yogī should smear his body with Bhasma etc. not mixed with water. He should eschew things too hot or not at all hot. He should forego salt. He should always subsist on milk.

## \|\| 1.41.135 \|\|

*brahmacārī jitakrodho jitalobho vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*abdamitthaṃ sadābhyāsātsa yogīti nigadyate \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. He should practise celibacy; subdue anger and covetousness. He should be free from jealousy. If he practises continuously thus for a year, he is called a Yogī.

## \|\| 1.41.136 \|\|

*mahāmudrāṃ nabhomudrāmuḍḍīyānaṃ jalaṃdharam \|*  
*mūlabaṃdhaṃ tu yo vetti sa yogī yogasiddhibhāk \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. The Yogī who perfectly understands (and practises) Mahāmudrā, Nabhomudrā, Uḍḍīyāna, Jālandhara and Mūlabandha possesses all the Yogic Siddhis.

## \|\| 1.41.137 \|\|

*śodhanaṃ nāḍījālasya ghaṭanaṃ caṃdrasūryayoḥ \|*  
*rasānāṃ śoṣaṇaṃ samyaṅmahāmudrābhidhīyate \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. Purification of the system of Nāḍīs (blood vessels), coupling of Candra and Sūrya (Nāḍīs) and perfect drying up of the Rasas is called Mahāmudrā.

## \|\| 1.41.138-139 \|\|

*yoniṃ vāmāṃghriṇā'pīḍya kṛtvā vakṣasthale hanum \|*  
*hastābhyāṃ prasṛtaṃ pādaṃ dhārayeddakṣiṇaṃ ciram \|\| 138 \|\|*

*prāṇena kukṣimāpūrya ciraṃ saṃrecayecchanaiḥ \|*  
*eṣā proktā mahāmudrā mahāghaughavināśinī \|\| 139 \|\|*

138-139. (Another explanation) The genital organ is covered (supported) with the left foot; the chin is placed on the chest and the right leg is stretched and held by both the hands for a long time. The inside is filled with Prāṇa and Recana (exhaling) is carried out slowly. This is called Mahāmudrā and it dispels great sins.

## \|\| 1.41.140 \|\|

*caṃdrāṃge tu samabhyasya sūryāṃge punarabhyaset \|*  
*yāvattulyā bhavetsaṃkhyā tato mudrāṃ visarjayet \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. This Mudrā is to be practised at the outset in Candrāṅga (Iḍā). Then the practice is transferred to Sūryāṅga (Piṅgalā) till the numbers (of Pūraka, Kuṃbhaka and Recaka) become equal. Then the Mudrā is abandoned.

## \|\| 1.41.141-142 \|\|

*na hi pathyamapathyaṃ vā rasāḥ sarvepi nīrasāḥ \|*  
*api ghoraṃ viṣaṃ pītaṃ pīyūṣamivajīryati \|\| 141 \|\|*

*kṣayakuṣṭhagudāvarta gulmājīrṇapurogamāḥ \|*  
*tasya doṣāḥ kṣayaṃ yāṃti mahāmudrāṃ ca yobhyaset \|\| 142 \|\|*

141-142. To a person who practises Mahāmudrā, nothing is unwholesome food. He has no prescribed regimen in regard to diet. All (poisonous) juices are devoid of their poisonous nature. Even if terrific poison is imbibed it can be digested like nectar. All ailments like consumption, leprosy, piles, swelling, indigestion etc. are removed.

## \|\| 1.41.143 \|\|

*kapālakuhare jihvā praviṣṭā viparītagā \|*  
*bhruvoraṃtargatā dṛṣṭirmudrā bhavati khecarī \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. The tongue is turned backward and enters the cerebral hollow of the skull. Vision is fixed in between the eyebrows. This is the Khecarīmudrā (Nabhomudrā).

## \|\| 1.41.144 \|\|

*na pīḍyate śaraugheṇa na ca lipyeta karmaṇā \|*  
*bādhyate na sa kālena yo mudrāṃ vetti khecarīm \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. He who understands Khecarīmudrā is never afflicted by volleys of arrows; is never affected by Karma. He is not tormented by Kāla (Death, time).

## \|\| 1.41.145 \|\|

*cittaṃ carati khe yasmā jihvā carati khe gatā \|*  
*tenaiṣā khecarī nāma mudrā siddhairniṣevitā \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Since the mind traverses the firmament and the tongue too moves therein, this Mudrā resorted to by Siddhas is named Khecarī.

## \|\| 1.41.146 \|\|

*yāvadbiṃduḥ sthito dehe tāvanmutyubhayaṃ kutaḥ \|*  
*yāvadbaddhā nabhomudrā tāvadbiṃdurna gacchati \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. As long as the semen virile is retained there is no fear of death. As long as the Nabhomudrā (Khecarī) is practised the semen virile does not go away (from the body).

## \|\| 1.41.147 \|\|

*uḍḍīnaṃ kurute yasmādahorātraṃ mahākhagaḥ \|*  
*uḍīyānaṃ tataḥ proktaṃ tatra baṃdho vidhīyate \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. Since the Mahākhaga (Great Bird—the principal vital air) makes its upward flight day and night, this Yogic activity is called Uḍḍīyāna. The same Bandha is being laid down (explained).

## \|\| 1.41.148 \|\|

*jaṭhare paścimaṃ tānaṃ nābherūrdhvaṃ ca dhārayet \|*  
*uṅḍīyāno hyayaṃ baṃdho mṛtyorapi bhayaṃ tyajet \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. The Paścima Tāna is to be placed on the belly above the navel (on the middle part of the extended feet—Comm.). This is the Uḍḍīyāna Bandha. (Hereby) one should eschew the fear of even death. (? Obscure)

## \|\| 1.41.149 \|\|

*badhnāti hi śirājālamadhogāmi nabhojalam \|*  
*eṣa jālaṃdharo baṃdhaḥ kaṃṭhe duḥkhaughanāśanaḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. The network of Śirās (tubular vessels) checks the water of the firmament (i.e., the juice from the Moon within the body) at the neck. This Jālandhara Bandha is destructive of clusters of miseries.

## \|\| 1.41.150 \|\|

*jālaṃdhare kṛte baṃdhe kaṃṭhasakocalakṣaṇe \|*  
*na pīyūṣaṃ patatyagnau na ca vāyuḥ pradhāvati \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. When the Jālandhara Bandha which is characterised by drawing in of the neck and placing it (the chin) on the chest (Comm.) is practised the nectar (trickling down from the “moon” in the forehead) does not fall down into the (gastric) fixe, nor is the wind provoked.

## \|\| 1.41.151 \|\|

*pārṣṇibhāgena saṃpīḍya yonimākuṃcayedgudam \|*  
*apānamūrdhvamākṛṣya mūlabaṃdho vidhīyate \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. The aspirant should press the privy parts with the heel and make the anus shrink after dragging up the wind Apāna. It is thus that Mūlabandha is practised.

## \|\| 1.41.152 \|\|

*apānaprāṇayoraikye kṣayo mūtrapurīṣayoḥ \|*  
*yuvā bhavati vṛddhopi satataṃ mūlabaṃdhanāt \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. When Apāna and Prāṇa get mixed together faeces and urine become reduced. By practising Mūlabandha constantly, even an old man becomes young.

## \|\| 1.41.153 \|\|

*prāṇāpānavaśo jīvaḥ ūrddhvādhaḥ paridhāvati \|*  
*vāmadakṣiṇamārgeṇa caṃcalo na sthitiṃ labhet \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. The Jīva (individual soul) is under the control of Prāṇa and Apāna and it moves up and down through the left and right paths (i.e., through Iḍā and Piṅgalā) Hence it is unsteady.

## \|\| 1.41.154 \|\|

*guṇabaddho yathā pakṣī gatopyākṛṣyate punaḥ \|*  
*guṇairbaddhastathā jīvaḥ prāṇāyāmena kṛṣyate \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. If a bird is tied with a string, it can be pulled back even if it goes away. Similarly the Jīva fettered by Guṇas (strings, the three qualities of Sattva etc.) can be pulled back by means of Prāṇāyāma.

## \|\| 1.41.155 \|\|

*apānaḥ karṣati prāṇaṃ prāṇopānaṃ ca karṣati \|*  
*ūrdhvādhaḥ saṃsthitāvetau saṃyojayati yogavit \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. Apāna pulls Prāṇa and Prāṇa pulls Apāna. The aspirant conversant with Yoga joins together these two, stationed above and below.

## \|\| 1.41.156 \|\|

*hakāreṇa bahiryāti sakāreṇa viśetpunaḥ \|*  
*haṃsahaṃsetyato maṃtraṃ jīvo japati sarvadā \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. The breath goes out with the HA sound and comes with the sound of SA. Hence Jīva always recites the Mantra Haṃsa, Haṃsa.

## \|\| 1.41.157 \|\|

*ṣaṭśatāni divārātrau sahasrāṇyekaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*etatsaṃkhyānvitaṃ maṃtraṃ jīvo japati sarvadā \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. Jīva always recites this Mantra, twenty-one thousand six hundred time, in the course of everyday and night (i.e., 900 times per hour).

## \|\| 1.41.158 \|\|

*ajapā nāma gāyatrī yogināṃ mokṣadāyinī \|*  
*asyāḥ saṃkalpamātreṇa naraḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. This Mantra is called Ajapā Gāyatrī. It bestows salvation unto the Yogī. By mere thought of this Mantra, a man gets rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.41.159-163 \|\|

*aṃtarāyā bhavaṃtīha yogino yogahānidāḥ \|*  
*śrūyate dūragā vārtā dūrasthaṃ dṛśyate puraḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

*yojanānāṃ śataṃ yātuṃ śaktiḥsyānnimiṣārdhataḥ \|*  
*aciṃtitāni śāstrāṇi kaṃṭhapāṭhī bhavaṃti hi \|\| 160 \|\|*

*dhāraṇāśa ktiratyugrā mahābhāro laghurbhavet \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ kṛśaḥ kṣaṇaṃ sthūlaḥ kṣaṇamalpaḥ kṣaṇaṃ mahān \|\| 161 \|\|*

*parakāyaṃ praviśati tiraścāṃ vetti bhāṣitam \|*  
*divyagaṃdhaṃ tanau dhatte divyāṃ vāṇīṃ pravakti ca \|\| 162 \|\|*

*prārthyate divyakanyābhirdivyaṃ dhārayate vapuḥ \|*  
*ityādayoṃtarāyāḥ syuryogasaṃsiddhisūcakāḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

159-163. The following spiritual powers indicating perfect mastery of Yoga become obstacles to the Yogī bringing in loss of Yogic power. News of far-off events is heard. Objects existing far away are seen in front. There comes the ability to travel a hundred Yojanas in half a moment. Sacred treatises are learnt by heart even without being pondered over. The power of retention in memory becomes excessive. Even great burdens becomes light. The Yogī can become lean in a moment; stout in another; tiny in a moment and huge in another. He can enter the physical body of another and understand the speech of animals. He can emit divine fragrance from his body and utter divine speech. He is even sought by celestial maidens and acquires celestial body.

## \|\| 1.41.164 \|\|

*yadyebhiraṃtarāyairna kṣipyate'syeha mānasam \|*  
*tadagre tatsamāpnoti padaṃ brahmādi durlabham \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. If the mind of the Yogī is not distracted by these obstacles here, he attains the rare status of Brahman etc.

## \|\| 1.41.165 \|\|

*yatprāpya na nivarteta yatprāpya na ca śocati \|*  
*tallabhyate ṣaḍaṃgena yogena kalaśodbhava \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. O Pot-born One, by means of the Yogic practice with the six ancillaries, one attains that form which one does not lose nor repents or regrets after the attainment.

## \|\| 1.41.166 \|\|

*ekena janmanā yogaḥ kathamitthaṃ prasidhyati \|*  
*ṛte ca yogasaṃsiddheḥ kathaṃ muktirihāpyate \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. How can such a Yoga be mastered in a single birth? Without the Yogic perfection, how can salvation be obtained?

## \|\| 1.41.167 \|\|

*ubhe eva hi nirvāṇavartmanī kila kuṃbhaja \|*  
*kiṃ vā kāśyāṃ tanutyāgaḥ kiṃ vā yogoyamīdṛśaḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. There are only two ways for the acquisition of salvation, O Pot-born One; either one casts off the body at Kāśī or acquires such a Yoga as this.

## \|\| 1.41.168 \|\|

*caṃcaleṃdriyavṛttitvātkalikalmaṣajṛṃbhaṇāt \|*  
*alpāyuṣāṃ tathā nṛṇāṃ kveha yoga mahodayaḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. How-can there be Yogic achievement for men of short span of life, in view of the unsteadiness of sense-organs and the expansion of the sins of Kali Age?

## \|\| 1.41.169 \|\|

*ataeva hi jaṃtūnāṃ mahodayapadapradaḥ \|*  
*sadaiva sa dayāvārdhiḥ kāśyāṃ viśveśvaraḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. Hence, for all creatures, Viśveśvara, the ocean of mercy, stationed in Kāśi, is the bestower of the highly elevated status.

## \|\| 1.41.170 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ sukhena kaivalyaṃ yathālabhyeta jaṃtubhiḥ \|*  
*yogayuktyādyupāyaiśca na tathānyatra kutracit \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. Salvation is attained easily by living beings at Kāsī, but not so easily elsewhere even through Yogic and other means.

## \|\| 1.41.171 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ svadehasaṃyogaḥ samyagyoga udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*mucyate neha yogena kṣipramanyena kenacit \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. The union with the body itself (i.e., living) at Kāsī is cited as perfect Yoga. Here no one is liberated by any other means of Yoga so quickly.

## \|\| 1.41.172 \|\|

*viśveśvaro viśālākṣī dyunadīkālabhairavaḥ \|*  
*śrīmānḍhuṃḍhirdaṃḍapāṇiḥ ṣaḍaṃgo yoga eṣa vai \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. Viśveśvara, Viśālākṣī, the celestial river, Kālabhairava, the glorious Ḍhunḍhi (i.e., Gaṇeśa) and Daṇḍapāṇi (Kārttikeya?)—these constitute the Yoga of six limbs.

## \|\| 1.41.173 \|\|

*etatṣaḍaṃgayo yogaṃ nityaṃ kāśyāṃ niṣevate \|*  
*saṃprāpya yoganidrāṃ sa dīrghāmamṛtamaśnute \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. If anyone practises this Yoga of six Aṅgas at Kāśī constantly, he attains the prolonged Yogic slumber and imbibes Amṛta (Nectar).

## \|\| 1.41.174 \|\|

*oṃkāraḥ kṛttivāsāśca kedāraśca triviṣṭapaḥ \|*  
*vīreśvarothaviśveśaḥ ṣaḍaṃgoyamihāparaḥ \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. Another set of six-limbs includes (the Liṅgas) Oṃkāra, Kṛttivāsāḥ (Elephant-hide-clad), Kedāra, Triviṣṭapa (heaven or lord of heaven), Vīreśvara and Viśveśa.

## \|\| 1.41.175 \|\|

*pādodakāsisaṃbheda jñānodamaṇikarṇikāḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍaṃgoyaṃ mahāyogo brahmadharmahradāvapi \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. The confluences of Pādodaka (i.e., Varaṇā) and Asi (with Gaṅgā), Jñānavāpī, Maṇikarṇikā, Brahmahrada, Dharmahrada constitute another great Yoga of six Aṅgas.

## \|\| 1.41.176 \|\|

*ṣaḍaṃgasevanādasmādvārāṇasyāṃ narottama \|*  
*na jātu jāyate jaṃturjananī jaṭhare punaḥ \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. If a creature practises this Ṣaḍaṅga Yoga at Vārāṇasī, O excellent one among men, it never gets birth in the mother’s womb.

## \|\| 1.41.177 \|\|

*gaṃgāsnānaṃ mahāmudrā mahāpātakanāśanī \|*  
*etanmudrākṛtābhyāsopyamṛtatvamavāpnuyāt \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. Ablution in Gaṅgā is the Mahāmudrā that destroys great sins. One who practises this Mudrā attains immortality.

## \|\| 1.41.178 \|\|

*kāśīvīthiṣu saṃcāro mudrā bhavati khecarī \|*  
*khecaro jāyate nūnaṃ khecaryā mudrayānayā \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. Wandering around in the streets of Kāśī is Khecarī Mudrā. As a result of this Mudrā the devotee becomes Khecara (‘moving in the firmament’ i.e., Brahman itself).

## \|\| 1.41.179 \|\|

*uḍḍīya sarvato deśādyānaṃ vārāṇasīṃ prati \|*  
*uṅḍīyāno mahābaṃdha eṣa muktyai prakalpate \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. Fleeing towards Vārāṇasī from the regions all-around is the great Bandha named Uḍḍīyāna. This is conducive to salvation.

## \|\| 1.41.180 \|\|

*jalasya dhāraṇaṃ mūrdhni viśveśa snānajanmanaḥ \|*  
*eṣa jālaṃdharo baṃdhaḥ samastasuradurlabhaḥ \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. Keeping the water arising from the ablution of Viśveśa on the head is the Bandha named Jālandhara which is inaccessible even to the entire host of Suras.

## \|\| 1.41.181 \|\|

*vṛto vighnaśatenāpi yanna kāśīṃ tyajetsudhīḥ \|*  
*mūlabaṃdhaḥ smṛto hyeṣa duḥkhamūlanikṛṃtanaḥ \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. If a sensible man does not forsake Kāśī though surrounded by a hundred difficulties, that itself is remembered as Mūlabandha that destroys the root of miseries.

## \|\| 1.41.182 \|\|

*iti yogaḥ samākhyāto mayā te dvividho mune \|*  
*saṣaḍaṃgaḥ samudraśca muktaye śaṃbhubhāṣitaḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. Thus, O sage, two types of Yoga have been explained to you, one with the six Aṅgas and the other with Mudrā. It has been propounded by Śaṃbhu for the attainment of salvation.

## \|\| 1.41.183 \|\|

*yāvanneṃdriya vaiklavyaṃ yāvadvyādhirna bādhate \|*  
*yāvatkālavilaṃbosti tāvadyogarato bhavet \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. One should be engaged in the practice of Yoga as long as the sense-organs do not become feeble, as long as one is not afflicted with ailments and there is some delay for the arrival of god of Death.

## \|\| 1.41.184 \|\|

*ubhayoryogayormadhye kāśīyogoyamuttamaḥ \|*  
*kāśīyogaṃ samabhyasya prāpnuyādyogamuttamam \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. Between the two types of Yoga, this Yoga of Kāśī is the best one. By practising Kāśīyoga one shall attain the excellent Yoga i.e., the identity of the soul and the Absolute.

## \|\| 1.41.185 \|\|

*ādhivyādhisahāyinyā jarayā mṛtyuliṃgayā \|*  
*kālaṃ nikaṭato jñātvā kāśīnāthaṃ samāśrayeta \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. One should realize that the god of Death is nearby when old age attended with mental and physical illness comes indicating death. Then one should resort to the Lord of Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.41.186 \|\|

*kāśīnāthaṃ samāśritya kutaḥ kālabhayaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*kruddhopi jīvahṛtkālastacca kāśyāṃ sumaṃgalam \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. Where is the fear of Kāla for men after resorting to Kāśīnātha. Even the taking away of life by angry Kāla in Kāśī is very auspicious.

## \|\| 1.41.187 \|\|

*ātithyenehasiyathā pratīkṣetātithiṃ kṛtī \|*  
*kāśyāṃ kālaṃ tathāyāṃtaṃ bhāgyavānsaṃpratīkṣate \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. Just as a righteous man awaits a guest at the time of hospitality, so also the fortunate one at Kāsī awaits the arrival of Kāla (death).

## \|\| 1.41.188 \|\|

*kaliḥ kālaḥ kṛtaṃkarma trikaṃṭakamitīritam \|*  
*etattrayaṃ na prabhavedānaṃdavanavāsinām \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. Kali Age, Kāla and the Karma performed by one—these are called Trikaṇṭakas (‘three thorns’). These three are ineffective in the case of the inhabitants of Ānandavana.

## \|\| 1.41.189 \|\|

*anyatrātarkitaḥ kālaḥ kalayiṣyatyasaṃśayam \|*  
*kālādabhayamiccheccettataḥ kāśīṃ samāśrayet \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. In places other than Kāśī, unexpected death undoubtedly afflicts one. If one wishes freedom from fear of death, one should resort to Kāśī.

## Chapter 42 - Means of Dodging Kāla

## \|\| 1.42.1 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ nikaṭataḥ kālo jñāyate haranaṃdana \|*  
*tāni cihnāni katicidbrūhi me paripṛcchataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Agasti said:

1\. How is it known that Kāla (death) is nearby, O son of Hara? Tell me a few of those indications as I ask.

## \|\| 1.42.2 \|\|

*kumāra uvāca \|*  
*vadāmi kālacihnāni jāyaṃte yāni dehinām \|*  
*mṛtyau nikaṭamāpanne mune tāni niśāmaya \|\| 2 \|\|*

Kumāra said:

2\. I shall tell those signs which appear in men when death is imminent, O sage. Listen to them.

## \|\| 1.42.3 \|\|

*yāmyanāsāpuṭe yasya vāyurvāti divāniśam \|*  
*akhaṃḍameva tasyāyuḥ kṣayatyabdatrayeṇa hi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. If one breathes in and out through the right nostril alone day and night, his life, even though unbroken, comes to an end within three years.

## \|\| 1.42.4 \|\|

*ahorātraṃ tryahorātraṃ ravirvahati saṃtatam \|*  
*abdamekaṃ ca tasyeha jīvanāvadhirucyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. If the air blows constantly for two or three days and nights through Ravi (the right tubular vessel) it is said that his life limit is a year.

## \|\| 1.42.5 \|\|

*vahennāsāpuṭayuge daśāhāni niraṃtaram \|*  
*vātaścetsaha saṃkrāṃtistayā jīveddinatrayam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If the wind (breath) blows through both the nostrils continuously for ten days, along with its egression, the person lives only for three days.

## \|\| 1.42.6 \|\|

*nāsāvartma dvayaṃ hitvā mātariśvā mukhādvahet \|*  
*śaṃseddinadvayādarvākprayāṇaṃ tasya cādhvani \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Leaving off its two-fold path through the nostrils if the breath blows through the mouth, the person’s departure along the path of death before the end of two days can be foretold.

## \|\| 1.42.7 \|\|

*akasmādevayatkāle mṛtyuḥ sannihito bhavet \|*  
*ciṃtanīyaḥ prayatnena sa kālo mṛtyubhīruṇā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The time when death shall come all of a sudden, should be well-thought of by a person afraid of death.

## \|\| 1.42.8 \|\|

*sūrye saptamarāśisthe janmarkṣasthe niśākare \|*  
*pauṣṇaḥ sa kālo draṣṭavyo yadā yāmye ravirvahet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. If the Sun is in the seventh house in the Zodiac and the Moon is in the star of nativity and the breath flows through the right (nostril), that time should be seen as Pauṣṇakāla (time of which the Sun is the deity).

## \|\| 1.42.9 \|\|

*akasmādvīkṣate yastu puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇapiṃgalam \|*  
*tasminneva kṣaṇe'rūpaṃ sa jīvedvatsaradvayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. At that time (of Pauṣṇakāla) if anyone were to see a black and tawny person and immediately some other form, he will live for two years.

## \|\| 1.42.10 \|\|

*yasya bījaṃ malaṃ mūtraṃ kṣutaṃ mūtraṃ malaṃ tu vā \|*  
*ihaikadā patedyasya abdaṃ tasyāyuriṣyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If semen, faeces and urine or sneeze, urine and faeces were to fall out simultaneously, his life extends but to a year.

## \|\| 1.42.11 \|\|

*iṃdranīlanibhaṃ vyomni nāgavṛṃdaṃ ya īkṣate \|*  
*itastataḥ prasṛmaraṃ ṣaṇmāsaṃ na sa jīvati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. If anyone sees in the sky groups of Nāgas (serpents, elephants) resembling sapphire and moving about, he shall not live for six months.

## \|\| 1.42.12 \|\|

*vyabhrehni vāripūrṇāsyaḥ pṛṣṭhīkṛtya divākaram \|*  
*phūtkṛtyāśviṃdracāpaṃ na paśyetṣaṇmāsajīvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On a day when there is no cloud, a person should stand with the sun behind him and fill his mouth with water. He shall then spit it out forcibly and quickly. If he does not see a rainbow, then his life will extend to only six months.

## \|\| 1.42.13-14 \|\|

*aruṃdhatīṃ dhruvaṃ caiva viṣṇostrīṇipadāni ca \|*  
*āsannamṛtyurnopaśyeccaturthaṃ mātṛmaṃḍalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*aruṃdhatī bhavejjihvā dhruvo nāsāgramucyate \|*  
*viṣṇoḥ padāni bhrūmadhye netrayormātṛmaṃḍalam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. One whose death is imminent does not see Arundhatī, Dhruva, the three footsteps of Viṣṇu and the fourth one, the region of Mātṛs (Mothers). Arundhatī means the tongue; the tip of the nose is mentioned as Dhruva; the steps of Viṣṇu are in the middle of the brows; and the region of the Mātṛs is the middle of the eyes.

## \|\| 1.42.15 \|\|

*vetti nīlādivarṇasya kaṭamlādirasasyahi \|*  
*akasmādanyathābhāvaṃ ṣaṇmāsena sa mṛtyubhāk \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If anyone perceives blue and other colours or bitter, sour and other tastes otherwise (not in the proper colour or taste without any proper reason such as eye-ailment or fever), he faces death within six months.

## \|\| 1.42.16 \|\|

*ṣaṇmāsamṛtyormartyasya kaṃṭhoṣṭharasanā radāḥ \|*  
*śuṣyaṃti satataṃ tadvadvicchāyāstālupaṃcamāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. If a man is sure to die within six months, his throat, lips, tongue, teeth and, the fifth one, palate—all these become parched and lustreless.

## \|\| 1.42.17 \|\|

*retaḥ karajanetrāṃtā nīlimānaṃ bhajaṃti cet \|*  
*tarhi kīnāśanagarīṃ ṣaṣṭhemāsi vrajennaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If the semen, fingers and extremities of the eyes turn blue, the man goes to the city of Yama in the sixth month.

## \|\| 1.42.18 \|\|

*saṃpravṛtte nidhuvane madhyeṃte kṣauti cennaraḥ \|*  
*niścitaṃ paṃcame māsi dharmarājātithirbhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. If a man engaged in sexual intercourse sneezes in the middle or at the end, it is certain that he will become the guest of Dharmarāja (god of Death) in the fifth month.

## \|\| 1.42.19 \|\|

*drutamāruhyaśaraṭhastrivarṇo yasya mastake \|*  
*prayāti yāti tasyāyuḥ ṣaṇmāsena parikṣayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. If a three-coloured (namely of blue, red and yellow colour) chameleon suddenly climbs on to the head and goes away, his life becomes extinct within six months.

## \|\| 1.42.20 \|\|

*susnātasyāpi yasyāśu hṛdayaṃ pariśuṣyati \|*  
*caraṇau ca karau vāpi trimāsaṃ tasya jīvitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If after taking excellent bath, the heart (chest) feet or hands become immediately dried up, his life limit is the period of three months.

## \|\| 1.42.21 \|\|

*pratibiṃbaṃ bhavedyasya padakhaṃḍapadākṛti \|*  
*pāṃsau vā kardame vāpi paṃcamāsānsa jīvati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If the imprint on dust or mud of the foot of anyone has the shape of a broken foot, he lives but five more months.

## \|\| 1.42.22 \|\|

*chāyā prakaṃpate yasya dehabaṃdhepi niścale \|*  
*kṛtāṃtadūtā badhnaṃti caturthe māsi taṃ naram \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If the shadow of anyone trembles even when the physical form is steady, the messengers of Yama will bind that man in the fourth month.

## \|\| 1.42.23 \|\|

*nijasya pratibiṃbasya nīrājyamukurādiṣu \|*  
*uttamāṃgaṃ na yaḥ paśyetsamāsena vinaśyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. If anyone does not see the head of his own reflection in water, ghee, mirror etc., he perishes in a month.

## \|\| 1.42.24-26 \|\|

*matirbhraśyetskhaledvāṇī dhanuraidraṃ nirakṣitai \|*  
*rātrau caṃdradvayaṃ cāpi divā dvau ca divākarau \|\| 24 \|\|*

*divā ca tārakācakraṃ rātrau vyomavitārakam \|*  
*yugapacca caturdikṣu śākraṃ kodaṃḍamaṃḍalam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bhūruhe bhūdharāgre ca gaṃdharvanagarālayam \|*  
*divāpiśāca nṛtyaṃ ca ete paṃcatvahetavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. These are the indicators of death. If the mind swerves, gets confused, if the speech falters, if he sees rainbow-like form (when there is no rainbow), two moons in the nights, two suns in the day, galaxy of stars by the day, the extensive sky, rainbows all-round simultaneously, Gandharva city (imaginary city) on the top of a tree or mountain and the dance of ghosts and devils by the day (he will die soon).

## \|\| 1.42.27 \|\|

*sarveṣveteṣu cihneṣu yadyekamapi vīkṣate \|*  
*tadā māsāvadhiṃ mṛtyuḥ pratīkṣeta na cādhikam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Even if he sees anyone of these signs, death shall await only the period of a month and not more.

## \|\| 1.42.28 \|\|

*karāvaruddha śravaṇaḥ śṛṇoti na yadā dhvanim \|*  
*sthūlaḥ kṛśaḥ kṛśasthūlastadāmāsānnivartate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If by closing the ears with the hands, a man does not hear any sound, if a stout man (suddenly becomes) lean or a lean one stout, he returns (i.e., dies) within a month.

## \|\| 1.42.29 \|\|

*yaḥ paśyedātmanaśchāyāṃ dakṣiṇāśā samāśritām \|*  
*dināni paṃca jīvitvā paṃcatvamupayāti saḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If anyone sees his shadow resting in the southern direction, he lives for five days and meets with death.

## \|\| 1.42.30-31 \|\|

*prohyate bhakṣyate vāpi piśācāsuravāyasaiḥ \|*  
*bhūtaiḥ pretaiḥ śvabhirgṛdhrairgomāyukharasūkaraiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*rāsabhaiḥ karabhaiḥ kīśaiḥ śvenairaśvatarairbakaiḥ \|*  
*svapne sa jīvitaṃ tyaktvā varṣāṃte yamamīkṣate \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. If in his dream anyone sees himself carried on the back or devoured by Piśācas, Asuras, crows, goblins, ghosts, dogs, vultures, jackals, camels, pigs, donkeys, monkeys, herons, mules and cranes, he ceases to live by the end of a year and comes face to face with Yama.

## \|\| 1.42.32 \|\|

*gaṃdhapuṣpāṃśukaiḥ śoṇaiḥ svāṃ tanuṃ bhūṣitāṃ naraḥ \|*  
*yaḥ paśyetsvapnasamaye so'ṣṭau māsānanityaho \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If during dream any man sees his own body adorned with fragrant red flowers, red perfumes or red clothes, Alas, he lives only for eight months.

## \|\| 1.42.33 \|\|

*pāṃsurāśi ca valmīkaṃ yūpadaṃḍamathāpi vā \|*  
*yodhirohati vai svapne sa ṣaṣṭhe māsi naśyati \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. If anyone mounts an anthill, sacrificial post or heap of dust in dream, he perishes in six months.

## \|\| 1.42.34-35 \|\|

*rāsabhārūḍhamātmānaṃ tailābhyaktaṃ ca muṃḍitam \|*  
*nīyamānaṃ yamāśāṃ yaḥ svapne paśyetsvapūrvajān \|\| 34 \|\|*

*svamaulau svatanau vāpi yaḥ paśyetsvapnago naraḥ \|*  
*tṛṇāni śuṣkakāṣṭhāni ṣaṣṭhe māsi na tiṣṭhati \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. If, in dream, a man sees himself mounted on a donkey with the body smeared with oil or the; head shaved, if he sees his ancestors in dream being taken to the southern direction, or if a man sees grasses or dry twigs on his head or body, he does not live in the sixth month.

## \|\| 1.42.36 \|\|

*lohadaṃḍadharaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇavāsasam \|*  
*svayaṃ yogre sthitaṃ paśyetsa trīnmāsānna laṃghayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. If a man sees a black man wearing black clothes and holding an iron rod standing in front, he cannot live beyond three months.

## \|\| 1.42.37 \|\|

*kālī kumārī yaṃ svapne badnīyādbāhu pāśakaiḥ \|*  
*sa māsena samīkṣeta nagarīṃśamanoṣitām \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If anyone is embraced by a dark-complexioned virgin in dream, he sees the city of Yama within a month.

## \|\| 1.42.38 \|\|

*naro yo vānarārūḍho yāyātprācīdiśaṃ svapan \|*  
*dinaiḥ sa paṃcabhireva paśyetsaṃyaminīṃ purīm \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If in dream a man goes towards the east riding a monkey, he sees Saṃyaminī (city of Yama) within five days.

## \|\| 1.42.39 \|\|

*kṛpaṇopi vadānyaḥ syādvadānyaḥ kṛpaṇo yadi \|*  
*prakṛtervikṛtiścetsyāttadā paṃcatvamṛcchati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If a miserly person becomes munificent and if a munificent one becomes miserly, if the nature undergoes aberration, then he faces death.

## \|\| 1.42.40 \|\|

*etāni kālacihnāni saṃtyanyāni bahūnyapi \|*  
*jñātvābhyasennaro yogamathavākāśikāṃ śrayet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The significant indications of (the advent of) Kāla (god of Death) are many. After knowing them a man should resort to Yoga.

## \|\| 1.42.41 \|\|

*na kālavaṃcanopāyaṃ munenyamavayāmyaham \|*  
*vinā mṛtyujayaṃ kāśīnāthaṃ garbhāvarodhakam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Sage, I am not aware of any other means of deceiving Kāla except Mṛtyuñjaya (‘Conqueror of Death’—Śiva), the Lord of Kāśī who prevents future births.

## \|\| 1.42.42 \|\|

*tāvadgarjaṃti pāpāni tāvadgarjedyamo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*yāvadviśveśaśaraṇaṃ naro na nirato vrajet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Sins roar and King Yama roars only as long as a devotee does not resort to Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 1.42.43 \|\|

*prāptaviśveśvarāvāsaḥ pītottaravahāpayāḥ \|*  
*spṛṣṭa viśveśasalliṃgaḥ kaśca yāti na vaṃdyatām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Who does not become respectable (even to gods) if he has reached the residence of Viśveśvara, drunk the waters of Gaṅgā flowing towards the North and touched the excellent Liṅga of Viśveśa?

## \|\| 1.42.44 \|\|

*kariṣyetkupitaḥkālaḥ kiṃkāśīvāsināṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*kāle śivaḥ svayaṃ karṇe yatra maṃtropadeśakaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Even if angry, what will Kāla do to the men dwelling in Kāśī where Śiva himself whispers the Mantra of redemption into the ears at the proper time.

## \|\| 1.42.45 \|\|

*yathā prayāti śiśutā kaumāraṃ ca yathā gatam \|*  
*satvaraṃ gatvaraṃ tadvadyauvanaṃ cāpi vārdhakama \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Just as infancy passes off, just as childhood goes off the way it comes, so also the period of youth and old age is what vanishes quickly.

## \|\| 1.42.46 \|\|

*yāvannahi jarākrāṃtiryāvanneṃdriyavaiklavam \|*  
*tāvatsarvaṃ phalgurūpaṃ hitvā kāśīṃ śrayetsudhīḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. As long as there is no onslaught of old age, as long as there is no feebleness in the sense-organs, a sensible man should eschew everything insignificant and seek refuge in Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.42.47 \|\|

*anyāni kālalakṣmāṇi tiṣṭhaṃtu kalaśodbhava \|*  
*jaraiva prathamaṃ lakṣma citraṃ tatrāpi bhīrnahi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. May other signs of the advent of Kāla stand aside, O Pot-born One. Old age itself is the first sign. It is surprising that none is much afraid of that even.

## \|\| 1.42.48 \|\|

*parābhūto hi jarayā sarvaiśca paribhūyate \|*  
*hṛtatāruṇyamāṇikyo dhanahīnaḥ pumāniva \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. When overcome with old age, one is insulted by all like a man devoid of wealth, when the ruby of the prime of youth is taken away.

## \|\| 1.42.49 \|\|

*sutāvākyaṃ na kurvaṃti patnī premāpi muṃcati \|*  
*bāṃdhavā naiva manyaṃte jarasāśleṣitaṃ naram \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Sons do not carry out his behest, wife gives up love and kinsmen do not mind him when the man is in the embrace of old age.

## \|\| 1.42.50 \|\|

*āśliṣṭaṃ jarayā dṛṣṭvā parayoṣidviśaṃkitā \|*  
*bhavetparāṅmukhī nityaṃ praṇayinyapi kāminī \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Even a loving wife turns her face away on seeing (the husband) embraced by old age, naturally suspicious as if of another (rival) woman.

## \|\| 1.42.51 \|\|

*na jarā sadṛśo vyādhirna duḥkhaṃ jarayā samam \|*  
*kārayitryapamānasya jaraiva maraṇaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. There is no sickness on a par with old age; there is no misery on a par with old age; old age itself is death unto men because it causes loss of respect.

## \|\| 1.42.52 \|\|

*na jīyate tathā kālastapasā yogayuktibhiḥ \|*  
*yathā cireṇakālena kāśīvāsādvijīyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Neither by penance nor through Yogic practice, can Kāla be so conquered as he is conquered through stay in Kāśī without any delay.

## \|\| 1.42.53 \|\|

*vināyajñairvinādānairvinā vratajapādibhiḥ \|*  
*vinātipuṇyasaṃbhāraiḥ kaḥ kāśīṃ prāptumīhate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Who feels a keen desire to attain Kāśī without excessive store of Puṇya (merit), without Yajñas, without Dānas (gifts) and without Vratas, Japas, etc.?

## \|\| 1.42.54 \|\|

*kāśīprāptirayaṃ yogaḥkāthīprāptiridaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*kāśīprāptiridaṃ dānaṃ kāśīprāptiḥ śivaikatā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Attainment of Kāśī is Yoga; attainment of Kāśī is penance; attainment of Kāśī is Dāna; and attainment of Kāśī is identity with Śiva.

## \|\| 1.42.55 \|\|

*kaḥ kalikothavā kālaḥ kā jarā kiṃ ca duṣkṛtam \|*  
*kā rujaḥ keṃtarāyā vā śritā vārāṇasī yadi \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If Vārāṇasī is resorted to, what is Kali Age, who is Kāla, what is old age, what is evil, sin, what is pain and ailment, what are obstacles? (All these are insignificant and ignorable.)

## \|\| 1.42.56-57 \|\|

*kalistāneva bādheta kālastāṃśca jighāṃsati \|\| 56 \|\|*

*enāṃsi tāṃśca bādhaṃte ye na kāśīṃ samāśritāḥ \|*  
*kāśīsamāśritā yaiśca yaiśca viśveśvarorcitaḥ \|*  
*tārakaṃ jñānamāsādya te muktāḥ karmapāśataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. Kali Age afflicts them, Kāla desires to kill them and sins afflict and torment them who have not resorted to Kāśī. Those who have resorted to Kāśī and worshipped Viśveśvara, get rid of the bondage of Karmas by attaining the Tāraka Jñāna.

## \|\| 1.42.58 \|\|

*dhanino na tathā saukhyaṃ prāpnuvaṃti narāḥ kvacit \|*  
*yathā nidhanataḥ kāśyāṃ labhate sukhamavyayam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Rich men do not get as much happiness as is obtained inexhaustibly by meeting with death at Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.42.59 \|\|

*varaṃ kāśīsamāvāsī nāsīno dyusadāṃ padam \|*  
*duḥkhāṃtaṃ labhate pūrvaḥ sukhāṃtaṃ labhate paraḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Blessed is one who duly resides in Kāśī and not one who occupies the region of heaven-dwellers. The former acquires the end of misery and the latter the end of happiness.

## \|\| 1.42.60 \|\|

*sthitopi bhagavanīśo maṃdaraṃ cārukaṃdaram \|*  
*kāśīṃ vinā ratiṃ nā'pa divodāsanṛpoṣitām \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Though Lord Īśa was stationed on Mandara abounding in lovely caves, he did not feel pleased without Kāśī where King Divodāsa was staying.

## Chapter 43 - King Divodāsa’s Valour

## \|\| 1.43.1 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*divodāsaṃ narapatiṃ kathaṃ devastrilocanaḥ \|*  
*kāśīṃ saṃtyājayāmāsa kathamāgācca maṃdarāt \|*  
*etadākhyānamākhyāhi śrotṝṇāṃ pramude bhagoḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Agasti said:

1\. How did the Three-eyed Lord make King Divodāsa abandon Kāśī and how did he come from Mandara? O lord, relate this anecdote for the joy of the listeners.

## \|\| 1.43.2 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*maṃdaraṃ gatavāndevo brahmaṇo vākya gauravāt \|*  
*tapasā tasya saṃtuṣṭo maṃdarasyaiva bhūbhṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

2\. Due to the importance (given) to Brahmā’s request and becoming pleased with the penance of that mountain Mandara, the Lord went to Mandara.

## \|\| 1.43.3 \|\|

*gate viśveśvare deve maṃdaraṃ girisuṃdaram \|*  
*giriśena samaṃ jagmurapi sarve divaukasaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When Lord Viśveśvara went to Mandara, a beautiful mountain, all the heaven-dwellers too went along with Giriśa (Lord Śiva).

## \|\| 1.43.4 \|\|

*kṣetrāṇi vaiṣṇavānīha tyaktvā viṣṇurapi kṣiteḥ \|*  
*prayāto maṃdaraṃ yatra devadeva umādhavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Abandoning the Vaiṣṇava shrines hereof on the earth, Lord Viṣṇu too went to Mandara where the Lord of the Devas, the consort of Umā, resided.

## \|\| 1.43.5 \|\|

*sthānāni gāṇapatyāni gaṇeśopi tato vrajat \|*  
*hitvāhamapi vipreṃdra gatavānmaṃdaraṃ prati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Abandoning all the holy places pertaining to Gaṇapati Gaṇeśa went there. I too, O eminent Brāhmaṇa, went towards Mandara.

## \|\| 1.43.6 \|\|

*sūraḥ saurāṇi saṃtyajya gataścāyatanādaram \|*  
*svaṃsvaṃ sthānaṃ kṣitau tyaktvā yayuranyepi nirjarāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Abandoning all the places sacred to Sun-god, Sun too quickly went away from his abode. All the other Devas too went after leaving their respective sacred places (on the earth).

## \|\| 1.43.7 \|\|

*gateṣu devasaṃgheṣu pṛthivyāḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*cakāra rājyaṃ nirdvaṃdvaṃ divodāsaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When all the groups of Devas had gone away from the earth, the valorous King Divodāsa ruled the unrivalled kingdom.

## \|\| 1.43.8 \|\|

*vidhāya rājadhānīṃ sa vārāṇasyāṃ suniścalām \|*  
*edhāṃ cakre mahābuddhiḥ prajādharmeṇa pālayan \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Making the eternal city of Vārāṇasī his capital, that highly intelligent king righteously protected the subjects and made them prosperous.

## \|\| 1.43.9 \|\|

*sūryavatsa pratapitā durhṛdāṃ hṛdi netrayoḥ \|*  
*somavatsuhṛdāmāsīnmānaseṣu svakeṣva'pi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He became scorcher of the hearts and eyes of wicked-hearted ones like the sun, and to all the friends of good hearts he was like the moon to their eyes and minds.

## \|\| 1.43.10 \|\|

*akhaṃḍamākhaṃḍalavatkodaṃḍakalayanraṇe \|*  
*palāyamānairālokiśatrusainyabalāhakaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. By the armies of the enemies fleeing like clouds he was seen wielding with ease his unbroken bow which was like that of Indra and twanging it on the battlefield.

## \|\| 1.43.11 \|\|

*sa dharmarājavajjāto dharmādharmavivecakaḥ \|*  
*adaṃḍyānmaṇḍayanrājā daṃḍyāṃśca paridaṃḍayan \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Like Dharmarāja (Yama), he became the discriminator of piety and impiety, honouring those who should not be punished and punishing those who deserved punishment.

## \|\| 1.43.12 \|\|

*dhanaṃjaya ivādhākṣītparāraṇyānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*pāśīva pāśayāṃcakre vairicakraṃ vidūragaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He destroyed the enemies like fire burning down numerous forests. Even from far-off he fettered the group of enemies like Varuṇa.

## \|\| 1.43.13 \|\|

*sobhūtpuṇyajanādhīśo ripurākṣasavardhanaḥ \|*  
*jagatprāṇasamānaśca jagatprāṇanatatparaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He became the lord (protector) of meritorious persons like Nirṛti, the lord of Puṇyajanas (Rākṣasas). He cut off the demon-like enemies like Nirṛti who made his friends, the Rākṣasas, prosperous. Like wind, he was eagerly engaged in making the universe breathe and live.

## \|\| 1.43.14 \|\|

*rājarājaḥ sa evābhūtsarveṣāṃ dhanadaḥ satām \|*  
*sa eva rudramūrtiśca prekṣiṣṭa ripubhī raṇe \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He was Rājarāja (‘king of kings’, Kubera) bestowing wealth on all good people. He was seen like Rudra in physical form by the enemies in battle.

## \|\| 1.43.15 \|\|

*viśveṣāṃ sa hi devānāṃ tapasā rūpadhṛgyataḥ \|*  
*viśvedevāstatastaṃ tu stuvaṃti ca bhajaṃti ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Since by means of his austerities he assumed the forms of all the Devas, they all eulogized and worshipped him.

## \|\| 1.43.16 \|\|

*asādhyaḥ sa hi sādhyānāṃ vasubhyo vasunādhikaḥ \|*  
*grahāṇāṃ vigrahadharo dasrato'jasrarūpabhāk \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He could not be conquered by Sādhyas (a class of Devas). He was superior to Vasus in wealth. He had the physical form of Planets and he prevented them from being malignant. He had more beauty than Dasras (Aśvins).

## \|\| 1.43.17 \|\|

*marudgaṇānagaṇayaṃstuṣitāṃstoṣayanguṇaiḥ \|*  
*sarvavidyādharo yastu sarvavidyādhareṣvapi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He did not mind the group of Maruts. He pleased Tuṣitas through his good qualities. Among all the Vidyādharas, he was the greatest of Vidyādharas (‘possessor of learning’).

## \|\| 1.43.18 \|\|

*agarvāneva gaṃdharvānyaścakre nijagītibhiḥ \|*  
*rarakṣuryakṣarakṣāṃsi taddurgaṃ svargasodaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He made Gandharvas bereft of pride by his singing. Yakṣas and Rākṣasas protected his fortress that was on a par with heaven.

## \|\| 1.43.19 \|\|

*nāgānāgāṃsi cakruśca tasya nāgabalīyasaḥ \|*  
*danujāmanujākāraṃ kṛtvā taṃ ca siṣevire \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Nāgas (serpents) did not perpetrate anything evil unto him who was more powerful than the Nāgas (serpents, elephants). Danujas (Demon) assumed human form and served him.

## \|\| 1.43.20-21 \|\|

*jātā guhyacarā yasya guhyakāḥ parito nṛṣu \|*  
*saṃseviṣyāmahe rājannasurāstvāṃ svavaibhavaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vayaṃ yatastvadviṣaye surāvāso'pi durlabhaḥ \|*  
*aśikṣayatkṣitipateriha yasya turaṃgamān \|*  
*āśugaścāśugāmitvaṃ pāvamāne pathisthitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Guhyakas became his secret spies all-round among men. (To him Asuras said,) “O king, we shall serve you through our wealth and power, because in your territory residence is impossible even for Suras. Āśuga (Wind-god) taught his horses the ability to run fast, because he was in the path of Pāvamāna (‘the treatise on training horses’).

## \|\| 1.43.22 \|\|

*agajānyasya tu gajānnagavarṣmasuvarṣmaṇaḥ \|*  
*ajasra dānino dṛṣṭvā bhavannanyepi dāninaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On seeing his elephants whose origin was the mountainous region and whose bodies were on a par with the mountains and who were incessantly exuding ichor (Dāna) others also became givers of (religious) gifts (Dāna).

## \|\| 1.43.23 \|\|

*sadojire ca boddhāro yoddhāraścaraṇājire \|*  
*na yasya śāstrairvijitā na śastraiḥ kenacitkvacit \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In his assemblies the scholarly propounders were not conquered by anyone at any place in scriptural lores. In his battlefield the warriors were not conquered by anyone at any place by means of weapons.

## \|\| 1.43.24 \|\|

*na netraviṣaye jātā viṣaye yasyabhūbhṛtaḥ \|*  
*sadā naṣṭapadā dveṣyāstadā'naṣṭapadāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In the realm of that king the enemies were never seen Anaṣṭapadāḥ (‘those whose position was not lost’); in his realm the subjects were never seen Naṣṭapadāh (‘those whose positions were lost’).

## \|\| 1.43.25 \|\|

*kalāvāneka evāsti tridivepi divaukasām \|*  
*tasya kṣoṇibhṛtaḥ kṣoṇyāṃ janāḥ sarve kalālayāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Even in heaven there is only one Kalāvān (‘Master of arts’, the Moon) among the heaven-dwellers; but in the realm of that king, all were Kalālayas (‘abodes of arts’).

## \|\| 1.43.26 \|\|

*eka eva hi kāmosti svarge sopyaṃgavarjitaḥ \|*  
*sāṃgopāṃgāśca sarveṣāṃ sarve kāmā hi tadbhuvi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. There is only one Kama in heaven and he is devoid of limbs; but in his realm the Kāmas (Kama = 1. god of love 2. desire) of everyone were complete in their limbs and parts of limbs (had their desires fulfilled in all respects).

## \|\| 1.43.27 \|\|

*tasyopavartanepyeko na śruto gotrabhitkvacit \|*  
*svarge svargasadāmīśo gotrabhitparikīrtitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In his realm, no one was anywhere heard to be Gotrabhid (‘breaker of family tradition’). In heaven the lord of the heaven-dwellers is glorified as Gotrabhid. (Gotrabhid—‘who chopped off the wings of mountains’).

## \|\| 1.43.28 \|\|

*kṣayī ca tasya viṣaye kopyākarṇi na kenacit \|*  
*triviṣṭape kṣapānāthaḥ pakṣepakṣe kṣayīṣyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. No one was heard in his realm by anyone to be a Kṣayī (‘suffering from consumptive disease’). In heaven the lord of the night (Moon) is expected to wane in the different fortnights (Kṣayī).

## \|\| 1.43.29-31 \|\|

*nāke navagrahāḥ saṃti deśāstasyā'navagrahāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ svarlokepyeka eva prakāśate \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhāḥ sarveṣāṃ tatpaurāṇāmihālayāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*saptāśva ekaḥ svarloke nitarāṃ bhāsateṃ'śumān \|*  
*sadaṃśukāḥ pratidinaṃ bahvaśvāstatpuraukasaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. In heaven there are Nava Grahas (‘Nine Planets’). His lands are Anavagrahas (‘have no drought’).

Even in heaven there is only one Hiraṇyagarbha (Brahmā). The abodes of all the inhabitants of his realm have gold within (i.e. are Hiraṇyagarbhas).

There is only one Aṃśumān (‘the Sun, having rays or raiments’) blazing in heaven with but seven horses. But his citizens have many good silk clothes and many horses everyday.

## \|\| 1.43.32 \|\|

*sadapsarā yathāsvarbhūstatpuryapisadapsarāḥ \|*  
*ekaiva padmā vaikuṃṭhe tasya padmākarāḥ śatam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Just as the heavenly region is Sadapsarāḥ (‘having excellent celestial damsels’), so also his city is Sadapsarāḥ (‘having lakes with excellent water’). In the world of Vaikuṇṭha, there is only one Padmā (Goddess Lakṣmī) but he has a hundred Padmākaras (‘abodes of Padmā’, ‘lotus ponds’).

## \|\| 1.43.33 \|\|

*anītayaśca tadgrāmānārājapuruṣāḥ kvacit \|*  
*gṛhegṛhetra dhanadā nāka eko'lakāpatiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. His villages are Anītis (‘having no divine calamities’ and ‘having no justice’) but there are no Arājapuruṣas (‘men spreading anarchy’ or ‘men with no royal glory’). In heaven there is only one Dhanada i.e. Kubera, the lord of Alakā, here in every house there are Dhanadas (Kuberas, donors of wealth).

## \|\| 1.43.34 \|\|

*divodāsasya tasyaivaṃ kāśyāṃ rājyaṃ praśāsataḥ \|*  
*gataṃ varṣaṃ dinaprāyaṃ śaradāmayutāṣṭakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Even as that Divodāsa was ruling Kāśī thus, every year passed off like a day and thus eighty thousand years elapsed.

## \|\| 1.43.35 \|\|

*gīrvāṇā vipratīkāramatha tasya cikīrṣavaḥ \|*  
*guruṇā maṃtrayāṃcakrurdharmavartmānuyāyinaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even as he followed the path of righteousness, the Devas who were desirous of taking malafide action against him took counsel with Guru (Jupiter).

## \|\| 1.43.36 \|\|

*bhavādṛśāmiva mune prāyaśo dharmacāriṇām \|*  
*vibudhā vidadhatyeva mahatīrāpadāṃtatīḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O sage, the Devas usually bring about great disasters to persons of righteous activities like you.

## \|\| 1.43.37 \|\|

*yadyapyasau dharādhīśo vyādhinoddurdharādhvaraiḥ \|*  
*tānadhvarabhujo'tyaṃtaṃ tathāpi suhṛdo na te \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Although this king very much propitiated those partakers of the offerings (gods) in the fire by means of sacrifices very difficult to be performed, yet they were not friendly towards him.

## \|\| 1.43.38 \|\|

*svabhāva eva dyusadāṃ parotkarṣāsahiṣṇutā \|*  
*bali bāṇa dadhīcyādyairaparāddhaṃ kimatra taiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Inability to bear the prosperity of others is but the nature of these heaven-dwellers. In what way was offence committed by Bali, Bāṇa, Dadhīci and others against them?

## \|\| 1.43.39 \|\|

*aṃtarāyā bhavaṃtyeva dharmasyāpi padepade \|*  
*tathāpi na nijo dharmo dharmadhībhirvimucyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Obstacles do indeed happen at every step in the performance of piety. Still their own duty is never forsaken by pious-minded ones.

## \|\| 1.43.40 \|\|

*adharmiṇaḥ samedhaṃte dhanadhānyasamṛddhibhiḥ \|*  
*adharmādeva ca paraṃ samūlaṃ yāṃtyadhogatim \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Unrighteous ones do flourish with abundance of wealth and grain; but due to the same unrighteousness they face downfall along with their roots (completely).

## \|\| 1.43.41 \|\|

*prajāḥ pālayatastasya putrāniva nijaurasān \|*  
*ripuṃjayasya nālpopi babhūvādharmasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Not even an iota of unrighteousness was incurred by that king who protected his subjects like his own bosom-born progeny and who conquered the enemies.

## \|\| 1.43.42 \|\|

*ṣāḍguṇyavedinastasya triśaktyūrjitacetasaḥ \|*  
*caturopāyavittasya na raṃdhraṃ vividuḥ surāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The Suras did not come to know of any vulnerable point in that king who was aware of the six Guṇas (expedients of political success). His mind was very powerful on account of the three Śaktis, viz. intellect, army (or physical prowess) and brilliance, and he was perfectly conversant with clever strategic means.

## \|\| 1.43.43 \|\|

*buddhimaṃtopi vibudhā vipratīkartumudyatāḥ \|*  
*manāgapi na saṃśekurapakartuṃ tadīśituḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Although they were intelligent and they endeavoured to harm him, the Devas did not succeed in doing the least harm to that king.

## \|\| 1.43.44 \|\|

*ekapatnīvratāḥ sarve pumāṃsastasya maṃḍale \|*  
*nārīṣu kācinnaivāsīdapativratadharmiṇī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. All the men in his realm were steadfast in their vow of having only one wife each. Among women there was no one who was not chaste.

## \|\| 1.43.45 \|\|

*anadhīto na viprobhūdaśūronaiva bāhujaḥ \|*  
*vaiśyonabhijño naivāsīdarthopārjanakarmasu \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. No Brāhmaṇa remained without learning. No Kṣatriya was unheroic and no Vaiśya was without an adequate knowledge of the means of earning wealth.

## \|\| 1.43.46 \|\|

*ananyavṛttayaḥ śūdrā dvijaśuśrūṣaṇaṃ prati \|*  
*tasya rāṣṭre samabhavandivodāsasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In the realm of that King Divodāsa, Śūdras had unswerving devotion to the service unto the twice-born.

## \|\| 1.43.47 \|\|

*avipluta brahmacaryāstadrāṣṭre brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ gurukulādhīnā vedagrahaṇatatparāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. In his kingdom religious students maintained their celibacy unaffected. They were always obedient to their preceptor’s family and desirous of learning the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.43.48 \|\|

*ātithyadharmapravaṇā dharmaśāstravicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*nityasādhusamācārā gṛhasthāstasya sarvataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The householders everywhere were keen in the observance of their duties of entertaining guests, masters of the scriptures and always behaved honourably and decently.

## \|\| 1.43.49 \|\|

*tṛtīyāśramiṇo yasminvanavṛttikṛtādarāḥ \|*  
*niḥspṛhā grāmavārtāsu vedavartmānusāriṇaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Those who were in the third stage of their life, scrupulously abided by the conduct prescribed for hermits without any desire for the activities of the village and followed the Vedic path.

## \|\| 1.43.50 \|\|

*sarvasaṃgavinirmuktā nirmuktā niṣparigrahāḥ \|*  
*vāṅmanaḥkarmadaṃḍāḍhyā yatayo yatra niḥspṛhāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The ascetics therein eschewed all desires and were free from attachments of every sort. They maintained the three Daṇḍas (signifying mastery over) speech, mind and physical action.

## \|\| 1.43.51 \|\|

*anyenulomajanmānaḥ pratilo mabhavā api \|*  
*svapāraṃparyato dṛṣṭaṃ manāgvartma na tatyajuḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Persons of mixed castes (whether born of the regular order, i.e. husband of a superior caste and wife of an inferior one, or vice versa and of the irregular order, i.e. husband of an inferior caste and wife of a superior one) never swerved in the least from the path traditionally inherited by them.

## \|\| 1.43.52 \|\|

*anapatyā na tadrāṣṭre dhanahīnopi kopi na \|*  
*avṛddhasevī no kaścidakāṃḍamṛtibhākca na \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In that realm there were no men without children, no one devoid of wealth, no one who did not serve the elders and no one who met with death prematurely and unaccountably.

## \|\| 1.43.53 \|\|

*na cāṭā naiva vācāṭā vaṃcakā no na hiṃsakāḥ \|*  
*na pāṣaṃḍā na vai bhaṃḍā na raṃḍā na ca śauṃḍikāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. There were no garrulous persons or fickle ones, no cheats or persons of violent nature, no heretics and no imbeciles, none dying childless and no liquor-sellers.

## \|\| 1.43.54 \|\|

*śrutighoṣo hi sarvatra śāstravādaḥ padepade \|*  
*sarvatra subhagālāpā mudāmaṃgalagītayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Everywhere there was heard the loud sound of Vedic chanting; at every place there debate on scriptural literature was held; everywhere there were pleasing melodious auspicious songs.

## \|\| 1.43.55 \|\|

*vīṇāveṇupravādāśca mṛdaṃgā madhurasvanāḥ \|*  
*somapānaṃ vinānyatra pānagoṣṭhī na karṇagā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. There were heard the sounds of lutes and flutes and drums of sweet melody. Excepting the intake of the Soma juice, no other sort of drinking was heard of.

## \|\| 1.43.56 \|\|

*māṃsāśinaḥ puroḍāśe naivānyatra kadācana \|*  
*na durodariṇo yatra nādhamarṇā na taskarāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Therein meat-eating was practised only with respect to the sacrificial Puroḍāśa (oblation) and never elsewhere. There were no gamesters there; no one in debts and no thieves.

## \|\| 1.43.57 \|\|

*putrasya pitroḥ padayoḥ pūjanaṃ devapūjanam \|*  
*upavāso vrataṃ tīrthaṃ devatārādhanaṃ param \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Adoration of the feet of his parents (was considered by a son as) worship of gods, holy fasts, vow and observance, holy spot and the greatest worship of the deities.

## \|\| 1.43.58 \|\|

*nārīṇāṃ bhartṛpad yorarcanaṃ tadvacaḥśrutiḥ \|*  
*samarcayaṃti satatamanujā nijamagrajam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. To women worship of the feet of the husband was the worship of the lord; his word is (as authoritative as) the Vedas. All men always worshipped their elder brothers.

## \|\| 1.43.59 \|\|

*saparyayaṃti muditā bhṛtyāḥ svāmipadāṃbujam \|*  
*hīnavarṇairagravarṇo varṇyate guṇagauravaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Servants joyously worshipped the lotus-like feet of their masters. The persons of superior caste were extolled by those of inferior caste on account of deference for good qualities.

## \|\| 1.43.60 \|\|

*varivasyaṃti bhūyopi trikālaṃ kāśidevatāḥ \|*  
*sarvatra sarve vidvāṃsaḥ samarcyaṃte manorathaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. They worshipped the deities of Kāśī thrice a day. Everywhere all the learned men were worshipped by laymen with great zeal.

## \|\| 1.43.61 \|\|

*vidvadbhiśca taponiṣṭhāstaponiṣṭhairjiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*jiteṃdriyairjñānaniṣṭhā jñānibhiḥ śivayoginaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Persons steadfast in austerities were worshipped by scholars. Those who had conquered the sense-organs were adored by those who were steadfast in penance. Those who were well-established in knowledge were adored by those who had mastered the sense-organs and Śiva Yogins were adored by those who were well-established in knowledge.

## \|\| 1.43.62 \|\|

*maṃtrapūtaṃ mahārhaṃ ca vidhiyuktaṃ susaṃskṛtam \|*  
*vāḍavānāṃ mukhāgnau ca hūyate'harniśaṃ haviḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Day and night sacrificial offerings well-consecrated, sanctified by Mantras and of great worth were duly made in the fire constituting the mouth of the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.43.63 \|\|

*vāpīkūpataḍāgānāmārāmāṇāṃ padepade \|*  
*śucibhirdravyasaṃbhāraiḥ kartāro yatra bhūriśaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. In that realm, at every step, there were many persons who dug wells, tanks and lakes and planted parks utilizing (their) wealth acquired by legitimate means.

## \|\| 1.43.64 \|\|

*yadrāṣṭre hṛṣṭapuṣṭāśca dṛśyaṃte sarvajātayaḥ \|*  
*aniṃdyasevā saṃpannā vināmṛgayu saunikān \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. In his realm people of all castes were seen delighted and well-nourished. Excepting hunters and animal killers, all were richly endowed with a desire to be engaged in uncensurable services.

## \|\| 1.43.65 \|\|

*itthaṃ tasya mahījāneḥ sarvatra śucivartinaḥ \|*  
*unmiṣaṃtopyanimiṣā manākchidraṃ na lebhire \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Thus that king was pure in every respect. The Devas who were given to find fault could not find even the least weak point in that king.

## \|\| 1.43.66 \|\|

*athovācāmara gururdevānapacikīrṣukān \|*  
*tasminrājani dharmiṣṭhe variṣṭhe maṃtravediṣu \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The preceptor of Devas said thus to the Devas who were desirous of harming that virtuous king who was the foremost among those who were conversant with Mantras.

## \|\| 1.43.67 \|\|

*gururuvāca \|*  
*saṃdhivigrahayānāsti saṃ śrayaṃ dvaidhabhāvanam \|*  
*yathā sa rājā saṃvetti na tathātrāpi kaścana \|\| 67 \|\|*

Guru said:

67\. Here no one knows (the six expedients in politics viz.) Sandhi, Vigraha, Yāna, Āsana, Saṃśraya and Dvaidhībhāvana (i.e. peace, war, marching against, halting, seeking shelter and duplicity) as that king.

## \|\| 1.43.68 \|\|

*upāyopyeka evāsti caturṣviha divaukasaḥ \|*  
*bhedo nāma sa cetsidhyettapobalini tatra hi \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O heaven-dwellers, among the four Upāyas (means of strategy) there is only one, namely Bheda (sowing dissensions) which perhaps may be successful in regard to that king who is very powerful due to his austerities.

## \|\| 1.43.69 \|\|

*tena yadyapi bhūbhartrā bhūmerdevā vivāsitāḥ \|*  
*tathāpi bhūriśastatra saṃtyasmatpakṣapātinaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Devas have been banished from the earth by that king. Yet there are many there who are partial and sympathetic towards us.

## \|\| 1.43.70 \|\|

*kālo nimiṣamātropi yānvinā na sukhaṃ vrajet \|*  
*asmākamapi tasyāpi saṃti te tatra mānitāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. They are honourd by him too as well as by us. Even for a moment he will not be happy without them.

## \|\| 1.43.71 \|\|

*aṃtarbahiścarā nityaṃ sarvaviśraṃbha bhūmayaḥ \|*  
*samāgateṣu teṣvatra sarvaṃ naḥ setsyati priyam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. They keep moving in and out constantly. They are objects of trust unto everyone. If once they come here, all that we desire can be achieved.

## \|\| 1.43.72 \|\|

*samākarṇya ca te sarve tridaśā gīṣpatīritam \|*  
*nirṇītavaṃtastasyārthaṃ tasmādaṃtarbahiścarān \|*  
*abhinaṃdyātha taṃ sarve procuritthaṃ bhavediti \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. On hearing the words uttered by Gīṣpati (i.e. Bṛhaspati) all the Devas understood the implications thereof. Hence they duly honoured those spies who moved within and without and said, “It shall be so.”

## \|\| 1.43.73 \|\|

*tataḥ śakraḥ samāhūya vītihotraṃ puraḥsthitam \|*  
*ūce madhurayā vācā bahumānapuraḥsaram \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Thereafter Śakra (Indra) called Vītihotra (god Fire) standing in front and spoke to him sweetly with great reverence.

## \|\| 1.43.74 \|\|

*havyavāhana yā mūrtistava tatra pratiṣṭhitā \|*  
*tāmupāsaṃhara kṣipraṃ viṣayāttasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. “O Havyavāhana, withdraw immediately your form established there in the realm of that king.

## \|\| 1.43.75 \|\|

*samāgatāyāṃ tanmūrtau sarvānaṣṭāgrayaḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*havyakavyakriyāśūnyā virajiṣyaṃti rājani \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. When that form comes back, all the subjects with their sacred fires having extinguished, shall become deprived of the rites of Havya and Kavya and so will be averse to the king.

## \|\| 1.43.76 \|\|

*prajāsu ca viraktāsu rājyakāmadughāsu vai \|*  
*kṛcchreṇopārjito'pārtho rājaśabdo bhaviṣyati \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Bereft of the attachment of the subjects—the wish-yielding divine cow of the kingdom, the title Rājā (a king, a delighter of the subjects) acquired with very great difficulty, shall become meaningless.

## \|\| 1.43.77 \|\|

*prajānāṃ raṃjanādrājā yeyaṃ rūḍhirupārjitā \|*  
*tasyāṃ rūḍhyāṃ pranaṣṭāyāṃ rājyameva vinaṃkṣyati \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. A king is called so (Rājā) because he makes the people delighted. This is the conventional meaning acquired (by the word). If that convention gets spoilt and lost the very kingdom shall perish.

## \|\| 1.43.78 \|\|

*prajāvirahito rājā kośadurgabalādibhiḥ \|*  
*samṛddhopyacirānnaśyetkūlasaṃstha iva drumaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The king alienated from the subjects will before long perish, though he may be richly endowed with treasury, fortress, army etc., like a tree on the bank (of a river).

## \|\| 1.43.79 \|\|

*trivargasādhanāhetuḥ prākprajaiva mahīpateḥ \|*  
*kṣīṇavṛttyāṃ prajāyāṃ vai trivargaḥ kṣīyate svayam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The means of achieving the three aims of life for a king is his subjects at the very outset. If the subjects become weak, the threefold objective gets weakened.

## \|\| 1.43.80 \|\|

*kṣīṇe trivarge saṃkṣīṇā gatirlokadvayātmikā \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. When the three-fold aim gets weakened the attainment (of the pleasures) of the two worlds too becomes very weak.”

## \|\| 1.43.81 \|\|

*itīṃdravacanādvahnirahnāya kṣoṇimaṃḍalāt \|*  
*ācakarṣa nijāṃ mūrtiṃ yogamāyā balānvitaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. At these words of Indra, god Fire endowed with Yogic Māyā quickly withdrew his form from the region of the earth.

## \|\| 1.43.82 \|\|

*ninye na kevalaṃ tretāṃ jāṭharāgnimapi prabhuḥ \|*  
*vajriṇo vacasā vahnirnijaśaktisamanvitam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. At the instance of the Thunderbolt-wielding Lord, god Fire withdraw not only the Tretāgnis (the three types of sacrificial fires) but also the gastric fire having the power of digesting foodstuffs.

## \|\| 1.43.83-84 \|\|

*vahnau svarlokamāpanne jāte madhyaṃdine nṛpaḥ \|*  
*kṛtamādhyāhnikastūrṇaṃ prāviśadbhojyamaṃḍapam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*mahānasādhikṛtayo vepamānāstato muhuḥ \|*  
*kṣudhārtamapi bhūpālamidaṃ maṃdaṃ vyajijñapan \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. When god Fire had gone back to the heavenly region, at midday, the king concluded the midday rites and quickly entered the dining hall. The trembling officials in charge of the kitchen submitted as follows to the hungry king.

## \|\| 1.43.85-86 \|\|

*sūpakārā ūcuḥ \|*  
*atyahaskaratejaska pratāpavijitānala \|*  
*kiṃcidvijñaptukāmāḥ smopyakāṃḍeraṇapaṃḍita \|\| 85 \|\|*

*yadi viśruṇayedrājanbhavānabhayadakṣiṇām \|*  
*tadā vijñāpayiṣyāmaḥ prabaddhakarasaṃpuṭāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

The Cooks said:

85-86. O king, you have excelled the Sun by means of your brilliance and god Fire by means of your exploits. Though it is untimely, we are desirous of submitting something, O king skilled in fighting battles. If you accord to us freedom from fear, we shall intimate to you with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.43.87 \|\|

*bhrūsaṃjñayākṛtādeśāḥ praśastāsyenabhūbhujā \|*  
*mṛdu vijñāpayāṃcakruḥ pākaśālādhikāriṇaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. When the command was given with an indication from his eyebrows by the king of esteemed countenance, the officials in charge of the Royal Kitchen submitted softly:

## \|\| 1.43.88 \|\|

*na jānīmo vayaṃ nātha tvatpratāpabhayārditaḥ \|*  
*kusṛtyātha kayā vidvānnaṣṭo vaiśvānaraḥ purāt \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. “O lord, we are not fully aware by what mischievous means Vaiśvānara (god Fire), terrified much at your exploits and fully conscious (of the consequences), vanished from the city.

## \|\| 1.43.89 \|\|

*kṛśānau kṛśatāṃ prāpte kathaṃ pākakriyā bhavet \|*  
*tathāpi sūryapākena siddhā paktirhi kācana \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. How can there go regular cooking acitivity when fire has vanished? Still some cooking has been completed by us with solar power.

## \|\| 1.43.90 \|\|

*prabhorādeśamāsādya tāmihaivānayāmahe \|*  
*manyāmahe ca bhūjāne paktiradyatanī śubhā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. On getting your lordship’s command we shall bring it here. O king, we think that today’s cooking is good.”

## \|\| 1.43.91 \|\|

*śrutvāṃdhasikavākyaṃ sa mahāsattvo mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*nṛpatiściṃtayāmāsa devānāṃ vai kṛtaṃ tvidam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. On hearing the words of the cooks that highly intelligent king of noble temperament thought that it was the mischief done by Devas.

## \|\| 1.43.92-96 \|\|

*kṣaṇaṃ saṃśīlayaṃstatra dadarśa tapasobalāt \|*  
*na kevalaṃ jahau gehaṃ hutabhukcaudarīrdarīḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*apyahāsīditolokājjagāma ca surālayam \|*  
*bhavatviha hi kā hānirasmākaṃ jvalane gatai \|\| 93 \|\|*

*teṣāmevavicārācca hānireṣā suparvaṇām \|*  
*tadbalena ca kiṃ rājyaṃ mayedamurarīkṛtam \|\| 94 \|\|*

*pitāmahena mahato gauravātpratipāditam \|*  
*iti ciṃtayatastasya madhyalokaśatakratoḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*paurāḥ samāgatā dvāri saha jānapadairnaraiḥ \|*  
*dvāsthena cājñayā rājñastatasteṃtaḥ praveśitāḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

92-96. Presently he meditated and visualized by means of the power of his penance that god Fire abandoned not only the kitchen but also the cavities of belly and went away to the abode of the gods, away from the earth.

‘Let it be so. What harm has been done to us when god Fire has left? The harm is that of the gods thanks to the disorderly activity (i.e. cessation of sacrifices etc.). Has the kingdom been taken over by me on the strength of their power? It has been assigned to me by the Creator, Brahmā, with due weightage.’

While that king who ruled the middle world (Earth) like Indra was thinking thus, the citizens came to the royal threshold along with the people of the surrounding countryside. At the king’s behest they were allowed to enter by the doorkeeper.

## \|\| 1.43.97-98 \|\|

*dattvopadaṃ yathārhaṃ te praṇemuḥ kṣoṇivajriṇam \|*  
*kecitsaṃbhāṣitā rājñādarasodarayā girā \|\| 97 \|\|*

*kecicca samudā dṛṣṭyā kecicca karasaṃjñayā \|*  
*visarjitā sanā rājñā bahumānapuraḥsaram \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. They were given due precedence and approach and they bowed down to the king (the Indra on the Earth). Some of them were addressed by the king in a voice indicating reverence. Some were welcomed with eyes beaming with delight. Some were received with gestures of the hands. They left their seats and were received by the king with due deference.

## \|\| 1.43.99 \|\|

*tejire bhejire sarve ratnārciḥ parisevite \|*  
*vijitāmodasaṃdohe surānokahasaurabhaiḥ \|*  
*rājñaḥ śataśalākasthacchatrasyacchāyayāśubhe \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. All of them resorted to the courtyard. It was served (lighted) with the rays of precious stones. The fragrance thereof surpassed that of celestial trees (in sweetness). It was auspicious and splendid due to the shade of the royal umbrellas of a hundred ribs.

## \|\| 1.43.100-111 \|\|

*viśāṃpatirathovāca tanmukhacchāyayeritam \|*  
*vijñāya tadabhiprāyamalaṃbhītyā puraukasaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*vikārakāribhirlekhairyadinīto'nalo bhuvaḥ \|*  
*etāvataiva kiṃ siddhayenmayi teṣāṃ parābhavaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*cikīrṣurahamevāsaṃ paurāḥ kāryamidaṃpurā \|*  
*paraṃ hyupekṣitaprāyaṃ diṣṭyā taiḥ smāritaṃ cirāt \|\| 102 \|\|*

*gato'nalo'bhavadbhadraṃ jagatprāṇopi yātvitaḥ \|*  
*varuṇaḥ puṣpavaṃtābhyāmavilaṃbaṃ prayātvitaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*ahameva hi parjanyo bhaviṣyāmi tapobalāt \|*  
*mude janapadānāṃ ca sarvasasyasamṛddhidaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*tapoyogabalenāhamātmānaṃ parikalpya ca \|*  
*tridhāvahnisvarūpeṇa paktīṣṭivyuṣṭikṛttamaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

*aṃtarbahiśca yo dvedhā nabhasvatpadavī dadhat \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva vetsyāmi tvaṃtaḥkaraṇaceṣṭitam \|\| 106 \|\|*

*vidhāya cāṃbhasīṃ mūrtiṃ sarvajīvaikajīvanīm \|*  
*prajāḥ saṃjīvayipyāmi kiṃ jaḍairviṣaye mama \|\| 107 \|\|*

*yadā khe tamasā paurā grasyete śaśibhāskarau \|*  
*tadā na kiṃ vinā tābhyāṃ jīvāmaḥ kṣitimaṃḍale \|\| 108 \|\|*

*śriyaṃ cāṃdramasīṃ prāpya hlādayiṣyāmyahaṃ prajāḥ \|*  
*niśācareṇa kimiha kṣayiṇā ca kalaṃkinā \|\| 109 \|\|*

*asmatkule mūlabhūto bhāskaro mānya eva naḥ \|*  
*sa tiṣṭhatu sukhenātra yātāyātaṃ karotu ca \|\| 110 \|\|*

*sa eko jagatāmātmā viśeṣātkuladevatā \|*  
*sopakartuṃ na vettyeva tasyedaṃ vratamuttamam \|\| 111 \|\|*

100-111. Then the king, having come to know their purpose as evinced by their facial colour (expression), began to speak:

“O citizens, do not be afraid. If fire is taken away from the earth by the Devas committing mischief, does it by itself amount to an attack on me by them?

O citizens, I myself had a desire of doing this but did not bring it into effect. Fortunately it has been recalled after a long time.

Fire has gone away. That is good. Let god Wind too go away from here. Let Varuṇa too along with the Sun and the Moon, go away without delay.

By means of the power of my penance I myself shall be Indra, the bestower of the abundance of all vegetation to the delight of the realm all-round.

Thanks to the power of penance and Yoga, I shall divide myself into the three forms of fire for carrying out the activities of cooking, sacrificial rites and warming (those affected by chillness).

I shall adopt the duty of Wind within (the body) and outside (in the world) and become capable of knowing the internal activities of everyone.

I shall assume the form of water, the sole enlivener of all creatures, and resuscitate all the subjects. Of what use are the waters in my realm?

When the Moon and the Sun are overwhelmed by Tamas (Rāhu at the time of eclipse), O citizens, do we not keep alive without them in the world?

I shall make the subjects delighted by assuming the splendour of the Moon. Of what avail is the night-stalking Moon that wastes away and is defiled by a stigma?

Bhāskara (the Sun) is the founder of our dynasty. He is decidedly worthy of our respect. Let him remain happily and carry on his movements to and fro.

He alone is the very soul of all the worlds. Particularly he is our family deity. He does not stoop to commit any harm. That is his excellent vow.”

## \|\| 1.43.112 \|\|

*iti narapativāksudhārasaughaṃ śrutipuṭakaiḥ paripīya pauravargaḥ \|*  
*vikasitavadanāṃbujo jagāmanijanijamālayamādhimuktacittaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. After imbibing these nectar-like words of the king through the cups of their ears, the citizens with their faces beaming with delight went away to their respective abodes without any worry in their minds.

## \|\| 1.43.113 \|\|

*kṣitipatirapi tattathā vidhāya tapasosādhyamihāsti kiṃ trilokyām \|*  
*ativahnyarkamasau dadhaccatejo dyusadāṃ śalyamivoccakairbabhūva \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. The king too did accordingly. What is it that cannot be achieved by penance in the three worlds? Adopting the refulgence far excelling that of fire and the Sun, he became, as it were, a great thorn in the heart of the heaven-dwellers.

## Chapter 44 - Description of Kāśī

## \|\| 1.44.1-2 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*atha maṃdarakaṃdarodarollasada samadyuti ratnamaṃdire \|*  
*paritaḥ samadhiṣṭhitāmare nijaśikharairvasanīkṛtāṃbare \|\| 1 \|\|*

*nivasañjagadīśvaro haraḥ kṛśarajanīśa kalāmanoharaḥ \|\| \|*  
*labhate sma na śarma śaṃkaraḥ prasaratkāśiviyogaja jvaraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1-2.
