Hara, the Lord of the universe, beautified with the digit of the crescent moon, was staying in his palace studded with precious stones and shining with the splendour of jewels within the caves of Mandara. The place was very high in the firmament, surrounded by the peaks of the mountain and the Devas were occupying the seats all-around. Yet Śaṅkara did not feel delighted because of the rising fever born of the separation from Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.44.3 \|\|

*virahānalaśāṃtaye tadā samalepi tripurāriṇāpi yaḥ \|*  
*malayodbhava paṃka eṣa sa pratipedehyadhunā pipāṃsutām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In order to calm down the scorching fire of separation, sandal-paste from Malaya was smeared on his body by the Lord, the enemy of the three Puras. That had dried up and assumed the form of the ash (on his body).

## \|\| 1.44.4 \|\|

*paritāpaharāṇi padminīnāṃ mṛdulānyapi kaṃkaṇīkṛtāni \|*  
*gaditāni yadīśvareṇa sarpāstadabhūtsatyamahomaheśvarecchā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Tender stalks of lotus were tied round his hands like bracelets for the removal of the scorching heat. The Lord then shouted out that they were serpents (so stinging and scorching). That turned out to be a fact. Alas! The wish of the Great Lord (prevails).

## \|\| 1.44.5 \|\|

*yadu dugdhanidhiṃ nimathyadevairmṛdusāraḥ samakarṣi pūrṇacaṃdraḥ \|*  
*sa babhūva kṛśo viyogatapteśvaramūrdhoṣmaparikṣaraccharīraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The cool full-moon that had been drawn out by the Devas after churning the Ocean of Milk became lean and thin with its body wasting away due to the heat of the head of the Lord scorched by the fire of separation.

## \|\| 1.44.6 \|\|

*yadadīdharadeṣa jātatāpaḥ pṛthule maulijaṭāni kuṃjakoṇe \|*  
*paritāpaharāṃ harastadānīṃ dyunadīṃ tāmadhunāpi nojjihīte \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On being scorched (with the heat of separation from Kāśī) Hara does not let go even today the heat-quelling celestial river which he had held up in a corner of his extensive matted hair.

## \|\| 1.44.7 \|\|

*mahato virahasya śaṃkaraḥ prasabhaṃtasyavaśī vaśaṃgataḥ \|*  
*vividena suraiḥ sadogatairapi saṃvītasutāpaveṣṭitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Śaṅkara of habitual, perfect self-control had become a victim of a great (fire of) separation, but since he covered it up perfectly, he was not known to be so by the Suras present in his assembly.

## \|\| 1.44.8 \|\|

*aticitramidaṃ yadātmanā śucirapyeṣa kṛpīṭayoninā \|*  
*svapurīvirahodbhavena vai paritāpyeta jagattrayeśvaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This is very surprising that the pure Lord of the three worlds should be scorched by the fire arising from the separation from his own city, even though the fire is his own form.

## \|\| 1.44.9 \|\|

*nijabhālatalaṃ kalānidheḥ kalayā nityamalaṃkaroti yaḥ \|*  
*sa tadīśvaramapyatāpayadvidhureko viparīta eva tu \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Lord always adorns his forehead with a digit of the moon. Still that moon scorched the Lord. When one is in misery who is not against one?

## \|\| 1.44.10 \|\|

*garalaṃ galanālikātale vilasedasya na tena tāpitaḥ \|*  
*amṛtāṃśu tuṣāradīdhiti pracayaireva tu tāpito'dbhutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The poison is shining in the throat but he is not scorched thereby. It is surprising that he is scorched by the clusters of cod, nectar-like rays of the moon.

## \|\| 1.44.11 \|\|

*vilasaddharicaṃdanodakacchaṭayā tadvirahāpanuttaye \|*  
*hṛdayā hi tayāpyadūyata prasaradbhogiphaṭābhavairna tu \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He was afflicted with the mass of Haricandana (sandal-paste) water applied over the chest for the removal of the heat of separation but not with the poison issuing from the spreading hoods of the serpents.

## \|\| 1.44.12 \|\|

*sakalabhramameṣa nāśayetsragahitvādyapadeśajaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*idamadbhutamasya yadbhramaḥ sphuṭamālyepi mahāhisaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This Lord Hara is capable of destroying all the erroneous conceptions such as those of serpents in garlands. It is surprising that he too had the misconception of a serpent in a distinctly visible garland.

## \|\| 1.44.13 \|\|

*smṛtimātrapathaṃgatopi yastrividha tāpamapākarotyalam \|*  
*sa hi kāśiviyogatāpitaḥ svagataṃ kiṃcidajalpadityajaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. That unborn Lord (Śiva) is capable of destroying the three Tāpas (distresses) merely on being remembered. But he too was distressed due to the separation from Kāśī. He then began to prattle thus:

## \|\| 1.44.14 \|\|

*api kāśi samāgato'nilo yadi gātrāṇi pariṣvajenmama \|*  
*davathuḥ pariśāṃtimeti tannahi mānī parigāhanairapi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. ‘Even if the wind blowing from Kāśī were to embrace my limbs, the heat therein may subside but not by diving into a vast expanse of snow.

## \|\| 1.44.15 \|\|

*agamiṣyadahokathaṃ satāpo nanu dakṣāṃgajayāya edhitaḥ \|*  
*mamajīvātulatā jhaṭityalaṃ hyabhaviṣyanna himādrijā yadi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The distress of mine was heightened by the separation of the daughter of Dakṣa. How could it have subsided if the daughter of Himālaya, the creeper that enlivens me, had not manifested immediately?

## \|\| 1.44.16 \|\|

*na tathojjhitadehayātayā mama dakṣodbhavayāmano'dunot \|*  
*avimuktaviyogajanmanāpari dūyeta yathā mahoṣmaṇā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When Dakṣa’s daughter cast off her body, my mind was distressed, but it was not as much as the present distress due to the great heat arising from the separation from Avimukta.

## \|\| 1.44.17 \|\|

*ayi kāśi mudā kadā punastava lapsye sukhamaṃgasaṃgajam \|*  
*atiśītalitāni yena me'dbhutagātrāṇi bhavaṃti tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O Kāśī, when will I have the joyous pleasure of coming into contact with you whereby all my limbs shall cool down instantaneously and surprisingly?

## \|\| 1.44.18 \|\|

*ayi kāśi vināśitāghasaṃghe tavaviśleṣajaāśuśukṣaṇiḥ \|*  
*amṛtāṃśukalāmṛdudravairaticitraṃhaviṣeva vardhate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O Kāśī, you have destroyed all sins. The fire due to the separation from you gets increased through the cool drops of the digits of the nectar-rayed moon as though through the offerings of ghee. It is really surprising.

## \|\| 1.44.19 \|\|

*agamanmama dakṣajā viyogajo davathuḥ prāgghimavatsutauṣadhena \|*  
*adhunā khalu naiva śāṃtimīyāṃ yadi kāśīṃ na vilokayehamāśu \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Formerly my fever (heat) due to the separation from Dakṣa’s daughter vanished due to the remedy in the form of Himavān’s daughter. Indeed now I will not attain peace unless I see Kāśī quickly.’

## \|\| 1.44.20 \|\|

*manaseti gṛṇaṃstadā śivaḥ sutarāṃ saṃvṛtatāpavaikṛtaḥ \|*  
*jagadaṃbikayā dhiyāṃ jananyā kathamapyeṣa viyukta ityamāni \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Śiva had perfectly concealed the aberration due to distress. But when he began to lament mentally, he was somehow understood by the mother of the universe and of all the intellects, as lamenting for separation from something.

## \|\| 1.44.21 \|\|

*priyayā vapuṣordhayānayāpyaparijñāta viyogakāraṇaḥ \|*  
*vacanairupacaryate sma sapraṇataprāṇinidāghadāraṇaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Even by that beloved who was a half part of his body, the cause of Śiva’s grief of separation was not understood. She, therefore, addressed the following probing words to the Lord who dispels the distress of all living beings that bow unto him.

## \|\| 1.44.22 \|\|

*śrīpārvatyuvāca \|*  
*tava sarvaga sarvamasti haste vilasadyoga viyoga eva kaste \|*  
*tava bhūtiraho vibhūtidātrī sakalāpatkalikāpi bhūtadhātrī \|\| 22 \|\|*

Śrī Pārvatī said:

22\. O omnipresent one, everything is within the grasp of your hand. What separation do you have, O Lord endowed with Yogic power? Sacred ash besmeared by you bestows prosperity (on the devotees). (By your grace) the entire earth is rid all of adversities.

## \|\| 1.44.23 \|\|

*tvadanīkṣaṇataḥ kṣaṇādvibho pralayaṃ yāṃti jagaṃti śocyavat \|*  
*cyavate bhavataḥ kṛpālavāditaropīśanayastvayoṃkṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Lord, in the absence of your supervision in a moment all the worlds become annihilated and undergo miserable plight. O Lord, if anyone is not favoured by you with the least of mercy, he undergoes downfall as an alien.

## \|\| 1.44.24 \|\|

*bhavataḥ paritāpahetavo na bhavaṃtīṃdu divākarāgnayaḥ \|*  
*nayanāniyatastrinetra te'mī praṇayinyastilasajjalā ca maulau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The moon the sun and fire do not cause distress unto you, O Three-eyed One, because they are your eyes. Your beloved with refulgent water i.e. Gaṅgā is on your head itself.

## \|\| 1.44.25 \|\|

*bhujagābhujagāḥ sadaiva te'mī na viṣaṃ saṃkramate ca nīlakaṃṭha \|*  
*ahamasmi ca vāmadeva vāmā tava vāmaṃvapuratra cittayuktā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. These serpents always resort to your arms (as ornaments). O Blue-throated One, no poison affects you. O Vāmadeva, I am the splendid woman constituting your left side here and acting favourably to your mental predilection.

## \|\| 1.44.26 \|\|

*iti saṃsṛtisaṃbījajananyābhihite hite \|*  
*girāṃ niguṃphe giriśo vaktumapyādade giram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When this was uttered in a way conducive to welfare by the mother of the seed of the worldly existence, with a selected collection of words, Giriśa (Śiva) began to speak (in reply).

## \|\| 1.44.27 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ayi kāśītyaṣṭamūrtirbhavo bhāvāṣṭakobhavat \|*  
*satvaraṃ śivayājñāyi dhruvaṃ kāśyāhṛtoharaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

27\. O Kāśī, the Lord having eight cosmic forms, Bhava, Hara, has been certainly captivated by you, Kāśī.

This is understood by Śivā (Pārvatī) quickly.

## \|\| 1.44.28 \|\|

*athabālasakhī bhūta tattatkānanavīrudham \|\| śivāprastāvayāṃcakre vimuktāṃ muktidāṃ purīm \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thereupon Śivā (Pārvatī) described Avimukta, the city that bestows salvation, the sylvan creepers whereof had been her childhood friends.

## \|\| 1.44.29 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*gaganatalamilitasalile pralayepi bhava triśūlapari vidhṛtām \|*  
*kṛtapuṃḍarīkaśobhāṃ smaraharakāśīṃ purīṃ yāvaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:

29\. O Smarahara (Śiva), we shall go to Kāśī, the city that is held on the trident by Bhava at the time of deluge, when the water reached upto the sky, where it assumed the splendour of a lotus.

## \|\| 1.44.30 \|\|

*dharādhareṃdrasya dharātisuṃdarā na māṃ tathāsyāpi dhinoti dhūrjaṭe \|*  
*dharāgatāpīha na yā dhruvaṃdharā purīdhurīṇā tava kāśikā yathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Dhūrjaṭi, even the realm of (my father) the Lord of mountains does not delight me so much as your Kāśikā, the foremost city which is no part of the earth though it is on the earth (as it is held aloft by the Lord on his trident).

## \|\| 1.44.31 \|\|

*na yatra kāśyāṃ kalikālajaṃ bhayaṃ na yatra kāśyāṃ maraṇātpunarbhavaḥ \|*  
*na yatra kāśyāṃ kaluṣodbhavaṃ bhayaṃ kathaṃ vibho sā nayanātithirbhavet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O Lord, how will that city of Kāśī become the object of our vision, the city where there is no fear arising from Kali Age, the city wherein (if) one dies, he is not reborn, the city where there is no fear arising from sins.

## \|\| 1.44.32 \|\|

*kimatra no saṃti puraḥ sahasraśaḥ padepade sarvasamṛddhibhūmayaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ na kāśī sadṛśīdṛśoḥ padaṃ kvacidgatā me bhavatā śape śiva \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Don’t we have thousands of cities everywhere abounding in all types of prosperities? But I swear by you, none like Kāśī has come within the range of my vision, O Śiva.

## \|\| 1.44.33 \|\|

*triviṣṭape saṃti na kiṃ puraḥ śataṃ samastakautūhalajanmabhūmayaḥ \|*  
*tṛṇī bhavaṃtīha ca tāḥ puraḥpuraḥ padaṃ purāre bhavato bhavadviṣaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Aren’t there hundred cities in Heaven, the source of origin of all fanciful things? But, O Purāri (Śiva), in comparison with the city of thine, the destroyer of worldly sufferings, they are all worthless.

## \|\| 1.44.34 \|\|

*na kevalaṃ kāśiviyogajo jvaraḥ prabādhate tvāṃ tu tathā yathātra mām \|*  
*upāya eṣotra nidāghaśāṃtaye purī tu sā vā mamajanmabhūratha \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The fever due to the separation from Kāśī does not effect you as much as it affects me. For the quiescence of the distress, the only remedy is that city or my native land.

## \|\| 1.44.35 \|\|

*mayā na mene mamajanmabhūmikā viyogajanmā paridāghaīśitaḥ \|*  
*avāpyakāśīṃ paritaḥ praśāṃtidāṃ samastasaṃtāpavighātahetukām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O Lord, after attaining Kāśī, the bestower of peace all round, the cause of the destruction of all sorts of distress, the distress due to the separation from my native land has not been thought of by me.

## \|\| 1.44.36 \|\|

*na mokṣalakṣmyotra samakṣamīkṣitāstanūbhṛtā kenacideva kutracit \|*  
*avaimyahaṃ śarmada sarvaśarmadā sarūpiṇī muktirasau hi kāśikā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The Lakṣmīs of salvation have not been directly perceived by any embodied being anywhere. I am aware, O Lord, O bestower of happiness, indeed Kāśikā is the salvation akin in form to the bestower of all happiness and welfare.

## \|\| 1.44.37 \|\|

*na muktirastīha tathā samādhinā sthireṃdriyatvojjhita tatsamādhinā \|*  
*kratukriyābhirna na vedavidyayā yathā hi kāśyāṃ parihāya vigraham \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Neither by performing meditation on the Absolute (Brahma), avoiding unsteadiness of sense-organs, nor by (performance of) Kratu (sacrifice) and other rites, nor by Vedic knowledge and lore, is salvation attainable as easily as by casting off the body at Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.44.38 \|\|

*na nākaloke sukhamasti tādṛśaṃ kutastu pātālatale'tisuṃdare \|*  
*vārtāpi martye sukhasaṃśrayā kva vā kāśyāṃ hi yādṛktanumātradhāriṇi \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Nowhere is such happiness possible as is found in Kāśī. It is neither in heaven nor elsewhere in the world. How can it be found even in Pātāla which is so very beautiful. Where can be even a talk of happiness in the mortal world?

## \|\| 1.44.39 \|\|

*kṣetre triśūlinbhavato'vimukte vimuktilakṣmyā na kadāpi mukte \|*  
*manopi yaḥ prāṇivaraḥ prayuṃkte ṣaḍaṃgayogaṃ sa sadaiva yuṃkte \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O trident -bearing Lord! Your holy place Avimukta is never bereft of the Lakṣmī (glory) of salvation. If a meritorious creature were to exercise (control over) his mind there, he will always be practising the Yoga with the six ancillaries.

## \|\| 1.44.40 \|\|

*ṣaḍaṃgayogānnahi tādṛśī nṛbhiḥ śarīrasiddhiḥ sahasātra labhyate \|*  
*sukhena kāśīṃ samavāpya yādṛśīdṛśau sthirīkṛtya śiva tvayi kṣaṇam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Through the Yoga with six ancillaries, men cannot achieve that bodily Yoga-Siddhi instantaneously which one attains very easily, O Śiva, by fixing the eyes on you for a moment after reaching Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.44.41 \|\|

*varaṃ hi tiryaktvamabuddhivaibhavaṃ na mānavatvaṃ bahubuddhibhājanam \|*  
*akāśisaṃdarśananiṣphalodayaṃ samaṃtataḥ puṣkarabudbudopamam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Better indeed is a brute without the gift of intellect and not a human possessing the power of intellect, which refuses to be benefited by failing to visit Kāśī (by postponing to go there) as life is transient resembling a bubble of water on a lotus leaf.

## \|\| 1.44.42 \|\|

*dṛśau kṛtārthe kṛtakāśidarśane tanuḥkṛtārthā śivakāśivāsinī \|*  
*manaḥkṛtārthaṃ dhṛtakāśisaṃśrayaṃ mukhaṃ kṛtārthaṃ kṛtakāśisaṃmukham \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The two eyes that have seen Kāśī are blessed; O Śiva, the body that resides in Kāśī is blessed; the mind that has resorted to Kāśī is blessed; the face is blessed that has been turned towards Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.44.43 \|\|

*varaṃ hi tatkāśirajoti pāvanaṃ rajastamodhvaṃsi śaśiprabhojjvalam \|*  
*kṛtapraṇāmairmaṇikarṇikā bhuve lalāṭagaṃyadbahumanyate suraiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Even a dust particle of Kāśī is excessively sacred and always destroys Rajas and Tamas qualities. It is as brilliant as the splendour of the moon. It is held in great esteem by the Suras when it sticks to their forehead touching in making obeisance to the region around Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 1.44.44 \|\|

*na devaloko na ca satyaloko na nāgaloko maṇikarṇikāyāḥ \|*  
*tulāṃ vrajedyatra mahāprayāṇakṛcchrutirbhavedbrahmarasāyanāspadam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Neither the world of Devas, nor Satyaloka, nor the world of serpents can be on a par with Maṇikarṇikā, because the ear of a person who dies at that place becomes fit to receive Brahmarasāyana (Praṇava or Rāmamantrarāja).

## \|\| 1.44.45 \|\|

*mahāmahobhūrmaṇikarṇikāsthalī tamastatiryatra sameti saṃkṣayam \|*  
*paraḥ śatairjanmabhiredhitāpi yā divākarāgnīṃdukarairanigrahā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The region of Maṇikarṇikā is the source of excellent refulgence, where the expanse of darkness (i.e. ignorance) which is accumulated and increased in the course of hundreds of births and which cannot be quelled by fire or the rays of the sun and the moon, gets destroyed.

## \|\| 1.44.46 \|\|

*kimu nirvāṇapadasya bhadrapīṭhaṃ mṛdulaṃ talpamathonumokṣalakṣmyāḥ \|*  
*athavā maṇikarṇikāsthalī paramānaṃdasukaṃdajanmabhūmiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Is (It is as if) the region of Maṇikarṇikā, the throne of ultimate salvation or the soft bed of the Lakṣmī of salvation, or the source of origin of the great bulbous root (i.e. the prime cause) of the highest bliss?

## \|\| 1.44.47 \|\|

*samatītavimuktajaṃtusaṃkhyā kriyate yatra janaiḥ sukhopaviṣṭaiḥ \|*  
*vilasaddyuti sūkṣmaśarkarābhiḥ svavapuḥpātamahotsavābhilāṣaiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. By means of minute particles of refulgent pebbles persons who are happily seated (in Maṇikarṇikā) count the number of those creatures who have previously attained salvation there. They themselves eagerly await the destruction of their bodies, which constitutes a great festival unto them.

## \|\| 1.44.48 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*aparṇāparivarṇyeti purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ mune \|*  
*punarvijñāpayāmāsa kāśīprāptyai pinākinam \|\| 48 \|\|*

Skanda said:

48\. After describing the city of Vārāṇasī thus, O sage, Aparṇā (Pārvatī) once again urged the Pināka-wielding Lord to proceed to Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.44.49 \|\|

*śrīpārvatyuvāca \|*  
*pramathādhipa sarveśa nityasvādhīnavartana \|*  
*yathānaṃdavanaṃ yāyāṃ tathā kuru varaprada \|\| 49 \|\|*

Śrī Pārvatī said:

49\. O Lord of Pramathas, O Lord of all, O bestower of boons, you are ever independent in your existence. Kindly see that I am enabled to go to Ānandavana.

## \|\| 1.44.50 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*jitapīyūṣamādhuryāṃ kāśīstavanasuṃdarīm \|*  
*athākarṇyāhamudito giriśo girijāṃ giram \|\| 50 \|\|*

Skanda said:

50\. On hearing this Giriśa became pleased. He spoke unto Girijā whose words had excelled even nectar in sweetness and who was brilliant in the exposition of Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.44.51 \|\|

*śrīdevadeva uvāca \|*  
*ayi priyatame gauri tvadvā gamṛtasīkaraiḥ \|*  
*āpyāyitosmi nitarāṃ kāśīprāptyai yatedhunā \|\| 51 \|\|*

Śrī Devadeva said:

51\. O my beloved Gaurī, I have been thrilled and refreshed by the sprays of nectar in the form of your words. Now I shall endeavour to reach Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.44.52 \|\|

*tvaṃ jānāsi mahādevi mama yattanmahadvratam \|*  
*abhuktapūrvamanyena vastūpāśnāmi netarat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O great goddess, you are aware that I enjoy only that thing which is not enjoyed by others and not other things.

## \|\| 1.44.53 \|\|

*pitāmahasya vacanāddivodāse mahīpatau \|*  
*dharmeṇa śāsati purīṃ ka upāyo vidhīyatām \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. As, at the behest of the Grandfather (Brahmā) King Divodāsa is administering the city righteously what remedy should be employed?

## \|\| 1.44.54 \|\|

*kathaṃ sa rājā dharmiṣṭhaḥ prajāpālanatatparaḥ \|*  
*viyojyate puraḥ kāśyā divodāso mahīpatiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. How can that righteous King Divodāsa who is eager to protect the subjects, be dislodged from that city of Kāśī?

## \|\| 1.44.55 \|\|

*adharmavartino yasmādvighnaḥ syānnetarasya tu \|*  
*tasmātkaṃ preṣayāmīśe yastaṃ kāśyā viyojayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Since there can be obstacles only on the path of the unrighteous and not that of others, O goddess, whom should I send there who will dislodge him from Kāśī?

## \|\| 1.44.56 \|\|

*dharmavartmānusaratāṃ yo vighnaṃ samupācaret \|*  
*tasyaiva jāyate vighnaḥ pratyuta premavardhini \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If anyone puts in obstacles to those who follow the righteous path, he himself will face obstacles on the other hand, O enhancer of love.

## \|\| 1.44.57 \|\|

*vinācchidreṇa taṃ bhūpaṃ notsādayitumutsahe \|*  
*mayaiva hi yato rakṣyāḥ priye dharmadhuraṃdharāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Without any fault (on his part), I am not enthusiastic enough to assail him. Indeed, O dear one, those who strictly adhere to righteousness should be protected by me.

## \|\| 1.44.58 \|\|

*na jarā tamatikrāmenna taṃ mṛtyurjirghāṃsati \|*  
*vyādhayastaṃ na bādhaṃte dharmavartmabhṛdatrayaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Old age will not afflict him. Death will not desire to take away his life. Ailments do not torment him who sticks to the path of righteousness here.

## \|\| 1.44.59 \|\|

*iti saṃciṃtayandevo yoginīcakramagrataḥ \|*  
*dadarśātimahāprauḍhaṃ gāḍhakāryasya sādhanam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Even as the Lord was thinking thus, he saw in front of him a group of Yoginīs of great maturity, capable of accomplishing hard tasks.

## \|\| 1.44.60 \|\|

*atha devyā samālocya vyomakeśo mahāmune \|*  
*yoginīvṛṃdamāhūya jagau vākyamidaṃ haraḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. After discussing the matter with the goddess, O great sage Vyomakeśa, Hara called the group of Yoginīs and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.44.61-63 \|\|

*satvaraṃ yāta yoginyo mama vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*yatra rājā divodāso rājyaṃ dharmeṇa śāstyalam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*svadharmavicyutaḥ kāśīṃ yathā tūrṇaṃ tyajennṛpaḥ \|*  
*tathopacarata prājñā yogamāyābalānvitāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*yathā punarnavīkṛtya purīṃ vārāṇasīmaham \|*  
*itaḥ prayāmi yoginyastathā kṣipraṃ vidhīyatām \|\| 63 \|\|*

61-63. “O Yoginīs, hasten to my city Vārāṇasī where King Divodāsa rules the kingdom with adequate adherence to righteousness. O intelligent Yoginīs equipped with the power of Yoga and Māyā, proceed in that manner which will make the king swerve from his duty and abandon Kāśī. O Yoginīs, quickly carry out such means as will enable me to go to Vārāṇasī after renovating it.”

## \|\| 1.44.64 \|\|

*iti prasādamāsādya śāsanaṃ śirasā vahan \|*  
*kṛtapraṇāmo niryāto yoginīnāṃ gaṇastataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Having accepted with bowing heads this behest considering it as a divine favour, the group of Yoginīs bowed down again and departed therefrom.

## \|\| 1.44.65 \|\|

*yayurākāśamāviśya manasopya tiraṃhasā \|*  
*parasparaṃ bhāṣamāṇā yoginyastā mudānvitāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Those Yoginīs were highly delighted. With a speed far exceeding that of the mind, they passed through the sky talking to one another.

## \|\| 1.44.66-67 \|\|

*adya dhanyatarāḥ smo vai devadevena yatsvayam \|*  
*kṛtaprasādāḥ prahitāḥ śrīmadānaṃdakānanam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*adya sadyo mahālābhāvabhūtāṃ notidurlabhau \|*  
*trinetrarājasaṃmānastathā kāśī vilokanam \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. “Today we are further blessed because the Lord of Devas himself bestowed his favour and sent us to the glorious Ānandakānana. Today all of a sudden we had two rare advantages, the honour conferred by the Three-eyed Lord and the opportunity to visit Kāśī.”

## \|\| 1.44.68 \|\|

*iti muditamanāḥ sa yoginīnāṃ nikuraṃvastvathamaṃdarādrikuṃjāt \|*  
*nabhasi laghukṛtaprayāṇavego nayanātithyamalaṃbhayatpurīṃ tām \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Thus, the delighted group of Yoginīs departed from the pleasure-grove in the Mandara mountain, travelled through the sky quickly and espied that city.

## Chapter 45 - The Arrival of Sixty-four Yoginīs

## \|\| 1.45.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*atha tadyoginīvṛṃdaṃ dūrāddṛṣṭiṃ prasārya ca \|*  
*svanetradairghyanirmāṇaṃ praśaśaṃsa phalānvitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. Then that group of Yoginīs extended their visions from afar and praised the length of their vision which had become fruitful.

## \|\| 1.45.2 \|\|

*divyaprāsādamālānāṃ patākāścalapallavāḥ \|*  
*sādaraṃ dūramārgasthānpāṃthānāhvayatīriva \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. They praised also the festoons and banners of the groups of divine places, the tips of which were fluttering as though they were inviting respectfully the wayfarers on the paths far away.

## \|\| 1.45.3 \|\|

*caṃcatprāsādamāṇikyairvijṛṃbhitamarīcibhiḥ \|*  
*sunīlamapi ca vyomavīkṣyamāṇaṃ sunirmalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. They also praised the blue sky that appeared to be bright due to the glittering rubies in the places with increased rays.

## \|\| 1.45.4 \|\|

*devatvaṃ māyayācchādya veṣaṃ kārpaṭikocitam \|*  
*vidhāya kāśīmaviśadyoginīcakramakramam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They concealed their divinity by means of their Māyā and assumed the guise befitting Karpaṭikās (an order of ascetics wearing red garments). Thus the group of Yoginīs entered Kāśī in an irregular order (not simultaneously in a group).

## \|\| 1.45.5 \|\|

*kāciccayoginī bhūtā kācijjātā tapasvinī \|*  
*kācidbabhūva sairaṃdhrī kācinmāsopavāsinī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. One of them adopted the form of a woman Yoginī or a Kāpālikā, another became a woman ascetic, one of them became a Sairandhrī (a female attendant) and another (assumed the form of) one fasting for a month.

## \|\| 1.45.6 \|\|

*mālākāravadhūḥ kācitkācinnāpitasuṃdarī \|*  
*sūtikarmavicārajñā 'parā bhaiṣajyakovidā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. One of them became wife of a gardener, another a beautiful maiden of a barber conversant with the activities connected with cases of delivery and another an adept in science of medicine.

## \|\| 1.45.7 \|\|

*vaiśyā ca kācidabhavatkrayavikrayacaṃcurā \|*  
*vyālagrāhiṇyabhūtkāciddāsīdhātrī ca kācana \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A certain Yoginī became a Vaiśya woman—very clever in buying and selling. One of them became a serpent-charmer and another a governess and another a slave girl.

## \|\| 1.45.8 \|\|

*ekā ca nṛtyakuśalā tvanyā gānaviśāradā \|*  
*aparā veṇuvādajñā parā vīṇādharābhavat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. One of them became a woman expert in dancing and another an adept in singing. Another became a flute player and still another a lute player.

## \|\| 1.45.9 \|\|

*mṛdaṃgavādanajñānyā kācittāla kalāvatī \|*  
*kācitkārmaṇatattvajñā kācinmauktikaguṃphikā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. One Yoginī became one conversant with playing on the Mṛdaṅga drum and a certain one an expert in the art of beating time. One of them was a specialist in the art of seduction and another a maker of pearl-necklaces.

## \|\| 1.45.10 \|\|

*gaṃdhabhāgavidhijñānyā kācidakṣakalālayā \|*  
*ālāpollāsakuśalā kāciccatvaracāriṇī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. One became expert in the art of apportioning scents; one was a specialist in the game of dice; another was an adept conversationalist and a certain one became a Catvāracāriṇī (a mendicant woman roaming in quadrangles).

## \|\| 1.45.11 \|\|

*vaṃśādhirohaṇe dakṣā rajjumārgeṇa cetarā \|*  
*kācidvātulaceṣṭā'bhūtpathi cīvaraveṣṭanā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One of them became a clever woman climbing a bamboo pole and another a rope-walker. One became a lunatic with curious pranks and another clothed herself with rags picked from the highway.

## \|\| 1.45.12 \|\|

*apatyadā'napatyānāṃ parā tatrapure'vasat \|*  
*kācitkarāṃghrirekhāṇāṃ lakṣaṇāni ciketi ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. One lived in that city as one capable of blessing the childless with children. Another was an expert in palmistry.

## \|\| 1.45.13 \|\|

*citralekhana naipuṇyātkācijjanamanoharā \|*  
*vaśīkaraṇamaṃtrajñā kācittatra cacāra ha \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A certain (Yoginī) captivated the minds of the common people through her skill in drawing pictures. A certain one roamed there proclaiming herself an expert in the spells of captivating persons.

## \|\| 1.45.14 \|\|

*guṭikāsiddhidā kācitkācidaṃjanasiddhidā \|*  
*dhātuvādavidagdhānyā pādukāsiddhidā parā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One of them was bestower of supernatural powers through Guṭikās (pills); one of them was able to bestow Añjana Siddhi (supernatural power through use of collyrium); another was an expert in Dhātuvāda (Alchemy) and another bestowed Pādukā Siddhi (transport to a desired place by touching the sandals).

## \|\| 1.45.15 \|\|

*agnistaṃbha jalastaṃbha vākstaṃbhaṃ cāpyaśikṣayat \|*  
*khecarītvaṃ dadau kācidadṛśyatvaṃ parā dadau \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. One of them taught the arts of Agnistaṃbha (‘arresting fire’), Jalastaṃbha (‘preventing the movement of water’) and Vākstaṃbha (‘arresting the power of speech’); one of them offered Khecaritva (‘the ability to walk in the sky’) and another one offered the power of being invisible.

## \|\| 1.45.16 \|\|

*kācidākarpaṇīṃ siddhiṃ dadāvuccāṭanaṃ parā \|*  
*kācinnijāṃgasauṃdarya yuvacittavimohinī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One of them offered the Ākarṣiṇī Siddhi (‘the power to drag to oneself woman or man desired); another offered Uccāṭana (upsetting and unsettling persons of stability); a certain one enamoured the minds of young men through the beauty of her limbs.

## \|\| 1.45.17-19 \|\|

*ciṃtitārthapradā kācitkācijjyotiḥ kalāvatī \|*  
*ityādi veṣabhāṣābhiranukṛtya samaṃtataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*pratyaṃgaṇaṃ pratigṛhaṃ prāviśadyoginīgaṇaḥ \|*  
*itthamabdaṃcaraṃtyastā yoginyo'harniśaṃ puri \|\| 18 \|\|*

*na cchidraṃ lebhire kvāpi nṛpavighnacikīrṣavaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sametya tāḥ sarvā yoginyo vaṃdhyavāṃchitāḥ \|*  
*tasthuḥ saṃmaṃtrya tatraiva na gatā maṃdaraṃ punaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. One of them could bestow anything thought of; one of them was an expert in astrology.

In such disguises and professions, the group of Yoginīs entered every house and every yard around. Thus they spent a year roaming about in the city day and night. They were desirous of creating obstacles unto the king, but could not find any inlet or loophole. Their desired missions were not fulfilled. All these Yoginīs gathered together and stayed there taking counsel together. They never went back to Mandara.

## \|\| 1.45.20 \|\|

*prabhukāryamaniṣpādya sadaḥ saṃbhāvanaidhitaḥ \|*  
*kaḥ puraḥ śaknuyātsthātuṃ svāmino kṣatavigrahaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “If one had been honoured in the open assembly (by being entrusted with a task) but could not carry out the task and if the one is not even wounded, can that one stand in front of the lord and master?”

## \|\| 1.45.21-23 \|\|

*anyacca ciṃtitaṃ tābhiryoginībhiridaṃ mune \|*  
*prabhuṃ vināpi jīvāmo na tu kāśīṃ vinā punaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*prabhūruṣṭopi sadbhṛtye jīvikāmātrahārakaḥ \|*  
*kāśīharetkarādbhraṣṭā puruṣārthacatuṣṭayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nādyāpi kāśīṃ saṃtyajya tadārabhya mahāmune \|*  
*yoginyonyatra tiṣṭhaṃti caraṃtyopi jagattrayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Further, the following steps were thought of by the Yoginīs, O sage. ‘We can very well live without the Lord but not without Kāśī. Even if the master is angry with the servant, he can only take away the means of livelihood. But, if Kāśī slips out from the grasp, it may take away all the four aims of life.’

O great sage, ever since then, till today the Yoginīs never left Kāśī and stayed elsewhere, though they wander through all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.45.24-28 \|\|

*prāpyāpi śrīmatīṃ kāśīṃ yastitikṣati durmatiḥ \|*  
*sa eva pratyuta tyakto dharmakāmārthamuktibhiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kaḥ kāśīṃ prāpya durbuddhiraparatra yiyāsati \|*  
*mokṣanikṣepa kalaśīṃ tucchaśrīkṛtamānasaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vimukhopīśvarosmākaṃ kāśīsevanapuṇyataḥ \|*  
*saṃmukho bhavitā puṇyaṃ kṛtakṛtyāḥ sma tadvayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*dinaiḥ katipayaireva sarvajñopi sameṣyati \|*  
*vinā kāśīṃ na ramate yato'nyatra trilocanaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śaṃbhoḥ śaktiriyaṃ kāśī kācitsarvairagocarā \|*  
*śaṃbhureva hi jānīyādetasyāḥ paramaṃ sukham \|\| 28 \|\|*

24-28. (The Yoginīs thought further:) ‘Even after coming to Kāśī, the glorious city, if any wretched-minded man were to think of leaving it, it is he who will be, on the other hand, abandoned by the four Puruṣārthas, viz. Dharma, Artha, Kāma and Mukti. After coming to Kāśī which man of wretched intellect desires to go elsewhere with his mind dwelling on insignificant glory? Kāśī is, as it were, the treasure-chest of salvation. Even if the master turns away his face from us (to express his displeasure), he will see us face to face (to express his pleasure) due to the merit of resorting to Kāśī.

The Lord will be our own merit personified. Hence we shall be contented that we have done our duty.

The Lord, omniscient Śiva, will be coming here in a few days, because the Three-eyed Lord does not feel happy elsewhere except at Kāśī.

This Kāśī is the Śakti (power) of Śaṃbhu. It is not perceptible to all. Śaṃbhu alone knows its greatest happiness.’

## \|\| 1.45.29 \|\|

*iti niścitya manasi śaṃbhorānaṃdakānane \|*  
*atiṣṭhadyoginīvṛṃdaṃ kayācinmāyayāvṛtam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Having concluded thus in their minds, the group of Yoginīs stayed back in the Ānandakānana of Śaṃbhu, enveloping themselves with an indescribable Māyā.

## \|\| 1.45.30-31 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ samākarṇya muniḥ punaḥ papraccha ṣaṇmukham \|*  
*kāni kāni ca nāmāni tāsāṃ tāni vadeśvara \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bhajanādyoginīnāṃ ca kāśyāṃ kiṃ jāyate phalam \|*  
*kasminparvaṇi tāḥ pūjyāḥ kathaṃ pūjyāśca tadvada \|\| 31 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

30-31. On hearing this, the sage asked the Six-faced Lord again: “O Lord, what are their names? Enumerate them. What benefit accrues by worshipping the Yoginīs at Kāśī? What is the holy occasion on which they are to be worshipped? How are they to be worshipped? Mention that.”

## \|\| 1.45.32 \|\|

*śrutvetipraśnamaumeyo yoginīsaṃśrayaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca mune vacmi śṛṇotvavahito bhavān \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On hearing these questions concerning the Yoginīs, the son of Umā replied: “O sage, I shall mention. May Your Holiness listen attentively.”

## \|\| 1.45.33 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*nāmadheyāni vakṣyāmi yoginīnāṃ ghaṭodbhava \|*  
*ākarṇya yāni pāpāni kṣayaṃti bhavināṃ kṣaṇāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

Skanda said:

33\. O Pot-born One, I shall mention the names of the Yoginīs, on hearing which all the sins of the persons of worldly existence perish instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.45.34-41 \|\|

*gajānanā siṃhamukhī gṛdhrāsyā kākatuṃḍikā \|*  
*uṣṭragrīvā hayagrīvā vārāhī śarabhānanā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ulūkikā śivārāvā mayūrī vikaṭānanā \|*  
*aṣṭavaktrā koṭarākṣī kubjā vikaṭalocanā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śuṣkodarī lalajjihvā śvadaṃṣṭrā vānarānanā \|*  
*ṛkṣākṣī kekarākṣī ca bṛhattuṃḍā surāpriyā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kapālahastā raktākṣī śukī śyenī kapotikā \|*  
*pāśahastā daṃḍahastā pracaṃḍā caṃḍavikramā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*śiśughnī pāpahaṃtrī ca kālī rudhirapāyinī \|*  
*vasādhayā garbhabhakṣā śavahastāṃtramālinī \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sthūlakeśī bṛhatkukṣiḥ sarpāsyā pretavāhanā \|*  
*daṃdaśūkakarā krauṃcī mṛgaśīrṣā vṛṣānanā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*vyāttāsyā dhūmaniḥśvāsā vyomaikacaraṇordhvadṛk \|*  
*tāpanī śoṣaṇīdṛṣṭiḥ koṭarī sthūlanāsikā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vidyutprabhā balākāsyā mārjārī kaṭapūtanā \|*  
*aṭṭāṭṭahāsā kāmākṣī mṛgākṣī mṛgalocanā \|\| 41 \|\|*

34-41. The sixty-four names of the Yoginīs\[2\]: (1) Gajānanā, (2) Siṃhamukhī, (3) Gṛdhrāsyā, (4) Kākatuṇḍikā, (5) Uṣṭragrīvā, (6) Hayagrīvā, (7) Vārāhī, (8) Śarabhānanā, (9) Ulūkikā, (10) Śivārāvā, (11) Mayūrī, (12) Vikaṭānanā, (13) Aṣṭavakrā, (14) Koṭarākṣī, (15) Kubjā, (16) Vikaṭalocanā, (17) Śuṣkodarī, (18) Lalajjihvā, (19) Śvadaṃṣṭrā, (20) Vānarānanā, (21) Ṛkṣākṣī, (22) Kekarākṣī, (23) Bṛhattuṇḍa, (24) Surāpriyā, (25) Kapālahastā, (26) Raktākṣī, (27) Śukī, (28) Śyenī, (29) Kapotikā, (30) Pāśahastā, (31) Daṇḍahastā, (32) Pracaṇḍā Caṇḍavikramā, (33) Śiśughnī, (34) Pāpahantrī, (35) Kālī, (36) Rudhirapāyinī, (37) Vasādhayā, (38) Garbhabhakṣā, (39) Śavahastā, (40) Āntramālinī, (41) Sthūlakeśī, (42) Bṛhatkukṣī, (43) Sarpāsyā, (44) Pretavāhanā, (45) Dandaśūkakarā, (46) Krauñcī, (47) Mṛgaśīrṣā, (48) Vṛṣānanā, (49) Vyāttāsyā, (50) Dhūmaniḥśvāsā, (51) Vyomaikacaraṇā, (52) Urdhvadṛk, (53) Tāpanīdṛṣṭi, (54) Śoṣanīdṛṣti, (55) Koṭarī, (56) Sthūlanāsikā, (57) Vidyutprabhā, (58) Balākāsyā, (59) Mārjārī, (60) Kaṭapūtanā, (61) Aṭṭāṭṭahāsā, (62) Kāmākṣī, (63) Mṛgākṣī, (64) Mṛgalocanā.

## \|\| 1.45.42 \|\|

*nāmānīmāni yo martyaścatuḥṣaṣṭiṃ dinedine \|*  
*japettrisaṃdhyaṃ tasyeha duṣṭabādhā praśāmyati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If any man repeats these sixty-four names everyday at dawn, midday and dusk, all his sufferings due to evil spirits become subsided.

## \|\| 1.45.43 \|\|

*na ḍākinyo na śākinyo na kūṣmāṃḍā na rākṣasāḥ \|*  
*tasya pīḍāṃ prakurvaṃti nāmānīmāni yaḥ paṭhet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Neither Ḍākinīs nor Śākinīs, neither Kūṣṃāṇḍas nor Rākṣasas afflict him who recites these names.

## \|\| 1.45.44 \|\|

*śiśūnāṃ śāṃtikārīṇi garbhaśāṃtikarāṇi ca \|*  
*raṇe rājakule vāpi vivāde jayadānyapi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. They give peace to infants and the unborn. They accord victory in battle, royal household and debates.

## \|\| 1.45.45 \|\|

*labhedabhīpsitāṃ siddhiṃ yoginīpīṭhasevakaḥ \|*  
*maṃtrāṃtarāṇyapi japaṃstatpīṭhe siddhibhāgbhavet \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He who serves Yoginī Pīṭhas (pedestals) shall obtain desired powers. One who repeats other Mantras in front of their pedestals shall also achieve powers.

## \|\| 1.45.46 \|\|

*balipūjopahāraiśca dhūpadīpasamarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*kṣipraṃ prasannā yoginyaḥ prayaccheyurmanorathān \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The Yoginīs become quickly pleased with oblations, adorations and offerings and dedications of incense and lamps and they shall fulfil all desires.

## \|\| 1.45.47 \|\|

*śaratkāle mahāpūjāṃ tatra kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*havīṃṣi hutvā maṃtrajño mahatīṃ siddhimāpnuyāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. In autumnal season a devotee conversant with Mantras, should perform a great Pūjā in accordance with the injunctions and make ghee offerings. He shall attain great benefit.

## \|\| 1.45.48 \|\|

*ārabhyāśvayujaḥśuklāṃ tithiṃ pratipadaṃ śubhām \|*  
*pūjayennavamīyāvannaraściṃtitamāpnuyāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In the month of Aśvayuj (October-November), beginning with the first lunar day of the bright half and ending with the ninth day, a man should worship (the Yoginīs). He shall obtain whatever is desired.

## \|\| 1.45.49 \|\|

*kṛṣṇapakṣasya bhūtāyāmupavāsī narottamaḥ \|*  
*tatra jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā mahatīṃ siddhimāpnuyāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The excellent man should observe fast on the fourteenth day in the dark half and keep awake during the night. He shall obtain great benefit.

## \|\| 1.45.50-51 \|\|

*praṇavādicaturthyantairnāmabhirbhaktimānnaraḥ \|*  
*pratyekaṃ havanaṃ kṛtvā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ niśi \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sasarpiṣā guggulunā laghukoli pramāṇataḥ \|*  
*yāṃ yāṃ siddhimabhīpseta tāṃtāṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. The devotee should repeat all the names affixing the Praṇava in the beginning and using them in the Dative case and perforin one hundred and eight Havanas for each name at night with Guggulu (aromatic gum resin) mixed with ghee, making each lump of the size of a small Badarī fruit. He shall obtain great benefit and whatever power he may desire, the man shall obtain it.

## \|\| 1.45.52-54 \|\|

*caitrakṛṣṇapratipadi tatra yātrā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*kṣetravighnaśāṃtyarthaṃ kartavyā puṇyakṛjjanaiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*yātrā ca sāṃvatsarikīṃ yo na kuryādavajñayā \|*  
*tasya vighnaṃ prayacchaṃti yoginyaḥ kāśivāsinaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*agre kṛtvā sthitāḥ sarvāstāḥ kāśyāṃ maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*tannamaskāramātreṇa naro vighnairna bādhyate \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. On the first day in the dark half of Caitra a Pilgrimage (Yātrā) should be performed assiduously for the purpose of quelling obstacles to the holy spot by meritorious persons. If anyone staying in Kāśī, out of contempt or indifference, does not perform the annual pilgrimage, the Yoginīs create obstacles unto him. Keeping all of them ahead at Kāśī in Maṇikarṇikā, a devout man should perform obeisance. Merely on account of this he can ward off all obstacles.

## Chapter 46 - Description of Lolārka

## \|\| 1.46.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*gatetha yoginīvṛṃde devadevo ghaṭodbhava \|*  
*kāśīpravṛttiṃ jijñāsuḥ prāhiṇodaṃśumālinam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: There are twelve Āditya (Sun-god) temples at Banaras. Lolarka \[Lolārka?\] is the most important and famous. It is located in the extreme south of Vārāṇasī, near the confluence of Asi and Gaṅgā. The two copper-plate grants of Gāhadwal kings (after their baths here) show its ancient importance (BCL 177).

Skanda said:

1\. After the group of Yoginīs had departed, O Pot-born One, the Lord of Devas who was desirous of knowing the situation in Kāśī sent the Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.46.2 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*saptāśva tvarito yāhi purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ śubhām \|*  
*yatrāsti sa divodāso dharmamūrtirmahīpatiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Lord of Devas said:

2\. O Seven-horsed One, go quickly to the splendid city of Vārāṇasī where Divodāsa, a Dharma incarnate, is the ruler.

## \|\| 1.46.3 \|\|

*tasya dharmavirodhena yathātatkṣetramudvaset \|*  
*tathā kuruṣva bho kṣipraṃ māvamaṃsthāśca taṃ nṛpam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Do something quickly so that the holy spot gets ruined due to the king’s transgression of the path of piety. But do not think lightly of that king.

## \|\| 1.46.4 \|\|

*dharmamārga pravṛttasya kriyate yāvamānanā \|*  
*sā bhavedātmano nūnaṃ mahadenaśca jāyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. If insult or disrespect is shown towards anyone treading the path of piety, that will surely recoil on oneself. Great sin too will befall.

## \|\| 1.46.5 \|\|

*tavabuddhivikāsena cyavate cetsa dharmataḥ \|*  
*tadā sā nagarī bhāno tvayodvāsyā'sahaiḥ karaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If due to your intellectual skill he swerves from the path of virtue, O Sun, you can devastate that city with your fierce rays.

## \|\| 1.46.6 \|\|

*kāmakrodhau lobhamohau matsarāhaṃkṛtī api \|*  
*te tatra na bhavetāṃ yattatkālopi na taṃ jayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The notorious bad qualities of lust and anger, greed and delusion, rivalry and arrogance have no place in him. Hence even the god of Death cannot conquer him.

## \|\| 1.46.7 \|\|

*yāvaddharme sthirābuddhiryāvaddharmesthiraṃ manaḥ \|*  
*tāvadvighnodayaḥ kvāsti vipadyapi rave nṛṣu \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. As long as the intellect is well-established in piety, as long as the mind is steadfast in piety, O Sun-god, whence can be the rise of obstacles in the case of men even in adversities?

## \|\| 1.46.8 \|\|

*sarveṣāmiha jaṃtūnāṃ tvaṃ vetsi bradhnaceṣṭitam \|*  
*ataeva jagaccakṣurvraja tvaṃ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Bradhna (Sun-god), you are aware of the activities of all creatures. Hence you are called Jagaccakṣuḥ (‘The eye of the universe’). Go, then for the accomplishment of the task.

## \|\| 1.46.9 \|\|

*ravirādāya devājñāṃ mūrtimanyāṃ prakalpya ca \|*  
*nabhodhvagāmahorātraṃ kāśīmabhimukho'bhavat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Sun took the order of the Lord, and assumed another form capable of going along the sky both day and night. He then proceeded towards Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.46.10 \|\|

*manasātīvalolo'bhūtkāśīdarśanalālasaḥ \|*  
*sahasracaraṇopyaicchattadā khe naikapādatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Sun was very much eager to see Kāśī. Though he had a thousand feet (rays), he still yearned for more feet (rays).

## \|\| 1.46.11 \|\|

*haṃsatvaṃ tasya sūryasya tadā saphalatāmagāt \|*  
*sadā nabhodhvanīnasya kāśīṃ prati yiyāsataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The state of being Haṃsa (‘one who goes continuously’) of the Sun became meaningful and fruitful because he was desirous of going towards Kāśī and so was proceeding along the sky continuously.

## \|\| 1.46.12 \|\|

*atha kāśīṃ samāsādya raviraṃtarbahiścaran \|*  
*manāgapi na tadbhūpe dharmadhvastimavekṣata \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After reaching Kāśī, the Sun moved within and without (Kāśī) but could not see even the least of an instance of deviation from piety in the case of the king.

## \|\| 1.46.13 \|\|

*vibhāvasurvasankāśyāṃ nānārūpeṇa vatsaram \|*  
*kvacinnāvasaraṃ prāpa tatra rājñi sudharmiṇi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Sun stayed in Kāśī for a year in various guises, but could not find any loophole in that righteous king.

## \|\| 1.46.14 \|\|

*kadācidatithirbhūto durlabhaṃ prārthayanraviḥ \|*  
*na tasya rājño viṣaye durlabhaṃ kiṃcidaikṣata \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The Sun sometimes became a guest seeking something very difficult to get; but he did not see anything rare to be got in the realm of that king.

## \|\| 1.46.15 \|\|

*kadācidyācako jāto bahudopi kadāpyabhūt \|*  
*kadāciddīnatāṃ prāptaḥ kadācidgaṇakopyabhūt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Sometimes he became a beggar; sometimes he became a bestower of many things. Sometimes he became one in a wretched state and sometimes he became an astrologer.

## \|\| 1.46.16 \|\|

*vedabāhyāṃ kriyāṃ cāpi kadācitpratyapādayat \|*  
*kadācitsthāpayāmāsa dṛṣṭapratyayamaihikam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Sometimes he performed rites beyond the pale of Vedas. Sometimes he established the philosophy of this-worldliness believing in only what is perceived.

## \|\| 1.46.17 \|\|

*kadācijjaṭilo jātaḥ kadācicca digaṃbaraḥ \|*  
*sa kadācijjāṃguliko viṣavidyāviśāradaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Sometimes he became one with matted hair. Sometimes he remained a nude mendicant. He sometimes became a snake-doctor, and expert in antidotes against poisons.

## \|\| 1.46.18 \|\|

*sarvapāṣaṃḍadharmajñaḥ kadācidbrahmavādyabhūt \|*  
*aiṃdrajālika āsīcca kadācidbhrāmayañjanān \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Sometimes he became one well-versed in all heretical doctrines; sometimes an expounder of Brahma (Absolute). He became a juggler sometimes making people perplexed by creating illusions.

## \|\| 1.46.19 \|\|

*nānāvratopadeśaiśca kadācitsa pativratāḥ \|*  
*kṣobhayāmāsa bahuśaḥ sadṛṣṭāṃta kathānakaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Sometimes he made chaste ladies much agitated through instructions in different kinds of vows and observances with many narratives as illustration.

## \|\| 1.46.20 \|\|

*kāpālika vratadharaḥ kadāciccābhavaddvijaḥ \|*  
*kadācidapi vijñānī dhātuvādī kadācana \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Sometimes he became a Brāhmaṇa engaged in the vow of a Kāpālika; sometimes a Vijñānin (follower of Buddhist Vijñānavāda; sometimes a Dhātuvādin, alchemist—MW Com.)

## \|\| 1.46.21 \|\|

*kvacidvipraḥ kvacidrājaputro vaiśyoṃtyajaḥ kvacita \|*  
*brahmacārī kvacidabhūdgṛhī vanacaraḥ kvacit \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. At some places he became a Brāhmaṇa; somewhere a royal prince, a Vaiśya or a Śūdra; somewhere he became a religious student observing celibacy; somewhere a householder and somewhere a forest-dweller.

## \|\| 1.46.22 \|\|

*yatiḥ kadāciditi sarūpairabhrāmayajjanān \|*  
*sarvavidyāsu kuśalaḥ sarvajñaścābhavatkvacit \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Sometimes he became a recluse. Thus he tried to make the people confused. In some places, he became (posed to be) omniscient, an expert in all lores.

## \|\| 1.46.23 \|\|

*iti nānāvidhai rūpaiścarankāśyāṃ graheśvaraḥ \|*  
*na kadāpi jane kvāpi cchidraṃ prāpa kadācana \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thus the Lord of Planets wandered in Kāśī in different forms. But, nowhere did he find at any time any vulnerable point in the people.

## \|\| 1.46.24 \|\|

*tato niniṃda cātmānaṃ ciṃtārtaḥ kaśyapātmajaḥ \|*  
*dhikparapreṣyatāṃ yasyāṃ yaśo labhyeta na kvacit \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The son of Kaśyapa (i.e. Sun-god) became very worried with thoughts and censured himself. “Fie upon being one who runs an errand for others, wherein no fame is obtained.”

## \|\| 1.46.25 \|\|

*mārtaṃḍa uvāca \|*  
*maṃdaraṃ yadi yāmyadya sadyastatkruddhyatīśvaraḥ \|*  
*aniṣpāditakāryārthe mayi sāmānyabhṛtyavat \|\| 25 \|\|*

Mārtaṇḍa said:

25\. If I want to go back to Mandara now, the Lord will get angry immediately with me, because I have not fulfilled the task. He will become angry as though I am an ordinary servant.

## \|\| 1.46.26 \|\|

*kopamapyurarīkṛtya yadi yāyāṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*kathaṃ tiṣṭhe purastasya tarhi vai mūḍhabhṛtyavat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. If somehow I go there, how shall I stand in front of him like a foolish servant?

## \|\| 1.46.27 \|\|

*athoṃkṛtyāvahelaṃ vā yāmi cecca kathaṃcana \|*  
*krodhānnirīkṣettryakṣo māṃ viṣaṃ peyaṃ tadā mayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If I somehow go there accepting (pocketing) the insult, the Three-eyed Lord may stare at me angrily. Poison should be drunk by me then.

## \|\| 1.46.28 \|\|

*harakopānale nūnaṃ yadi yātaḥ pataṃgatām \|*  
*pitāmahopi māṃ trātuṃ tadā śakṣyati nasphuṭam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If I became a victim to the fire of wrath of Lord Hara like a moth, even the Grandfather (Brahmā) will not be able to save me.

## \|\| 1.46.29 \|\|

*sthāsyāmyatraiva tannityaṃ na tyakṣyāmi kadācana \|*  
*kṣetrasaṃnyāsavidhinā vārāṇasyāṃ kṛtāśramaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Hence I shall stay here forever. I will never leave this. I shall establish my hermitage in Vārāṇasī in accordance with the injunctions regarding (permanent stay) in a holy spot.

## \|\| 1.46.30 \|\|

*puraḥ purāreḥ kāyārthamanivedyeha tiṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*yatpāpaṃ bhāvi me tasya kāśīpāpasyaniṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. If I stay back here without intimating the non-fulfilment of the task to Purāri (Śiva), I may incur sin; but Kāśī itself shall be the means of redemption from that sin.

## \|\| 1.46.31 \|\|

*anyānyapi ca pāpāni mahāṃtyalpāni yāni ca \|*  
*kṣayaṃti tāni sarvāṇi kāśīṃ praviśatāṃ satām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Other sins too, whether great or small, of the good people who have entered Kāśī, become reduced entirely.

## \|\| 1.46.32 \|\|

*buddhipūrvaṃ mayā caitanna pāpaṃ samupārjitam \|*  
*purāriṇaiva hi purā'śāsi dharmo hi rakṣyatām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. This sin has not been incurred by me knowingly. At the outset, it was ordained by Purāri himself: “May Dharma be protected.”

## \|\| 1.46.33 \|\|

*dharmo hi rakṣito yena dehe satvaragatvare \|*  
*trailokyarakṣitaṃ tena kiṃ kāmārthaiḥ surakṣitaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. While the body is of quickly vanishing nature, if Dharma is protected by anyone, it is as though the three worlds have been protected by him. Of what avail are love and wealth, even if protected well.

## \|\| 1.46.34 \|\|

*rakṣaṇīyo yadi bhavetkāmaḥ kāmāriṇā katham \|*  
*kṣaṇādanaṃgatāṃ nīto bahūnāṃ sukhakāryapi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If Kāma (love) is to be protected, why then was he made Anaṅga (bodiless), though he had been the bestower of happiness on many?

## \|\| 1.46.35 \|\|

*arthaścetsarvathārakṣya iti kaiścidudāhṛtam \|*  
*tatkathaṃ na hariścaṃdro'rakṣatkuśikanaṃdane \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. If it has been asserted by many that Artha (Wealth) should be always protected, then how did Hariścandra not protect it in the case of Viśvāmitra?

## \|\| 1.46.36 \|\|

*dharmastu rakṣitaḥ sarvairapidehavyayena ca \|*  
*śibiprabhṛtibhūpālairdadhīcipramukhairdvijaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Dharma has been safeguarded by all, even at the cost of the body by Śibi and other kings as well as by Dadhīci and other Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.46.37 \|\|

*ayameva hi vai dharmaḥ kāśīsevanasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*ruṣitādapi rudrānmāṃ rakṣiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. This Dharma itself arising from rendering service to Kāśī will certainly protect me even from the infuriated Rudra.

## \|\| 1.46.38 \|\|

*avāpya kāśīṃ duṣprāpāṃ ko jahāti sacetanaḥ \|*  
*ratnaṃ karasthamutsṛjya kaḥ kācaṃ saṃjighṛkṣati \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After attaining Kāśī very difficult to be attained, which sensible being forsakes it? Who will desire to collect worthless pieces of glass after giving up a jewel in one’s hand.

## \|\| 1.46.39 \|\|

*vārāṇasīṃ samutsṛjya yastvanyatra yiyāsati \|*  
*hatvā nidhānaṃ pādena sorthamicchati bhikṣayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He who desires to go elsewhere leaving Kāśī, kicks off a treasure with his foot and wishes to get wealth through begging for alms.

## \|\| 1.46.40 \|\|

*putramitrakalatrāṇi kṣetrāṇi ca dhanāni ca \|*  
*pratijanmeha labhyaṃte kāśyekā naiva labhyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Sons, friends, wives, fields and riches are obtained in every birth but Kāśī alone is not attained.

## \|\| 1.46.41 \|\|

*yena labdhā purī kāśī trailokyoddharaṇakṣamā \|*  
*trailokyaiśvaryaduṣprāpaṃ tena labdhaṃ mahāsukham \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A great happiness that is very difficult to achieve even with the riches of all the three worlds has been acquired by that man by whom the city of Kāśī capable of redeeming the three worlds, has been attained.

## \|\| 1.46.42 \|\|

*kupitopi hi me rudrastejohāniṃ vidhāsyati \|*  
*kāśyāṃ ca lapsye tattejo yadvai svātmāvabodhajam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Indeed the angry Rudra may cause some reduction in my splendour. But in Kāśī, I will achieve that splendour arising from the realization of the self.

## \|\| 1.46.43 \|\|

*itarāṇīha tejāṃsi bhāsaṃte tāvadeva hi \|*  
*khadyotābhāni yāvanno jṛṃbhate kāśijaṃ mahaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Other luminaries shine with a modicum of light of a glowworm only as long as the splendour arising from Kāśī does not flourish.

## \|\| 1.46.44 \|\|

*iti kāśīprabhāvajño jagaccakṣustamonudaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā dvādaśadhātmānaṃ kāśīpuryāṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus the dispeller of darkness, the eye of the universe, conversant with the power of Kāśī divided himself into twelve and established himself in the city of Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.46.45-47 \|\|

*lolārka uttarārkaśca sāṃbādityastathaiva ca \|*  
*caturtho drupadādityo mayūkhāditya eva ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

*khakholkaścāruṇādityo vṛddhakeśavasaṃjñakau \|*  
*daśamo vimalādityo gaṃgādityastathaiva ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

*dvādaśaśca yamādityaḥ kāśipuryāṃ ghaṭodbhava \|*  
*tamo'dhikebhyo duṣṭebhyaḥ kṣetraṃ rakṣaṃtyamī sadā \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. O Pot-born One, the following are the twelve Ādityas (Suns): (1) Lolārka, (2) Uttarārka, (3) Sāṃbāditya, (4) Drupadāditya, the fourth, (5) Mayūkhāditya, (6) Khakholka, (7) Aruṇāditya, (8) Vṛddhāditya, (9) Keśavāditya, (10) Vimalāditya, (11) Gaṅgāditya, and (12) Yamāditya, the twelfth one, in the city of Kāśī. They always protect the holy spot from evil ones with dominant Tāmasa quality.

## \|\| 1.46.48 \|\|

*tasyārkasya manololaṃ yadāsītkāśidarśane \|*  
*ato lolārka ityākhyā kāśyāṃ jātā vivasvataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Since the mind of the Sun became very eager (Lola) to see Kāśī, the Sun in Kāśī acquired the name Lolārka.

## \|\| 1.46.49 \|\|

*lolārkastvasisaṃbhede dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśisthitaḥ \|*  
*yogakṣemaṃ sadā kuryātkāśīvāsi janasya ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Lolārka is established in the southern direction (of Kāśī) at the confluence of Asi (with Gaṅgā). He shall always make the inhabitants of Kāśī achieve and preserve the good.

## \|\| 1.46.50 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣasya saptamyāṃ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vā ravivāsare \|*  
*vidhāya vārṣikīṃ yātrāṃ naraḥ pāpai pramucyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. By performing the annual pilgrimage on the seventh lunar day in Mārgaśīrṣa or on the sixth day falling on a Sunday, a man is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.46.51 \|\|

*kṛtāni yāni pāpāni naraiḥ saṃvatsarāvadhi \|*  
*naśyaṃti kṣaṇatastāni ṣaṣṭhyarke loladarśanāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Whatever sins have been committed by men during the year, are destroyed the very moment. One sees Lolārka on the sixth lunar day falling on Sunday.

## \|\| 1.46.52 \|\|

*naraḥ snātvāsisaṃbhede saṃtarpya pitṛdevatāḥ \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ vidhāya vidhinā pitrānṛṇyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. By taking the holy bath at the confluence of Asi (and Gaṅgā), by propitiating the Pitṛs and the deities and by duly performing Śrāddha, one gets free from the indebtedness to the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.46.53 \|\|

*lolārkasaṃgame snātvā dānaṃ homaṃ surārcanam \|*  
*yatkiṃcitkriyate karma tadānaṃtyāya kalpate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Whatever sacred rite is performed, like Dāna, Homa and Arcanā of the deities, at the confluence (of Asi and Gaṅgā) known as ‘Lolārka-Saṅgama’ is capable of according never-ending benefit.

## \|\| 1.46.54 \|\|

*sūryoparāge lolārke snānadānādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*kurukṣetrāddaśaguṇā bhavaṃtīha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The rites of holy ablution, Dāna etc. at Lolārka at the time of a solar eclipse shall undoubtedly be ten times more efficacious than that at Kurukṣetra.

## \|\| 1.46.55 \|\|

*lolārke rathasaptamyāṃ snātvā gaṃgāsisaṃgame \|*  
*saptajanmakṛtaiḥ pāpairmukto bhavati tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On the Rathasaptamī day (i.e. seventh day in the bright half of Māgha) a devotee should take his holy dip at the confluence of Gaṅgā and Asi. Immediately he becomes free from the sins incurred in the course of seven births.

## \|\| 1.46.56 \|\|

*pratyarkavāraṃ lolārkaṃ yaḥ paśyati śucivrataḥ \|*  
*na tasya duḥkhaṃ lokesminkadācitsaṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If anyone pays a visit to Lolārka on every Sunday, observing the vows of cleanliness, he will never have any misery in this world

## \|\| 1.46.57 \|\|

*na tasya duḥkhaṃ no pāmā na dadrurna vicarcikā \|*  
*lolārkamarke yaḥ paśyettatpādodakasevakaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He who visits Lolārka on Sundays or imbibes the water washing the god’s feet, will never have any misery, nor such skin-diseases as Pāma, Dadru or Vicarcikā (itches, scabs etc.).

## \|\| 1.46.58 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāmuṣitvāpi yo lolārkaṃ na sevate \|*  
*sevaṃte taṃ naraṃ nūnaṃ kleśāḥ kṣudvyādhisaṃbhavāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. If anyone even after staying in Vārāṇasī does not serve Lolārka, pains and miseries arising from hunger and sickness will certainly afflict him.

## \|\| 1.46.59 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ kāśitīrthānāṃ lolārkaḥ prathamaṃ śiraḥ \|*  
*tatoṃ'gānyanyatīrthāni tajjalaplāvitānihi \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Lolārka is the first and foremost of all holy Tīrthas in Kāśī. Other Tīrthas are only subsidiaries. They are watered by its holy waters.

## \|\| 1.46.60 \|\|

*tīrthāṃtarāṇi sarvāṇi bhūmīvalayagānyapi \|*  
*asisaṃbhedatīrthasya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. All the other Tīrthas existing in the entire range of the earth do not deserve even a fraction of one-sixteenth of the holy Tīrtha, of the confluence of Asi (and Gaṅgā).

## \|\| 1.46.61 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva tīrthānāṃ snānādyallabhyate phalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samyagāpyeta narairgaṃgāsisaṃgame \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. From the holy ablution, at the confluence of Asi and Gaṅgā one gets the entire benefit that is acquired by the holy ablution in all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.46.62 \|\|

*nārthavādoyamuditaḥ stutivādo na vai mune \|*  
*satyaṃ yathārthavādoyaṃ śraddheyaḥ sadbhirādarāt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O sage, this is not a mere eulogical utterance, nor is it flattery. This is truly a statement of facts. It should be respectfully believed by all good people.

## \|\| 1.46.63 \|\|

*yatra viśveśvaraḥ sākṣādyatra svargataraṃgiṇī \|*  
*mithyā tatrānumanyaṃte tārkikāścānusūyakāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Where Viśveśvara is directly present, where there is the celestial river, there only sophists and jealous ones regard it as untrue.

## \|\| 1.46.64 \|\|

*udāharaṃti ye mūḍhāḥ kutarkabaladarpitāḥ \|*  
*kāśyāṃ sarverthavādoyaṃ te viṭkīṭā yugeyuge \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. All those foolish ones, arrogant of their power, who indulge in sophistical reasoning and say that this is a mere eulogical utterance, become worms in faeces in every Yuga.

## \|\| 1.46.65 \|\|

*kasyacitkāśitīrthasya mahimno mahatastulām \|*  
*nādhirohenmune nūnamapi trailokyamaṃḍapaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O sage, indeed even all the three worlds will never be on a par with the greatness of anyone of the holy Tīrthas in Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.46.66 \|\|

*nāstikā vedabāhyāśca śiśnodaraparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*aṃtyajātāśca ye teṣāṃ puraḥ kāśī na varṇyatām \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Kāśī should not be extolled before these atheists, those who are outside the ken of the Vedas, those who value the penis and the belly and the low-born ones.

## \|\| 1.46.67 \|\|

*lolārkakaraniṣṭaptā asidhāra vikhaṃḍitāḥ \|*  
*kāśyāṃ dakṣiṇadigbhāge na viśeyurmahāmalāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Being scorched by the rays of Lolārka and being cut (obstructed) by the current of the river Asi, persons of great sins cannot enter Kāśī.

Being heated by the hands of brave persons brilliant like Lolārka and cut down by the edge of their swords, Kāśī-haters, the great sinners, cannot enter Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.46.68 \|\|

*mahimānamimaṃ śrutvā lolārkasya narottamaḥ \|*  
*na duḥkhī jāyate kvāpi saṃsāre duḥkhasāgare \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. On hearing the greatness of Lolārka, an excellent man never experiences misery in the ocean of sorrow in the worldly existence.

## Chapter 47 - Description of Uttarārka

## \|\| 1.47.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*athottarasyāmāśāyāṃ kuṃḍamarkākhyamuttamam \|*  
*tatra nāmnottarārkeṇa raśmimālī vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The site of Uttarārka is near Bakaria Kuṇḍa (‘Uttarārka Kuṇḍa’ in the Text), just south of today’s Grand Trunk Road. The original temple was destroyed by Muslims and its ruins were transformed into Muslim structures. M.A. Sherring discovered here a Sun disc with relief carvings of the Sun, thus confirming the site of this Sun-god. (BCL 179)

Skanda said:

1\. There is an excellent Kuṇḍa (holy pool) in the northern side, named Ārka. The Sun established himself there with the name of Uttarārka.

## \|\| 1.47.2 \|\|

*tāpayanduḥkhasaṃghātaṃ sādhūnāpyāyayanraviḥ \|*  
*uttarārko mahātejāḥ kāśīṃ rakṣati sarvadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Scorching (dispelling) the cluster of miseries and making good people flourish, Uttarārka, the Sun of great splendour, ever protects Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.47.3 \|\|

*tatretihāso yo vṛttastaṃ niśāmaya suvrata \|*  
*vipraḥ priyavrato nāma kaścidātreya vaṃśajaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O holy sage of excellent vows, please listen to the historical event that happened there. There was a certain Brāhmaṇa named Priyavrata born of the family of Atri.

## \|\| 1.47.4 \|\|

*āsītkāśyāṃ śubhācāraḥ sadātithijanapriyaḥ \|*  
*bhāryā śubhavratā tasya babhūvātimanoharā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He was in Kāśī, ever devoted to guests and doing only what is splendid. His wife named Śubhavratā was extremely charming.

## \|\| 1.47.5 \|\|

*bhartṛśuśrūṣaṇaratā gṛhakarmasupeśalā \|*  
*tasyāṃ sa janayāmāsa kanyāmekāṃ sulakṣaṇām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. She was ever engaged in serving her husband. She was skilful in domestic works. He begot of her a daughter of excellent features.

## \|\| 1.47.6 \|\|

*mūlarkṣaprathamepāde tathā keṃdre bṛhaspatau \|*  
*vavṛdhe sā gṛhe pitroḥ śukle pakṣe yathā śaśī \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. She was born in the first quarter of the constellation Mūla while Bṛhaspati (Jupiter) was in the Kendra (fourth, seventh or tenth zodiacal position from the Lagna). Like the Moon in the bright half, she grew up day by day.

## \|\| 1.47.7 \|\|

*surūpā vinayācārā pitrośca priyakāriṇī \|*  
*atīva nipuṇā jātā gṛhopaskaramārjane \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. She was beautiful in form. Her behaviour was modest. She delighted her parents by doing what was pleasing to them. She was very clever in keeping household articles and utensils clean.

## \|\| 1.47.8 \|\|

*yathāyathā samaidhiṣṭa sā kanyā pitṛmaṃdire \|*  
*tathātathā pitustasyāściṃtā saṃvavṛdhetarām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. As the girl was growing up in the parental abode, the worry of her father too increased day by day.

## \|\| 1.47.9-10 \|\|

*kasmai deyā varā kanyā suramyeyaṃ sulakṣaṇā \|*  
*asyā anuguṇo labhyaḥ kva mayā vara uttamaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kulena vayasā cāpi śīlenāpi śrutena ca \|*  
*rūpeṇārthenasaṃyuktaḥ kasmai dattā sukhaṃ labhet \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. He began to think thus: ‘To whom is this beautiful girl of excellent features to be given? Where is that excellent bridegroom befitting her to be obtained by me? He should be endowed with nobility of faith, youth, good habits, learning, comely features and adequate wealth. To whom should she be given so that she may be happy?’

## \|\| 1.47.11 \|\|

*iti ciṃtayatastasya jvarobhūdatidāruṇaḥ \|*  
*yaściṃtākhyo jvaraḥ puṃsāmauṣadhairnāpi śāmyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. As he worried thus his fever became excessively terrible. The fever named worry in the case of men does not subside through medicines.

## \|\| 1.47.12 \|\|

*tanmūlarkṣavipākena ciṃtākhyena jvareṇa ca \|*  
*sa vipraḥ paṃcatāṃ prāptastyaktvā sarvaṃ gṛhādikam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12 As a result of that constellation Mūla and that of the fever called worry, the Brāhmaṇa met with his death forsaking everything such as the house etc.

## \|\| 1.47.13 \|\|

*pitaryuparate tasyāḥ kanyāyāḥ sā jananyapi \|*  
*śubhavratā parityajya tāṃ kanyāṃ patimanvagāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When the father of the girl died, the mother too named Śubhavratā followed her husband leaving behind her virgin daughter.

## \|\| 1.47.14 \|\|

*dharmoyaṃ sahacāriṇyā jīvatājīvatāpi vā \|*  
*patyā sahaiva sthātavyaṃ pativratayujā sadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This is the eternal duty of a chaste wife who is expected to follow righteous conduct, that she should remain with her husband living or not living.

## \|\| 1.47.15 \|\|

*nāpatyaṃ pāti no mātā na pitā naiva bāṃdhavāḥ \|*  
*patyuścaraṇaśuśrūṣā pāyādvai kevalaṃ striyam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Neither the progeny nor her own mother nor father nor other kinsmen accord protection to a woman. It is the service alone rendered to the feet of her husband that protects a woman.

## \|\| 1.47.16-21 \|\|

*sulakṣaṇāpi duḥkhārtā pitroḥ paṃcatvamāptayoḥ \|*  
*aurdhvadaihikamāpādya daśāhaṃ vinivartya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ciṃtāmavāpa mahatīmanāthā dainyamāgatā \|*  
*kathamekākinī pitrā mātrāhīnā bhavāṃbudheḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dustaraṃ pāramāpsyāmi strītvaṃ sarvābhibhāvi yat \|*  
*na kasmaicidvarāyāhaṃ pitṛbhyāṃ pratipāditā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tadadattā kathaṃ svairamahamanyaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe \|*  
*vṛtopi na kulīnaścedguṇavānna ca śīlavān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*svādhīnopi na tattena vṛtenāpi hi kiṃ bhavet \|*  
*iti saṃciṃtayaṃtī sā rūpaudāryaguṇānvitā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yuvabhirbahubhirnityaṃ prārthitāpi muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*na kasyāpi dadau bālā praveśaṃ nija mānase \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. The girl though endowed with excellent features became highly miserable, when her parents died. All the funeral rites were completed and the tenth day ceremonies too were concluded. Bereft of a gurdian \[guardian?\] and meeting with wretchedness, she became extremely worried: ‘I am alone without my father and mother. How can I cross the ocean of worldly existence that is excessively difficult to cross? Womanhood comes into clash with everything. I have not been given over to anyone by my parents. Having not been handed over by them, how can I woo another bridegroom? What if he is neither meritorious nor of good habits, despite being wooed by me? Though he may be independent, what will happen when he is wooed?’ That girl richly endowed with the qualities of beauty, munificence etc., was pressingly approached frequently by many young men. Yet the girl did not give to anyone free access to her mind.

## \|\| 1.47.22 \|\|

*pitroruparatiṃ dṛṣṭvā vātsalyaṃ ca tathāvidham \|*  
*niniṃda bahudhātmānaṃ saṃsāraṃ ca niniṃda ha \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. She had witnessed the death of her parents. Remembering their excessive fondness, she cursed her own self and cursed the entire world.

## \|\| 1.47.23-25 \|\|

*yābhyāmutpāditā cāhaṃ yābhyāṃ ca paripālitā \|*  
*pitarau kutra tau yātau dehino dhiganityatām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*aho dehopyahoṃgatvaṃ yathā pitroḥ puro mama \|*  
*iti niścitya sā bālā vijiteṃdriya mānasā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*brahmacaryaṃ dṛḍhaṃ kṛtvā tapa ugraṃ cacāra ha \|*  
*uttarārkasya devasya samīpe sthiramānasā \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-24a. “Where have my parents gone, the parents who gave birth to me and protected me? Fie upon the transience of the embodied ones! Alas! Even my body is only a part of my parents. Just as my parents have gone, this too may go away.”

24b-25. On deciding thus that girl performed a very severe penance sustaining steadfast celibacy in close vicinity of Lord Uttarārka. She conquered the sense-organs and the mind and stabilised the mind.

## \|\| 1.47.26 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tapasyamānāyāmekācchāgī laghīyasī \|*  
*tatra pratyahamāgatya tiṣṭhettatpurato'calā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. While she was performing penance, a very tiny kid used to come there everyday and stand still in front of her.

## \|\| 1.47.27 \|\|

*tṛṇaparṇādikaṃ kiṃcitsāyamabhyavahṛtya sā \|*  
*tatkuṃḍapītapānīyā svasvāmisadanaṃ vrajet \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In the evening it used to eat some grass or leaves and drink the water from that pool. Then it used to go back to the abode of its master.

## \|\| 1.47.28 \|\|

*tata itthaṃ vyatītāsu paṃcaṣā susamāsu ca \|*  
*līlayā vicarandevastatra devyā sahāgataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thus five or six years passed off. Once the Lord, sportingly wandering about, along with the Goddess came there.

## \|\| 1.47.29 \|\|

*sannidhāvuttarārkasya tapasyatīṃ sulakṣaṇām \|*  
*sthāṇuvanniścalāṃ sthāṇuradrākṣīttapasā kṛśām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Sthāṇu saw Sulakṣaṇā performing penance near Uttarārka, steady like a pillar and grown emaciated due to the penance.

## \|\| 1.47.30 \|\|

*tato girijayā śaṃbhurvijñaptaḥ karuṇātmanā \|*  
*vareṇānugṛhāṇemāṃ baṃdhuhīnāṃ sumadhyamām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereupon Lord Śaṃbhu was requested by the Daughter of the Mountain moved with pity, “Kindly bless this beautiful girl devoid of kinsmen by bestowing on her a boon.”

## \|\| 1.47.31 \|\|

*śarvāṇīgiramākarṇya tataḥ śarvaḥ kṛpānidhiḥ \|*  
*samādhimīlitākṣīṃ tāmuvāca varado haraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On hearing the words of Śarvāṇī, Śarva, the storehouse of mercy, Hara, the bestower of boons, spoke to her, as she remained in her state of meditation with closed eyes.

## \|\| 1.47.32 \|\|

*sulakṣaṇe prasannosmi varaṃ varaya suvrate \|*  
*ciraṃ khinnāsi tapasā kaste'stīha manorathaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “O Sulakṣaṇā! I am pleased. O girl of excellent vows, choose your boon. You are fatigued due to the penance of long duration. What is your desire?”

## \|\| 1.47.33 \|\|

*sāpi śaṃbhorgiraṃ śrutvā mukhapīyūṣavarṣiṇīm \|*  
*mahāsaṃtāpaśamanīṃ locane udamīlayat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On hearing the words of Śaṃbhu shedding nectar from the mouth that suppressed excessive distress, she opened her eyes.

## \|\| 1.47.34 \|\|

*tryakṣaṃ pratyakṣamāvīkṣya varadānonmukhaṃ puraḥ \|*  
*devīṃ ca vāmabhāgasthāṃ praṇanāma kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On directly perceiving in front of her the Three-eyed Lord eager to bestow boons and the Goddess stationed to his left side, she joined her palms in reverence and bowed down.

## \|\| 1.47.35 \|\|

*kiṃ vṛṇe yāvaditthaṃ sā ciṃtayeccārumadhyamā \|*  
*tāvattayāniraikṣiṣṭa varākī barkarī puraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even as that girl of charming waist thought thus, ‘What shall I choose?’ the tiny goat kid was seen in front by her.

## \|\| 1.47.36-37 \|\|

*ātmārthaṃ jīvalokesminko na jīvati mānavaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ paropakārārthaṃ yo jīvati sa jīvati \|\| 36 \|\|*

*anayā mattapovṛtti sākṣiṇyā bahvanehasam \|*  
*asevyahaṃ tadetasyai varayāmi jagatpatim \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. ‘Which man does not live in this world of creatures for his own sake? But he who lives for the sake of rendering help to others, lives really. For many years I have been attended to by this (kid) who is a witness of my penance and holy rites. Hence I shall request the Lord of the universe for some boon on its behalf.’

## \|\| 1.47.38-39 \|\|

*parāmṛśya manasyetatprāha tryakṣaṃ sulakṣaṇā \|*  
*kṛpānidhe mahādeva yadi deyo varo mama \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ajaśāvī varākyeṣā tarhi prāganugṛhyatām \|*  
*vaktuṃ paśutvānnovetti kiṃcinmadbhaktipeśalā \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. After considering this in her mind Sulakṣaṇā said to the Three-eyed Lord: “O Mahādeva, O storehouse of mercy, if a boon is to be given to me, then at the outset may this poor insignificant kid of a goat be blessed. She has the same lovely devotion to me but does not know how to speak it out, being an animal itself.”

## \|\| 1.47.40 \|\|

*iti vācaṃ niśamyeśaḥ paropakṛtiśālinīm \|*  
*sulakṣaṇāyā nitarāṃ tutoṣa praṇatārtihā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On hearing these words of Sulakṣaṇā, showing (eagerness for) helping others, Īśa, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow down to him, became all the more pleased.

## \|\| 1.47.41 \|\|

*devadavastataḥ prāha devi paśya girīṃdraje \|*  
*sādhūnāmīdṛśī buddhiḥ paropakaraṇorjitā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then the Lord of the Devas said: “O Goddess, O Daughter of the Lord of mountains, see this. The intellect of good persons is of this nature—it is all the more powerful with (the readiness of) helping others.

## \|\| 1.47.42 \|\|

*te dhanyāḥ sarvalokeṣu sarvadharmāśrayāśca te \|*  
*yataṃte sarvabhāvena paropakaraṇāya ye \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Those who endeavour for helping others in all earnestness are the blessed ones, in all the worlds. They are the supports of all kinds of piety.

## \|\| 1.47.43 \|\|

*saṃcayāḥ sarvavastūnāṃ ciraṃ tiṣṭhati no kvacit \|*  
*suciraṃ tiṣṭhate caikaṃ paropakaraṇaṃ priye \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The gathering together of all the worldly objects does not last long. O my beloved, ony one thing—rendering help to others, lasts for a long time.

## \|\| 1.47.44 \|\|

*dhanyā sulakṣaṇā caiṣā yogyā'nugrahakarmaṇi \|*  
*brūhi devi varo deyaḥ ko'syaicchāgyai ca kaḥ priye \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. This Sulakṣaṇā is blessed and capable of obliging others. O my beloved Goddess, tell me, what boon should be given to her? What should be given to this kid?”

## \|\| 1.47.45 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*sarvasṛṣṭikṛtāṃ kartaḥ sarvajñapraṇatārtihan \|*  
*sulakṣaṇā śubhācārā sakhī mestu śubhodyamā \|\| 45 \|\|*

The Goddess said:

45\. O Creator of all creators! O omniscient one! O destroyer of the distress of those who bow down to you! May this Sulakṣaṇā of excellent conduct and splendid effort be my companion.

## \|\| 1.47.46-52 \|\|

*yathā jayā ca vijayā yathā caiva jayaṃtikā \|*  
*śubhānaṃdā sunaṃdā ca kaumudī ca yathormilā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*yathā caṃpakamālā ca yathā malayavāsinī \|*  
*karpūralatikā yadvadgaṃdhadhārā yathā śubhā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*aśokā ca viśokā ca yathā malayagaṃdhinī \|*  
*yathā caṃdananiḥśvāsā yathā mṛgamadottamā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yathā ca kokilālāpā yathā madhurabhāṣiṇī \|*  
*gadyapadyanidhiryadvadanuktajñā yathā ca sā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*dṛgaṃcaleṃgitajñā ca yathā kṛtamanorathā \|*  
*gānacittaharā yadvattathāstveṣā sulakṣaṇā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*atipriyā bhavitrī me yadbāla brahmacāriṇī \|*  
*anenaiva śarīreṇa divyāvayavabhūṣaṇā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*divyāṃbarā divyagaṃdhā divyajñānasamanvitā \|*  
*samayā māṃ sadaivāstāṃ caṃcaccāmaradhāriṇī \|\| 52 \|\|*

46-52. May this Sulakṣaṇā be one of my companions like Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantikā, Śubhā, Nandā, Sunandā, Kaumudī, Ūrmilā, Caṃpakamālā, Malayavāsinī, Karpūralatikā, the splendid Gandhadharā, Aśokā, Viśokā, Malayagandhinī, Candananiḥśvāsā, the excellent Mṛgamadā, Kokilālāpā, Madhurabhāṣiṇī, Gadyapadyanidhi, Anuktajñā, Dṛgañcalā, Iṅgitajñā, Kṛtamanorathā and Gānacittaharā. Since she is a celibate ever since childhood, she will become my greatest favourite. Let her be so in this same body with divine limbs and ornaments, divine garments, divine unguents and endowed with divine knowledge. Let her be near me forever, holding the moving chowries.

## \|\| 1.47.53 \|\|

*eṣāpi kāśirājasya kumāryastviha barkarī \|*  
*atraiva bhogānsaṃprāpya muktiṃ prāpsyatyanuttamām \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Let this kid be born as the princess of the king of Kāśī. After enjoying the pleasures here, she will attain the excellent salvation.

## \|\| 1.47.54 \|\|

*anayā tvarkakuṃḍesminpuṣye māsi raverdine \|*  
*snātaṃ tvanudite sūrye śītādakṣubdhacittayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. This kid has bathed in this Arkakuṇḍa on the Sunday in the Puṣya month (December-January) before sunrise without being afflicted in the mind by chillness.

## \|\| 1.47.55 \|\|

*rājaputrī tataḥ puṇyādastveṣā śubhalocanā \|*  
*varadānaprabhāveṇa tava viśveśvara prabho \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O Lord Viśveśvara, by your power of besotwing boons, let this (kid) be a princess of splendid vision due to merit.

## \|\| 1.47.56 \|\|

*barkarīkuṃḍamityākhyā tvarkakuṃḍasya jāyatām \|*  
*etasyāḥ pratimā pūjyā bhaviṣyatyatra mānavaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Let this Arkakuṇḍa be also known by another name Barkari Kuṇḍa. Its idol (image) should be worshipped by men here.

## \|\| 1.47.57 \|\|

*uttarārkasya devasya puṣye māsi raverdine \|*  
*kāryā sā vatsarīyātrā na taiḥ kāśīphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The annual pilgrimage of Lord Uttarārka should be performed on a Sunday in the month of Puṣya by devotees desirous of the benefit of Kāśī

## \|\| 1.47.58 \|\|

*mṛḍānyābhihi taṃ sarvaṃ kṛtvaitadviśvago vibhuḥ \|*  
*viśvanātho viveśātha prāsādaṃ svamatarkitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After carrrying out everything mentioned by Mṛḍānī, the all-powerful omnipresent Lord Viśvanātha unexpectedly entered his own palace.

## \|\| 1.47.59 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*lolārkasya ca māhātmyamuttarārkasya ca dvija \|*  
*kathitaṃ te mahābhāga sāṃbādityaṃ niśāmaya \|\| 59 \|\|*

Skanda said:

59\. O Brāhmaṇa of great fortune, the greatness of Lolārka and Uttarārka has been described to you. Now listen to the legend of Sāṃbāditya.

## \|\| 1.47.60 \|\|

*śrutvaitatpuṇyamākhyānaṃ śubhaṃ lolottarārkayoḥ \|*  
*vyādhibhirnābhibhūyeta na dāridryeṇa bādhyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. On hearing the excellent meritorious narrative of Lolārka and Uttarārka, no man will be afflicted with diseases or poverty.

## Chapter 48 - The Greatness of Sāṃbāditya

## \|\| 1.48.1-2 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣva maitrāvaruṇe dvāravatyāṃ yadūdvahaḥ \|*  
*dānavānāṃ vadhārthāya bhuvobhārāpanuttaye \|\| 1 \|\|*

*āvirāsītsvayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇavartmapratāpavān \|*  
*vāsudevo jagaddhāma devakyā vasudevataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Now, a small shrine of Sāṃbāditya is near Suraj Kuṇḍa (Sūrya Kuṇḍa; near Godaulia crossing in the heart of the city). But the plinth of the destroyed temple shows that it was an extensive temple. BCL 180-181 notes: Two Sun-discs lying under a tree in a rubble near the ruins, are witness to the ancient impressive temple.

Skanda said:

1-2. Listen, O Maitrāvaruṇi, Vāsudeva, the abode of the universe, manifested himsef as Kṛṣṇa with fiery brilliance in Devakī through Vasudeva in Dvārakā. He was the greatest among Yādavas. (He manifested himself) for reducing the burden of the earth by slaying demons.

## \|\| 1.48.3 \|\|

*sāśītilakṣaṃ tasyāsankumārā arkavarcasaḥ \|*  
*svarge pitādṛśā bālāḥ suśīlā na hi kuṃbhaja \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A hundred thousand and eighty sons of solar refulgence were born to him. O Pot-born One, even in heaven, there are no such boys of excellent behaviour.

## \|\| 1.48.4 \|\|

*atīvarūpasaṃpannā atīva sumahābalāḥ \|*  
*atīva śastraśāstrajñā atīva śubhalakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They were richly endowed with supreme handsomeness. They were extremely powerful. They were highly conversant with scriptures and the art of wielding weapons. They had highly splendid characteristics.

## \|\| 1.48.5-8 \|\|

*tāṃdraṣṭuṃ mānasaḥ putro brahmaṇastapasāṃnidhiḥ \|*  
*kṛtavalkalakaupīno dhṛta kṛṣṇājināṃbaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|gṛhītabrahmadaṃḍaśca trivṛnmauṃjī sumekhalaḥ \|*  
*urasthalastha tulasī mālayā samalaṃkṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*gopīcaṃdananiryāsa lasadaṃgavilepanaḥ \|*  
*tapasā kṛśasarvāṃgo mūrto jvalanavajjvalan \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ājagāmāṃbaracaro nārado dvārakāpurīm \|*  
*viśvakarmavinirmāṇāṃ jitasvargapurīśriyam \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. Once Nārada came to see the city of Dvārakā built by Viśvakarman, which surpassed even the celestial city in excellence. Nārada was a mental son of Brahmā and a storehouse of penance. He had a bark garment as loin cloth and a deer hide as the (upper) garment. He held a Brahmadaṇḍa (staff held by a religious student). He had a girdle of three-stringed Muñja grass. A Tulasī garland embellished his chest. Liquid paste of Gopīcandana was the unguent shining on his body. All his limbs were emaciated due to austerities. He shone like a personified form of fire. He came by the aerial path.

## \|\| 1.48.9 \|\|

*taṃdṛṣṭvā nāradaṃ sarve vinamratarakaṃdharāḥ \|*  
*prabaddha mūrdhāṃjalayaḥ praṇemurvṛṣṇinaṃdanāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing Nārada all the Vṛṣṇī folk bent down their necks in humility. With joined palms held over the head they bowed down to him.

## \|\| 1.48.10 \|\|

*sāṃbaḥ svarūpasauṃdarya garvasarvasvamohitaḥ \|*  
*na nanāma muniṃ tatra hasaṃstadrūpasaṃpadam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Sāṃba who was deluded by everything that he possessed such as comely features and charm, did not bow down to the sage. He was laughing at the excellence (?) of the form (of the sage).

## \|\| 1.48.11 \|\|

*sāṃbasya tamabhiprāyaṃ vijñāya sa mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*viveśa sumahāramyaṃ nāradaḥ kṛṣṇamaṃdiram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After knowing perfectly well what Sāṃba thought, the great sage Nārada entered the extremely beautiful palace of Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 1.48.12 \|\|

*kṛṣṇotha dṛṣṭvā'gacchaṃtaṃ pratyudgamya ca nāradam \|*  
*madhuparkeṇa saṃpūjya svāsane copaveśayat \|\| 12 \|\|*
