12\. On seeing Nārada coining, Kṛṣṇa rose up to welcome him, honoured him with Madhuparka and made him share his own seat.

## \|\| 1.48.13 \|\|

*kṛtvā kathā vicitrārthāstata ekāṃtavartinaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇasya karṇe'kathayannāradaḥ sāṃbaceṣṭitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After conversing with him on a variety of topics Nārada whispered into Kṛṣṇa’s ears the misbehaviour of Sāṃba when Kṛṣṇa was alone.

## \|\| 1.48.14 \|\|

*avaśyaṃ kiṃcidatrā'sti yaśodānaṃdavardhana \|*  
*prāyaśastanna ghaṭate'saṃbhāvyaṃ nātha vāstriyām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “O delighter of Yaśodā; here there is something (unusual). Generally it does not happen but perhaps there is nothing that is impossible in the case of women.

## \|\| 1.48.15 \|\|

*yūnāṃ tribhuvanasthānāṃ sāṃbo'tīva surūpavān \|*  
*svabhāvacaṃcalākṣīṇāṃ cetovṛttiḥ sucaṃcalā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Sāṃba is the most handsome of all young men in the three worlds. Fickle indeed is the mind of women whose eyes are by nature tremulous.

## \|\| 1.48.16 \|\|

*apekṣaṃte na mugdhākṣyaḥ kulaṃ śīlaṃ śrutaṃ dhanam \|*  
*rūpameva samīkṣaṃte viṣameṣu vimohitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. These beautiful-eyed damsels, when deluded by the god of Love, do not care to follow the norms of noble birth, good conduct, learning or riches. They see only charming features.

## \|\| 1.48.17 \|\|

*athavā viditaṃ no te vallavīnāṃ viceṣṭitam \|*  
*vināṣṭaunāyikāḥ kṛṣṇa kāmayaṃte'balāhyamum \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Or perhaps there is nothing not known to you in regard to the activities of the cowherd lasses. Excepting your eight crowned queens, all the other ladies are enamoured of him.”

## \|\| 1.48.18 \|\|

*vāmabhruvāṃ svabhāvācca nāradasya ca vākyataḥ \|*  
*vijñātā'khilavṛttāṃtastathyaṃ kṛṣṇopyamanyata \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Kṛṣṇa knowing as he did the natural inclinations of beautiful women and relying on Nārada’s words, believed what Nārada had reported as true.

## \|\| 1.48.19 \|\|

*tāvaddhairyaṃcalākṣīṇāṃ tāvaccetovivekitā \|*  
*yāvannārthī viviktastho vivikterthini nānyathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. ‘Ladies of tremulous eyes have fortitude and discretion only as long as the seeker of love is not in a secluded spot. If he is in a secluded spot, their fortitude and discretion become inoperative. They become otherwise.’

## \|\| 1.48.20 \|\|

*itthaṃ vivecayaṃścitte kṛṣṇaḥ krodhanadīrayam \|*  
*vivekasetunā'stabhya nāradaṃ prāhiṇotsudhīḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thinking thus in his mind, Kṛṣṇa checked the current of the river of his fury by means of the dam of discretion. The wise Kṛṣṇa bade goodbye to Nārada.

## \|\| 1.48.21 \|\|

*sāṃbasya vaikṛtaṃ kiṃcitkvacitkṛṣṇonavaikṣata \|*  
*gate devamunau tasminvīkṣamāṇopyaharniśam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After the departure of the celestial sage, though Kṛṣṇa watchfully observed day and night, he could not perceive any misbehaviour on the part of Sāṃba.

## \|\| 1.48.22-23 \|\|

*kiyatyapi gate kāle punarapyāyayau muniḥ \|*  
*madhye līlāvatīnāṃ ca jñātvā kṛṣṇamavasthitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bahiḥ krīḍaṃtamāhūya sāṃbamityāha nāradaḥ \|*  
*yāhi kṛṣṇāṃtikaṃ tūrṇaṃ kathayāgamanaṃ mama \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. After the lapse of some time, the sage came again. On coming to know that Kṛṣṇa was in the midst of the sporting women, Nārada called Sāṃba who was playing outside and said thus: “Go immediately to Kṛṣṇa and inform him that I have come.”

## \|\| 1.48.24-28 \|\|

*sāṃbopi yāmi noyāmi kṣaṇamitthamaciṃtayat \|*  
*kathaṃ rahaḥstha pitaraṃ yāmi straiṇasakhaṃprati \|\| 24 \|\|*

*na yāmi ca kathaṃ vākyādasyāhaṃ brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*jvaladaṃgārasaṃkāśa sphuratsarvāṃgatejasaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*praṇamatsukumāreṣu vrīḍitoyaṃ mayaikadā \|*  
*idānīmapi no yāyāmasya vākyānmahāmuneḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*atyāhitaṃ tadastīha tadāgodvayadarśanāt \|*  
*pituḥ kopopi suślāghyo mayi no brāhmaṇasya tu \|\| 27 \|\|*

*brahmakopāgninirdagdhāḥ prarohaṃti na jātucit \|*  
*aparāgnivinirdagdhāro haṃte dāvadagdhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

24-28. Sāṃba hesitated for a while, thinking: ‘Should I go? Should I not go? How can I go to my father who is in a lonely spot in the company of women? How can I disobey this Brahmacārin who is like a blazing charcoal? There is dazzling brilliance all over his body. Once I had ridiculed him while all the other boys were bowing down. If now too I refuse to go, disobeying thereby this great sage, there shall be greater danger in view of the two sins and defaults. A father’s anger towards me is better than that of a Brāhmaṇa towards me. Those who are burnt down by the fire of the wrath of a Brāhmaṇa never flourish. Those who ae \[are?\] burnt down by other (kinds of) fires do grow again like things reduced to ash by a forest fire.’

## \|\| 1.48.29-30 \|\|

*iti dhyātvā kṣaṇaṃ sāṃbo'viśadaṃtaḥpuraṃpituḥ \|*  
*madhye straiṇasabhaṃkṛṣṇaṃ yāvajjāṃbavatīsutaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dūrātpraṇamya vijñaptiṃ sa cakāra saśaṃkitaḥ \|*  
*tāvattamanvagacchacca nāradaḥ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. After reflecting thus for a short while, Sāṃba, the son of Jāṃbavatī, entered the apartment of his father. Even as he hesitatingly bowed down to Kṛṣṇa in the midst of the assembly of ladies from fear and reported to him Nārada too followed him to accomplish what he intended.

## \|\| 1.48.31 \|\|

*sasaṃbhramotha kṛṣṇopi dṛṣṭvā sāṃbaṃ ca nāradam \|*  
*samuttasthau paridadhatpītakauśeyamaṃbaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On seeing Sāṃba and Nārada, Kṛṣṇa stood up in a flurry and put on the yellow silk cloth.

## \|\| 1.48.32 \|\|

*utthite devakīsūnau tāḥ sarvā api gopikāḥ \|*  
*vilajjitāḥ samuttasdhurgṛhṇaṃtyaḥ svaṃsvamaṃbaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. When the son of Devakī got up, all those cowherdesses bashfully stood up tucking up their respective clothes.

## \|\| 1.48.33 \|\|

*mahārhaśayanīye taṃ haste dhṛtvā mahāmunim \|*  
*samupāveśayatkṛṣṇaḥ sāṃbaśca krīḍituṃ yayau \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Kṛṣṇa grasped the hands of the great sage and made him sit on the couch of great value. Sāṃba went away to play.

## \|\| 1.48.34 \|\|

*tāsāṃ skhalitamālokya tiṣṭhaṃtīnāṃ puro muniḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇalīlādravībhūtavarāṃgānāṃ jagau harim \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Due to Kṛṣṇa’s dalliance with them, all those ladies had experienced orgasm with drenched vaginal apertures. On seeing them dripping even as they stood in front of him, the sage said to Kṛṣṇa:

## \|\| 1.48.35 \|\|

*paśyapaśya mahābuddhe dṛṣṭvā jāṃbavatīsutam \|*  
*imāḥ skhalitamāpannāstadrūpakṣubdhacetasaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. “O my dear intelligent fellow! Lo and behold. On seeing the son of Jāṃbavatī these ladies are dripping because their minds are agitated by his comely features.”

## \|\| 1.48.36 \|\|

*kṛṣṇopi sāṃbamāhūya sahasaivāśapatsutam \|*  
*sarvā jāṃbavatītulyāḥ paśyaṃtamapi durvidheḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Though Sāṃba looked upon everyone like (his mother) Jāṃbavatī, Kṛṣṇa called his son and cursed him due to the adverse action of fate:

## \|\| 1.48.37 \|\|

*yasmāttvadrūpamālokya gopālyaḥ skhalitā imāḥ \|*  
*tasmātkuṣṭhī bhava kṣipramakāṃḍāgamanena ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. “Be a leper because it was on seeing your handsome features that these lasses experienced this drenching of their organs. Further you had intruded untimely.”

## \|\| 1.48.38 \|\|

*vepamāno mahāvyādhibhayātsāṃbopi dāruṇāt \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṃ prasādayāmāsa bahuśaḥ pāpaśāṃtaye \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Trembling on account of the terrible fear of the great disease, Sāṃba pleaded in many ways for the purpose of quelling the sin.

## \|\| 1.48.39 \|\|

*kṛṣṇopyanena saṃjānansāṃbaṃ svasutamaurasam \|*  
*abravītkuṣṭhamokṣāya vraja vaiśveśvarīṃ purīm \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. By this time Kṛṣṇa realized (his mistake) and told his bosom-born son Sāṃba: “To get the cure from leprosy, go to the city of Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 1.48.40 \|\|

*tatra bradhnaṃ samārādhya prakṛtiṃ svāmavāpsyasi \|*  
*mahainasāṃ kṣayo yatra nāsti vārāṇasīṃ vinā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. By propitiating the Sun-god there, you will regain your normal state. Excepting in Vārāṇasī there is no quelling of great sins elsewhere.

## \|\| 1.48.41 \|\|

*yatra viśveśvaraḥ sākṣādyatra svargāpagā ca sā \|*  
*yeṣāṃ mahainasāṃ dṛṣṭā munibhirnaiva niṣkṛtiḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ viśuddhirastyeva prāpya vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After reaching the city of Vārāṇasī where Viśveśvara is directly present and where there is the celestial river, there is surely redemption and purity, removing those great sins for which no remedy has been seen even by sages.

## \|\| 1.48.42 \|\|

*na kevalaṃ hi pāpebhyo vārāṇasyāṃ vimucyate \|*  
*prākṛtebhyopi pāpebhyo mucyate śaṃkarājñayā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. At Vārāṇasī, not only from (self-incurred) sins is one liberated, but also from Prākṛta sins (sins foisted on one by Prakṛti), at the behest of Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.48.43 \|\|

*purā purāriṇā sṛṣṭamavimuktaṃ vimuktaye \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva jaṃtūnāṃ kṛpayāṃte tanutyajām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Formerly, due to his great mercy, Avimukta was created by Purāri for the liberation of all creatures that give up their bodies in the end.

## \|\| 1.48.44 \|\|

*tatrānaṃdavane śaṃbhostavaśāpa nirākṛtiḥ \|*  
*sāṃba tattveritaṃ yāhi nānyathā śāpanirvṛtiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O Sāṃba, the curse on you will be exonerated there in the Ānandavana of Śaṃbhu. Hence listen. There is no redemption from the curse otherwise.”

## \|\| 1.48.45 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ samāpṛcchya karmanirmuktaceṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*nāradaḥ kṛtakṛtyaḥ sanyayāvākāśavartmanā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Nārada, the living-liberated soul, free from of all binding Karmas, became happy on having concluded his mission. He took leave of Kṛṣṇa and went away by the aerial path.

## \|\| 1.48.46 \|\|

*sāṃbo vārāṇasīṃ prāpya samārādhyāṃśumālinam \|*  
*kuṃḍaṃ tatpṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā nijāṃ prakṛtimāptavān \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After going to Vārāṇasī and propitiating the Sun-god, Sāṃba left the Kuṇḍa. He regained normalcy.

## \|\| 1.48.47 \|\|

*sāṃbādityastadārabhya sarvavyādhiharo raviḥ \|*  
*dadāti sarvabhaktebhyo'nāmayāḥ sarvasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Ever since then, the Sun-god Sāṃbāditya has become dispeller of all ailments. On all his devotees he bestows all riches free from evil and illness.

## \|\| 1.48.48 \|\|

*sāṃbakuṃḍe naraḥ snātvā ravivāre'ruṇodaye \|*  
*sāṃbādityaṃ ca saṃpūjya vyādhibhirnābhibhūyate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. If anyone takes his holy dip in Sāṃbakuṇḍa early at dawn on a Sunday and worships the deity Sāṃbāḍitya, he is never afflicted by diseases.

## \|\| 1.48.49 \|\|

*na strī vaidhavyamāpnoti sāṃbādityasya sevanāt \|*  
*vaṃdhyā putraṃ prasūyeta śuddharūpasamanvitam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. No woman meets with widowhood after the worship of Sāṃbāditya. Even a barren woman will give birth to a son endowed with pure handsome features.

## \|\| 1.48.50 \|\|

*śuklāyāṃ dvija saptamyāṃ māghe māsi raverdine \|*  
*mahāparva samākhyātaṃ raviparva samaṃ śubham \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O Brāhmaṇa, the seventh lunar day in the bright half of the month of Māgha, especially if it falls on a Sunday, is called a day of great festival. It is as auspicious as solar eclipse.

## \|\| 1.48.51 \|\|

*mahārogātpramucyeta tatra snātvāruṇodaye \|*  
*sāṃbādityaṃ prapūjyāpi dharmamakṣayamāpnuyāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. By taking the holy bath early at dawn, one is rid of even great diseases. By worshipping Sāṃbāditya, one acquires inexhaustible piety.

## \|\| 1.48.52 \|\|

*sannihatyāṃ kurukṣetre yatpuṇyaṃ rāhudarśane \|*  
*tatpuṇyaṃ ravisaptamyāṃ māghe kāśyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. There is no doubt in this that on Ravisaptamī day in Māgha at Kāśī one gets the same merit (Puṇya) as one acquires at the time of the Solar (or Lunar) eclipse by being present in Kurukṣetra.

## \|\| 1.48.53-54 \|\|

*madhaumāsi ravervāre yātrā sāṃvatsarī bhavet \|*  
*aśokaistatra saṃpūjya kuṃḍe snātvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sāṃbādityaṃ naro jātu na śokairabhibhūyate \|*  
*saṃvatsarakṛtātpāpādbahirbhavati tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. On a Sunday, in the month of Madhu (Caitra) the annual pilgrimage and festivities take place. The devotee should worship Sāṃbāditya with Aśoka flowers after taking the holy bath in accordance with the injunctions. The devotee will never be afflicted with grief. Instantaneously he becomes freed from the sins incurred throughout the year.

## \|\| 1.48.55 \|\|

*viśveśātpaścimāśāyāṃ sāṃbenātra mahātmanā \|*  
*samyagārādhitā mūrtirādityasya śubhapradā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In the western quarter of Viśveśa, the splendid idol of the Sun-god bestowing auspiciousness was perfectly propitiated by the noble-souled Sāṃba.

## \|\| 1.48.56 \|\|

*iyaṃ bhaviṣyā tanmūrtiragaste tvatpuro'kathi \|*  
*tāmabhyarcya namaskṛtya kṛtvāṣṭau ca pradakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*naro bhavati niṣpāpaḥ kāśīvāsa phalaṃ labhet \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. This future image thereof has been told to you, O Agasti. By circumambulating it eight times and by worshipping and bowing to it, a man becomes free of sins. He shall attain the benefit of stay in Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.48.57 \|\|

*sāṃbādityasya māhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ te mahāmate \|*  
*yacchrutvāpi naro jātu yamalokaṃ na paśyati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O highly intelligent one, the greatness of the deity Sāṃbāditya has been narrated to you, on hearing which no man will ever see the world of Yama.

## \|\| 1.48.58 \|\|

*idānīṃ draupadādityaṃ kathayiṣyāmi tenagha \|*  
*tathā draupadaādityaḥ saṃsevyo bhaktasiddhidaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Now, O sinless one, I shall describe Draupadāditya. This Draupada Āditya should be served. He is the bestower of supernatural powers on his devotees.

## Chapter 49 - Description of Draupadāditya and Mayūkhāditya

## \|\| 1.49.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*pārāśaryamune vyāsa kumāraḥ kuṃbhajanmane \|*  
*yadāvadatkathāmetāṃ tadā kva drupadātmajā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Draupadāditya is in the west of Viśvanātha Temple and is under a tree. Mayūkhāditya is inside Maṅgalā Devī Temple.

Sūta said:

1\. O Sage Vyāsa, O son of Parāśara, there was no daughter of Drupada when Kumāra (Skanda) narrated this story to the Pot-born Sage.

## \|\| 1.49.2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*purāṇasaṃhitāṃ sūta brūte traikālikīṃ kathām \|*  
*saṃdeho nātra kartavyo yatastadgocarokhilam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

2\. The Purāṇasaṃhitā is proclaimed as the story of all the three aspects of time (past, present, future). No doubt is to be entertained in this regard, because everything is comprised therein.

## \|\| 1.49.3 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ākarṇaya mune pūrvaṃ paṃcavaktro haraḥ svayam \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ paṃcadhā bhūtvā prādurāsījjagaddhitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Skanda said:

3\. Listen, O sage. Formerly, the five-faced Hara divided himself in five forms and manifested on the earth for the sake of the welfare of the universe.

## \|\| 1.49.4 \|\|

*umāpi ca jagaddhātrī drupadasya mahībhujaḥ \|*  
*yajato vahnikuṃḍācca prāduścakreti suṃdarī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Umā, the mother of the universe, also manifested herself as a very beautiful lady from the sacrificial fire pit of king Drupada.

## \|\| 1.49.5 \|\|

*paṃcāpi pāṃḍutanayāḥ sākṣādrudravapurdharāḥ \|*  
*avateruriha svargādduṣṭasaṃhārakārakāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The five sons of Pāṇḍu were the embodied forms of Rudra taking incarnations on the earth from heaven for the destruction of the wicked ones.

## \|\| 1.49.6 \|\|

*nārāyaṇopi kṛṣṇatvaṃ prāpya tatsāhacaryakṛt \|*  
*udvṛttavṛttaśamanaḥ sadvṛttasthitikārakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Lord Nārāyaṇa attained the form of Kṛṣṇa and accompanied them as the suppressor of the activities of the evil-doers and the sustainer of the good.

## \|\| 1.49.7 \|\|

*pratapaṃtaḥ pṛthivyāṃ te pārthāśceruḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*udayānudayau tasminsaṃpadāṃ vipadāmapi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Those sons of Pṛthā shone brilliantly and secured great prosperity and extinction of adversities.

## \|\| 1.49.8 \|\|

*kadācitte mahāvīrā bhrātṛvyapratipāditām \|*  
*vipattimāpya mahatīṃ babhūvuḥ kānanaukasaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Once those great warriors encountered great danger brought about by adversaries and they had to live in forests.

## \|\| 1.49.9 \|\|

*pāṃcālyapi ca tatpatnī pativyasanatāpitā \|*  
*dharmajñā prāpya tanvaṃgī bradhnamārādhayadbhṛśam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Pāñcālī, their wife, was distressed on account of the misery of her husbands. The lady of tender limbs, given to virtuous conduct, went to Kāśī to the Sun-god and assiduously propitiated him.

## \|\| 1.49.10 \|\|

*ārādhitotha savitā tayā drupadakanyayā \|*  
*sadarvī sapidhānāṃ ca sthālikāmakṣayāṃ dadau \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On being propitiated by the daughter of Drupada, the Sun-god gave her an inexhaustible vessel with a lid and a ladle.

## \|\| 1.49.11-18 \|\|

*uvāca ca prasannātmā bhāskaro drupadātmajām \|*  
*ārādhayaṃtīṃ bhāvena sarvatra śucimānasām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sthālyaitayā mahābhāge yāvaṃto'nnārthino janāḥ \|*  
*tāvaṃtastṛptimāpsyaṃti yāvacca tvaṃ na bhokṣyase \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhuktāyāṃ tvayi riktaiṣā pūrṇabhaktā bhavipyati \|*  
*rasavadvyaṃjananidhiricchābhakṣyapradāyinī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*itthaṃ varastayā labdhaḥ kāśyāmādityato mune \|*  
*aparaśca varo dattastasyai devena bhāsvatā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*raviruvāca \|*  
*viśveśāddakṣiṇebhāge yo māṃ tvatpurataḥ sthitam \|*  
*ārādhayiṣyati naraḥ kṣudbādhā tasya naśyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

*anyaśca me varo datto viśveśena pativrate \|*  
*tapasā parituṣṭena taṃ niśāmaya vacmi te \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prāgrave tvāṃ samārādhya yo māṃ drakṣyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*tasya tvaṃ duḥkhatimiramapānuda nijaiḥ karaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ato dharmāpriye nityaṃ prāpya viśveśvarādvaram \|*  
*kāśīsthitānāṃ jaṃtūnāṃ nāśayāmyaghasaṃcayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

11-18. Delighted in his mind the Sun-god said to the daughter of Drupada, who had propitiated him devoutly and whose mind was pure in every respect:

“O blessed lady, as long as you do not take food, all those who seek food, irrespective of their number, will become satisfied. This vessel, full of cooked food, the storehouse of delicious side dishes and the bestower of all the desired foodstuffs will become empty when you have taken food.”

## \|\| 1.49.14 \|\|

*itthaṃ varastayā labdhaḥ kāśyāmādityato mune \|*  
*aparaśca varo dattastasyai devena bhāsvatā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This boon was attained by her at Kāśī. Another boon was also given to her by the lord, Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.49.15 \|\|

*raviruvāca \|*  
*viśveśāddakṣiṇebhāge yo māṃ tvatpurataḥ sthitam \|*  
*ārādhayiṣyati naraḥ kṣudbādhā tasya naśyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

Ravi said:

15\. If a man propitiates me while standing on the right side of Viśveśvara and keeping you in front, he will never have distress due to hunger.

## \|\| 1.49.16 \|\|

*anyaśca me varo datto viśveśena pativrate \|*  
*tapasā parituṣṭena taṃ niśāmaya vacmi te \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O chaste lady, another boon has been granted to me by Viśveśa who was pleased with my penance. Listen, I shall narrate it to you.

## \|\| 1.49.17 \|\|

*prāgrave tvāṃ samārādhya yo māṃ drakṣyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*tasya tvaṃ duḥkhatimiramapānuda nijaiḥ karaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “O Ravi, if any man visits me after worshipping you at the outset, you will remove the darkness of his misery with your own rays.”

## \|\| 1.49.18 \|\|

*ato dharmāpriye nityaṃ prāpya viśveśvarādvaram \|*  
*kāśīsthitānāṃ jaṃtūnāṃ nāśayāmyaghasaṃcayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Hence, O righteous lady, after attaining this boon from Viśveśvara, I am dispelling forever the collection of sins of the creatures stationed at Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.49.19 \|\|

*ye māmatra bhajiṣyaṃti mānavāḥ śraddhayānvitāḥ \|*  
*tvadvarodyatapāṇiṃ ca teṣāṃ dāsyāmi ciṃtitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. To these people endowed with faith, who worship me with hands raised aloft to grant boon unto you, I will grant whatever they wish.

## \|\| 1.49.20-21 \|\|

*bhavatīṃ matsamīpasthāṃ yudhiṣṭhirapativratām \|*  
*viśveśāddakṣiṇebhāge daṃḍapāṇeḥ samīpataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yercayiṣyaṃti bhāvena puruṣā vāstriyopi vā \|*  
*teṣāṃ kadācinno bhāvi bhayaṃ priyaviyogajam \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. If men or women with great fervour worship you, the chaste wife of Yudhiṣṭhira, stationed near me in the vicinity of Daṇḍapāṇi towards the right (south) of Viśveśa, they will never experience the fear due to separation from the near and dear ones.

## \|\| 1.49.22 \|\|

*na vyādhijaṃ bhayaṃ kvāpi na kṣuttṛḍdoṣasaṃbhavam \|*  
*draupadīkṣaṇataḥ kāśyāṃ tava dharmapriyenaghe \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. They will nowhere have fear of illness or that arising from the faults of hunger and thirst, O Draupadī, O sinless beloved of Dharmaputra, after visiting you.

## \|\| 1.49.23 \|\|

*iti dattvā varāndeva ādityaḥ sarvadaḥ satām \|*  
*śaṃbhumārādhayāmāsa dharmaṃ draupadyupāyayau \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After granting these boons, the Sun-god, the bestower of everything on the good, began to propitiate Śaṃbhu and Draupadī went back to Yudhiṣṭhira.

## \|\| 1.49.24 \|\|

*ādityasya kathāmetāṃ draupadyārādhitasya vai \|*  
*yaḥ śroṣyati naro bhaktyā tasyainaḥ kṣayameṣyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If any man listens with devotion to the story of Āditya propitiated by Draupadī, his sins will become dispelled.

## \|\| 1.49.25 \|\|

*skaṃda uva \|ca \|*  
*draupadādityamāhātmyaṃ saṃkṣepātkathitaṃ mayā \|*  
*mayūkhādityamāhātmyaṃ śṛṇvidānīṃ ghaṭodbhava \|\|\|\| 25 \|\|*

Skanda said:

25\. O Pot-born One, the greatness of Draupadāditya has been narrated succinctly by me. Listen to the greatness of Mayūkhāditya now.

## \|\| 1.49.26 \|\|

*purā paṃcanade tīrthe triṣulokeṣu viśrute \|*  
*sahasraraśmirbhagavāṃstapastepe sudāruṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Formerly, the thousand-rayed Sun-god performed a fierce penance in the holy spot of Pañcanada renowned in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.49.27-29 \|\|

*pratiṣṭhāpya mahāliṃgaṃ gabhastīśvara saṃjñitam \|*  
*gaurīṃ ca maṃgalā nāmnīṃ bhaktamaṃgaladāṃ sadā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*divyavarṣasahasraṃ tu śatena guṇitaṃ mune \|*  
*ārādhayañśivaṃ somaṃ somārdhakṛtaśekharam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*svarūpatastu tapanastrilokītāpanakṣamaḥ \|*  
*tatotitīvra tapasā jajvāla nitarāṃ mune \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. He installed the great Liṅga named Gabhastīśvara and Gaurī, the perpetual bestower of auspiciousness on the devotees, named Maṅgalā. He propitiated Lord Śiva who has made the crescent moon his crest jewel, along with Umā, O sage, for a period of a thousand celestial years multiplied by a hundred. By means of his natural refulgence the Sun is capable of scorching the three worlds. Hence he shone all the more brilliantly, O sage, due to his severe austerities.

## \|\| 1.49.30 \|\|

*mayūkhaistatra savitustrailokyadahanakṣamaiḥ \|*  
*tataṃ samastaṃ tatkāle dyāvābhūmyoryadaṃtaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At that time the entire space between heaven and earth was overspread by the rays of the Sun, capable of burning the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.49.31 \|\|

*vaimānikairviṣṇupade tatyaje ca gatāgatam \|*  
*tīvre pataṃgamahasi pataṃgatvabhayādiva \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. All movements (travel to and fro) through the firmament were abandoned by Devas moving about in aerial chariots, as if they were afraid of being reduced to the state of locust in the fierce heat of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.49.32 \|\|

*mayūkhā eva dṛśyaṃte tiryagūrdhvamadhopi ca \|*  
*ādityasya na cādityo nīpapuṣpasthiteriva \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Above, below and obliquely too, only the rays of the Sun were seen and not the Sun himself as in the case of the Kadaṃba bud where the pericarp is not seen but only the petals.

## \|\| 1.49.33 \|\|

*tasyavai mahasāṃ rāśestaporāśestaporciṣām \|*  
*cakaṃpe sādhvasāttīvrā trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The three worlds including the mobile and immobile beings trembled due to the fear of the flames of penance of the Sun, a mass of refulgence.

## \|\| 1.49.34 \|\|

*sūrya ātmāsya jagato vedeṣu paripaṭhyate \|*  
*sa eva cejvālayitā ko nastrātā bhavediha \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. “The Sun is the very soul of this universe, mobile and immobile.” So it is said in the Vedas. If he himself were to be one who burns who can be our protector?

## \|\| 1.49.35 \|\|

*jagaccakṣurasau sūryo jagadātmaiṣa bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*jagadyoyanmṛtaprāyaṃ prātaḥprātaḥ prabodhayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. This Sun is the eye of the universe. This Bhāskara is the soul of the universe. He wakens up and enlivens the universe, almost dead (during night), every morning.

## \|\| 1.49.36 \|\|

*tamoṃdhakūpapatitamudyanneṣa dinedine \|*  
*prasārya paritaḥ pāṇīnprāṇijātaṃ samuddharet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Rising up everyday, spreading his hands (rays) all-round, he lifts up the entire living beings that have fallen in the blinding well of darkness.

## \|\| 1.49.37 \|\|

*udite'trodimo nityamastaṃ yātyastamāpnumaḥ \|*  
*udaye'nudaye tasmādasmākaṃ kāraṇaṃ raviḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When the Sun rises, we rise up. When he sets, we lie down and rest. Hence Ravi is the cause of our rising and taking rest.

## \|\| 1.49.38 \|\|

*iti vyākulitaṃ viśvaṃ paśyanviśveśvaraḥ svayam \|*  
*viśvatrātā varaṃ dātuṃ saṃjagme tigmaraśmaye \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Viśveśvara, the protector of the universe, saw the entire universe agitated thus. So he went (there) to grant boons to the Sun.

## \|\| 1.49.39 \|\|

*mayūkhamālinaṃ śaṃbhurālokyāti suniścalam \|*  
*samādhi vismṛtātmānaṃ visismāya tapaḥ prati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On seeing the Sun with the full complement of rays remaining very steady, forgetting himself in mental absorption, he became wonder-struck in regard to his penance.

## \|\| 1.49.40 \|\|

*uvāca ca prasannātmā śrīkaṃṭhaḥ praṇatārtihṛt \|*  
*alaṃ taptvā varaṃ brūhi dyumaṇe mahasāṃ nidhe \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Śrīkaṇṭha, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow down, became pleased in his mind and said: “O Dyumaṇi (Crest-jewel of the firmament i.e. the Sun), O storehouse of refulgence, enough of your penance. Tell me the boon you wish to have.”

## \|\| 1.49.41 \|\|

*niruddheṃdriyavṛttitvādbradhno dhyānasamādhinā \|*  
*na jagrāha vacaḥ śaṃbhordvitriruktopyakarṇavat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Since the Sun had controlled the activities of all the sense-organs through mental absorption and meditation he did not grasp the words of Śaṃbhu though repeated two or three times as though he had no ears.

## \|\| 1.49.42 \|\|

*kāṣṭhībhūtaṃ tu taṃ jñātvā śivaḥ pasparśa pāṇinā \|*  
*mahātapaḥ samudbhūta saṃtāpāmṛtavarṣiṇā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Realizing that he had become a log of wood as it were, Śiva touched him with his hands shedding nectar, dispelling the distress due to the great penance.

## \|\| 1.49.43 \|\|

*tata unmīlayāṃcakre locane viśvalocanaḥ \|*  
*tasyodayamiva prāpya prage paṃkajinīvanī \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then the Sun (Viśvalocana—‘the eye of the universe’) opened his eyes like a cluster of lotuses (that open up their petals) in the morning when he himself rises.

## \|\| 1.49.44 \|\|

*parivyapetasaṃtāpastapanaḥ sparśanādvibhoḥ \|*  
*avagrahitasasyaśrīrullalāsa yathāṃbudāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. With all his distress dispelled by the touch of the Lord, the Sun became glad like vegetation, the glory of which was tarnished by drought, becoming flourishing once again due to the clouds.

## \|\| 1.49.45 \|\|

*mitro netrātithīkṛtya tryakṣaṃ pratyakṣamagrataḥ \|*  
*daṃḍavatpraṇanāmoccaistuṣṭāva ca pinākinam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The Sun directly looked at the Three-eyed Lord who was visible in front, prostrated in front of him like a log of wood, and eulogized the Pināka-wielding Lord loudly:

## \|\| 1.49.46 \|\|

*raviruvāca \|*  
*devadeva jagatāṃpate vibho bharga bhīma bhava caṃdrabhūṣaṇa \|*  
*bhūtanātha bhavabhītihāraka tvāṃ natosmi natavāṃchitaprada \|\| 46 \|\|*

Ravi said: (Prayer to Śiva: vv 46-53)

46\. I bow unto you, O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the worlds, O all-powerful one, O Bharga (the bestower of happiness), O Bhīma (terrible), O Bhava (the place of origin), O lord having the moon as ornament, O lord of goblins, O destroyer of the fear of worldly existence, O bestower of the desired things on those who bow down!

## \|\| 1.49.47 \|\|

*caṃdracūḍamṛḍa dhūrjaṭe hara tryakṣa dakṣa śatataṃtuśātana \|*  
*śāṃtaśāśvata śivāpate śiva tvāṃ natosmi natavāṃchitaprada \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Candracūḍa, O Mṛḍa, O Dhūrjaṭi, O Hara, O Tryakṣa, O destroyer of the sacrifice of Dakṣa, O quiescent one, O everlasting Lord, O Śivā’s consort, O Śiva, I bow unto you, the giver of the desired things to those who bow down.

## \|\| 1.49.48 \|\|

*nīlalohita samīhitārtha dahe dvyekalocana virūpalocana \|*  
*vyomakeśapaśupāśanāśana tvāṃ natosmi natavāṃchitaprada \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O Nīlalohita, O bestower of desired objects, O threeeyed one, O Virūpalocana, O Vyomakeśa, O destroyer of the bondage of living beings, I bow down unto you, the giver of the desired things to those who bow down.

## \|\| 1.49.49 \|\|

*vāmadevaśitikaṃṭhaśūlabhṛccaṃdraśekhara phaṇīṃdrabhūṣaṇa \|*  
*kāmakṛtpaśupate maheśvara tvāṃ natosmi natavāṃchitaprada \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O Vāmadeva, O Śrīkaṇṭha, O trident-bearing Lord with moon for crest-jewel, O Lord with serpents for ornaments, O Lord of souls bringing about the desired things, O Maheśvara, I bow unto you, the fulfiller of the desires of those who bow down.

## \|\| 1.49.50 \|\|

*tryaṃbaka tripurasūdaneśvara trāṇakṛttrinayanatrayīmaya \|*  
*kālakūṭa dalanāṃtakāṃtaka tvāṃ natosmi natavāṃchitaprada \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O Tryaṃbaka, O Tripurasūdana, O Īśvara, O Trāṇakṛt (Saviour), O Trinayana, O Trayīmaya, O Kālakūṭadalana (‘one who rendered the poison ineffective’), O destroyer of the god of Death, I bow unto you, the bestower of the desires of those who bow down.

## \|\| 1.49.51 \|\|

*śarvarīrahitaśarvasarvagasvargamārgasukhadāpavargada \|*  
*aṃdhakāsuraripo kapardabhṛttvāṃ natosmi natavāṃchitaprada \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Śarva, devoid of Māyā, O omnipresent one, O bestower of the happiness of the path of heaven, O enemy of the demon Andhaka, O Lord with matted hairs, I bow down unto you, the bestower of the desires of those who bow down.

## \|\| 1.49.52 \|\|

*śaṃkarogragirijāpate pate viśvanāthavidhiviṣṇu saṃstuta \|*  
*vedavedyaviditā'khileṃgi tatvāṃ natosmi natavāṃchitaprada \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O Śaṅkara, O Ugra, O Lord, O Lord of the Daughter of Mountain, O Viśvanātha, O Lord eulogized by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, O Lord capable of being known only through the Vedas, O Lord who have understood the internal thoughts and wishes of everyone, I bow unto you, the bestower of the desire of those who bow down.

## \|\| 1.49.53 \|\|

*viśvarūpapararūpa varjitabrahmajihmarahitāmṛtaprada \|*  
*vāṅamanoviṣayadūradūragatvāṃ natosmi natavāṃchitaprada \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O Viśvarūpa (omniformed god), O great one, O Lord devoid of forms, O Brahman, devoid of deception, O bestower of Amṛta (Nectar, freedom from death), O Lord beyond the ken of the mind and words, O Dūraga (‘one who has gone far’), I bow unto you, the bestower of the desires of those who bow down.

## \|\| 1.49.54 \|\|

*itthaṃ parītya mārtaṃḍo mṛḍaṃ devaṃ mṛḍānikām \|*  
*atha tuṣṭāva prītātmā śivavāmārdhahāriṇīm \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After praying to Lord Mṛḍa thus, Mārtaṇḍa (the Sun) who was delighted in his mind eulogized Mṛḍānikā who appropriated half the body of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.49.55 \|\|

*raviruvāca \|*  
*devi tvadīyacaraṇāṃbujareṇugaurīṃ bhālasthalīṃ vahati yaḥ praṇatipravīṇaḥ \|*  
*janmāṃtarepi rajanīkaracārulekhā tāṃ gaurayatyatitarāṃ kila tasya puṃsaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

Ravi said: (Prayer to the goddess: vv 55-62)

55\. O goddess, if anyone efficient in the activity of bowing down, renders his forehead grey by means of the dust particles of thy lotus-like feet, the beautiful digit of the moon makes his forehead all the more bright.

## \|\| 1.49.56 \|\|

*śrīmaṃgale sakalamaṃgalajanmabhūme śrīmaṃgale sakalakalmaṣatūlavahne \|*  
*śrīmaṃgale sakaladānavadarpahaṃtri śrīmaṃgale'khilamidaṃ paripāhi viśvam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O Śrī Maṅgalā, the source of origin of every auspicious features, O Śrī Maṅgalā, the fire that burns all sins like cotton, O Śrī Maṅgalā, the dispeller of the arrogance of all the Dānavas, O Śrī Maṅgalā, protect this entire universe.

## \|\| 1.49.57 \|\|

*viśveśvari tvamasi viśvajanasya kartrī tvaṃ pālayitryasi tathā pralayepihaṃtrī \|*  
*tvannāmakīrtanasamullasadacchapuṇyā srotasvinī harati pātakakūlavṛkṣān \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O Viśveśvarī (goddess of the universe), you are the creator of the people of all the worlds; you are the protectress and the destroyer at the time of the ultimate annihilation. The river of great pure merit arising out of the repetition of thy names dispels all the sins as though they were the trees on its banks.

## \|\| 1.49.58 \|\|

*mātarbhavāni bhavatī bhavatīvraduḥkhasaṃbhārahāriṇi śaraṇyamihāsti nānyā \|*  
*dhanyāsta eva bhuvaneṣu ta eva mānyā yeṣu sphurettavaśubhaḥ karuṇākaṭākṣaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O mother Bhavānī, O destroyer of the entire collection of the fierce miseries of worldly existence, you alone are the refuge. There is no one else. Only they are blessed in all the worlds, only they are worthy of honour, they, in whom your splendid glance of mercy falls and shines.

## \|\| 1.49.59 \|\|

*ye tvā smaraṃti satataṃ sahajaprakāśāṃ kāśīpurīsthitimatīṃ natamokṣalakṣmīm \|*  
*tānsaṃsmaretsmaraharo dhṛtaśuddhabuddhīnnirvāṇarakṣaṇavicakṣaṇapātrabhūtān \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Those who remember you always, you who have the innate brilliance, who are stationed in Kāśī, who constitute the glory of salvation unto those who bow down, are remembered by Lord Smarahara (‘Destroyer of the god of Love’) as the people of pure intellect and clever and deserving to have salvation and protection.

## \|\| 1.49.60 \|\|

*mātastavāṃghriyugalaṃ vimalaṃ hṛdisthaṃ yasyāsti tasya bhuvanaṃ sakalaṃ karastham \|*  
*yo nāmateja eti maṃgalagauri nityaṃ siddhyaṣṭakaṃ na parimuṃcati tasya geham \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O mother, if anyone retains in his heart the pair of your feet free from impurities, the entire universe is within the grasp of his hands. If, O Maṅgalā-Gaurī, anyone repeats your name everyday, the eight Siddhis never leave his house.

## \|\| 1.49.61 \|\|

*tvaṃ devi vedajananī praṇavasvarūpā gāyatryasi tvamasi vai dvijakāmadhenuḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ vyāhṛtitrayamihā'khilakarmasiddhyai svāhāsvadhāsi sumanaḥ pitṛtṛptihetuḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O goddess, you are of the form of Praṇava, the mother of Vedas; you are Gāyatrī; you are the wish-yielding cow of the twice-borns. You are the three Vyāhṛtis (Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ) here for the fulfilment of all Karmas. You are Svāhā, the giver of the satisfaction to Devas, and Svadhā, the giver of satisfaction to Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.49.62 \|\|

*gauri tvameva śaśimaulini vedhasi tvaṃ sāvitryasi tvamasi cakriṇi cārulakṣmīḥ \|*  
*kāśyāṃ tvamasyamalarūpiṇi mokṣalakṣmīstvaṃ me śaraṇyamiha maṃgalagauri mātaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O Goddess, O mother, you are Gaurī in respect to the Moon-crested Lord; you are Sāvitrī in respect to Vedhas (Brahmā); you are the charming Lakṣmī in respect to the Discus-bearing Lord Viṣṇu. O fine-featured goddess, you, the glory of salvation in Kāśī, O Maṅgalā-Gaurī, you are my refuge.

## \|\| 1.49.63 \|\|

*stutveti tāṃ smaraharārdhaśarīraśobhāṃ śrīmaṃgalāṣṭaka mahāstavanena bhānuḥ \|*  
*devīṃ ca devamasakṛtparitaḥ praṇamya tūṣṇīṃ babhūva savitā śivayoḥ purastāt \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. After eulogizing the goddess who is the splendour of half of Śiva’s body, through the great prayer called Śrī Maṅgalāṣṭaka, the Sun circumambulated the goddess and the Lord many times, bowed down and stood silent in front of Śiva and Śivā.

## \|\| 1.49.64 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhadraṃ te prasannosmi mahāmate \|*  
*mitramannetrago nityaṃ prapaśye taccarācaram \|\| 64 \|\|*

The Lord of Devas said:

64\. Rise up, rise up. Welfare unto you, O highly intelligent one, O Mitra, I am delighted. You are always present in my eye. I see the mobile and immobile beings (through you).

## \|\| 1.49.65 \|\|

*mama mūrtirbhavānsūrya sarvajño bhava sarvagaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ mahasāṃ rāśiḥ sarveṣāṃ sarvakarmavit \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Sūrya, you are my cosmic form. Be omniscient and omnipresent, the mass of all splendours, the knower of all the activities of everyone.

## \|\| 1.49.66-76 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ sarvaduḥkhāni bhaktānāṃ tvaṃ nirākuru \|*  
*tvayā nāmnāṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā yadaṣṭakamudīritam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*anena māṃ pariṣṭutya naro madbhaktimāpsyati \|*  
*aṣṭakaṃ maṃgalāgauryā maṃgalāṣṭakasaṃjñakam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*anena maṃgalāgaurīṃ stutvā maṃgalamāpsyati \|*  
*catuḥṣaṣṭyaṣṭakaṃ stotraṃ maṃgalāṣṭakameva ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

*etatstotravaraṃ puṇyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*dūradeśāṃtarasthopi japannityaṃ narottamaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*trisaṃdhyaṃ pariśuddhātmā kāśīṃ prāpsyati durlabhām \|*  
*anena stotrayugmena japtena pratyahaṃ nṛbhiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*dhruvadainaṃdinaṃ pāpaṃ kṣālitaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*na tasya dehino dehe jātu citkilbiṣasthitiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*trikālaṃ yojayennityametatstotradvayaṃśubham \|*  
*kiṃjaptairbahubhiḥ stotraiścaṃcalaśrīpradairnṛṇām \|\| 72 \|\|*

*etatstotradvayaṃ dadyātkāśyāṃ naiḥśreyasīṃ śriyam \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena mānavairmokṣakāṃkṣibhiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*etatstotradvayaṃ japyaṃ tyaktvā stotrāṇyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*prapaṃca āvayoreva sarva eṣa carācaraḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tadāvayoḥstavādasmānniṣprapaṃco jano bhavet \|*  
*samṛddhimāpya mahatīṃ putrapautravatīmiha \|\| 75 \|\|*

*aṃte nirvāṇamāpnoti japanstotramidaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*anyacca śṛṇu saptāśva graharāja divākara \|\| 76 \|\|*

66-69a. You will dispel all the miseries of all the devotees. With my sixty-four names, you have uttered a prayer of eight verses. Any man will attain excellent devotion unto me by eulogizing me with this prayer. The eight verses of the prayer of Maṅgalāgaurī will be known as Maṅgalāṣṭaka. By eulogizing Maṅgalāgaurī with this prayer, one will acquire auspiciousness. The octave containing sixty-four names and this Maṅgalāṣṭaka are holy excellent prayers destructive of all sins.

69b-74a. Any excellent man in exile in far-off lands should repeat this thrice everyday. He shall become purified in soul and will attain Kāśī very rarely obtained. If these two prayers are repeated everyday by men, all their sins incurred everyday will be washed. There is no doubt about this. In the body of that embodied one no sin can stay, the one who repeats this splendid pair of hymns thrice a day always. Of what avail are the many prayers that could only grant transient glories to the men on being repeated? This pair of prayers shall accord the glory of salvation in Kāśī. Hence these two prayers should be assiduously repeated by men desirous of salvation by eschewing many other hymns.

74b-76. All this Prapañca (world) consisting of mobile and immobile beings, has evolved from us both. Hence by means of this eulogy of ours, people can be rid of the Prapañca. After attaining great prosperity along with sons and grandsons, the man who repeats this prayer acquires salvation in the end, O Saptāśva (‘one having seven horses’). O Divākara, the king of Planets, listen to something more.

## \|\| 1.49.77-86 \|\|

*tvayā pratiṣṭhitaṃ liṃgaṃ gabhastīśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*sevitaṃ bhaktibhāvena sarvasiddhisamarpakam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tvayā gabhastimālābhiścāṃpeyāṃbujakāṃtibhiḥ \|*  
*yadarcitvaiśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ sarvabhāvena bhāskara \|\| 78 \|\|*

*gabhastīśvara ityākhyāṃ tato liṃgamavāpsyati \|*  
*arcayitvā gabhastīśaṃ snātvā paṃcanade naraḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*na jātu jāyate māturjaṭhare dhūtakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*imāṃ ca maṃgalāgaurīṃ nārī vā puruṣopi vā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*caitraśuklatṛtīyāyāmupoṣaṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*mahopacāraiḥ saṃpūjya dukūlābharaṇādibhiḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā gītanṛtyakathādibhiḥ \|*  
*prātaḥ kumārīḥ saṃpūjya dvādaśācchādanādibhiḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*saṃbhojyaparamānnādyairdattvānyebhyopi dakṣiṇām \|*  
*homaṃ kṛtvā vidhānena jātavedasa ityṛcā \|\| 83 \|\|*

*aṣṭottaraśatābhiśca tilājyāhutibhiḥ prage \|*  
*ekaṃ gomithunaṃ dattvā brāhmaṇāya kuṭuṃbine \|\| 84 \|\|*

*śraddhayā samalaṃkṛtya bhūṣaṇairdvijadaṃpatī \|*  
*bhojayitvā mahārhānnaiḥ prīyetāṃ maṃgaleśvarau \|\| 85 \|\|*

*iti maṃtraṃ samuccārya prātaḥ kṛtvātha pāraṇam \|*  
*na durbhagatvamāpnoti na dāridryaṃ kadācana \|\| 86 \|\|*

77-80a. The Liṅga named Gabhastīśvara has been installed by you and served with devotional fervour. It will yield all Siddhis. The Liṅga will get the name Gabhastīśvara, O Sun, because the Liṅga of the Lord has been devoutly worshipped by you through clusters of rays having the lustre of Caṃpaka and lotuses. If a man takes his holy bath in Pañcanaḍa and adores Gabhastīśvara, he becomes rid of all sins. He is never born in any mother’s womb.

80b-86. Any devotee, man or woman, should worship Maṅgalāgaurī in the following manner. Fast is observed on the third lunar day in the bright half of Caitra. The deity is worshipped with all great means of services, silk clothes, ornaments etc. The devotee keeps awake in the night through dances, songs and holy discourses and the like. The next morning, twelve virgins are to be honoured with coverings (clothes) etc. They must be fed with excellent, sweet, cooked food. Others should be one given monetary gifts, accompanied by recitation of the Mantra beginning with Jātavedas (TA 1.18.1). In the dawn, there should be one hundred and eight Tila-Ājya Āhutis (offerings of gingelly seed and ghee into the fire). To a Brāhmaṇa burdened with a family, a pair of cows (or bulls) should be offered. A Brāhmaṇa couple should be embellished with ornaments faithfully and fed with rich, cooked foodstuffs accompained by uttering the recitation of the Mantra “May Maṅgalā and Īśvara be pleased”. The devotee breaks fast in the morning. This devotee never incurs wretchedness or poverty.

## \|\| 1.49.87 \|\|

*na vai saṃtānavicchittiṃ bhogocchittiṃ na jātucit \|*  
*strī vaidhavyaṃ na cāpnoti na nāyoṣidviyogabhāk \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. He never meets with break in the line of progeny. He never faces cessation of pleasures and enjoyments. The woman never attains widowhood. Nor does the man become separated from his wife.

## \|\| 1.49.88 \|\|

*pāpāni vilayaṃ yāṃti puṇyarāśiśca labhyate \|*  
*api vaṃdhyā prasūyeta kṛtvaitanmaṃgalāvratam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. All the sins become extinct. Heaps of Merits are acquired. Even a barren lady begets child after performing this Maṅgalāvrata.

## \|\| 1.49.89 \|\|

*etadvratasya karaṇātkurūpatvaṃ na jātucit \|*  
*kumārī viṃdatetyaṃtaṃ guṇarūpayutaṃ patim \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Ugliness in form can always be warded off by performing this Vrata. A virgin gets a husband equipped with excellent qualities and handsome features.

## \|\| 1.49.90-93 \|\|

*kumāropi vrataṃ kṛtvā viṃdati striyamuttamām \|*  
*saṃti vratāni bahuśo dhanakāmapradāni ca \|\| 90 \|\|*

*nāpnuyurjātucittāni maṃgalāvratatulyatām \|*  
*kartavyā cābdikī yātrā madhau tasyāṃ tithau naraiḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*sarvavighnapraśāṃtyarthaṃ sadā kāśīnivāsibhiḥ \|*  
*aparaṃ dyumaṇe vacmi tava cātra tapasyataḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*mayūkhā eva khe dṛṣṭā na ca dṛṣṭaṃ kalevaram \|*  
*mayūkhāditya ityākhyā tataste ditinaṃdana \|\| 93 \|\|*

90-93. A bachelor gets an excellent wife after performing this Vrata. There are many Vratas according riches and desires. But they will never be on a par with Maṅgalāvrata. The annual pilgrimage should be performed on that lunar day (third day in the bright half) in the month of Madhu by the men residing in Kāśī for the sake of subduing all obstacles. O Dyumaṇi (Sun-god), I shall mention another thing. While you were performing penance only the rays were seen and not your body. Hence, O son of Aditi, your name shall be Mayūkhāditya.

## \|\| 1.49.94 \|\|

*tvadarcanānnṛṇāṃ kaścinna vyādhiḥ prabhaviṣyati \|*  
*bhaviṣyati na dāridryaṃ ravivāre tvadīkṣaṇāt \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. If you are adored, no sickness can afflict men. If you are visited on Sundays no one will incur poverty.

## \|\| 1.49.95 \|\|

*itthaṃ mayūkhādityasya śivo dattvā bahūnvarān \|*  
*tatraivāṃtarhito bhūto ravistatraiva tasthivān \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. After granting many boons to Mayūkhāditya thus, Śiva vanished there and the Sun stood there itself.

## \|\| 1.49.96 \|\|

*śrutvākhyānamidaṃ puṇyaṃ mayūkhādityasaṃśrayam \|*  
*draupadādityasahitaṃ naro na nirayaṃ vrajet \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. If a man listens to this meritorious narrative of Mayūkhāditya along with that of Draupadāditya, he shall never go to hell.

## Chapter 50 - Description of Khakholkāditya

## \|\| 1.50.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ tathādityā ye cānye tānvadāmyataḥ \|*  
*kalaśodbhava te prītyā sarve sarvāghanāśanāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The story of rivalry between Kadrū and Vinatā and Garuḍa’s exploit is based on Mbh, Ādi, Chs. 20-34.—The deity Khakholkāditya is now in Kāmeśvara Temple. (BCL 362).

Skanda said:

1\. O Pot-born One, there are other Ādityas also in Vārāṇasī. Henceforth, I shall gladly describe them to you. All of them are destroyers of all sins.

## \|\| 1.50.2 \|\|

*khakholko nāma bhagavānāditya parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*triviṣṭapottare bhāge sarvavyādhivighātakṛt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Āditya deity to the north Triviṣṭapa (the shrine of Śiva) is glorified by the name Khakholka (or Khaṣolka). He is the destroyer of all ailments.

## \|\| 1.50.3-4 \|\|

*yathā khakholka ityākhyā tasyādityasya tacchṛṇu \|*  
*purā kadrūśca vinatā dakṣasya tanaye śubhe \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kaśyapasya ca te patnyau mārīceḥ prākprajāpateḥ \|*  
*krīḍaṃtyāvekadānyonyaṃ mune te ūcatustviti \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Listen how the name Khakholka was attained by that Āditya. Two splendid daughters of Dakṣa, Kadrū and Vinatā, became wives of Kaśyapa, son of Marīci and a fromer Prajāpati (Patriarch). Once, while they were playing together, O sage, they said thus:

## \|\| 1.50.5 \|\|

*kadrūruvāca \|*  
*vinate tvaṃ vijānāsi yadi tadbrūhi megrataḥ \|*  
*akhaṃḍitā gatistesti yato gaganamaṃḍale \|\| 5 \|\|*

Kadrū said:

5\. O Vinatā, if you know, tell it to me as you have unobstructed movement in the firmament.

## \|\| 1.50.6 \|\|

*yosāvuccaiḥśravā vājī śrūyate savitūrathe \|*  
*kiṃ rūpaḥsosti śabalo dhavalo vā vadāśu me \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. We hear that there is a horse named Uccaiśśravā in the chariot of Savitṛ (Sun). Tell me quickly whether it is white in colour or variegated.

## \|\| 1.50.7 \|\|

*paṇaṃ ca kuru kalyāṇi tubhyaṃ yo rocatenaghe \|*  
*evameva na yātyeṣa kālakrīḍanakaṃ vinā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O auspicious lady, O sinless one, bet a wager on this, whatever you like. Time cannot pass this way alone without some pastime.

## \|\| 1.50.8 \|\|

*vinatovāca \|*  
*kiṃ paṇena bhaginyatra kathayāmyevameva hi \|*  
*tvajjaye kā ca me prītirmajjaye kiṃ nu te sukham \|\| 8 \|\|*

Vinatā said:

8\. O my sister, what is the necessity of betting in this regard? I shall speak simply (without bet). What pleasure can I have, if you win? What joy will you have, in case I win?

## \|\| 1.50.9 \|\|

*jñātvā paṇo na kartavyo mithaḥ snehamabhīpsatā \|*  
*dhruvamekasya vijaye krodhonsyeha jāyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Knowingly no one should bet a wager, if mutual friendship is desired. Certainly, at the victory of one, the other-will get infuriated.

## \|\| 1.50.10 \|\|

*kadrūruvāca \|*  
*krīḍeyaṃ nātra bhagini kāraṇaṃ kimapi krudhaḥ \|*  
*khelasya vyavahāroyaṃ paṇe yatkiṃciducyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

Kadrū said:

10\. O dear sister, this is only a play. There is no cause for anger in this. This is only a playful transaction and something is mentioned in regard to the wager.

## \|\| 1.50.11 \|\|

*vinatovāca \|*  
*tathā kuru yathā prītistavāsti pavanāśini \|*  
*atha tāṃ vinatāmāha kadrūḥ kuṭilamānasā \|\| 11 \|\|*

Vinatā said:

11\. O serpentess! Do as you please.

Therupon Kadrū of a crooked mind, said to Vinatā:

## \|\| 1.50.12 \|\|

*tasyāstu sā bhaveddāsī parājīyeta yā yayā \|*  
*asminpaṇe imāḥ sarvāḥ sakhyaḥ sākṣiṇya eva nau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “She who is defeated shall become the slave of her by whom she is defeated. In this matter of wager all these friends of ours are the witnesses.”

## \|\| 1.50.13 \|\|

*ityanyonyaṃ paṇīkṛtya sarpiṇyapi patattriṇī \|*  
*uvāca karburaṃ kadrūraśvaṃ śvetaṃ garutmatī \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When the serpentess and the bird betted the wager thus, Kadrū said that the horse was variegated in colour and the winged one (Vinatā) told that it was white.

## \|\| 1.50.14 \|\|

*kadāgaṃtavyamiti ca cakrāte te gamāvadhim \|*  
*jagmatuśca viramyātha krīḍanātsvasvamālayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. They both fixed the time when they should go. Thereafter, they stopped their play and went to their respective bodes.

## \|\| 1.50.15-18 \|\|

*vinatāyāṃ gatāyāṃ tu kadrūrāhūya cāṃgajān \|*  
*uvāca yāta vai putrā drutaṃ vacanato mama \|\| 15 \|\|*

*turaṃgamuccaiḥśravasaṃ prodbhūtaṃ kṣīranīradheḥ \|*  
*surāsurairmathyamānānmaṃdarāghātasādhvasāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kāryakāraṇarūpasya sādṛśyamadhigacchati \|*  
*atastaṃ kṣīravarṇābhaṃ kalmāṣayata putrakāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tasya vāladhimadhyāsya kṛṣṇakuṃtalatāṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*tathā tadaṃgalomāni vidhattaviṣasītkṛtaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. When Vintatā had gone away, Kadrū called her sons and said: “My sons, at my behest all of you go quickly. Go quickly to the horse Uccaiśśravas that had come out of the Milk Ocean that was being churned and being agitated by Mandara hitting it.

An effect gets the features similar to those of the cause. Hence it has the colour of milk. Dear sons, make it dark in colour. Occupy its tail and assume the form of dark hairs. Make the hairs too on its body dark by means of poisonous puffs of air.”

## \|\| 1.50.19 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vaco mātuḥ kādraveyāḥ parasparam \|*  
*saṃmaṃtrya mātaraṃ procuḥ kadrūṃ kadrūpamāgatāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On hearing these words of their mother, the sons of Kadrū consulted one another. Becoming furious, they told their mother:

## \|\| 1.50.20 \|\|

*nāgā ūcuḥ \|*  
*mātarvayaṃ tvadāhvānādvihāya krīḍanaṃ balāt \|*  
*prāptāḥ prahṛṣṭā mṛṣṭānnaṃ dāsyatyadya prasūriti \|\| 20 \|\|*

The Serpents said:

20\. Mother, when you called us, we left our games and came here delighted that our mother will give us sweets to eat.

## \|\| 1.50.21 \|\|

*mṛṣṭaṃ tiṣṭhatu taddūraṃ viṣādapyadhikaṃ kaṭu \|*  
*tattvayā vādiyanmaṃtrairauṣadhairnopaśāmyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Far from giving sweets, you have uttered what is more caustic than even poison. This is not going to be subdued either by Mantras or by medicines.

## \|\| 1.50.22 \|\|

*vayaṃ na yāmo yadbhāvyaṃ tadasmākaṃ bhavatviha \|*  
*iti proktaṃ viṣāsyaistaistadā kuṭilagāmibhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. We are not going. Let anything befall us.

This was uttered by those poison-mouthed, crooked-gaited ones.

## \|\| 1.50.23-24 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*anyepi ye kuṭilagāḥ pararaṃdhraniṣeviṇaḥ \|*  
*akarṇāḥ kūrahṛdayāḥ pitarau vrīḍayaṃti te \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pitrorgiraṃ nirākṛtya ye tiṣṭheyuḥ sudurmadāḥ \|*  
*atyāhitamiha prāpya gaccheyuste'cirāllayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

Skanda said:

23-24. There are others too with crooked gaits and cruel hearts who make their parents ashamed. They resort to (take advantage of) the loopholes of others. They don’t pay heed. They set at nought the words of their parents and remain highly arrogant. Such ones will court great danger here and ere long will perish.

## \|\| 1.50.25 \|\|

*teṣāṃ vacanamākarṇya nayāma iti soragī \|*  
*śaśāpa tānkrudhāviṣṭā nāgāṃścāgaḥ samāgatān \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing the words (of her sons), “We are not going”, the serpentess became angry and cursed them—the serpents who had committed an offence (of disobedience).

## \|\| 1.50.26 \|\|

*tārkṣyasya bhakṣyā bhavata yūyaṃ madvākyalaṃghanāt \|*  
*jātamātrāśca sarpiṇyo bhakṣayaṃtu svabālakān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “Because you have transgressed my words, you will become prey unto Tārkṣya. Let all female serpents eat their young ones immediately after the birth.”

## \|\| 1.50.27 \|\|

*iti śāpānalādbhītaiḥ kaiścitpātālamāśritam \|*  
*jijīviṣubhiranyaiśca dvitraiścakre prasūvacaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The nether worlds were resorted to by some of them who were afraid of the fire of curse. The behest of the mother was carried out by a few who were eager to be alive.

## \|\| 1.50.28 \|\|

*te pucchamauccaiḥśravasamadhigamya mahādhiyaḥ \|*  
*sunīlacikurābhāsaṃ cakruraṃgaṃ ca karburam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Those extremely sensible ones got on to the tail of Uccaiśśravas and made it resemble one with very dark hairs. They made its body variegated in colour.

## \|\| 1.50.29 \|\|

*tatkṣveḍānala dhūmaughaiḥ phūtkārabharaniḥsṛtaiḥ \|*  
*mātṛvākkṛtijāddharmānna dagdhā bhānubhānubhiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. It was brought about by the columns of smoke of their poisonous fire augmented by puffs and sighs issuing forth. They were not burnt by the rays of the Sun because of the merit of carrying out the behest of their mother.

## \|\| 1.50.30 \|\|

*vinatāpṛṣṭhamāruhya kadrūḥ snehavaśāttataḥ \|*  
*viyanmārgamalaṃkṛtya dadarśoṣṇāṃśumaṃḍalam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then out of affection, Kadrū got on to the back of Vinatā and went by the path of the sky. She saw then the solar disc.

## \|\| 1.50.31-34 \|\|

*tigmaraśmiprabhāveṇa vyākulībhūtamānasā \|*  
*kadrustataḥ khagīṃ prāha visrabdhaṃ vinate vraja \|\| 31 \|\|*

*uṣṇagoruṣṇagobhirme tāpyate nitarāṃ tanuḥ \|*  
*visrabdhāhaṃ svabhāvena tvaṃ sāpekṣāhi sarvataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*svarūpeṇa pataṃgī tvaṃ pataṃgosau sahasraguḥ \|*  
*ataeva na te bādhā gagane tāpasaṃbhavā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*viyatsarasi haṃsoyaṃ bhavatī haṃsagāminī \|*  
*caṃḍaraśmipratāpāgnistvāmato neha bādhate \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. Kadrū then became excessively agitated in her mind due to the ferocity of the Sun. She told the bird: “O Vinatā, proceed gingerly. My body is extremly scorched by the hot rays of the Sun. I am cautious by nature and you are wholly hopeful (sāpekṣā?). You are Pataṅgī in form and the Sun is also Pataṅga (a flier). Hence you do not have any affliction in the sky arising from scorching heat. This Sun is a Haṃsa (Swan) in the lake of the sky. You are one with the gait of a Swan. Hence the fierce fire of the hot-rayed Sun does not harm you.”

## \|\| 1.50.35-57 \|\|

*khagīmudgīyamānāṃ khe punarūce bileśayā \|*  
*trāhitrāhi bhaginyatra yāvonyatra viyatpathaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vinate vinatāṃ māṃ tvaṃ kiṃ nāvasi patattriṇī \|*  
*tava dāsī bhaviṣyāmi tvaducchiṣṭaniṣeviṇī \|\| 36 \|\|*

*yāvajjīvamahaṃ bhūyāṃ tvatpādodakapāyinī \|*  
*khakholkāni patedeṣā bhṛśagadgadabhāṣiṇī \|\| 37 \|\|*

*mūrcchāṃ gatavatī pakṣapuṭau dhṛtvā biḍoragī \|*  
*sakhyulkāni patedeṣā vaktavye tviti saṃbhramāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

*khakholketi yaduktā gīḥ kadrvā saṃbhrātacetasā \|*  
*tadā khakholkanāmārkaḥ stuto vinatayā bahu \|\| 39 \|\|*

*manāgatigmatāṃ prāpte khe prayāti vivasvati \|*  
*tābhyāṃ turaṃgamo darśi kiṃcitkirmīravānrathe \|\| 40 \|\|*

*uktā vinatayaivaiṣā tāpopahatalocanā \|*  
*krūrā sarīsṛpī satyavādinyā viśvamānyayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kadru tvayā jitaṃ bhadre yata uccaiḥśravā hayaḥ \|*  
*caṃdraraśmiprabhopyeṣa kalmāṣa iva bhāsate \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vidhirbalīyānbhujagi citraṃ jayaparājaye \|*  
*krūropi vijayī kvāpi tvakrūropi parājayī \|\| 43 \|\|*

*vinatāvinatādhārā vadaṃtīti yathāgatam \|*  
*kadrūniveśanaṃ prāptā tasyā dāsyamacīkarat \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kadācidvinatādarśi suparṇanāśrulocanā \|*  
*vicchāyā malinā dīnā dīrghaniḥśvāsavatyapi \|\| 45 \|\|*

*suparṇa uvāca \|*  
*prātaḥprātaraho mātaḥ kva yāsi tvaṃ dinedine \|*  
*sāyamāyāsi ca kuto vicchāyā dīnamānasā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kuto niḥśvasisi proccairaśrupūrṇa vilocanā \|*  
*yathā klībasutā yoṣidyathāpati tiraskṛtā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*brūhi mātarjhaṭityadya kuto dūnāsi pattriṇi \|*  
*mayi jīvati te bāle kālepi kṛtasādhvase \|\| 48 \|\|*

*aśrunirmāṇakaraṇe kāraṇaṃ kiṃ tapasvini \|*  
*sucaritrā sunārīṣu nāmaṃgalamiheṣyate \|\| 49 \|\|*

*dhiktāṃśca putrānyanmātā teṣu jīvatsu duḥkhabhāk \|*  
*varaṃ vaṃdhyaiva sā yasyāḥ sutā vaṃdhyamanorathāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*ityūrjasvalamākarṇya vacaḥ sūnorgarutmataḥ \|*  
*vinatā prāha taṃ putraṃ mātṛbhaktisamanvitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ahaṃ dāsyasmi re bāla kadrvāśca krūracetasaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭhe vahāmi tāṃ nityaṃ tatputrānapi putraka \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kadācinmaṃdaraṃ yāmi kadācinmalayācalam \|*  
*kadācidaṃtarīpeṣu careyaṃ tadudanvatām \|\| 53 \|\|*

*yatrayatra nayeyuste kādraveyāḥ sudurmadāḥ \|*  
*vrajeyaṃ tatratatrāhaṃ tadadhīnā yataḥ suta \|\| 54 \|\|*

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*dāsītvakāraṇaṃ mātaḥ kiṃ te jātaṃ sulakṣaṇe \|*  
*dakṣaprajāpateḥ putri kaśyapasyapriye'naghe \|\| 55 \|\|*

*vinatovāca garuḍaṃ purāvṛttamaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dāsītvakāraṇaṃ yadvadādityāśvavilokanam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*śrutveti garuḍaḥ prāha mātaraṃ satvaraṃ vraja \|*  
*pṛcchādya mātastānduṣṭānkādraveyānidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

35-57. Again the serpentess said to the bird about to fly high in the sky, “Sister, save me, save me. We shall go away from the path of the sky. O Vinatā, why don’t you protect me, humble that I am? You are a bird. I shall be your slave taking in what you leave off after eating. I shall drink the water washing your feet as long as I live.”

## \|\| 1.50.38 \|\|

*mūrcchāṃ gatavatī pakṣapuṭau dhṛtvā biḍoragī \|*  
*sakhyulkāni patedeṣā vaktavye tviti saṃbhramāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The serpentess then went into a swoon taking hold of the wings (of Vinatā). Where she ought to have said “O friend, a firebrand is about to fall”, she became agitated and very falteringly said, “Khakholka may fall”.

## \|\| 1.50.39 \|\|

*khakholketi yaduktā gīḥ kadrvā saṃbhrātacetasā \|*  
*tadā khakholkanāmārkaḥ stuto vinatayā bahu \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Since the word Khakholka was uttered by Kadrū whose mind was extremely agitated, the Sun was diversely eulogized by Vinatā in the name of Khakholka.

## \|\| 1.50.40 \|\|

*manāgatigmatāṃ prāpte khe prayāti vivasvati \|*  
*tābhyāṃ turaṃgamo darśi kiṃcitkirmīravānrathe \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. While the Sun proceeded along the sky, he became slightly cool. Then the horse fitted to the chariot was seen slightly dark in colour.

## \|\| 1.50.41 \|\|

*uktā vinatayaivaiṣā tāpopahatalocanā \|*  
*krūrā sarīsṛpī satyavādinyā viśvamānyayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The cruel serpentess whose eyes were bedevilled by the heat, was then told by Vinatā who was worthy of being honoured by the world and who spoke the truth:

## \|\| 1.50.42-43 \|\|

*kadru tvayā jitaṃ bhadre yata uccaiḥśravā hayaḥ \|*  
*caṃdraraśmiprabhopyeṣa kalmāṣa iva bhāsate \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vidhirbalīyānbhujagi citraṃ jayaparājaye \|*  
*krūropi vijayī kvāpi tvakrūropi parājayī \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. “O gentle Kṛdrū, you have won. Though the horse Uccaiśśravas has the lustre of the rays of the moon, it appears as though it is dark-complexioned.

It is wonderful, O serpentess, that fate is all-powerful in regard to the matters of victory and defeat. The cruel one becomes victorious somewhere and the mild one too becomes the vanquished.”

## \|\| 1.50.44 \|\|

*vinatāvinatādhārā vadaṃtīti yathāgatam \|*  
*kadrūniveśanaṃ prāptā tasyā dāsyamacīkarat \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Vinatā, the receptacle of humility, said thus as they proceeded ahead. After reaching the abode of Kadrū, she became her slave.

## \|\| 1.50.45 \|\|

*kadācidvinatādarśi suparṇanāśrulocanā \|*  
*vicchāyā malinā dīnā dīrghaniḥśvāsavatyapi \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Once Vinatā was seen with her eyes filled with tears by Suparṇa (Garuḍa). She was in a wretched condition without the facial colour and purity. She was sighing deeply.

## \|\| 1.50.46-50 \|\|

*suparṇa uvāca \|*  
*prātaḥprātaraho mātaḥ kva yāsi tvaṃ dinedine \|*  
*sāyamāyāsi ca kuto vicchāyā dīnamānasā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kuto niḥśvasisi proccairaśrupūrṇa vilocanā \|*  
*yathā klībasutā yoṣidyathāpati tiraskṛtā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*brūhi mātarjhaṭityadya kuto dūnāsi pattriṇi \|*  
*mayi jīvati te bāle kālepi kṛtasādhvase \|\| 48 \|\|*

*aśrunirmāṇakaraṇe kāraṇaṃ kiṃ tapasvini \|*  
*sucaritrā sunārīṣu nāmaṃgalamiheṣyate \|\| 49 \|\|*

*dhiktāṃśca putrānyanmātā teṣu jīvatsu duḥkhabhāk \|*  
*varaṃ vaṃdhyaiva sā yasyāḥ sutā vaṃdhyamanorathāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

46-50. “Alas, my mother, where do you go in the morning everyday and return in the evening, pale and afflicted in mind?

Wherefor do you sigh deeply with the eyes full of tears like a woman whose sons are impotent and who has been discarded by her husband.

O mother, O winged one, tell me quickly why you are very vexed even as I, your child, am alive, I who have terrified even Kāla (god of Death).

O lady in a pitiable codition! What is the cause of your shedding tears? Nothing inauspicious is expected in a woman of excellent conduct.

Fie upon those sons whose mother is miserable even as they are alive! It would rather be better that she whose sons are ineffective in their ambitions, remain barren and childless.”

## \|\| 1.50.51 \|\|

*ityūrjasvalamākarṇya vacaḥ sūnorgarutmataḥ \|*  
*vinatā prāha taṃ putraṃ mātṛbhaktisamanvitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On hearing these forceful words of Garuḍa, her son, Vinatā spoke to the son who was full of devotion to his mother:

## \|\| 1.50.52-54 \|\|

*ahaṃ dāsyasmi re bāla kadrvāśca krūracetasaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭhe vahāmi tāṃ nityaṃ tatputrānapi putraka \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kadācinmaṃdaraṃ yāmi kadācinmalayācalam \|*  
*kadācidaṃtarīpeṣu careyaṃ tadudanvatām \|\| 53 \|\|*

*yatrayatra nayeyuste kādraveyāḥ sudurmadāḥ \|*  
*vrajeyaṃ tatratatrāhaṃ tadadhīnā yataḥ suta \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. “O my son, I am the slave of Kadrū of cruel mentality. O my son, everyday I bear her and her sons too on my back. Sometimes I go to Mandara, sometimes to Malaya mountain and sometimes to an island with lakes in the famous oceans. Wherever the haughty sons of Kadrū take me I too go, O son, because I am a slave unto them.”

## \|\| 1.50.55 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*dāsītvakāraṇaṃ mātaḥ kiṃ te jātaṃ sulakṣaṇe \|*  
*dakṣaprajāpateḥ putri kaśyapasyapriye'naghe \|\| 55 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

55\. Oh daughter of Dakṣaprajāpati! O sinless beloved of Kaśyapa! O mother of excellent features, what is the cause of your slavery?

## \|\| 1.50.56 \|\|

*vinatovāca garuḍaṃ purāvṛttamaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dāsītvakāraṇaṃ yadvadādityāśvavilokanam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Vinatā related to Garuḍa all those previous events that brought about her slavery, along with the fact of seeing the horse of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.50.57-58 \|\|

*śrutveti garuḍaḥ prāha mātaraṃ satvaraṃ vraja \|*  
*pṛcchādya mātastānduṣṭānkādraveyānidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*yaddurlabhaṃ hi bhavatāṃ yatrātyaṃtaruciśca vaḥ \|*  
*maddāsītvavimokṣāya tadyācadhvaṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. On hearing this, Garuḍa told his mother: “Go quickly, dear mother, and ask those wicked sons of Kadrū in these words: ‘Whatever be the thing for which you have any great desire, even if it be very rare and difficult to be got, you can ask for it in lieu of redeeming me from slavery. I shall give it to you.’”

## \|\| 1.50.59 \|\|

*tathākarocca vinatā tepi śrutvā tadīritam \|*  
*sarpāḥ saṃmaṃtrya tāṃ procurvinatāṃ hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Vinatā did so. On hearing what was uttered by her, the serpents were delighted in their minds. They consulted one another and spoke to her:

## \|\| 1.50.60 \|\|

*mātṛśāpavimokṣāya yadi dāsyati naḥ sudhām \|*  
*tadā samīhitaṃ testu na dāsyatyatha dāsyasi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. “If, in order to remove the curse of our mother, he gives us heavenly nectar, you can have what you desire. If he does not give, you continue to be a slave.”

## \|\| 1.50.61 \|\|

*ityoṃkṛtya samāpṛcchya kadrūṃ drutagatiḥ khagī \|*  
*garutmaṃtaṃ samācaṣṭa dṛṣṭvā saṃhṛṣṭamānasam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Accepting that offer and taking leave of Kadrū, the bird of quick motion (Vinatā) saw Garuḍa who was glad in his mind and told him (everything).

## \|\| 1.50.62 \|\|

*nāgāṃtakastataḥ prāha mātaraṃ ciṃtayāturām \|*  
*ānītaṃ viddhi pīyūṣaṃ mātarme dehi bhojanam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The enemy of serpents then said to his mother who was excessively worried: “Mother, know that the heavenly nectar is already brought. Give me my food.”

## \|\| 1.50.63-67 \|\|

*vinatā prāha taṃ putraṃ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhā \|*  
*bhoḥ suparṇārṇavaṃ tūrṇaṃ yāhi maṃgalamastu te \|\| 63 \|\|*

*saṃti tatrāpi bahuśo niṣādā matsyaghātinaḥ \|*  
*velātaṭanivāsāśca tānbhakṣaya durātmanaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*paraprāṇairnijaprāṇānye puṣṇaṃtīha durdhiyaḥ \|*  
*śāsanīyāḥ prayatnena śreyastacchāsanaṃ param \|\| 65 \|\|*

*bahuhiṃsākṛtāṃ hiṃsā bhavetsvargasya sādhanam \|*  
*vihiṃsiteṣu duṣṭeṣu rakṣyate bhūriśo yataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*niṣādeṣvapi cedvipraḥ kaścidbhavati putraka \|*  
*saṃrakṣaṇīyo yatnena bhakṣaṇīyo na karhicit \|\| 67 \|\|*

63-67. Vinatā experienced horripilation due to joy and said to her son: “O Suparṇa, go to the ocean quickly. Good luck to you! There are many Niṣāda fishermen with their houses at the seashore. Eat those wicked-souled ones. Those evil-minded ones who live on others’ lives, should be chastised assiduously. Their chastisement is very much conducive to welfare. Violence done unto those who indulge in great violence shall be a means to the attainment of heaven, for people are protected when the wicked ones are killed. But, O son, if there is any Brāhmaṇa among those fish-killing Niṣādas, he should be assiduously protected. He is never to be eaten.”

## \|\| 1.50.68 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*matsyādināṃ vasanmadhye kathaṃ jñeyo dvijo mayā \|\| abhakṣyo yastvayā proktastaccihnaṃ kiṃ canāttha me \|\| 68 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

68\. How can a Brāhmaṇa residing among the fish-eating ones be known and recognized by me? Tell me some significant things about that person who is said by you as one who should not be eaten.

## \|\| 1.50.69-71 \|\|

*vinatovāca \|*  
*yajñasūtraṃ gale yasya sottarīyaṃ sunirmalam \|*  
*nityadhautāni vāsāṃsi bhālaṃ tilaka lāṃchitam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*sapavitrau karau yasya yannīvī kuśagarbhiṇī \|*  
*yanmauliḥ saśikhāgraṃthiḥ sa jñeyo brāhmaṇastvayā \|\| 70 \|\|*

*uccaredṛgyajuḥsāmnāmṛcamekāmapīha yaḥ \|*  
*gāyatrīmātramaṃtropi sa vijñeyo dvijastvayā \|\| 71 \|\|*

Vinatā said:

69-71. There is a sacred thread free from impurities round his neck along with the upper cloth. The clothes are washed everyday. The forehead is marked by a Tilaka. His hands have the Pavitra. The knot of his cloth keeps Kuśa grass within. His hairs do have a tuft. He is to be known as a Brāhmaṇa by you. He who recites at least one verse from Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman or he who recites the Gāyatrī Mantra should be known by you as a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.50.72-73 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*madhye sadā niṣādānāṃ yo vasejjanani dvijaḥ \|*  
*tasyaiteṣvekamapyeva na manye lakṣmabodhakam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*lakṣmāṃtaraṃ samācakṣva dvijabodhakaraṃ prasūḥ \|*  
*yena vijñāya taṃ vipraṃ tyajeyamapi kaṃṭhagam \|\| 73 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

72-73. O mother, I do not consider anyone of these things as a significant feature of a Brāhmaṇa who may be living for ever in the midst of the Niṣādas.

Dear mother, tell me another characteristic feature making him known as a Brāhmaṇa, whereby realizing him as a Brāhmaṇa I can free him, should he be caught in my throat.

## \|\| 1.50.74-75 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vinatā prāha yaste kaṃṭhagatoṃ'gaja \|*  
*khadirāṃgāravaddahyāttamapākuru dūrataḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*dvijamātrepi yā hiṃsā sā hiṃsā kuśalāya na \|*  
*deśaṃ vaṃśaṃ śriyaṃ svaṃ ca nirmūlayati kālataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. On hearing it, Vinatā said: “O my son, cast him off, the person who may scorch you like a burning Khadira charcoal when he is caught up in your throat.

The injury to any Brāhmaṇa is never conducive to welfare. In due course it annihilates the land, the family, the glory and the wealth.”

## \|\| 1.50.76 \|\|

*niśamya kāśyapiritiprasūpādaupraṇamya ca \|*  
*gṛhītāśīryayau śīghraṃ khamārgeṇa khageśvaraḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. On hearing this, the lord of the birds, the son of Kaśyapa, bowed down to the feet of his mother. After taking her blessings he quickly went by the aerial path.

## \|\| 1.50.77-78 \|\|

*dūrādālokayāṃcakre niṣādānmatsyajīvinaḥ \|*  
*pakṣau vidhūya pakṣīṃdro rajasāpūrya rodasī \|\| 77 \|\|*

*aṃdhīkṛtya diśobhāgānabdhirodhasyupāviśat \|*  
*vyādāya vadanaṃ ghoraṃ mahākaṃdarasannibham \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. He saw from a distance the Niṣādas who live on fish. The lord of the birds shook his wings, filled heaven and earth with dust particles. He blinded the various regions of the quarters and finally sat on the seashore opening his mouth widely like a huge cave.

## \|\| 1.50.79-81 \|\|

*kāṃdiśīkā niṣādāstu viviśustatra ca svayam \|*  
*manvāneṣvatha paṃthānaṃ teṣu kaṃṭhaṃ viśatsvapi \|\| 79 \|\|*

*jajvāleṃgalasaṃsparśo dvijastatkaṃṭhakaṃdalīm \|*  
*prākpraviṣṭānatho tārkṣyo niṣādānaudarīṃ darīm \|\| 80 \|\|*

*praveśya kaṃṭhatālusthaṃ taṃ vijñāya dvijasphuṭam \|*  
*bhayādudagirattūrṇaṃ mātṛvākyena yaṃtritaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

79-81. The Niṣādas who ran helter-skelter due to fear entered

his mouth themselves. While they were entering the throat considering it to be their own path, a certain Brāhmaṇa burned his cave-like throat with a scalding touch, like that of a burning charcoal. Thereupon Tārkṣya made those who had previously entered go into the cavity of his belly and realizing the person stationed in the throat and the palate to be a Brāhmaṇa quickly vomited him out, as he was checked by the words of his mother.

## \|\| 1.50.82 \|\|

*tamudgīrṇaṃ naraṃ dṛṣṭvā pakṣirāṭsamabhāṣata \|*  
*kastvaṃ jātyāsi nigada mama kaṃṭhavidāhakṛt \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. On seeing the man vomited out, the king of birds spoke, “Who are you by caste? You are burning my throat. Tell me.”

## \|\| 1.50.83 \|\|

*sa tadāheti viprohaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ sangaruḍāgrataḥ \|*  
*vasāmyeṣu niṣādeṣu jātimātropajīvakaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. On being asked, he spoke thus to Garuḍa: “I am a Brāhmaṇa. I live among these Niṣādas making use of my caste alone as sustenance.”

## \|\| 1.50.84 \|\|

*taṃ preṣya garuḍo dūraṃ bhakṣayitvātha bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*nabho vikṣobhayāṃcakre pralayānila sannibhaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. After sending him away and eating most of the others, Garuḍa, blowing like a violent gust of wind at the time of deluge, made the sky agitated.

## \|\| 1.50.85 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tigmatejaskaṃ jvālātatadigaṃtaram \|*  
*jvaladdāvānalaṃ śailamiva bibhyurdivaukasaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. On seeing him fiery with brilliance, enveloping the quarters with flames and appearing like a mountain with blazing forest fires, heaven-dwellers became afraid.

## \|\| 1.50.86 \|\|

*te sannahyaṃta yuddhāya sajjīkṛta balāyudhāḥ \|*  
*adhyāsya vāhanānyāśu sarve varmabhṛtaḥ surāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Making the armies and the weapons ready, mounting their respective vehicles and wearing the coats of mail, the Suras got ready for battle.

## \|\| 1.50.87-89 \|\|

*tiryaggatīravirnāyaṃ nāyamagniḥ sadhūmavān \|*  
*kṣaṇaprabhāpyasau naiva ko naḥ sammukha etyasau \|\| 87 \|\|*

*na daityeṣu prabhedṛksyānnākṛtirdānaveṣviyam \|*  
*mahāsādhvasadaḥ koyamasmākaṃ hṛtprakaṃpanaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*yāvatsaṃbhāvayaṃtīti nītijñā api nirjarāḥ \|*  
*tāvaddudhāva svau pakṣau pakṣirājo mahābalaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

87-89. The Devas well-versed in polity began to think: ‘This person is proceeding obliquely. Hence he is not the Sun. He is not fire which emits smoke (This person does not). He is not lightning (which is momentary). Who is this person who has come in front of us? Such a splendour is not to be found among Daityas. Such a form is not among Dānavas. Who is this that creates terror in us? He is making our heart tremble.’ Even as the Devas were puzzled thus, the king of birds of excessive strength shook his wings.

## \|\| 1.50.90 \|\|

*nipetuḥ pakṣavātena sāyudhāśca savāhanāḥ \|*  
*na jñāyaṃte kva saṃprāptā vātyayā pārṇatārṇavat \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Due to the gust of wind raised by his wings (those Suras) fell down along with their weapons and vehicles. It was not known where they were thrown like things made of leaves and grasses.

## \|\| 1.50.91 \|\|

*atha teṣu praṇaṣṭeṣu buddhyā vijñāya pakṣirāṭ \|*  
*kośāgāraṃ sudhāyāḥ sa tatrāpaśyacca rakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. When they had been destroyed, the king of birds pursued intelligently and found out the treasure house of nectar and also the guards thereof.

## \|\| 1.50.92 \|\|

*śastrāstrodyatapāṇīṃstānsurānādhūya sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa kartarīyaṃtramamṛtoparisaṃsthitam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. He made those Suras with raised weapons and missiles in their hands, scattered around. Thereafter he saw a mechanical device in the form of scissors placed above the nectar (-receptacle).

## \|\| 1.50.93 \|\|

*manaḥpavanavegena bhramamāṇaṃ mahārayam \|*  
*apispṛśaṃtaṃ maśakaṃ yatkhaṃḍayati koṭiśaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. It was moving rapidly with the speed of mind and wind. Even if a mosquito was to come into contact with it, it would be cut into millions of pieces.

## \|\| 1.50.94-100 \|\|

*upopaviśya pakṣīṃdrastasya yaṃtrasya nirbhayaḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ vicārayāmāsa kimatra karavāṇyaho \|\| 94 \|\|*

*spraṣṭuṃ na labhyate caitadvātyā na prabhavediha \|*  
*ka upāyotra kartavyo vṛthā jāto mamodyamaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*na balaṃ prabhavedatra na kiṃcidapi pauruṣam \|*  
*aho prayatno devānāmetatpīyūṣarakṣaṇe \|\| 96 \|\|*

*yadi me śaṃkare bhaktirnirdvaṃdvātīva niścalā \|*  
*tadā sa devadevo māṃ viyunaktu mahā'dhiyā \|\| 97 \|\|*

*yadyahaṃ mātṛbhaktosmi svāminaḥ śaṃkarādapi \|*  
*tadā me buddhiratrāstu pīyūṣaharaṇaṃ kṣamā \|\| 98 \|\|*

*ātmārthaṃ nodyamaścāyaṃ hṛtstho vettīti viśvagaḥ \|*  
*māturdāsyavimokṣāya yatehamamṛtaṃ prati \|\| 99 \|\|*

*jaritau pitarau yasya bālāpatyaśca yaḥ pumān \|*  
*sādhvī bhāryā ca tatpuṣṭyai doṣo'kṛtyepi tasya na \|\| 100 \|\|*

94-100. The lord of birds sat fearlessly near that machine and thought for a moment:

‘Oh! what shall I do here? It is not possible to touch this. Even the wind is not powerful enough in this regard. What means is to be employed? Alas, my effort has become fruitless.

Force cannot be effective here nor manliness. Wonderful indeed is the care and effort of Devas in regard to the security of the heavenly nectar.

If my devotion to Śaṅkara is undisputed and steady, may that Lord of Devas bless me with great presence of mind.

If I am devoted to my mother even more than to Śaṅkara. Let my keen intellect be capable of taking away the heavenly nectar.

This effort on my part is not for my own selfish ends. This that omnipresent Lord knows. I am endeavouring for the heavenly nectar to redeem my mother from slavery.

If one’s parents are pretty old, if one’s children are very young and if one’s wife is chaste and loyal, there is no harm even in one’s improper act for their sustenance.’

## \|\| 1.50.101-104 \|\|

*iti ciṃtayatastasya buddhirāsīnmahātmanaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*dehaṃ cakāra sotyaṃtamaṇīyāṃsamaṇorapi \|*  
*paramāṇusahasrāṃśaṃ kṛtvā rūpaṃ mahādbhutam \|\| 102 \|\|*

*praviśya kartarīyaṃtramadhodehasya lāghavāt \|*  
*bibhyattadyaṃtrato dehaṃ vaṃcayanvāyukhaṃḍanāt \|*  
*mūlamutpāṭya tarasā gṛhītvā'mṛtabhājanam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*niryayau pāvane mārge krośatsu svargasadmasu \|\| 104 \|\|*

101-104. Even as he thought thus, the noble-souled one had an idea. He made his form minuter than the minutest. He assumed a highly miraculous form, a thousandth of the size of an atom and entered the mechanical device of the scissors below, due to the minuteness of his body. He was afraid of the machine and saved his body from being cut even by the wind therefrom. He uprooted it quickly and seized the receptacle of the heavenly nectar. Even as the heaven-dwellers were shouting, he came out along the path of the wind.

## \|\| 1.50.105 \|\|

*tathā vaikuṃṭhanāthaṃ te gatvā procuḥ sudhābhujaḥ \|*  
*nirjitya nīyate cakrinsudhā no jīvitaṃ param \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The nectar-imbibers (Devas) went to the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha and said, “O Discus-bearing Lord, we are defeated and the nectar, our own very life, is being carried away.”

## \|\| 1.50.106-107 \|\|

*ityākarṇya haristebhyo'bhayaṃ dattvā tvarāyutaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā yuddhaṃ ca sumahadviṃśārkaghaṭikādvayam \|\| 106 \|\|*

*śuṃbhadevyoryathāsūta garuḍastatra cādhikaḥ \|*  
*tadā prasanno bhagavānmahāyuddhena sarvadaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

106-107. On hearing this Hari granted them freedom from fear. Hurriedly he fought with him (Garuḍa) a battle on a par with that of the demon Śuṃbha and the Goddess, O Sūta. The great battle lasted for sixty-four Ghaṭikās. Garuḍa was superior therein. The Lord, the bestower of everything, became pleased with the great battle.

## \|\| 1.50.108 \|\|

*gatvā garuḍamāhedaṃ prasannosmi khageśvara \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇīhi bhadraṃ te jitavṛṃdāravṛṃdaka \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. He went to Garuḍa and said, “O lord of birds, I am delighted. Welfare unto you, the conqueror of the group of Devas. Choose a boon.”

## \|\| 1.50.109 \|\|

*hasitvā garuḍaḥ prāha viśvarūpaṃ janārdanam \|*  
*ahameva prasannosmi tvaṃ prārthaya varadvayam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Garuḍa laughed and said to the omniformed Lord Janārdana, “I too am delighted. You can choose two boons.”

## \|\| 1.50.110 \|\|

*tataḥ kaiṭabhajitprāha vainateyaṃ mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*vṛtaṃvṛtaṃ mahodāra dehidehi varadvayam \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Thereupon the conqueror of Kaiṭabha delightfully said to the son of Vinatā, “O liberal-minded one, chosen, chosen. Grant me, grant me the two boons.”

## \|\| 1.50.111-112 \|\|

*iti viṣṇūditaṃ śrutvā prahasannāha pakṣirāṭ \|*  
*kiṃ vilaṃbena tadbrūhi dattaṃ dattaṃ varadvayam \|\| 111 \|\|*

*alabdhalābhe saṃjāte dyūtādi vijayodaye \|*  
*dātavyaṃ sudhiyāpātre sadā lābhajayau kva vā \|\| 112 \|\|*

111-112. On hearing these words utterd by Viṣṇu, the lord of birds laughingly said: “Of what avail is the delay? Hence tell me. The two boons are given, are given. Even if there is no acquisition of profit in a game of dice etc. attended with success and prosperity, a fair-minded one should give (the due) to the deserving one. How can one expect profit and successs always?”

## \|\| 1.50.113 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*balavānasi pakṣīṃdra tanme vāhanatāṃ vraja \|*  
*eko varoyaṃ varada dvitīyaṃ śṛṇu kāśyapa \|\| 113 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

113\. O lord of birds, you are strong. Hence be my vehicle. O gianter of boons, this is one of the boons. O son of Kaśyapa, listen to the second one.

## \|\| 1.50.114-115 \|\|

*darśayitvāmṛtaṃ prājña mātṛdāsyavimokṣakam \|*  
*dvijihvebhyaḥ kuru tathā drāgaśnaṃti na te yathā \|\| 114 \|\|*

*deyā sudhā sudhābhugbhyo dvitīyostu varo mama \|*  
*tatheti sa pratijñāya niryayau pakṣirāḍdivaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

114-115. O wise one, just show to the serpents the nectar brought for the redemption of your mother from slavery. Manage it in such a way that they do not eat it immediately. The heavenly nectar should be given to the Devas. Let this be my second boon.

The lord of birds promised, “So be it” and departed from heaven.

## \|\| 1.50.116-119 \|\|

*sa mātaraṃ vinirmocya dāsyātkāśyapanaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*nāgānāṃ purato dhṛtvā mahāmṛtakamaṃḍalum \|\| 116 \|\|*

*amṛtaṃ pātukāmāṃstānityācaṣṭa mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*nāgāḥ śucitvamāsādya bhoktavyaiṣā sudhā śubhā \|\| 117 \|\|*

*nocedaśucibhiḥ spṛṣṭā snānādi parivarjitaiḥ \|*  
*yāsyatyadṛśyatāmeṣā sudhā'nimiṣarakṣitā \|\| 118 \|\|*

*sāmānyamapi yadrakṣyaṃ spṛśyate'śucibhiḥ kvacit \|*  
*haraṃti tadrasaṃ devāstacca tiṣṭhati nīrasam \|\| 119 \|\|*

116-119. That son of Kaśyapa released his mother from slavery. He placed the great pot of the heavenly nectar in front of the serpents. The extremely intelligent one spoke to them as they were desirous of drinking the nectar: “O serpents, this splendid nectar should be swallowed after making yourselves clean (after bathing). If not, this nectar, well-preserved by the winkless ones (Devas), is likely to vanish when touched by unclean people devoid of bath etc. If, even an ordinary foodstuff is touched anywhere by unclean people the Devas take away its essential juice and it remains insipid,”

## \|\| 1.50.120 \|\|

*ityuktvā sahito mātrā vainateyo viniryayau \|*  
*kuśāsane ca tairukto dhṛtvā pīyūṣabhājanam \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. After saying this and placing the pot of nectar on a mat of Kuśa grass at their request, Garuḍa went out with his mother.

## \|\| 1.50.121-122 \|\|

*yāvatsnātuṃ gatāḥ sarpāstāvatpīyūṣabhājanam \|*  
*ādāya viṣṇunā dattaṃ devebhya iva jīvitam \|\| 121 \|\|*

*āgatya bhujagāḥ snātvā na dṛṣṭvāmṛtabhājanam \|*  
*aho pratāritā nītamamṛtaṃ ceti cukruśuḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*
