121-122. While the serpents had gone for their bath the pot of nectar was taken away by Viṣṇu and given to Devas as if it were their very life. After their bath, the serpents returned. Not seeing the pot of nectar they shouted: “Alas! We have been cheated. The nectar has been taken away.”

## \|\| 1.50.123 \|\|

*tataḥ paryalihandarbhānpīyūṣasparśakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*āstāṃ tāvatsudhā dūraṃ jihvāsteṣāṃ dvidhābhavan \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Thereafter, desirous of contact with the nectar, they licked the Darbha grass. Far from getting the nectar, they got their tongues split into two.

## \|\| 1.50.124 \|\|

*anyepyanyāyalabdhārthaṃ ye bubhukṣaṃti kevalam \|*  
*tanno pariṇatiṃ gacchedbhoktuṃ vātairna labhyate \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. In the case of others too, if they are desirous of enjoying something got through illegitimate means, they do not get any chance to enjoy. Their effort does not become fruitful.

## \|\| 1.50.125 \|\|

*nyāyādhvasthena tārkṣyeṇa sudhā prāptātidurlabhā \|*  
*labdhāpyanyāyato nāgairdṛṣṭamātrā kṣaṇādgatā \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. The very rare Sudhā was obtained by Garuḍa who was ready to abide by just means. Though acquired by the serpents, it disappeared in a moment after being seen, because they had obtained it by unjust means.

## \|\| 1.50.126 \|\|

*atha dāsyādvinirmuktā vinatovāca khecaram \|*  
*putra kāśīṃ prayāsyāmi dāsyapāpāpanuttaye \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Then, released from the state of slavery, Vinatā told the sky-walker (Garuḍa): “O son, I will go to Kāśī for eradicating the sin of slavery.

## \|\| 1.50.127 \|\|

*tāvatpāpāni jṛṃbhaṃte nānājanmārjitānyapi \|*  
*yāvatkāśī na hṛtsaṃsthā punarbhavavighātinī \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Even all those sins incurred in the course of many births, appear to be very great as long as Kāśī, the destroyer of rebirth, is not retained in the heart.

## \|\| 1.50.128 \|\|

*kāśīsmaraṇamātreṇa kiṃ citraṃ yadaghaṃ vrajet \|*  
*garbhavāsopi naśyeta viśveśānugrahātparāt \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. What wonder is there that sins disappear merely by thinking of Kāśī? Due to the great blessings of Viśveśvara, even the possibility of rebirth disappears.

## \|\| 1.50.129 \|\|

*yatra viśveśvaraḥ sākṣāttārāpativibhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tārayettārakadroṇyā dustarādbhavasāgarāt \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Where Viśveśvara is directly present, the Lord with the Moon for an ornament shall redeem the devotees from the ocean of worldly existence through the raft of the Tāraka Mantra.

## \|\| 1.50.130 \|\|

*viśveśānugṛhītānāṃ vicchinnākhilakarmaṇām \|*  
*bhavetkāśīṃ prati matirnetareṣāṃ kadācana \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. The idea of going to Kāśī shall occur only in the minds of those who are blessed by Viśveśa and whose Karmas have been destroyed. Never does it occur to the minds of the others.

## \|\| 1.50.131 \|\|

*kāśīṃ prati mano yeṣāṃ niḥśeṣakṣālitainasām \|*  
*ta eva mānavā loke satyaṃ nṛpa śavopare \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Only they are human beings, whose mind is attracted to Kāśī and whose sins have been washed off. It is true that others are beasts in human form.

## \|\| 1.50.132 \|\|

*taireva kālo vijitasta eva hi gatainasaḥ \|*  
*apunargarbhavāsāste prāptā vārāṇasīha yaiḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Those alone who have attained Vārāṇasī, have defeated Kāla; only they are free from sins and they have no further birth.

## \|\| 1.50.133 \|\|

*śreyasāṃ bhājanaṃ caitannṛjanmana mudhā nayet \|*  
*devānāmapiduṣprāpyaṃ kāśīsaṃdarśanādṛte \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. One should not waste this human life, the means to the highest good. Without a visit to Kāśī that good is inaccessible even to Devas.

## \|\| 1.50.134 \|\|

*kaḥ kaliḥ kothavā kālaḥ kiṃ vā karmāṇyanekadhā \|*  
*parānaṃdapradaṃ kṣetramavimuktaṃ yadīkṣitam \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. If the holy place Avimukta is visited, Kali has no power. What can Kāla do or the different types of Karmas do?

## \|\| 1.50.135 \|\|

*te garbhavāse tiṣṭhaṃti punaste garbhavāsinaḥ \|*  
*ye na garbhavanacchetrīṃ sevaṃte varaṇāmasim \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Those who do not resort to Varaṇā and Asi capable of striking the forest of frequent births, remain in the womb; they continue to be born in a womb.”

## \|\| 1.50.136 \|\|

*niśamyeti vacaḥ prāha tārkṣyo natvātha mātaram \|*  
*ahamapyāgamiṣyāmi kāśīṃ draṣṭuṃ śivārcitām \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. On hearing these words, Garuḍa said after bowing down to his mother, “I shall also come to visit Kāśī honoured by Śiva.”

## \|\| 1.50.137 \|\|

*māturājñāmatha prāpya jananyā saha pakṣirāṭ \|*  
*kṣaṇādvārāṇasīṃ prāpa mokṣanikṣepabhūmikām \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. Getting the permission of his mother, the lord of birds, accompanied by his mother, instantaneously reached Vārāṇasī, the place ensuring salvation.

## \|\| 1.50.138-140 \|\|

*ubhāvapi ca tepāte tapa ugraṃ mahāmatī \|*  
*saṃsthāpya śāṃbhavaṃ liṃgaṃ patattrīṃdro'caleṃdriyaḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

*nāmnā khakholkamādityaṃ saṃsthāpya vinatā śubham \|*  
*acireṇaiva kālena mahatastapasastayoḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

*kāśyāṃ prasannau saṃjātau devau śaṃkarabhāskarau \|*  
*garuḍasthāpitālliṃgādāvirāsīdumāpatiḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

138-140. Both the higly intelligent ones performed very severe penance. The lord of birds with steady sense-organs, installed Śaṃbhu’s Liṅga and Vinatā installed the splendid one named Khakholka Āditya. Ere long due to their great penance Lord Śaṅkara and Bhāskara became pleased. Umāpati came out of the Liṅga installed by Garuḍa.

## \|\| 1.50.141-146 \|\|

*garuḍāya varānprādātsa bahūnatidurlabhān \|*  
*khageṃdra mama bhaktosi tava jñānaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 141 \|\|*

*vetsyasi tvaṃ rahasyaṃ me yanna jñātaṃ surairapi \|*  
*tvayaitatsthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ garuḍeśvarasaṃjñitam \|\| 142 \|\|*

*paramajñānadaṃ puṃsāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ samarcitam \|\| anyacca śṛṇu pakṣīṃdra hitaṃ te vacmi sāṃpratam \|\| 143 \|\|*

*asāvahaṃ sa vai viṣṇurmāstu te bhedadṛkca nau \|*  
*evaṃ tasyaiva pakṣīṃdra daityeṃdra balahāriṇa \|\| 144 \|\|*

*prāpya satpatratāṃ patriṃstvamapyarcyo bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*iti dattvā varaṃ śaṃbhuḥ svabhaktāya garutmate \|\| 145 \|\|*

*tatraivāṃtarhito jāto garuḍopi hariṃ yayau \|*  
*hare rathatvaṃ saṃprāpya sopi pūjyo'bhavadbhuvi \|\| 146 \|\|*

141-146. He granted many rare boons to Garuḍa: “O lord of birds, you are my devotee. You will acquire knowledge. All my secrets not known to the Suras will be understood by you. This Liṅga installed by you is named Garuḍeśvara. If seen, touched and worshipped, it bestows perfect knowledge on men. Listen to one thing more, O lord of birds. I shall tell you something beneficial. You should not see me and Viṣṇu as different. O lord of birds, becoming the vehicle of the Lord, the destroyer of the power of lords of Daityas, you will also be worthy of adoration.”

After granting this boon to Garuḍa, his devotee, Śaṃbhu vanished there itself. Garuḍa went to Lord Viṣṇu. Becoming the vehicle of Hari, he became worthy of adoration on the earth.

## \|\| 1.50.147-149 \|\|

*tapasyaṃtīmathālokya kadācidvinatāṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*śivasyaiva parāmūrtiḥ khakholko nāma bhāskaraḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

*dattvā varaṃ ca pāpaghnaṃ śivajñānasamanvitam \|*  
*kāśīvāsijanāneka bhavapāpakṣayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

*vinatāditya ityākhyaḥ khakholkastatra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*itthaṃ khakholka ādityaḥ kāśīvighnatamoharaḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

147-149. Lord Bhāskara, the greatest cosmic form of Śiva and named Khakholka, once saw Vinatā performing penance. He granted her the boon of destruction of sins along with the knowledge of Śiva. He remained there in Kāśī and was named Vinatāditya (also). He destroyed the various sins of the residents of Kāśī. Thus is Khakholka Āditya, the destroyer of darkness and obstacles in Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.50.150-151 \|\|

*tasya darśanamātreṇa sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*kāśyāṃ paiśaṃgile tīrthe khakholkasya vilokanāt \|*  
*naraściṃtitamāpnoti nīrogo jāyate kṣaṇāt \|\| 150 \|\|*

*naraḥ śrutvaitadākhyānaṃ khakholkādityasaṃbhavam \|*  
*garuḍeśena sahitaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 151 \|\|*

150-151. In Kāśī, in the holy Tīrtha named Paiśaṅgila (Pilipilā Tīrtha), a devotee should visit Khakholka. Merely by the sight thereof, he is freed from all sins. The man attains whatever he thinks of. Instantaneously he becomes free from illness. By listening to this narrative of Khakholka Āditya along with that of Garuḍeśa one is freed from all sins.

:: End of Kāśīkhaṇḍa Pūrvārdha ::

## Section 2 - Uttarārdha

## Chapter 51 - Description of Sun-gods Called Aruṇa, Vṛddha etc.

## \|\| 2.51.1 \|\|

*atha śrīkāśīkhaṃḍottarārdhaṃ prārabhyate \|*  
*śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ \|*  
*agastiruvāca \|*  
*pārvatī hṛdayānaṃda sarvajñāṃgabhava prabho \|*  
*kiṃcitpraṣṭumanāḥ svāmiṃstadbhavānvaktumarhati \|\| 1 \|\|*

\[Note: This chapter describes the legend of the following Sun-gods. Their names and locations are noted as below: 1. Aruṇāditya — In Trilocana Temple; 2. Vṛddhāditya — South of Viśālākṣī Temple at Mīrā Ghāṭa; 3. Keśavāditya — In Ādi-Keśava Temple; 4. Vimalāditya — In Jaṅgambāḍi area—south of Goduliā crossing; 5. Gaṅgāditya — At Lalitā Ghāṭa; 6. Yamāditya — At Yama Tīrtha near Vīreśvara.\]

Obeisance to Śrī Gaṇeśa:

Agasti enquired:

1\. O delighter of the heart of Pārvatī, O Lord born of the body of the Omniscient Lord, I wish to ask something. O Lord, it behoves you to explain it.

## \|\| 2.51.2 \|\|

*dakṣa prajāpateḥ putrī kaśyapasya parigrahaḥ \|*  
*garutmataḥ prasūḥ sādhvī kuto dāsyamavāpa sā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. How did that chaste lady, a daughter of Patriarch Dakṣa, a wife of Kaśyapa and mother of Garuḍa become a slave?

Skanda replied:

## \|\| 2.51.3 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*haṃjikātvaṃ yathā prāptā vinatā sā tapasvinī \|*  
*tadapyahaṃ samākhyāmi niśāmaya mahāmate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I shall recount to you, O highly intelligent one, how that pitiable lady Vinatā got into slavery; listen.

## \|\| 2.51.4 \|\|

*kadrūrajījanatputrāñśataṃ kaśyapataḥ purā \|*  
*ulūkamaruṇaṃ tārkṣyamasūta vinatā trayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Formerly Kadrū gave birth to a hundred sons of Kaśyapa and Vinatā to three, namely Ulūka, Aruṇa and Tārkṣya.

## \|\| 2.51.5 \|\|

*kauśiko rājyamāpyāpi śreṣṭhatvātpakṣiṇāṃ mune \|*  
*nirguṇatvācca taiḥ sarvaiḥ sa rājyādavaropitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In view of his being the eldest, Kauśika (i.e. Ulūka) attained the kingship of birds; but since he was bereft of virtues, he was dethroned from the kingdom by all those birds.

## \|\| 2.51.6-7 \|\|

*krūrākṣoyaṃ divāṃdhoyaṃ sadā vakranakhastvasau \|*  
*atīvodvegajanakaṃ sarveṣāmasya bhāṣaṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*itthaṃ tasya guṇagrāmānvikathya bahuśaḥ khagāḥ \|*  
*nādyāpi vṛṇvate rājye kamapi svairacāriṇaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. “This (bird) is evil-eyed; he is blind by day; he is always crooked-nailed; his voice causes extreme alarm to everyone.” Thus those birds censured its qualities in various ways. Hence they did not select anyone else as a king. They moved about as they pleased.

## \|\| 2.51.8 \|\|

*kauśiketha tathāvṛtte putravīkṣaṇalālasā \|*  
*aṃḍaṃ prasphoṭayāmāsa madhyamaṃ vinatā tadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Since Kauśika’s lot had been so, Vinatā was excessively eager to see a son. Hence she broke open the egg of the middle one.

## \|\| 2.51.9 \|\|

*pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu prasphoṭya ghaṭasaṃbhava \|*  
*tadabheditayautsukyādaṃḍamaṣṭamake śate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The egg was to be broken after completion of one thousand years, O Pot-born Sage. But out of eagerness, the egg was broken open by her in eight-hundredth year.

## \|\| 2.51.10 \|\|

*tāvatsarvāṇi gātrāṇi tasyātimahasaḥ śiśoḥ \|*  
*ūrvoruparisiddhāni daṃḍāṃtarnivāsinaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. By that time all the limbs of that highly refulgent child staying within that egg, had become full-fledged above the thighs only.

## \|\| 2.51.11 \|\|

*aṃḍānnirgatamātreṇa krodhāruṇamukhaśriyā \|*  
*ardhaniṣpannadehena śiśunā śāpitā prasūḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. As soon as it came out of the egg, the mother was cursed by that child with semi-fledged limbs. The splendour of his face was Aruṇa (red) with rage.

## \|\| 2.51.12-13 \|\|

*janayitri tvayā dṛṣṭvā kādraveyānsvalīlayā \|*  
*khelato māturutsaṃge yadaṃḍaṃ vyādhita dvidhā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tadaniṣpanna sarvāṃgaḥ śapāmi tvā vihaṃgame \|*  
*teṣāmevaidhi dāsī tvaṃ sapatnyaṃga bhuvāmiha \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. “O my mother, the sons of Kadrū were seen playing in the lap of their mother gracefully by you and the egg was broken open. Hence, I have become one with incompletely developed limbs. I, therefore, curse you. O bird! Be the slave of those very children born of your co-wife.”

## \|\| 2.51.14 \|\|

*vepamānātha tacchāpādidaṃ provāca pakṣiṇī \|*  
*anūro brūhi me śāpāvasānaṃ māturaṃgaja \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Trembling due to that curse, the bird spoke thus, “O Anūru (thighless one), my son, tell me the end (redemption) of the curse, unto your mother.”

## \|\| 2.51.15 \|\|

*anūruruvāca \|*  
*aṃḍaṃ tṛtīyaṃ mā bhiṃdhi hyaniṣpannaṃ mameva hi \|*  
*asminnaṃḍe bhaviṣyo yaḥ sa te dāsyaṃ hariṣyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Anūru said: “Do not break open that third egg. It is unfledged like mine. He who is to be born out of this egg, will redeem you from slavery.”

## \|\| 2.51.16 \|\|

*ityuktvā soruṇogacchaduḍḍīyānaṃdakānanam \|*  
*yatra viśveśvaro dadyādapi paṃgoḥ śubhāṃ gatim \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After saying thus, Aruṇa flew unto the sacred place called Ānandakānana, where Viśveśvara bestowed blessedness even on that crippled one.

## \|\| 2.51.17 \|\|

*etatte pṛcchataḥ khyātaṃ vinatā dāsyakāraṇam \|*  
*mune prasaṃgato vacmi aruṇādityasaṃbhavam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus the cause of the slavery of Vinatā has been recounted to you as per your query. O sage, incidentally I shall tell you the origin of Aruṇāditya.

## \|\| 2.51.18 \|\|

*anūrutvādanūruryoruṇaḥ krodhāruṇo yataḥ \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ tapastaptvā tenārādhi divākaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. This child was called Anūru because he had no thighs. He was known as Aruṇa because his (face) had become red in colour due to anger. Penance was performed by him at Vārāṇasī and the Sun-god was propitiated.

## \|\| 2.51.19 \|\|

*sopi prasanno dattvātha varāṃstasmā anūrave \|*  
*ādityastasya nāmnābhūdaruṇāditya ityapi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. That Lord too became pleased and granted boons to that Anūru. The Sun-god became known as Aruṇāditya after his name.

## \|\| 2.51.20 \|\|

*arka uvāca \|*  
*tiṣṭhānūro mama rathe sadaiva vinatātmaja \|*  
*jagatāṃ ca hitārthāya dhvāṃtaṃ vidhvaṃsayanpuraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

The Sun-god said:

20\. O Anūru, son of Vinatā, stay forever in my chariot in front of me, dispelling the darkness for the welfare of all the worlds.

## \|\| 2.51.21 \|\|

*atra tvatsthāpitāṃ mūrtiṃ ye bhajiṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ mahādevottare teṣāṃ kuto bhayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If men worship the idol installed by you here in Vārāṇasī, to the north of Mahādeva idol, they will have nothing to fear from anywhere.

## \|\| 2.51.22 \|\|

*yercayiṣyaṃti satatamaruṇādityasaṃjñakam \|*  
*māmatra teṣāṃ no duḥkhaṃ na dāridryaṃ na pātakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Neither misery, nor poverty, nor sins will affect those who always worship me designated as Aruṇāditya.

## \|\| 2.51.23 \|\|

*vyādhibhirnābhibhūyaṃte no pasargaiśca kaiścana \|*  
*śokāgninā na dahyaṃte hyaruṇādityasevanāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By resorting to Aruṇāditya they can ward off the affliction from all ailments. They are not affected by evil phenomena, nor are they burned by the fire of grief.

## \|\| 2.51.24 \|\|

*atha syaṃdanamāropya nītavānaruṇaṃ raviḥ \|*  
*adyāpi sa rathe saure prātareva samudyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereafter the Sun-god made Aruṇa mount his chariot and took him away. Even today Aruṇa rises at dawn in the solar chariot.

## \|\| 2.51.25 \|\|

*yaḥ kuryātprātarutthāya namaskāraṃ dinedine \|*  
*aruṇāya sasūryāya tasya duḥkhabhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Whence can there be fear from misery unto him who gets up in the morning everyday and offers obeisance to Aruṇa along with the Sun-god?

## \|\| 2.51.26 \|\|

*aruṇādityamāhātmyaṃ yaḥ śroṣyati narottamaḥ \|*  
*na tasya duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃcidbhaviṣyati kadācana \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. If any excellent man listens to the greatness of Aruṇāditya, he will never incur any sin.

## \|\| 2.51.27 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*vṛddhādityasya māhātmyaṃ śṛṇu te kathayāmyaham \|*  
*yasya śravaṇamātreṇa naro no duṣkṛtaṃ bhajet \|\| 27 \|\|*

Skanda said:

27\. Listen to the greatness of Vṛddhāditya. I shall narrate it to you. The very act of listening to it makes a man avoid sinful acts.

## \|\| 2.51.28 \|\|

*purātra vṛddhahārīto vārāṇasyāṃ mahātapāḥ \|*  
*mahātapaḥ samṛddhyarthaṃ samārādhitavānravim \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Here at Vārāṇasī formerly an old great sage named Hārīta propitiated the Sun-god for the sake of great abundance of penance.

## \|\| 2.51.29 \|\|

*mūrtiṃ saṃsthāpya śubhadāṃ bhāsvataḥ śubhalakṣaṇām \|*  
*dakṣiṇena viśālākṣyā dṛḍhabhaktisamanvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Endowed with firm devotion, he installed the image of the Sun towards the south of Viśālākṣī. The image had all auspicious characteristics and was intended to bestow auspiciousness.

## \|\| 2.51.30 \|\|

*tuṣṭastasmai varaṃ prādādbradhno vṛddhatapasvine \|*  
*alaṃ vilaṃbya yācasva kaste deyo varo mayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Bradhna (the Sun-god), being pleased with him, granted a boon unto that old austere sage. He said, “Do not delay. Request me. What boon should be given by me to you?”

## \|\| 2.51.31 \|\|

*sotha prasannāddyumaṇeravṛṇīta varaṃ muniḥ \|*  
*yadi prasanno bhagavānyuvatvaṃ dehi me punaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. That sage chose the boon from the delighted Sun-god, the jewel of firmament: “If the Lord is pleased, grant me youth once again.

## \|\| 2.51.32 \|\|

*tapaḥkaraṇa sāmarthyaṃ sthavirasya na me yataḥ \|*  
*punastāruṇyamāptohaṃ cariṣyāmyuttamaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Since I have reached old age, I have no capacity to perform penance. Having regained my youth, I shall perform an excellent penance.

## \|\| 2.51.33 \|\|

*tapa eva paro dharmastapa eva paraṃ vasu \|*  
*tapa eva paraḥ kāmo nirvāṇaṃ tapa eva hi \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Penance alone is the greatest virtue. Penance alone is the greatest wealth. Penance alone is the great (Puruṣārtha called) love. Penance is certainly salvation.

## \|\| 2.51.34 \|\|

*ṛtena tapasaḥ kvāpi labhyā aiśvaryasaṃpadaḥ \|*  
*padaṃ dhruvādibhiḥ prāpi kevalaṃ tapaso balāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Prosperity and riches can be obtained anywhere without penance. Good position was obtained by Dhruva and others only on the strength of penance.

## \|\| 2.51.35 \|\|

*tatastapaścariṣyāmi lokadvayamahattvadam \|*  
*prāpya tvadvaradānena yauvanaṃ sarvasaṃmatam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thanks to your liberal gift of the boon, I shall regain youth honoured by all and thereafter perform penance that bestows greatness in both the worlds.

## \|\| 2.51.36 \|\|

*dhigjarāṃprāṇināmatra yayā sarvo virajyati \|*  
*jarātureṃdriyagrāme striyopi nayataḥ svasāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Fie upon old age of living beings here! Thereby all become estranged because even women do not remain under one’s control, when one’s sense-organs are afflicted with old age.

## \|\| 2.51.37 \|\|

*varaṃ maraṇamevāstu mā jarāstvatiśocyakṛt \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca maraṇaṃ jarā duḥkhaṃ kṣaṇekṣaṇe \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Even death is preferable to old age that causes excessive misery. Death is painful for a moment, but the pain of old age occurs every moment.

## \|\| 2.51.38 \|\|

*kāṃkṣaṃti dīrghatapase ciramāyurjiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*dhanaṃ dānāya putrāya kalatraṃ muktaye dhiyam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Men who have conquered their sense-organs, desire longevity for the sake of long continued penance, wealth for the purpose of donation, a wife for procreating a son, and intellect for attaining salvation.”

## \|\| 2.51.39 \|\|

*vṛddhasyavārdhakaṃ bradhnastatkṣaṇādapahṛtya vai \|*  
*dadau ca cārutā hetuṃ tāruṇyaṃ puṇyasādhanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Bradhna (the Sun-god) removed the senility of the old man immediately and granted him youth that produces charm and becomes the means of attaining merit.

## \|\| 2.51.40 \|\|

*evaṃ sa vṛddhahārīto vārāṇasyāṃ mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya yauvanaṃ bradhnāttapa ugraṃ cacāra ha \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After attaining youth from Bradhna thus, that great old sage Hārīta performed a fierce penance in Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.51.41 \|\|

*vṛddhenārādhito yasmāddhārītena tapasvinā \|*  
*ādityo vārdhakaharo vṛddhādityastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thereafter that deity Ādītya \[Āditya?\] who dispels senility is remembered as Vṛddhāditya, because he had been propitiated by the old sage Hārīta.

## \|\| 2.51.42 \|\|

*vṛddhādityaṃ samārādhya vārāṇasyāṃ ghaṭodbhava \|*  
*jarā durgati rogaghnaṃ bahavaḥ siddhimāgatāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Many have attained supernatural powers, O Pot-born One, by propitiating in Vārāṇasī, Vṛddhāditya, the destroyer of old age, wretchedness and ailments.

## \|\| 2.51.43 \|\|

*vṛddhādityaṃ namaskṛtya vārāṇasyā ravau naraḥ \|*  
*labhedabhīpsitāṃ siddhiṃ na kvaciddurgatiṃ labhet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. By bowing down to Vṛddhāditya at Vārāṇasī on a Sunday, a man shall obtain the desired benefit. He will not meet with wretchedness.

## \|\| 2.51.44 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ śṛṇu mune keśavādityamuttamam \|*  
*yathā tu keśavaṃ prāpya savitā jñānamāptavān \|\| 44 \|\|*

Skanda said:

44\. Hear, henceforth, O sage, about the excellent Keśavāditya and how the Sun-god attained (spiritual) knowledge after associating with Keśava.

## \|\| 2.51.45 \|\|

*vyomni saṃcaramāṇena saptāśvenādikeśavaḥ \|*  
*ekadā darśibhāvena pūjayaṃlliṃgamaiśvaram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Once, Ādikeśava was seen worshipping the Liṅga of Īśvara by Saptāśva (seven-horsed one = the Sun-god) who was proceeding ahead in the firmament.

## \|\| 2.51.46 \|\|

*kautukādiva uttīrya hare ravirupāviśat \|*  
*niḥśabdo niścalaḥ svastho mahāścaryasamanvitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Out of curiosity, Ravi descended from heaven and sat silently, motionlessly, steadily near Hari and was greatly amazed.

## \|\| 2.51.47 \|\|

*pratīkṣamāṇovasaraṃ kiṃcitpraṣṭumanā harim \|*  
*hariṃ visarjitārcaṃ ca praṇanāma kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Desirous of asking Hari something and awaiting the opportunity thereof, he bowed down to Hari when the latter had concluded the adoration. He kept his palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 2.51.48 \|\|

*svāgataṃ te hariḥ prāha bahumānapuraḥsaram \|*  
*svābhyāśaṃ āsayāmāsa bhāsvaṃtaṃ natakaṃdharam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. “Welcome to you”, said Hari with great respect. He made the Sun-god who had bowed down, sit near him.

## \|\| 2.51.49 \|\|

*athāvasaramālokya lokacakṣuradhokṣajam \|*  
*natvā vijñāpayāmāsa kṛtānujño'surāriṇā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Seeing that it was a suitable opportunity and having got the permission of the destroyer of Asuras, Lokacakṣus (‘the eye of the world’—the Sun) bowed down to Adhokṣaja (Viṣṇu) and submitted as follows:

## \|\| 2.51.50 \|\|

*raviruvāca \|*  
*aṃtarātmāsi jagatāṃ viśvaṃbhara jagatpate \|*  
*tavāpi pūjyaḥ kopyasti jagatpūjyātra mādhava \|\| 50 \|\|*

Ravi said:

50\. O Viśvaṃbhara, O Lord of the universe, you are the immanent soul of all the worlds. O Mādhava, worthy of being adored by the universe, is there anyone worthy of being adored here, even by you?

## \|\| 2.51.51 \|\|

*tvattaścāvirbhavedetattvayi sarvaṃ pralīyate \|*  
*tvameva pātā sarvasya jagato jagatāṃnidhe \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O resort of all the worlds, all this (visible world) manifests from you. Everything gets dissolved in you. You alone are the protector of the entire universe.

## \|\| 2.51.52 \|\|

*ityāścaryaṃ samālokya prāptosmyatra tavāṃtikam \|*  
*kimidaṃ pūjyate nātha bhavatā bhavatāpahṛt \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. I have come to you after seeing this surprising thing. What is this that is being worshipped, O Lord, by you, the destroyer of the distress of worldly existence?

## \|\| 2.51.53 \|\|

*iti śrutvā hṛṣīkeśaḥ sahasrāṃśorudīritam \|*  
*uccairmāśaṃsa saptāśvaṃ vārayankarasaṃjñayā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. On hearing this speech of the thousand-rayed Sun, Hṛṣīkeśa (Lord Viṣṇu) stopped the Sun-god with a gesture of his hand as though saying, “Do not speak loudly.”

## \|\| 2.51.54 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*devadevo mahādevo nīlakaṃṭha umāpatiḥ \|*  
*eka eva hi pūjyotra sarvakāraṇakāraṇam \|\| 54 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

54\. The Blue-throated Consort of Umā, the great Lord, the Lord of Devas alone is worthy of being adored here. He is the cause of all causes.

## \|\| 2.51.55 \|\|

*atra trilocanādanyaṃ samarcayatiyolpadhīḥ \|*  
*salocanopi vijñeyo locanābhyāṃ vivarjitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If anyone of deficient intellect worships someone other than the Three-eyed Lord, he should be considered as one devoid of eyes, though actually he may have eyes.

## \|\| 2.51.56 \|\|

*eko mṛtyuṃjayaḥ pūjyo janmamṛtyujarāharaḥ \|*  
*mṛtyuṃjayaṃ kilābhyarcya śveto mṛtyuṃjayobhavat \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Mṛtyuñjaya alone is worthy of being adored. He removes birth, death and old age. Indeed, by worshipping Mṛtyuñjaya, Śveta (ketu) was able to vanquish death.

## \|\| 2.51.57 \|\|

*kālakālaṃ samārādhya bhṛṃgī kālaṃ jigāyavai \|*  
*śailādimapi tatyāja mṛtyurmṛtyuṃjayārcakam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. By propitiating Kālakāla (Śiva), Bhṛṅgī vanquished Kāla (god of Death). Mṛtyu (god of Death) spared the son of Śilāda (Nandi) and others who worshipped Mṛtyuñjaya.

## \|\| 2.51.58 \|\|

*vijigye tripuraṃ yastu helayaikeṣu mokṣaṇāt \|*  
*taṃ samabhyarcya bhūteśaṃ ko na pūjyatamo bhavet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Who will not become the most adorable of all by worshipping Bhūteśa who vanquished the Tripuras sportingly by discharging a single arrow?

## \|\| 2.51.59 \|\|

*trijagajjayino hetostryakṣasyārādhanaṃ param \|*  
*ko nārādhayati bradhnasārasya smaravidviṣaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The propitiation of the Three-eyed Lord is the noblest act, since he is the cause of the victory over the three worlds. O Bradhna, who does not adore the enemy of Smara, who is the vital essence of all?

## \|\| 2.51.60 \|\|

*yasyākṣipakṣmasaṃkocājjagatsaṃkocametyadaḥ \|*  
*vikasvaraṃ vikāsācca kasya pūjyatamo na saḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. To whom is Lord Śiva not the most adorable one? This whole universe becomes shrunk (destroyed) when his eyelashes close and becomes full-fledged when his eyes open.

## \|\| 2.51.61 \|\|

*śaṃbhorliṃgaṃ samabhyarcya puruṣārthacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*prāpnotyatra pumānsadyo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. By worshipping the Liṅga of Śaṃbhu here, a man attains all the four aims of life immediately. No hesitation need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 2.51.62 \|\|

*samarcya śāṃbhavaṃ liṃgamapijanmaśatārjitam \|*  
*pāpapuṃjaṃ jahātyeva pumānatra kṣaṇāddhruvam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Certainly after worshipping Śaṃbhu’s Liṅga here, a man instantly gets rid of heaps of sins acquired in the course of hundreds of births.

## \|\| 2.51.63 \|\|

*kiṃkiṃ na saṃbhavedatra śivaliṃgasamarcanāt \|*  
*putrāḥ kalatra kṣetrāṇi svargo mokṣopyasaṃśayam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Undoubtedly what things—sons, wives, lands, heaven, liberation from Saṃsāra, will not happen (be obtained) by worshipping (Śiva)?

## \|\| 2.51.64 \|\|

*trailokyaiśvaryasaṃpattirmayā prāptā sahasrago \|*  
*śivaliṃgārcanādekātsatyaṃsatyaṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O Thousand-rayed One, by the sole worship of Śivaliṅga the riches and prosperities of all the three worlds have been attained by me. It is true, it is certainly true all the times.

## \|\| 2.51.65 \|\|

*ayameva paroyogastvidameva paraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*idameva paraṃ jñānaṃ sthāṇuliṃgaṃ yadarcyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. This alone is the greatest Yoga, this alone is the greatest austerity, this alone is the greatest wisdom whereby Śivaliṅga is worshipped.

## \|\| 2.51.66 \|\|

*yairliṃgaṃ sakṛdapyatra pūjitaṃ pārvatīpateḥ \|*  
*kuto duḥkhabhayaṃ teṣāṃ saṃsāre duḥkhabhājane \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. In this wide world, the receptacle of misery, whence can there be the fear of misery unto those by whom the Liṅga of Pārvatī’s Lord has been worshipped even once?

## \|\| 2.51.67 \|\|

*sarvaṃ parityajya rave yo liṃgaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*na taṃ pāpāni bādhaṃte mahāṃtyapi divākara \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O Ravi, O Divākara, even great sins do not harass him who has sought refuge in the Liṅga forsaking everything else.

## \|\| 2.51.68 \|\|

*liṃgārcane bhavedvṛddhisteṣāmevātra bhāskara \|*  
*yeṣāṃ punarbhavacchedaṃ cikīrṣati maheśvaraḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O Bhāskara, interest in the worship of the Liṅga here, shall occur only in those persons whose severance from the mundane existence, Maheśvara wishes to bring into effect.

## \|\| 2.51.69 \|\|

*na liṃgārādhanātpuṇyaṃ triṣulokeṣu cāparam \|*  
*sarvatīrthābhiṣekaḥ syālliṃgasnānāṃbu sevanāt \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. There is nothing else in all the three worlds more meritorious than the propitiation of the Liṅga. One shall have (the benefit of) having the holy bath in all the Tīrthas by resorting to the holy water with which the Liṅga is bathed.

## \|\| 2.51.70 \|\|

*tasmālliṃgaṃ tvamapyarka samarcaya maheśituḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptaṃ paramāṃ lakṣmīṃ mahātejobhi jṛṃbhaṇīm \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Hence, O Arka, you too worship the Liṅga of Maheśvara in order to acquire the greatest glory increasing with the greatest refulgence.

## \|\| 2.51.71 \|\|

*iti śrutvā harervākyaṃ tadārabhya sahasraguḥ \|*  
*vidhāya sphāṭikaṃ liṃgaṃ munedyāpi samarcayet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. On hearing these words of Hari, the Thousand-rayed Lord made a crystal Liṅga, O sage, and has been worshipping it ever since and even today.

## \|\| 2.51.72 \|\|

*gurutvena tadākalya vivasvānādikeśavam \|*  
*tatropatiṣṭhatedyāpi uttareṇādikeśavāt \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Vivasvān (Sun-god) chose Ādikeśava as his preceptor and is worshipping there to the north of Ādikeśava.

## \|\| 2.51.73 \|\|

*ataḥ sa keśavādityaḥ kāśyāṃ bhaktatamonudaḥ \|*  
*samarcitaḥ sadā deyānmanaso vāṃchitaṃ phalam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Hence that Liṅga is called Keśavāditya. He is the destroyer of the darkness of devotees. On being adequately worshipped, he shall bestow for ever everything desired in the mind.

## \|\| 2.51.74 \|\|

*keśavādityamārādhya vārāṇasyāṃ narottamaḥ \|*  
*paramaṃ jñānamāpnoti yena nirvāṇabhāgbhavet \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. By propitiating Keśavāditya in Vārāṇasi, a good man acquires highest wisdom whereby he attains salvation too.

## \|\| 2.51.75 \|\|

*tatra pādodake tīrthekṛtasarvodakakriyaḥ \|*  
*vilokya keśavādityaṃ mucyate janmapātakaiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. In the holy Tīrtha Pādodaka at the confluence of Gaṅgā and Varaṇā, one should perform the ritualistic offering of water to one’s predecessors and should visit Keśavāditya. He is liberated from congenital sins.

## \|\| 2.51.76-77 \|\|

*agaste rathasaptamyāṃ ravivāro yadāpyate \|*  
*tadā pādodake tīrthe ādikeśava sannidhau \|\| 76 \|\|*

*snātvoṣasi naro maunī keśavādityapūjanāt \|*  
*saptajanmārjitātpāpānmukto bhavati tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. O Agasti, on the Rathasaptamī day (seventh day of the bright half of Māgha) coinciding with a Sunday, a devotee should take bath early in the morning in the Pādodaka Tīrtha in front of Ādikeśava. He should observe silence and worship Keśavāditya. Instantaneously, he shall be absolved of the sins incurred in the course of seven births.

## \|\| 2.51.78-81 \|\|

*yadyajjanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ mayā saptasu janmasu \|*  
*tanme rogaṃ ca śokaṃ ca mākarī haṃtu saptamī \|\| 78 \|\|*

*etajjanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yacca janmāṃtarārjitam \|*  
*manovākkāyajaṃ yacca jñātājñāte ca ye punaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*iti saptavidhaṃ pāpaṃ snānānme saptasaptike \|*  
*saptavyādhisamāyuktaṃ hara mākari saptami \|\| 80 \|\|*

*etanmaṃtratrayaṃ japtvā snātvā pādodake naraḥ \|*  
*keśavādityamālokya kṣaṇānniṣkaluṣo bhavet \|\| 81 \|\|*

78-81. Three Mantras:

“(a) May the Saptamī of the month of Makara dispel all my sins acquired in the course of seven births and the illness and grief attending them. (b) May these seven types of sins: (i) committed in the current birth, (ii) acquired in the previous birth, (iii) mental ones, (iv) verbal ones, (v) physical ones, (vi) known ones, (vii) unknown ones, be dispelled, (c) O Saptasaptikā (the Solar Śakti), the Saptamī of Makara destroys these seven forms of sins, by my holy bath. Dispel them along with the seven ailments.”

By repeating these three Mantras and by taking the holy dip in Pādodaka and also by visiting Keśavāditya a man shall be free from sins instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.51.82 \|\|

*keśavādityamāhātmyaṃ śṛṇvañśraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*naro na lipyate pāpaiḥ śivabhaktiṃ ca viṃdati \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. One who listens to the greatness of Keśavāditya with faith, is never smeared with sins. He acquires devotion unto Śiva.

## \|\| 2.51.83 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ śṛṇu mune vimalādityamuttamam \|*  
*harikeśavane ramye vārāṇasyāṃ vyavasthitam \|\| 83 \|\|*

Skanda said:

83\. Henceforth, listen O sage, to the excellent Vimalāditya stationed in the beautiful forest of Harikeśavana in Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.51.84-85 \|\|

*uccadeśebhavatpūrvaṃ vimalo nāma bāhujaḥ \|*  
*sa prāktanātkarmayogādvimale pathyapi sthitaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*kuṣṭharogamavāpyoccaistyaktvā dārāngṛhaṃ vasu \|*  
*vārāṇasīṃ samāsādya bradhnamārādhayatsudhīḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. Formerly, there was a Kṣatriya named Vimala in the ‘Ucca Deśa’ (in the country called ‘Ucca’ or in a hilly country). Though he abided by the path devoid of impurities, he contracted the foul disease of leprosy as a result of the previous Karmas. He left his wife, home and riches. The sensible man repaired to Vārāṇasī and propitiated Bradhna (the Sun-god).

## \|\| 2.51.86 \|\|

*karavīrairjapābhiśca gaṃdhakaiḥ kiṃśukaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*raktotpalairaśokaiśca sa samānarca bhāskaram \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. He worshipped the Sun-god with the fragrant flowers of Japā, Karavīra, excellent Kiṃśuka, red lotuses and Aśoka.

## \|\| 2.51.87-89 \|\|

*vicitraracanairmālyaiḥ pāṭalācaṃpakodbhavaiḥ \|*  
*kuṃkumāgurukarpūramiśritaiḥ śoṇacaṃdanaiḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*devamohanadhūpaiśca bahvāmodatatāṃbaraiḥ \|*  
*karpūravartidīpaiśca naivedyairghṛtapāyasaiḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*arghadānaiśca vidhivatsaureḥ stotrajapairapi \|*  
*evaṃ samārādhayatastasyārko varadobhavat \|\| 89 \|\|*

87-89. He offered garlands of Pāṭala and Caṃpaka flowers with exquisite workmanship. He offered red sandal mixed with saffron, agallochum and camphor. He offered Devamohana incenses filling the whole atmosphere with profuse perfume, lights with Karpūra, lamps with wicks and also milk and ghee puddings for Naivedya. He offered different kinds of arghyas, repeated hymns and prayers of the Sun-god in accordance with the (specific) injunctions. While he was propitiating thus, the Sun-god became the bestower of boons.

## \|\| 2.51.90 \|\|

*uvāca ca varaṃ brūhi vimalāmalaceṣṭita \|*  
*kuṣṭhaśca te prayātveṣa prārthayānyaṃ varaṃ punaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. He said: “O Vimala of spotless activities, mention the boon you would have. Let this leprosy of yours disappear. Request for another boon.”

## \|\| 2.51.91-94 \|\|

*ākarṇya vimalaścetthamālāpaṃ raśmimālinaḥ \|*  
*praṇato daṃḍavadbhūmau saṃprahaṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*śanairvijñāpayāṃcakra ekacakrarathaṃ ravim \|*  
*jagaccakṣurameyātmanmahādhvāṃtavidhūnana \|\| 92 \|\|*

*yadi prasanno bhagavanyadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*tadā tvadbhaktiniṣṭhā ye kuṣṭhaṃ māstu tadanvaye \|\| 93 \|\|*

*anyepi rogā mā saṃtu māstu teṣāṃ daridratā \|*  
*māstu kaścana saṃtāpastvadbhaktānāṃ sahasrago \|\| 94 \|\|*

91-94. On hearing these words of the Sun-god, Vimala bowed down in prostration on the ground, with hairs standing on end due to exhilaration. He submitted to the Sun-god having monowheeled chariot: “O eye of the universe, O incomprehensible soul, O dispeller of great darkness, if the holy Lord is pleased, if a boon may be granted to me, then let there be no leprosy in the whole family of those who are steadfast in devotion unto you. O Thousand-rayed One, let there not be other ailments too; let there be no poverty and let there be no distress unto your devotees.”

## \|\| 2.51.95 \|\|

*\|śrīsūrya uvāca \|*  
*tathāstviti mahāprājña śṛṇvanyaṃ varamuttamam \|*  
*tvayeyaṃ pūjitā mūrtirevaṃ kāśyāṃ mahāmate \|\| 95 \|\|*

Śrī Sūrya said:

95\. Let it be so, O highly intelligent one. Listen to another excellent boon. This idol has been adored by you, O extremely intelligent one.

## \|\| 2.51.96 \|\|

*asyāḥ sānnidhyamatrāhaṃ na tyakṣyāmi kadācana \|*  
*prathitā tava nāmnā ca pratimaiṣā bhaviṣyati \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. I will never leave off the vicinity of this idol. This image will be popularly known after your name.

## \|\| 2.51.97 \|\|

*vimalāditya ityākhyā bhaktānāṃ varadā sadā \|*  
*sarvavyādhi nihaṃtrī ca sarvapāpakṣayaṃkarī \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Its name shall be Vimalāditya. It shall always be the bestower of boons on devotees. It shall dispel all ailments and all sins.

## \|\| 2.51.98 \|\|

*iti dattvā varānsūryastatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*vimalo nirmalatanuḥ sopi svabhavanaṃ yayau \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. After granting these boons, the Sun vanished there itself. Vimala, with a clean spotless body went to his abode.

## \|\| 2.51.99 \|\|

*itthaṃ sa vimalādityo vārāṇasyāṃ śubhapradaḥ \|*  
*tasya darśanamātreṇa kuṣṭharogaḥ praṇaśyati \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Thus is the Vimalāditya at Vārāṇasī the bestower of auspiciousness. Merely by visiting him, the foul disease of leprosy becomes completely destroyed (cured).

## \|\| 2.51.100 \|\|

*yaścaitāṃ vimalādityakathāṃ vai śṛṇuyānnaraḥ \|*  
*prāpnoti nirmalāṃ śuddhiṃ tyajyate ca manomalaiḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. A man who listens to this story of Vimalāditya attains spotless purity. He gets rid of all mental impurities.

## \|\| 2.51.101 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*gaṃgādityosti tatrānyo viśveśāddakṣiṇena vai \|*  
*tasya darśanamātreṇa naraḥ śuddhimiyādiha \|\| 101 \|\|*

Skanda said:

101\. There is another (deity) Gaṅgāditya to the south of Viśveśa. A man attains purity merely by seeing it.

## \|\| 2.51.102 \|\|

*yadā gaṃgā samāyātā bhagīrathapuraskṛtā \|*  
*tadā gaṃgāṃ pariṣṭotuṃ ravistatraiva saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. When Gaṅgā arrived with Bhagīratha leading her, the Sun-god stationed himself there in order to eulogize Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 2.51.103 \|\|

*adyāpyaharniśaṃ gaṃgāṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*pariṣṭauti prasannātmā gaṃgābhaktavarapradaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Even to this day, Bhāskara faces Gaṅgā day and night and eulogizes her. He is delighted in his soul and bestows boon on the devotees of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 2.51.104 \|\|

*gaṃgādityaṃ samārādhya vārāṇasyāṃ narottamaḥ \|*  
*durgatiṃ jātu na kvāpi labhate na ca rogabhāk \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. An excellent man who propitiates Gaṅgāditya in Vārāṇasī, never attains wretchedness at any place. Nor does he fall ill.

## \|\| 2.51.105 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*anyacchṛṇu mahābhāga yamādityasya saṃbhavam \|*  
*yacchrutvāpi naro jātu yamalokaṃ na paśyati \|\| 105 \|\|*

Skanda said:

105\. O blessed one, listen to another thing connected with Yamāditya. On hearing it, a man never sees the world of Yama.

## \|\| 2.51.106 \|\|

*yameśātpaścime bhāge vīreśātpūrvato mune \|*  
*yamādityaṃ naro dṛṣṭvā yamalokaṃ na paśyati \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. By visiting Yamāditya, O sage, to the west of Yameśa and to the east of Vlreśa a devotee never sees the world of Yama.

## \|\| 2.51.107 \|\|

*yamatīrthe naraḥ snātvā bhūtāyāṃ bhaumavāsare \|*  
*yameśvaraṃ vilokyāśu sarvaiḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. After taking bath in Yama Tīrtha on a Tuesday coinciding with the fourteenth lunar day, the devotee should visit Yameśvara. He is quickly absolved of all sins.

## \|\| 2.51.108 \|\|

*yamatīrthe yamaḥ pūrvaṃ taptvā suvimalaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*yameśaṃ ca yamādityaṃ pratyaṣṭhādbhaktasiddhidam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Formerly Yama performed pure penance in Yama Tīrtha. Then he installed Yameśa and Yamāditya that bestow supernatural powers.

## \|\| 2.51.109 \|\|

*yamena sthāpito yasmādādityastatra kuṃbhaja \|*  
*ataḥ sa hi yamādityo yāmīṃ harati yātanām \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. O Pot-born One, since Āditya was installed there by Yama, he is known as Yamāḍitya and he removes the torture arising from Yama.

## \|\| 2.51.110 \|\|

*yameśaṃ ca yamādityaṃ yamena sthāpitaṃ naman \|*  
*yamatīrthe kṛtasnāno yamalokaṃ na paśyati \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. One who bows to Yameśa and Yamāditya installed by Yama and takes his holy dip in Yamatīrtha does not see the world of Yama.

## \|\| 2.51.111 \|\|

*yamatīrthe caturdaśyāṃ bharaṇyāṃ bhaumavāsare \|*  
*tarpaṇaṃ piṃḍadānaṃ ca kṛtvā pitranṛṇī bhavet \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. One becomes free from indebtedness to Pitṛs by performing libations and offerings of balls of rice in Yama Tīrtha on the fourteenth lunar day on a Tuesday with Bharaṇī constellation.

## \|\| 2.51.112-114 \|\|

*abhilaṣyaṃti satataṃ pitaro narakaukasaḥ \|*  
*bhaumai bharaṇyāṃ bhūtāyāṃ yadi yogoyamuttamam \|\| 112 \|\|*

*kāśyāṃ kaścidyame tīrthe kṛtvā snānaṃ mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*api yastarpaṇaṃkuryātsatilaṃ no vimuktaye \|\| 113 \|\|*

*kiṃ gayā gamanaiḥ puṃsāṃ kiṃ śrāddhairbhūridakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*yadi kāśyāṃ yame tīrthe yogesmiñśrāddhamāpyate \|\| 114 \|\|*

112-114. The Pitṛs dwelling in Narakas always desire thus: “If this excellent combination of a Tuesday with Bharaṇī and the fourteenth lunar day occurs and if some highly intelligent (scion of our family) takes his holy bath in Yama Tīrtha at Kāśī and offers libations along with gingelly seeds, it shall be conducive to our liberation. If Śrāddha is performed in this combination at Yama Tīrtha at Kāśī, of what avail is the pilgrimage to Gayā and Śrāddhas with enormous Dakṣiṇās?”

## \|\| 2.51.115 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā yame tīrthe pūjayitvā yameśvaram \|*  
*yamādityaṃ namaskṛtya pitṝṇāmanṛṇo bhavet \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. One should be free from indebtedness to the Pitṛs by performing Śrāddha in Yama Tīrtha, adoring Yameśvara and bowing down to Yamāditya.

## \|\| 2.51.116 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*iti te dvādaśādityāḥ kathitā pāpanāśanāḥ \|*  
*yatsaṃbhavaṃ samākarṇya naro na nirayī bhavet \|\| 116 \|\|*

Skanda said:

116\. Thus (the propitiation of) twelve Ādityas who dispel sins has been explained to you. On listening to the origin of these, a man does not fall into a hell.

## \|\| 2.51.117 \|\|

*anyepi saṃti ghaṭaja ravibhaktairanekaśaḥ \|*  
*kāśyāṃ saṃsthāpitāḥ sūryā guhyakārkādayaḥ kila \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. O Pot-born Sage, there are many other Ādityas too installed in Kāśī such as Guhyakārka etc., by devotees of the Sun-god.

## \|\| 2.51.118 \|\|

*śrutvādhyāyānimānpuṇyāndvādaśādityasūcakān \|*  
*śrāvayitvāpi no martyo durgatiṃ yāti kutracit \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. By listening to these holy Adhyāyas (chapters 45 to 51) explaining the twelve Ādityas and by narrating them to others a man can avert disasters. He never attains wretchedness.

## Chapter 52 - Description of Daśāśvamedha

## \|\| 2.52.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*gabhastimālinigate kāśīṃ trailokyamohinīm \|*  
*punaściṃtāmavāpoccairmaṃdarastho mune haraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Daśāśvamedha Ghāṭa is the most popular Ghāṭa in Vārāṇasī. In ancient times it was called Rudrasarovara. But it got its name Daśāśvamedha when God Brahmā performed ten horse-sacrifices here under the sponsorship of King Divodāsa. The Brahmeśvara Liṅga established by Brahmā is in a low-lying building inundated every year in floods. The Daśāśvamedheśvara Liṅga is in the compound of Śītalā Devī. Godāvarī (now called Goduliā Nālā) joined Gaṅgā at this Ghāṭa and this had additional sanctity due to this confluence.—The original Ghāṭa is the southern side of the modern Daśāśvamedha Ghāṭa. The northern Ghāṭa was formerly called Prayāga Ghāṭa and was an independent one. (BCL 226-8)

Skanda said:

1\. After the Sun had gone to Kāśī that is fascinating to all the three worlds, O sage, Hara who was stationed in Mandara reached a high degree of anxiety:

## \|\| 2.52.2 \|\|

*nādyāpyāyāṃti yoginyo nādyāpyāyāti tigmaguḥ \|*  
*pravṛttirapi me kāśyāścitramatyaṃta durlabhā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. ‘The Yoginīs have not returned till this day. Nor has the fierce-rayed Sun-god. It is surprising that I have no tidings about Kāśī. It has become very difficult to get.

## \|\| 2.52.3 \|\|

*kimatra citraṃ yatkāśī madīyamapimānasam \|*  
*niścalaṃ caṃcalayati gaṇanā ketaresure \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Or, what is surprising in this: If Kāśī makes even my steady mind fickle and unsteady, what then is the position in regard to other Suras?

## \|\| 2.52.4 \|\|

*adhākṣipamahaṃ kāmaṃ trijagajjittvaraṃdṛśā \|*  
*aho kāśyabhilāṣotra māmeva dunuyāttarām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I burned down Kāma, the conqueror of the three worlds, by my glance. Alas! the desire for Kāśī burns all the more and torments me.

## \|\| 2.52.5 \|\|

*kāśīpravṛttimanveṣṭuṃ kaṃ vā prahiṇuyāmitaḥ \|*  
*jñātuṃ ka eva nipuṇo yataḥ sa caturānanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Whom shall I send next to seek the tidings of Kāśī? Brahmā alone is capable of knowing it because he is four-faced (or clever-faced).’

## \|\| 2.52.6 \|\|

*ityāhūya vidhātāraṃ bahumānapuraḥsaram \|*  
*tatropaveśya śrīkaṃṭhaḥ provāca caturānanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After thinking thus, Śrīkaṇṭha invited the Creator (Brahmā) with great deal of respect. After he had taken a seat, he spoke to him:

## \|\| 2.52.7 \|\|

*yoginyaḥ preṣitāḥ pūrvaṃ preṣitotha sahasraguḥ \|*  
*nādyāpi te nivartaṃte kāśyāḥ kalaśasaṃbhava \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “At first the Yoginīs were sent. Then the thousand-rayed Sun was sent. Till today, they have not returned from Kāśī, O Lotus-born One.

## \|\| 2.52.8 \|\|

*sā samutsukayetkāśī lokeśa mama mānasam \|*  
*prākṛtasya janasyeva caṃcalākṣīva kācana \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Lord of the worlds, that Kāśī creates eagerness in my mind like a tremulous-eyed girl in that of an ordinary man.

## \|\| 2.52.9 \|\|

*maṃdaretra ratirme na bhṛśaṃ suṃdarakaṃdare \|*  
*anacchatucchapānīye nakrasyevālpapalvale \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Though Mandara here abounds in beautiful caves, I do not feel drawn towards it like a crocodile which does not revel in a small lake where the water is shallow as well as turbid.

## \|\| 2.52.10 \|\|

*nā bādhiṣṭa tathā māṃ sa tāpo hālāhalodbhavaḥ \|*  
*kāśīvirahajanmātra yathā māmatibādhate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. That burning sensation arising from the poison Halāhala did not so torment me as this one arising from the separation of Kāśī which afflicts me very much.

## \|\| 2.52.11 \|\|

*śītaraśmiḥ śiraḥsthopi varṣanpīyūṣasīkaraiḥ \|*  
*kāśīviśleṣajaṃ tāpaṃ nāho gamayituṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Though the cool-rayed Moon is situated on my head and sheds nectarine drops as it were, it is not capable of dispelling the distress arising from the separation from Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.52.12 \|\|

*vidhe vidhehi me kāryamārya dhurya mahāmate \|*  
*yāhi kāśīmitastūrṇaṃ yatasva ca mamehite \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O Brahmā, O highly intelligent one, O foremost among noble ones, go hence to Kāśī quickly and do an investigation for me in this regard as desired by me.

## \|\| 2.52.13 \|\|

*brahmaṃstvameva tadvetsi kāśī tyajanakāraṇam \|*  
*maṃdopi na tyajetkāśīṃ kimu yo vetti kiṃcana \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O Brahmā, you alone know the reason for my leaving Kāśī. Even a dull-witted one may not leave Kāśī. What to say in the case of one who knows something!

## \|\| 2.52.14 \|\|

*adyaiva kiṃ na gaccheyaṃ kāśīṃ brahmansvamāyayā \|*  
*divodāsaṃ svadharmasthaṃ na tūllaṃghitumutsahe \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Brahmā, why don't I go myself to Kāśī along with my Māyā (Pārvatī—the Śakti) today itself? But I am not eager to assail Divodāsa who abides by his Dharma.

## \|\| 2.52.15 \|\|

*vidhe sarvavidheyāni tvameva vidadhāsi yat \|*  
*iti ceti ca vaktavyaṃ tvayyapārthamatokhilam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O Brahmā, since you carry out everything that has to be done, the instruction ‘Do this and this’ is entirely meaningless in your case.

## \|\| 2.52.16 \|\|

*ariṣṭaṃ gaccha paṃthāste śubhodarko bhavatvalam \|*  
*ādāyājñāṃ vidhi mūrdhni yayau vārāṇasīṃ mudā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Go safe without any ill-luck. May your path lead to auspiciousness.”

Brahmā took the order with a bowed head and went joyously to Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.52.17 \|\|

*sitahaṃsarathastūrṇaṃ prāpya vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyamivātmānamamanyata tadātmabhūḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The Self-born Lord with white Swan as his vehicle reached the city of Vārāṇasī quickly and considered himself blessed, as one who has done his duty.

## \|\| 2.52.18 \|\|

*haṃsayānaphalaṃ medya jātaṃ kāśīsamāgame \|*  
*kāśī prāptau yataḥ proktā aṃtarāyāḥ padepade \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. ‘In this contact with Kāśī, I have gained the benefit of having the Swan as a vehicle, since they say that there are obstacles in regard to the attainment of Kāśī at every step.

## \|\| 2.52.19 \|\|

*dṛśi dhāturabhūdya madṛśo prāpya sānvayaḥ \|*  
*spaṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭipathaṃ prāptā yadeṣā'naṃdavāṭikā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The root dṛś (to see) has become meaningful in regard to my Dṛśau (eyes) since this Ānandavāṭikā has come clearly within the range of my vision.

## \|\| 2.52.20 \|\|

*svayaṃ siṃcati yā madbhiḥ svābhiḥ svargataraṃgiṇī \|*  
*yatrānaṃdamayā vṛkṣā yatrānaṃdamayā janāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The celestial river itself waters it with its own current. The trees are blissful here. The people are full of bliss here.

## \|\| 2.52.21 \|\|

*nirviśaṃti sadā kāśyāṃ phalānyānaṃdavaṃtyapi \|*  
*sadaivānaṃdabhūḥ kāśī sadaivānaṃdadaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. All the fruits in Kāśī give delight for ever. Kāśī is a perpetual source of delight. Śiva is a perpetual bestower of bliss.

## \|\| 2.52.22-25 \|\|

*ānaṃdarūpā jāyaṃte tena kāśyāṃ hi jaṃtavaḥ \|*  
*caraṇau carituṃ vittastāveva kṛtināmiha \|\| 22 \|\|*

*caraṇau vicaretāṃyau viśvabhartṛ purī bhuvi \|*  
*tāveva śravaṇau śrotuṃ saṃvidā te bahuśrutau \|\| 23 \|\|*

*iha śrutimatāṃ puṃsāṃ yābhyāṃ kāśī śrutā sakṛt \|*  
*tadeva manute sarvaṃ manastviha manasvināma \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yenānumanyate caiṣā kāśī sarvapramāṇabhūḥ \|*  
*buddhirbudhyati sā sarvamiha buddhimatāṃ satām \|*  
*yayaitaddhūrjaṭerdhāma dhṛtaṃ sva viṣayīkṛtam \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. Hence, all the creatures in Kāśī become bliss embodied. Only those feet that traverse the ground in the city of Viśvabhartṛ (Śiva) and become blessed, know how to traverse. Only those ears of great learning, of persons well-versed in the Vedas here know how to hear, because Kāśī has been heard by them once. Only the mind of diligent person here meditates properly because Kāśī, the source of all authorities, is pondered over by it. The intellect of intelligent persons here comprehends everything, because the abode of Dhūrjaṭi has been made its object.

## \|\| 2.52.26 \|\|

*varaṃ tṛṇāni dhānyāni tāni vātyāhatānyapi \|*  
*kāśyāṃ yānyā pataṃtīha na janāḥ kāśyadarśanāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Better indeed are those grains and grass blades, even though wafted by wind and fallen within Kāśī, than those people who have not seen Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.52.27 \|\|

*adya me saphalaṃ cāyuḥ parārdhadvaya saṃmitam \|*  
*yasminsati mayā prāpi duṣprāpā kāśikā purī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Today, my life-span extending over two Parārdhas has become fruitful, because in the course of that period the city of Kāśikā, rare to be visited, has been attained by me.

## \|\| 2.52.28 \|\|

*aho me dharmasaṃpattirahome bhāgyagauravam \|*  
*yadadrākṣiṣamadyāhaṃ kāśīṃ sucira ciṃtitām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Wonderful is my asset of righteousness, astonishing is the weightiness of my fortune, since I have seen Kāśī today that has been thought over for a long time.

## \|\| 2.52.29 \|\|

*adya me svatapo vṛkṣo manorathaphalairalam \|*  
*śivabhaktyaṃbunā siktaḥ phalitoti bṛhattaraiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The tree of my austerities sprinkled with the water of devotion to Śiva, has borne the abundant fruits of all cherished desires.

## \|\| 2.52.30 \|\|

*mayā vyadhāyi bahudhā sṛṣṭiḥ sṛṣṭiṃ vitanvatā \|*  
*paramanyādṛśī kāśī svayaṃ viśveśa nirmitiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Various things have been created by me in the course of my creative activities. But Kāśī that has been created by Viśveśa is unique in itself.’

## \|\| 2.52.31 \|\|

*iti hṛṣṭamanā vedhā dṛṣṭvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*vṛddhabrāhmaṇarūpeṇa rājānaṃ ca dadarśa ha \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Brahmā, who was delighted in his mind after viewing the city of Vārāṇasī, assumed the form of an aged Brāhmaṇa and visited the king.

## \|\| 2.52.32 \|\|

*jalārdrākṣatapāṇiśca svastyuktvā pṛthivībhuje \|*  
*kṛtapraṇāmo rājñātha bheje taddattamāsanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. With raw rice-grains wet with water in his hand, he proclaimed Svasti unto the king. He was saluted by the king and offered a seat which he occupied.

## \|\| 2.52.33 \|\|

*kṛtamāno nṛpatinā sobhyutthānāsanādibhiḥ \|*  
*vipro vyajijñapadbhūpaṃ pṛṣṭāgamanakāraṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The king duly honoured him by standing up and offering the seat and the like. On being asked the purpose of his visit, the Brāhmaṇa said to the king:

## \|\| 2.52.34 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*bhūpāla bahukālīnosmyahamatra ciraṃtanaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ tu māṃ naiva jānāsi jāne tvāṃ hi ripuṃjayam \|\| 34 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

34\. O king, I am an aged person staying here for a long time. You may not know me but I know that you are Ripuñjaya (in your previous birth) or conqueror of enemies!

## \|\| 2.52.35 \|\|

*paraḥśatā mayā dṛṣṭā rājāno bhūridakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*vijitānekasaṃgrāmā yāyajūkā jiteṃdriyāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Hundreds of kings have been seen by me. They distributed much by way of monetary gifts. They successfully fought many battles. They regularly performed sacrifices. They controlled their sense-organs.

## \|\| 2.52.36 \|\|

*viniṣkṛtāriṣaḍvargāḥ suśīlāḥ sattvaśālinaḥ \|*  
*śrutasyapāradṛśvāno rājanītivicakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. They eschewed the group of six enemies (lust, anger etc.). They were of excellent conduct. They possessed Sattva quality. They mastered learning. They were experts in statecraft and polity.

## \|\| 2.52.37 \|\|

*dayādākṣiṇyanipuṇāḥ satyavrataparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*kṣamayā kṣamayātulyā gāṃbhīryajitasāgarāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. They are clever yet merciful and chivalrous. They abide by the vow of truthfulness. They are on a par with the Earth in forbearance. By their majesty and gravity they have excelled oceans.

## \|\| 2.52.38 \|\|

*jitaroṣarayāḥ śūrāḥ saumyasauṃdaryabhūmayaḥ \|*  
*ityādi guṇasaṃpannāḥ susaṃcitayaśodhanāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. They have conquered anger and are brave. They are the source of origin of gentleness and of handsome features, being richly endowed with these and other good qualities. Thus they have amassed good reputation as their asset.

## \|\| 2.52.39 \|\|

*paraṃ dvitrāḥ pavitrā ye rājarṣe tava sadguṇāḥ \|*  
*teṣveṣu rājasu mama prāyaśo na dṛśaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. But, O saintly king, generally among these kings, two or three of your extremely sacred, good qualities have not been seen by me.

## \|\| 2.52.40 \|\|

*prajānijakuṭuṃbastvaṃ tvaṃ tu bhūdevadaivataḥ \|*  
*mahātapaḥ sahāyastvaṃ pathānānye tathā nṛpāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. You consider your subjects as members of your family. You consider Brāhmaṇas as your deity. You have great austerities to your credit. In this regard the other kings are unlike you.

## \|\| 2.52.41 \|\|

*dhanyo mānyosi ca satāṃ pūjanīyosi sadguṇaiḥ \|*  
*devā api divodāsa tvattrāsānna vimārgagāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Divodāsa, you are blessed. You are worthy of honour due to your good qualities. You are worthy of the adoration of all good persons. Afraid of you, even the Devas do not go astray.

## \|\| 2.52.42 \|\|

*kiṃ naḥ stutyā tava nṛpa dvijānāmaspṛhāvatām \|*  
*kiṃ kurmastvadguṇagrāmāḥ stāvakānnaḥ prakurvate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Of what avail unto you, O king, is the panegyric of Brāhmaṇas like me who are devoid of desires? What can we do? The group of your good qualities makes us your eulogizers.

## \|\| 2.52.43 \|\|

*goṣṭhī tiṣṭhatviyaṃ tāvatprastutaṃ staumi sāṃpratam \|*  
*yaṣṭukāmosmyahaṃ rājaṃstvāṃ sahāyamato vṛṇe \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. May this chitchat be set apart. I shall state the thing relevant at present. O king, I am desirous of performing a sacrifice. Hence I seek your help.

## \|\| 2.52.44 \|\|

*tvayā rājanvatī caiṣā'vaniḥ sarvardhibhājanam \|*  
*ahaṃ cāstidhano rājannyāyopāttamahādhanaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O king, this kingdom has a benign king in you. It is the receptacle of all prosperities. I have some assets in the form of great wealth accumulated by legitimate means.

## \|\| 2.52.45 \|\|

*iyaṃ ca rājadhānī te karmabhūmāvanuttamā \|*  
*yasyāṃ kṛtānāṃ kāryāṇāṃ saṃvartepi na saṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In this land of Karmas, the capital city is the most excellent one. Even on the day of annihilation, there is not reduction in the power to yield benefits in the case of the holy rites.

## \|\| 2.52.46 \|\|

*saṃcitaṃ yaddhanaṃ puṃbhirnayasanmārgagāmibhiḥ \|*  
*tatkāśyāṃ viniyujyeta kleśāyetarathā bhavet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The wealth amassed by persons abiding by the righteous path, should be utilized in Kāśī. Otherwise it will be conducive to pain and distress.

## \|\| 2.52.47 \|\|

*mahimānaṃ paraṃ kāśyāḥ kopi veda na bhūpate \|*  
*ṛte trinayanācchaṃbhoḥ sarvajñānapradāyinaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O king, no one understands the excellent greatness of Kāśī, except the three-eyed Śaṃbhu, the bestower of all wisdom.

## \|\| 2.52.48 \|\|

*manye dhanyatarosi tvaṃ bahujanmaśatārjitaiḥ \|*  
*sukṛtaiḥ pāsi yatkāśīṃ viśvabhartuḥ parāṃ tanum \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I think that you are highly blessed since you rule Kāśī, the excellent Tanu (physical form) of Viśvabhartṛ (Lord Śiva), as a result of merits incurred in the course of many hundreds of births.

## \|\| 2.52.49 \|\|

*kāśī trijagatīsārastrivedī sāra eva vai \|*  
*trivargottarasāraśca nirṇīteti maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. This has been decided by great sages that Kāśī is the essence of the three worlds, the essence of the three Vedas and the greatest essence of the three aims of life.

## \|\| 2.52.50 \|\|

*viśveśānugraheṇaiva tvayaiṣā pālyate purī \|*  
*ekasyāpyavanātkāśyāṃ trailokyamavitaṃ bhavet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This city is protected, thanks to the blessings of Viśveśa, by you. By the protection of even one in Kāśī (it is as good as) the three worlds protected.

## \|\| 2.52.51 \|\|

*anyacca te hitaṃ vacmi yadi te rocate'nagha \|*  
*prīṇanīyaḥ sadaivaiko viśveśaḥ sarvakarmabhiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O sinless one, I shall mention another thing conducive to your welfare if it appeals to you. Viśveśa alone should always be propitiated by means of all rites.

## \|\| 2.52.52 \|\|

*anyadevadhiyā rājanviśveśaṃ paśya mā kvacit \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇviṃdra caṃdrārkā krīḍeyaṃ tasya dhūrjaṭeḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Never look upon the Lord of the universe like other gods, O king. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, Candra and Arka are mere playthings of Dhūrjaṭi.

## \|\| 2.52.53 \|\|

*viprairudarkamicchadbhiḥ śikṣaṇīyā yato nṛpāḥ \|*  
*atastava hitaṃ khyātaṃ kiṃ vā me ciṃtayānayā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. What is conducive to your welfare has been told by me, since kings should be properly advised by Brāhmaṇas desirous of their ultimate benefit. Otherwise what have I to do with such (anxious) thoughts?

## \|\| 2.52.54-57 \|\|

*iti joṣaṃ sthitaṃ vipraṃ pratyuvāca nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ mayā hṛdi dhṛtaṃ yattvayoktaṃ dvijottama \|\| 54 \|\|*

*rājovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ yiyakṣamāṇasya tava sāhāyyakarmaṇi \|*  
*dāsosmi yajñasaṃbhārānnayameko śato'khilān \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yadasti mekhilaṃ tatra saptāṃgepi bhavānprabhuḥ \|*  
*yajasvaikamanābrahmansiddhaṃ manyasva vāṃchitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*rājyaṃ karomi yadbrahmansvārthaṃ tanna manāgapi \|*  
*putraiḥ kalatrairdehenaparopakṛtaye yate \|\| 57 \|\|*

54-57. When the Brāhmaṇa kept quiet after speaking this, the excellent king replied:

## \|\| 2.52.58 \|\|

*rājñāṃ kratukriyābhyopi tīrthebhyopi samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*prajāpālanamevaiko dharmaḥ prokto manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

The king said:

O excellent Brāhmaṇa, whatever has been spoken by you has been grasped by me in the heart. I am at your service in the matter of helping you who are desirous of performing sacrifice.

Take away all the requisites for the sacrifice from my treasury. Whatever I have in the kingdom consisting of seven constituent elements, you are the lord unto that entirely. With single-minded attention go ahead with the sacrifice. Consider that everything you desire has already been accomplished. In my rule over the kingdom, O Brāhmaṇa, I have no selfish interest. I do endeavour for helping others with my own person, sons and wives.

58\. It has been said by learned men that for kings the sole duty is the protection of the subjects. It is far superior to sacrificial rites and even Tīrthas.

## \|\| 2.52.59 \|\|

*prajāsaṃtāpajovahnirvajrāgnerapi dāruṇaḥ \|*  
*dvitrāndahati vajrāgniḥ pūrvo rājyaṃ kulaṃ tanum \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The fire arising out of the suffering of the subjects is fiercer and more terrible than the fire of thunderbolt which can reduce to ash two or three persons (only) whereas the former destroys the kingdom, the family and the physical frame (of the king).

## \|\| 2.52.60 \|\|

*yadāvabhṛthasisrāsurbhaveyaṃ dvijasattama \|*  
*tadā viprapadāṃbhobhirabhiṣekaṃ karomyaham \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, whenever I feel the desire for having the valedictory bath after a sacrifice, I bathe myself with the waters from the feet of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 2.52.61 \|\|

*havanaṃ brāhmaṇamukhe yatkaromi dvijottama \|*  
*manye kratukriyābhyopi tadviśiṣṭaṃ mahāmate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The offerings I make in the mouth of a Brāhmaṇa, O excellent Brāhmaṇa of high intelligence, are, I think, better than sacrificial rites.

## \|\| 2.52.62 \|\|

*abhilāṣeṣu sarveṣu jāgartyeko hṛdīha me \|*  
*adyāpi mārgaṇaḥ kopi draṣṭavyaḥ svatanorapi \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Among all the desires in my heart, this one is more dominant that at least someone should be seen today requesting for something, even my own body.

## \|\| 2.52.63 \|\|

*aho ahobhirbahubhiḥ phalito me manorathaḥ \|*  
*yattvaṃ medya gṛhe prāptaḥ kiṃcitprārthayituṃ dvija \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Oh! Good! My desire has become fulfilled after many days that today you have come to my abode begging for something, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.52.64 \|\|

*ekāgramānaso vipra yajñānvipuladakṣiṇān \|*  
*bahūnyajakṛtaṃ viddhi sāhāyyaṃ sarvavastuṣu \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. With the mind concentrated, O Brāhmaṇa, perform many sacrifices with ample monetary gifts. Take it that assistance in everything has been rendered already.

## \|\| 2.52.65 \|\|

*iti rājño mahābuddherdharmaśīlasya bhāṣitam \|*  
*śrutvā tuṣṭamanāḥ sraṣṭā kratusaṃbhāramāharat \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. On hearing this speech of the virtuous and highly intelligent king, Brahmā, the Creator, became pleased in his mind. He gathered together the requisites for sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.52.66 \|\|

*sāhāyyaṃ prāpya rājarṣerdivodāsasya padmabhūḥ \|*  
*iyāja daśabhiḥ kāśyāmaśvamedhairmahāmakhaiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Getting the help of the saintly King Divodāsa, the Lotus-born One performed in Kāśī ten great horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.52.67 \|\|

*adyāpi homadhūmoghairyadvyāptaṃ gaganāṃtaram \|*  
*tadā prabhṛti na vyoma nīlimānaṃ jahātyadaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. As the interspaces of the firmament were pervaded by the columns of smoke from the Homas, the firmament has not given up the bluish colour ever since.

## \|\| 2.52.68 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ daśāśvamedhākhyaṃ prathitaṃ jagatītale \|*  
*tadā prabhṛti tatrāsīdvārāṇasyāṃ śubhapradam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Since that time onwards, that Tīrtha has become well-known all over the world. The Tīrtha named Daśāśvamedha in Vārāṇasī is the bestower of auspiciousness.

## \|\| 2.52.69 \|\|

*purā rudrasaro nāma tattīrthaṃ kalaśodbhava \|*  
*daśāśvamedhikaṃ paścājjātaṃ vidhiparigrahāt \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Formerly that Tīrtha was known by the name Rudrasaras. It later became ‘Daśāśvamedhika’ due to its taking over by Brahmā.

## \|\| 2.52.70 \|\|

*svardhunyatha tataḥ prāptā bhagīrathasamāgamāt \|*  
*atīva puṇyavajjātamatastattīrthamuttamam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Thereafter, the heavenly river came into contact with it in association with Bhagīratha. Hence that excellent Tīrtha became extremely meritorious and sacred.

## \|\| 2.52.71 \|\|

*vidhirdaśāśvamedheśaṃ liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya tatra vai \|*  
*sthitavānna gatodyāpi kvāpi kāśīṃ vihāya tu \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. After installing the Liṅga Daśāśvamedheśa there, Brahmā stayed there itself. Even till today he has not left Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.52.72 \|\|

*rājño dharmaratestasya cchidraṃ nāvāpa kiṃcana \|*  
*ataḥ purāreḥ purato vrajitvā kiṃ vadedvidhiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He did not find any vulnerable point in that king who was extremely interested in pious acts. Hence what could Brahmā have said after going to Lord Śiva?

## \|\| 2.52.73 \|\|

*kṣetraprabhāvaṃ vijñāya dhyāyanviśveśvaraṃ śivam \|*  
*brahmeśvaraṃ ca saṃsthāpya vidhistatraiva saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He realized the power of the holy place. Meditating on Śiva, the Lord of the universe, Brahmā installed Brahmeśvara and remained there itself.

## \|\| 2.52.74 \|\|

*parātanuriyaṃ kāśī viśveśasyeti niścitam \|*  
*asyāḥ saṃsevanācchaṃbhurna kupyati puro mayi \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. It is certain that Kāśī is the supreme form of Viśveśa. Since I serve it, Śambhu will not get angry with me.

## \|\| 2.52.75 \|\|

*kaḥ prāpya kāśīṃ durmedhāḥ punastyaktumiheha te \|*  
*anekajanmajanitakarmanirmūlanakṣamām \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Who is silly enough to leave after arriving at Kāśī capable of removing Karmas acquired in the course of many births?

## \|\| 2.52.76 \|\|

*viśvasaṃtāpasaṃhartuḥ sthāne viśvapatestanuḥ \|*  
*saṃtāpyatetarāṃ kāśyā viśleṣaja mahāgninā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. It is but natural that the body of the Lord of Viśva, the annihilator of the distress of the universe, should feel all the more distressed through the great fire of separation from Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.52.77 \|\|

*prāpya kāśīṃ tyajedyastu samastāghaughanāśinīm \|*  
*nṛpaśuḥ sa parijñeyo mahāsaukhyaparāṅamukhaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. After attaining Kāśī, the destroyer of masses of sins, if anyone, leaves it, he should be known as a human beast, averse to the supreme bliss.

## \|\| 2.52.78 \|\|

*nirvāṇalakṣmīṃ yaḥ kāṃkṣettyaktvā saṃsāradurgatim \|*  
*tena kāśī na saṃtyājyā yadyāptaiśādanugrahāt \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. If Kāśī is attained by the blessings of Īśa, it should not be abandoned by a person desirous of the glory of liberation after discarding the hellish worldly evils.

## \|\| 2.52.79 \|\|

*yaḥ kāśīṃ saṃparityajya gacchedanyatra durmatiḥ \|*  
*tasya hastatalādgaccheccaturvargaphalodayaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. If anyone of wicked intention abandons Kāśī and goes elsewhere, the outcome of the fruit of the four aims of life surely slips down from his hands.

## \|\| 2.52.80 \|\|

*nibarhaṇī madhaughasya supuṇya paribṛṃhiṇīm \|*  
*kaḥ prāpya kāśīṃ durmedhāstyajenmokṣasukhapradām \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Who is silly enough to abandon it after attaining Kāśī, the destroyer of mass of sin, the heightener of excellent merit and the bestower of the bliss of salvation?

## \|\| 2.52.81 \|\|

*satyaloke kva tatsaukhyaṃ kva saukhyaṃ vaiṣṇave pade \|*  
*yatsaukhyaṃ labhyate kāśyāṃ nimeṣārdhaniṣevaṇāt \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Where does one get that happiness in Satyaloka? Where is that happiness in the region of Viṣṇu—the happiness that is obtained in Kāśī even after resorting to it for half a minute.

## \|\| 2.52.82 \|\|

*vārāṇasīguṇagaṇānnirṇīya druhiṇastviti \|*  
*vyāvṛtya maṃdaragiriṃ na punaḥ pratyagānmune \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. After having come to this decision about the various good qualities of Vārāṇasī, O sage, Druhiṇa (God Brahmā) did not return to Mandara mountain.

## \|\| 2.52.83 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*mitrāvaruṇayoḥ putra mahimānaṃ bravīmi te \|*  
*kāśyāṃ daśāśvamedhasya sarvatīrthaśiromaṇeḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

Skanda said:

83\. O son of Mitra and Varuṇa, I shall narrate the greatness of Daśāśvamedha in Kāśī, the crest-jewel of all holy spots.

## \|\| 2.52.84 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhikaṃ prāpya sarvatīrthottamottamam \|*  
*yatkiṃcitkriyate karma tadakṣayamiheritam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Whatever sacred rite, even if it is very small, is performed after reaching Daśāśvamedhika, the most excellent of all excellent Tīrthas, it is said to be everlasting.

## \|\| 2.52.85-86 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyo de vatārcanam \|*  
*saṃdhyopāstistarpaṇaṃ ca śrāddhaṃ pitṛsamarcanam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*daśāśvamedhike tīrthe sakṛtsnātvā narottamaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā daśāśvamedheśaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. Holy bath, liberal gifts, Japa, Homa, Svādhyāya, worship of a deity, offer of twilight prayers, libation and Śrāddha in veneration of the ancestors, everything in Daśāśvamedha is holy. By taking a single bath in Daśāśvamedha Tīrtha and by visiting the Lord of Daśāśvamedha, an excellent man is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 2.52.87 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe prāpya pratipadaṃ tithim \|*  
*daśāśvamedhike snātvā mucyate janmapātakaiḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. On the first day of the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha, the devotee should take the holy dip in the Daśāśvamedha Tīrtha. He is rid of congenital sins.

## \|\| 2.52.88 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe śukla dvitīyāyāṃ snātvā rudrasarovare \|*  
*janmadvayakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. By taking a holy dip in the Rudra Sarovara on the second day of the bright half of Jyeṣṭha, the sins committed in two births perish instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.52.89 \|\|

*evaṃ sarvāsu tithiṣu kramasnāyī narottamaḥ \|*  
*āśuklapakṣadaśami pratijanmāghamutsṛjet \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. An excellent man, taking bath on the days in the following order (i.e. third day, fourth day etc.) till the tenth day in the bright half of the month shall get rid of the sins of as many births (e.g. second day—two births, third day—three births, fourth day—four births etc.).

## \|\| 2.52.90 \|\|

*tithiṃ daśaharāṃ prāpya daśajanmāghahāriṇīm \|*  
*daśāśvamedhike snāto yāmīṃ paśyenna yātanām \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. On the Daśaharā day that removes the sins of ten births, the devotee should take his holy dip in the Daśāśvamedhika Tīrtha. He shall never experience the torture of Yama.

## \|\| 2.52.91 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ daśāśvamedheśaṃ dṛṣṭvā daśaharā tithau \|*  
*daśajanmārjitaiḥ pāpaistyajyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. By visiting Daśāśvamedheśa Liṅga on the Daśaharā Tithi, one is undoubtedly absolved of sins acquired in the course of ten births.

## \|\| 2.52.92 \|\|

*snāto daśaharāyāṃ yaḥ pūjayelliṃgamuttamam \|*  
*bhaktyā daśāśvamedheśaṃ na taṃ garbhadaśā spṛśet \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. If one takes his holy dip on the Daśaharā day and worships the excellent Daśāśvamedheśa Liṅga with great devotion, the fate of being conceived in a womb never touches him.

## \|\| 2.52.93 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe pakṣaṃ rudrasare naraḥ \|*  
*kurvanvai vārṣikīṃ yātrāṃ na vighnairabhibhūyate \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. In the Rudrasaras, the man should perform the annual pilgrimage extending over the whole of a fortnight in the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha. He is never assailed by obstacles.

## \|\| 2.52.94 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhāvabhṛthairyatphalaṃ samyagāpyate \|*  
*daśāśvamedhe tannūnaṃ snātvā daśaharā tithau \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Certainly, one obtains the benefit of the valedictory baths of ten horse-sacrifices by taking the holy dip in the Daśāśvamedha Tīrtha on the Daśaharā day.

## \|\| 2.52.95 \|\|

*svardhunyāḥ paścime tīre natvā daśahareśvaram \|*  
*na durdaśāmavāpnoti pumānpuṇyatamaḥ kvacit \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. On the western bank of the celestial river, one should bow down to Daśahareśvara. He is the holiest of the holy. He never experiences wretchedness.

## \|\| 2.52.96 \|\|

*yatkāśyāṃ dakṣiṇadvāramaṃtargehasya kīrtyate \|*  
*tatra brahmeśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. What is glorified as the southern door of the inner shrine at Kāśī, there the devotee should visit Brahmeśvara. He shall be honoured in the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 2.52.97 \|\|

*iti brāhmaṇaveṣeṇa vārāṇasyāṃ mahādhiyā \|*  
*druhiṇena sthitaṃ tāvadyāvadviśveśvarāgamaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Thus till the arrival of Viśveśvara, the highly intelligent Druhiṇa stayed in Vārāṇasī in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.52.98 \|\|

*divodāsopi rājeṃdro vṛddhabrāhmaṇarūpiṇe \|*  
*brahmaṇe kṛtayajñāya brahmaśālāmakalpayat \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The eminent king Divodāsa got a Brahmaśālā built for the sake of Brahmā in the guise of an aged Brāhmaṇa, when he concluded the Yajña.

## \|\| 2.52.99 \|\|

*brahmeśvarasamīpe tu brahmaśālā manoharā \|*  
*brahmā tatrāvasadvyoma brahmaghoṣairninādayan \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The beautiful Brahmaśālā is near Brahmeśvara. Brahmā set his abode there making the atmosphere reverberating with the recitation of Vedic passages.

## \|\| 2.52.100 \|\|

*iti te kathito brahmanmahimātimahattaraḥ \|*  
*daśāśvamedhatīrthasya sarvāghaughavināśanaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Thus, O holy Brāhmaṇa, the extremely great importance of the Daśāśvamedha Tīrtha has been recounted to you. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 2.52.101 \|\|

*śrutvādhyāyamimaṃ puṇyaṃ śrāvayitvā tathaiva ca \|*  
*brahmalokamavāpnoti śraddhayā mānavottamaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. By listening to this holy chapter and narrating it with faith (Śraddhā), an excellent man obtains the world of Brahmā.

## Chapter 53 - Śiva’s Attendants Go to Vārāṇasī

## \|\| 2.53.1 \|\|

*agastiruvāca \|*  
*apūveṃyaṃ kathā khyātā brahmaṇo brahmavittama \|*  
*kiṃ cakāra punaḥ śaṃbhustatra brahmaṇyapi sthite \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śiva’s Attendants Go to Vārāṇasī

Agasti said:

1\. O Lord who are the foremost among the knowers of Brahman, an unusually interesting story of Brahmā has been narrated. What did Śaṃbhu do, when Brahmā too stayed there itself?

## \|\| 2.53.2 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇvagastya mahābhāga kāśyāṃ brahmaṇyapisthite \|*  
*giriśaściṃtayāmāsa bhṛśamudvignamānasaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

2\. O Agastya, O blessed one, when Brahmā too stayed at Kāśī, Giriśa who was extremely afflicted in mind, began to think.

## \|\| 2.53.3 \|\|

*purī sā yādṛśī kāśī vaśīkaraṇabhūmikā \|*  
*na tādṛśīdṛśīhāsītkvacinme prāyaśo dhruvam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. ‘That city of Kāśī is a fascinating place. Such a city has never come within the range of my vision.

## \|\| 2.53.4 \|\|

*yo yo yāti purīṃ tāṃ tu sa sa tatraiva tiṣṭhati \|*  
*abhūvannanuyoginyo'yoginyaḥ kāśisaṃgatāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Whoever goes to that city stays behind. Indeed the Yoginīs having come into contact with Kāśī have become Ayoginīs (non-Yoginīs).

## \|\| 2.53.5 \|\|

*akiṃcitkaratāṃ prāptaḥ sa sahasrakaropyaram \|*  
*vidhirvidhānadakṣopi na me sa savidhobhavat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Even the thousand-rayed Sun has become ineffective. Even Vidhi, clever in arranging everything, has not been able to accomplish my object.’

## \|\| 2.53.6-7 \|\|

*ciṃtayanniti deveśo gaṇānārahūya bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*preṣayāmāsa bho yāta kṣipraṃ vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kiṃ kurvaṃti tu yoginyaḥ kiṃ karoti sa bhānumān \|*  
*gatvā vitta tvarāyuktā vidhiśca vidadhāti kim \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. After thinking thus, the Lord of Devas called many of his attendants and sent them saying, “Oh, go quickly to the city of Vārāṇasī. After going quickly, find out what the Yoginīs do. What is that Sun-god doing and what Vidhi is doing.”

## \|\| 2.53.8-15 \|\|

*nāmagrāhaṃ tataḥ'praiṣīdbahumāna puraḥsaram \|*  
*śaṃkukarṇa mahākāla ghaṭākarṇa mahodara \|\| 8 \|\|*

*somanaṃdinnaṃdiṣeṇa kāla piṃgala kukkuṭa \|*  
*kuṃḍodara mayūrākṣa bāṇa gokarṇa tāraka \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tilaparṇa smṛlakarṇa dṛmicaṃḍa prabhāmaya \|*  
*sukeśa viṃdate chāga kapardinpiṃgalākṣaka \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vīrabhadra kirātākhya caturmukha nikuṃbhaka \|*  
*paṃcākṣabhārabhūtākhya tryakṣa kṣemaka lāṃgalin \|\| 11 \|\|*

*virādha sumukhāṣāḍhe bhavaṃto mama sūnavaḥ \|*  
*yathemau skaṃdaheraṃbau naigameyo yathā tvayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yathā śākhaviśākhau ca yathemau naṃdibhṛṃgiṇau \|*  
*bhavatsu vidyamāneṣu mahāvikramaśāliṣu \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kāśīpravṛttiṃ no jāne divodāsanṛpasya ca \|*  
*yoginyarkavidhīnāṃ ca taddvau yātaṃ bhavatsvamū \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śaṃkukarṇamahākālau kālasyāpi prakaṃpanau \|*  
*jñātuṃ vārāṇasīvārtāmāyātaṃ catvarānvitau \|\| 15 \|\|*

8-15. He called them by their respective names and sent them with due honour. O Śaṅkukarṇa, O Mahākāla, Ghaṇṭākarṇa, Mahodara, Somanandin, Nandiṣeṇa, Kālapiṅgala, Kukkuṭa, Kuṇḍodara, Mayūrākṣa, Bāṇa, Gokarṇa, Tāraka, Tilaparṇa, Sthūlakarṇa, Dṛmicaṇḍa, Prabhāmaya, Sukeśa, Vindati, O Chāga, Kapardin, Piṅgalākṣaka, Vīrabhadra, O Kirāta, Caturmukha, Nikumbhaka, Pañcākṣa, O Bhārabhūta, Tryakṣa, Kṣemaka, Lāṅgalin, Virādha, Sumukha, Āṣāḍhi—all of you are my sons just as these Skanda and Heraṃba, like this, Naigameya, like this Śākha and Viśākha and Nandī and Bhṛṅgī. Despite your presence, though you possess excessive valour, I do not get any news of Kāśī, nor of King Divodāsa, nor of the Yoginīs, the Sun and Brahmā. Hence let two of you go. This Śaṅkukarṇa and Mahākāla are capable of making even Kāla tremble. Let them go to find out the news of Vārāṇasī and let them return hurriedly.”

## \|\| 2.53.16-17 \|\|

*kṛtapratijñau to tūrṇaṃ prāpya vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*śaṃkukarṇamahākālau vismṛtya śāṃbhavīṃ giram \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yathaiṃdrajālikīṃ dṛṣṭvā māyāmiha vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇena mohamāyāti kāśīṃ vīkṣya tathaiva tau \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Taking a vow accordingly, they quickly reached the city of Vārāṇasī. Just as one, howsoever clever he may be, gets deluded the very moment he sees the tricks of a juggler, so were Śaṅkukarṇa and Mahākāla enamoured as soon as they saw Kāśī.

They thought thus:

## \|\| 2.53.18 \|\|

*aho mohasya māhātmyamaho bhāgyaviparyayaḥ \|*  
*nirvāṇarāśiṃ yatkāśīṃ prāpya yāṃtyanyato'budhāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Oh, how wonderful is the great power of delusion! Oh, what a misfortune! The unwise go away elsewhere after attaining Kāśī, the mass of liberation.

## \|\| 2.53.19 \|\|

*tatyaje yairiyaṃ kāśī mahāśīrvādabhūbhikā \|*  
*teṣāṃ karatalānmuktiḥ prāptāpi parito gatā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Even the salvation which has been achieved slips out of the hands of those persons by whom Kāśī, the ground of great blessings, has been abandoned.

## \|\| 2.53.20 \|\|

*yatra sarvāvabhṛthataḥ snānamātraṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*apyuṣṇīkṛtapānīyaistāṃ kāśīṃ kaḥ parityajet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If one takes bath even with hot water at Kāśī even the valedictory baths of all Yajñas are excelled. Who shall abandon (such) Kāśī?

## \|\| 2.53.21 \|\|

*yatraikapuṣpadānena śivaliṃgasya mūrdhani \|*  
*daśasauvarṇikaṃ puṇyaṃ kastāṃ kāśīṃ parityajet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Even if a single flower is offered on the top of Śiva Liṅga at Kāśī the merit thereof is the same as that of a gift of ten gold pieces? Who shall leave that Kāśī?

## \|\| 2.53.22 \|\|

*yatra daṃḍapraṇāmena apyekena śivāgrataḥ \|*  
*tucchameṃdrapadaṃprāhustāṃ kāśīṃ ko vimuṃcati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. They say that even the position of Indra is insignificant (in comparison with the status) one obtains by means of a single prostration in front of Siva at Kāśī. Who will forsake that Kāśī?

## \|\| 2.53.23 \|\|

*yatraikadvijamātraṃ tu bhojayitvā yathecchayā \|*  
*vājapeyādhikaṃ puṇyaṃ tāṃ kāśīṃ ko vimuṃcati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By feeding a single Brāhmaṇa to his satisfaction at Kāśī, one gets more merit than that of Vājapeya (sacrifice). Who will forsake that Kāśī?

## \|\| 2.53.24 \|\|

*ekāṃ gāṃ yatra dattvā vai vidhivadbrāhmaṇāya vai \|*  
*labhedayuta gopuṇyaṃ kastāṃ kāśīṃ tyajetsudhīḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By duly making the gift of a single cow to a Brāhmaṇa at Kāśī, one gets the merit of gifting ten thousand cows. Which sensible man forsakes that Kāśī?

## \|\| 2.53.25 \|\|

*ekaliṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yatra saṃsthāpitaṃ bhavet \|*  
*api trailokyamakhilaṃ tāṃ kāśīṃ kaḥ samujjhati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. By installing a single Liṅga at Kāśī, one establishes the lordship of three worlds. Who will forsake that Kāśī?

## \|\| 2.53.26 \|\|

*pariniścitya tāvitthaṃ liṃge saṃsthāpya puṇyade \|*  
*tatraiva saṃsthitiṃ prāptau kāśīṃ nādyāpi muṃcataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*
