26\. Both of them resolved thus; they installed two meritorious Liṅgas and permanently stayed there. They have never left (Kāśī) till today.

## \|\| 2.53.27 \|\|

*śaṃkukarṇeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ śaṃkukarṇa ga ṇārcitam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā na jāyate jaṃturjātu māturmahodare \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. By visiting Śaṅkukarṇeśvara Liṅga adored by the attendant Śaṅkukarṇa, a creature is never born in the great womb of any mother.

## \|\| 2.53.28 \|\|

*viśveśādvāyudigbhāge śaṃkukarṇeśvaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*saṃpūjya na viśedatra ghore saṃsārasāgare \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. By worshipping Śaṅkukarṇeśvara on the north-western side of Viśveśa, a man never re-enters the terrible ocean of mundane existence.

## \|\| 2.53.29 \|\|

*mahākāleśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ mahākālagaṇārcitam \|*  
*arcayitvā ca natvā ca stutvā kālabhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Where can one have any fear after bowing down to, adoring and eulogizing Mahākāleśvara Liṅga adored by the attendant Mahākāla?

## \|\| 2.53.30 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śaṃkukarṇe mahākāle ciraṃtana vilaṃbite \|*  
*jñātvā sarvajñanāthotha prāhaipīdaparau gaṇau \|\| 30 \|\|*

Skanda said:

30\. Śaṅkukarṇa and Mahākāla were late by a great deal of time. Knowing this the omniscient Lord despatched two other Gaṇas.

## \|\| 2.53.31 \|\|

*ghaṃṭākarṇa tvamāgaccha mahodara mahāmate \|*  
*kāśīṃ yātaṃ yuvāṃ tūrṇaṃ jñātuṃ tatratya ceṣṭitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “O Ghaṇṭākarṇa, you come. O highly intelligent Mahodara, both of you go to Kāśī quickly to know the situation there.”

## \|\| 2.53.32 \|\|

*ityagaste gaṇau tau tu gatvā kāśīṃ mahāpurīm \|*  
*vyāvṛtyādyāpi no yātau kvāpi tatraiva saṃsthitau \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thus, these two Gaṇas after reaching the great city Kāśī, have not returned till today. They remained at some place there itself.

## \|\| 2.53.33 \|\|

*ghaṃṭākarṇeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ ghaṃṭākarṇa gaṇottamaḥ \|*  
*kāśyāṃ saṃsthāpya vidhivatsvayaṃ tatraiva nirvṛtaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After duly installing Ghaṇṭākarṇeśvara Liṅga at Kāśī, the excellent Gaṇa Ghaṇṭākarṇa took excessive delight in it.

## \|\| 2.53.34 \|\|

*kuṃḍaṃ tatraiva saṃsthāpya liṃgasnapanakarmaṇe \|*  
*nādyāpi sa tyajetkāśīṃ dhyāyaṃlliṃgaṃ tathaiva hi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He dug a sacred pit there itself for performing the

rite of ablution of the Liṅga and meditating upon the Liṅga in the usual manner does not leave Kāśī till today.

## \|\| 2.53.35 \|\|

*mahodaropi tatprācyāṃ śivadhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*mahodareśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ dhyāyedadyāpi kuṃbhaja \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. To the west thereof, Mahodara became engrossed in meditating on Śiva. Even today, O Pot-born Sage, he meditates on Mahodareśvara Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.53.36 \|\|

*mahodareśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā vārāṇasyāṃ dvijottama \|*  
*kadācidapi vai mātuḥ praviśennaudarīṃ darīm \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, after visiting Mahodareśvara in Vārāṇasī, one never enters the cavity of a mother’s belly.

## \|\| 2.53.37 \|\|

*ghaṃṭākarṇa hrade snātvā dṛṣṭvā vyāseśvaraṃ vibhum \|*  
*yatra kutra vipannopi vārāṇasyāṃ mṛto bhavet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. After taking the holy dip in the Ghaṇṭākarṇahraḍa and visiting Lord Vyāseśvara, if a devotee dies elsewhere, he will be deemed one that has died at Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.53.38 \|\|

*ghaṃṭākarṇe mahātīrthe śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*api durgatimāpannānuddharetsaptapūrvajān \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After duly performing Śrāddha in the great Tīrtha, a devotee shall redeem seven ancestors, even if they are suffering in hell.

## \|\| 2.53.39 \|\|

*nimajjyādyāpi tatkuṃḍe kṣaṇa yovahito bhavet \|*  
*viśveśvaramahāpūjā ghaṃṭārāvāñśṛṇoti saḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Even today, after dipping down in that holy pit, if one becomes very attentive for a moment, he surely hears the ringing sound of the bells of the great worship of Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 2.53.40-41 \|\|

*vadaṃti pitaraḥ kāśyāṃ ghaṃṭākarṇemalejale \|*  
*dātā tilodakasyāpi vaṃśe naḥ kopi jāyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

*yadvaṃśyā munayaḥ kāśyāṃ ghaṃṭākarṇe mahāhrade \|*  
*kṛtodakakriyāḥ prāptāḥ parāṃ siddhiṃ ghaṭodbhava \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. O Pot-born One, the ancestors say: “Will not there be one offering gingelly seeds and water in our family in the pure waters of Ghaṇṭākarṇa?” Persons belonging to their family, after performing the libatory rite in the great Hrada Ghaṇṭākarṇa at Kāśī have attained great supernatural powers.

## \|\| 2.53.42-43 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ghaṃṭākarṇe gaṇe yāte prayāte ca mahodare \|*  
*visismāya smaradveṣṭā maulimāṃdolayanmuhuḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*uvāca ca manasyeva haraḥ smitvā punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*mahāmohanavidyāsi kāśi tvāṃ paryavaimyaham \|\| 43 \|\|*

Skanda said:

42-43. When the Gaṇa Ghaṇṭākarṇa had gone and when Mahodara too had gone, the Enemy of Smara (Lord Śiva) became wonderstruck. Shaking his head frequently and smiling again and again, Hara said in his mind: ‘Oh Kāśī! I know you well that you have a great power of bewitching others.

## \|\| 2.53.44 \|\|

*purāvidaḥ praśaṃsaṃti tvāṃ mahāmohahāriṇīm \|*  
*kāśīṃtviti na jānaṃti mahāmohanabhūriyam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Those who are conversant with the affairs of yore praise you as the destroyer of great delusion. But they do not know this aspect of Kāśī that it is a place possessing a great power of creating delusion.

## \|\| 2.53.45 \|\|

*preṣayiṣyāmyahaṃ sarvānbhavatī mohayiṣyati \|*  
*iti samyagvijānāmi kāśi tvāṃ mohanoṣadhim \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. I shall be sending all others and you will enchant them. Thus I know, Kāśī, you, the enchanting herb.

## \|\| 2.53.46 \|\|

*tathāpi preṣayiṣyāmi yāvānmesti paricchadaḥ \|*  
*nodyamādviramaṃtīha jñāninaḥ sādhyakarmaṇi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Still I shall send all the attendants I have. Wise men do not stop their endeavour in a task that has to be accomplished.

## \|\| 2.53.47 \|\|

*nodyamādviratiḥ kāryā kvāpi kārye vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*pratikūlopi khidyeta vidhistatsatatodyamāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Stopping of endeavour should never be resorted to by wise people. Their continuous endeavour can even avert adverse fate.

## \|\| 2.53.48 \|\|

*śītoṣṇabhānū svarbhānu grastāvapi nabhoṃgaṇe \|*  
*gatiṃ na tyajatodyāpi prakrāṃtavya kṛtodyamau \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The Sun and the Moon in the firmament, though assailed by Svarbhānu (Rāhu) never abandon till today their endeavour in regard to what they have undertaken.

## \|\| 2.53.49 \|\|

*ekatra haṃti kāryāṇi prātikūlyādvidhirmuhuḥ \|*  
*ekatrakaraṇīyāni setsyaṃtyatra bhṛśodyamāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Being adverse in one place, fate frequently frustrates actions. In another place all the actions become fruitful by concentration on adequate effort.

## \|\| 2.53.50 \|\|

*daivaṃ pūrvakṛtaṃ karma kathyate netaratpunaḥ \|*  
*tannirākaraṇe yatnaḥ svayaṃ kāryo vipaścitā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. It is the Karma performed before (in previous birth) that is called Daiva (fate) and not anything else. Effort should be made by a sensible man to eradicate it.

## \|\| 2.53.51 \|\|

*bhājanopasthitaṃ daivādbhojyaṃ nāsyaṃ svayaṃ viśet \|*  
*hastavaktrodyamāttacca praviśedaudarīṃ darīm \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Foodstuff that is kept in a vessel does not enter the mouth merely by force of fate. By the actions of hands and mouth, it shall enter the cavity of the belly!

## \|\| 2.53.52 \|\|

*ityudyamaṃ samarthyeśo niścitaṃ daivajitvaram \|*  
*punaśca preṣayāṃcakre gaṇānpaṃcamahārayān \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After justifying endeavour as one that certainly triumphs over fate, the Lord sent five Gaṇas of great impetuosity.

## \|\| 2.53.53 \|\|

*somanaṃdī naṃdiṣeṇaḥ kālapiṃgalakukkuṭāḥ \|*  
*tedyāpi na nivartaṃte kāśyāṃ jīvāmṛtā yathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. They were Somanandī, Nandiṣeṇa, Kāla, Piṅgala and Kukkuṭa. They too have not returned till today, just as dead Jīvas do not.

## \|\| 2.53.54 \|\|

*tepi svanāmnā liṃgāni śaṃbhusaṃtuṣṭi kāmyayā \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpya sthitāḥ kāśyāṃ viśvanirvāṇajanmani \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. With a desire to propitiate Śaṃbhu, they too installed Liṅgas after their names and stayed at Kāśī, the source of origin of salvation.

## \|\| 2.53.55 \|\|

*somanaṃdīśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā liṃgaṃ naṃdavane param \|*  
*somaloke parānaṃdaṃ prāpnuyādbhaktimānnaraḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. By visiting the great Somanandīśvara Liṅga in Nandavana, a man with devotion shall attain the greatest bliss in Somaloka.

## \|\| 2.53.56 \|\|

*taduttare vilokyātha naṃdiṣeṇeśvaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*ānaṃdasenāṃ saṃprāpya jayenmṛtyumapi kṣaṇāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. By visiting Nandiṣeṇeśvara to the north thereof, a man shall get an Ānandasenā (immense delight) and instantaneously conquer even death.

## \|\| 2.53.57 \|\|

*kāleśvaraṃ mahāliṃgaṃ gaṃgāyāḥ paścimottare \|*  
*praṇamya kālapāśena no badhyeta kadācana \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. By bowing down to the great Liṅga Kāleśvara to the north-west of Gaṅgā, one shall avert being bound with the noose of Kāla for ever.

## \|\| 2.53.58 \|\|

*piṃgaleśvaramabhyarcya kāleśātkiṃciduttare \|*  
*labhate piṃgalajñānaṃ yena tanmayatāṃ vrajet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. By adoring Piṅgaleśvara, a little to the north of Kāleśa, one shall obtain knowledge of the form of Piṅgala and attain identity therewith.

## \|\| 2.53.59 \|\|

*kukkuṭeśvara liṃgasya yetra bhaktiṃ vitanvate \|*  
*kukkuṭāṃḍākṛtestasya na te garbhamavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Those who display devotion to Kukkuṭeśvara Liṅga having the shape of hen’s egg will never be born in a womb.

## \|\| 2.53.60 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*somanaṃdi prabhṛtiṣu mune paṃcagaṇeṣvapi \|*  
*ānaṃdakānanaṃ prāpya sthiteṣu sthāṇurabravīt \|\| 60 \|\|*

Skanda said:

60\. When the five Gaṇas, O sage, beginning with Somanandī stayed on at Ānandakānana, Sthāṇu said:

## \|\| 2.53.61-63 \|\|

*kāryamasmākamevaitadyadi samyagvimṛśyate \|*  
*anenopādhināpyete tatra tiṣṭhaṃtu māmakāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*pramatheṣu praviṣṭeṣu māyāvīryamahatsvapi \|*  
*ahameva praviṣṭosmi vārāṇasyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*krameṇa preṣayiṣyāmi yosti me svaparicchadaḥ \|*  
*tatra sarveṣu yāteṣu tato yāsyāmyahaṃ punaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

61-63. “This alone should be done by us, if due reflection is made. Let these persons of mine stay there under this pretext. Even if the Pramathas of greatness and virility enter Vārāṇasī, it is beyond doubt that even (it is as good as) I have entered it. I shall send successively whatever attendant I have. When all have gone, I shall also go.”

## \|\| 2.53.64 \|\|

*saṃpradhāryeti hṛdaye devadevena śūlinā \|*  
*praiṣiṣṭa pramathānāṃ tu tato gaṇacatuṣṭayam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. After deciding thus within the heart, four of his Pramatha Gaṇas were sent by the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 2.53.65 \|\|

*kuṃḍodaro mayūrākhyo bāṇo gokarṇa eva ca \|*  
*māyābalaṃ samāśritya kāśīṃ praviviśurgaṇāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The Gaṇas named Mayūra, Kuṇḍodara, Bāṇa and Gokarṇa resorted to their Māyā power and entered Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.53.66 \|\|

*kṛtvopāyaśataṃ taistu divodāsasya saṃbhrame \|*  
*yadaikopi samartho na tadā tatraiva saṃsthitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. They employed hundreds of means, but none of them was capable of making Divodāsa agitated or confused.

## \|\| 2.53.67 \|\|

*aparādhaśateṣvīśaḥ kena tuṣyati karmaṇā \|*  
*saṃpradhāryeti te cakrurliṃgārādhanamuttamam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. ‘By which action does the Lord become satisfied, if hundreds of offences were committed.’ Pondering thus, they carried on the excellent propitiation of the Liṅgas.

## \|\| 2.53.68 \|\|

*ekasmiñśāṃbhave liṃge vidhinātra samarcite \|*  
*kṣamettryakṣoparādhānāṃ śataṃ mokṣaṃ ca yacchati \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. If a single Liṅga of Śaṃbhu was duly adored here, the Three-eyed Lord may forgive a hundred offences and bestow salvation.

## \|\| 2.53.69 \|\|

*na tuṣyati tathā śaṃbhuryajñadānatapovrataiḥ \|*  
*yathā tuṣyetsakṛlliṃge vidhinābhyarcite sati \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Śaṃbhu is not satisfied with Yajñas, Dānas, Tapas and Vratas to the same extent as when a Liṅga is duly adored even once.

## \|\| 2.53.70 \|\|

*liṃgārcanavidhānajño liṃgārcanarataḥ sadā \|*  
*tryakṣa eva sa vijñeyaḥ sākṣāddvyakṣopi mānavaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. If he is conversant with the procedure of Liṅga worship and is always engaged in the worship of the Liṅga, even if the man possessed two eyes he should be directly conceived as three-eyed.

## \|\| 2.53.71 \|\|

*na gośatapradānena na svarṇaśatadānataḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhyate puṃbhiryatsakṛlliṃgapūjanāt \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Neither by the gift of a hundred cows nor by the gift of a hundred gold pieces, is that benefit obtained by men which they get by worshipping the Liṅga once (only).

## \|\| 2.53.72 \|\|

*aśvamedhādibhiryāgairna tatphalamavāpyate \|*  
*yatphalaṃ labhyate martyairnityaṃ liṃgaprapūjanāt \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. That benefit is not obtained by Yagas like horse-sacrifice, which is obtained by men by worshipping the Liṅga always.

## \|\| 2.53.73 \|\|

*snāpayitvā vidhānena yo liṃgasnapanodakam \|*  
*triḥ pibettrividhaṃ pāpaṃ tasyehāśu praṇaśyati \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. After duly bathing the Liṅga, if the devotee sips thrice the water with which it is bathed, the three types of his sins perish quickly.

## \|\| 2.53.74 \|\|

*liṃga snapanavārbhiryaḥ kuryānmūrdhnyabhiṣecanam \|*  
*gaṃgāsnānaphalaṃ tasya jāyatetra vipāpmanaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. He who bathes his head with the water of the ablution of the Liṅga gets the benefit of holy dip in Gaṅgā, and he becomes free from sin here itself

## \|\| 2.53.75 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ samarcitaṃ dṛṣṭvā yaḥ kuryātpraṇatiṃ sakṛt \|*  
*saṃdeho jāyate tasya punardehanibaṃdhane \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. After visiting an adored Liṅga, if anyone bows down to it even once, doubt arises in respect to his becoming embodied (in the next birth, i.e. he is not born again).

## \|\| 2.53.76 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ yaḥ sthāpayedbhaktyā saptajanmakṛtādaghāt \|*  
*mucyate nātra saṃdeho viśuddhaḥ svargabhāgbhavet \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. If anyone instals \[installs\] a Liṅga with devotion, there is no doubt in this that he becomes free from sins committed in the course of seven births. On being purified, he attains heaven.’

## \|\| 2.53.77 \|\|

*vicāryeti gaṇaiḥ kāśyāṃ svāmidrohopaśāṃtaye \|*  
*pratiṣṭhitāni liṃgāni mahāpātakabhiṃdyapi \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. After thinking thus, Liṅgas that destroy great sins were installed in Kāśī by the Gaṇas for quelling the offence against the master.

## \|\| 2.53.78 \|\|

*kuṃḍodareśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvā lolārkasannidhau \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. By visiting Kuṇḍodareśvara Liṅga near Lolārka, one becomes rid of all sins and is honoured in the world of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.53.79 \|\|

*kuṃḍodareśvarālliṃgātpratīcyāmasirodhasi \|*  
*mayūreśvaramabhyarcya na garbhaṃ pratipadyate \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. One is never conceived in womb, if one adores Mayūreśvara on the banks of Asi to the west of Kuṇḍodareśvara Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.53.80 \|\|

*mayūreśapratīcyāṃ ca liṃgaṃ bāṇeśvaraṃ mahat \|*  
*tasya darśanamātreṇa sarvaiḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The great Bāṇeśvara-Liṅga is to the west of Mayūreśa. Merely by visiting it, one is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 2.53.81 \|\|

*gokarṇeśaṃ mahāliṃgamaṃtargehasya paścime \|*  
*dvāre samarcya vai kāśyāṃ na vighnairabhibhūyate \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. To the west of Antargeha (inner shrine) a devotee should worship the great Liṅga Gokarṇeśa in Kāśī at its very entrance. He is never assailed by obstacles.

## \|\| 2.53.82 \|\|

*gokarṇeśvara bhaktasya paṃcatva samaye sati \|*  
*jñānabhraṃśo na jāyeta kvacidapyaṃtamṛcchataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. When the devotee of Gokarṇeśvara dies, wherever he dies, he does not experience loss of knowledge.

## \|\| 2.53.83 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*cirayatsugaṇeṣveṣu caturṣvapigaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*mahimānaṃ mahattvaṃ tu tatkāśyāḥ paryavarṇayat \|\| 83 \|\|*

Skanda said:

83\. While these four attendants were delaying, the Lord of Gaṇas described the greatness and importance of Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.53.84 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavyā māyayā viśvaṃ bhrāmyetātra yayākhilam \|*  
*dhruvaṃ mūrtimatī saiṣā kāśī viśvaikamohinī \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. ‘The whole universe is deluded by the Māyā of Viṣṇu. Indeed, this Kāśī is the personified form thereof. It is the sole enchanter of the universe.

## \|\| 2.53.85 \|\|

*apāsya sodarāndārānputraṃ kṣetraṃ gṛhaṃ vasu \|*  
*apyaṃgīkṛtya nidhanaṃ sarve kāśīmupāsate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Setting aside brothers, wives, son, land, house and wealth, even facing death, all resort to Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.53.86 \|\|

*maraṇādapi no kāśyāṃ bhayaṃ yatra manāgapi \|*  
*gaṇāstatra tu tiṣṭhaṃtaḥ kuto mattopi bibhyati \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. While there is nothing to fear from even death at Kāśī, why should the Gaṇas staying there be afraid even of me?

## \|\| 2.53.87 \|\|

*maraṇaṃ maṃgalaṃ yatra vibhūtiryatra bhūṣaṇam \|*  
*kaupīnaṃ yatra kauśeyaṃ kāśī kutropamīyate \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. To which can Kāśī be compared, where death is an auspicious thing, ashes an embellishment and a loincloth a silk garment?

## \|\| 2.53.88 \|\|

*nirvāṇaramaṇī yatra raṃkaṃ vā'raṃkameva vā \|*  
*brāhmaṇaṃ vā śvapākaṃ vā vṛṇīte prāṃtyabhūṣaṇam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. There the maiden (in the form) of Salvation chooses everyone having Prāntyabhūṣaṇa (the Tāraka Upadeśa at the time of death as an embellishment), whether he is rich or poor, a Brāhmaṇa or a Cāṇḍāla.

## \|\| 2.53.89 \|\|

*mṛtānāṃ yatra jaṃtūnāṃ nirvāṇapadamṛcchatām \|*  
*koṭyaṃśenāpi na samā api śakrādayaḥ surāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Even Śakra and other Suras are not on a par with a ten-millionth part of the creatures meeting with death at Kāśī and attaining salvation.

## \|\| 2.53.90 \|\|

*yatra kāśyāṃ mṛto jaṃturbrahmanārāyaṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*prabaddha mūrdhāṃjalibhirnamasyetātiyatnataḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. A creature that dies at Kāśī is bowed to intently by Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa and others with joined palms on their heads.

## \|\| 2.53.91 \|\|

*yatra kāśyāṃ śavatvepi jaṃturnāśucitāṃ vrajet \|*  
*atastatkarṇasaṃsparśaṃ karomyahamapi svayam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. In the state of a corpse, the creature does not become unclean in Kāśī. Hence I myself touch its ear.

## \|\| 2.53.92 \|\|

*yastu kāśīti kāśīti dvistrirjapati puṇyavān \|*  
*api sarvapavitrebhyaḥ sa pavitrataro mahān \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A meritorious person who repeats twice or thrice the word Kāśī is holier than all holy things. He is the greatest (of all).

## \|\| 2.53.93 \|\|

*yena kāśī hṛdi dhyātā yena kāśīha sevitā \|*  
*tenāhaṃ hṛdi saṃdhyātastenāhaṃ sevitaḥ sadā \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. I have been meditated upon in the heart, I have been served always by that person by whom Kāśī has been meditated upon in the heart and by whom Kāśī has been served.

## \|\| 2.53.94 \|\|

*kāśīṃ yaḥ sevate jaṃturnirvikalpena cetasā \|*  
*tamahaṃ hṛdaye nityaṃ dhārayāmi prayatnataḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. If a living being serves Kāśī with unfaltering mind, I retain him always in my heart assiduously.

## \|\| 2.53.95 \|\|

*svayaṃ vastumaśaktopi vāsayettīrthavāsinam \|*  
*apyekamapi mūlyena sa vastuḥphalabhāgdhruvam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. If one is unable to stay personally, one should make at least one person stay there by hiring him as a resident of the holy place. Certainly, he gets the benefit of the one who resides.

## \|\| 2.53.96 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ vasaṃti ye dhīrā āpaṃcatva viniścayāḥ \|*  
*jīvanmuktāstu te jñeyā vaṃdyāḥ pūjyāsta eva hi \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Those intelligent men of fortitude, who resolve to stay in Kāśī until death, should be known as liberated ones even while alive. They alone are venerable and adorable.’

## \|\| 2.53.97 \|\|

*itthaṃ vimṛśya bahuśaḥ sthāṇurvārāṇasīguṇān \|*  
*gaṇānanyānsamāhūya prāhiṇotprītipūrvakam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. After reflecting thus on the merits of Vārāṇasī many times, Sthāṇu called other Gaṇas and joyously sent them.

## \|\| 2.53.98 \|\|

*tārakatvaṃ samāgaccha gacchāti svacchamānasa \|*  
*divodāso vṛṣāvāso yāmadhīṣṭe varāṃ purīm \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. “O Tāraka come on; O clear-minded one, go to that city which Divodāsa, the abode of righteousness, rules.

## \|\| 2.53.99-101 \|\|

*tilaparṇa sdhūlakarṇa dṛmicaṃḍa prabhāmaya \|*  
*sukeśa viṃdate chāga kapardinpiṃgalākṣaka \|\| 99 \|\|*

*vīrabhadra kirātākhya caturmukha nikuṃbhaka \|*  
*paṃcākṣa bhārabhūtākhya tryakṣa kṣemakalāṃgalin \|\| 100 \|\|*

*virādha sumukhāṣāḍhe yāṃtu sarve pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*ete gaṇā mahābhāgāḥ svāmibhaktā dṛḍhavratāḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

99-101. O Tilaparṇa, O Sthūlakarṇa, O Dṛmicaṇḍa, O Prabhāmaya, O Sukeśa, O Vindati, O Chāga, O Kapardin, O Piṅgalākṣaka, O Vīrabhadra, O Gaṇa named Kirāta, O Caturmukha, O Nikuṃbhaka, O Pañcākṣabhāra, O Bhūtakya, O Tryakṣa, O Kṣemaka, O Lāṅgalin, O Virādha, O Sumukha, O Āṣāḍhi, let all the Gaṇas, the blessed ones devoted to their master and of steady resolve, go separately.”

## \|\| 2.53.102 \|\|

*kṛtvā māyā bahuvidhā bahurūpā vicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*animeṣekṣaṇāstasthuḥ kṣoṇīśacchidrakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Desirous of finding out a vulnerable point in the king, they kept awake with winkless eyes. Those clever Gaṇas adopted many Māyās, forms and shapes.

## \|\| 2.53.103 \|\|

*aparujñāta tacchidrā vidrāvitayaśodhanāḥ \|*  
*āḥ kimetadahojātaṃ niniṃduḥ svamitīha te \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Unable to find out his weakness, they wasted the wealth of their reputation and they uttered in disgust, “Ah! What has befallen?” They censured themselves.

## \|\| 2.53.104 \|\|

*gaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*dhigasmānsvāminā nityaṃ kṛtasaṃbhāvanānmuhuḥ \|*  
*manuṣyamātramapyatra yairekaṃ na vaśīkṛtam \|\| 104 \|\|*

Gaṇas said:

104\. Fie upon us who were always honoured by our Lord! It is however pitiful indeed that not even a single man could be brought under our control here.

## \|\| 2.53.105 \|\|

*bahumānena dānena sauhārdena mahīyasā \|*  
*kṛtaprasādāṃstryakṣeṇa dhiṅnastatkāryavaṃcakān \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Fie upon us who have failed to do the duty toward the Three-eyed Lord who has bestowed favours upon us along with great honour, gift and friendship!

## \|\| 2.53.106 \|\|

*kā gatirno bhavitrīha svāmikṛtyapramādinām \|*  
*aṃdhaṃ tamomaye loke dhruvaṃ vāso bhaviṣyati \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. What fate shall befall us, since we have blundered in our duty towards our master? Certainly, our residence shall be in a world full of blinding darkness.

## \|\| 2.53.107 \|\|

*akṛtasvāmikāryāṇāmaho jīvitadhāriṇām \|*  
*akṣateṃdriyavṛttīnāṃ durgatiśca pade pade \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Alas! At every step those persons will suffer, who do not fulfil the task of the Lord, yet continue to live with unimpaired activities of the sense-organs.

## \|\| 2.53.108 \|\|

*labdhasaṃbhāvanānāṃ ca nyakkṛtasvāmikarmaṇām \|*  
*bhṛtyānāṃ bhūribhājāṃ ca bhaṃgurāḥ syurmanorathāḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The desires of the servants who take a lot after being honoured, but who spoil the task of the Lord, become frustrated.

## \|\| 2.53.109 \|\|

*aniṣpāditakāryārthā ye mukhaṃ prekṣayaṃtyaho \|*  
*apatrapāḥ puro bhartustairbhūrbhāravatītviyam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. This earth becomes burdened with those servants who do not fulfil the task of their masters and who shamelessly stand in front of the Lord and stare at his face!

## \|\| 2.53.110 \|\|

*nādrīṇāṃ na samudrāṇāṃ na drumāṇāṃ mahīyasām \|*  
*bhūtadhātryāstathā bhāro yathā svāmidruhāṃ mahān \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. The earth, the mother of living beings, does not have great unbearable burden, because of mountains, oceans and huge trees but due to that of the traitors to the Lord.

## \|\| 2.53.111 \|\|

*aho paurāṇikī gāthā smṛtāsmābhiraniṃditā \|*  
*tadarthamavalaṃbyeha sthāsyāmaḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Ha! A famous ancient Gāthā (verse) has been remembered by us. It is for that purpose that we will stay here with steady resolve to stick to it.

## \|\| 2.53.112 \|\|

*anākalitapuṇyānāṃ parikṣīṇadhanāyuṣām \|*  
*sarvopāyavihīnānāṃ gatirvārāṇasīpurī \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The city of Vārāṇasī is the refuge unto those who have not acquired Puṇyas, whose wealth and longevity have become reduced and who are devoid of all means.

## \|\| 2.53.113 \|\|

*apuṇyabhārakhinnānāṃ paścāttāpamupeyuṣām \|*  
*viṣvagūrdhvagatīnāṃ ca gatirvārāṇasīpurī \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. The city of Vārāṇasī is the refuge unto those who are depressed due to the weight of sins, who experience repentance and who move up and around everywhere.

## \|\| 2.53.114 \|\|

*svāmidruhaḥ kṛtaghnāśca ye ca viśraṃbhaghātakāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti muktvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. There is no refuge anywhere except at the city of Vārāṇasī to those who are disloyal traitors to their masters, who are ungrateful and who kill treacherously.

## \|\| 2.53.115 \|\|

*itthaṃ niścitya gāthārthaṃ pramathā avatasthire \|*  
*avijñātasvarūpāśca divodāsena bhūbhujā \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. After deciding this to be the meaning (implication) of the Gāthā, the Pramathas remained there without their forms being known to King Divodāsa.

## \|\| 2.53.116 \|\|

*na bubodha sa bhūpālo nitarāṃ buddhimānapi \|*  
*vibudhānvividhākāraiḥ sthitānīśaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Though that king was extremely intelligent, he did not come to know (the existence) of those sensible Gaṇas stationed there in various forms and shapes by the power of Īśa.

## \|\| 2.53.117 \|\|

*citraṃ na citraguptopi vetti vārāṇasīsthitān \|*  
*jaṃtūnkā gaṇanānyeṣāṃ martyalokanivāsinām \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. It is surprising that not even Citragupta knows those creatures stationed in Vārāṇasī. Nothing need be said about others residing in the mortal world!

## \|\| 2.53.118 \|\|

*avicchinna prabhāvāṇāmaparicchinna tejasām \|*  
*kṛtaliṃgapratiṣṭhānāṃ nāṃtaṃ prāpnoti dharmarāṭ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Dharmarāṭ (Lord Yama) never gauges fully persons of unbroken power and influence, of unlimited brilliance, who have installed the Liṅgas.

## \|\| 2.53.119 \|\|

*iti te pramathāḥ sarve ghaṭodbhava mahāmune \|*  
*kṛtaliṃgārcanāḥ kāśīṃ nādyāpyujjhaṃti śarmadām \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Thus, O Pot-born Great Sage, all those Pramathas who have been regularly worshipping Liṅgas do not leave even today Kāśī, the bestower of welfare.

## \|\| 2.53.120 \|\|

*tārakeśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ tārakākhyo gaṇottamaḥ \|*  
*tārakajñānadaṃ puṃsāṃ mune'dyāpi samarcayet \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. O sage, the excellent Gaṇa named Tāraka worships even today the great Liṅga Tārakeśa that bestows the redeeming Tāraka Jñāna.

## \|\| 2.53.121 \|\|

*tārakeśvaraliṃgasya kṛtvā bhaktisuniścalām \|*  
*sukhena tārakajñānaṃ labhyate tairnarottamaiḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. After showing steady devotion to Tārakeśvara Liṅga, Tāraka knowledge is easily acquired by excellent men.

## \|\| 2.53.122 \|\|

*tilaparṇeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tilaparṇa pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*tilapramāṇamapyatra dṛṣṭvā pāpaṃ na saṃbhavet \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. By visiting Tilaparṇeśvara Liṅga installed by Tilaparṇa, there cannot remain sin, even of the size of a gingelly seed sticking to one.

## \|\| 2.53.123 \|\|

*sthūlakarṇeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ paripūjya narottamaḥ \|*  
*na durgatimavāpnoti puṇyamāpnoti cottamam \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. After duly performing the worship of Sthūlakarṇeśvara Liṅga, a man attains excellent merit. He never attains a wretched state.

## \|\| 2.53.124 \|\|

*dṛmicaṃḍeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tathā liṃgaṃ prabhāmayam \|*  
*ārādhya tatpratīcyāṃ ca na pāpairabhibhūyate \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. To the west thereof, the devotee should propitiate Dṛmicaṇḍeśvara Liṅga and Prabhāmaya Liṅga. He is never assailed by sins.

## \|\| 2.53.125 \|\|

*prabhāmayeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvānyatrāpi saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*prabhāmayena yānena śivaloke vrajetsudhīḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. After visiting Prabhāmayeśvara Liṅga, even if the devotee dies elsewhere, he shall go to Śivaloka through a Prabhāmaya (refulgent) vehicle.

## \|\| 2.53.126 \|\|

*sukeśeśvaramabhyarcya harikeśavane naraḥ \|*  
*ṣāṭkauśikamayaṃ dehaṃ dhārayenna punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. After adoring Sukeśeśvara in the Harikeśa grove, the devotee does not bear the Ṣāṭkauśika (‘made of the six dhātus’) body repeatedly.

## \|\| 2.53.127 \|\|

*viṃdatīśaṃ narobhyarcya bhīmacaṃḍī samīpataḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā pracaṃḍamapyeno mokṣaṃ viṃdati śāśvatam \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. By adoring Vindatīśa near Bhīmacaṇḍī, the man casts off even the most horrible sin and attains eternal salvation.

## \|\| 2.53.128 \|\|

*chāgaleśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ pitrīśvarasamīpagam \|*  
*vilokya paśuvatkopi na pāpaṃ prākṛtaṃ spṛśet \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. By visiting the great Liṅga Chāgaleśa stationed near Pitrīśvara, no one touches even Prākṛta sin like a brute.

## Chapter 54 - The Greatness of Piśācamocana Tīrtha

## \|\| 2.54.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*kuṃbhasaṃbhava vakṣyāmi śṛṇotvavahito bhavān \|*  
*kapardīśasya liṃgasya mahāmāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This tank \[viz., Piśācamocana-tīrtha\] is on the western skirt of Vārāṇasī. By performing Śrāddha of a person who died in an accident etc., the (dead) person becomes free from the state of a goblin. People drive spike in the trunk of a tree in the temple area. (BCL 267-268)

Skanda said:

1\. O Pot-born One, I shall narrate the greatness and importance of Kapardīśa Liṅga. May Your Holiness kindly listen attentively.

## \|\| 2.54.2-3 \|\|

*kapardī nāma gaṇapaḥ śaṃbhoratyaṃtavallabhaḥ \|*  
*pitrīśāduttare bhāge liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya śāṃbhavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kuṃḍaṃ cakhāna tasyāgre vimalodaka saṃjñakam \|*  
*yasya toyasya saṃsparśādvimalo jāyate naraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. A certain leader of the Gaṇas named Kapardin, a very great lover of Śaṃbhu, installed the Liṅga of Śaṃbhu to the north of Pitrīśa. In front of it, he dug a pit named Vimalodaka. The very touch of the water thereof makes man free from impurities.

## \|\| 2.54.4 \|\|

*itihāsaṃ pravakṣyāmi tatra tretāyuge purā \|*  
*yathāvṛttaṃ kuṃbhayone śravaṇātpātakāpaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I shall narrate a traditional legend exactly as the events took place there formerly in Tretā Yuga. O Kuṃbhayoni, listening to it dispels sin.

## \|\| 2.54.5 \|\|

*ekaḥ pāśupata śreṣṭho vālmīkiriti saṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*tapaścacāra sa muniḥ kapardīśaṃ samarcayan \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There was an excellent Pāśupata (devotee of Paśupati) named Vālmīki. The sage performed penance adoring Kapardīśa.

## \|\| 2.54.6-7 \|\|

*ekadā sa hi hemaṃte mārge māsi tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*snātvā tatra mahātīrthe madhyāhne vimalodake \|\| 6 \|\|*

*cakāra bhasmanā snānamāpādatalamastakam \|*  
*liṃgasya dakṣiṇebhāge kṛtamādhyāhnikakriyaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Once in the Hemanta season in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, that ascetic took his bath in the holy Tīrtha Vimalodaka at midday and then took Bhasmasnāna (smearing holy ash) all-over the body. He performed all the midday holy rites on the right side of the Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.54.8-9 \|\|

*nyastamastakapāṃsuśca saṃdhyāmādhyātmikīṃ smaran \|*  
*japanpaṃcākṣarīṃ vidyāṃ dhyāyandevaṃ kapardinam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kṛtvā saṃhāramārgeṇa sapramāṇaṃ pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*huḍuṃkṛtya huḍuṃkṛtya huḍuṃkṛtya triruccakaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. He placed (applied) the holy dust on the forehead, he meditated on the identity of the soul and the Absolute, repeated the Pañcākṣarī Vidyā (namaḥ śivāya) and then pondered over Lord Kapardin. After making the prescribed number of circumambulations along the Saṃhāra Mārga (Apasavya or anticlock-wise direction), he then loudly uttered ‘Oṃ huḍuṃ’ thrice.

## \|\| 2.54.10-12 \|\|

*praṇavaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā ṣaḍjādisvarabhedataḥ \|*  
*gītaṃ vidhāya sānaṃdaṃ sanṛtyaṃ hastakānvitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*aṃgahārairmanohāri cārī maṃḍalasaṃyutam \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ tatra sarastīre upaviṣṭo mahātapāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*adrākṣīdrākṣasaṃ ghoramatīva vikṛtākṛtim \|*  
*śuṣkaśaṃkhakapolāsyaṃ nimagnā piṃgalocanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Prefixing the Praṇava he uttered the Svaras (musical notes) Ṣaḍja etc. and sang. With great delight he danced depicting the Hasta Mudrās, Aṅgahāras, delightful Cārīmaṇḍalas etc. The sage of great penance then sat for a short while on the banks of the lake. Then he saw a terrible Rākṣasa of hideous features. The bones at the temples and cheeks were dried up. The whole face was pale. The tawny eyes were sunk in their cavities.

## \|\| 2.54.13 \|\|

*rūkṣasphuṭitakeśāgraṃ mahālaṃba śirodharam \|*  
*atīva cipiṭa ghrāṇaṃ śuṣkauṣṭhamatidaṃturam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The ends of hairs were rough and dishevelled. The neck was very long and lean, the nose flat to the extreme, the lips dry and the teeth long and projected.

## \|\| 2.54.14 \|\|

*mahāviśālamauliṃ ca prordhvībhūtaśiroruham \|*  
*pralaṃbakarṇapālīkaṃ piṃgalaśmaśrubhīṣaṇam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. His head was very huge. The hairs on the scalp stood erect. The lobes of ears were hanging loose. He was terrible with his tawny moustache and beard.

## \|\| 2.54.15 \|\|

*pralaṃbita lalajjihvamatyutkaṭa kṛkāṭikam \|*  
*sthūlāsthi jatru saṃsthānaṃ dīrghaskaṃdhadvayotkaṭam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The lolling, hanging tongue was fearful; the back of the neck was very rough. The bones of the collar region were stout, tough and the two broad shoulders increased his ferociousness.

## \|\| 2.54.16 \|\|

*nimagnakakṣākuharaṃ śuṣkahrasva bhujadvayam \|*  
*viralāṃgulihastāgraṃ natapīna nakhāvalim \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The armpits were deep; the pair of arms were dry and short. The fingers of the palms were separated. The big nails were depressed.

## \|\| 2.54.17 \|\|

*viśuṣka pāṃsulotkroḍaṃ pṛṣṭhalagnodaratvacam \|*  
*kaṭītaṭena vikaṭaṃ nirmāṃsatrikabaṃdhanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The chest was excessively rough and dusty and slightly protruding; the skin of the belly seemed to touch the back. He was fierce with the ample waist and hips. The sacral bone was devoid of flesh.

## \|\| 2.54.18 \|\|

*pralaṃba sphigyugayutaṃ śuṣkamuṣkālpamehanam \|*  
*dīrghanirmāṃsalorūkaṃ sthūlajānvasthipaṃjaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The two buttocks were loose and suspended. The penis was short with shrunk testicles. The thigh-bones were free from (i.e., without) flesh and long. The stout bones of the kneecap appeared like a cage of bones.

## \|\| 2.54.19 \|\|

*asthicarmāvaśeṣaṃ ca śirājālitavigraham \|*  
*śirālaṃ dīrghajaṃghaṃ ca sthūlagulphāsthibhīṣaṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Mere skin and bones had remained in his body; the entire physical form seemed to be full of sinews and tubular vessels. The shanks were long. He was terrible with the big bones of the ankles.

## \|\| 2.54.20 \|\|

*ativistṛta pādaṃ ca dīrghavakrakṛśāṃgulim \|*  
*asthicarmāvaśeṣeṇa śirātāḍitavigraham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The feet were very broad. The toes were long, thin and crooked. The entire body was prominent with the skin and bone over-spread with sinews.

## \|\| 2.54.21 \|\|

*vikaṭaṃ bhīṣaṇākāraṃ kṣutkṣāmamatilomaśam \|*  
*dāvadagdhadrumākāramati caṃcalalocanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He was awful, terrible in size with thick growth of hairs. He appeared to be very hungry. He looked like a tree burnt in forest fire. The eyes were rolling and unsteady.

## \|\| 2.54.22-24 \|\|

*mūrtaṃ bhayānakamiva sarvaprāṇibhayapradam \|*  
*hṛdayākaṃpanaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ pretaṃ vṛddhatāpasaḥ \|*  
*atidīnānanaṃ kastvamiti dhairyeṇa pṛṣṭavān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kutastvamiha saṃprāptaḥ kasmātte gatirīdṛśī \|*  
*anukrośadhiyārakṣaḥ pṛcchāmi vada nirbhayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*asmākaṃ tāpasānāṃ ca na bhayaṃ tvadvidhānmanāk \|*  
*śivanāmasahasrāṇāṃ vibhūtikṛtavarmaṇām \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. He looked an embodiment of the (poetic) sentiment of fear (Bhayānaka). He struck terror in all living beings. On seeing that ghost terrifying the hearts of onlookers though piteous in the face, the old ascetic boldly asked him: “Who are you? Whence have you come here? Wherefore is this condition of yours? O Rākṣasa, I am asking with a compassionate heart. Speak out without fear. We ascetics are adequately protected with the holy ash as a coat of mail. We repeat the thousand names of Śiva (for welfare).”

## \|\| 2.54.25 \|\|

*tāpasodīritamiti tadrakṣaḥ prītipūvarkam \|*  
*niśamya prāṃjaliḥ prāha taṃ kṛpāluṃ tapodhanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing the utterance of the ascetic joyously, the Rākṣasa said to the sympathetic sage, with palms joined in reverence:

## \|\| 2.54.26 \|\|

*rākṣasa uvāca \|*  
*anukrośosti yadi te bhagavaṃstāpasottama \|*  
*svavṛttāṃtaṃ tadā vacmi śṛṇuṣvāvahitaḥ kṣaṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

Rākṣasa said:

26\. O holy Sir, O excellent ascetic, if you have any sympathy, listen for a short while with great attention. I shall recount the facts about me.

## \|\| 2.54.27 \|\|

*pratiṣṭhānābhidhānosti deśo godāvarī taṭe \|*  
*tīrthapratigraharucistatrāsaṃ brāhmaṇastvaham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On the banks of Godāvarī, there is a region named Pratiṣṭhāna. I was a Brāhmaṇa living there on Tīrtha-pratigraha (‘monetary gifts from pilgrims’).

## \|\| 2.54.28 \|\|

*tena karmavipākena prāptosmi gatimīdṛśīm \|*  
*marusthale mahāghore tarutoyavivarjite \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. As a result of that act, I have attained this miserable plight in a desert region which is highly terrible, devoid of water and trees.

## \|\| 2.54.29 \|\|

*gato bahutaraḥ kālastatra me vasato mune \|*  
*kṣudhitasya tṛṣārtasya śītatāpasahasya ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O sage, I have spent a great deal of time in residing there, hungry, distressed with thirst and enduring chillness and heat.

## \|\| 2.54.30 \|\|

*varṣatyapi mahāmeghe dhārāsārairdivāniśam \|*  
*prāvṛṭkāle'nile vāti kiṃcitprāvaraṇaṃ na me \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When huge clouds shower great downpour day and night, when the wind blows in the rainy season, I do not have anything to cover myself.

## \|\| 2.54.31 \|\|

*parvaṇyadattadānā ye kṛtatīrthapratigrahāḥ \|*  
*ta imāṃ yonimṛcchaṃti mahāduḥkha nibaṃdhanīm \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Those who do not make monetary gifts on festive occasions but accept Tīrtha-pratigraha (Dakṣiṇā from pilgrims) attain birth like this, involving great misery.

## \|\| 2.54.32 \|\|

*gate bahutithe kāle marubhūmau mune mayā \|*  
*dṛṣṭo brāhmaṇadāyāda ekadā kaścidāgataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After a great deal of time had elapsed, O sage, once a Brāhmaṇa boy was seen arriving there at the desert region.

## \|\| 2.54.33 \|\|

*sūryodayamanuprāpya saṃdhyāvidhivivarjitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā mūtrapurīṣe tu śaucācamanavarjitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. At the time of sunrise, he did not perform the Sandhyā rites. After urinating and voiding the bowels, he did not perform the purificatory rites of Śauca and Ācamana.

## \|\| 2.54.34 \|\|

*muktakacchamaśaucaṃ ca saṃdhyākarmavivarjitam \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā taccharīrehaṃ saṃkrāṃto bhogalipsayā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On seeing him devoid of Śauca and Sandhyā Karmas and behaving like a Muktakaccha (Buddhist heretic) I passed into his body for the purpose of enjoyment.

## \|\| 2.54.55 \|\|

*vimṛśyeti sa vai citte piśācaṃ prāha sattamaḥ \|*  
*vimalode sarasyasminsnāhi re pāpanuttaye \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O sage, because of my ill luck that Brāhmaṇa boy came to this holy city along with a merchant due to greed of wealth.

## \|\| 2.54.36 \|\|

*aṃtaḥpuri praviṣṭobhūtsa dvijo munisattama \|*  
*taccharīrādbahirbhūtastvahaṃ pāpaiḥ samaṃ kṣaṇāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O excellent sage, that Brāhmaṇa went into the interior of the city. Along with his sins I came out of his body instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.54.37 \|\|

*praveśo nāsti cāsmākaṃ pretānāṃ tapasāṃ nidhe \|*  
*mahatāṃ pātakānāṃ ca vārāṇasyāṃ śivājñayā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. By the command of Śiva, O storehouse of austerities, we ghosts and great sins do not have the right of entry in Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.54.38 \|\|

*adyāpi tāni pāpāni tadbahirnirgamecchayā \|*  
*bahireva hi tiṣṭhaṃti sīmni pramathasādhvasāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Even today those sins wait outside for him to come out. They are afraid of the Pramathas guarding the border.

## \|\| 2.54.39 \|\|

*adya śvo vā paraśvo vā sa bahirnirgamiṣyati \|*  
*ityāśayā sthitāḥ smo vai yāvadadya tapodhana \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O ascetic, till today we stood waiting with the hope that he would come out today, tomorrow or the day after.

## \|\| 2.54.40 \|\|

*nādyāpi sa bahirgacchennādyāpyāśā prayāti naḥ \|*  
*ityāsmahe nirādhārā āśāpāśa niyaṃtritāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Even today he has not come out. Even today our hope does not cease to be. Thus, fettered by the ropes of hope, we stay on though without any ground to stand on.

## \|\| 2.54.41 \|\|

*citramadyatanaṃ vacmi tapasviṃstanniśāmaya \|*  
*atīva bhāvi kalyāṇamiti manye'dhunaiva hi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. I shall speak of today’s miracle. O ascetic, listen to it now itself. I think something very good is bound to happen.

## \|\| 2.54.42 \|\|

*āprayāgaṃ pratidinaṃ prayāmaḥ kṣudhitā vayam \|*  
*āhārakāmyayā kvāpi paraṃ no kiṃcidāpnumaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Everyday with great hunger we go as far as Prayāga with a desire for something to eat, but we do not get it anywhere.

## \|\| 2.54.43 \|\|

*saṃti sarvatra phalinaḥ pādapāḥ pratikānanam \|*  
*jalāśayāśca svacchāpāḥ saṃti bhūmyāṃ padepade \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Everywhere, in every forest, there are fruit-bearing trees. There are reservoirs with clear water on the earth at every step.

## \|\| 2.54.44 \|\|

*anyānyapi ca bhakṣyāṇi sarveṣāṃ sulabhānyaho \|*  
*pānānyapi vicitrāṇi saṃti bhūyāṃsi sarvataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. There are other types of foodstuff easily accessible to all. There are plenty of varieties of beverages everywhere.

## \|\| 2.54.45-47 \|\|

*paraṃ no dṛggatānyeva dūre dūre vrajaṃtyaho \|*  
*daivādadyaikamāyāṃtaṃ dṛṣṭvā kārpaṭikaṃ mune \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasyāṃtikamahaṃ prāptaḥ kṣudhayā paripīḍitaḥ \|*  
*prasahya bhakṣayāmyenamiti matvā tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*yāvattaṃ tu jighṛkṣāmi tāvattadvadanāṃbujāt \|*  
*śivanāmapavitrā vāṅniragādvighnahāriṇī \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. But, the moment they come within our sight they move far away. Fortunately, O sage, on seeing a pilgrim today afflicted with hunger as I was, I approached him thinking that I should eat him forcibly. I was about to seize him quickly when words purified by the name of Śiva came out of his lotus-like mouth—words which removed all obstacles.

## \|\| 2.54.48 \|\|

*śivanāmasmaraṇato madīyamapi pātakam \|*  
*maṃdībhūtaṃ tatastena praveśaṃ labdhavānaham \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. By remembering Śiva’s name, my sin too became reduced. Hence I got entrance here.

## \|\| 2.54.49 \|\|

*sīmasthaiḥ pramathairnāhaṃ sadyo dṛggocarīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*śivanāmaśrutau yeṣāṃ tānna paśyedyamopi yat \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. I was not immediately observed by the Pramathas at the border, since Yama too does not see those who have Śiva’s name always sounding in their ears.

## \|\| 2.54.50 \|\|

*aṃtargehasya sīmānaṃ prāptastena sahādhunā \|*  
*sa tu kārpaṭiko madhyaṃ praviṣṭohamihasthitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Now I came as far as the border of Antargeha (Inner Shrine) along with him. That pilgrim went into the inside. I have stayed behind.

## \|\| 2.54.51 \|\|

*ātmānaṃ bahumanyehaṃ tvāṃ vilokyādhunā mune \|*  
*māmuddhara kṛpālo tvaṃ yonerasmātsadāruṇāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O sage, having seen you, I regard myself honoured now. O merciful one, save me from this terrible state.

## \|\| 2.54.52-54 \|\|

*iti pretavacaḥ śrutvā sa kṛpālustapodhanaḥ \|*  
*manasā ciṃtayāmāsa dhiṅnijārthodyamānnarān \|\| 52 \|\|*

*svodaraṃ bhara yaḥ sarve paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥ \|*  
*sa eva dhanyaḥ saṃsāre yaḥ parārthodyataḥ sadā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tapasādya nijenāhaṃ pretametamaghāturam \|*  
*māmeva śaraṇaṃ prāptamuddhariṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. On hearing these words of the ghost, that compassionate ascetic thought in his mind: ‘Fie upon those men who work only for their own sake! All the beasts, birds etc. are mere fillers of their own bellies. In this world only he is blessed who is always engaged for the sake of others. With my power of penance, I shall undoubtedly redeem this sin-distressed ghost who has sought refuge in me.’

## \|\| 2.54.55-56 \|\|

*vimṛśyeti sa vai citte piśācaṃ prāha sattamaḥ \|*  
*vimalode sarasyasminsnāhi re pāpanuttaye \|\| 55 \|\|*

*piśāca te piśācatvaṃ tīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*kapardīśekṣaṇādadya kṣaṇātkṣīṇaṃ vinaṃkṣyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. After reflecting thus in his mind the excellent sage said to the Piśāca: “Take bath in this lake Vimaloda for the sake of quelling your sins. By the power of this Tīrtha and the visit paid to Kapardīśa, O Piśāca, your Piśācahood will become weak and then perish.”

## \|\| 2.54.57 \|\|

*śrutveti sa munervākyaṃ pretaḥ prāha praṇamya tam \|*  
*prītātmā prītamanasaṃ prabaddhakarasaṃpuṭaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On hearing these words of the sage who was delighted in his mind, the ghost with joy in his heart, bowed down to him. With the palms joined together he said to him:

## \|\| 2.54.58-59 \|\|

*pānīyaṃ pātumapi no labheyaṃ munisattama \|*  
*snānasya kā kathā nātha rakṣeyurjaladevatāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*pānasyāpyatra kā vārtā jalasparśopi durlabhaḥ \|*  
*iti pretoktamākarṇya sa bhṛśaṃ prītimānabhūt \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. “O excellent sage, O my lord, I do not get water even to drink, where then is the possibility of bath? As the deities of water will protect it, there can be talk of drinking here? Even the touch of water is very difficult to get.”

On hearing this statement of the ghost, he experienced great pleasure.

## \|\| 2.54.60 \|\|

*uvāca ca tapasvī taṃ jagaduddharaṇakṣamaḥ \|*  
*gṛhāṇemāṃ vibhūtiṃ tvaṃ lalāṭaphalake kuru \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The ascetic who was capable of redeeming the whole universe said: “You take this holy ash and apply it to your broad forehead.

## \|\| 2.54.61 \|\|

*asmādvibhūtimāhātmyātpreta kopi na kutracit \|*  
*bādhā karoti kasyāpi mahāpātakinopyaho \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Due to the greatness of this holy ash, O ghost, no one anywhere will harass or create obstacles to even great sinners.

## \|\| 2.54.62 \|\|

*bhālaṃ vibhūtidhavalaṃ vilokya yamakiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*pāpinopi palāyaṃte bhītāḥ pāśupatāstrataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On seeing the forehead of even a sinner whitened by the Vibhūti (holy ash), the servants of Yama become terrified of the Pāśupata missile and take to flight.

## \|\| 2.54.63 \|\|

*asthidhvajāṃkitaṃ dṛṣṭvā yathā pāṃthā jalāśayam \|*  
*dūraṃ yaṃti tathā bhasma bhālāṃkaṃ yamakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. On seeing a pond marked (spoiled) with bones, banners etc., wayfarers keep themselves away from them, and similarly the servants of Yama from one who is marked with holy ash and flowers.

## \|\| 2.54.64 \|\|

*kṛtabhūti tanutrāṇaṃ śivamaṃtrairnarottamam \|*  
*nopasarpaṃti niyatamapi hiṃsrāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Even the beasts of prey all-round never approach an excellent man fortified with Bhūti as a protecting coat of mail and guarded by Śivamantras.

## \|\| 2.54.65 \|\|

*bhaktyā bibharti yo bhasma śivamaṃtrapavitritam \|*  
*bhāle vakṣasi dormūle na taṃ hiṃsaṃti hiṃsakāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. If anyone devoutly smears with Bhasma sanctified by Śiva Mantra, the forehead, the chest, the root of the arm, cruel beings do not injure him.

## \|\| 2.54.66-67 \|\|

*sarvebhyo duṣṭasattvebhyo yato rakṣedaharniśam \|*  
*rakṣatyeṣā tataḥ proktā vibhūtirbhūtikṛdyataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*bhāsanādbhartsanādbhasma pāṃsuḥ pāṃsutvadāyataḥ \|*  
*pāpānāṃ kṣāraṇātkṣāro budherevaṃ nirucyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. The holy ash is declared as Rakṣā because it guards us day and night from all the wicked animals. Since it causes prosperity it is called Vibhūti. Since it illuminates (Bhāsana) the world or dispels (Bhartsana) Avidyā and its creations, it is called Bhasma. Since it minces sins it is called Pāṃsu. And since it eradicates (Kṣāraṇa) sin, it is called Kṣāra. The terms are thus (etymologically) explained by scholars.”

## \|\| 2.54.68 \|\|

*gṛhītvā dhāramadhyātsa bhasma pretakare'rpayat \|*  
*sopyādarātsamādāya bhāladeśe nyaveśayat \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He took the Bhasma from its receptacle and placed it in the hand of the ghost. He received it with veneration and applied it over the forehead.

## \|\| 2.54.69 \|\|

*vibhūtidhāriṇaṃ vīkṣya piśācaṃ jaladevatāḥ \|*  
*jalāvagāhanaparaṃ vārayāṃcakrire na tam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. On seeing the Piśāca marked with Vibhūti, the deities of waters did not prevent him as he was ready to dive into water.

## \|\| 2.54.70 \|\|

*snātvā pītvā sa nirgacchedyāvattasmājjalāśayāt \|*  
*tāvatpaiśācyamagamaddivyadehamavāpa ca \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. By the time he took his bath, drank water and came out of the lake his Piśācahood disappeared. He attained a divine body.

## \|\| 2.54.71 \|\|

*divyamālāṃbaradharo divyagaṃdhānulepanaḥ \|*  
*divyayānaṃ samāruhya vartma prāptotha pāvanam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Wearing divine garlands and garments, applying divine scents and unguents he got into a divine vehicle and reached the aerial path.

## \|\| 2.54.72 \|\|

*gacchatā tena gagane sa tapasvī namaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*proccaiḥ provāca bhagavanmocitosmi tvayānagha \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. As he went along the sky that ascetic was bowed down to by the Piśāca. He spoke loudly, “O sinless holy Sir, I have been liberated by you.

## \|\| 2.54.73 \|\|

*tasmātkadaryayonitvādatīva pariniṃditāt \|*  
*asya tīrthasya māhātmyāddivyadehamavāptavān \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Thanks to the greatness of this Tīrtha. I attained a divine physical form far different from that miserable birth extremely censured (by all).

## \|\| 2.54.74 \|\|

*piśācamocanaṃ tīrthamadyārabhya samākhyayā \|*  
*anyeṣāmapi paiśācyamidaṃ snānāddhariṣyati \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. From today onwards, this Tīrtha shall be known by the name Piśācamocana. Through ablution, this Tīrtha shall eradicate Piśācahood of others as well.

## \|\| 2.54.75-76 \|\|

*asmiṃstīrthe mahāpuṇye ye snāsyaṃtīha mānavāḥ \|*  
*piṃḍāṃśca nirvapiṣyaṃti saṃdhyātarpaṇapūrvakam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*daivātpaiśācyamāpannāsteṣāṃ pitṛpitāmahāḥ \|*  
*tepi paiśācyamutsṛjya yāsyaṃti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. If in this highly meritorious Tīrtha, men take their holy dip, offer balls of rice along with Sandhyā prayers and libations, their Pitṛs and Pitāmahas who by ill-luck had acquired Piśācahood will cast off the same and attain the greatest goal (Mokṣa).

## \|\| 2.54.77 \|\|

*adyaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ mārgemāsi taponidhe \|*  
*atra snānādikaṃ kāryaṃ paiśācyaparimocanama \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Today, O ascetic, on the fourteenth lunar day of the bright half of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, the rites of ablution etc. should be carried out (as they are) conducive to the eradication of Piśācahood.

## \|\| 2.54.78 \|\|

*imāṃ sāṃvatsarīṃ yātrāṃ ye kariṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*tīrthapratigrahātpāpānniḥsariṣyaṃti te narāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Those men who perform annual pilgrimage here will be liberated from the sin of Tīrtha-pratigraha (acceptance of dāna in a Tīrtha).

## \|\| 2.54.79 \|\|

*piśācamocane snātvā kapardīśaṃ samarcya ca \|*  
*kṛtvā tatrānnadānaṃ ca naronyatrāpi nirbhayāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. By taking the holy dip at Piśācamocana, worshipping Kapardīśa and making gift of cooked food there, men can be fearless elsewhere (i.e. there is no need to be afraid of death elsewhere).

## \|\| 2.54.80 \|\|

*mārgaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ kapardīśvara saṃnidhau \|*  
*snātvānyatrāpi maraṇānna paiśācyamavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. On the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of Mārgaśīrṣa, if a devotee takes his holy dip (in the Tīrtha) before Kapardīśa, he shall not attain Piśācahood even if he dies elsewhere.”

## \|\| 2.54.81 \|\|

*ityuktvā divyapuruṣo bhūyobhūyo namasya tam \|*  
*tapodhanaṃ mahābhāgo divyāṃ gatimavāptavān \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. After saying thus the divine person bowed down to that ascetic again and again. The blessed one attained divine goal.

## \|\| 2.54.82 \|\|

*tapodhanopi taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāścaryaṃ ghaṭodbhava \|*  
*kapardīśvaramārādhya kālānnirvāṇamāptavān \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. O Pot-born One, after witnessing that great miracle, the ascetic propitiated Kapardīśvara and attained salvation in due course of time.

## \|\| 2.54.83 \|\|

*piśācamocanaṃ tīrthaṃ tadārabhya mahāmune \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ parāṃ khyātimagamatsarvapāpahṛt \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Beginning with this, O great sage, the Tīrtha at Vārāṇasī, Piśācamocana, the destroyer of all sins, attained great renown.

## \|\| 2.54.84 \|\|

*paiśācamocane tīrthe saṃbhojya śivayoginam \|*  
*koṭibhojyaphalaṃ samyagekaika parisaṃkhyayā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. If in the Paiśācamocana Tīrtha one feeds a single Śivayogin, one attains the benefit of feeding ten million persons.

## \|\| 2.54.85 \|\|

*śrutvādhyāyamimaṃ puṇyaṃ naro niyatamānasaḥ \|*  
*bhūtaiḥ pretaiḥ piśācaiśca kadācinnābhibhūyate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. By listening to this holy chapter with restrained mind, a man is never attacked by goblins, ghosts and vampires.

## \|\| 2.54.86 \|\|

*bālagrahābhibhūtānāṃ bālānāṃ śāṃtikārakam \|*  
*paṭhanīyaṃ prayatnena mahākhyānamidaṃ param \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. This great narrative should be assiduously read to bring about peace and quiescence among children attacked by Bālagrahas (‘goblins attacking children’).

## \|\| 2.54.87 \|\|

*idamākhyānamākarṇya gacchandeśāṃtaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*coravyāghrapiśācādyairnābhibhūyeta kutracit \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. If a man proceeds to another land, after listening to this narrative, he will be nowhere assailed by thieves, tigers, Piśācas etc.

## Chapter 55 - Ganeśa Proceeds on a Mission to Kāśī

## \|\| 2.55.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*anyepi ye gaṇāstatra kāśyāṃ liṃgāni cakrire \|*  
*tāṃśca te kathayiṣyāmi kuṃbhayone niśāmaya \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. O Kuṃbhayoni (Pot-born Sage), listen. I shall speak to you about the Liṅgas that the other Gaṇas installed there at Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.55.2 \|\|

*gaṇena piṃgalākhyena piṃgalākhyeśasaṃjñitam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ śaṃbhoḥ kapardīśādudagdiśi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Liṅga of Śaṃbhu named Piṅgalākhyeśa was installed to the north of Kapardīśa by the Gaṇa named Piṅgala.

## \|\| 2.55.3 \|\|

*tasya darśanamātreṇa pāpānāṃ jāyate kṣayaḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadro mahāprīto devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Merely by visiting it, sins are eradicated. Vīrabhadra was a great favourite of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 2.55.4 \|\|

*vīrabhadreśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ dhyāyedadyāpi niścalaḥ \|*  
*tasya darśanamātreṇa vīrasiddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Even today, one should steadily meditate upon Vīrabhadreśvara Liṅga. Merely by visiting it attainment of heroic powers takes place.

## \|\| 2.55.5 \|\|

*avimukteśvarātpaścādvīrabhadreśvaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*samarcya na raṇe bhaṃgaṃ kadācidapi cāpnuyāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By worshipping Vīrabhadreśvara behind Avimukteśvara, one shall be victorious. He will never face obstacles or defeat in battle.

## \|\| 2.55.6 \|\|

*vīrabhadraḥ svayaṃ sākṣādvīramūrtidharo mune \|*  
*saṃharedviprasaṃghātamavimuktanivāsināma \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O sage, Vīrabhadra himself possesses the body of a hero. He destroys the mass of obstacles of the residents of Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.55.7 \|\|

*bhadrayā bhadrakālyā ca bhāryayā śubhayā yutam \|*  
*vīrabhadraṃ narobhyarcya kāśīvāsaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. By worshipping Vīrabhadra accompanied by his auspicious and splendid spouse Bhadrakālī a man obtains the benefit of residence at Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.55.8 \|\|

*kirātena kirāteśaṃ liṃgaṃ kāśyāṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*kedārāddakṣiṇe bhāge bhaktānāmabhayapradam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Kirāteśa Liṅga was installed to the south of Kedāra in Kāśī by Kirāta. It bestows freedom from fear on the devotees.

## \|\| 2.55.9 \|\|

*caturmukho gaṇaḥ śrīmānvṛddhakāleśa sannidhau \|*  
*caturmukheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ dhyāyedadyāpi niścalaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A glorious Gaṇa, Caturmukha, is meditating steadily even today on Caturmukheśvara Liṅga near Vṛddhakāleśa.

## \|\| 2.55.10 \|\|

*bhaktāścaturmukheśasya caturānanavaddivi \|*  
*pūjyaṃte surasaṃghātaiḥ sarvabhogasamanvitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The devotees of Caturmukheśa are honoured by the groups of Suras in heaven including Brahmā. They are endowed with all pleasures.

## \|\| 2.55.11 \|\|

*nikuṃbheśvaramālokya nikuṃbhagaṇapūjitam \|*  
*pūjayitvā vrajangrāmaṃ kāryasiddhimavāpnuyāt \|*  
*kubereśa samīpetu śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After visiting Nikuṃbheśvara adored by the Gaṇa Nikuṃbha and worshipping it, if one proceeds to (his) village one shall surely attain the fulfilment of the task. He is honoured in Śivaloka near Kubereśa.

## \|\| 2.55.12 \|\|

*paṃcākṣeśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ mahādevasya dakṣiṇe \|*  
*samabhyarcya naraḥ kāśyāṃ jātismṛtimavāpnuyāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After duly adoring Pañcakeśa, the great Liṅga to the south of Mahādeva in Kāśī, the man shall attain the power of remembering previous birth.

## \|\| 2.55.13 \|\|

*bhārabhūteśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ bhārabhūtagaṇārcitam \|*  
*aṃtargṛhottaradvāri dhyātvā śivapure vaset \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. By meditating on Bhārabhūteśvara Liṅga adored by Bhārabhūta Gaṇa, at the northern gate of Antargṛha, the devotee shall stay in Śivapura.

## \|\| 2.55.14 \|\|

*bhārabhūteśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ yaiḥ kāśyāṃ na vilokitam \|*  
*bhārabhūtāḥ pṛthivyāste'vakeśina iva drumāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Those by whom Bhārabhūteśvara Liṅga has not been visited in Kāśī, have become burdens unto the earth like non-fruit-bearing trees.

## \|\| 2.55.15 \|\|

*gaṇena tryakṣasaṃjñena liṃgaṃ tryakṣeśvaraṃ param \|*  
*trilocanapurobhāge śīlyetādyāpi kuṃbhaja \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Tryakṣeśvara, a great Liṅga, is being meditated upon even today by the Gaṇa named Tryakṣa in front of the Threeeyed Lord, O Pot-born One.

## \|\| 2.55.16 \|\|

*tasya liṃgasya ye bhaktāste tu dehāvasānataḥ \|*  
*tryakṣā eva prajāyaṃte nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Those who are devotees of that Liṅga become threeeyed ones (like Śiva) on death. No doubt need be entertained in this regard.

## \|\| 2.55.17 \|\|

*kṣemako nāma gaṇapaḥ kāśyāṃ mūrtidharaḥ svayam \|*  
*viśveśvaraṃ sarvagataṃ dhyāyedadyāpi niścalaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The leader of Gaṇas named Kṣemaka who assumed a form himself in Kāśī, even today steadily meditates on the omnipresent Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 2.55.18 \|\|

*kṣemakaṃ pūjayedyastu vārāṇasyāṃ mahāgaṇam \|*  
*vighnāstasya pralīyaṃte kṣemaṃ syācca padepade \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. If a devotee worships Kṣemaka, a great Gaṇa, in Vārāṇasī, all his obstacles get dissolved. There shall be welfare (for him) at every step.

## \|\| 2.55.19 \|\|

*deśāṃtaraṃ gato yastu tasyāgamanakāmyayā \|*  
*kṣemakaṃ pūjanīyotra kṣemeṇāśu sa āvrajet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. If someone has gone to another land, Kṣemaka should be worshipped with a desire for his safe return. He will immediately return safe and sound.

## \|\| 2.55.20 \|\|

*lāṃgalīśvaramālokya liṃgaṃ lāṃgalinārcitam \|*  
*viśveśāduttarebhāge na naro rogabhāgbhavet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By visiting Lāṅgalīśvara adored by Lāṅgalin on the northern side of Viśveśa a man never falls ill.

## \|\| 2.55.21 \|\|

*lāṃgalīśaṃ sakṛtpūjya paṃcalāṃgaladānajam \|*  
*phalaṃ prāpnotyavikalaṃ sarvasaṃpatkaraṃ param \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By worshipping even once Lāṅgalīśa, one obtains the entire benefit of the gift of five ploughs. It endows all (kinds of) riches.

## \|\| 2.55.22 \|\|

*virādheśvaramārādhya virādhagaṇapūjitam \|*  
*sarvāparādhayuktopi nāparādhyati kutracit \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. By propitiating Virādheśvara worshipped by the Gaṇa named Virādha, one is free from crimes though one might have committed all the offences.

## \|\| 2.55.23 \|\|

*dinedineparādho yaḥ kriyate kāśivāsibhiḥ \|*  
*sa yāti saṃkṣayaṃ kṣipraṃ virādheśa samarcanāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A crime committed by the residents of Kāśī, becomes wiped off instantaneously by the adoration of Virādheśa.

## \|\| 2.55.24 \|\|

*nairṛte daṃḍhapāṇastu virādheśaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*natvā sarvāparādhebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By assiduously bowing down to Virādheśa to the southwest of Daṇḍapāṇi, one is freed from all offences; there is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.55.25 \|\|

*sumukheśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ sumukhākhyagaṇārcitam \|*  
*paścimābhimukhaṃ liṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvā pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. By visiting Sumukheśa, a great Liṅga, that faces west and that was adored by the Gaṇa named Sumukha, one is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 2.55.26 \|\|

*snātvā pilipilā tīrthe sumukheśaṃ vilokya ca \|*  
*sadaiva sumukhaṃ paśyeddharmarājaṃ na durmukham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By taking the holy dip in Pilipilā Tīrtha and visiting Sumukheśa one will always see the pleasant-faced Dharmarāja (god of Death) and not the wry-faced one.

## \|\| 2.55.27 \|\|

*āṣāḍhinārcitaṃ liṃgamāṣāḍhīśvarasaṃjñakam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvāṣāḍhayāṃ naro bhaktyā sarvaiḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. By devoutly visiting on the new-moon day in the month of Āsāḍha, the Liṅga named Āṣāḍhīśvara adored by Āṣāḍhī, a man becomes rid of all sins.

## \|\| 2.55.28 \|\|

*udīcyāṃ bhārabhūteśādāṣāḍhīśaṃ samarcayan \|*  
*āṣāḍhyāṃ paṃcadaśyāṃ vai na pāpaiḥ paritapyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. By worshipping Āṣāḍhīśa to the north of Bhārabhūteśa, on the new-moon day of the month of Āṣāḍha, one is never distressed by sins.

## \|\| 2.55.29 \|\|

*śuciśuklacaturdaśyāṃ paṃcadaśyāmathāpi vā \|*  
*kṛtvā sāṃvatsarīṃ yātrāmanenā jāyate naraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By undertaking the annual Yātrā (pilgrimage) on the fourteenth or fifteenth lunar day in the Śuci months of Jyeṣṭha and Āṣāḍha in the bright half, a man becomes free from sins.

## \|\| 2.55.30-31 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*mune gaṇeṣu caiteṣu vārāṇasyāṃ sthiteṣviti \|*  
*svanāmnā sthāpya liṃgāni viśveśaparituṣṭaye \|\| 30 \|\|*

*viśveśaściṃtayāṃ cakre punaḥ kāśīpravṛttaye \|*  
*kaṃ vā hitaṃ prahityādya nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ bhaje \|\| 31 \|\|*

Skanda said:

30-31. O sage, when these Gaṇas stayed behind in Vārāṇasī after installing Liṅgas after their names for the delight of Viśveśa, Viśveśa thought again regarding the city of Kāśī: ‘Which good one shall I send today and get the greatest delight?

## \|\| 2.55.32 \|\|

*yoginyastigmagurvedhāḥ śaṃkukarṇamukhāgaṇāḥ \|*  
*vyāvṛttyanāgatāḥ kāśyāḥ siṃdhugā iva siṃdhavaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Yoginīs, the hot-rayed Sun, the Creator, the Gaṇas beginning with Śaṅkukarṇa—these have not returned from Kāśī like the rivers that flow into the ocean.

## \|\| 2.55.33 \|\|

*dhuvaṃ kāśyāṃ praviṣṭā ye te praviṣṭā mamodare \|*  
*teṣāṃ vinirgamo nāsti dīptegnau haviṣāmiva \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Certainly those who have entered Kāśī have entered my abdomen. They have no outlet like Havis offered in a well-kindled fire.

## \|\| 2.55.34 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ hi saṃsthitiḥ kāśyāṃ liṃgārcanaratātmanām \|*  
*ta eva mama liṃgāni jaṃgamāni na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Those who are engaged in the worship of Liṅgas and have permanent stay in Kāśī are undoubtedly my mobile Liṅgas.

## \|\| 2.55.35 \|\|

*sthāvarā jaṃgamāḥ kāśyāmacetanasacetanāḥ \|*  
*sarve mamaiva liṃgāni tebhyo druhyaṃti durdhiyaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Mobile and immobile, sentient and otherwise—all are my Liṅgas. Those who hate them are wicked ones.

## \|\| 2.55.36 \|\|

*vāci vārāṇasī yeṣāṃ śrutau vaiśveśvarī kathā \|*  
*ta eva kāśī liṃgāni varāṇyarcyānyahaṃ yathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Those in whose mouth there is Vārāṇasī, those in whose ears there is the story of Viśveśvara—only they are the Liṅgas of Kāśī worthy of being worshipped as I am.

## \|\| 2.55.37 \|\|

*vārāṇasīti kāśīti rudrāvāsa iti sphuṭam \|*  
*mukhādvinirgataṃ yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ na prabhavedyamaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Yama will not overpower them from whose mouths these clear words—Vārāṇasī, Kāśī and Rudravāsa—come out.

## \|\| 2.55.38 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānanaṃ prāpya ye nirānaṃdabhūmikām \|*  
*anyāṃ hṛdāpi vāṃchaṃti nirānaṃdāḥ sadātra te \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Those who, after reaching Ānanda Kānana, yearn for any other place (city) that is not the place of bliss, remain always devoid of bliss here.

## \|\| 2.55.39 \|\|

*adyaiva vāstumaraṇaṃ bahukālāṃtarepi vā \|*  
*kalikāla bhiyā puṃsāṃ kāśī tyājyā na karhicit \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Let death come today or after a long time, Kāśī should never be abandoned by men for fear of Kali (Age) and Kāla (god of Death).

## \|\| 2.55.40 \|\|

*avaśyaṃbhāvino bhāvā bhaviṣyaṃti padepade \|*  
*salakṣmīnilayāṃ kāśīṃ te tyajaṃti kuto dhiyaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Inevitable events will take place at every step. It is persons without intellect who abandon Kāśī that is the abode of prosperity.

## \|\| 2.55.41 \|\|

*varaṃ vighnasahasrāṇi soḍhavyāni padepade \|*  
*kāśyāṃ nānyatra nirvighnaṃ vāṃchedrājyamapi kvacit \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. It is better to endure thousands of obstacles at every step in Kāśī and not elsewhere. One should never desire an unimpeded kingdom anywhere else.

## \|\| 2.55.42 \|\|

*kiyannimeṣasaṃbhogyāḥ saṃti lakṣmyāḥ padepade \|*  
*paraṃ niraṃtarasukhā'mutrāpyatrāpi kā śikā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. How many moments (eye-winkings) can prosperity be enjoyed continuously? But Kāśikā yields great pleasure continuously here and hereafter.

## \|\| 2.55.43 \|\|

*viśvanātho hyahaṃ nāthaḥ kāśikāmuktikāśikā \|*  
*sudhātaraṃgā svargaṃgā trayyeṣā kinna yacchati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. I, the Lord of the universe, am the lord (here). Kāśikā is the illuminator of salvation. The celestial river has nectarine waves. What is it that this combination of three does not bestow?

## \|\| 2.55.44 \|\|

*paṃcakrośyāparimitā tanureṣā purī mama \|*  
*avicchinnapramāṇardhirbhaktanirvāṇakāraṇam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. This city is limited to five Krośas (Krośa = three Kms.); but its prosperity is of unlimited extent. It is the cause of the salvation of a devotee.

## \|\| 2.55.45 \|\|

*saṃsārabhārakhinnānāṃ yātāyātakṛtāṃ sadā \|*  
*ekaiva me purī kāśī dhruvaṃ viśrāmabhṛmikā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Certainly my city, Kāśī, alone is the place of permanent rest for those who come and go and are distressed due to the burden of the worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.55.46 \|\|

*maṃḍapaḥ kalpavallīnāṃ manorathaphalairalam \|*  
*phalitaḥ kāśikākhyoyaṃ saṃsārādhvajuṣāṃ sadā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. This pavilion of wish-yielding creepers bearing abundant fruits of fulfilled cherished desires, is called Kāśikā. It is always at the disposal of wayfarers of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.55.47 \|\|

*cakravarteriyaṃ chatraṃ vicitraṃ sarvatāpahṛt \|*  
*kāśīnirvāṇarājasya mamaśūlocca daṃḍavat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. This Kāśī is the wonderful and distress-dispelling umbrella of the emperor Nirvāṇarāja (‘king of liberation’). Its supporting rod is my lifted-up trident.

## \|\| 2.55.48 \|\|

*nirvāṇalakṣmīṃ ye puṇyāḥ parivāṃchaṃti līlayā \|*  
*niraṃtarasukhaprāptyai kāśī tyājyā na tai nṛbhiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. For the acquisition of incessant happiness, Kāśī should never be abandoned by men of meritorious nature who sportingly desire the glory of salvation.

## \|\| 2.55.49 \|\|

*mamānaṃdavane ye vai niraṃ tara vanaukasaḥ \|*  
*mokṣalakṣmīphalānyatra susvādūni labhaṃti te \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Those who permanently take up their residence in my Ānandavana get here the tasty fruits of the glorious salvation.

## \|\| 2.55.50 \|\|

*nirmamaṃ cāpi nirmohaṃ yā māmapi vimohayet \|*  
*kairna saṃsmaraṇīyā sā kāśī viśvavimohinī \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Kāśī enchants even me despite the fact that I am Nirmama (free from desire of possessions) and Nirmoha (free from delusion). By whom should not that enchantress of the universe be remembered?

## \|\| 2.55.51 \|\|

*nāmāpi madhuraṃ yasyāḥ parānaṃdaprakāśakam \|*  
*kāśyāḥ kāśīti kāśīti sā kaiḥ puṇyairna japyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Her very name is also sweet. It manifests the greatest bliss. Why is she not repeated in Japa by those with merits in possession?

## \|\| 2.55.52 \|\|

*kāśīnāmasudhāpānaṃ ye kurvaṃti niraṃtaram \|*  
*teṣāṃ vartma bhavatyeva sudhāma vasudhāmayam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If people incessantly imbibe the nectarine name of Kāśī, their pathway certainly becomes lustrous and nectarine.

## \|\| 2.55.53 \|\|

*mamatārahitasyāpi mama sarvātmano dhruvam \|*  
*ta eva māmakā loke ye kāśīnāma jāpakāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I am the Ātman of all. I am free from Mamatā (sense of possession). Indeed in this world only those who repeat the name of Kāśī are the people belonging to me.

## \|\| 2.55.54 \|\|

*rahasyamiti vijñāya vārāṇasyā gaṇeśvaraiḥ \|*  
*sabrahmayoginī bradhraiḥ sthitaṃ tatraiva nānyathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. It was after knowing this secret of Vārāṇasī that the Gaṇeśvaras along with the Yoginīs, the Sun and Brahmā stayed there itself and not with any other purpose.

## \|\| 2.55.55 \|\|

*anyathā tāśca yoginyaḥ saraviḥ sapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*te gaṇā māṃ parityajya kathaṃ tiṣṭheyuranyataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If not, how can those Yoginīs, Sun-god, Brahmā and those Gaṇas forsake me and stay elsewhere?

## \|\| 2.55.56 \|\|

*atīva bhadraṃ saṃjātaṃ kāśyāṃ tiṣṭhatsu teṣu hi \|*  
*ekopi bheda prabhavedrājye rājyāṃtaraṃ vinā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A great good has resulted by their staying behind in Kāśī. Even one of them may be able to create split in the kingdom without (the assistance) of another country (intervening).

## \|\| 2.55.57 \|\|

*labdhapraveśāstāvaṃtaste sarve matsvarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*yatiṣyaṃti yatovaśyaṃ madāgamanahetave \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Those who have gained entry are entirely persons having my forms. They will surely try for my arrival there.

## \|\| 2.55.58 \|\|

*anyānapi preṣayāmi matpārśvaparivartinaḥ \|*  
*ye te tatra sthitāḥ śreṣṭhā apigaṃtāsmyahaṃ tataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. I shall send others too from my attendants. Though those who have gone there are all excellent ones, yet I too shall go.’

## \|\| 2.55.59-60 \|\|

*vicāryeti mahādevaḥ samāhūya gajānanam \|*  
*prāhiṇotkathayitveti gaccha kāśīmitaḥ suta \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tatrasthitopi saṃsiddhayai yatasva sahito gaṇaiḥ \|*  
*nirvighnaṃ kuru cāsmākaṃ nṛpe vighnaṃ samācara \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. After reflecting thus Mahādeva called Gajānana and sent him after telling him thus: “O my son, go to Kāśī from here. Staying there, endeavour for the accomplishment of our purpose along with the Gaṇas without any obstacle. Create obstacles in the case of the king.”

## \|\| 2.55.61 \|\|

*ādhāya śāsanaṃ mūrdhni gaṇādhīśotha dhūrjaṭeḥ \|*  
*pratasthe tvaritaḥ kāśīṃ sthitijñaḥ sthitihetave \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Keeping the command of Dhūrjaṭi on his head, Gaṇādhīśa well conversant with the situation, hastened to Kāśī for a stay there.

## Chapter 56 - Manifestation of the Māyā of Gaṇeśa

## \|\| 2.56.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*atheśājñāṃ samādāya gajavaktraḥ pratasthivān \|*  
*śaṃbhoḥ kāśyāgamopāyaṃ ciṃtayanmaṃdarādritaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. Thereafter, pondering on the means of facilitating Śaṃbhu’s arrival at Kāśī, the Elephant-faced One set off from Mandara mountain, duly taking up the behest of Īśa.

## \|\| 2.56.2 \|\|

*prāpya vārāṇasīṃ tūrṇamāśu syaṃdanago vibhuḥ \|*  
*vāḍavīṃ mūrtimālaṃbya prāviśacchakunaiḥ stutaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Lord reached Vārāṇasī quickly proceeding on a fast chariot. He assumed the form of a Brāhmaṇa and entered at a time when good ones eulogized him.

## \|\| 2.56.3 \|\|

*nakṣatrapāṭhako bhūtvā vṛddhaḥ pratyavarodhagaḥ \|*  
*cacāra madhye nagaraṃ paurāṇāṃ prītimāvahan \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He became an old astrologer visiting every house. He moved about in the city delighting the citizens.

## \|\| 2.56.4 \|\|

*svayameva niśābhāge svapnaṃ saṃdarśayannṛṇām \|*  
*prātasteṣāṃ gṛhāngatvā teṣāṃ vakti balābalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He himself showed dreams to the men during the night and went to their houses in the morning explaining the benefits or otherwise thereof.

## \|\| 2.56.5 \|\|

*bhavadbhiradya rātrau yaddṛṣṭaṃ svapnaviceṣṭitam \|*  
*bhavatkautūhalotpattyai tadeva kathayāmyaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “In order to kindle your enthusiasm, I shall recount the various activities seen by you in dream in the night today.

## \|\| 2.56.6 \|\|

*svapatā bhavatā rātrau turye yāme mahāhradaḥ \|*  
*adarśi tatra ca bhavānmajjanmajjaṃstaṭaṃgataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. While sleeping at night a big, deep pond was seen by you in the fourth Yāma. You reached the bank after sinking in the same a couple of times.

## \|\| 2.56.7 \|\|

*tadaṃbupicchile paṃke magnonmagnosi bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*duḥsvapnasyāsya ca mahānvipākoti bhayapradaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. You sank down and got up many times in the mud slimy with its waters. The outcome of this bad dream shall cause you great fear.

## \|\| 2.56.8 \|\|

*kāṣāyavasano muṃḍaḥ praikṣyaho bhavatāpi yaḥ \|*  
*paritāpaṃ mahāneṣa janayiṣyati dāruṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A person with shaven head and wearing ochre-coloured robes was seen by you. He will cause you terrible distress.

## \|\| 2.56.9 \|\|

*rātrau sūryagraho dṛṣṭo mahāniṣṭakaro dhruvam \|*  
*aiṃdradhanurdvayaṃ rātrau yadaloki na tacchubham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The eclipse of the Sun was seen at night. It will certainly cause great evil. The fact that you saw two rainbows at night, is not conducive to auspiciousness.

## \|\| 2.56.10 \|\|

*pratīcyāṃ ravirāgatya prodyaṃtaṃ vyomni śītagum \|*  
*pātayāmāsa bhūpṛṣṭhe tadrājyabhayasūcakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Sun came to the West and made the Moon fall to the ground even as he was about to rise up in the sky. This indicates something fearful to the entire kingdom.

## \|\| 2.56.11 \|\|

*yugapatketuyugalaṃ yudhyamānaṃ parasparam \|*  
*yadadarśi na tadbhadraṃ rāṣṭrabhaṃgāya kevalam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A pair of banners fighting each other were seen. It is not good. It may only bring about split in the kingdom.

## \|\| 2.56.12 \|\|

*viśīryatkeśadaśanaṃ nīyamānaṃ ca dakṣiṇe \|*  
*ātmānaṃ yatsamadrākṣīḥ kuṭuṃbasyāpi bhīṣaṇam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. You saw yourself being carried to the South even as your hairs and teeth were dropping down. This forebodes something awful to the family.

## \|\| 2.56.13 \|\|

*prāsādadhvajabhaṃgoyastvayaikṣata niśākṣaye \|*  
*rājyakṣayakaraṃ viddhi mahotpātāya niścitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. As the night came to a close, you saw the banner on the top of the palace break down. Know that this will certainly cause ruin of the kingdom. It will cause a great danger.

## \|\| 2.56.14 \|\|

*nagarī plāvitā svapne taraṃgaiḥ kṣīranīradheḥ \|*  
*pakṣaistricaturaiḥ śaṃke mahāśaṃkāṃ puraukasām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the dream, the city was flooded with the waves of the ocean of milk. I suspect a great danger to the citizens within three or four fortnights.

## \|\| 2.56.15 \|\|

*svapne vānarayānena yattvamūḍhosi dakṣiṇām \|*  
*atastadvaṃcanopāyaḥ puratyāgo mahāmate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Since in your dream you have been carried in a monkey-vehicle towards the South, O highly intelligent one, the means to nullify its effect is leaving the city for good.

## \|\| 2.56.16 \|\|

*rudatī yā tvayā dṛṣṭā mahilaikā niśātyaye \|*  
*muktakeśī vivasanā sā nārī śrīrivodgatā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The crying woman that you saw towards the close of the night, without clothes and with the hairs dishevelled is the goddess of glory that has departed.

## \|\| 2.56.17 \|\|

*devālayasya kalaśo yattvayā vīkṣitaḥ patan \|*  
*dinaiḥ katipayaireva rājyabhaṃgo bhaviṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The pot-like pinnacle on the top of the temple was seen by you falling down. Within a few days the kingdom will split.

## \|\| 2.56.18 \|\|

*purī parivṛtā svapne mṛgayūthaiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*rorūyamāṇairatyarthaṃ māsenaivodvasī bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the dream the city was surrounded by excessively crying herds of deer (barking dogs—Comm.). It will be abandoned (uninhabited) within a month.

## \|\| 2.56.19 \|\|

*ātāyiyūkagṛdhrādyaiḥ purīmuparicāribhiḥ \|*  
*sūcyatetyāhitaṃ kiṃciddhruvamatra nivāsinām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Certainly some grave mishap unto the residents of this place is being indicated by these falcons, owls, vultures etc. hovering over this city.”

## \|\| 2.56.20 \|\|

*svapnotpātāniti bahūñśaṃsañśaṃsannitastataḥ \|*  
*bahūnuccāṭayāṃcakre sa vighneśaḥ puraukasaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In this way, recounting often these evil forebodings of bad dreams, that Lord of Obstacles expelled many of the city-dwellers.

## \|\| 2.56.21 \|\|

*keṣāṃcitpurato vādīdgrahacāraṃ pradarśayan \|*  
*ekarāśisthitāḥ sauri sitabhaumā na śobhanāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He pointed out to some that the transits of the Planets were not good. “Saturn, Venus and Mars are in the same zodiac.

## \|\| 2.56.22 \|\|

*soyaṃ dhūmagraho vyomni bhittvā saptarṣimaṃḍalam \|*  
*prayātaḥ paścimāmāśāṃ sa nāśāya viśāṃpateḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. This Dhumagraha (Ketu) has pierced through the region of the Great Bear in the firmament and has gone to the West. That indicates ruin unto the king.

## \|\| 2.56.23 \|\|

*aticāragato maṃdaḥ punarvakrādhva saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*pāpagrahasamāyukto na yuktoyamiheṣyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Saturn has gone beyond the zodiac and thereafter is in its regress-path. It is associated with evil Planets (like Rāhu, Ketu and Mars). It is not considered good.

## \|\| 2.56.24 \|\|

*vyatīte vāsare yoyaṃ bhūkaṃpaḥ samapadyata \|*  
*kaṃpaṃ janayate'tīva hṛdo mepi puraukasaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O citizens, the earthquake that happened yesterday seems to cause great trepidation even in my heart.

## \|\| 2.56.25 \|\|

*udīcyādakṣiṇāśāyāṃ yeyamulkā pradhāvitā \|*  
*vilīnā ca viyatyeva sa nirghātaṃ na sā śubhā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. This meteor rose from the North and went quickly towards the South. It then got dissolved in the sky itself with a violent gust of wind and thunderstroke. It is not auspicious.

## \|\| 2.56.26 \|\|

*unmūlito mahāmūlo mahānilarayeṇa yaḥ \|*  
*catvare caityavṛkṣoyaṃ mahotpātaṃ praśaṃsati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. This Caityavṛkṣa (holy fig tree) despite its being deep-rooted has been uprooted by the velocity of the violent gust of wind and it has fallen down in the quadrangle. It indicates a great evil.

## \|\| 2.56.27 \|\|

*sūryodayamanuprāpya prācyāṃ śuṣkatarūpari \|*  
*karaṭo rāraṭītyeṣa kaṭūtkaṭa bhayapradaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. At sunrise the crow has perched itself on the top of a dried-up tree in the East and begins to crow harshly making others very much afraid.

## \|\| 2.56.28 \|\|

*madhye vipaṇi yatūrṇaṃ kauciccāraṇyacāriṇau \|*  
*mṛgau mṛgayatāṃ yātau paurāṇāṃ purato'hitau \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Two deer have dodged the hunters and have gone fast through the middle of the shopping complex in front of the citizens. They are inauspicious to them.

## \|\| 2.56.29 \|\|

*rasālaśālamukulaṃ vīkṣyate yaccharadyadaḥ \|*  
*mahākālabhayaṃ manyepyakālepi puraukasām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Even in this autumn season, birds are seen untimely on the mango and Śāla trees. I think it is foreboding of great fear and danger to the inhabitants of the city.”

## \|\| 2.56.30 \|\|

*sādhvasaṃjanayitveti keciduccāṭitāḥ puraḥ \|*  
*tena vighnakṛtāpaurāḥ kapaṭadvijarūpiṇā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus, terror was generated by Vighneśvara in the guise of a false Brāhmaṇa and some citizens were driven away from (forced to quit) the city.

## \|\| 2.56.31 \|\|

*atha madhyevarodhaṃ sa praviśya nijamāyayā \|*  
*dṛṣṭārthameva kathayanstrīṇāṃ visraṃbhabhūrabhūt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. By using his Māyā power he entered the female apartments and by recounting events experienced by them, he became an object of confidence of the women.

## \|\| 2.56.32 \|\|

*tava putraśataṃ jajñe saptonaṃ śubhalakṣaṇe \|*  
*teṣvekasturagārūḍho bāhyālyāṃ patito mṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “O lady of auspicious features, hundred sons less by seven were born to you. One of them was riding a horse over a bridge outside, when he fell down and died.

## \|\| 2.56.33 \|\|

*aṃtarvatnī tviyaṃ kanyā janayiṣyati śobhanām \|*  
*eṣā hi durbhagā pūrvaṃ sāṃprataṃ subhagā'bhavat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. This pregnant woman will give birth to a splendid daughter. This woman had been wretched before but now she has become blessed and fine.

## \|\| 2.56.34 \|\|

*asau hi rājño rājñīnāmatyaṃtamihavallabhā \|*  
*muktālaṃkṛtiretasyai rājñā dattā nijorasaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. This woman is extremely endearing to the king and the queens. A pearl.ornament from his own bosom has been given to her by the king.

## \|\| 2.56.35 \|\|

*paṃcasaptadinānyeva jātānītīha tarkyate \|*  
*asyai rājñā prasādena grāmau dātumudīritau \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. I think only five or seven days have passed by. Two villages have been promised to be given to her by the king as his favour.”

## \|\| 2.56.36 \|\|

*iti dṛṣṭārthakathanai rājñīmānyobhavaddvijaḥ \|*  
*varṇayaṃti ca tā rājñaḥ parokṣepi guṇānbahūn \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. By saying various things directly experienced, thus, the Brāhmaṇa became one worthy of being honoured by the queens. They began to describe his many good qualities indirectly to the king.

## \|\| 2.56.37 \|\|
