*aho yādṛgasau vipraḥ sarvatrātivicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*suśīlaśca surūpaśca satyavāṅmitabhāṣaṇaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. “How wonderful! This Brāhmaṇa is handsome and has good behaviour in the same way as he is clever in everything. He is truthful and speaks sparingly.

## \|\| 2.56.38 \|\|

*alolupa udāraśca sadācāro jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*api svalpena saṃtuṣṭaḥ pratigrahaparāṅmukhaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He is not greedy. He is liberal-minded. His conduct is good. He has perfect control over the senses. He is satisfied with even a little. He is averse to accepting monetary gifts.

## \|\| 2.56.39 \|\|

*jitakrodhaḥ prasannāsyastvanasūyuravaṃcakaḥ \|*  
*kṛtajñaḥ prītisumukhaḥ parivādaparāṅmukhaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Anger is subdued by him. His face beams with pleasure. He is never malicious or deceitful. He is grateful. His countenance is cheerful. He is averse to calumny and slander.

## \|\| 2.56.40 \|\|

*puṇyopadeṣṭā puṇyātmā sarvavrataparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*śuciḥ śucicaritraśca śrutismṛtiviśāradaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He counsels what is meritorious. He is a pious-souled one. He observes all vows scrupulously. He is clean and his activities are clean. He is efficient in Śrutis and Smṛtis.

## \|\| 2.56.41 \|\|

*dhīraḥ puṇyetihāsajñaḥ sarvadṛksarvasaṃmataḥ \|*  
*kalākalāpakuśalo jyotiḥśāstraviduttamaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He is intelligent and conversant with the holy legends and myths. He is honoured by all and he looks at everything keenly. He is adept in a number of arts. He is the best among those conversant with the treatises on Astronomy.

## \|\| 2.56.42 \|\|

*kṣamī kulīno'kṛpaṇo bhoktā nirmalamānasaḥ \|*  
*ityādi guṇasaṃpannaḥ kopi kvāpi na dṛggataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He has forbearance. He is of noble birth. He is not miserly. He enjoys keeping the mind free from impurities. No one else has been seen elsewhere so richly endowed with these good qualities.”

## \|\| 2.56.43 \|\|

*itthaṃ tāstadguṇagrāmaṃ varṇayaṃtyaḥ padepade \|*  
*kālaṃ vinodayaṃti sma aṃtaḥpuracarāḥ striyaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thus those women of the inner apartment spent their time enumerating his good qualities every now and then.

## \|\| 2.56.44 \|\|

*ekadāvasaraṃ prāpya divodāsasya bhūbhujaḥ \|*  
*rājñī līlāvatī nāma rājñe taṃ vinyavedayat \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Once the chief queen of King Divodāsa named Līlāvatī spoke to the king about him on a suitable occasion.

## \|\| 2.56.45 \|\|

*rājanvṛddho guṇairvṛddho brāhmaṇaḥ suvicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ekosti sa tu draṣṭavyo mūrto brahmanidhiḥ paraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “O king, there is an aged, learned Brāhmaṇa having a number of excellent qualities. He is a great embodiment and storehouse of the Brāhmaṇical virtues and Veḍìc knowledge. You must meet him.”

## \|\| 2.56.46 \|\|

*rājñī rājñā kṛtānujñā sakhīṃ preṣya vicakṣaṇām \|*  
*ānināya ca taṃ vipraṃ brāhmaṃ teja ivāṃgavat \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The permission having been given by the king, the queen sent her clever female companion and brought that Brāhmaṇa who appeared like an embodied form of Brāhmaṇical splendour.

## \|\| 2.56.47 \|\|

*rājāpi dūrādāyāṃtaṃ ta vilokyamahīsuram \|*  
*yatrākṛtirguṇāstatra jaharṣeti vadanhṛdi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. From a distance the king saw the Brāhmaṇa coming and mentally thought thus, ‘Good qualities are present where excellent form and features are found.’ He became delighted.

## \|\| 2.56.48 \|\|

*padairdvitrairnṛpatinā kṛtābhyutthānasatkṛtiḥ \|*  
*caturnigamajābhiḥ sa tamāśīrbhiranaṃdayat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. By going a few steps forward, the king received and honoured him duly. He delighted the king by means of benedictory passages taken from the four Vedas.

## \|\| 2.56.49 \|\|

*kṛtapraṇāmo rājñā sa sādaraṃ dattamāsanam \|*  
*bhejetha kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ sa rājñā tena bhūpatiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The king duly bowed down to the Brāhmaṇa and offered him a seat which he occupied. The king and the Brāhmaṇa mutually enquired about each other’s welfare.

## \|\| 2.56.50 \|\|

*parasparaṃ kuśalinau kuśalau ca kathāgame \|*  
*praśnottarābhyāṃ saṃtuṣṭau dvijavarya kṣamābhṛtau \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The excellent Brāhmaṇa and the king were adepts in the art of conversation. They were pleased at the (mutual) questions and answers.

## \|\| 2.56.51 \|\|

*kathāvasāne rājñātha gehaṃ visasṛje dvijaḥ \|*  
*labdhamānamahāpūjaḥ sa svamāśramamāviśat \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. At the end of the dialogue the Brāhmaṇa was respect fully sent home by the king. Having received great honour and due deference he entered his hermitage.

## \|\| 2.56.52 \|\|

*gate'tha svāśramaṃ vipre divodāso nareśvaraḥ \|*  
*līlāvatyāḥ puro vipraṃ varṇayāmāsa bhūriśaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. When the Brāhmaṇa had gone back to his hermitage, King Divodāsa extolled the Brāhmaṇa before Līlāvatī profusely.

## \|\| 2.56.53 \|\|

*mahādevi mahāprājñe līlāvati guṇapriye \|*  
*yathāśaṃsi tathā viprastatopi guṇavattaraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “O great queen Līlāvatī, O highly intelligent lady fond of good qualities, the Brāhmaṇa has been duly praised. He is more meritorious than the way in which he is eulogized.

## \|\| 2.56.54 \|\|

*atītaṃ vetti sakalaṃ vartamānamavaiti ca \|*  
*praṣṭavyaḥ prātarāhūya bhaviṣyaṃ kiṃcideṣa vai \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He knows everything that has already taken place. He understands the present. In the morning, he is to be called and asked to tell something about the future.”

## \|\| 2.56.55 \|\|

*mahāvibhava saṃbhārairmahābhogairanekadhā \|*  
*vyuṣṭāyāṃ sa nṛpo rātryāṃ prātarāhūtavāndvijam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. When the night dawned, the king invited the Brāhmaṇa in the morning and offered him many kinds of enjoyable things and rich presents.

## \|\| 2.56.56 \|\|

*satkṛtya taṃ dvijaṃ bhaktyā dukūlādi pradānataḥ \|*  
*ekāṃte taṃ dvijaṃ rājā papraccha nijahṛtsthitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He duly welcomed the Brāhmaṇa, devoutly offering him a silk-cloth and other things. When they were alone, the king asked the Brāhmaṇa what had been cherished in the heart.

## \|\| 2.56.57 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*dvijavaryo bhavānekaḥ pratibhātīti niścitam \|*  
*yathātattvavatī te dhīrna tathānyasya me matiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

The king said:

57\. It is certain that you alone appear to me the greatest among Brāhmaṇas. It is my opinion that the intellect of no one else is as much conversant with truth as thine.

## \|\| 2.56.58 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ tu mahāprājñaṃ śāṃtaṃ dāṃtaṃ taponidhim \|*  
*kiṃcitpraṣṭumanā vipra tadākhyāhi yathārthavat \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On seeing you as a highly intelligent storehouse of austerities, having control over the mind and the sense-organs, O Brāhmaṇa, I am inclined to ask you something which please tell me truthfully.

## \|\| 2.56.59 \|\|

*śāsiteyaṃ mayā pṛthvī na tathānyaistu pārthivaiḥ \|*  
*yāvadbhūti mayā bhuktā divyā bhogā anekadhā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. This kingdom has been ruled by me, not so by other kings. Divine pleasures have been enjoyed by me to the (utmost) extent of my prosperity.

## \|\| 2.56.60 \|\|

*nijaurasebhyopyadhikaṃ rātriṃdivamataṃdritam \|*  
*vinirjitya haṭhādduṣṭānprajeyaṃ paripālitā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Without the least lassitude by day or by night, the wicked ones have been controlled by me by force and the subjects have been protected more than my own bosom-born progeny.

## \|\| 2.56.61 \|\|

*dvijapādārcanātkiṃcitsukṛtaṃ vedmi nāparam \|*  
*anenāparikathyena kathiteneha kiṃ mama \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Of what avail is my enumeration not worthy of being repeated? I know that I have some merit due to the adoration of the feet of Brāhmaṇas. Nothing much.

## \|\| 2.56.62 \|\|

*nirvismamiva me cetaḥ sāṃprataṃ sarvakarmasu \|*  
*vicāryārya śubhodarkamata ākhyāhi sattama \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. My mind is not inclined and drawn towards any of the activities. Hence, O noble and excellent Sir, ponder over and tell me what is going to be conducive to welfare.

## \|\| 2.56.63 \|\|

*dvija uvāca \|*  
*api svalpataraṃ kṛtyaṃ yadbhavedbhūbhujāmiha \|*  
*ekāṃte tattu pṛṣṭena vaktavyaṃ sudhiyā sadā \|\| 63 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

63\. Even the minutest duty of kings should always be explained by a wise man when asked privately.

## \|\| 2.56.64 \|\|

*amātyenāpyapṛṣṭena na vaktavyaṃ nṛpāgrataḥ \|*  
*mahāpamānabhītena stokamapyatra kiṃcana \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. But even the least should not be explained even by the minister when not asked, as he is sure to be afraid of great dishonour.

## \|\| 2.56.65 \|\|

*pṛṣṭaścetkathayāmīha mā tatra kuru saṃśayam \|*  
*tatkṛte tava gaṃtā vai mano nirvedakāraṇam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. On being asked, I shall tell. Do not entertain any doubt on that account. If what I say is carried out, you shall understand the cause of your dejection and disinterestedness.

## \|\| 2.56.66 \|\|

*śṛṇu rājanmahābuddhe nāyathārthaṃ bravīmyaham \|*  
*vikrāṃtosyatiśūrosi bhāgyavānasi sarvadā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O king of excellent intellect, listen. I shall not say anything contrary to the fact (truth). You are valorous, extremely courageous and powerful. You are always fortunate.

## \|\| 2.56.67 \|\|

*puṇyena yaśasā buddhyā saṃpannosti bhavānyathā \|*  
*manye tathāmarāvatyāṃ tridaśeśopi naiva hi \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. I think that even in Amarāvatī, the Lord of the gods (Indra) is not as richly endowed with merit, renown and intellect.

## \|\| 2.56.68 \|\|

*sudhiyā tvāṃ guruṃ manye prasādena sudhākaram \|*  
*tejasāsti bhavānarkaḥ pratāpenāśuśukṣaṇiḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. I consider you on a par with Guru (Preceptor of the Devas) in view of the excellent intellect; on a par with the Moon in view of brightness and serenity; you are the very Sun in brilliance and on a par with Fire in respect of your valorous exploit.

## \|\| 2.56.69 \|\|

*prabhaṃjano balenāsi śrīdosi śrīsamarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śāsanena bhavānrudro nirṛtistvaṃ raṇāṃgaṇe \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. You are on a par with the Wind-god in respect of your strength; on a par with Kubera through gifting of wealth; on a par with Rudra in respect of the ability to chastise; you are the very Nirṛti on the battlefield.

## \|\| 2.56.70 \|\|

*duṣṭapāśayitā pāśī yamo niyamane'satām \|*  
*iṃdanāttvaṃ maheṃdrosi kṣamayā tvamasi kṣamā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. You are Pāśī (Varuṇa) who binds the wicked; in regard to the act of controlling the evil ones you are like Yama; you are on a par with Mahendra in respect of your great prosperity; you are on a par with the Earth in forbearance.

## \|\| 2.56.71 \|\|

*maryādayā bhavānabdhirmahattve himavānasi \|*  
*bhārgavo rājanītyāsi rājyena manunā samaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. In the act of abiding by the bounds of morality, you are the ocean; in regard to greatness, you are Himālaya. You are Śukra in royal polity and in the act of ruling a land you are on a par with Manu.

## \|\| 2.56.72 \|\|

*saṃtāpahartāṃbudavatpavitro gāṃganāmavat \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva jaṃtūnāṃ kāśīva sugatipradaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. You are the dispeller of distress like a cloud; holy like the name of Gaṅgā; you are the bestower of excellent goal on all creatures like Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.56.73 \|\|

*rudraḥ saṃhārarūpeṇa pālanena caturbhujaḥ \|*  
*vidhivattvaṃ vidhātāsi bhāratī te mukhāṃbuje \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. In the matter of annihilation you are Rudra; in according protection you are the four-armed Viṣṇu; you are the creator like Brahmā and the Goddess of Speech is in your lotus-like mouth.

## \|\| 2.56.74 \|\|

*tvatpāṇipadme kamalā tvatkrodhesti halāhalaḥ \|*  
*amṛtaṃ tava vāgeva tvadbhujāvaśvinīsutau \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Kamalā (Goddess of wealth) is in your lotus-like hand; there is the poison Halāhala in your anger; your speech is on a par with the divine nectar; your arms are the veritable Aśvinīsutas.

## \|\| 2.56.75 \|\|

*tatkiṃ yattvayi bhūjānau sarvadevamayo hyasi \|*  
*tasmāttava śubhodarko mayā jñātosti tattvataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Everything powerful is in you, O king, because you are the very embodiment of all the Devas. Hence, what is conducive to your auspiciousness is known to me truly.

## \|\| 2.56.76 \|\|

*ārabhyādya dinādbhūpa brāhmaṇo'ṣṭādaśehani \|*  
*udīcyaḥ kaścidāgatya dhruvaṃ tvāmupadekṣyati \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Calculating from today, O king, on the eighteenth day, a Brāhmaṇa from the North will certainly come to you and advise you.

## \|\| 2.56.77 \|\|

*tasya vākyaṃ tvayā rājankartavyamavicāritam \|*  
*tataste hṛtsthitaṃ sarvaṃ setsyatyeva mahāmate \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. His behest should be unhesitatingly carried out by you, O king. Thereby, O highly intelligent one, whatever you have cherished in your heart will be realized.

## \|\| 2.56.78 \|\|

*ityuktvā pṛcchya rājānaṃ labdhānujño dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*viveśa svāśramaṃ tuṣṭo nṛpopyāścaryavānabhūt \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. After saying so, the excellent Brāhmaṇa took leave of the king. After receiving his consent, he joyously entered his hermitage. The king was very much surprised (at the events).

## \|\| 2.56.79 \|\|

*itthaṃ vighnajitā sarvā purī svātmavaśīkṛtā \|*  
*sapaurā sāvarodhā ca sanṛpā nijamāyayā \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Thus the entire city including the king, the subjects and the royal Antaḥpura (female apartment) was brought under his influence by Vighnajit through his own power of Māyā.

## \|\| 2.56.80 \|\|

*kṛtakṛtyamivātmānaṃ tato matvā sa vighnajit \|*  
*vidhāya bahudhātmānaṃ kāśyāṃ sthitimavāpa ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. After considering himself one who has fulfilled his duties, that Lord Vighnajit took various guises himself and stayed on in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.56.81 \|\|

*yadā sa na divodāsaḥ prāgāsītkuṃbhasaṃbhava \|*  
*tadātanaṃ nijaṃ sthānamalaṃcakre gaṇādhipaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Gaṇādhipa adorned his own spot of that time, O Pot-born One, when Divodāsa himself was not present formerly.

## \|\| 2.56.82-83 \|\|

*divodāse narapatau viṣṇunoccāṭite sati \|*  
*punarnavīkṛtāyāṃ ca nagaryāṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 82 \|\|*

*svayamāgatya devena maṃdarātsuṃdarāṃ purīm \|*  
*vārāṇasīṃ prathamatastuṣṭuve gaṇanāyakam \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. When King Divodāsa was expelled by Viṣṇu and the city was renovated by Viśvakarman, the Lord himself came to the beautiful Vārāṇasī city from Mandara and eulogized Gaṇanāyaka at the outset.

## \|\| 2.56.84 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ stuto bhagavatā devadevena vighnajit \|*  
*kathaṃ ca bahudhātmānaṃ sa cakāra vināyakaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

Agastya said:

84\. How was Vighnajit eulogized by the Lord of Devas? How did Vināyaka take various guises himself

## \|\| 2.56.85 \|\|

*kenakena sa vai nāmnā kāśipuryāṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*iti sarvaṃ samāsena kathayasva ṣaḍānana \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. By what names did he establish himself in the city of Kāśī? O Six-faced One, tell all those things briefly.

## \|\| 2.56.86 \|\|

*ityudīritamākarṇya kuṃbhayoneḥ ṣaḍānanaḥ \|*  
*yathāvatkathayāmāsa gaṇarāja kathāṃ śubhām \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. On hearing this utterance of the Pot-born One the Six-faced Lord related to him the auspicious story of Gaṇarāja based on facts.

## Chapter 57 - Manifestation of Dhuṇḍhi Vināyaka and Fifty-six Vināyakas

## \|\| 2.57.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*viśveśo viśvayā sārdhaṃ mayā ca munisattama \|*  
*mahāśākhaviśākhābhyāṃ naṃdibhṛṃgipurogamaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

\[Note: Ḍhuṇḍhi Vināyaka alias Ḍhuṇḍhirāja has a prime position at the centre of Kāśī. He is to be worshipped by pilgrims on entrance to Kāśī. His name is derived from ḍhuḍh—‘to search, to find’ (v 33 in this chapter). Śiva got entrance into Kāśī through his machinations. Hence this name.

This chapter gives the locations of the fifty-six Vināyakas at Kāśī. These Vināyakas are arrayed at the eight directional points in seven concentric circles centring around Ḍhuṇḍhirāja near the Viśvanātha Temple, as follows: (See vv 59-114).—

I. (1) Arka, (2) Durga, (3) Bhīmacaṇḍa, (4) Dehalī; (5) Uddaṇḍa, (6) Pāśapāṇi, (7) Kharva, (8) Siddhivināyka; II. (1) Laṃbodara, (2) Kūṭadanta, (3) Śālakaṭaṇṭaka, (4) Kūṣmāṇḍa, (5) Muṇḍavināyaka, (6) Vikaṭadvija, (7) Rājaputra, (8) Praṇava; III. (1) Vakratuṇḍa, (2) Ekadanta, (3) Trimukha, (4) Pañcāsya, (5) Heraṃba, (6) Vighnarāja, (7) Varada, (8) Modakapriya; IV. (1) Abhayada, (2) Siṃhatuṇḍa, (3) Kūṇītākṣa, (4) Kṣipraprasādana, (5) Cintāmaṇi, (6) Dantahasta, (7) Picaṇḍila, (8) Uddaṇḍamuṇḍa. V. (1) Sthūladanta, (2) Kalipriya, (3) Caturdanta, (4) Dvituṇḍa, (5) Jyeṣṭha, (6) Gajavināyaka, (7) Kālavināyaka, (8) Nāgeśa; VI. (1) Maṇikarṇa, (2) Āśāvināyaka, (3) Sṛṣṭigaṇeśa, (4) Yakṣavighneśa, (5) Gajakarṇa, (6) Citraghaṇṭa, (7) Sthūlajaṅgha, (8) Mitravināyaka; VII. (1)—(5) Moda and others, (6) Jñānavināyaka, (7) Dvāravighneśa, (8) Avimuktavināyaka.\]

Skanda said:

Lord Viśveśa entered the auspicious city of Vārāṇasī.

1\. O excellent sage, Viśveśa was accompanied by Viśvā (Goddess Pārvatī), Mahāśākha, Viśākha and myself. Nandi and Bhṛṅgī proceeded ahead.

## \|\| 2.57.2 \|\|

*naigameyena sahito rudraiḥ sarvatra saṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*devarṣibhiḥ samāyuktaḥ sanakādyairabhiṣṭutaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He was accompanied by Naigameya and surrounded on all sides by Rudras; he was eulogized by Sanaka and others and attended upon by the celestial sages.

## \|\| 2.57.3 \|\|

*samastāyatanādhīśairdikpālairabhinaṃditaḥ \|*  
*tīrthairdarśita tīrthaśca gaṃdharvairgītamaṃgalaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He was hailed with joy by the commanders of all the Āyatanas (regional shrines) and by the Guardians of the Quarters. All the holy Tīrthas displayed their holy waters. Gandharvas sang songs of auspicious import.

## \|\| 2.57.4 \|\|

*kṛtapūjopsarobhiśca nṛtyahastakapallavaiḥ \|*  
*viyatyanāhatairvādyaiḥ samaṃtādanumoditaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He was adored by celestial damsels who danced with the gestures of the hands resembling tender sprouts. He was greeted all round in the firmament by means of musical instruments sounding automatically.

## \|\| 2.57.5 \|\|

*ṛṣīṇāṃ brahmanirghoṣairbadhirīkṛtadiṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*kṛtastutiścāraṇaughairvimānairabhitovṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. All the quarters reverberated with the deafening sounds of the Vedic chants by the sages. The groups of Cāraṇas eulogized him. He was surrounded everywhere by aerial chariots.

## \|\| 2.57.6 \|\|

*triviṣṭapa vadhūmuṣṭibhraṣṭairlājairitastataḥ \|*  
*abhivṛṣṭo mahādevaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The great Lord who was showered with parched grains slipping down through the fists of the ladies of heaven, experienced horripilation due to excess of joy.

## \|\| 2.57.7 \|\|

*dattamālyopahāraśca bahuvidyādharī gaṇaiḥ \|*  
*yakṣaguhyakasiddhaiśca khecarairabhinaṃditaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Many groups of Vidyādhara women offered him garlands as presents. He was greeted and hailed by Yakṣas, Guhyakas, Siddhas and other sky-traversers.

## \|\| 2.57.8 \|\|

*kṛtapraveśa śakuno mṛgaiḥ śakunibhiḥ puraḥ \|*  
*kiṃnarībhiḥ prahaṣṭāsyaiḥ kiṃnarairupavarṇitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Animals and birds went ahead indicating the auspicious omens of the time of entry. Kṛnnarīs and Kinnaras with beaming faces extolled him.

## \|\| 2.57.9 \|\|

*viṣṇunā ca mahālakṣmyā brahmaṇā viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*naṃdinātha gaṇeśena āviṣkṛtamahotsavaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Great festivity was celebrated and displayed by Viṣṇu, Mahālakṣmī, Brahmā, Viśvakarman, Nandin and Gaṇeśa.

## \|\| 2.57.10 \|\|

*nāgāṃganābhiḥ paritaḥ kṛtanīrājanāvidhiḥ \|*  
*praviveśa mahādevaḥ purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ śubhām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Nāga damsels performed the rites of Nīrājana (waving of the lights) all round. Thus the great Lord entered the auspicious city of Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.57.11 \|\|

*paśyatāṃ sarvadevānāmavaruhya vṛṣeṃdrataḥ \|*  
*pariṣvajya gaṇādhīśaṃ provāca vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Even as all the Devas were watching, the Bull-emblemed Lord got down from the great bull, embraced the Lord of Gaṇas and spoke:

## \|\| 2.57.12 \|\|

*yadahaṃ prāptavānasmi purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ śubhām \|*  
*mayāpyatīva duṣprāpyāṃ sa prasādo sya vai śiśoḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “The fact that I have reached the auspicious city of Vārāṇasī, very difficult of access even to me, is due to the favour of this child alone.

## \|\| 2.57.13 \|\|

*yadduṣprasādhyaṃ hi piturapi trijagatītale \|*  
*tatsūnunā susādhyaṃ syādatra dṛṣṭāṃtatā mayi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. What is difficult to be accomplished even by a father in all the three worlds can be easily accomplished by a son. The instance for the same is I myself.

## \|\| 2.57.14 \|\|

*anena gajavaktreṇa svabuddhivibhaveriha \|*  
*kāśīprāptiryathā me syāttathā kiṃcidanuṣṭhitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. By the powers of his intellect, something has been achieved by this Elephant-faced One in order to facilitate my entrance into Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.57.15 \|\|

*putravānahamevāsmi yacca me ciraciṃtitam \|*  
*svapauruṣeṇa kṛtavānabhilāṣaṃ karasthitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I have really become one blessed with a son inasmuch as he has accomplished through his manliness a long-cherished desire of mine.”

## \|\| 2.57.16 \|\|

*ityuktvā tripurīhartā puruhūtādibhiḥ stutaḥ \|*  
*parituṣṭāvasaṃhṛṣṭaḥ spaṣṭagīrbhirgajānanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After saying this, the destroyer of the three cities oft-eulogized by Indra and others, joyously eulogized the Elephantfaced One with dear words.

## \|\| 2.57.17 \|\|

*śrīkaṃṭha uvāca \|*  
*jaya vighnakṛtāmādya bhaktanirvighnakāraka \|*  
*avighnavighnaśamana mahāvighnaikavighnakṛt \|\| 17 \|\|*

Śrīkaṇṭha said:

17\. Be victorious, O foremost one among those who cause obstacles. You are the cause of freedom from obstacles unto your devotees. O one free from obstacles, O subduer of obstacles, O one with great obstacles reduced to a single obstacle!

## \|\| 2.57.18 \|\|

*jaya sarvagaṇādhīśa jaya sarva gaṇāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*gaṇapraṇatapādābja gaṇanātītasadguṇa \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Be victorious, O Lord of all Gaṇas! be victorious, O leader of all Gaṇas, O one whose lotus-like feet are bowed to by the Gaṇas, O one with countless good qualities!

## \|\| 2.57.19 \|\|

*jaya sarvaga sarveśa sarvabuddhyekaśevadhe \|*  
*sarvamāyāprapaṃcajña sarvakarmāgrapūjita \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Be victorious, O omnipresent one, O Lord of all, O single treasure-house of all intellects, O one conversant with all the worlds of Māyā, O Lord worshipped at the beginning in the course of all rites!

## \|\| 2.57.20 \|\|

*sarvamaṃgalamāṃgalya jaya tvaṃ sarvamaṃgala \|*  
*amaṃgalopaśamana mahāmaṃgalahetuka \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O auspicious one among all auspicious ones! Be victorious, O cause of auspiciousness unto all. O subduer of inauspiciousness! O cause of salvation! O most auspicious of all auspicious things!

## \|\| 2.57.21 \|\|

*jaya sṛṣṭikṛtāṃ vaṃdya jaya sthitikṛtānata \|*  
*jaya saṃhṛtikṛtstutya jayasatkarmasiddhida \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Be victorious, O one worthy of the adoration of those who create (like Brahmā and others), O one bowed to by the one who sustains (i.e. Viṣṇu), O one who is venerable to the one who causes annihilation (Rudra)! Be victorious, O one who bestows success in the performance of good acts.

## \|\| 2.57.22 \|\|

*siddhavaṃdyapadāṃbhoja jayasiddhividhāyaka \|*  
*sarvasiddhyekanilaya mahāsiddhyṛddhisūcaka \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O one whose lotus-like feet are worthy of the adoration to Siddhas! Be victorious, O granter of the fulfilment of desires. O sole storehouse of all Siddhis (the eight supernatural powers)! O indicator of great Siddhis and prosperities!

## \|\| 2.57.23 \|\|

*aśeṣaguṇanirmāṇa guṇātīta guṇāgraṇī \|*  
*paripūrṇacaritrārtha jaya tvaṃ guṇavarṇita \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O creator of all Guṇas! O one beyond all the Guṇas! O leader of all good qualities! O one with perfect conduct! O one identical with wealth! Be victorious, O you who are extolled!

## \|\| 2.57.24 \|\|

*jaya sarvabalādhīśa balārāti balaprada \|*  
*balākojjvala daṃtāgra bālābālaparākama \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Be victorious, O Lord of all armies! O bestower of strength on the enemy of Bala (i.e. Indra)! O one with the tips of the teeth as bright as cranes! O young boy of great valour!

## \|\| 2.57.25 \|\|

*anaṃtamahimādhāra dharādhara vidāraṇa \|*  
*daṃtāgraprotāṃ daṅnāga jayanāgavibhūṣaṇa \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Lord, O support of infinite greatness, O piercer of the mountain (Krauñca), O one who has lifted up the Elephants of the Quarters by the tips of the tusks! Be victorious, O (Lord) with serpents for ornaments!

## \|\| 2.57.26 \|\|

*ye tvāṃnamaṃti karuṇāmaya divya mūrte sarvainasāmapi bhuvo bhuvimuktibhājaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sadaiva harasīhamahopasargānsvargāpavargamapi saṃpradadāsi tebhyaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O merciful Lord of divine form, those who bow down to you on the earth attain salvation though they may be the doers of all sinful acts. You always remove all their great calamities. You bestow on them heavenly pleasures and salvation too.

## \|\| 2.57.27 \|\|

*ye vighnarāja bhavatā karuṇākaṭākṣaiḥ saṃprekṣitāḥ kṣititale kṣaṇamātramatra \|*  
*teṣāṃ kṣayaṃti sakalānyapikilviṣāṇi lakṣmīḥ kaṭākṣayatitānpuruṣottamānhi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O Vighnarāja, those who are perceived even for a moment on the earth by means of your benign glances have all their sins reduced. They are Puruṣottamas (Viṣṇus, most excellent ones among men) and Lakṣmī looks at them with benign glances.

## \|\| 2.57.28 \|\|

*ye tvāṃ stuvaṃti natavighnavighātadakṣa dākṣāyaṇīhṛdayapaṃkajatigmaraśme \|*  
*śrūyaṃta eva ta iha prathitā na citraṃ citraṃ tadatra gaṇapā yadaho ta eva \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O Lord who are expert in destroying promptly the obstacles of those who bow down, you are like the Sun unto the lotus-like heart of Dākṣāyaṇī. Those who eulogize thee are heard to have become renowned. There is nothing surprising in it. It is surprising that only they are the leaders of Gaṇas.

## \|\| 2.57.29 \|\|

*ye śīlayaṃti satataṃ bhavatoṃghriyugmaṃ te putrapautradhanadhānyasamṛddhibhājaḥ \|*  
*saṃśīlitāṃghrikamalā bahubhṛtyavargairbhūpālabhogyakamalāṃ vimalāṃ labhaṃte \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Those who regularly adore the pair of your feet do flourish with plenty of sons, grandsons, wealth and grain. Their lotus-like feet shall be regularly eulogized by many servants. They will obtain untainted wealth and fortune worthy of being enjoyed by kings.

## \|\| 2.57.30 \|\|

*tvaṃ kāraṇaṃ paramakāraṇakāraṇānāṃ vedyosi vedaviduṣāṃ satataṃ tvamekaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ mārgaṇīyamasi kiṃcana mūlavācāṃ vācāmagocaracarācaradivyamūrte \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O ultimate cause of all causes, you are the cause of all. You alone are worthy of being known by Vedic scholars for ever. O Lord of divine form incapable of being expressed by ordinary words, you are something worthy of being sought after by the original words (of the scriptures).

## \|\| 2.57.31 \|\|

*vedā vidaṃti na yathārthatayā bhavaṃtaṃ brahmādayopi na carācara sūtradhāra \|*  
*tvaṃ haṃsi pāsi vidadhāsi samastamekaḥ kastestutivyatikaro manasāpyagamya \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Vedas do not know you really, O stage-manager of the mobile and the immobile beings. Even Brahmā and others do not know you. You alone annihilate, protect and create everything. O Lord who cannot be comprehended even mentally, how is it possible to eulogize you adequately?

## \|\| 2.57.32 \|\|

*tvadduṣṭadṛṣṭiviśikhairnihatānnihanmi daityānpurāṃdhakajalaṃdharamukhyakāṃśca \|*  
*kasyāsti śaktiriha yastvadṛtepi tucchaṃ vāṃchedvidhātu miha siddhidakāryajātam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I have killed the Daityas, the chief of whom were Tripuras, Andhaka and Jalandhara who had already been destroyed by the arrows of your angry glances. Excepting you who has the power even to wish for the success of the tasks that yield benefits even if they were to be insignificant.

## \|\| 2.57.33 \|\|

*anveṣaṇe ḍhuṃḍhirayaṃ prathitostidhātuḥ sarvārthaḍhuṃḍhitatayā tava ḍhuṃḍhi nāma \|*  
*kāśīpraveśamapi ko labhatetra dehī toṣaṃ vinā tava vināyakaḍhuṃḍhirāja \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The root Ḍhūṇḍh is well-known to mean “to search for”. Your name Ḍhuṇḍhi is due to the fact that you search for everything that your devotees require (and bestow on them). O Ḍhuṇḍhirāja, O Vināyaka, which embodied soul can obtain access to Kāśī too without your pleasure?

## \|\| 2.57.34 \|\|

*ḍhuṃḍhe praṇamyapuratastavapādapadmaṃ yo māṃ namasyati pumāniha kāśivāsī \|*  
*tatkarṇamūlamadhigamya purā diśāmi tatkiṃcidatra na punarbhavatāsti yena \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If a resident of Kāśī bows down to your lotus-like feet first and then bows down to me, I reach up to the root of his ear and impart (the Tāraka Mantra), before the departure of the lifebreath, something whereby he is not reborn in the world.

## \|\| 2.57.35 \|\|

*snātvā naraḥ prathamato maṇikarṇikāyāmuddhūlitāṃghriyugalastu sacailamāśu \|*  
*devarṣimānavapitṝnapi tarpayitvā jñānodatīrthamabhilabhya bhajettatastvām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A devotee takes his holy bath in Maṇikarṇikā along with the cloth worn and walks ahead (not minding) the feet getting soiled. He offers libation to the celestial sages, human beings and the manes. He then comes to Jñānodatīrtha (Jñānavāpī) and worships you.

## \|\| 2.57.36 \|\|

*sāmodamodakabharairvaradhūpadīpairmālyaiḥ sugaṃdhabahulairanulepanaiśca \|*  
*saṃprīṇyakāśinagarīphaladānadakṣaṃ proktvātha māṃ ka iha sidhyati naiva ḍhuṃḍhe \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. First the devotee should propitiate you by means of huge quantities of sweetmeat of great flavour, incense, lights, garlands and sweet-smelling unguents, and then me capable of bestowing the benefit of Kāśī. O Ḍhuṇḍhi, thereby who does not flourish?

## \|\| 2.57.37 \|\|

*tīrthāṃtarāṇi ca tataḥ kramavarjitopi saṃsādhayanniha bhavatkaruṇākaṭākṣaiḥ \|*  
*dūrīkṛtasvahitaghātyupasargavargo ḍhuṃḍhe labhedavikalaṃ phalamatra kāśyām \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A devotee may undertake pilgrimage to Tīrthas and that too without the conventional order. Even then, due to your benign, merciful glances, all the obstacles and calamities antagonistic to his own welfare, shall be removed, O Dhuṇḍhi, and he will obtain the complete benefit here at Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.57.38 \|\|

*yaḥ pratyahaṃ namati ḍhuṃ ḍhivināyakaṃ tvāṃ kāśyāṃ prage pratihatākhilavighnasaṃghaḥ \|*  
*no tasya jātu jagatītalavarti vastu duṣprāpamatra ca paratra ca kiṃcanāpi \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If anyone bows down to you, O Ḍhuṇḍhi Vināyaka, everyday early in the morning at Kāśī, all the obstacles shall be removed and no object on the surface of the earth shall be inaccesible to him here and hereafter.

## \|\| 2.57.39 \|\|

*yo nāma te japati ḍhuṃḍhivināyakasya taṃ vai japaṃtyanudinaṃ hṛdi siddhayoṣṭau \|*  
*bhogānvibhujya vividhānvibudhopabhogyānnirvāṇayā kamalayā vriyate sa cāṃte \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If anyone repeats the name of Ḍhuṇḍhi Vināyaka, all the eight Siddhis will repeat his name in the heart everyday. He will enjoy different kinds of pleasures worthy of being enjoyed by Devas. In the end he will be wooed by Goddess Nirvāṇa Kamalā (Glory of Liberation).

## \|\| 2.57.40 \|\|

*dūre sthitopyaharahastava pādapīṭhaṃ yaḥ saṃsmaretsakalasiddhida ḍhuṃḍhirāja \|*  
*kāśīsthite ravikalaṃ saphalaṃ labheta naivānyathā na vitathā mama vākkadācit \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O Ḍhuṇḍhirāja, O bestower of all Siddhis, even if one staying far off remembers the pedestal of your feet everyday, he will get the entire benefit of staying in Kāśī. My words cannot be contradicted or falsified at any time.

## \|\| 2.57.41 \|\|

*jāne vighnānasaṃkhyātānvinihaṃtumanekadhā \|*  
*kṣetrasyāsya mahābhāga nānārūpairihasthitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O blessed one, I know that it is for the removal of innumerable obstacles that you have assumed different forms and stay here in this holy spot.

## \|\| 2.57.42 \|\|

*yāni yāni ca rūpāṇi yatrayatra ca tenagha \|*  
*tāni tatra pravakṣyāmi śṛṇvaṃtvete divaukasaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Let these heaven-dwellers listen. I shall mention all those forms of yours, O sinless one, assumed in the different areas.

## \|\| 2.57.43 \|\|

*prathamaṃ ḍhuṃḍhirājosi mama dakṣiṇato manāk \|*  
*āḍhuṃḍhya sarvabhaktebhyaḥ sarvārthānsaṃprayacchasi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. First, you are Dhuṇḍhirāja slightly to my right. You seek out and bestow all the desired objects and wealth on the devotees.

## \|\| 2.57.44 \|\|

*aṃgāravāsaravatīmiha yaiścaturthīṃ saṃprāpya modakabharaiḥ parimodavadbhiḥ \|*  
*pūjā vyadhāyi vividhā tava gaṃdhamālyaistānatra putravidadhāmi gaṇāngaṇeśa \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O son, O Gaṇeśa, if diverse kinds of adoration are performed unto you on the Caturthī (fourth day) coinciding with a Tuesday with huge quantities of Modakas (sweetmeats) of fragrant flavour and scented garlands, I make them Gaṇas.

## \|\| 2.57.45 \|\|

*ye tvāmiha prati caturthi samarcayaṃti ḍhuṃḍhe vigāḍhamatayaḥ kṛtinasta eva \|*  
*sarvāpadāṃ śirasi vāmapadaṃ nidhāya samyaggajānana gajānanatāṃ labhaṃte \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Those who worship you on every Caturthī with concentration of mind, O Ḍhuṇḍhi, are really blessed. O elephantfaced one, they will place their left foot on the head of all miseries and mishaps and attain the status of the Elephantfaced One.

## \|\| 2.57.46 \|\|

*māghaśuklacaturthyāṃ tu naktavrataparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*ye tvāṃ ḍhuṃḍhercayiṣyaṃti te'rcyāḥ syurasuradruhām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Ḍhuṇḍhi, the devotees who observe Naktavrata (taking food only at night) and worship you on the fourth day of the bright half of Māgha will be worthy of being worshipped by the enemies of Asuras.

## \|\| 2.57.47 \|\|

*vidhāya vārṣikīṃ yātrāṃ caturthīṃ prāpya tāpasīm \|*  
*śuklāṃ śuklatilairbaddhvā prāśnīyāllaḍḍukānvratī \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The devotee shall cover (make) Laḍḍus with white gingelly seeds and eat them on the bright Caturthī of Māgha after undertaking the annual pilgrimage.

## \|\| 2.57.48 \|\|

*kāryā yātrā prayatnena kṣetrasiddhimabhīpsubhiḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ caturthyāṃ tvatprītyai ḍhuṃḍhe sarvopasargahṛt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On that Caturthī, O Ḍhuṇḍhi, the Yātrā (pilgrimage) should be assiduously performed by those who wish for fulfilment of the worship at the holy spot, for your propitiation. It shall remove all calamities.

## \|\| 2.57.49 \|\|

*tāṃ yātrāṃ nātrayaḥ kuryānnaivedyatilalaḍukaiḥ \|*  
*upasargasahasraistu sa haṃtavyo mamājñayā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He who does not perform that Yātrā nor offers Naivedya with Laḍḍus of gingelly seeds should be at my bidding struck with thousands of obstacles.

## \|\| 2.57.50 \|\|

*homaṃ tilājyadravyeṇa yaḥ kariṣyati bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ caturthyāṃ maṃtrajñastasya maṃtraḥ prasetsyati \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. A devotee conversant with the Mantras shall devoutly perform Homa with gingelly seeds, ghee and other requisites on that Caturthī. His Mantra will become fruitful.

## \|\| 2.57.51 \|\|

*vaidiko'vaidiko vāpi yo maṃtraste gajānana \|*  
*japtastvatsaṃnidhau ḍhuṃḍhe siddhiṃ dāsyati vāṃchitām \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Gajānana, O Ḍhuṇḍhi, the Mantra, be it Vedic or otherwise, should be repeated in your presence. It will then accord the desired Siddhis (fulfilment of desires).

## \|\| 2.57.52 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*imāṃ stutiṃ mamakṛtiṃ yaḥ paṭhiṣyati sanmatiḥ \|*  
*na jātu taṃ tu vighnaughāḥ pīḍayiṣyaṃti niścitam \|\| 52 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

52\. It is certain that a person of excellent mind who reads this eulogy composed by me will never be afflicted by obstacles.

## \|\| 2.57.53 \|\|

*ḍhauṃḍhīṃ stutimimāṃ puṇyāṃ yaḥ paṭheḍḍhuṃḍhi saṃnidhau \|*  
*sānnidhyaṃ tasya satataṃ bhajeyuḥ sarvasiddhayaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. If anyone recites this meritorious eulogy of Ḍhuṇḍhi in the presence of Ḍhuṇḍhi, all the Siddhis will stay near him always.

## \|\| 2.57.54 \|\|

*imāṃ stutiṃ naro japtvā paraṃ niyatamānasaḥ \|*  
*mānasairapi pāpaistairnābhibhūyeta karhicit \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After repeating this eulogy with adequately controlled mind, the devotee shall never be assailed by mental sins at any time.

## \|\| 2.57.55 \|\|

*putrānkalatraṃ kṣetrāṇi varāśvānvaramaṃdiram \|*  
*prāpnuyācca dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ ḍhuṃḍhistotraṃ japannaraḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The man who repeats the prayer unto Ḍhuṇḍhi shall attain wives, sons, land, excellent horses, excellent houses, wealth and foodgrains.

## \|\| 2.57.56 \|\|

*sarvasaṃpatkaraṃ nāma stotrametanmayeritam \|*  
*prajaptavyaṃ prayatnena muktikāmena sarvadā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. This eulogy uttered by me is named Sarvasaṃpatkara (‘Giver of all prosperities’). It should be assiduously repeated always by one who desires salvation.

## \|\| 2.57.57 \|\|

*japtvā stotramidaṃ puṇyaṃ kvāpi kārye gamiṣyataḥ \|*  
*puṃsaḥ puraḥ sameṣyaṃti niyataṃ sarvasiddhayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. If anyone is desirous of going anywhere for a specific purpose, he should go after repeating this meritorious prayer. Invariably all the Siddhis (achievements) shall come face to face to him.

## \|\| 2.57.58 \|\|

*anyacca kathayāmyatra śṛṇvaṃtvete divaukasaḥ \|*  
*ḍhuṃḍhinā kṣetrarakṣārthaṃ yatrayatra sthitiḥ kṛtā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. I shall mention another thing also. Let those heaven-dwellers listen. I shall mention the places where Ḍhuṇḍhi had stayed for the sake of guarding the holy spot.

First Circle of Vināyakas:

## \|\| 2.57.59 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ gaṃgāsi saṃbhede nāmatorkavināyakaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭorkavāsare puṃbhiḥ sarvatāpapraśāṃtaye \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. At the confluence of Gaṅgā and Asi at Kāśī is the Vināyaka named Arkavināyaka. If he is visited on Sundays by people, he will subdue all distresses.

## \|\| 2.57.60 \|\|

*durgo nāma gaṇādhyakṣaḥ sarvadurgatināśanaḥ \|*  
*kṣetrasya dakṣiṇe bhāge pūjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Gaṇādhyakṣa named Durga is the destroyer of all wretchedness. It is in the southern region of the holy spot and should be assiduously worshipped.

## \|\| 2.57.61 \|\|

*bhīmacaṃḍī samīpe tu bhīmacaṃḍavināyakaḥ \|*  
*kṣetranairṛtadeśastho dṛṣṭo haṃti mahābhayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. On the south-west of the holy spot near Bhīmacaṇḍī is Bhīmacaṇḍavināyaka. On being visited he removes great fear.

## \|\| 2.57.62 \|\|

*kṣetrasya paścime bhāge sa dehalivināyakaḥ \|*  
*sarvānnivārayedvighnānbhaktānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On the western side of the holy spot is Dehalivināyaka. There is no doubt about this that he will remove all the obstacles of the devotees.

## \|\| 2.57.63 \|\|

*kṣetravāyavyadigbhāge uddaṃḍākhyo gajānanaḥ \|*  
*uddaṃḍānapi vighnaughānbhaktānāṃ daṃḍayetsadā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. On the north-western side of the holy place is the Gajānana named Uddaṇḍa. He will always strike down massive groups of obstacles.

## \|\| 2.57.64 \|\|

*kāśyāḥ sadottarāśāyāṃ pāśapāṇirvināyakaḥ \|*  
*vināyakānpāśayati bhaktyā kāśīnivāsinām \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On the north of Kāśī, Pāśapāṇi-Vināyaka (Vināyaka with the Pāśa, noose, in his hand) always binds obstacles due to the devotion of the residents of Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.57.65 \|\|

*gaṃgāvaraṇayoḥ saṃge ramyaḥ kharvavināyakaḥ \|*  
*akharvānapi vighnaughānbhaktānāṃ kharvayetsatām \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The beautiful Kharvavināyaka is at the confluence of Gaṅgā and Varaṇā. He will subdue and shorten even huge obstacles of good devotees.

## \|\| 2.57.66 \|\|

*prācyāṃ tu kṣetrarakṣārthaṃ siddhaḥ siddhivināyakaḥ \|*  
*paścime yamatīrthasya sādhakakṣiprasiddhidaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. To the east of the holy spot Siddhivināyaka is always ready to protect the holy spot. It is on the west of Yamatīrtha and is a prompt bestower of powers on a Sādhaka (aspirant).

## \|\| 2.57.67 \|\|

*bāhyāvaraṇagāścaite kāśyāmaṣṭau vināyakāḥ \|*  
*uccāṭayatyabhaktāṃśca bhaktānāṃ sarvasiddhidāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. These eight Vināyakas are on the outer ring of Kāśī. They expel non-devotees and bestow all the Siddhis on the devotees.

Second Circle of Vināyakas:

## \|\| 2.57.68 \|\|

*dvitīyāvaraṇe caiva ye rakṣaṃti vināyakāḥ \|*  
*avimuktamidaṃ kṣetraṃ tānahaṃ kathayāmyataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Henceforth I shall mention those Vināyakas who protect this holy spot Avimukta on the second external ring.

## \|\| 2.57.69 \|\|

*svardhunyāḥ paścime kūle uttarerkavināyakāt \|*  
*laṃbodaro gaṇādhyakṣaḥ kṣālayedvighnakardamam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. On the western bank of the heavenly river, to the north of Arkavināyaka is Laṃbodara Gaṇādhyakṣa (‘Leader of Gaṇas’) who washes off all the mud of obstacles.

## \|\| 2.57.70 \|\|

*tatpaścimekūṭadaṃta udagdurgavināyakāt \|*  
*durgopasargasaṃhartā rakṣetkṣetramidaṃ sadā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. To the west thereof and to the north of Durga-Vināyaka is Kūṭadanta. He is the annihilator of difficulties and calamities. He always protects this holy place.

## \|\| 2.57.71 \|\|

*bhīmacaṃḍa gaṇādhyakṣātkiṃcidīśānadiggataḥ \|*  
*kṣetrarakṣogaṇādhyakṣaḥ pūjyaḥ śālakaṭaṃkaṭaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Slightly to the north-east of Bhīmacaṇḍa Gaṇeśa is Śālakaṭaṃkaṭa, the protector of this holy spot. This Gaṇādhyakṣa is worthy of being adored.

## \|\| 2.57.72 \|\|

*prācyā dehalivighneśātkūśmāṃḍākhyo vināyakaḥ \|*  
*pūjanīyaḥ sadā bhaktermahotpāta praśāṃtaye \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The Vināyaka named Kūṣmāṇḍa is situated on the east of Dehalivighneśa. He is to be worshipped always by the devotees for the suppression of great mishaps and calamities.

## \|\| 2.57.73 \|\|

*uddaṃḍākhyādgaṇapaterāśuśukṣaṇidiksthitaḥ \|*  
*mahāprasiddhaḥ saṃpūjyo bhaktairmuṃḍavināyakaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Muṇḍavināyaka stationed in the south-east direction of the Gaṇapati named Uddaṇḍa is extremely renowned. He is to be adored well by devotees.

## \|\| 2.57.74 \|\|

*pātāle tasya dehosti muṃḍaṃ kāśyāṃ vyavasthitama \|*  
*ataḥ sa gīyate kāśyāṃ devo muṃḍavināyakaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. His body is stationed in Pātāla. The head is situated in Kāśī. Hence the Lord in Kāśī is spoken as Muṇḍavināyaka.

## \|\| 2.57.75 \|\|

*pāśapāṇergaṇeśānāddakṣiṇe vikaṭadvijam \|*  
*pūjayitvā gaṇapatiṃ gāṇapatyapadaṃ labhet \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. One shall attain the position of the lordship of Gaṇas by worshipping the Gaṇapati Vikaṭadvija to the south of the Gaṇeśāna (named) Pāśapāṇi.

## \|\| 2.57.76 \|\|

*kharvākhyānnairṛtebhāge rājaputro vināyakaḥ \|*  
*bhraṣṭarājyaṃ ca rājānaṃ rājānaṃ kurute'rcitaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The Vināyaka named Rājaputra is on the south-west of the Lord named Kharva. On being worshipped, he will reinstate a king who has lost his kingdom.

## \|\| 2.57.77 \|\|

*gaṃgāyāḥ paścime kūle praṇavākhyo gaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*avācyāṃ rājaputrācca praṇataḥ praṇayeddivam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The Gaṇādhipa named Praṇava is on the western bank of Gaṇgā and to the south of Rājaputra. On being bowed down to he will lead (a devotee) to heaven.

## \|\| 2.57.78 \|\|

*dvitīyāvaraṇe kāśyāmaṣṭāvete vināyakāḥ \|*  
*utsādayeyurvighnaughānkāśī sthitinivāsinām \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. These eight Vināyakas are situated in Kāśī in the second external ring. They will dispel all the obstacles of those who permanently stay in Kāśī.

Third Circle of Vināyakas:

## \|\| 2.57.79 \|\|

*kṣetre tṛtīyāvaraṇe kṣetrarakṣākṛtaḥ sadā \|*  
*ye vighnarājāḥ saṃtīha te vaktavyā mayādhunā \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Those Vighnarājas who are stationed in this holy spot on the third external ring, according protection always, should be mentioned by me now.

## \|\| 2.57.80 \|\|

*udagvahāyāḥ svardhunyā ramye rodhasi vighnarāṭ \|*  
*laṃbodarādudīcyāṃ tu vakratuṃḍoghasaṃghahṛt \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Vakratuṇḍa, the remover of mass of sins, is stationed to the north of Laṃbodara who is on the beautiful bank of the heavenly river.

## \|\| 2.57.81 \|\|

*kūṭadaṃtādgaṇapaterudīcyāmekadaṃtakaḥ \|*  
*sadopasargasaṃsargātpāyādānaṃdakānanam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Ekadantaka stationed on the north of the Gaṇapati Kūṭadanta shall always protect Ānandakānana from calamities.

## \|\| 2.57.82 \|\|

*kāśībhayaharo nityamaiśyāṃ śālakaṭaṃkaṭāt \|*  
*trimukho nāma vighneśaḥ kapisiṃhadvipānanaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The monkey-lion-elephant-faced Vighneśa named Trimukha (Three-faced) is situated to the north-east of Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa. He is the remover of the fear of (people of) Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.57.83 \|\|

*kūśmāṃḍātpūrvadigbhāge paṃcāsyo nāma vighnarād \|*  
*paṃcāsyasyaṃdanavaraḥ pāti vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The Vighnarāṭ named Pañcāsya is in the eastern direction of Kūṣmāṇḍa. With an excellent chariot (drawn by) lions, he protects the city of Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.57.84 \|\|

*heraṃbākhyaḥ sadāgneyyāṃ pūjyo muṃḍavināyakāt \|*  
*aṃbāvatpūrayetkāmānsarveṣāṃ kāśivāsinām \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The Lord named Heraṃba stationed in the south-east of Muṇḍavināyaka is worthy of being worshipped always. He will fulfil the desires of all the residents of Kāśī like Aṃbā (Goddess).

## \|\| 2.57.85 \|\|

*avācyāmarcayeddhīmānsiddhyai vikaṭadaṃtataḥ \|*  
*vighnarājaṃ gaṇapatiṃ sarvavighnavināśanam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. For the purpose of Siddhi, a wise devotee should worship the Gaṇapati (named) Vighnarāja who destroys all obstacles. He is stationed to the south of Vikaṭadanta.

## \|\| 2.57.86 \|\|

*vināyakādrājaputrātkiṃcidrakṣodiśisthitaḥ \|*  
*varadākhyo gaṇādhyakṣaḥ pūjyo bhaktavarapradaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The Gaṇādhyakṣa named Varada stationed slightly in the south-west direction from the Vināyaka (named) Rājaputra, should be worshipped. He is the bestower of boons on the devotees.

## \|\| 2.57.87 \|\|

*yāmyāṃ praṇavavighneśādgaṇeśo modakapriyaḥ \|*  
*pūjyaḥ piśaṃgilā tīrthe devanadyāstaṭe śubhe \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The Gaṇeśa (named) Modakapriya is stationed to the south of Praṇavavighneśa on the auspicious bank of the celestial river in the Piśaṅgila Tīrtha. He is worthy of being adored.

Fourth Circle of Vināyakas:

## \|\| 2.57.88 \|\|

*caturthāvaraṇe kāśyāṃ bhaktavighnavināśakāḥ \|*  
*draṣṭavyā hṛṣṭacetobhiḥ spaṣṭamaṣṭau vināyakāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Eight Vināyakas should be clearly visualised by men with delighted minds in Kāśī on the fourth external ring. They are the destroyers of the obstacles of the devotees.

## \|\| 2.57.89 \|\|

*vakratuṃḍādudagdiksthaḥ svaḥsiṃdho rodhasisthitaḥ \|*  
*vināyakostyabhayadaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhayanāśanaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The Vināyaka Abhayada who is the destroyer of the fear of all, is stationed on the bank of the heavenly river in the northern direction from Vakratuṇḍa.

## \|\| 2.57.90 \|\|

*kauberyāmekadaśanātsiṃhatuṃḍo vināyakaḥ \|*  
*upasargagajānhaṃti vārāṇasi nivāsinām \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The Vināyaka (named) Siṃhatuṇḍa is stationed on the north of Ekadaśana (Ekandanta). He destroys the elephants in the form of calamities of the inhabitants of Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.57.91 \|\|

*kūṇitākṣo gaṇādhyakṣastrituṃḍādīśa diksthitaḥ \|*  
*mahāśmaśānaṃ satataṃ pāyādduṣṭakudṛṣṭitaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The Gaṇādhyakṣa (named) Kūṇitākṣa is stationed in the north-eastern direction of Trituṇḍa (Trimukha). He will protect Māhāśmaśāna (i.e. Kāśī) from the evil eye of the wicked.

## \|\| 2.57.92 \|\|

*prācyāṃ paṃcāsyataḥ pāyātpurīṃ kṣipraprasādanaḥ \|*  
*kṣipraprasādanārcātaḥ kṣipraṃ sidhyaṃti siddhayaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Kṣipraprasādana stationed to the east of Pañcāsya shall protect the city. Siddhis are quickly attained by the worship of Kṣipraprasādana.

## \|\| 2.57.93 \|\|

*heraṃbādvahnidigbhāge ciṃtāmaṇi vināyakaḥ \|*  
*bhaktaciṃtāmaṇiḥ sākṣācciṃtitārtha samarpakaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Cintāmaṇi Vināyaka is stationed to the south-east of Heraṃba. He is like Cintāmaṇi (wish-yielding stone) unto the devotees. He will directly present (to the devotees) whatever is thought of by them.

## \|\| 2.57.94 \|\|

*vighnarājādavācyāṃ tu daṃtahasto gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*likhedvighnasahasrāṇi nṛṇāṃ vārāṇasīdruhām \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The Gaṇeśvara (named) Dantahasta is towards the south of Vighnarāja. He will be (commanding) thousands of obstacles to harass men who hate Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.57.95 \|\|

*varadādyātudhānyāṃ ca yātudhānagaṇāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*devaḥ piciṃḍilo nāma purīṃ rakṣedaharniśam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. The Lord named Piciṇḍila is to the south-west of Varada. He is surrounded by Yātudhānas (demons) and protects the city day and night.

## \|\| 2.57.96 \|\|

*dṛṣṭaḥ pilipilātīrthe dakṣiṇe modakapriyāt \|*  
*uddaṃḍa muṃḍo heraṃbo bhaktebhyaḥ kiṃ na yacchati \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. What is it that the Heraṃba named Uddaṇḍamuṇḍa does not bestow on devotees when visited? He is stationed in Pilipilā Tīrtha to the south of Modakapriya (Vināyaka).

Fifth Circle of Vināyakas:

## \|\| 2.57.97 \|\|

*prākāre paṃcame kāśyāṃ dvicatuṣka vināyakāḥ \|*  
*kurvaṃti rakṣāṃ kṣetrasya ye tānatra bravīmyaham \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. I shall now mention the Vināyakas twice-four (= eight) in number, stationed in Kāśī on the fifth external ring and protecting the holy spot.

## \|\| 2.57.98 \|\|

*tīre svargataraṃgiṇyā uttare cābhayapradāt \|*  
*sthūladaṃto gaṇeśānaḥ sthūlāḥ siddhīrdiśetsatām \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The Gaṇeśāna named Sthūladanta is stationed on the bank of the heavenly river to the north of Abhayaprada. To the good, he bestows enormous Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.57.99 \|\|

*siṃhatuḍādudagbhāge kalipriya vināyakaḥ \|*  
*kalahaṃ kārayennityamanyonyaṃ tairthikadruhām \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The Vināyaka (named) Kalipriya is stationed to the north of Siṃhatuṇḍa. Among those who harass the devotees flocking to the Tīrtha, he creates natural quarrel always.

## \|\| 2.57.100 \|\|

*kūṇitākṣāttathaiśānyāṃ caturdaṃto vināyakaḥ \|*  
*tasya darśanamātreṇa vighnasaṃghaḥ kṣayetsvayam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The Vināyaka named Caturdanta is on the north-east of Kūṇitākṣa. Masses of obstacles shall perish merely by visiting this Lord.

## \|\| 2.57.101 \|\|

*kṣipraprasādanādaiṃdryāṃ dvituṃḍo gaṇanāyakaḥ \|*  
*agrataḥ pṛṣṭhataścāpi bibharti sadṛśīṃ śriyam \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The Gaṇanāyaka named Dvituṇḍa is stationed to the east of Kripraprasādana. He looks equally majestic both in front and behind.

## \|\| 2.57.102-103 \|\|

*tasya saṃdarśanātpusāṃ bhavecchrīḥ sarvatomukhī \|*  
*jyeṣṭho nāma gaṇādhyakṣo jyeṣṭho me putrasaṃpadi \|\| 102 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ saṃpūjyo jyeṣṭhatāptaye \|*  
*sthito vahnidiśo bhāge ciṃtāmaṇi vināyakāt \|\| 103 \|\|*

102a. By visiting him, men will attain all-round glory and splendour.

102b-103. The Gaṇādhyakṣa named Jyeṣṭha is the eldest of my numerous sons. He is stationed to the south-east of Cintāmaṇi Vināyaka. For the acquisition of surpassing excellence he should be adored well on the fourteenth day in the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha.

## \|\| 2.57.104 \|\|

*daṃtahastādyamāśāyāṃ pūjyo gajavināyakaḥ \|*  
*tasya saṃpūjanādbhaktyā gajāṃtā śrīravāpyate \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Gaja-Vināyaka is to be adored in the southern direction of Dantahasta. By worshipping him devoutly prosperity with elephants will be attained.

## \|\| 2.57.105 \|\|

*piciṇḍilādgaṇapateryāmyāṃ kālavināyakaḥ \|*  
*bhayaṃ na kālakalitaṃ tasya saṃsevanānnṛṇām \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Kāla-Vināyaka is to the south of the Gaṇapati named Piciṇḍila. By resorting to him, men will not have the fear of the god of Death

## \|\| 2.57.106 \|\|

*uddaṃḍamuṃḍādgaṇapātkī nāśadiśi saṃsthitam \|*  
*nāgeśaṃ gaṇapaṃ dṛṣṭvā nāgaloke mahīyate \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The devotee is honoured in Nāgaloka by visiting the Gaṇapa named Nāgeśa stationed in the southern direction from the Gaṇapa named Uddaṇḍamuṇḍa.

Sixth Circle of Vināyakas:

## \|\| 2.57.107 \|\|

*atha ṣaṣṭhāvaraṇagāḥ procyaṃte vighnanāyakāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ nāmaśravādeva puṃsāṃ siddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Hereafter the Vighnanāyakas stationed on the sixth external ring are being mentioned. Merely by listening to their names men will achieve supernatural power.

## \|\| 2.57.108 \|\|

*maṇikarṇo gaṇapatiḥ prācyāṃ vighnavighātakṛt \|*  
*āśāvināyako vahnyāṃ bhaktāśāṃ pūrayansthitaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The Gaṇapati named Maṇikarṇa is the destroyer of obstacles in the east. Āśā Vināyaka is stationed in the southeast fulfilling the hopes and desires of a devotee.

## \|\| 2.57.109 \|\|

*yāmyāṃsṛṣṭigaṇeśaśca sṛṣṭisaṃhārasūcakaḥ \|*  
*nairṛtyāṃ yakṣavighneśaḥ sarvavighnaharaḥ paraḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Sṛṣṭigaṇeśa in the south is the indicator of creation and annihilation. Yakṣa Vighneśa in the south-west is the destroyer of all obstacles and is the greatest.

## \|\| 2.57.110 \|\|

*pratīcyāṃ gajakarṇaśca sarveṣāṃ kṣemakārakaḥ \|*  
*citraghaṃṭo gaṇapatirvāyavyāṃ pālayetpurīm \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Gajakarṇa in the west is the cause of welfare to all. The Gaṇapati named Citraghaṇṭa protects the city in the north-west.

## \|\| 2.57.111-112 \|\|

*sthūlajaṃghaudīcyāṃ ca śamayecchamināmagham \|*  
*aiśyāmaiśīpurīṃ pāyātsamaṃgalavināyakaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

*yamatīrthādudīcyāṃ ca pūjyo mitravināyakaḥ \|*  
*saptamāvaraṇe ye ca tāṃśca vakṣye vināyakān \|\| 112 \|\|*

111-112. In the north Sthūlajaṅgha subdues the sins of those who control their minds. That auspicious Vināyaka named Mitravināyaka protects the city of Īśa in the north-east. He is to be worshipped in the north of Yama Tīrtha.

Seventh Circle of Vināyakas:

I shall mention the Vināyakas stationed on the seventh external ring.

## \|\| 2.57.113-114 \|\|

*modādyāḥ paṃcavighneśāḥ ṣaṣṭho jñānavināyakaḥ \|*  
*saptamo dvāravighneśo mahādvārapuraścaraḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

*aṣṭamaḥ sarvakaṣṭaughānavimuktavināyakaḥ \|*  
*avimukte mama kṣetre haretpraṇatacetasām \|\| 114 \|\|*

113-114. The five Vighneśas are Moda and others; the sixth one is Jñānavināyaka; the seventh one is Dvāravighneśa present in front of the great door. Avimukta Vināyaka, the eighth one, removes all the distress of those with humble minds in my holy spot Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.57.115 \|\|

*ṣaṭpaṃcāśadgajamukhānetānyaḥ saṃsmariṣyati \|*  
*dūradeśāṃtarasthopi sa mṛto jñānamāpnuyāt \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. He who remembers these fifty-six Gajamukhas even when he is in a far-off country, shall attain knowledge on death.

## \|\| 2.57.116 \|\|

*ḍhuṃḍhistutiṃ mahāpuṇyāṃ ṣaṭpaṃcāśadgajānanām \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhiṣyati puṇyātmā tasya siddhiḥ padepade \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. If a devotee recites this meritorious eulogy of Ḍhuṇḍhi involving fifty-six Gajānanas, he becomes a meritorious-souled one. He gets supernatural powers at every step.

## \|\| 2.57.117 \|\|

*ime gaṇeśvarāḥ sarve smartavyā yatra kutracit \|*  
*mahāvipatsamudrāṃtaḥ pataṃtaṃ pāṃti mānavam \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Wherever one may be, all these Gaṇeśvaras should be remembered. They protect a man falling into the ocean of great calamity.

## \|\| 2.57.118 \|\|

*iti stutiṃ mahāpuṇyāṃ śrutvā caitānvināyakān \|*  
*jātuvighnairnabādhyeta pāpebhyopi prahīyate \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. On hearing this eulogy of great merit and these Vìnāyakas, one is never afflicted by obstacles. One is rid of all sins too.

## \|\| 2.57.119-120 \|\|

*ityuktvā devadevopi mahotsavitamānasaḥ \|*  
*kṛtābhiṣeko brahmādyaistebhyo dattvābhivāṃchitam \|\| 119 \|\|*

*saṃprasādya yathāyogaṃ sarvānucita caṃcuraḥ \|*  
*aviśadrājasadanaṃ viśvakarmavinirmitam \|\| 120 \|\|*

119-120. After saying this, the Lord of the Devas became highly joyous in his mind. He was coronated by Brahmā and others. He granted them whatever they desired. Efficient that he was in doing the proper thing, he entertained all of them duly. He then entered the royal palace built by Viśvakarmaṇ

## \|\| 2.57.121 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ stuto bhagavatā devadevena vighnajit \|*  
*itthaṃ ca bahudhātmānaṃ sa cakāra vināyakaḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

Skanda said:

121\. Thus Vighnajit (‘Subduer of obstacles’ i.e. Gaṇeśa) was eulogized by the Lord of Devas. That Vināyaka created thus many of his own forms.

## \|\| 2.57.122 \|\|

*etāni tasya nāmāni ḍhuṃḍhirājasya kuṃbhaja \|*  
*japitvā yāni manujo lapsyate nijavāṃchitam \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. O Pot-born One, by repeating these names of Ḍhuṇḍhirāja, a man shall get whatever he desires.

## \|\| 2.57.123 \|\|

*anyepi tatra vai bhedāstasya ḍhuṃḍhergaṇeśituḥ \|*  
*bhaktaiḥ samarcitā bhaktyā hyasaṃkhyātāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. There are thousands, nay innumberable, forms of the Gaṇeśa Ḍhuṇḍhi there, devoutly worshipped by many devotees.

## \|\| 2.57.124 \|\|

*bhagīrathagaṇādhyakṣo hariścaṃdravināyakaḥ \|*  
*kapardākhyo gaṇapatistathā biṃduvināyakaḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. They are Bhagīratha, Gaṇādhyakṣa, Hariścandra, Vināyaka, the Gaṇapati named Kaparda and then Binduvināyaka.

## \|\| 2.57.125 \|\|

*ityādyāstatra vighneśāḥ pratibhaktapratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmapyarcanātpuṃsāṃ jāyaṃte sarvasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. These and others are the Vighneśas installed by everyone of the devotees. By worshipping them too men do attain all riches.

## \|\| 2.57.126 \|\|

*śrutvādhyāyamimaṃ puṇyaṃ naraḥ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sarvavighnānsamutsṛjya labhate vāṃchitaṃ padam \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. By listening to this meritorious chapter with faith, a man gets rid of all obstacles and obtains the desired position.

## Chapter 58 - Attainment of Salvation by Divodāsa

## \|\| 2.58.1 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ cakāra haraḥ skaṃda maṃdarādrigatastadā \|*  
*vilaṃbamālaṃbayati tasminnapi gajānane \|\| 1 \|\|*

Agastya said:

1\. O Skanda, what did Hara do while in the Mandara mountain when even Gajānana was causing delay?

## \|\| 2.58.2 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇvagastya kathāṃ puṇyāṃ kathyamānāṃ mayādhunā \|*  
*vārāṇasyekaviṣayāmaśeṣāghaughanāśinīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

2\. O Agastya, listen to the meritorious story being narrated by me now. Its theme is Vārāṇasī alone and it is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 2.58.3 \|\|

*karīṃdravadane tatra kṣetravarye'vimuktake \|*  
*vilaṃbabhājitryakṣeṇa praikṣikṣipramadhokṣajaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When the Elephant-faced One was delaying in Avimuktaka, the excellent one among holy spots, Adhokṣaja (Viṣṇu) was quickly met by the Three-eyed Lord.

## \|\| 2.58.4 \|\|

*proktotha bahuśaśceti bahumānapuraḥsaram \|*  
*tathā tvamapi mākārṣīryathā prākprasthitaiḥ kṛtam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He was addressed thus many times with great respect: “Do not do (it) yourself what was done by others who had gone there before.”

## \|\| 2.58.5 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*udyamaḥ prāṇibhiḥ kāryo yathābuddhi balābalam \|*  
*paraṃ phalaṃti karmāṇi tvadadhīnāni śaṃkara \|\| 5 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

5\. O Śaṅkara, endeavour must be made by all living beings in accordance with their intellect, strength and weakness. But they bear fruits according to your (direction).

## \|\| 2.58.6 \|\|

*acetanāni karmāṇi svataṃtrāḥ prāṇinopi na \|*  
*tvaṃ ca tatkarmaṇāṃ sākṣī tvaṃ ca prāṇipravartakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Actions (Karmas by themselves) are insentient. Even living beings are not free themselves. You are the witness unto their acts and also the prime mover of living beings compelling them to work.

## \|\| 2.58.7 \|\|

*kiṃtu tvatpādabhaktānāṃ tādṛśī jāyate matiḥ \|*  
*yayā tvameva kathayeḥ sādhvanenatvanuṣṭhitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. But in regard to the devotees of your feet, the mental inclination is such that you yourself will say, “Excellent work has been done by him.”

## \|\| 2.58.8 \|\|

*yatkiṃcidiha vai karmastokaṃ vā'stokameva vā \|*  
*tatsiddhyatyeva giriśa tvatpādasmṛtyanuṣṭhitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Whatever work is performed here, whether it be very small or great in size, O Giriśa, that fructifies if it is performed with due recollection of your feet.

## \|\| 2.58.9 \|\|

*susiddhamapi vai kāryaṃ subuddhyāpi svanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*atvatpadasmṛtikṛtaṃ vinaśyatyeva tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If a task is well-prepared (planned), perfectly carried out with keen intellect, it is bound to perish instantaneously, should it be performed without due remembrance of your feet.

## \|\| 2.58.10 \|\|

*śaṃbhunā preṣitenādya sūdyamaḥ kriyate mayā \|*  
*tvadbhaktisaṃpattimatāṃ saṃpannaprāya eva naḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Excellent effort will be made by me today as I have been sent by Śaṃbhu. In regard to us richly endowed with devotion unto you, the task is practically accomplished.

## \|\| 2.58.11 \|\|

*atīva yadasādhyaṃ syātsvabuddhibalapauruṣaiḥ \|*  
*tatkāryaṃ hi susiddhaṃ syāttvadanudhyānataḥ śiva \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A task may be extremely unachievable by solely depending on one’s own intellect, strength and endeavour; O Śiva, the same task can be easily accomplished by meditation on you.

## \|\| 2.58.12 \|\|

*yāṃti pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ye bhavaṃtaṃ bhavaṃ vibho \|*  
*bhavaṃti teṣāṃ kāryāṇi purobhūtāni te bhayāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. All the tasks of those persons, O Lord, who circumambulate you, O Bhava, and then proceed ahead, become already accomplished due to the fear of you.

## \|\| 2.58.13 \|\|

*jātaṃ viddhi mahādeva kāryametatsuniścitam \|*  
*kāśīprāveśikaściṃtya śubhalagnodayaḥ param \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Know, O Mahādeva, that this task has been accomplished certainly. The only thing is that the auspicious hour for the entry into Kāśī should be thought of.

## \|\| 2.58.14 \|\|

*athavā kāśisaṃprāptau na ciṃtyaṃ hi śubhāśubham \|*  
*tadaiva hi śubhaḥ kālo yadaivāpyeta kāśikā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Or, neither the auspicious nor the inauspicious time need be considered in regard to the time for arrival at Kāśī. That alone is the auspicious moment when Kāśī is within reach.

## \|\| 2.58.15 \|\|

*śaṃbhuṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇamya ca punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*pratasthe'tha salakṣmīko maṃdarādgaruḍadhvajaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After circumambulating and bowing down to Śaṃbhu again and again, the Garuḍa-emblemed Lord set off from Mandara along with Lakṣmī.

## \|\| 2.58.16 \|\|

*dṛśoratithitāṃ nītvā viṣṇurvārāṇasīṃ tataḥ \|*  
*puṃḍarīkākṣa ityākhyāṃ saphalīkṛtavānmudā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After making Vārāṇasī the guest (object) of his eyes (vision), he joyously made his name Puṇḍarīkākṣa (Lotus-eyed One) meaningful.

## \|\| 2.58.17 \|\|

*gaṃgāvaraṇayorviṣṇuḥ saṃbhede svacchamānasaḥ \|*  
*prakṣālya pāṇicaraṇaṃ sacailaḥ snātavānatha \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Viṣṇu of pure mind washed his hands and feet in the confluence of Gaṅgā and Varaṇā and took his bath with the clothes on.

## \|\| 2.58.18 \|\|

*tadāprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ pādodakamitīritam \|*  
*pādau yadādau śubhadau kṣālitau pītavāsasā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then onwards, that Tīrtha came to be called Pādodaka because his feet, the bestower of auspiciousness, were washed at the outset by the Yellow-robed Lord.

## \|\| 2.58.19 \|\|

*tatra pādodake tīrthe ye snāsyaṃtīha mānavāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ vinaśyati kṣipraṃ pāpaṃ saptabhavārjitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. If men take their bath in Pādodaka Tīrtha, their sins accumulated in the course of seven births, perish quickly.

## \|\| 2.58.20 \|\|

*tatra śrāddhaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā dattvā caiva tilodakam \|*  
*saptasapta tathā sapta svavaṃśyāṃstārayiṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By offering Śrāddha there and libations with water and gingelly seeds, one will be able to redeem the members of his family three times seven in number.

## \|\| 2.58.21 \|\|

*gayāyāṃ yādṛśī tṛptirlabhyate prapitāmahaiḥ \|*  
*tīrthe pādodake kāśyāṃ tādṛśī labhyate dhruvam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In the Tīrtha (called) Pādodaka at Kāśī the satisfaction obtained by the great-grandfathers is the same as obtained by them at Gayā, indeed.

## \|\| 2.58.22 \|\|

*kṛtapādodaka snānaṃ pītapādodakodakam \|*  
*dattapādodapānīyaṃ naraṃ na nirayaḥ spṛśet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Niraya (Hell) will never touch a man who takes his bath in Pādodaka, drinks the water thereof and offers the same water (as libation).

## \|\| 2.58.23 \|\|

*viṣṇupādodake tīrthe prāśya pādodakaṃ sakṛt \|*  
*jātucijjananīstanyaṃ na pibediti niścitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After drinking Pādodaka once in the Viṣṇu Pādodaka Tīrtha, it is certain that one will never drink the milk of the breasts of a mother (i.e. will get Mokṣa).

## \|\| 2.58.24 \|\|

*sacakra śālagrāmasya śaṃkhena snāpitasya ca \|*  
*adbhiḥ pādodakasyāṃbu pibannamṛtatāṃ vrajet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A devotee who bathes a Śālagrāma having a discus inscribed (i.e. within it) sprinkled with a conch (filled) with waters of Pādodaka and drinks the water thereof will become immortal.

## \|\| 2.58.25 \|\|

*viṣṇupādodake tīrthe viṣṇupādodakaṃ pibet \|*  
*yadi tatsudhayā kiṃ nu bahukālīnayātayā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. If one drinks Viṣṇu Pādodaka in the Viṣṇu Pādodaka Tīrtha, of what avail is heavenly nectar that has been in existence for a long time?

## \|\| 2.58.26 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ pādodake tīrthe yaiḥ kṛtā nodakakriyāḥ \|*  
*janmaiva viphalaṃ teṣāṃ jalabudbuda saśriyām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. If the holy rites with water are not performed at Kāśī with Pādodaka, their very life is futile. They are on a par with a bubble of water in regard to their splendour.

## \|\| 2.58.27-28 \|\|

*kṛtanityakriyo viṣṇuḥ salakṣmīkaḥ sakāśyapiḥ \|*  
*upasaṃhṛtya tāṃ mūrtiṃ trailokyavyāpinīṃ tathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vidhāya dārṣadīṃ mūrtiṃ svahastenādikeśavaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ saṃpūjayāmāsa sarvasiddhisamṛddhidām \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Accompanied by Lakṣmī and Garuḍa, Viṣṇu performed the daily rites. He withdrew his form pervading the three worlds and fashioned a stone image with his own hands. Ādikeśava himself adored that image, the bestower of all prosperities and Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.58.29 \|\|

*ādikeśavanāmnīṃ tāṃ śrīmūrtiṃ pārameśvarīm \|*  
*saṃpūjya martyo vaikuṃṭhaṃ manyate svagṛhāṃgaṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By worshipping that brilliant image of the great Lord, named Ādikeśava, a man considers Vaikuṇṭha the very courtyard of his house.

## \|\| 2.58.30 \|\|

*śvetadvīpa iti khyātaṃ tatsthānaṃ kāśisīmani \|*  
*śvetadvīpe vasaṃtyeva narāstanmūrtisevakāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. That area within the limits of Kāśī is well-known as Śvetadvīpa. Men who serve that image do reside in Śvetadvīpa (Region of Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 2.58.31 \|\|

*kṣīrābdhisaṃjñaṃ tatrānyattīrthaṃ keśavatogrataḥ \|*  
*kṛtodakakriyastatra vasetkṣīrābdhirodhasi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. There is another Tīrtha in front of Keśava named Kṣīrābdhi. One who performs holy rites with water there, will stay on the shores of the Ocean of Milk.

## \|\| 2.58.32 \|\|

*tatra śrāddhaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā gāṃ dattvā ca payasvinīm \|*  
*yathoktasarvābharaṇāṃ kṣīrode vāsayetpitṝn \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If a man performs Śrāddha there and gifts away a milch cow along with all ornaments as laid down, he will be able to make his forefathers stay in the Ocean of Milk.

## \|\| 2.58.33 \|\|

*ekottaraśataṃ vaṃśyānnavetpāyasa kardamam \|*  
*kṣīrodarodhaḥ puṇyātmā bhaktyā tatraikadhenudaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. One who devoutly gifts a single cow there becomes a meritorious-souled one on the shores of the Milk Ocean and can make hundred and one generations of his family move to the Milk Ocean with plenty of ‘mud’ i.e. cream produced by the milk.

## \|\| 2.58.34 \|\|

*bahvīśca naicikīrdattvā śraddhayātra sadakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*śayyottarāṃśca pratyekaṃ pitṝṃstatra suvāsayet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A devotee should offer many excellent cows here with faith along with monetary gifts. He will be able to make everyone of his forefathers live there with comfortable quilts for sound sleep.

## \|\| 2.58.35 \|\|

*kṣīrodāddakṣiṇe tatra śaṃkhatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*tatrāpi saṃtarpyapitṝnviṣṇulokemahīyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. To the south of Kṣīroda is the excellent Śaṅkha Tīrtha. By offering water-libations there unto the Pitṛs, one is honoured in Viṣṇuloka.

## \|\| 2.58.36 \|\|

*tadyāmyāṃ cakratīrthaṃ ca pitṝṇāmapi durlabham \|*  
*tatrāpi vihitaśrāddho mucyate paitṛkādṛṇāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. To the south thereof is the Cakra Tīrtha which is something very inaccessible even to the forefathers. One who performs Śrāddha (there) becomes free from indebtedness to forefathers.

## \|\| 2.58.37 \|\|

*tatsaṃnnidhau gadātīrthaṃ viṣvagādhinibarhaṇam \|*  
*tāraṇaṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ vai kāraṇaṃ cainasāṃ kṣaye \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The Gadā Tīrtha is very near it. It is destructive of all mental anguish; it causes the redemption of the Pitṛs and the destruction of all sins.

S8. Beyond that is the Padma Tīrtha. After taking the holy bath there and offering libations to the Manes duly one is never deficient in fortune and wealth.

## \|\| 2.58.39 \|\|

*tatraiva ca mahālakṣmyāstīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*svayaṃ yatra mahālakṣmīḥ snātā trailokyaharṣadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. There itself is the Tīrtha of Mahālakṣmī renowned in all the three worlds. Mahālakṣmī herself, the delighter of the three worlds, took her holy ablution there.

## \|\| 2.58.40 \|\|

*tatra tīrthe kṛtasnāno dattvā ratnāni kāṃcanam \|*  
*paṭṭāṃbarāṇi viprebhyo na lakṣmyā parihīyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. One who takes his holy bath in that Tīrtha and gifts jewels and gold and silk clothes to Brāhmaṇas never becomes deficient in fortune and prosperity.

## \|\| 2.58.41 \|\|

*yatrayatra hi jāyeta tatratatra samṛddhimān \|*  
*pitaropi hi suśrīkāstasya syustīrthagauravāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Due to the great efficacy of the Tīrtha, wherever he is born he becomes prosperous. His forefathers become brilliant and glorious.

## \|\| 2.58.42 \|\|

*tatrāsti hi mahālakṣmyā mūrtistrailokyavaṃditā \|*  
*tāṃ praṇamya naro bhaktyā na rogī jāyate kvacit \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. An image of Mahālakṣmī is there and it is adored by all the three worlds. By bowing down to her devoutly a man never suffers from sickness anywhere.

## \|\| 2.58.43 \|\|

*nabhasya bahulāṣṭamyāṃ kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ niśi \|*  
*samabhyarcya mahālakṣmīṃ vratī vrataphalaṃ labhet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The devotee should keep awake on the night of the eighth lunar day in the dark half of Bhādrapada and worship Mahālakṣmī. He will obtain the benefit of the holy vow.

## \|\| 2.58.44 \|\|

*tārkṣya tīrthaṃ hi tatrāsti tārkṣyakeśavasannidhau \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro bhaktyā saṃsārāhiṃ na paśyati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. There, in the vicinity of Tārkṣyakeśava, is the Tārkṣya Tīrtha. By taking the holy bath there a man never sees the serpent (in the form) of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.58.45 \|\|

*tadagre nāradaṃ tīrthaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*brahmavidyopadeśaṃ ca prāptavānyatra nāradaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Beyond that is the Nārada Tīrtha that destroys great sins. It is here that Nārada got the instruction in Brahmavidyā.

## \|\| 2.58.46 \|\|

*tatra snāto naraḥ samyagbrahmavidyāmavāpnuyāt \|*  
*keśavāttena tatroktaḥ kāśyāṃ nāradakeśavaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. A man who takes his holy dip there, shall obtain Brahmavidyā perfectly from Keśava. Hence, in Kāśī, he is said to be Nāradakeśava.

## \|\| 2.58.47 \|\|

*arcayitvā naro bhaktyā devaṃ nāradakeśavam \|*  
*jananyā jaṭharaṃ pīṭhamadhyāste na kadācana \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After worshipping devoutly Lord Nāradakeśava the devotee never occupies a place in the womb of any mother.

## \|\| 2.58.48 \|\|

*prahlādatīrthaṃ tasyāgre yatra prahlādakeśavaḥ \|*  
*tatra śrāddhādikaṃ kṛtvā vipṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Prahlāda Tīrtha is beyond it, where the Lord is Prahlādakeśava. By performing Śrāddha etc. there a devotee is honoured in the world of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.58.49 \|\|

*āṃbarīṣamahātīrthamaghaghnaṃ tasya sannidhau \|*  
*tatraudakīṃ kriyāṃ kurvanniṣkāluṣyaṃ labhennaraḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Very near it is the great Aṃbarīṣa Tīrtha that destroys sins. Performing holy rites with water there a man gets liberated from sins.

## \|\| 2.58.50 \|\|

*ādityakeśavaḥ pūjya ādikeśava pūrvataḥ \|*  
*tasya saṃdarśanādeva mucyate coccapātakaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Ādityakeśava to the east of Ādikeśava is worthy of being adored. Merely by visiting it, a devotee is liberated from great sins.

## \|\| 2.58.51 \|\|

*dattātreyeśvaraṃ tīrthaṃ tatraivādigadādharaḥ \|*  
*pitṝnsaṃtarpya tatraiva jñānayogamavāpnuyāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The Tīrtha (named) Dattātreyeśvara is there itself; so also Ādigadādhara. By propitiating the forefathers there itself, a devotee shall acquire Jñānayoga (‘Path of knowledge’).

## \|\| 2.58.52 \|\|

*bhṛgukeśavapūrveṇa tīrthaṃ vai bhārgavaṃ param \|*  
*tatra snāto naraḥ prājño bhavedbhārgavavatsudhīḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The great Bhārgava Tīrtha is towards the east of Bhṛgukeśava. A man who takes his holy bath there shall become a wise man, a man of excellent intellect like Bhārgava.

## \|\| 2.58.53 \|\|

*tatra vāmanatīrthaṃ ca prācyāṃ vāmanakeśavāt \|*  
*pūjayitvā ca taṃ viṣṇuṃ vasedvāmanasannidhau \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. There to the east of Vāmanakeśava is Vāmana Tīrtha. By worshipping that Viṣṇu, a devotee shall stay near Vāmana.

## \|\| 2.58.54 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇaṃ tīrthaṃ naranārāyaṇātpuraḥ \|*  
*tatra tīrthe kṛtasnāno naro nārāyaṇo bhavet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In front of Naranārāyaṇa is the Tīrtha named Naranārāyaṇa. A man who takes his holy bath in the Tīrtha there, shall become Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 2.58.55 \|\|

*yajñavārāha tīrthaṃ ca tadagre pāpanāśanam \|*  
*pratimajjanatastatra rājasūya kratoḥ phalam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Beyond that is Yajñavārāha Tīrtha that destroys sins. By taking baths therein, one gets the merit of a Rājasūya sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.58.56 \|\|

*vidāranārasiṃhākhyaṃ tatra tīrthaṃ sunirmalam \|*  
*snāto vidārayettatra pāpaṃ janmaśatārjitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. There is a Tīrtha entirely free from impurities there, named Vidāraṇa-narasiṃha. One who takes his holy bath there shall tear off the sins acquired in the course of a hundred births.

## \|\| 2.58.57 \|\|

*gopigoviṃda tīrthaṃ ca gopigoviṃdapūrvataḥ \|*  
*snātvā tatra samabhyarcya viṣṇuṃ viṣṇupriyo bhavet \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. To the east of Gopīgovinda is the Tīrtha named Gopīgovinda. After taking the holy bath there and worshipping Viṣṇu, a devotee shall become a favourite of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.58.58 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ lakṣmīnṛsiṃhākhyaṃ gopigoviṃda dakṣiṇe \|*  
*na lakṣmyā tyajyate kvāpi tattīrthaṃ parimajjanāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. To the south of Gopīgovinda is the Tīrtha named Lakṣmīnṭsiṃha. By taking holy dips in the Tīrtha, one is never abandoned by the Goddess of Fortune.

## \|\| 2.58.59 \|\|

*tadagre śeṣatīrthaṃ ca śeṣamādhavasannidhau \|*  
*tarpitānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca yatra tṛptirna śiṣyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Beyond it, near Śeṣamādhava is Śeṣa Tīrtha. The satisfaction of the forefathers to whom libation is offered there, is thorough.

## \|\| 2.58.60 \|\|

*śaṃkhamādhavatīrthaṃ ca tadavācyāṃ sunirmalam \|*  
*kṛtodako narastatra bhavetpāpopi nirmalaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. To the south thereof is Śaṅkha Mādhava Tīrtha entirely free from impurities. A man who performs holy rites with water there, shall become free from impurities though he be a sinner.

## \|\| 2.58.61-62 \|\|

*tadagre ca hayagrīvaṃ tīrthaṃ paramapāvanam \|*  
*tatra snātvā hayagrīvaṃ keśavaṃ paripūjya ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

*piṃḍaṃ ca tatra nirvāpya hayagrīvasya sannidhau \|*  
*hāyagrīvīṃ śriyaṃ prāpya samucyeta sapūrvajaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. Beyond it is the extremely sacred Tīrtha named Hayagrīva. After taking the holy ablution there and worshipping Hayagrīvakeśava, and also offering balls of rice in the presence of Hayagrīva, a devotee shall attain the splendour of Hayagrīva and get liberated along with his forefathers.

## \|\| 2.58.63 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*prasaṃgato mayaitāni tīrthāni kathitāni te \|*  
*bhūmau tilāṃtarāyāṃ yattatra tīrthānyaneśaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

Skanda said:

63\. All these Tīrthas have been enumerated to you incidentally because even on a ground extending as much as a gingelly seed there at Kāśī, there are many Tīrthas.

## \|\| 2.58.64 \|\|

*uddiṣṭānāṃ tu tīrthānāmeteṣāṃ kalaśodbhava \|*  
*nāmamātramapi śrutvā niṣpāpo jāyate naraḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O Pot-born One, even by hearing the names of these Tīrthas specially enumerated by me, a man becomes free of sins.

## \|\| 2.58.65 \|\|

*idānīṃ prastutaṃ vipra śṛṇu vakṣyāmi tegrataḥ \|*  
*vaikuṃṭhanātho yaccakre śaṃkhacakragadādharaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Now, O Brāhmaṇa, I shall mention to you the relevant topic. Listen to what the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, the wielder of conch, discus and club, did.

## \|\| 2.58.66 \|\|

*tasyāṃ mūrtau samāveśya kaiśavyāmatha keśavaḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhoḥ kārye kṛtamanā aṃśāṃśāṃśena nirgataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After entering into the image of Keśava, Lord Keśava came out of it by a bit of a bit of a part because he had decided in his mind to do something pertaining to the task of Śaṃbhu.

## \|\| 2.58.67 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*aṃśāṃśāṃśena niścakre kuto bhoścakrapāṇinā \|*  
*kva nirgataṃ ca hariṇā prāpya kāśīṃ ṣaḍānana \|\| 67 \|\|*

Agastya said:

67\. Oh! Where did the Lord with the discus in his hand go out by a bit of a bit of his part? O Six-faced One, after reaching Kāśī, where did Hari go out?

## \|\| 2.58.68 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*sāmastyena yadarthaṃ na nirgataṃ viṣṇunā mune \|*  
*bruve tatkāraṇamiti kṣaṇamātraṃ niśāmaya \|\| 68 \|\|*

Skanda said:

68\. O sage, why did Viṣṇu not go out completely? I shall mention the reason thereof. Listen to me for a moment.

## \|\| 2.58.69 \|\|

*saṃprāpya puṇyasaṃbhāraiḥ prājño vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*na tyajetsarvabhāvena mahālābhairapīritaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. One attains the city of Vārāṇasī by a great deal of Puṇya. Thereafter, a wise man should not abandon it even if tempted by great benefits.

## \|\| 2.58.70 \|\|

*ataḥ pratikṛtiḥ svīyā tatra kāśyāṃ murāriṇā \|*  
*pratitasthe kalaśajastokāṃśena ca nirgatam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Hence, O Pot-born One, his image was installed by Murāri at Kāśī and he went out partially by a bit.

## \|\| 2.58.71 \|\|

*kiṃcitkāśyā udīcyāṃ ca gatvā devena cakriṇā \|*  
*svasthityai kalpitaṃ sthānaṃ dharmakṣetramitīritam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. After going a little to the north of Kāśī the Discusbearing Lord created an area called Dharmakṣetra for his own stay.

## \|\| 2.58.72 \|\|

*tatastu saugataṃ rūpaṃ śiśrāya śrīpatiḥ svayam \|*  
*atīva suṃdarataraṃ trailokyasyāpimohanam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thereafter the Lord of Lakṣmī himself assumed the form of (a follower of) Buddha, that was very beautiful, fascinating unto the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.58.73 \|\|

*śrīḥ parivrājikā jātā nitarāṃ subhagākṛtiḥ \|*  
*yāmālokya jagatsarvaṃ citranyastamivāsthitam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Śrī (Lakṣmī) became a Parivrājikā (female mendicant) exquisitely beautiful in form. On seeing her, the entire universe remained (motionless) as though painted in a picture.

## \|\| 2.58.74 \|\|

*viśvayoniṃ jagaddhātrīṃ nyastahastāgrapustakām \|*  
*garutmānapi tacchiṣyo jāto lokottarākṛtiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. On seeing the mother of the universes, the source of the universe, with a book placed on the palms of the hand, the entire universe stood motionless. Garuḍa assumed the best of forms and became their disciple.

## \|\| 2.58.75 \|\|

*atyadbhuta mahāprājño niḥspṛhaḥ sarvavastuṣu \|*  
*guruśuśrūṣaṇaparo nyastahastāgrapustakaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. He had a wonderfully brilliant intellect. He was devoid of desire for all the objects. He was engaged in attending to his preceptor. He had a book on the palms of his hands.

## \|\| 2.58.76 \|\|

*apṛcchatparamaṃ dharmaṃ saṃsāravinimocakam \|*  
*ācāryavaryaṃ saumyāsyaṃ prasannātmānamuttamam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. He asked his preceptor about the greatest of virtues that can facilitate release from worldly bondage. The excellent preceptor was gentle-faced and delighted in himself.

## \|\| 2.58.77 \|\|

*dharmārthaśāstrakuśalaṃ jñānavijñānaśālinam \|*  
*susvaraṃ supadavyakti susnigdhamṛdubhāṣiṇam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. He was an adept in the treatises on Dharma and Artha. He was endowed with wisdom and perfect in general and specialized knowledge. He was of sweet, sonorous voice. He spoke softly and lovingly uttering the words distinctly.

## \|\| 2.58.78 \|\|

*staṃbhanoccāṭanākṛṣṭi vaśīkarmādikovidam \|*  
*vyākhyānasamayākṛṣṭa pakṣiromāṃcakāriṇam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. He was proficient in the magical art of stunning, exorcising, attracting persons to him and keeping them under his control. So also in various other activities. At the time of his lecture, even birds were attracted and he could make them experience thrill.

## \|\| 2.58.79 \|\|

*pītatadgītapīyūṣa mṛgapūgairupāsitam \|*  
*mahāmodabharākrāṃta vātacāṃcalyahāriṇam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. He was served by excellent deer which imbibed the nectar-like songs he sang. He checked the swift motion of winds by giving them a great deal of joy.

## \|\| 2.58.80-81 \|\|

*vṛkṣairapi patatpuṣpacchalaiḥkṛtasamarcanam \|*  
*tataḥprovāca puṇyātmā puṇyakīrtiḥ sa saugataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*śiṣyaṃ vinayakīrtiṃ taṃ mahāvinayabhūṣaṇam \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. He was adored even by the trees under the pretext of the falling of flowers. Then that meritorious-souled follower of Buddha (named) Puṇyakīrti said to his disciple Vinayakīrti, endowed with great humility:

## \|\| 2.58.82 \|\|

*puṇyakīrtiruvāca \|*  
*tvayā vinayakīrte yo dharmaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*vakṣyāmyahamaśeṣeṇa śṛṇuṣva tvaṃ mahāmate \|\| 82 \|\|*

Puṇyakīrti said:
