82\. O Vinayakīrti, the eternal virtue has been asked by you. I shall explain it entirely, O highly intelligent one. Listen.

## \|\| 2.58.83 \|\|

*anādisiddhaḥ saṃsāraḥ kartṛkarmavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ prādurbhavedeṣa svayameva vilīyate \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The world has been in existence since beginningless time. It manifests itself (automatically) by itself and it gets dissolved by itself.

## \|\| 2.58.84 \|\|

*brahmādistaṃbaparyaṃtaṃ yāvaddehanibaṃdhanam \|*  
*ātmaivaikeśvarastatra na dvitīyastadīśitā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. In all embodied beings beginning with Brahmā up to a blade of grass, the soul alone is the real master (Īśvara) therein. There is no other (external being like God as) controller thereof.

## \|\| 2.58.85 \|\|

*yadbrahmaviṣṇurudrādyāstathākhyā dehināmimāḥ \|*  
*ākhyā yathāsmadādīnāṃ puṇyakīrtyādirucyate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The names Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra etc. are mere names of the embodied ones, like out own names Puṇyakīrti etc.

## \|\| 2.58.86 \|\|

*deho yathā smadādīnāṃ svakālena vilīyate \|*  
*brahmādi maśakāṃtānāṃ svakālāllīyate tathā \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Just as our body perishes in due course, so also the bodies of everything from Brahmā to a mosquito perish when their (respective) time arrives.

## \|\| 2.58.87 \|\|

*vicāryamāṇe dehesminnakiṃcidadhikaṃ kvacit \|*  
*āhāro maithunaṃ nidrā bhayaṃ sarvatra yatsamam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. If it is pondered over (it is evident) that there is nothing special about the body (of anyone). Intake of food, sexual intercourse, sleep and fear are common to all.

## \|\| 2.58.88 \|\|

*nijāhāraparīmāṇaṃ prāpya sarvopi dehabhṛt \|*  
*sadṛśīmeva saṃtṛptiṃ prāpnuyānnādhiketarām \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Every embodied one attains the same (degree of) satisfaction after getting its own usual quantity of food; no more (degree of satisfaction) in any case.

## \|\| 2.58.89 \|\|

*yathā vitṛṣitāḥ syāma pītvā peyaṃ mudā vayam \|*  
*tṛṣitāstu tathānyepi na viśeṣolpakodhikaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Just as we become free from thirst after joyously drinking some beverage, so also others who are thirsty; there is no difference great or small (in the satisfaction derived after drinking).

## \|\| 2.58.90 \|\|

*saṃtu nāryaḥ sahasrāṇi rūpalāvaṇyabhūmayaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ nidhuvane kāle hyekaivehopayujyate \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Let there be thousands of women with exquisite beauty and seductive charms; but at the time of intercourse only one can be enjoyed.

## \|\| 2.58.91 \|\|

*aśvāḥ paraḥ śatāḥ saṃtu saṃtvanekepyanekaṣāḥ \|*  
*adhirohe tathāpyeko na dvitīyastathātmanaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Let there be hundreds of horses and let there be many elephants, but at the time of riding, only one is enough; no second (is required).

## \|\| 2.58.92 \|\|

*paryaṃkaśāyināṃ svāpe sukhaṃ yadupapadyate \|*  
*tadeva saukhyaṃ nidrāyāmiha bhūśāyināmapi \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. At the time of sleeping the same pleasure is experienced irrespective of sleeping on a couch or on bare ground.

## \|\| 2.58.93 \|\|

*yathaiva maraṇādbhītirasmadādi vapuṣmatām \|*  
*brahmādikīṭakāṃtānāṃ tathā maraṇato bhayam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Just as we embodied ones are afraid of death, so also all those beginning with Brahmā and ending with insects, are afraid of death.

## \|\| 2.58.94 \|\|

*sarvetanubhṛtastulyā yadi buddhyā vicāryate \|*  
*idaṃ niścitya kenāpi no hiṃsyaḥ kopi kutracit \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. If we intelligently ponder (it is evident that) all embodied beings are equal. After decisively thinking thus, no one should be violently injured by anyone, anywhere at any time.

## \|\| 2.58.95 \|\|

*dharmo jīvadayā tulyo na kvāpi jagatītale \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kāryā jīvadayā nṛbhiḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. There is no other virtue on a par with compassion for living beings anywhere on the surface of the earth. Hence mercy should be assiduously practised by men.

## \|\| 2.58.96 \|\|

*ekasminrakṣite jīve trailokyaṃ rakṣitaṃ bhavet \|*  
*ghātite ghātitaṃ tadvattasmādrakṣenna ghātayet \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. If one living being is protected, all the three worlds would get protected; if one is killed, all are killed. Hence one should protect (and) not kill (others).

## \|\| 2.58.97 \|\|

*ahiṃsā paramo dharma ihoktaḥ pūrvasūribhiḥ \|*  
*tasmānna hiṃsā kartavyā narairnarakabhīrubhiḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Non-violence has been stated as the greatest virtue by the ancient wise men (or teachers). Hence violence should not be practised by men who are afraid of hell.

## \|\| 2.58.98 \|\|

*na hiṃsā sadṛśaṃ pāpaṃ trailokye sacarācare \|*  
*hiṃsako narakaṃ gacchetsvargaṃ gacchedahiṃsakaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. In all the three worlds consisting of mobile and immobile beings, there is no sin like violence or injury. One indulging in violence goes to hell and one who abstains from it goes to heaven.

## \|\| 2.58.99 \|\|

*saṃti dānānyanekāni kiṃ taistuccha phalapradaiḥ \|*  
*abhīti dānasadṛśaṃ paramekamapīha na \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. There are many kinds of gifts. Of what avail are they, yielding but insignificant fruit? There is nothing like the gift of freedom from fear.

## \|\| 2.58.100 \|\|

*iha catvāri dānāni proktāni paramarṣibhiḥ \|*  
*vicārya nānāśāstrāṇi śarmaṇetra paratra ca \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. After poring over and reflecting upon different kinds of scriptural texts here, four types of gifts have been mentioned by the great sages for the sake of welfare here and hereafter.

## \|\| 2.58.101 \|\|

*bhītebhyaścābhayaṃ deyaṃ vyādhitebhyastathauṣadham \|*  
*deyā vidyārthināṃ vidyā deyamannaṃ kṣudhāture \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Freedom from fear should be offered to those who are afraid; medicine should be given to those who are afflicted with ailments; learning should be imparted to those who seek lores; and cooked food should be given to one (who is) distressed with hunger.

## \|\| 2.58.102 \|\|

*aviciṃtya prabhāvaṃ hi maṇimaṃtrauṣadhībalam \|*  
*tadabhyasyaṃ prayatnena nānārthopārjanāya vai \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The power of Maṇi (miraculous gems), Mantra (spell) and Auṣadha (medicine) is indeed incomprehensible. That should be assiduously practised for the purpose of earning different kinds of riches.

## \|\| 2.58.103 \|\|

*arthānupārjya bahuśo dvādaśāyatanāni vai \|*  
*paritaḥ paripūjyāni kimanyairiha pūjitaiḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. After acquiring wealth in various ways, the twelve Āyatanas around should be worshipped well. Of what avail is the worship of other things (deities)?

## \|\| 2.58.104 \|\|

*paṃcakarmeṃdriyāṇyeva paṃcabuddhīṃdriyāṇi ca \|*  
*manobuddhiriha proktaṃ dvādaśāyatanaṃ śubham \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The auspicious twelve Āyatanas include the five organs of action, the five sense-organs, the mind and the intellect.

## \|\| 2.58.105 \|\|

*ihaiva svarganarakau prāṇināṃ nānyataḥ kvacit \|*  
*sukhaṃ svargaḥ samākhyāto duḥkhaṃ naraka eva hi \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Heaven and hell exist here itself (in this world), nowhere else. Happiness is what is termed as heaven and misery what is called hell.

## \|\| 2.58.106 \|\|

*sukheṣu bhujyamāneṣu yatsyāddeha visajarnam \|*  
*ayameva paro mokṣo na mokṣo'nyaḥ kvacitpunaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. If the body is cast off when happiness is being enjoyed, it is the ultimate salvation; there is no other salvation.

## \|\| 2.58.107 \|\|

*vāsanāsahitakleśa samucchede sati dhruvam \|*  
*vijñāno paramo mokṣo vijñeyastattvaciṃtakaiḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. When Kleśa (distress) is destroyed along with the Vāsanā (Avidyā, nescience) there is Vijñānoparama (cessation of Vijñāna). This would be known as Mokṣa (salvation) by persons who ponder over reality.

## \|\| 2.58.108 \|\|

*prāmāṇikī śrutiriyaṃ procyate vedavādibhiḥ \|*  
*na hiṃsyātsarvabhūtāni nānyā hiṃsāpravartikā \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. This authoritative statement is quoted by the followers of the Vedas: “One should not injure or kill any living being.” There is no other Vedic statement directing one to kill or injure.

## \|\| 2.58.109 \|\|

*agnīṣomīyamiti yā bhrāmikā sā'satāmiha \|*  
*na sā pramāṇaṃ jñātṝṇāṃ paśvālaṃbhanakārikā \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. The Śruti exhorting one to perform Agniṣomīya (Agniṣṭoma) etc. is something that misleads others and is quoted by evil men. That Śruti which prescribed killing of sacrificial animals is not authoritative in the view of those who know.

## \|\| 2.58.110 \|\|

*vṛkṣāṃśchittvā paśūnhatvā kṛtvā rudhirakardamama \|*  
*dagdhvā vahnau tilājyādi citraṃ svargo'bhilapyate \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. It is surprising that heaven is sought after cutting trees, killing animals, making slush of blood and by burning gingelly seeds, ghee etc.

## \|\| 2.58.111 \|\|

*ityevaṃ dharmajijñāsāṃ puṇyakīrtau prakurvati \|*  
*pāraṃparyeṇa tacchrutvā paurā yātrāṃ pracakrire \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. While Puṇyakīrti was expatiating on Dharma in this manner, the citizens heard about this from others successively and proceeded (towards him).

## \|\| 2.58.112 \|\|

*parivrājika yāpyevaṃ samākṛṣṭāḥ purāṃganāḥ \|*  
*tayā vijānakaumudyā sarvavidyāvidagdhayā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The women of the city were attracted by that Parivrājikā named Vijñānakaumudī who was very proficient in all lores.

## \|\| 2.58.113 \|\|

*tatastāsāṃ purastātsā bauddhadharmānavīvadat \|*  
*dṛṣṭārthapratyayakarāndehasaukhyaikasādhanāna \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Before them she elaborated on the tenets of Buddha, exhorting them to believe only those things that are directly seen and adopting only the means of acquiring happiness of the body.

## \|\| 2.58.114 \|\|

*vijñānakaumudyuvāca \|*  
*ānaṃdaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ śrutyaivaṃ yannigadyate \|*  
*tattathaiveha maṃtavyaṃ mithyā nānātvakalpanā \|\| 114 \|\|*

Vijñānakaumudī said:

114\. This is mentioned by Śruti that Ānanda (bliss) is the form of Brahman. That should be accepted as it is. The view of its diversity is baseless.

## \|\| 2.58.115 \|\|

*yāvatsvasthamidaṃ varṣma yāvanneṃdriyaviklavaḥ \|*  
*yāvajjarā ca dūresti tāvatsaukhyaṃ prasādhayet \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. One should achieve happiness as long as this body is strong and healthy and the sense-organs are not feeble, even as old age is far off.

## \|\| 2.58.116 \|\|

*asvāsthyeṃdriyavaikalye vārdhake tu kutaḥ sukham \|*  
*śarīramapi dātavyamarthibhyotaḥ sukhepsubhiḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Where can there be happiness when there is deficiency in the sense-organs and health is not normal? Hence even the body should be given over to suppliants (before old age) by those who wish for happiness.

## \|\| 2.58.117 \|\|

*yācamānamanovṛtti prīṇaneyasya no janiḥ \|*  
*tena bhūrbhāravatyeṣā samudrāgadrumairnahi \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. The earth is (really) burdened by those people who are not ready to satisfy the desire of those who beg, and not on account of oceans, mountains and trees.

## \|\| 2.58.118 \|\|

*satvaro gatvaro dehaḥ saṃcayāḥ saparikṣayāḥ \|*  
*iti vijñāya vijñātā dehe saukhyaṃ prasādhayet \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. The body is bound to pass off quickly and everything hoarded is attended with the certainty of loss. After realizing this a sensible man should endeavour for the happiness of the body.

## \|\| 2.58.119 \|\|

*śva vāyasa kṛmīṇāṃ ca pratibhojyamidaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*bhasmāṃtaṃ taccharīraṃ ca vede satyaṃ prapadyate \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Ultimately the body is bound to be a prey to dogs, crows and worms. The truth that the body is reduced to ashes in the end, has been accepted in the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.58.120 \|\|

*mudhā jātivikalpoyaṃ lokeṣu parikalpyate \|*  
*mānuṣye sati sāmānye kodhamaḥ kotha cottamaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. The classification (of people) into various castes is futile in this world. When the state of being human is common (to all), who is high and who is low?

## \|\| 2.58.121 \|\|

*brahmādi sṛṣṭireṣeti procyate vṛddhapūruṣaiḥ \|*  
*tasya sraṣṭuḥ sutau dakṣa marīcī ceti viśrutau \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. It is said by elderly persons that this entire creation is that of Brahmā and others. Dakṣa and Marīci are reputed to be the sons of that creator.

## \|\| 2.58.122 \|\|

*mārīcinā kaśyapena dakṣakanyāḥ sulocanāḥ \|*  
*dharmyeṇa kila mārgeṇa pariṇītāstrayodaśa \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. (It is said that) thirteen charming-eyed daughters of Dakṣa were married in a way approved by scriptures to Kaśyapa, the son of Marīci.

## \|\| 2.58.123 \|\|

*apīdānīṃtanairmartyairalpabuddhiparākramaiḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ gamyastvagamyoyaṃ vicāraḥ kriyate mudhā \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. “This man is worthy of (carnal) approach. This man is not (so).” Futile is such consideration by people of this age who are deficient in intellect and valour.

## \|\| 2.58.124 \|\|

*mukhabāhūrupajjātaṃ cāturvarṇyamihoditam \|*  
*kalpaneyaṃ kṛtā pūrvairna ghaṭeta vicārataḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. The four castes are said to have originated from the mouth, arms, thighs and feet (of the Cosmic Being). This belief evolved by the forefathers does not stand to reason.

## \|\| 2.58.125 \|\|

*ekasyāṃ ca tanau jātā ekasmādyadi vā kvacit \|*  
*catvārastanayāstatkiṃ bhinnavarṇatvamāpnuyuḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. If four sons are born to one (woman) from one (man), will they be different in castes?

## \|\| 2.58.126 \|\|

*varṇāvarṇavivekoyaṃ tasmānna pratibhāsate \|*  
*ato bhedo na maṃtavyo mānuṣye kenacitkvacit \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. This discrimination between caste and caste does not appear (to be correct) to the mind. Hence nobody should entertain discrimination between man and man at any time and at any place.

## \|\| 2.58.127 \|\|

*vijñānakaumudīvāṇīmityākarṇya purāṃganāḥ \|*  
*bharttṛśuśrūṣaṇavatīṃ vijahurmatimuttamām \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. On hearing this speech of Vijñānakaumudī the women of the city gave up their excellent mind to serve their husbands.

## \|\| 2.58.128 \|\|

*abhyasyākarṣaṇīṃ vidyāṃ vaśīkṛtimatīmapi \|*  
*puruṣāḥ saphalīcakruḥ paradāreṣu mohitāḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. By practising the black magic of attracting and winning over (others) men who were fascinated by the wives of others succeeded in their objective.

## \|\| 2.58.129 \|\|

*aṃtaḥpuracarā nāryastathā rājakumārakāḥ \|*  
*paurāḥ purāṃganāścāpi sarve tābhyāṃ vimohitāḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Royal ladies living in inner apartments, princes, citizens and city women were deluded by both of them.

## \|\| 2.58.130-131 \|\|

*vaṃdhyānāṃ cāpi vaṃdhyātvaṃ sā parivrājikāharat \|*  
*taistaiśca kārmaṇopāyairasau bhāgyavatīḥ striyaḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

*saubhāgyabhāgyasaṃpannā vyadhādvijñānakaumudī \|*  
*kasyaicidaṃjanaṃ dattaṃ kasyaicittilakauṣadham \|\| 131 \|\|*

130-131. That lady-mendicant removed the barrenness of barren women with various special devices. Vijñānakaumudī made women with husbands alive, blessed with conjugal bliss. To some she gave (medicated) collyrium, to some others medicine called Tilaka (Comm.).

## \|\| 2.58.132 \|\|

*vaśīkaraṇamaṃtraiśca tathā bahvyopi dīkṣitāḥ \|*  
*maṃtrāñjapeyuḥ kāścicca yaṃtrāṇyanyā likhaṃti ca \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Many (women) were initiated (into Buddhism) with Mantras effective in bringing (others) under control. Some were muttering Mantras while others were drawing Maṇḍalas (magical designs).

## \|\| 2.58.133 \|\|

*kāścijjuhvati kuṃḍāgnau nānādravyāṇi niścalāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sarveṣu paureṣu nijadharmeṣu sarvathā \|*  
*parāṅmukheṣu jāteṣu prollalāsa vṛṣetaraḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Some women sitting steady in front of fire-pit began to offer various material as oblations into the sacrificial fire.

## \|\| 2.58.134 \|\|

*siddhayokṛṣṭapacyādyā naṣṭā enaḥ praveśanāt \|*  
*āsītkuṃṭhitasāmarthyo nṛpopi sa manāṅmanāk \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Best results such as the growth of vegetation without cultivation (and others like provision of honey in cups of leaves from trees) became defunct because of the rise of sins. Slowly the power of the king also got blunted.

## \|\| 2.58.135 \|\|

*dūrasthitopi vighneśo nṛpaṃ nirviṇṇamānasam \|*  
*cakāra rājyakaraṇe ḍhuṃḍhirājo ripuṃjayam \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Though he was stationed far away, Vighneśa (named) Ḍhuṇḍhirāja made King Ripuñjaya (‘conqueror of enemies’) dejected in his mind and disinclined to administer the kingdom.

## \|\| 2.58.136 \|\|

*ajīgaṇaddivodāsopyaṣṭādaśa dināvadhim \|*  
*kadā gaṃtā sa vai vipro yo māṃ samupadekṣyati \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Divodāsa kept count of the eighteen-day period: “When will that Brāhmaṇa who will be instructing me, arrive?”

## \|\| 2.58.137 \|\|

*itthamaṣṭādaśe prāpte divase divaseśvare \|*  
*prāpte madhyaṃ nabhobhāgaṃ dvāraṃ prāpto dvijottamaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. When the eighteenth day arrived and the sun reached the zenith of the sky, that excellent Brāhmaṇa came to the gate.

## \|\| 2.58.158 \|\|

*avaṃtopi prajāḥ svīyā nijadharmamanuvratāḥ \|*  
*purā te tripurāḥ śūrāḥ śivabhaktiparā api \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. It was Adhokṣaja (Viṣṇu) himself under the name of Puṇyakīrti from Dharmakṣetra who came to the king in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.58.139 \|\|

*dvitraiḥ pavitrairbahudhā jayajīveti vādibhiḥ \|*  
*sametaḥ sa ito vipro mūrtimāniva pāvakaḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. The Brāhmaṇa who came was as though fire itself having assumed a physical form. He was accompanied by two or three other holy persons repeating blessings: “Jaya (Be victorious); Jiva (Be alive).”

## \|\| 2.58.140 \|\|

*vilokya taṃ samāyātaṃ dūrādutkaṃṭhito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*mene bhavedgururayaṃ yukto madupadeśane \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. On seeing him coming from a distance, the anxious king considered him a preceptor capable of imparting to him instructions.

## \|\| 2.58.141 \|\|

*abhigamya ca taṃ rājā praṇamya ca punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*gṛhīta svastivacano nināyāṃtaḥpuraṃ dvijam \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. The king approached him and bowed down to him frequently. Having received him with welcoming words, he took the Brāhmaṇa into the inner apartment.

## \|\| 2.58.142-143 \|\|

*madhuparkeṇa vidhinā taṃ saṃpūjya janādhipaḥ \|*  
*vyapetādhvaśramaṃ svasthaṃ prollasanmukhapaṃkajam \|\| 142 \|\|*

*nivedya khādyavastūni kṛtakṛtya kriyāvidhim \|*  
*paritṛptaṃ sukhāsīnaṃ papraccha brāhmaṇaṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

142-143. The king offered Madhuparka (mixture of honey, curds etc.) and adored him duly. When he dispelled the fatigue due to the journey and attained normal state, with his lotuslike face beaming with pleasure, he offered him foodstuffs to eat and did everything needed. The king then asked the Brāhmaṇa who was contented and comfortably sitting:

## \|\| 2.58.144 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*khinnosmi vipravaryāhaṃ rājyabhāraṃ samudvahan \|*  
*khedo nāstyeva hi paraṃ vairāgyamiva jāyate \|\| 144 \|\|*

The king said:

144\. Bearing the burden of the administration of the kingdom, I am afflicted, O excellent Brāhmaṇa. Actually, I have no distress but a slight loss of interest has appeared.

## \|\| 2.58.145 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ me nirvṛtirbhavet \|*  
*pakṣadvayyeva yāteti mama ciṃtayato dvija \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. What shall I do? Where shall I go? How can I be happy? O Brāhmaṇa, two fortnights have elapsed since I am worried thus.

## \|\| 2.58.146 \|\|

*asīmaṃ sukhasaṃtānaṃ bhuktaṃ rājyaṃ mayā dvija \|*  
*parikṣīṇavipakṣaṃ ca tryakṣaiśvaryamiva sphuṭam \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. With all my enemies having been destroyed completely unlimited series of pleasures has been enjoyed by me like the Three-eyed Lord (Śiva) in a manifest form.

## \|\| 2.58.147 \|\|

*svasāmarthyādahaṃ jātaḥ parjanyāgnyanilātmakaḥ \|*  
*prajāśca pālitāḥ samyakputrā iva nijaurasāḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. By my own ability, I became identical with Parjanya, Agni and Anila. The subjects have been protected well like my own bosom-born children.

## \|\| 2.58.148 \|\|

*tarpitāścāpi bhūdevā vasubhiśca dinedine \|*  
*ekamevāparāddhaṃ ca mayā rājyaṃ praśāsatā \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. Brāhmaṇas have been propitiated everyday with money. While ruling the kingdom I have committed only one offence.

## \|\| 2.58.149 \|\|

*devāstṛṇīkṛtāḥ sarve svatapobaladarpataḥ \|*  
*tacca prajopakārārthaṃ na svārthaṃ bhavatā śape \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. All the Devas have been slighted by me due to the arrogance born of the power of my penance. But I swear by you that, that too I did only to render help to my subjects and not for my own sake.

## \|\| 2.58.150 \|\|

*adhunā gururedhitvaṃ mama bhāgyodayāgataḥ \|*  
*rājyaṃ tu prakaromyevaṃ nyakkṛtāṃtakasādhvasam \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. Now do become my spiritual preceptor. It is due to the rise of my good luck that you have come here. I shall continue to rule the kingdom thus without caring for and fearing the god of Death.

## \|\| 2.58.151 \|\|

*akālakālakalanaṃ mama rājye na kutracit \|*  
*jarāvyādhidaridrebhyo mamarājyepi no bhayam \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. Nowhere in my kingdom is the likelihood of an untimely attack by the god of Death nor is there the fear of old age, sickness and poverty.

## \|\| 2.58.152 \|\|

*kopi dharmetarāṃ vṛttiṃ na śrayenmayi śāsati \|*  
*dharmodayājanāḥ sarve sarve saṃti sukhodayāḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. While I rule no one shall resort to an unrighteous activity. All the people grow richer in piety. All of them have a rise in prosperity and happiness.

## \|\| 2.58.153-154 \|\|

*sadvidyāvyasanāḥ sarve sarvesanmārga caṃcurāḥ \|*  
*athavā yadi kalpāṃtaṃ tiṣṭhedāyustatopi kim \|\| 153 \|\|*

*sarve bhogyāstathā bhāṃti yathā carvita carvaṇam \|*  
*kiṃ piṣṭapeṣaṇenātra rājyena dvijapuṃgava \|\| 154 \|\|*

153-154. All the people engage themselves passionately in the pursuit of excellent learning; all are experts in traversing the path of good people. Or, what do we get even if the longevity extends up to the end of a Kalpa? All the objects of pleasure appear like chewing what is already chewed. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, of what avail is the kingdom which is like pressing of what is already pressed?

## \|\| 2.58.155 \|\|

*kimapyupadiśa prājña garbhavāsopaśāṃtaye \|*  
*athavā tvāṃ prapannasya mama kiṃ ciṃtanairimaḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. O wise one, advise something for the prevention of further stay in the womb. Or, of what avail are the thoughts like these for me who have sought refuge in you?

## \|\| 2.58.156-157 \|\|

*yadeva kathayasyadya tatkariṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|*  
*tvadvilokanamātreṇa sarva eva manorathāḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

*anyeṣāmapi jāyaṃte jātaprāyā mamaiva tu \|*  
*jāne devavirodhena ke ke na pralayaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

156-157. Undoubtedly I shall do whatever you say today. By your mere sight all the desires of others too become fulfilled. They have almost become so in my case. I know this. Who have not (i.e. all have) become doomed due to the animosity of Devas?

## \|\| 2.58.158-164 \|\|

*avaṃtopi prajāḥ svīyā nijadharmamanuvratāḥ \|*  
*purā te tripurāḥ śūrāḥ śivabhaktiparā api \|\| 158 \|\|*

*dharāmayaṃ rathaṃ kṛtvā dhanuḥ kṛtvā himācalam \|*  
*vedāṃśca vājinaḥ kṛtvā guṇaṃ kṛtvā ca vāsukim \|\| 159 \|\|*

*viriṃciṃ sārathiṃ kṛtvā kṛtvā viṣṇuṃ ca pattriṇam \|*  
*rathacakre puṣpavaṃtau pratodaṃ praṇavātmakam \|\| 160 \|\|*

*tārāgrahamayānkīlānvarūthaṃ gaganātmakam \|*  
*dhvajadaṃḍasumeruṃ ca prāṃśukalpataruṃ dhvajam \|\| 161 \|\|*

*yoktrāṇi cakṣuḥśravasaśchaṃdāsyaṃgāni rakṣakān \|*  
*bhallaṃ kālāgnirudrākhyaṃ puṃkhīkṛtya prabhaṃjanam \|\| 162 \|\|*

*hareṇaikeṣupātena līlayā bhasmasātkṛtāḥ \|*  
*baliryajñakṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kṛtvā kapaṭakharvatām \|\| 163 \|\|*

*pātālaṃ gamitaḥ pūrvaṃ hariṇā vikramaistribhiḥ \|*  
*vṛttavānapi vai vṛtraḥ sutrāmṇā vinisūditaḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

158-164. The Tripuras were heroic and much devoted to Siva. They were the followers of their own duty. They used to protect their own subjects. Still they were reduced to ashes playfully by letting fall a single arrow, by Hara who constructed his chariot out of the earth, made Himalaya the bow, who made Vedas the horses, Vāsuki the bow string, Viriñci, god Brahmā, the charioteer, Viṣṇu the arrow, the sun and the moon as the wheels of the chariot, Praṇava as the whip, the stars and the planets becoming the pegs, the sky as the wooden fender for protection in the chariot, Sumeru as the flagstaff, the lofty Kalpa tree as the banner, serpents as the ropes for binding the Vedas (horses) and the Aṅgas as the bodyguard, Kālāgnirudra being made the arrowhead and the wind the feathered part.

Bali who was the most excellent one among those who performed Yajñas was formerly driven to the nether regions by Harī who fraudulently disguised himself as a dwarf and took three steps.

Vṛtra who was of good behaviour was killed by Sutrāman (Indra).

## \|\| 2.58.165 \|\|

*dadhīcirapi vipreṃdro devairasthikṛte hataḥ \|*  
*pūrvavairamanusmṛtya jayārthaṃ yudhyato hareḥ \|*  
*kuśāstrairvijitasyājau tenaiva ca dadhīcinā \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. Bearing in mind the previous enmity of Hari who was defeated by Dadhīci by means of Kuśa grass, although he fought for victory, that leading Brāhmaṇa Dadhīci was killed by the Devas for the sake of his bones.

## \|\| 2.58.166 \|\|

*śivabhaktasya bāṇasya doḥsahasraṃ purā hariḥ \|*  
*ciccheda saṃkhye kiṃ tenāparāddhaṃ sādhuvartinā \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. The thousand arms of Bāṇa, a devotee of Śiva, were cut off by Hari formerly during a battle. What offence did that excellent one of good conduct commit?

## \|\| 2.58.167 \|\|

*tasmādvirodho bhadrāya na bhaveddevataiḥ saha \|*  
*devebhyo madbhayaṃ nāsti satpathīnasya vai manāk \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. Hence antagonizing the Devas cannot be conducive to welfare. But since I tread the path of the good, I do not have the slightest fear from the Devas.

## \|\| 2.58.168 \|\|

*yajñairdevatvamāpannā gīrvāṇā vāsavādayaḥ \|*  
*yajñairdānaistapobhiśca tebhyopyādhikyamasti me \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. Vāsava and other Devas have attained Devahood through Yajñas. But I have superiority over them due to Yajñas, Dānas and Tapas.

## \|\| 2.58.169 \|\|

*astu nyūnatvamādhikyaṃ kimanenādhunā mama \|*  
*iṃdriyoparamaḥ prāptaḥ sukhadastavadarśanāt \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. Let there be superiority or inferiority. Of what importance is this to me now? This meeting with you, has provided a pleasant pause in the activities of the sense-organs.

## \|\| 2.58.170 \|\|

*idānīṃ diśa me tāta karmanirmūlanakṣamam \|*  
*upāyaṃ tvamupāyajña yena nirvṛtimāpnuyām \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. Now, O great one, who are conversant with the requisite means that is capable of uprooting Karmas, grant that unto me, whereby I shall get beatitude.

## \|\| 2.58.171 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*gaṇeśāveśavaśato rājñeti yadudīritam \|*  
*tadākarṇya hṛṣīkeśaḥ prāha brāhmaṇaveṣabhṛt \|\| 171 \|\|*

Skanda said:

171\. On hearing the words uttered by the king thus due to the entry of Gaṇeśa, Hṛṣikeśa who was in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa said:

## \|\| 2.58.172 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*sādhusādhu mahāprājña nṛpacūḍāmaṇe'nagha \|*  
*mayā yadupadeṣṭavyaṃ tattvayaiva nirūpitam \|\| 172 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

172\. O highly intelligent one, O sinless one, O crest jewel among kings, well-said, (very) well-said! What should have been given as advice by me has been well-indicated by you.

## \|\| 2.58.173 \|\|

*tvamādāveva nirvṛttaḥ paraṃ me mānado hyasi \|*  
*kṣāliteṃdriyapaṃkaśca sutapaḥ svacchavāribhiḥ \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. At the very outset you have already washed off all the impurities of the sense-organs through the pure waters of excellent penance and hence have become the best bestower of honour on me.

## \|\| 2.58.174 \|\|

*yaduktaṃ bhavatā bhūpa tatsarvaṃ tathyameva hi \|*  
*tava śaktiṃ ca jānāmi viraktiṃ ca mahāmate \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. What has been said by you, O king, is entirely true, O highly intelligent one. I know your power as well as disinterestedness (in worldly affairs).

## \|\| 2.58.175 \|\|

*na bhavatsadṛśo rājā bhuvi bhūto bhaviṣyati \|*  
*rājyaṃ bhoktuṃ tvayājñāyi yuktaṃ yattu mumukṣasi \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. A king like you has never been before nor will there ever be. You knew well how to enjoy the kingdom. It is but proper that you wish to abandon it now.

## \|\| 2.58.176 \|\|

*virodhepi hi devānāṃ tvayā nāpakṛtaṃ kvacit \|*  
*dharmetarapraveśaśca tava rāṣṭrepi nobhavat \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. In spite of the opposition from the Devas no offence has been committed by you. Nor has occurrence of non-righteousness taken place in your kingdom.

## \|\| 2.58.177 \|\|

*pravartitābhirbhavatā prajābhiryadanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*dharme dharmaṃ svadharmajña tena tṛptā divaukasaḥ \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. What piety has been observed by your subjects under your guidance and persuasion has made the heaven-dwellers satisfied.

## \|\| 2.58.178 \|\|

*eka eva hi te doṣo hṛdi me pratibhāsate \|*  
*kāśyā viśveśvaro dūraṃ yatkṛto bhavatā kila \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. Only one defect in you occurs in my mind, and it is the fact that Viśveśvara has been made to stay far away from Kāśī by you.

## \|\| 2.58.179 \|\|

*mahāṃtamaparādhaṃ te jāne bhūjāni sattama \|*  
*imaṃ tatpāpaśāṃtyai ca vacmyupāyaṃ mahattaram \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. This I know is the greatest offence on your part, O most excellent one among the rulers of the earth. I shall now tell you the best means of quelling that sin.

## \|\| 2.58.180 \|\|

*saṃkhyāsti yāvatī dehe dehino romasaṃbhavā \|*  
*tāvatopyaparādhā vai yāṃti liṃga pratiṣṭhayā \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. Even granting that one has committed as many sins as there are hairs on the body, all those sins vanish if one installs a Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.58.181 \|\|

*ekaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ yena liṃgamatreśabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tenātmanā samaṃ viśvaṃ jagadetatpratiṣṭhitam \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. If a single Liṅga is installed here with due devotion to Īśa, it is as though the entire universe has been established by him.

## \|\| 2.58.182 \|\|

*ratnākare ratnasaṃkhyā saṃkhyāvidbhirapīṣyate \|*  
*liṃgapratiṣṭhā puṇyasya na tu saṃkhyeti likhyate \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. The counting of the number of jewels in the ocean is possible by those who are experts in calculation. But the extent of the merit of the installation of Liṅgas cannot be written down.

## \|\| 2.58.183 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kuru liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*tayā liṃga pratiṣṭhityā kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. Hence with all endeavour make a Liṅga installed. By that installation of the Liṅga, you will become blessed and contented.

## \|\| 2.58.184 \|\|

*ityuktvā brāhmaṇo dadhyau kṣaṇaṃ niścalamānasaḥ \|*  
*uvāca ca prahṛṣṭāsyo rājānaṃ pāṇinā spṛśan \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. After saying this, the Brāhmaṇa meditated for a short while with unwavering mind. Thereafter he touched the king with his hand with his countenance beaming with delight and said thus:

## \|\| 2.58.185 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*anyacca kiṃcitpaśyāmi bhūpāla jñānacakṣuṣā \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā tadapi prājñasattama \|\| 185 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

185\. O king, I see another thing also through my vision of knowledge. O most excellent one among wise men, listen to that too with adequate attention.

## \|\| 2.58.186 \|\|

*dhanyosi kṛtakṛtyosi mānyosi mahatāmapi \|*  
*japyaṃ ca tava nāmeha prātaḥ śubhaphalepsunā \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. You are blessed. You have fulfilled your task. You are worthy of being honoured even by great men. Your very name should be uttered in morning by one who wishes to attain auspicious benefit.

## \|\| 2.58.187 \|\|

*divodāsa tvadabhyāśādapi dhanyatarā vayam \|*  
*tepi dhanyatarā martye ye tvadākhyāṃ pracakṣate \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. O Divodāsa, thanks to your presence and proximity. We are highly blessed. Among mortal beings those who utter your name are also blessed.

## \|\| 2.58.188 \|\|

*smāyaṃ smāyaṃ jagau vipro maulimāṃdolayanmuhuḥ \|*  
*hṛdyeva bahuśo hṛṣṭaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. The Brāhmaṇa continued to say smilingly, shaking his head repeatedly, highly delighted in his heart with joyous horripilation.

## \|\| 2.58.189 \|\|

*aho bhāgyodayaścāsya aho nairmalyamasya vai \|*  
*yadenamaniśaṃ dhyāyeddhyeyo viśveśvaro'khilaiḥ \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. “Oh! The purity of this one (is excellent)! Oh! The rise of the fortune of this one (is praiseworthy) since one should meditate on him always! Viśveśvara should be meditated upon by all.

## \|\| 2.58.190 \|\|

*aho udarka etasya na kaiścitpratipadyate \|*  
*asmākamapi yaddūramadavīyastadasya yat \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. Oh! The resulting fate of this (king) cannot be obtained by anyone (else)! What is far away from even us is not far away from him.”

## \|\| 2.58.191 \|\|

*hṛdyālocyeti viprotha varṇayitvā kṣitīśvaram \|*  
*āviścakāra tatsarvaṃ yatsamādhāvalokayat \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. After considering thus within his heart, the Brāhmaṇa extolled the king and disclosed everything that he saw during his meditation.

## \|\| 2.58.192 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*rājaṃstavādya phalito manoratha mahādrumaḥ \|*  
*anenaiva śarīreṇa tvaṃ gatāsi paraṃ padam \|\| 192 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

192\. O king, the tree of your cherished desire has borne fruit today. You will be attaining the greatest position with this very body.

## \|\| 2.58.193 \|\|

*yathā viśveśvaro nityaṃ tvāmeva hṛdi śīlayet \|*  
*tathāsmadādīnapi na dvijāṃstatpādalocanān \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. Viśveśvara does not have any consideration in his heart for people like us nor for a Brāhmaṇa whose eyes are directed towards his feet in the same manner as he has for you in his heart.

## \|\| 2.58.194 \|\|

*kṛtaliṃgapratiṣṭhaṃ tvāṃ saptame hyadya vāsarāt \|*  
*divyavimānamāgatya netumeṣyati śāṃbhavam \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. Since you have installed a Liṅga, a divine aerial chariot of Śaṃbhu will be coming on the seventh day from today to take you away.

## \|\| 2.58.195 \|\|

*rājaṃstvaṃ vetsi kasyāyaṃ vipākaḥ sukṛtasya te \|*  
*vārāṇasyāḥ puraḥ samyaksevanādityavaimyaham \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. O king, you know what that merit is, whereof this is the result. I too know that it is due to your service to the city of Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.58.196 \|\|

*ekamapyatra yaḥ pāyādvārāṇasyāṃ sthitaṃ janam \|*  
*tasyāpyevaṃ vipākosti dehāṃte rājasattama \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. O excellent one among kings, even if one takes care of a single resident of Vārāṇasī, one will have this same benefit at the time of the death of his body.

## \|\| 2.58.197 \|\|

*iti śrutvā sa rājarṣirdivodāsaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*brāhmaṇāya saśiṣyāya prādātprītobhivāṃchitam \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. On hearing this, the valorous, saintly king Divodāsa who was delighted, granted to the Brāhmaṇa and his disciples what they desired.

## \|\| 2.58.198 \|\|

*atha saṃprīṇitaṃ vipraṃ praṇamya ca muharmuhuḥ \|*  
*provāca rājā saṃhṛṣṭastāritosmi bhavārṇavāt \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. After repeatedly bowing down to the propitiated Brāhmaṇa, the joyous king said, “I have been redeemed from the ocean of worldly existence.”

## \|\| 2.58.199 \|\|

*brāhmaṇopi prahṛṣṭātmā paripūrṇamanorathaḥ \|*  
*samāpṛcchya mahīnāthaṃ sveṣṭaṃ deśaṃ jagāma ha \|\| 199 \|\|*

199\. The Brāhmaṇa too was delighted in his heart with his desires fulfilled. He took leave of the king and went to the place of his choice.

## \|\| 2.58.200-202 \|\|

*vilokya kāśīṃ parito māyādvijavapurhariḥ \|*  
*bhūyobhūyo vicāryāpi kimatrātīva pāvanam \|\| 200 \|\|*

*sthānaṃ yaccāhamadhyāsya nijabhaktānaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*neṣyāmi paramaṃ dhāma viśveśānugrahātparāt \|\| 201 \|\|*

*saṃpradhāryeti bhagavāndṛṣṭvā pāṃcanadaṃ hradam \|*  
*tatra kṛtvā vidhisnānaṃ tatastatraiva saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 202 \|\|*

200-202. Hari who was in the guise of a sham Brāhmaṇa pondered over this frequently. ‘What is that spot highly sacred, which I can occupy and take all my devotees to the highest abode with the great blessings of Viśveśa?’ After seeing the Hrada (whirlpool) Pañcanada he decided thus, took his holy dip there duly, and stationed himself there.

## \|\| 2.58.203 \|\|

*pratīkṣamāṇo lakṣmīśo maṃkṣutryakṣasamāgamam \|*  
*tārkṣyaṃ prasthāpayāṃcakre rājavṛttāṃtavedinam \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. Expecting an early personal contact with the Threeeyed Lord, the Lord of Lakṣmī sent Tārkṣya to convey the news about the king.

## \|\| 2.58.204-208 \|\|

*divodāsopi rājeṃdro vipreṃdraṃ parivarṇayan \|*  
*āhūya prakṛtīḥ sarvāḥ sāmātyānmaṃḍaleśvarān \|\| 204 \|\|*

*adhyakṣānapi sarvāṃśca kośāśvebhādideśitān \|*  
*putrānpaṃcaśataṃ prāgryaṃ sutaṃ ca samaraṃjayam \|\| 205 \|\|*

*purohitaṃ pratīhāramṛtvijogaṇakāndvijān \|*  
*sāmaṃtānrājaputrāṃśca sūpakārāṃścikitsakān \|\| 206 \|\|*

*vaideśikānapi bahūnnānākāryasamāgatān \|\| sāṃtapurāṃ ca mahiṣīṃ vṛddhagopālabālakān \|\| 207 \|\|*

*sarvānprovāca hṛṣṭātmā prabaddhakarasaṃpuṭaḥ \|*  
*yathā sa brāhmaṇaḥ prāha dinasaptāvadhi sthitim \|\| 208 \|\|*

204-208. The eminent king Divodāsa extolled the leader of Brāhmaṇas and summoned all the subjects, the vassal kings along with their ministers, the keeper of the treasury, cavalry, elephant army etc., the eldest son Samarañjaya and five hundred other sons, the priest, the Ṛtviks, the Brāhmaṇas, the watchmen, the princes of vassal kingdoms, the cooks, the physicians, many foreigners who had arrived on various missions, the crowned queen along with the other members of the Inner Apartment, the elders, the cowherds, and the children, with great delight. He joined his arms in deference and said to them what the Brāhmaṇa had told regarding the seven-day limit.

## \|\| 2.58.209-210 \|\|

*āścaryaṃ teṣu śṛṇvatsu viṣaṇṇavadaneṣu ca \|*  
*svayaṃ rājagṛhaṃ nītvā kumāraṃ samaraṃjayam \|\| 209 \|\|*

*abhiṣicya mahābuddhiḥ paurāñjānapadānapi \|*  
*prasādīkṛtya puṇyātmā punaḥ kāśīmagānnṛpaḥ \|\| 210 \|\|*

209-210. Even as they were listening to the miracle with sad faces, the king himself took Prince Smarañjaya to the royal palace (outside Kāśī). The king of keen intellect and meritorious soul crowned his son and granted favours to the citizens and dwellers of the surrounding districts. He then went back to Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.58.211 \|\|

*āgatya kāśīṃ medhāvī sa bhūpālo ripuṃjayaḥ \|*  
*prāsādaṃ kārayāmāsa svardhunyāḥ paścime taṭe \|\| 211 \|\|*

211\. After returning to Kāśī that highly intelligent king who had conquered his enemies got a palace built on the western bank of the celestial river.

## \|\| 2.58.212 \|\|

*ripūnpramathya samare yāvatī śrīrupārjitā \|*  
*tāvatyā sa hi bhūpālaḥ śivālayamacīklṛpat \|\| 212 \|\|*

212\. That king built a shrine of Siva spending the whole of the amount he had won by defeating the enemies in battle.

## \|\| 2.58.213 \|\|

*bhūpālalakṣmīrakhilā yattatra viniyojitā \|*  
*bhūpālaśrīriti khyātā tataḥ sābhūrabhūcchubhā \|\| 213 \|\|*

213\. Since the wealth and fortune of the kings had been entirely utilized there, that auspicious part of the land became well-known as Bhūpālaśrī.

## \|\| 2.58.214 \|\|

*divodāseśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya ripuṃjayaḥ \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyamivātmānamamanyata nareśvaraḥ \|\| 214 \|\|*

214\. The king, the conqueror of enemies, installed the Liṅga Divodāseśvara and considered himself blessed for having fulfilled his tasks.

## \|\| 2.58.215-218 \|\|

*athaikasmindine rājā talliṃgaṃ vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*samabhyarcya namaskṛtya yāvattuṣṭāva tuṣṭidam \|\| 215 \|\|*

*tāvannabhoṃgaṇādāśu divyaṃ yānamavātarat \|*  
*pārṣadaiḥ paritaḥ kīrṇaṃ śūlakhaṭvāṃgapāṇibhiḥ \|\| 216 \|\|*

*atyādityāgnitejobhirbhālanetraiḥ kapardibhiḥ \|*  
*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśairaṃgairdīptanabhoṃgaṇaiḥ \|\| 217 \|\|*

*vibhūṣāhi phaṇāratna jyotiḥ pūjita vigrahaiḥ \|*  
*nityaprakāśasaṃtrasta tamaḥśrita śirodharaiḥ \|\| 218 \|\|*

215-218. On a certain day the king worshipped that Liṅga duly, bowed down to it and eulogized the Liṅga that accorded him satisfaction. By that time a divine aerial chariot came down quickly from the sky with the attendants sprawled about in it all-round. They had tridents and Khaṭvāṅgas (skull-topped clubs) in their hands. Their splendour surpassed the dazzling radiance of the Sun and fire. They had eyes in their foreheads and had matted hairs. Their limbs shining like pure crystals illuminated the sky. Their physical forms had venerable appearance due to the jewels on the hoods of the serpents which constituted their ornaments. Their necks appeared to be resorted to (i.e. had blue tinge) by the darkness terrified by the perpetual brilliance.

## \|\| 2.58.219-222 \|\|

*cāmaravyagrahastāgra rudrakanyāśatāvṛtam \|*  
*atha pāriṣadai rājā divyasraganulepanaiḥ \|\| 219 \|\|*

*divyairdukūlanepathyairalaṃcakre mudānvitaiḥ \|*  
*trinetrīkṛtasadbhāla śyāmīkṛtaśirodharam \|\| 220 \|\|*

*sugaurīkṛtasarvāṃgaṃ kapardīkṛta maulijam \|*  
*caturbhujīkṛtatanuṃ bhūṣaṇīkṛtapannagam \|\| 221 \|\|*

*caṃdrārdhīkṛtamūrdhānaṃ ninyustaṃ pārṣadā divam \|\| 222 \|\|*

219-222. The aerial chariot was surrounded by hundreds of Rudrakanyās with the fingers of their hands busily engaged in moving chowries.

Thereafter the king was embellished by the attendants in a joyous mood, with divine garlands, unguents and silk robes. His excellent forehead became three-eyed. His throat became blue. All his limbs were rendered white. His hairs became matted. His body had four arms and was adorned with serpents. A crescent-shaped moon adorned his head. The attendants then took the king to heaven.

## \|\| 2.58.223-224 \|\|

*tadā prabhṛti tattīrthaṃ bhūpālaśrīriti śrutam \|*  
*tatra śrāddhādikaṃ kṛtvā dānaṃ dattvā svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 223 \|\|*

*divodāseśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā samabhyarcya ca bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*rājñaścākhyāyikāṃ śrutvā na naro garbhamāviśet \|\| 224 \|\|*

223-224. Ever since then, that holy Tīrtha became renowned as Bhūpālaśrī. The devotees should perform Śrāddha etc. there. They shall make monetary gifts in accordance with their capacity. They should visit Divodāseśvara and worship him devoutly. They shall then listen to the narrative about the king. No such devotee shall ever be reborn in a womb.

## \|\| 2.58.225 \|\|

*ākhyānametannṛpaterdivodāsasya pāvanam \|*  
*paṭhitvā pāṭhayitvāpi naraḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 225 \|\|*

225\. A man who reads and teaches or causes to read this sacred narrative of King Divodāsa becomes liberated from sins.

## \|\| 2.58.226 \|\|

*divodāsaśubhākhyānaṃ śrutvā yaḥ samaraṃ viśet \|*  
*na jātu jāyate tasya bhayaṃ vairikṛtaṃ kvacit \|\| 226 \|\|*

226\. If anyone enters a battlefield after listening to the auspicious account of Divodāsa, he need not have any fear from the enemies.

## \|\| 2.58.227 \|\|

*divodāsa kathā puṇyā mahotpāta nikṛṃtanī \|*  
*paṭhanīyā prayatnena sarvavighnopaśāṃtaye \|\| 227 \|\|*

227\. The meritorious story of Divodāsa destroys great calamities. It should be read assiduously for the suppression of all obstacles.

## \|\| 2.58.228 \|\|

*nāvṛṣṭirjāyate tatra nākālamaraṇādbhayam \|*  
*daivodāsī kathā yatra sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 228 \|\|*

228\. Where the story of Divodāsa that destroys all sins is read, there is neither drought nor fear from premature death.

## \|\| 2.58.229 \|\|

*asyākhyānasya paṭhanādviṣṇoriva manorathāḥ \|*  
*saṃpūrṇatāṃ gamiṣyaṃti śaṃbhościṃtitakāriṇaḥ \|\| 229 \|\|*

229\. By reading this narrative, all desires will become fulfilled like those of Viṣṇu who carried out what Śaṃbhu had thought of.

## Chapter 59 - Pañcanada Comes into Being

## \|\| 2.59.1-3 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*sarvajña hṛdayānaṃda gaurīcuṃbitamūrdhaja \|*  
*tārakāṃtaka ṣaḍvaktra tāriṇe bhadrakāriṇe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvajñānanidhe tubhyaṃ namaḥ sarvajñasūnave \|*  
*sarvathā jitamārāya kumārāya mahātmane \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kāmārimardhanārīśaṃ vīkṣya kāmakṛtaṃ kila \|*  
*yo jigāya kumāropi māraṃ tasmai namostu te \|\| 3 \|\|*

\[Note: Pañcanada is Pañcagaṅgā, one of the five sacred-most Tīrthas on Gaṅgā. Before Gaṅgā was brought there by Bhagīratha there were two streams (rivulets)—Dhūtapāpā and Kiraṇā, joining the pool called Dharmanada. At Prayāga Gaṅgā was joined by Yamunā and Sarasvatī. These three rivers coming from Prayāga, assimilated the local two rivulets Dhūtapāpā and Kiraṇā. The confluence of the five rivers at this place became known as Pañcagaṅgā Tīrtha and the fine Ghāṭa here is known Pañcagaṅgā Ghāṭa. (BCL, p. 237)

Today, to the north of the bathing Ghāṭ is a trickle of water called Dhūtapāpā. To the south (of what is called Lakṣmaṇa Bal Ghāṭ), there is a rectangular Kuṇḍa opening towards Gaṅgā and it is called the “river” Kiraṇā. In fact these Purāṇic ‘rivers’ are symbolically represented today.

The present chapter describes how this spot became “Pañcanada” (Pañcagaṅgā).\]

Agastya said:

1-3. O Six-faced Lord, O delighter of the heart of Sarvajña (Omniscient Śiva), whose hairs have been kissed by Gaurī, O slayer of Tāraka, O storehouse of all knowledge, obeisance to you, the son of Sarvajña, the cause of welfare and the redeemer. Obeisance to the noble-souled Kumāra who conquered Māra completely in every respect. I offer obeisance to you who, after perceiving Kāmāri (enemy of Kama, Śiva), Ardhanārīśa (the Lord half of whom is female) as brought about by Kāma (Love) conquered Māra though yet a Kumāra (a person of tender age)

## \|\| 2.59.4 \|\|

*yaduktaṃ bhavatā skaṃda māyādvijavapurhariḥ \|*  
*kāśyāṃ paṃcanadaṃ tīrthamadhyāsātīva pāvanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Lord Skanda, it has been mentioned by you that Hari with a sham physical form of a Brāhmaṇa, occupied the extremely holy Tīrthas (called) Pañcanada at Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.59.5 \|\|

*bhūrbhuvaḥsvaḥ pradeśeṣu kāśīparamapāvanam \|*  
*tatrāpi hariṇājñāyi tīrthaṃ paṃcanadaṃ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Kāśī is the most sacred Tīrtha among all the regions of Bhū, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ (the three worlds). Even therein the extremely sacred Tīrtha called Pañcanada came to be known by Hari.

## \|\| 2.59.6 \|\|

*kutaḥ paṃcanadaṃ nāma tasya tīrthasya ṣaṇmukha \|*  
*kutaśca sarvatīrthebhyastadāsītpāvanaṃ param \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Whence, O Six-faced One, is the name Pañcanada (was given) unto that Tīrtha? How did it become the holiest of all Tīrthas?

## \|\| 2.59.7-8 \|\|

*kathaṃ ca bhagavānviṣṇuraṃtarātmā jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ jagatāṃ pātā kartā hartā ca līlayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*arūpo rūpamāpanno hyavyakto vyaktatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*nirākāropi sākāro niṣprapaṃcaḥ prapaṃcabhāk \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Lord Viṣṇu is the immanent soul, the Lord of the universe, the protector, the creator and the playful destroyer of all the worlds. How did he happen to have a form though he is formless? How did he, the unmanifest one, become manifest? How did he, one without shape, happen to be one with shape? How did he who is transcendent, happen to be immanent in the world?

## \|\| 2.59.9-11 \|\|

*ajanmānekajanmā ca tvanāmāsphuṭanāmabhṛt \|*  
*nirālaṃbo'khilālaṃbo nirguṇopi guṇāspadam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ahṛṣīkohṛṣīkeśo pyanaṃghrirapisarvagaḥ \|*  
*upasaṃhṛtya rūpaṃ svaṃ sarvavyāpī janārdanaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sthitaḥ sarvātmabhāvena tīrthe paṃcanade pare \|*  
*etadākhyāhi ṣaḍvaktra paṃcavaktrādyathā śrutam \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. He who has no birth, took many births; he who is nameless, took many distinct names; he who has no support, is the supporter of everything; he who is devoid of attributes, became the basis of attributes; he who has no sense-organs, became the Lord of sense-organs; he who has no legs, has become the traverser of all places. How did the omnipresent Janārdana withdraw his form and station himself at Pañcanada, the most excellent Tīrtha, in the form of being the soul of all?

O Six-faced Lord, narrate this as it has been heard by you from the Five-faced Lord.

## \|\| 2.59.12 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*kathayāmi kathāmetāṃ namaskṛtya maheśvaram \|*  
*sarvāghaugha praśamanīṃ sarvaśreyovidhāyinīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

Skanda said:

12\. After bowing down to Maheśvara, I shall tell this story that subdues all sins and brings about all welfare.

## \|\| 2.59.13 \|\|

*yathā paṃcanadaṃ tīrthaṃ kāśyāṃ prathitimāgatam \|*  
*yannāmagrahaṇādeva pāpaṃ yāti sahasradhā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I shall tell how the Tīrtha called Pañcanada at Kāśī became well-known. Merely by repeating its name, sin gets shredded into a thousand bits.

## \|\| 2.59.14 \|\|

*prayāgopi ca tīrtheśo yatra sākṣātsvayaṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*pāpināṃ pāpasaṃghātaṃ prasahya nijatejasā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Prayāga is the Lord of all Tīrthas. It forcibly draws out the sins of sinners through its own power.

## \|\| 2.59.15-17 \|\|

*haraṃti sarvatīrthāni prayāgasya balena hi \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi tīrthāni māghe makarage ravau \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pratyabdaṃ nirmalāni syustīrtharāja samāgamāt \|*  
*prayāgaścāpi tīrtheṃdraḥ sarvatīrthārpitaṃ malam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mahāghināṃ mahāghaṃ ca haretpāṃcanadādbalāt \|*  
*yaṃ saṃcayati pāpaughamāvarṣaṃ tīrthanāyakaḥ \|*  
*tamekamajjanādūrje tyajetpaṃcanade dhruvam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. It is by the power of Prayāga that all the Tīrthas remove the sins of sinners. In the month of Māgha when the Sun is in the Zodiac of Capricorn they come into contact with the king of Tīrthas (i.e. Prayāga) every year and get rid of their impurities. Prayāga, the Lord of all Tīrthas, gets rid of all the impurities dumped into it by all the other Tīrthas and also the great sins of great sinners, thanks to the power of Pañcanada. Throughout the year the Tīrtha Nāyaka (‘Lord of the Tīrthas’ i.e. Prayāga) gathers together masses of sins. In the month of Kārttika, by a single dip into Pañcanada, all those sins are dispelled.

## \|\| 2.59.18 \|\|

*yathā paṃcanadotpattistathā ca kathayāmyaham \|*  
*niśāmaya mahābhāga mitrāvaruṇanaṃdana \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. I shall mention how Pañcanada originated. O blessed son of Mitra and Varuṇa, listen.

## \|\| 2.59.19 \|\|

*purā vedaśirā nāma munirāsīnmahātapāḥ \|*  
*bhṛguvaṃśa samutpanno mūrto veda ivāparaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Formerly there was a sage of great penance named Vedaśiras, born in the family of Bhṛgu. It was as though he was another embodied form of the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.59.20 \|\|

*tapasyatastasya muneḥ purodṛggocaraṃ gatā \|*  
*śucirapsarasāṃ śreṣṭhā rūpalāvaṇyaśālinī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. While that sage was performing the penance, Śuci, the most excellent one of the celestial damsels, endowed with beauty and well-shaped limbs came into his view.

## \|\| 2.59.21 \|\|

*tasyā darśanamātreṇa parikṣubdhaṃ munermanaḥ \|*  
*caskaṃda sa munistūrṇaṃ sātha bhītā varāpsarāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Merely at her sight the mind of the sage became extremely agitated. He had an emission of semen immediately. The excellent celestial damsel became frightened.

## \|\| 2.59.22 \|\|

*dūrādeva namaskṛtya tamṛṣiṃ sābhyabhāṣata \|*  
*atīva vepamānāṃgī śucistacchāpabhītitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. She bowed down to him from a distance. Śuci’s limbs shook excessively due to her fear of the curse of the sage. She spoke to him:

## \|\| 2.59.23-24 \|\|

*nāparādhnomyahaṃ kiṃcinmahogratapasāṃnidhe \|*  
*kṣaṃtavyaṃ me kṣamādhāra kṣamārūpāstapasvinaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*munīnāṃ mānasaṃ prāyo yatpadmādapi tanmṛdu \|*  
*striyaḥ kaṭhorahṛdayāḥ svarūpeṇaiva sattama \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. “O storehouse of extremely rigorous penance, I have not committed even the least offence. (If so) I should be excused. O receptacle of forgiveness and forbearance, ascetics are personified forgiveness. The minds of sages are generally softer than even a lotus. O extremely good one, in their own form, women are hard-hearted.”

## \|\| 2.59.25 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vacastasyāḥ śucerapsaraso muniḥ \|*  
*vivekasetunā staṃbhīnmahāroṣanadīrayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing these words of that celestial damsel Śuci, the sage curbed the flow of the great current of anger by means of the dam of discrimination.

## \|\| 2.59.26 \|\|

*uvāca ca prasannātmā śuce śucirasi dhruvam \|*  
*na me'lpopi hi doṣotra na te doṣosti suṃdari \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Pleased within himself he said: “O Śuci, you are indeed Śuci (pure). In this matter there is no fault on my part nor on yours, O fair lady.

## \|\| 2.59.27 \|\|

*vahnisvarūpā lalanā navanīta samaḥ pumān \|*  
*anabhijñā vadaṃtīti vicārānmahadaṃtaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. ‘Young maidens are of the form of fire and men are like butter’, so say those who are less informed. If we ponder there is a great difference.

## \|\| 2.59.28 \|\|

*snihyeduddhṛtasāropi vahneḥ saṃsparśamāpya vai \|*  
*citraṃ stryākhyā samādānātpumānsnihyati dūrataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Even butter melts only on coming into contact with fire, but it is wonderful that man melts even from a distance, merely when the name of a woman is mentioned.

## \|\| 2.59.29 \|\|

*ataḥ śuce na bhetavyaṃ tvayā śuci manogate \|*  
*atarkitopasthitayā tvayā ca skhalitaṃ mayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Hence, O Śuci of pure mind, you need not be afraid, Since you came unexpectedly, I had the emission of semen.

## \|\| 2.59.30 \|\|

*skhalanānna tathā hānirakāmāttapaso muneḥ \|*  
*yathā kṣaṇāṃdhīkaraṇāddhāniḥ koparayādareḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. If a sage is free from lust there is no harm in this emission of semen as much as there would be from a fit of anger which is inimical as well as blinding within a moment.

## \|\| 2.59.31 \|\|

*kopāttapaḥ kṣayaṃ yāti saṃcitaṃ yatsukṛcchrataḥ \|*  
*yathābhrapaṭalaṃ prāpya prakāśaḥ puṣpavaṃtayoḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The power of penance accumulated with very great difficulty becomes reduced due to anger, like the lustre of the sun and the moon when covered with a patch of cloud.

## \|\| 2.59.32 \|\|

*anarthakāriṇaḥ krodhātkvārthānāṃparijṛbhaṇam \|*  
*kva vā khalajanotsedhātsādhūnāṃ parivardhanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. How can wealth and human aspiration flourish, should there be anger, the cause of ruin and disaster? How can good people prosper if wicked people gain the upper hand?

## \|\| 2.59.33 \|\|

*amarṣe karṣati mano manobhū saṃbhavaḥ kutaḥ \|*  
*vidhuṃtude tudatyuccairvidhuṃ kutrāsti kaumudī \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. When anger grips the mind, how can love stir out? When Rāhu completely eclipses the Moon, how can there be the moonlight?

## \|\| 2.59.34 \|\|

*jvalato roṣadāvāgneḥ kva vā śāṃtitaroḥ sthitiḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭā kenāpi kiṃ kvāpi siṃhātkalabhasusthatā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When the forest-fire of anger blazes, how can the tree of peace stand safe and sound? Has the safety and soundness of a baby elephant been seen anywhere by anyone when a lion is nearby?

## \|\| 2.59.35 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pratīpaḥ pratighātukaḥ \|*  
*caturvargasya dehasya pariheyo vipaścitā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Hence anger which is antagonistic to and destructive of the four aims of life should be eschewed by a sensible man.

## \|\| 2.59.36 \|\|

*idānīṃ śṛṇu kalyāṇi kartavyaṃ yattvayā śuce \|*  
*amoghabījā hi vayaṃ tadbījamurarī kuru \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Now, O fair lady Śuci, listen, what should be done by you. Our semen never goes waste. Hence accept it (within you).

## \|\| 2.59.37 \|\|

*etasminrakṣite vīrye pariskanne tvadīkṣaṇāt \|\| tvayā tava bhavitrekaṃ kanyāratnaṃ mahāśuci \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Should this semen that got emitted at your sight be taken care of by you, an extremely pure jewel of a female child will be born of you,”

## \|\| 2.59.38 \|\|

*ityuktā tena muninā punarjāteva sāpsarāḥ \|*  
*mahāprasāda ityuktvā muneḥ śukramajīgilat \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On being addressed thus by the sage, that celestial lady was reborn as it were. “This is your great favour”, saying so she swallowed the semen of the sage.

## \|\| 2.59.39 \|\|

*atha kālena divyastrī kanyāratnamajījanat \|*  
*atīva nayanānaṃdi nidhānaṃ rūpasaṃpadām \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In due course of time the celestial lady gave birth to a jewel of a female child that was the storehouse of loveliness, delighting much the eyes of onlookers.

## \|\| 2.59.40 \|\|

*tasyaiva vedaśirasa āśrame tāṃ nidhāya sā \|*  
*śucirapsarasāṃ śreṣṭhā jagāma ca yathepsitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Leaving her in the hermitage of Sage Vedaśiras, Śuci, the most excellent one among the celestial damsels, went somewhere as she pleased.

## \|\| 2.59.41 \|\|

*tāṃ ca vedaśirāḥ kanyāṃ snehena samavardhayat \|*  
*kṣīreṇa svāśramasthāyā hariṇyā hariṇīkṣaṇām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. By means of the milk of a doe in his own hermitage, Vedaśiras affectionately brought up that doe-eyed girl.

## \|\| 2.59.42 \|\|

*munirnāma dadau tasyai dhūtapāpeti cārthavat \|*  
*yannāmoccāraṇenāpi kaṃpate pātakāvalī \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The sage gave her a meaningful name Dhūtapāpā (‘One who has shaken off sins’) by merely uttering which all the clusters of sins quake (through fear).

## \|\| 2.59.43 \|\|

*sarvalakṣaṇaśobhāḍhyāṃ sarvāvayava suṃdarīm \|*  
*munistatyāja notsaṃgātkṣaṇamātramapi kvacit \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. She had all the characteristic features of brilliance. She was beautiful in every limb. The sage did not keep her away from his lap even for a moment.

## \|\| 2.59.44 \|\|

*dinedine vardhamānāṃ tāṃ paśyanmumude bhṛśam \|*  
*kṣīranīradhivadramyāṃ niśi cāṃdramasīṃ kalām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Looking at her growing steadily day by day, he was extremely glad like that Ocean of Milk looking at the beautiful digit of the moon at night.

## \|\| 2.59.45 \|\|

*athāṣṭavārṣikīṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ kanyāṃ sa munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*kasmai deyeti saṃcitya tāmeva samapṛcchata \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On observing that she reached the age of eight, the great sage thought within himself: ‘To whom is she to be given?’ and so asked her directly:

## \|\| 2.59.46 \|\|

*vedaśirā uvāca \|*  
*ayi putri mahābhāge dhūtapāpe śubhekṣaṇe \|*  
*kasmai dadyāvarāya tvāṃ tvamevākhyāhi taṃ varam \|\| 46 \|\|*

Vedaśiras said:

46\. O my blessed daughter, O Dhūtapāpā of splendid eyes, to which bridegroom shall I give you? You yourself tell about that bridegroom.

## \|\| 2.59.47 \|\|

*atisnehārdracittasya janetuśceti bhāṣitam \|*  
*niśamya dhūtapāpā sā provāca vinatānanā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On hearing this utterance of her father whose mind was drenched with excessive affection, that girl Dhūtapāpā said with her face lowered:

## \|\| 2.59.48 \|\|

*dhūtapāpovāca \|*  
*janetaryadyahaṃ deyā suṃdarāya varāya te \|*  
*tadā tasmai prayaccha tvaṃ yamahaṃ kathayāmi te \|\| 48 \|\|*

Dhūtapāpā said:

48\. Dear father, if you consider that I should be given away to a handsome bridegroom, then give me unto that person of whom I am telling you now.

## \|\| 2.59.49 \|\|

*tubhyaṃ ca rocate tāta śṛṇotvavahito bhavān \|*  
*sarvebhyotipavitro yo yaḥ sarveṣāṃ namaskṛtaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He should appeal to you too, dear father. May you be pleased to listen attentively?

He should be the holiest of all. He should be one devoutly bowed to by all.

## \|\| 2.59.50 \|\|

*sarve yamabhilaṣyaṃti yasmātsarvasukhodayaḥ \|*  
*kadācidyo na naśyeta yaḥ sadaivānuvartate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He should be one whom all love, from whom all happiness originates, who never perishes and who continues to be ever present.

## \|\| 2.59.51 \|\|

*ihāmutrāpi yo rakṣenmahāpadudayāddhruvam \|*  
*sarve manorathā yasmātparipūrṇā bhavaṃti hi \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He must be one who certainly guards from the rise of great calamities here in this world as well as hereafter, by whom all cherished desires get fulfilled.

## \|\| 2.59.52 \|\|

*dinedine ca saubhāgyaṃ vardhate yasya sannidhau \|*  
*nairaṃtaryeṇa yatsevāṃ kurvato na bhayaṃ kvacit \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He must be one in whose presence conjugal bliss shall increase day by' day and by continuously carrying out whose service, there should be nothing to fear.

## \|\| 2.59.53 \|\|

*yannāmagrahaṇādeva kepi vādhāṃ na kurvate \|*  
*yadādhāreṇa tiṣṭhaṃti bhuvanāni caturdaśa \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He should be one on mentioning whose name, no one can harass and with whom as support, the fourteen worlds stand steady.

## \|\| 2.59.54 \|\|

*evamādyā guṇā yasya varasya varaceṣṭitam \|*  
*tasmai prayaccha māṃ tāta mama tepīhaśarmaṇe \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. For your welfare as well as that of mine, dear father, give me unto that Vara (excellent one, bridegroom) who possesses these and other good qualities and whose activities are excellent.

## \|\| 2.59.55-58 \|\|

*etacchrutvāpi tā tasyā bhṛśaṃ mudamavāpa ha \|*  
*dhanyosmi dhanyā me pūrve yeṣāmaiṣā sutānvaye \|\| 55 \|\|*

*dhruvā hi dhūtapāpāsau yasyā īdṛgvidhā matiḥ \|*  
*īdṛgvidhairguṇagaṇairgarimṇā kotra vai bhavet \|\| 56 \|\|*

*athavā sa kathaṃ labhyo vinā puṇyabharodayam \|*  
*iti kṣaṇaṃ samādhāya manaḥ sa munipuṃgavaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*jñānena taṃ samālocya varamīdṛgguṇodayam \|*  
*dhanyāṃ kanyāṃ babhāṣetha śṛṇu vatse śubhaiṣiṇi \|\| 58 \|\|*

55-57a. On hearing this, her father experienced great joy: “I am blessed. My ancestors are blessed in whose family there is a daughter like her. Certainly this girl whose intellect is thus inclined is verily (as her name indicates) Dhūtapāpā (‘one whose sins are shaken off’). Who can he be here who is really endowed with qualities like these. Or, how can he be obtained without the appearance of the fruit of great merits?”

57b-58. Then the eminent sage concentrated his mind for a while and visualized by his spiritual knowledge, a bridegroom with such good qualities. Then he spoke to the blessed girl:

## \|\| 2.59.59 \|\|

*pitovāca \|*  
*varasya ye tvayā proktā guṇā ete vicakṣaṇe \|*  
*eṣāṃ guṇānāmādhāro varostīti viniścitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

The Father said:

59\. Listen, O wise girl! Verily there certainly exists a bridegroom, the receptacle of the good qualities as enumerated by you.

## \|\| 2.59.60 \|\|

*paraṃ sa sukhalabhyo na nitarāṃ subhagākṛtiḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ paṇena sa krayyaḥ sutīrthavipaṇau kvacit \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He who is extremely handsome in his features, cannot be easily obtained. He should be purchased (won over) by means of penance as the price in a market in the form of some excellent Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.59.61 \|\|

*tīrthabhāraiḥ sa sulabho na kaulīnyena kanyake \|*  
*na vedaśāstrābhyasanairna caiśvaryabalena vai \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O (my) daughter, he cannot be easily obtained through a lot of wealth, ör through nobility of birth, or by the study and practice of the Vedas and Scriptures or through the power of prosperity.

## \|\| 2.59.62 \|\|

*na sauṃdaryeṇa vapuṣā na buddhyā na parākramaiḥ \|*  
*ekayaiva manaḥ śuddhyā karaṇānāṃ jayena ca \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Neither by the beauty of physical form can he be obtained, nor by intellect and never by valour. The only means (to obtain him) is the purity of the mind through subduing the sense-organs.

## \|\| 2.59.63 \|\|

*mahātapaḥ sahāyena damadānadayāyujā \|*  
*labhyate sa mahāprājño nānyathā sadṛśaḥ patiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. That befitting husband of great intellect is to be obtained with the help of great austerity together with Dama (controlling the sense-organs). Dāna (gifts) and Dayā (compassion).

## \|\| 2.59.64 \|\|

*iti śrutvātha sā kanyā pitaraṃ praṇipatya ca \|*  
*anujñāṃ prārthayāmāsa tapase kṛtaniścayā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On hearing these words that girl bowed down to her father. Having decided to perform penance, she requested her father for the requisite permission.

## \|\| 2.59.65 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*kṛtānujñā janetrā sā kṣetre paramapāvane \|*  
*tapastatāpa paramaṃ yadasādhyaṃ tapasvibhiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

Skanda said:

65\. On being permitted by her father, she performed a great penance in the extremely sacred spot (of Avimukta)—a penance not easily performed even by ascetics.

## \|\| 2.59.66 \|\|

*kva sā bālātimṛdvaṃgī kva ca tattādṛśaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*kaṭhoravarṣmasaṃsādhyamaho saccetaso dhṛtiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. (What a great contrast!) Where is that girl of exquisitely soft limbs? Where is such an uncommon penance of that sort which can be performed only with a sturdy physical frame? Wonderful is the fortitude of persons of excellent mental setup!

## \|\| 2.59.67 \|\|

*dhārāsārā suvarṣāsu mahāvātavatīṣvalam \|*  
*śilāsu sāvakāśāsu sā bahvīranayanniśāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. In rainy season when there was continuous downpour together with violent gusts of wind, she spent many nights on large slabs of stone.

## \|\| 2.59.68 \|\|

*śrutvā garjaravaṃ ghoraṃ dṛṣṭvā vidyuccamatkṛtīḥ \|*  
*āsārasīkaraiḥ klinnā na cakaṃpe manākca sā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. She did not tremble even slightly when she heard the terrible thundering sound, nor when she saw the dazzling streaks of lightning and when she got drenched in torrential downpour.

## \|\| 2.59.69 \|\|

*taḍitsphuraṃtītvasakṛttamisrāsu tapovane \|*  
*yātāyātaṃ karotīva draṣṭuṃ tattapasaḥ sthitim \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. During dark nights there were frequent flashes of lightning in the penance grove. It appeared as though it passed to and fro inspecting her practice of penance.

## \|\| 2.59.70 \|\|

*tapartureva sākṣācca kumārī kaitavātkila \|*  
*paṃcāgnīnparidhāyātra tapasyati tapovane \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Verily the season of summer itself had come down to the penance grove under the guise of that girl and started performing penance with five fires all-round.

## \|\| 2.59.71 \|\|

*jalābhilāṣiṇī bālā na manāgapi sā pibat \|*  
*kuśāgratoyapṛṣataṃ paṃcāgniparitāpitā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Though scorched by the five fires the girl never felt thirsty for water, nor did she drink even a drop from the tip of a Kuśa.

## \|\| 2.59.72 \|\|

*romāṃca kaṃcukavatī vepamānatanucchadā \|*  
*paryakṣipatkṣapāḥ kṣāmā tapasā haimanīśca sā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. She appeared to be wearing a shawl in the form of horripilation; her very skin trembled; she was lean and emaciated through the penance. Thus she spent the early wintry nights.

## \|\| 2.59.73 \|\|

*niśīthinīṣu śiśire śrayaṃtī sārasaṃ rasam \|*  
*mene sā sārasaiḥ keyamudyatādyeti padminī \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. In late winter during the nights she resorted to the lakes, when she was thought by the Sārasa birds there as though a new lotus-plant had sprung up.

## \|\| 2.59.74 \|\|

*manasvināmapi manorāgatāṃ sṛjate madhau \|*  
*tadoṣṭhapallavādrāgo jahre mākaṃdapallavaiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Even the minds of ascetics become passionate during spring but the passion of her mind and the reddish tinge of her lips were taken over by the sprouts of mango trees.

## \|\| 2.59.75 \|\|

*vasaṃte nivasaṃtī sā vane bālācalaṃmanaḥ \|*  
*cakre tapasyapi śrutvā kokilā kākalīravam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. During her stay in the forest in spring season, that girl kept her mind steadily engaged in penance though she heard the Kākalī sound of the cuckoos.

## \|\| 2.59.76 \|\|

*baṃdhujīve'dhararuciṃ kalahaṃse kalāgatīḥ \|*  
*nikṣepamiva sā kṣiptvā śaradyāsīttaporatā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. In autumn she became engaged in the penance, after depositing as it were the lustre of her lips in the Bandhujīva (China rose) and the charming gaits in the swan.

## \|\| 2.59.77 \|\|

*apāstabhogasaṃparkā bhogināṃ vṛttimāśritā \|*  
*kṣududbodhanirodhāya dhūtapāpā tapasvinī \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The ascetic girl Dhūtapāpā who had eschewed all contacts with pleasures resorted to the practice of Bhogins (‘those who enjoy’, serpents) (i.e. the only intake was air) in order to prevent the rise of hunger.

## \|\| 2.59.78 \|\|

*śāṇena maṇivallīḍhā kṛśāpyāyādanarghatām \|*  
*tathāpi tapasā kṣāmā didīpe tattanustarām \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Just as a jewel when whetted on a whetting stone attains greater lustre, so also her body, though lean on account of the penance, shone all the more.

## \|\| 2.59.79 \|\|

*nirīkṣya tāṃ tapasyaṃtīṃ vidhiḥ saṃśuddhamānasām \|*  
*upetyovāca suprajñe prasannosmi varaṃ vṛṇu \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. On seeing her in continuous penance with purity of mind, Brahmā approached her and said: “O girl of excellent intellect, I am pleased. Choose a boon.”

## \|\| 2.59.80 \|\|

*sā caturvaktramālokya haṃsayānoparisthitam \|*  
*praṇamya prāṃjaliḥ prītā provācātha prajāpatim \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. On seeing the Four-faced Lord seated on his vehicle, the swan, she became delighted. Bowing down with palms joined in deference, she spoke to the Grand Patriarch:

## \|\| 2.59.81 \|\|

*dhūtapāpovāca \|*  
*pitāmaha varo mahyaṃ yadi deyo varaprada \|*  
*sarvebhyaḥ pāvanebhyopi kuru māmatipāvanīm \|\| 81 \|\|*

Dhūtapāpā said:

81\. O Grandfather, O bestower of boons, if a boon is to be granted to me, make me the purest of all pure ones.

## \|\| 2.59.82 \|\|

*sraṣṭā tadiṣṭamākarṇya nitarāṃ tuṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvācātha tāṃ bālāṃ vimalāṃ vimaleṣiṇīm \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. On hearing of her desire, the Creator was excessively delighted and contented in his mind. He spoke in reply to that pure girl seeking purity:

## \|\| 2.59.83 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*dhūtapāpe pavitrāṇi yāni saṃtyatra sarvataḥ \|*  
*tebhyaḥ pavitramatulaṃ tvamedhi varato mama \|\| 83 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

83\. O Dhūtapāpā, by my boon, do become the most sacred and purest without parallel of all the pure things here all-round.

## \|\| 2.59.84 \|\|

*tisraḥ koṭyo'rdhakoṭī ca saṃti tīrthāni kanyake \|*  
*divi bhuvyaṃtarikṣe ca pāvanānyuttarottaram \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. O girl, there are three and a half crores of pure Tīrthas in heaven, on the earth and in the atmosphere. They are capable of purifying more and more.

## \|\| 2.59.85 \|\|

*tāni sarvāṇi tīrthāni tvattanau pratiloma vai \|*  
*vasaṃtu mama vākyena bhava sarvātipāvanī \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. At my behest may all those Tīrthas reside in your body in every pore of hair. Be the most sanctifying of all.

## \|\| 2.59.86 \|\|

*ityuktvāṃtardadhe vedhāḥ sāpi nirdhūtakalmaṣā \|*  
*dhūtapāpoṭajaṃ prāptātho vedaśirasaḥ pituḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. After saying this, Brahmā vanished. That girl Dhūtapāpā whose sins had become dispelled went to the hut of Vedaśiras, her father.

## \|\| 2.59.87 \|\|

*kadācittāṃ samālokya khelaṃtīmuṭajājire \|*  
*dharmastattapasākṛṣṭaḥ prārthayāmāsa kanyakām \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Once Dharma who had been attracted by her power of penance, saw her sporting about in the courtyard of the hut. He requested the girl:

## \|\| 2.59.88 \|\|

*dharma uvāca \|*  
*pṛthuśroṇi viśālākṣi kṣāmodari śubhānane \|*  
*krītaḥ svarūpasaṃpattyā tvayāhaṃ dehi me rahaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

Dharma said:

88\. O fair lady of splendid countenance, O slender-bellìed one of huge buttocks and large eyes, ī have been bought as it were by thy richly beautiful form; grant me the pleasure of secret intercourse.

## \|\| 2.59.89 \|\|

*nitarāṃ bādhate kāmastvatkṛte māṃ sulocane \|*  
*ajñātanāmnā sā tena prārthitetyasakṛdgrahaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. O fair-eyed One, thanks to thee, the Lord of Love harasses me excessively.

Thus she was often requested in secret by that (Dharma) whose name she did not know.

## \|\| 2.59.90 \|\|

*uvāca sā pitā dātā taṃ prārthaya sudurmate \|*  
*pitṛpradeyā yatkanyā śrutireṣā sanātanī \|\| 90 \|\|*

She said:

90\. My father should be the giver. O wretch of wicked intention, request him because a girl should be given in marriage by her father. This is the injunction of the eternal Sruti.

## \|\| 2.59.91 \|\|

*niśamyeti vaco dharmo bhāvinorthasya gauravāt \|*  
*punarnibaṃdhayāṃcakre 'padhṛtirdhṛtiśālinīm \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. After hearing these words, Dharma continued his importunity to that girl of forbearance, he himself having lost it due to the gravity of what was destined to happen.

## \|\| 2.59.92 \|\|

*dharma uvāca \|*  
*na prārthayehaṃ subhage pitaraṃ tava suṃdari \|*  
*gāṃdharveṇa vivāhena kuru me tvaṃ samīhitam \|\| 92 \|\|*

Dharma said:

92\. O beautiful girl of great fortune, I do not (wish to) request your father. Carry out my desire through the Gāndharva form of marriage.

## \|\| 2.59.93 \|\|

*iti nirbaṃdhavadvākyaṃ sā niśamya kumārikā \|*  
*pituḥ kanyāphalaṃditsuḥ punarāheti taṃ dvijam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. On hearing these importunate words, that girl wished to pay regard due to her father because of her being a daughter. She therefore, spoke to the Brāhmaṇa thus:

## \|\| 2.59.94 \|\|

*are jaḍamate mā tvaṃ punarbrūhīti yāhyataḥ \|*  
*ityuktopi kumāryā sa nātiṣṭhanmadanāturaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. “O dull-witted one, do not speak thus again. Go away from here.” Though admonished thus by the girl, he did not remain quiet because he was utterly afflicted by god of Love.

## \|\| 2.59.95 \|\|

*tataḥ śaśāpa taṃ bālā prabalā tapaso balāt \|*  
*jaḍosi nitarāṃ yasmājjalādhāro nado bhava \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Then the girl cursed him, having become powerful due to her penance: “Since you are utterly insensible, become a river, a receptacle of water.”

## \|\| 2.59.96 \|\|

*iti śaptastayā sotha tāṃ śaśāpa krudhānvitaḥ \|*  
*kaṭhorahṛdaye tvaṃ tu śilā bhava sudurmate \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Cursed thus by her he too became angry and cursed her thus: “O wicked-minded one of hard heart, become a rock.”

## \|\| 2.59.97 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ityanyonyasya śāpena mune dharmo nado'bhavat \|*  
*avimukte mahākṣetre khyāto dharmanado mahān \|\| 97 \|\|*

Skanda said:

97\. Thus on account of their mutual curse, O sage, Dharma became a river in the great Tīrtha named Avimukta. It became well-known as the great Dharmanada.

## \|\| 2.59.98 \|\|

*sāpyāha pitaraṃ trastā svaśilātvasya kāraṇam \|*  
*dhyānena dharmaṃ vijñāya muniḥ kanyāmathābravīt \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Very much frightened, she told her father the reason of her becoming a rock. By means of his meditation, the sage understood that it was Dharma and said to his daughter:

## \|\| 2.59.99 \|\|

*mā bhaiḥ putri kariṣyāmi tava sarvaṃ śubhodayam \|*  
*tacchāpo nānyathā bhūyāccaṃdrakāṃtaśilā bhava \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. “Do not be afraid, dear daughter. I shall do unto you everything that will end in an auspicious result. His curse cannot become otherwise. Become a lunar stone.

## \|\| 2.59.100 \|\|

*caṃdrodayamanuprāpya dravībhūtatanustataḥ \|*  
*dhunī bhava sute sādhvi dhūtapāpeti viśrutā \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. When the moon rises you will become melted, dear daughter, and be a river, dear chaste one, well-reputed as Dhūtapāpā.

## \|\| 2.59.101 \|\|

*sa ca dharmanadaḥ kanye tava bhartā suśobhanaḥ \|*  
*tairguṇaiḥ paripūrṇāṃgo ye guṇāḥ prārthitāstvayā \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. O girl, that Dharmanada is your splendid husband. He possesses all those good qualities as expressed by you.

## \|\| 2.59.102 \|\|

*anyacca śṛṇu sadbuddhe mamāpi tapaso balāt \|*  
*dvairūpyaṃ bhavatorbhāvi prākṛtaṃ ca dravaṃ ca vai \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. O wise one, listen to one thing more. By the power of my penance there shall be two forms of both of you, the original and the liquidized.”

## \|\| 2.59.103 \|\|

*ityāśvāsya pitā kanyāṃ dhūtapāpāṃ paraṃtapa \|*  
*caṃdrakāṃtaśilābhūtāmanujagrāha buddhimān \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. O scorcher of enemies, thus the father consoled the daughter. The wise sage blessed her duly when she became a lunar stone.

## \|\| 2.59.104 \|\|

*tadārabhya mune kāśyāṃ khyāto dharmanado hradaḥ \|*  
*dharmo dravasvarūpeṇa mahāpātakanāśanaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Ever since then, O sage the Hrada (still Pond) became famous as Dharmanada in Kāśī. In the liquid form Dharma is the destroyer of great sins.

## \|\| 2.59.105 \|\|

*dhunī ca dhūtapāpā sā sarvatīrthamayī śubhā \|*  
*harenmahāghasaṃghātānkūlajāniva pādapān \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. That splendid river Dhūtapāpā consists of all Tīrthas. It shall remove masses of great sins as though they are trees growing on its banks.

## \|\| 2.59.106 \|\|

*tatra dharmanade tīrthe dhūtapāpā samanvite \|*  
*yadā na svardhunī tatra tadā bradhnastapo vyadhāt \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Before the advent of the celestial river Bradhna (the Sun-god) performed a penance in that Tīrtha called Dharmanada along with Dhūtapāpā.

## \|\| 2.59.107 \|\|

*gabhastimālī bhagavāngabhastīśvara sannidhau \|*  
*śīlayanmaṃgalāṃ gaurīṃ tapa ugraṃ cacāra ha \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. The Ray-garlanded Lord (the Sun-god) meditated on Maṅgalā Gaurī in the presence of Gabhastīśvara (Siva) and performed his fierce penance.

## \|\| 2.59.108 \|\|

*nāmnā mayūkhādityasya tīrthe tatra tapasyataḥ \|*  
*kiraṇebhyaḥ pravavṛte mahāsvedotikhedataḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. While he was performing the penance in the name of Mayûkhāditya, great sweat issued forth from his rays due to the strain involved.

## \|\| 2.59.109 \|\|

*kiraṇebhyaḥ pravṛttāyā mahāsvedasya saṃtatiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sā kiraṇānāma jātā puṇyā taraṃgiṇī \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. The continuous perspiration that issued forth from the rays, became a holy river named Kiraṇā.

## \|\| 2.59.110 \|\|

*mahāpāpāṃdhatamasaṃ kiraṇākhyā taraṃgiṇī \|*  
*dhvaṃsayetsnānamātreṇa militā dhūtapāpayā \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. In conjunction with Dhūtapāpā, the river named Kiraṇā shall destroy the darkness of the mass of great sins merely through the holy bath therein.

## \|\| 2.59.111 \|\|

*ādau dharmanadaḥ puṇyo miśrito dhūtapāpayā \|*  
*yayā dhūtāni pāpāni sarvatīrthīkṛtātmanā \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. At the outset, the holy Dharmanada joined Dhūtapāpā whereby all sins were destroyed because it consisted of all Tīrthas.

## \|\| 2.59.112 \|\|

*tatopi militāgatya kiraṇā raviṇaidhitā \|*  
*yannāmasmaraṇādeva mahāmohoṃdhatāṃ vrajet \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Kiraṇā augmented by the Sun joined with her. Merely by remembering the name of Kiraṇā great delusion becomes destroyed.

## \|\| 2.59.113 \|\|

*kiraṇā dhūtapāpe ca tasmindharmanade śubhe \|*  
*sravaṃtyau pāpasaṃhartryau vārāṇasyāṃ śubhadrave \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Kiraṇā and Dhūtapāpā fall into the auspicious Dharmanada. These two rivers in Vārāṇasī with their holy waters destroy all sins.

## \|\| 2.59.114 \|\|

*tato bhāgīrathī prāptā tena dailīpinā saha \|*  
*bhāgīrathī samāyātā yamunā ca sarasvatī \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Thereafter Bhāgīrathī arrived there along with Bhagīratha, son of Dilīpa. Yamunā and Sarasvatī came there like Bhāgīrathī.

## \|\| 2.59.115 \|\|

*kiraṇā dhūtapāpā ca puṇyatoyā sarasvatī \|*  
*gaṃgā ca yamunā caiva paṃcanadyotra kīrtitāḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Five rivers are glorified here: Kiraṇā, Dhūtapāpā, Sarasvatī of holy waters, Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

## \|\| 2.59.116 \|\|

*ataḥ paṃcanadaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*tatrāpluto na gṛhṇīyāddehaṃ nā pāṃcabhautikam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Hence the Tīrtha became renowned in all the three worlds by the name Pañcanada. A man who takes his holy dip therein does not take up a physical form consisting of the five elements.

## \|\| 2.59.117 \|\|

*asminpaṃcanadīnāṃ ca saṃbhedeghaughabhedini \|*  
*snānamātrātprayātyeva bhittvā brahmāṃḍamaṃḍapam \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. In this confluence of five rivers that destroys masses of sins, one should take one’s ablution whereby one passes off splitting the pavilion of the cosmos.

## \|\| 2.59.118 \|\|

*tīrthāni saṃti bhūyāṃsi kāśyāmatra padepade \|*  
*na paṃcanadatīrthasya koṭyaṃśena samānyapi \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. There are many Tīrthas here in Kāśī at every step, but they are not on a par even with a ten-millionth part of Pañcanada Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.59.119 \|\|

*prayāge māghamāse tu samyaksnātasya yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ syāddinaikena kāśyāṃ paṃcanade dhruvam \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. By taking the holy dip on a single day in Pañcanada at Kāśī that benefit one certainly gains which one gains by taking sedulous bath in Prayāga for the whole of the month of Māgha.

## \|\| 2.59.120 \|\|

*snātvā paṃcanade tīrthe kṛtvā ca pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*biṃdumādhavamabhyarcya na bhūyo janmabhāgbhavet \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. After bathing in Pañcanada Tīrtha and offering libations to the forefathers, a devotee should worship Bindumādhava. He will not be reborn.

## \|\| 2.59.121 \|\|

*yāvatsaṃkhyāstilādattāḥ pitṛbhyo jalatarpaṇe \|*  
*puṇye paṃcanade tīrthe tṛptiḥ syāttāvadābdikī \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. The contentment of the forefathers shall be for as many years as there are gingelly seeds in the libation to the forefathers in the holy Tīrtha of Pañcanada.

## \|\| 2.59.122 \|\|

*śraddhayā yaiḥ kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ tītheṃ paṃcanade śubhe \|*  
*teṣāṃ pitāmahā muktā nānāyoni gatā api \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. If Śrāddha is offered with great faith in the splendid Tīrtha of Pañcanada, the forefathers shall become liberated, though they might have taken birth in different species of creatures.

## \|\| 2.59.123 \|\|

*yamaloke pitṛgaṇairgātheyaṃ parigīyate \|*  
*mahimānaṃ pāṃcanadaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrāddhavidhānataḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. On observing the greatness of Pañcanada in respect to the injunctions regarding Śrāddha this Gāthā (folk rhyme) is being sung by the groups of ancestors in the world of Yama.

## \|\| 2.59.124 \|\|

*asmākamapi vaṃśyotra kaścicchrāddhaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*kāśyāṃ paṃcanadaṃ prāpya yena mucyāmahe vayam \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. “Will someone belonging to our family come to Pañcanada at Kāśī and perform Śrāddha whereby we shall get liberated?”

## \|\| 2.59.125 \|\|

*iyaṃ gāthā pratidinaṃ śrāddhadevasya sannidhau \|*  
*pitṛbhiḥ parigīyeta kāśyāṃ paṃcanadaṃ prati \|\| 125 \|\|*
