125\. This Gāthā pertaining to Pañcanada at Kāśī is being sung everyday in front of Śrāddhadeva (god of Death) by the forefathers.

## \|\| 2.59.126 \|\|

*tatra paṃcanade tīrthe yatkiṃciddīyate vasu \|*  
*kalpakṣayepi na bhavettasya puṇyasya saṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. If even the least of money is given away there in the Pañcanada Tīrtha there shall be no reduction to that Puṇya (merit) even if the Kalpa comes to a close.

## \|\| 2.59.127 \|\|

*vaṃdhyāpi varṣaparyaṃtaṃ snātvā paṃcanade hrade \|*  
*samarcya maṃgalāṃ gauṃrīṃ putraṃ janayati dhruvam \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Even a barren woman shall certainly give birth to a son after taking a holy bath in the Pañcanada Hrada for a year and worshipping Maṅgalā Gaurī.

## \|\| 2.59.128 \|\|

*jalaiḥ pāṃcanadaiḥ puṇyairvāsasā pāriśodhitaiḥ \|*  
*mahāphalamavāpnoti snapayitveṣṭadevatām \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. If the deity of one’s own choice be bathed with the holy waters of Pañcanada filtered with a cloth, the devotee shall attain great benefit.

## \|\| 2.59.129 \|\|

*paṃcāmṛtānāṃ kalaśairaṣṭottaraśatonmitaiḥ \|*  
*tulitodhikatāṃ yāto biṃduḥ paṃcanadāṃbhasaḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. A drop of water of Pañcanada when weighed against hundred and eight potfuls of Amṛta has excelled (those pitchers of Nectar).

## \|\| 2.59.130 \|\|

*paṃcakūrcena pītena yātra śuddhirudāhṛtā \|*  
*sā śuddhiḥ śraddhayā prāśya biṃduṃ pāṃcanadāṃbhasaḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. By taking in a drop of Pañcanada water with faith, one gets as much purity as is cited as the benefit of taking in Pañcakūrca (Pañcagavya).

## \|\| 2.59.131 \|\|

*bhavedavabhṛthasnānādrājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ \|*  
*yatphalaṃ tacchataguṇaṃ snānātpāṃcanadāṃbhasā \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. By taking the holy bath in the waters of Pañcanada one gets hundred times the benefit that one gets after Avabhṛtha (valedictory) baths after Rājasūya and Aśvamedha.

## \|\| 2.59.132 \|\|

*rājasūyāśvamedhau ca bhavetāṃ svargasādhanam \|*  
*ābrahmaghaṭikādvaṃdvaṃ muktyai pāṃcanadāplutiḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Rājasūya and Aśvamedha may very well be the means of achieving heaven; but the holy bath in Pañcanada is conducive to salvation for two Ghaṭikās of Brahmā.

## \|\| 2.59.133 \|\|

*svargarājyābhiṣekopi na tathā saṃmataḥ satām \|*  
*abhiṣekaḥ pāṃcanado yathānalpasukhapradaḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Coronation in the heavenly kingdom is not as much worthy of honour to good people as the holy dip in Pañcanada which accords immense pleasure.

## \|\| 2.59.134 \|\|

*varaṃ vārāṇasīṃ prāpya bhṛtyaḥ paṃcanadokṣiṇām \|*  
*nānyatra sevakībhūta bhūpakoṭirnareśvaraḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Better to go to Vārāṇasī and be a servant to those who sprinkle themselves with the waters of Pañcanada than be a king elsewhere with million kings as servants.

## \|\| 2.59.135 \|\|

*yairna paṃcanade snātaṃ kārtike pāpahāriṇi \|*  
*te'dyāpi garbhe tiṣṭhaṃti punaste garbhavāsinaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Those who do not take their holy dips in Pañcanada in the month of Kārttika that removes all sins, continue to stay in a mother’s womb even today. They are doomed to be in the womb again.

## \|\| 2.59.136 \|\|

*kṛte dharmanadaṃ nāma tretāyāṃ dhūtapāpakam \|*  
*dvāpare biṃdutīrthaṃ ca kalau paṃcanadaṃ smṛtam \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. In Kṛtayuga the Tīrtha is named Dharmanada; in Tretā it is Dhūtapāpaka; in Dvāpara it is Bindu Tīrtha and it is remembered as Pañcanada in Kali age.

## \|\| 2.59.137 \|\|

*śataṃ samāstapastaptvā kṛte yatprāpyate phalam \|*  
*tatkārtike paṃcanade sakṛtsnānena labhyate \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. What is obtained as benefit in Kṛtayuga after performing penance for a hundred years is obtained as benefit by a single bath in Pañcanada in the month of Kārttika.

## \|\| 2.59.138 \|\|

*iṣṭāpūrteṣu dharmeṣu yāvajanmakṛteṣu yat \|*  
*anyatra syātphalaṃ tatsyādūrje dharmanadāplavāt \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. By performing holy ablution in Dharmanada in the month of Kārttika, one shall get the same benefit as is obtained elsewhere by performing holy rites such as Iṣṭāpūrtas for the whole life.

## \|\| 2.59.139 \|\|

*na dhūtapāpa sadṛśaṃ tīrthaṃ kvāpi mahītale \|*  
*yadekasnānato naśyedaghaṃ janmatrayārjitam \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. There is no Tīrtha anywhere on the earth like Dhūtapāpā where a single holy dip destroys sins accumulated in the course of three births.

## \|\| 2.59.140 \|\|

*biṃdutīrthe naro dattvā kāṃcanaṃ kṛṣṇalonmitam \|*  
*na daridro bhavetkvāpi na svarṇena viyujyate \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. By gifting gold to the extent of a Kṛṣṇala (a Raktika) in Bindu Tīrtha a man is never kept in want of gold. He will never be poor.

## \|\| 2.59.141 \|\|

*gobhūtilahiraṇyāśva vāsonnasragvibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*yatkiṃcidbiṃdutīrthetra dattvākṣayamavāpnuyāt \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. At Bindu Tīrtha any of these things can be gifted: a cow, a plot of land, gingelly seeds, gold, a horse, clothes, cooked food, garland or ornaments. Thereby one gets those things perennially.

## \|\| 2.59.142 \|\|

*ekāmapyāhutiṃ dattvā samiddhegnau vidhānataḥ \|*  
*puṇye dharmanade tīrthe koṭihomaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. By offering a single Āhuti in a well-kindled fire in accordance with the injunctions at the holy Tīrtha called Dharmanada, one obtains the benefit of ten million Homas.

## \|\| 2.59.143 \|\|

*na paṃcanadatīrthasya mahimānamanaṃtakam \|*  
*kopi varṇayituṃ śaktaścaturvarga śubhaukasaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. No one is capable of extolling adequately the infinite greatness of Pañcanada Tīrtha which is the splendid abode of all the four aims of life.

## \|\| 2.59.144 \|\|

*śrutvākhyānamidaṃ puṇyaṃ śrāvayitvāpi bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. By listening to this meritorious narrative and making others listen devoutly, one becomes purified in the soul of all sins and is honoured in the world of Viṣṇu.

## Chapter 60 - Manifestation of Bindumādhava

## \|\| 2.60.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*uktā paṃcanadotpattirmitrāvaruṇanaṃdana \|*  
*idānīṃ kathayiṣyāmi mādhavāviṣkṛtiṃ parām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Bindu Mādhava temple was built at the top of Pañcagaṅgā Ghāṭa. Its glory is described by Tulasīdāsa (16th cent.). The European traveller Tavernier (17th cent.) notes this ‘great Pagoda’ as most impressive. But the temple was destroyed by the orders of Aurangzeb and a mosque was built there. Today the temple called Bindu Mādhava is located in an inconspicuous building in the shadow of the big mosque of Aurangzeb. (BCL 206-207)

Skanda said:

1\. The origin of Pañcanada has been narrated, O Son of Mitra and Varuṇa. Now I shall narrate the great story of the manifestation of Mādhava.

## \|\| 2.60.2 \|\|

*yāṃ śrutvā śraddhayā dhīmānpāpebhyo mucyate kṣaṇāt \|*  
*na ca śriyā viyujyeta saṃyujyeta vṛṣeṇa ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On hearing it with faith, an intelligent man shall become liberated instantaneously from sins. He will not be separated from wealth and glory. He will be united with virtue.

## \|\| 2.60.3-5 \|\|

*āgatya maṃdarādadrerupeṃdraścaṃdraśekharam \|*  
*āpṛcchya tārkṣyarathagaḥ kṣaṇādvārāṇasīṃ purīm \|\| 3 \|\|*

*divo dāsaṃ mahīpālaṃ samuccāṭya svamāyayā \|*  
*sthitvā pādodake tīrthe keśavākhya svarūpataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*mahimānaṃ paraṃ kāśyāṃ vicārya suvicārya ca \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā paṃcanadaṃ tīrthaṃ parāṃ mudamavāpa ha \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Upendra took leave of the Moon-crested Lord and reached the city of Vārāṇasī riding on his vehicle Garuḍa. He completed the journey in a moment after starting from the mountain Mandara. By means of his Māyā, he evicted King Divodāsa. Thereafter he stationed himself in the Pādodaka Tīrtha by the name and form of Keśava. He thought of the greatness of Kāśī. On seeing the Tīrtha of Pañcanada he became extremely delighted.

## \|\| 2.60.6 \|\|

*uvāca ca prasannātmā puṃḍarīkavilocanaḥ \|*  
*agaṇyā api vaikuṃṭha guṇā vigaṇitā mayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The delighted lotus-eyed Lord said: “The good qualities of Vaikuṇṭha cannot be fully reckoned. Still they have been ignored by me.

## \|\| 2.60.7 \|\|

*kva kṣīranīradhau saṃti tāvaṃto nirmalā guṇāḥ \|*  
*yāvaṃto vijayaṃ tetra kāśyāṃ paṃcanade hrade \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The number of spotless qualities as are conspicuously present in the whirlpool of Pañcanada in Kāśī are not present in the Ocean of Milk.

## \|\| 2.60.8 \|\|

*śvetadvīpepi sāmagrī kva guṇānāṃ garīyasī \|*  
*īdṛśī yādṛśī kāśyāṃ dhūtapāpesti pāvanī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Even in Śvetadvīpa where is that big collection of good qualities like what is present in the Tīrtha named Dhūtapāpā? It is extremely holy and sacred.

## \|\| 2.60.9 \|\|

*mude kaumodakī sparśastathā na mama jāyate \|\| dhūtapāpāṃbu saṃparko yathā bhavati sarvathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The contact with Kaumodakī is not so much conducive to my joy as is the touch of the holy waters of Dhūtapāpā in every respect.

## \|\| 2.60.10 \|\|

*na kṣīranīradhijayā sukhaṃ me śliṣṭagātrayā \|*  
*tathā bhavedyathātra syātspṛṣṭayā dhūtapāpayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Even when the Daughter of the Milky Ocean (Lakṣmī) touches my limbs, I do not get that much pleasure as I get here when touched by Dhūtapāpā.”

## \|\| 2.60.11-13 \|\|

*itthaṃ paṃcanade tīrthe kṣīranīradhijādhavaḥ \|*  
*saṃpreṣya tārkṣyaṃ tryakṣāgre vṛttāṃtaviniveditum \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ānaṃdakānanabhavaṃ divodāsa kṣamāpateḥ \|*  
*saṃvarṇayanguṇagrāmaṃ puṇyaṃ pāṃcanadodbhavam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sukhopaviṣṭaḥ saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sudṛṣṭirviṣṭaraśravāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭavāṃstapasā juṣṭamapuṣṭāṃgaṃ tapodhanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. He had already sent Tārkṣya (Garuḍa) to the presence of the Three-eyed Lord to intimate the events of Ānadakānana; and he described the good qualities of King Divodāsa and the merit arising from Pañcanada. Thereafter the Consort of the Daughter of the Ocean of Milk (Viṣṇu) became highly pleased when he was comfortably seated there thus.

Viṣṭaraśrava (Viṣṇu) of keen vision saw a sage engaged in penance. His limbs were not well-nourished (i.e. emaciated).

## \|\| 2.60.14-22 \|\|

*sa ṛṣistaṃ samabhyetya puṃḍarīkākṣamacyutam \|*  
*upopaviṣṭakamalaṃ vanamālāvirājitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śaṃkhapadmagadācakra caṃcatkaracatuṣṭayam \|*  
*kaustubhodbhāsitoraskaṃ pītakauśeyavāsasam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sunīleṃdīvararuciṃ susnigdha madhurākṛtim \|*  
*nābhīhradalasatpadma supāṭalaradacchadam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dāḍimībījadaśanaṃ kirīṭadyotitāṃbaram \|*  
*deveṃdravaṃditapadaṃ sanakādipariṣṭutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*divyarṣibhirnāradādyaiḥ parigītamahodayam \|*  
*prahlādādyairbhāgavataiḥ parinaṃditamānasam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dhṛtaśārṅgadhanurdaṃḍaṃ daṃḍitākhiladānavam \|*  
*madhukaiṭabhahaṃtāraṃ kaṃsavidhvaṃsasūcakam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kaivalyaṃ yatparaṃ brahma nirākāramagocaram \|*  
*taṃ puṃ mūrtyā pariṇataṃ bhaktānāṃ bhaktihetutaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vedāviduryadākāraṃ naivopaniṣadoditam \|*  
*brahmādyā na ca gīrvāṇāścakre netrātithiṃ satam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*praṇanāma mudāyuktaḥ kṣitivinyastamastakaḥ \|*  
*sa ṛṣistaṃ hṛṣīkeśamagnibiṃdurmahātapāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

14-22. That sage Agnibindu of great austerities approached the lotus-eyed Acyuta. He joyously bowed down to him placing his head on the ground. He could espy the Lord (lit. make him the guest of his eyes) whose form and size neither the Vedas nor the Upaniṣaḍs nor the Devas beginning with Brahmā could understand. The Upaniṣads could not describe him. The Lord was like this.

He was adorned with sylvan flower garlands. He was seated close to Kamalā (Goddess Lakṣmī). He had the conch, lotus, mace and discus hanging from his four hands. His chest shone with the jewel Kaustubha. He was clad in yellow robes. His complexion had the lustre of a blue lotus. His form was sweet and shining. A lotus gracefully came out of his deep naval. His lips were excessively reddish in tinge. His teeth resembled the seeds of a pomegranate. His crown brightened the atmosphere. His feet were adored by the Lord of Devas. He was eulogized by Sanaka and others. His glory and greatness was sung about by Nārada and other divine sages. His mind was extremely delighted by Prahlāda and other devotees of the Lord. He had chastised all the Dānavas. He held the bow called Śārṅga. He was the slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha. He was the indicator of the death of Kaṃsa. By the devotion of devotees the very Kaivalya, the invisible and formless supreme Brahman, had become manifested in human form in him.

## \|\| 2.60.23-24 \|\|

*tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā maulibaddhakarāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*adhyastavistīrṇaśilaṃ balidhvaṃsinamacyutam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tatra paṃcanadābhyāśe mārkaṃḍeyādi sevite \|*  
*goviṃdamagnibiṃduḥ sa stutavāṃstuṣṭamānasaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. His (Agnibindu’s) palms joined in reverence were kept close to his head and he prayed with great devotion. There, very near Pañcanada frequently resorted to by Mārkaṇḍeya and others, that sage Agnibindu eulogized Acyuta who caused Bali’s downfall. Delighted in mind he prayed to Govinda who had occupied a large rocky slab.

## \|\| 2.60.25 \|\|

*agnibiṃduruvāca \|*  
*oṃ namaḥ puṃḍarīkākṣa bāhyāṃtaḥ śaucadāyine \|*  
*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

Agnibindu said:

\[Agnibindu’s Prayer\]

25\. Oṃ, obeisance to you who accord external and internal purity, O lotus-eyed one. You are the thousand-headed, thousandeyed and thousand-footed Puruṣa.

## \|\| 2.60.26 \|\|

*namāmi te padadvaṃdvaṃ sarvadvaṃdvanivārakam \|*  
*nirdvaṃdvayā dhiyā viṣṇo jiṣṇvādi suravaṃdita \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. With an unfettered intellect, I bow down to the pair of your feet that dispel all Dvandvas (the three types of distresses inimical to human life), O Viṣṇu who are saluted by Jiṣṇu (Indra) and other Suras.

## \|\| 2.60.27 \|\|

*yaṃ stotuṃ nādhigacchaṃti vāco vācaspaterapi \|*  
*tamīṣṭe ka iha stotuṃ bhaktiratra balīyasī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Who is competent to eulogize him wherefor even the words of Vācaspati (Preceptor of Devas) do not get a chance? (But) devotion is all-powerful here (Hence I do pray).

## \|\| 2.60.28 \|\|

*api yo bhagavānīśo manaḥprācāmagocaraḥ \|*  
*samādṛśairalpadhībhiḥ kathaṃ stutyo vacaḥ paraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. (You are) that Supreme Lord and Master, who is beyond the ken of mind and words. How can he who is beyond words be adequately prayed to by people of paltry intellect like me?

## \|\| 2.60.29 \|\|

*yaṃ vāco na viśaṃtīśaṃ manatīha mano na yam \|*  
*mano girāmatītaṃ taṃ kaḥ stotuṃ śaktimānbhavet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Who can be powerful enough to eulogize him who is beyond mind and words, the Lord whom words cannot penetrate and whom mind cannot worship with comprehension.

## \|\| 2.60.30 \|\|

*yasya niḥśvasitaṃ vedāḥ sa ṣaḍaṃgapadakramāḥ \|*  
*tasya devasya mahimā mahānkairavagamyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. By whom is the supreme excellence of that Lord understood, whose breath is the collection of the Vedas along with the six Aṅgas (ancillaries) recited in Pada and Krama Pāṭhas.

## \|\| 2.60.31 \|\|

*ataṃdritamanobuddhīṃdriyā yaṃ sanakādayaḥ \|*  
*dhyāyaṃtopi hṛdākāśe na viṃdaṃti yathārthataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Sanaka and others possess minds, intellects and senses without the least lethargy and they meditate upon him. Yet they do not get him exactly in the Hṛdākāśa (ethereal space of the heart).

## \|\| 2.60.32 \|\|

*nāradādyairmunivarairābāla brahmacāribhiḥ \|*  
*gīyamānacaritropi na samyagyodhigamyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. His acts are being sung about by Nārada and other excellent sages who observe celibacy from childhood. Yet he is not perfectly understood.

## \|\| 2.60.33 \|\|

*taṃsūkṣmarūpamajamavyayamekamādyaṃ bahmādyagocaramajeyamanaṃtaśaktim \|*  
*nityaṃ nirāmayamamūrtamaciṃtyamūrtiṃ kastvāṃ carācara carācarabhinna vetti \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O Lord who are identical with the mobile and immobile beings due to Māyā but are really different from them, none understands you. You are subtle in form, unborn, immutable, single, the primordial one, imperceptible to Brahmā and others, invincible, of infinite powers, perpetual, free from ailments, unembodied and of imponderable form.

## \|\| 2.60.34-35 \|\|

*ekaikameva tava nāmaharenmurāre janmārjitāghamaghināṃ ca mahāpadāḍhyam \|*  
*dadyātphalaṃ ca mahitaṃ mahato makhasya japtaṃ mukuṃdamadhusūdanamādhaveti \|\| 34 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇeti narakārṇava tāraṇeti dāmodareti madhuheti caturbhujeti \|*  
*viśvaṃbhareti virajeti janārdaneti kvāstīha janma japatāṃ kva kṛtāṃtabhītiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Everyone of your names, O Murāri, shall dispel the sins of sinners accumulated in the course of many births and likely to bring in great prosperity. These names shall accord the honoured benefit of great Yajñas, when uttered repeatedly—the names Mukunda, Madhusūdana, Mādhava, Nārāyaṇa, Narakārṇavatāraṇa, Dāmodara, Madhuhā, Caturbhuja, Viśvaṃbhara, Virajas and Janārdana. Where is the fear from the god of Death unto those who repeat the names? They will not be reborn.

## \|\| 2.60.36 \|\|

*ye tvāṃ trivikrama sadā hṛdi śīlayaṃti kādaṃbinī rucira rociṣamaṃbujākṣam \|*  
*saudāmanīvilasitāṃśukavītamūrte tepi spṛśaṃti tava kāṃtimaciṃtyarūpām \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Lord Trivikrama whose form is clothed in silk cloth that shines splendidly like the lightning streak, those who always meditate upon you in their hearts, you, the lotus-eyed one having the sparkling splendour of the cluster of clouds, came into contact with your splendour of imponderable form.

## \|\| 2.60.37 \|\|

*śrīvatsalāṃchanaharecyutakaiṭabhāre goviṃdatārkṣya rathakeśavacakrapāṇe \|*  
*lakṣmīpate danujasūdana śārṅgapāṇe tvadbhaktibhāji na bhayaṃkvacidasti puṃsi \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Hari having a curl of hair named Śrīvatsa on your breast, O Acyuta, O slayer of Kaiṭabha, O Govinda having Garuḍa as your vehicle, O Keśava having the discus in your hand, O consort of Lakṣmī, O slayer of Danujas (demons) having the Śārṅga bow in your hand, there is no fear for a man endowed with devotion unto you.

## \|\| 2.60.38 \|\|

*yairarcitosi bhagavaṃstulasīprasūnairdūrīkṛtaiṇamadasaurabhadivyagaṃdhaiḥ \|*  
*tānarcayaṃti divi devagaṇāḥsamastā maṃdāradāmabhiralaṃ vimalasvabhāvān \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. With the garlands of the flowers of the celestial tree Mandāra, the entire hosts of Devas assiduously adore those persons of character and conduct free from impurities, by whom, O Lord, you have been worshipped with Tulasī flowers having divine fragrance that dispels the fragrance of musk.

## \|\| 2.60.39 \|\|

*yadvāci nāma tava kāmadamabjanetra yacchrotrayostava kathā madhurākṣarāṇi \|*  
*yaccittabhittilikhitaṃ bhavatosti rūpaṃ nīrūpabhūpapadavī nahi tairdurāpā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Even the status of kings is not difficult to obtain for those people, O lotus-eyed one with no form in reality, in whose speech rests your name that bestows all cherished desires, in whose ears reverberate the sweet words of your stories and in the wall of whose minds is indelibly engraved your form.

## \|\| 2.60.40 \|\|

*ye tvāṃ bhajaṃti satataṃ bhuviśeṣaśāyiṃstāñchrīpate pitṛpatīṃdra kuberamukhyāḥ \|*  
*vṛṃdārakā divi sadaiva sabhājayaṃti svargāpavargasukhasaṃtatidānadakṣa \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Vṛndārakas (Devas), the chiefs among whom are Yama, Indra and Kubera, always venerate in heaven those who adore you always, O Śrīpati who rest on the couch of the serpent Śeṣa and are efficient in granting a series of pleasures of heaven and salvation.

## \|\| 2.60.41 \|\|

*ye tvāṃ stuvaṃti satataṃ divitānstuvaṃti siddhāpsaromaragaṇā lasadabjapāṇe \|*  
*viśrāṇayatyakhilasiddhidakovinā tvāṃ nirvāṇacārukamalāṃ kamalāyatākṣa \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Lord with the lotus shining in the hand, groups of Siddhas, Devas and celestial damsels eulogize in heaven those people who always eulogize you. O Lord, O bestower of all supernatural powers, who have eyes as large as a lotus, excepting you who grants the charming glory of ultimate salvation?

## \|\| 2.60.42 \|\|

*tvaṃ haṃsi pāsi sṛjasi kṣaṇataḥ svalīlā līlāvapurdhara viriṃcinatāṃghriyugma \|*  
*viśvaṃ tvameva paraviśvapatistvameva viśvasyabījamasi tatpraṇatosmi nityam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Lord who adopt physical forms sportingly, O Lord the pair of whose feet are bowed to by Brahmā, you destroy, you protect and you create all as your sporting activities instantaneously. O supreme one, you alone are the entire universe; you alone are the Lord of the universe; you are the seed of the universe. Hence I always bow unto you.

## \|\| 2.60.43 \|\|

*stotā tvameva danujeṃdraripo stutistvaṃ stutyastvameva sakalaṃ hi bhavānihaikaḥ \|*  
*tvatto na kiṃcidapi bhinnamavaimi viṣṇo tṛṣṇāṃ sadā kṛṇuhi me bhavajāṃbhavāre \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O foe of the Lord of Danujas (Demons), you are the eulogizer, you are the eulogy and you alone are the object worthy of being eulogized. I do not think that anything is different from you, O Viṣṇu. O Lord inimical to the mundane existence, dispel my eagerness (thirst) for worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.60.44 \|\|

*iti stutvā hṛṣīkeśamagnibiṃdurmahātapāḥ \|*  
*tasthau tūṣṇīṃ tato viṣṇuruvāca varado munim \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After eulogizing Hṛṣīkeśa thus, Agnibindu of great austerities remained silent. Then Viṣṇu, the bestower of boons, spoke to the sage:

## \|\| 2.60.45 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*agnibiṃdo mahāprājña mahatā tapasāṃnidhe \|*  
*varaṃ varaya suprītastavādeyaṃ na kiṃcana \|\| 45 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

45\. O highly intelligent Agnibindu, O storehouse of great austerities, I am highly pleased. Choose your boon. There is nothing which cannot be given to you.

## \|\| 2.60.46 \|\|

*agnibiṃduruvāca \|*  
*yadi prītosi bhagavanvaikuṃṭheśa jagatpate \|*  
*kamalākāṃta taddehi yadiha prārthayāmyaham \|\| 46 \|\|*

Agnibindu said:

46\. If you are pleased, O Lord, O Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, O Lord of the universe, O consort of Lakṣmī, grant me what I am requesting for.

## \|\| 2.60.47 \|\|

*kṛtānujñotha hariṇā bhrūbhaṃgena sa tāpasaḥ \|*  
*kṛtapraṇāmo hṛṣṭātmā varayāmāsa keśavam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Being permitted by Hari with a gesture of his eyebrows that sage became highly delighted. After bowing down he chose the boon from Keśava.

## \|\| 2.60.48 \|\|

*bhagavansarvagopīha tiṣṭha paṃcanade hrade \|*  
*hitāya sarva jaṃtūnāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. “For the sake of the welfare of all creatures, particularly of those who are desirous of liberation, stay here in the whirlpool of Pañcanada, O Lord, although you are omnipresent.

## \|\| 2.60.49 \|\|

*lakṣmīśe na varo mahyameṣa deyo'vicārataḥ \|*  
*nānyaṃ varaṃ samīhehaṃ bhaktiṃ ca tvapadāṃbuje \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. This boon should be unhesitatingly granted to me by the Lord of Lakṣmī, so also (grant me) devotion unto your lotus-like feet. I do not desire any other boon.”

## \|\| 2.60.50 \|\|

*iti śrutvā varaṃ tasyāgnibiṃdormadhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*prītaḥ paropakārārthaṃ tathetyāhābdhijāpatiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On hearing thus about the boon of Agnibindu, the Slayer of Madhu became pleased. For the sake of helping others, the Consort of the Daughter of the Ocean (i.e. of Lakṣmī) said, “So be it.”

## \|\| 2.60.51 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*agnibiṃdo muniśreṣṭha sthāsyāmyahamiha dhruvam \|*  
*kāśībhaktimatāṃ puṃsāṃ muktimārgaṃ samādiśan \|\| 51 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

51\. Certainly I shall stay here, directing the path of salvation unto persons having devotion to Kāśī, O Agnibindu who are the most excellent one among sages.

## \|\| 2.60.52 \|\|

*mune punaḥ prasannosmi varaṃ brūhi dadāmi te \|*  
*atīva mama bhaktosi bhaktistestu dṛḍhā mayi \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O sage, I am highly delighted. Mention a boon further I shall grant you. You are already a great devotee of mine. May your devotion to me be firmer.

## \|\| 2.60.53 \|\|

*ādāveva hi tiṣṭhāsurahamatra taponidhe \|*  
*tatastvayā samabhyarthi sthāsyāmyatra sadaiva hi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O storehouse of austerities, even at the outset I have been desirous of staying here. Then it has been requested for by you. I shall stay here forever.

## \|\| 2.60.54 \|\|

*prāpya kāśīṃ sudurmedhāḥ kastyajejjñānavānyadi \|*  
*anarghyaṃ prāpya māṇikyaṃ hitvā kācaṃ ka īhate \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If anyone has any sense, who is dull-headed enough to leave Kāśī after reaching it? After acquiring a ruby of inestimable value who will desire a piece of glass abandoning that (ruby)?

## \|\| 2.60.55 \|\|

*alpīyasā śrameṇeha vapuṣo vyayamātrataḥ \|*  
*avaśyaṃ gatvarasyāśu yathāmuktistathā kva hi \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. With a very little effort, merely by casting off the body here, the body that has to go in any case, one gets salvation. Where else can one have it thus?

## \|\| 2.60.56 \|\|

*vinimayya jarājīrṇaṃ dehaṃ pārthivamatra vai \|*  
*prājñāḥ kimu na gṛhṇīyuramṛtaṃ nairjaraṃ vapuḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Why won’t a sensible man take up the immortal divine physical form by exchanging the earthly body already worn out by old age?

## \|\| 2.60.57 \|\|

*na tapobhirna vā dānairna yajñairbahudakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*anyatra labhyate mokṣo yathā kāśyāṃ tanu vyayāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Neither by austerities, nor by monetary gifts nor through Yajñas in which much is given away as gifts, is salvation obtained in the manner it is obtained at Kāśī through giving up the body.

## \|\| 2.60.58 \|\|

*api yogaṃ hi yuṃjānā yogino yatamānasāḥ \|*  
*naikenajanmanā muktāḥ kāśyāṃ muktā vapurvyayāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Even those who practise Yogic exercises, even the Yogins of well-restrained minds are not liberated in a single birth. But people are liberated through the loss of the body (i.e. death) in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.60.59 \|\|

*idameva mahādānamidameva mahattapaḥ \|*  
*idameva vrataṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yatkāśyāṃ mriyate tanuḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The fact that the body courts death in Kāśī is itself a great Dāna; it is the great austerity, and it is the most excellent Vrata.

## \|\| 2.60.60 \|\|

*sa eva vidvāñjagati sa eva vijiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*sa eva puṇyavāndhanyo labdhvā kāśīṃ na yastyajet \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He who does not leave Kāśī after reaching Kāśī alone is the most sensible scholar in the world; he alone is meritorious and blessed.

## \|\| 2.60.61 \|\|

*tāvatsthāsyāmyahaṃ cātra yāvatkāśī mune tviha \|*  
*pralayepi na nāśosyāḥ śivaśūlāgra susthiteḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O sage, I shall stay here as long as Kāśī exists. Being propped up on the tip of the trident of Siva, even at the time of Pralaya (final annihilation) it has no destruction.

## \|\| 2.60.62-65 \|\|

*ityākarṇya giraṃ viṣṇoragnibiṃdurmahāmuniḥ \|*  
*prahṛṣṭaromā provāca punaranyaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe \|\| 62 \|\|*

*māpate mama nāmnātra tīrthe paṃcanade śubhe \|*  
*abhaktebhyopi bhaktebhyaḥ sthito muktiṃ sadādiśa \|\| 63 \|\|*

*yetra paṃcanade snātvā gatvā deśāṃtareṣvapi \|*  
*narā paṃcatvamāpannā muktiṃ tebhyopi vai diśa \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yetu paṃcanade snātvā tvāṃ bhajiṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*calācalāpi dvairūpā mā tyākṣīcchrīśca tānnarān \|\| 65 \|\|*

62-65. On hearing these words of Viṣṇu, the great sage Agnibindu said with hairs standing up due to delight: “I shall choose another boon. O Consort of Lakṣmī, stay here in the auspicious Tīrtha of Pañcanada adopting my name and grant salvation to devotees as well as to non-devotees. Grant salvation unto those people also who take their holy ablution here in Pañcanada but go to other lands and die there. Although she (Lakṣmī) has the twin forms of being steady and unsteady, let not Śrī forsake those men who adore you after taking the holy bath in Pañcanaḍa.”

## \|\| 2.60.66 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*evamastvagnibiṃdotra bhavatā yadvṛtaṃmune \|*  
*tvannāmno'rdhena me nāma mayā saha bhaviṣyati \|\| 66 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

66\. O Agnibindu, O sage, let what has been sought by you be so. My name shall occur along with half of your name and also of Mā (Lakṣmī) (Hence Bindu-Mā-dhava).

## \|\| 2.60.67 \|\|

*biṃdumādhava ityākhyā mama trailokyaviśrutā \|*  
*kāśyāṃ bhaviṣyati mune mahāpāpaugha ghātinī \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. My name Bindumādhava shall be well-known in all the three worlds. O sage, in Kāśī it will be (considered) as one that destroys groups of great sins.

## \|\| 2.60.68 \|\|

*ye māmatra narāḥ puṇyāḥ puṇye paṃcanade hrade \|*  
*sadā saparyayiṣyaṃti teṣāṃ saṃsārabhīḥ kutaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Where is the fear from worldly existence to those who will always adore me here in the meritorious whirlpool of Pañcanaḍa? They are blessed men.

## \|\| 2.60.69 \|\|

*vasusvarūpiṇī lakṣmīrlakṣmīrnirvāṇasaṃjñikā \|*  
*tatpārśvagā sadā yeṣāṃ hṛdi paṃcanade hyaham \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. If people keep me in their hearts as stationed in Pañcanada always, Lakṣmī in the form of Vasu (Wealth) and Lakṣmī named after salvation (i.e. Mokṣalakṣmī) shall always be at their sides.

## \|\| 2.60.70 \|\|

*yairna paṃcanadaṃ prāpya vasubhiḥ prīṇitā dvijāḥ \|*  
*āśulabhyavipattīnāṃ teṣāṃ tadvasuroditi \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. After reaching Pañcanada, if Brāhmaṇas are not propitiated with monetary gifts, they will be likely to be overwhelmed by disaster quickly and their riches will weep (i.e. will be lost).

## \|\| 2.60.71 \|\|

*ta eva dhanyā lokesminkṛtakṛtyāsta eva hi \|*  
*prāpya yairmama sāṃnidhyaṃ vasavo mama sātkṛtāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Only they are blessed in this world; they alone are to be considered as having fulfilled their tasks if after reaching my vicinity all the riches are dedicated to me.

## \|\| 2.60.72 \|\|

*biṃdutīrthamidaṃ nāma tava nāmnā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*agnibiṃdo muniśreṣṭha sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O Agnibindu who are the most excellent one among the sages, this Tīrtha shall be known as Bindu Tīrtha after your name. It will be destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 2.60.73 \|\|

*kārtike biṃdutīrthe yo brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*snāsyatyanudite bhānau bhānujāttasya bhīḥ kutaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. If in the month of Kārttika, a devotee strictly abides by the vow of celibacy and takes the holy ablution in the Bindu Tīrtha before sunrise, why should he be afraid of Yama, the son of Sun-god?

## \|\| 2.60.74 \|\|

*api pāpasahasrāṇi kṛtvā mohena mānavaḥ \|*  
*ūrje dharmanade snāto niṣpāpo jāyate kṣaṇāt \|\| \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Even after, out of delusion, committing thousands of sins, if a man takes his holy bath in Dharmanada in the month of Kārttika, he will become free from sins instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.60.75 \|\|

*yāvatsvasthosti dehoyaṃ yāvanneṃdriyaviklavaḥ \|*  
*tāvadvratāni kurvīta yato dehaphalaṃ vratam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. As long as the body is healthy, as long as there is no weakness in the sense-organs, a devotee should observe the holy vows because a vow has the body as its fruit.

## \|\| 2.60.76 \|\|

*ekabhaktena naktena tathaivāyācitena ca \|*  
*upavāsena dehoyaṃ saṃśodhyo śucibhājanam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. This body, the receptacle of uncleanliness, should be purified by means of fasting or taking a single meal or living on what is obtained without begging.

## \|\| 2.60.77 \|\|

*kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇādīni kartavyāni prayatnataḥ \|*  
*aśuciḥ śucitāmeti kāyo yadvratadhāraṇāt \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Kṛcchracāndrāyaṇa and other Vratas should be observed assiduously since this impure body becomes pure by the observance of vows.

## \|\| 2.60.78 \|\|

*vrataiḥ saṃśodhite dehe dharmo vasati niścalaḥ \|*  
*arthakāmau sanirvāṇau tatra yatra vṛṣa sthitiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Dharma stays firm in the body purified by Vratas. Artha and Kama along with Mokṣa stay there where Dharma too stays.

## \|\| 2.60.79 \|\|

*tasmādvratāni satataṃ caritavyāni mānavaiḥ \|*  
*dharmasānnidhya kartṛṇi caturvargaphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Hence those Vratas that contribute to the attainment of Dharma should be observed by men who are desirous of the gain of the fourfold aim of life.

## \|\| 2.60.80 \|\|

*sadā kartuṃ na śaknoti vratāni yadi mānavaḥ \|*  
*cāturmāsyamanuprāpya tadā kuryātprayatnataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. If a man is unable to observe Vratas always, he should at least perform them during the Cāturmāsya (four months of rainy season from Āṣāḍha to Kārttika).

## \|\| 2.60.81-82 \|\|

*bhūśayyā brahmacaryaṃ ca kiṃcidbhakṣyaniṣedhanam \|*  
*ekabhaktādi niyamo nityadānaṃ svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*purāṇaśravaṇaṃ caiva tadarthācaraṇaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*akhaṃḍadīpodbodhaśca mahāpūjeṣṭadaivate \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. Some of the Vratas are: Lying down on bare ground, celibacy, abstaining from eating certain foodstuffs, the vow of taking single meal etc., some Dāna everyday in accordance with one’s capacity, listening to the Purāṇas, acting in accordance with the themes therein, maintaining continuous lights of lamps (before deities), keeping awake and the great worship of the deity of one’s choice.

## \|\| 2.60.83 \|\|

*prabhūtāṃkurabījāḍhye deśe cāpi gatāgatam \|*  
*yatnena varjayeddhīmānmahādharmavivṛddhaye \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. For the purpose of increasing piety, a sensible man should assiduously avoid going to and fro in places with seeds and seedlings in abundance.

## \|\| 2.60.84 \|\|

*asaṃbhāṣyā na saṃbhāṣyāścāturmāsya vratasthitaiḥ \|*  
*maunaṃ cāpi sadā kāryaṃ tathyaṃ vaktavyameva vā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Persons with whom conversation is prohibited should not be talked to by those who maintain Cāturmāsya Vratas. They will maintain silence always or should speak only the truth.

## \|\| 2.60.85 \|\|

*niṣpāvāṃśca masūrāṃśca kodravānvarjayedvratī \|*  
*sadā śucibhirāstheyaṃ spraṣṭavyo nāvratī janaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. An observer of Vratas should avoid grains and lentils like Niṣpāva, Masūra and Kodrava. One should always stay among clean people. A non-observer of vows should not be touched.

## \|\| 2.60.86 \|\|

*daṃtakeśāṃbarādīni nityaṃ śodhyāni yatnataḥ \|*  
*aniṣṭaciṃtā no kāryā vratinā hṛdyapi kvacit \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Teeth, hairs, clothes etc. should be scrupulously washed everyday. No evil thought should be entertained in the heart by an observer of vows.

## \|\| 2.60.87 \|\|

*dvādaśasvapi māseṣu vratino yatphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*cāturmāsyavratabhṛtāṃ tatphalaṃ syādakhaṃḍitam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Those who scrupulously maintain the Cāturmāsya Vratas are entitled to complete benefit as an observer of vows in all the twelve months.

## \|\| 2.60.88 \|\|

*caturṣvapi ca māseṣu na sāmarthyaṃ vrate yadi \|*  
*tadorje vratinā bhāvyamapyabdaphalamicchatā \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. If one lacks physical power for the observance of Vratas even in the stipulated four months, he should maintain the Vratas at least in the month of Kārttika, should he wish for the benefit of the year-long Vratas.

## \|\| 2.60.89 \|\|

*avrataḥ kārtiko yeṣāṃ gato mūḍhadhiyāmiha \|*  
*teṣāṃ puṇyasya leśopi na bhavetsūkarātmanām \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. If a person was silly enough to pass the month of Kārttika without the observances of Vratas, he is a pig-souled one. Such persons will not deserve even the least of merits.

## \|\| 2.60.90 \|\|

*kṛcchraṃ vā cātikṛcchraṃ vā prājāpatyamathāpi vā \|*  
*saṃprāpte kārtike māsi kuryācchaktyāti puṇyavān \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. At the advent of the month of Kārttika a highly meritorious devotee should observe Kṛcchra, Atikṛcchra or Prājāpatya.

## \|\| 2.60.91 \|\|

*ekāṃtaraṃ vrataṃ kuryāttrirātra vratameva vā \|*  
*paṃcarātraṃ saptarātraṃ saṃprāpte kārtike vratī \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. When the month of Kārttika has arrived one will observe Vratas like Fasts (e.g.), Ekāntaravrata (fasts on alternate days), Trirātra Vrata (meal once in three days), Pañcarātra (meal once in five days) or Saptarātra (meal once in seven days).

## \|\| 2.60.92 \|\|

*pakṣavrataṃ vā kurvīta māsopoṣaṇameva vā \|*  
*norjo vaṃdhyo vidhātavyo vratinā kenacitkvacit \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A devotee may observe the Vrata once in a fortnight or once in the month. No observer of Vratas shall make the month of Kārttika barren (vowless) anywhere.

## \|\| 2.60.93 \|\|

*śākāhāraṃ payohāraṃ phalāhāramathāpi vā \|*  
*caredyavānnāhāraṃ vā saṃprāpte kārtike vratī \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. In the month of Kārttika, an observer of Vratas should stick to the diet of vegetables, milk, fruits or cooked barley grains.

## \|\| 2.60.94 \|\|

*nityanaimittikaṃ snānaṃ kuryādūrje vratī naraḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryaṃ caredūrje mahāvrataphalārthavān \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. A man of Vratas should perform Nitya Snāna (bathing everyday) or Naimittika Snāna (bath on ceremonious occasions). Seeking the benefit of the great Vrata the devotee should observe celibacy in the month of Kārttika.

## \|\| 2.60.95 \|\|

*bāhulaṃ brahmacaryeṇa yaḥ kṣipecchucimānasaḥ \|*  
*samastaṃ hāyanaṃ tena brahmacaryakṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. If a devotee of pure mind passes the dark half of the month while strictly observing celibacy, it will be on a par with the performance of Brahmacarya throughout the year.

## \|\| 2.60.96 \|\|

*yastu kārtikikaṃ māsamupavāsaiḥ samāpayet \|*  
*apyabdamapi teneha bhavetsamyagupoṣitam \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. If a devotee concludes the month of Kārttika with fasts, it is as good as though the whole year is spent by him in holy fasts.

## \|\| 2.60.97 \|\|

*śākāhārapayohārairūrjoṃ yairativāhitaḥ \|*  
*akhaṃḍitā śarattena tadāhāreṇa yāpitā \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. If a devotee passes the month of Kārttika sticking to the diet of vegetables and milk, it is as good as the whole Śarat (autumn) has been spent by him with that diet.

## \|\| 2.60.98 \|\|

*patrabhojī bhavedūrje kāṃsyaṃ tyājyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*yo vratī kāṃsyabhojī syānna tadvrataphalaṃ labhet \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. One shall take food only on leaves in the month of Kārttika. Bell-metal vessel should be scrupulously avoided. If a devotee takes food in bell-metal vessels, he shall not get the benefit of that Vrata.

## \|\| 2.60.99 \|\|

*kāṃsyasya niyame dadyātkāṃsyaṃ sarpiḥ prapūritam \|*  
*ūrje na bhakṣayetkṣaudramatikṣudragatipradam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. If one invariably (takes food) in a bell-metal vessel, he should make gift of a bell-metal vessel filled with ghee. During the month of Kārttika one should not take in honey which gives inferior birth.

## \|\| 2.60.100 \|\|

*madhutyāge ghṛtaṃ dadyātpāyasaṃ ca saśarkaram \|*  
*abhyaṃge'bhyavahāre ca tailamūrje vivarjayet \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. If one abandons honey one should make the gift of ghee or milk pudding with sugar. One should avoid oil in the month of Kārttika for application over the body or taking in as food.

## \|\| 2.60.101 \|\|

*bhūyātsa nārakī dehī tatrābhyaṃgādyatonagha \|*  
*tailatyāge tilāndadyāddroṇamātrānsa kāṃcanān \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. For, O sinless one, that embodied soul shall become a resident of hell on smearing himself with oil on that occasion. If one has eschewed oil, one should make a gift of gingelly seeds measuring a Droṇa supplemented with gold.

## \|\| 2.60.102 \|\|

*kārtike matsyabhojī yaḥ sa taimīṃ yonimṛcchati \|*  
*bāhule māṃsabhojī yaḥ sa kṛmiḥpūyaśoṇite \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. He who eats fish in the month of Kārttika is reborn in the species of whales. One who eats fish in the dark half of the month, becomes a worm in purulent blood.

## \|\| 2.60.103-104 \|\|

*māṃsāśinopi ye bhūpāstyajeyustepi kārtike \|*  
*matsyamāṃsāni saṃtyajya kārttike vratatatparaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*matsyamāṃsādanāddoṣādbahirbhavati niścitam \|*  
*niyame matsyamāṃsānāṃ dadyātkārtikike vratī \|*  
*kūśmāṃḍāni samāṣāṇi daśasvarṇayutānyapi \|\| 104 \|\|*

103-104. Kings who habitually eat meat should abstain from it in the month of Kārttika. One who is engaged in the observance of Vratas after eschewing fish and flesh shall become exonerated from the fault of eating fish and flesh certainly. If there is restraint in fish and flesh in the month of Kārttika, the observer of the Vrata shall make a gift of an ashgourd along with blackgram and ten gold pieces.

## \|\| 2.60.105 \|\|

*kārtike mīnabhojī yaḥ sośnātyamṛtamevahi \|*  
*sughaṃṭāṃ satilāṃ maunī sahiraṇyāṃ pradāpayet \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. He who takes food silently in the month of Kārttika really takes in nectar. An observer of the vow of silence shall make a gift of an excellent bell accompanied with gingelly seeds and gold.

## \|\| 2.60.106 \|\|

*kārtike lavaṇaṃ tyaktaṃ yena vratabhṛtā satā \|*  
*tyaktāḥ sarve rasāstena tattyāgī gāṃ pradāpayet \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. A virtuous man observing Vrata in Kārttika who eschews salt has actually abandoned all juices. That observer of Vrata should make gift of a cow.

## \|\| 2.60.107 \|\|

*bhūśayyāṃ kārtike kurvanna bhuvaṃ saṃspṛśedvratī \|*  
*paryaṃkaṃ bhūśayo dadyātsatūlaṃ sopadhānakam \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. One who observes the vow of lying down on bare ground will not touch the earth again (i.e. will not be born again). An observer of the vow of lying down on the earth shall make gift of a palanquin with cotton and pillows.

## \|\| 2.60.108 \|\|

*dīpaṃ yaḥ kārtike dadyādakhaṃḍaṃ ghṛtavartikam \|*  
*mohāṃdha tamasaṃ prāpya sa na gacchati durgatim \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. He who makes the gift of continuous unextinguished light with wicks soaked in ghee, never attains the disaster of being in the blinding darkness of delusion.

## \|\| 2.60.109 \|\|

*yaḥ kuryātkārtike māse rajanyāṃ dīpakaumudīm \|*  
*tāmisraṃ cāṃdhatāmisraṃ na sa paśyetkadācana \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. He who makes Dīpakaumudī (the splendour of moonlight through lamps) at night in the month of Kārttika shall never see the hells of Tāmisra and Andhatāmisra.

## \|\| 2.60.110 \|\|

*pāpāṃdhakārasaṃkruddhaḥ kārtike dīpadānataḥ \|*  
*krodhāṃdhakāritamukhaṃ bhāskariṃ sa na vīkṣate \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. One who is angry with the darkness of sins through the gifts of lamps in Kārttika, never sees the son of the Sun-god (i.e. Yama) with the face darkened due to anger.

## \|\| 2.60.111 \|\|

*sa uddyotamayaṃ paśyettrailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*prabodhayenmamāgre yo dīpaṃ sojvalavartikam \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. He who illuminates in front of me a lamp with dazzling wicks, shall see the three worlds including mobile and immobile beings flooded with light.

## \|\| 2.60.112 \|\|

*paṃcāmṛtānāṃ kalaśairūrje māṃ snāpayennaraḥ \|*  
*kṣīrābdhitaṭamāsādya vasetkalpaṃ sa puṇyavān \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. A man who bathes me with pots of Pañcāmṛta becomes very meritorious. He will stay there for the period of a Kalpa after reaching the shores of the Ocean of Milk.

## \|\| 2.60.113 \|\|

*pratikṣapaṃ kārtikike kurvañjyotsnāṃ pradīpajām \|*  
*mamāgre bhaktisaṃyukto garbhadhvāṃtaṃ na saṃviśet \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. He who makes moonlight arising from lamps on every night in the month of Kārttika in front of me, becomes endowed with devotion. He will never enter the dark area of a womb.

## \|\| 2.60.114 \|\|

*ājyavartikamūrje yo dīpaṃ megre prabodhayet \|*  
*buddhibhraṃśaṃ na cāpnoti mahāmṛtyubhaye sati \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. One who illuminates a light in front of me with the wick soaked in ghee in the month of Kārttika, never meets with slips of intellect even when there is the great fear of death.

## \|\| 2.60.115 \|\|

*kārtike māsi me yātrā yaiḥ kṛtā bhaktitatparaiḥ \|*  
*biṃdutīrthe kṛtasnānaisteṣāṃ muktirna dūrataḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Salvation is not very far off from those devotees who take their holy bath in the Bindu Tīrtha in the month of Kārttika and organize Yātrā (religious procession and congregational worship) unto me.

## \|\| 2.60.116-119 \|\|

*vratinaḥ kārtike māsi snātasya vidhivanmama \|*  
*dāmodaragṛhāṇārghyaṃ danujeṃdraniṣūdana \|\| 116 \|\|*

*snāne naimittike kṛṣṇa kārtike pāpaśoṣaṇe \|*  
*gṛhṇātvarghyaṃ mayā dattaṃ rādhayā sahito bhavān \|\| 117 \|\|*

*imau maṃtrau samuccārya yorghyaṃ mahyaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*suvarṇaratna puṣpāṃbu yujā śaṃkhena puṇyavān \|\| 118 \|\|*

*suvarṇapūrṇapṛthivī saṃkalpodakapūrvakam \|*  
*tena dattā bhavetsamyaksupātrāya suparvaṇi \|\| 119 \|\|*

116-119. The devotee repeats the following two Mantras: “O Dāmodara, O slayer of the king of Dānavas, accept my Arghya; I am observing the Vrata in the month of Kārttika, after taking the holy ablution.

O Kṛṣṇa, may Your Lordship accept in company with Rādhā, the Arghya, offered by me in the course of the Naimittika (periodical as per certain condition) Snāna (holy bath) in the month of Kārttika that dispels sins.” He who thus offers Arghya unto me through a conchshell with water flowing out over gold, jewels and flowers is a meritorious person. He should conceive it as the entire earth filled with gold when offering the Arghya water; it will be as though a befitting thing has been gifted by him to a deserving person on the occasion of a holy festival.

## \|\| 2.60.120-129 \|\|

*ekādaśīṃ samāsādya prabodhakaraṇīṃ mama \|*  
*biṃdutīrthakṛtasnāno rātrau jāgaraṇānvitaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*dīpānprobodhya bahuśo mamālaṃkṛtya śaktitaḥ \|*  
*tauryatrikavinodena purāṇaśravaṇādibhiḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

*mahāmahotsavaṃ kṛtvā yāvatpūrṇā tithirbhavet \|*  
*tatrānnadānaṃ bahuśaḥ kṛtvāmatprītaye naraḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

*mahāpātakayuktopi na viśetpramadodaram \|*  
*biṃdumādhavanāmānaṃ yo māmatra samarcayet \|\| 123 \|\|*

*biṃdutīrthakṛtasnāno nirvāṇaṃ sa hi viṃdati \|*  
*ādimādhavanāmāhaṃ pūjyaḥ satyayuge mune \|\| 124 \|\|*

*anaṃtamādhavo jñeyastretāyāṃ sarvasiddhidaḥ \|*  
*śrīdamādhavasaṃjñohaṃ dvāpare paramārthakṛt \|\| 125 \|\|*

*kalau kalimaladhvaṃsī jñeyohaṃ biṃdumādhavaḥ \|*  
*kalau kalmaṣasaṃpannā na māṃ viṃdaṃti mānavāḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

*mamaiva māyayā mūḍhā bhedavādaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*mama bhaktiṃ prakurvāṇā ye viśveśaṃ dviṣaṃti vai \|\| 127 \|\|*

*vidviṣo mama te jñeyāḥ piśācapadagāminaḥ \|*  
*paiśācīṃ yonimāpyāpi kālabhairavaśāsanāt \|\| 128 \|\|*

*triṃśadvarṣa sahasrāṇi uṣitvā duḥkhasāgare \|*  
*viśveśānugrahādeva tato mokṣamavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

120-124a. On Prabodhinī Ekādaśī day (the eleventh day in the bright half of the lunar month of Kārttika) a devotee should take his holy dip in the Bindu Tīrtha. He should keep awake the whole of the night. In accordance with his capacity he should light many lamps after adoring me. There should be sound of musical instruments in triple symphony as an entertainment. He should listen to Purāṇas etc. There shall be great festivities till the Tithi (lunar day) is complete. In order to propitiate me, he should make ample gifts of cooked food. Even though he might have committed great sins, he will not thereafter enter the womb of a woman.

He who takes his holy bath in the Bindu Tīrtha and worships me here in the name of Bindumādhava attains salvation.

124b-126a. O sage, in Satyayuga I should be worshipped with the name of Ādimādhava. In Tretā I should be known as Anantamādhava, the bestower of all Siddhis (supernatural powers). In Dvāpara I named Śrīmādhava bring about the fulfilment of the greatest aim. In Kali age I, Bindumādhava, should be known as the destroyer of the impurities of Kali.

126b-127a. In Kali age men burdened with sins do not attain me, being deluded by my Māyā alone. They are eagerly engrossed in arguing about the differences.

127b-129. Persons though performing many devotional rites aimed at me should be known as my enemies if they are inimical to Viśveśa. They attain the status of Piśācas (vampires). After being born as Piśācas, they will have to spend thirty thousand years in the ocean of misery at the bidding of Kālabhairava. Thereafter, by the blessings of Viśveśa alone they will attain salvation.

## \|\| 2.60.130 \|\|

*tasmāddveṣo na kartavyo viśveśe paramātmani \|*  
*viśveśa dveṣiṇāṃ puṃsāṃ prāyaścittaṃ yato nahi \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Hence hatred should not be entertained against Viśveśa, the Supreme Atman, because there is no expiatory rite unto those who hate Viśveśa.

## \|\| 2.60.131 \|\|

*manasāpi hi viśveśaṃ vidviṣaṃtīha ye'dhamāḥ \|*  
*adhyāsateṃdhatāmisraṃ mṛtāstenyatra saṃtatam \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Those base men who hate Viśveśa even mentally shall, after death, enter the hell Andhatāmisra forever.

## \|\| 2.60.132 \|\|

*śivaniṃdāparā ye ca ye pāśupataniṃdakāḥ \|*  
*vidviṣo mama te jñeyā patato narake'śucau \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Those who are engaged in censuring Śiva and those who censure the Pāśupata cult and devotees, should be known as my enemies. They fall into a dirty hell.

## \|\| 2.60.133 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśati koṭīṣu narakeṣu krameṇa hi \|*  
*kalpaṃ kalpaṃ vaseyuste ye viśveśvaraniṃdakāḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Those who hate and censure Viśveśvara shall successively rot in twenty-eight crores of hells spending a Kalpa in each.

## \|\| 2.60.134 \|\|

*viśveśānugrahaṃ prāpya munehamapi muktidaḥ \|*  
*madbhaktaistadviśeṣeṇa sevyo viśveśvaro'niśam \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. It is because I have attained the blessings of Viśveśa, O sage, that I too am a bestower of salvation. Hence Viśveśvara should always be resorted to, particularly by my devotees.

## \|\| 2.60.135 \|\|

*iyaṃ vārāṇasī jñeyā mune pāśupatasthalī \|*  
*tasmātpaśupatiḥ sevyaḥ kāśyāṃ niśreyasārthibhiḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. This Vārāṇasī should be known, O sage, as a Pāśupata Sthalī (holy spot pertaining to Śiva). Hence Paśupati (Śiva) should be resorted to in Kāśī by those who seek salvation.

## \|\| 2.60.136 \|\|

*atra paṃcanade tīrthe snāti viśveśvaraḥ svayam \|*  
*ūrje sadaiva sagaṇaḥ saskaṃdaḥ saparicchadaḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Here in this Pañcanada Tīrtha Viśveśvara himself always takes his holy ablution in the month of Kārttika along with his Gaṇas, attendants and Skanda.

## \|\| 2.60.137 \|\|

*brahmā savedaḥ samakho brahmāṇyādyāśca mātaraḥ \|*  
*saptābdhayaḥ sasaritaḥ snāṃtyūrje dhūtapāpake \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. Brahmā, the Vedas, Yajñas, Brahmāṇī and other mothers, the seven oceans, rivers—all these take their holy bath in Dhūtapāpā in the month of Kārttika.

## \|\| 2.60.138 \|\|

*sacetanā hi yāvaṃtastrailokye dehadhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*tāvaṃtaḥ snātumāyāṃti kārtike dhūtapāpake \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. The entire sentient beings and embodied ones in all the three worlds come to Dhūtapāpakā for taking their holy dip in the month of Kārttika.

## \|\| 2.60.139 \|\|

*yairna paṃcanade snātaṃ prāpya kārtikikaṃ śubham \|*  
*jalabududavatteṣāṃ vṛthājanma śarīriṇām \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Those embodied ones who have not taken their holy dip in Pañcanada in the auspicious month of Kārttika waste their lives as futile as the bubbles in water.

## \|\| 2.60.140 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānanaṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyaṃ pāṃcanadaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*tatopi mama sānnidhyamagnibiṃdo mahāmune \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Anandakānana is meritorious. Pañcanada is more meritorious than that. My vicinity is more so, O great sage Agnibindu.

## \|\| 2.60.141 \|\|

*anenaivānumānena viddhi paṃcanadasya vai \|*  
*mahimānaṃ mahāprājña sarvatīrthottamottamam \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. In the same way, by implication know the greatness of Pañcanada which is the most excellent one among all excellent Tīrthas, O highly intelligent one.

## \|\| 2.60.142-143 \|\|

*śrutvāpi yaṃ mahāprājño mahāpāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*viṣṇormukhāditi śrutvā sognibiṃdurmahāmuniḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

*punaḥ praṇamya papraccha biṃdumādhavamacyutam \|\| 143 \|\|*

142-143. Merely by hearing about it, a highly intelligent one becomes liberated from great sins.

After hearing this directly from Viṣṇu’s mouth, Agnibindu, the great sage, bowed down and further asked Bindumādhava, Acyuta:

## \|\| 2.60.144-145 \|\|

*agnibiṃduruvāca \|*  
*bhagavañchrotumicchāmi biṃdumādhava tadvada \|*  
*katidhā tava rūpāṇi kāśyāṃ saṃti janārdana \|\| 144 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyāṇyapi kānīha tāni me kathayācyuta \|*  
*yāni saṃpūjyate bhaktāḥ prāpsyaṃti kṛtakṛtyatām \|\| 145 \|\|*

Agnibindu said:

144-145. O Lord, I wish to hear. O Bindumādhava, narrate it. O Janārdana, how many forms have you in Kāśī? What are those likely to occur in future? Tell me those by worshipping which your devotees will attain blessed contentment, O Acyuta.

## Chapter 61 - The Greatness of Vaiṣṇava Tīrthas

## \|\| 2.61.1-2 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*ṣaḍāsya mādhavākhyānaṃ śrutaṃ me pāpanāśanam \|*  
*mahimāpi śrutaḥ śreyānsamyakpaṃcanadasya vai \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yadagnibiṃdunā pṛcchi mādhavo daityasūdanaḥ \|*  
*tasyottaraṃ samākhyāhi yathākhyātaṃ madhudviṣā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Agastya enquired:

1-2. O Six-faced Lord, the narration of Mādhava that is destructive of sins has been heard by me. The excellent greatness of Pañcanada too has been heard perfectly. Tell me what the Slayer of Madhu replied when Agnibindu asked Mādhava, the destroyer of Daityas.

Skanda replied:

## \|\| 2.61.3 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇvagastya maharṣe tvaṃ kathyamānaṃ mayādhunā \|*  
*mādhavena yathācakṣi munaye cāgnibiṃdave \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Listen, O great sage Agastya, to what is being related by me now, as told by Mādhava to Sage Agnibindu.

## \|\| 2.61.4 \|\|

*biṃdumādhava uvāca \|*  
*ādau pādodake tīrthe viddhi māmādikeśavam \|*  
*agnibiṃdo mahāprājña bhaktānāṃ muktidāyakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Bindumādhava said:

4\. O highly intelligent Agnibindu, at the outset know me as Ādikeśava in the Pādodaka Tīrtha, the bestower of salvation on the devotees.

## \|\| 2.61.5 \|\|

*avimukte'mṛte kṣetre yercayaṃtyādikeśavam \|*  
*te'mṛtatvaṃ bhajaṃtyeva sarvaduḥkhavivarjitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Those who worship Ādikeśava in the immortal nectarine holy spot Avimukta do attain immortality free from all miseries.

## \|\| 2.61.6 \|\|

*saṃgameśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpyādikeśavaḥ \|*  
*darśanādaghahaṃ nṛṇāṃ bhuktiṃ muktiṃ diśetsadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After installing the great Saṅgameśa Liṅga that destroys sins of men by its very sight, Ādikeśava always accords worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 2.61.7 \|\|

*yāmyāṃ pādodakācchvetadvīpatīrthaṃ mahattaram \|*  
*tatrāhaṃ jñānado nṛṇāṃ jñānakeśavasaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. To the south of Pādokada there is the greater Tīrtha of Śveta Dvīpa. Under the name of Jñānakeśava I bestow knowledge on men there.

## \|\| 2.61.8 \|\|

*śvetadvīpe naraḥ snātvā jñānakeśavasannidhau \|*  
*na jñānādbhraśyate kvāpi jñānakeśavapūjanāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After taking the holy ablution in the presence of Jñānakeśava in Śveta Dvīpa, a man should worship Jñānakeśava. He never slips down from knowledge (into ignorance).

## \|\| 2.61.9 \|\|

*tārkṣyakeśavanāmāhaṃ tārkṣyatīrthe narottamaiḥ \|*  
*pūjanīyaḥ sadā bhaktyā tārkṣya vatte priyā mama \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. I am named Tārkṣyakeśava in the Tīrtha named Tārkṣyatīrtha. I should always be worshipped by excellent men with devotion. They become dear to me like Tārkṣya.

## \|\| 2.61.10 \|\|

*tatraiva nārade tīrthesmyahaṃ nāradakeśavaḥ \|*  
*brahmavidyopadeṣṭā ca tattīrthāpluta varṣmaṇām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There itself in the Nārada Tīrtha, I am Nāradakeśava, the instructor in Brahmavidyā unto those whose bodies are washed in that Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.61.11 \|\|

*prahlādatīrthaṃ tatraiva nāmnā prahlādakeśavaḥ \|*  
*bhaktaiḥ samarcanīyohaṃ mahābhakti samṛddhaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Prahlāda Tīrtha is also there itself. It should be adored under the name Prahlādakeśava by devotees for the increase of great devotion.

## \|\| 2.61.12 \|\|

*tīrtheṃ'barīṣe tatrāhaṃ nāmnaivādityakeśavaḥ \|*  
*pātakadhvāṃtanicayaṃ dhvaṃsayāmīkṣaṇādapi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There in the Aṃbarīṣa Tīrtha under the name Ādityakeśava I destroy the mass of the darkness of sins even due to mere visit.

## \|\| 2.61.13 \|\|

*dattātreyeśvarādyāmyāmahamādigadādharaḥ \|*  
*harāmi tatra bhaktānāṃ saṃsāragadasaṃcayam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. To the south of Dattātreyeśvara, I, Ādigadādhara, remove the series of illnesses of worldly existence of the devotees there.

## \|\| 2.61.14 \|\|

*tatraiva bhārgave tīrthe bhṛgukeśava nāmataḥ \|*  
*kāśīnivāsinaḥ puṃso bibharmi ca manorathaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. There itself, in the Bhārgava Tīrtha, under the name of Bhṛgukeśava I fulfil the cherished desires of the men residing in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.61.15 \|\|

*vāmanākhyemahātīrthe manaḥprārthitade śubhe \|*  
*pūjyohaṃ śubhamicchadbhirnāmnā vāmanakeśavaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the great Tīrtha named Vāmanatīrtha which is auspicious and which accords everything prayed for even mentally, I should be worshipped in the name of Vāmanakeśava by persons desirous of auspiciousness.

## \|\| 2.61.16 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇe tīrthe naranārāyaṇātmakam \|*  
*bhaktāḥ samarcya māṃ syurvai naranārāyaṇātmakāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the Naranārāyaṇa Tīrtha, the devotees worship me in the form of Naranārāyaṇa and then attain identity with Naranārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 2.61.17 \|\|

*tīrthe yajñavarāhākhye yajñavārāhasaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*naraiḥ samarcanīyohaṃ sarvayajñaphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the holy place named Yajñavārāhatīrtha I should be worshipped by men desirous of the fruits of Yajñas under the name Yajñavārāha.

## \|\| 2.61.18 \|\|

*vidāranarasiṃhohaṃ kāśīvighnavidāraṇaḥ \|*  
*tannāmni tīrthe saṃsevyastīrthopadravaśāṃtaye \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. I, named Vidāranarasiṃha, dispel the obstacles of Kāśī. I should be resorted to in the Tīrtha named so for quelling the torments of the Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.61.19 \|\|

*gopīgoviṃdatīrthe tu gopīgoviṃdasaṃjñakam \|*  
*samarcya māṃ naro bhaktyā mama māyāṃ na saṃspṛśet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By worshipping me named Gopīgovinda devoutly in the Gopīgovinda Tīrtha, a man can avoid the touch of my Māyā.

## \|\| 2.61.20 \|\|

*mune lakṣmīnṛsiṃhosmi tīrthe tannāmni pāvane \|*  
*diśāmi bhaktiyuktebhyaḥ sadānaiḥ śreyasīṃ śriyam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O sage, I am Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha in the holy Tīrtha named so. To those endowed with devotion, I always accord the glory of salvation.

## \|\| 2.61.21 \|\|

*śeṣamādhavanāmāhaṃ śeṣatīrthe'ghahāriṇi \|*  
*viśrāṇayāmyaśeṣāśca viśeṣānbhaktaciṃtitān \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In the Śeṣatīrtha that dispels sins, I am named Śeṣamādhava. I distribute among devotees all things desired by them.

## \|\| 2.61.22 \|\|

*śaṃkhamādhavatīrthe ca snātvā māṃ śaṃkhamādhavam \|*  
*śaṃkhodakena saṃsnāpya bhavecchaṃkhanidheḥ patiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After taking the holy dip in the Śaṅkhamādhava Tīrtha and bathing me, Śaṅkhamādhava, with water through a conchshell, a devotee shall become lord of the treasure Śaṅkhanidhi.

## \|\| 2.61.23 \|\|

*hayagrīve mahātīrthe māṃ hayagrīvakeśavam \|*  
*praṇamya prāpnuyānnūnaṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃpadam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the great Hayagrīvatīrtha a devotee bows down to me, Hayagrīvakeśava. Thereby he shall attain certainly the great region of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.61.24 \|\|

*bhīṣmakeśavanāmāhaṃ vṛddhakāleśapaścime \|*  
*upasargānhare bhīṣmānsevito bhaktiyuktitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. To the west of Vṛddhakāleśa, I am named Bhīṣmakeśava. When resorted to with Bhaktiyoga, I dispel terrible torments and calamities.

## \|\| 2.61.25 \|\|

*nirvāṇakeśavaścāhaṃ bhaktanirvāṇasūcakaḥ \|*  
*lolārkāduttarebhāge lolatvaṃ cetaso hare \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. To the north of Lolārka, I am Nirvāṇakeśava showing (the path of) salvation to devotees and I dispel the fickleness of mind.

## \|\| 2.61.26 \|\|

*vaṃdyastrilokasuṃdaryā yāmyāṃ yo māṃ samarcayet \|*  
*kāśyāṃ khyātaṃ tribhuvanakeśavaṃ na sa garbhabhāk \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. To the south of Trilokasundarī I am well-known in Kāśī as Tribhuvanakeśava. A venerable devotee who adores me thus does not enter any womb (attaining Mokṣa).

## \|\| 2.61.27 \|\|

*jñānavāpyāḥ purobhāge viddhi māṃ jñānamādhavam \|*  
*tatra māṃ bhaktitobhyarcya jñānaṃ prāpnoti śāśvatam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In front of Jñānavāpī know me as Jñānamādhava. By worshipping me there with devotion, one attains eternal wisdom.

## \|\| 2.61.28 \|\|

*śvetamādhavasaṃjñohaṃ viśālākṣyāḥ samīpataḥ \|*  
*śvetadvīpeśvaraṃ rūpaṃ kuryāṃ bhaktyā samarcitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. I am named Śvetamādhava in the vicinity of Viśālākṣī. Adored with devotion I make the devotee of the form of Śvetadvīpeśvara.

## \|\| 2.61.29 \|\|

*udagdaśāśvamedhānmāṃ prayāgākhyaṃ ca mādhavam \|*  
*prayāgatīrthe susnāto dṛṣṭvā pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. To the north of Daśāśvamedha, a devotee should worship me in the name of Prayāgamādhava after taking the holy bath in Prayāgatīrtha. By visiting me, he becomes free from all sins.

## \|\| 2.61.30 \|\|

*prayāgagamane puṃsāṃ yatphalaṃ tapasi śrutam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ syāddaśaguṇamatra snātvā mamāgrataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. By taking the holy dip here in front of me, one gets ten times the benefit reputed to result from going to Prayāga in the month of Māgha.

## \|\| 2.61.31 \|\|

*gaṃgāyamunayoḥ saṃge yatpuṇyaṃ snānakāriṇām \|*  
*kāśyāṃ matsannidhāvatra tatpuṇyaṃ syāddaśottaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Here in Kāśī in my presence the merit of those who take their holy dips is ten times the merit at the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

## \|\| 2.61.32 \|\|

*dānāni rāhugrasterke dadatāṃ yatphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*kurukṣetre hi tatkāśyāmatraiva syāddaśādhikam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Here in Kāśī one gets ten times more benefit than what is obtained in Kurukṣetra by those who make gifts when the Sun is swallowed by Rāhu (i.e. during solar eclipse).

## \|\| 2.61.33 \|\|

*gaṃgottaravahā yatra yamunā pūrvavāhinī \|*  
*tatsaṃbhedaṃ naraḥ prāpya mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Where Gaṅgā flows northwards and Yamunā eastwards, a man who goes to that confluence is rid of the sin of Brāhmaṇa’s slaughter.

## \|\| 2.61.34 \|\|

*vapanaṃ tatra kartavyaṃ piṃḍadānaṃ ca bhāvataḥ \|*  
*deyāni tatra dānāni mahāphalamabhīpsunā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There one should get the head shaved; balls of rice should be offered with emotional fervour and great Dānas should be made by one who wishes to get great benefit.

## \|\| 2.61.35 \|\|

*guṇāḥ prajāpatikṣetre ye sarve samudīritāḥ \|*  
*avimukte mahākṣetre'saṃkhyātāśca bhavaṃti hi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. All those good points which were enumerated in the Prajāpatikṣetra become innumerable in the great Avimuktakṣetra.

## \|\| 2.61.36 \|\|

*prayāgeśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ tatra tiṣṭhati kāmadam \|*  
*tatsānnidhyācca tattīrthaṃ kāmadaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The great Liṅga named Prayāgeśa stands there granting the desired object. Thanks to its nearness, the Tīrtha is glorified as Kāmada.

## \|\| 2.61.37 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ māghaḥ prayāge yairna snāto makarārkagaḥ \|*  
*aruṇodayamāsādya teṣāṃ niḥśreyasaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If people do not take their holy baths at dawn in the month of Māgha at Kāśī and in Prayāga when the Sun is in Capricorn, how can they attain salvation?

## \|\| 2.61.38 \|\|

*kāśyudbhave prayāge ye tapasi snāṃti saṃyatāḥ \|*  
*daśāśvamedhajanitaṃ phalaṃ teṣāṃ bhaveddhruvam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Those who have self-control and take holy baths in the month of Māgha, in the Prayāga at Kāśī certainly will attain the benefit arising from ten horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.61.39-40 \|\|

*prayāgamādhavaṃ bhaktyā prayāgeśaṃ ca kāmadam \|*  
*prayāge tapasi snātvā yercayaṃtyanvahaṃ sadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*dhanadhānyasutarddhīste labdhvā bhogānmanoramān \|*  
*bhuktveha paramānaṃdaṃ paraṃ mokṣamavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Those who devoutly worship everyday Prayāgamādhava and the wish-yielding Prayāgeśa after taking the holy dip in Prayāga in the month of Māgha, obtain wealth, grain, sons, and properties and enjoy pleasures delighting the mind in this world and attain the greatest bliss of salvation (in the next world).

## \|\| 2.61.41 \|\|

*māghe sarvāṇi tīrthāni prayāgamaviyāṃti hi \|*  
*prācyudīcī pratīcīto dakṣiṇādhastathordhvataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In the month of Māgha all the Tīrthas flow into Prayāga from east, north, west, south, nether region and heavenly region.

## \|\| 2.61.42 \|\|

*kāśīsthitāni tīrthāni mune yāṃti na kutracit \|*  
*yadi yāṃti tadā yāṃti tīrthatrayamanuttamam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O sage, the Tīrthas stationed in Kāśī do not go anywhere. If at all they go, they go to the three excellent Tīrthas.

## \|\| 2.61.43 \|\|

*āyāṃtyūrje paṃcanade prātaḥprātarmamāṃtikam \|*  
*mahāghaughapraśamane mahāśreyovidhāyini \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In the month of Kārttika everyday in the morning they come to me in the Pañcanada Tīrtha which subdues masses of great sins and produces welfare.

## \|\| 2.61.44 \|\|

*prāpya māghamaghāriṃ ca prayāgeśa samīpataḥ \|*  
*prātaḥprayāge saṃsnāṃti sarvatīrthāni māmanu \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In the month of Māgha that is inimical to sins, all the Tīrthas take their bath near Prayāgeśa after me.

## \|\| 2.61.45 \|\|

*samāsādya ca madhyāhnamabhiyāṃti ca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*saṃsnātuṃ sarvatīrthāni muktidāṃ maṇikarṇikām \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In the midday all the Tīrthas go for their bath everyday to Maṇikarṇikā that accords salvation.

## \|\| 2.61.46 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ rahasyaṃ paramametatte kathitaṃ mune \|*  
*yathā tīrthatrayīśreṣṭhā svasvakāle viśeṣataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O sage, this great secret in Kāśī has been narrated to you, how the three Tīrthas are superior especially at their own times.

## \|\| 2.61.47 \|\|

*anyadrahasyaṃ vakṣyāmi na vācyaṃ yatrakutracit \|*  
*abhakteṣu sadā gopyaṃ na gopyaṃ bhaktimajjane \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. I shall tell you another secret. It should not be divulged anywhere and everywhere. It should be strictly kept secret from non-devotees. It should not be concealed from people of devotion.

## \|\| 2.61.48 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ sarvāṇi tīrthāni ekaikāduttarottaram \|*  
*mahaināṃsi prahaṃtyeva prasahya nija tejasā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. All the Tīrthas in Kāśī are superior one to the other. Assailing with their splendour, they dispel great sins.

## \|\| 2.61.49 \|\|

*etadeva rahasyaṃ te vārāṇasyā udīryate \|*  
*utkṣipyaikāṃguliṃ tathyaṃ śreṣṭhaikā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Lifting up one single finger this secret of Vārāṇasī is being told to you that only Maṇikarṇikā is the most superior one.

## \|\| 2.61.50 \|\|

*garjaṃti sarvatīrthāni svasvadhiṣṇyagatānyaho \|*  
*kevalaṃ balamāsādya sumahanmāṇikarṇikam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Only after resorting to the great power pertaining to Maṇikarṇikā all Tīrthas, sticking to their respective abodes, roar.

## \|\| 2.61.51-52 \|\|

*pāpāni pāpināṃ hatvā mahāṃtyapi bahūnyapi \|*  
*kāśītīrthāni madhyāhne prāyaścittacikīrṣayā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*parvasvaparvasvapi vā nityaṃ niyamavaṃ tyaho \|*  
*nirmalāni bhavaṃtyeva vigāhya maṇikarṇikām \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. After dispelling many great sins of sinners, the Kāśī Tīrthas become desirous of expiation. Whether it is the day of specific astrological importance or otherwise, they observe certain regulations and submerge into Maṇikarṇikā at midday. They thus do become pure.

## \|\| 2.61.53 \|\|

*viśveśo viśvayā sārdhaṃ sadopamaṇikarṇikam \|*  
*madhyaṃdinaṃ samāsādya saṃsnāti prativāsaram \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Everyday at midday Viśveśa in the company of Viśvā takes his holy ablution near Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 2.61.54 \|\|

*vaikuṃṭhādapyahaṃ nityaṃ madhyāhne maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*vigāhe padmayā sārdhaṃ mudā paramayā mune \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. With great joy I reach Maṇikarṇikā travelling from Vaikuṇṭha everyday and take the holy plunge along with Padmā, O sage.

## \|\| 2.61.55 \|\|

*sakṛnmamākhyāṃ gṛṇatāṃ nirharanyadaghānyaham \|*  
*harināmasamāpannastadbalānmāṇikarṇikāt \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I am competent to remove the sins of those who utter even once my name; hence I have attained the title Hari. That is the power pertaining to Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 2.61.56 \|\|

*satyalokātpratidinaṃ haṃ sayānaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*mādhyāhnika vidhānāya samāyānmaṇikarṇikām \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Everyday Pitāmaha (Brahmā) comes to Maṇikarṇikā riding his vehicle, the Swan, from Satyaloka, for the performance of midday rituals.

## \|\| 2.61.57 \|\|

*iṃdrādyā lokapālāśca marīcyādyā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*mādhyāhnikīṃ kriyāṃ kartuṃ samīyurmaṇikarṇikām \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The Guardians of the Quarters beginning with Indra, the great sages beginning with Marīci come to Maṇikarṇikā for performing the midday rites.

## \|\| 2.61.58 \|\|

*śeṣavāsukimukhyāśca nāgā vai nāgalokataḥ \|*  
*samāyāṃtīha madhyāhne saṃsnātuṃ maṇikarṇikām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. From the world of serpents, the serpents, the chiefs of whom are Śeṣa and Vāsuki, come to Maṇikarṇikā at midday for taking their holy bath.

## \|\| 2.61.59 \|\|

*carācareṣu sarveṣu yāvaṃtaśca sacetanāḥ \|*  
*tāvaṃtaḥ snāṃti madhyāhne maṇikarṇī jalemale \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. All the sentient ones among all mobile and immobile beings do take their holy bath at midday in the waters of Maṇikarṇikā (which are) free from impurities.

## \|\| 2.61.60 \|\|

*ke māṇikarṇikeyānāṃ guṇānāṃ sugarīyasām \|*  
*śaktā varṇayituṃ viprā'saṃkhyeyānāṃ madādibhiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Which qualities among the weightiest (greatest) qualities of Maṇikarṇikā that cannot be enumerated by me and others, can possibly be described, O Brāhmaṇa?

## \|\| 2.61.61 \|\|

*cīrṇānyugrāṇyaraṇyeṣu taistapāṃsi tapodhanaiḥ \|*  
*yairiyaṃ hi samāsādi muktibhūrmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Those saints by whom this Maṇikarṇikā, the ground for salvation has been attained, have actually performed intense austerities in the forests.

## \|\| 2.61.62 \|\|

*viśrāṇitamahādānāsta eva narapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*carame vayasi prāptā yaireṣā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Those excellent men who successfully reached Maṇikarṇikā in their last years are definitely those by whom great gifts have been donated.

## \|\| 2.61.63 \|\|

*cīrṇasarvavratāste tu yathoktavidhinā dhruvam \|*  
*yaiḥ svatalpīkṛtā māṇikarṇikeyī sthalī mṛduḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Those by whom the soft ground of Maṇikarṇikā has been converted into their bed have definitely observed all Vratas exactly according to their respective injunctions.

## \|\| 2.61.64 \|\|

*ta eva dhanyā martyesminsarvakratuṣu dīkṣitāḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā puṇyārjitāṃ lakṣmīmaikṣiyairmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. They alone are blessed ones among mortal beings, they are (on a par with) those who have been initiated into all Kratus (sacrifices), if they have seen Maṇikarṇikā after spending their wealth acquired by meritorious means.

## \|\| 2.61.65 \|\|

*kṛtā nānāvidhā dharmā iṣṭāpūrtāstu tairnṛbhiḥ \|*  
*vārdhakaṃ samanuprāpya prāpi yairmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. If in their old age Maṇikarṇikā has been reached, then definitely many kinds of pious rites as well as Iṣṭāpūrtas, (must) have been performed by those men.

## \|\| 2.61.66 \|\|

*ratnāni sadukūlāni kāṃcanaṃ gajavājinaḥ \|*  
*deyāḥ prājñena yatnena sadopamaṇikarṇikam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Jewels, silk clothes, gold, elephants and horses should be assiduously gifted away near Maṇikarṇikā by a sensible and intelligent man.

## \|\| 2.61.67 \|\|

*puṇyenopārjitaṃ dravyamatyalpamapi yairnaraiḥ \|*  
*dattaṃ tadakṣayaṃ nityaṃ munedhimaṇikaṇiṃkam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. If money acquired through legitimate meritorious means, be it even so little, is given (as Dāna) at Maṇikarṇikā, O sage, it becomes everlasting unto those men.

## \|\| 2.61.68 \|\|

*kuryādyathoktamapyekaṃ prāṇāyāmaṃ narottamaḥ \|*  
*yastena vihito nūnaṃ ṣaḍaṃgo yoga uttamaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. If an excellent man performs a single Prāṇāyāma as laid down in the scriptures, it is as good as the excellent Yoga has been practised along with its six ancillaries.

## \|\| 2.61.69 \|\|

*japtvaikāmapi gāyatrīṃ saṃprāpya maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*labhedayutagāyatrījapanasya phalaṃ sphuṭam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. By reciting the Gāyatrī only once after reaching Maṇikarṇikā, one certainly attains the benefit of reciting the Gāyatrī ten thousand times.

## \|\| 2.61.70 \|\|

*ekāmapyāhutiṃ prājño dattvopamaṇikarṇikam \|*  
*yāvajjīvāgnihotrasya labhedavikalaṃ phalam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Offering a single Āhuti (oblation into sacrificial fire) near Maṇikarṇikā a sensible man derives undiminished benefit of the performance of Agnihotra throughout the life.

## \|\| 2.61.71 \|\|

*iti śrutvā harervākyamagnibiṃdurmahātapāḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya mahābhaktyā punaḥ papraccha mādhavam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. On hearing these words of Hari, Agnibindu of great penance, bowed down with great devotion and asked Mādhava further:

## \|\| 2.61.72 \|\|

*agnibiṃduruvāca \|*  
*viṣṇo kiyatparīmāṇā puṇyaiṣā maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*brūhi me puṃṅarīkākṣa natvattastattvavitparaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

Agnibindu said:

72\. O Viṣṇu, what is the extent of this meritorious Maṇikarṇikā? Tell me, O lotus-eyed one. No one else is more conversant with truth (in this matter) than you.

## \|\| 2.61.73 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*āgaṃgā keśavādā ca hariścaṃdrasya maṃḍapāt \|*  
*āmadhyāddevasaritaḥ svardvārānmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 73 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

73\. Maṇikarṇikā extends from Gaṅgākeśava to the Maṇḍapa (pavilion) of Hariścandra and from the middle of the divine river up to Svardvāra.

## \|\| 2.61.74 \|\|

*sthūlametatparīmāṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ca pravadāmi te \|*  
*hariścaṃdrasya tīrthāgre hariścaṃdravināyakaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. This one is the gross extent. I shall mention to you the subtle one. Hariścandravināyaka is in front of the Tīrtha of Hariścandra.

## \|\| 2.61.75-76 \|\|

*sīmāvināyakaścātra maṇikarṇī hradottare \|*  
*sīmāvināyakaṃ bhaktyā pūjayitvā narottamaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*modakaiḥ sopacāraiśca prāpnuyānmaṇikarṇikām \|*  
*hariścaṃdre mahātīrthe tarpayeyuḥ pitāmahān \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. Sīmāvināyaka (Vināyaka at the boundary) is to the north of the whirlpool of Maṇikarṇikā. After devoutly adoring Sīmāvināyaka by means of Modakas (sweetmeats) along with the requisite services, an excellent man should go to Maṇikarṇikā. Devotees should offer libations to the Manes in the great Hariścandra Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.61.77-82 \|\|

*śataṃ samāḥsu tṛptāḥ syuḥ prayacchaṃti ca vāṃcchitam \|*  
*hariścaṃdre mahātīrthe snātvā śraddhānvito naraḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*hariścaṃdreśvaraṃ natvā na satyātparihīyate \|*  
*tataḥ parvatatīrthaṃ ca parvateśvara saṃnidhau \|\| 78 \|\|*

*adhiṣṭhānaṃ mahāmerormahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*tatra snātvārcayitveśaṃ kiṃciddattvā svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*adhyāsya meruśikharaṃ divyānbhogānsamaśnute \|*  
*kaṃbalāśvataraṃ tīrthaṃ parvateśvara dakṣiṇe \|\| 80 \|\|*

*kaṃbalāśvatareśaṃ ca tattīrthātpaścime śubham \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe kṛtasnānastalliṃgaṃ yaḥ samarcayet \|\| 81 \|\|*

*api tasya kule jātā gītajñāḥ syuḥ śriyānvitāḥ \|*  
*cakrapuṣkariṇī tatra yonicakra nivāriṇī \|\| 82 \|\|*

77-82. The ancestors shall become propitiated for a hundred years. They will accord the desired benefit.

After taking the holy bath in the great Hariścandra Tīrtha, a man endowed with faith should bow down to Hariścandreśvara. He will never swerve from truth.

Beyond that, in the vicinity of Parvateśvara is the Parvatatīrtha which is the basis of Mahāmeru and is destructive of great sins.

After taking the holy bath there, adoring Īśa, gifting something in accordance with one’s capacity and occupying the peak of Meru, a devotee enjoys celestial pleasures.

Kambalāśvatara Tīrtha is to the south of Parvateśvara. The auspicious Liṅga named Kambalāśvatareśa is to the west of that Tīrtha. If a devotee takes his holy bath in that Tīrtha and adores that Liṅga, persons born in his family shall become persons conversant with music and equipped with glory. Cakrapuṣkariṇī there is conducive to the avoidance of Yonicakra (cycle of births).

## \|\| 2.61.83 \|\|

*saṃsāracakre gahane yatra snāto viśennanā \|*  
*cakrapuṣkariṇī tīrtha mamādhiṣṭhānamuttamam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Cakrapuṣkariṇī Tīrtha is my excellent resort. A man who takes his holy bath there does not enter the dense entangled cycle of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.61.84 \|\|

*samāḥ parārdhasaṃkhyātāstatra taptaṃ mahātapaḥ \|*  
*tatra pratyakṣatāṃ yāto mama viśveśvaraḥ paraḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Great penance was performed by me there for so many years extending to a Parārdha in number. Viśveśvara, the great Lord, then became visible to me.

## \|\| 2.61.85 \|\|

*tatra labdhaṃ mayaiśvaryamavināśi mahattaram \|*  
*cakrapuṣkariṇī caiva khyātābhūnmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. There, very great and indestructible power and prosperity was acquired by me. Cakrapuṣkariṇī became well-known as Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 2.61.86 \|\|

*dravarūpaṃ parityajya lalanārūpadhāriṇī \|*  
*pratyakṣarūpiṇī tatra mayaikṣi maṇikarṇikā \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Abandoning the liquid form there, Maṇikarṇikā appeared directly to me having assumed the form of a woman.

## \|\| 2.61.87-90 \|\|

*tasyā rūpaṃ pravakṣyāmi bhaktānāṃ śubhadaṃ param \|*  
*yadrūpadhyānataḥ puṃbhirāṣaṇmāsaṃ trisaṃdhyataḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*pratyakṣarūpiṇī devī dṛśyate maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*caturbhujā viśālākṣī sphuradbhālavilocanā \|\| 88 \|\|*

*paścimābhimukhī nityaṃ prabaddhakarasaṃpuṭā \|*  
*iṃdīvaravatīṃ mālāṃ dadhatī dakṣiṇe kare \|\| 89 \|\|*

*varodyate kare savye mātuluṃga phalaṃ śubham \|*  
*kumārīrūpiṇī nityaṃ nityaṃ dvādaśavārṣikī \|\| 90 \|\|*

87-90. I shall mention her physical form that bestows auspiciousness profusely on the devotees. If men meditate on that form thrice a day for six months, Maṇikarṇikā will appear as a visible goddess. She has four arms and large eyes. Her eye in the forehead sparkles. She faces the west always with palms joined together. She holds a garland of blue lotuses in her right hand. In the lifted left hand in the gesture of according boons, there is a splendid pomegranate fruit. She is in the form of a virgin always. Always twelve years old.

## \|\| 2.61.91 \|\|

*śuddhasphaṭikakāṃtiśca sunīla snigdhamūrddhajā \|*  
*jitapravālamāṇikya ramaṇīya radacchadā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Her lustre is like that of pure crystal. Her glossy hairs are dark blue in colour. Her beautiful lips have surpassed corals and rubies.

## \|\| 2.61.92 \|\|

*pratyagraketakīpuṣpalasaddhammilla mastakā \|*  
*sarvāṃga muktābharaṇā caṃdrakāṃtyaṃśukāvṛtā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A fresh Ketakī flower in full bloom adores the braided hairs on her head. Pearl necklaces and ornaments beautify her limbs. She is cīad in silk cloth having the lustre of the moon.

## \|\| 2.61.93 \|\|

*puṃḍarīkamayīṃ mālāṃ saśrīkāṃ bibhratī hṛdi \|*  
*dhyātavyānena rūpeṇa mumukṣubhiraharniśam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. She also wears a splendid garland of lotuses on her bosom. She should be meditated day and night in this form in the heart by those who are desirous of salvation.

## \|\| 2.61.94 \|\|

*nirvāṇalakṣmībhavanaṃ śrīmatīmaṇikarṇikā \|*  
*maṃtraṃ tasyāśca vakṣyāmi bhaktakalpadrumābhidham \|*  
*yasyāvartanataḥ siddhyedapi siddhyaṣṭakaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The glorious Maṇikarṇikā is the abode of Nirvāṇalakṣmī (‘Glory of Salvation’). I shall mention a Mantra named Bhakta-Kalpadruma (‘wish-yielding celestial tree unto devotees’) pertaining to her. If this is repeated, even the eight supernatural powers will be acquired by men.

## \|\| 2.61.95-96 \|\|

*vāgbhavamāyālakṣmīmadanapraṇavānvadetpūrvam \|*  
*bhāṃtyaṃ biṃdūpetaṃ maṇipadamatha karṇike sahṛtpraṇavapuṭaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*maṃtraḥsuradrumasamaḥ samastasukhasaṃtatiprado japyaḥ \|*  
*tithibhiḥ parimitavarṇaḥ paramapadaṃ diśati niśitadhiyām \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. First Mantra: “vāgbhavabīja—aiṃ, māyā-bīja is hrīṃ, lakṣmībīja—śrīṃ, madanabīja is klīṃ, praṇava—oṃ, bhāntyam—ma, hṛt-namaḥ. Hence the Mantra of fifteen syllables \[oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ oṃ maṇikarṇikāyai namaḥ om\]. This Mantra consisting of fifteen syllables is on par with the celestial tree. It accords all series of happiness. It should be repeated. To the persons of pure Sattva quality, it accords the highest region.

## \|\| 2.61.97 \|\|

*tārastāratṛtīyo biṃdvaṃtomaṇipadaṃ tataḥ karṇike \|*  
*praṇavātmipadaṃ kena ma iti manusaṃkhyavarṇamanuḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Second Mantra is om maṃ maṇikarṇike praṇavātmike namaḥ. It has fourteen syllables.

## \|\| 2.61.98 \|\|

*ayaṃ maṃtro'niśaṃ japyaḥ puṃbhirmuktimabhīpsubhiḥ \|*  
*homo daśāṃśakaḥ kāryaḥ śraddhābaddhādarairnṛbhiḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. This Mantra should always be repeated by men desirous of salvation. The Homa should be performed one-tenth in number by men with faith and eagerness.

## \|\| 2.61.99 \|\|

*pariplutaiḥ puṃḍarīkairgavyena haviṣāsphuṭaiḥ \|*  
*saśarkareṇa medhāvī sakṣaudreṇa sadāśuciḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. An intelligent devotee always remaining pure shall perform the Homa with lotuses soaked in milk products and Havis together with sugar and honey.

## \|\| 2.61.100 \|\|

*trilakṣamaṃtra japyena mṛto deśāṃtareṣvapi \|*  
*avaśyaṃ muktimāpnoti maṃtrasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. If the Mantra is repeated three hundred thousand times, even if the devotee dies in other lands, he certainly attains salvation by the power of this Mantra.

## \|\| 2.61.101 \|\|

*sauvarṇīṃ pratimā kāryā navaratnasamanvitā \|*  
*pūrvoktarūpasaṃpannā saṃpūjyā sā prayatnataḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. A gold image decorated with freshly cut diamonds should be worshipped assiduously. The form of the image should be as described before.

## \|\| 2.61.102 \|\|
