*saṃpūjyāvā sadā gehe narairmokṣaikakāṃkṣibhiḥ \|*  
*maṇikarṇyāmathākṣepyā samabhyarcya prayatnataḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. By men who desire only salvation, the image should be worshipped in the house or after worshipping assiduously should be thrown into Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 2.61.103 \|\|

*saṃsārabhīrubhiḥ puṃbhiḥ śraddhābaddhādarairiha \|*  
*upāyaḥ samanuṣṭheyo hyapi dūranivāsibhiḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Even if they are staying far away, means should be resorted to by men (who being) afraid of the worldly existence, have faith and eagerness.

## \|\| 2.61.104 \|\|

*maṇikarṇyāṃ kṛtasnāno maṇikarṇīśa vīkṣaṇāt \|*  
*jananī jaṭharāvāse vasatiṃ na labhennaraḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. One who takes the holy bath in Maṇikarṇikā should visit Maṇikarṇīśa. Thereby the man does not stay further in the womb of a mother.

## \|\| 2.61.105 \|\|

*maṇikarṇīśvaraṃ liṃgaṃṃ purāsaṃsthāpitaṃ mayā \|*  
*prāgdvāreṃtargṛhasyātra samarcyo mokṣakāṃkṣibhiḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Maṇikarṇīśvara Liṅga was installed by me formerly in the eastern entrance of the Antargṛha (Inner Shrine). Here Maṇikarṇīśvara should be worshipped by those who desire salvation.

## \|\| 2.61.106 \|\|

*tataḥ pāśupataṃ tīrthamavācyāṃ maṇikarṇitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtodakakriyastatra paśyetpaśupatīśvaram \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. To the south of Maṇikarṇī is the Pāśupata Tīrtha. A devotee should perform all the rites like water-libations there and visit Paśupatīśvara.

## \|\| 2.61.107 \|\|

*yatra pāśupato yoga upadiṣṭaḥ pinākinā \|*  
*mamāpi vidhimukhyānāṃ surāṇāṃ paśupāśahṛt \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. It is there that Pāśupata Yoga was imparted by the Pināka-wielding Lord. It is he who removes the ignorance and bondage of Suras, the chief of whom is Brahmā, and also my bondage.

## \|\| 2.61.108-109 \|\|

*ataḥ paśupatiryatra liṃgarūpadharaḥ svayam \|*  
*paśupāśavimokṣāya nityaṃ kāśyāṃ prakāśate \|\| 108 \|\|*

*tatra caitra caturdaśyāṃ śuklāyāṃ śucimānasaiḥ \|*  
*kāryā yātrā prayatnena rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ tathā \|\| 109 \|\|*

108-109. Paśupati has assumed the form of a Liṅga himself and shines always in Kāśī for the removal of the bondage of the individual souls. There, on the fourteenth day in the bright half of the month of Caitra, men of pure minds should assiduously perform Yātrā (religious festival, procession etc.). They should keep awake at night.

## \|\| 2.61.110 \|\|

*pūjayitvā paśupatimupoṣaṇaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*paśupāśairna badhyaṃte darśe vihitapāraṇāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Devotees should fast on the fourteenth day (in the bright half of all months) and then worship the Lord. They must have Pāraṇā (ritualistic breaking of fast) on the new-moon day. Thereby they are never fettered by Māyā.

## \|\| 2.61.111 \|\|

*rudrāvāsastatastīrthaṃ tīrthātpāśupatātpuraḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā narairarcyo rudrāvāseśvaro haraḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Beyond that, in front of Pāśupata Tīrtha, is Rudrāvāsa Tīrtha. After taking their bath there, men should worship Hara, Rudrāvāseśvara.

## \|\| 2.61.112 \|\|

*maṇikarṇīśvarādyāmyāṃ rudrāvāseśvaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*samārādhya vaselloke rudrāvāse na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. By propitiating Rudrāvāseśvara to the south of Maṇikarṇīśvara a man (devotee) should undoubtedly stay in the world of Rudrāvāsa.

## \|\| 2.61.113 \|\|

*viśvatīrthaṃ tato yāmyāṃ viśvaistīrthairadhiṣṭhitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro bhaktyā viśvanāthaṃ vilokayet \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. To the south thereof is the Viśva Tīrtha occupied by all the Tīrthas of the world. After taking the holy bath there devoutly, a devotee should visit Viśvanātha.

## \|\| 2.61.114 \|\|

*viśvāṃ gaurīṃ ca tadanu pūjayitvāti bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*viśvasya pūjyo bhavati tato viśvamayo bhavet \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Thereafter he should adore with great devotion Viśvā i.e. Gaurī. He will thereby become venerable unto the whole universe. He should identify himself with the entire cosmos.

## \|\| 2.61.115 \|\|

*muktitīrthaṃ ca tadanu tatrāpi kṛtamajjanaḥ \|*  
*mokṣeśvaraṃ tatobhyarcya mokṣamāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Thereafter, is the Mukti Tīrtha. A devotee should take his holy ablution there also and worship Mokṣeśvara. He will undoubtedly attain salvation.

## \|\| 2.61.116 \|\|

*avimukteśvarātpaścānmokṣeśaṃ vīkṣya mānavaḥ \|*  
*na punarmānaveloke yātāyātaṃ karotyaho \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. After visiting Mokṣeśvara behind Avimukteśvara a man never moves about in this mortal world.

## \|\| 2.61.117 \|\|

*avimukteśvaraṃ tīrthaṃ muktitīrthānmanākpare \|*  
*tatrāplutyāvimukteśamarcayitvā vimucyate \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Avimukteśvara Tīrtha is beyond Mukti Tīrtha. A devotee should take holy dip there and worship Avimukteśa. He will become liberated.

## \|\| 2.61.118 \|\|

*tatpare tārakaṃ tīrthaṃ yatra viśveśvaraḥ svayam \|*  
*ācaṣṭe tārakaṃ brahmamṛtakarṇemṛtātmakam \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Beyond that is the Tāraka Tīrtha where Viśveśvara himself mentions the Tāraka Brahma which is like ambrosia unto the ears of the dead.

## \|\| 2.61.119 \|\|

*susnātastārake tīrthe tārakeśvara darśanāt \|*  
*saṃsārasāgaraṃ tīrtvā tārayetsvapitṝnapi \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. A devotee who takes his holy bath in the Tāraka Tīrtha and visits Tārakeśvara, crosses the ocean of worldly existence and redeems his own ancestors also.

## \|\| 2.61.120 \|\|

*tatrābhyāśe skaṃdatīrthaṃ tatrāplutya narottamaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ṣaḍānanaṃ caiva jahyātṣāṭkauśikīṃ tanum \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Very near is Skanda Tīrtha. An excellent man who plunges therein and visits the Six-faced Lord eschews the (physical) body having six Kośas (sheaths i.e. skin, flesh, blood, semen, bone and marrow).

## \|\| 2.61.121 \|\|

*tārakeśvara pūrveṇa dṛṣṭvā devaṃ ṣaḍānanam \|*  
*vasetṣaḍānane loke kaumāraṃ vapurudvahan \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. By visiting the Six-faced Lord to the east of Tārakeśvara, a devotee can assume the body of Lord Kumāra and stay in the Ṣaḍānana world.

## \|\| 2.61.122 \|\|

*ḍhuṃḍhitīrthaṃ tataḥ puṇyaṃ narastatra kṛtodakaḥ \|*  
*ḍhuṃḍhiṃ gaṇapatiṃ stutvā na vighnairabhibhūyate \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Beyond that is the meritorious Ḍhuṇḍhi Tīrtha. A man should perform all the rites in water there and eulogize Ḍhuṇḍhi Gaṇapati. He is never assailed by obstacles.

## \|\| 2.61.123-125 \|\|

*bhavānītīrthamatulaṃ ḍhuṃḍhitīrthasya dakṣiṇe \|*  
*tatra snātvā vidhānena bhavānīṃ paripūjya ca \|\| 123 \|\|*

*dukūle ratnanepathyairnaivedyairbahuvistaraiḥ \|*  
*puṣpairdhūpaiḥ pradīpaiśca bhavānī śo prapūjya ca \|\| 124 \|\|*

*samastamarcitaṃ tena trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*bhavānīśaṃkarau kāśyāmarcitau śraddhayā tu yaiḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

123-125. The unparalleled Bhavānī Tīrtha is to the south of Ḍhuṇḍhi Tīrtha. A devotee should take his holy bath there and worship Bhavānī by means of silk garments embellished with jewels, Naivedya, foodstuffs of a great variety, flowers, incense and lights. Worshipping Bhavānī and Īśa is as though all the three worlds including the mobile and immobile beings have been worshipped. Bhavānī and Śaṅkara should be worshipped with great faith.

## \|\| 2.61.126-127 \|\|

*caitrāṣṭamyāṃ mahāyātrāṃ bhavānyāḥ kārayetsudhīḥ \|*  
*aṣṭādhikāḥ prakartavyāḥ śatakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇāḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

*pradakṣriṇīkṛtātena saptadvīpavatī mahī \|*  
*saśailā sasamudrā ca sāśramā ca sakānanā \|\| 127 \|\|*

126-127. A wise devotee should arrange for the great Yātrā of Bhavānī on the eighth day in Caitra. One hundred and eight circumambulations should be made. Thereby it is as though the entire earth consisting of the seven continents has been circumambulated by him along with mountains, hermitages, forests and oceans.

## \|\| 2.61.128 \|\|

*aṣṭau pradakṣiṇā deyāḥ pratyahaṃ tuṣṭitatparaiḥ \|*  
*namanīyau prayatnena bhavānīśaṃkarau sadā \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. Eight circumambulations are to be made everyday by those who are satisfied with that much. Bhavānī and Śaṅkara are to be always bowed to assiduously.

## \|\| 2.61.129 \|\|

*bhaktānāṃ kāmadā nityaṃ bhavānī vāsasāṃ pradā \|*  
*ato bhavānī saṃpūjyā kāśyāṃ tīrthanivāsibhiḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Bhavānī accords to devotees what they desire. Bhavānī always bestows garments. Hence Bhavānī should be worshipped in Kāśī by the residents of the Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.61.130 \|\|

*yogakṣemaṃ sadā kuryādbhavānī kāśivāsinām \|*  
*tasmādbhavānī saṃsevyā satataṃ kāśivāsibhiḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Bhavānī always accords to the residents of Kāśī what they do not have and preserves what they acquire. Hence Bhavānī should always be resorted to by the residents of Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.61.131 \|\|

*bhikṣaṇīyā sadā bhikṣā bhikṣuṇā mokṣakāṃkṣiṇā \|*  
*yato bhikṣāpradā kāśyāṃ viśveśasya kuṭuṃbinī \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Alms should always be prayed of her by a mendicant desirous of salvation, since Viśveśa’s consort is the giver of alms at Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.61.132 \|\|

*gṛhamadhyetra viśveśo bhavānī tatkuṭuṃbinī \|*  
*sarvebhyaḥ kāśisaṃsthebhyo mokṣabhikṣāṃ prayacchati \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Here in the house is Viśveśa. Bhavānī is the lady of his house. She gives the alms in the form of salvation to all the residents of Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.61.133 \|\|

*duṣprāpamapi yatkiṃcitkāśīkṣetranivāsinām \|*  
*tatsuprāpyaṃ karotyeva bhavānī pūjitā nṛbhiḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. On being worshipped by men, Bhavānī makes easily available what is difficult to attain, to the residents of Kāśīkṣetra.

## \|\| 2.61.134 \|\|

*kuryājjāgaraṇaṃ rātrau mahāṣṭamyāṃ vratī naraḥ \|*  
*prātarbhavānīmabhyarcya prāpnuyādvāṃchitaṃ phalam \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. A man observing Vrata on the Mahāṣṭamī day shall keep awake during the night and worship Bhavānī in the morning. He will acquire the desired benefit.

## \|\| 2.61.135 \|\|

*śukreśātpaścimāśāyāṃ bhavānīṃ yo'bhivīkṣate \|*  
*sarve manorathāstasya siddhyaṃtīha na saṃ śayaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. There is no doubt in this that all the desires of the devotee will be fulfilled, if he visits Bhavānī to the west of Śukreśa.

## \|\| 2.61.136 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ sadaiva vastavyaṃ snātavyottaravāhinī \|*  
*bhavānīśaṃkarau sevyau prāptavye bhuktimuktike \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. If enjoyment of pleasures and salvation are to be acquired, one should always reside in Kāśī, should take bath in (the river Gaṅgā) flowing northwards and serve Bhavānī and Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 2.61.137 \|\|

*mātarbhavāni tava pādarajobhavāni mātarbhavāni tavadāsataro bhavāni \|*  
*mātarbhavāni nabhavāni yathābhavesmiṃstvadbhāgbhavānyanudinaṃ na punarbhavāni \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. The Mantra: “O Mother Bhavānī, I shall become the dust of your feet. O Mother Bhavānī, I shall become the most obedient among your slaves. O Mother Bhavānī, I shall always become a devotee of yours if I should not be born in this world. I shall not have rebirth in the world.”

## \|\| 2.61.138 \|\|

*tiṣṭhatā gacchatā vāpi svapatā jāgratāpi vā \|*  
*ayamatra sadā japyaḥ sukhāptyai kāśivāsinā \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. For the purpose of the attainment of happiness this Mantra should always be repeated by the residents of Kāśī, while standing, walking, sleeping or keeping awake.

## \|\| 2.61.139 \|\|

*īśānatīrthaṃ tatraiva bhavānītīrthasannidhau \|*  
*tatra snāto ya īśānamarcayenna sa janmabhāk \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Īśāna Tīrtha is also there near Bhavānī Tīrtha. He who takes his holy bath there and worships Īśāna does not take birth again.

## \|\| 2.61.140 \|\|

*jñānatīrthaṃ ca tatraiva jñānadaṃ savardā nṛṇām \|*  
*kṛtābhiṣekastattīrthe dṛṣṭvā jñāneśvaraṃ śivam \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Jñāna Tīrtha too is there, that bestows wisdom on men. One should take bath in that Tīrtha and visit Śiva Jñāneśvara.

## \|\| 2.61.141 \|\|

*jñānavāpīsamīpastho jñāneśo yaiḥ samarcitaḥ \|*  
*jñānabhraṃśo na teṣāṃ syādapi paṃcatvamṛcchatām \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. If Jñāneśa stationed near Jñānavāpī is worshipped by people, they will never meet with loss of wisdom even when they die.

## \|\| 2.61.142-143 \|\|

*śailāditīrthaṃ tatraiva paramarddhi prakāśakam \|*  
*tatra śrāddhādikaṃ kṛtvā dattvā dānaṃ svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

*śailādīśvaramālokya jñānavāpyā udagdiśi \|*  
*labhedgaṇatvapadavīṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 143 \|\|*

142-143. There alone is Śailādi Tīrtha that gives greatest prosperity and glory. There a devotee should perform Śrāddha etc., make gifts in accordance with one’s capacity and visit Śailādīśvara to the north of Jñānavāpī. He will attain the status of a Gaṇa. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 2.61.144 \|\|

*naṃditīrthādavācyāṃ tu viṣṇutīrthaṃ paraṃ mama \|*  
*tatra piṃḍānvinirvāpya pitṝṇāmanṛṇo bhavet \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. To the south of Nandī Tīrtha is my Viṣṇu Tīrtha. There a devotee should offer rice-balls and become free from indebtedness to Pitṛs.

## \|\| 2.61.145 \|\|

*viṣṇutīrthe kṛtasnāno yo māṃ viṣṇuṃ vilokayet \|*  
*viśveśāddakṣiṇepārśve viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. After taking the holy bath, the devotee should visit me, Viṣṇu, on the right side of Viśveśa. He will go to the world of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.61.146-147 \|\|

*yaḥ pratyekādaśīṃ prāpya śayanīṃ bodhinīṃ tathā \|*  
*kuryājjāgaraṇaṃ rātrau mama mūrtisamīpataḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

*prātaḥ samarcya māṃ bhaktyā bhojayitvā dvijānapi \|*  
*dattvā gāḥ kāṃcanaṃ bhūmiṃ na bhūyo bhūmibhāgbhavet \|\| 147 \|\|*

146-147. During every Ekādaśī (11th day), Śayanī (Ekādaśī in the bright half of Āṣāḍha) and Bodhinī (Ekādaśī in the bright half of Kārttika) the devotee should keep awake at night near my image. At dawn he should worship me devoutly, feed Brāhmaṇas and make gifts of cows, gold and plots of land. He does not come to the earth again.

## \|\| 2.61.148 \|\|

*kṛtvā tatra vratotsargaṃ vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*samyagvrataphalaṃ dhīmānprāpnotyeva mamājñayā \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. There the devotee can finally conclude the Vrata without being very parsimonious in spending money. At my bidding, the intelligent devotee shall attain the benefit of the Vrata perfectly.

## \|\| 2.61.149-150 \|\|

*mama tīrthādavācyāṃ tu tī rthaṃ paitāmahaṃ śubham \|*  
*tatra śrāddhavidhānena tarpayitvā pitāmahān \|\| 149 \|\|*

*pitāmaheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ brahmanāloparisthitam \|*  
*pūjayitvā naro bhaktyā brahmalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 150 \|\|*

149-150. The auspicious Paitāmaha Tīrtha is to the south of my Tīrtha. There the devotee should propitiate ancestors through the performance of Śrāddhas and worship Pitāmaheśvara Liṅga stationed above Brahmanāla with devotion. The man will attain Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.61.151 \|\|

*brahmasrotaḥ samīpe tu kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham \|*  
*parāmakṣayatāmeti śubhameva tataścaret \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. A Karma performed near Brahmasrotas whether auspicious or inauspicious attains great Akṣayatā (state of permanence). Hence one shall do only what is auspicious.

## \|\| 2.61.152 \|\|

*atyalpamapi yatkarma kṛtamatra śubhāśubham \|*  
*pralayepi na tasyāsti pralayo munisattama \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. O excellent sage, whatever has been done here whether auspicious or inauspicious, ever if it be so very little, is not lost even at the time of final annihilation.

## \|\| 2.61.153 \|\|

*nābhitīrthamidaṃ proktaṃ nābhibhūtaṃ yataḥ kṣiteḥ \|*  
*api brahmāṃḍagolasya nābhireṣā śubhodayā \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. This is called Nābhi Tīrtha because it is as though the navel of the earth. This is the navel of the spherical cosmic egg and it causes rise of prosperity.

## \|\| 2.61.154 \|\|

*sā māṇikarṇikeyīyaṃ nābhirgāṃbhīryabhūmikā \|*  
*brahmāṃḍagolakaṃ sarvaṃ yasyāmeti layodayam \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. It is the navel of Maṇikarṇikā, the ground of depth (gāmbhīryabhūmikā?). It is in this that the entire cosmic egg merges and it is from this that is comes forth.

## \|\| 2.61.155 \|\|

*brahmanālaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|*  
*tatsaṃgame naraḥ snātvā koṭijanma malaṃ haret \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. Brahmanāla is a great Tīrtha well-known in all the three worlds. By taking his holy bath in its confluence a man shakes off the impurities of ten million births.

## \|\| 2.61.156 \|\|

*brahmanāle patedyeṣāmapi kīkasamātrakam \|*  
*brahmāṃḍamaṃḍapāṃtaste na viśaṃti kadācana \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. If even a bone were to fall into Brahmanāla those people never enter the pavilion of the cosmic egg.

## \|\| 2.61.157 \|\|

*tato bhāgīrathestīrthaṃ brahmanālācca dakṣiṇe \|*  
*tatra snātvā naraḥ samyaṅmucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. Beyond that, to the south of Brahmanāla is the Bhāgīrathī Tīrtha. By taking his holy bath there a man is completely rid of the sin of Brāhmaṇa’s murder.

## \|\| 2.61.158 \|\|

*bhāgīrathīśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ svargadvārasya sannidhau \|*  
*darśanādbrahmahatyāyāḥ puraścaraṇamucyate \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. The Liṅga called Bhāgīrathīśvara is in the vicinity of Svargadvāra. The sight of that Liṅga is said to effect the Puraścaraṇa of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 2.61.159 \|\|

*aśubhāṃ gatimāpannā yasya pūrve pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*tena bhāgīrathī tīrthe tarpaṇīyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. If one’s ancestors had fallen into inauspicious state (Hells), one should assiduously offer libations unto them in the Bhāgīrathī Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.61.160 \|\|

*tatra bhāgīrathe tīrthe śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā tu brahmaloke nayetpitṝn \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. He should perform Śrāddha in accordance with the injunctions in the Bhāgīrathī Tīrtha and feed Brāhmaṇas. Thereby he will take the ancestors to Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.61.161-163 \|\|

*taddakṣiṇe mahātīrthaṃ khurakartari saṃjñitam \|*  
*golokādāgatābhiśca gobhiryatkhurakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*sthapuṭīkṛtabhūbhāgaṃ tatastatkhura kartari \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe kṛtasnānaḥ kṛtapiṃḍodakakriyaḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

*khurakartarīśaṃ liṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvā golokamāpnuyāt \|*  
*godhanairna vimucyeta talliṃgasya samarcanāt \|\| 163 \|\|*

161-163. To the south thereof is the great Tīrtha named Khurakartari. Cows which arrived from Goloka have made the ground here uneven by means of the tips of their hoofs. Hence it is called Khurakartari. The devotee should take his holy bath in that Tīrtha, offer balls of rice, perform all the rites in water and visit Khurakartarīśa Lìṅga. He will thereby attain Goloka. He will never be devoid of cattle wealth, thanks to the worship of that Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.61.164-165 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe khurakartaryā mārkaṃḍaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*kṛtaśrāddhavidhānaśca tasmiṃstīrthe'ghahāriṇi \|\| 164 \|\|*

*mārkaṃḍeyeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvāyurdīrghamāpnuyāt \|*  
*brahmatejobhivṛddhiṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca paramāṃ bhuvi \|\| 165 \|\|*

164-165. To the south of Khurakartari is the excellent Mārkaṇḍa Tīrtha. A devotee who performs all the Śrāddha rites in that Tīrtha that dispels sins, and visits Mārkaṇḍeyeśvara Liṅga shall attain longevity, increase in the Brāhmaṇical splendour and greatest renown in the world.

## \|\| 2.61.166-167 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhatīrthaṃ paramaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*tarpayitvā pitṝṃstatra vasiṣṭheśaṃ vilokya ca \|\| 166 \|\|*

*naro na lipyate pāpairjanmatrayasamarjitaiḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaloke vasati brahmateja samanvitaḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

166-167. Vasiṣṭha Tīrtha is the greatest destroyer of great sins. After offering libations to Pitṛs there and visiting Vasiṣṭheśa, a man can prevent getting contamination with the sins acquired in the course of three births. Fully equipped with Brāhmaṇical splendour, he stays in Vasiṣṭhaloka.

## \|\| 2.61.168 \|\|

*tatraivārudhaṃtī tīrthaṃ strīṇāṃ saubhāgyavadharnam \|*  
*pativratābhistattīrthaṃ gāhanīyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. There itself is the Arundhatī Tīrtha that heightens the conjugal bliss of women. That Tīrtha should particularly be plunged into by chaste women.

## \|\| 2.61.169 \|\|

*pauṃścalyajanito doṣastattīrthaparimajjanāt \|*  
*kṣaṇādvināśa māgacchedaruṃdhatyāḥ prabhāvataḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. The sin arising from harlotry shall instantaneously vanish if one plunges into that Tīrtha. That is due to the power of Arundhatī.

## \|\| 2.61.170 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeyeśvarātprācyāṃ vasiṣṭheśvara pūjanāt \|*  
*niṣpāpo jāyate martyo mahatpuṇyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. By worshipping Vasiṣṭheśvara to the east of Mārkaṇḍeyeśvara a man becomes rid of sins. He will acquire great merit.

## \|\| 2.61.171 \|\|

*mūrtī vasiṣṭhāruṃdhatyostatra pūjye prayatnataḥ \|*  
*na strī vaidhavyamāpnoti na pumānstrī viyogitām \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. The images of Vasiṣṭha and Arundhatī should be assiduously worshipped there. A woman does not become a widow nor does a man become separated from his wife.

## \|\| 2.61.172-173 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhatīrthato yāmyāṃ narmadātīrthamuttamam \|*  
*vidhāya śrāddhaṃ medhāvī narmadeśaṃvilokya ca \|\| 172 \|\|*

*tatra dattvā mahādānaṃ padmayānavimucyate \|*  
*tatastrisaṃdhyaṃ vai tīrthaṃ trisaṃdhyeśvara pūrvataḥ \|\| 173 \|\|*

172-173. To the south of Vasiṣṭha Tīrtha is the excellent Narmadā Tīrtha. After performing Śrāddha there a wise person should visit Narmadeśa and make great gifts there. He is never abandoned by Padmā (Goddess of Fortune). Beyond that, to the east of Trisandhyeśvara is the Trisandhyā Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.61.174 \|\|

*tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā kṛtvā saṃdhyāṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*saṃdhyākāla vilopotthapātakairnābhibhūyate \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. A man who takes his holy bath there, and offers Sandhyā prayers in accordance with the injunctions is not assailed by sins arising from the omission and irregularity of performing Sandhyā prayers.

## \|\| 2.61.175 \|\|

*trisaṃdhyeśvaramālokya kṛtasaṃdhyasttrikālataḥ \|*  
*trivedāvartajaṃ puṇyaṃ prāpnuyācchraddhayā dvijaḥ \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. A Brāhmaṇa who visits Trisandhyeśvara and perforins Sandhyā rites thrice a day with great faith, shall attain the merit of reciting three Vedas.

## \|\| 2.61.176 \|\|

*tato'nuyoginītīrthaṃ narastatra kṛtāplavaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tu yoginīpīṭhaṃ yogasiddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. Beyond that is the Yoginī Tīrtha. A man who takes a plunge therein and visits Yoginīpīṭha shall attain Yogic Siddhī.

## \|\| 2.61.177-179 \|\|

*agasti tīrthe tatrāsti mahāghaugha vighātakṛt \|*  
*tatra snātvā prayatnena dṛṣṭvāgastīcaśvaraṃ vibhum \|\| 177 \|\|*

*agastikuṃḍe ca tataḥ saṃtarpya ca pitāmahān \|*  
*agastinā sametāṃ ca lopāmudrāṃ praṇamya ca \|\| 178 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sarvakleśavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*gacchetsa pūrvajaiḥ sārdhaṃ śivalokaṃ narottamaḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

177-179. Agasti Tīrtha that dispels masses of great sins is there. An excellent man who takes his holy bath there assiduously, visits Lord Agastīśvara, offers libations to the grandfathers thereafter in Agastikuṇḍa and bows down to Lopāmudrā accompanied by Agasti, shall become rid of all sins and free from all distresses. He will go to Śivaloka along with his ancestors.

## \|\| 2.61.180 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe'gastyatīrthācca tīrthamastyatipāvanam \|*  
*gaṃgākeśavasaṃjñaṃ ca sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. To the south of Agastya Tīrtha there is a highly sacred Tīrtha named Gaṅgākeśava which destroys all sins.

## \|\| 2.61.181 \|\|

*tatra me śubhadāṃ mūrtiṃ mune tattīrthasaṃjñikām \|*  
*saṃpūjya śraddhayā dhīmānmama loke mahīyate \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. There, O sage, the intelligent devotee who worships my auspicious image named after the Tīrtha (i. e. Gaṅgā-Keśaveśvara) with great faith, is honoured in my world.

## \|\| 2.61.182 \|\|

*tatra piṃḍānvinirvāpya dattvā dānaṃ svaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*śatasāṃvatsarīṃ tṛptiṃ pitṝṇāṃ sa samarpayet \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. By offering rice-balls there and offering Dānas in accordance with his capacity, he should proffer contentment unto the Pitṛs extending over a hundred years.

## \|\| 2.61.183 \|\|

*maṇikarṇī parīmāṇametatte kīrtitaṃ mahat \|*  
*sīmāvināyakādyāmyāṃ sarvavighnavighātanāt \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. Thus the extent of Maṇikarṇī has been narrated to you. It is to the south of Sīmāvināyaka who dispels obstacles.

## \|\| 2.61.184 \|\|

*vairocaneśvarātprācyāmahaṃ vaikuṃṭhamādhavaḥ \|*  
*tatra māṃ bhaktitobhyarcya vaikuṃṭhārcāmavāpnuyāt \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. I am Vaikuṇṭha Mādhava (stationed) to the east of Vairocaneśvara. By worshipping me with devotion there the devotee shall attain the benefit of being worshipped in Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 2.61.185 \|\|

*vīramādhavasaṃjñohaṃ vīreśātpaścime mune \|*  
*tatra vratī samabhyarcya na yāmīṃ yātanāṃ labhet \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. I am named Vīramādhava to the west of Vīreśa, O age. If the observer of vows worships me there, he does not meet with the torture of Yama.

## \|\| 2.61.186 \|\|

*kālamādhavanāmāhaṃ kālabhairava sannidhau \|*  
*kaliḥ kālo na kalayenmadbhaktamiti niścitam \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. I am named Kālamādhava in the vicinity of Kālabhairava. It is certain that neither Kali nor Kāla affects my devotee.

## \|\| 2.61.187 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣasya śuklāyāmekādaśyāmupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*tatra jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā yamaṃ nālokayetkvacit \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. The devotee should observe fast on the eleventh day in the bright half of Mārgaśīrṣa and keep awake during the night. He shall not meet with Yama anywhere.

## \|\| 2.61.188 \|\|

*nirvāṇanarasiṃhohaṃ pulastīśvaradakṣiṇe \|*  
*bhakto nirvāṇamāpnoti tanmṛrtinamanādapi \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. To the south (right) of Pulastīśvara, I am (called) Nirvāṇanarasiṃha. Even by bowing down to that image the devotee attains salvation.

## \|\| 2.61.189 \|\|

*mahābalanṛsiṃhohamoṃkārātpūrvato mune \|*  
*dūtānmahābalānyāmyānna paśyettu tadarcakaḥ \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. O sage, to the east of Oṃkāra, I am (called) Mahābala Nṛsiṃha. One who worships that image does not see the extremely strong messengers of Yama.

## \|\| 2.61.190 \|\|

*pracaṃḍanarasiṃhohaṃ caṃḍabhairavapūrvataḥ \|*  
*pracaṃḍamapyaghaṃ kṛtvā niṣpāpmā syāttadarcanāt \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. I am (called) Pracaṇḍanarasiṃha to the east of Caṇḍabhairava. By worshipping that image, the devotee shall be free from sins even if he has committed very grave ones.

## \|\| 2.61.191 \|\|

*ahaṃ girinṛsiṃhosmi taddehalivināyakāt \|*  
*prācyāṃ prabalapāpau ghagajānāṃ pravidāraṇaḥ \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. To the east of Dehalivināyaka I am (called) Girinṛsiṃha, the tearer of elephants in the form of masses of powerful sins.

## \|\| 2.61.192 \|\|

*mahābhayaharaścāhaṃ narasiṃho mahāmune \|*  
*pitāmaheśvarātpaścādbhakta sādhvasasādhvasaḥ \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. O great sage, I, Narasiṃha, am the remover of great fears too, to the west of Pitāmaheśvara, creating alarm unto the fright of devotees.

## \|\| 2.61.193 \|\|

*atyugranarasiṃhohaṃ kalaśeśvarapaścime \|*  
*atyugramapi pāpaughaṃ harāmi śraddhayārcitaḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. To the west of Kalaśeśvara, I am (called) Atyugranarasiṃha. If worshipped with faith, I remove even the mass of very fierce sins.

## \|\| 2.61.194 \|\|

*jvālāmālīnṛsiṃho'haṃ jvālāmukhyāḥ samīpataḥ \|*  
*saṃjvālayāmi pāpaugha tṛṇāni paripūjitaḥ \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. In the vicinity of Jvālāmukhī I am (called) Jvālāmālīnṛsiṃha. When adored perfectly, I burn down the grasses in the form of the masses of sins.

## \|\| 2.61.195 \|\|

*kolāhalanṛsiṃhosmi daityadānavamardanaḥ \|*  
*mamanāmasamuccārādaghakolāhalo yataḥ \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. I am (called) Kolāhalanṛsiṃha, the subduer of Daityas and Dānavas, because there arises chaotic noise among sins when my name is uttered.

## \|\| 2.61.196 \|\|

*kaṃkālabhairavo yatra kāśīrakṣaṇadakṣadhīḥ \|*  
*tatra māṃ bhaktitobhyarcya nopasargairnirudhyate \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. If a devotee worships me devoutly in the place where there is Kaṅkālabhairava who is intelligent and efficient in the protection of Kāśī, he is never interrupted by torments.

## \|\| 2.61.197 \|\|

*viṭaṃkanarasiṃhosmi nīlakaṃṭheśvarādanu \|*  
*tatra māṃ śraddhayā pūjya naro bhavati nirbhayaḥ \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. Behind Nīlakaṇṭheśvara I am (called) Viṭaṅkanarasiṃha. A man becomes free from fear by worshipping me there with great faith.

## \|\| 2.61.198 \|\|

*anaṃtavāmanaścāhamanaṃ teśvarasannidhau \|*  
*anaṃtānyapi bhaktasya kaluṣāṇi hare'rcitaḥ \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. In the vicinity of Ananteśvara, I am (called) Anantavāmana. On being worshipped, I remove even the endless sins of the devotee.

## \|\| 2.61.199 \|\|

*dadhivāmanasaṃjñohaṃ bhaktānāṃ dadhibhaktadaḥ \|*  
*yannāmasmaraṇādeva na daridro naro bhavet \|\| 199 \|\|*

199\. I am named Dadhivāmana (because) I bestow curd-rice on the devotees. Merely by remembering the name (of that Lord), a man ceases to be poor.

## \|\| 2.61.200 \|\|

*trivikramosmyahaṃ kāśyāmudīcyāṃ ca trilocanāt \|*  
*dadāmi pūjito lakṣmīṃ harāmi vṛjinānyapi \|\| 200 \|\|*

200\. In Kāśī to the north of the Three-eyed Lord, I am (called) Trivikrama. On being Worshipped, I bestow wealth and remove sins.

## \|\| 2.61.201 \|\|

*balivāmananāmāhaṃ balinā paripūjitaḥ \|*  
*balibhadreśvarātprācyāṃ bhaktānāṃ balavardhanaḥ \|\| 201 \|\|*

201\. I am called Balivāmana. I was worshipped by Bali. To the east of Balibhadreśvara, I am the augmenter of the strength of the devotees.

## \|\| 2.61.202 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe bhavatīrthācca tāmradvīpādihāgataḥ \|*  
*nāmnā tāmravarāhosmi bhaktānāṃ ciṃtitārthadaḥ \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. To the right (south) of Bhava Tīrtha, I am Tāmravarāha by name. I came here from Tāmradvīpa. I am the bestower of what the devotees desire.

## \|\| 2.61.203-204 \|\|

*mune dharaṇivārāhaḥ prayāgeśvarasannidhau \|*  
*snātvā vārāhatīrthetra dṛṣṭvā māṃ kiṭi rūpiṇam \|\| 203 \|\|*

*saṃpūjya bahubhāvena na viśedyonisaṃkaṭam \|*  
*tatrālpamapi dattvānnaṃ dharādānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 204 \|\|*

203-204. O sage, (I am) Dharaṇīvarāha in the vicinity of Prayāgeśvara. The devotee should take his holy bath in the Varāha Tīrtha, visit me here in the form of a Boar and worship me with great fervour. He will never face the torture of being in a womb. By giving a very small quantity of cooked food, he acquires the benefit of a gift of lands.

## \|\| 2.61.205 \|\|

*mahākaluṣagaṃbhīra sāgare nipatañjanaḥ \|*  
*mama bhaktyuḍupaṃ prāpya pralayepi na majjati \|\| 205 \|\|*

205\. People sinking into the deep ocean of great sins will not get drowned even in Pralaya after obtaining the raft of devotion unto me.

## \|\| 2.61.206 \|\|

*ahaṃ kokāvarāhosmi kiṭīśvarasamīpataḥ \|*  
*tatra māṃ pūjayanmartyo labhate ciṃtitaphalam \|\| 206 \|\|*

206\. In the vicinity of Kiṭīśvara, I am (called) Kokāvarāha. A man worshipping me there gets whatever fruit is desired by him.

## \|\| 2.61.207-208 \|\|

*nārāyaṇāḥ śataṃ paṃca śataṃ ca jalaśāyinaḥ \|*  
*triṃśatkamaṭharūpāṇi matsyarūpāṇi viṃśatiḥ \|\| 207 \|\|*

*gopālāśca śataṃ sāṣṭaṃ buddhāḥ saṃti sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*triṃśatarāmāśca rāmā ekottaraṃśatam \|\| 208 \|\|*

207-208. There are a hundred Nārāyaṇas, five hundred Jalaśāyins, thirty in the form of tortoise, twenty in the form of fish, a hundred and eight Gopālas, Buddhas are thousands in number, Paraśurāmas are thirty in number and there are a hundred and one Rāmas.

## \|\| 2.61.209 \|\|

*viṣṇurūposmyahaṃ caiko muktimaṃḍapamadhyataḥ \|*  
*munekṛtaprasādena viśveśena śritaḥ svayam \|\| 209 \|\|*

209\. I am only one in the form of Viṣṇu resorting to the middle of the pavilion of Mukti (salvation) by the grace of Viśveśa who himself gave me that favour.

## \|\| 2.61.210 \|\|

*nārāyaṇasvarūpeṇa gaṇāścakragadodyatāḥ \|*  
*kurvaṃti rakṣāṃ kṣetrasya parito niyutāni ṣaṭ \|\| 210 \|\|*

210\. There are six million Gaṇas in the form of Nārāyaṇa with the discus and the club lifted up. They keep watch around the holy spot.

## \|\| 2.61.211-212 \|\|

*sognibiṃduriti śrutvā saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ papraccha medhāvī mūrtibhedānvada prabho \|\| 211 \|\|*

*hitāya nijabhaktānāṃ mama saṃdehaśāṃtaye \|*  
*kati te mūrtayonaṃta kathaṃ jñeyāstathā vada \|\| 212 \|\|*

211-212. On hearing this, Agnibindu became delighted with hairs standing on ends. The intelligent sage asked further: “O Lord, mention the different forms for the welfare of your devotees and to quell my doubts. O infinite one, how many are your Mūrtis? How are they to be known? Tell this.”

## \|\| 2.61.213-214 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacastasyāgnibiṃdostapasāṃ nidheḥ \|*  
*uvāca bhagavānviṣṇurmūrtibhedānanukramāta \|\| 213 \|\|*

*yāñśrutvāpi hi no martyo yamagocaratāṃ vrajet \|*  
*keśavādīṃścaturviṃśadbhedānāha prajāpatiḥ \|\| 214 \|\|*

213-214. On hearing the words of Agnibindu, the storehouse of austerities, Lord Viṣṇu mentioned the different Mūrtis in due order. On hearing these, a man can avoid being a victim of Yama. Prajāpati (i.e. Viṣṇu) mentioned twenty-four different Mùrtis beginning with Keśava.

## \|\| 2.61.215 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*agnibiṃdo mahāprājña śṛṇu te kathayāmyaham \|*  
*ādyadakṣiṇahastācca viddhi sṛṣṭikramānmune \|\| 215 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

215\. O Agnibindu of great intellect! Listen, I am enumerating to you (the different forms), O sage. Beginning with the first right-hand (upper) one understand these things in the Sṛṣṭi order (clock-wise).

## \|\| 2.61.216 \|\|

*śaṃkhacakragadāpadmairmūrtiṃ jānīhi kaiśavīm \|*  
*pūjitā yā nṛṇāṃ kuryācciṃtitārthamasaṃśayam \|\| 216 \|\|*

216\. Understand the Mūrti of Keśava through Śaṅkha (upper right hand), Cakra (upper left hand), Gadā (lower left hand) and Padma (lower right hand). On being worshipped, this Mūrti shall undoubtedly fulfil the wish (of the worshipper).

## \|\| 2.61.217 \|\|

*madhuhā paricetavyaḥ śaṃkhapadmagadāsibhiḥ \|*  
*vairiṇo nāśamāyāṃti tanmūrtiparisevanāt \|\| 217 \|\|*

217\. (The Mūrti) Madhuhā should be understood through Śaṅkha (upper right hand), Padma (upper left hand), Gadā (lower left hand) and Cakra (lower right hand). By serving this Mūrti, enemies become destroyed.

## \|\| 2.61.218 \|\|

*saṃkarṣaṇaḥ samarcyotra śaṃkhābjārigadāyudhaḥ \|*  
*tanmūrtipūjanājjātu jaṃturna syātpunarbhavī \|\| 218 \|\|*

218\. (The Mūrti) Saṅkarṣaṇa should be worshipped with the following as weapons: Śaṅkha (upper right hand), Padma (upper left hand), Cakra (lower left hand) and Gadā (lower right hand). If this Mūrti is worshipped, the creature is never reborn.

## \|\| 2.61.219 \|\|

*śaṃkhakaumodakīcakrapadmairdāmodarorcyate \|*  
*dadāti vittaṃ putrāṃśca godhanaṃ dhānyameva hi \|\| 219 \|\|*

219\. Dāmodara is worshipped with Śaṅkha, Kaumodakī (Gadā), Cakra and Padma (in the order mentioned above). He bestows wealth, sons, cattle-wealth and grains.

## \|\| 2.61.220 \|\|

*vāmanaḥ śaṃkhacakrābjagadābhirupalakṣitaḥ \|*  
*lakṣmīvaṃtaṃ janaṃ kuryādgṛhepi paridhāritaḥ \|\| 220 \|\|*

220\. Vāmana is equipped with Śaṅkha, Cakra, Padma and Gadā. When installed in the house, he makes people prosperous.

## \|\| 2.61.221 \|\|

*pāṃcajanyaṃ gadāṃpadmaṃ citramūrti sudarśanam \|*  
*pradyumnaḥ pūjyate martyairbahudyumnaṃ prayacchati \|\| 221 \|\|*

221\. Pāñcajanya (i.e. Śaṅkha), Gadā, Padma and Sudarśana (i.e. Cakra) of variegated forms (indicate) Pradyumna who is worshipped by men. He bestows much wealth.

## \|\| 2.61.222 \|\|

*ūrdhvavāmakarātsṛṣṭyā viṣṇvādyaṃ ṣaṭkamucyate \|*  
*yasya smaraṇamātreṇa vilīyaṃtegharāśayaḥ \|\| 222 \|\|*

222\. The six Mūrtis beginning with Viṣṇu are mentioned beginning with upper left hand in the clock-wise order. Merely by remembering it heaps of sins become dissolved.

## \|\| 2.61.223 \|\|

*śaṃkhāribhyāṃ gadābjābhyāṃ pūjyo viṣṇuḥ śriye naraiḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhapadmagadācakrairmādhavaḥ paramarddhidaḥ \|\| 223 \|\|*

223\. For prosperity, Viṣṇu (equipped) with Śaṅkha, Cakra, Gadā and Padma should be worshipped by men. Mādhava with Śaṅkha, Padma, Gadā and Cakra is the bestower of greatest prosperity.

## \|\| 2.61.224 \|\|

*dhyeyo'niruddhaḥ saṃsiddhyai śaṃkhābjārigadodyataḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhena gadayā cakrāṃbujābhyāṃ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 224 \|\|*

224\. For perfect achievement Aniruddha should be medidated upon as having Śaṅkha, Padma, Cakra and Gadā lifted up. Puruṣottama (should be meditated upon) as equipped with Śaṅkha, Gadā, Cakra and Padma.

## \|\| 2.61.225 \|\|

*adhokṣajo janiharaḥ śaṃkhāryabjagado mune \|*  
*śaṃkhakaumodakīpadmacakrairdhyeyo janārdanaḥ \|\| 225 \|\|*

225\. With Śaṅkha, Cakra, Padma and Gadā, O sage, Adhokṣaja is the remover of further rebirth. Janārdana with Śaṅkha, Kaumodakī (Gadā), Padma and Cakra should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.61.226 \|\|

*adhovāmakarātsṛṣṭyā ṣaḍagoṃvidādi mūrtayaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ goviṃdo bibhṛyātsadā \|\| 226 \|\|*

226\. The six Mūrtis beginning with Govinda (have the weapons) clock-wise beginning with left lower hand. Govinda always wields Śaṅkha (lower left hand), Cakra (lower right hand), Gadā (upper right hand) and Padma (upper left hand).

## \|\| 2.61.227 \|\|

*śaṃkhapadmagadācakrairarcyo lakṣmyai trivikramaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhābjacakraṃ bibhrāṇo gadāvāñśrīdharaḥ śriye \|\| 227 \|\|*

227\. Trivikrama should be worshipped for good fortune with Śaṅkha (lower left hand), Padma (lower right hand), Gadā (right upper hand) and Cakra (left upper hand). Śrīdhara wielding Śaṅkha, Padma, Cakra and Gadā is for prosperity.

## \|\| 2.61.228 \|\|

*hṛṣīkeśaśca śaṃkhena gadācakrāṃbujairmataḥ \|*  
*nṛsiṃhaḥ śaṃkhacakrābhyāṃ padmena gadayohyate \|\| 228 \|\|*

228\. Hṛṣīkeśa is esteemed with Śaṅkha, Gadā, Cakra and Padma. Nṛsiṃha is comprehended through Śaṅkha, Cakra, Padma and Gadā.

## \|\| 2.61.229 \|\|

*acyuta śaṃkhabhṛnnityaṃ gadāpadmarathāṃgavān \|*  
*dakṣiṇādhaḥ karādūhyā vāsudevādayaśca ṣaṭ \|\| 229 \|\|*

229\. Acyuta is a permanent holder of Śaṅkha along with Gadā, Padma and Cakra. The six Mūrtis beginning with Vāsudeva should be comprehended beginning with right lower hand.

## \|\| 2.61.230 \|\|

*vāsudevaśca śaṃkhāri gadājalajabhṛtsadā \|*  
*śaṃkhāṃbuja gadācakrī dhyeyo nārāyaṇo nṛbhiḥ \|\| 230 \|\|*

230\. Vāsudeva always holds Śaṅkha (right lower hand), Cakra (right upper hand), Gadā (upper left hand) and Padma (lower left hand).

## \|\| 2.61.231 \|\|

*śaṃkhī padmī padmanābho jñeyaścakrī gadī mune \|*  
*upeṃdraḥ śaṃkhavānnityaṃ gadāri kamalāyudhaḥ \|\| 231 \|\|*

231\. O sage, Padmanābha should be known as having Śaṅkha, Padma, Cakra and Gadā. Upendra has always Śaṅkha along with Gadā, Cakra and Padma as his weapons.

## \|\| 2.61.232 \|\|

*harirharedaghaṃ śaṃkhī cakrī padmī gadī nṛṇām \|*  
*śaṃkhena gadayā padmacakrābhyāṃ kṛṣṇa ucyate \|\| 232 \|\|*

232\. Equipped with Śaṅkha, Cakra, Padma and Gadā Hari removes the sins of men. Kṛṣṇa is said to be with Śaṅkha, Gadā, Padma and Cakra.

## \|\| 2.61.233 \|\|

*ete bhedā mayā khyātāḥ svamūrtīnāṃ mahāmune \|*  
*yānvijñāya dhruvaṃ martyo bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca viṃdati \|\| 233 \|\|*

233\. O great sage, these different Mùrtis of mine have been enumerated, knowing which a man certainly obtains enjoyment of pleasures and liberation.

## \|\| 2.61.234 \|\|

*evaṃ vadati goviṃde munaye cāgnibiṃdave \|*  
*pakṣīṃdraḥ pakṣavikṣiptavipakṣo'kṣipathaṃ gataḥ \|\| 234 \|\|*

234\. While Govinda was narrating to Sage Agnibindu thus, the Lord of Birds who sets aside his enemies by means of his wings, came within the range of vision.

## \|\| 2.61.235 \|\|

*prāha ca praṇipatyāśu tryakṣasyāgamanaṃ mudā \|*  
*saṃbhrameṇa hṛṣīkeśaḥ kveśa ityavadattataḥ \|\| 235 \|\|*

235\. After quickly bowing down, he joyously announced the arrival of the Three-eyed Lord. Thereupon Hṛṣīkeśa excitedly said, “Where is the Lord?”

## \|\| 2.61.236 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*pratyakṣaḥ kriyatāmeṣa mahāvṛṣabhaketanaḥ \|*  
*yasya dhvajasya ratnārciḥ pūrayedrodasīmimām \|\| 236 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

236\. May this great Bull-emblemed Lord be perceived, the lustre of the jewels of whose banner fills the space between heaven and earth.

## \|\| 2.61.237-240 \|\|

*lokalocananirmāṇa saphalīkaraṇakṣamam \|*  
*koṭimārtaṃḍavidyota pradyotita digānanam \|\| 237 \|\|*

*nirīkṣya puṃḍarīkākṣastryakṣasya vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*vimānināṃ vimānaughaiḥ parītagaganāṃgaṇam \|\| 238 \|\|*

*mahāvādyani nādaughaiḥpratisvānita kaṃdaram \|*  
*vidyādharī parikṣipta puṣpāṃjali sugaṃdhitam \|\| 239 \|\|*

*praṇamya dūrādapica saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*abhyutthātuṃ manaścakre śaṃkhacakragadādharaḥ \|\| 240 \|\|*

237-240. The bull-emblemed chariot was very exquisite. It was capable of making the creating of the eyes of the people fruitful. The faces of the quarters were brightened with the splendour of ten million suns as it were. The entire courtyard of the firmament was covered with aerial chariots of Devas. The caves of mountains echoed with the sounds of great musical instruments. And it was rendered fragrant by handfuls of flowers scattered by Vidyādhara damsels. The Louts-eyed Lord saw the chariot of the Three-eyed Lord from afar and became delighted. Hairs stood on ends and he bowed down his head. The Lord who wielded Śaṅkha, Cakra and Gada desired to get up.

## \|\| 2.61.241 \|\|

*agnibiṃdumatha prāha muktidastu mudāṃnidhiḥ \|*  
*idaṃ sudarśanaṃ cakraṃ spṛśāsavyenapāṇinā \|\| 241 \|\|*

241\. The bestower of salvation, the storehouse of joys told Agnibindu, “Touch this Sudarśana Cakra with your right hand.”

## \|\| 2.61.242 \|\|

*agnibiṃduritiproktaḥ spṛśedyāvatsudarśanam \|*  
*tāvatsudarśano jātaḥ paramānugrahāddhareḥ \|\| 242 \|\|*

242\. On being told, Agnibindu touched Sudarśana. Immediately he became Sudarśanaḥ (‘of excellent knowledge and wisdom’) due to the favour of Hari.

## \|\| 2.61.243 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*jyotīrūpotha sa muniḥ kaustubhe jyotiṣāṃ tanau \|*  
*ekībhūtaḥ kalaśaja biṃdumādhavasevanāt \|\| 243 \|\|*

Skanda said:

243\. By his service of Bindumādhava, the sage assumed the form of luminous splendour, O Pot-born One. He merged as one into Kaustubha, the form of splendour.

## \|\| 2.61.244 \|\|

*biṃdumādhavapādābja bhramarīkṛtamānasāḥ \|*  
*agnibiṃdūpamāṃyāṃti kalaśodbhava niścitam \|\| 244 \|\|*

244\. O Pot-born One, it is definite that those who had made their minds function like bees around the louts-like feet of Bindumādhava became comparable to Agnibindu.

## \|\| 2.61.245 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ sadaiva vastavyaṃ draṣṭavyo biṃdumādhavaḥ \|*  
*śrotavyamidamākhyānaṃ jetavyā jagatāṃgatiḥ \|\| 245 \|\|*

245\. One should always stay in Kāśī. Bindumādhava should be visited. This narrative is to be heard. The (good) goal of the worlds should be attained.

## \|\| 2.61.246 \|\|

*puṇyā paṃcanadotpattiḥ puṇyā mādhavasaṃkathā \|*  
*puṇyo vārāṇasī vāsaḥ saṃbhavetpuṇyajanmanām \|\| 246 \|\|*

246\. The Origin of Pañcanada is conducive to merit. The story of Mādhava is conducive to merit. The residence in Vārāṇasī is meritorious. All this occurs to those of meritorious births.

## \|\| 2.61.247 \|\|

*agnibiṃdoḥ stutiṃ yotra mādhavāgre paṭhiṣyati \|*  
*samṛddhasarvakāmaḥ sa mokṣalakṣmīpatirbhavet \|\| 247 \|\|*

247\. He who reads Agnibindu’s prayer here in front of Mādhava shall have his desires richly fulfilled. He will become master of the glory of salvation.

## \|\| 2.61.248 \|\|

*śrāddhakāle sadā japya midamākhyānamuttamam \|*  
*dvijānāṃ bhuṃjamānānāṃ purastātparatṛptaye \|\| 248 \|\|*

248\. For the sake of highest satisfaction, this excellent narrative should be recited always at the time of Śrāddha, in front of the Brāhmaṇas who take their food.

## \|\| 2.61.249 \|\|

*japtavyamidamākhyānaṃ parvakāle viroṣataḥ \|*  
*puṇye paṃcanadābhyāśe puṇyalakṣmīvivṛddhaye \|\| 249 \|\|*

249\. This narrative should be particularly repeated at the time of festivals, in the holy vicinity of Pañcanada, for the increase of the glory of merit.

## \|\| 2.61.250 \|\|

*paṭhitavyaḥ prayatnena biṃdumādhavasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*śrotavyaḥ parayā bhaktyā bhuktimuktisamṛddhaye \|\| 250 \|\|*

250\. For the fullest realization of enjoyment of pleasures and salvation, the story of the manifestation of Bindumādhava should be assiduously read and listened to with great devotion.

## \|\| 2.61.251 \|\|

*saṃprāpte vāsare viṣṇo rātrau jāgaraṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*śrutvākhyānamidaṃ puṇyaṃ vaikuṃṭhe vasatiṃ labhet \|\| 251 \|\|*

251\. At the time of Harivāsara (i.e. Ekādaśī) a devotee should keep awake during the night. By listening to this narrative of great merit, he will attain residence in Vaikuṇṭha.

## Chapter 62 - Manifestation of the Bull-emblemed, Lord

## \|\| 2.62.1-6 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā skaṃda na tṛptosmi tava vaktreritāṃ kathām \|*  
*atyāścaryakaraṃ proktamākhyānaṃ baiṃdumādhavam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi devadevasamāgamam \|*  
*tārkṣyāttryakṣaḥ samākarṇya divodāsasya ceṣṭitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*viṣṇumāyāprapaṃcaṃ ca kimāha garuḍadhvajam \|*  
*ke ke ca śaṃbhunā sārdhaṃ samīyurmaṃdarādgireḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*brahmaṇeśaḥ kathaṃ dṛṣṭastrapākulita cakṣuṣā \|*  
*kimāha deva brahmāṇaṃ kimuktaṃ bhāsvatāpi ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yoginībhiḥ kimākhyāyi gaṇāhrīṇāḥ kimabruvan \|*  
*etadākhyāhi me skaṃda mahatkautūhalaṃ mayi \|\| 5 \|\|*

*imaṃ praśnaṃ niśamyaiśirmuneḥ kalaśajanmanaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca namaskṛtya śivau praṇatasiddhidau \|\| 6 \|\|*

Agastya said:

1-6. O Skanda, I am not satiated by hearing the story narrated by you. The wonderful description of Bindumādhava has been heard. I desire to hear now the contact between the Lords of Devas. After hearing from Tārkṣya about the activities of Divodāsa and the display of Viṣṇu’s Māyā what did the Threeeyed Lord tell the Garuḍa-emblemed Lord? Who were all those who came from the Mandara mountain along with Śaṃbhu? How was Īśa faced by Brahmā whose eyes were overcome with shame? What did the Lord say to Brahmā? What was said by the Sun-god? What was narrated by the Yoginīs? What did the ashamed Gaṇas say? Describe all this to me, O Skanda. I am very eager to hear.

On hearing these questions of the Pot-born Sage, the son of īśa replied after bowing down to Śiva and Śivā, the bestowers of supernatural powers on those who bow down to them.

## \|\| 2.62.7 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*mune śṛṇu kathāmetāṃ sarvapātakanāśinīm \|*  
*aśeṣavighnaśamanīṃ mahāśreyobhivardhinīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

Skanda said:

7\. O sage, listen to this story that dispels all sins, that subdues obstacles without leaving anything behind and increases great welfare.

## \|\| 2.62.8-9 \|\|

*atha devo'suraripuḥ śrutvā śaṃbhusamāgamam \|*  
*dvijarājāya sa mudā samadātpāritoṣikam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*āyānaṃ śaṃsate śaṃbhorupavārāṇasipriyam \|*  
*brahmāṇamagrataḥ kṛtvā tataścābhyudyayau hariḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Thereafter (Viṣṇu) the Lord inimical to Asuras joyously gave a reward to the king of birds, on hearing the arrival of Śaṃbhu, when he announced the happy arrival of Śaṃbhu near Vārāṇasī. Then Hari kept Brahmā at the head and proceeded forward.

## \|\| 2.62.10 \|\|

*vivasvatā sametaśca tairgaṇaiḥ parito vṛtaḥ \|*  
*yoginībhiranūdyāto gaṇeśamupasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He was accompanied by the Sun-god; he was surrounded by the Gaṇas and followed by the Yoginīs. He was in close touch with Gaṇeśa. (He went hand-in-hand with Gaṇeśa—Comm.).

## \|\| 2.62.11 \|\|

*athanetrātithīkṛtya devadevaṃ vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*maṃkṣu tārkṣyādavāruhya praṇanāma śriyaḥ patiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Immediately after seeing the Bull-emblemed Lord of Devas, the Consort of Śrī quickly got down from Tārkṣya and bowed to him.

## \|\| 2.62.12 \|\|

*pitāmahopi sthaviro bhṛśaṃ namraśirodharaḥ \|*  
*praṇatena mṛḍenaiva praṇamanvinivāritaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The aged Pitāmaha bent down his head immediately. He was prevented from bowing down further by Mṛḍa (Śiva) himself to whom he had already bowed down.

## \|\| 2.62.13 \|\|

*svastyabhyuditapāṇiśca rudrasūktairamaṃtrayat \|*  
*akṣatānyatha sārdrāṇi darśayansaphalānyajaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Showing raw rice grains which were wet along with fruits, the Unborn Lord (Brahmā) chanted Rudra Sūktas with a hand raised up by way of hailing (Svasti).

## \|\| 2.62.14 \|\|

*mauliṃ pādābjayoḥ kṛtvā gaṇeśaḥ satvaro nataḥ \|*  
*mūrdhnyupājighrayāṃcakre haro harṣādgajānanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Gaṇeśa hurriedly prostrated keeping his head on the two lotus-like feet (of Śiva). With great pleasure Hara kissed the head of Gajānana (smelt the crown of the head).

## \|\| 2.62.15 \|\|

*abhyupāveśayaccāpi pariṣvajya nijāsane \|*  
*somanaṃdi prabhṛtayaḥ praṇemurdaṃḍavadgaṇāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He embraced him and made him sit in his own seat. Somanandī and other Gaṇas prostrated themselves like a log of wood.

## \|\| 2.62.16 \|\|

*yoginyopi praṇamyeśaṃ cakrurmaṃgalagāyanam \|*  
*taraṇiḥ praṇanāmātha pramathādhipatiṃ haram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After bowing down to Īśa, the Yoginīs sang auspicious songs. Then the Sun-god bowed down to Hara, the Lord of Pramathas.

## \|\| 2.62.17 \|\|

*khaṃḍeṃduśekharaścātha upasiṃhāsanaṃ harim \|*  
*samupāveśayadvāmapārśve mānapuraḥsaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thereafter the Crescent-moon-crested Lord (Śiva) made Hari sit near his throne on the left side with due honour.

## \|\| 2.62.18 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ dakṣiṇe bhāge pariviśrāṇitāsanam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā saṃbhāvitāḥ sarve śarveṇa praṇatā gaṇāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He offered a seat to Brahmā and made him sit on the right side. All the Gaṇas who had bowed down to him were glanced (kindly) at and honoured thereby by Śarva.

## \|\| 2.62.19 \|\|

*maulicālanamātreṇa yoginyopi prasāditāḥ \|*  
*saṃtoṣito raviścāpi viśeti karasaṃjñayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Yoginīs were favoured by a nodding gesture of the head. Ravi (Sun-god) was rendered satisfied with a gesture of the hand indicating “Sit”.

## \|\| 2.62.20 \|\|

*atha śaṃbhuṃ śatadhṛtiḥ prabaddhakarasaṃpuṭaḥ \|*  
*parivijñāpayāṃcakre prasannavadanāṃbujam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereafter, Brahmā joined his hands together in reverence and submitted to Śaṃbhu whose lotus-like face was beaming with pleasure:

## \|\| 2.62.21 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*bhagavandevadeveśa kṣaṃtavyaṃ girijāpate \|*  
*vārāṇasīṃ samāsādya yadahaṃ nāgataḥ punaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

21\. O Lord, O Lord of Devas, O consort of the Daughter of the Mountain, let me be forgiven for not returning after coming to Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.62.22 \|\|

*prasaṃgatopi kaḥ kāśīṃ prāpya caṃdravibhūṣaṇa \|*  
*kiṃcidvidhātuṃ śaktopi tyajetsthaviratāṃ dadhat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Moon-adorned Lord, who will abandon Kāśī even after casually visiting it? Even when he is old, who will abandon it, if he is capable of doing something?

## \|\| 2.62.23 \|\|

*svarūpato brāhmaṇatvādapākartuṃ na śakyate \|*  
*atha śakto vyapākartuṃ kaḥ puṇye saṃcikīrṣati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Being a Brāhmaṇa, it is not possible to do anything harmful, or even if one is capable of harming, who will desire to do it to a meritorious person?

## \|\| 2.62.24 \|\|

*vibhorapi samājñeyaṃ dharmavartmānusāriṇi \|*  
*na kiṃcidapakartavyaṃ jānatā kenacitkvacita \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. This is the command of the esteemed Lord too that no sensible man should deliberately commit harassment in regard to a person following the righteous path.

## \|\| 2.62.25 \|\|

*kastādṛśi mahījānau puṇyavartmanyataṃdrite \|*  
*kāśīpāle divodāse manāgapi viruddhadhīḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Who will have any adverse intention towards Divodāsa, the king of Kaśī, even slightly? He is a king of such meritorious activities, always alert in following the path of righteousness.

## \|\| 2.62.26-30 \|\|

*niśamyeti vacastuṣṭaḥ śrīkaṃṭhoti viśuddhadhīḥ \|*  
*hasanprovāca dhātāraṃ brahmansarvamavaimyaham \|\| 26 \|\|*

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*ādau tāvadadoṣaṃ hi brahmatvaṃ brāhmaṇasya te \|*  
*vājimedhādhvarāṇāṃ ca tatopi daśakaṃ kṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tatopi vihitaṃ brahmanbhavatā paramaṃ hitam \|*  
*aparādhasahasrāṇi yalliṃgaṃ sthāpitaṃ mama \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yenaikamapi me liṃgaṃ sthāpitaṃ yatra kutracit \|*  
*tasyāparādhaleśopi nāsti sarvāparādhinaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*aparādhasahasrepi brāhmaṇaṃ yoparādhnuyāt \|*  
*dinaiḥ katipayaireva tasyaiśvaryaṃ vinaśyati \|\| 30 \|\|*

26-30. On hearing these words, Śrīkaṇṭha of pure intellect became pleased. Laughingly he said to Brahmā:

## \|\| 2.62.31 \|\|

*iti bruvati deveśepyaṃtarucchvasitaṃ gaṇaiḥ \|*  
*samātṛbhiḥ samaṃtācca vilokyāsyaṃ parasparam \|\| 31 \|\|*

The Lord of Devas said:

O Brahmā, I know everything. First you are a Brāhmaṇa; your defects are to be condoned. Further you have performed ten horse-sacrifices. Further still, much welfare has been carried out by you, O Brahmā. Against thousands of offences, my Liṅga has been installed. Even if one Liṅga of mine was installed by one anywhere, no trace of offence on him remains, even if he may have committed all the offences. If anyone commits any offence against a Brāhmaṇa, though he (the Brāhmaṇa) may have committed a thousands offences, his wealth will perish in a few days.

31\. While the Lord of Devas said this, the Gaṇas and the Mothers heaved sighs of relief looking around at one another’s face.

## \|\| 2.62.32 \|\|

*arkopyavasaraṃ jñātvā natvā śaṃbhuṃ vyajijñapat \|*  
*prasannāsyamumākāṃtaṃ dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭacarācaraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On realizing the opportune moment, Arka (the Sun-god) who looks after mobile and immobile beings, noticed Ṣaṃbhu, the consort of Umā (pleased in his mind) with a beaming face, and submitted thus:

## \|\| 2.62.33-36 \|\|

*arka uvāca \|*  
*nātha kāśīmito gatvā yathāśakti kṛtopadhiḥ \|*  
*akiṃcitkaratāṃ prāptaḥ sahasrakaravānapi \|\| 33 \|\|*

*svadharmapālake tasmindivodāse dharāpatau \|*  
*niścitāgamanaṃ jñātvā devasyāhamiha sthitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*pratīkṣamāṇo deveśa tvadāmanamuttamam \|*  
*vibhajya bahudhātmānaṃ tvadārādhanatatparaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*manorathadrumaścādya phalitaḥ śrīmadīkṣaśāt \|*  
*kiṃcidbhaktilavāṃbhobhiḥ sikto dhyānena puṣpitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Arka said:

33-36. O Lord, after proceeding to Kāśī from youṛ presence, and adopting some strategic steps, I found that I was utterly inefficient though I have a thousand rays, in respect to King Divodāsa who performed his duty righteously, I stayed behind here knowing fully well that Your Lordship will certainly come here. O Lord of Devas, I have been awaiting your esteemed arrival. I divided myself into many forms and was eagerly engaged in propitiating you. My cherished desire has become fruitful now, thanks to the glorious sight of Your Lordship. The tree of my desire was sprinkled with the waters of a modicum of devotion and it has blossomed due to meditation.

## \|\| 2.62.37-38 \|\|

*ityudīritamākarṇya ravervairavilocanaḥ \|*  
*provāca devadeveśo nāparādhyasi bhāskara \|\| 37 \|\|*

*mamaiva kāryaṃ vihtiṃ tvaṃ yadatra vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*yasyāṃ surapraveśo na tasminrājani śāsati \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. On hearing this utterance of Ravi, the Sun-eyed Lord of Devas said: “O Bhāskara (Sun), you are not at fault. You have actually carried out my task since you preferred to stay here where the Suras had no access while that king was ruling.”

## \|\| 2.62.39 \|\|

*iti sūraṃ samāśvāsya devadeva kṛpānidhiḥ \|*  
*gaṇānāśvāsayāmāsa vrīḍā namraśirodharān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After consoling the Sun-god thus, the Lord of Devas, the storehouse of mercy, consoled the Gaṇas who remained bowing down due to shame.

## \|\| 2.62.40 \|\|

*yoginyopi sudṛṣṭvātha śaṃbhunā saṃprasāditāḥ \|*  
*trapābharasamākrāṃta kaṃdharā iva saṃ gatāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Yoginīs too were keenly observed by Śaṃbhu and appeased. They stood close together with their necks pressed down as it were due to the weight of shame.

## \|\| 2.62.41 \|\|

*tato vyāpārayāṃcakre tryakṣo netrāṇi cakriṇi \|*  
*harirna kiṃcidapyūce sarvajñāgre mahāmanāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then the Three-eyed Lord passed his eyes towards the Discus-bearing Lord. Before Sarvajña (Omniscient Śiva), the magnanimous Hari did not say anything.

## \|\| 2.62.42 \|\|

*īśopi śrutavṛttāṃtastārkṣyādgaṇapa śārṅgiṇoḥ \|*  
*manasaiva prasannobhūnna kiṃcitparyabhāṣata \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Īśa who had already heard from Garuḍa the activities of Gaṇeśa and Śārṅgin became mentally pleased, and did not say anything.

## \|\| 2.62.43-44 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāptā golokātpaṃca dhenavaḥ \|*  
*sunaṃdā sumanāścāpi suśīlā surabhistathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*paṃcamī kapilā cāpi sarvāghaughavighaṭṭinī \|*  
*vātsalyadṛṣṭyā bhargasya tāsāmūdhāṃsi susruvuḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. In the meantime five divine cows came there from Goloka, namely Sunandā, Sumanāḥ, Suśīlā, Surabhi and Kapilā the fifth one, the destroyer of all masses of sins. Due to the fondling glance of Bharga (Śiva) their udders flowed.

## \|\| 2.62.45 \|\|

*vavarṣuḥ payasāṃ pūraistadūdhāṃsi payodharāḥ \|*  
*dhārāsārairavicchinnaistāvadyāvaddhrado'bhavat \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. (Like) clouds, their udders showered continuous and unbroken streams of milk till a whirlpool formed itself there.

## \|\| 2.62.46 \|\|

*payaḥpayodhiriva sa dvitīyaḥ praikṣi pārṣadaiḥ \|*  
*deveśa samadhiṣṭhānāttattīrthamabhavatparam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. It was perceived by the attendants like a second Ocean of Milk. With the presence of the Lord of Devas that became a great Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.62.47 \|\|

*kapilā hrada ityākhyāṃ cakre tasya maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tato devājñayā sarve snātāstatra divaukasaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Maheśvara named it Kapilā Hrada (‘Pool of Kapilā’). Thereafter at the behest of the Lord all the heaven-dwellers took their holy ablution there.

## \|\| 2.62.48 \|\|

*āvirāsustatastīrthādatha divyapitāmahāḥ \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā te surāḥ sarve tarpayāṃcakrire mudā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thereupon, the divine grandfathers emerged from the Tīrtha. On seeing them all the Suras joyously offered libations.

## \|\| 2.62.49 \|\|

*agniṣvāttā barhiṣada ājyapāḥ somapāstathā \|*  
*ityādyā divyapitarastṛptāḥ śaṃbhuṃ vyajijñapan \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The divine grandfathers such as Agnīṣvāttas, Barhiṣads, Ājyapas and Somapas as well as others became propitiated. They prayed to Śaṃbhu:

## \|\| 2.62.50-52 \|\|

*devadeva jagannātha bhaktānāmabhayaprada \|*  
*asmiṃstīrthe tvadabhyāśājjātā nastṛptirakṣayā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tasmācchaṃbho varaṃ dehi prasannenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*iti divyapitṝṇāṃ sa śrutvā vākyaṃ vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*śṛṇvatāṃ sarvadevānāmidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*śarvaḥ sarvapitṝṇāṃ vai paratṛptikaraṃ param \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-51a. “O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the universe, O bestower of freedom from fear unto the devotees! We had everlasting contentment in this Tīrtha due to your vicinity. Hence, O Śaṃbhu, grant us a boon with a delighted mind.”

51b-52. On hearing the words of the divine ancestors, Śarva, the Bull-emblemed Lord, said these words with great satisfaction to all the Pitṛs, even as all the Devas were listening:

## \|\| 2.62.53-54 \|\|

*śrīdevadeva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu viṣṇo mahābāho śṛṇu tvaṃ ca pi tāmaha \|*  
*etasminkāpile tīrthe kāpileya payobhṛte \|\| 53 \|\|*

*ye piṃḍānnirvapiṣyaṃti śraddhayā śrāddhadānataḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ pitṝṇāṃ saṃtṛptirbhaviṣyati mamājñayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

The Lord of Devas said:

53-54. Listen, O Viṣṇu of mighty arms; listen you, O Pitāmaha.

If in this Kapilā Tīrtha filled with the milk of Kapilā (and other cows) devotees offer riceballs with great faith as Śrāddha offerings, their ancestors will be pleased at my behest.

## \|\| 2.62.55 \|\|

*anyaṃ viśeṣaṃ vakṣyāmi mahātṛptikaraṃ param \|*  
*kuhūsomasamāyoge dattaṃ śrāddhamihākṣayam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I shall speak another extremely satisfying thing. The Śrāddha offered here when Monday and new-moon day coincide, is everlasting in its benefit.

## \|\| 2.62.56 \|\|

*saṃvartakāle saṃprāpte jalarāśirjalānyapi \|*  
*kṣīyaṃte na kṣayatyatra śrāddhaṃ somakuhū kṛtam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. During Saṃvarta period (i.e. ‘annihilation of all created beings’) all waters and water reservoirs dry up and perish; but the Śrāddha performed here during the new-moon-Mon-day conjunction is never wasted.

## \|\| 2.62.57 \|\|

*amāsomasamāyoge śrāddhaṃ yadyatra labhyate \|*  
*tīrthe kāpiladhāresmingayayā puṣkareṇa kim \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. If a Śrāddha can be performed here in the Kāpiladhāra Tīrtha during new-moon-Monday conjunction, of what avail is Gayā and Puṣkara?

## \|\| 2.62.58 \|\|

*gadādharabhavānyatra yatra tvaṃ ca pitāmaha \|*  
*vṛṣadhvajosmyahaṃ yatra phalgustatra na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Where you are, O Gadādhara, O Pitāmaha, where you too are and where I the bull-emblemed one am, there certainly is the river Phalgu (the river in Gayā).

## \|\| 2.62.59 \|\|

*divyāṃtarikṣabhaumāni yāni tīrthāni sarvataḥ \|*  
*tānyatra nivasiṣyaṃti darśe somadinānvite \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. All those Tīrthas, stationed in heaven, firmament and earth will reside here on a day when new-moon coincides with Monday.

## \|\| 2.62.60 \|\|

*kurukṣetre naimiṣe ca gaṃgāsāgarasaṃgame \|*  
*grahaṇe śrāddhato yatsyāttattīrthe vārṣabhadhvaje \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. What is obtained through performing Śrāddha at the time of eclipses in Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa and the confluence of Gaṅgā and the ocean can be obtained in the Tīrtha of Vṛṣabhadhvaja.

## \|\| 2.62.61-64 \|\|

*asya tīrthasya nāmāni yāni divya pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*tānyahaṃ kathayiṣyāmi bhavatāṃ tṛptidānyalam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*madhusraveti prathamameṣā puṣkariṇī smṛtā \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyā tato jñeyā tato'sau kṣīranīradhiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*vṛṣabhadhvajatīrthaṃ ca tīrthaṃ paitāmahaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*tato gadādharākhyaṃ ca pitṛtīrthaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tataḥ kāpiladhāraṃ vai sudhākhaniriyaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ śivagayākhyaṃ ca jñeyaṃ tīrthamidaṃ śubham \|\| 64 \|\|*

61-64. O divine grandfathers, I shall tell you all the names of the Tlrtha. They are the bestowers of satisfaction on you all.

At first this Puṣkariṇī is remembered as (1) Madhusravā. Thereafter it should be known as (2) Kṛtakṛtyā, then (3) Kṛīranīradhi, (4) Vṛṣabhadhvaja Tīrtha, (5) Pitāmaha Tīrtha, (6) Gadādhara Tīrtha, (7) Pitṛ Tīrtha, (8) Kāpiladhāra, (9) Sudhākhani, and (10) Śivagayā. Thus this auspicious Tīrtha is known by ten names.

## \|\| 2.62.65 \|\|

*etāni daśa nāmāni tīrthasyāsya pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*bhavatāṃ tṛptikārīṇi vināpi śrāddhatarpaṇaiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O grandfathers, these are the ten names of this Tīrtha. Even without Śrāddhas and libations they bring in satisfaction unto you all.

## \|\| 2.62.66 \|\|

*sūryeṃdu saṃgame yetra pitṝṇāṃ tṛptikāmukāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayiṣyaṃti teṣāṃ śrāddhamanaṃtakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Those who are desirous of the satisfaction of the Pitṛs, should feed Brāhmaṇas at the time of the conjunction of the sun and the moon (new-moon day). Their Śrāddha is infinite (in fruit).

## \|\| 2.62.67 \|\|

*śrāddhe pitṝṇāṃ saṃtṛptyai dāsyaṃti kapilāṃ śubhām \|*  
*yetra teṣāṃ pitṛgaṇo vasetkṣīrodarodhasi \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. If a devotee makes gifts of auspicious Kapilā (tawny) cows at the time of Śrāddha for the satisfaction of the Pitṭs, the ancestors shall stay on the shores of the Milk Ocean.

## \|\| 2.62.68 \|\|

*vṛṣotsargaḥ kṛto yaistu tīrthesminvārṣabhadhvaje \|*  
*aśvamedhapuroḍāśaiḥ pitarastena tarpitāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. If Vṛṣotsarga (setting free a young bull to roam at will) is performed in this Tīrtha of Vṛṣabhadhvaja, the Pitṛs will be propitiated as though through the Puroḍāśa (oblations) in horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.62.69 \|\|

*gayātoṣṭaguṇaṃ puṇyamasmiṃstīrthe pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*amāyāṃ somayuktāyāṃ śrāddhaiḥ kāpiladhārike \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O grandfathers, through Śrāddhas in the Kāpiladhārika Tīrtha on a new-moon day coinciding with a Monday, the merit is eight times that performed at Gayā.

## \|\| 2.62.70 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ garbhe'bhavatsrāvo ye' daṃtajananāmṛtāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tṛptirbhavennūnaṃ tīrthe kāpiladhārike \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Those who become dead through abortion and those who die before teeth are cut, become redeemed through the Kāpiladhārika Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.62.71 \|\|

*adattamauṃjīdānā ye ye cādāraparigrahāḥ \|*  
*tebhyo nirvāpitaṃ piṃḍamiha hyakṣayatāṃ vrajet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Balls of rice offered here for the redemption of (those who die) before the investiture with the sacred thread and before marriage, become everlasting.

## \|\| 2.62.72 \|\|

*agnidāhamṛtā ye vai nāgnidāhaśca yeṣu vai \|*  
*te sarve tṛptimāyāṃti tīrthe kāpiladhārike \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. In the Kāpiladhārika Tīrtha, all these become satisfied: those who die on being burnt by fire (accidental) and those who are not cremated in fire.

## \|\| 2.62.73 \|\|

*aurddhvadaihikahīnā ye ṣoḍaśa śrāddhavarjitāḥ \|*  
*te tṛptimadhigacchaṃti ghṛtakulyāṃ nivāpataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Those who were denied religious funeral rites and (the requisite) sixteen Śrāddhas get satisfaction by offering oblation at Ghṛtakulyā (i.e. Kṛtakṛtyā).

## \|\| 2.62.74 \|\|

*aputrāśca mṛtā ye vai yeṣāṃ nāstyukapradaḥ \|*  
*tepi tṛptiṃ parāṃ yāṃti madhusravasi tarpitāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. If libations are offered in Madhusravā all these derive satisfaction: those who die without male issues or heir for offering libations.

## \|\| 2.62.75 \|\|

*apamṛtyumṛtā ye vai coravidyujjalādibhiḥ \|*  
*teṣāmiha kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ jāyate sugatipradam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. To those who meet with unnatural death or are killed by thieves, through lightning strokes or by drowning in water Śrāddha can be offered here and that yields good goal.

## \|\| 2.62.76 \|\|

*ātmaghātena nidhanaṃ yaiṣāmihavikamarṇām \|*  
*tepi tṛptiṃ labhaṃtetra piṃḍaiḥ śivagayākṛtaiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Those who commit misdeeds and commit suicide also derive satisfaction (of redemption) through balls of rice offered at Śivagayā.

## \|\| 2.62.77 \|\|

*pitṛgotre mṛtā ye vai mātṛpakṣe ca ye mṛtāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmatra kṛtaḥ piṃḍo bhavedakṣayatṛptidaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The balls of rice offered here to the dead ancestors of father’s Gotra and mother’s side, shall become the yielders of everlasting satisfaction.

## \|\| 2.62.78 \|\|

*patnīvarge mṛtā ye vai mitravarge ca ye mṛtāḥ \|*  
*te sarve tṛptimāyāṃti tarpitā vārṣabhadhvaje \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. If libations are offered at Vṛṣabhadhvaja Tīrtha, those who die among the relatives on wife’s side or on friend’s side also derive satisfaction.

## \|\| 2.62.79 \|\|

*brahmakṣatraviśāṃ vaṃśe śūdravaṃśeṃ'tyajeṣu ca \|*  
*yeṣāṃ nāmagṛhītvātra dīyate te samuddhṛtāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Whether the dead ones belong to the families of Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras or Antyajas, if their names are uttered and offerings are made, they become redeemed.

## \|\| 2.62.80 \|\|

*tiryagyoni mṛtā ye vai ye piśācatvamāgatāḥ \|*  
*tepyūrdhvagatimāyāṃti tṛptāḥ kāpiladhārike \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Through offering libations in the Kāpiladhārika Tīrtha all these are lifted to higher status: those who die during transmigration among brutes or those who become ghosts and vampires.

## \|\| 2.62.81 \|\|

*ye tu mānuṣalokesminpitaro martyayonayaḥ \|*  
*te divyayonayaḥ syurvai madhusravasi tarpitāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. If libations are offered in Madhusravas, the Pitṛs who are reborn among men in the mortal world become celestial beings.

## \|\| 2.62.82 \|\|

*ye divyaloke pitaraḥ puṇyairdevatvamāgatāḥ \|*  
*te brahmaloke gacchaṃti tṛptāstīrthe vṛṣadhvaje \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. If libations are offered in the Vṛṣabhadhvaja Tīrtha, those Pitṛs who, through Puṇyas, have gone to the celestial world and assumed the form of Devas, go to Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.62.83 \|\|

*kṛte kṣīramayaṃ tīrthaṃ tretāyāṃ madhumatpunaḥ \|*  
*dvāpare sarpiṣā pūrṇaṃ kalau jalamayaṃ bhavet \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. This Tīrtha is full of milk in Kṛtayuga; full of honey in Tretā, full of ghee in Dvāpara and full of water in Kali age.

## \|\| 2.62.84-86 \|\|

*sīmābahirgatamapi jñeyaṃ tīrthamidaṃ śubham \|*  
*madhye vārāṇasi śreṣṭhaṃ mama sānnidhyato naraiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*kāśīsthitairyato darśi dhvajo meṣavṛṣalāṃchanaḥ \|*  
*vṛṣadhvajena nāmnātaḥ sthāsyāmyatra pitāmahāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*pitāmahena sahito gadādharasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*raviṇā pārṣadaiḥ sārdhaṃ tuṣṭaye vaḥ pitāmahāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

84-86. This Tīrtha should be known as auspicious though it is beyond the frontiers. Within Vārāṇasī this is very excellent due to my close presence. Since my banner with the emblem of a bull was observed by the men staying in Kāśī, O grandfathers, I shall stay here under the name of Vṛṣabhadhvaja in the company of Pitāmaha (Brahmā), Gadādhara, Ravi and the attendants for your satisfaction, O grandfathers.

## \|\| 2.62.87 \|\|

*iti yāvadvaraṃ datte pitṛbhyo vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*tāvannadī samāgatya praṇamyeśaṃ vyajijñapat \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Even as, with these words, the Bull-bannered Lord was granting boons to the grandfathers, Nandin came there, bowed down to the Lord and submitted:

## \|\| 2.62.88-94 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*vihitaḥ syadanaḥ sajjastatostu vijayodayaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭau kaṃṭhīravā yatra yatrokṣṇāmaṣṭakaṃ śubham \|\| 88 \|\|*

*yatrebhāḥ paribhāṃtyaṣṭau yatrāṣṭau javino hayāḥ \|*  
*manaḥ saṃyamanaṃ yatra kaśāpāṇi vyavasthitam \|\| 89 \|\|*

*gaṃgāyamunayorīṣe cakre pavanadevatā \|*  
*sāyaṃprātarmaye cakre chatraṃ dyaurmaṃḍalaṃ śuci \|\| 90 \|\|*

*tārāvalīmayāḥ kīlā āheyā upanāyakāḥ \|*  
*śrutayo mārgadarśinyaḥ smṛtayo rathaguptayaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇādhūrdṛḍhā yatra makhā yatrābhirakṣakāḥ \|*  
*āsanaṃ praṇavo yatra gāyatrīpādapīṭhabhūḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*sāṃgā vyāhṛtayo yatra śubhā sopānavīthikāḥ \|*  
*sūryācaṃdramasau yatra satataṃ dvārarakṣakau \|\| 93 \|\|*

*agnirmakaratuṃḍaśca rathabhūḥ kaumudīmayī \|*  
*dhvajadaṃḍo mahāmeruḥ patākā haskaraprabhā \|\| 94 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

88-94. The chariot has been kept ready. May the victory procession start. There are eight lions there (i.e. Mūlaprakṛti and the seven Tattvas beginning with Mahat). There are eight splendid bulls (eight Dhātus—constituents of the body). Eight elephants (those of the quarters) shine there. There are eight fast horses (Citta, Ahaṃkāra, Buddhi and five sense-organs). The controlling mind with whip in hand is seated there. The chariot poles are Gaṅgā and Yamuna. Mornings and evenings are the two wheels presided over by Pavana (Wind-god). The clean umbrella is the region of heaven. Clusters of stars constitute the nails. Serpents are the binding cords. Śrutis are the path finders. Smṛtis are the protecting chariot-fenders. Dakṣiṇā is the firm yoke. Makhas (Sacrifices) are the guards. Praṇava is the seat. Gāyatrī is the footstool. The Vyāhṛtis with the ancillaries are the series of steps. The Sun and the Moon are the perpetual gatekeepers. Agni is the snout-like projection, shaped like an alligator. Moonlight constitutes the chariot-ground. Mahāmeru is the flagstaff. The lustre of the Sun is the banner. The Goddess of Speech herself is the holder of chariot.

## \|\| 2.62.95-98 \|\|

*svayaṃ vāgdevatā yatra caṃcaccāmaradhāriṇī \|*  
*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śailādineti vijñapto devadeva umāpatiḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*kṛtanīrājanavidhiraṣṭabhirdevamātṛbhiḥ \|*  
*pinākapāṇiruttasthau dattahastotha śārṅgiṇā \|\| 96 \|\|*

*ninādo divyavādyānāṃ rodasī paryapūrayat \|*  
*gītamaṃgalagīrbhiśca cāraṇairanuvardhitaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*tena divyaninādena badhirīkṛtadiṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*āhūtā iva ājagmurviṣvagbhuvanavāsinaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

Skanda said:

95-98. The Lord of Devas, the Consort of Umā, was informed thus by Śailādi (Nandikeśvara). The eight divine Mothers performed the Nīrājana rite. Thereupon the Pināka-wielding Lord stood up supported by the hands of Śārṅgin (Viṣṇu). The sound of the divine musical instruments filled the space between heaven and earth. It was heightened by the Cāraṇas who sang auspicious songs. The quarters became deafened by that divine sound. As though summoned by it, the residents of all the worlds around came there.

## \|\| 2.62.99 \|\|

*devākoṭyastrayastriṃśadgaṇāḥ koṭyayutadvayam \|*  
*navakoṭyastu cāmuṃḍā bhairavyaḥ koṭisaṃmitāḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The Devas were thirty-three crores in number; the Gaṇas were one crore and two hundred thousand; there were nine crores of Cāmuṇḍās and one crore Bhairavīs.

## \|\| 2.62.100 \|\|

*ṣaḍānanāḥ kumārāśca mayūravaravāhanāḥ \|*  
*mamānugāḥ samāyātāḥ koṭayoṣṭau mahābalāḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Eight crores of highly powerful followers of mine came there; they were six-faced, Kumāras and peacock-vehicled.

## \|\| 2.62.101 \|\|

*āyayuḥ koṭayaḥ sapta sphuratparaśupāṇayaḥ \|*  
*picaṃḍilā mahāvegā vighnavighnā gajānanāḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Seven crores of elephant-faced gods with huge bellies came there in great speed. Wielding shining axes in their hands, they are reputed to be obstacles unto obstacles.

## \|\| 2.62.102 \|\|

*ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi munayo brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*tāvatopi samājagmustatratye gṛhamedhinaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Eighty-six thousand sages expounding the Vedas came there. There were as many householders too.

## \|\| 2.62.103 \|\|

*nāgānāṃ koṭayastisraḥ pātālatalavāsinām \|*  
*dānavānāṃ ca daityānāṃ dve dve koṭī śivātmanām \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. There were three crores of serpents residing in the nether regions; two crores of each of these—the Dānavas and the Daityas of auspicious souls.

## \|\| 2.62.104 \|\|

*gaṃdharvā niyutānyaṣṭau koṭyardhaṃ yakṣarakṣasām \|*  
*vidyādharāṇāmayutaṃ niyutadvayasaṃyutam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. There were eight million Gandharvas; Yakṣas and Rākṣasas were half a crore (five million). Vidyādharas were two million and one hundred thousand.

## \|\| 2.62.105 \|\|

*tathā ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi divyāścāpsarasaḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*gomātaro'ṣṭau lakṣāṇi suparṇānyayutāni ṣaṭ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. There were sixty thousand celestial damsels of great splendour, eight hundred thousand Gomātṛs (Cow-mothers) and six hundred thousand Suparṇas.

## \|\| 2.62.106 \|\|

*sāgarāḥ sapta saṃprāptā nānāratnopadapradāḥ \|*  
*saritāṃ ca sahasrāṇi trīṇi paṃcāyutāni ca \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The seven Oceans came there proffering different kinds of jewels. There were fifty-three thousand Rivers.

## \|\| 2.62.107 \|\|

*girayo'ṣṭau sahasrāṇi vanaspatiśatatrayam \|*  
*ājagmurdiggajā aṣṭau yatra devaḥ pinākadhṛk \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Eight thousand Mountains, three hundred Vanaspatis (varieties of trees and herbs) and eight Diggajas (elephants supporting the quarters) came to the place where the Pināka-yielding Lord was present.

## \|\| 2.62.108 \|\|

*etaiḥ sametaḥ saṃtuṣṭaḥ pariṣṭuta itastataḥ \|*  
*śrīkaṃṭho rathamāruhya kāśīṃ prāviśaduttamām \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Accompanied by these and eulogized everywhere there the contented Lord Śrīkaṇṭha rode in the chariot and entered the auspicious Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.62.109 \|\|

*sa girīṃdrasutastryakṣo mudāṃ dhāma mudāṃ khaniḥ \|*  
*kāśīṃ praikṣiṣṭa saṃhṛṣṭastriviṣṭapa samutkaṭām \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Accompanied by the Daughter of Lord of Mountains, the Three-eyed Lord, the abode of joys, the mine of bliss saw Kāśī which is far better than even heaven.

## \|\| 2.62.110 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śrutvākhyānamidaṃ puṇyaṃ koṭijanmāghanāśanam \|*  
*paṭhitvā pāṭhayitvā ca śivasāyujyamāpnuyāt \|\| 110 \|\|*

Skanda said:

110\. By listening to this meritorious narrative that destroys the sins of ten million births, by reading it and by making it read (by others) one shall attain identity with Śiva.

## \|\| 2.62.111 \|\|

*śrāddhakāle viśeṣeṇa paṭhanīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*akṣayaṃ tadbhavecchrāddhaṃ pitṛtuṣṭikaraṃ param \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Particularly during the Śrāddha period this should be assiduously read. That Śrāddha shall be everlasting and extremely pleasing to the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 2.62.112 \|\|

*vṛṣabhadhvaja māhātmyaṃ paṭhitvā śivasannidhau \|*  
*pratyahaṃ varṣamātraṃ tu hyaputraḥ putravānbhavet \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. By reading the greatness of Vṛṣabhadhvaja (Tīrtha) in the presence of Śiva everyday for a year, a man without a son will beget a son.

## \|\| 2.62.113 \|\|

*viśveśituḥ saṃpraveśo yaḥ kāśyāṃ samudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*paramānaṃdakaṃdasya bījametatsuniścitam \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. The story of the grand entry into Kāśī of Viśveśvara that has been narrated is certainly the seed of the bulbous root of great bliss.

## \|\| 2.62.114 \|\|

*paṭhitvaitanmudākhyānaṃ praviśedyo navaṃ gṛham \|*  
*sa sarvasaukhyanilayo bhavedeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. After joyously reading this narrative one should enter a new house. There is no doubt in this that he will be the enjoyer of every kind of happiness.

## \|\| 2.62.115 \|\|

*trailokyānaṃdajanakametadākhyānamuttamam \|*  
*asya śravaṇamātreṇa viśveśaḥ saṃprasīdati \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. This excellent narrative causes delight unto the three worlds. Merely by listening to this Viśveśvara becomes pleased.

## \|\| 2.62.116 \|\|

*alabhyalābho devasya jātotra hi yataḥ paraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kāśī praveśākhyaṃ japyamākhyānamuttamam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Since the Lord had the great acquisition of what was unobtainable, the narrative named Kāśīpraveśa is an excellent Japya (holy text to be recited).

## Chapter 63 - The Story of Jyeṣṭheśa

## \|\| 2.63.1 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā kāśīṃ dṛgānaṃdāṃ tārakāre purāriṇā \|*  
*kimakāri samācakṣva prāptāṃ bahumanorathaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Agastya said:

1\. O Slayer of Tāraka, tell me what was done by Purāri (Śiva) after seeing Kāśī that gives delight to the eyes and was attained as fulfilment of his highly cherished desires.

## \|\| 2.63.2 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*pativratāpate 'gastya śṛṇu vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*mṛgāṃkalakṣmaṇotkaṃṭhaṃ kāśī netrātithīkṛtā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

2\. O husband of a chaste lady (Lopāmudrā), O Agastya, listen, I shall tell you everything in full. Kāśī was made a guest of his vision (i.e. attained) with great eagerness by the Moon-crested Lord.

## \|\| 2.63.3 \|\|

*atha sarvajñanāthena bhaktavatsalacetasā \|*  
*jaigīṣavyo muniśreṣṭho guhāṃ tastho nirīkṣitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Thereafter, Jaigīṣavya, an excellent sage, was seen living within a cave by Lord Saravajña (Śiva) whose mind is very affectionate towards his devotees.

## \|\| 2.63.4-5 \|\|

*yamanehasamārabhya madaṃrādriṃ viniryayau \|*  
*adrīṃdra sutayā sārdhaṃ rudreṇokṣeṃdragāminā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*taṃ vāsaraṃ puraskṛtya jagrāha niyamaṃ dṛḍham \|*  
*jaigīṣavyo mahāmedhāḥ kuṃbhayone mahākṛtī \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Ever since the day Rudra set out to the Mandara mountain riding on the Lord of Bulls along with the Daughter of the Mountain, O Pot-born One, the blessed Jaigīṣavya of great intellect took a firm resolve:

## \|\| 2.63.6 \|\|

*viṣamekṣaṇa pādābjaṃ samīkṣiṣye yadā punaḥ \|*  
*tadāṃbuvipruṣamapi bhakṣayiṣyāmi cetyaho \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. ‘I shall take in even a drop of water only when I shall be able to see the louts-like feet of the Three-eyed Lord.’

## \|\| 2.63.7 \|\|

*kutaściddhāraṇāyogādathavā śaṃbhvanugrahāta \|*  
*anaśnannapibanyogī jaigīṣavyaḥ sthito mune \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O sage, perhaps due to his Yogic Dhāraṇā power or due to Śaṃbhu’s grace, Yogi Jaigīṣavya managed to survive without eating and without drinking.

## \|\| 2.63.8 \|\|

*taṃ śaṃbhureva jānāti nānyo jānāti kaścana \|*  
*ataeva tataḥ prāptaḥ prathamaṃ pramathādhipaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. None else but only Śaṃbhu knew this fact. For the same reason as soon as he returned from that place (Mandara), the Lord of Pramathas came there at the outset.

## \|\| 2.63.9 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ somavārānurādhayoḥ \|*  
*tatparvaṇi mahāyātrā kartavyā tatra mānavaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Hence men should perform great religious festival there on the fourteenth day in the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha or when Monday coincides with Anurādhā Star.

## \|\| 2.63.10 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhasthānaṃ tataḥ kāśyāṃ tadābhūdapi puṇyadam \|*  
*tatra liṃgaṃ samabhavatsvayaṃ jyeṣṭheśvarābhidham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Therefore, that spot in Kāśī became a very important place of pilgrimage according merit. There the Liṅga named Jyeṣṭheśvara manifested itself.

## \|\| 2.63.11 \|\|

*talliṃgadarśanātpuṃsāṃ pāpaṃ janmaśatārjitam \|*  
*tamorkodayamāpyeva tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Just as darkness vanishes as soon as the Sun rises, so sin incurred in the course of a hundred births is destroyed instantaneously as soon as the Liṅga is seen by men.

## \|\| 2.63.12 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhavāpyāṃ naraḥ snātvā tarpayitvā pitāmahān \|*  
*jyeṣṭheśvaraṃ samālokya na bhūyo jāyate bhuvi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If a man takes his holy bath in Jyeṣṭhavāpī, offers libations to the ancestors and visits Jyeṣṭheśvara, he is not reborn on the earth thereafter.

## \|\| 2.63.13 \|\|

*āvirāsītsvayaṃ tatra jyeṣṭheśvara samīpataḥ \|*  
*sarvasiddhipradā gaurī jyeṣṭhāśreṣṭhā samaṃtataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There very near Jyeṣṭheśvara Gaurī who bestows all spiritual powers all-round, appeared as Jyeṣṭhā and Śreṣṭhā.

## \|\| 2.63.14 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe māsi sitāṣṭamyāṃ tatra kāryo mahotsavaḥ \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ sarvasaṃpatsamṛddhaye \|\| 14 \|\|*
