14\. For the sake of increase in wealth, a great festival should be celebrated there on the eighth day in the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha and the devotees should keep awake during the night.

## \|\| 2.63.15 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhāṃ gaurīṃ namaskṛtya jyeṣṭhavāpī pariplutā \|*  
*saubhāgyabhājanaṃ bhūyādyoṣā saubhāgyabhāgapi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A woman who plunges herself into the Jyeṣṭhavāpī and bows down to Jyeṣṭhā Gaurī shall enjoy conjugal bliss and great fortune.

## \|\| 2.63.16 \|\|

*nivāsaṃ kṛtavāñśaṃbhustasminsthāne yataḥ svayam \|*  
*nivāseśa iti khyātaṃ liṃgaṃ tatra paraṃ tataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Since Śaṃbhu himself made his stay there at that spot, the great Liṅga there became well-known thereafter as Nivāsésa.

## \|\| 2.63.17 \|\|

*nivāseśvaraliṃgasya sevanātsarvasaṃpadaḥ \|*  
*nivasaṃti gṛhe nityaṃ nityaṃ pratipadaṃ punaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By resorting to Nivāseśvara Liṅga riches of all kinds abide in the house at every step.

## \|\| 2.63.18 \|\|

*kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ vidhānena jyeṣṭhasthāne narottamaḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhāṃ tṛptiṃ dadātyeva pitṛbhyo madhusarpiṣā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After performing Śrāddha in accordance with the injunctions in Jyeṣṭha Sthāna, a most excellent man gives excellent satisfaction to the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 2.63.19 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhatīrthe naraḥ kāśyāṃ dattvā dānāni śaktitaḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhānsvargānavāpnoti naro mokṣaṃ ca gacchati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By making many gifts in accordance with his capacity in the Jyeṣṭha Tīrtha in Kāśī, a man attains excellent heaven and salvation as well.

## \|\| 2.63.20 \|\|

*jyeṣṭheśvaro rcyaḥ prathamaṃ kāśyāṃ śreyorthibhirnaraiḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhāgaurī tatobhyarcyā sarvajyeṣṭhamabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. At the outset, Jyeṣṭheśvara should be worshipped in Kāśī by men who seek welfare. Then Jyeṣṭhā Gaurī should be worshipped by men who desire to attain the state of being the most excellent one among all.

## \|\| 2.63.21 \|\|

*atha naṃdinamāhūya dhūrjaṭiḥ sa kṛpānidhiḥ \|*  
*śṛṇvatāṃ sarvadevānāmidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thereafter, calling Nandin, Dhūrjaṭi, the storehouse of mercy, spoke these words even as all the Devas were listening:

## \|\| 2.63.22 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śailāde praviśāśu tvaṃ guhāstyatra manoharā \|*  
*tadaṃtaresti me bhakto jaigīṣavyastapodhanaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

22\. O son of Śilāda, there is a beautiful cave here; you enter it quickly; therein stays my devotee, Sage Jaigīṣavya.

## \|\| 2.63.23 \|\|

*mahāniyamavānnaṃdistvagasthisnāyu śeṣitaḥ \|*  
*tamihānaya madbhaktaṃ maddarśana dṛḍhavratam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He practises great observances and restraints. Only the skin, bones and sinews are left of him. Fetch unto me my devotee, steadfast in his resolve to see me.

## \|\| 2.63.24 \|\|

*yadāprabhṛtyagāṃ kāśyā maṃdaraṃ sarvasuṃdaram \|*  
*mahāniyamavāneṣa tadārabhyojjhitāśanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Ever since I left Kāśī and went to Mandara, a most beautiful (mountain), he has observed great restraints and has stopped taking in food.

## \|\| 2.63.25 \|\|

*gṛhāṇa līlākamalamidaṃ pīyūṣapoṣaṇam \|*  
*anena tasya gātrāṇi spṛśa sadyaḥ subṛṃhiṇā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Take this toy-lotus which will nourish him like nectar. Touch his limbs with this which will cause excellent nourishment.

## \|\| 2.63.26 \|\|

*tato naṃdī samādāya tallīlākamalaṃ vibhoḥ \|*  
*praṇamya devadeveśamāviśadgahvarāṃ guhām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thereupon, Nandin took that toy-lotus of the Lord, bowed down to the Lord of the chiefs of Devas and entered the deep cave.

## \|\| 2.63.27 \|\|

*naṃdī dṛṣṭvātha taṃ tatra dhāraṇādṛḍhamānasam \|*  
*tapogni pariśuṣkāṃgaṃ kamalena samaspṛśat \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On seeing him with his mind fixed in the Dhāraṇā state and the limbs dried up in the fire of austerities, Nandin touched him with the lotus.

## \|\| 2.63.28 \|\|

*tapāṃte vṛṣṭisaṃyogācchālūra iva koṭare \|*  
*ullalāsa sa yogīṃdraḥ sparśamātrāttadabjajāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. At the very touch of that lotus, that eminent Yogin became happy and fresh like a frog in a crevice at the end of summer, due to the association (touch) of rain.

## \|\| 2.63.29 \|\|

*atha naṃdī samādāya satvaraṃ munipuṃgavam \|*  
*devadevasya pādāgre namaskṛtya nyapātayat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then Nandin immediately took the great sage with him, bowed down in front of the Lord of Devas and made him (the sage) fall at his feet.

## \|\| 2.63.30 \|\|

*jaigīṣavyotha saṃbhrāṃtaḥ purato vīkṣya śaṃkaram \|*  
*vāmāṃgasanniviṣṭādritanayaṃ praṇanāma ha \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Seeing Śaṅkara in front, Jaigīṣavya became bewildered. He bowed down to the Lord with the Daughter of the Mountain resting on his left side.

## \|\| 2.63.31 \|\|

*praṇamya daṃḍavadbhūmau pariluṭhya samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā sa muniścaṃdraśekharam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After prostrating himself like a log of wood on the ground and rolling round, the sage eulogized the moon-crested Lord with great devotion.

## \|\| 2.63.32 \|\|

*jaigīṣavya uvāca \|*  
*namaḥ śivāya śāṃtāya sarvajñāya śubhātmane \|*  
*jagadānaṃdakaṃdāya paramānaṃdahetave \|\| 32 \|\|*

Jaigīṣavya said:

(Prayer by Jaigīṣavya)

32\. Obeisance to Śiva, the quiescent, omniscient Lord of auspicious soul, the bulbous root (concentrated form) of the bliss of the universe, the cause of supreme delight!

## \|\| 2.63.33 \|\|

*arūpāya sarūpāya nānārūpadharāya ca \|*  
*virūpākṣāya vidhaye vidhiviṣṇustutāya ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. (Obeisance) to the Lord endowed with form, without form and having different forms; to the three-eyed Lord eulogized by Vidhi (Brahmā) and Viṣṇu; to the cause of extreme blessedness.

## \|\| 2.63.34 \|\|

*sthāvarāya namastubhyaṃ jaṃgamāya namostute \|*  
*sarvātmane namastubhyaṃ namaste paramātmane \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Obeisance to you, the stationary one; obeisance to you, the mobile one; obeisance to you, the soul of all. Hail to you, the supreme soul!

## \|\| 2.63.35 \|\|

*namastrailokyakāmyāya kāmāṃgadahanāya ca \|*  
*namo śeṣaviśeṣāya namaḥ śeṣāṃgadāya te \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Obeisance to the Lord cove table to the three worlds; to the Lord who burned down the physical form of Kama; obeisance to the Lord according special significance to things, to the entire (creation); obeisance to you having Śeṣa as your bracelet.

## \|\| 2.63.36 \|\|

*śrīkaṃṭhāya namastubhyaṃ viṣakaṃṭhāya te namaḥ \|*  
*vaikuṃṭhavaṃdyapādāya namo'kuṃṭhitaśaktaye \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Bow to you, O Śrīkaṇṭha; obeisance to you having poison sticking to the throat; obeisance to the Lord whose feet are venerable unto Vaikuṇṭha (Viṣṇu); obeisance to the Lord of unobstructed prowess.

## \|\| 2.63.37 \|\|

*namaḥ śaktyardhadehāya videhāya sudehine \|*  
*sakṛtpraṇāmamātreṇa dehidehanivāriṇe \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Obeisance to the Lord half of whose body is taken over by Śakti; obeisance to the Lord without physical form; to the Lord having excellent physical form; to the lord who prevents further acquisition of a body by an embodied soul when bowed down to even once.

## \|\| 2.63.38 \|\|

*kālāya kālakālāya kālakūṭa viṣādine \|*  
*vyālayajñopavītāya vyālabhūṣaṇadhāriṇe \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Obeisance to the Lord identified with Kāla (Time); to Kālakāla (‘Slayer of god of Death’); to the Lord who devoured the poison Kālakūṭa; to the Lord having serpents for the sacred thread; to the Lord wearing serpents as ornaments.

## \|\| 2.63.39 \|\|

*namaste khaṃḍaparaśo namaḥ khaṃḍeṃ dudhāriṇe \|*  
*khaṃḍitāśeṣa duḥkhāya khaḍgakheṭakadhāriṇe \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Obeisance to you, O Khaṇḍaparaśu (Śiva); obeisance to the Lord wearing (on his head) the crescent moon; to the Lord who dispels the misery of everyone; to the Lord equipped with sword and shield.

## \|\| 2.63.40 \|\|

*gīrvāṇagītanāthāya gaṃgākallolamāline \|*  
*gaurīśāya girīśāya giriśāya guhāraṇe \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Obeisance to the Lord sung about by Devas; to the Lord having the waves of Gaṅgā serving the purpose of a garland; to the consort of Gaurī; to the Lord of the mountain; to Giriśa; to the begetter of Guha.

## \|\| 2.63.41 \|\|

*caṃdrārdhaśuddhabhūṣāya caṃdrasūryāgnicakṣuṣe \|*  
*namaste carmavasana namo digvasanāyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Obeisance to the Lord having the crescent moon for his excellent ornament; to the Lord having the moon, the sun and fire as eyes; obeisance to you, O Lord with hides for robes; obeisance to you the quarters-clad (nude one).

## \|\| 2.63.42 \|\|

*jagadīśāya jīrṇāya jarājanmaharāya te \|*  
*jīvāyate namastubhyaṃ jaṃjapūkādihāriṇe \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. To the Lord of the universe, to the elderly one, to you the dispeller of birth and old age; obeisance to the enlivener; obeisance to you, the dispeller of the sins of those who mutter prayers repeatedly.

## \|\| 2.63.43 \|\|

*namo ḍamaruhastāya dhanurhastāya te namaḥ \|*  
*trinetrāya namastubhyaṃ jagannetrāya te namaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Obeisance to the Lord holding the Ḍamaru (a hand-drum) in his hands; obeisance to you having the bow in the hand; obeisance to you the three-eyed one; obeisance to you, the eye of the universe.

## \|\| 2.63.44 \|\|

*triśūlavyagrahastāya namastripathagādhara \|*  
*triviṣṭapādhināthāya trivedīpaṭhitāya ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Obeisance to the Lord holding the trident, O holder of Gaṅgā of the triple stream (flowing through three worlds); to the over-lord of the heaven, praised in all the three Vedas.

## \|\| 2.63.45 \|\|

*trayīmayāya tuṣṭāya bhaktatuṣṭipradāya ca \|*  
*dīkṣitāya namastubhyaṃ devadevāya te namaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. (Obeisance) to the Lord identified with the three Vedas; to the satisfied one; to the bestower of satisfaction on the devotees. Obeisance to you, the initiated one; obeisance to you, the Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 2.63.46 \|\|

*dāritāśeṣapāpāya namaste dīrghadarśine \|*  
*dūrāya duravāpyāya doṣanirdalanāya ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Obeisance to you, the Lord who have taken away all the sins completely; to the long-visioned one; to the Lord staying far off; to the Lord difficult of access; to the destroyer of defects.

## \|\| 2.63.47 \|\|

*doṣākara kalādhāra tyaktadoṣāgamāya ca \|*  
*namo dhūrjaṭaye tubhyaṃ dhattūrakusumapriya \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O lord, O holder of the digits of the moon; to the Lord accessible only to those who are free from defects; obeisance to you, O Dhūrjaṭi, O Lord fond of Dhattūra flowers.

## \|\| 2.63.48 \|\|

*namo dhīrāya dharmāya dharmapālāya te namaḥ \|*  
*nīlagrīva namastubhyaṃ namaste nīlalohita \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Obeisance to the intelligent one, the righteous one; obeisance to you, the protector of piety. O blue-throated Lord, obeisance to you; obeisance to you of red-blue complexion.

## \|\| 2.63.49 \|\|

*nāmamātrasmṛtikṛtāṃ trailokyaiśvaryapūraka \|*  
*namaḥ pramathanāthāya pinākodyatapāṇaye \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O Lord who fill with (endow with) prosperity and abundance of the three worlds, those who merely remember your names; obeisance to the Lord of Pramathas; to the Lord holding the Pināka in the raised hand.

## \|\| 2.63.50 \|\|

*paśupāśavimokṣāya paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ \|*  
*nāmoccāraṇamātreṇa mahāpātakahāriṇe \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Obeisance to the Lord of Paśus (individual souls); to the Lord releasing the souls from bondage; to the Lord removing great sins even when only the names are uttered.

## \|\| 2.63.51 \|\|

*parātparāya pārāya parāparaparāya ca \|*  
*namo'pāracaritrāya supavitrakathāya ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. (Obeisance) to the Lord beyond the Para (Unmanifest); to the Lord who redeems persons; to the Lord beyond cause and effect. Obeisance to the Lord whose acts are beyond comprehension; to the Lord whose stories are very sacred.

## \|\| 2.63.52 \|\|

*vāmadevāya vāmārdhadhāriṇe vṛṣagāmine \|*  
*namo bhargāya bhīmāya natabhītiharāya ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Obeisance to Vāmadeva; to the Lord half of whose body is female; to the Lord moving about on a bull; obeisance to Bharga; to Bhīma and to the remover of the fear of those who bow down.

## \|\| 2.63.53 \|\|

*bhavāya bhavanāśāya bhūtānāṃpataye namaḥ \|*  
*mahādeva namastubhyaṃ maheśa mahasāṃpate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Obeisance to Bhava; to the destroyer of worldly existence; obeisance to the Lord of living beings. O great Lord, obeisance to you; O Maheśa, O Lord of splendours.

## \|\| 2.63.54 \|\|

*namo mṛḍānīpataye namo mṛtyuṃjayāya te \|*  
*yajñāraye namastubhyaṃ yakṣarājapriyāya ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Obeisance to the consort of Mṛḍānī; obeisance to you, the conqueror of Death; obeisance to you, the destroyer of (Dakṣa’s) sacrifice; to the Lord of whom the king of Yakṣas is a favourite.

## \|\| 2.63.55 \|\|

*yāyajūkāya yajñāya yajñānāṃ phaladāyine \|*  
*rudrāya rudrapataye kadrudrāya ramāya ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. To the performer of Yajña; to the bestower of the fruit of Yajñas; obeisance to Rudra; to the Lord of Rudras; to the Lord who rejects despicable cooked food; to you, O bestower of fortune.

## \|\| 2.63.56 \|\|

*śūline śāśvateśāya śmaśānāvanicāriṇe \|*  
*śivāpriyāya śarvāya sarvajñāya namostu te \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Obeisance to the trident-bearing Lord; to the permanent lord; to the Lord moving about in the cremation ground; to the lover of Śivā; obeisance to Śarva, the omniscient one.

## \|\| 2.63.57 \|\|

*harāya kṣāṃtirūpāya kṣetrajñāya kṣamākara \|*  
*kṣamāya kṣitihartre ca kṣīragaurāya te namaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Obeisances to Hara, forbearance incarnate, O forgiver; to you identified with Kṣetrajña (individual soul); to one who is powerful; to the destroyer of Kṣiti (Earth); obeisance to you, fair-complexioned as milk.

## \|\| 2.63.58 \|\|

*aṃdhakāre namastubhyamādyaṃtarahitāya ca \|*  
*iḍādhārāya īśāya upedreṃdrastutāya ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Obeisance to you, O slayer of Andhaka; to the Lord devoid of beginning and end; to the sustainer of the earth; to īśa who is eulogized by Indra and Upendra (Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 2.63.59 \|\|

*umākāṃtāya ugrāya namaste ūrdhvaretase \|*  
*ekarūpāya caikāya mahadaiśvaryarūpiṇe \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Obeisance to the lover of Umā; obeisance to you, O Ugra (fierce one); to Ūrdhvaretas (of sublimated sexual urge i.e. who have controlled sexual energy); to the Lord having a single form; to the single one, whose form is great prosperity.

## \|\| 2.63.60 \|\|

*anaṃtakāriṇe tubhyamaṃbikāpataye namaḥ \|*  
*tvamoṃkāro vaṣaṭkāro bhūrbhuvaḥsvastvameva hi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Obeisance to you of infinite capacity for action. Obeisance to the consort of Ambikā. You are Oṃkāra, Vaṣaṭkāra and you alone are the three worlds, viz. Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ.

## \|\| 2.63.61 \|\|

*dṛśyādṛśya yadatrāsti tatsarvaṃ tvamu mādhava \|*  
*stutiṃ kartuṃ na jānāmi stutikartā tvameva hi \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O Lord of Umā, you are all that exist here, visible or invisible. I do not know how to pray; you alone are one who enables the eulogizer to pray.

## \|\| 2.63.62 \|\|

*vācyastvaṃ vācakastvaṃ hi vākca tvaṃ praṇatosmi te \|*  
*nānyaṃ vedmi mahādeva nānyaṃ staumi maheśvara \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. You are the person to be addressed; you are the speaker; you alone are the speech; I bow down to you, O Mahādeva; I do not know anyone else; O Maheśvara, I do not eulogize anyone else.

## \|\| 2.63.63 \|\|

*nānyaṃ namāmi gaurīśa nānyākhyāmādade śiva \|*  
*mūkonyanāmagrahaṇe badhironyakathāśrutau \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O Consort of Gaurī, I do not bow down to anyone else; O Śiva, I do not utter anyone else’s name; I am dumb in regard to the expression of another’s name; I am deaf is respect to listening to another’s story.

## \|\| 2.63.64 \|\|

*paṃguranyābhigamane'smyaṃdho'nyaparivīkṣaṇe \|*  
*eka eva bhavānīśa ekakartā tvameva hi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. I am lame in regard to the act of approaching another (god) and blind in looking up to anyone else. You are the only lord; you are the only creator.

## \|\| 2.63.65 \|\|

*pātā hartā tvamevaiko nānātvaṃ mūḍhakalpanā \|*  
*atastvameva śaraṇaṃ bhūyobhūyaḥ punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. You alone are the protector and the annihilator. Diversity is a misconception of the ignorant. Hence you alone are the refuge more and more, again and again.

## \|\| 2.63.66-67 \|\|

*saṃsārasāgare magnaṃ māmuddhara maheśvara \|*  
*iti stutvā maheśānaṃ jaigīṣavyo mahāmuniḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*vācaṃyamo bhavatsthāṇoḥ purataḥ sthāṇusannibhaḥ \|*  
*iti stutiṃ samākarṇya muneścaṃdravibhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*uvāca ca prasannātmā varaṃ brūhīti taṃ munim \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. O Maheśvara, lift me up drowning in the ocean of worldly existence.

After eulogizing Maheśāna thus, Jaigīṣavya, the great sage, kept quiet before Sthāṇu (Śiva) like a pillar.

On hearing this prayer of the sage, the Lord adorned with the moon, became delighted and said to the sage, “Ask for a boon.”

## \|\| 2.63.68 \|\|

*jaigīṣavya uvāca \|*  
*yadi prasanno deveśa tatastava padāṃbujāt \|*  
*mā bhavāni bhavānīśa dūraṃ dūrapadaprada \|\| 68 \|\|*

Jaigīṣavya said:

68\. If the Lord of Devas is pleased, O Lord of Bhavānī, O bestower of the remote (inaccessible) status (Mokṣa), let me not be far off from your lotus-like feet.

## \|\| 2.63.69 \|\|

*aparaśca varo nātha deyoyamavicārataḥ \|*  
*yanmayā sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ tatra sānnidhyamastu te \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O Lord, this is another boon which should be. given without hesitation: May there be your presence in the Liṅga installed by me.

## \|\| 2.63.70 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*jaigīṣavya mahābhāga yaduktaṃ bhavatānagha \|*  
*tadastu sarvaṃ tebhīṣṭaṃ varamanyaṃ dadāmi ca \|\| 70 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

70\. O blessed Jaigīṣavya, O sinless one, may everything mentioned by you take place. Further, I shall grant you another desirable boon.

## \|\| 2.63.71 \|\|

*yogaśāstraṃ mayā dattaṃ tava nirvāṇasādhakam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ yogināṃ madhye yogācāryo'stu vai bhavān \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The Yogaśāstra that will facilitate the achievement of salvation is passed on to you. You will be the foremost Yogācārya among all Yogins.

## \|\| 2.63.72 \|\|

*rahasyaṃ yogavidyāyā yathāvattvaṃ tapodhana \|*  
*saṃvetsyase prasādānme yena nirvāṇamāpsyasi \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O ascetic, with my favour, you will understand correctly the secret of Yogavidyā whereby you will attain salvation.

## \|\| 2.63.73 \|\|

*yathā nadī yathā bhṛṃgī somanaṃdī yathā tathā \|*  
*tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi bhakto me jarāmaraṇavarjitaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. You will be my devotee devoid of old age and death like Nandin, Bhṛṅgin and Somanandin.

## \|\| 2.63.74 \|\|

*saṃti vratāni bhūyāṃsi niyamāḥ saṃtyanekadhā \|*  
*tapāṃsi nānā saṃtyatra saṃti dānānyanekaśaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. There are many Vratas; there are many varieties of holy observances and restraints. There are many kinds of austerities and there are many types of Dānas.

## \|\| 2.63.75 \|\|

*śreyasāṃ sādhanānyatra pāpaghnānyapi sarvathā \|*  
*paraṃ hi paramaścaiṣa niyamo yastvayā kṛtaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. There are many ways of attaining the good and destroying sins. But greater than everything else is the holy observance practised by you.

## \|\| 2.63.76 \|\|

*paro hi niyamaścaiṣa māṃ vilokya yadaśyate \|*  
*māmanālokya yadbhuktaṃ tadbhuktaṃ kevalatvagham \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. This is the greatest holy observance that food is taken in only after seeing me. If anything is eaten without seeing and visiting me, it means only consumption of sin.

## \|\| 2.63.77 \|\|

*asamarcya ca yo bhuṅkte patrapuṣpaphalairapi \|*  
*retobhakṣī bhavenmūḍhaḥ sa janmānyekaviṃśatim \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. He who takes in leaves, fruits or flowers without worshipping (me) shall become deluded with the regular intake of semen (as food) for twenty-one births.

## \|\| 2.63.78 \|\|

*mahato niyamasyāsya bhavatānuṣṭhitasya vai \|*  
*nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśī mātrāmapyanye niyamā yamāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Other Niyamas and Yamas do not deserve even a sixteenth part of the great holy observance practised by you.

## \|\| 2.63.79 \|\|

*ato maccaraṇābhyāśe tvaṃ nivatsyasi sarvathā \|*  
*ato naiḥśreyasīṃ lakṣmīṃ tatraiva prāpsyasi dhruvam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Henceforth you will be near the feet of mine in every respect forever. Hence there itself you will certainly attain the glory of ultimate salvation.

## \|\| 2.63.80 \|\|

*jaigīṣavyeśvaraṃ nāma liṃgaṃ kāśyāṃ sudurlabham \|*  
*trīṇi varṣāṇi saṃsevya labhedyogaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The Liṅga named Jaigīṣavyeśvara in Kāśī shall be the most precious of all. There is no doubt in this that after serving (that Liṅga) for three years one will attain Yoga.

## \|\| 2.63.81 \|\|

*jaigīṣavyaguhāṃ prāpya yogābhyasanatatparaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsena labhetsiddhiṃ vāñchitāṃ madanugrahāt \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. With my blessings, a devotee eagerly engaged in practising Yoga after entering the cave of Jaigīṣavya, shall attain the desired fulfilment within six months.

## \|\| 2.63.82 \|\|

*tava liṃgamidaṃ bhaktaiḥ pūjanīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*vilokyā ca guhā ramyā parāsiddhimabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. This Liṅga of yours should be assiduously worshipped and the beautiful cave should be visited by devotees who desire the greatest achievement.

## \|\| 2.63.83 \|\|

*atra jyeṣṭheśvarakṣetre tvalliṃgaṃ sarvasiddhidam \|*  
*nāśayedaghasaṃghāni dṛṣṭaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ samarcitam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Hence in this Jyeṣṭheśvara Kṣetra, your Liṅga that yields all spiritual powers will, on being seen, touched and worshipped, destroy masses of sins.

## \|\| 2.63.84 \|\|

*asmiñjyeṣṭheśvarakṣetre saṃbhojya śivayoginaḥ \|*  
*koṭibhojyaphalaṃ samyagekaikaparisaṃkhyayā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. If Śivayogins are fed in this Jyeṣṭheśvara Kṣetra the benefit thereof shall be that of feeding ten millions for each one (of the Yogins so fed).

## \|\| 2.63.85 \|\|

*jaigīṣavyeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ gopanīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*kalau kaluṣabuddhīnāṃ purataśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Jaigīṣavyeśvara Liṅga should be assiduously guarded, especially in the Kali age, from those of perverted intellect.

## \|\| 2.63.86 \|\|

*kariṣyāmyatra sāṃnidhyamasmiṃlliṃge tapodhana \|*  
*yogasiddhipradānāya sādhakebhyaḥ sadaiva hi \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. O ascetic, I shall make my presence felt in this Liṅga forever, in order to bestow Yogic powers on the aspirants.

## \|\| 2.63.87 \|\|

*dade śṛṇu mahābhāga jaigīṣavyāparaṃ varam \|*  
*tvayedaṃ yatkṛtaṃ stotraṃ yogasiddhikaraṃ param \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Listen, O blessed Jaigīṣavya, I shall grant another boon. The prayer composed and recited by you will be highly conducive to the achievement of Yogic power.

## \|\| 2.63.88 \|\|

*mahāpāpaughaśamanaṃ mahāpuṇyapravardhanam \|*  
*mahābhītipraśamanaṃ mahābhaktivivardhanam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. It will subdue great sins; it will increase great merits; it will suppress all great fears; it will increase great devotion.

## \|\| 2.63.89-91 \|\|

*etatstotrajapātpuṃsāmasādhyaṃ naiva kiṃcana \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena japanīyaṃ susādhakaiḥ 4 \|\| 89 \|\|*

*iti dattvā varaṃ tasmai smarāriḥ smeralocanaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa brāhmaṇāṃ statra sametānkṣetravāsinaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*niśamyākhyānamatulametatprājñaḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*niṣpāpo jāyate martyo nopasargaiḥ prabādhyate \|\| 91 \|\|*

89-91. Nothing is impossible to attain through the recitation of this prayer. Hence it should be assiduously recited by excellent aspirants.

After granting this boon to him, the smiling destroyer of Kāma turned towards the Brāhmaṇas residing in the holy spot who had assembled there.

## Chapter 64 - The Secret of Jyeṣṭheśvara

## \|\| 2.64.1-2 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā bhūdevatāḥ śaṃbhuṃ kimācakhyuḥ ṣaḍānana \|*  
*kānikāni ca liṃgāni tatra tānyapicakṣva me \|\| 1 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhasthāne mahāpuṇye devadevasya vallabhe \|*  
*āścaryaṃ kimabhūttatra tadācakṣva ṣaḍānana \|\| 2 \|\|*

Agastya said:

1-2. O Six-faced One, what did the Brāhmaṇas say on seeing Śaṃbhu? Tell me also what different Liṅgas are there. What miracle happened in the highly meritorious holy spot Jyeṣṭhasthāna much appreciated by the Lord of the Devas? Tell me, O Six-faced One.

Skanda replied:

## \|\| 2.64.3 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇvagastya yathā pṛcchi bhavatā tadbravīmyaham \|*  
*maṃdarādriṃ yadā devo gatavānbrahmagauravāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Listen, O Agastya. I shall tell you what has been asked by you. In deference to Brahmā, the Lord went to Mountain Mandara.

## \|\| 2.64.4 \|\|

*tadā nirāśrayā viprāḥ kṣetrasaṃnyāsinonaghāḥ \|*  
*upākṛtāścāvirataṃ mahākṣetrapratigrahāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then those Brāhmaṇas, the sinless Sannyāsins of the holy spot (compelled to) desist from accepting monetary gifts, became bereft of support.

## \|\| 2.64.5 \|\|

*khātaṃkhātaṃ ca daṃḍāgrairbhūmiṃ kaṃdādivṛttayaḥ \|*  
*cakruḥ puṣkariṇīṃ ramyāṃ daṃḍakhātābhidhāṃ mune \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. They sustained themselves with bulbous roots etc. Digging incessantly the ground with the tips of thick sticks, they created a beautiful pond named Daṇḍakhāta.

## \|\| 2.64.6 \|\|

*tattīrthaṃ paritaḥ sthāpya mahāliṃgānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*maheśārādhanaparāstapaścakruḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Around that holy Tīrtha, they installed many great Liṅgas. Eager to propitiate Maheśa, they assiduously performed penance.

## \|\| 2.64.7 \|\|

*vibhūtidhāriṇo nityaṃ nityarudrākṣadhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*liṃgapūjāratā nityaṃ śatarudriyajāpinaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Always smeared with holy ash and wearing Rudrākṣa, they were ever engaged in the adoration of Liṅgas. They regularly repeated the Śatarudriya passages also.

## \|\| 2.64.8 \|\|

*te śrutvā devadevasya punarāgamanaṃ mune \|*  
*tapaḥkṛśā atitarāmāsurānaṃda medurāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O sage, when they heard of the return of the Lord of Devas, though they were lean due to austerities, they became filled with pleasure.

## \|\| 2.64.9 \|\|

*dvijāḥ paṃcasahasrāṇi carato vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*daṃḍakhātānmahātīrthādājagmurdevadarśane \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Five thousand Brāhmaṇas who were practising severe austerities, came from Daṇḍakhāta, the great Tīrtha, for the vision of the Lord.

## \|\| 2.64.10 \|\|

*tīrthānmaṃdākinī nāmno dvijāḥ pāśupatavratāḥ \|*  
*śivaikārādhanaparāḥ sametā ayutonmitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. From the holy spot named Mandākinī Tīrtha the Brāhmaṇas engaged in Pāśupata Vrata, solely propitiating Śiva, came there in a body numbering ten thousand.

## \|\| 2.64.11 \|\|

*haṃsatīrthātpariprāptā ayutaṃ triśatottaram \|*  
*śatadurvāsasastīrthādekādaśa śatādhikam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Ten thousand three hundred sages reached there from Haṃsa Tīrtha. One thousand two hundred came from the Tīrtha of Durvāsas.

## \|\| 2.64.12 \|\|

*matsyodaryāḥ parāpetuḥ sahasrāṇi ṣaḍeva hi \|*  
*kapālamocanātsapta śatānyabhyāgatā dvijāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Six thousand Brāhmaṇas came from Matsyodarī; seven hundred came from Kapālamocana.

## \|\| 2.64.13 \|\|

*ṛṇamocanatastīrthātsahasraṃ dviśatādhikam \|*  
*vaitaraṇyā api mune dvijānāmayutārdhakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One thousand two hundred came from the Tīrtha named Ṛṇamocana. O sage, five thousand came from Vaitaraṇī.

## \|\| 2.64.14 \|\|

*tataḥ pṛthūdakātkuṃḍātpṛthunā parikhānitāt \|*  
*ayāsiṣurdvijānāṃ ca śatānyeva trayodaśa \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. From the holy pit named Pṛthūdaka caused to be dug by King Pṛthu, one thousand three hundred Brāhmaṇas set off.

## \|\| 2.64.15 \|\|

*tathaivāpsarasaḥ kuṃḍānmenakākhyācchatadvayam \|*  
*urvaśīkuṃḍataḥ prāptāḥ sahasraṃ dviśatādhikam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. From the holy pit named after the celestial damsel Menakā, two hundred came. From Urvaśī Kuṇḍa one thousand two hundred came.

## \|\| 2.64.16 \|\|

*tathairāvatakuṃḍācca brāhmaṇāstriśatāni ca \|*  
*gaṃdharvāpsarasaḥ sapta śatāni dviśatāni ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Similarly from Airāvata Kuṇḍa three hundred Brāhmaṇas came. From Gandharvāpsaras Tīrtha, nine hundred Brāhmaṇas came.

## \|\| 2.64.17 \|\|

*vṛṣeśatīrthādājagmurnavatiḥ saśatatrayā \|*  
*yakṣiṇīkuṃḍataḥ prāptāḥ sahasraṃ triśatottaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. From Vṛṣeśa Tīrtha, three hundred ninety came. From Yakṣiṇī Kuṇḍa came one thousand three hundred.

## \|\| 2.64.18 \|\|

*lakṣmītīrthātparaṃ jagmuḥ ṣoḍaśaiva śatāni ca \|*  
*piśācamocanātsapta sahasrāṇi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. From Lakṣmī Tīrtha came one thousand six hundred. Seven thousand excellent Brāhmaṇas came from Piśācamocana.

## \|\| 2.64.19 \|\|

*pitṛkuṃḍācchataṃsāgraṃ dhruvatīrthācchatāni ṣaṭ \|*  
*mānasākhyācca saraso dviśatī saśatatrayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. From Pitṛ Kuṇḍa, a few more than a hundred came; From Dhruva Tīrtha, six hundred; five hundred from Mānasa Saras.

## \|\| 2.64.20 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā vāsukihṛdātsahasrāṇi daśaiva tu \|*  
*tathaivāṣṭaśataṃ draṣṭuṃ jānakīkuṃḍato dvijāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. From Vāsukihrada ten thousand Brāhmaṇas came. Similarly from Jānakī Kuṇḍa eight hundred Brāhmaṇas came to see the Lord.

## \|\| 2.64.21 \|\|

*kāśīnāthamanuprāptāḥ paramānaṃdadāyinam \|*  
*tathā gautamakuṃḍācca śatāninava cāgatāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. They all came to the Lord of Kāśī, the bestower of supreme bliss. Similarly from Gautama Kuṇḍa nine hundred Brāhmaṇas came.

## \|\| 2.64.22 \|\|

*tīrthāddurgatisaṃharturbāhmaṇāḥ pratipedire \|*  
*ekādaśaśatānyeva draṣṭuṃ devamumāpatim \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. From the Durgatisaṃhartṛ Tīrtha one thousand one hundred Brāhmaṇas came there to see the Lord, Consort of Umā.

## \|\| 2.64.23 \|\|

*asīsaṃbhedamārabhya gaṃgātīrasthitā dvijāḥ \|*  
*āsaṃgameśvarāttatra pariprāptā ghaṭodbhava \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Pot-born One, the Brāhmaṇas residing on the banks of Gaṅgā from the confluence of Asī till the Saṅgameśvara Tīrtha, came there.

## \|\| 2.64.24 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśasahasrāṇi tathā paṃcaśatānyapi \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ paṃcapaṃcāśadgaṃgātīrātsamāgatāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Eighteen thousand five hundred fifty-five Brāhmaṇas came there from the banks of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 2.64.25-26 \|\|

*sārdradūrvākṣatakaraiḥ sapuṣpaphalapāṇibhiḥ \|*  
*sugaṃdhamālyahastaiśca brāhmaṇairjayavādibhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*stuto maṃgalasūktaiśca praṇataśca punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*tebhyo dattābhayaḥ śaṃbhuḥ papraccha kuśalaṃ mudā \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. With auspicious Sūktas (hymns) Śaṃbhu was eulogized by the Brāhmaṇas shouting slogans of victory. They had wet rice-grains and Dūrvā grass, flowers and fruits and garlands of fragrant flowers in their hands. He was bowed down to repeatedly. After granting them freedom from fear, Śaṃbhu gladly enquired after their welfare.

## \|\| 2.64.27 \|\|

*tataste brāhmaṇāḥ procuḥ prabaddhakarasaṃpuṭāḥ \|*  
*kṣetre nivasatāṃ nātha sadānaḥ kuśalodayaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereafter with the hands joined in reverence, the Brāhmaṇas said: “O Lord, to us the residents of the holy spot, there is always increase in happiness and welfare.

## \|\| 2.64.28 \|\|

*viśeṣataḥ kṛto'smābhiḥ sākṣānnayanagocaraḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ yatsvarūpaṃ śrutayo na viduḥ paramārthataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Particularly you have been made visible to our eyes, you whose real form even the Śrutis did not know really.

## \|\| 2.64.29-30 \|\|

*sadaivākuśalaṃ teṣāṃ ye tvatkṣetraparāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*caturdaśāpi vai lokāsteṣāṃ nityaṃ parāṅmukhāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yeṣāṃ hṛdi sadaivāste kāśītvāśīviṣāṃ gada \|*  
*saṃsārāśīviṣaviṣaṃ na teṣāṃ prabhavetkvacit \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Those who are averse to your holy spot will not have happiness at any time. All the fourteen worlds will always turn away their faces from them. O Lord who have serpents as bracelets, if Kāśī is always in the hearts of people, the poison of the serpent of worldly existence will not be effective in regard to them anywhere.

## \|\| 2.64.31 \|\|

*garbharakṣāmaṇirmaṃtraḥ kāśīvarṇadvayātmakaḥ \|*  
*yasya kaṃṭhe sadā tiṣṭhettasyākuśalatā kutaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The two-syllabled Mantra KĀ-ŚĪ is the jewel which destroys rebirth (i.e. leads to Mokṣa). How can then be the negation of welfare, if it is retained in the throat?

## \|\| 2.64.32 \|\|

*sudhāṃ pibati yo nityaṃ kāśīvarṇadvayātmikām \|*  
*sa nairjarīṃ daśāṃ hitvā sudhaiva parijāyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He who always drinks the nectar in the form of the two-syllables KĀ-ŚĪ, gives up (six) changes such as old age and becomes immortal and liberated.

## \|\| 2.64.33 \|\|

*śrutaṃ karṇāmṛtaṃ yena kāśītyakṣarayugmakam \|*  
*na samākaṇaryatyeva sa punargarbhajāṃ kathām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He by whom the pair of syllables acting as nectar unto the ears, namely, KĀ-ŚĪ has been heard never hears the story arising from conception.

## \|\| 2.64.34 \|\|

*kāśī rajopi yanmūrdhni patedapyanilāhatam \|*  
*caṃdraśekharatanmūrdhā bhaveccaṃdrakalāṃkitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If the dust of Kāśī, being wafted by the wind, were to fall on a head, that head becomes characterised by the digit of the moon, O Moon-crested Lord.

## \|\| 2.64.35 \|\|

*prasaṃgatopi yannetrapathamānaṃdakānanam \|*  
*yātaṃ tetra na jāyaṃte nekṣeranpitṛkāna nam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even if casually, Ānandakānana were to come within the range of the vision of people, they are not reborn here (and hence) they never see the cremation ground.

## \|\| 2.64.36 \|\|

*gacchatā tiṣṭhatā vāpi svapatā jāgratāthavā \|*  
*kāśītyeṣa mahāmaṃtro yena japtaḥ sanirbhayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. If anyone were to repeat this great Mantra, namely Kāśī, while moving about, standing, sleeping or walking, he becomes free from fear.

## \|\| 2.64.37 \|\|

*yena bījākṣarayugaṃ kāśīti hṛdi dhāritam \|*  
*abījāni bhavaṃtyeva karmabījāni tasya vai \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If the two Bījākṣaras Kā-śī (KĀ is the Bīja of Kāma and ŚA is the Bīja of Śrī) were to be retained in the heart, all the Karmabījas (seeds of Karmas) become ineffective in regard to him.

## \|\| 2.64.38 \|\|

*kāśī kāśīti kāśīti japato yasya saṃsthitiḥ \|*  
*anyatrāpi satastasya puro muktiḥ prakāśate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If anyone were to die muttering Kāśī-Kāśī-Kāśī even while staying elsewhere, salvation shines in front of him.

## \|\| 2.64.39 \|\|

*kṣemamūrtiriyaṃ kāśī kṣemamūrtirbhavānbhava \|*  
*kṣemamūrtistripathagā nānyatkṣematrayaṃ kvacit \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. This Kāśī is weal incarnate. O Bhava, you are the weal in person. The triple stream Gaṅgā is the form of weal. This triad of weal exists nowhere else.”

## \|\| 2.64.40 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānāmiti vacaḥ kṣetrabhaktivibṛṃhitam \|*  
*niśamya girijākāṃtastutoṣa nitarāṃ haraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On hearing these words fully expressive of devotion to the holy spot from the Brāhmaṇas, Hara, the lover of the Daughter of the Mountain, became highly pleased.

## \|\| 2.64.41 \|\|

*provāca ca prasannātmā dhanyā yūyaṃ dvijarṣabhāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāmihedṛśī bhaktirmama kṣetretipāvane \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The Lord, delighted within, said: “Blessed are you, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, since you have such a devotion to my holy place of excessive sanctity.

## \|\| 2.64.42 \|\|

*jāne sattvamayā jātāḥ kṣetrasyāsya niṣevaṇāt \|*  
*nīrajaskā vitamasaḥ saṃsārārṇavapāragāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I know that you have all become fully endowed with Sattva Guṇa by resorting to this holy spot, free from Rajas and Tamas and hence capable of crossing the ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.64.43 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāstu ye bhaktāste bhaktā mama niścitam \|*  
*jīvanmuktā hi te nūnaṃ mokṣalakṣmyā kaṭākṣitāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Those who are devotees of Vārāṇasī are certainly my devotees. They are certainly living-liberated ones, the objects of the benign glances of the glory of salvation.

## \|\| 2.64.44 \|\|

*yaiśca kāśīsthito jaṃturalpakopi virodhitaḥ \|*  
*tairvai viśvaṃbharā sarvā mayā saha virodhitā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Those by whom the meanest of creatures stationed in Kāśī, has been antagonized, have actually antagonized the entire earth along with me.

## \|\| 2.64.45 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāḥ stutimapi yo niśamyānumodate \|*  
*api brahmāṃḍamakhilaṃ dhruvaṃ tenānumoditam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He who rejoices on hearing the eulogy of Vārāṇasī has actually congratulated joyously the entire cosmic egg.

## \|\| 2.64.46 \|\|

*nivasaṃti hi ye martyā asminnānaṃdakānane \|*  
*mamāṃtaḥkaraṇe te vai nivaseyurakalmaṣāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Those men who reside in this Ānandakānana are free from sins. They will reside within my mind.

## \|\| 2.64.47 \|\|

*nivasaṃti mama kṣetre mama bhaktiṃ prakurvate \|*  
*mama liṃgadharā ye tu tānevopadiśāmyaham \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Those who stay in my holy spot and do devotional acts unto me, those who bear the distinguishing marks of my devotees, only to them do I impart the means of salvation.

## \|\| 2.64.48 \|\|

*nivasaṃti mama kṣetre mama bhaktiṃ na kurvate \|*  
*mama liṃgadharā ye no na tānupadiśāmyaham \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I do not impart to them (salvation), to those who neither stay here, nor are devoted unto me, nor bear the significant marks.

## \|\| 2.64.49 \|\|

*kāśī nirvāṇanagarī yeṣāṃ citte prakāśate \|*  
*te matpuraḥ prakāśaṃte naiḥśreyasyā śriyā vṛtāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. If Kāśī, the city of salvation, shines in the hearts of people, they shine before me and are enveloped by the glory of salvation.

## \|\| 2.64.50 \|\|

*mokṣalakṣmīriyaṃ kāśī na yebhyaḥ parirocate \|*  
*svarlakṣmīṃ kāṃkṣamāṇebhyaḥ patitāste na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Those to whom this Kāśī, the glory of salvation, does not appeal are undoubtedly fallen ones, inferior to those who desire the glory of heavenly pleasures.

## \|\| 2.64.51 \|\|

*kāthīṃ saṃkākṣamāṇānāṃ puruṣārthacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*puraḥ kiṃkaravattiṣṭhenmamānugrahato dvijāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The four aims of life of those who eagerly wish for Kāśī, shall stand in front of them like servants, O Brāhmaṇas, with my favour.

## \|\| 2.64.52 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānane hyatra jvaladdāvānalosmyaham \|*  
*karmabījāni jaṃtūnāṃ jvālaye na prarohaye \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. I am the blazing fire of forest in the Ānandakānana here. I burn down the seeds of Karmas of the creatures; I do not let them grow.

## \|\| 2.64.53 \|\|

*vastavyaṃ satataṃ kāśyāṃ yaṣṭavyohaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*jetavyau kalikālau ca raṃtavyā muktiraṃganā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. One should always stay in Kāśī. I should be adored assiduously. Kali and Kāla should be overcome. The lady Mukti (Salvation) should be enjoyed.

## \|\| 2.64.54 \|\|

*prāpyāpi kāśīṃ durbuddhiryo na māṃ parisevate \|*  
*tasya hastagatāpyāśu kaivalyaśrīḥ praṇaśyati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Even after reaching Kāśī, a man of evil intellect, who does not serve me properly (will find) that the glory of salvation though within the grasp of his hands, perishes quickly.

## \|\| 2.64.55 \|\|

*dhanyā madbhaktilakṣmāṇo brāhmaṇāḥ kāśivāsinaḥ \|*  
*yūyaṃ yaccetaso vṛtterna dūrehaṃ na kāśikā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Blessed are you Brāhmaṇas, residents of Kāśī, noted prominently for devotion. I am not far from your thoughts nor is so Kāśikā.

## \|\| 2.64.56 \|\|

*dātavyo vo varaḥ kotra vriyatāṃ me yathāruci \|*  
*preyāṃso me yato yūyaṃ kṣetrasaṃnyāsakāriṇaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. What boon should be given to you here? Choose it from me as you please, since you, the Sannyāsins of the holy spot, are my favourites.

## \|\| 2.64.57 \|\|

*iti pītvā maheśānamukhakṣīrābdhijāṃ sudhām \|*  
*paritṛptā dvijāḥ sarve vavrurvaramanuttamam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On imbibing the nectar emanating from the ocean of milk of the mouth of Maheśāna, all the Brāhmaṇas became satisfied. They chose an excellent boon.

## \|\| 2.64.58 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*umāpate maheśāna sarvajña vara eṣa naḥ \|*  
*kāśī kadāpi na tyājyā bhavatā bhavatāpahṛt \|\| 58 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

58\. O omniscient Maheśāna, consort of Umā, this is our boon. Kāśī, the dispeller of the distress of the worldly existence, should never be abandoned by you.

## \|\| 2.64.59 \|\|

*vacanādbrāhmaṇānāṃ tu śāpo mā prabhavatviha \|*  
*kadācidapi keṣāṃcitkāśyāṃ mokṣāṃtarāyakaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In view of the prayer of the Brāhmaṇas let not any curse pronounced by anyone be an obstacles unto salvation, at any time; let is not be effective in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.64.60 \|\|

*tava pādābuṃjadvaṃdve nirdvaṃdvā bhaktirastu naḥ \|*  
*ā kalevarapātaṃ ca kāśīvāsostu noniśam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Let our devotion to the pair of your lotus-like feet be unaffected by the opposing pairs of entities. Let our stay in Kāśī be continuous till death.

## \|\| 2.64.61 \|\|

*kimanyena vareṇeśa deya eṣa varo hi naḥ \|*  
*avadhehyaṃdhakadhvaṃsinvaramanyaṃ vṛṇīmahe \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Of what avail is another boon. This boon itself should be given to us. But, note, O Slayer of Andhaka, still we shall choose another boon.

## \|\| 2.64.62 \|\|

*tava pratinidhī kṛtyāsmābhistvadbhaktibhāvitaiḥ \|*  
*pratiṣṭhiteṣu liṃgeṣu sānnidhyaṃ bhavato'stviha \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Let there be your presence in the Liṅgas as your representation installed by us, purified by the devotion unto you.

## \|\| 2.64.63 \|\|

*śrutveti teṣāṃ vākyāni tathāstviti pinākinā \|*  
*proce'nyopi varo datto jñānaṃ vaśca bhaviṣyati \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. On hearing these utterances of those Brāhmaṇas the Pināka-wielding Lord said: “So be it”: and another boon was also granted, namely “You will be endowed with knowledge.”

## \|\| 2.64.64 \|\|

*punaḥ provāca deveśo niśāmayata bho dvijāḥ \|*  
*hitaṃ vaḥ kathayāmyatra tadanuṣṭhīyatāṃ dhruvam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The Lord of Devas said further: “O Brāhmaṇas, listen. I shall tell you what is beneficial to you. Let it be certainly carried out.

## \|\| 2.64.65 \|\|

*sevyottaravahā nityaṃ liṃgamarcyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*damo dānaṃ dayā nityaṃ kartavyaṃ muktikāṃkṣibhiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The north-flowing river (Gaṅgā) should always be resorted to. The Liṅga should be assiduously adored. Self-control, offering gifts and compassion for others should be practised always by those who desire salvation.

## \|\| 2.64.66 \|\|

*idameva rahasyaṃ ca kathitaṃ kṣetravāsinām \|*  
*matiḥ parahitā kāryā vācyaṃ nodvegakṛdvacaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. This alone is mentioned as the secret of the inhabitants of the holy spot. Thoughts for others’ welfare should be entertained. Words causing grief and affliction should not be uttered.

## \|\| 2.64.67 \|\|

*manasāpi na kartavyamenotra vijigīṣuṇā \|*  
*atratyamakṣayaṃ yasmātsukṛtaṃ sukṛtetaram \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Sins should not be committed here by persons desirous of eminence, since good and evil deeds committed here are everlasting.

## \|\| 2.64.68 \|\|

*anyatra yatkṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatkāśyāṃ pariṇaśyati \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ kṛtaṃ pāpamaṃtargehe praṇaśyati \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The sin committed elsewhere perishes in Kāśī. The sin committed in Vārāṇasī perishes in Antargeha (Inner sanctum Sanctorum of Kāśī).

## \|\| 2.64.69 \|\|

*aṃtargehe kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ paiśācyanarakāvaham \|*  
*piśācanarakaprāptirgacchatyeva bahiryadi \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The sin committed in Antargeha causes Paiśācya (state of being a vampire) and downfall in hell. If the sin is committed outside, the attainment of vampirehood and hell goes away (after entering Antargeha).

OR: If a man commits a sin within Antargṛha and goes (out of Vārāṇasī), he gets the vampirehood and hell.

## \|\| 2.64.70 \|\|

*na kalpakoṭibhiḥ kāśyāṃ kṛtaṃ karma pramṛjyate \|*  
*kiṃtu rudrapiśācatvaṃ jāyate'trāyutatrayam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. A Karma done in Kāśī is not wiped off even in crores of Kalpas, but to those who die here Rudrapiśācatva happens for thirty thousand (divine years).

## \|\| 2.64.71-72 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ sthito yo vai pātakeṣu rataḥ sadā \|*  
*yoniṃ prāpyāpi paiśācīṃ varṣāṇāmayutatrayam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*punaratraiva nivasañjñānaṃ prāpsyatyanuttamam \|*  
*tena jñānetha saṃprāpte mokṣamāpsyatyanuttamam \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. If a person staying in Kāśī is always engaged in sinful activities, he attains the species of Piśācas continuing for thirty thousand years. Thereafter he continues to stay here. He will attain excellent knowledge. Therefore, when knowledge is attained, he will attain perfect salvation.

## \|\| 2.64.73 \|\|

*duṣkṛtāni vidhāyeha bahiḥ paṃcatvamāgatāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ gatiṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇuta dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. In the case of those who commit sins here, but die elsewhere, I shall tell you the goal reached by them. Listen, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 2.64.74 \|\|

*yāmākhyā me gaṇāḥ saṃti ghorā vikṛtamūrttayaḥ \|*  
*mūṣāyāṃ te dhamaṃtyādau kṣetraduṣkṛtakāriṇaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. There are some Gaṇas of mine called Yāmas. They are ferocious and hideous in forms. At the outset they put evildoers of the holy spot in a crucible and blow.

## \|\| 2.64.75 \|\|

*nayaṃtyanūpaprāyāṃ ca tataḥ prācīṃ durāsadām \|*  
*varṣākāle durācārānpātayaṃti mahājale \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Thereafter, in rainy season they take the persons of evil action to the eastern marshy places rarely accessible (to others). They then put them in the vast expanse of water.

## \|\| 2.64.76 \|\|

*jalaukābhiḥ sapakṣābhirdaṃdaśūkairjalodbhavaiḥ \|*  
*durnivāraiśca maśakairdaśyaṃte te divāniśam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. They are bitten day and night by winged leeches, aquatic reptiles and mosquitoes that cannot be warded off.

## \|\| 2.64.77 \|\|

*tato yāmairhimartau te nīyaṃte'drau himālaye \|*  
*aśanāvaraṇairhīnāḥ kleśyaṃte te divāniśam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Thereafter in the season of winter, they are taken to the Himālaya mountain. They \[are?\] deprived of food and clothing, are subjected to great distress day and night.

## \|\| 2.64.78 \|\|

*marusthale tato grīṣme vārivṛkṣavivarjite \|*  
*divākarakaraistīvraistāpyaṃte te pipāsitāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thereafter, in summer season, they are kept in desert region devoid of water and vagetation \[vegetation?\]. They are (continuously) kept thirsty and scorched by the rays of the sun.

## \|\| 2.64.79 \|\|

*kleśitāste gaṇairugrairyātanābhiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*itthaṃ kālamasaṃkhyātamānīyaṃte tatastviha \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. They are tortured and harassed by the ferocious Gaṇas all-round in this manner for an unlimited period of time and ultimately brought here.

## \|\| 2.64.80-81 \|\|

*nivedayaṃti te yāmāḥ kālarājāṃtike tataḥ \|*  
*kālarājopi tāndraṣṭvā karmasaṃsmārya duṣkṛtam \|\| 80 \|\|*

*vivastrānkṣuttṛṣārtāṃśca lagnapṛṣṭhodaratvacaḥ \|*  
*anyai rudrapiśācaiśca sahasaṃyojayatyapi \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. Those Yāmas convey the information to the presence of Kālarāja. Inspecting them Kālarāja reminds them of their sinful actions. He unites them with other Rudrapiśācas keeping them naked, distressed by hunger and thirst and having the skins at the belly and back touching each other.

## \|\| 2.64.82 \|\|

*tato rudrapiśācāste bhairavānucarāḥ sadā \|*  
*sahaṃte klamamatyarthaṃ kṣuttṛṣṇogratvasaṃbhavam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Thereafter, those Rudrapiśācas continue to be the attendants of Bhairava and endure much fatigue arising from the severity of hunger and thirst.

## \|\| 2.64.83-84 \|\|

*āhāraṃ rudhironmiśraṃ te labhaṃte kadācana \|*  
*evaṃ tryayutasaṃkhyākaṃ kālaṃ tatrātiduḥkhitāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*śmaśānastaṃbhamabhito nīyaṃte kaṃṭhapāśitāḥ \|*  
*pipāsitā api na teṃ'busparśamapi cāpnuyuḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. Occasionally they get some food and that too contaminated with blood. Thus, they remain there in an excessively miserable condition for a period of thirty thousand years. With cords round their necks, they are taken around the impaling stake in the cremation ground. Although very thirsty, they do not get any opportunity to even touch water.

## \|\| 2.64.85 \|\|

*atha saṃkṣīṇapāpāste kālabhairavadarśanāt \|*  
*ihaiva dehino bhūtvā mucyaṃte te mamājñayā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. When ultimately at the sight of Kālabhairava their sins become destroyed, they are born here itself and become liberated at my behest.

## \|\| 2.64.86 \|\|

*tasmānna kāmayetātra vāṅmanaḥkarmaṇāpyaghaha m \|*  
*śucau pathi sadā stheyaṃ mahālābhamabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Hence one should not feel drawn towards sinful activities, thoughts and utterances. Those who desire to attain great benefit, should always abide by the path of purity.

## \|\| 2.64.87 \|\|

*nāvimukte mṛtaḥ kaścinnarakaṃ yāti kilbiṣī \|*  
*mamānugrahamāsādya gacchatyeva parāṃ gatim \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. No sinner dying in Avimukta falls into hell. With my favour, he attains the greatest goal (Mokṣa).

## \|\| 2.64.88 \|\|

*anāśanaṃ yaḥ kurute madbhakta iha suvrataḥ \|*  
*na tasya punarāvṛttiḥ kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. If my devotee of excellent holy vows observes fast, he will not return (to the worldly existence) even in the course of a hundred crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 2.64.89 \|\|

*aśāśvatamidaṃ jñātvā mānuṣyaṃ bahukilviṣam \|*  
*avimuktaṃ sadā sevyaṃ saṃsārabhayamocakam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Realizing that the life of human beings is not permanent and it is full of sins, Avimukta should always be resorted to. It causes release from the fear of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.64.90 \|\|

*nānyatpaśyāmi jaṃtūnāṃ muktvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*sarvapāpapraśamanīṃ prāyaścittaṃ kalau yuge \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Excepting the city of Vārāṇasī that suppresses all sins, I do not see any other means of expiation in the Kali age for the creatures.

## \|\| 2.64.91 \|\|

*janmāṃtarasahasreṣu yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam \|*  
*avimuktaṃ praviṣṭasya tatsarvaṃ vrajati kṣayam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Whatever sin has been incurred and accumulated in the course of thousands of previous births, becomes dispelled entirely as soon as one enters Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.64.92 \|\|

*janmāṃtarasahasreṣu yuṃjanyogī yadāpnuyāt \|*  
*tadihaiva paro mokṣo maraṇādadhi gamyate \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. On death here itself the greatest salvation is obtained, which the Yogin is likely to get after practising Yoga in the course of thousands of births.

## \|\| 2.64.93 \|\|

*tiryagyonigatāḥ sattvā ye vimuktakṛtālayāḥ \|*  
*kālena nidhanaṃ prāptāstepi yāṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Animals of the lower strata having their habitation in Avimukta attain the greatest goal (Mokṣa) after meeting with death in due course.

## \|\| 2.64.94 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ na sevaṃte ye mūḍhāstamasāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*viṇmūtraretasāṃ madhye te vasaṃti punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Those deluded ones enveloped in darkness (ignorance) who do not resort to Avimukta, frequently stay in the midst of faeces, urine and seminal fluid (in the womb).

## \|\| 2.64.95 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ samāsādya yo liṃgaṃ sthāpayetsudhīḥ \|*  
*kalpakoṭiśatairvāpi nāsti tasya punarbhavaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. If a sensible man reaches Avimukta and installs a Liṅga, he has no rebirth even in the course of hundreds of crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 2.64.96 \|\|

*grahanakṣatratārāṇāṃ kālena patanaṃ dhruvam \|*  
*avimukte mṛtānāṃ tu patanaṃ naiva vidyate \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Certain indeed is the downfall of planets, constellations and stars in the course of time. But there is no problem of a downfall in the case of those who die in Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.64.97 \|\|

*brahmahatyāṃ naraḥ kṛtvā paścātsaṃyatamānasaḥ \|*  
*prāṇāṃstyajati yaḥ kāśyāṃ sa mukto nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. After committing murder of a Brāhmaṇa, if one later repents and gains mental control and meets with his death in Kāśī, he undoubtedly becomes liberated.

## \|\| 2.64.98 \|\|

*striyaḥ pativratā yāśca mama bhaktisamāhitāḥ \|*  
*avimukte mṛtā viprā yāṃti tāḥ paramāṃ gatim \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Chaste women with mental purity and concentration due to devotion unto me, attain the greatest goal, O Brāhmaṇas, if they die in Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.64.99 \|\|

*atrotkramaṇakālehaṃ svayameva dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*diśāmi tārakaṃ brahma dehī syādyena tanmayaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, at the time of death I myself impart Tāraka Brahman whereby an embodied soul becomes identical with that (Supreme Soul).

## \|\| 2.64.100 \|\|

*manmanā mama bhaktaśca mayi sarvārpitakriyaḥ \|*  
*yathā mokṣamihāpnoti na tathānyatrakutracit \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Nowhere else does anyone attain Mokṣa like my devotee here itself, with the mind centred round me and all his activities dedicated to me.

## \|\| 2.64.101 \|\|

*maraṇaṃ niścitaṃ jñātvā gatiṃ cāsukharūpiṇīm \|*  
*calamāgaṃtukaṃ sarvaṃ tataḥ kāśīṃ samāśrayet \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. After realizing that death is certain and inevitable, return (to life) is full of misery and every created thing is unsteady (i.e. what comes surely goes away) one should resort to Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.64.102 \|\|

*kāśī samāśritā yaistu manovākkāyakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*tānatra nirmaladhiyo nivārṇaśrīḥ samāśrayet \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The Glory of Salvation will resort to those men of pure intellect by whom Kāśī is resorted to in thought, word and deed.

## \|\| 2.64.103 \|\|

*kāśīsthitaikamapi yaḥ prīṇayennyāyajairdhanaiḥ \|*  
*tena trailokyamakhilaṃ prīṇitaṃ tu mayā saha \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. It is as good as the entire three worlds including me have been pleased by him, if a person could please at least a single person residing in Kāśī through wealth legitimately earned.

## \|\| 2.64.104 \|\|

*yaḥ prīṇayati puṇyātmā nirvāṇanagarī naram \|*  
*pumarthena sthiternityaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ prīṇayāmi tam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. If a meritorious soul propitiates a man of the City of Salvation, through abundance, by granting (four) aims of life, O Brāhmaṇas, I too propitiate him.

## \|\| 2.64.105 \|\|

*divodāsopi rājarṣiḥ kāśīṃ dharmeṇa pālayan \|*  
*sadeho matpadaṃ prāpto yato na punarāgatiḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The saintly king Divodāsa, righteously protecting Kāśī, has attained my region along with his physical body. There is no return from that region.

## \|\| 2.64.106 \|\|

*atra yogastathā jñānaṃ muktirekena janmanā \|*  
*ato vimuktamāsādya nānyadgacchettapovanam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Here within a single birth, Yoga, knowledge and salvation (are attained). Hence after reaching Avimukta one should not go to another penance-grove.

## \|\| 2.64.107 \|\|

*mokṣaṃ sudurlabhaṃ jñātvā saṃsāraṃ cātibhīṣaṇam \|*  
*aśmanā caraṇau hatvā kālamatra pratīkṣayet \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. After fully comprehending that salvation is difficult to attain, and the worldly existence excessively terrible, one should hit (one’s) feet with a stone and wait for Kāla, here.

## \|\| 2.64.108 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ parityajya yadā yāsyaṃti durdhiyaḥ \|*  
*hasiṣyaṃti tadā bhūtānyanyonyakaratāḍanaiḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. When men of defiled intellect leave Avimukta and go elsewhere, Bhūtas (living beings, spirits) will laugh clapping the hands together (at that).

## \|\| 2.64.109 \|\|

*prāpya vārāṇasīṃ puṇyāṃ siddhikṣetramanuttamam \|*  
*pariniṣkrāṃtumanyatra kasya jaṃtormatirbhavet \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Which creature will be mentally inclined to go out after coming to the meritorious Vārāṇasī, the most excellent holy spot?

## \|\| 2.64.110 \|\|

*mahādānena cānyatra yatphalaṃ labhyate naraiḥ \|*  
*avimukte tu kākiṇyāṃ dattāyāṃ tadavāpyate \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. The benefit obtained by men through Mahādānas (most valuable gifts) elsewhere is obtained when (only) a Kākiṇī (20 Varāṭikās, 1/4th (one fourth of a Paṇa) is given away in Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.64.111 \|\|

*ekaṃ samarcayelliṃgaṃ tapastapyeta cāparaḥ \|*  
*tayormadhye tu sa śreṣṭho yo liṃgaṃ pūjayediha \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. One man may worship a Liṅga. Another may perform penance. Between these two, he who worships the Liṅga is superior.

## \|\| 2.64.112 \|\|

*tīrthāṃtare gavāṃ koṭiṃ vidhivadyaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*ekāhaṃ yo vasetkāśyāṃ kāśīvāsī tayorvaraḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. One has duly gifted away a crore of cows in the other holy spots. The other stays in Kāśī for a single day. Between these two, the resident of Kāśī is better.

## \|\| 2.64.113 \|\|

*anyatra brāhmaṇānāṃ tu koṭiṃ saṃbhojya yatphalam \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ tu caikena bhojitena tadāpyate \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. The benefit that is obtained by feeding a crore of Brāhmaṇas elsewhere, can be obtained if a single person is fed in Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.64.114 \|\|

*sannihatyāṃ kurukṣetre rāhugraste divākare \|*  
*tulāpuruṣadānena kāśībhikṣā samā bhavet \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Giving alms in Kāśī shall be on a par with Tulāpuruṣadāna (giving things equal in weight of the devotee as a gift) on Sannihati in Kurukṣetra when there is solar eclipse.

## \|\| 2.64.115 \|\|

*mameha paramaṃ jyotirāpātālādvyavasthitam \|*  
*atītya saptalokādīnanaṃtaṃ liṃgarūpadhṛk \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Here my great luminous splendour is established from Pātāla. It has gone beyond the seven worlds. The infinite firmament has taken the form of Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.64.116 \|\|

*pṛthivyaṃtepi ye liṃgamavimuktaṃ smaraṃti me \|*  
*kaluṣaiste vimucyaṃte mahadbhiriti niścitam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. It is certain that those who remember my Avimukta Lṅga even at an extremity of the earth, are liberated from great sins.

## \|\| 2.64.117 \|\|

*asminkṣetre tu ye nāhaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ samarcitaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya tārakaṃ jñānaṃ na sa bhūyobhijāyate \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. One by whom I am seen, touched and worshipped in this holy spot, acquires Tāraka Jñāna. He is not reborn.

## \|\| 2.64.118 \|\|

*yo māmiha samabhyarcya mriyatenyatrakutracit \|*  
*janmāṃtarepi māṃ prāpya sa vimukto bhaviṣyati \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. One who worships me here but dies elsewhere, attains me in the next birth. He will then be liberated.”

## \|\| 2.64.119 \|\|

*ityuktvā kṣetramāhātmyaṃ dvijānāmagrato haraḥ \|*  
*paśyatāmeva teṣāṃ tu tatraivāṃtarhitobhavat \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. After telling the greatness of the holy spot before the Brāhmaṇas, Hara vanished there itself even as they were watching.

## \|\| 2.64.120 \|\|

*tepi sākṣādvirūpākṣaṃ pratyakṣīkṛtya vāḍavāḥ \|*  
*prahṛṣṭamanaso'tyaṃtaṃ prayayuḥ svasvamāśrayam \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Those Brāhmaṇas too, after seeing the Three-eyed Lord directly, became extremely delighted in their minds. They then returned to their respective hermitages.

## \|\| 2.64.121 \|\|

*śaṃbhorvākyaṃ viniścitya sarvajñasya kṛpānidheḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā kāryāṃtaraṃ viprā liṃgānyeva samarciṣuḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. After thinking over the speech of Śaṃbhu, the storehouse of mercy, the Brāhmaṇas abandoned other activities and worshipped the Liṅgas.

## \|\| 2.64.122 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*paṭhitvā pāṭhayitvā ca rahasyākhyānamuttamam \|*  
*śraddhāluḥ pātakairmuktaḥ śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 122 \|\|*

Skanda said:

122\. By reading and causing the excellent narration of the secret to be read, a faithful devotee becomes rid of the sins and is honoured in the world of Śiva.

## Chapter 65 - Manifestation of Parāśareśvarādi Liṅgas

## \|\| 2.65.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*jyeṣṭheśvarasya parito yāni liṃgāni kuṃbhaja \|*  
*tāni paṃcasahasrāṇi munīnāṃ siddhidānyalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. O Pot-born One, the Liṅgas around Jyeṣṭheśvara are five thousand in number. They are perfectly capable of according spiritual powers to the sages.

## \|\| 2.65.2 \|\|

*parāśareśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ jyeṣṭheśāduttare mahat \|*  
*tasya darśanamātreṇa nirmalaṃ jñānamāpyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Parāśareśvara Liṅga is a great Liṅga to the north of Jyeṣṭheśa. Merely by seeing it, pure knowledge is gained.

## \|\| 2.65.3 \|\|

*tatraiva siddhidaṃ liṃgaṃ māṃḍavyeśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*na tasya darśanājjātu durbuddhiṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There itself is the Liṅga called Māṇḍavyeśvara which accords Siddhis. By visiting it, a man does not become evil-minded.

## \|\| 2.65.4 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ ca śaṃkareśākhyaṃ tatraiva śubhadaṃ sadā \|*  
*bhṛgunārāyaṇastatra bhaktānāṃ sarvasiddhidaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Liṅga named Saṅkareśa is there itself. It bestows auspiciousness always. The Deity Bhṛgunārāyaṇa there bestows all spiritual powers on devotees.

## \|\| 2.65.5 \|\|

*jābālīśvara saṃjñaṃ ca liṃgaṃ tatrātisiddhidam \|*  
*tasya saṃdarśanājjātu na jaṃturdurgatiṃ vrajet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The Liṅga named Jābālīśvara there also accords great Siddhis. If one visits it, one will never attain evil state or go to hell.

## \|\| 2.65.6 \|\|

*sumaṃtu muninā śreṣṭhastatrādityaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*tasya saṃdarśanādeva kuṣṭhavyādhiḥ praśāmyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Śreṣṭha Āditya (Excellent Sun-god) has been installed there by Sage Sumantu. As a result of visiting it, the disease of leprosy is cured.

## \|\| 2.65.7 \|\|

*bhairevī bhīṣaṇā nāma tatra bhīṣaṇarūpiṇī \|*  
*kṣetrasya bhīṣaṇaṃ sarvaṃ nāśayedbhāvatorcitā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Goddess Bhairavī there is named Bhīsanā. She has a terrible form. On being worshipped eagerly and fervently, she destroys everything terrible.

## \|\| 2.65.8 \|\|

*tatropajaṃghane liṃgaṃ karmabaṃdhavimokṣaṇam \|*  
*nṛbhiḥ saṃsevitaṃ bhaktyā ṣaṇmāsātsiddhidaṃ param \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Liṅga of Upajaṅghani there liberates (the devotees) from the bondage of Karmas. Devoutly resorted to by men, this great Liṅga bestows spiritual powers within six months.

## \|\| 2.65.9 \|\|

*bhāradvājeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ liṃgaṃ mādrīśvaraṃ varam \|*  
*ekatra saṃsthite dve tu draṣṭavye sukṛtātmanā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Liṅga named Bhāradvājeśvara and Mādrīśvara are excellent. These two are situated in one place and they should be visited together by a person of meritorious soul.

## \|\| 2.65.10 \|\|

*aruṇi sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ tatraiva kalaśodbhava \|*  
*tasya liṃgasya sevātaḥ sarvāmṛddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O Pot-born One, the Liṅga installed by Aruṇi is also there. By doing its service, one shall attain all prosperities.

## \|\| 2.65.11 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ vājasaneyākhyaṃ tatrāstyatimanohṛram \|*  
*tasya saṃdarśanātpuṃsāṃ vājapeyaphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There is a very beautiful Liṅga called Vājasaneya there. By visiting it men shall attain the benefit of Vājapeya.

## \|\| 2.65.12-21 \|\|

*kaṇveśvaraṃ śubhaṃ liṃgaṃ liṃgaṃ kātyāyaneśvaram \|*  
*vāmadeveśvaraṃ liṃgamautathyeśvarameva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*hārīteśvarasaṃjñaṃ ca liṃgaṃ vai gālaveśvaram \|*  
*kuṃbherliṃgaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ tathā vai kausumeśvaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

*agnivarṇeśvaraṃ caiva naidhruveśvarameva ca \|*  
*vatseśvaraṃ mahāliṃgaṃ parṇādeśvarameva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*saktuprastheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ kaṇādeśaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*anyattatra mahāliṃgaṃ māṃḍūkāya nirūpitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vābhraveyeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ śilāvṛttīśvaraṃ tathā \|*  
*cyavaneśvara liṃgaṃ ca śālaṃkāyanakeśvaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kaliṃdameśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ liṃgamakrodhaneśvaram \|*  
*liṃgaṃ kapotavṛttīśaṃ kaṃkeśaṃ kuṃtaleśvarama \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kaṃṭheśvaraṃ kaholeśaṃ liṃgaṃ tuṃburupūjitam \|*  
*matageśaṃ marutteśaṃ magadheyeśvaraṃ tathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*jātūkarṇeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ jaṃbūkeśvarameva ca \|*  
*jārudhīśaṃ jaleśaṃ ca jālmeśaṃ jālakeśvaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evamādīni liṃgāni ayutārdhāni kuṃbhaja \|*  
*smaraṇāddarśanātsparśādarcanānnamanātstuteḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*na jātu jāyate jaṃtoḥ kaluṣasya samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ śubhaliṃgānāṃ jyeṣṭhasthāneti pāvane \|\| 21 \|\|*

12-21. The Various Liṅgas in the Holy Region around Jyeṣṭha Sthāna:

Kaṇveśvara is the auspicious Liṅga, Kātyāyaneśvara Liṅga, Vāmadeveśvara Liṅga, Autathyeśvara, the Liṅga named Hārīteśvara, Gālaveśvara Liṅga, the Liṅga of Kuṃbhi of great merit, Kausumeśvara, Agnivarṇeśvara, Naidhruveśvara, Vatseśvara the great Liṅga, Parṇādeśvara, Saktuprastheśvara Liṅga, Kaṇādeśa, another great liṅga there installed by Māṇḍūkāyani, Bābhraveyeśvara Liṅga, Śilāvṛttīśvara, Cyavaneśvara Liṅga, Śālaṅkāyanakeśvara, Kalindameśvara Liṅga, Akrodhaneśvara Liṅga, Kapotavṛttīśa Liṅga, Kaṅkeśa, Kuntaleśvara, Kaṇṭheśvara, Kaholeśa, the Liṅga adored by Tuṃbaru, Mataṅgeśa, Marutteśa, Magadheyeśvara, Jātūkarṇeśvara Liṅga, Jaṃbukeśvara, Jārudhīśa, Jaleśa, Jalmeśa, Jālakeśvara—these and other Liṅgas number about five thousand. O Pot-born One, if a man remembers, visits, touches, adores, bows down to and eulogizes these auspicious Liṅgas in the excessively sacred Jyeṣṭhasthāna, there arises no sin in him.

## \|\| 2.65.22 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ekadā tatra yadvṛttaṃ jyeṣṭhasthāne mahāmune \|*  
*tadahaṃ te pravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvāghavināśanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

Skanda said:

22\. O great sage, listen; I shall tell you what happened here at the Jyeṣṭhasthāna. It is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 2.65.23 \|\|

*svairaṃ viharatastatra jyeṣṭhasthāne maheśituḥ \|*  
*kautukenaiva cikrīḍa śivā kaṃdukalīlayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Even as Maheśa was enjoying himself as he pleased at Jyeṣṭhasthāna, Śivā too played eagerly games with her ball.

## \|\| 2.65.24 \|\|

*udaṃca nnyaṃcadaṃgānāṃ lāghavaṃ paritanvatī \|*  
*niḥśvāsāmodamudita bhramarākulitekṣaṇā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. She demonstrated the sprightliness of her limbs that moved up and down. As the bees hovered round her, being attracted by the fragrance of her breath, her eyes became slightly disturbed.

## \|\| 2.65.25 \|\|

*bhraśyaddha mmillasanmālya sthapuṭīkṛta bhūmikā \|*  
*svidyatkapolapatrālī sravadaṃbukaṇojjvalā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. As her tresses of hairs became loosened, the excellent garland fell down and covered the ground. Drops of perspiration flowing down her cheeks washed away the lines of cosmetic painting and made her shine all the more.

## \|\| 2.65.26 \|\|

*sphuṭaccolāṃśukapathaniryadaṃgaprabhāvṛtā \|*  
*ullasatkaṃdukāsphālātiśoṇitakarāṃbujā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The brilliance of her body was completely revealed as the upper cloth over her breasts was tossed about. The lotus-like palms of the goddess became excessively red as she continuously beat the springing ball.

## \|\| 2.65.27-29 \|\|

*kaṃdukānuga sadṛṣṭi nartita bhrūcalatāṃcalā \|*  
*mṛḍānī kila khelaṃtī dadṛśe jagadaṃbikā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*aṃtarikṣacarābhyāṃ ca ditijābhyāṃ manoharā \|*  
*kaṭākṣitābhyāmiva vai samupasthitamṛtyunā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vidalotpala saṃjñābhyāṃ dṛptābhyāṃ varato vidheḥ \|*  
*tṛṇīkṛtatrijagatī puruṣābhyāṃ svadorbalāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. Her eyebrows seemed to dance as her eyes closely followed the ball. Mṛḍānī, the beautiful mother of the universe, was playing thus and she was seen by the Ditijas (demons) named Vidala and Utpala who happened to go through the firmament. They were extremely haughty, due to the boons they had received from Brahmā. They were so mighty that they considered all the men in all the three worlds as worthless as grass. In fact, they were caught within the range of vision of the god of Death present nearby.

## \|\| 2.65.30 \|\|

*devīṃ parijihīrṣū tau viṣameṣu prapīḍitau \|*  
*divovateratuḥ kṣipraṃ māyāṃ svīkṛtya śāṃbarīm \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Afflicted by the god of Love, they were eager to abduct the goddess and hence they quickly descended from the sky, resorting to sorcery.

## \|\| 2.65.31-32 \|\|

*dhṛtvā pāraṣadīṃ mūrtimāyātāvaṃbikāṃtikam \|*  
*tāvatyaṃtaṃ sudurvṛttāvaticaṃcalamānasā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sarvajñena parijñātau cāṃcalyāllocanodbhavāt \|*  
*kaṭākṣitātha devena durgādurgārighātinī \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. In the guise of the attendants of the Lord, they came near the mother divine. Those extremely wicked and fickle-minded demons were recognized by Sarvajña, Śiva, the omniscient one through their tremulous eyes. Presently Durgā, the destroyer of terrible enemies, was glanced at significantly.

## \|\| 2.65.33 \|\|

*vijñāya netrasaṃjñāṃ tu sarvajñārdha śarīriṇī \|*  
*tenaiva kaṃdukenātha yugapannijaghāna tau \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Understanding the significance of the glance the goddess sharing half the body of the omniscient Lord simultaneously killed both of them with that very ball.

## \|\| 2.65.34 \|\|

*mahābalau mahādevyā kaṃdukena samāhatau \|*  
*paribhramya paribhramya tau duṣṭau vinipetatuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34 Hit with the ball by the great goddess, the wicked demons of great prowess whirled round and round and collapsed.

## \|\| 2.65.35-36 \|\|

*vṛṃtādiva phale pakve tālādanilalolite \|*  
*daṃbholinā parihate śṛṃgeiva mahāgireḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tau nipātya mahādaityāvakāryakaraṇodyatau \|*  
*tataḥ pariṇatiṃ yāto liṃgarūpeṇa kaṃdukaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Those great Daityas, the wicked ones, who had attempted a criminal misdeed, fell down like two ripe fruits shaken off from the stalk by wind or like peaks of a great mountain struck down by thunderbolt. Thereafter the ball transformed itself unto a Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.65.37 \|\|

*kaṃdukeśvarasaṃjñaṃ ca talliṃgamabhavattadā \|*  
*jyeṣṭheśvara samīpe tu sarvaduṣṭanivāraṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It became a Liṅga named Kandukeśvara very near Jyeṣṭheśvara. It wards off all evil-minded ones.

## \|\| 2.65.38 \|\|

*kaṃdukeśa samutpattiṃ yaḥ śroṣyati mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati yo bhaktastasya duḥkhabhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. How can fear of misery assail that devotee who listens joyously to the manifestation of Kandukeśa and adores it?

## \|\| 2.65.39 \|\|

*kaṃdukeśvara bhaktānāṃ mānavānāṃ nirenasām \|*  
*yogakṣemaṃ sadā kuryādbhavānī bhayanāśinī \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Bhavānī who eradicates fear, brings about the Yogakṣema (‘acquisition and preservation of desired objects’) to men who are devotees of Kandukeśvara and are devoid of sins.

## \|\| 2.65.40 \|\|

*mṛḍānī tasya liṃgasya pūjāṃ kuryātsadaiva hi \|*  
*tatraiva devyā sānnidhyaṃ pārvatyā bhaktasiddhidam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Mṛḍānī always worships that Liṅga. There itself is the perpetual presence of Goddess Pārvatī according spiritual powers to the devotees.

## \|\| 2.65.41 \|\|

*kaṃdukeśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ kāśyāṃ yairna samarcitam \|*  
*kathaṃ teṣāṃ bhavanīśau syātāṃ sarvepsitapradau \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. How can Bhavānī and Īśa be the bestowers of all desired things on those men by whom Kandukeśa, the great Liṅga, has not been worshipped?

## \|\| 2.65.42 \|\|

*draṣṭavyaṃ ca prayatnena talliṃgaṃ kaṃdukeśvaram \|*  
*sarvopasargasaṃghātavighātakaraṇaṃ param \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. That Liṅga named Kandukeśvara should be visited assiduously. It is destructive of all the masses of torments and calamities.

## \|\| 2.65.43 \|\|

*kaṃdukeśvara nāmāpi śrutvā vṛjinasaṃtatiḥ \|*  
*kṣipraṃ kṣayamavāpnoti tamaḥ prāpyoṣṇaguṃ yathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Even on hearing the very name of Kandukeśvara, a mass of sins becomes destroyed immediately like darkness meeting with the hot-rayed sun.

## \|\| 2.65.44 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*saṃśṛṇuṣva mahābhāga jyeṣṭheśvara samīpataḥ \|*  
*yadvṛttāṃtamabhūdvipra paramāścaryakṛddhruvam \|\| 44 \|\|*

Skanda said:

44\. Listen, O blessed one, O Brāhmaṇa, listen to what took place near Jyeṣṭheśvara. It is certainly extremely wonderful.

## \|\| 2.65.45-46 \|\|

*daṃḍakhāte mahātīrthe devarṣipitṛtṛptide \|*  
*tapyamāneṣu vipreṣu niṣkāmaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*daityo duṃdubhinirhrādo duṣṭaḥ prahlādamātulaḥ \|*  
*devāḥ kathaṃ sujeyāḥ syurityupāyamaciṃtayat \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. When Brāhmaṇas were performing great austerities without any desire or motive in Daṇḍakhāta, the great Tīrtha that accords satisfaction unto the Devas, sages and forefathers, the wicked Daitya (named) Dundubhinirhrāda, the maternal uncle of Prahlāda, thought about the means of easily conquering the Devas.

## \|\| 2.65.47-48 \|\|

*kiṃ balāśca kimāhārāḥ kimādhārā hi devatāḥ \|*  
*vicārya bahuśo daityastattvaṃ vijñāya niścitam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*avaśyamagrajanmāno hetavotra vicārataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānhaṃtumasakṛtkṛtavānudyamaṃ tataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. He thought over this many times: ‘What is the source of their (Devas’) strength? What is the food of the Devas? What is their support?’ He came to this decision which, he thought, was the real fact: ‘Certainly on consideration Brāhmaṇas seem to be the real causes.’ So, thereafter, he endeavoured to kill Brāhmaṇas frequently.

## \|\| 2.65.49 \|\|

*yataḥ kratubhujo devāḥ kratavo vedasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*te vedā brāhmaṇādhīnāstato devabalaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. ‘Since the Devas live on Kratus (Yajñas), the Kratus are based on the Vedas and those Vedas are in the custody of Brāhmaṇas, Brāhmaṇas constitute the power of the Devas.

## \|\| 2.65.50 \|\|

*niścitaṃ brāhmaṇādhārāḥ sarve vedāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*gīrvāṇā brāhmaṇabalā nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. It is certain that all the Vedas along with Indra have the support of Brāhmaṇas. There need not be any hesitation in concluding that Brāhmaṇas are the power behind the Devas.

## \|\| 2.65.51 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā yadi naṣṭāḥ syurvedā naṣṭāstataḥ svayam \|*  
*āmnāyeṣu praṇaṣṭeṣu vinaṣṭāḥ śatataṃtavaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. If Brāhmaṇas are annihilated, the Vedas are automatically destroyed. When the Vedas are destroyed, Yajñas get destroyed.

## \|\| 2.65.52 \|\|

*yajñeṣu nāśaṃ gacchatsu hṛtāhārāstataḥ surāḥ \|*  
*nirbalāḥ sukhajeyāḥ syurjiteṣu tridaśeṣvatha \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. When Yajñas are ruined, Devas become deprived of their food and so weak that they can be easily conquered.

## \|\| 2.65.53-54 \|\|

*ahameva bhaviṣyāmi mānyastrijagatīpatiḥ \|*  
*āhariṣyāmi devānāmakṣayāḥ sarvasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*nirvekṣyāmi sukhānyeva rājye nihatakaṃṭake \|*  
*iti niścitya durbuddhiḥ punaściṃtitavānmune \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. When Devas are conquered, I myself will become the honoured Lord of the three worlds. I shall then take away all the unlimited riches of Devas. When the troublesome fellows have been destroyed in the kingdom, I will solely enjoy pleasures.’

After deciding thus, O sage, he directed his thoughts in the following direction:

## \|\| 2.65.55 \|\|

*dvijāḥ kva saṃti bhūyāṃso brahmatejotibṛṃhitāḥ \|*  
*śrutyadhyayana saṃpannāstapobala samanvitāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. ‘Where do those Brāhmaṇas with abundant Brāhmaṇical brilliance, richly endowed with the study of the Vedas and possessing the power of penance, live mostly?

## \|\| 2.65.56 \|\|

*bhūyasāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ tu sthānaṃ vārāṇasī bhavet \|*  
*tānādāvupasaṃhṛtya yāmi tīrthāṃtaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Vārāṇasī must be the spot where Brāhmaṇas preponderate. After destroying them at the outset, I shall go to the other Tīrthas.

## \|\| 2.65.57 \|\|

*yatrayatra hi tīrtheṣu yatrayatrāśrameṣu ca \|*  
*saṃti sarve'grajanmānaste mayādyāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Whatever may be those Tīrthas, whatever may be those hermitages where there are Brāhmaṇas, all those Brāhmaṇas are to be devoured by me all-round.’

## \|\| 2.65.58 \|\|

*iti duṃdubhinirhrādo matiṃ kṛtvā kulocitām \|*  
*prāpyāpi kāśīṃ durvṛtto māyāvī nyavadhīddvijān \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After deciding thus as befitting his race, the wicked Māyāvī (one capable of sorcery) came to Kāśī and killed Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 2.65.59 \|\|

*samitkuśānsamādātuṃ yatra yāṃti ddhijottamāḥ \|*  
*araṇye tatra tānsarvānsa bhakṣayati durmatiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Wherever excellent Brāhmaṇas went to collect sacrificial twigs and Darbha grass in the forest, the evil-minded Daitya (attacked and) devoured them.

## \|\| 2.65.60 \|\|

*yathā kopi na vettyeva tathācchanno'bhavatpunaḥ \|*  
*vane vanecaro bhūtvā yādorūpī jalāśaye \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He took the form of a hunter in the forest or an aquatic animal under the water and hid himself so that no one could recognise him.

## \|\| 2.65.61 \|\|

*adṛśyarūpī māyāvī devānāmapyagocaraḥ \|*  
*divādhyānaparastiṣṭhenmunivanmunimadhyagaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. That Daitya endowed with Māyā-power remained invisible even to Devas. Sometimes he used to sit in the guise of a sage engrossed in meditation like an ascetic during daytime.

## \|\| 2.65.62 \|\|

*praveśamuṭajānāṃ ca nirgamaṃ ca vilokayan \|*  
*yāminyāṃ vyāghrarūpeṇa brāhmaṇānbhakṣayedbahūn \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He used to watch them entering the huts and going out. Then at night he assumed the form of a tiger and devoured many Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 2.65.63 \|\|

*niḥśabdameva nayati natyajedapi kīkasam \|*  
*itthaṃ nipātitā viprāstena duṣṭena bhūriśaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He used to carry them off without making any noise. He did not leave behind even their bones. Thus many Brāhmaṇas were killed by that wicked demon.

## \|\| 2.65.64 \|\|

*ekadā śivarātrau tu bhaktastveko nijoṭaje \|*  
*saparyāṃ devadevasya kṛtvā dhyānasthitobhavat \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Once on the Śivarātri day, a certain devotee performed the adoration of the Lord of Devas in his hut and remained in meditation.

## \|\| 2.65.65 \|\|

*sa ca duṃdubhinirhrāda daityeṃdro baladarpitaḥ \|*  
*vyāghra rūpaṃ samāsthāya tamādātuṃ matiṃ dadhe \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Haughty on account of his strength, Dundubhinirhrāda, the king of Daityas, assumed the form of a tiger and desired to seize him.

## \|\| 2.65.66 \|\|

*taṃ bhaktaṃ dhyānamāpannaṃ dṛḍhacittaṃ śivekṣaṇe \|*  
*kṛtāstramaṃtravinyāsaṃ taṃ krāṃtumaśakanna saḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. He could not attack that devotee engaged in meditation with a firm resolve to realise Śiva, because he (the devotee) had uttered the Astra-Mantra with due Vinyāsas (protective arrangement by Mantra) thereof.

## \|\| 2.65.67 \|\|

*atha sarvagataḥ śaṃbhurjñātvā tasyāśayaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*daityasya duṣṭarūpasya vadhāya vidadhe dhiyam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Thereupon, Śaṃbhu, the omnipresent one, Hara, understood the intention of the wicked Daitya and decided to kill him.

## \|\| 2.65.68 \|\|

*yāvadāditsati vyāghrastāvadāvirabhūddharaḥ \|*  
*jagadrakṣāmaṇistryakṣo bhaktarakṣaṇa dakṣadhīḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Even as the tiger was about to seize him, Hara, the esteemed protector-jewel of the universe against evil-spirits, efficient in the means of protecting the devotees, appeared before him.

## \|\| 2.65.69 \|\|

*rudramāyāṃtamālokya tadbhaktārcita liṃgataḥ \|*  
*daityastenaiva rūpeṇa vavṛdhe bhūdharopamaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. On seeing Rudra coming out of the Liṅga worshipped by that devotee, the Daitya grew in size, comparable to a big mountain, retaining the same form (of a tiger).

## \|\| 2.65.70 \|\|

*sāvajñamathasarvajñaṃ yāvatpaśyati dānavaḥ \|*  
*tāvadāyāṃtamādāya kakṣāyaṃtre nyapīḍayat \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The Dānava looked at Sarvajña with contempt (and went ahead). On seeing him come, the Lord squeezed him within his machine-like armpit and pressed.

## \|\| 2.65.71-74 \|\|

*paṃcāsyastvatha paṃcāsyaṃ muṣṭyā mūrdhanyatāḍayat \|*  
*sa ca tenaiva rūpeṇa kakṣāniṣpeṣaṇena ca \|\| 71 \|\|*

*atyārtamaraṭadvyāghro rodasī paripūrayan \|*  
*tena nādena sahasā saṃ pravepitamānasāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tapodhanāḥ samājagmurniśi śabdānusārataḥ \|*  
*tatreśvaraṃ samālokya kakṣīkṛta mṛgeśvaram \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tuṣṭuvuḥ praṇatā sarve śarvaṃ jayajayākṣaraiḥ \|*  
*paritrātā jagattrātaḥ pratyūhāddāruṇāditaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

71-74. The Pañcāsya (tiger) struck at Pañcāsya (Lord Śiva) with his fist on his head.

Being pressed and squeezed within the armpit the tiger retaining its form howled and roared in distress. His cries filled heaven and earth. With their minds trembling due to that sudden roar, the ascetics came there following the sound in the darkness of the night. There they saw the Lord with the king of beasts locked up in the armpit.

## \|\| 2.65.75 \|\|

*anugrahaṃ kurudhveśa tiṣṭhātraiva jagadguro \|*  
*anenaiva hi rūpeṇa vyāghreśa iti nāmataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. “O Īśa, bless us. O Preceptor of the universe, stay here itself in this selfsame form adopting the name Vyāghreśa.

## \|\| 2.65.76 \|\|

*kuru rakṣāṃ mahādeva jyeṣṭhasthānasya sarvadā \|*  
*anyebhyopyupasargebhyo rakṣa nastīrthavāsinaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. O great Lord, afford protection to Jyeṣṭhasthāna always. Save us, the residents of the Tīrtha, from other torments and calamities.”

## \|\| 2.65.77-80 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vacasteṣāṃ devaścaṃdravibhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tathetyuktvā punaḥ prāha śṛṇudhvaṃ dvijapuṃgavāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*yo māmanena rūpeṇa drakṣyati śraddhayātra vai \|*  
*tasyopasargasaṃghātaṃ ghātayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*etalliṃgaṃ samabhyarcya yo yāti pathi mānavaḥ \|*  
*cauravyāghrādisaṃbhūta bhayaṃ tasya kuto bhavet \|\| 79 \|\|*

*maccaritramidaṃ śrutvā smṛtvā liṃgamidaṃ hṛdi \|*  
*saṃgrāme praviśanmartyo jayamāpnoti nānyathā \|\| 80 \|\|*

77-80. On bearing their words, the Moon-embellished Lord said: “So be it” and continued thus, “O eminent Brāhmaṇas, listen. Undoubtedly I shall destroy the mass of calamities of that man who will visit me here faithfully, in this form itself. If a man worships this Liṅga and goes ahead on his journey, he will not have any fear arising from thieves, tigers etc.

After listening to this story of mine and remembering the Liṅga the man may enter battlefield. He will win (the battle). Not otherwise.”

## \|\| 2.65.81 \|\|

*ityuktvā devadevaśastasmiṃlliṃge layaṃ yayau \|*  
*savismayāstato viprāḥ prātaryātā yathāgatam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. After saying thus, the Lord of the chiefs of Devas merged into that Liṅga. Surprised and dismayed thereby, the Brāhmaṇas went back in the morning to the places where they had come from.

## \|\| 2.65.82 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*tadā prabhṛti kuṃbhottha liṃgaṃ vyāghreśvarābhidham \|*  
*jyeṣṭheśāduttarebhāge dṛṣṭaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ bhayāpaham \|\| 82 \|\|*
