Skanda said:

82\. Ever since then, O Pot-born One, the Liṅga came to be kṇown by the name Vyāghreśvara. It is to the north of Jyeṣṭheśa. If visited and touched, it removes fear.

## \|\| 2.65.83 \|\|

*vyāghreśvarasya ye bhaktāstebhyo bibhyati kiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*yāmā api mahākrūrā jayajīveti vādinaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The servants of Yama are afraid of the devotees of Vyāghreśvara. Even if the Yāmas (servants of Yama) are very cruel, they will deign to say, “Be victorious. Be alive.”

## \|\| 2.65.84 \|\|

*parāśareśvarādīnāṃ liṃgānāmiha saṃbhavam \|*  
*śrutvā naro na lipyeta mahāpātakakardamaiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. On hearing the manifestation of Parāśareśvara and other Liṅgas here, a man can avoid being smeared with the mud of great sins.

## \|\| 2.65.85 \|\|

*kaṃdukeśa samutpattiṃ vyāghre śāvirbhavaṃ tathā \|*  
*samākarṇya naro jātu nopasargaiḥ pradūyate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. On listening to the stories of the manifestation of Kandukeśa and Vyāghreśa, a man will never be distressed due to calamities.

## \|\| 2.65.86 \|\|

*uṭajeśvara liṃgaṃ tu vyāghreśātpaścime sthitam \|*  
*bhaktarakṣārthamudbhūtaṃ syātsamabhyarcya nirbhayaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Uṭajeśvara Liṅga is situated to the west of Vyāghreśa. It has sprung up for the sake of according protection to the devotee. One shall be free from fear after worshipping it.

## Chapter 66 - Śaileśa and Other Liṅgas

## \|\| 2.66.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*jyeṣṭheśvarasya parito liṃgānyanyāni yāni tu \|*  
*tāni te kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇu vātāpitāpana \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. I shall narrate to you the details of the other Liṅgas around Jyeṣṭheśvara. Listen, O scorcher of Vātāpi.

## \|\| 2.66.2 \|\|

*jyeṣṭheśāddakṣiṇe bhāge liṃgamapsarasāṃ śubham \|*  
*tatraivāpsarasaḥ kūpaḥ saubhāgyodakasaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. To the right (south) side of Jyeṣṭheśa is the auspicious Liṅga of celestial damsels. There itself is the well of the celestial damsels named Saubhāgyodaka.

## \|\| 2.66.3 \|\|

*tatkūpajalasusnāto vilokyāpsaraseśvaram \|*  
*na daurbhāgyamavāpnoti nārī vā puruṣothavā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Those men or women who take their holy bath in the water of that well and visit Apsaraseśvara never meet with misfortune.

## \|\| 2.66.4 \|\|

*tatraiva kukkuṭeśākhyaṃ liṃgaṃ vāpīsamīpagam \|*  
*tasya pūjanataḥ puṃsāṃ kuṭuṃbaṃ parivardhate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There itself, near the tank, is a Liṅga named Kukkuṭeśa. By worshipping it the family of the men flourishes and becomes prosperous.

## \|\| 2.66.5 \|\|

*pitāmaheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ jyeṣṭhavāpītaṭe śubham \|*  
*tatra śrāddhaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā pitṝṇāṃ mudamarpayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The auspicious Pitāmaheśvara Liṅga is on the bank of Jyeṣṭhavāpī. By offering Śrāddha there, the man will make the forefathers joyous.

## \|\| 2.66.6 \|\|

*pitāmaheśānnairṛtyāṃ pūjanīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*gadādhareśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ pitṝṇāṃ paritṛptidam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. To the south-west of Pitāmaheśa, Gadādhareśvara Liṅga should be worshipped with great care. It accords satisfaction to the forefathers.

## \|\| 2.66.7 \|\|

*diśi puṇyajanākhyāyāṃ liṃgājjyeṣṭheśvarānmune \|*  
*vāsukīśvarasaṃjñaṃ ca liṃgamarcyaṃ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O sage, in the south-west quarter of Jyeṣṭheśvara is a Liṅga named Vāsukīśvara. It should be worshipped completely.

## \|\| 2.66.8 \|\|

*tatra vāsukikuṃḍe ca snānadānādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*sarpabhītiharāḥ puṃsāṃ vāsukīśaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Holy ablution, Dāna and other rites there in the Vāsukikuṇḍa remove the fear of men from serpents due to the power of Vāsukīśa.

## \|\| 2.66.9 \|\|

*yaḥ snāto nāgapaṃcamyāṃ kuṃḍe vāsukisaṃjñite \|*  
*na tasya viṣasaṃsargo bhavetsarpasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If anyone takes his holy bath in the Vāsukikuṇḍa on the Nāgapañcamī day, he will never be touched (affected) by the poison issuing forth from serpents.

## \|\| 2.66.10 \|\|

*kartavyā nāgapañcamyāṃ yātrā varṣāsu tatra vai \|*  
*nāgāḥ prasannā jāyaṃte kule tasyāpi sarvadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The religious festival should be performed on the Nāgapañcamī day during rainy season there. Serpents become pleased always with that family.

## \|\| 2.66.11 \|\|

*tatkuṇḍātpaścime bhāge liṃgaṃ vai takṣakeśvaram \|*  
*pūjanīyaṃ prayatnena bhaktānāṃ sarvasiddhidam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On the western side of that Kuṇḍa is Takṣakeśvara Liṅga. It should be carefully worshipped. It accords all the spiritual powers to the devotees.

## \|\| 2.66.12 \|\|

*munestasyottare bhāge kuṇḍaṃ takṣakasaṃjñitam \|*  
*kṛtodakakriyastatra na sarpairabhibhūyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O sage, to the north thereof is the Takṣakakuṇḍa. One who performs libations and other rites in water there, is never attacked by serpents.

## \|\| 2.66.13 \|\|

*tatkuṇḍāduttare bhāge kṣetraṃ kṣemakaraḥ sadā \|*  
*bhaktānāṃ sādhvasadhvaṃsī kapālī nāma bhairavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. To the northern side of that Kuṇḍa is Bhairava named Kapālī, who destroys the agitation and fear of the devotees and always accords welfare to the entire holy spot.

## \|\| 2.66.14 \|\|

*bhairavasya mahākṣetraṃ tadvai sādhakasiddhidam \|*  
*tatra saṃsādhitā vidyāḥ ṣaṇmāsātatsiddhimāpnuyuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. That great holy spot of Bhairava accords fulfilment of a spiritual endeavour of an aspirant. The Vidyās (Mantras) repeatedly practised there attain fulfilment within six months.

## \|\| 2.66.15 \|\|

*tatra caṇḍī mahāmuṇḍā bhaktavighnopaśāṃtidā \|*  
*balipūjopahārādyaiḥ pūjyā svābhīṣṭasiddhaye \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. There Goddess Caṇḍī with a huge head destroys great obstacles of the devotees. For the achievement of one’s cherished desires, she should be worshipped with the requisite offerings of adoration, oblations etc.

## \|\| 2.66.16 \|\|

*tasyā yātrāṃ tu yaḥ kuryānmahāṣṭamyāṃ narottamaḥ \|*  
*yaśasvī putrapautrāḍhyo lakṣmīvāṃścāpi jāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. An excellent man who makes the pilgrimage to her (holy spot) on the Mahāṣṭamī day becomes famous, wealthy and endowed with sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 2.66.17 \|\|

*mahāmuṇḍā pratīcyāṃ tu catuḥsāgaravāpikā \|*  
*tasyāṃ snāto bhavetsnātaḥ sāgareṣu caturṣvapi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. To the west of Mahāmuṇḍā (‘goddess with a huge head’) is a well-called Catuḥsāgara Vāpikā. One who takes holy bath therein, shall (be deemed to) have taken his bath in all the four oceans.

## \|\| 2.66.18 \|\|

*mahāprasiddhaṃ tatsthānaṃ catuḥsāgarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*catvāri tatra liṃgāni sāgaraiḥ sthāpitāni ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. That holy spot is extremely well-known. It is named Catuḥsāgara. There are four Liṅgas there installed by four Oceans.

## \|\| 2.66.19 \|\|

*tasyā vāpyāścaturdikṣu pūjitāni dahaṃtyagham \|*  
*taduttare mahāliṃgaṃ vṛṣabheśvarasaṃjñitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Liṅgas on the four sides of that tank, burn sins on being worshipped. To the north of it is a Liṅga named Vṛṣabheśvara.

## \|\| 2.66.20 \|\|

*harasya vṛṣabheṇaiva sthāpitaṃ tatsvabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tasya darśanataḥ puṃsāṃ ṣaṇmāsānmuktirudbhavet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. That has been installed by the Bull of Hara himself out of his devotion (to Hara). By visiting it men will attain salvation within six months.

## \|\| 2.66.21-22 \|\|

*vṛṣeśvarādudīcyāṃ tu gaṃdharveśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*gaṃdharvakuṇḍaṃ tatprācyāṃ tatra snātvā narottamaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*gaṃdharveśvaramabhyarcya dattvā dānāni śaktitaḥ \|*  
*santarpya pitṝdevāṃśca gaṃdharvaiḥ saha modate \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. To the north of Vṛṣeśvara is (a Liṅga) named Gandharveśvara. To the east of it is Gandharvakuṇḍa. An excellent man should take his holy bath there, worship Gandharveśvara, make gifts in accordance with his capacity and offer libations to the forefathers and Devas. He will rejoice in the company of Gandharvas.

## \|\| 2.66.23 \|\|

*karkoṭanāmā nāgosti gandharveśvarapūrvataḥ \|*  
*tatra karkoṭavāpī ca liṃgaṃ karkoṭakeśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. There is a serpent named Karkoṭa to the east of Gandharveśvara. A well called Karkoṭavāpī and a Liṅga named Karkoṭakeśvara are also there.

## \|\| 2.66.24 \|\|

*tasyāṃ vāpyāṃ naraḥ snātvā karkoṭeśaṃ samarcya ca \|*  
*karkoṭanāgamārādhya nāgaloke mahīyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A man who takes his bath in that Vāpī (tank), adores Karkoṭeśa and propitiates Karkoṭa Nāga is honoured in the world of Nāgas (Serpents).

## \|\| 2.66.25 \|\|

*karkoṭa nāgo yairdṛṣṭastadvāpyāṃ vihitodakaiḥ \|*  
*kramate na viṣaṃ teṣāṃ dehe sthāvarajaṃgamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. If Karkoṭa Nāga is visited by men who perform all the rites in the water of Karkoṭavāpī, no poison (originating) from mobile and immobile beings will affect them.

## \|\| 2.66.26 \|\|

*karkoṭeśātpratīcyāṃ tu dhuṃdhumārīśvarābhidham \|*  
*talliṃgābhyarcanātpuṃsāṃ na bhavedvairijaṃ bhayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. To the west of Karkoṭeśa is a Liṅga named Dhundhumārīśvara. The worship of that Liṅga dispels the fear of men from enemies.

## \|\| 2.66.27 \|\|

*purūraveśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tadudīcyāṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*draṣṭavyaṃ tatprayatnena caturvargaphalapradam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. To the north thereof is stationed Purūraveśvara Liṅga. It should be visited with effort. It accords fulfilment of the four aims of life.

## \|\| 2.66.28 \|\|

*diggajenārcitaṃ liṃgaṃ supratīkena tatpuraḥ \|*  
*supratīkeśvaraṃ nāmnā yaśobalavivardhanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. To the east thereof is a Liṅga adored by the elephant of the quarter named Supratīka. It is named Supratīkeśvara. It increases fame and strength.

## \|\| 2.66.29 \|\|

*saraśca supratīkākhyaṃ tatpuro bhāsate mahat \|*  
*tatra snātvā ca talliṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvā dikpatitāṃ labhet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A great lake named Supratīka shines in front of it. By taking holy dip in it and by visiting that Liṅga, a devotee attains the position of the Lords of the quarters.

## \|\| 2.66.30 \|\|

*tatrāstyekā mahāgaurī nāmnā vijayabhairavī \|*  
*rakṣārthamuttarādvāri sthitā pūjyeṣṭasiddhaye \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A Mahāgaurī deity Vijayabhairavī is also there. She is stationed in the northern gateway for the sake of protection. For the attainment of a desired object, she should be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.66.31 \|\|

*varaṇāyāstaṭe ramye gaṇau huṃḍanamuṃḍanau \|*  
*kṣetrarakṣāṃ vidhattastau vighnastaṃbhana kārakau \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On the beautiful banks of Varaṇā are the Gaṇas Huṇḍaṇa and Muṇḍaṇa. They watch and guard the holy spot. They eradicate all obstacles.

## \|\| 2.66.32 \|\|

*tau draṣṭavyau prayatnena kṣetranirvighna hetave \|*  
*huṃḍaneśaṃ muṃḍaneśaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā sukhī bhavet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. They are to be visited with effort for the purpose of keeping the holy spot free from obstacles. After visiting Huṇḍaṇeśa and Muṇḍaṇeśa a devotee shall become happy.

## \|\| 2.66.33 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ilvalāre kathāmekāṃ śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhava \|*  
*varaṇāyāstaṭe ramye yadvṛtta pūrvamuttamam \|\| 33 \|\|*

Skanda said:

33\. O Enemy (killer) of Ilvala, be attentive. Listen to a story of what happened as an excellent event on the charming banks of Varaṇā formerly.

## \|\| 2.66.34 \|\|

*ekadādrīṃdramālokya menā saṃhṛṣṭamānasam \|*  
*umāṃ saṃsmṛtya niḥśvasya provāceti pativratā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Once on seeing the Lord of the Mountains delighted in his mind, the chaste lady Menā, who was reminded of Umā, heaved a sigh and she spoke thus:

## \|\| 2.66.35 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*āryaputra na jānāmi pravṛttimapi kāṃcana \|*  
*vivāhasamayādūrdhvaṃ tasyā gauryā girīśvara \|\| 35 \|\|*

Menā said:

35\. O son of venerable elders (Āryaputra), O Lord of Mountains, I have no news of Gaurī ever since her marriage.

## \|\| 2.66.36 \|\|

*sa vṛṣeṃdragatirdevo bhasmoraga vibhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*mahāpitṛvanāvāso digvāsāḥ kvāsti saṃprati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Where is that Lord now—he who habitually moves about on a stately bull, wears ornaments of serpents and ashes, whose habitation is the extensive cremation ground and who is clad with nothing but the bare quarters?

## \|\| 2.66.37 \|\|

*aṣṭau yā mātaro dṛṣṭā brāhmī prabhṛtayaḥ priya \|*  
*svasvarūpāstā manye'haṃ bālikāḥ kaṣṭahetavaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O beloved one, I think that the eight mothers Brāhmī etc. who appear in their exquisite forms, may cause some distress to the girl.

## \|\| 2.66.38 \|\|

*tasyaikasya na kopyanyostyadvitīyasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*tadudaṃtapravṛttyai ca kriyatāmudyamo vibho \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. That Trident-bearing Lord is without a second; he has no one else. Hence, O lord, may effort be made to get some news about him.

## \|\| 2.66.39 \|\|

*tasyāḥ priyāyā vākyena tadapatyapriyo giriḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ sāsramumā vātsalyasannagīḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. At the speech of his beloved wife, the Mountain fond of his child, spoke these words with tears, his speech being obstructed by excessive affection for Umā.

## \|\| 2.66.40 \|\|

*girirāja uvāca \|*  
*ahameva gamiṣyāmi tasyā mene gaveṣaṇe \|*  
*nitarāṃ bādhate prema tadadṛṣṭyagnidūṣitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

The Lord of Mountains said:

40\. I myself shall go, O Menā, to enquire after her. My fondness for her is being scorched unduly, due to the fire-like fact of not being able to see her.

## \|\| 2.66.41 \|\|

*yadā prabhṛti sā gaurī nirgatā mama sadmataḥ \|*  
*manye mene tadārabhya padmasadmā viniryayau \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Ever since Gaurī set out from my house, I think the Goddess of Fortune too has gone out of my house.

## \|\| 2.66.42 \|\|

*tadālāpāmṛtadhayau na me śabdagrahau priye \|*  
*prāṇeśvari tadārabhya syātāṃ śabdāṃtaragrahau \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O my beloved, accustomed to imbibe the nectarine lisping words of her, my ears have ceased to pay heed to other words ever since that day.

## \|\| 2.66.43 \|\|

*jaivātṛkī yatohnaḥ syāddūrībhūtā dṛśormama \|*  
*aho jaivātṛkī jyotsnā tatohnoti dunoti mām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Ever since my long-lived daughter went out of my sight, even moonlight causes great distress to me.

## \|\| 2.66.44 \|\|

*ityuktvādāya ratnāni vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca \|*  
*dharādhareṃdro niryātaḥ śubhalagnabalodaye \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After saying this the Lord of Mountains took with him jewels and clothes of various kinds and set out when the time was auspicious.

## \|\| 2.66.45 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*kāni kāni ca ratnāni kiyaṃtyapi ca ṣaṇmukha \|*  
*yānyādāya pratasthe sa tāni me brūhi pṛcchataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

Agastya said:

45\. O Six-faced Lord, what were those jewels and how many of them did he take with him, when he set. out? Tell me even as I ask.

## \|\| 2.66.46 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*tulā muktāphalānāṃ tu koṭidvaya parīmitāḥ \|*  
*tathā vāritarāṇāṃ ca hīrakāṇāṃ tulā śatam \|\| 46 \|\|*

Skanda said:

46\. (He took with him) two crores of Tulās (weight of a hundred Palas) of pearls and a hundred Tulās of white shining diamonds.

## \|\| 2.66.47 \|\|

*navalakṣādhikaṃ vipra ṣaḍasrāṇāṃ sutejasām \|*  
*lakṣadvayaṃ vidūrāṇāṃ tulāvimalavarcasāma \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Brāhmaṇa, there were more than nine lakhs of a hundred Tulās highly brilliant (diamonds) of six angles (six cut faces). There were two hundred thousand Tulās of Vidūras (Lapis lazuli) of spotless splendour.

## \|\| 2.66.48 \|\|

*koṭayaḥ padmarāgāṇāṃ paṃcāvaihi tulā mune \|*  
*puṣparāga tulālakṣaṃ guṇitaṃ navasaṃkhyayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O sage, know that there were five crores of Tulās of rubies and nine hundred thousand Tulās of topaz.

## \|\| 2.66.49 \|\|

*tathā gomeda ratnānāṃ tulālakṣamitā munai \|*  
*iṃdranīlamaṇīnāṃ ca tulāḥ koṭyardha saṃmitāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O sage, in the same way (he took with him) there a hundred thousand Tulās of Gomeda jewels and half a crore of Tulās of blue sapphires.

## \|\| 2.66.50 \|\|

*garuḍodgāraratnānāṃ tulāḥ prayutasaṃmitāḥ \|*  
*śuddhavidrumaratnānāṃ tulāśca navakoṭayaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. There were a million emeralds and nine crores of Tulās of pure coral.

## \|\| 2.66.51 \|\|

*aṣṭāṃgābharaṇānāṃ ca saṃkhyā kartuṃ na śakyate \|*  
*vāsasāṃ ca vicitrāṇāṃ komalānāṃ tathā mune \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O, sage, it is impossible to calculate the number of the ornaments intended for the eight different parts of the bodies or of the clothes of tender fabric of diverse colours.

## \|\| 2.66.52 \|\|

*cāmarāṇi ca bhūyāṃsi dravyāṇyāmodavaṃti ca \|*  
*suvarṇadāsadāsyādīnyasaṃkhyātāni vai mune \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. There were many Cāmaras and fragrant articles. O sage, innumerable were the gold pieces, slaves (men and women) etc.

## \|\| 2.66.53 \|\|

*sarvāṇyapi samādāya pratasthe bhūdhareśvaraḥ \|*  
*āgatya varaṇātīraṃ dūrātkāśīmalokayat \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The Lord of Mountains took all these things and set out. After coming to the banks of Varaṇā he looked at Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.66.54 \|\|

*anekaratnanicayaiḥ khacitā'khilabhūmikām \|*  
*nānāprāsādamāṇikyajyotistatatatāṃbarām \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. All the different storeys (of the buildings there) were studded with many gems. The extensive firmament above was lighted up by the splendour of the rubies of the various palatial buildings.

## \|\| 2.66.55 \|\|

*saudhāgravividhasvarṇakalaśojvaladiṅmukhām \|*  
*jayaṃtīvaijayaṃtīnāṃ nikaraistridivasthalīm \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The different quarters shone brightly, due to the golden pinnacles of the mansions. Through the different banners such as Jayantī and Vaijayantī, the city appeared like heaven.

## \|\| 2.66.56 \|\|

*mahāsiddhyaṣṭakasyāpi krīḍābhavanamadbhutam \|*  
*jitakalpadumavanāṃ vanaiḥ sarvaphalāvanaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It was the wonderful sports-ground of the great eight Siddhis. Due to the various groves abounding in all kinds of fruits, it far excelled the gardens of Kalpa trees.

## \|\| 2.66.57 \|\|

*iti kāśīsamṛddhiṃ sa vilokyābhūdvilajjitaḥ \|*  
*uvāca ca manasyeva bhūdhareṃdra idaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On seeing the exuberance and opulence of Kāśī thus, the Lord of Mountains became ashamed. He spoke these words to his own mind.

## \|\| 2.66.58-62 \|\|

*prāsādeṣu pratolīṣu prākāreṣu gṛheṣu ca \|*  
*gopureṣu vicitreṣu kapāṭeṣu taṭeṣvapi \|\| 58 \|\|*

*maṇimāṇikyaratnānāmucchalaccārurociṣām \|*  
*jyotirjālairjaṭilitaṃ yayedamavalokyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

*dyāvābhūmyoraṃtarālaṃ tatheti samavaimyaham \|*  
*īdṛksaṃpattisaṃbhāraḥ kuverasyāpi no gṛhe \|\| 60 \|\|*

*api vaikuṃṭhabhuvane netarasyeha kā kathā \|*  
*iti yāvadgirīṃdrosau saṃbhāvayati cetasi \|\| 61 \|\|*

*tāvatkārpaṭikaḥ kaścittallocanapathaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*āhūya bahumānaṃ tamapṛcchaccācaleśvaraḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

58-61a. ‘The jewels and the rubies put forth excellent lustre on the palaces, streets, ramparts, houses, turrets, doors of diverse kinds etc. The space between heaven and earth is fully brightened with the masses of lustre. I know that such opulence and abundance does not find a place even with the abode of Kubera. It does not exist even in the region of Vaikuṇṭha. What to say of other (worlds)?’

61b-62. Even as the Lord of Mountains was thinking thus in his mind, a pilgrim came within his view. The Lord of Mountains beckoned to him respectfully and asked him:

## \|\| 2.66.63 \|\|

*himavānuvāca \|*  
*haṃho kārpaṭika śreṣṭha adhyāsvaitadihāsanam \|*  
*svapurodaṃtamākhyāhi kimapūrvamihādhvaga \|\| 63 \|\|*

Himavān said:

63\. O excellent pilgrim, sit on this seat. O traveller, tell me the details of your city. What are the special characteristics of this place? What unprecedented thing has happened?

## \|\| 2.66.64 \|\|

*kotra saṃpratyadhiṣṭhātā kimadhiṣṭhātṛ ceṣṭitam \|*  
*yadi jānāsi tatsarvamihācakṣva mamāgrataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Who is the chief administrative head here now? What are his activities? If you know tell everything to me.

## \|\| 2.66.65 \|\|

*sopi kārpaṭikastasya girirājasya bhāṣitam \|*  
*samākarṇya samācaṣṭuṃ mune samupacakrame \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. On hearing the speech of the Lord of Mountains, O sage, the pilgrim began to narrate:

## \|\| 2.66.66-67 \|\|

*kārpaṭika uvāca \|*  
*ācakṣe śṛṇu rājeṃdra yatpṛṣṭosmi tvayākhilam \|*  
*ahāni paṃcaṣāṇyeva vyatikrāṃtāni mānada \|\| 66 \|\|*

*samāyāte jagannāthe parvateṃdra sutāpatau \|*  
*suṃdarānmaṃdarādadrerdivodāse gate divi \|\| 67 \|\|*

The Kārpaṭika (pilgrim) said:

66-67. I shall narrate, O eminent king, listen; I shall mention everything that you ask. O honoured one, only five or six days have elapsed since the arrival of the Consort of the Daughter of the Lord of Mountains, the Lord of the universe from the beautiful Mandara mountain after Divodāsa had gone to heaven.

## \|\| 2.66.68 \|\|

*yo vai jagadadhiṣṭhātā sodhiṣṭhātātra sarvagaḥ \|*  
*sarvadṛksarvadaḥ śarvaḥ kathaṃ na jñāyate vibho \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He who is omnipresent and the presiding deity of the entire universe is the ruler and administrator here. He is Śarva, the bestower of everything. He has vision all-round. O lord, how is he not known (to you)?

## \|\| 2.66.69 \|\|

*manye dṛṣatsvarūposi dṛṣadopi kaṭhoradhīḥ \|*  
*yato viśveśvaraṃ kāśyāṃ na vetsi girijāpatim \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. I think you have a stony form, a heart harder than stone, since you do not know the Consort of the Daughter of the Mountain, Viśveśvara in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.66.70 \|\|

*svabhāvakaṭhinātmāpi sa varaṃ himavāngiriḥ \|*  
*prāṇādhika sutā dānādyo dhinodviśvanāyakam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Better indeed is that mountain Himālaya, though his interior is naturally hard, because he propitiated the Ruler of the universe by giving (in marriage) his daughter dearer to him than his very vital breath.

## \|\| 2.66.71 \|\|

*bibhratsahaja kāṭhinyaṃ jāto gaurīgururguruḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhuṃ prapūjya sutayā srajā viśvagurorapi \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Though Gaurī’s father has congenital hardness, he has become worthy of the esteem of even Viśvaguru (Brahmā), because he had propitiated Śaṃbhu by means of his daughter who was like a garland (worthy of being worn on the head).

## \|\| 2.66.72 \|\|

*ceṣṭitaṃ tasya ko veda vedavedyasya ceśituḥ \|*  
*manāgiti ca jānehaṃ tacceṣṭitamidaṃ jagat \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Who can profess to know the activity of that Lord worthy of being known only through the Vedas? I know only this much that the entire universe is activised by him.

## \|\| 2.66.73 \|\|

*adhiṣṭhātā mayā khyātastathādhiṣṭhātṛ ceṣṭitam \|*  
*apūrvaṃ yattvayāpṛṣṭaṃ tadākhyāmi ca tacchṛṇu \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The presiding deity (of this city) has been mentioned by me. So also the activity of the said presiding deity. The unprecedented thing about which you have asked, I shall now mention. Listen.

## \|\| 2.66.74 \|\|

*śubhe jyeṣṭheśvarasthāne sāṃprataṃ sa umāpatiḥ \|*  
*kāśīṃ prāpya mudā tiṣṭhedgirirājāṃgajā sakhaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The Companion of the Daughter of the King of Mountains rejoices on having come to Kāśī. At present, he, the Consort of Umā, is stationed in the excellent Jyeṣṭheśvara Sthāna.

## \|\| 2.66.75 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*yadā yadā sa girijā mṛdunāmākṣarāmṛtam \|*  
*āviṣkaroti pathiko'drīṃdro hṛṣyettadātadā \|\| 75 \|\|*

Skanda said:

75\. Whenever that traveller uttered the nectar-like letters that constitute the tender name of Girijā, the Lord of Mountains became excessively delighted.

## \|\| 2.66.76 \|\|

*umānāmāmṛtaṃ pītaṃ yeneha jagatītale \|*  
*na jātu jananīstanyaṃ sa pibetkuṃbhasaṃbhava \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. If the nectar-like name Umā has been imbibed by anyone in the universe, O Pot-born One, he will no more suck the breasts of a mother thereafter.

## \|\| 2.66.77 \|\|

*umetidvyakṣaraṃ maṃtraṃ yo'harniśamanusmaret \|*  
*na smareccitraguptastaṃ kṛtapāpamapi dvija \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. If anyone remembers day and night, the two-syllabled Mantra, namely Umā, O Brāhmaṇa, Citragupta will not remember him even if he were a sinner.

## \|\| 2.66.78-79 \|\|

*punaḥ śuśrāva himavānhṛṣṭaḥ kārpaṭikoditam \|*  
*kārpaṭika uvāca \|*  
*rājanviśveśvarārtheyaḥ prāsādo viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 78 \|\|*

*nirmīyate sunirmāṇo janmi nirvāṇadāyinaḥ \|*  
*tadapūrvaṃ na karṇābhyāmapyākarṇitavānaham \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. Again the delighted Himavān heard the utterance of the Kārpaṭika.

## \|\| 2.66.80 \|\|

*yatrātimitratejobhiḥ śalākābhiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*maṇimāṇikyaratnānāṃ prāsādebhittayaḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

The Kārpaṭika said:

O king, have you not even heard with your ears that unprecedented thing viz. that a big mansion is being built by Viśvakarman for the sake of Viśveśvara, the bestower of salvation on all living beings? The mansion is being built elaborately.

80\. There the walls of the palace all-round are made of (bars of) jewels, and rubies. Their splendour excels even the brilliance of the Sun.

## \|\| 2.66.81 \|\|

*yatra saṃti śataṃ staṃbhā bhāsvaṃto dvādaśottarāḥ \|*  
*ekaikaṃ bhuvanaṃ dhartumaṣṭāṣṭāviti kalpitāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. There are one hundred and twelve sparkling pillars as though eight of them were intended to support each of the (fourteen) worlds.

## \|\| 2.66.82 \|\|

*caturdaśasu yā śobhā viṣṭapeṣu samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*tasminvimāne sāstīha śatakoṭiguṇottarā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. In that palace the splendour and beauty all-round is hundred crores of times more than what exists in the fourteen worlds.

## \|\| 2.66.83 \|\|

*caṃdrakāṃtamaṇīnāṃ ca staṃbhādhāra śilāśca yāḥ \|*  
*citraratnamayaistaṃbhaiḥ staṃbhitāstatprabhābharāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The foundation slabs of lunar stone jewels that have the sparkling lustre of the pillars made of jewels of diverse colours are covered by those pillars.

## \|\| 2.66.84 \|\|

*padmarāgeṃdranīlānāṃ śālīnāḥ śālabhaṃjikāḥ \|*  
*nīrājayaṃtyahorātraṃ yatra rajapradīpakaiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Dolls of remarkable splendour made of blue sapphire and rubies hold jewel-set lamps and perform Nīrājana (‘waving of lamps’) rites day and night.

## \|\| 2.66.85-86 \|\|

*sphuratsphaṭikanirmāṇa ślakṣṇa padmaśilātale \|*  
*anekaratnarūpāṇi vicitrāṇi samaṃtataḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*āraktapītamaṃjiṣṭha nīlakirmīravarṇakaiḥ \|*  
*vinyastānīva bhāsaṃte citre citrakṛtāyataḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. On the glossy rocky platform shaped like a lotus and made of glittering crystals, various forms of objects made of gems appear as though perfectly set up by a painter in his picture. They have various colours like pale red, yellow, madder, blue and spotted.

## \|\| 2.66.87 \|\|

*dṛkpicchilā vilokyaṃte māṇikyastaṃbharājayaḥ \|*  
*yato'vimukte svakṣetre mokṣalakṣmyaṃkurā iva \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Rows of ruby-studded pillars dazzle the eyes. They appear like the sprouts of the Glory of Salvation in the surrounding holy spot Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.66.88 \|\|

*ratnākarebhyaḥ sarvebhyo gaṇā ratnoccayānbahūn \|*  
*rāśīṃścakruḥ samānīya yatrādriśikharopamān \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Near that palace huge heaps of jewels resembling peaks of mountains have been made by the Gaṇas who brought them from various oceans.

## \|\| 2.66.89 \|\|

*yatra pātālatalato nāgānāṃ kośaveśmataḥ \|*  
*gaṇairmaṇigaṇāḥ sarve samāhṛtya girīkṛtāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The Gaṇas have brought masses of jewels from the treasuries of the-Nāgas from the nether worlds and have heaped them near the palace like huge mountains.

## \|\| 2.66.90 \|\|

*śivabhaktaḥ svayaṃ yatra paulastyaḥ svadrikūṭataḥ \|*  
*koṭihāṭakakūṭāni ānayāmāsa rākṣasaiḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The devotee of Śiva, the son of Pulastya (i.e. Kubera) has caused crores of gold peaks to be brought through Rākṣasas from the excellent mountain (Meru) and dumped there (near the palace).

## \|\| 2.66.91 \|\|

*prāsādanirmitiṃ śrutvā bhaktā dvīpāṃtarasthitāḥ \|*  
*māṇikyāni samājahruryathāsaṃkhyānyaho nṛpa \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. O king, on hearing that a palace is being built, the devotees residing in other Dvīpas (continents) have brought numerous ruby pieces.

## \|\| 2.66.92 \|\|

*ciṃtāmaṇiḥ svayaṃ yatra kamarṇe viśvakarmaṇe \|*  
*viśrāṇayedahorātraṃ vicitrāṃściṃ titānmaṇīn \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Cintāmaṇi (wish-yielding divine jewel) itself has distributed all kinds of jewels wished for by Viśvakarman in the course of his building activity day and night.

## \|\| 2.66.93 \|\|

*nānāvarṇapatākāśca yatra kalpamahīruhaḥ \|*  
*analpāḥ kalpayaṃtyeva nityabhaktisamanvitāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The wish-yielding celestial trees yielded many banners of different colours with great devotion everyday there.

## \|\| 2.66.94 \|\|

*abdhayo yatra satataṃ dadhikṣīrekṣusarpiṣām \|*  
*paṃcāmṛtānāṃ kalaśaiḥ snapayaṃti dinedine \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Day by day, the oceans of curds, milk, sugarcane juice and ghee bathe it continuously with pots of Pañcāmṛtas.

## \|\| 2.66.95 \|\|

*yatra kāmadughā nityaṃ snapayenmadhudhārayā \|*  
*svadugdhayā svayaṃ bhaktyā viśveśaṃ liṃgarūpiṇam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. There the divine wish-yielding cow, Kāmadhenu, bathes devoutly Lord Viśveśa in the form of a Liṅga with currents of honey milked by herself.

## \|\| 2.66.96 \|\|

*gaṃdhasārarasairyaṃ ca sevate malayācalaḥ \|*  
*karpūraraṃbhā karpūrapūrairbhaktyā niṣevate \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Mountain Malayācala serves the Lord by means of sandal juice. The divine camphor-producing trees named Karpūrāraṃbhā serve devoutly the Lord by means of masses of camphor.

## \|\| 2.66.97 \|\|

*ityādya pūrvaṃ yatrāsti pratyahaṃ śaṃkarālaye \|*  
*kathaṃ taṃ tvamumākātaṃ na vetsi kaṭhināśaya \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. These are the various unprecedented wonderful things that happen everyday in the abode of Śaṅkara. How is it, O hard-hearted one, that you do not know the Lover of Umā?

## \|\| 2.66.98 \|\|

*iti tasya samṛddhiṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā jāmāturadrirāṭa \|*  
*trapayā paribhūtobhūnnitarāṃ kuṃbhasaṃbhava \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. On perceiving such an opulence of his son-in-law, the King of Mountains was overwhelmed with excessive shame, O Pot-born One.

## \|\| 2.66.99 \|\|

*tasmai kārpaṭikāyātha sa dattvā pāritoṣikam \|*  
*punaściṃtāparojāto'drirāṭkārpaṭike gate \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The King of Mountains gave a handsome reward to the Kārpaṭika and when he went away, he was lost in thought.

## \|\| 2.66.100 \|\|

*uvāceti manasyeva vismayotphullalocanaḥ \|*  
*aho bhadramidaṃ jātaṃ yattvayā śrāvi śarmabhāk \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. With his eyes bulging out due to dismay, he said to himself: ‘It is good, O ashamed one, since you have heard (what should be heard).

## \|\| 2.66.101-102 \|\|

*yāvatsaṃpattisaṃbhāraḥ śrūyate dṛśyatetra vai \|*  
*jāmāturatra sadane līlā trijagatīpateḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*tataḥ prābhṛtakastuccho nitarāṃ pratibhāti me \|*  
*kanyārthaṃ yo mayā nīto jāmātuḥ paritoṣakṛt \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. So much of rich opulence is seen here in the abode of my son-in-law who sports about and who is the Lord of the three worlds that the presents brought by me for my daughter and to satisfy my son-in-law appear to me worthless.

## \|\| 2.66.103 \|\|

*ahaṃ manye tathaivāsau yathādarśi mayā purā \|*  
*vṛddhokṣamātrasaṃpattiḥ sarvakarmaparāṅmukhaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. I have been thinking that he continues to be what I had seen of him formerly, as one with a senile, feeble bull as his sole asset and one averse to all active pursuits.

## \|\| 2.66.104 \|\|

*nainaṃ kopi vijānīyānnānvayosya kadā'cana \|*  
*nāmāpi yasya naikaṃ ca kiṃdeśīyaśca nohyate \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. No one knows him fully. He had no family at any time. He does not have even a single name. It cannot even be guessed as to which family he belongs.

## \|\| 2.66.105 \|\|

*kiṃvṛttaśca kimācāro nāmamātreṇa ceśvaraḥ \|*  
*aiśvaryasūcakaṃ vastu yasya kiṃcinna lakṣyate \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. What is his conduct? What are his activities? He is an Īśvara (Lord) only in name. There is nothing to be seen around him that would indicate his prosperity and affluence.

## \|\| 2.66.106 \|\|

*sosau nirvāṇasaṃpattiṃ raṃkāyāpi dadātyaho \|*  
*sumukhaḥ sarvakarmāṇi phalavaṃti karoti saḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. He who was so before, has begun to bestow riches in the form of salvation on even the meanest of a wretch. With a pleasant face, he makes all rites fruitful.

## \|\| 2.66.107 \|\|

*vedavedyo hi sarvajño yatsaṃtāno'khilaṃ jagat \|*  
*yaṃ na kopi hi vedādau vedavedyaḥ sa eṣa vai \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. He is the omniscient one to be known only through the Vedas. The entire universe is his progeny. He is one whom no one has known even at the outset. It is he who is (reputed to be) one who should be known through the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.66.108 \|\|

*yonabhijñaḥ sadājñātaḥ sa sarvajñoyameva hi \|*  
*yasyaikamapi no nāma puṃsā jñeyaṃ na kenacit \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. He alone is the omniscient one who always has remained misunderstood and unknowable. Not even a single name of his can be fully comprehended by any man.

## \|\| 2.66.109 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ sarvanāmāni yasya nāmāni niścitam \|*  
*sosau hi sarvadeśīyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ sarvasiddhidaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. It is certain, he bears all the names of everyone as his names. He belongs to all climes and regions. He is bestower of all supernatural powers on all.

## \|\| 2.66.110-112 \|\|

*yasya deśo na vidito yastu vṛttiparāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*ācārahīnamiva yaṃ purā'paśyaṃ kaṭhoradhīḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

*śrutismṛtī yataḥ sarvamācāraṃ vitta eva hi \|*  
*nāmamātreṇa niyataṃ yamajñāsiṣamīśvaram \|\| 111 \|\|*

*sākṣādīśvara evaiṣa sonyeṣvaiśvaryasūcakaḥ \|*  
*api sarvaguṇādhāro guṇātītaḥ parāparaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

110-112. His native land is unknown. He is averse to all avocations, whom, hard-hearted that I have been, I had viewed formerly as one devoid of all good conduct. But he is actually one from whom the Śrutis and Smṛtis learn all good conduct. He whom I had taken to be an Īśvara only in name is the real Īśvara, one who displays his affluence through others. He is the basis of all Guṇas; he is beyond all Guṇas. He is both Para (cause) and Apara (effect).

## \|\| 2.66.113 \|\|

*arvācīna ihāpyeṣa parācīnaḥ parātparaḥ \|*  
*bhūdharāṇāmahaṃ nātho viśvanātha umāpatiḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. He is junior to me. He is elder to me and beyond me. He is greater (and older) than the greatest (the elder-most). I am the Lord of Mountains. Umā’s husband is the Lord of the universe.

## \|\| 2.66.114 \|\|

*ahaṃ pramitasaṃpattiraprameya dhanohyasau \|*  
*tucchaprābhṛta kastasmānnedānīmasya darśanam \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. I am one of limited assets. He is one with immense, immeasurable wealth. The presents I have are worthless and insignificant. This is not the opportune moment to meet him.

## \|\| 2.66.115-116 \|\|

*kariṣyetha kariṣyāmi vyāvṛttyāgatya karhicit \|*  
*saṃpradhāryeti manasi sāyaṃ sa ca girīśvaraḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*āhūya sarvānanugānpārvatīyānmahābalān \|*  
*ādiṣṭavānidaṃ vākyaṃ sarve yūyaṃ balādhikāḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

115-116. After returning (home) and coming back later I shall do something.’

After resolving thus in his mind, the Lord of Mountains called together all his followers in the evening, all the mountains of great prowess. He gave them the order in these words:

“All of you are greater in power than others.

## \|\| 2.66.117 \|\|

*kurvaṃtvekaṃ mamādeśaṃ yāvannodyati bhānumān \|*  
*tāvacchivālayaṃ caikaṃ vidadhatvatra satvaram \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. You have to carry out this sole behest of mine before sunrise (tomorrow). Erect a temple of Śiva hurriedly.

## \|\| 2.66.118-121 \|\|

*yasminkṛte kṛtārthaḥ syāmiha loke paratra ca \|*  
*samāgatyeha kāśyāṃ yaḥ kuryādekaṃ śivālayam \|\| 118 \|\|*

*tena trailokyamakhilaṃ sālayaṃ kṛtameva hi \|*  
*tena dattāni dānāni mahāṃti vidhipūrvakam \|\| 119 \|\|*

*suparvaṇi supātrāya sutātha śraddhayādhikam \|*  
*yena svavittamānena dharmopārjita vittataḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ śaṃbhormahāsadma na taṃ padmā tyajetkvacit \|*  
*tapāṃsi tena taptāni śīrṇaparṇāśanānyapi \|\| 121 \|\|*

118-121. If this is carried out, I shall become contented here in this world and in the other world too. If anyone erects a temple of Śiva after coming to Kāśī, it is as good as he has made all the three worlds equipped with temples. It is as meritorious as though all great gifts have been duly made by him on an excellent day of festivity to a deserving person with more faith than even for his daughter’s sake. If the great abode of Śaṃbhu is built by anyone in accordance with his wealth acquired through righteous means, the Goddess of Fortune will never forsake him. It is as though all austerities involving the sole intake of withered leaves have been performed by him.

## \|\| 2.66.122 \|\|

*vārāṇasīṃ samāsādya yenākāri śivālayaḥ \|*  
*aśeṣāḥ suviśeṣāḍhyā iṣṭāṃstena mahāmakhāḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. If after reaching Kāśī, a Śiva temple is caused to be built by anyone, it is as though all the excellent and great Makhas (sacrifices) have been performed by him.

## \|\| 2.66.123-124 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānane yena devadevālayaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*iti tasya samādeśaṃ samākarṇyānugāstataḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

*cakrurdevālayaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yāvadvyuṣṭā na yāminī \|*  
*tāvacchaileśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ śaileśena pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*caṃdrakāṃtamaṇeścaṃcatkāṃtiścetitamaṃḍapam \|\| 124 \|\|*

123-124. If the temple of the Lord of Devas is built in Ānandakānana, it is as though all sacrifices have been performed by him with special excellence.”

On hearing his command thus, the followers built an excellent temple before the night dawned. At the same time Śaileśvara Liṅga was installed by the Lord of Mountains. The entire Maṇḍapa (Pavilion) was rendered white due to the sparking lustre of lunar-stone jewels.

## \|\| 2.66.125 \|\|

*alekhayatpraśastiṃ ca praśastākṣaramālinīm \|*  
*vyācakṣāṇāṃ nijāṃ sarvaṃ gotrebhyopyadhikonnatim \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. He caused a laudatory inscription too to be made with excellent writings of the characters, mentioning his superiority over all the other mountains.

## \|\| 2.66.126-127 \|\|

*tato'ruṇodaye jāte snātvā paṃcanade hrade \|*  
*śailarājaḥ kālarājaṃ namaskṛtya samarcya ca \|\| 126 \|\|*

*tatra rāśiṃ samutsṛjya paritastavarito yayau \|*  
*pārvatīyairanugataḥ sarvairapi nijālayam \|\| 127 \|\|*

126-127. Thereafter, at the break of dawn the King of Mountains took his holy dip in the whirlpool of Pañcanada, bowed down to Kālarāja, worshipped him and discharged the heap (of jewels) all-round. He hurriedly left the place followed by his attendants, the Mountains, and went back to his abode.

## \|\| 2.66.128-130 \|\|

*tataḥ prātaḥ samālokya gaṇau huṃḍanamuṃḍano \|*  
*hṛṣṭau devālayaṃ ramyaṃ varaṇāyāstaṭe śubhe \|\| 128 \|\|*

*adṛṣṭapūrvadevāya nivedayitumāgatau \|*  
*tau tu dṛṣṭvā mahādevamumādarśitadarpaṇam \|\| 129 \|\|*

*praṇamya daṃḍavadbhūmau kṛtāṃjalipuṭau gaṇau \|*  
*kṛtābhyanujño bhrūkṣepādvijñaptimatha cakratuḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

128-130. In the morning the two Gaṇas, Huṇḍaṇa and Muṇḍaṇa, saw the beautiful temple of the Lord on the auspicious bank of Varaṇā and became delighted. They came to Mahādeva to intimate to the Lord about the temple not seen before. On seeing Mahādeva to whom Umā was showing the mirror, the two Gaṇas prostrated themselves on the ground before him and stood with palms joined in reverence. When the permission was granted with a gesture from the eyebrows, they submitted:

## \|\| 2.66.131-132 \|\|

*devadeva na jānīvaḥ kenaciddṛḍhabhaktinā \|*  
*atīva ramyaḥ prāsādo nirmito varaṇātaṭe \|\| 131 \|\|*

*āsāyaṃ naikṣicāvābhyāṃ dṛṣṭodyaiva prage vibho \|*  
*gaṇoditamitīśāno niśamyāha girīṃdrajām \|\| 132 \|\|*

131-132. “O Lord of Devas, we do not know (by whom) a very beautiful palace has been erected on the banks of Varaṇā. He must be someone of steadfast devotion. O Lord, till last evening it was not seen by us both. It has been seen only this morning.” On hearing this utterance of the Gaṇas, Īśāna spoke to the Daughter of the Lord of Mountains.

## \|\| 2.66.133-134 \|\|

*vijñātasarvavṛttāṃtaḥ sarvajñopyanabhijñavat \|*  
*acaleṃdrāgajeyāvastatprāsādavilokane \|\| 133 \|\|*

*ityuktveśaḥ sagirijo niragātsagaṇo mune \|*  
*mahāsyaṃdanamāruhya prāsādaṃ draṣṭumutsukaḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

133-134. Though the omniscient Sarvajña (Śiva) had come to know of everything, he spoke like one who did not know: “O Daughter of the King of Mountains, we shall go to see that palace.” After saying this, Īśa set out along with his Gaṇas and the Daughter of the Mountain, O sage, riding on a great chariot since he was eager to see the palace.

## \|\| 2.66.135 \|\|

*athāluloke giriśaḥ prāsādaṃ varaṇātaṭe \|*  
*atīva ramyaracanaṃ yāminīmātranirmitam \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Giriśa saw the palace on the banks of Varaṇā. Though it had been built in the course of a single night, its structure was extremely beautiful.

## \|\| 2.66.136 \|\|

*syaṃdanādavaruhyātha garbhāgāramavīviśat \|*  
*dadarśa ca mahāliṃgaṃ caṃdrakāṃtaśilāmayam \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Getting down from the chariot, he entered the sanctum sanctorum where he saw the great Liṅga entirely made of lunar-stone.

## \|\| 2.66.137 \|\|

*dedīpyamānaṃ mahasā mokṣalakṣmyaṃkurākṛti \|*  
*dṛṣṭiprasādajananaṃ punarjananaśātanam \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. It was extremely sparkling with its brilliance. It was like a sprout of the glory of salvation. It accorded great pleasure to the eyes. It was destructive of the likelihood of rebirth.

## \|\| 2.66.138 \|\|

*kenedaṃ sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ yāvajjijñāsatīśvaraḥ \|*  
*tāvaddarśa purataḥ praśastiṃ kartṛsūcikām \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. While Īśvara evinced a desire to know by whom the Liṅga was installed, he saw before him the laudatory inscription commemorating the constructor.

## \|\| 2.66.139 \|\|

*vācayitveva ca manāṅmanasyeva manojahṛt \|*  
*uvāca devo diṣṭyeti prekṣasvātmapituḥ kṛtim \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. After reading it as it were a little within his mind, the Slayer of Kama said to the goddess: “Well; see your own father’s creation.”

## \|\| 2.66.140-142 \|\|

*umā śrutyeti saṃhṛṣṭā kadaṃbakusumaśriyam \|*  
*ānaṃdāṃkuralakṣmīvadaṃgeṣu paribibhratī \|\| 140 \|\|*

*tato vyajijñapaddevaṃ devī pādau praṇamya ca \|*  
*asmiṃlliṃgavare nātha tvayā stheyamaharniśam \|\| 141 \|\|*

*asya liṃgasya ye bhaktā śaileśasya maheśituḥ \|*  
*tebhyastvaṃ mahatīmṛddhiṃ dāsyasīha paratra ca \|\| 142 \|\|*

140-142. On hearing it, Umā was extremely delighted. She had experienced horripilation all over her body. It was as though the sprouts of the glory of bliss spread over her body attaining the splendour of Kadamba flowers. Thereafter the goddess bowed down to the feet of the Lord and said: “O Lord, you must station yourself in this excellent Liṅga day and night. To those devotees of this great Śaileśa Liṅga of Maheśa you will grant great opulence here and glory hereafter.”

## \|\| 2.66.143-144 \|\|

*tatheti deva uktvā tāṃ pārvatīṃ punarabravīt \|*  
*varaṇāyāṃ kṛtasnānaiḥ śaileśo yaiḥ samarcitaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

*pitṝnsaṃtarpya ca mudā dattvā dānāni śaktitaḥ \|*  
*na teṣāṃ punarāvṛttiratra saṃsāravartmani \|\| 144 \|\|*

143-144. After saying “So be it”, the Lord said to Pārvatī further: “The devotees should take their holy dip in Varaṇā and worship Śaileśa. They should offer libation to the forefathers and joyously make gifts in accordance with their capacity. They will never experience a return to the worldly life.

## \|\| 2.66.145 \|\|

*śailaiśvare mahāliṃge nityaṃ sthāsyāmyahaṃ śubhe \|*  
*pradāsyāmi parāṃ muktimetalliṃgārcake jane \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. O fair lady, I shall be ever present in the great Śaileśvara Liṅga. I shall grant salvation to those people who worship this Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.66.146 \|\|

*śaileśvaraṃ ye drakṣyaṃti varaṇāyāḥ surodhasi \|*  
*teṣāṃ kāśyāṃ nivasatāṃ duḥkhaṃ nābhibhaviṣyati \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. No misery shall ever assail those residents of Kāśī who see Śaileśvara on the excellent banks of Varaṇā.”

## \|\| 2.66.147 \|\|

*umayāpi varo dattastatra liṃge ghaṭodbhava \|*  
*śaileśvarasya ye bhaktāste me putrā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. A boon was granted by Umā in respect to the Liṅga there, O Pot-born One: “There is no doubt about this that the devotees of Śaileśvara are my own sons.”

## \|\| 2.66.148 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāva \|\| \|*  
*iti śaileśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ kathitaṃ te mahāmune \|*  
*idānīṃ kathayiṣyāmi ratneśvarasamudbhavam \|\| 148 \|\|*

Skanda said:

148\. Thus Śaileśvara Liṅga has been described to you, O great sage. Now, I shall explain to you the origin of Ratneśvara.

## \|\| 2.66.149 \|\|

*śrutvā śaileśa māhātmyaṃ śraddhayā parayā naraḥ \|*  
*pāpakaṃcukamutsṛjya śivalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. After hearing the greatness of Śaileśa with great faith, a man will give up the slough of sin and attain Śivaloka.

## Chapter 67 - In Praise of Ratneśvara

## \|\| 2.67.1-2 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*ratneśvarasamutpatiṃ kathayasva ṣaḍānana \|*  
*ratnabhūtaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ yatkāśyāṃ parivarṇyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kosya liṃgasya mahimā kenaitacca pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*etaṃ vistarato brūhi gaurīhṛdayanaṃdana \|\| 2 \|\|*

Note: Ratneśvara Liṅga is in the middie of the road from Maidagin to Mṛtyuñjaya. (BCL 358).

Agastya said:

1-2. O Six-faced Lord, narrate to me the origin of Ratneśvara, the great Liṅga in Kāśī reputed to be made of jewels. What is the greatness of this Liṅga? By whom has it been installed? Describe this in detail, O delighter of the heart of Gauri.

## \|\| 2.67.3 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ratneśvarasya māhātmyaṃ kathayiṣyāmi te mune \|*  
*yathā ca ratnaliṃgasya prādurbhāvo'bhavadbhuvi \|\| 3 \|\|*

Skanda said:

3\. O sage, I shall tell you the greatness of Ratneśvara and how that Liṅga manifested itself on the earth.

## \|\| 2.67.4 \|\|

*śrutaṃ nāmāpi liṃgasya yasya janmatrayārjitam \|*  
*vṛjinaṃ nāśayettasya prādurbhāvaṃ bruve mune \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O sage, I shall narrate how that Liṅga came to appear. This is a Liṅga the name of which, when heard, shall destroy sins accrued in the course of three births.

## \|\| 2.67.5-6 \|\|

*śailarājena ratnāni yāni puṃjīkṛtānyaho \|*  
*uttare kālarājasya tāni tasya girervṛṣāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sarvaratnamayaṃ liṃgaṃ jātaṃ tatsukṛtātmanaḥ \|*  
*śakracāpasamacchāyaṃ sarvaratnadyutiprabham \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The jewels that were kept in a heep by the King of Mountains to the north of Kālarāja (Kālabhairava) became a Liṅga consisting of all jewels, due to the meritoriousness of that Mountain. It has the lustre of all the previous stones and the splendour of Indra’s bow (Rainbow).

## \|\| 2.67.7-9 \|\|

*talliṃgadarśanādeva jñānaratnamavāpyate \|*  
*śaileśvaraṃ samālokya śivau tatra samāgatau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yatra ratnamayaṃ liṃgamāvirbhūtaṃ svayaṃ mune \|*  
*tasya sphuratprabhājālaistatamaṃbaramaṃḍalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tatra dṛṣṭvā śubhaṃ liṃgaṃ sarvaratnasamudbhavam \|*  
*bhavānyadṛṣṭapūrvā hi paripapraccha śaṃkaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. The jewel of wisdom is obtained merely at the sight of that Liṅga.

After visiting Śaileśvara, Śiva and Śivā came to the place where, O sage, the Ratnamaya Liṅga constituted of jewels, had manifested itself. The vast region of the firmament was pervaded by its sparkling clusters of lustre. On seeing that splendid Liṅga created out of all Ratnas and not seen before, Bhavānī asked Saṅkara:

## \|\| 2.67.10-12 \|\|

*devadeva jagannātha sarvabhaktābhayaprada \|*  
*kutastyametalliṃgaṃ dvisaptapātālamūlavat \|\| 10 \|\|*

*jvālājaṭilitākāśaṃ prabhābhāsita diṅmukham \|*  
*kimākhyaṃ kiṃ svarūpaṃ ca kiṃ prabhāvaṃ bhavāṃtaka \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yasya saṃvīkṣaṇādeva manometīva hṛṣṭavat \|*  
*ihaiva ramate nātha kathayaitatprasādataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. “O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the universe, O bestower of freedom from fear on all devotees, whence has this Liṅga come? Its root penetrates as far as Pātāla. With its flames and rays it permeates the sky fully. Through its lustre it illuminates the quarters. What is its name? What is its form? O dispeller of Bhava (worldly existence), what is its power? Mere sight of this delights my mind, which feels pleased here alone. O Lord, be pleased to describe it.”

## \|\| 2.67.13 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇvaparṇe samākhyāmi yattvayā pṛcchi pārvati \|*  
*svarūpametalliṃgasya sarvatejonidheḥ param \|\| 13 \|\|*

The Lord of Devas said:

13\. O Aparṇā, Listen. I shall tell you, O Pārvatī, what you have been asking, the features of this Liṅga, the receptacle of all brilliance.

## \|\| 2.67.14 \|\|

*tava pitrā himavatā girirājena bhāmini \|*  
*tvāmuddiśya mahāratnasaṃbhārotrāpyanāyi hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O fair lady, for your sake a huge collection of jewels was brought here by your father Himavān, the Lord of Mountains.

## \|\| 2.67.15 \|\|

*atra tāni ca ratnāni rāśīkṛtya himādriṇā \|*  
*sukṛtopārjitānyeva yayau svasadanaṃ punaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. All these jewels had been acquired by Himādri through his own merit. He kept all those Ratnas (jewels) as a heap here and went back to his abode.

## \|\| 2.67.16 \|\|

*tavārthaṃ vāmamārthaṃ vā śraddhayā yatsamarpyate \|*  
*kāśyāṃ tasya parīpāko bhavedīdṛgvidho'naghe \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O sinless lady, whether it is for your sake or for my sake, whatever is offered with great faith at Kāśī will bear the fruit in this manner.

## \|\| 2.67.17 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ ratneśvarākhyaṃ vai matsvarūpaṃ hi kevalam \|*  
*asya prabhāvo hi mahānvārāṇasyāmume dhruvam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. This Liṅga named Ratneśvara has my form and features alone. In Vārāṇasī its influence is very great, indeed, O Umā.

## \|\| 2.67.18 \|\|

*sarveṣāmiha liṃgānāṃ ratnabhūtamidaṃ param \|*  
*ato ratneśvaraṃ nāma paraṃ nirvāṇaratnadam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It is the very crest-jewel of all the Liṅgas here. Hence its name Ratneśvara. It bestows the greatest jewel in the form of salvation.

## \|\| 2.67.19 \|\|

*anenaiva suvarṇena pitrā rāśīkṛtena ca \|*  
*prāsādamasya liṃgasya vidhāpaya maheśvari \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O Māheśvarī, get a mansion erected for this Liṅga with this gold kept in a heap by your father.

## \|\| 2.67.20 \|\|

*liṃgaprāsādakaraṇātkhaṃḍasphuṭita saṃskṛteḥ \|*  
*liṃgasthāpanajaṃ puṇyaṃ helayaiveha labhyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The merit of installing a Liṅga can be easily obtained by getting the mansion of the Liṅga built by a person of manifested fervour.

## \|\| 2.67.21 \|\|

*tatheti bhagavatyoktvā gaṇāḥ prāsādanirmitau \|*  
*somanaṃdi prabhṛtayo 'saṃkhyā vyāpāritā mune \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Saying “So be it”, the goddess engaged the numerous Gaṇas beginning: with Somanandin in the construction of the mansion, O sage.

## \|\| 2.67.22 \|\|

*gaṇaiśca kāṃcanamayo nānākautukacitritaḥ \|*  
*nirmame yāmamātreṇa prāsādo meruśṛṃgavat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Within a Yāma (3 hours) a golden palace resembling the peak of Meru was built by the Gaṇas. The palace had many wonderful things enhancing its variegated character.

## \|\| 2.67.23 \|\|

*devī pradṛṣṭavadanā dṛṣṭvā prāsādanirmitim \|*  
*gaṇebhyo vyataradbhūri samānaṃ pāritoṣikam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. As evidenced by her beaming face, the goddess became highly delighted on seeing the completed construction of the mansion. She honoured the Gaṇas by distributing presents among them.

## \|\| 2.67.24 \|\|

*punaśca devī papraccha praṇipātapuraḥsaram \|*  
*mahimānaṃ mahādevaṃ liṃgasyāsya mahāmune \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Again, after due obeisance, the goddess asked Mahādeva about the greatness of this Liṅga, O great sage.

## \|\| 2.67.25 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*liṃgaṃ tvanādisaṃsiddhametaddevi śubhapradam \|*  
*āvirbhūtamidānīṃ ca tvatpituḥ puṇyagauravāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

The Lord of Devas said:

25\. O Devī, this Liṅga has already been in existence as it is beginningless; but it manifested itself due to the greatness of the merit of your father.

## \|\| 2.67.26 \|\|

*guhyānāṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ kṣetre'smiściṃtitapradam \|*  
*kalau kaluṣabuddhīnāṃ gopanīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. This is the greatest among great secrets in this holy spot. It accords whatever is thought of. In Kali age, it should be carefully kept as a secret from persons of defiled intellect.

## \|\| 2.67.27 \|\|

*yathā ratnaṃ gṛhe guptaṃ na kaiścijjñāyate paraiḥ \|*  
*avimukte tathā liṃgaṃ ratnabhūtaṃ gṛhe mama \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Just as a precious stone kept hidden in the house is not known to others, so also is this Liṅga evolved out of Ratnas in my house Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.67.28 \|\|

*yāni brahmāṃḍamadhyetra saṃti liṃgāni pārvati \|*  
*tairarcitāni sarvāṇi ratneśo yaiḥ samarcitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If Ratneśa is adored, O Pārvatī, it is as though all the Līṅgas in the entire universe have been worshipped by them.

## \|\| 2.67.29 \|\|

*pramādenāpi yairgauri liṃgaṃ ratneśamarcitam \|*  
*te bhavaṃtyeva niyataṃ saptadvīpeśvarā nṛpāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Gaurī, if people were to adore Ratneśa Liṅga even by some mistake, they will invariably become kings ruling the seven continents.

## \|\| 2.67.30 \|\|

*trailokye yāni vastūni ratnabhūtāni tāni tu \|*  
*ratneśvaraṃ samabhyarcya sakṛtprāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. By adoring once the Liṅga named Ratneśvara, a man obtains all the objects which in value or importance are on a par with jewels in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.67.31 \|\|

*pūjayiṣyaṃti ye liṃgaṃ ratneśaṃ kāmavarjitāḥ \|*  
*te sarve madgaṇā bhūtvā prāṃte drakṣyaṃti māmiha \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Those who worship Ratneśvara Liṅga without any desire will become my Gaṇas in the end and see me here.

## \|\| 2.67.32 \|\|

*rudrāṇāṃ koṭijapyena yatphalaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhyate devi ratneśasya samarcanāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Oh goddess, by adoring Ratneśa, that merit is obtained which, it is proclaimed, is the merit of chanting the Rudriya Mantras a crore times.

## \|\| 2.67.33 \|\|

*liṃge cānādisaṃsiddhe yadvṛttaṃ tadbravīmi te \|*  
*itihāsaṃ mahāścaryaṃ sarvapāpanikṛṃtanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. With respect to this Liṅga that has been existing without a beginning there is an event that happened before. I shall tell you that wonderful legend which will destroy all sins.

## \|\| 2.67.34-36 \|\|

*pureha nartakī kācidāsīnnāṭyārthakovidā \|*  
*saikadā phālgune māsi śivarātryāṃ kalāvatī \|\| 34 \|\|*

*nanarta jāgaraṃ prāpya jagau gītaṃ ca peśalam \|*  
*svayaṃ ca vādayāmāsa nānāvādyāni vādyavit \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tena tauryatrikeṇāpi prīṇayitvātha sā naṭī \|*  
*ratneśvaraṃ mahāliṃgaṃ deśamiṣṭaṃ jagāma ha \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. Formerly there was a dancing girl here named Kalāvatī. She was an adept in the art of dance. Once in the month of Phālguna, on the Śivarātri day, she kept awake throughout the night, danced and sang very sweetly. She was clever in playing on musical instruments too which she herself played. That dancing girl thus propitiated Ratneśvara Mahāliṅga by means of triple symphony and returned to her desired land.

## \|\| 2.67.37 \|\|

*kāladharmavaśaṃyātā tatra sā varanartakī \|*  
*sutā gaṃdharvarājasya vasubhūterbabhūva ha \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. There that excellent dancer met with death. She became the daughter of Vasubhūti, a king of Gandharvas.

## \|\| 2.67.38 \|\|

*saṃgītasya savādyasya tasya lāsyasyapuṇyataḥ \|*  
*tatreśāgre kṛtasyeha jāgare śivarātrije \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. That was due to the merit she acquired through music, instrumental and vocal, and dance displayed before the Lord during the period of keeping awake on the Śivarātri night.

## \|\| 2.67.39 \|\|

*ramyā ratnāvalī nāma rūpalāvaṇyaśālinī \|*  
*kalākalāpakuśalā madhurālāpavādinī \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. She became famous by the name Ratnāvalī. She was beautiful with exquisite form and features. She was clever in all fine arts. Her speech was very sweet.

## \|\| 2.67.40 \|\|

*piturānaṃdakṛnnityaṃ vasubhūterghaṭodbhava \|*  
*sarvagāṃdharvakuśalā guṇaratnamahākhaniḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O Pot-born One(?), she delighted her father Vasubhūti always as she was very clever in all Gandharva arts and a veritable mine of the gems of good qualities.

## \|\| 2.67.41 \|\|

*mune sakhītrayaṃ tasyāścāru cāturyabhājanam \|*  
*śaśilekhānaṃgalekhā citralekheti nāmataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O sage(?), she had three female companions of great skill and cleverness. Their names were Śaśilekhā, Anaṅgalekhā and Citralekhā.

## \|\| 2.67.42 \|\|

*tisṛbhistābhirekatra vāgdevīpariśīlitā \|*  
*tābhyaḥ sarvāḥ kalāḥ prādātpariprītā sarasvatī \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Along with those three girls she (Ratnāvalī) meditated on the goddess of speech in one place. The delighted Sarasvatī granted all of them all the arts.

## \|\| 2.67.43 \|\|

*prāpya ratnāvalī gauri sā janmāṃtaravāsanām \|*  
*ratneśvarasya liṃgasya jagrāha niyamaṃ śubham \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O Gaurī, due to the latent impressions of her practice in the previous birth, Ratnāvalī imposed upon herself the auspicious vow and observance of Ratneśvara Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.67.44-45 \|\|

*ratnabhūtasya liṃgasya kāśyāṃ ratneśvarasya vai \|*  
*nityaṃ saṃdarśanaṃ prāpya vakṣyāmyapi vaco mukhe \|\| 44 \|\|*

*itthaṃ niyamavatyāsītsā gaṃdharvasutottamā \|*  
*tābhiḥ sakhībhiḥ sahitā nityaṃ liṃgaṃ ca paśyati \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Her vow was: “It is only after visiting the jewel-made Liṅga in Kāśī of Ratneśvara everyday that I will utter a word.” That excellent daughter of the Gandharva used to visit the Liṅga everyday accompanied by those friends.

## \|\| 2.67.46 \|\|

*ekadārādhya ratneśaṃ mamaitalliṃgamuttamam \|*  
*samānarca ca sā bālā ramyayā gītamālayā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Once after propitiating this excellent Liṅga of mine, that girl adored me with a series of sweet songs.

## \|\| 2.67.47 \|\|

*sakhyaḥ pradakṣiṇīkartuṃ liṃgaṃ tisro'pyume gatāḥ \|*  
*tasyā gītena tuṣṭohaṃ liṃgastho varadobhavam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Umā, all the three friends had gone away for circumambulation. Satisfied by her songs, remaining stationed in the Liṅga, I granted a boon:

## \|\| 2.67.48 \|\|

*yastvayā raṃsyate rātrāvadya gaṃdharvakanyake \|*  
*tavanāmasamānākhyaḥ sa te bhartā bhaviṣyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. “O Gandharva girl, he who has a name similar to yours and will have his dalliance with you this night, will become your husband.”

## \|\| 2.67.49 \|\|

*iti liṃgāṃbudherjātāṃ paripīya vacaḥsudhām \|*  
*babhūvānaṃdasaṃdoha maṃtharātīva hrīmatī \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. After imbibing the nectar-like words that issued from the Liṅga even as the nectar issued from the ocean, she became highly delighted as well as bashful too.

## \|\| 2.67.50 \|\|

*gatātha vyomamārgeṇa sakhībhiḥ svapiturgṛham \|*  
*kathayaṃtī nijodaṃtaṃ tamālīnāṃ puro mudā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thereafter, along the aerial path she went to her father’s house in the company of her companions when she joyously divulged the news of the boon to the companions.

## \|\| 2.67.51 \|\|

*tābhirdiṣṭyeti diṣṭyeti sakhībhiḥ parinaṃditā \|*  
*adya te vāṃchitaṃ bhāvi ratneśasya samarcanāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. She was congratulated by the companions saying, “Excellent! Good fortune! Good luck!” They said further: “Today your desire will become fulfilled, due to your adoration of Ratneśvara.

## \|\| 2.67.52 \|\|

*yadyāyāti sa te rātrāvadya kaumārahārakaḥ \|*  
*coro bāhulatāpāśaiḥ pāśitavyotiyatnataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If to-night that person who will take away your virginity comes, that thief should be carefully fettered with the cords of your creeper-like arms.

## \|\| 2.67.53 \|\|

*gocarīkriyatesmābhiryathā sa sukṛtaikabhūḥ \|*  
*prātareva tava preyānratneśādiṣṭa iṣṭakṛt \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. (If he is fettered) that fortunate fellow, your lover, directed by Ratneśa can be seen by us in the morning as the person granting you your desired boon.

## \|\| 2.67.54 \|\|

*yātāsvasmāsu hṛṣṭāsu bhavatī śayagauravāt \|*  
*aho ratneśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ pratyakṣīkṛtavatyasi \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. It is a miracle that you could see the Lord directly in the Ratneśvara Liṅga, due to your weighty merit, when we had gone away delightedly.

## \|\| 2.67.55 \|\|

*ahobhāgyodayo nṛṇāmaho puṇyasamucchrayaḥ \|*  
*ekasyaiva bhavetsiddhiryadekatrāpi tiṣṭhatām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Wonderful is the outcome of the fortune of men. Wonderful is the excess of their merit. Realization of the desire occurs only to one while many are standing together in one place.

## \|\| 2.67.56 \|\|

*satyaṃ vadaṃti nāsatyaṃ daivaprādhānyavādinaḥ \|*  
*daivameva phaledekaṃ nodyamo nāparaṃ balam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. ‘It is the fate alone that becomes fruitful. Neither endeavour nor any other powerful thing.’ So say those who support the contention of those who give importance to fate. They speak truth not falsehood.

## \|\| 2.67.57 \|\|

*bhavatyā api cāsmākameka eva hi codyamaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ daivaṃ phalatyekaṃ yathā tava na naḥ puraḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Your endeavour as well as ours is one and the same. But fate makes one fruitful as in your case, and not so in our case.

## \|\| 2.67.58 \|\|

*lokānāṃ vyavahāroyamāliproktaprasaṃgataḥ \|*  
*paraṃ manorathāvāptistava yā saiva naḥ sphuṭam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. But, O friend, it is only what is generally believed by people that is given expression to by us incidentally. But actually the fulfilment of your cherished desire is clearly the same as that of ours.”

## \|\| 2.67.59 \|\|

*iti saṃvyāharaṃtīnāmanaṃtodhvā'titucchavat \|*  
*kṣaṇāttāsāṃ vyatikrāṃtaḥ prāptāśca svaṃsvamālayam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Even as they were speaking thus, a long, endless way was left behind by them in a moment as though it was very insignificant. They reached their respective abodes.

## \|\| 2.67.60 \|\|

*atha prātaḥ samutthāya punarekatra saṃgatāḥ \|*  
*sā ca maunavatī tābhiḥ paribhukteva lakṣitā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Again in the morning, they all got up and gathered together in one place. She was silent but was clearly seen by them as though she had been sexually enjoyed.

## \|\| 2.67.61 \|\|

*tūṣṇīṃ prāpyātha kāśīṃ sā snātvā maṃdākinījale \|*  
*sakhībhiḥ sahitāpaśyalliṃgaṃ ratneśvaraṃ mama \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Remaining silent throughout, she reached Kāśī and took her bath in the waters of Mandākinī along with her companions. She visited my Liṅga named Ratneśvara.

## \|\| 2.67.62 \|\|

*nirvartya niyamaṃ sātha lajjāmukulitekṣaṇā \|*  
*nirbaṃdhena vayasyābhiḥ paripṛṣṭā jagāda ha \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After fulfilling the conditions of her vow and observances, she became nervously bashful with eyes shrinking like buds. On being persistently asked by her friends she said:

## \|\| 2.67.63-66 \|\|

*ratnāvalyuvāca \|*  
*atha ratneśa yātrāyāḥ prayātāsu svamaṃdiram \|*  
*bhavatīṣu smaraṃtyeva tadratneśavaco'mṛtam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*saviśeṣāṃgasaṃskārā'viśaṃ saṃveśamaṃdiram \|*  
*nidrādaridranayanā tadvilokanalālasā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*balātsvapnadaśāṃ prāptā bhāvinorthasya gauravāt \|*  
*ātmavismaraṇe hetū tato me dvau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*taṃdrī tadaṃgasaṃsparśau mama bodhāpahārakau \|*  
*taṃdryā paravaśā cāsaṃ tatastatsparśanena ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

Ratnāvalī said:

63-66. After concluding the journey to the shrine of Ratneśvara when you all returned to your respective abodes, I continued to remember the nectar-like words of Ratneśa. After elaborate and scrupulous make-up and embellishment of the limbs, I entered the bed chamber. As I was overzealous for seeing him, my eyes were deprived of sleep. But due to the weightiness of the inevitability of the future events, I was led to a dreamy state forcibly. There had been two causes for my self-forgetfulness. Utter lassitude and the gentle touch of his limbs dispelled my consciousness. I was already helpless due to lassitude and further due to his touch.

## \|\| 2.67.67-70 \|\|

*na jāne tvatha kiṃ vṛttaṃ kāhaṃ kvāhaṃ sa cātha kaḥ \|*  
*taṃ nirjigamiṣuṃ sakhyo yāvaddhartuṃ prasāritaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*doḥ kaṃkaṇena ripuṇā kvaṇitaṃ tāvadutkaṭam \|*  
*mahatā siṃjitenāhaṃ tenālpaparibodhitā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*sukhasaṃtānapīyūṣa hrade parinimajya vai \|*  
*kṣaṇena tadviyogāgnikīlāsu patitā balāt \|\| 69 \|\|*

*kiṃkulīyaḥ sa no vedmi kiṃdeśīyaḥ kimākhyakaḥ \|*  
*dunoti nitarāṃ sakhyastadviśleṣānalo mahān \|\| 70 \|\|*

67-70. I do not know what happened thereafter including who I was, where I was and who he was. As he was about to go out, dear friends, I stretched my arms to catch hold of him, when my bangles behaved inimically jingling excessively. I was brought to the state of wakefulness slightly on account of that loud sound. After being submerged in the nectarine whirlpool of continuous pleasure, I was forcibly made to fall within a moment into the flames of the fire of separation from him. I do not know to which family he belongs or to which land. I do not know what his name is. But, O friends, the great fire of separation from him distresses me very much.

## \|\| 2.67.71-75 \|\|

*analpotkalitaṃ cetaḥ punastatsaṃgamāśayā \|*  
*prāṇānāṃ me yiyāsūnāmekameva mahauṣadham \|\| 71 \|\|*

*vayasyā niśibhuktasya tasyaiva punarīkṣaṇam \|*  
*bhavatīnāmadhīnaṃ ca tatpunardarśanaṃ mama \|\| 72 \|\|*

*kā'līkamālayo vakti snigdhamugdhesakhījane \|*  
*taddarśanena sthāsyaṃti prāṇā yāsyaṃti cānyathā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*daśamyavasthā sannahyedbādhituṃ mādhunā bhṛśam \|*  
*iti tasyā giraḥ śrutvā dūnāyā nitarāṃ ca tāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*pravepamānahṛdayāḥ procurvīkṣya parasparam \|\| 75 \|\|*

71-75. My mind is excessively anxious with the hope of a subsequent contact with him. There is only one effective medicine for the vital breaths which are about to depart from the body, O friends, and that is seeing again that man enjoyed in the night. The chance for a second vision of him for me depends upon you all, O my companions. Which girl will utter a lie to her friends charming and affectionate? The vital breaths will continue within me if he is seen. Otherwise they will depart. The tenth state (of certain death) will get ready to afflict me.

## \|\| 2.67.76 \|\|

*sakhya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yasya grāmo na no nāma nānvayo nāpi budhyate \|*  
*sa kathaṃ prāpyate bhadre ka upāyo vidhīyatām \|\| 76 \|\|*

On hearing these words of that distressed girl, they too experienced trepidation of the heart. They looked at each other and said:

The Girl Companions said:

76\. O fair lady, how is he to be found out when neither his name, nor his native village, nor his ancestry are known? What means of remedy can be employed?

## \|\| 2.67.77-79 \|\|

*iti ratnāvalī śrutvā sasaṃdehāṃ ca tadgiram \|*  
*vayasyāstadavāptau me yūyaṃ kuṃṭhi mumūrcha ha \|\| 77 \|\|*

*ityardhoktena sā bālā yūyaṃ kuṃṭhitaśaktayaḥ \|*  
*yadvaktavyaṃ tviti tayā yūyaṃ kuṃṭhīti bhāṣitam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*tatastāstvaritāḥ sakhyaḥ paritāpopahārakān \|*  
*bahuśaḥ śītalopāyānvyadhurmohapraśāṃtaye \|\| 79 \|\|*

77-79. On hearing their words expressive of doubts, that girl could say only partially what she wanted to say. Before completing her statement she swooned. She evidently wanted to say, “O my friends, you have no power in the task of enabling me to meet him again.” Thereupon the female companions did everything necessary to remove distress and restore consciousness by applying cooling materials.

## \|\| 2.67.80 \|\|

*vyapaiti na yadā mūrchā tattacchītopacārataḥ \|*  
*tasyāstadaikayānītaṃ ratneśasnapanodakam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. When she could not be brought back to consciousness from the swoon by means of the cooling process, Ratneśa-Snapanodakam \[Snapanodaka\] (the water with which the Ratneśvara Liṅga was bathed) was brought by one of the friends.

## \|\| 2.67.81 \|\|

*tadukṣaṇātkṣaṇādeva tanmūrchā virarāma ha \|*  
*suptotthiteva sāvādīnmuhuḥ śivaśiveti ca \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. When she was sprinkled with it, she was revived from the state of swooning immediately, as though she woke from sleep. Just then she began to say, “Śiva! Śiva!”

## \|\| 2.67.82 \|\|

*skadaṃ uvāca \|*  
*śraddhāvatāṃ svabhaktānāmupasarge mahatyapi \|*  
*nopāyāṃtaramastyeva vineśa caraṇodakam \|\| 82 \|\|*

Skanda said:

82\. Even when there is great calamity and torment no devotee with abiding faith has any other remedy except the water with which the feet of the Lord have been washed.

## \|\| 2.67.83 \|\|

*ye vyādhayopi duḥsādhyā bahiraṃtaḥ śarīragāḥ \|*  
*śraddhayeśodakasparśātte naśyaṃtyeva nānyathā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Even those ailments within the body or outside the body (i.e. internal and external ailments) which are incurable, perish by touching (and sipping) the water of the Lord with great faith. Not otherwise.

## \|\| 2.67.84 \|\|

*sevitaṃ yena satataṃ bhagavaccaraṇodakam \|*  
*taṃ bāhyābhyaṃtaraśuciṃ nopasarpati durgatiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. He, by whom the water from the feet of the Lord has been resorted to, becomes pure within and without. No wretched state overtakes him.

## \|\| 2.67.85 \|\|

*ādhibhautikatāpaṃ ca tāpaṃ vāpyādhidaivikam \|*  
*ādhyātmikaṃ tathā tāpaṃ harecchrīcaraṇodakam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The water from the glorious feet (of the Lord) shall dispel all the three types of distress—that caused by other living beings or bhūtas (elements), that by supernatural beings, and that caused by bodily ailments.

## \|\| 2.67.86 \|\|

*vyapetasaṃjvarā cātha gaṃdharvatanayā mune \|*  
*ucitajñeti hovāca tāḥ sakhīḥ srigdhadho radhīḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The daughter of the Gandharva got rid of her feverish ailment. Tender and decisively bold in her intellect and fully aware of what was relevant, she said thus to her companions:

## \|\| 2.67.87 \|\|

*ratnāvalyuvāca \|*  
*śaśilekhenaṃgalekhe citralekhe madīhitaṃ \|*  
*yūyaṃ kuṃṭhitasāmarthyāḥ kuto vastāḥ kalāḥ kva vā \|\| 87 \|\|*

Ratnāvalī said:

87\. O Śaśilekhā, Anaṅgalekhā and Citralekhā, how are you all incapacitated to fulfil my desire? Where are your famous arts and skills?

## \|\| 2.67.88 \|\|

*matpriyaprāptaye samyagupāyo'sti mayekṣitaḥ \|*  
*ratneśvarānugrahato'nutiṣṭhata hi taṃ hitāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. With the favour of Ratneśvara, an effective means of getting at my lover has been perceived by me. You wish me well. So carry it out.

## \|\| 2.67.89 \|\|

*śaśilekhebhilaṣitaprāptyai lekhāṃstvamālikha \|*  
*saṃlikhānaṃgalekhe tvaṃ yūnaḥ sarvāvanīcarān \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. O Śaśilekhā, you draw all the Devas for the purpose of getting at the desired one. O Anaṅgalekhā, you draw all the young men moving about all over the earth.

## \|\| 2.67.90 \|\|

*citrage citralekhe tvaṃ pātālatalaśāyinaḥ \|*  
*kiṃcidāvirbhavaccāru tāruṇyālaṃkṛtīṃllikha \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. O Citralekhā, you draw pictures of all those who are in the nether worlds embellished with the freshness of youth.

## \|\| 2.67.91 \|\|

*athākaṇyeti tāḥ sakhyastaccāturyaṃ pravarṇya ca \|*  
*lilikhuḥ kramaśaḥ sakhyo yūno yauvana śevadhīn \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. On hearing this, those companions praised her cleverness and drew the pictures of the young men richly endowed with prime of youth.

## \|\| 2.67.92 \|\|

*niryatkaumāralakṣmīkānpuṃvattva śrīsamāvṛtān \|*  
*prātaḥsaṃdhyeva gaṃdharvī nṛpādyāṃstānavaikṣata \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The Gandharva girl who was (fresh and beautiful) like dawn, looked at those kings and others possessing glorious forms above the state of boyhood and fully endowed with the vigour of manhood.

## \|\| 2.67.93 \|\|

*sarvānsuranikāyānsā vyalokata śubhekṣaṇā \|*  
*na cāṃcalyaṃ jahāvakṣṇosteṣu svarlokavāsiṣu \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. That girl of splendid eyes looked at all the Suras, but did not give up the unsteadiness of her eyes in regard to those heaven-dwellers.

## \|\| 2.67.94 \|\|

*tato madhyamalokasthānmunirājakumārakān \|*  
*vilokyāpi na sā prītiṃ kvāpyāpa premanirbharā \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Next even after seeing the sages and princes residing in the middle world (i.e. Earth) the love-lorn girl did not get any pleasure anywhere.

## \|\| 2.67.95 \|\|

*atha ratnāvalī bālā karṇābhyarṇavilocanā \|*  
*dṛśau vyāpārayāmāsa balisadmayuvasvapi \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Thereafter, Ratnāvalī, a girl with excellent eyes extending up to the ears, saw the pictures of the young men of the nether worlds.

## \|\| 2.67.96 \|\|

*ditijāndanujānvīkṣya sā gaṃdharvī kumārakān \|*  
*ratiṃ babaṃdha na kvāpi tāpitā mānmathaiḥ śaraiḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. That Gandharva girl saw the young men of Daityas and Danujas but did not feel any attraction for them. She became all the more distressed by the arrows of Manmatha.

## \|\| 2.67.97 \|\|

*sudhākara karaspṛṣṭāpyatidūnāṃgayaṣṭikā \|*  
*paśyaṃtī nāgayūnaḥ sā kiṃciducchvasitā'bhavat \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Her tender limbs became excessively distressed even when the nectarine rays of the moon touched her. Seeing the serpent youths she heaved a slight sigh.

## \|\| 2.67.98 \|\|

*bhoginastānvilokyāpi citraṃcitragatānatha \|*  
*manātsaṃbhuktabhogeva kṣaṇamāsītkumārikā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Even when she saw those Bhogins (Serpents, enjoyers of pleasure) painted in the picture, it is surprising that the princess became for a moment as though she had enjoyed the pleasures.

## \|\| 2.67.99 \|\|

*yūnaḥ pratyekamadrākṣīdaśeṣāñcheṣa vaṃśajān \|*  
*takṣakānvayagāṃstadvadatha vāsukigotrajān \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. She saw severally all the youths born of Śeṣa family, Takṣaka family as well as Vāsuki family.

## \|\| 2.67.100 \|\|

*pulīkānaṃta karkoṭa bhadrasaṃtānagānapi \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā nāgakumārāṃstāñchaṃkhacūḍamathaikṣata \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. After seeing the scions of the families of Pulīka, Ananta, Karkoṭa and Bhadra and other Nāga youths she saw Śaṅkhacūḍa.

## \|\| 2.67.101 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍekṣaṇādeva parāṃ lajjāṃ babhāra sā \|*  
*udbhinnapulakāpyāsīdaṃgapratyaṃga saṃdhiṣu \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Merely at the sight of Śaṅkhacūḍa she became excessively bashful. She experienced horripilation in every limb and joint.

## \|\| 2.67.102 \|\|

*tattrapābharato'jñāyi tatkaumāraharo varaḥ \|*  
*tayā vaidagdhyavarayā kṣaṇataścitralekhayā \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. From that excess of bashfulness her lover who deprived her of her virginity was inferred by Citralekhā, the most skilful of all.

## \|\| 2.67.103 \|\|

*atha citrapaṭī citralekhā citrapaṭāṃcalam \|*  
*parikṣipyāvṛṇottūrṇaṃ parihāsaikapeśalā \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Thereupon Citralekhā, clever in practical jokes, quickly threw the hem of a variegated cloth over the painting canvas and covered it.

## \|\| 2.67.104 \|\|

*ratnāvalī citralekhāṃ hriyā maunāvalaṃbinī \|*  
*dṛśā kuṭilayādrākṣītprasphuraddaśanāṃbarā \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Keeping quiet due to bashfulness, Ratnāvalī looked at Citralekhā with a crooked glance, while her lips throbbed.

## \|\| 2.67.105 \|\|

*kaṭākṣitānaṃgalekhā tayātha śaśilekhayā \|*  
*citralekhāparikṣipta paṭāṃcalamapākarot \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Anaṅgalekhā was glanced at suggestively by Śaśilekhā. She removed the hem of the variegated cloth thrown over by Citralekhā.

## \|\| 2.67.106 \|\|

*vasubhūtisutā sātha kanyā ratnāvalī śubhā \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍānvavāye taṃ ratnacūḍamavaikṣata \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The daughter of Vasubhūti, the splendid girl Ratnāvalī, saw Ratnacūḍa in the midst of the members of his (Ratnacūḍa’s) family.

## \|\| 2.67.107 \|\|

*tadīkṣaṇakṣaṇāddṛṣṭirānaṃdāśrubhirāvṛtā \|*  
*kapolabhittirabhavatsvedodakaṇikāṃcitā \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. At the very moment when he was seen, her eyes were filled with tears of joy. Her cheeks were covered with drops of perspiration.

## \|\| 2.67.108 \|\|

*cakaṃpe gātralatikā dhṛtaromāṃcakaṃcukā \|*  
*citranyasteva tastaṃbha kṣaṇaṃ mukulitānanā \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Her creeper-like tender body trembled with hairs standing on ends all over. With eyes closed giving them the appearance of buds, she stood (motionless) as though painted in a picture.

## \|\| 2.67.109 \|\|

*tataḥ sā citralekhā tāmetyāśvāsayadāturām \|*  
*mautsukyaṃ vraja gaṃdharvi siddhastedya manorathaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Thereupon Citralekhā came near the distressed girl and comforted her: “Do not be worried, O Gandharva girl. Now your desire has been fulfilled.

## \|\| 2.67.110 \|\|

*etasyāvagataṃ sarvaṃ deśanāmānvayādikam \|*  
*mā viṣīdālisulabhastveṣa ratneśvarārpitaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. O friend, do not grieve over (anything). Everything concerning this (lover) has become known, such as nature, land, name, lineage etc. Moreover he is easy of access, since he has been given to you by Ratneśvara.

## \|\| 2.67.111 \|\|

*aho sadṛgvarāvāptyā ratneśenāsi toṣitā \|*  
*uttiṣṭha yāmaḥ sadanaṃ ratneśaḥ sarvadohinaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Indeed, you have been made satisfied by Ratneśa through the acquisition of a befitting bridegroom. Get up. We shall go home. Ratneśa is the bestower of everything on us.”

## \|\| 2.67.112 \|\|

*atha devavaśādyāṃtyastā dṛṣṭā gaganādhvagāḥ \|*  
*subāhunā dānavena pātālatalavāsinā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. As they were travelling by the aerial path they were seen by chance by Subāhu, a Dānava, residing in the nether worlds.

## \|\| 2.67.113 \|\|

*gṛhītvā tāścatasropi niragāddānavo gṛham \|*  
*harirvikaṭadaṃṣṭrāsyaḥ prāṃtare hariṇīriva \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Carrying off all those four like a lion with awful fangs and jaw seizing hinds in a desolate forest, he set out towards his abode.

## \|\| 2.67.114 \|\|

*tāstaṃ vilokya gaṃdharvyo daṃṣṭrāvikaṭitānanam \|*  
*rudhirāruṇanetraṃ ca jātā vepathubhūmayaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. On seeing the Dānava with a countenance rendered hideous through his curved fangs and the eyes blood-red, those Gandharva girls began to tremble (through great fear).

## \|\| 2.67.115 \|\|

*hā mātarhā pitastrāhi hā vidhe mā vidhehi tat \|*  
*yadetatkartumārabdhamanāthāsvatiniṣṭhuram \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. “O mother, O father, save us. Alas! Fate, do not let this happen that is about to happen in a cruel way to helpless girls.

## \|\| 2.67.116 \|\|

*hā daiva maṃdabhāgyābhiḥ kimasmābhiranuṣṭhitam \|*  
*sukṛtetaravārtāpi no citte vyāhṛtā kvacit \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Alas! O Fate, what is it that we, the unfortunate ones, have done? Is even a sinful word ever uttered even mentally?

## \|\| 2.67.117 \|\|

*śiśukrīḍanakaṃ hitvā hitvā ratneśvarārcanam \|*  
*pitroḥ svādhīna sacceṣṭā iṣṭaṃ vidmo na kiṃcana \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Excepting children’s toys, excepting the adoration of Ratneśvara and excepting the good acts by way of being the dependents of our parents, we do not know of anything self-willed.

## \|\| 2.67.118 \|\|

*adhobhuvanagā dīnā hīnānāthena kotra naḥ \|*  
*trāti trāṇārthinīrbālāḥ śaṃbho ratneśa sarvaga \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. We are going towards the nether worlds. We are wretched. We do not have anyone to help and lead. We are feeble girls seeking succour, O omnipresent Ratneśa, O Śaṃbhu, who are there to protect us?”

## \|\| 2.67.119 \|\|

*itthaṃ gaṃdharvatanayā vilapaṃtīḥ kṛpāturam \|*  
*śuśrāva nāgarājosau ratnacūḍo mahāmanāḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. As the Gandharva girls were lamenting thus like afflicted ones seeking compassion the magnanimous Ratnacūḍa, the king of Serpents, heard them.

## \|\| 2.67.120 \|\|

*kosau matsvāmino nāma ratneśasya maheśituḥ \|*  
*liṃgarājasya gṛhṇāti karmabaṃdhanabhedinaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. “Who is this uttering the name of my Lord Ratneśa, the great Lord of Liṅgas, the Lord who severs the bondage of Karma?”

## \|\| 2.67.121 \|\|

*punarapyārtarāvaṃ sa śrutvā bālāmukheritam \|*  
*ratneśa rakṣarakṣeti gṛhītāstro viniryayau \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Again he heard the cry of distress issuing from the mouths of those girls: “O Ratneśa, save, save us.” On hearing it, he seized his weapons and set out.

## \|\| 2.67.122 \|\|

*taṃ vasārasapānena mahāmāṃsaniṣevaṇāt \|*  
*atyaṃtonmatta duśceṣṭaṃ ratnacūḍo niraikṣata \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Ratnacūḍa saw that demon of evil activities who was excessively frantic and furious by imbibing liquid suet and human flesh.

## \|\| 2.67.123-126 \|\|

*adhyākṣipacca re duṣṭa śiṣṭakanyāpahāraka \|*  
*maddṛṣṭigocaraṃ yātaḥ kva yāsyasyadya re'dhama \|\| 123 \|\|*

*mama bāṇahataprāṇaḥ prayāṇaṃ kuru durmate \|*  
*ārtatrāṇodyatamate vaivasvatapuraṃ prati \|\| 124 \|\|*

*ratneśvarasya yairnāma pralayāpadyapi sphuṭam \|*  
*gṛhītaṃ na bhavādṛgbhyasteṣu bhītirbhayātmasu \|\| 125 \|\|*

*ratneśvaramahānāma kṛtatrāṇāstu ye narāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ janmajarāvyādhi kalikālabhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

123-126. He rebuked him thus: “O wretched one, O abductor of cultured girls, having come within my view, where will you go, you base one?

O evil-minded one, your life-breath will be knocked off by my arrows as my mind is determined to save the distress ones. So proceed ahead in your journey towards the city of Yama.

At the time of danger or even of utter annihilation, if people utter the name of Ratneśvara with terrified minds, they need not entertain fear from people like you.

If men are given succour by the great name of Ratneśvara, they need not be afraid of rebirths, old age, sickness, Kali age and the god of Death.”

## \|\| 2.67.127 \|\|

*ityuktvā tā bhayatrastāstanmukhaprahitekṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*vyāghraghrātā iva mṛgīrmābhaiṣiṣṭetyuvāca saḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*
