127\. After saying thus (to the demon), he assured and said, “Do not be afraid”, to those terror-stricken (girls) with their eyes turned towards his face like hinds sniffed at by a tiger.

## \|\| 2.67.128 \|\|

*ityāśvāsyātha gaṃdharvīḥ sa vai bhujagarājajaḥ \|*  
*ākarṇapūrṇamākṛṣya kodaṃḍaṃ prāhiṇoccharam \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. After consoling the Gandharva girls thus, that son of the Serpent king drew the bowstring fully up to his ear and discharged the arrow.

## \|\| 2.67.129 \|\|

*sopi kruddho danujarāṭpadāspṛṣṭabhujaṃgavat \|*  
*āviddhya kāladaṃḍābhaṃ parighaṃ vyasṛjanmahat \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. That king of demons who became infuriated like a serpent kicked by foot, whirled with great force a huge iron bar that resembled the staff of the god of Death and hurled it.

## \|\| 2.67.130 \|\|

*hṛdi ratneśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ yasya samyagvijṛṃbhate \|*  
*alātadaṃḍavattasminkāladaṃḍopi jāyate \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. If Ratneśvara Liṅga manifests prominently within the heart, even the thick staff of Kāla is but a small firebrand in his case.

## \|\| 2.67.131 \|\|

*aṃtareva sa ciccheda parighaṃ svamaheṣubhiḥ \|*  
*durvṛtasya yathehāyurvicchidyetāṃtaraiva hi \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. With his great arrows, he (Ratnacūḍa) split the iron bar into two while it was in the middle (in the air) like the life of one of wicked activity gets cut short in the prime.

## \|\| 2.67.132-134 \|\|

*tatosya bāṇaṃ cikṣepa kālānalasamaprabham \|*  
*sa bāṇastasya hṛdayaṃ praviśya pragaveṣya ca \|\| 132 \|\|*

*prāṇānasya viniryātya svayaṃ tūṇamagātpunaḥ \|*  
*hṛdisthaṃ tasya daurātmyaṃ sarvaṃ vijñāya tattvataḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

*digaṃganāpuraḥ khyātumiva nāgāśugo gataḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

132-134. Thereafter, he discharged an arrow having the lustre of Kālānala (Death-fire) against the demon. That arrow entered his heart, searched scrupulously within (and understood the wickedness within his heart), dislodged the life breath within and returned to the quiver by itself. Probably the arrow of the serpent prince had gone to proclaim these things to the Maidens of the Quarters.

## \|\| 2.67.135 \|\|

*anyāyopārjitairdravyairyaḥ sukhaṃ bhoktumicchati \|*  
*tāni dravyāṇi yāṃtyeva sa prāṇāni kutaḥ sukhama \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. (The arrow might have said:) “If anyone wishes to enjoy happiness through articles acquired by illegitimate means, those articles along with his vital breaths do vanish. Where is his happiness then?”

## \|\| 2.67.136-138 \|\|

*iti taṃ dānavaṃ hatvā nāgarājo mahābalī \|*  
*pratyuvācātha tāḥ kanyāḥ kā yūyaṃ kasya cātmajāḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

*durātmanā kutonena saṃgatā danujanmanā \|*  
*kva vā ratneśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ bhavatībhirvilokitam \|\| 137 \|\|*

*yasya nāmākṣaroccārādvyapeta paramāpadaḥ \|*  
*yṛyamāśu tadākhyāta yena jānāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

136-138. After killing the Dānava in this manner, the mighty king of Serpents spoke to the girls: “Who are you? Whose daughters? How did you come into contact with this wicked demon? Where was Ratneśvara Liṅga seen by you all? By uttering the syllables constituting his name you could have got rid of the great dangers. You all tell it quickly so that I can get at the facts.”

## \|\| 2.67.139 \|\|

*iti śrutvā girastasya nitarāṃ premanirbharāḥ \|*  
*parasparaṃ mukhaṃ vīkṣya kosau syāddṛṣṭapūrvavat \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. On hearing these excessively loving and endearing words, the girls (whispered to each other) looking at each other’s face: “Who is this resembling someone seen before?

## \|\| 2.67.140 \|\|

*akāraṇa sakhā kosau prāṃtare samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*nijaprāṇānpaṇīkṛtya yena trātā sma bālikāḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Who is this friendly person without an ulterior motive? He has somehow made his presence in the desolate wilderness staking his life. He has saved us, the girls.

## \|\| 2.67.141 \|\|

*asya saṃdarśanādeva svabhāva capalānyapi \|*  
*maṃtharāṇīṃdriyāṇistu paripīya sudhāmiva \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. The senses are fickle naturally, but on seeing him they have become relieved (i.e. calmed down) as if nectar has been imbibed (by them).

## \|\| 2.67.142 \|\|

*yātumanyatra no netre protsahete yathā tathā \|*  
*anyadvastvaṃtaraṃ prekṣya ramaṇīyataraṃtvapi \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. Even after seeing another more beautiful object, our eyes are not inclined to proceed elsewhere.

## \|\| 2.67.143 \|\|

*vacaḥpīyūṣamādhurya nitarāṃ prāpya naḥ śrutī \|*  
*śabdāṃtaragrahāpekṣāṃ na kurvāte svajanmanaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. After tasting the sweetness of the nectarine words, our ears do not evince any expectation of grasping other words from the source.

## \|\| 2.67.144 \|\|

*āpnutaḥ paṃgutāmetau pādau naścaṃcalāvapi \|*  
*amuṃ yuvānamālokya coraṃ naḥ sanmanomaṇeḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. These feet though they are usually active in moving about, have become lame even though they have perceived this youth who is the thief of the excellent jewel of our minds.”

## \|\| 2.67.145 \|\|

*iti bruvaṃtyastā bālāḥ parasparamanulbaṇam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvāpi citramadhyasthaṃ vividustanna bālikāḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Thus those girls spoke to each other in undertone. Though those girls had already seen him in the picture standing amidst (others), they did not recognize him.

## \|\| 2.67.146 \|\|

*atīva bhīṣaṇākāra danujasyātisādhvasāt \|*  
*aṃdhībhūtekṣaṇāstaṃ nājñāsiṣurhariṇīkṣaṇāḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. Those fawn-eyed ones perhaps did not see him clearly because their eyes had been rendered blind due to the excessive agitation caused by the confrontation with the demon of extremely terrible form and features.

## \|\| 2.67.147-149 \|\|

*ūcuśca taṃ yuvānaṃ tā nijajīvitarakṣiṇam \|*  
*yadaṃga bhavatā pṛṣṭaṃ snehanirbharacetasā \|\| 147 \|\|*

*tadācakṣāmahe sarvamavadhehi kṣaṇaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*iyaṃ gaṃdharvarājasya vasubhūtestanūdbhavā \|\| 148 \|\|*

*kanyā ratnāvalī nāma guṇaratnamahākhaniḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ vayasyā etasyāśchāyevānugatāḥ sadā \|\| 149 \|\|*

147-149. They spoke to that youth who had saved their lives: “Indeed, Sir, what has been asked by your esteemed self with an endearing mind, we shall explain completely. Please be attentive for a moment. This is the daughter of Vasubhūti, the king of Gandharvas, Ratnāvalī by name. This girl is a veritable mine of the gems of good qualities. We are her friends, following her always like a shadow.

## \|\| 2.67.150 \|\|

*ārabhya bālyamapyeṣā liṃgaṃ ratneśvarābhidham \|*  
*yāṃti pitrāpyanujñātā kāśyāmarcayituṃ sadā \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. Ever since her childhood, she has been going to Kāśī always for worshipping the Liṅga named Ratneśvara. She has been permitted by her father too.

## \|\| 2.67.151-152 \|\|

*varopi dattastenāsyai prasannenātha śaṃbhunā \|*  
*hariṣyatīti yaḥ svapne kaumāraṃ te kumārike \|\| 151 \|\|*

*tava nāmasamānākhyaḥ sa te bhartā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yuvānaṃ svapnabhoktāraṃ prāpyāpyeṣā suduḥkhitā \|\| 152 \|\|*

151-152. A boon has been granted to her by the delighted Lord Śaṃbhu: ‘(Someone) having his name similar to yours, O virgin, will violate your virginity in dream. He will be your husband.’ This girl is excessively sad after enjoying the youth with whom she had dalliance during the dream.

## \|\| 2.67.153 \|\|

*punastadvirahotthena vahninātīva tāpitā \|*  
*kalākauśalyato'smābhiḥ sopi citre pradarśitaḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. She is further distressed much with the fire of separation from him. Through our skill in arts that youth has been shown to her in a picture.

## \|\| 2.67.154 \|\|

*yasya na grāma nāmāpi nānvayopyavabudhyate \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā citralikhitamapyeṣā jīvitā punaḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. She has been revived by seeing him painted in a picture, albeit the name of his residence or family was not known.

## \|\| 2.67.155-159 \|\|

*tato ratneśvaraṃ natvā svagṛhāyotsukābhavat \|*  
*yāṃtīstato'nayā sārdhaṃ prāṃtare gaganā dhvani \|\| 155 \|\|*

*atarkitā yamaścāsmāndhṛtvā pātālamāviśat \|*  
*anaṃtaraṃ bhavāneva taṃ vetti danujādhamam \|\| 156 \|\|*

*aṃga ityeva vṛttāṃto nijo'smābhirudīritaḥ \|*  
*prasādaṃ kuru cāsmākaṃ puraḥ kosi kṛpānidhe \|\| 157 \|\|*

*yadā prabhṛti cāsmābhiḥ sa dṛṣṭo duṣṭadānavaḥ \|*  
*tadāprabhṛti no netre vidyuteva hataprabhe \|\| 158 \|\|*

*kāṃdiśīkā bhayatrātarna vidmaḥ kiṃcideva hi \|*  
*kva vayaṃ kā vayaṃ kastvaṃ kiṃ jātaṃ kiṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 159 \|\|*

155-159. Thereafter, we bowed down to Ratneśvara. She was eager to return to her abode. We were also going along with her when in an isolated place in the aerial path, a certain base demon came there all of a sudden. Seizing us he entered the nether worlds. Subsequently your esteemed self, yourself have known the base fellow. Indeed, Sir, our personal information has been narrated to you. O storehouse of mercy, be gracious enough to reveal to us who you are. Ever since that evil demon was seen by us our eyes have become blinded as though lightning has struck them down. We are ones who flee due to fear, O saviour from fear; we do not know anything. Where are we? Who are we? Who are you? What has happened? What is about to happen?”

## \|\| 2.67.160 \|\|

*niśamyeti sa puṇyātmā nāgarājakumārakaḥ \|*  
*āśvāsya tā bhayatrastāḥ provācedaṃ ca puṇyadhīḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. On hearing this, the prince of serpents, a meritorious soul with decent intellect, consoled those terror-stricken girls speaking thus:

## \|\| 2.67.161 \|\|

*mayā saha samāyāta ratneśaṃ darthayāmi vaḥ \|*  
*ityāhūya sa tā ninye krīḍāvāpīṃ sukhodakām \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. “Come with me. I shall show Ratneśvara to you.” Inviting them thus, he led them to the tank of sports with pleasing excellent water.

## \|\| 2.67.162 \|\|

*vitritramaṇisopānāṃ haṃsakokakṛtāravām \|*  
*kavīnāṃ vāsitavyājātsvāgataṃ kurvatīmiva \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. The steps leading to the water were made of gems of different colours. Swans and ruddy geese were chirping loudly. It appeared as though the tank itself was welcoming them under the pretext of the shrill cries of the aquatic birds.

## \|\| 2.67.163 \|\|

*tatra tenābhyanujñātāḥ krīḍāvāpyāṃ nimajjya tāḥ \|*  
*sacailapuṣpābharaṇāḥ pronmamajjustataḥ punaḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. There in accordance with his instructions, they got into the sport tank along with their clothes, flowers and ornaments and then emerged therefrom.

## \|\| 2.67.164-165 \|\|

*bahirnirgatya gaṃdharvyaḥ paśyaṃtyaḥ sthagitā iva \|*  
*ratneśālayamālokya kālarājasamīpataḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

*parasparaṃ tataḥ procurgaṃdharvyo vismitā iva \|*  
*svapnoyaṃ kiṃ nu vā satyaṃ khelo ratneśvarasya vā \|\| 165 \|\|*

164-165. After coming out, the Gandharva girls found themselves made invisible as it were. On seeing the temple of Ratneśa near Kālarāja, they spoke to one another in great surprises: “Is this a dream or reality? Or is this a playful trick of Ratneśvara?

## \|\| 2.67.166 \|\|

*vayameva hi vā bhrāṃtā gaṃdharvyo na vayaṃ kimu \|*  
*kimetannaiva jānīma aiṃdrajālika khelavat \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. Are we ourselves under some illusion? Are we not Gandharva girls at all? What is this, we do not know. This is something like the play of a juggler.

## \|\| 2.67.167 \|\|

*eṣottaravahā gaṃgā sphuṭameva bhavediha \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍasya vāpyeṣā śaṃkhacūḍālayastvasau \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. This is Gaṅgā flowing northwards, it is quite clear. This is the tank of Śaṅkhacùḍa. This is the temple of Śaṅkhacūḍa.

## \|\| 2.67.168 \|\|

*etatpaṃcanadaṃ tīrthameṣa vāgīśvarālayaḥ \|*  
*yasya saṃdarśanādeva vāgvibhūtirvijṛṃbhate \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. This is the Paṅcanada Tīrtha. This is the temple of Vāgīśvara, a visit to which results in the enhancement of eloquent speech.

## \|\| 2.67.169 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍeśvaraścaiṣa śaṃkhacūḍapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*yasya saṃdarśanātpuṃsāṃ na bhayaṃ kālasarpajam \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. This is Śaṅkhacūḍeśvara installed by Śaṅkhacūḍa. The visit to this Lord removes the fear arising from Kālasarpa (Black Serpent, i.e. god of Death).

## \|\| 2.67.170 \|\|

*eṣā maṃdākinī nāma dīrghikā puṇyatoyabhūḥ \|*  
*yasyāṃ kṛtodakā martyā martyaloke viśaṃti na \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. This is the pool named Mandākinī, the receptacle of meritorious holy waters. Men performing all the water rites herein, do not re-enter the mortal world.

## \|\| 2.67.171 \|\|

*asāvāśāpurī devī yā stutā tripurāriṇā \|*  
*tripuraṃ jetukāmena maṃdākinyāstaṭe śubhe \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. This is Goddess Āśāpurī on the splendid banks of Mandākinī. She was eulogized by Tripurāri (Śiva) when he was desirous of conquering Tripura.

## \|\| 2.67.172 \|\|

*yādyāpi pūjitā martyairāśāṃ pūrayaterthinām \|*  
*maṃdākinyāḥ pratīcyāṃ tu eṣa siddhyaṣṭakeśvaraḥ \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. Even today when she is adored by men, she fulfills the hopes and ambitions of the suppliants.

This deity Siddhyaṣṭakeśvara is to the west of Mandākinī.

## \|\| 2.67.173 \|\|

*bhavedyasya saparyāto gṛhe siddhyaṣṭakaṃ sphuṭam \|*  
*kuṃḍasiddhyaṣṭakākhyaṃ ca tatraiva virajodakam \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. By his adoration one will clearly get the eight Siddhis in one’s house. There itself is the holy pit named Siddhyaṣṭaka with waters free from Rajas (dust particles, Rajas quality).

## \|\| 2.67.174 \|\|

*yatra snātvā kṛtaśrāddho virajasko divaṃ vrajet \|*  
*mūrtyastāḥ siddhayaścāṣṭau yāḥ kāśyāṃ sarvasiddhidāḥ \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. One who takes his holy bath here and performs Śrāddha, shall go to heaven free from Rajas quality. Those eight Siddhis are corporeal spiritual powers granting all the Siddhis in Kaśi \[Kāśī?\].

## \|\| 2.67.175 \|\|

*sarvasiddhipradaścāsau mahārājavināyakaḥ \|*  
*vināyakāḥ praṇaśyaṃti yasmai praṇamatāṃ nṛṇām \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. This deity Mahārāja Vināyaka is the bestower of all Siddhis. If men bow down to him their obstacles perish.

## \|\| 2.67.176 \|\|

*asau siddheśvarasyoccaiḥ prāsādaḥ kāṃcanojjvalaḥ \|*  
*ratnadhvajapatākāśca siddhiḥ syādyadvilokanāt \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. This is the lofty palace of Siddheśvara shining with gold and having gem-set flagstaff and banners. By visiting this deity one shall attain Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.67.177 \|\|

*kṣetrasya madhyame \|\| bhāge madhyameśvara eṣa vai \|*  
*madhyādholokayormadhye na vasedyasya vīkṣaṇāt \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. In the middle portion of the holy spot is the deity Madhyameśvara. By visiting this deity one can terminate one’s stay in the middle and nether worlds.

## \|\| 2.67.178 \|\|

*madhyameśaṃ samabhyarcya naro madhyamaviṣṭape \|*  
*āsamudrakṣitīṃdraḥ syāttato mokṣaṃ ca viṃdati \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. By adoring Madhyameśa ardently men shall become lords of the Earth extending to the oceans. Thereafter, one attains salvation.

## \|\| 2.67.179 \|\|

*airāvateśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tatprācyāmiṣṭasiddhikṛt \|*  
*dṛśyate yatpatākāyāṃ ramya airāvato gajaḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. Airāvateśvara Liṅga is towards the east thereof. It causes the achievement of the desired objects. In the banner thereof is seen the elephant Airāvata.

## \|\| 2.67.180 \|\|

*vṛddhakāleśvarasyaiṣa prāsādo ratnanirmitaḥ \|\| \|*  
*pratidarśaṃ vasedyatra rātrau caṃdraḥ satārakaḥ \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. This is the place of Vṛddhakāleśvara built with jewels. On the night of every new-moon day, the Moon stays there along with the stars.

## \|\| 2.67.181 \|\|

*yasya saṃdarśanānnṛṇāṃ na kālaḥ prabhavedbhave \|*  
*na kaliḥ prabhavetsatyaṃ na ca kalmaṣarāśayaḥ \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. If the deity is visited by men, Kāla will not be powerful in the worldly existence. Kali will not be powerful. Truly, heaps of sins will not be powerful.”

## \|\| 2.67.182 \|\|

*iti yāvatkathāṃ cakruḥ saṃbhrāṃtā iva bālikāḥ \|*  
*tāvadvasuvibhūtiḥ sa gaṃdharvastvarayā yayau \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. Even as the excited girls were discussing Vasuvibhūti, the Ganḍdharva, came there hurriedly.

## \|\| 2.67.183-187 \|\|

*nāradācchrutavṛttāṃtaḥ subāhudanujanmanaḥ \|*  
*ratnāvalī sutā prītā sasakhīkā yathāhṛtā \|\| 183 \|\|*

*ratneśvarātsamāyāṃtī śūnye gaganavartmani \|*  
*yathānayacca pātālaṃ yathā yuddhamabhūtpunaḥ \|\| 184 \|\|*

*yathā ratneśa bhaktena ratnacūḍena ghātitaḥ \|*  
*sa subāhurdanujanurmaheṣvāsena ceṣuṇā \|\| 185 \|\|*

*yathā ca pṛṣṭavṛttāṃto vāpīmārgeṇa cānayat \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍasya vāpīṃ tāṃ pātāleṣu pravartinīm \|\| 186 \|\|*

*yathā ca prāpya niryātāḥ kāśīṃ dṛṣṭvāpi bālikāḥ \|*  
*bhṛśaṃ saṃbhrāṃtimāpannāḥ paśyaṃtyopi samutsukāḥ \|\| 187 \|\|*

183-187. He had heard everything beginning with the news regarding the demon Subāhu; how his daughter Ratnāvalī who was pleased (on account of the boon from Ratneśvara) was abducted along with her friends while returning from the shrine of Ratneśvara in an isolated place in the aerial path; how he took them to Pātāla; how a fight ensued; how he was killed by Ratnacūḍa, a devotee of Ratneśa; how that demon Subāhu was killed by that great warrior wielding a big bow with a single arrow; how (Ratnacūḍa) who was asked about the news, brought them through the sport tank to Śaṅkhacūḍa’s tank which extended to Pātāla too; how they saw Kāśī when they emerged therefrom and; how they became extremely excited though they eagerly saw everything.

## \|\| 2.67.188 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā gaṃdharvarājastāṃ punarjātāmivātmajām \|*  
*savayasyāmanāmlānamukhapaṃkajasuśriyam \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. The king of Gandharvas saw his daughter as though she was reborn. The natural beauty of her lotus-like face was a bit faded due to fear lurking yet. She was there along with her friends.

## \|\| 2.67.189 \|\|

*pariṣvajya samāghrāya lalāṭaphalakaṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*aṃkamāropya papraccha sarvaṃ vṛttāṃtamādarāt \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. He embraced her again and again, sniffed at her head and kissed her forehead. He took her on his lap and eagerly asked her about all the events.

## \|\| 2.67.190 \|\|

*atha sā kathayāmāsa danujāpahṛteḥ kathām \|*  
*ratneśvaraṃ varāvāptiṃ svapnāvasthāṃ vihāya ca \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. She told him the details of the story of the abduction omitting the acquisition of the boon from Ratneśvara and the incident of the dream.

## \|\| 2.67.191 \|\|

*ratnāvalīmanovṛttiṃ vijñāyātha mukheṃgitaiḥ \|\| śaśilekhā samācaṣṭa spaṣṭavarṇaiḥ savistaram \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. Understanding perfectly what Ratnāvalī was thinking in her mind through her facial gestures, Śaśilekhā narrated in clear terms everything in detail.

## \|\| 2.67.192 \|\|

*tutoṣa nitarāṃ sotha gaṃdharvādhipatiḥ kṛtī \|*  
*prabhāvaṃ varṇayāmāsa mudā ratneśvarasya ca \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. The king of Gandharvas became pleased and considered himself blessed. He joyously extolled the prowess of Ratneśvara.

## \|\| 2.67.193-198 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ākarṇaya muniśreṣṭha viṃdhyavṛddhi vivardhana \|*  
*pratyahaṃ ratnacūḍopi vāpīmārgeṇa saṃyamī \|\| 193 \|\|*

*nāgalokātsamāgatya snātvā maṃdākinī jale \|*  
*ratneśvaraṃ samabhyarcya ratnāṃjalyaṣṭakena vai \|\| 194 \|\|*

*suvarṇapaṃkajānyaṣṭau samarpayati hṛṣṭavat \|*  
*ekadā svapnasamaye ratneśo liṃgarūpadhṛk \|\| 195 \|\|*

*ratnacūḍamuvācedaṃ nijabhaktaṃ dṛḍhavratam \|*  
*dānavena hṛtāṃ kanyāṃ mocayiṣyati yāṃ bhavān \|\| 196 \|\|*

*taṃ dānavaṃ raṇe jitvā sā te patnī bhaviṣyati \|*  
*iti smaranvaraṃ sotha nāgarājo mahāmanāḥ \|\| 197 \|\|*

*tāṃ kanyāṃ dānavaṃ hatvā vimocya nija vīryataḥ \|*  
*vāpīmārgeṇa pātālādānināya punarmahīm \|\| 198 \|\|*

Skanda said:

193-198. Listen, O excellent sage, O restrainer of the growth of Vindhya. Everyday Ratnacūḍa who had perfect control over his senses, used to come out from Nāgaloka through the path of the tank. After taking his holy bath in the waters of Mandākinī, he worshipped Ratneśvara offering eight handfuls of gems. Then he joyously placed eight golden lotuses (near the deity). Once during sleep, Ratneśa in the form of a Liṅga spoke to Ratnacūḍa, his devotee of steadfast vows: “You will rescue a girl abducted by a demon after defeating him in battle. She will become your wife.” That magnanimous king of serpents remembered this boon. After killing the demon he released the girl by his prowess. Through the path of the tank he brought her to the earth once again.

## \|\| 2.67.199-203 \|\|

*svayaṃ ca sādhayāṃcakre pratyahaṃ niyamaṃ sudhīḥ \|*  
*liṃgaṃ samarcayitvātha kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam \|\| 199 \|\|*

*yāvadbahiḥ samāgacchedramyādratneśamaṃḍapāta \|*  
*tāvadgaṃdharvarājāya tābhiḥ sa vasubhūtaye \|\| 200 \|\|*

*soyaṃ soyaṃ yuvā dhanyastarjanyagreṇa darśitaḥ \|*  
*gaṃdharvarājastaṃ dṛṣṭvā nāgarājakumārakam \|\| 201 \|\|*

*atīvasmeranayanaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*manasyenaṃ ca saṃvarṇya tadrūpaṃ savayonvayam \|\| 202 \|\|*

*dhanyosmyanugṛhītosmi ratneśena varārpaṇāt \|*  
*kanyā dhanyatarā ceyamanurūposti yatpatiḥ \|\| 203 \|\|*

199-203. Thereafter he did as he was wont to do everyday. The wise youth worshipped the Liṅga, circumambulated and came out of the beautiful Maṇḍapa of Ratneśvara. Thereupon he was repeatedly pointed out to Vasubhūti, the king of Gandharvas, with the tip of the index finger by them, “This is that blessed youth.”

On seeing the prince of serpents, the king of Gandharvas became delighted with hairs standing on ends. His eyes beamed with smile in his face. He thought in his mind thus after seeing him, of youthful form and nobility of birth: ‘I am blessed. I have been favoured by Ratneśa by offering me an excellent bridegroom This girl too is blessed, because her husband is quite suitable to her.’

## \|\| 2.67.204-206 \|\|

*saṃpradhāryeti hṛdyenaṃ samākārya ca suṃdaram \|*  
*pṛṣṭvā tannāmagotraṃ ca gaṇayitvā balābalam \|\| 204 \|\|*

*ratneśvarasya puratastasmai kanyāṃ dadau mudā \|*  
*nītvā gaṃdharvalokaṃ ca kṛtakautukamaṃgalam \|\| 205 \|\|*

*madhuparkeṇa saṃpūjya pāṇimagrāhayattataḥ \|*  
*vaivāhikena vidhinā dadau ratnānyanekaśaḥ \|\| 206 \|\|*

204-206. After thinking thus he called the charming youth to him and asked him his name and family. He considered the pros and cons and before Ratneśvara gave his daughter to him joyously he took him to the world of Gandharvas and performed all the auspicious rites. He honoured him with Madhuparka and made him hold her hand (in marriage ceremony). As required by the due marital rite, he gave him many jewels.

## \|\| 2.67.207 \|\|

*śaśilekhānaṃgalekhā citralekhāpi kuṃbhaja \|*  
*vijñāpya svajanetāraṃ varayāmāsa taṃ patim \|\| 207 \|\|*

207\. Śaśilekhā, Anaṅgalekhā and Citralekhā too informed their respective parents and wooed him as their husband.

## \|\| 2.67.208 \|\|

*upayamya catasropi sa gaṃdharvasutāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*ratnacūḍo jagāmātha tābhiḥ svapitṛmaṃdiram \|\| 208 \|\|*

208\. After marrying all the four splendid Gandharva girls Ratnacūḍa went to the palace of his father along with them.

## \|\| 2.67.209-210 \|\|

*yathā catasṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ śrutibhiḥ praṇavaḥ śivam \|*  
*svapitroścaraṇau natvā navoḍhābhiḥ sa nāgarāṭ \|\| 209 \|\|*

*viniveditavṛttāṃto ratneśānugrahasya ca \|*  
*uvāsa tābhiḥ sasukhaṃ pitṛbhyāmabhinaṃditaḥ \|\| 210 \|\|*

209-210. He went to his father like Praṇava proceeding towards Siva along with the four Śrutis. The king of serpents prostrated at the feet of his parents along with the newly wedded brides. He duly informed him about the grace of Ratneśa. He was congratulated duly by the parents and he spent the days happily along with them.

## \|\| 2.67.211 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ratneśvarasya liṃgasya mama sthāvararūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ sarvadasyāsya prabhāvo girije'tulaḥ \|\| 211 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

211\. O Daughter of the Mountain, Ratneśvara is my immobile Liṅga. It bestows everything on everyone. It’s power is unparalleled.

## \|\| 2.67.212 \|\|

*asmiṃlliṃge parāṃ siddhi prāptāḥ siddhāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*guptamāsīdidaṃ liṃgamadya yāvatsumadhyame \|\| 212 \|\|*

212\. In this Liṅga thousands of Siddhas have attained great spiritual powers. O lady of slender waist, till today this Liṅga remained hidden.

## \|\| 2.67.213 \|\|

*tava pitrā himavatā mama bhaktena sarvathā \|*  
*puṇyārjitairmahāratnai ratneśaḥ prakaṭīkṛtaḥ \|\| 213 \|\|*

213\. Ratneśa has been brought into manifestation through great jewels acquired through merit by Himavān, your father and a devotee of mine in all respects.

## \|\| 2.67.214 \|\|

*asmiṃlliṃge mama prītirnitarāmadrirājaje \|*  
*vārāṇasyāmidaṃ liṃgaṃ pūjanīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 214 \|\|*

214\. O Daughter of the King of Mountains, I love this Liṅga very much. This Liṅga should be assiduously worshipped in Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.67.215 \|\|

*nānā ratnāni labhyaṃte ratneśānugrahādume \|*  
*strīratnaputraratnādi svargamokṣāvapi priye \|\| 215 \|\|*

215\. O Umā, O my beloved, by the blessings of Ratneśa many jewels are acquired, jewel of a son, jewel of a wife etc. and even heavenly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 2.67.216 \|\|

*yo'tra ratneśvaraṃ natvā mṛto deśāṃtareṣvapi \|*  
*na sa svargādihāgacchetkalpakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 216 \|\|*

216\. One who bows down to Ratneśvara but dies elsewhere never returns from heaven even after hundreds of crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 2.67.217 \|\|

*asitāyāṃ caturdaśyāmupoṣya niśi jāgarāt \|*  
*ratneśasannidhau devi mama sānnidhyamāpnuyāt \|\| 217 \|\|*

217\. A devotee should observe fast on the fourteenth day in the dark half and keep awake at night in the vicinity of Ratneśvara. He will attain Sānnidhya i.e. proximity to me.

## \|\| 2.67.218 \|\|

*asya liṃgasya pūrveṇa tvayā janmāṃtare priye \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇīśvaraṃ ligaṃ madbhaktyātra pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 218 \|\|*

218\. O my beloved, in your previous birth, due to your devotion to me, Dākṣāyaṇīśvara Liṅga was installed by you to the east of this Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.67.219 \|\|

*tasya saṃdarśanādeva na naro yāti durgatim \|*  
*aṃbikā nāma gaurī tvaṃ tatrāhaṃ cāṃbikeśvaraḥ \|\| 219 \|\|*

219\. A man can avoid going to wretched state by visiting it. There your name is Aṃbikā and I am Aṃbikeśvara.

## \|\| 2.67.220 \|\|

*mūrtaḥ ṣaḍānanastatra tava putraḥ sumadhyame \|*  
*etattrayaṃ naro dṛṣṭvā na garbhaṃ praviśedume \|\| 220 \|\|*

220\. O lady of excellent waist, your son Ṣaḍānana is also in the form of an image there. O Umā, by visiting these three a man can avoid re-entry into a womb (i.e. is liberated).

## \|\| 2.67.221 \|\|

*ratneśvarasya māhātmyaṃ mayā te samudīritam \|*  
*gopanīyaṃ prayatnena kalikalmaṣacetasām \|\| 221 \|\|*

221\. The greatness of Ratneśvara has been described to you by me. It should be carefully kept secret from persons whose minds are defiled by the sins of Kali age.

## \|\| 2.67.222 \|\|

*idaṃ ratneśvarākhyānaṃ yaḥ paṭhiṣyati sarvadā \|*  
*saputrapautrapaśubhirna viyujyeta karhicit \|\| 222 \|\|*

222\. He who reads always this narrative of Ratneśvara is never separated from sons, grandsons and cattle wealth.

## \|\| 2.67.223 \|\|

*śrutvā ratneśvarotpatiṃ setihāsāṃ narottamaḥ \|*  
*anūḍho labhate satyaṃ kanyāratnaṃ kulocitam \|\| 223 \|\|*

223\. On hearing the origin of Ratneśvara along with the legends thereon, an excellent bachelor obtains an excellent jewel of a girl, befitting his family. This is true.

## \|\| 2.67.224 \|\|

*kanyāpīmaṃ samākarṇya tvitihāsaṃ manoramam \|*  
*śraddhayā satpatiṃ prāpya bhaviṣyati pativratā \|\| 224 \|\|*

224\. A girl who listens to this fascinating legend with faith gets a good husband and will be a chaste lady.

## \|\| 2.67.225 \|\|

*itihāsamimaṃ śrutvā nārī vā puruṣopivā \|*  
*na jātviṣṭaviyogāgni tāpena paritapyate \|\| 225 \|\|*

225\. On hearing this Itihāsa (legend) no man or woman will be distressed due to the fire of separation from the beloved ones.

## Chapter 68 - The Origin of Kṛttivāsas

## \|\| 2.68.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*anyacca śṛṇu vipreṃdra vṛttātaṃ tatra saṃbhavam \|*  
*mahāścaryaprajananaṃ mahāpātakahāri ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This Liṅga is to the north-cast of Maidagin. It is one most ancient Liṅga in Kāśī. The temple was destroyed by Aurangazeb and a mosque was built but it is opened to Hindus on Śivarātri day.

Skanda said:

1\. Listen to another event, O eminent Brāhmaṇa, that happened there. It causes great wonder and dispels great sins.

## \|\| 2.68.2 \|\|

*itthaṃ kathāṃ prakurvāṇe ratnaśesya maheśvare \|*  
*kolāhalo mahānāsīttrātatrāteti sarvataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. While Maheśvara was narrating the story of Ratneśa thus, there was heard a great tumultuous cry everywhere, “Save, save.”

## \|\| 2.68.3 \|\|

*mahiṣāsuraputrosau samāyāti gajāsuraḥ \|*  
*pramathanpramathānsarvānnijavīrya madoddhataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. “This son of demon Mahiṣa, the demon Gajāsura is coming here, crushing all the Pramathas. He is haughty and proud due to his prowess.

## \|\| 2.68.4 \|\|

*yatrayatra dharāyāṃ sa caraṇaṃ pramiṇoti hi \|*  
*acalollolayāṃcakre tatratatrāsya bhārataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Wherever he sets his foot, the ground (under his feet) shakes there due to his weight.

## \|\| 2.68.5 \|\|

*ūruvegena taravaḥ pataṃti śikharaiḥ saha \|*  
*yasya dordaṃḍaghātena cūrṇāḥ syuśca śiloccayāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By the force of his thighs trees fall down. On being hit by his baton-like arms, mountains and their peaks get crushed to powder.

## \|\| 2.68.6 \|\|

*yasya maulijasaṃgharṣādgha nāvyoma tyajaṃtyapi \|*  
*nīlimānaṃ na cādyāpi jahyustakleśasaṃgajam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Getting entangled with his hairs, clouds leave off the sky but do not give up the blue colour due to the contact thereof.

## \|\| 2.68.7 \|\|

*yasya niḥśvāsasaṃbhārairuttaraṃgā mahābdhayaḥ \|*  
*nadyopyamaṃdakallolā bhavaṃti timibhiḥ saha \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. By the heavy exhalation of his breath oceans get surged up with high tides, while rivers along with aquatic animals, become full of heavy waves.

## \|\| 2.68.8 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi navayasya samucchrayaḥ \|*  
*tāvāneva hi vistārastanormāyāvinosya hi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The body of this demon, an adept in sorcery, is nine thousand Yojanas in height and as many in girth.

## \|\| 2.68.9 \|\|

*yannetrayoḥ piṃgalimā tathā taralimā punaḥ \|*  
*vidyutā nojjhyate'dyāpi soyamāyāti satvaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The tawny colour and the glaring lustre of his eyes has gone over to lightning-streak, which is not given up even today (by it). And here he dashed hurriedly.

## \|\| 2.68.10 \|\|

*yāṃyāṃ diśaṃ samabhyeti soyaṃ duḥsaha dānavaḥ \|*  
*sāsā samī bhavedasya sādhvasādiva digdhruvam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Whichever quarter this irresistible Dānava approaches, it becomes level and even throughout without ups and downs, as if by the terror of him certainly.

## \|\| 2.68.11 \|\|

*brahmalabdhavaraścāyaṃ tṛṇīkṛtajagattrayaḥ \|*  
*avadhyohaṃ bhavāmīti strīpuṃsaiḥ kāmanirjitaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Having acquired boons from Brahmā, this demon considers the three worlds as insignificant as a blade of grass (thinking within), ‘I cannot be killed by women or men overwhelmed by lust.’

## \|\| 2.68.12 \|\|

*tatastriśūlahetistamāyāṃtaṃ daityapuṃgavam \|*  
*vijñāyāvadhyamanyena śūlenābhijaghāna tam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Trident-wielding Lord knew that the great Daitya rushing towards him could not be killed by anything else and hit him with the trident.

## \|\| 2.68.13 \|\|

*protastena triśūlena sa ca daityo gajāsuraḥ \|*  
*chatrīkṛtamivātmānaṃ manyamāno jagau haram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Pierced through by the trident (and raised aloft) the demon Gajāsura thought that he was made to resemble an umbrella. He said to Hara (Śiva):

## \|\| 2.68.14 \|\|

*gajāsura uvāca \|*  
*triśūlapāṇe deveśa jāne tvāṃ smarahāriṇam \|*  
*tava haste mama vadhaḥ śreyāneva purāṃtaka \|\| 14 \|\|*

Gajāsura said:

14\. O Trident-armed Lord of Devas, I know that you are the slayer of Smara (Lord of love). O destroyer of Puras, my death at your hands is conducive to my welfare indeed.

## \|\| 2.68.15 \|\|

*kiṃcidvijñaptumicchāmi avadhehi mameritam \|*  
*satyaṃ bravīmi nāsatyaṃ mṛtyuṃjaya vicāraya \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I wish to submit something. Please attend to what I say. I tell you the truth, not the untruth. O Mṛtyuñjaya (‘conqueror of death’) consider this.

## \|\| 2.68.16 \|\|

*tvameko jagatāṃ vaṃdyo viśvasyopari saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ tvadupariṣṭācca sthitosmī ti jitaṃ mayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. You are the only Lord worthy of the reverence of all the worlds. You are stationed above the entire universe and I am now stationed above (you). Hence this is my victory!

## \|\| 2.68.17 \|\|

*dhanyosmyanugṛhītosmi tvattriśūlāgrasaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*kālena sarvairmartavyaṃ śreyase mṛtyurīdṛśaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If I am to die at the tip of your trident I am blessed. I have been favoured. Everyone has to die in due course of time. But a death like this is conducive to welfare.

## \|\| 2.68.18 \|\|

*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā devadevaḥ kṛpānidhiḥ \|*  
*provāca prahasañchaṃbhurghaṭodbhava gajāsuram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On hearing these words of his, the Lord of Devas, the storehouse of compassion, Saṃbhu laughingly replied to Gajāsura, O Pot-born One:

## \|\| 2.68.19 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*gajāsura prasannosmi mahāpauruṣaśevadhe \|*  
*svānukūla varaṃ brūhi dadāmi sumate'sura \|\| 19 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

19\. O Gajāsura with great manliness as your asset, I am delighted. Mention a boon befitting you. I shall grant it, O Asura of good intellect.

## \|\| 2.68.20-21 \|\|

*ityākarṇya sa daityeṃdraḥ pratyuvāca maheśvaram \|*  
*gajāsura uvāca \|*  
*yadi prasanno digvāsastadā nityaṃ vasāna me \|\| 20 \|\|*

*imāṃ kṛttiṃ virūpākṣa tvattriśūlāgnipāvitām \|*  
*svapramāṇāṃ sukhasparśāṃ raṇāṃgaṇapaṇīkṛtām \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. On hearing this, that great Daitya replied to Maheśvara:

## \|\| 2.68.22 \|\|

*iṣṭagaṃdhiḥ sadaivāstu sadaivāstvatikomalā \|*  
*sadaiva nirmalā cāstu sadaivāstvatimaṃḍanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

Gajāsura said:

O Lord with the quarters for your robes, if you are pleased, O three-eyed one, always wear this hide of mine. It has been sanctified by the fire from your trident. It fits you in size. It is smooth to touch. It has been won as a stake in the battlefield.

22\. May it always have a pleasing odour. May it always be very tender. May it always be free from impurities. May it always be an excellent decoration.

## \|\| 2.68.23 \|\|

*mahātapo'nalajvālāḥ prāpyāpi suciraṃ vibho \|*  
*na dagdhā kṛttireṣā me puṇyagaṃdhanidhistataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Lord, though it was subjected to the flames of the fire of great penance for a long time (or as it had survived the fire of your third eye), this hide has never been burnt. Hence it is the storehouse of merit and fragrance.

## \|\| 2.68.24 \|\|

*yadi puṇyavatī naiṣā mamakṛttirdigaṃbara \|*  
*tadā tvadaṃgasaṃgosyāḥ kathaṃ jāto raṇāṃgaṇe \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If my hide Rad not been meritorious, O quarter-clad one, how could it have come into contact with you in the battlefield?

## \|\| 2.68.25 \|\|

*anyaṃ ca me varaṃ dehi yadi tuṣṭosi śaṃkara \|*  
*nāmāstu kṛttivāsāste prārabhyādyatanaṃ dinam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Śaṅkara, if you are pleased, grant me another boon. From today onwards, may you have the name ‘Kṛttivāsas.’

## \|\| 2.68.26 \|\|

*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā tathetyuktvā ca śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*punaḥprovāca taṃ daityaṃ bhaktinirmalamānasam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On hearing these words of his, Śaṅkara said, “So be it” and further said to that Daitya whose mind was purified by devotion:

## \|\| 2.68.27-28 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|\| \|*  
*śṛṇu puṇyanidhe daitya varamanyaṃ sudurlabham \|*  
*avimukte mahākṣetre raṇa tyakta kalevara \|\| 27 \|\|*

*idaṃ puṇyaśarīraṃ te kṣetresminmuktisādhane \|*  
*mama liṃgaṃ bhavatvatra sarveṣāṃmuktidāyakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

27-28. O storehouse of merit, O great Daitya, listen to another rare boon. You have cast off your body in a battle in the great holy spot Avimukta. May this holy body of yours become my Liṅga in this holy spot, the means of salvation, the bestower of salvation on all here.

## \|\| 2.68.29 \|\|

*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva liṃgānāṃ śirobhūtamidaṃ varam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. This will be known by the name Kṛttivāseśvara. It will be destructive of great sins. It will be at the top (i.e. greatest) of all Liṅgas. It will be the most excellent.

## \|\| 2.68.30 \|\|

*yāvaṃti saṃti liṃgāni vārāṇasyāṃ mahāṃtyapi \|*  
*uttamaṃ tāvatāmetaduttamāṃgavaduttamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. It will be the most excellent of all the Liṅgas in Vārāṇasī, even of the greatest ones. It will be the most excellent one (among them) like the head.

## \|\| 2.68.31 \|\|

*mānavānāṃ hitāyātra sthāsyehaṃ saparigrahaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭenānena liṃgena pūjitena stutena ca \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyo bhavenmartyaḥ saṃsāraṃ na viśetpunaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. For the sake of the welfare of men, I shall stay here along with the members of my family and followers. When this Liṅga is visited, worshipped and eulogized, the man will become blessed. He will not reenter the world.

## \|\| 2.68.32-38 \|\|

*rudrāḥ pāśupatāḥ siddhā ṛṣayastattvaciṃtakāḥ \|*  
*śāṃtā dāṃtā jitakrodhā nirdvaṃdvā niṣparigrahāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*avimukte sthitā ye tu mama bhaktā mumukṣavaḥ \|*  
*mānāpamānayostulyāḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāṃcanāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kṛttivāseśvare liṃge sthāsyehaṃ tadanugrahe \|*  
*daśakoṭisahasrāṇi tīrthāni prativāsaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

*trikālamāgamiṣyaṃti kṛttivāse na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kalidvāparasaṃbhūtā narāḥ kalmaṣabuddhayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sadācāravinirmuktāḥ satyaśaucaparāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*māyayā daṃbhalobhābhyāṃ mohāhaṃkṛtisaṃyutāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śūdrānnasevino viprā jihvālā atilālasāḥ \|*  
*saṃdhyāsnānajapejyāsu dūrīkṛta manodhiyaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ prāpya sarvapāpavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*sukhena mokṣameṣyaṃti yathā sukṛtinastathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

32-38. I shall stay in the Kṛttivāseśvara liṅga in order to bless all those who stay in Avimukta—Rudras, Pāśupatas, Siddhas, sages, philosophers, quiescent ones, men with control of sense-organs, those who have conquered anger, persons unafflicted by the opposing pairs (such as pleasure and pain), those who do not have possessions, those who are devoted to me, those who are desirous of salvation, those who are equally unaffected by honour and insult, and those who view a lump of clay, a stone and a piece of gold alike.

Undoubtedly three times everyday, ten thousand crores of Tīrthas approach Kṛttivāsa. All these become rid of their sins when they approach Kṛttivāseśvara: Men of Kali and Dvāpara ages with foul and sinful intellect, those who do not follow the practice of the good, those who are averse to truthfulness and cleanliness, those who are carried away by Māyā, hypocrisy, covetousness, delusion and egotism, Brāhmaṇas partaking of the cooked food of Śùdras, gourmets, gourmands, too greedy ones, and those whose minds are far removed from Sandhyā prayers, holy baths, Japas and adorations. They will attain salvation easily like persons of great meritorious deeds.

## \|\| 2.68.39-41 \|\|

*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ sevyaṃ kāśyāṃ tato naraiḥ \|*  
*janmāṃtarasahasreṣu mokṣonyatra sudurlabhaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kṛttivāseśvare liṃge labhyastvekena janmanā \|*  
*pṛrvajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tapodānādibhiḥ śanaiḥ \|*  
*naśyetsadyo vinaśyeta kṛttivāse śvarekṣaṇāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ yercayiṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*praviṣṭāste śarīre me teṣāṃ nāsti punarbhavaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. Hence Kṛttivāseśvara Liṅga in Kāśī should be resorted to by men. Salvation which cannot be easily achieved elsewhere in thousands of births can be obtained in Kṛttivāseśvara Liṅga within a single birth. The sins committed in the previous births shall perish slowly due to penance, Dāna etc. But if Kṛttivāseśvara is visited they perish immediately. Men who worship Kṛttivāseśvara Liṅga have actually entered my body. They are not reborn.

## \|\| 2.68.42 \|\|

*avimukte'tra vastavyaṃ japtavyaṃ śatarudriyam \|*  
*kṛttivāseśvaro devo draṣṭavyaśca punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In Avimukta, people should stay here. They should chant Śatarudriya Mantras and Lord Kṛttivāseśvara should be visited again and again.

## \|\| 2.68.43 \|\|

*saptakoṭimahārudraiḥ sujaptairyatphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhyate kāśyāṃ pūjanātkṛttivāsasaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. By worshipping Kṛttivāsas in Kāśī, one obtains that benefit which is obtained when seven crores of Mahārudra Mantras are chanted flawlessly,

## \|\| 2.68.44 \|\|

*māgha kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāmupoṣya niśi jāgṛyāt \|*  
*kṛttivāseśamabhyarcya yaḥ sa yāyātparāṃ gatim \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On the fourteenth day in the dark half of Māgha a devotee should observe fast, worship Kṛttivāseśa and keep awake at night. He will attain the great goal.

## \|\| 2.68.45 \|\|

*śuklāyāṃ paṃcadaśyāṃ yaścaitryāṃ kartā mahotsavam \|*  
*kṛttivāseśvare liṃge na sa garbhaṃ pravakṣyete \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He who celebrates great festival on the full-moon day in Caitra month around Kṛttivāseśvara Liṅga will not enter any womb.

## \|\| 2.68.46 \|\|

*kathayitveti deveśastatkṛttiṃ parigṛhya ca \|*  
*gajāsurasya mahatīṃ prāvṛṇoddharidaṃbaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After saying this, the Quarter-clad Lord of Devas accepted the great hide of Gajāsura and wore it.

## \|\| 2.68.47 \|\|

*mahāmahotsavo jātastasminnahani kuṃbhaja \|*  
*kṛttivāsatvamāpede yasmindevo digaṃbaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Pot-born One, there was a great celebration of a festival on that day when the Quarter-clad attained Kṛttivāsatva (state of wearing the hide).

## \|\| 2.68.48 \|\|

*yatracchatrīkṛto daityaḥ śūlamāropya bhūtale \|*  
*tacchūlotpāṭanājjātaṃ tatra kuṃḍaṃ mahattaram \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. When the trident was lifted up at the place where the Daitya was impaled on the trident and raised up as an umbrella, a great holy Kuṇḍa (pit) took shape (was formed).

## \|\| 2.68.49 \|\|

*tasminkuṃḍe naraḥ snātvā kṛtvā ca pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtakṛtyo naro bhavet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A devotee should take his holy bath in that Kuṇḍa, offer libations to the ancestors and visit Kṛttivāseśvara. He will be blessed.

## \|\| 2.68.50 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe tu yadvṛttaṃ tadagaste niśāmaya \|*  
*kākā haṃsatvamāpannāstattīrthasya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Skanda said:

50\. Listen, O Agastya, to what happened in that Tīrtha. By the power of that Tīrtha crows got transformed into swans.

## \|\| 2.68.51-53 \|\|

*ekadā kṛttivāse tu caitryāṃ yātrā'bhavatpurā \|*  
*annaṃ rāśīkṛtaṃ tatra hyupahārasamudbhavam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*bahudevalakairvipra taṃ dṛṣṭvā pakṣiṇo milan \|*  
*parasparaṃ tadannārthaṃ yudhyaṃto vyomavartmani \|\| 52 \|\|*

*balipuṣṭairapuṣṭāṃgā raṭataḥ karaṭāḥ kaṭu \|*  
*valibhiścātipuṣṭāṃgairabalāścaṃcubhirhatāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. Formerly there was a religious festival at Kṛttivāsa on the full-moon day in the month of Citrā. The cooked rice offered was obtained and kept in a heap by many priests. O Brāhmaṇa, birds flocked there on seeing it and they began to fight with one another in the sky for the cooked rice. The crows with limbs not developed well began to crow in harsh sounds when hit by the crows of fully developed limbs. The weaker ones were struck down by the stronger ones.

## \|\| 2.68.54 \|\|

*te hanyamānā nyapataṃstasminkuṃḍe nabhoṃgaṇāt \|*  
*āyuḥśeṣeṇa saṃtrātā haṃsībhūtāstu vāyasāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On being struck down, they fell down into that Kuṇḍa from the sky above. Since they were destined to live further, the crows were saved. They were transformed into swans.

## \|\| 2.68.55-56 \|\|

*āścaryavaṃtastatratyā yātrāyāṃ militā janāḥ \|*  
*ūcuraṃgulinirdeśairaho paśyata paśyata \|\| 55 \|\|*

*asmāsu vīkṣamāṇeṣu kākāḥ kuṃḍetra ye patan \|*  
*dhārtarāṣṭrāstu te jātāstīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. People assembled there for the festival became surprised. Pointing out to them with their fingers, they exclaimed, “See, O Lord! Even as we were watching, the crows which fell into the Kuṇḍa here became Dhārtarāṣṭras (swans with black-feet and beaks), due to the power of this Tīrtha.”

## \|\| 2.68.57 \|\|

*haṃsatīrthaṃ tadārabhya kṛttivāsa samīpataḥ \|*  
*nāmnā khyātamabhūlloke tatkuṃḍaṃ kalaśodbhava \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Ever since then, O Pot-born One, that Kuṇḍa near Kṛttivāsa became well-known in the world by the name Haṃsa Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.68.58 \|\|

*atīva malinātmāno mahāmalina karmabhiḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇānnirmalatāṃ yāṃti haṃsatīrthakṛtodakāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Those who become highly defiled in their souls due to excessively dirty, sinful activities become pure instantaneously when they perform all the water rites at Haṃsa Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.68.59 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ sadaiva vastavyaṃ snātavyaṃ haṃsatīrthake \|*  
*draṣṭavyaḥ kṛttivāseśaḥ prāptavyaṃ paramaṃ padam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. One should always live in Kāśī, should bathe in Haṃsa Tīrtha, Kṛttivāsa should be visited and the greatest position (Mokṣa) should be attained.

## \|\| 2.68.60 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ liṃgānyanekāni mune saṃti padepade \|*  
*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ sarvaliṃgaśiraḥ smṛtam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O sage, at every step, there are many Liṅgas in Kāśī. But Kṛttivāseśvara Liṅga is remembered as the head of all the Liṇgas.

## \|\| 2.68.61 \|\|

*kṛttivāsaṃ samārādhya bhaktiyuktena cetasā \|*  
*sarvaliṃgārādhanajaṃ phalaṃ kāśyāmavāpyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. After propitiating Kṛttivāsa with the mind full of devotion, one attains the benefit arising from the worship of all the Liṅgas in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.68.62 \|\|

*japo dānaṃ tapo homastarpaṇaṃ devatārcanam \|*  
*samīpe kṛttivāsasya kṛtaṃ sarvamanaṃtakam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Whatever rite is performed in the vicinity of Kṛttivāsa—Japa, Dana, Tapas and Homa, libations and adoration of the deity, becomes endless in its benefit.

## \|\| 2.68.63 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ tvanādisaṃsiddhametatkalaśasaṃbhava \|*  
*punardevasya sānnidhyādāvirāsīnmaheśituḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. This Tīrtha has been in existence from times immemorial, O Pot-born One. It manifested itself, due to the presence of Lord Maheśa.

## \|\| 2.68.64 \|\|

*etāni siddhaliṃgānicchannāni syuryugeyuge \|*  
*avāpya śaṃbhusānnidhyaṃ punarāvirbhavaṃti hi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. These Siddha Liṅgas become concealed in the different Yugas. Buy by the presence of Śaṃbhu, they manifest themselves again.

## \|\| 2.68.65 \|\|

*haṃsatīrthasya parito liṃgānāmayutaṃ mune \|*  
*pratiṣṭhitaṃ munivarairatrāsti dviśatottaram \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Around Haṃsa Tīrtha, O sage, there are ten thousand and two hundred Liṅgas installed here by excellent sages.

## \|\| 2.68.66 \|\|

*ekaikaṃ siddhidaṃ nṛṇāmavimuktanivāsinām \|*  
*liṃgaṃ kātyāyaneśādi cyavaneśāṃ tameva hi \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Everyone of these Liṅgas, beginning with Kātyāyaneśa and ending with Cyavaneśa, accords spiritual powers to the residents of Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.68.67 \|\|

*lomaśeśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ lomaśena pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*kṛttivāsaḥ pratīcyāṃ tu taddṛṣṭvā kvāṃtakādbhayam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The great Lomaśeśa Liṅga was installed by Lomaśa to the west of Kṛttivāsas. If a devotee visits it, where is the fear of the god of Death?

## \|\| 2.68.68 \|\|

*mālatīśaṃ śubhaṃ liṃgaṃ kṛttivāsottare mahat \|*  
*saparyayitvā talliṃgaṃ rājā gajapatirbhavet \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The great auspicious Mālatīśa Liṅga is to the north of Kṛttivāsa. By adoring that Liṅga a king becomes lord of elephants.

## \|\| 2.68.69 \|\|

*aṃtakeśvara saṃjñaṃ ca liṃgaṃ tadrudradiksthitam \|*  
*atipāpopi niṣpāpo jāyate tadvilokanāt \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The Liṅga called Antakeśvara is stationed to the north thereof. One even with great sins becomes rid of all sins by visiting it.

## \|\| 2.68.70 \|\|

*janakeśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ tatpārśve jñānadaṃ param \|*  
*talliṃga varivasyāto brahmajñānamavāpyate \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The great Janakeśa Liṅga at its side is the great bestower of knowledge. By worshipping that Liṅga knowledge of Brahman is attained.

## \|\| 2.68.71 \|\|

*taduttare mahāmūrtirasitāṃgosti bhairavaḥ \|*  
*tasya darśanataḥ puṃsāṃ na bhavedyamadarśanam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. To the north thereof is Bhairava of dark-coloured limbs and a huge image By visiting it men can ward off the sight of Yama.

## \|\| 2.68.72 \|\|

*śuṣkodarī ca tatrāsti devī vikaṭalocanā \|*  
*kṛttivāsādudīcyāṃ tu kāśīpratyūha bhakṣiṇī \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Goddess Śuṣkodarī with awful eyes is also there to the north of Kṛttivāsa. She devours the obstacles of Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.68.73 \|\|

*agnijihvosti vetālastasyā devyāstu nairṛte \|*  
*dadāti vāṃchitāṃ siddhiṃ sorcito bhaumavāsare \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. To the south-west of the goddess is the Vetāla (Spirit, ghost) named Agnijihva. Adored on Tuesday, he bestows all desired objectives and powers.

## \|\| 2.68.74 \|\|

*vetālakuṃḍaṃ tatrāsti sarvavyādhivighātakṛt \|*  
*tatkuṃḍodakasaṃsparśādvraṇavisphoṭarugvrajet \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. There is the Vetālakuṇḍa there that dispels all ailmerits. Cuts, tumours and other ailments and pain vanish when the waters of the Kuṇḍa come into contact with them.

## \|\| 2.68.75 \|\|

*vetālakuṃḍe susnāto vetālaṃ praṇipatya ca \|*  
*labheta vāṃchitāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ sarvadehibhiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A devotee who scrupulously takes his holy bath in the Vetālakuṇḍa and bows down to Vetāla shall obtain all the desired objectives difficult of access to all embodied beings.

## \|\| 2.68.76 \|\|

*gaṇosti tatra dvibhujaścatuṣpātpaṃcaśīrṣakaḥ \|*  
*tasya saṃvīkṣaṇādeva pāpaṃ yāti sahasradhā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. There is the Gaṇa there with two arms, four feet and five heads. Immediately after visiting it, sins are destroyed and split into a thousand.

## \|\| 2.68.77 \|\|

*taduttare mune rudraśtuḥśṛṃgosti bhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tripādastu dviśīrṣā ca hastāḥ syuḥ sapta eva hi \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. O Sage, to the north thereof is Rudra, the terrible one, with four horns (Vedas), three feet (the Savanas), two heads (the Prāyaṇīya, introductory rite, and Udayanīya, concluding rite). He has seven hands (the Vedic Metres).

## \|\| 2.68.78-81 \|\|

*rorūyate vṛṣākārastridhā baddhaḥ sa kuṃbhaja \|*  
*kāśīvighrakarā ye ca ye kāśyāṃ pāpabuddhayaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ ca saṃchidāṃ kartumahaṃ dhṛtakuṭhārakaḥ \|*  
*ye kāśyāṃ vighnahartāro ye kāśyāṃ dharmabuddhayaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*sudhāghaṭakaraścāhaṃ tadvaṃśapariṣekakṛt \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā vṛṣarudraṃ vai pūjayitvā tu bhaktitaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*mahāmahopacāraiśca na vighnairabhibhūyate \|*  
*maṇipradīpo nāgo'sti tasmādrudrādudagdiśi \|\| 81 \|\|*

78-81. O Pot-born One, he (Lord Rudra) cries out as follows, in the shape of Vṛṣa (Bull, Dharma) and bound in three ways (by means of Mantras, Brāhmaṇas and Kalpas): “Those who are evil-intentioned ones in Kāśī and those who bring in obstacles to Kāśī—it is to cut them off that I am holding the dagger. Those who are pious-minded in Kāśī and those who remove obstacles in Kāśī—it is to make their families flourish that I hold the Amṛta jar in my hand.”

If a devotee visits Vṛṣarudra and worships him with devotion and great means of service, he is never assailed by obstacles.

To the northern quarter of Rudra is the serpent deity named Maṇipradīpa.

## \|\| 2.68.82-83 \|\|

*maṇikuṃḍaṃ tadagre tu viṣavyādhiharaṃ param \|*  
*tasminkuṃḍe kṛtasnānastaṃ nāgaṃ parivīkṣya ca \|\| 82 \|\|*

*maṇimāṇikyasaṃpūrṇa gajāśvarathasaṃkulam \|*  
*strīratnaputraratnaiśca samṛddhaṃ rājyamāpnuyāt \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. Beyond it is Maṇikuṇḍa. It is a great holy Kuṇḍa that dispels poison and ailments. A devotee should take his holy ablution in the Kuṇḍa and visit the serpent-deity. He should obtain a kingdom full of jewels and rubies, abounding in elephants, horses and chariots and richly endowed with excellent wives and sons.

## \|\| 2.68.84-85 \|\|

*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ kāśyāṃ yairna vilokitam \|*  
*te martyaloke bhārāya bhuvo bhūtā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*kṛttivāsaḥ samutpattiṃ ye śroṣyaṃtīha mānavāḥ \|*  
*talliṃgadarśanācchreyo lapsyaṃte nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. There is no doubt in this that if Kṛttivāseśvara Liṅga in Kāśī has not been visited those people will be mere burdens of the world.

## Chapter 69 - The Assembly of Sixty-eight Holy Spots

## \|\| 2.69.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇvagastya taporāśe kāśyāṃ liṃgāni yāni vai \|*  
*sevitāni nṛṇāṃ muktyai bhaveyurbhāvitātmanām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. Listen, O Agastya, O mass of penance, to the description of all the Liṅgas in Kāśī which, if resorted to, shall be conducive to the salvation of men of purified souls.

## \|\| 2.69.2 \|\|

*kṛttiprāvaraṇaṃ yatra kṛtaṃ devena līlayā \|*  
*rudrāvāsa iti khyātaṃ tatsthānaṃ sarvasiddhidam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The spot where the hide was sportingly worn by the Lord, is well-known as Rudrāvāsa. It accords all spiritual powers.

## \|\| 2.69.3 \|\|

*sthite tatromayā sārdhaṃ svecchayā kṛttivāsasi \|*  
*āgatya naṃdī vijñaptiṃ cakre praṇatipūrvakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When Kṛttivāsa stationed himself voluntarily there along with Umā, Nandin came there and submitted after due obeisance:

## \|\| 2.69.4 \|\|

*devadeveśa viśveśa prāsādāḥ sumanoharāḥ \|*  
*sarvaratnamayā ramyāḥ sāṣṭāṣaṣṭirabhūdiha \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. “O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, O Lord of the universe, sixty-eight very fascinating and charming mansions full of jewels have sprung up here.

## \|\| 2.69.5 \|\|

*bhūrbhuvaḥsvastale yāni śubhānyāyatanāni hi \|*  
*muktidānyapi tānīha mayānītāni sarvataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Whatever splendid holy shrines are there in the three worlds—Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ—capable of bestowing salvation, have been brought here by me from all-round.

## \|\| 2.69.6 \|\|

*yato yacca samānītaṃ yatra yacca kṛtāspadam \|*  
*kathayiṣyāmyahaṃ nātha kṣaṇaṃ tadavadhāryatām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Which has been brought from where, which has been installed in what place, I shall describe, O Lord. Be pleased to attend for a short while.

## \|\| 2.69.7 \|\|

*sthāṇurnāma mahāliṃgaṃ devadevasya mokṣadam \|*  
*kurukṣetrādihodbhūtaṃ kalāśeṣosti tatra vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The salvation-giving great. Liṅga of the Lord of Devas named Sthāṇu, has sprung up here from Kurukṣetra. Only a sixteenth part thereof is present there.

## \|\| 2.69.8 \|\|

*tadagre sannihatyākhyā mahāpuṣkariṇī śubhā \|*  
*lolārka paścime bhāge kurukṣetrasthalī tu sā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In front of it there is the great splendid Puṣkariṇī (holy lake) named Sannihati to the western side of Lolārka. It is (called) the holy spot Kurukṣetra Sthaīa.

## \|\| 2.69.9 \|\|

*tatra snātaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ taptaṃ dattaṃ śubhārthibhiḥ \|*  
*kurukṣetrādbhavetsatyaṃ koṭikoṭiguṇādhikam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Whatever holy rite is performed there, say, holy bath, offerings, Japas, penance and monetary gifts, by those who seek welfare, shall truly be crores of crores (of times) more beneficial than those at Kurukṣetra.

## \|\| 2.69.10 \|\|

*naimiṣāddevadevotra brahmāvartena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*tatrāṃśamātraṃ saṃsthāpya kāśyāmāvirabhūdvibho \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O Lord, accompanied by Brahmāvarta the Lord of Devas has manifested himself in Kāśī from Naimiṣa, after leaving a mere part there.

## \|\| 2.69.11-17 \|\|

*ḍhuṃḍhirājottarebhāge siddhidaṃ sādhakasya vai \|*  
*liṃgaṃ vai devadevākhyaṃ tadagre kūpa uttamaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*brahmāvarta iti khyātaḥ punarāvṛttihṛnnṛṇām \|*  
*tatkūpādbhiḥ kṛtasnāno devadevaṃ samarcya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tatpuṇyaṃ naimiṣāraṇyātkoṭikoṭiguṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*gokarṇāyatanādatra svayamāvirabhūnmahat \|\| 13 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ mahābalaṃ nāma sāṃbādityasamīpataḥ \|*  
*darśanātsparśanādyasya kṣaṇādeno mahābalam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vātāhatastūlarāśiriva vidrāti dūrataḥ \|*  
*kapālamocanapuro dṛṣṭvā liṃgaṃ mahābalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*mahābalamavāpnoti nivārṇanagaraṃ vrajet \|*  
*ṛṇamocanataḥ prācyāṃ prabhāsātkṣetrasattamāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śaśibhūṣaṇasaṃjñaṃ tu liṃgamatra pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*talliṃgasevanānmartyaḥ śāśibhūṣaṇatāṃ vrajet \|\| 17 \|\|*

11-17. To the northern side of Ḍhuṇḍhirāja is the Liṅga called Devadeva (Lord of the Devas) which bestows all spiritual powers on the aspirant. Beyond it is the excellent well, well-known as Brahmāvarta, which dispels the likelihood of coming back (into this world) in the case of men. A devotee should take his bath in the waters of that well and adore Devadeva. The merit thereof is known as crores of crores of times that at Naimiṣāraṇya.

From the shrine and holy spot of Gokarṇa has sprung up here voluntarily the great Liṅga named Mahābala in the vicinity of Sāṃbāditya. By visiting and touching it, every powerful (great) sin is thrown far off like a mass of cotton wafted by wind.

By visiting Mahābala Liṅga in front of Kapālamocana, a devotee attains great power and he will attain the city of salvation.

The Liṅga named Śaśibhūṣaṇa has been installed here to the east of Ṛṇamocana. It was brought from the excellent holy spot Prabhāsa. By resorting to that Liṅga a man will attain the state of the Moon-embellished Lord (i.e. Śiva).

## \|\| 2.69.18 \|\|

*prabhāsakṣetrayātrāyāḥ puṇyaṃ prāpnoti koṭikṛt \|*  
*ujjayinyā mahākālaḥ svayamatrāgato vibhuḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He attains crores of times more the merit from the religious festival at Prabhāsakṣetra.

Lord Mahākāla has himself come here from Ujjayinī.

## \|\| 2.69.19-23 \|\|

*yannāmasmaraṇādeva na bhayaṃ kalikālataḥ \|*  
*praṇavākhyānmahāliṃgātprācyāṃ kalmaṣanāśanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*mahākālābhidhaṃ liṃgaṃ darśanānmokṣadaṃ param \|*  
*ayogaṃdheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ puṣkarāttīrthasattamāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

*āvirāsīdiha mahatpuṣkareṇa sahaiva tu \|*  
*matsyodaryuttarebhāge dṛṣṭvā 'yogaṃdhamīśvaram \|\| 21 \|\|*

*snātvā'yogaṃdhakuṃḍe tu bhavāttārayate pitṝn \|*  
*mahānādeśvaraṃ liṃgamaṭṭahāsādihāgatam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*trilocanādudīcyāṃ tu taddṛṣṭamuktaye matam \|*  
*mahotkaṭeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ marutkoṭādihāgatam \|*  
*kāmeśvarottare bhāge dṛṣṭaṃ vimalasiddhidam \|\| 23 \|\|*

19-23. Merely by remembering his name, a devotee ceases to have the fear of Kali and Kāla. This Liṅga named Mahākāla is situated to the east of the great Liṅga named Praṇava. Through its visit, it bestows great salvation and it destroys all sins.

Ayogandheśvara Liṅga has manifested itself here from the excellent Puṣkara Tīrtha along with Puṣkara (holy lake). A devotee should visit Lord Ayogandha in the northern side of Matsyodarī and take his holy bath in Ayogandhakuṇḍa. He redeems his ancestors from the worldly existence.

Mahānādeśvara Liṅga has come here from the holy spot Aṭṭahāsa. It is to the north of Trilocana. If visited, it is conducive to salvation.

Mahotkaṭeśvara Liṅga has come here from the holy spot Marutkoṭa. It is to the northern side of Kāmeśvara. When visited, it accords spiritual powers devoid of impurities.

## \|\| 2.69.24 \|\|

*viśvasthānādihāyātaṃ liṃgaṃ vai vimaleśvaram \|*  
*svarlīnātpaścime bhāge dṛṣṭaṃ vimalasiddhidam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Vimaleśvara Liṅga has come here from the holy spot Viśvasthāna. It is to the western side of Svarlīna. If visited, it accords spiritual powers devoid of impurities.

## \|\| 2.69.25 \|\|

*mahāvrataṃ mahāliṃgaṃ maheṃdrādiha saṃsthitam \|*  
*skaṃdeśvara samīpe tu mahāvrataphalapradam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The great Mahāvrata Liṅga has come over here from the Mahendra mountain. It is in the vicinity of Skandeśvara. It bestows the merit of great Vratas (holy observances and vows).

## \|\| 2.69.26-29 \|\|

*vṛṃdārakarṣivṛṃdānāṃ stuvatāṃ prathame yuge \|*  
*utpannaṃ yanmahāliṃgaṃ bhūmiṃ bhittvā sudurbhidām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mahādeveti tairuktaṃ yanmanorathapūraṇāta \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ mahādevastadārabhyābhavacca yat \|\| 27 \|\|*

*muktikṣetraṃ kṛtaṃ yena mahāliṃgena kāśikā \|*  
*avimukte mahādevaṃ yo drakṣyatyatramānavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śaṃbhuloke gamastasya yatratatra mṛtasya hi \|*  
*avimukte prayatnena tatsaṃsevyaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. In the course of the first Yuga i.e. Kṛtayuga when the groups of celestial sages were reciting the prayers, a great Liṅga appeared after piercing through the ground which was very difficult to break through. Since their desire was fulfilled, they proclaimed it “Mahādeva”. Ever since then, it became Mahādeva in Kāśī. It was by that great Liṅga that Kāśikā was made the holy spot of salvation. A man who visits Mahādeva here in Avimukta, shall surely go to Śaṃbhu’s world wherever he may die. That Liṅga should be assiduously resorted to in Avimukta by those who desire salvation.

## \|\| 2.69.30 \|\|

*kalpāṃtarepi na tyaktaṃ kadāpyānaṃdakānanam \|*  
*yena liṃgasvarūpeṇa mahādevena sarvathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Ānandakānana has never been given up by Mahādeva in the form of Liṅga even in the course of other Kalpas.

## \|\| 2.69.31 \|\|

*tatprasādoyamatulaḥ sarvaratnamayaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhatīrthācca pratīcyāṃ kṣetrarakṣakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Its shrine (of the Liṅga) of auspicious form is incomparable. It consists of all gems. It is the favour of that Lord Mahādeva.

## \|\| 2.69.32 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāmadhiṣṭhātrī devatā sābhilāṣadā \|*  
*mahādeveti saṃjñā vai sarvaliṃgasvarūpiṇī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. That is the presiding deity in Vārāṇasī fulfilling all desires. It is in the form of all Liṅgas and is named Mahādeva.

## \|\| 2.69.33 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ mahādevo dṛṣṭo yairliṃgarūpadhṛk \|*  
*tena trailokyaliṃgāni dṛṣṭānīha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Undoubtedly all the Liṅgas of the three worlds have been seen by the person who has seen Mahādeva having form of Liṅga in Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.69.34 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ mahādevaṃ samabhyarcya sakṛnnaraḥ \|*  
*ābhūtasaṃplavaṃ yāvacchivaloke vasenmudā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. By worshipping Mahādeva once in Vārāṇasī, a man will joyously reside in Śiva’s world until the annihilation of all living beings.

## \|\| 2.69.35 \|\|

*pavitraparvaṇi sadā śrāvaṇe māsi yatnataḥ \|*  
*liṃge pavitramāropya mahādeve na garbhabhāk \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The Mahādeva Liṅga should be assiduously invested with the sacred thread or Kuśa grass in the month of Śrāvaṇa on the fourteenth day. The devotee shall never be in a womb (thereafter).

## \|\| 2.69.36-57 \|\|

*pitāmaheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ gayātīrthādihāgatam \|*  
*phalgruprabhṛtibhistīrthaiḥ sārdhakoṭyaṣṭasaṃmitaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dharmeṇa yatra vai taptaṃ yugānāmayutaṃ śatam \|*  
*sākṣīkṛtya mahāliṃgaṃ śrīmaddharmeśvarābhidham \|\| 37 \|\|*

*pitāmaheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tatrābhyarcya naro mudā \|*  
*triḥsaptakulasaṃyukto mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*prayāgāttīrtharājācca śūlaṭaṃko maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tīrtharājena sahitaḥ sthita āgatya vai svayam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*nirvāṇamaṃḍapādramyādavācyāmatinirmalaḥ \|*  
*prāsādo meruṇā yasya spardhate kāṃcanojvalaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*devenaiva varo datto yatra pūrvaṃ yugāṃtare \|*  
*pūjyo maheśvaraḥ kāśyāṃ prathamaṃ kaluṣāpahaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*yaḥ prayāga iha snāto namasyati maheśvaram \|*  
*samabhyarcya vidhānena mahāsaṃbhāravistaraiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*prayāgasnānajātpuṇyācchūlaṭaṃka vilokanāt \|*  
*sa prāpnuyānna saṃdehaḥ puṇyaṃ koṭiguṇottaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

*śaṃkukarṇānmahākṣetrānmahāteja itīritam \|*  
*liṃgamāvirabhūdatra mahātejovivṛddhidam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*mahātejonidhistasya prāsādotīvanirmalaḥ \|*  
*jvālājaṭilitākāśo māṇikyaireva nirmitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*talliṃgadarśanātsparśātstavanācca samarcanāt \|*  
*prāpyate tatparaṃ dhāma yatra gatvā na śocate \|\| 46 \|\|*

*vināyakeśvarātpūrvaṃ mahātejaḥ samarcanāt \|*  
*tejomayena yānena yāti māheśvaraṃ padam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*rudrakoṭisamākhyātāttīrthātparamapāvanāt \|*  
*mahāyogīśvaraṃ liṃgamāviścakre svayaṃ param \|\| 48 \|\|*

*pārvatīśvara liṃgasya samīpe sarvasiddhikṛt \|*  
*talliṃgadarśanātpuṃsāṃ koṭiliṃga phalaṃ bhavet \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tatprāsādasya parito rudrāṇāṃ koṭisaṃmitāḥ \|*  
*prāsādāramyasaṃsthānā nirmitā rudramūrtibhiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*kāśyāṃ rudrasthalī sā tu paṭhyate vedavādibhiḥ \|*  
*rudrasthalyāṃ mṛtā ye vai kṛmikīṭapataṃgakāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*paśupakṣimṛgā martyā mlecchā vāpyatha dīkṣitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu rudrībhūtānāṃ punarāvṛttiratra na \|\| 52 \|\|*

*janmāṃtarasahasreṣu yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam \|*  
*rudrasthalīṃ praviṣṭasya tatsarvaṃ vrajati kṣayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*akāmo vā sakāmo vā tiryagyonigatopi vā \|*  
*rudrasthalyāṃ tyajanprāṇānparaṃ nirvāṇamāpnuyāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

*svayamekāṃbarātkṣetrātkṛttivāsā ihāgataḥ \|*  
*kṛttivāsasi liṃgetra svayameva vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*asminsthāne svabhaktānāṃ sāṃbaḥ sarṣigaṇo vibhuḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ copadiśedbrahma śrutau śrutibhirīḍitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kṣetretra siddhide prāptaścaṃḍīśo marujāṃgalāt \|*  
*pracaṃḍapāpasaṃghātaṃ khaṃḍayecchatadhekṣaṇāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

36-57. Accompanied by Phalgu and other Tīrthas numbering eight and a half cores, Pitāmaheśvara Liṅga came here from Gayā Tīrtha at the place where Dharma performed austerities for one million Yugas keeping as witness the great Liṅga named Dharmeśvara.

## \|\| 2.69.38 \|\|

*pitāmaheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tatrābhyarcya naro mudā \|*  
*triḥsaptakulasaṃyukto mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A man should joyously worship Pitāmaheśvarā Liṅga there. There is no doubt about this that he gets liberated along with twenty-one generations of his family.

## \|\| 2.69.39-43 \|\|

*prayāgāttīrtharājācca śūlaṭaṃko maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tīrtharājena sahitaḥ sthita āgatya vai svayam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*nirvāṇamaṃḍapādramyādavācyāmatinirmalaḥ \|*  
*prāsādo meruṇā yasya spardhate kāṃcanojvalaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*devenaiva varo datto yatra pūrvaṃ yugāṃtare \|*  
*pūjyo maheśvaraḥ kāśyāṃ prathamaṃ kaluṣāpahaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*yaḥ prayāga iha snāto namasyati maheśvaram \|*  
*samabhyarcya vidhānena mahāsaṃbhāravistaraiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*prayāgasnānajātpuṇyācchūlaṭaṃka vilokanāt \|*  
*sa prāpnuyānna saṃdehaḥ puṇyaṃ koṭiguṇottaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

39-43. From Prayāga, the kings of Tīrthas, Maheśvara named Śùlaṭaṅka came here by himself accompanied by the Tīrtharāja himself and stayed south of the beautiful Nirvāṇamaṇḍapa. The pure mansion of that Lord excels Mount Meru. It is refulgent like gold. It is a boon granted by the Lord himself in a previous Yuga. Maheśvara should be worshipped at the outset in Kāśī. He dispels all sins.

One who takes his holy bath in Prayāga (stationed) here, bows down to Maheśvāra after adoring in accordance with the injunctions, with elaborate requisites of services, and visits Śūlaṭaṅka undoubtedly obtains merit crores of times more than that arising from the holy bath at (the original) Prayāga.

## \|\| 2.69.44 \|\|

*śaṃkukarṇānmahākṣetrānmahāteja itīritam \|*  
*liṃgamāvirabhūdatra mahātejovivṛddhidam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. From Śaṅkukarṇa, a great holy spot, the Liṅga called Mahātejas appeared here. It bestows increase in great splendour.

## \|\| 2.69.45 \|\|

*mahātejonidhistasya prāsādotīvanirmalaḥ \|*  
*jvālājaṭilitākāśo māṇikyaireva nirmitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. His mansion is the storehouse of great splendour. It is extremely pure. It pervades the sky with its sparkling flame-like splendour. It is (as if) solely constructed with rubies.

## \|\| 2.69.46 \|\|

*talliṃgadarśanātsparśātstavanācca samarcanāt \|*  
*prāpyate tatparaṃ dhāma yatra gatvā na śocate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. By visiting, touching, eulogizing and adoring that Liṅga, that greatest region is attained, on reaching which no one comes to grief.

## \|\| 2.69.47 \|\|

*vināyakeśvarātpūrvaṃ mahātejaḥ samarcanāt \|*  
*tejomayena yānena yāti māheśvaraṃ padam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. By adoring Mahātejas to the east of Vināyakeśvara the devotee goes to the region of Maheśvara in a fire-like resplendent vehicle.

## \|\| 2.69.48 \|\|

*rudrakoṭisamākhyātāttīrthātparamapāvanāt \|*  
*mahāyogīśvaraṃ liṃgamāviścakre svayaṃ param \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The great Mahāyogīśvara Liṅga revealed itself from the extremely sacred Tīrtha named Rudrakoṭi.

## \|\| 2.69.49 \|\|

*pārvatīśvara liṃgasya samīpe sarvasiddhikṛt \|*  
*talliṃgadarśanātpuṃsāṃ koṭiliṃga phalaṃ bhavet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. It is in the vicinity of Pārvatīśvara Liṅga. It bestows all miraculous powers. By visiting that Liṅga, men get the merit of (visiting) a crore of Liṅgas.

## \|\| 2.69.50 \|\|

*tatprāsādasya parito rudrāṇāṃ koṭisaṃmitāḥ \|*  
*prāsādāramyasaṃsthānā nirmitā rudramūrtibhiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. All-round the mansion thereof, mansions of beautiful structure, about a crore in number, belonging to Rudras, have been erected by Rudramūrtis.

## \|\| 2.69.51-54 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ rudrasthalī sā tu paṭhyate vedavādibhiḥ \|*  
*rudrasthalyāṃ mṛtā ye vai kṛmikīṭapataṃgakāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*paśupakṣimṛgā martyā mlecchā vāpyatha dīkṣitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu rudrībhūtānāṃ punarāvṛttiratra na \|\| 52 \|\|*

*janmāṃtarasahasreṣu yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam \|*  
*rudrasthalīṃ praviṣṭasya tatsarvaṃ vrajati kṣayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*akāmo vā sakāmo vā tiryagyonigatopi vā \|*  
*rudrasthalyāṃ tyajanprāṇānparaṃ nirvāṇamāpnuyāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

51-54. That is called Rudrasthalī at Kāśī by expounders of the Vedas. Those who die in Rudrasthalī, whether they be worms, insects, locusts, animals, birds, beasts, men of barbarian descent or learned Dīkṣitas, become Rudras. They (who have become Rudras) do not have any return to the world. All the sins accumulated in the course of thousands of births, become entirely destroyed as soon as the devotee enters Rudrasthalī. The devotee may be desirous (of fruits) or free from desires or one born as a brute (non-human being), but if that being dies at Rudrasthalī, he will attain the supreme liberation.

## \|\| 2.69.55 \|\|

*svayamekāṃbarātkṣetrātkṛttivāsā ihāgataḥ \|*  
*kṛttivāsasi liṃgetra svayameva vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Kṛttivāsas has come down here voluntarily from the holy spot Ekāṃbara (Bhuvaneśvara) and stationed here in the Kṛttivāsas Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.69.56 \|\|

*asminsthāne svabhaktānāṃ sāṃbaḥ sarṣigaṇo vibhuḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ copadiśedbrahma śrutau śrutibhirīḍitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In this holy spot the Lord in the company of Aṃbā and hosts of sages, imparts into the ears of his own devotees the knowledge of Brahman revered by the Śrutis.

## \|\| 2.69.57 \|\|

*kṣetretra siddhide prāptaścaṃḍīśo marujāṃgalāt \|*  
*pracaṃḍapāpasaṃghātaṃ khaṃḍayecchatadhekṣaṇāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. From Marujāṅgala (Marwar, Rajasthan) Caṇḍīśa has come down to the Siddhi-bestowing holy spot here. Merely through his look, he will split the mass of Fierce sins into a hundred parts.

## \|\| 2.69.58 \|\|

*pāśapāṇigaṇādhyakṣa samīpe yaḥ prapaśyati \|*  
*caṃḍīśvaraṃ mahāliṃgaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. He who visits the great Caṇḍīśvara Liṅga in the vicinity of Gaṇādhyakṣa, armed with the noose, attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 2.69.59 \|\|

*kālaṃjarānnīlakaṃṭhastiṣṭhedatra svayaṃ vibhuḥ \|*  
*gaṇeśāddaṃtakūṭākhyātsamīpe bhavanāśanaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Lord Nīlakaṇṭha himself has arrived here from the Kālañjara mountain. He is the destroyer of worldly existence and has stationed himself in the vicinity of the Gaṇas called Dantakūṭa.

## \|\| 2.69.60 \|\|

*nīlakaṃṭheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ kāśyāṃ yaiḥ paripūjitam \|*  
*nīlakaṃṭhāsta eva syustaeva śaśibhūṣaṇāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Those devotees by whom Nīlakaṇṭheśvara Liṅga in Kāśī has been duly adored, shall themselves become blue-throated moon-embellished ones.

## \|\| 2.69.61 \|\|

*kāśmīrādiha saṃprāptaṃ liṃgaṃ vijayasaṃjñitam \|*  
*sadā vijayadaṃ puṃsāṃ prācyāṃ śālakaṭaṃkaṭāt \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The Liṅga with the epithet Vijaya has come down here from Kāśmīra. (It has stationed itself) to the east of Śālakaṭaṃkaṭa and always bestows success on men.

## \|\| 2.69.62 \|\|

*raṇe rājakule dyūte vivāde sarvadaiva hi \|*  
*vijayo jāyate puṃsāṃ vijayeśa samarcanāt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. By adoring Vijayeśa, men become always victorious in battle, royal palace, gaining table and scholastic disputation.

## \|\| 2.69.63 \|\|

*ūrdhvaretāstridaṃḍāyāḥ saṃprāptotra svayaṃ vibhuḥ \|*  
*kūśmāṃḍakaṃ gaṇādhyakṣaṃ puraskṛtya vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. From Tridaṇḍa city Lord Ūrdhvaretas himself has arrived here. He has established himself keeping in front of him Kūṣmāṇḍaka, the presiding officer of the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 2.69.64 \|\|

*ūrdhvāṃ gatimavāpnoti vīkṣaṇādūrdhvaretasaḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvaretasi ye bhaktā na hi teṣāmadhogatiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. By viewing Ūrdhvaretas a devotee attains an elevated status. There is no question of going downwards (in status etc.) in the case of the devotees of Ūrdhvaretas.

## \|\| 2.69.65 \|\|

*maṃḍaleśvarataḥ kṣetrālliṃgaṃ śrīkaṃṭhasaṃjñitam \|*  
*vināyakānmaṃḍasaṃjñāduttarasyāṃ vyavasthitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The Liṅga named Śrīkaṇṭha (has come) from the holy spot Maṇḍaleśvara and established itself to the north of Vināyaka called Maṇḍa.

## \|\| 2.69.66 \|\|

*śrīkaṃṭhasya ca ye bhaktāḥ śrīkaṃṭhā eva te narāḥ \|*  
*neha śriyā viyujyaṃte na paratra kadācana \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Men who are devoted to Śrīkaṇṭha are Śrīkaṇṭhas themselves. They are not. short of glory and fortune either here or hereafter.

## \|\| 2.69.67 \|\|

*chāgalāṃḍānmahātīrthātkapardīśvavarasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*piśācamocane tīrthe svayamāvirabhūdvibhuḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The Lord with the appellation Kapardīśvara himself manifested in the Piśācamocana Tīrtha from the great Chāgalāṇḍa Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.69.68 \|\|

*kapardīśaṃ samabhyarcya na naro nirayaṃ vrajet \|*  
*na piśācatvamāpnoti kṛtvātrāpyaghamuttamam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. One who assiduously worships Kapardīśa, does not fall into hell, nor does he become a vampire even if he commits the most heinous sin.

## \|\| 2.69.69 \|\|

*āmrātakeśvarātkṣetrālliṃgaṃ sūkṣmeśa saṃjñitam \|*  
*svayamabhyāgataṃ cātra kṣetre vai śreyasāṃpade \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. From the holy place Āmrātakeśvara, the Liṅga named Sūkṣmeśa has arrived in this holy spot, the source of all welfare.

## \|\| 2.69.70 \|\|

*vikaṭa dvijasaṃjñasya gaṇeśasya samīpataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sūkṣmeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ gatiṃ sūkṣmāmavāpnuyāt \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. By visiting Sūkṣmeśvara Liṅga in the vicinity of Gaṇeśa called Vikaṭadvija, one attains the subtle goal.

## \|\| 2.69.71 \|\|

*saṃprāptamiha deveśaṃ jayaṃtaṃ madhukeśvarāt \|*  
*laṃbodarādgaṇapateḥ purastāttadavasthitam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. (The Liṅga named) Deveśa Jayanta has arrived here from the holy spot Madhukeśvara. It is stationed in front of Gaṇapati (named) Laṃbodara.

## \|\| 2.69.72 \|\|

*jayaṃteśvaramālokya snātvā gaṃgājale śubhe \|*  
*prāpnuyādvāṃchitāṃ siddhiṃ sarvatra vijayī bhavet \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. One who takes his holy bath in the splendid waters of Gaṅgā and visits Jayanta shall attain the miraculous powers desired. He will be victorious everywhere.

## \|\| 2.69.73-76 \|\|

*prāduścakāra deveśaḥ śrīśailāttripurāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*śrīśailaśikharaṃ dṛṣṭvā yatphalaṃ samudīritam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tripurāṃtakamālokya tatphalaṃ helayāpyate \|*  
*viśverātpaścime bhāge tripurāṃtakamīśvaram \|\| 74 \|\|*

*saṃpūjya parayā bhaktyā na naro garbhamāviśet \|*  
*saumyasthānādihāyāto bhagavānkukkuṭeśvaraḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*vakratuṃḍa gaṇādhyakṣa samīpe sopatiṣṭhate \|*  
*taddarśanādarcanācca karasthāḥ sarvasiddhayaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

73-76. Tripurāntaka, the Lord of Devas, manifested from Śrīśaila. The merit that has been mentioned as obtained by visiting the summit of Śrīśaila, can be easily obtained by visiting Tripurāntaka.

If a man worships with great devotion Lord Tripurāntaka on the western side of Viśveśa, he does not enter a womb.

Lord Kukkuṭeśvara has come here from Saumyasthāna. He is stationed in the vicinity of Gaṇeśa called Vakratuṇḍa. By visiting and adoring him, all miraculous powers can be acquired.

## \|\| 2.69.77 \|\|

*jāleśvarāttriśūlī ca svayamīśaḥ samāgataḥ \|*  
*kūṭadaṃtādgaṇapateḥ purastātsarvasiddhidaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Lord Triśūlī has himself come here from the holy spot Jāleśvara (stationed) in front of Gaṇapati (named) Kūṭadanta. He bestows all Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.69.78 \|\|

*rāmeśvarānmahākṣetrājjaṭīdevaḥ samāgataḥ \|*  
*ekadaṃtottare bhāge sorcitaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Lord Jaṭī has come from the great holy spot Rāmeśvara. He is on the northern side of Ekadanta. If worshipped, he bestows all desired things.

## \|\| 2.69.79 \|\|

*trisaṃdhyātkṣetrato devastryaṃbakosti samāgataḥ \|*  
*trimukhātpūrvadigbhāge pūjitastryaṃbakatvakṛt \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Lord Tryaṃbaka has come from the holy spot Trisandhya. He is on the eastern side of Trimukha. If worshipped, he accords the state of Tryaṃbaka.

## \|\| 2.69.80 \|\|

*hareśvaro hariścaṃdrātkṣetrādatra samāgataḥ \|*  
*hariścaṃdreśvarapuraḥ pūjito jayadaḥ sadā \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Hareśvara has come here from the holy spot Hariścandra (and is) in front of Hariścandreśvara. If worshipped, he always bestows victory.

## \|\| 2.69.81-82 \|\|

*iha śarvaḥ samāyātaḥ sthānānmadhyamakeśvarāt \|*  
*caturvedeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ purodhāya vyavasthitam \|\| 81 \|\|*

*śarvaṃ liṃgaṃ samabhyarcya kāśyāṃ paramasiddhikṛt \|*  
*na jātu jaṃtupadavīṃ prāpnuyātkvāpi mānavaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. Sarva has come here from (the holy place) Madhyamakeśvara. It is established keeping (itself) in front of Caturvedeśvara Liṅga. The Liṅga Sarva in Kāśī bestows the highest attainment (Mokṣa). By worshipping the Liṅga called Śarva no man falls into the status (category) of a lower being.

## \|\| 2.69.83 \|\|

*sthaleśvarānmahāliṃgaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ paraṃtviha \|*  
*yatra yajñeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ sarvaliṃgaphalapradam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Another great Liṅga has appeared here from Sthaleśvara (at a place) where is Yajñeśvara Liṅga. It bestows the benefits of all Liṅgas.

## \|\| 2.69.84 \|\|

*mahāliṃgaṃ samabhyarcya mahāśraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*mahatīṃ śriyamāpnoti loketra ca paratra ca \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. By worshipping Mahā Liṅga, a devotee having great faith attains great glory in this world as well as in the other.

## \|\| 2.69.85 \|\|

*iha liṃgaṃ sahasrākṣaṃ suvarṇākhyātsamāgatam \|*  
*yasya saṃdarśanātpuṃsāṃ jñānacakṣuḥ prajāyate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Sahasrākṣa Liṅga has come here from the holy spot named Suvarṇa. By visiting it men obtain the eye (vision) of knowledge.

## \|\| 2.69.86 \|\|

*śaileśvarādavācyāṃ tu sahasrākṣeśvaraṃ vibhum \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā janmasahasrāṇāṃ śatānāṃ pātakaṃ tyajet \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. By visiting Lord Sahasrākṣeśvara (which is) to the south of Śaileśvara, a devotee can cast off the sins of hundreds and thousands of births.

## \|\| 2.69.87 \|\|

*harṣitāddharṣitaṃ cātra prādurāsīttamoharam \|*  
*liṃgaṃharṣapradaṃ puṃsāṃ darśanātsparśanādapi \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. From the holy spot Harṣita has appeared the Liṅga Harṣita that dispels darkness. On being visited and touched, it bestows delight on men.

## \|\| 2.69.88 \|\|

*maṃtreśvara samīpe tu prāsādo harṣiteśituḥ \|*  
*tadvilokanataḥ puṃsāṃ nityaṃ harṣa paraṃparā \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The mansion (shrine) of Harṣiteśvara is in the vicinity of Mantreśvara. By visiting it men will always enjoy series of delightful events.

## \|\| 2.69.89 \|\|

*iha svayaṃ samāyāto rudro rudramahālayāt \|*  
*yasya darśanato yāṃti rudraloke narāḥ sphuṭam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Rudra himself has come here from Rudramahālaya. By visiting it men clearly pass on to the world of Rudra.

## \|\| 2.69.90 \|\|

*yaistu rudreśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ kāśyāmatra samarcitam \|*  
*te rudrarūpiṇo martyā vijñeyā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. There is no doubt in this that those men by whom Rudreśvara Liṅga here in Kāśī has been worshipped should be known as embodiments of Rudra.

## \|\| 2.69.91 \|\|

*tripureśa samīpe tu dṛṣṭvā rudreśvaraṃ vibhum \|*  
*rudrāsta iva vijñeyā jīvaṃtopi mṛtā api \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. If Lord Rudreśvara is visited in the vicinity of Tripureśa, those devotees are to be known as on a par with Rudra, whether alive or dead.

## \|\| 2.69.92 \|\|

*āgādiha mahādevo vṛṣeśo vṛṣabhadhvajāt \|*  
*bāṇeśvarasya liṃgasya samīpe vṛṣadaḥ sadā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The great Lord Vṛṣeśa has come here from the holy spot Vṛṣabhadhvaja. He is in the vicinity of Bāṇeśvara Liṅga. He always bestows piety.

## \|\| 2.69.93 \|\|

*ihāgataṃ tu kedārādīśāneśvara saṃjñitam \|*  
*taddraṣṭavyaṃ pratīcyāṃ ca liṃgaṃ prahlādakeśavāt \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The Liṅga named Īśāneśvara has come here from the holy spot Kedāra, That should be visited in the west of Prahlādakeśava.

## \|\| 2.69.94 \|\|

*īśāneśaṃ samabhyarcya snātvottaravahāṃbhasi \|*  
*vasedīśānanagare īśānasadṛśaprabhaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. A devotee who takes his holy bath in the waters of the north-flowing (Gaṅgā) river and worships Īśāneśa, shall stay in the city of Īśāna with splendour like that of Īśāna.

## \|\| 2.69.95 \|\|

*bhairavādbhairavī mūrtiratrāyātā manoharā \|*  
*saṃhārabhairavo nāma draṣṭavyaḥ sa prayatnataḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. The beautiful Mūrti (image, form) Bhairavī has come here from the holy spot Bhairava. Its name is Saṃhārabhairava. It should be assiduously visited.

## \|\| 2.69.96 \|\|
