*lābhāḥ saṃtūdyamavatāṃ girīśeha paraḥ śatāḥ \|*  
*paraṃ paroyaṃ lābhotra yattvaṃ dṛggocarī bhaveḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

The Birds said:

Obeisance to you, O destroyer of worldly birth, O Lord of helpless ones, O omniscient one, O three-eyed Lord, what boon should be desired by us beyond this that we have been seen (by you) despite our being of the brutish category?

15\. May there be hundreds and hundreds of profits, O Giriśa, unto the persons of great enterprise and efforts here; but this is the greatest profit that you should be within the range of our vision.

## \|\| 2.79.16 \|\|

*yadetaddṛśyate nātha tatsarvaṃ kṣaṇabhaṃguram \|*  
*abhaṃguro bhavānekastvatsaparyāpyabhaṃgurā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Lord, these things that are visible are entirely momentary. You alone are permanent and free from destruction. The worship done unto you is not momentary (in yielding fruit).

## \|\| 2.79.17 \|\|

*vicitrajanmakoṭīnāṃ smṛtirnotra parisphuret \|*  
*etattapasviracitaliṃgapūjā vilokanāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By viewing the adoration of the Liṅga performed by this sage (Yama), we are able to recollect crores of our births of diverse nature.

## \|\| 2.79.18 \|\|

*devayonirapi prāptā ciramasmābhirīśitaḥ \|*  
*divyāṃganā sahasrāṇi tatra bhuktvā svalīlayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O Lord, we have, had our births in the category (life) of the celestial ones for a long time. Thousands of divine damsels had been enjoyed sportively.

## \|\| 2.79.19 \|\|

*āsurī dānavī nāgī nairṛtī cāpi kainnarī \|*  
*vidyādharī ca gāṃdharvī yonirasmābhirarjitā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. We have had our births in the womb of Asuras, Dānavas, Nāgas, Nairṛtas, Kinnaras, Vidyādharas and Gandharvas.

## \|\| 2.79.20 \|\|

*naratve bhūpatitvaṃ ca pariprāptamanekaśaḥ \|*  
*jale jalacaratvaṃ ca sthale ca sthalacāritā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. While being human we have attained the status of kings many times; in water (we had) the state of aquatic beings and on the ground the state of ground walkers.

## \|\| 2.79.21 \|\|

*vane vanaukaso jātā grāmeṣu grāmavāsinaḥ \|*  
*dātāro yācitāraśca rakṣitāraśca ghātukāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. We have been forest-dwellers in the forests, rustic ones in villages; we have been donors and beggars, protectors and murderers.

## \|\| 2.79.22 \|\|

*sukhinopi vayaṃ jātā duḥkhino vayamāsma ca \|*  
*jetāraśca vayaṃ jātāḥ parājetāra eva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. We have been happy and we have been miserable too. We had become the victorious ones as well as the vanquished ones.

## \|\| 2.79.23 \|\|

*adhītinopi mūrkhāśca svāminaḥ sevakā api \|*  
*caturṣu bhūtagrāmeṣu uttamādhamamadhyamāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. We have been serious students and the dullest fools; we have been masters as well as servants. We have had births in the four types of living beings (oviparous, viviparous, sweat-born and shooting shrubs) of high level, medium level and the basest one.

## \|\| 2.79.24 \|\|

*abhūma bhūriśaḥ śaṃbho na kvāpi sthairyamāgatāḥ \|*  
*itoyonestato yonau tato yonestatonyataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. From one womb to another and to a third therefrom, we have various forms. O Śaṃbhu, but nowhere did we have any stability.

## \|\| 2.79.25-26 \|\|

*pinākinkvāpi na prāpi sukhaleśo manāgapi \|*  
*idānīṃ puṇyasaṃbhārairdharmeśvaravilokanāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tāpaneḥsutapo vahnijvālāprajvalitainasaḥ \|*  
*saṃvīkṣya tryakṣa sākṣāttvāṃ kṛtakṛtyā babhūvima \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. O Pināka-wielding One, not even the least quantum of happiness was attained by us anywhere. But now, thanks to our accumulated merits, we have visited Dharmeśvara. Our sins have been burnt by the flames of the fire of the austerities of the son of Tapana (the Sun-god). O Three-eyed Lord, on seeing you directly we have become blessed. We feel the satisfaction of having achieved our objective.

## \|\| 2.79.27-28 \|\|

*tathāpi cedvaro deyastiryakṣvasmāsu dhūrjaṭe \|*  
*kṛpaṇeṣvapi śocyeṣu jñānaṃ sarvajña dehi tat \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yena jñānena muktāḥ smo'muṣmātsaṃsārabaṃdhanāt \|*  
*yaṃtritāḥ prākṛtaiḥ pāśairadurbhedyaiśca mādṛśaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Still, if a boon is to be given, O Dhūrjaṭi, O omniscient one, grant that knowledge to the miserable, pitiable creatures like us—knowledge whereby we can be released from this worldly bondage. We are fettered and by the bonds of Māyā not to be easily cut by persons like we.

## \|\| 2.79.29 \|\|

*aiṃdraṃ padaṃ na vāṃchāmo na cāṃdraṃ nānyadeva hi \|*  
*vāñchāmaḥ kevalaṃ mṛtyuṃ kāśyāṃ śaṃbho'punarbhavam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Śaṃbhu, we do not covet the position of Indra, not that of the Moon, nor do we covet anything else. We desire only the death at Kāśī after which there is no rebirth.

## \|\| 2.79.30 \|\|

*tvatsānnidhyādvijānīmaḥ sarvajña sakalaṃ vayam \|*  
*yathā caṃdanasaṃsargātsarve surabhayo drumāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O omniscient one, we understand everything due to your presence in the vicinity, just as all trees gain fragrance due to contact with a Sandal tree.

## \|\| 2.79.31 \|\|

*etadeva paraṃ jñānaṃ saṃsārocchittikāraṇam \|*  
*vapurvisarjanaṃ kāle yattavānaṃdakānane \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. This itself is (the cause of) the great knowledge that brings about the destruction of worldly existence, namely casting off of the body at the proper time in your Ānandakānana.

## \|\| 2.79.32 \|\|

*nirmathya viṣvagvāgjālaṃ sārabhūtamidaṃ param \|*  
*brahmaṇodīritaṃ pūrvaṃ kāśyāṃ muktistanutyajām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Formerly this great essence has been extracted and stated by Brahmā after churning the entire verbal expanse: (There is) ‘Salvation to those who cast off the body at Kāśī.’

## \|\| 2.79.33 \|\|

*yadvācyaṃ bahubhirgraṃthaistadaṣṭābhirihākṣaraiḥ \|*  
*hariṇoktaṃ ravipuraḥ kaivalyaṃ kāśisaṃsthitau \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. What could be expounded through many passages was uttered by Hari to Ravi (the Sun) in eight syllables: “Kaivalya (Salvation) in dying at Kāśī” (kaivalyam kāśīsaṃsthitau).

## \|\| 2.79.34 \|\|

*yājñavalkyo munivaraḥ proktavānmunisaṃsadi \|*  
*raveradhītya nigamānkāśyāmaṃte paraṃ padam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The excellent sage Yājñavalkya said in the assembly of sages: “Having studied the Nigamas (scriptures) from Ravi (Sun-god), the great position (salvation is to be gained) in Kāśī in the end.”

## \|\| 2.79.35 \|\|

*svāmināpi jagaddhātrī purato maṃdarācale \|*  
*idameva purā proktaṃ kāśīnirvāṇajanmabhūḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Formerly this alone was said by you too to Jagaddhātrī (Goddess Pārvatī, the mother of the universe) on the Mandāra Mountain: “Kāśī is the birth-place of salvation.”

## \|\| 2.79.36 \|\|

*kṛṣṇadvaipāyanopyevaṃ śaṃbho vakṣyati nānyathā \|*  
*yatraviśveśvaraḥ sākṣānmuktistatra padepade \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Śaṃbhu, Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana (Vyāsa) too will be saying this, “Where Viśveśvara is directly present salvation is acquired there at every step.”

## \|\| 2.79.37 \|\|

*vadaṃtyanyepi munayastīrthasaṃnyāsakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*ciraṃtanā lomaśādyāḥ kāśikā muktikāśikā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Other ancient sages, Lomaśa and others, who establish holy spots, say, “Kāśikā is the illuminator of salvation.”

## \|\| 2.79.38 \|\|

*vayamapyevaṃ jānīmo yatra svargataraṃgiṇī \|*  
*ānaṃdakānane śaṃrbhomokṣastatraiva niścitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. We too know thus: Certainly there alone is salvation, in Ānandakānana, where the celestial river flows.

## \|\| 2.79.39 \|\|

*bhūtaṃ bhāvi bhaviṣyaṃ yatsvarge martye rasātale \|*  
*tatsarvameva jānīmo dharmeśānugrahātparāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. We know everything that happens in heaven, in the mortal world and in the nether worlds—the past, the present and the future, due to the great blessings of Dharmeśa.

## \|\| 2.79.40 \|\|

*ato hiraṇyagarbhoktaṃ hariproktaṃ munīritam \|*  
*bhavatoktaṃ ca nikhilaṃ śaṃbho jānīmahe vayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. That is how, O Śaṃbhu, we know all these, the utterances of Hiraṇyagarbha (Brahmā), Hari, the sage and Your Lordship as well.

## \|\| 2.79.41 \|\|

*karāmalakavatsarvametadbrahmāṃḍagolakam \|*  
*asmadvāggocare'styeva dharmapīṭhaniṣevaṇāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Due to our resorting to Dharmapīṭha, the entire Cosmic Egg is within the range of our verbal expression like a fruit of Emblic myrobalan on the palm.

## \|\| 2.79.42 \|\|

*dharmarājasya tapasā tiryañcopi vayaṃ vibho \|*  
*jātāḥ sma nirvikalpaṃ hi sarvajñānasya bhājanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Lord, even we, birds, have become the possessors of undoubted knowledge in its entirety, due to the power of penance of Dharmarāja.

## \|\| 2.79.43-45 \|\|

*madhuraṃ mṛdulaṃ satyaṃ svapramāṇaṃ susaṃskṛtam \|*  
*hitaṃ mitaṃ sadṛṣṭāṃtaṃ śrutvā pakṣisubhāṣitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*devotivismayāpanno 'varṇayatpīṭhagauravam \|*  
*trailokyanagare cātra kāśīrājagṛhaṃ mama \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tatrāpi bhogabhavanamanarghyamaṇinirmitam \|*  
*mokṣalakṣmīvilāsākhyaḥ prāsādo meti śarmabhūḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. On hearing the speech of the birds, beneficial, soft, sweet, truthful, self-evident through experience, polished, brief (to the point), explained with illustration, the Lord became excessively surprised. He himself then extolled the magnificence of the Pīṭha: “Among all the cities in the three worlds, Kāśī is my royal palace. There too the mansion of enjoyment is built of jewels of inestimable value. My palace named Mokṣalakṣmīvilāsa (‘Graceful sport of the Goddess of the glory of Salvation’) is the place -of origin of great weal.

## \|\| 2.79.46 \|\|

*patattriṇo pimucyaṃte yaṃ kurvāṇāḥ pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*svecchayā vicaraṃtaḥ khe khecarā api devatāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. By circumambulating it, even birds become liberated. So also the Devas who walk in the firmament and move about as they please.

## \|\| 2.79.47 \|\|

*mokṣalakṣmīvilāsākhya prāsādasya vilokanāt \|*  
*śarīrāddūrato yāti brahmahatyāpi nānyathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. By viewing the palace named Mokṣalakṣmīvilāsa even the sin of the slaughter of a Brāhmaṇa goes away from the body. Not by any other means.

## \|\| 2.79.48 \|\|

*mokṣalakṣmīvilāsasya kalaśo yairnirīkṣataḥ \|*  
*nidhānakalaśāstāṃstu na muṃcaṃti padepade \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Nidhānahalaśas (‘treasure pots’) do not become separated anywhere from those people by whom the Kalaśa (pinnacle-dome) of Mokṣalakṣmīvilāsa is seen.

## \|\| 2.79.49 \|\|

*dūratopi patākāpi mama prāsādamūrdhagā \|*  
*netrātithī kṛtā yaistu nityaṃ te'tithayo mama \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. They will always be my guests—they by whom the banner fluttering aloft my palace was seen even from far away.

## \|\| 2.79.50 \|\|

*bhūmiṃ bhittvā svayaṃ jātastatprāsādamiṣeṇa hi \|*  
*ānaṃdākhyasya kaṃdasya kopyeṣa paramoṃkuraḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This is a great mysterious shooting sprout of the bulbous root named Ānanda, which has pierced the ground and issued forth under the pretext of that palace.

## \|\| 2.79.51 \|\|

*brahmādisthāvarāṃtāni yatra rūpaṇyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*māmevopāsate nityaṃ citraṃ citragatānyapi \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. There, many forms beginning with Brahmā and ending with an immobile being are painted in pictures, and it is surprising that (even) they adore me always.

## \|\| 2.79.52 \|\|

*sasaudho mekhile loke sthānaṃ paramanirvṛteḥ \|*  
*ratiśālā sa me ramyā sa me viśvāsabhūmikā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In the entire world that mansion is the sole place of my greatest happiness. It is the beautiful chamber of my sports. It is my ground of confidence.

## \|\| 2.79.53 \|\|

*mama sarvagatasyāpi prāsādoyaṃ parāspadam \|*  
*paraṃ brahma yadāmnātaṃ paramopaniṣadgirā \|*  
*amūrtaṃ tadahaṃ mūrto bhūyāṃ bhaktakṛpāvaśāt \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Although I am omnipresent, this palace is my great resort. I am that Supreme Brahmā well-known through the great words of the Upaniṣads. Though unembodied I shall also become embodied to do favour to the devotees.

## \|\| 2.79.54 \|\|

*naiḥśreyasyāḥ śriyo dhāma tadyāmyāṃ maṃḍaposti me \|*  
*tatrāhaṃ satataṃ tiṣṭhe tatsadomaṃḍapaṃ mama \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. To the south thereof is the Dhāman (abode) of the Naiḥśreyasī Śrī (‘Glory of Salvation’)—my pavilion. I stay there always. That is my Sadomaṇḍapa (‘Assembly Hall’).

## \|\| 2.79.55 \|\|

*nimeṣārdhapramāṇaṃ ca kālaṃ tiṣṭhati niścalaḥ \|*  
*tatra yastena vai yogaḥ samabhyastaḥ samāḥ śatam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If anyone stands there motionless for the duration of half a Nimeṣa, it is as good as if Yoga has been practised by him for a hundred years.

## \|\| 2.79.56 \|\|

*nirvāṇamaṃḍapaṃ nāma tatsthānaṃ jagatītale \|*  
*tatrarcaṃ saṃjapannekāṃ labhetsarvaśruteḥ phalam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. That spot is named Nirvāṇamaṇḍapa. It is well-known all-over the earth. One who chants (even) a single ṚK (Vedic verse) there, shall obtain the benefit.

## \|\| 2.79.57 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādapyekaṃ muktimaṃḍape \|*  
*tenāṣṭāṃgaḥ samabhyasto yogo'nyatrāyutaṃ samāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. If anyone performs a single Prāṇāyāma in the Mukti Maṇḍapa it is on a par with the eight-limbed (of eight stages) Yoga practised elsewhere for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 2.79.58 \|\|

*nirvāṇamaṃḍape yastu japedekaṃ ṣaḍakṣaram \|*  
*koṭirudreṇa japtena yatphalaṃ tasya tadbhavet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. If anyone utters the six-syllabled Mantra (i.e. oṃ namaḥ śivāya) once in Nirvāṇamaṇḍapa, he will derive the same benefit as is obtained by repeating the Rudra Mantra a crore times.

## \|\| 2.79.59 \|\|

*śucirgaṃgāṃbhasi snāto yo japecchatarudriyam \|*  
*nirvāṇamaṃḍape jñeyaḥ sa rudro dvijaveṣabhṛt \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A devotee who takes his bath in the water of Gaṅgā remains pure (in body, mind and speech). One who repeats Śatarudriya in Nirvāṇamaṇḍapa should be known as Rudra himself in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.79.60 \|\|

*brahmayajñasakṛtkṛtvā mama dakṣiṇamaṃḍape \|*  
*brahmalokamavāpyātha paraṃ brahmādhigacchati \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. By performing Brahma Yajña in the southern Maṇḍapa once, one attains Brahmaloka and realizes the Supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 2.79.61 \|\|

*dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇāni setihāsāni tatra yaḥ \|*  
*paṭhennirabhilāṣuḥ sansa vasenmama veśmani \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. If without any personal desire, one reads Dharma Śāstra, Purāṇas and Itihāsas there, one shall stay in my abode.

## \|\| 2.79.62 \|\|

*tiṣṭhediṃdriyacāpalyaṃ yo nivārya kṣaṇaṃ kṛtī \|*  
*nirvāṇamaṃḍapenyatra tena taptaṃ mahattapaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. If one stands in the Nirvāṇamaṇḍapa for a moment with the fickleness of the senses dispelled, he will be blessed as one who has done his duty, whereas elsewhere he has to perform a great penance (to get the same result).

## \|\| 2.79.63 \|\|

*vāyubhakṣaṇatonyatra yatpuṇyaṃ śaradāṃ śatam \|*  
*tatpuṇyaṃ ghaṭikārdhena maunaṃ dakṣiṇamaṃḍape \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. By observing silence for half a Ghaṭikā in the Southern Maṇḍapa, one attāins the same merit as is obtained elsewhere through the austerity of living solely on the intake of wind for a hundred years.

## \|\| 2.79.64 \|\|

*mitaṃ kṛṣṇalakenāpi yodadyānmuktimaṃḍape \|*  
*svarṇaṃ sauvarṇayānena sa tu saṃcarate divi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If in the Muktimaṇḍapa anyone makes a gift of gold, even if it be a Kṛṣṇalaka (i.e. Ratti) in weight, he moves about in heaven in a golden vehicle.

## \|\| 2.79.65 \|\|

*tatraikaṃ jāgaraṃ kuryādyasminkasmindinepi yaḥ \|*  
*upoṣitorcayelliṃgaṃ sa sarvavratapuṇyabhāk \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. A devotee may perform the rite of Jāgaraṇa (‘keeping awake at night’) there on any day after observing fast. Then he should adore the Liṅga. He will attain the merit of having observed all Vratas.

## \|\| 2.79.66 \|\|

*tatra dattvā mahādānaṃ tatra kṛtvā mahāvratam \|*  
*tatrādhītyākhilaṃ vedaṃ cyavate na naro divaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. By making great gifts there, by performing great Vratas there and by learning all the Vedas there, the man does not fall from the heavenly region.

## \|\| 2.79.67 \|\|

*prayāṇaṃ kurvate yasya prāṇā me muktimaṃḍape \|*  
*samāmanupraviṣṭotra tiṣṭhedyāvadahaṃ khalu \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. A man whose vital airs make their exit in my Mukti Maṇḍapa, will enter me and become stationed here as long as I stay here.

## \|\| 2.79.68 \|\|

*jalakrīḍāṃ sadā kuryāṃ jñānavāpyāṃ sahomayā \|*  
*yadaṃbupānamātreṇa jñānaṃ jāyeta nimarlam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. In Jñānavāpī I shall have aquatic sports always along with Umā. Merely by drinking the water thereof, one gets knowledge devoid of impurities.

## \|\| 2.79.69 \|\|

*tajjalakrīḍanasthānaṃ mama prītikaraṃ mahat \|*  
*amuṣminrājasadane jāḍyahṛjjalapūritam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. That spot for aquatic sports is extremely delightful to me. in this royal abode, it is filled with water that dispels sluggishness.

## \|\| 2.79.70 \|\|

*tatprāsādapurobhāge mama śṛṃgāramaṃḍapaḥ \|\| śrī \|*  
*pīṭhaṃ taddhi vijñeyaṃ niḥśrīkaśrīsamarpaṇam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. In front of that palace is my Śṛṅgāramaṇḍapa (Pavilion for enjoyment, elegant dress and makeup etc.). This should be known as Śrī Pīṭha bestowing glory and wealth on those who are devoid of it.

## \|\| 2.79.71-75 \|\|

*madarthaṃ tatra yo dadyāddukūlāni śucīnyaho \|*  
*mālyāni suvicitrāṇi yakṣakardamavaṃti ca \|\| 71 \|\|*

*nānā nepathyavastūni pūjopakaraṇā'nyapi \|*  
*sa śriyālaṃkṛtastiṣṭhedyatra kutrāpi sattamaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*nirvāṇalakṣmīrvṛṇute taṃ nirvāṇapadāptaye \|*  
*yatra kutrāpi nidhanaṃ prāpnuyādapi sa dhruvam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*mokṣalakṣmīvilāsākhya prāsādasyottare mama \|*  
*aiśvaryamaḍapaṃ ramyaṃ tatraiśvaryaṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 74 \|\|*

*matprāsādaiṃdradigbhāge jñānamaṃḍapamasti yat \|*  
*jñānaṃ diśāmi satataṃ tatra māṃ dhyāyatāṃ satām \|\| 75 \|\|*

71-75. A person who makes for my sake gifts of pure silk clothes, garlands of various kinds, together with Yakṣakardama (fragrant ointment prepared with saffron, camphor etc.), ornaments and embellishments of various kinds and the materials required for worship, shall be adorned with glory. Wherever that excellent man may stay, the Glory of Salvation will woo him for accepting the acquisition of the status of salvation. It does not matter where he meets with his death (he will certainly have salvation).

## \|\| 2.79.74 \|\|

*mokṣalakṣmīvilāsākhya prāsādasyottare mama \|*  
*aiśvaryamaḍapaṃ ramyaṃ tatraiśvaryaṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. To the north of the palace called Mokṣalakṣmīvilāsa is the beautiful Aiśvarya Maṇḍapa (Pavilion of opulence and Royal Glory). It is there that I bestow Aiśvarya (opulence).

## \|\| 2.79.75 \|\|

*matprāsādaiṃdradigbhāge jñānamaṃḍapamasti yat \|*  
*jñānaṃ diśāmi satataṃ tatra māṃ dhyāyatāṃ satām \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. To the eastern side of my palace, there is the Jñāna Maṇḍapa. There I grant the (spiritual) knowledge to the good people who meditate on me.

## \|\| 2.79.76 \|\|

*bhavāni rājasadane mamāsti hi mahānasam \|*  
*yattatropahṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ nirviśāmi mudaiva tat \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. In the royal mansion of Bhavānī (?) there is my culinary hall which I enter joyously to accept whatever is offered there, which yields merits (to the donor).

## \|\| 2.79.77 \|\|

*viśālākṣyā mahāsaudhe mama viśrāmabhūmikā \|*  
*tatra saṃsṛtikhinnānāṃ viśrāmaṃ śrāṇayāmyaham \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. My floor of rest (Viśrāmabhūmikā) is the great mansion of Viśālākṣī. There I bestow ultimate rest (salvation) on those who are distressed due to worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.79.78 \|\|

*niyamasnānatīrthaṃ ca cakrapuṣkariṇī mama \|*  
*tatra snānavatāṃ puṃsāṃ tannairmalyaṃ diśāmyaham \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Cakrapuṣkariṇī is the Tīrtha for my regular (midday) bath. To those persons who take their holy bath there, I grant that freedom from impurities (salvation).

## \|\| 2.79.79 \|\|

*yadāhuḥ paramaṃ tattvaṃ yadāhurbrahmasattamam \|*  
*svasaṃvedyaṃ yadāhuśca tattatrāṃte diśāmyaham \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. At the end there, I grant that which they call the supreme truth, that which they mention as the excellent Brahman, that the realization of which emerges from within.

## \|\| 2.79.80 \|\|

*yadāhustārakaṃ jñānaṃ yadāhuratinirmalam \|*  
*svātmārāmaṃ yadāhuśca tattatrāṃte diśāmyaham \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. At the end there, I grant that which they call the knowledge giving redemption, that which they call supremely pure and that which they call that resting within its own soul.

## \|\| 2.79.81 \|\|

*jaganmaṃgalabhūryātra paramā maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*vipāśayāmi tatrāhaṃ karmabhiḥ pāśitānpaśūn \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Here there is the excellent Maṇikarṇikā which is the source of auspiciousness unto the universe. There I redeem from fetters Paśus (ignorant beings) bound by Karmas.

## \|\| 2.79.82 \|\|

*nirvāṇaśrāṇane yatra pātrāpātraṃ na ciṃtaye \|*  
*ānaṃdakānane tanme dānasthānaṃ divāniśam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. In the matter of granting salvation there, I never think whether they deserve it or not. In Ānandakānana that is my place of giving gifts day and night.

## \|\| 2.79.83 \|\|

*bhavāṃbudhau mahāgādhe prāṇinaḥ parimajjataḥ \|*  
*bhūtvaiva karṇadhāroṃte yatra saṃtārayāmyaham \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. To the living beings which get drowned in the most unfathomable ocean of worldly existence I become the sole helmsman and I take them across (the ocean of Saṃsāra).

## \|\| 2.79.84 \|\|

*saubhāgyabhāgyabhūryā vai vikhyātā maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*dadāmi tasyāṃ sarvasvamagrajāyāṃtyajāya vā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Maṇikarṇikā is very famous as the fortunate source of conjugal bliss. There I give everything unto both a Brāhmaṇa and a Śūdra.

## \|\| 2.79.85 \|\|

*mahāsamādhisaṃpannairvedāṃtārtha niṣevibhiḥ \|*  
*duṣprāponyatra yo mokṣaḥ śocyairapi sa labhyate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. In Maṇikarṇikā even pitiable ones attain that salvation which is very difficult to obtain elsewhere even by those who resort to the knowledge of Brahman and those richly endowed with the practice of great Samādhi (i.e. Yoga).

## \|\| 2.79.86 \|\|

*dīkṣito vā divākīrtiḥ paṃḍito vāpyapaṃḍitaḥ \|*  
*tulyo me mokṣadīkṣāyāṃ saṃprāpya maṇikarṇikām \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Whether he be an initiated one or a Cāṇḍāla, whether an erudite scholar or an illiterate fellow, once he comes to Maṇikarṇikā everyone is equal unto me in the matter of granting salvation.

## \|\| 2.79.87 \|\|

*yattyāgenyatra kṛpaṇastatprāpya maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*dadāmi jaṃtumātrāya sarvasvaṃ cirasaṃcitam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. After reaching Maṇikarṇikā I give unto all creatures everything that was accumulated for a long time, the asset of liberation, in granting which I am miserly elsewhere.

## \|\| 2.79.88-89 \|\|

*yadi daivādiha prāptastrisaṃyogo'tidurghaṭaḥ \|*  
*avicāraṃ tadā deyaṃ sarvasvaṃ cirasaṃcitam \|\| 88 \|\|*

*śarīramatha saṃpattiratha sā maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*trisaṃyogoyamaprāpyo devairiṃdrādikairapi \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. If by chance the extremely difficult simultaneous combination of three entities is obtained here, unhesitatingly should one accept the entire thing that had been accumulated for a long time. This simultaneous combination of three viz. physical body, wealth and Maṇikarṇikā, is unobtainable to even Indra and other Devas.

## \|\| 2.79.90 \|\|

*punaḥ punarvicāryeti jaṃtumātrebhya eva ca \|*  
*nirvāṇalakṣmīṃ yacchāmi sadopamaṇikarṇikam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. After considering this again and again I perpetually grant the glory of salvation to all creatures (without any distinction) who approach Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 2.79.91 \|\|

*muktidā na mahī sā me vārāṇasyāṃ mahīyasī \|*  
*tanmahī rajasā sāmyaṃ trilokyapi na codvahet \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. In Vārāṇasī that is the spot for the grant of salvation for me. In all the three worlds there is nothing similar to the dust particles of that spot.

## \|\| 2.79.92 \|\|

*paraṃ liṃgārcanasthānamavimukteśvareśvaram \|*  
*tatra pūjāṃ sakṛtkṛtvā kṛtakṛtyo naro bhavet \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Avimukteśvareśvara is the greatest spot of adoration of the Liṅga. By worshipping it there even once, a man will have the satisfaction of having done his duty.

## \|\| 2.79.93 \|\|

*sāyaṃ pāśupatīṃ saṃdhyāṃ kuryāṃ paśupatīśvare \|*  
*vibhūtidhāraṇāttatra paśupāśairna badhyate \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. I shall perform the evening Sandhyā rite in accordance with Pāśupata cult in the Paśupatīśvara shrine. By applying the holy ash there, a devotee can avoid Paśupāśa (bonds of Paśus, ignorant souls).

## \|\| 2.79.94 \|\|

*prātaḥsadhyākaromyeva sadoṃkāraniketane \|*  
*tatraikāpi kṛtā saṃdhyā sarvapātakakṛṃtanī \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. I am always preforming the early morning Sandhyā rite in Oṃkāraniketana. Even a single Sandhyā rite performed there destroys all sins.

## \|\| 2.79.95 \|\|

*vasāmi kṛttivāsehaṃ sadā prati caturdaśi \|*  
*atra jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā caturdaśyāṃ na garbhabhāk \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Always on every Caturdaśī (fourteenth lunar day) I stay in Kṛttivāsa. A devotee who performs Jāgaraṇa (keeping awake) rite on the Caturdaśī day here is not born in a womb thereafter.

## \|\| 2.79.96 \|\|

*ratneśvarorcito dadyānmahāratnāni bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*ratnaiḥ samarcya talliṃgaṃ strīratnādi labhennaraḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. If devoutly adored, Ratneśvara bestows great gems. A man who adores that Liṅga with gems, shall get the jewel of a woman and such other things.

## \|\| 2.79.97 \|\|

*viṣṭapatritayāṃtaḥsthopyahaṃ liṃge triviṣṭape \|*  
*tiṣṭhāmi satataṃ bhaktamanorathasamṛddhaye \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Though I am stationed in all the three worlds, I abide in the Triviṣṭapa Liṅga always for facilitating the fulfilment of the desires of devotees.

## \|\| 2.79.98 \|\|

*virajaskaṃ mahāpīṭhaṃ tatra saṃsevya mānavaḥ \|*  
*virajā jāyate nūnaṃ caturnada kṛtodakaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. There the man will serve the great Pīṭha called Virajaska. Thereby he definitely becomes free from Rajas quality. He will perform all aquatic rites in Caturnada (i.e. Pilipilā Tīrtha).

## \|\| 2.79.99 \|\|

*mahādeve mahāpīṭhaṃ mama sādhakasiddhidam \|*  
*tatpīṭhadarśanādeva mahāpāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. In the Mahādeva Liṅga my great Pīṭha accords spiritual powers to aspirants. Merely by visiting that Pīṭha one is rid of great sins.

## \|\| 2.79.100 \|\|

*pitṛprītipradaṃ pīṭhaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajasaṃjñakam \|*  
*pitṛtarpaṇakṛttatra pitṝṃstārayati kṣaṇāt \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The Pīṭha entitled Vṛṣabhadhvaja accords delight to the ancestors. One who offers libation to the ancestors there instantly redeems the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 2.79.101 \|\|

*ādikeśavapīṭhehamādikeśavarūpadhṛk \|*  
*śvetadvīpaṃ naye bhaktānvaiṣṇavānativallabhān \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. I assume the form of Ādi Keśava in Ādikeśavapīṭha. I lead all the loving devotees of Viṣṇu to Śvetadvīpa.

## \|\| 2.79.102 \|\|

*tatraiva maṃgalāpīṭhe sarvamaṃgaladāyini \|*  
*upa paṃcanade tīrthe bhaktānsaṃtārayāmyaham \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. There itself near the Pañcanaḍa Tīrtha, in the Maṅgalāpīṭha that bestows all auspiciousness, I redeem the devotees.

## \|\| 2.79.103 \|\|

*biṃdumādhavarūpeṇa yatrāhaṃ vaiṣṇavāñjanān \|*  
*naye paṃcanadasnātāṃstadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. That is the greatest region of Viṣṇu where I lead in the form of Bindumādhava the devotees of Viṣṇu who take their bath in Pañcanada.

## \|\| 2.79.104 \|\|

*paṃcamudre mahāpīṭhe ye vīreśvarasevakāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ paramanirvāṇaṃ kālenālpena jāyate \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Within a short time they attain the greatest salvation—they who serve Vīreśvara in the great Pīṭha called Pañcamudra.

## \|\| 2.79.105 \|\|

*tatra siddheśvarīpīṭhe caṃdreśvara samīpataḥ \|*  
*tatra saṃnidhikartṝṇāṃ siddhiḥ ṣaṇmāsato bhavet \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. There, in the vicinity of Candreśvara in Siddheśvarīpīṭha, spiritual powers can be attained within six months by those who make themselves present there.

## \|\| 2.79.106 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ ca yoginīpīṭhe yogasiddhividhāyini \|*  
*siddhīruccāṭanādyāśca kairna labdhāḥ susādhakaiḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Uccāṭana (magical power of expulsion) and other Siddhis are obtained by many Sādhakas (spiritual practitioners) in Yoginīpīṭha that bestows Yogasiddhi in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.79.107 \|\|

*anekānīha pīṭhāni saṃti kāśyāṃ padepade \|*  
*paraṃ dharmeśapīṭhasya kācicchaktiranuttamā \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. There are many Pīṭhas in Kāśī at every step. But the power of Dharmeśa Pīṭha is something unique and very excellent.

## \|\| 2.79.108 \|\|

*yatrāmī bālakīrāśca nirmalajñānabhājanam \|*  
*āsuḥ sadupadeśānme trātatrāteti bhāṣiṇaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. It is there that these young parrots who were crying, ‘Save, save’ became the receptacles of pure knowledge due to my good advice and instruction.

## \|\| 2.79.109 \|\|

*etaddharmeśvaraṃ pīṭhaṃ tyajāmyadyadināvadhi \|*  
*na kadācittaraṇijatvattapovanamuttamam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. O son of Taraṇi (Sun-god), I shall never leave off your excellent penance-grove from today, nor this Dharmeśvara Pīṭha.

## \|\| 2.79.110 \|\|

*mamānugrahataḥ kīrānetānpaśya raveḥ suta \|*  
*divyavimānamāruhya gaṃtāro matpuraṃ mahat \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. O son of Ravi, see these parrots. They will be going to my great city, with my blessings, seated in a divine aerial chariot.

## \|\| 2.79.111 \|\|

*tatra bhuktvā ciraṃ bhogāñjñānaṃ prāpya mayeritam \|*  
*iha muktimavāpsyaṃti tvatsaṃsargātinirmalāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. There, they will enjoy pleasures for a long time and acquire the knowledge imparted by me. They are extremely pure, due to your contact. They will attain salvation here.”

## \|\| 2.79.112 \|\|

*ityuktavati deveśe kailāsaśikharopamam \|*  
*divyaṃ vimānamāpannaṃ rudrakanyāpariṣkṛtam \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. When the Lord of Devas said thus, a divine aerial chariot comparable to the peak of Kailāsa came there embellished with Rudra-Kanyās.

## \|\| 2.79.113 \|\|

*āruhyate na yānena divyarūpavarāḥ khagāḥ \|*  
*kailāsamabhisaṃjagmurdharmamāpṛcchyate'malāḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Those pure birds assumed divine forms and took leave of Dharma. They then went to Kailāsa, riding in that vehicle.

## Chapter 80 - The Vrata Called Manorathatṛtīyā

## \|\| 2.80.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*kuṃbhodbhūta tadāścaryaṃ vilokya jagadaṃbikā \|*  
*uvāca śaṃbhuṃ praṇatā praṇatārtiharaṃ param \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. O Pot-born One, on seeing that wonderful incident Jagadaṃbikā bowed down to the great Lord Śaṃbhu, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow down and said:

## \|\| 2.80.2 \|\|

*aṃbikovāca \|*  
*asya pīṭhasya māhātmyaṃ mahādeva maheśvara \|*  
*tiraścāmapi yajjātaṃ jñānaṃ saṃsāramocanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Anibikā said:

2\. O great Lord, O Maheśvara, it is the greatness of this Pīṭha that even brutish (non-human) creatures attained knowledge that facilitates release from worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.80.3 \|\|

*ataḥ prabhāvaṃ vijñāya dharmapīṭhasya dhūrjaṭe \|*  
*dharmeśvarasamīpehaṃ sthāsyāmyadya dināvadhi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Therefore, having understood the power of Dharmapīṭha, O Dhūrjaṭi, I shall stay in the vicinity of Dharmeśvara from this day onwards.

## \|\| 2.80.4 \|\|

*atra liṃge tu ye bhaktāḥ striyo vā puruṣāstu vā \|*  
*teṣāmabhīṣṭāṃ saṃsiddhiṃ sādhayiṣyāmyahaṃ sadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I shall always enable the devotees of this Liṅga, be they men or women, to achieve the fulfilment of their desire.

## \|\| 2.80.5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*sādhukṛtaṃ tvayā devi kṛtavatyā parigraham \|*  
*asyeha dharmapīṭhasya manorathakṛtaḥ satām \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

5\. You have done well, O Goddess, in adopting and supporting this Dharmapīṭha that enables good people to realize their desires.

## \|\| 2.80.6 \|\|

*ta eva viśvabhoktāro viśvamānyāsta eva hi \|*  
*ye tvāṃ viśvabhujāmatra pūjayiṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Only they are the enjoyers of all, only they are worthy of being honoured by all, who adore you, O Viśvabhuje, here.

## \|\| 2.80.7 \|\|

*viśve viśvabhuje viśvasthityutpattilayaprade \|*  
*narāstvadarcakāścātra bhaviṣyaṃtyamalātmakāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Viśvabhuje, the bestower (cause) of the origin, sustenance and annihilation of Viśva (the universe), people all over the world who worship you here, will become men of pure souls.

## \|\| 2.80.8 \|\|

*manorathatṛtīyāyāṃ yaste bhaktiṃ vidhāsyati \|*  
*tanmanorathasaṃsiddhirbhavitrī madanugrahāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. If anyone performs devotional rites unto you on the third lunar day (in the bright half of Caitra) called Manoratha Tṛtīyā, whatever he desires will be realized, due to my blessings.

## \|\| 2.80.9 \|\|

*nārī vā puruṣo vātha tvadvratācaraṇātpriye \|*  
*manorathāniha prāpya jñānamaṃte ca lapsyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O beloved, whether it is a woman or a man, the devotee who performs your Vrata realizes all desires and in the end obtains (spiritual) knowledge.

## \|\| 2.80.10 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*manorathatṛtīyāyāṃ vrataṃ kīdṛkkathā katham \|*  
*kiṃ phalaṃ kaiḥ kṛtaṃ nātha kathayaitatkṛpāṃ kuru \|\| 10 \|\|*

Devī said:

10\. O Lord, be pleased to tell this: What sort of Vrata is Manoratha Tṛtīyā? What is the story? What is the benefit? By whom has it been observed?

## \|\| 2.80.11 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi yathā pṛṣṭaṃ bhavatyā bhavatāriṇi \|*  
*manorathavrataṃ caitadguhyādguhyataraṃ param \|\| 11 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

11\. Listen, O Goddess, O redeemer from worldly existence, I shall answer what has been asked by you. This Manoratha Vrata is a greater secret than the greatest one.

## \|\| 2.80.12 \|\|

*pulomatanayā pūrvaṃ tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*kiṃcinmanorathaṃ prāptuṃ na cāpa tapasaḥ phalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Pulomā’s daughter (i.e. Śacī) formerly performed a great penance in order to attain some desire, but she did not get the benefit of the penance.

## \|\| 2.80.13 \|\|

*apūpujattato māṃ sā bhaktyā paramayā mudā \|*  
*gītena sarahasyena kalakaṃṭhīkalena hi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thereupon, she worshipped me joyously with great devotion. She had a sweet melodious voice and she worshipped to the accompaniment of music with the secret (implied) therein.

## \|\| 2.80.14 \|\|

*tadgānenātisaṃtuṣṭo mṛdunā madhureṇa ca \|*  
*sutālena suraṃgeṇa dhātumātrākalāvatā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I was extremely delighted by her song which was soft and sweet; the Tāla (beating the time), the setting, the Dhātu (Tānas), Māna and Kāla were excellent.

## \|\| 2.80.15 \|\|

*provāca tāṃ varaṃ brūhi prasannosmi pulomaje \|*  
*anena ca sugītena tvanayā liṃgapūjayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I said, “O Pulomajā, speak out the boon you wish to have. I am delighted by this excellent song and the adoration of the Liṅga.”

## \|\| 2.80.16 \|\|

*pulomajovāca \|*  
*yadi prasanno deveśa tadā yo me manorathaḥ \|*  
*taṃ pūraya mahādeva mahādevī mahāpriya \|\| 16 \|\|*

Pulomajā said:

16\. If the Lord of Devas is pleased, O Mahādeva, the great beloved of the great goddess, fulfil the desire I do cherish.

## \|\| 2.80.17 \|\|

*sarvadeveṣu yo mānyaḥ sarvadeveṣu suṃdaraḥ \|*  
*yāyajūkeṣu sarveṣu yaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sostu me patiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. May he be my husband, he who is honoured among all Devas, is the most handsome among all the Devas, is the most excellent one among the regular performers of sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.80.18 \|\|

*yathābhilaṣitaṃ rūpaṃ yathābhilaṣitaṃ sukham \|*  
*yathābhilaṣitaṃ cāyuḥ prasanno dehi me bhava \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O Bhava, delighted that you are, grant me beauty as desired, happiness as desired and span of life as desired.

## \|\| 2.80.19 \|\|

*yadāyadā ca patyā me saṃgaḥ syāddhṛtsukhecchayā \|*  
*tadātadā ca taṃ dehaṃ tyaktvānyaṃ dehamāpnuyām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Whenever with a hearty desire for happiness I do have physical contact with my husband, let me have another body after casting off that one.

## \|\| 2.80.20 \|\|

*sadā ca liṃgapūjāyāṃ mama bhaktiranuttamā \|*  
*bhava bhūyādbhavahara jarāmaraṇahāriṇī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Bhava, O destroyer of worldly existence, let my devotion to the adoration of the Liṅga be excellent, removing old age and death.

## \|\| 2.80.21 \|\|

*bharturvyayepi vaidhavyaṃ kṣaṇamātramapīha na \|*  
*mama bhāvi mahādeva pātivratyaṃ ca yātu mā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Even at the departure of the husband, let me not have widowhood even for a moment. O Mahādeva, but my chastity shall not be violated.

## \|\| 2.80.22 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*imaṃ manorathaṃ tasyāḥ paulomyāḥ purasūdanaḥ \|*  
*samākarṇya kṣaṇaṃ smitvā prāheśo vismayānvitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Skanda said:

22\. On hearing this desire of Paulomī, the Lord, the destroyer of Puras, became surprised for a moment. Smilingly he said:

## \|\| 2.80.23 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*pulomakanye yaścaiṣa tvayākāri manorathaḥ \|*  
*lapsyase vratacaryātastatkuruṣva jiteṃdriye \|\| 23 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

23\. O daughter of Pulomā, you will have this desire that you have cherished fulfilled through the observance of a Vrata. Perform it, O lady, with the sense-organs controlled.

## \|\| 2.80.24 \|\|

*manorathatṛtīyāyāścaraṇena bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tatprāptaye vrataṃ vakṣye tadvidhehi yathoditam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It will be fulfilled by the observance of Manorathatṛtīyā. I shall describe the Vrata for the fulfilment thereof. Perform it as recounted.

## \|\| 2.80.25 \|\|

*tena vratena cīrṇena mahāsaubhāgyadena tu \|*  
*avaśyaṃ bhavitā bāle tava caivaṃ manorathaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. If that Vrata which yields great conjugal bliss is performed, O girl, your desire shall definitely be fulfilled.

## \|\| 2.80.26 \|\|

*pulomakanyāvoca \|*  
*kāruṇyavāridhe śaṃbho praṇataprāṇi sarvada \|*  
*kimātmikātha kā śaktiḥ kā pūjyā tatra devatā \|\| 26 \|\|*

Pulomā-Kanyā said:

26\. O Śaṃbhu, O ocean of compassion, O bestower of everything on the living beings who bow down, of what nature is that Vrata? What is its efficacy. What deity has to be invoked there?

## \|\| 2.80.27 \|\|

*kadā ca tadvidhātavyamiti kartavyatā ca kā \|*  
*ityākarṇya śivo vākyaṃ tāṃ tu praṇijagāda ha \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When should it be performed? What is the mode of procedure?

On hearing these words, Śiva spoke to her:

## \|\| 2.80.28 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*manorathatṛtīyāyāṃ vrataṃ paulomi tacchubham \|*  
*pūjyā viśvabhujā gaurī bhujaviṃśatiśālinī \|\| 28 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

28\. O Paulomī, that splendid Vrata is to be observed on Manorathatṛtīyā. Goddess Viśvabhujā Gaurī, having twenty arms, should be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.80.29 \|\|

*varado'bhayahastaśca sākṣasūtraḥ samodakaḥ \|*  
*devyāḥ purastādvratinā pūjya āśāvināyakaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Āśāvināyaka should be worshipped before the goddess by the observer of the Vrata. He is the bestower of boon and grantor of freedom from fear with the gestures of his hand. A rosary and sweetmeat are held in the hands.

## \|\| 2.80.30-35 \|\|

*caitraśukla tṛtīyāyāṃ kṛtvā vai daṃtadhāvanam \|*  
*sāyaṃtanīṃ ca nirvartya nātitṛptyā bhujikriyām \|\| 30 \|\|*

*niyamaṃ ceti gṛhṇīyājjitakrodho jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*saṃtyaktāspṛśya saṃsparśaḥ śucistadgatamānasaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prātarvrataṃ cariṣyāmi mātarviśvabhujenaghe \|*  
*vidhehi tatra sāṃnidhyaṃ manmanorathasiddhaye \|\| 32 \|\|*

*niyamaṃ ceti saṃgṛhya svapedrātrau śubhaṃ smaran \|*  
*prātarutthāya medhāvī vidhāyāvaśyakaṃ vidhim \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śaucamācamanaṃ kṛtvā daṃtakāṣṭhaṃ samādadet \|*  
*aśokavṛkṣasya śubhaṃ sarvaśokaniśātanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*nityaṃtanaṃ ca niṣpādya vidhiṃ vidhividāṃvaraḥ \|*  
*snātvā śuddhāṃbaraḥ sāyaṃ gaurīpūjāṃ samācaret \|\| 35 \|\|*

30-35. On the eve of Caitra Śukla Tṛtīyā, the devotee first cleans his teeth. After the performance of the evening rites (Sandhyā prayers etc.) he should take a meal in moderate quantity, not for full satiation. Controlling anger, curbing the sense-organs, he should be pure, avoiding the touch of those precluded from being touched and keep the mind fixed on the deity. Then he should formally resolve to take up the Vrata: ‘I shall observe the Vrata in the morning, O faultless mother Viśvabhujā. Please do be present there for the fulfilment of my desire.’ After succinctly stating and formally adopting the Vrata, he should go to sleep at night meditating on auspicious things. The sensible devotee should get up early in the morning and go through the essential daily routine. After Śauca purificatory rites like Śauca and Ācamana, he should take up the tooth-brush twig of Aśoka tree which is auspicious and destructive of all grief. The day routine is duly concluded and the excellent devotee conversant with the rules enjoined shall take his bath again the evening. Wearing pure (fresh) clothes, he shall perform the adoration of Gaurī.

## \|\| 2.80.36-39 \|\|

*ādau vināyakaṃ pūjya ghṛtapūrānnivedya ca \|*  
*tatorcayedviśvabhujāmaśokakusumaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*aśokavartinaivedyairdhūpaiścāgurusaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*kuṃkumenānulipyādāvekabhaktaṃ tataścaret \|\| 37 \|\|*

*aśokavartisahitairghṛtapūrairmanoharaiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ caitratṛtīyāyāṃ vyatītāyāṃ pulomaje \|\| 38 \|\|*

*rādhādiphālgunāṃtāsu tṛtīyāsu vrataṃ caret \|*  
*krameṇa daṃtakāṣṭhāni kathayāmi tavānaghe \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. At the outset Vināyaka is to be worshipped with the Naivedya offering of Ghṛtapūra (sweetmeat). Then the devotee worships Viśvabhujā with excellent Aśoka flowers. Aśokavarti (wick of Aśoka twig), Naivedya offerings, incense of agallochum etc. should be offered. The deity is smeared with Kuṃkuma (saffron powder). Ekabhakta (single ball of rice) should be then offered along with Aśokavarti lamp and charming Ghṛtapūras. Thus Caitra Tṛtīyā passes off, O daughter of Pulomā. The devotee should observe the Vrata on all the Tṛtīyās beginning with Vaiśākha and ending with Phālguna. I shall describe the twigs to be used as tooth-brush in the proper order:

## \|\| 2.80.40-42 \|\|

*anulepanavastūni kusumāni tathaiva ca \|*  
*naivedyāni gajāsyasya devyāścāpi śubhavrate \|\| 40 \|\|*

*annāni caikabhaktasya śṛṇutāni phalāptaye \|*  
*jaṃbvapāmārga khadira jātī cūtakadaṃbakam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*plakṣoduṃbarakharjūrī bījapūrī sadāḍimī \|*  
*daṃtakāṣṭha drumā ete vratinaḥ samudāhṛtāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. I shall describe the objects used as unguent and also the flowers. O Girl of auspicious Vratas, I shall describe the Naivedya of Gaṇanāyaka and the goddess. I shall describe the cooked food for Ekabhakta also. Listen to them for the purpose of acquiring the desired benefit. The following twigs are to be used as tooth-brush (in those eleven months in due order): Jaṃbū, Apāmārga, Khadira, Jāti, Cūta, Kadambaka, Plakṣa, Uduṃbara, Kharjūri, Bijapūrī and Dāḍimī. These are the trees from which the tooth-brush twigs should be taken by the persons observing the Vrata.

## \|\| 2.80.43-46 \|\|

*siṃdūrāguru kastūrī caṃdanaṃ raktacaṃdanam \|*  
*gorocanā devadāru padmākṣaṃ ca niśādvayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*prītyānulepanaṃ bāle yakṣakardamasaṃbhavam \|*  
*sarveṣāmapyalābhe ca praśasto yakṣakardamaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kastūrikāyā dvau bhāgau dvau bhāgau kuṃkumasya ca \|*  
*caṃdanasya trayo bhāgāḥ śaśinastveka eva hi \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yakṣakardama ityeṣa samastasuravallabhaḥ \|*  
*anulipyātha kusumairarcayedvacmi tānyapi \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-46. O girl, the unguent shall be as follows: Sindūra (saffron), agallochum, musk, sandal, red sandal, Gorocanā, Devadāru, lotus-seed, turmeric (for two months) and Yakṣakardama. If anyone or all of the previous are not available, then Yakṣakardama is recommended. This Yakṣakardama is a favourite of Devas and is prepared as follows: Take two parts of musk, two parts of saffron, three parts of sandal and one part of camphor. After smearing with the unguent, the devotee should worship with flowers. I shall mention those also.

## \|\| 2.80.47-52 \|\|

*pāṭalā mallikā padma ketakī karavīrakaḥ \|*  
*utpalai rājacaṃpaiśca naṃdyāvartaiśca jātibhiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*kumārībhiḥ karṇikārairalābhetacchadaiḥ saha \|*  
*sugaṃdhibhiḥ prasūnoghaiḥ sarvālābhepi pūjayet \|\| 48 \|\|*

*karaṃbho dadhibhaktaṃ ca sacūtarasamaṃḍakāḥ \|*  
*pheṇikā vaṭakāścaiva pāyasaṃ ca saśarkaram \|\| 49 \|\|*

*samudgaṃ saghṛtaṃ bhaktaṃ kārttike vinivedayet \|*  
*iṃḍerikāśca laḍḍūkā māghe laṃpasikā śubhā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*muṣṭikāḥ śarkarāgarbhāḥ sarpiṣā parisādhitāḥ \|*  
*nivedyāḥ phālgune devyai sārdhaṃ vighnajitā mudā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*nivedayedyadannaṃ hi ekabhaktapi tatsmṛtam \|*  
*anyannivedya saṃmūḍho bhuṃjāno'nyatpatedadhaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

47-52. The flowers are Pāṭalā, Mallikā, Lotus, Ketakī, Karavīra, Lilies, Rājacampa, Nandyāvarta, Jāti, Kumārī and Karṇikāra. If any flower is not available the leaf thereof can be used. If all these flowers are not available, the devotee should worship with some fragrant flowers that he can get.

In the month of Kārttika the following can be joyously offered as Naivedya to the goddess along with Vighneśvara: Karaṃbha (flour mixed with curds), rice mixed with curds, gruel with mango juice, Phaṇikās, Vaṭakas, milk pudding with sugar, rice with green gram and ghee. In the month of Māgha, Inderikā, Laḍḍus, and the splendid Lampasikā should be offered. In the month of Phālguna, Muṣṭikā with sugar within and fried in ghee should be offered as Naivedya. What is offered in ghee should be used for Ekabhakta (single meal). A devotee offering anything else as Naivedya or partaking of the same incurs downfall. He is deluded.

## \|\| 2.80.53-54 \|\|

*pratimāsaṃ tṛtīyāyāmevamārādhya vatsaram \|*  
*vratasaṃpūrtaye kuryātsthaṃḍile'gnisamarcanam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*jātavedasamaṃtreṇa tilājyadraviṇena ca \|*  
*śatamaṣṭādhikaṃ homaṃ kārayedvidhinā vratī \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. The devotee should continue to worship thus for a year, worshipping on the Tṛtīyā of every month. In order to complete the Vrata, the devotee should worship fire on the ground repeating Jātavedasa Mantra and offering gingelly seeds and clarified butter as well as monetary gifts. The devotee performing the Vrata should offer one hundred and eight Āhutis in accordance with the rules.

## \|\| 2.80.55 \|\|

*sadaiva nakte pūjoktā sadā nakte tu bhojanam \|*  
*nakta eva hi homo'yaṃ nakta eva kṣamāpanam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. It is prescribed that the adoration is to be performed in the night always; the meal is taken always at nights. This Homa is also at night and Kṣamāpanā (request for forgiveness) is also at night.

## \|\| 2.80.56-61 \|\|

*gṛhāṇa pūjāṃ me bhaktyā mātarvighnajitā saha \|*  
*namostu te viśvabhuje pūrayāśu manoratham \|\| 56 \|\|*

*namo vighnakṛte tubhyaṃ nama āśāvināyaka \|*  
*tvaṃ viśvabhujayā sārdhaṃ mama dehi manoratham \|\| 57 \|\|*

*etau maṃtrau samuccārya pūjyā gaurīvināyakau \|*  
*vratakṣamāpane deyaḥ paryaṃkastūlikānvitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*upadhānyā samāyukto dīpīdaparṇasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*ācāryaṃ ca sapatnīkaṃ paryaṃka upaveśya ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

*vratī samarcayedvastraiḥ karakarṇavibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*sugaṃdhacaṃdanairmālyairdakṣiṇābhirmudānvitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*dadyātpayasvinīṃ gāṃ ca vratasyaparipūrtaye \|*  
*tathopabhogavastūnicchatropānatkamaṃḍalum \|\| 61 \|\|*

56-61. Gaurī and Vināyaka are to be worshipped with these two Mantras: “O mother accept this devout adoration of mine along with that of Vighneśvara. Obeisance to you; O Viśvabhujā, fulfil my desire quickly. Obeisance to you, O destroyer of obstacles; obeisance, O Āśāvināyaka. You do grant me my desire along with Viśvabhujā.” At the time of concluding the Vrata, the following should be made over as gifts: a cot with cotton mattress, pillow, a doll for holding the lamp and a mirror.

The presiding preceptor and his wife should be made to sit on the cot and the devotee observing the Vrata should joyously honour them with garments, ornaments for the hands and ears, sweet scents, sandal-paste, garlands and monetary gifts. In order to make the Vrata perfect he should also give a milch cow, objects of utility and pleasure, umbrella, footwear and waterpot.

## \|\| 2.80.62-65 \|\|

*manorathatṛtīyāyā vratametanmayā kṛtam \|*  
*nyūnātiriktaṃ saṃpūrṇametadastu bhavadgirā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*ityācāryaṃ samāpṛcchya tathetyuktaśca tena vai \|*  
*āsīmāṃtamanuvrajya dattvānyebhyopi śaktitaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*naktaṃ samācaretpoṣyaiḥ sārdhaṃ suprītamānasaḥ \|*  
*prātaścaturthyāṃ saṃbhojya caturaśca kumārakān \|\| 64 \|\|*

*abhyarcya gaṃdhamālyādyairdvādaśāpi kumārikāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ saṃpūrṇatāṃ yāti vratametatsunirmalam \|\| 65 \|\|*

62-65. The Ācārya should be addressed thus: “This Vrata of Manoratha Tṛtīyā has been performed by me. If it is deficient or redundant, let it be perfectly balanced at your words (of blessings).” Then the devotee takes leave of the preceptor and the latter says, “So be it.” The devotee follows the preceptor till the external boundary (of the village etc.). Gifts are made to others also in accordance with the capacity of the devotee.

The night is spent along with the dependents in good humour. On the Caturthī day in the morning, four boys and twelve virgin girls are (to be) honoured with scented garlands and fed duly. Thus this pure Vrata becomes complete.

## \|\| 2.80.66-68 \|\|

*kāryaṃ manorathāvāptyai sarvairetadvrataṃ śubham \|*  
*patnīṃ manoramāṃ kulyāṃ manovṛttyanusāriṇīm \|\| 66 \|\|*

*tāriṇīṃ duḥkhasaṃsārasāgarasya pativratām \|*  
*kurvannetadvrataṃ varṣaṃ kumāraḥ prāpnuyātsphuṭam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*kumārī patimāpnoti svāḍhyaṃ sarvaguṇādhikam \|*  
*suvāsinī labhetputrānpatyuḥ saukhyamakhaṃḍitam \|\| 68 \|\|*

66-68. For the sake of realizing one’s wishes this excellent Vrata should be performed by all. A bachelor performing this Vrata for a full year will clearly acquire a pleasing wife belonging to a noble family. She will be closely following his mental predilections. She will be chaste and redeem him from the ocean of miserable worldly existence. A virgin will get a husband rich and endowed with all good qualities. An auspicious woman with a living husband will get sons and unobstructed (continuous) happiness of the husband.

## \|\| 2.80.69-70 \|\|

*durbhagā subhagāsyācca dhanāḍhyā syāddaridriṇī \|*  
*vidhavāpi na vaidhavyaṃ punarāpnoti kutracit \|\| 69 \|\|*

*gurviṇī ca śubhaṃ putraṃ labhate sucirāyuṣam \|*  
*brāhmaṇo labhate vidyāṃ sarvasaubhāgyadāyinīm \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. An unfortunate woman will become fortunate; a poor one rich; a widow will never become a widow (in the next birth); a pregnant woman gives birth to a son of long life. A Brāhmaṇa will acquire learning which will confer all luck.

## \|\| 2.80.71 \|\|

*rājyabhraṣṭo labhedrājyaṃ vaiśyo lābhaṃ ca viṃdati \|*  
*ciṃtitaṃ labhate śūdro vratasyāsya niṣevaṇāt \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. By resorting (observing) to this Vrata a dethroned king will regain his kingdom; a Vaiśya acquires profit; a Śūdra attains all that he wished for.

## \|\| 2.80.72 \|\|

*dharmārthī dharmamāpnoti dhanārthī dhanamāpnuyāt \|*  
*kāmī kāmānavāpnoti mokṣārthī mokṣamāpnuyāt \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. A seeker after piety acquires piety; one desirous of wealth will obtain wealth; a lustful man will get all that he loves and a seeker of salvation, salvation.

## \|\| 2.80.73 \|\|

*yo yo manoratho yasya sa taṃ taṃ viṃdate dhruvam \|*  
*manorathatṛtīyāyā vratasya caraṇādvratī \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. By performing the Vrata of Manoratha Tṛtīyā the devotees shall certainly get whatever desire is cherished by them.

## \|\| 2.80.74 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ niśamya śivataḥ śivā saṃtuṣṭamānasā \|*  
*punaḥ papraccha viśveśaṃ prabaddhakarasaṃpuṭā \|\| 74 \|\|*

Skanda said:

74\. On hearing from Śiva thus, Śivā was delighted in her mind. With palms joined in reverence, she asked Viśveśa again:

## \|\| 2.80.75 \|\|

*anyatra ye vrataṃ caitatkariṣyaṃti sadāśiva \|*  
*te kathaṃ pūjayiṣyaṃti māṃ ca āśāvināyakam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. “O Sadāśiva, if the devotees perform this Vrata elsewhere, how will they worship me and Āśāvināyaka?”

## \|\| 2.80.76 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā devi sarvasaṃdehabhedini \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ samarcyā tvaṃ viśve pratyakṣarūpiṇī \|\| 76 \|\|*

Śiva said:

76\. You have asked pertinently, O goddess, who dispel all suspicious. O Viśvā, you are directly visible in Vārāṇasī and as such you should be worshipped there.

## \|\| 2.80.77 \|\|

*āśā vighnajitā sārdhaṃ sarvāśāpūrtikāriṇā \|*  
*hāriṇānaṃtavighnānāṃ mama kṣetra śubhārthinā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. You will be worshipped along with Āśā-Vināyaka who fulfils all hopes and desires, who removes infinite number of obstacles and seeks the auspiciousness of my holy place.

## \|\| 2.80.78-79 \|\|

*kṣipramāgamayitvā ca natvā dūraṃgatānapi \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyānvidhāyātha ciṃtitaiḥ samanorathaiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*anyatra vratibhirviśve kāṃcanīpratimā tava \|*  
*paṃcakṛṣṇalakādūrdhvaṃ kāryā vighnahṛtopi ca \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. Those who perform this Vrata elsewhere should fetch (all concerned persons) quickly, make obeisance to those who are far removed and make them contented with (the realization) of their desires. O Viśvā, they must make images of gold of yours as well as that of Vighneśvara with gold more in weight than five Kṛṣṇalakas (Rattīs).

## \|\| 2.80.80 \|\|

*ācāryāya vratī dadyād vratāṃte pratimā dvayam \|*  
*sakṛtkṛte vratī cāsminkṛtakṛtyo vratī bhavet \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The devotee should make a gift of both the images at the conclusion of the Vrata to the Ācārya. If this Vrata is performed (even) once, the performer of the Vrata shall become blessed and contented.

## \|\| 2.80.81 \|\|

*tataḥ pulomajā devi śrutvaitadvratamuttamam \|*  
*kṛtvā manorathaṃ prāpa yathābhivāṃchitaṃ hṛdi \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Then, O Goddess, after hearing of this excellent Vrata, Pulomajā performed it and realized her desire in the manner she had wished in her heart.

## \|\| 2.80.82 \|\|

*aruṃdhatyā vasiṣṭhopi labdho'tri'nasūyayā \|*  
*sunītyottānapādācca dhruvaḥ prāptoṃ'gajottamaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Vaśiṣṭha was obtained by Arundhatī and Atri by Anasūyā. Dhruva, the most excellent of all sons, was obtained by Sunīti from Uttānapāda.

## \|\| 2.80.83 \|\|

*sunītedurbhargatvaṃ ca punarasmādvratādgatam \|*  
*caturbhujaḥ patiḥ prāptaḥ kṣīranīradhijanmanā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The wretchedness and misery of Sunīti vanished by performing this Vrata again. The four-armed husband was acquired by Goddess Lakṣmī, the daughter of the Ocean of Milk.

## \|\| 2.80.84 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena suśroṇi kṛtaṃyena vrataṃ tvidam \|*  
*vratāni tena sarvāṇi kṛtāni vratinā dhruvam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Why need more be told? O lady of excellent hips, if this Vrata is performed by anyone, it is as though all the Vratas have been performed by him.

## \|\| 2.80.85 \|\|

*śrutvā dhīmānkathāṃ puṇyāṃ punastadgatamānasaḥ \|*  
*śubhabuddhimavāpnoti pāpairapi vimucyate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. A sensible man should listen to this meritorious story with concentration of mind. He attains auspicious intellect and gets rid of all sins.

## Chapter 81 - The Legend of Dharmeśvara

## \|\| 2.81.1 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*dharmatīrthasya māhātmyaṃ kīdṛgdevena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*skaṃda devyai samākhyātaṃ tadākhyāhi kṛpāṃ kuru \|\| 1 \|\|*

Agastya said:

1\. O Skanda, be pleased to tell me how the greatness of the Dharma Tīrtha was narrated by Lord Śaṃbhu to the Goddess. Have mercy on me.

## \|\| 2.81.2 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*viṃdhyonnatihṛdākhyāmi dharmatīrthasamudbhavam \|*  
*ākarṇaya mahāprājña yathā devena bhāṣitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

2\. O subduer of the loftiness of Vindhya, O highly intelligent one, listen. I shall narrate the origin of Dharma Tīrtha as explained by the Lord.

## \|\| 2.81.3 \|\|

*vṛtraṃ nihatya vṛtrārirbrahmahatyāmavāptavān \|*  
*anutaptotha papraccha prāyaścittaṃ purohitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After killing Vṛtra, Indra incurred the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter. Being distressed excessively, he asked his preceptor the mode of expiation (of that sin).

## \|\| 2.81.4 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*yadi tvaṃ devarājemāṃ brahmahatyāṃ sudustyajām \|*  
*apānunutsustadyāhi kāśīṃ viśveśapālitām \|\| 4 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:

4\. O king of Devas, if you are desirous of dispelling this sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter which is usually very difficult to get rid of, go to Kāśī protected by Viśveśa.

## \|\| 2.81.5 \|\|

*nānyatkiṃcitkvaciddṛṣṭaṃ brahmahatyāmahauṣadham \|*  
*rājadhānīṃ parityajya śakra viśveśituḥ parām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O Śakra, except the great capital city of Viśveśa, no other great remedy for the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter is seen anywhere.

## \|\| 2.81.6 \|\|

*bhairavasyāpihastāgrādapatadvaidhasaṃ śiraḥ \|*  
*yatrānaṃdavane tatra vṛtraśatro vraja drutam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O enemy of Vṛtra, go quickly to that place in Ānandavana where the head of Brahmā fell from the tip of the hand of Bhairava.

## \|\| 2.81.7 \|\|

*sīmānamapi saṃprāpya śakrānaṃdavanasya hi \|*  
*brahmahatyā palāyeta vepamānā nirāśrayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Reaching even the outskirts of Ānandavana, O Śakra, Brahma-Hatyā (sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter) shall flee trembling, without anyone to support (her).

## \|\| 2.81.8 \|\|

*anyeṣāmapi pāpānāṃ mahāpāpajuṣāmapi \|*  
*nāśayitrī parā kāśī viśveśa samadhiṣṭhitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Kāśī presided over by Viśveśa, is the great destroyer of other sins also of even great sinners.

## \|\| 2.81.9 \|\|

*mahāpātakato muktiḥ kāśyāme va śatakrato \|*  
*mahāsaṃsārato muktiḥ kāśyāmeva na cānyataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O Śatakratu (Indra, the performer of a hundred sacrifices), it is only in Kāśī that one gets liberated from great sins. It is only in Kāśī that one gets liberation from the great worldly existence, not other places.

## \|\| 2.81.10 \|\|

*nirvāṇanagarī kāśī kāśī sarvāghasaṃghahṛt \|*  
*viśveśituḥ priyā kāśī dyauḥ kāśī sadṛśī nahi \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Kāśī is the city of salvation; Kāśī dispels all sins. Kāśī is very dear to Viśveśa. Even heaven is not like Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.81.11 \|\|

*brahmahatyābhayaṃ yasya yasya saṃsārato bhayam \|*  
*jātucittena na tyājyā kāśikā muktikāśikā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Kāśikā, the illuminator of salvation, should never be abandoned by one who is afraid of the sin of Brahmahatyā or by one who is afraid of the worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.81.12 \|\|

*jaṃtūnāṃ karmabījānāṃ yatra dehavisarjane \|*  
*na jātucitprarohosti haradṛṣṭyāptaśuṣmaṇām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If they cast off their bodies there, the seeds of the Karmas of the creatures do not germinate because they are burnt up by the eye of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.81.13 \|\|

*tāṃ kāśīṃ prāpya vṛtrāre vṛtrahatyāpanuttaye \|*  
*samārādhaya viśveśaṃ viśvamuktipradāyakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O enemy of Vṛtra, for the purpose of dispelling the sin of the slaughter of Vṛtra go to that famous Kāśī and propitiate Viśveśa, the bestower of salvation on all the world.

## \|\| 2.81.14 \|\|

*bṛhaspateriti vaco niśamya sa sahasradṛk \|*  
*āyāddrutataraṃ kāśīṃ mahāpātakaghātukām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On hearing these words of Bṛhaspati, the thousand-eyed Indra came hurriedly to Kāśī, the destroyer of great sins.

## \|\| 2.81.15-16 \|\|

*snātvottaravahāyāṃ ca dharmeśaṃ paritaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*ārādhayanmahādevaṃ brahmadvatyāpa nuttaye \|\| 15 \|\|*

*mahārudrajapāsaktaḥ sutrāmātha trilocanam \|*  
*dadarśa liṃgamadhyasthaṃ svabhāsā dīpitāṃbaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. After taking his bath in the north-flowing river (Gaṅgā) for the purpose of expelling the sin of Brahmahatyā, he went round Dharmeśa and stood worshipping Mahādeva. Sutrāmā (Indra) was engrossed in chanting the Mahārudra Mantra. He saw the Three-eyed Lord stationed in the middle of the Liṅga brightening the atmosphere with his own radiance.

## \|\| 2.81.17 \|\|

*punastuṣṭāva vedoktai rudrasūktairanekadhā \|*  
*viniṣkramya tato liṃgādāvirbhūya bhavovadat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Again he eulogized many times with Rudra Sūkta, as mentioned in the Vedas. Thereupon Bhava came out of the Liṅga, manifested himself and said:

## \|\| 2.81.18 \|\|

*śacīpate prasannosmi varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*kiṃ deyaṃ drutamākhyāhi dharmapīṭhakṛtāspada \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “O husband of Śacī, I am pleased. Choose your boon. O Suvrata (‘one of excellent Vratas’), you have sought refuge in Dharmapīṭha; what should be granted to you? Tell me quickly.”

## \|\| 2.81.19 \|\|

*śrutveti devadevasya sa premavacanaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*sarvajña kiṃte'viditaṃ tamuvāceti vṛtrahā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On hearing these loving words of the Lord of Devas, the Slayer of Vṛtra said thus: “O omniscient one, what is it that is not known to you?”

## \|\| 2.81.20 \|\|

*tatastatkṛpayānunno dharmapīṭhaniṣevaṇāt \|*  
*niṣpādya tīrthaṃ tatreśo'tra snāhīṃdreti cābravīt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Urged by compassion for him, since he served Dharmapīṭha, Īśa created a Tīrtha there and said, “O Indra, take your bath here.”

## \|\| 2.81.21 \|\|

*tatreṃdraḥ snānamātreṇa divyagaṃdho'bhavatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*avāpa ca ruciṃ cāruṃ prāktanīṃ śātayājñikīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. No sooner did Indra take his bath there than he became endowed with divine fragrance. He regained his previous exquisite splendour as the performer of a hundred sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.81.22 \|\|

*tadāścaryamatho dṛṣṭvā munayo nāradādayaḥ \|*  
*parisasnurmudāyuktā dharmatīrthe'ghahāriṇi \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On seeing that miracle, Nārada and other sages joyously took their holy bath in Dharma Tīrtha, the dispeller of sins.

## \|\| 2.81.23 \|\|

*atarpayanpitṝndivyānvyadhuḥ śrāddhāni śraddhayā \|*  
*dharmeśaṃ snāpayāmāsustattīrthāmbubhṛtairghaṭaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. They offered libations to the celestial Pitṛs and performed Śrāddha with great faith. With potfuls of the waters of that Tīrtha they bathed Dharmeśa.

## \|\| 2.81.24 \|\|

*tadā prabhṛti tattīrthaṃ dharmāṃdhuriti viśrutam \|*  
*brahmahatyādi pāpānāmakleśaṃ kṣālanaṃ param \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Ever since then, that Tīrtha became famous by the name Dharmāndhu (Dharma Kūpa). It is the greatest Tīrtha that washes off sins like that of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter without any strain.

## \|\| 2.81.25 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ tīrtharājasya snānena parikīrtyate \|*  
*sahasraguṇitaṃ tatsyāddharmāṃdhu snānamātrataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Merely by taking bath in Dharmāndhu, one gets a thousand times as much benefit as is proclaimed to be the benefit of a bath in Tīrtharāja (Prayāga).

## \|\| 2.81.26 \|\|

*gaṃgādvāre kurukṣetre gaṃgāsāgarasaṃgame \|*  
*yatphalaṃ labhate martyo dharmatīrthe tadāpnuyāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In Dharma Tīrtha one obtains the same benefit as in Gaṅgā Dvāra, Kurukṣetra and in the confluence of Gaṅgā and the ocean.

## \|\| 2.81.27 \|\|

*narmadāyāṃ sarasvatyāṃ gautamyāṃ siṃhage gurau \|*  
*snātvā yatphalamāpyeta dharmakūpe tadāpnuyāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In Dharmakūpa that benefit is obtained which one gets by taking holy dip in Narmadā, in Sarasvatī and in Gautamī (Godāvarī) when Guru (Jupiter) is in the Zodiac Siṃha (Leo).

## \|\| 2.81.28 \|\|

*mānase puṣkare caiva dvārike sāgare tathā \|*  
*tīrthe snātvā phalaṃ yatsyāttatsyāddharmajalāśaye \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In the Dharmajalāśaya, the same benefit is obtained which one gets by taking a holy bath in the Tīrthas of Mānasa, Puṣkara and the ocean around Dvārakā.

## \|\| 2.81.29 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ sūkarakṣetre caitryāṃ gaurīmahāhrade \|*  
*śaṃkhoddhāre haridine yatphalaṃ tatphalaṃ tviha \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Here the benefit is the same as in the holy spot Sūkara on the Kārttikī day, in Gaurī Mahāhrada (in Kedāra) on the Caitrī day and in Śaṅkhoddhāra on the day sacred to Viṣṇu (Ekādaśī day).

## \|\| 2.81.30 \|\|

*tīrthadvayaṃ pratīkṣaṃte sisnāsūnpitaro narān \|*  
*gaṃgāyāṃ dharmakūpe ca piṃḍanirvapaṇāśayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. With the hope of receiving balls of rice, Pitṛs expect men to take their holy dips in the two Tīrthas, viz. Gaṅgā and Dharmakūpa.

## \|\| 2.81.31 \|\|

*pitāmahasamīpe vā dharmeśasyāgratotha vā \|*  
*phalgau ca dharmakūpe ca mādyaṃti prapitāmahāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Great-grandfathers become elated in Phalgu Tīrtha near Pitāmaha, and in Dharmakūpa in front of Dharmeśa.

## \|\| 2.81.32 \|\|

*dharmakūpe naraḥ snātvā paritarpya pitāmahān \|*  
*gayāṃ gatvā kimadhikaṃ kartā pitṛmudāvaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After taking the holy dip in Dharmakūpa and offering the libations to the ancestors, what more can a man expect to do to delight the Pitṛs by going to Gayā?

## \|\| 2.81.33 \|\|

*yathā gayāyāṃ tṛptāḥ syuḥ piṃḍadāne pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*dharmatīrthe tathaiva syurna nyūnaṃ naiva cādhikam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In Dharma Tīrtha too the ancestors become pleased by the offer of balls of rice as in Gayā, to the same extent, neither less nor more.

## \|\| 2.81.34 \|\|

*te dhanyāḥ pitṛbhaktāste prīṇitāstaiḥ pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*paitrādṛṇāddharmatīrthe niṣkṛtiryaiḥ kṛtā sutaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. They are blessed devotees of their Pitṛs; the Pitāmahas are propitiated by them; they are the sons who become free from indebtedness to the Piṭrs in Dharma Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.81.35 \|\|

*tattīrthasya prabhāveṇa niṣpāpobhūtkṣaṇena ca \|*  
*praṇamya devadeveśamiṃdro'gādamarāvatīm \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Due to the power of that Tīrtha Indra became sinless instantly. After bowing down to the Lord of Devas, he went to Amarāvatī.

## \|\| 2.81.36 \|\|

*apāro mahimā tasya dharmatīrthasya kuṃbhaja \|*  
*tatkūpe svaṃ nirīkṣyāpi śrāddhadānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Pot-born One, the greatness of Dharma Tīrtha is unfathomable. Even by seeing one’s own reflection in that Kūpa (holy well) one shall obtain the benefit of the offer of a Śrāddha.

## \|\| 2.81.37 \|\|

*tatrāpi kākiṇī mātraṃ yacchetpitṛmude naraḥ \|*  
*akṣayaṃ phalamāpnoti dharmapīṭhaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A man need make the gift of only a Kākiṇī there for the delight of the Piṭrs. He will have everlasting benefit due to the power of Dharmapīṭha.

## \|\| 2.81.38 \|\|

*tatra yo bhojayedviprānyatinotha tapasvinaḥ \|*  
*sikthe sikthe labhetsotha vājapeyaphalaṃ sphuṭam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If a person feeds Brāhmaṇas, ascetics or sages, he will clearly obtain the benefit of a Vājapeya sacrifice for everyone of the particle of rice (they eat).

## \|\| 2.81.39 \|\|

*prāpyāmarāvatīṃ śakrastato diviṣadāṃ puraḥ \|*  
*dharmapīṭhasya māhātmyaṃ mahatkāśyāmavarṇayat \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After reaching Amarāvatī, Indra extolled in the presence of the heaven-dwellers the greatness of Dharmapīṭha in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.81.40 \|\|

*āgatya punarapyatra śaṃbhorānaṃdakānane \|*  
*munivṛṃdārakaiḥ sārdhaṃ liṃgamasthāpayaddhariḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Again he went to Ānandakānana of Śaṃbhu accompanied by the sages and the Devas and installed a Liṅga there.

## \|\| 2.81.41 \|\|

*tārakeśātpaścimata iṃdreśvaramitīritam \|*  
*tasya saṃdarśanātpuṃsāmaiṃdraloko na dūrataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. This Liṅga is to the west of Tārakeśa and is called Indreśvara. The world of Indra will not be far from men who visit it.

## \|\| 2.81.42 \|\|

*taddakṣiṇe śacīśaśca svayaṃ śacyā pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*śacīśārcanataḥ strīṇāṃ saubhāgyamatulaṃ bhavet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. To the south thereof is Śacīśa installed by Śacī herself. By the worship of Śacīśa women will have unparalleled conjugal bliss.

## \|\| 2.81.43 \|\|

*tatsamīpesti raṃbheśo bahusaukhyasamṛddhidaḥ \|*  
*iṃdreśvarasya parito lokapāleśvaro paraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Near it is Raṃbheśa, the bestower of excessive happiness and great prosperity. All round Indreśvara is another deity Lokapāleśvara.

## \|\| 2.81.44 \|\|

*tadarcanātprasīdaṃti lokapālāḥ samṛddhidāḥ \|*  
*dharmeśātpaścimāśāyāṃ dharaṇīśaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*taddarśanena dhairyaṃ syādrājye rājakulādiṣu \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. By worshipping it the Guardians of the Quarters can be propitiated. They will bestow opulence. To the west of Dharmeśa is Dharaṇīśa. He is glorified much. By visiting him one will have courage in the kingdom, royal household etc.

## \|\| 2.81.45 \|\|

*dharmeśāddakṣiṇe pūjyaṃ tattveśākhyaṃ paraṃ naraiḥ \|*  
*tattvajñānaṃ pravarteta talliṃgasya samarcanāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. To the south of Dharmeśa, the great (Liṅga) named Tattveśa should be worshipped by men. By worshipping that Liṅga the knowledge of truth dawns uninterruptedly.

## \|\| 2.81.46 \|\|

*dharmeśātpūrvadigbhāge vairāgyeśaṃ samarcayet \|*  
*nivṛttiścetasastasya liṃgasya sparśanādapi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The devotee should worship Vairāgyeśa on the eastern side of Dharmeśa. By touching that Liṅga, the mind shall turn away (from worldly inclinations).

## \|\| 2.81.47 \|\|

*jñāneśvaraṃ tathaiśānyāṃ jñānadaṃ sarvadehinām \|*  
*aiśvaryeśamudīcyāṃ ca liṃgāddharmeśvarācchubhāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Jñāneśvara Liṅga to the north-east is the bestower of knowledge on all embodied beings. To the north of the splendid Dharmeśvara Liṅga is Aiśvaryeśa.

## \|\| 2.81.48 \|\|

*taddarśanādbhavennṛṇāmaiśvaryaṃ manasepsitam \|*  
*paṃcavaktrasya rūpāṇi liṃgānyetāni kuṃbhaja \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. By visiting it, men will attain opulence (as) mentally desired. These Liṅgas, O Pot-born One, are the forms of Pañcavaktra (five-faced Lord Śiva) (Dharaṇīśa, Tattveśa, Vairāgyeśa, Jñāneśvara and Aiśvaryeśa).

## \|\| 2.81.49 \|\|

*etānyavaśyaṃ saṃsevya naraḥ prāpnoti śāśvatam \|*  
*anyattatraiva yadvṛttaṃ tadākhyāmi mune śṛṇu \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A man should surely resort to these (Liṅgas). He attains salvation. Another event that happened there itself, I shall narrate. O sage, listen.

## \|\| 2.81.50 \|\|

*yacchrutvāpi naro ghore saṃsārābdhau na majjati \|*  
*kadaṃbaśikharo nāma viṃdhyapādo mahāniha \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On hearing it a man can avoid being drowned in the terrible ocean of worldly existence.

There is a great foot of Mountain Vindhya here named Kadaṃba Śikhara.

## \|\| 2.81.51-52 \|\|

*damasya putrastatrāsīddurdamo nāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*pitaryuparate rājyaṃ saṃprāpyāvijiteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*haretpuraṃdhrīḥ prasabhaṃ paurāṇāṃ kāmamohitaḥ \|*  
*asādhavaḥ priyāstasya sādhavo'priyatāṃ yayuḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. There was a king named Durdama, son of Dama. After the death of his father, he became the king. He had no control over his sense-organs. Overwhelmed with lust he used to abduct young women of the citizens. Intrinsically bad people were his favourites and good people turned enemies.

## \|\| 2.81.53 \|\|

*adaṃḍyāndaṃḍayāṃcakre daṃḍyeṣvāsītparāṅamukhaḥ \|*  
*sadaiva mṛgayāśīlaḥ so'bhūnmṛgayu saṃgataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He punished those who never deserved it. He was not inclined to punish culprits who deserved it. He was in the habit of hunting and was always in the company of hunters.

## \|\| 2.81.54-56 \|\|

*vivāsitāḥ svaviṣayāttena sanmatidāyinaḥ \|*  
*dharmādhikāriṇaḥ śūdrā brāhmaṇāḥ karadīkṛtāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*paradāreṣusaṃtuṣṭaḥ svadāreṣu parāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*ānarca jātucinnaiva devau duḥkhāṃtakāriṇau \|\| 55 \|\|*

*hāriṇau sarvapāpānāṃ sarvavāṃchitadāyinau \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ jagatīsārau śrīkaṃṭhaśrīpatīpatī \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. People who gave him sound advice were banished from the country by him. Śūdras were appointed as judicial authorities and Brāhmaṇas were taxed. He was contented with the wives of others and remained aloof from his legally wedded wives. He never worshipped Śiva and Viṣṇu, the Lords of all, the dispellers of misery and all sins, the bestowers of all desires, the very essence of the whole world.

## \|\| 2.81.57 \|\|

*svaprajāsveka udito dhūmaketurivāparaḥ \|*  
*durdamo nāma bhūpālaḥ kṣayāyā kāṃḍa eva hi \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. In regard to his subjects, the king named Durdama was like another comet rising up suddenly for their utter destruction.

## \|\| 2.81.58 \|\|

*sa kadācinmṛgayubhiḥ pāpardhi vyasanāturaḥ \|*  
*sārdhaṃ viveśāraṇyāni gṛṣṭipṛṣṭhānugo hayī \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Once that king of sinful prosperity, addicted to vices, entered forests along with hunters closely following a boar.

## \|\| 2.81.59 \|\|

*ekākī daivayogena durdamaḥ so'vanīpatiḥ \|*  
*dhanvī turaṃgamāruḍho'viśadānaṃdakānanam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. As luck would have it, that king Durdama riding on a horse and armed with a bow, entered Ānandakānana alone.

## \|\| 2.81.60 \|\|

*sa vilokyātha sarvatra pādapā navakeśinaḥ \|*  
*succhāyāṃśca suvistārāngataśrama ivābhavat \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He saw the trees all round fruitless but they were extensive and had plenty of shade. He felt his fatigue dispelled.

## \|\| 2.81.61 \|\|

*sugaṃdhena suśītena sumadena suvāyunā \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ saṃvījito rājā pallavavyajanaiḥ kujaiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. He was fanned for a moment as though by the trees with the sprouts for the fans through excellent wind, fragrant, cool and gentle.

## \|\| 2.81.62 \|\|

*kevalaṃ mṛgayā jātastatkhedo na vyapāvrajat \|*  
*ājanmajanitaḥ khedo niragāttadvanekṣaṇāt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On seeing that forest, the fatigue (of sin) congenital with him vanished; only the fatigue due to hunting did not subside (completely).

## \|\| 2.81.63 \|\|

*madhye vanaṃ sa cāpaśyatprāsādaṃ cuṃbitāṃbaram \|*  
*mahāratnaśalākānāṃ ramyamekamivākaram \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. In the middle of the forest he saw a palace kissing the sky above. It was the sole beautiful receptacle of great rods of gems and jewels.

## \|\| 2.81.64 \|\|

*athāvaruhya turagātsa bhūpālotivismitaḥ \|*  
*dharmeśamaṃḍapaṃ prāpya svātmānaṃ praśaśaṃsa ha \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. That king was highly surprised. He got down from the horse. On reaching Dharmeśamaṇḍapa he congratulated himself.

## \|\| 2.81.65-68 \|\|

*dhanyosmyahaṃ prasannosmi dhanye medya vilocane \|*  
*dhanyamadyatanaṃ cāharyadapaśyamimāṃ bhuvam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*punarniniṃda cātmānaṃ dharmapīṭha prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*dhiṅmāṃ durjanasaṃsargaṃ tyaktasajjanasaṃgamam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*jaṃtūdvegakaraṃ mūḍhaṃ prajāpīḍanapaṃḍitam \|*  
*paradāraparadravyāpahṛtyāsukhamāninam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*adyayāvanmama gataṃ vṛthājanmālpamedhasa \|*  
*dharmasthānānīdṛśāni yaddṛṣṭāni na kutracit \|\| 68 \|\|*

65-68. ‘I am blessed. I am delighted. My eyes have become blessed today. This very day is blessed since I espied this piece of land.’

Further, due to the power of Dharmapīṭha he cursed himself for his previous association with the wicked people to the exclusion of good people.

## \|\| 2.81.69 \|\|

*evaṃ bahu viniṃdya svaṃ natvā dharmeśvaraṃ vibhum \|*  
*āruhyāśvaṃ yayau rājā durdamo viṣayaṃ svakam \|\| 69 \|\|*

He said: “Fie upon me who have been outraging all creatures, who was an expert in afflicting the subjects harshly, who under delusion, considered myself happy by the abduction of other men’s wives and misappropriation of other men’s wealth!

Till today my life has been utterly futile. I have been deficient in sanity. It is a pity that religious sacred spots like this were not seen anywhere by me before.”

69\. After cursing himself thus very much, he bowed down to Lord Dharmeśvara. King Durdama then mounted his steed and went back to his kingdom.

## \|\| 2.81.70 \|\|

*tatomātyānsamāhūya kramāyātāṃściraṃtanān \|*  
*navīnānparinirvāsya paurāṃścāpi samāhvayat \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Then he invited all the old hereditary ministers dispensing with the services of all new appointees. He invited the citizens too.

## \|\| 2.81.71-73 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāṃścanamaskṛtya tebhyo vṛttīḥ pradāya ca \|*  
*putre rājyaṃ samāropya prajādharme niveśya ca \|\| 71 \|\|*

*paridaṃḍya ca daṃḍārhānsādhūṃśca paritoṣya ca \|*  
*dārānapi parityajya viṣayeṣu parāṅmukhaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*samāgacchadathaikākī kāśīṃ śreyovikāsinīm \|*  
*dharmeśvaraṃ samārādhya kālānnirvāṇamāptavān \|\| 73 \|\|*

71-73. He bowed down to Brāhmaṇas and allotted to them ample means of subsistence. After establishing the subjects on the righteous path, he crowned his son as the king. He punished those who deserved punishment and gave delight to good people. Averse to worldly pleasures, he set aside even his wives and went alone to Kāśī, the city that enhanced welfare. He propitiated Dharmeśvara and in due course attained salvation.

## \|\| 2.81.74 \|\|

*dharmeśadarśanānnityaṃ tathābhūtaḥ sa durdamaḥ \|*  
*babhūva damināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ prāṃte mokṣaṃ ca labdhavān \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. It is due to his visits to Dharmeśvara everyday that the uncontrollable Durdama of such a (bad) nature became the most excellent one among those who controlled their sense-organs and in the end attained salvation.

## \|\| 2.81.75 \|\|

*itthaṃ dharmeśa māhātmyaṃ mayā svalpaṃ nirūpitam \|*  
*dharmapīṭhasya māhātmyaṃ samyakko veda kuṃbhaja \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Thus the greatness of Dharmeśa has been narrated by me in short. O Pot-born One, who can adequately comprehend the greatness of Dharmapīṭha?

## \|\| 2.81.76 \|\|

*idaṃ dharmeśvarākhyānaṃ yaḥ śroṣyati narottamaḥ \|*  
*ājanmasaṃcitātpāpātsa mukto bhavati kṣaṇāt \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. He who listens to this narration of Dharmeśa is the most excellent one among men. He will instantly be rid of sins committed ever since birth.

## \|\| 2.81.77 \|\|

*śrāddhakāle viśeṣeṇa dharmeśākhyānamuttamam \|*  
*śrāvayedbrāhmaṇāndhīmānpitṝṇāṃ tṛptikāraṇam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. A sensible man will get this excellent narration of Dharmeśa recited particularly at the time of Śrāddha among Brāhmanas. It causes satisfaction to the Pitrs.

## \|\| 2.81.78 \|\|

*dharmākhyānamidaṃ śṛṇvannapi dūrasthitaḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*sarvapāparvinirmukto gaṃtāṃte śivamaṃdiram \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. A man of excellent intellect listening to this Dharmākhyāna even from a distance, will be freed from all sins. In the end he will go to the palace of Śiva.

## Chapter 82 - Exploits of Amitrajit

## \|\| 2.82.1 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*vīreśasya maheśāna śrūyate mahimā mahān \|*  
*parāṃ siddhiṃ paropatustatra siddhāḥ paraḥ śatāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:

1\. O Maheśāna, the greatness of Vīreśvara is being heard. Hundreds of persons have performed penances there and have attained great Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.82.2 \|\|

*kathamāvirbhavastasya kāśyāṃ liṃgavarasya tu \|*  
*āśusiddhipradasyeha tanme brūhi jagatpate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. How did that excellent Liṅga manifest there in Kāśī? It is a quick bestower of spiritual powers. O Lord of the universe, narrate this unto me.

## \|\| 2.82.3 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*niśāmaya mahādevi vīreśāvirbhavaṃ param \|*  
*yaṃ śrutvāpi naraḥ puṇyaṃ prāpnoti vipulaṃ śive \|\| 3 \|\|*

Maheśvara said:

3\. Listen, O great goddess, to the great manifestation of Vīreśa, O Śivā, on hearing which a man obtains a lot of merit.

## \|\| 2.82.4 \|\|

*āsīdamitrajinnāma rājā parapuraṃjayaḥ \|*  
*dhārmikaḥ sattvasaṃpannaḥ prajāraṃjanatatparaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There was a king named Amitrajit. He conquered the cities of his enemies. He was endowed with Sattva quality and was very righteous. He was always engaged in delighting his subjects.

## \|\| 2.82.5 \|\|

*yaśodhano vadānyaśca sudhīrbrāhmaṇadaivataḥ \|*  
*sadaivāvabhṛthasnānapariklinna śiroruhaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Fame was his asset; he was liberal in making gifts; he was intelligent and considered Brāhmaṇas as Devas. His hairs always remained wet because he took valedictory baths after the performance of sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.82.6 \|\|

*vinīto nītisaṃpannaḥ kuśalaḥ sarvakarmasu \|*  
*vidyābdhipāradṛśvā ca guṇavānguṇivatsalaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He was polite, versed in statesmanship, expert in all activities. He had mastered all (ocean-like) lores; he possessed good qualities and was a favourite of people of good qualities.

## \|\| 2.82.7 \|\|

*kṛtajño madhurālāpaḥ pāpakarmaparāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*satyavākchaucanilayaḥ svalpavāgvijiteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He was grateful; sweet in speech; averse to all sinful activities; truthful in speech; abode of cleanliness; a man of few words; he subdued his sense-organs.

## \|\| 2.82.8 \|\|

*raṇāṃgaṇe kṛtāṃtābhaḥ saṃkhyāvāṃśca sadojire \|*  
*kāminīkāmakelijño yuvāpi sthavirapriyaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In battlefield he resembled the god of Death in refulgence. In the assembly of the learned he shone as a learned person; he was completely conversant with the amorous sports of lustful women; though young he was a favourite of the aged.

## \|\| 2.82.9 \|\|

*dharmārthaidhitakośaśca samṛddhabalavāhanaḥ \|*  
*subhagaśca surūpaśca sumedhāḥ suprajāśrayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He got his treasury increased for use in pious acts. His armies and vehicles were plenty and well-equipped. He was wise and a refuge unto good subjects.

## \|\| 2.82.10 \|\|

*sthairya dhairya samāpanno deśakālavicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*manyamānaprado nityaṃ sarvadūṣaṇavarjitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He was endowed with steadfastness and courage; clever in the awareness of the proper time and place; he honoured all those worthy of honour always; he was free from faults.

## \|\| 2.82.11 \|\|

*vāsudevāṃghriyugale cetovṛttiṃ nidhāya saḥ \|*  
*cakāra rājyaṃ nirdvaṃdvaṃ viṣvagīti vivarjitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Dedicating his mind and thoughts to the pair of Vāsudeva’s feet, he ruled the kingdom without hostile elements and free from all calamities like too much of rain, absence of rain etc.

## \|\| 2.82.12 \|\|

*alaṃghyaśāsanaḥ śrīmānviṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|*
