*abhunakpracurānbhogānsamaṃtādviṣṇusātkṛtān \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With no one to transgress his command, he enjoyed glory. He was devoted to Viṣṇu and enjoyed pleasures after dedicating them to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.82.13 \|\|

*harerāyatanānyuccaiḥ pratisaudhaṃ padepade \|*  
*tasya rājye samabhavanmahābhāgyanidheḥ śive \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There were many lofty shrines of Viṣṇu in every mansion in the kingdom of that king, the storehouse of great fortune, O Śivā.

## \|\| 2.82.14-22 \|\|

*goviṃdagopagopāla gopījanamanohara \|*  
*gadāpāṇe guṇātīta guṇāḍhya garuḍadhvaja \|\| 14 \|\|*

*keśihṛtkaiṭabhārāte kaṃsāre kamalāpate \|*  
*kṛṣṇakeśava kaṃjākṣa kīnāśa bhayanāśana \|\| 15 \|\|*

*puruṣottama pāpāre puṃḍarīkavilocana \|*  
*pītakauśeyavasana padmanābha parātpara \|\| 16 \|\|*

*janārdana jagannātha jāhnavījalajanmabhūḥ \|*  
*janmināṃ janmaharaṇa jaṃjapūkāghanāśana \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śrīvatsavakṣaḥ śrīkāṃta śrīkara śreyasāṃ nidhe \|*  
*śrīraṃgaśārṅgakodaṃḍa śaure śītāṃśulocana \|\| 18 \|\|*

*daityāre dānavārāte dāmodara duraṃtaka \|*  
*devakīhṛdayānaṃda daṃdaśūkeśvareśaya \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viṣṇo vaikuṃṭhanilaya bāṇāre viṣṭaraśravaḥ \|*  
*viṣvaksena virādhāre vanamālinvanapriya \|\| 20 \|\|*

*trivikramatrilokīśa cakrapāṇe caturbhuja \|*  
*ityādīni pavitrāṇi nāmāni pratimaṃdiram \|\| 21 \|\|*

*strīvṛddhabālagopāla vadanodīritāni tu \|*  
*śrūyate yatrakutrāpi ramyāṇi madhuvidviṣaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

14-22. In every house the sweet names of the Enemy of Madhu were heard uttered by the tongues of women, children, old men and even cowherds, e.g. Govinda, Gopa, Gopāla, Gopī-jana-manohara (fascinating to the cowherdesses), Gadāpāṇi, Guṇātīta (beyond all attributes), Guṇāḍhya, Garuḍadhvaja (Garuḍa-emblemed), Keśihṛt (Killer of Keśi), Kaiṭabhārāti (enemy of Kaiṭabha), Kaṃsāri, Kamalāpati, Kṛṣṇa, Keśava, Kañjākṣa (Lotus-eyed), Kīnāśabhayanāśana (destroyer of the fear of the god of Death), Puruṣottama, Pāpāri, Puṇḍarīkavilocana, Pīta-kauśekavasana (clad in yellow silk), Padmanābha, Parātpara (greater than the greatest), Janārdana, Jagannātha, Jāhnavījalajanmabhūḥ (origin of the water of Gaṅgā), Janmināṃ janma-haraṇa (dispeller of the births of all living beings), Jañjapūkāghanāśana (destroyer of the sins of those who repeatedly utter the names), Śrīvatsavakṣas, Śrīkānta, Śrīkara, Śreyasāṃnidhi, Śrīraṅga, Śārṅgakodaṇḍa, Śauri, Śītāṃśulocana (Moon-eyed), Daityāri, Dānavārāti, Dāmodara, Durantaka (slayer of the wicked), Devakīhṛdayānanda, Dandaśūkeśvareśaya (lying on the couch of Serpent King), Viṣṇu, Vaikuṇṭhanilaya, Bāṇāri, Viṣṭaraśravas (heard in every seat) Viṣvaksena, Virādhāri, Vanamālin, Venapriya, Trivikrama, Trilokīśa, Cakrapāṇi, Caturbhuja etc.

## \|\| 2.82.23-24 \|\|

*surasākānanānyeva vilokyaṃte gṛhegṛhe \|*  
*caritrāṇi vicitrāṇi pavitrāṇyabdhijāpateḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*saudhabhittiṣu dṛśyaṃte citrakṛnnirmitāni tu \|*  
*ṛte harikathāyāstu nānyā vārtā niśamyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. In every house, groves and groves of Surasā (Tulasī) plants alone were seen. The sacred and wonderful activities of the Consort of the Ocean-born Goddess were seen painted in the pictures on the walls of the mansions. No other talk was heard except (that about) the story of Hari.

## \|\| 2.82.25 \|\|

*hariṇā naiva vidhyaṃte harināmāṃśadhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*tasya rājño bhayādvyādhairaraṇyasukhacāriṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Due to the fear of that king, Hariṇas (deer) that happily roamed about in forests were not killed by hunters because they had the name of Hari as a component part of their names.

## \|\| 2.82.26 \|\|

*na matsyā naiva kamaṭhā na varāhāśca kenacit \|*  
*hanyaṃte kvāpi tadbhītyā matsyamāṃsāśināpi vai \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Neither fish, nor tortoises, nor boars were killed by even meat-eaters, because they were afraid of him.

## \|\| 2.82.27 \|\|

*apyuttānaśayāstasya rāṣṭre mitrajitaḥ kvacit \|*  
*stanapānaṃ na kurvaṃti saṃprāpya harivāsaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On Harivāsara (i.e. eleventh lunar day) even sucking children did not drink breast-milk (of their mother) in the kingdom of Amitrajit.

## \|\| 2.82.28 \|\|

*paśavopi tṛṇāhāraṃ parityajya harerdine \|*  
*upoṣaṇaparā jātā anyeṣāṃ kā kathā nṛṇām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On Hari’s day (eleventh lunar day) even animals avoided grazing grass. They were keen in observing fast. What then will be the case of men?

## \|\| 2.82.29 \|\|

*mahāmahotsavaḥ sarvaiḥ puraukobhirvitanyate \|*  
*tasminpraśāsati bhuvaṃ saṃprāpte harivāsare \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. While he was ruling the earth, on Harivāsara great festivals were celebrated by all the citizens.

## \|\| 2.82.30 \|\|

*sa eva daṃḍyo'bhūttasya rājño mitrajitaḥ kṣitau \|*  
*yo viṣṇubhaktirahitaḥ prāṇairapi dhanairapi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Only one devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu became worthy of being punished with death or fine in the country of that King Amitrajit.

## \|\| 2.82.31 \|\|

*aṃtyajā api tadrāṣṭre śaṃkhacakrāṃkadhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya vaiṣṇavīṃ dīkṣāṃ dīkṣitā iva saṃbabhuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In his kingdom even Śūdras were stamped with the marks of conch and discus after initiation into Vaiṣṇava cult. They shone like those initiated in Yajñas etc.

## \|\| 2.82.32 \|\|

*śubhāni yāni karmāṇi kriyaṃte'nudinaṃ janaiḥ \|*  
*vāsudeve samarpyaṃte tāni tairaphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Everyday the auspicious rites performed by the people who never yearned for the benefits thereof, were dedicated to Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 2.82.33 \|\|

*vinā mukuṃdaṃ govidaṃ paramānaṃdamacyutam \|*  
*nānyo japyetamanyeta na bhajyeta janaiḥ kvacit \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Excepting Mukunda, Govinda, Acyuta, Paramānanda (the heightest bliss) no one (other deities) was chanted about, honoured or served by the people.

## \|\| 2.82.34 \|\|

*kṛṣṇa eva paro deva kṛṣṇaeva parāgatiḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇa eva paro baṃdhustasyāsīdavanīpateḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. To that king Kṛṣṇa alone was the greatest Lord; Kṛṣṇa alone was the ultimate goal; Kṛṣṇa alone was the greatest kinsman.

## \|\| 2.82.35 \|\|

*evaṃ tasminmahīpāle rājyaṃ samyakpraśāsati \|*  
*ekadā nāradaḥ śrīmāṃstaṃ didṛkṣuḥ samāyayau \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. While that king was ruling properly the kingdom, once the venerable Nārada came there to see him.

## \|\| 2.82.36 \|\|

*rājñā samarcitaḥ sotha madhuparka vidhānataḥ \|*  
*nārado varṇayāmāsa tamamitrajitaṃ nṛpam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Adored by the king in accordance with the injunctions with (curds mixed honey and water) Madhuparka etc. Nārada extolled that King Amitrajit.

## \|\| 2.82.37 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*dhanyosi kṛtakṛtyosi mānyopyasi divaukasām \|*  
*sarvabhūteṣu goviṃdaṃ paripaśyanviśāṃpate \|\| 37 \|\|*

Nārada said:

37\. Seeing only Govinda in all living beings, O king, you are blessed; you have fulfilled your task; you are worthy of being honoured by the heaven-dwellers.

## \|\| 2.82.38-39 \|\|

*yo veda puruṣo viṣṇuryo yajñapuruṣo hariḥ \|*  
*yoṃtarātmāsya jagataḥ kartā hartāvitā vibhuḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tanmayaṃ paśyato viśvaṃ tava bhūpālasattama \|*  
*darśanaṃ prāpya śubhadaṃ śucitvamagamaṃ param \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. O excellent one among kings, I have attained the greatest purity after seeing you, who see the entire universe pervaded by that Lord who is Vedapuruṣa Viṣṇu, who is Hari the Yajñapuruṣa, who is the immanent soul of this universe, who is the creator, protector and the destroyer of this world.

## \|\| 2.82.40 \|\|

*eka eva hi sārotra saṃsāre kṣaṇabhaṃgure \|*  
*kamalākāṃta pādābja bhaktibhāvo'khilapradaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the worldly existence that is transitory, there is only one thing of great essence, the devotional fervour to the lotuslike feet of the Consort of Kamalā (Goddess Lakṣmī). It is the bestower of everything.

## \|\| 2.82.41 \|\|

*parityajya hi yaḥ sarvaṃ vipṇumekaṃ sadā bhajet \|*  
*sumedhasaṃ bhajaṃte taṃ padārthāḥ sarva eva hi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. All the objects of the world resort to that wise and intelligent one who forsakes everything else and always resorts to Viṣṇu alone.

## \|\| 2.82.42 \|\|

*hṛṣīkeśe hṛṣīkāṇi yasya sthairyaṃ gatānyaho \|*  
*sa eva sthairyamāpnoti brahmāṃḍe'tīva caṃcale \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In the whole Cosmic Egg that is excessively changeable, only he attains steadiness, he whose sense-organs have been firmly attached to Hṛṣīkeśa.

## \|\| 2.82.43 \|\|

*yauvanaṃ dhanamāyuṣyaṃ padminījalabiṃduvat \|*  
*atīva capalaṃ jñātvā'cyutamekaṃ samāśrayet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. One should resort solely to Acyuta after realizing that youth, wealth and life are very fickle like a drop of water on a lotus leaf.

## \|\| 2.82.44 \|\|

*vāci cetasi sarvatra yasya devo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*sa eva sarvadā vaṃdyo nararūpī janārdanaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Only he is always worthy of being saluted whose speech, mind are pervaded by Lord Janārḍana. He is Janārḍana himself in the form of a man.

## \|\| 2.82.45 \|\|

*nirvyāja praṇidhānena śīlayitvā śriyaḥpatim \|*  
*puruṣottamatāṃ ko na prāptavāniha bhūtale \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On this earth who is there who has not attained the state of Puruṣottama (Viṣṇu, the best among men) by meditating on the Consort of Goddess Lakṣmī with sincere Praṇidhāna (deep mental absorption).

## \|\| 2.82.46 \|\|

*anayā viṣṇubhaktyā te saṃtuṣṭeṃdriyamānasaḥ \|*  
*upakartumanā brūyāṃ tanniśāmaya bhūpate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I have become delighted in all the senses and the mind by this devotion to Viṣṇu that you evince. I have decided in mind to help you. O king, listen to what I say.

## \|\| 2.82.47-51 \|\|

*bālā vidyādharasutā nāmnā malayagaṃdhinī \|*  
*krīḍaṃtī piturākroḍe hṛtā kaṃkālaketunā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*kapālaketuputreṇa dānavena balīyasā \|*  
*āgāminyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ tasyāḥ pāṇigrahṛṃ kila \|\| 48 \|\|*

*pātāle caṃpakāvatyāṃ nagaryāṃ sāsti sāṃpratam \|*  
*hāṭakeśātsamāgacchaṃstayā haṃsāśrunetrayā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭaḥ praṇamya vijñapto yathā tacca nithāmaya \|*  
*brahmacārinmuniśreṣṭha gaṃdhamādanaśailataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*bālakrīḍanakāsaktāṃ mohayitvā nināya saḥ \|*  
*kaṃkālaketurdurvṛtto durjayonyāstraghātataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

47-51. The daughter of a Vidyādhara, named Malayagandhinī was playing in the pleasure grove of her father. She was abducted by Kaṅkālaketu, a powerful Dānava and son of Kapālaketu. It is (proclaimed) that the marriage of the girl is to take place on the next Tṛtīyā. She is at present in Campakāvatī, a city in Pātāla. While I was returning from Hāṭakeśa 1 was seen by her with eyes filled with tears. After bowing down to me, she requested thus.” Listen to it, O celibate one, O most excellent one among sages. Kaṅkālaketu, the wicked one, has abducted me from the Gandhamādana Mountain after enchanting me (by his Māyā), as I was absorbed in childish play. He cannot be killed with any other weapon.

## \|\| 2.82.52 \|\|

*svasya triśūlaghātena mriyate nānyathā raṇe \|*  
*jagatparyākulīkṛtya nidrātyatravinirbhayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He is destined to die by the stroke (thrust) of his trident, not otherwise, in battle. (Now) he is fearlessly asleep here, after outraging the whole world.

## \|\| 2.82.55 \|\|

*viṣṇubhakto yuvā dhīmānputri tvāṃ pariṇeṣyati \|*  
*ā tṛtīyā tithi yathā tadvākyaṃ tathyatāṃ vrajet \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If any man who is fully aware of what he does, kills this wicked Dānava by means of the trident given by me and takes me back, it will be conducive to welfare.

## \|\| 2.82.54 \|\|

*yadatropacikīrṣustvaṃ rakṣa māṃ duṣṭadānavāt \|*  
*mamāpi hi varo datto bhagavatyā mahāmune \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If in this matter you are desirous of helping me, save me from the wicked Dānava. O great sage, a boon too has been granted to me by the goddess:

## \|\| 2.82.55-56 \|\|

*viṣṇubhakto yuvā dhīmānputri tvāṃ pariṇeṣyati \|*  
*ā tṛtīyā tithi yathā tadvākyaṃ tathyatāṃ vrajet \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tathā nimittamātraṃ tvaṃ bhava yatnaṃ samācara \|*  
*iti tadvacanādrājanviṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇam \|*  
*yuvānaṃ cāpi dhīmaṃtaṃ tvāmanu prāptavānaham \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. ‘An intelligent young devotee of Viṣṇu, O dear daughter, will marry you by the (next) Tṛtīyā.’ Do something yourself so that this statement (of the goddess) becomes true. You be the main cause alone.” O king, at this instance of that girl, I have come to you, who are an intelligent young man engrossed in devotion to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.82.57 \|\|

*tadgaccha kāryasiddhyai tvaṃ hatvā taṃ duṣṭadānavam \|*  
*ānayāśu mahābāho śubhāṃ malayagaṃdhinīm \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Hence, O king of mighty arms, go for the accomplishment of the task. After killing that wicked Dānava, bring back the splendid (girl) Malayagandhinī quickly.

## \|\| 2.82.58 \|\|

*sā tu vidyādharī jīvedvilokya tvāṃ nareśvara \|*  
*pārvatīvacanādduṣṭaṃ ghātayiṣyatyayatnataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. That Vidyādhara girl will manage to live on seeing you, O king. Without any (extra) effort she will cause the death of the wicked one through you, at the instance of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 2.82.59 \|\|

*iti nāradavākyaṃ sa niśamyāmitrajinnṛpaḥ \|*  
*analpotkaliko jāto vidyādharasutāṃ prati \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. On hearing these words of Nārada, King Amitrajit experienced a thrill raising the hairs on the body in regard to that Vidyādhara girl.

## \|\| 2.82.60 \|\|

*upāyaṃ cāpi papraccha gaṃtuṃ tāṃ caṃpakāvatīm \|*  
*nāradena punaḥ proktaḥ sa rājā girirājaje \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He asked him (the sage) the means to go to Caṃpakāvatī. O Daughter of the Lord of Mountains, that king was thus told by Nārada again.

## \|\| 2.82.61 \|\|

*tūrṇamarṇavamāsādya pūrṇimādivase nṛpa \|*  
*bhavāndrakṣyati potasthaḥ kalpavṛṃdārathasthitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. “On the full-moon day, O king, go quickly to the ocean. Seated on the boat you will see the divine Kalpa tree stationed in a chariot.

## \|\| 2.82.62 \|\|

*tatra divyāṃganā kāciddivyaparyaṃka saṃsthitā \|*  
*vīṇāmādāya gāyaṃtī gāthāṃ gāsyati susvaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. There you will see a celestial lady seated on a divine couch singing in a sweet voice the following Gāthā (verse set to music) holding the Vīṇā.

## \|\| 2.82.63 \|\|

*yatkarmavihitaṃ yena śubhaṃ vātha śubhetaram \|*  
*sa eva bhuṃkte tattathyaṃ vidhisūtraniyaṃtritaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. ‘A Karma, whether good or evil, done by one will certainly get its consequence experienced by the same person guided by the (invisible) thread of fate.’

## \|\| 2.82.64 \|\|

*gāthāmimāṃ sā saṃgīya sarathā sa mahīruhā \|*  
*saparyaṃkā kṣaṇādeva madhye siṃdhuṃ pravekṣyati \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. After singing this Gāthā, she will instantly dive into the deep ocean along with the chariot, tree and conch.

## \|\| 2.82.65 \|\|

*bhavānapyaviśaṃkaṃ ca tataḥ potānmahārṇave \|*  
*tāmanu vrajatu kṣipraṃ yajñavārāhamāstuvan \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Your Highness should unhesitatingly follow her into the great ocean quickly from the boat, eulogizing Yajñavarāha.

## \|\| 2.82.66 \|\|

*tato drakṣyasi pātāle nagarīṃ caṃpakāvatīm \|*  
*mahāmanoharā rājansahitāṃ bālayānayā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Thereafter you will see the beautiful city of Caṃpakāvatī in Pātalā along with that girl, O king.”

## \|\| 2.82.67-68 \|\|

*ityuktvāṃtarhito devi sa caturmukhanaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*rājāpyarṇavamāsādya yathoktaṃ parilakṣya ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

*viveśāṃtaḥsamudraṃ ca nagarīmāsasāda tām \|*  
*sātha vidyādharī bālā netraprāghuṇakī kṛtā \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. After saying thus, O goddess, the son of the Fourfaced Lord (Brahmā) vanished. The king reached the ocean and saw everything as it was described. He entered the ocean and reached that city. The Vidyāddhara girl too became the guest of his eyes (was seen).

## \|\| 2.82.69-71 \|\|

*tena rājñā trijagatī sauṃdaryaśrīrivaikikā \|*  
*pātāladevateyaṃ vā mamanetrotsavāya kim \|\| 69 \|\|*

*niraṇāyi madhudveṣṭrā sraṣṭuḥ sṛṣṭivilakṣaṇā \|*  
*kuhūrāhubhayādeṣā kāṃtiścāṃdramasī kimu \|\| 70 \|\|*

*yoṣidrūpaṃ samāśritya tiṣṭhate'trākuto'bhayā \|*  
*itthaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tāṃ nirvarṇya sa rājāgāttadaṃtikam \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-71. A girl was seen by that king, who appeared to be the sole glory of the beauty of all the three worlds. He thought for a short while: ‘Is this the deity of Pātāla created by Viṣṇu, the enemy of Madhu, for according festivity for my eyes? It is the very splendour of the Moon created completely different from the creation of Brahmā probably due to the fear of Rāhu and the New Moon. She stands here in the guise of a young woman having nothing to fear from anywhere.’ After reflecting thus the king went near her.

## \|\| 2.82.72-75 \|\|

*sā vilokyātha taṃ bālā nitarāṃ madhurākṛtim \|*  
*viśālorasthalatalaṃ pralaṃbatulasīsrajam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*śaṃkhacakrāṃkasubhaga bhujadvayavirājitam \|*  
*harināmākṣarasudhā sudhauta radanāvalim \|\| 73 \|\|*

*bhavānībhaktibījotthaṃ bhūruhaṃ puruṣākṛtim \|*  
*manorathaphalaiḥ pūrṇamāsīddhṛṣṭatanūruhā \|\| 74 \|\|*

*dolāparyaṃkamutsṛjya hrībharā namrakaṃdharā \|*  
*vepathuṃ ca pariṣṭabhya bālā provāca bhūpatim \|\| 75 \|\|*

72-75. The girl, saw that excessively handsome king with broad chest on which a Tulasī garland was seen hanging down. The pair of his excellent arms was marked with the figures of conch and discus. The two rows of his teeth were bright and sparkling as though they had been washed clean by the nectar of the letters constituting the names of Viṣṇu. He himself was like a tree growing out of the seed of the devotion to Bhavānī having the guise of a man and laden with the fruits of cherished desires. On seeing him she experienced horripilation caused by delight. The girl stepped down from the swinging couch with the shoulders stooping down due to bashfulness. Controlling the tremor, she spoke thus to the king:

## \|\| 2.82.76-78 \|\|

*kastvamatra kṛtāṃtasya bhavanaṃ madhurākṛte \|*  
*prāpto me maṃdabhāgyāyāścetovṛttiṃ niruṃdhayan \|\| 76 \|\|*

*yāvannāyāti subhaga sa kaṭhoratarākṛtiḥ \|*  
*atiparyākulīkṛtya trilokīṃ dānavo muhuḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*kaṃkālaketurdurvṛttastvavadhyaḥ parahetibhiḥ \|*  
*tāvadguptaṃ samātiṣṭha śastrāgāreti gahvare \|\| 78 \|\|*

76-78. “O handsome-featured one, who may be you? It appears as though you have entered the very abode of the god of Death. You have upset my mental feelings, ill-fated that I am. The wicked Dānava, Kaṅkālaketu is of hard features. He has frequently outraged the three worlds and he cannot be killed by the weapons of his enemies. O handsome one, as long as he does not come back stand well-concealed in the deep and spacious armoury.

## \|\| 2.82.79-80 \|\|

*na me kanyāvrataṃ bhaṃktuṃ sa samartha umā varāt \|*  
*āgāminyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ paraśvaḥ pāṇipīḍanam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*saṃcikīrṣati duṣṭātmā gatāyurmama śāpataḥ \|*  
*mā tadbhītiṃ kuru yuvaṃstatkāryaṃ bhavitāciram \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. Due to the boon of Umā, he is not competent to violate my modesty as a virgin. The vicious one desires to marry me the day after tomorrow, the next Tṛtīyā. Due to my curse, his life has practically come to an end. O young man, do not be afraid of him. His work will be over ere long.”

## \|\| 2.82.81 \|\|

*vidyādharyeti coktaḥ sa śastrāgāre nigūḍhavat \|*  
*sthito vīro mahābāhurdānavāgamane kṣaṇaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. On being advised thus by the Vidyādhara girl that warrior of mighty arms stayed concealed in the armoury awaiting the arrival of the Dānava.

## \|\| 2.82.82 \|\|

*atha sāyaṃ samāyāto dānavo bhīṣaṇākṛtiḥ \|*  
*triśūlaṃ kalayanpāṇau mṛtyorapi bhayāvaham \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. In the evening that Dānava of terrible features returned wielding in his hand the trident that instilled fear into even the god of Death.

## \|\| 2.82.83 \|\|

*āgatya dānavo raudraḥ pralayāṃbudanisvanaḥ \|*  
*vidyādharīṃ jagādeti madāghūrṇitalocanaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The ferocious Dānava roared on his arrival with his voice resembling the rambling sound of the clouds at the time of universal annihilation. He rolled his eyes in his inebriation and spoke to the Vidyādharī thus:

## \|\| 2.82.84 \|\|

*gṛhāṇemāni ratnāni divyāni varavarṇini \|*  
*kanyātvaṃ ca paraśvaste pāṇigrāhādapaiṣyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. “O lady of excellent complaxion, accept these jewels. With your marriage day after tomorrow, your virginity is coming to an end.

## \|\| 2.82.85-87 \|\|

*dāsīnāmayutaṃ prātardāsyāmi tava suṃdari \|*  
*āsurīṇāṃ surīṇāṃ ca dānavīnāṃ manoharam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*gaṃdharvīṇāṃ narīṇāṃ ca kinnarīṇāṃ śataṃśatam \|*  
*vidyādharīṇāṃ nāgīnāṃ yakṣiṇīnāṃ śatāni ṣaṭ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*rākṣasīnāṃ śatānyaṣṭau śatamapsarasāṃ varam \|*  
*etāste paricāriṇyo bhaviṣyaṃtyamalāśaye \|\| 87 \|\|*

85-87. O fair lady, I shall be giving ten thousand slave girls to you in the morning, all very charming. They are Asurīs, Surīs, Dānavīs (and of other classes). Besides them there will be hundred each of Gandharvīs, Nārīs (human being) and Kinnaris and six hundred each of Vidyādharīs, Nāgīs and Yakṣiṇīs. There will be eight hundred Rakṣasīs and a hundred excellent celestial women. O lady of pure thoughts, these will be your servants.

## \|\| 2.82.88 \|\|

*yāvatsaṃpattisaṃbhāro dikpālānāṃ gṛheṣu vai \|*  
*matparigrahatāṃ prāpya tāvatastvamiheśvarī \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. As my wedded wife here, you will be the owner of the entire assets and possessions of the Guardians of the Quarters in their abodes.

## \|\| 2.82.89-92 \|\|

*divyānbhogānmayā sārdhaṃ bhokṣyase matparigrahāt \|*  
*kadā paraśvo bhavitā yasminvaivāhiko vidhiḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*tvadaṃgasaṃgasaṃsparśa sukhasaṃdoha meduraḥ \|*  
*parāṃ nirvṛtimāpsyāmi paraśvo nikaṭaṃ yadi \|\| 90 \|\|*

*manorathāściraṃ yāvadyaṃ me hṛdi samedhitāḥ \|*  
*tānkṛtārthī kariṣyāmi paraśvastava saṃgamāt \|\| 91 \|\|*

*jitvā devānraṇe sarvāniṃdrādīnmṛgalocane \|*  
*trailokyaiśvaryasaṃpattestvāṃ kariṣyāmi ceśvarīm \|\| 92 \|\|*

89-92. Being married to me, you will enjoy all divine pleasures in my company. Oh, when will the day after tomorrow dawn when the rite of marriage is to take place? It will be full of a series of happiness arising from the intimate contact and touch of your limbs. Day after tomorrow I shall be getting the greatest thrill. It would have been more if the day was nearer. Day after tomorrow I shall be fulfilling all my desires cherished in my heart for a long time. O Fawn-eyed One, I shall make you the sole mistress of all my opulence spread over all the three worlds acquired by me after defeating in battle all the Devas beginning with Indra.”

## \|\| 2.82.93 \|\|

*ādhāyāṃke triśūlaṃ sve suṣvāpeti pralapya saḥ \|*  
*naramāṃsavasāsvāda pramatto vītasādhvasaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. After prattling thus, that demon who was in great intoxication due to the tasting of human flesh and suet, went to sleep without fear, keeping the trident in his own lap.

## \|\| 2.82.94-97 \|\|

*varaṃ smaraṃtī sā gauryā vidyādharakumārikā \|*  
*vijñāya taṃ pramattaṃ ca susuptaṃ cātinirbhayam \|\| 94 \|\|*

*āhūya taṃ naravaraṃ varaṃ sarvāṃgasuṃdaram \|\| \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktikṛtatrāṇaṃ prāṇanātheti jalpya ca \|\| 95 \|\|*

*śūlaṃ tadaṃkādādāya gṛhāṇemaṃ jahi drutam \|*  
*iti triśūlaṃ bālāto bālārkasadṛśadyuti \|\| 96 \|\|*

*samādāya mahābāhuḥ sa tadā mitrajinnṛpaḥ \|*  
*jaharṣa ca jagādoccairbālāyāścābhayaṃ diśan \|\| 97 \|\|*

94-97. Recollecting the boon of Gaurī and observing that the fearless demon was out of his senses and in deep sleep, the Vidyādhara girl called that excellent king exquisitely handsome in every limb and soundly protected by his devotion to Viṣṇu. She even muttered within herself, “Dear Lord.” Taking away the trident from the lap of the demon, she said: “Take this; kill him quickly.” On hearing this, King Amitrajit whose lustre was akin to that of the rising Sun, took the trident from the girl. The king of powerful arms joyously shouted, according freedom from fear to the timid girl.

## \|\| 2.82.98-99 \|\|

*vāmapādaprahāreṇa tamātāḍya sa nirbhayaḥ \|*  
*saṃsmaraṃścakriṇaṃ citte jagadrakṣāmaṇiṃ harim \|\| 98 \|\|*

*jargāda tiṣṭha re duṣṭa kanyādharṣaṇalālasa \|*  
*yudhyasvātra mayā sārdhaṃ na suptaṃ hanmyahaṃ ripum \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. Fearlessly, he kicked the demon with his left foot, remembering within his mind the discus-bearing Hari, the protective jewel of the universe. He said “O wicked flesh-eater, get up. Fight with me you who desire to outrage the modesty of a virgin. You are my enemy but I do not want to kill you while asleep.”

## \|\| 2.82.100-103 \|\|

*iti saṃśrutya saṃbhrāṃta utthāya sa danoḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*triśūlaṃ dehi me kāṃte provāceti muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*koyaṃ mṛtyugṛhaṃ prāptaḥ kasya ruṣṭo'dya cāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*ka āyuṣādya saṃtyakto yaḥ prāpto mama gocaram \|\| 101 \|\|*

*mama pracaṃḍa dordaṃḍa kaṃḍū kaṃḍūyana kṣamaḥ \|*  
*nālpo naroyaṃ bhavitā kiṃ triśūlena suṃdari \|\| 102 \|\|*

*mābhairme kautukaṃ paśya bhakṣyo'yaṃ mama sāṃpratam \|*  
*kālena matto bhītena svayamevopaḍhaukitaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

100-103. On hearing this, that Dānava got up in great excitement and said again and again, “My dear beloved, give me the trident.” He then continued: “Who is this fellow that has entered the abode of death? With whom is the ultimate killer (god of Death) angry? Who has fallen within my vision? This insignificant puny man will not be even competent to scratch my itching powerful arms. O fair lady, of what need then is my trident? Do not be afraid. See my fanciful sport. This fellow will now be my morsel. He has been sent as a present unto me by Kāla (god of Death) himself afraid of me.”

## \|\| 2.82.104 \|\|

*ityuktvā muṣṭighātena tenoccairdanusūnunā \|*  
*hṛdaye nihato rājā śilātikaṭhine drutam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. After saying this, the king was quickly hit in his chest as hard as rock, by the Dānava, with a blow of his fist with full force.

## \|\| 2.82.105 \|\|

*sa cakriṇā kṛtatrāṇaḥ pīḍāmalpīyasīmapi \|*  
*no veda kaṭhinoraskastatkaraṃ pratyutānudat \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The hard-chested king well-protected by the Discusbearing Lord, did not experience even the least pain; on the other hand it pained his (Demon’s) hand.

## \|\| 2.82.106 \|\|

*atha kopavatā rājñā hato vaktre capeṭayā \|*  
*āghūrṇitaśirā bhūmau patitvā punarutthitaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Then hit by the infuriated king with a blow from his outstretched hand on his face, the demon’s head shook. He fell down on the ground but soon got up.

## \|\| 2.82.107 \|\|

*uvāca ca vaco dhairyamavaṣṭabhya mahābalī \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Summoning up courage the excessively powerful demon then said:

## \|\| 2.82.108 \|\|

*dānava uvāca \|*  
*jñātaṃ na tvaṃ manuṣyosi nṛrūpeṇa caturbhujaḥ \|*  
*āyātaśchidramāsādya haṃtuṃ māṃ dānavāṃtakaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

Danava said:

108\. It is known that you are not a human being. You are the Four-armed Slayer of Dānavas, who has come here in the form of a man after getting a loophole, in order to kill me.

## \|\| 2.82.109 \|\|

*ekaṃ vidhehi madhubhidyadi tvaṃ balavānasi \|*  
*vihāyaitanmahacchūlaṃ yudhyasva svāyudhairmayā \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. O Madhubhid (‘Slayer of Madhu’), you (really think you) are powerful. Kindly do this much. Keep aside this great trident and fight with me with your own weapons.

## \|\| 2.82.110 \|\|

*tvayā kapaṭarūpeṇa balinaḥ kaiṭabhādayaḥ \|*  
*na balena hatāḥ saṃkhye hatā evacchalena hi \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Powerful (demons) Kaiṭabha and others were never killed by you in battle through your power. They were deceitfully killed by you in fraudulent disguise.

## \|\| 2.82.111 \|\|

*baliṃ pātālamanayastvaṃ nṛvāmanatāṃ dadhat \|*  
*nṛmṛgatvena bhavatā hiraṇyakaśipurhataḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. You took the form of a human dwarf and sent Bali to Pātāla. Hiraṇyakaśipu was killed by you by assuming the form partly human and partly beastly.

## \|\| 2.82.112 \|\|

*tvayā jaṭilarūpeṇa laṃkeśo vinipātitaḥ \|*  
*gopālaveṣamāsādya kaṃsādyā ghātitāstvayā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The Ruler of Laṅkā was felled down by you in the form of one with matted hairs. Kaṃsa and others were killed by you who had taken the guise of a cowherd.

## \|\| 2.82.113 \|\|

*strīrūpeṇāharastvaṃ tu vipralāpyā surānsudhām \|*  
*yādo rūpeṇa bhavatā śaṃkhādyāni hatā bahu \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. In the form of a woman you cheated the Asuras and took away the Sudhā (divine ambrosia). Śaṅkha and many others were killed by you in the form of aquatic animals.

## \|\| 2.82.114 \|\|

*māyāvināmagragaṇya sarvamarmajñasādhaka \|*  
*na tvattohaṃ bibhemyadya yadi śūlaṃ vihāsyasi \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. O you foremost among Māyāvins (deceivers), O knower of the vulnerable points of everyone, I am not at all afraid of you if only you will leave off this trident.

## \|\| 2.82.115 \|\|

*athavā dainyavacanaḥ kimebhiḥ kātarocitaiḥ \|*  
*na tyakṣyasi triśūlaṃ tvaṃ na tvāṃ jeṣyāmyahaṃ raṇe \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Or, of what avail are these piteous utterances worthy of only cowherds? you will not abandon the trident and I shall not defeat you in the battle.

## \|\| 2.82.116 \|\|

*avaśyameva martavyamadya prātaḥ śarīriṇā \|*  
*tvatkareṇa varaṃ mṛtyurbalenāpicchalena vā \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Indeed this embodied one has to die this morning. Better that it is at your hands, be it through strength or through deceit.

## \|\| 2.82.117 \|\|

*iyaṃ vidyādharī kanyā na mayā dūṣitā satī \|*  
*sākṣācchrīreva maṃtavyā tavārthaṃ rakṣitā mayā \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. This Vidyādharī girl has not been defiled by me. She is chaste. She should be considered to be Goddess Lakṣmī herself, guarded by me for your sake.”

## \|\| 2.82.118 \|\|

*ityuktvā vāmadordaṃḍaprahāreṇātiniṣṭhuram \|*  
*nijaghāna danoḥ sūnustaṃ śiloccayakaṃpinā \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. After saying this, the Dānava hit him with a blow of his left hand that could even shake a big mountain.

## \|\| 2.82.119 \|\|

*nṛpo vakṣaḥ prahāraṃ taṃ viṣahya raṇa mūrddhani \|*  
*lakṣīcakāra tadvakṣastriśūlaṃ tolayankare \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. In the course of the fight the king endured that blow on the chest, but balancing the trident in his hand he aimed at his chest.

## \|\| 2.82.120-122 \|\|

*nijaghāna mahābāhuḥ sa ca prāṇāñjahau kṣaṇāt \|*  
*itthaṃ kaṃkālaketuṃ sa nihatya surakaṃpanam \|\| 120 \|\|*

*vidyādharīṃ prapaśyaṃtīṃ prāha hṛṣṭatanūruhām \|*  
*nāradasya munervākyāttava suśroṇi vāṃchitam \|\| 121 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ mayā kṛtajñe kiṃ karavāṇyadhunā vada \|*  
*śrutveti tasya sā vākyaṃ prāha gaṃbhīracetasaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

120-122. The king of powerful arms hit him and he died instantly. After killing the demon Kaṅkālaketu thus, he spoke to the Vidyādhara girl who was watching with hairs rising up due to delight: “O lady of exquisites hips, at the instance of Sage Nārada I have carried out your desire. O lady who are aware of what has been done, tell me what (more) shall I do now.” On hearing these words of the king of magnanimous mind, she said:

## \|\| 2.82.123 \|\|

*malayagaṃdhinyuvāca \|*  
*athodāramate vīra nija prāṇaiḥ paṇīkṛtām \|*  
*kiṃ māṃ pṛcchasi jīvāto kulakanyā pradūṣitām \|\| 123 \|\|*

Malayagandhinī said:

123\. O liberal-minded hero. O my life-saving medicine, why do you ask me? I have already been bought by you with your own life at stake. I am the undefiled daughter of a noble family.

## \|\| 2.82.124 \|\|

*iti bruvatyāṃ kanyāyāṃ punaḥ svairacaro muniḥ \|*  
*atarkitāgamaḥ prāpto nārado devalokataḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. While the girl was saying so, Sage Nārada habitually roaming about as he pleased came there unexpectedly from the world of gods.

## \|\| 2.82.125 \|\|

*tatastutuṣatustau tu dṛṣṭvā taṃ munisattamam \|*  
*kṛtapraṇāmau muninā pariviśrāṇitāśiṣau \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. On seeing the excellent sage, they two were delighted. They bowed down their heads and were blessed by the sage.

## \|\| 2.82.126 \|\|

*pāṇigraheṇa vidhinā'bhiṣiktau nāradena tu \|*  
*jagmaturnāradādiṣṭa vartmanā kṛtamaṃgalau \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. They were sprinkled (with water) by Nārada after they had gone through the rite of clasping the hands (merrying). After the auspicious rite was over, they went along the path pointed out by Nārada.

## \|\| 2.82.127-128 \|\|

*tayā malayagaṃdhinyā yutaḥ so'mitrajinnṛpaḥ \|*  
*purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ prāpya paurairvihitamaṃgalām \|\| 127 \|\|*

*yadvīkṣaṇādapi naro nārakī naiva jātucit \|*  
*gatimāpnoti medhāvī tāṃ purīmaviśannṛpaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

127-128. Accompanied by Malayagandhinī, King Amitrajit reached the city of Vārāṇasī where auspicious ceremonies had been arranged by the citizens. The king entered that city, the mere sight of which enables wise man to avert the downfall into a hell.

## \|\| 2.82.129 \|\|

*yasyāṃ puryāṃ praveśaṃ na labhaṃte vāsavādayaḥ \|*  
*kaivalyajanayitryāṃ hi tāṃ purīmaviśannṛpaḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. The king entered that city where even Indra and others do not get free access and which causes the attainment of salvation.

## \|\| 2.82.130 \|\|

*api smṛtvā purīṃ yāṃ vai kāśīṃ trailokyakāṃkṣitām \|*  
*na naro lipyate pāpaistāṃ viveśa sa bhūpatiḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130" That king entered the city Kāśī remembering which a man averts the contingency of being contaminated by sins and which is desired by all the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.82.131 \|\|

*yasyāṃ puryāṃ praviṣṭo nā mahadbhirapi pātakaiḥ \|*  
*nābhibhūyeta tāṃ kāśīṃ prāviśatsa viśāṃpatiḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. That Lord of subjects entered that Kāśī, on entering which a man is never assailed by even great sins.

## \|\| 2.82.132 \|\|

*sāpi vidyādharī kāśī samṛddhiṃ vīkṣya dūrataḥ \|*  
*niniṃda svargalokaṃ ca pātālanagarīmapi \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Seeing the glory and opulence of Kāśī from afar, that Vidyādhara girl censured the heavenly world and even the city in Pātāla.

## \|\| 2.82.133 \|\|

*prāpyā mitrajitaṃ kāṃtaṃ tathā hṛṣṭā na sā vadhūḥ \|*  
*yathā dṛṣṭvāpyaho kāśīṃ paramānaṃdaketanam \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. That newly wedded girl was not delighted on getting Amitrajit as her husband as much as when she saw Kāśī, the wonderful abode of the highest bliss.

## \|\| 2.82.134 \|\|

*sā kṛtārthamivātmānaṃ manyamānā manasvinī \|*  
*tena patyā ca kāśyā ca parāṃ nirvṛtimāyayau \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Considering herself blessed, that lady of great mental ability acquired the greatest delight through her husband and (staying in) Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.82.135 \|\|

*sopyamitrajidāsādya patnīṃ malayagaṃdhinīm \|*  
*dharmapradhānaṃ saṃsevya kāmaṃ prāptottamaṃ sukham \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Attaining Malayagandhinī as his wife, King Amitrajit resorted to love with predominance of piety and so obtained the most excellent happiness.

## \|\| 2.82.136 \|\|

*saikadā taṃ patiṃ rājñī viṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇam \|*  
*raho vijñāpayāṃcakre patibhaktā sutārthinī \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. That queen, loyal to her husband and desirous of a son, once sincerely submitted to her husband engrossed in devotion to Lord Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.82.137 \|\|

*rājñyuvāca \|*  
*bhūpābhīṣṭatṛtīyāyāścariṣyāmi mahāvratam \|*  
*yadyanujñā bhavedbhartuḥ putrakāmārthitapradam \|\| 137 \|\|*

The Queen said:

137\. O king, if there is the consent of my husband. I shall take up the great Vrata of Abhīṣṭa Tṛtīyā that fulfils the cherished desire for a son.

## \|\| 2.82.138 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*devyabhīṣṭatṛtīyāyāṃ vrataṃ kīdṛgbhavedvada \|*  
*kā devatā tatra pūjyā vidhānaṃ cāpi kiṃ phalam \|\| 138 \|\|*

The King said:

138\. O queen, tell me. Of what nature is the Vrata of Abhīṣṭa Tṛtīyā? What is the deity to be worshipped therein? What is the benefit of the rite?

## \|\| 2.82.139 \|\|

*nārī patyananujñātā yā vratādi samācaret \|*  
*jīvaṃtī duḥkhinī sā syānmṛtā nirayamṛcchati \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. If a woman, without being permitted by her husband were to perform Vrata etc., she will become miserable if she lives, and will go to hell if she dies.

## \|\| 2.82.140 \|\|

*iti rājñoditā rājñī pravaktumupacakrame \|*  
*iti kartavyatāṃ tasya vratasya sarahasyakām \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. On being requested thus by the king, the queen began to narrate the mode of performing that Vrata along with its secret principle.

## Chapter 83 - Manifestation of Vīreśvara

## \|\| 2.83.1 \|\|

*rājñyuvāca \|*  
*avadhehi dharānātha kathayāmi yathātatham \|*  
*vratasyāsya vidhānaṃ ca phalaṃ cābhīṣṭadevatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Queen said:

1\. O king, pay attention. I shall describe the actual mode of performing this Vrata, its benefit and the desired deity.

## \|\| 2.83.2 \|\|

*purā puraḥ śrīdapatnyāḥ śrīmukhyā brahmasūnunā \|*  
*nāradena sutārthinyā vratametadudīritam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Formerly this Vrata was recounted by Nārada, the son of Brahmā, to Ṛddhi, the wife of Kubera, of glorious countenance who was desirous of a son.

## \|\| 2.83.3 \|\|

*cīrṇaṃ cātha tayā devyā putrobhūnnalakūbaraḥ \|*  
*anyābhirapi bahvībhiḥ putrāḥ prāptā vratāditaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It was duly performed by that goddess and the son Nala Kūbara was born. Due to this Vrata sons have been acquired by many other women too.

## \|\| 2.83.4 \|\|

*vidhināpyatra saṃpūjyā gaurī sarvavidhānavit \|*  
*stanaṃdhayena sahitā dhayatā stanamunmukham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Gaurī conversant with the mode of the rite should be duly worshipped along with the child sucking the breast milk with upturned face.

## \|\| 2.83.5-10 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣa tṛtīyāyāṃ śuklāyāṃ kalaśopari \|*  
*tāmrapātraṃ nidhāyaikaṃ taṃḍulaiḥ paripūritam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*avicchinnaṃ navīnaṃ ca rajanīrāgaraṃjitam \|*  
*vāsaḥ pātropari nyasya sūkṣmātsūkṣmataraṃ param \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tasyopari śubhaṃ padmaṃ raviraśmivikāsitam \|*  
*tatkarṇikāyā upari catuḥsvarṇavinirmitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vidhiṃ saṃpūjayedbhaktyā ratnapaṭṭābaṃrādibhiḥ \|*  
*puṣpairnānāvidhai ramyaiḥ phalairnāraṃgamukhyakaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sugaṃdhaiścaṃdanādyaiśca karpūra mṛganābhibhiḥ \|*  
*paramānnādi naivedyaiḥ pakvānnairbahubhaṃgibhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dhūpairagurumukhyaiśca ramye kusumamaṃḍape \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ viniṃdraiḥ paramotsavaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

5-10. On the third day in the bright half of Mārgaśīrṣa, the devotee places a pot upon which a copper pot is placed. This copper pot is (to be) filled with rice grains. A cloth, new, untorn and coloured with turmeric is to be placed (as a cover) on the copper pot. It will be of very fine texture. A splendid lotus blossomed by the rays of the Sun is placed upon it. An idol of Brahmā made of four gold coins (eighty Rattīs) is placed on the pericarp of the lotus and is adored devoutly with jewels, silk clothes etc., flowers of various kinds, and with sweet fruits such as oranges etc., sandal-paste and other fragrant substances, camphor and musk, Naivedya offerings such as milk pudding etc., and sweetmeats of diverse shapes and sizes and with incense in which Agallochum is prominent. At night the devotee and his people should keep awake in a flower-bedecked pavilion keeping the sleep away performing great festivities.

## \|\| 2.83.11-15 \|\|

*hastamātramite kuṃḍe jātavedasa ityṛcā \|*  
*ghṛtena madhunāplutya juhuyānmaṃtraviddvijaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sahasrakamalānāṃ ca smerāṇāṃ svayameva hi \|*  
*navaprasūtāṃ kapilāṃ suśīlāṃ ca payasvinīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dadyādācāryavaryāya sālaṃkārāṃ salakṣaṇām \|*  
*upoṣya daṃpatī bhaktyā navāṃbaravibhūṣitau \|\| 13 \|\|*

*prātaḥsnātvā caturthyāṃ ca saṃpūjyācāryamādṛtaḥ \|*  
*vastrairābharaṇairmālyairdakṣiṇābhirmudānvitau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sopaskarāṃ ca tāṃ mṛrtimācāryāya nivedayet \|*  
*samuccarannimaṃ maṃtraṃ vratakṛnmithunaṃ mudā \|\| 15 \|\|*

11-15. In the sacrificial pit a Hasta in diameter the Brāhmaṇa conversant with Mantras should consign into the fire full-blown thousand lotuses after soaking them with ghee and honey repeating the Mantra Jātavedase.

He should make the gift of a newly calved, tawny-coloured, well-behaved milch cow to the preceptor, with befitting ornaments. After devoutly observing the fast, the couple will wear fresh clothes.

In the morning of the Caturthī day, the joyous couple should honour the preceptor with clothes, ornaments, garlands and monetary gifts. The idol with all the requisite appurtenances should be given to the Ācārya. The couple observing the Vrata should repeat this Mantra.

## \|\| 2.83.16 \|\|

*namo viśvavidhānajñe vidhe vividhakāriṇi \|*  
*sutaṃ vaṃśakaraṃ dehi tuṣṭāmuṣmādvratācchubhāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “O creative energy! O Goddess conversant with the mode of creation of the universe and creating diverse things! Propitiated by this splendid Vrata, grant us a son who will continue the lineage.”

## \|\| 2.83.17 \|\|

*sahasaṃ bhojayitvātha dvijānāṃ bhaktipūrvakam \|*  
*bhuktaśeṣeṇa cānnena kuryādvai pāraṇaṃ tataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A thousand Brāhmaṇas should be fed with great devotion. (The Vrata-observing couple) should break the fast with the remaining food.

## \|\| 2.83.18 \|\|

*itthametadvrataṃ rājaṃścikīrṣāmi tvayā saha \|*  
*kuru caitatpriyaṃ mahyamabhīṣṭaphalalabdhaye \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O king, it is thus that I wish to observe the Vrata along with you. Do this favour unto me for the sake of the acquisition of the desired benefit.

## \|\| 2.83.19 \|\|

*iti bhūpālavaryeṇa śrutvā saṃhṛṣṭacetasā \|*  
*muneva taṃ samācīrṇaṃ sāṃtarvatnī babhūva ha \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The excellent king heard this with great delight in his mind. O sage, the Vrata was duly observed and she became pregnant.

## \|\| 2.83.20-22 \|\|

*tayātha prārthitā gaurī garbhiṇyā bhaktitoṣitā \|*  
*putraṃ dehi mahāmāye sākṣādviṣṇvaṃśasaṃbhavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*jātamātro vrajetsvargaṃ punagayāti cātra vai \|*  
*bhaktaḥ sadāśive'tyarthaṃ prasiddhaḥ sarvabhūtale \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vinaiva stanyapānena ṣoḍaśābdākṛtiḥ kṣaṇāt \|*  
*evaṃbhūtaḥ suto gauri yathā me syāttathākuru \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Gaurī who was propitiated with devotion was requested by the pregnant woman: “O Mahāmāyā, grant me a son born of a part of Viṣṇu. As soon as he is born, he will go to the heaven and return here. He will be a great devotee of Sadāśiva and become well-known in the entire world.

Without being fed at the breasts, he will instantly be a sixteen year old boy. O Gaurī, make if possible that such a son is born to me.”

## \|\| 2.83.23 \|\|

*mṛḍānyāpi tathetyuktā rājñī bhaktyātituṣṭayā \|*  
*atha kālena tanayaṃ mūlarkṣe sāpyajījanat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The words “So it will be” were uttered by Mṛḍānī who was much pleased with the devotion. In due course she gave birth to the son with the Mūla star at his nativity.

## \|\| 2.83.24 \|\|

*hitairamātyairatha sā vijñaptāriṣṭasaṃsthitā \|*  
*devi rājārthinī cettvaṃ tyaja duṣṭarkṣajaṃ sutam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Even as she lay in the lying-in-chamber she was informed by the ministers, her well-wishers, “O queen, if you seek (the well-being of) the king abandon the son born under the malignant star.”

## \|\| 2.83.25 \|\|

*sā maṃtrivākyamākarṇya kevalaṃ patidevatā \|*  
*atyākṣīttaṃ tathā prāptaṃ tanayaṃ nayakovidā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing the words of the ministers she who considered her husband as her deity and who was wise in following what is expedient, abandoned the son who was acquired in that manner.

## \|\| 2.83.26-30 \|\|

*dhātreyikāṃ samākārya prāhedaṃ sā nṛpāṃganā \|*  
*paṃcamudre mahāpīṭhe vikaṭā nāma mātṛkā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tadagre sthāpayitvāmuṃ bālaṃ dhātreyike vada \|*  
*gauryādattaḥ śiśurasau tavāgre viniveditaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*rājñyā patyuḥ priyeṣiṇyā maṃtrivijñaptinunnayā \|*  
*sāpi rājñyuditaṃ śrutvā śiśuṃ lāsya śaśiprabham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vikaṭāyāḥ puraḥ sthāpya gṛhaṃ dhātreyikā gatā \|*  
*atha sā vikaṭā devī samāhūya ca yoginīḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*uvāca nayata kṣipraṃ śiśuṃ mātṛgaṇāgrataḥ \|*  
*tāsāmājñāṃ ca kuruta rakṣatāmuṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

26-30. She summoned the nurse. The queen spoke this to her, “There is the Mātṛkā deity named Vikaṭā in the great Pañcamudra Mahāpīṭha. Dear nurse, place this child in front of her and submit thus, “This child is granted by Gaurī. He has been placed in front of you by the queen who desires the well-being of the husband and who has been urged by the ministers.” The nurse listened to the speech of the queen. She placed the child, gracefully shining like the moon, in front of Vikaṭā and went home. Then Goddess Vikaṭā summoned the Yoginīs and said, “Take the child immediately before the Mātṛgaṇa (group of Mother-deities) and do as they bid you do. Protect the child with great effort.”

## \|\| 2.83.31-34 \|\|

*yoginyo vikaṭāvākyātkhecaryastāḥ kṣaṇena tam \|*  
*ninyurgaganamārgeṇa brāhmyādyā yatra mātaraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*praṇamya yoginīvṛṃdaṃ taṃ śiśuṃ sūryavarcasam \|*  
*puro nidhāya mātṝṇāṃ provāca vikaṭoditam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*brahmāṇī vaiṣṇavī raudrī vārāhī nārasiṃhikā \|*  
*kaumārī cāpi māheṃdrī cāmuṃḍā caiva caṃḍikā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā taṃ bālakaṃ ramyaṃ vikaṭāpreṣitaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*papracchuryugapaḍḍiṃbhaṃ kaste tātaḥ prasūśca kaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. At the instance of Vikaṭā, the Yoginīs went through the sky and took him to the place where Brāhmī and other Mothers were. The Mothers are Brahmāṇī, Vaiṣṇavī, Raudrī, Vārāhī, Nārasiṃhikā, Kaumāri, Māhendrī, Cāmuṇḍā and Caṇḍikā. The group of Yoginīs bowed down and placed in front of the Mothers that boy who had the lustre of the Sun. On seeing the beautiful boy sent by Vikaṭā, they simultaneously asked the child, “Who is your father? Who is your mother?”

## \|\| 2.83.35-39 \|\|

*mātṛbhiśceti puṣṭaḥ sa yadā kiṃcinna vakti ca \|*  
*tadā tadyoginīcakraṃ prāha mātṛgaṇastviti \|\| 35 \|\|*

*rājyayogyo bhavatyeṣa mahālakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ \|*  
*punastatraiva netavyo yoginyastvavilaṃbitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*paṃcamudrā mahādevī tiṣṭhate yatra kāmyadā \|*  
*yasyāḥ saṃsevanānnṛṇāṃ nirvāṇaśrīradūrataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*sarvatraśubhajanminyāṃ kāśyāṃ muktiḥ padepade \|*  
*tathāpi saviśeṣaṃ hi tatpīṭhaṃ sarvasiddhikṛt \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tatpīṭhasevanādasya ṣoḍaśābdākṛteḥ śiśoḥ \|*  
*siddhirbhavitrī paramā viśveśānugrahātparāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

35-39. On being asked by the Mothers thus he did not say anything. Then the group of Mothers said to the great Yoginīs: “This (boy) is marked with excellent characteristics. He deserves a kingdom. O Yoginīs, he should be taken back to that place without delay, where the great goddess Pañcamudrā, the bestower of desires, stays. By resorting to her the glory of salvation does not remain far away from man.

There is salvation at every step, everywhere in Kāśī, the creator of auspiciousness. Still that Pīṭha is specially the cause of all spiritual powers. By resorting to that Pīṭha and due to the great blessings of Viśveśvara, Siddhi shall accrue to this child having the shape and size of a sixteen-year old boy.”

## \|\| 2.83.40-41 \|\|

*evaṃ mātṛgaṇāśīrbhiryoginībhiḥ kṣaṇena hi \|*  
*prāpito mātṛvākyena paṃcamudrāṃkitaṃ punaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*saṃprāpya tanmahāpīṭhaṃ svargalokādihāgataḥ \|*  
*ānaṃdakānane divyaṃ tatāpa vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Thus with the blessings of the group of Mothers the boy was instantly brought to the Mahāpīṭha marked with the five Mudrās at the instance of the Mothers. Thereafter from the heaven he came here to Ānandakānana and performed an extensive penance of divine quality.

## \|\| 2.83.42 \|\|

*tapasātīva tīvreṇa niścaleṃdriyacetasaḥ \|*  
*tasya rājakumārasya prasannobhūdumādhavaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Umādhava (Lord Śiva) became pleased with the very severe penance of that prince of steady mind and sense-organs.

## \|\| 2.83.43 \|\|

*āvirbabhūva purato liṃgarūpeṇa śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*provāca ca prasannosmi varaṃ brūhi nṛpāṃgaja \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Śaṅkara manifested himself to him in the form of a Liṅga and said, “I am pleased, O son of a king; speak out the boon (you will have).”

## \|\| 2.83.44-45 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*sarvajyotirmayaṃ liṃgaṃ purato vīkṣya vāṅmayam \|*  
*saptapātālamudbhidya sthitaṃ bṛhadanugrahāta \|\| 44 \|\|*

*praṇamya daṃḍavadbhūmau parituṣṭāva dhūrjaṭim \|*  
*sūktairjanmāṃtarābhyastaiḥ suhṛṣṭo rudradevataiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

Skanda said:

44-45. Seeing the Liṅga consisting of speech (Vedas) with all rediance \[radiance?\], standing before him penetrating through the seven nether worlds, due to the blessing of the Supreme Almighty, he bowed down lying on the ground like a log of wood and eulogized Dhūrjaṭi joyously through the Sūktas (hymns) with Rudra as their deity—the Sūktas he had repeatedly practised in the previous birth.

## \|\| 2.83.46 \|\|

*tataḥ prasanno bhagavāndevadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭastapasā tasya provāca vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then Lord Maheśvara, the bull-emblemed Lord of Devas became pleased with his penance and said:

## \|\| 2.83.47 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*varaṃ varaya saṃtapta tapasā kleśitaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*tvayedaṃ bālavapuṣā vaśīkṛtaṃ mano mama \|\| 47 \|\|*

Devadeva said:

47\. Choose a boon. By means of the penance performed by you, your tender body has been subjected to pain by you though still a boy in body. My mind has been captivated hence.

## \|\| 2.83.48 \|\|

*śivoktaṃ ca samākarṇya varadānaṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ ca prārthayāṃcakre parihṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On hearing the repeated speech of Śiva urging him to accept the gift of a boon, he became delighted experiencing horripilation. He requested for the boon.

## \|\| 2.83.49-52 \|\|

*kumāra uvāca \|*  
*devadevamahādeva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*tadatra bhavatā stheyaṃ bhavatāpahṛtā sadā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*asmiṃlliṃge sthitaḥ śaṃbho kuru bhaktasamīhitam \|*  
*vinā mudrādikaraṇaṃ maṃtreṇāpi vinā vibho \|\| 50 \|\|*

*diśa siddhiṃ parāmatra darśanātsparśanānnateḥ \|*  
*asya liṃgasya ye bhaktā manovākkāyakarmabhiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*sadaivānugrahasteṣu kartavyo vara eṣa me \|*  
*iti tadvratamākarṇya liṃgarūpovadatprabhuḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Kumāra said:

49-52. O Mahādeva, O Lord of Devas, if a boon has to be granted to me, Your Lordship shall stay here always alleviating the distress due to the worldly existence. O Śaṃbhu, do favour the devotees by granting what they desire, even as you are stationed in this Liṅga. They will get their desires realized even without showing the ritualistic Mudrās etc. O Lord, you grant the great Siddhi to those who merely visit, touch and bow even without chanting the Mantras. You must bless always those who are devoted to this Liṅga mentally, verbally and physically. This is my boon.

## \|\| 2.83.53-55 \|\|

*evamastu yaduktaṃ te vīravaiṣṇava sūnunā \|*  
*janeturviṣṇubhaktācca rājño'mitrajjito bhavān \|\| 53 \|\|*

*viṣṇvaṃśa evamutpanno mama bhaktiparāṃgaja \|*  
*vīravīreśvaraṃ nāma liṃgametattvadākhyayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*kāśyāṃ dāsyatyabhīṣṭāni bhaktānāṃ ciṃtitānyaho \|*  
*asmiṃlliṃge sadā vīra sthāsyāmyadyadināvadhi \|\| 55 \|\|*

On hearing about the boon he wished to have the Lord in the form of the Liṅga said:

53-55. “O Vīra, let what you, the son of a devotee of Viṣṇu, said, be real. Since your father King Amitrajit is a devotee of Viṣṇu, you are born with a part of Viṣṇu. You are son of one who is engrossed in devotion to me also. After your name this Liṅga will be known, O Vīra, as Vīreśvara Liṅga. At Kāśī it will bestow the cherished desires of the devotees, nay all that they think of. From today, O Vīra, I shall stay in this Liṅga always.

## \|\| 2.83.56 \|\|

*dāsyāmi ca parāṃ siddhimāśritebhyo na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ na mahimānaṃ me kalau kaścicca vetsyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Undoubtedly I shall grant great Siddhi unto those who resort to me. But no one will understand my greatness in the Kali age.

## \|\| 2.83.57-59 \|\|

*yastu vetsyati bhāgyena sa parāṃ siddhimāpsyati \|*  
*atra japtaṃ hutaṃ dattaṃ stutamarcitameva vā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*jīrṇoddhārādikaraṇamakṣayyaphalahetukam \|*  
*tvaṃ tu rājyaṃ paraṃ prāpya sarvabhūpāladurlabham \|\| 58 \|\|*

*bhuktvā bhogāṃśca vipulānaṃte siddhimavāpsyasi \|*  
*purī vārāṇasī ramyā sarvasmiñjagatītale \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. He who understands fortunately, will obtain the great Siddhi. Whatever Japa is performed, Homa is offered gifts are donated and deities adored and pious works such as renovation of dilapidated shrines etc. done, all these cause everlasting benefit.

As for you, you will attain the kingdom inaccessible to all other kings, enjoy pleasures of unlimited extent and in the end will attain Siddhi.

The city of Vārāṇasī is the most beautiful one in the entire world.

## \|\| 2.83.60-64 \|\|

*puṇyastatrāpi saṃbhedaḥ saritorasi gaṃgayoḥ \|*  
*tato'pi ca hayagrīvaṃ tīrthaṃ caivāti puṇyadam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*yatra viṣṇurhayagrīvo bhaktaciṃtitamarpayet \|*  
*hayagrīvācca vai tīrthādgajatīrthaṃ viśiṣyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

*yatra vai snānamātreṇa gajadānaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*kokāvarāhatīrthaṃ ca puṇyadaṃ gajatīrthataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*kokāvarāhamabhyarcya tatra no janmabhāgjanaḥ \|*  
*api kokāvarāhācca dilīpeśvarasannidhau \|\| 63 \|\|*

*dilīpatīrthaṃ suśreṣṭhaṃ sadyaḥ pāpaharaṃ param \|*  
*tataḥ sagaratīrthaṃ ca sagareśa samīpataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

60-64. There, the confluence of the rivers Asi and Gaṅgā is meritorious. Above that the Hayagrīva Tīrtha is more meritorious. It is here that Viṣṇu in the form of the horse-necked god accords what the devotees yearn for. Gaja Tīrtha is better than Hayagrīva-Tīrtha. It is here that one obtains the benefit of the gift of elephants, merely by taking a holy bath.

Kokāvarāha Tīrtha is more meritorious than Gaja Tīrtha. By worshipping Kokāvarāha people will cease to take births.

Dilīpa Tīrtha in the vicinity of Dilīpeśvara is more excellent than Kokāvarāha. It dispels sins immediately. More than this is the Sagaratīrtha in the vicinity of Sagareśa.

## \|\| 2.83.65-69 \|\|

*yatra majjannaro majjenna bhūyo duḥkhasāgare \|*  
*saptasāgaratīrthaṃ ca śubhaṃ sagaratīrthataḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*saptābdhisnānajaṃ puṇyaṃ yatra snātvā naro labhet \|*  
*mahodadhīti vikhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ saptābdhitīrthataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*sakṛdyatrāpluto dhīmāndahedaghamahodadhim \|*  
*cauratīrthaṃ tataḥ puṇyaṃ kapileśvara sannidhau \|\| 67 \|\|*

*pāpaṃ suvarṇacauryādi yatra snātvā kṣayaṃ vrajet \|*  
*haṃsatīrtha tatopīḍyaṃ kedāreśvara sannidhau \|\| 68 \|\|*

*haṃsa svarūpī yatrāhaṃ nayāmi brahmadehinaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

65-69. By getting himself immersed therein, a man averts getting immersed further in the ocean of misery. More auspicious than Sagara Tīrtha is the Saptasāgara Tīrtha, by taking the holy dip where a man attains the merit of taking the holy bath in all the seven seas. Better than Saptābdhitīrtha is the Tīrtha well-known as Mahodadhi. An intelligent man who takes his holy bath there at least once, burns the great ocean of sins. More meritorious than this is the Caura Tīrtha in the vicinity of Kapileśvara. Sins of stealing gold etc. shall perish by taking a holy bath there. Haṃsa Tīrtha in the vicinity of Kedāreśvara is more worthy of adoration. There I lead the embodied beings to Brahman in the form of a Haṃsa (Swan).

## \|\| 2.83.70 \|\|

*tatastribhuvanākhyasya keśavasyāti puṇyadam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ yatrāplutā martyā martyalokaṃ viśaṃti na \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Beyond that is the highly meritorious Tīrtha of Tribhuvana-Keśava. Men who take bath there do not enter the mortal world.

## \|\| 2.83.71 \|\|

*govyāghre śvara tīrthaṃ ca tatopyadhikameva hi \|*  
*svabhāvavairamutsṛjya yatrobhau siddhimāpatuḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. More than that is the Govyāghreśvara Tīrtha where both of them (Cow and Tiger) attained Siddhi by eschewing their natural enmity.

## \|\| 2.83.72 \|\|

*tatopi hi varaṃ vīra tīrthaṃ māṃdhātusaṃjñitam \|*  
*cakravartipadaṃ yatra prāptaṃ tena mahībhujā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O Vīra, more excellent than this is the holy spot named Māndhātṛ Tīrtha where that king (i.e. Māndhātā) attained the position of an Emperor.

## \|\| 2.83.73 \|\|

*tatopi mucukuṃdākhyaṃ tīrthaṃ cātīva puṇyadam \|*  
*yatra snāto naro jātu ripubhirnābhibhūyate \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. More meritorious than this is the Mucukunda Tīrtha. A man who takes his holy bath there is never attacked by enemies.

## \|\| 2.83.74 \|\|

*pṛthu tīrthaṃ tatopyuccaiḥ śreyasāṃ sādhanaṃ param \|*  
*pṛthvīśvaraṃ yatra dṛṣṭvā naraḥ pṛthvīpatirbhavet \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Pṛthu Tīrtha is a greater and higher means of all welfare than that. A man who visit Pṛthvīśvara there, will become Lord of the earth.

## \|\| 2.83.75 \|\|

*tataḥ paraśurāmasya tīrthaṃ cātīva siddhidam \|*  
*yatra kṣatravadhātpāpājjāmadagnyo vimuktavān \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. More than that is the highly Siddhi-bestowing Tīrtha of Paraśurāma, where the son of Jamadagni became liberated from the sin of killing Kṣatriyas.

## \|\| 2.83.76 \|\|

*adyāpi kṣatravadhajaṃ pāpaṃ tatra praṇaśyati \|*  
*ekena snānamātreṇa jñānājñānakṛtena ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Even today a sin due to the murder of a Kṣatriya perishes by means of a single bath performed knowingly or unknowingly.

## \|\| 2.83.77 \|\|

*tatopi śreyasāṃ kartṛ tīrthaṃ kṛṣṇāgrajasya hi \|*  
*yatra sūtavadhātpāpādbaladevo vimuktavān \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. A Tīrtha that causes welfare better than that is indeed that of Kṛṣṇa’s elder brother, where Baladeva became liberated from the sin of murdering a Sùta (narrator of Purāṇas, Romaharṣaṇa).

## \|\| 2.83.78 \|\|

*divodāsasya vai tīrthaṃ tatra rājño'timedhasaḥ \|*  
*tatra snāto naro jātu na jñānāccyavateṃ'tataḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The Tīrtha of King Divodāsa of excellent intellect, is also there. A man who bathes there at any time does not slip from knowledge till the end.

## \|\| 2.83.79 \|\|

*tatopi hi mahātīrthaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*yatra bhāgīrathī sākṣānmūrtirūpeṇa tiṣṭhati \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. A great Tīrtha better than that is destructive of all sins. It is there that Bhāgīrathī stands visible directly in the form of an image.

## \|\| 2.83.80 \|\|

*snātvā bhāgīrathī tīrthe kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ vidhānavit \|*  
*dattvā dānaṃ ca pātrebhyo na bhūyo garbhabhāgbhavet \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. If one takes the holy bath in the Bhāgīrathī Tīrtha, offers Śrāddha with a correct knowledge of its procedure and makes gifts to deserving persons, he will never be in a womb again.

## \|\| 2.83.81 \|\|

*harapāpaṃ ca bho vīra tīrthaṃ bhāgīrathītaṭe \|*  
*tatra snātvā kṣayaṃ yāṃti mahāpāpakulānyapi \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. O Vīra, Harapāpa Tīrtha is also on the banks of Bhāgīrathī. By taking the holy bath there, multitudes of great sins become destroyed.

## \|\| 2.83.82 \|\|

*yo niṣpāpeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tatra paśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*niṣpāpo jāyate vīra sa talliṃgekṣaṇātkṣaṇāt \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. A man who visit Niṣpāpeśvara Liṅga there becomes rid of sins, O Vīra, at that very instant (of visiting the Liṅga).

## \|\| 2.83.83 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhatīrthaṃ ca tatopi pravaraṃ matam \|*  
*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ yatra snātvā phalaṃ labhet \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Daśāśvamedha Tīrtha is considered more excellent than that. By taking the holy dip there, one attains the benefit of ten Aśvamedhas (horse-sacrifices).

## \|\| 2.83.84 \|\|

*tatopi śubhadaṃ vīra baṃdītīrthaṃ pracakṣate \|*  
*yatra snāto naro mucyedapi saṃsārabaṃdhanāt \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. They call Band! Tīrtha a better bestower of auspiciousness, O Vīra. By taking bath there, the man will be liberated from the worldly bondage.

## \|\| 2.83.85 \|\|

*hiraṇyākṣeṇa daityena bahuśo devatāḥ purā \|*  
*baṃdīkṛtā nigaḍitā stuṣṭuvurjagadaṃbikām \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Formerly many Devas were imprisoned by Demon Hiraṇyākṣa. They were fettered too and they eulogized Jagadaṃbikā (Mother of the universe).

## \|\| 2.83.86 \|\|

*tato viśṛṃkhalībhūtairvaṃditā yajjagajjaniḥ \|*  
*tadā prabhṛti baṃdīti gīyatedyāpi mānavaiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The Mother of the universe, who was bowed to by those Devas who had been freed from the fetters is being sung about since then as Bandī. Even now she is prayed to by men.

## \|\| 2.83.87 \|\|

*baṃdītīrthastu tatraiva mahānigaḍakhaṃḍanam \|*  
*tatra snāto vimucyeta sarvasmātkarmapāśataḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Bandī Tīrtha that breaks great fetters is there itself. One who bathes there is liberated from all bonds of Karmas.

## \|\| 2.83.88 \|\|

*baṃdītīrthaṃ mahāśreṣṭhaṃ kāśipuryāṃ viśāṃpate \|*  
*tatra snāto naro yāyādvimuktiṃ devyanugrahāt \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. O king, Bandītīrtha in the city of Kāśī is highly excellent. A man who bathes there will attain salvation due to the blessings of the goddess.

## \|\| 2.83.89 \|\|

*tatopi hi śreṣṭhataraṃ prayāgamiti viśrutam \|*  
*prayāgamādhavo yatra sarvayāgaphalapradaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. More excellent than that is well-known as Prayāga Tīrtha where Prayāgamādhava is the bestower of the benefit of all Yāgas.

## \|\| 2.83.90 \|\|

*kṣoṇīvarāhatīrthaṃ ca tatopi śubhadaṃ param \|*  
*tatra snāto naro jātu tiryagyoniṃ na gacchati \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Kṣoṇī-Varāha Tīrtha is a better bestower of auspiciousness than that. A man who bathes there is never born in brutish (non-human) species.

## \|\| 2.83.91 \|\|

*tataḥ kāleśvaraṃ tīrthaṃ vīraśreṣṭhataraṃ param \|*  
*kalikālau na bādhete yatra snātaṃ narottamam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Kāleśvara Tīrtha is greater and more excellent than that. Kali and Kāla do not affect and torment the excellent man who bathes there.

## \|\| 2.83.92 \|\|

*aśokatīrthaṃ tatraiva tatopyatitarāṃ śubham \|*  
*yatra snāto naro jātu nāpatecchokasāgare \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. There itself is Aśoka Tīrtha, more auspicious than that. A man who bathes there never falls into the ocean of misery.

## \|\| 2.83.93 \|\|

*tatoti nirmalataraṃ śakratīrthaṃ nṛpāṃgaja \|*  
*śukradvārā na jāyeta yatra snāto narottamaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. O son of the king, purer than that is the Śukra Tīrtha. The excellent man who bathes there is not reborn through semen virile.

## \|\| 2.83.94 \|\|

*tato'pi puṇyadaṃ rājanbhavānītīrthamuttamam \|*  
*yatra snātvā bhavānīśau dṛṣṭvā naiva punarbhavet \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Better merit-bestowing than that is the excellent Bhavānī Tīrtha, O king. If one takes bath there and visit Bhavānī and Īśa, one is never reborn.

## \|\| 2.83.95 \|\|

*prabhāsatīrthaṃ vikhyātaṃ tatopi śubhadaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*someśvarasya puratastatra snāto na garbhabhāk \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Prabhāsa Tīrtha is well-known as the bestower of auspiciousness on men more than that. It is in front of Someśvara. One who takes bath there is never born into a womb.

## \|\| 2.83.96 \|\|

*tato garuḍatīrthaṃ ca saṃsāraviṣanāśanam \|*  
*garuḍeśaṃ samabhyarcya tatra snātvā na śocati \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Beyond it is the Garuḍa Tīrtha destructive of the poison of worldly existence. After adoring Garuḍeśa and taking bath therein one does not meet with an occasion to feel sorry.

## \|\| 2.83.97 \|\|

*brahmatīrthaṃ tataḥ puṇyaṃ vīrabrahmeśvarātpuraḥ \|*  
*brahmavidyāmavāpnoti tatra snānena mānavaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. O Vīra, beyond that is the meritorious Brahma Tīrtha in front of Brahmeśvara. By taking his holy bath there, a man attains Brahmavidyā.

## \|\| 2.83.98 \|\|

*tato vṛddhārkatīrthaṃ ca vidhitīrthaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*tatrāpluto naro yāti ravilokaṃ sunirmalam \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Beyond it is Vṛddhārka Tīrtha and thereafter is Vidhi Tīrtha. A man who bathes there proceeds to the world of Ravi (Sun) free from impurities.

## \|\| 2.83.99 \|\|

*tato nṛsiṃhatīrthaṃ ca mahābhayanivāraṇam \|*  
*kālādapi kutastatra snātvā paribibheti ca \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Thereafter is the Nṛsīṃha Tīrtha that averts great fear. Why should one be afraid of even Kāla (god of Death) after bathing there?

## \|\| 2.83.100 \|\|

*tatopi puṇyadaṃ nṛṇāṃ tīrthaṃ citraratheśvaram \|*  
*yatra snātvā ca dattvā ca citraguptaṃ na paśyati \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Batter bestower of merit than that on men is the Citraratheśvara Tīrtha. If one takes bath there and makes gift, one does not see Citragupta.

## \|\| 2.83.101 \|\|

*dharmatīrthaṃ tataḥ puṇyaṃ dharmeśa purataḥ sthitam \|*  
*tatra śrāddhadikaṃ kṛtvā pitṝṇāmanṛṇo bhavet \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Beyond that is the meritorious Dharma Tīrtha stationed in front of Dharmeśa. One shall be free from indebtedness to ancestors after performing Śrāddha etc. there.

## \|\| 2.83.102 \|\|

*viśālatīrthaṃ vimalaṃ viśālaphaladaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā viśālākṣī dṛṣṭvā garbhena jāyate \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Beyond it is the Viśāla Tīrtha free from impurities and the bestower of extensive benefit. Having bathed there and visited Viśālākṣī, one is never reborn in a womb.

## \|\| 2.83.103 \|\|

*jarāsaṃdheśa tīrthaṃ ca jarāsaṃdheśasannidhau \|*  
*saṃsārajvarapīḍābhistatra snāto na muhyati \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Jarāsandheśa Tīrtha is in the vicinity of Jarāsandheśa. One who bathes there never becomes deluded by the afflictions of the fever of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.83.104 \|\|

*tato'pi lalitātīrthaṃ mahāsaubhāgyavardhanam \|*  
*snātvārcayitvā lalitāṃ na daridro na duḥkhabhāk \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Beyond that is the Lalitā Tīrtha that augments conjugal bliss. If one bathes there and adores Lalitā one never becomes poor and miserable.

## \|\| 2.83.105 \|\|

*tato gautamatīrthaṃ ca sarvapāpaviśodhanam \|*  
*snātvā piṃḍānvinirvāpya yatra śocati na kvacit \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Beyond it is the Gautamī Tīrtha that washes off all sins. After bathing there and offering balls of rice (to the Manes) one never bewails anything.

## \|\| 2.83.106-112 \|\|

*gaṃgākeśavatīrthaṃ ca tīrthaṃ cāgastya saṃjñakam \|*  
*tatastu yoginītīrthaṃ trisaṃdhyākhyaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 106 \|\|*

*tatastu nārmadaṃ tīrthaṃ tata āruṃdhateyakam \|*  
*vāsiṣṭhaṃ ca tatastīrthaṃ mārkaṃṇḍeyamanuttamam \|\| 107 \|\|*

*jñeyānyetāni tīrthāni puṇyadānyuttarottarama \|*  
*khurakartari saṃjñaṃ ca tatastīrthamanuttamam \|\| 108 \|\|*

*tatra śrāddhādikaraṇānnaromucyeta kilbiṣaiḥ \|*  
*tato bhagīrathaṃ tīrthaṃ rājarṣeratipuṇyadam \|\| 109 \|\|*

*tatrālpamapi yacchedyatkalpāṃtepyakṣayaṃ hi tat \|*  
*etebhyopi hi tīrthebhyo liṃgakoṭitrayādapi \|\| 110 \|\|*

*vīravīreśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ mahāśreṣṭhaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*vīratīrthe naraḥ snātvā vīreśaṃ paripūjya ca \|\| 111 \|\|*

*tīrtheṣveteṣu sarveṣu snāto bhavati nānyathā \|*  
*yastu vīreśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ naktamabhyarcayipyati \|*  
*tena trikoṭisaṃkhyāni liṃgānīhārcitāni vai \|\| 112 \|\|*

106-112. (There is) a series of Tīrthas beyond it, viz. Gaṅgākeśava Tīrtha, Agastya Tīrtha, Yoginī Tīrtha, Trisandhyākhya Tīrtha, Narmadā Tīrtha, Ārundhateyaka Tīrtha, Vaśiṣṭha Tīrtha, the excellent Mārkaṇḍeya Tīrtha. All these Tīrthas are the bestower of merit. The latter is more (efficacious) than the former (preceding). Then there is the excellent Tīrtha named Khurakartari. By performing Śrāddha and other rites a man will get rid of sins. Beyond it is the saintly King’s Tīrtha named Bhagīratha Tīrtha. It accords excessive merit. If anyone makes the gift of even the least of things there, it becomes everlasting in benefit even at the close of the Kalpa. More than these Tīrthas, more than the three crores of Liṅgas, O Vīra, this Vīreśvara Liṅga will be extremely excellent. If a man bathes in the Vīra Tīrtha and worships Vīreśa, it is as though he has bathed in all these Tīrthas, and not otherwise. If anyone worships Vīreśvara Liṅga at night it is as though three crores of Liṅgas have been worshipped by him here.

## \|\| 2.83.113 \|\|

*yastu kāmayate lakṣmīṃ muktidāṃ bhuktidāmapi \|*  
*tena vīreśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ saṃsevyamatiyatnataḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Vīreśvara Liṅga should be assiduously resorted to by the person who wishes for Lakṣmī, the bestower of salvation as well as worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 2.83.114 \|\|

*vidhāyaikaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ naro vīreśamarcayan \|*  
*bhūtāyāṃ naiva gṛhṇāti śarīraṃ pāṃcabhautikam \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. If a man performs a single act of Jāgaraṇa (keeping awake at night) and worships Vīreśa on the fourteenth lunar day, he does not take the body consisting of the five elements.

## \|\| 2.83.115 \|\|

*idaṃ liṃgaṃ sadābhyarcyaṃ siddhaiḥ saṃsiddhikāmukaiḥ \|*  
*aihikāmuṣmikānyasmātsarvānkāmānsamarthayet \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. This Liṅga should always be worshipped by those who have attained Siddhis as well as those who wish for Siddhis, because it causes the realization of all desires pertaining to this world as well as the other world.

## \|\| 2.83.116 \|\|

*paṃcāmṛtena snapanaṃ yaḥ kariṣyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*palepale phalaṃ tasya vīreśe ghaṭakoṭijam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. If a man bathes Vīreśa with Pañcāmṛta, he will attain the merit of a crore of pots of Pañcāmṛta bath for each moment’s duration.

## \|\| 2.83.117 \|\|

*yadanyatra phalaṃ liṃge koṭipuṣpa pradānataḥ \|*  
*tadekenaiva puṣpeṇa vīreśe nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. There is no doubt in this that with a single flower offered to Vīreśa one will get the benefit of offering a crore of flowers elsewhere.

## \|\| 2.83.118 \|\|

*ekāmapyāhutiṃ dattvā vīreśvarasamīpataḥ \|*  
*koṭihomaphalaṃ samyaṅnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. No doubt or hesitation need be felt in this regard that by offering a single Āhuti in the vicinity of Vireśvara, one will attain the benefit of a crore of Homas done perfectly.

## \|\| 2.83.119 \|\|

*sikthesikthe ca naivaidyai koṭisikthaphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*atyalpamapi vīreśe kṛtamakṣayatāṃ vrajet \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Even the least thing offered to Vīreśa gives inexhaustible benefit. In the Naivedya (food offering) the devotee gets the benefit of offering a crore of lumps of boiled rice for every lump that he offers.

## \|\| 2.83.120 \|\|

*apyekaṃ yo mahārudraṃ japedvīreśa sannidhau \|*  
*jāpayedvā bhavettasya koṭirudraphalaṃ dhruvam \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. If anyone repeats Mahārudra Mantra once or makes someone else repeat it once in the presence of Vīreśa, certainly he will attain the benefit of repeating Rudra Mantra a crore of times.

## \|\| 2.83.121 \|\|

*vratotsargādi vīreśe yatkṛtaṃ vratibhirnṛbhiḥ \|*  
*tatkoṭiguṇasaṃkhyākaṃ bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Whatever is performed by men observing Vratas such as the rite of Vratotsarga etc. (formal concluding rite after observance of vows etc.) will undoubtedly increase by a crore of times.

## \|\| 2.83.122 \|\|

*kṛtā aṣṭau namaskārā yena vīreśvarāgrataḥ \|*  
*aṣṭakoṭi namaskāraphalaṃ tasya na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. If the devotee performs eight Namaskāras (prostrations) in front of Vireśvara, he will obtain the benefit of eight crores of Namaskāras. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 2.83.123 \|\|

*sarvāsāṃ saṃpadāṃ sthānamidaṃ liṃgaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*vīraśveraṃ na saṃdeho vīra me varadānataḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. O Vīra, with my favour this Vireśvara Liṅga shall be the abode (cause) of all riches. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.83.124 \|\|

*jñānamutpatsyate puṃsāṃ tārakākhyaṃ mamājñayā \|*  
*jīvatāmeva tatsevyametalliṃgaṃ śubhārthibhiḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Even as they are alive, by my behest, men will have knowledge, entitled Tāraka (the redeemer). Hence this Liṅga should be resorted to by those who seek auspiciousness.”

## \|\| 2.83.125-127 \|\|

*etacchrutvā punaḥ prāha vīro mitrajitaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya devadeveśaṃ paripūrṇamanorathaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

*tīrthānyetāni deveśa yānyuktāni mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*kṛpayā punarapyeva tadanyāni vada prabho \|\| 126 \|\|*

*ādikeśavamārabhya tattīrthācca bhagīrathāt \|*  
*yeṣāṃ śravaṇamātreṇa niṣpāpo jāyate naraḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

125-127. On hearing this, the heroic son of Amitrajit said again after bowing down to the Lord of Devas with fully realized desires: “O Lord of Devas, all these Tīrthas have been narrated to me. O Lord, be pleased to recount other Tīrthas too. Kindly narrate the Tīrthas beginning with Ādikeśava and concluding with Bhagīratha Tīrtha. On hearing about these a man becomes free from sins.”

## \|\| 2.83.128 \|\|

*iti śrutvā maheśāno mahīpa tanayoditam \|*  
*punastīrthāni gaṃgāyāṃ vaktuṃ samupacakrame \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. On hearing this speech (request) of the prince, Maheśāna began to recount the Tīrthas in Gaṅgā.

## Chapter 84 - Tirthas from the Confluence of Gangā and Varaṇā up to Maṇikarṇikā

## \|\| 2.84.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ākarṇaya kṣoṇisura yathā sthāṇuracīkarat \|*  
*gaṃgāvaraṇayoḥ puṇyātsaṃbhedāttīrthabhūmikām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. O Brāhmaṇa, listen how Sthāṇu (Siva) created a holy spot by means of the meritorious confluence of Gaṅgā and Varaṇā.

## \|\| 2.84.2 \|\|

*saṃgame tatra niṣṇātaḥ saṃgameśaṃ samarcya ca \|*  
*naro na jātu jananī garbhasaṃgamavāpnuyāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A person who takes his holy bath in that confluence and worships Saṅgameśa, shall never again meet with the contact of a mother’s womb.

## \|\| 2.84.3 \|\|

*tatra pādodakaṃ tīrthaṃ yatra devena śārṅgiṇā \|*  
*ādau pādau kṣalitau tu maṃdarāccāgatena yat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Tīrtha called Pādodaka is there. It is there that the Lord wielding Śārṅga bow (i.e. Viṣṇu) washed his feet at the outset as soon as he came from Mandara.

## \|\| 2.84.4 \|\|

*vipṇupādodake tīrthe vārikāryaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*vyatīpātena niyataṃ bhūyaḥ sāṃsārikī gatiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On the Vyatīpāta day (New-Moon day on Sunday etc.) the devotee should perform all the rites such as offering water-libation in Viṣṇupādodaka Tīrtha. He will never have any return to the worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.84.5 \|\|

*kṛtapādodaka snānaḥ kṛtakeśavapūjanaḥ \|*  
*vītasaṃsāravasatiḥ kāśyāmāsīnnarottamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A person who bathed in Pādodaka Tīrtha and worshipped Keśava becomes an excellent man rid of the residence in Saṃsāra.

## \|\| 2.84.6 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ sā bhūmiruddiṣṭā śvetadvīpa iti dvijaiḥ \|*  
*tatra puṇyārjanaṃ kṛtvā śvetadvīpādhipo bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. That spot in Kāśī has been pointed out by Brāhmaṇas as Svetadvīpa. After acquiring merit there, the devotee shall become lord of Śvetadvīpa.

## \|\| 2.84.7 \|\|

*tataḥ pādodakāttīrthāttīrthaṃ kṣīrābdhisaṃjñakam \|*  
*tatrārjita mahāpuṇyo vasetkṣīrābdhirodhasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Beyond Pādodaka Tīrtha is the Tīrtha called Kṣīrābdhi (Milk Ocean). One who acquires merit there will stay on the shore of the Milk Ocean.

## \|\| 2.84.8 \|\|

*kṣīrodāddakṣiṇebhāge tīrthaṃ śaṃkhākhyanuttamam \|*  
*tatra snāto bhavennūnaṃ nāśaṃkhādinidheḥ patiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. To the southern side of Kṣīroda is the excellent Śaṅkha Tīrtha. A man who takes his bath there, will certainly become lord of the treasures, Śaṅkha etc.

## \|\| 2.84.9 \|\|

*arvākca śaṃkhatīrthādvai cakratīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*saṃsāracakre na patettattīrthajalamajjanāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Behind Śaṅkha Tīrtha is the excellent Cakra Tīrtha. By getting immersed in the waters of that Tīrtha, one averts fall into Saṃsāracakra (cycle of worldly existence).

## \|\| 2.84.10 \|\|

*gadātīrthaṃ tadagre tu saṃsāragadanāśanam \|*  
*tatra śrāddhādikaraṇātpaśyeddevaṃ gadādharam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Beyond that is Gadā Tīrtha that is destructive of the ailments of worldly existence. By performing Śrāddha etc. there, one shall see Lord Gadādhara.

## \|\| 2.84.11 \|\|

*padmākṛtpadmatīrthaṃ ca tadagre pitṛtṛptikṛt \|*  
*tatra snānādikaraṇātprāpnuyādaghasaṃkṣayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Beyond that is Padma Tīrtha that causes glorious fortune and satisfaction of the Pitṛs. By performing the rites of holy ablution etc. there one shall accomplish the reduction of sins.

## \|\| 2.84.12 \|\|

*tatastīrthaṃ mahālakṣmyā mahāpuṇyaphalapradam \|*  
*tatrābhyarcya mahālakṣmīṃ nirvāṇakamalāṃ labhet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereafter is the Tīrtha of Mahālakṣmī that bestows great merit. By adoring Mahālakṣmī there one shall obtain the glory of salvation.

## \|\| 2.84.13 \|\|

*tato gārutmataṃ tīrthaṃ saṃsāragaranāśanam \|*  
*kṛtodakakriyastatra vaikuṃṭhe vasatiṃ labhet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thereafter is Gārutmata Tīrtha that is destructive of the poison of worldly existence. One who performs rites such as offering water-libations there, achieves residence in Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 2.84.14 \|\|

*tato nāradatīrthaṃ ca brahmavidyaikakāraṇam \|*  
*tatra snānena muktaḥ syāddṛṣṭvā nāradakeśavam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereafter is Nārada Tīrtha, the sole cause of the attainment of Brahmavidyā (knowledge of the Absolute). By taking the holy bath there and viewing Nāradakeśava, one shall become liberated.

## \|\| 2.84.15 \|\|

*prahlādatīrthaṃ tadyāmye mahābhaktiphalapradam \|*  
*tatra vai snānamātreṇa viṣṇoḥ priyataro bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. To the south thereof is Prahlāda Tīrtha that bestows the benefit of devotion. Merely by taking the holy bath there one shall become extremely endearing to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.84.16 \|\|

*aṃbarīṣaṃ tatastīrthaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*tatra vai śubhakarmāṇo janā no garbhabhājanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereafter is Aṃbarīṣa Tīrtha that destroys great sins. People who perform auspicious rites there, do not enter a mother’s womb (i.e. are not reborn).

## \|\| 2.84.17 \|\|

*ādityakeśavaṃ nāma tadagre tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*kṛtābhiṣekastatrāpi labhetsvargābhiṣecanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thereafter is the excellent Tīrtha named Ādityakeśava. One who takes the ablution there too shall get coronation bath in heaven.

## \|\| 2.84.18 \|\|

*dattātreyasya tatrāsti tīrthaṃ trailokyapāvanam \|*  
*yogasiddhiṃ labhe tatra snānamātreṇa bhāvataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The Tīrtha of Dattātreya, the most sacred one in all the three worlds, is also there. By devoutly taking the holy bath therein, one shall attain perfection in Yoga (Yogasiddhi).

## \|\| 2.84.19 \|\|

*tadagre bhārgavaṃ tīrthaṃ mahājñānasamarpakam \|*  
*tatra snānavidhānena bhavedbhārgava lokabhāk \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Beyond that is Bhārgava Tīrtha that bestows great knowledge. By taking the holy bath duly there one shall attain Bhārgava’s world.

## \|\| 2.84.20 \|\|

*tato vāmanatīrthaṃ ca viṣṇusānnidhyahetukam \|*  
*tatra śrāddhavidhānena mucyate pitṛjādṛṇāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereafter is Vāmana Tīrtha that causes the presence of Viṣṇu. By performing Śrāddha rite there, one is liberated from indebtedness to Pitṛs.

## \|\| 2.84.21 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇākhyaṃ hi tatastīrthaṃ śubhapradam \|*  
*tattīrthamajjanātpuṃsāṃ garbhavāsaḥ sudurlabhaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thereafter is the Tīrtha called Naranārāyaṇa that bestows auspiciousness. By getting immersed in that Tīrtha, people rarely find residence in the womb.

## \|\| 2.84.22 \|\|

*yajñavārāhatīrthaṃ ca tato dakṣiṇataḥ śubham \|*  
*yatra snātasya vai puṃsāṃ rājasūyaphalaṃ dhruvam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. To the south thereof is the auspicious Yajñavarāha Tīrtha. Men who take their holy bath there, certainly obtain the benefit of Rājasūya.

## \|\| 2.84.23 \|\|

*vidāranārasiṃhākhyaṃ tīrthaṃ tatrāsti pāvanam \|*  
*yatraikasnānato naśyedagha janmaśatārjitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The holy Tīrtha named Vidāranārasiṃha is also there. By a single holy bath there the sin acquired in the course of a hundred births perishes.

## \|\| 2.84.24 \|\|

*gopīgoviṃdatīrthaṃ ca tato vaiṣṇavalokadam \|*  
*yasminsnāto naro vidvānna viṃdyādgarbhavedanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereafter is Gapīgovinda Tīrtha that bestows the world of Viṣṇu. A wise man who takes his holy bath there will never know the pain of being in a womb.

## \|\| 2.84.25 \|\|

*lakṣmīnṛsiṃhatīrthaṃ ca gopīgoviṃda dakṣiṇe \|*  
*nirvāṇalakṣmyā yatratyo vriyate tu narottamaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. To the south of Gopīgovinda is Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha Tīrtha. The excellent man stationed there is wooed by Nirvāṇalakṣmī (glory of salvation).

## \|\| 2.84.26 \|\|

*taddakṣiṇāyāṃ kāṣṭhāyāṃ śeṣatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*mahāpāpaugha śeṣopi na tiṣṭhedyannimajjanāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the southern direction thereof is the excellent Śeṣa Tīrtha. If one gets immersed there, no trace of one’s mass of great sins remains there.

## \|\| 2.84.27 \|\|

*śaṃkhamādhavatīrthaṃ ca tadyāmyāṃ diśi cottamam \|*  
*tattīrthasevanānnṛṇāṃ kutaḥ pāpabhayaṃ mahat \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In the southern direction thereof is Śaṅkha-Mādhava Tīrtha. Whence is the great fear of sin to men if they resort to that?

## \|\| 2.84.28 \|\|

*tatopi pāvanataraṃ tīrthaṃ tatkṣaṇasiddhidam \|*  
*nīlagrīvākhyamatulaṃ tatsnāyī sarvadā śuciḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thereafter is the Tīrtha called Nīlagrīva which is unparalleled. It is more sacred than Śaṅkhamādhava Tīrtha. It accords Siddhi at the same instant. One who bathes there, is always pure.

## \|\| 2.84.29 \|\|

*tatroddālakatīrthaṃ ca sarvāghaugha vināśanam \|*  
*dadāti mahatīmṛddhiṃ snānamātreṇa tannṛṇām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Uddālaka Tīrtha too is there. It is destructive of all the mass of sins. Merely with the holy bath there, it bestows on men great prosperity.

## \|\| 2.84.30 \|\|

*tataḥ sāṃkhyākhya tīrthaṃ ca sāṃkhyeśvara samīpataḥ \|*  
*tattīrthasevanātpuṃsāṃ sāṃkhyayogaḥ prasīdati \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereafter, in the vicinity of Sāṅkhyeśvara is the Tīrtha called Sāṅkhya. By resorting to that Tīrtha Sāṅkhya-Yoga becomes clear to man.
