## \|\| 2.84.31 \|\|

*svarlokādyatra saṃlīnaḥ svayaṃ deva umāpatiḥ \|*  
*ataḥ svarlīnatīrthaṃ ca svarlīneśvara sannidhau \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In the vicinity of Svarlīneśvara is Svarlīna Tīrtha, so called because Lord Umāpati himself got merged therein from the heavenly world.

## \|\| 2.84.32 \|\|

*tatra snānena dānena śraddhayā dvijabhojanaiḥ \|*  
*japahomārcanaiḥ puṃsāmakṣayaṃ sarvameva hi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. There all sacred rites of men such as the rites of ablution, making gifts, feeding Brāhmaṇas faithfully, Japas, Homas and Arcanās become indestructible.

## \|\| 2.84.33 \|\|

*mahiṣāsuratīrthaṃ ca tatsamīpeti pāvanam \|*  
*yatra taptvā sa daityeṃdro vijigye sakalānsurān \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The extremely sacred Mahiṣāsura Tīrtha is near it. That leader of demons could conquer all the Suras due to the penance he performed there.

## \|\| 2.84.34 \|\|

*tattīrthasevakodyāpi nāribhiḥ paribhūyate \|*  
*na pātakairmahadbhiśca prārthitaṃ ca phalaṃ labhet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A person resorting to that Tīrtha even today is never harassed by enemies nor by great sins. He will obtain the benefit sought.

## \|\| 2.84.35 \|\|

*bāṇatīrthaṃ ca tasyārāttatsahasrabhujapradam \|*  
*tatra snāto naro bhaktiṃ prāpnuyācchāṃbhavīṃ sthirām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Very near it is Bāṇa Tīrtha that bestows a thousand arms. A man taking his holy bath there will obtain (develop) steady devotion to Śaṃbhu.

## \|\| 2.84.36 \|\|

*gopratāreśvaraṃ nāma tadagre tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*aputropi taredyatra snāto vaitaraṇīṃ sukham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Beyond it is the excellent Tīrtha named Gopratāreśvara. If a man without a son takes his holy bath there, he will easily cross Vaitaraṇī.

## \|\| 2.84.37 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ hiraṇyagarbhākhyaṃ tadyāmye sarvapāpahṛt \|*  
*tatra snāto hiraṇyena mucyate na kadācana \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. To the south thereof is the Tīrtha called Hiraṇyagarbha which dispels all sins. One who takes the holy ablution there is never devoid of gold.

## \|\| 2.84.38 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇavatīrthaṃ ca sarvatīrthottamottamam \|*  
*jīvanmukto bhavettatra snānamātreṇa mānavaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Beyond that is Praṇava Tīrtha which is the most excellent of all excellent Tīrthas. A man will become liberated while still living merely by taking his holy bath there.

## \|\| 2.84.39 \|\|

*tataḥ piśaṃgilā tīrthaṃ darśanādapi pāpahṛt \|*  
*mune mamādhiṣṭhānaṃ vai tadagaste'ti siddhidam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Beyond it is Piśaṅgilā Tīrtha which dispels sins even by the vision thereof. O Sage Agastya, it is the site of my abode, the bestower of excellent Siddhi.

## \|\| 2.84.40 \|\|

*snātvā piśaṃgilā tīrthe dattvā dānaṃ ca kiṃcana \|*  
*kiṃ śocati kṛtātpāpādanyatrāpi mṛto yadi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If one takes his holy bath in Piśaṅgilā Tīrtha and makes the gift of something, why should he be afraid of the sin committed by him even if he dies elsewhere?

## \|\| 2.84.41 \|\|

*yo vai piśaṃgilā tīrthe snātvā māmarcayiṣyati \|*  
*bhaviṣyati sa me mittraṃ mitratejaḥ samaprabham \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A person who takes his holy bath in Piśaṅgilā Tīrtha and adores me, will become my friend having the lustre akin to that of the Sun.

## \|\| 2.84.42 \|\|

*tatastraiviṣṭapīdṛṣṭi nirmalīkṛta puṣkalam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ pilipilākhyaṃ vai manomalavināśanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thereafter is the Tīrtha named Pilipilā that is entirely sanctified by the vision of Triviṣṭapa (i.e. Lord Trilocana). It destroys the impurities of the mind.

## \|\| 2.84.43 \|\|

*tatra śrāddhādikaraṇāddīnānātha pratarpaṇāt \|*  
*mahatīṃ śriyamāpnoti mānavotīva niścalām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. By performing Śrāddha and other rites there and fully satisfying the distressed and the helpless ones, a man obtains great and steady prosperity.

## \|\| 2.84.44 \|\|

*tato nāgeśvaraṃ tīrthaṃ mahāghapariśodhanam \|*  
*tattīrthamajjanādeva bhavetsarvāghasaṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thereafter is Nāgeśvara Tīrtha that dispels great sins. By immersing oneself in that Tīrtha one can achieve the reduction of all sins.

## \|\| 2.84.45 \|\|

*taddakṣiṇe mahāpuṇyaṃ karṇādityākhyamuttamam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ yatrāpluto martyo bhāskarīṃ śriyamāvahet \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. To the south thereof is the excellent Tīrtha of great merit named Karṇāditya. A man who bathes in it will attain the brilliance of the Sun.

## \|\| 2.84.46 \|\|

*tato bhairavatīrthaṃ ca mahāghaughakṣayapradam \|*  
*caturarthodayakaraṃ sarvavighnanivāraṇam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thereafter is Bhairava Tīrtha that bestows the destruction of the masses of great sins, causes the rise of the fourfold aims of life and dispels all obstacles.

## \|\| 2.84.47 \|\|

*bhaumāṣṭamyāṃ tatra naraḥ snātvā saṃtarpayetpitṝn \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca bhairavaṃ kālaṃ kaliṃ kālaṃ ca saṃjayet \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On the Bhaumāṣṭamī day i.e. eighth lunar day coinciding with a Tuesday) if a man takes his holy bath there, offers libation to the Pitṛs and visits Kālabhairava, he will subdue Kali and Kāla.

## \|\| 2.84.48 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ kharvanṛsiṃhākhyaṃ tīrthādbharavataḥ puraḥ \|*  
*tatra snātasya vai puṃsaḥ kutoghajanitaṃ bhayam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The Tīrtha called Kharvanṛsiṃha is in front of Bhairava Tīrtha. How can a man who takes his holy bath there have the fear originating from sins?

## \|\| 2.84.49 \|\|

*mṛkaṃḍasya munestīrthaṃ tadyāmyāmatinirmalama \|*  
*tatra snānena martyānāṃ nāpāyamaraṇaṃ kvacit \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. To the south thereof is the exceedingly pure Tīrtha of Sage Mṛkaṇḍa. Men who take their holy bath there, will not meet with accidental death anywhere.

## \|\| 2.84.50 \|\|

*tataḥ paṃcanadākhyaṃ vai sarvatīrthaniṣevitam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ yatra naraḥ snātvā na saṃsārī punarbhavet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thereafter is the Tīrtha named Pañcanada which is resorted to by all Tīrthas. A man who takes his bath there, does not continue to be a worldly being (i.e. becomes free from Saṃsāra).

## \|\| 2.84.51 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍodaravartīni yāni tīrthāni sarvataḥ \|*  
*ūrje yatra samāyāṃti svāghaugha parinuttaye \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. All the Tīrthas of the entire Cosmic Egg enter that Tīrtha during the month of Kārttika for getting rid of their own sins.

## \|\| 2.84.52 \|\|

*sarvadā yatra sarvāṇi daśamyādidinatrayam \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃti tīrthavaryāṇi nijanairmalyahetave \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Always all these excellent Tīrthas stay there for three days from the Daśamī (tenth day) onwards for the sake of ridding themselves of their own impurities.

## \|\| 2.84.53 \|\|

*bhūriśaḥ sarvatīrthāni madhya kāśi padepade \|*  
*paraṃ pāṃcanadaḥ kaiścinmahimānāpi kutracit \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Within Kāśī, at every step, there are all sorts of Tīrthas. But the greatness of Pañcanada is unique. Nowhere else has it been obtained by any of them.

## \|\| 2.84.54 \|\|

*apyekaṃ kārtikasyāhastatra vai saphalīkṛtam \|*  
*japahomārcanādānaiḥ kṛtakṛtyāsta eva hi \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If people make at least one Kārttika day fruitful by means of Japa, Homa, Arcanā and Dāna, they alone are blessed ones who have fulfilled their tasks.

## \|\| 2.84.55 \|\|

*sarvāṇyapi ca tīrthāni yugapattulitānyapi \|*  
*nādhijanmuḥ paṃcanadyāḥ kalāyā api tulyatām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If all the Tīrthas (consolidated together) are simultaneously weighed against Pañcanada, they do not attain equality with even a sixteenth part of Pañcanada.

## \|\| 2.84.56 \|\|

*snātvā pāṃcanade tīrthe dṛṣṭvā vai biṃdumādhavam \|*  
*na jātu jāyate dhīmāñjananī jaṭharājire \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. An intelligent man who takes the holy bath in Pañcanada Tīrtha and visits Bindumādhava is never reborn in the belly of a mother.

## \|\| 2.84.57 \|\|

*tato jñānahadaṃ tīrthaṃ jaḍānāmapi jāḍyahṛt \|*  
*tatra snāto naro jātu jñānabhraṃśaṃ na cāpnuyāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thereafter is Jñānahrada Tīrtha which dispels the sluggishness and ignorance of even the dull-witted. A man who takes his holy bath there, never experiences loss of wisdom.

## \|\| 2.84.58 \|\|

*tatra jñānahrade snātvā dṛṣṭvā jñāneśvaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ tadadhigacchedvai yena no bādhyate punaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. A man should take his holy bath in Jñānahrada and visit Jñāneśvara. He will thereby obtain that knowledge by which he is never tormented (by ignorance).

## \|\| 2.84.59 \|\|

*tatosti maṃgalaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvāmaṃgalanāśanam \|*  
*tatrāvagāhanaṃ kṛtvā bhavenmaṃgalabhājanam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Thereafter is Maṅgala Tīrtha that destroys all inauspiciousness. By diving into it a devotee shall be the recipient of auspiciousness.

## \|\| 2.84.60 \|\|

*amaṃgalāni naśyeyurbhaveyurmaṃgalāni ca \|*  
*snāturvai maṃgale tīrthe namaskartuśca maṃgalam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. All inauspiciousness shall perish. Auspicious results take place. This happens in the case of a person who takes his bath in Maṅgala Tīrtha and bows down to Lord Maṅgala.

## \|\| 2.84.61 \|\|

*mayūkhamālinastīrthaṃ tadagre malanāśanam \|*  
*tatrāpluto gabhastīśaṃ vilokya vimalo bhavet \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Beyond that is the Tīrtha of the Sun which is destructive of impurities. One who takes the holy ablution there and visits Gabhastīśa shall be free from impurities.

## \|\| 2.84.62 \|\|

*makhatīrthaṃ tu tatraiva makhaiśvara samīpataḥ \|*  
*makhajaṃ puṇyamāpnoti tatra snāto narottamaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. There itself Makha Tīrtha is in the vicinity of Makheśvara. An excellent man who takes his holy bath there acquires the benefit and merit of performing a sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.84.63 \|\|

*tatpārśve biṃdutīrthaṃ ca paramajñānakāraṇam \|*  
*tatra śrāddhādikaṃ kṛtvā labhetsukṛtamuttamam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. By the side thereof is Bindu Tīrtha, the cause of the greatest knowledge. By performing Srāddha etc. there one shall get the excellent merit of good deeds.

## \|\| 2.84.64-65 \|\|

*pippalādasya ca munestīrthaṃ tadyāmyadiksthitam \|*  
*snātvā śanerdine tatra dṛṣṭvāvai pippaleśvaram \|\| 64 \|\|*

*pippalaṃ tatra sevitvā aśvattha iti maṃtrataḥ \|*  
*śanipīḍāṃ na labhate duḥsvapnaṃ cāpi nāśayet \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. The Tīrtha of Sage Pippalāda is situated to the south thereof. On a Saturday the devotee should take his holy bath there, visit Pippaleśvara and eat a Pippala fruit uttering the Mantra beginning with aśvatthe etc. He will never be afflicted by Saturn. It will destroy evil dreams too.

## \|\| 2.84.66 \|\|

*tatastāmravarāhākhyaṃ tīrthaṃ caivātipāvanam \|*  
*yatra snānena dānena na majjedaghasāgare \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Thereafter is the Tīrtha called Tāmra-Varāha. It is exceedingly sacred. If the devotee bathes there and makes some gifts, he will never become immersed in the ocean of sins.

## \|\| 2.84.67 \|\|

*tadagre kālagaṃgā ca kalikalmaṣanāśinī \|*  
*tasyāṃ snātvā naro dhīmāṃstatkṣaṇānniragho bhavet \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Beyond it is Kālagaṅgā that destroys the sins of the Kali age. A sensible man who bathes there becomes rid of sins instantly.

## \|\| 2.84.68 \|\|

*iṃdradyumnaṃ mahātīrthamiṃdradyumneśvarāgrataḥ \|*  
*toyakṛtyaṃ tatra kṛtvā lokamaiṃdramavāpnuyāta \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The great Indradyumna Tīrtha is in front of Indradyumneśvara. By performing aquatic rites there one shall attain the world of Indra.

## \|\| 2.84.69 \|\|

*tatastu rāmatīrthaṃ ca vīrarāmeśvarāgrataḥ \|*  
*tattīrthasnānamātreṇa vaiṣṇavaṃ lokamāpnuyāt \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Thereafter is Rāma Tīrtha in front of Vīrarāmeśvara. Merely by bathing in that Tīrtha one shall attain the world of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.84.70 \|\|

*tata aikṣvākavaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvāghaughavināśanam \|*  
*tatra snānena pūtātmā jāyate manujottamaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Thereafter is Aikṣvākava Tīrtha destructive of the masses of all sins. An excellent man becomes sanctified in his soul by taking his bath there.

## \|\| 2.84.71 \|\|

*maruttatīrthaṃ tatprāṃte marutteśvarasannidho \|*  
*tatra snātvā tamarcyeśaṃ mahadaiśvaryamāpnuyāt \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Marutta Tīrtha is by its side in the vicinity of Marutteśvara. By taking bath there and adorning the Lord, one shall attain great prosperity.

## \|\| 2.84.72 \|\|

*maitrāvaruṇatīrthaṃ ca tataḥ pātakanāśanam \|*  
*tatra piṃḍapradānena pitṝṇāṃ bhavati priyaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thereafter is Maitrāvaruṇa Tīrtha, destructive of sins. By offering balls of rice there, one becomes a favourite of the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 2.84.73 \|\|

*tatognitīrthavimalamagnīśa purato mahat \|*  
*agnilokamavāpnoti tattīrthaparimajjanāt \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Thereafter is the great and pure Agni Tīrtha in front of Agnīśa. By diving in that Tīrtha, one attains Agniloka.

## \|\| 2.84.74 \|\|

*aṃgāratīrthaṃ tatraiva aṃgāreśvarasannidhau \|*  
*tatrāṃgāra caturthyāṃ nu snātvā niṣpāpatāmiyāt \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. There itself in the vicinity of Aṅgāreśvara is Aṅgāra Tīrtha. On the Aṅgāra Caturthī day (the 4th in the dark half falling on Tuesday) a devotee taking his bath there becomes liberated from sins.

## \|\| 2.84.75 \|\|

*tato vai kalitīrthaṃ ca kalaśeśvarasannidhau \|*  
*snātvā talliṃgamabhyarcya kalikālānna bibhyati \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Thereafter is Kali Tīrtha in the vicinity of Kalaśeśvara. If one bathes there and adores that Liṅga, be need not be afraid of Kali age and Kāla (god of Death).

## \|\| 2.84.76 \|\|

*caṃdratīrthaṃ ca tatraiva caṃdreśvarasamīpataḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvārcya caṃdreśaṃ caṃdralokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. There itself is Candra Tīrtha in the vicinity of Candreśvara. By taking bath there and worshipping Candreśvara the devotee attains the world of the Moon.

## \|\| 2.84.77 \|\|

*tadagre vīratīrthaṃ ca vīreśvara samīpataḥ \|*  
*yaduktaṃ prāktavapurastīrthānāmuttamaṃ param \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Beyond that is Vīra Tīrtha in the vicinity of Vīreśvara which has already been mentioned to you. It is the greatest and most excellent of all Tīrthas.

## \|\| 2.84.78 \|\|

*vighneśatīrthaṃ ca tataḥ sarvavighnavighātakṛt \|*  
*jātucittatra saṃsnāto na vighnairabhibhūyate \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thereafter is Vighneśa Tīrtha that removes all obstacles. Even one who has perfectly bathed therein is not assailed by obstacles.

## \|\| 2.84.79 \|\|

*hariścaṃdrasya rājarṣastatastīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*yatra snāto naro jātu na satyāccayavate kacit \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Thereafter is excellent Tīrtha of the saintly King Hariścandra. One who takes his holy bath there, never swerves from truth.

## \|\| 2.84.80 \|\|

*hariścaṃdrasya tīrthe tu yacchreyaḥ samupārjitam \|*  
*tadakṣayaphalaṃ vīra iha loke paratra ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The merit acquired in the Tīrtha of Hariścandra, O Vīra, gives inexhaustible enjoyment in this world as well as the other.

## \|\| 2.84.81 \|\|

*tataḥ parvatatīrthaṃ ca parvateśa samīpataḥ \|*  
*sarvaparvaphalaṃ tasya snātvā parvaṇyaparvaṇi \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Thereafter is Parvata Tīrtha in the vicinity of Paravateśa. The holy bath therein whether on Parva Kāla or otherwise, yields the benefit of all festive occasions.

## \|\| 2.84.82 \|\|

*kaṃbalāśvataraṃ tīrthaṃ tatra sarvaviṣāpaham \|*  
*tatra snāto bhavenmartyo gītavidyāviśāradaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Kambaleśvara Tīrtha there eliminates all kinds of poisons. A man who takes his holy ablution becomes an expert in musical lore.

## \|\| 2.84.83 \|\|

*tataḥ sārasvataṃ tīrthaṃ sarvavidyopapādakam \|*  
*tiṣṭheyuḥ pitarastatra saha devarṣimānavaiḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Thereafter is Sārasvata Tīrtha that bestows all Lores. The Pitṛs shall be present there along with the celestial sages and human beings (Pitṭs of that category).

## \|\| 2.84.84 \|\|

*umātīrthaṃ tu tatraiva sarvaśaktisamanvitam \|*  
*aumeyalokaprāptyai syātsnānamātreṇa niścitam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Umā Tīrtha is there itself. It possesses all power. Merely by taking bath therein it will be conducive to the attainment of Umā’s world.

## \|\| 2.84.85 \|\|

*tatastrilokī vikhyātaṃ trilokyuddharaṇakṣamam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ śreṣṭhataraṃ vīra yadākhyā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Beyond that is the most excellent Tīrtha the name of which is Maṇīkarṇikā. It is well-known in all the three worlds. It is capable of uplifting the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.84.86 \|\|

*cakrapuṣkariṇītīrthaṃ tadādau viṣṇunā kṛtam \|*  
*tadākhyā karṇanādeva sarvaiḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. That is the same as Cakrapuṣkariṇī Tīrtha made at the outset by Viṣṇu. Merely by hearing its name one is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 2.84.87 \|\|

*svargaukasastrisaṃdhyaṃ vai japaṃti maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*yannāmagrahaṇaṃ puṃsāṃ śreyasaṃ paramāya hi \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The heaven-dwellers perform the Japa of Maṇikarṇikā in all the three Sandhyās (dawn, midday and dusk). The utterance of the name thereof is conducive to the great welfare of all men.

## \|\| 2.84.88 \|\|

*yaiḥ śrutā yaiḥ smṛtā vīra yairdṛṣṭā maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*ta eva kṛtino loke kṛtakṛtyāsta eva hi \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. O Vīra, only they are blessed, they can be considered as persons of fulfilled tasks by whom Maṇikarṇikā is heard, seen and remembered.

## \|\| 2.84.89 \|\|

*triloke ye japaṃtīha mānavā maṇikarṇikām \|*  
*japāmi tānahaṃ vīra trikālaṃ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. O Vīra, thrice a day I perform the Japa of those men of meritorious deeds who perform the Japa of Maṇikarṇikā in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.84.90 \|\|

*iṣṭaṃ tena mahāyajñaiḥ sahasraśatadakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*paṃcākṣarī mahāvidyā yenoktā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. If the five-syllabled great Mantra, Ma-ṇi-kar-ṇi-kā is uttered by anyone, it is as though he has performed many great Yajñas with a hundred thousand (gold coins) for Dakṣiṇā.

## \|\| 2.84.91 \|\|

*mahādānāni dattāni tena vai puṇyakarmaṇā \|*  
*yenāhamarcito vīra saṃprāpya maṇikarṇikām \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. O Vīra, if after reaching Maṇikarṇikā I am worshipped by anyone, he is a man of meritorious deeds, by whom great gifts have been donated.

## \|\| 2.84.92 \|\|

*maṇikarṇyaṃbubhiryena tarpitāḥ prapitāmahāḥ \|*  
*tena śrāddhāni dattāni gayāyāṃ madhupāyasaiḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. If the ancestors have been propitiated by anyone by means of the waters of Maṇikarṇikā, it is as though Śrāddhas have been performed by him at Gayā with honey and milk puddings.

## \|\| 2.84.93 \|\|

*maṇikarṇījalaṃ yena saṃpītaṃ śuddhabuddhinā \|*  
*kiṃ tasya somapānaistaiḥ punarāvṛttilakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Somapānas (‘Drinking Soma juice frequently’) are characterized by a return to this world. Of what avail is Somapāna (Drinking of Soma juice) to that man of purified intellect by whom the water of Maṇikarṇikā is drunk (as Mokṣa is attained thereby)?

## \|\| 2.84.94 \|\|

*te snātāḥ sarvatīrtheṣu mahāparvasubhūriśaḥ \|*  
*tathā ca sarvāvabhṛthairyaiḥ snātā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. If the holy ablution is performed in Maṇikarṇikā it is as though they have taken baths in all the Tīrthas again and again during the great Parva occasions. Similarly, they have had all the Avabhṭtha baths.

## \|\| 2.84.95 \|\|

*taiḥ surāḥ pūjitāḥ sarve brahmaviṣṇumukhā makhaiḥ \|*  
*yaiḥ svarṇakusumairatnairarcitā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. If Maṇikarṇikā is adored with gems and flowers of gold, it is as though they have worshipped all the Suras beginning with Brahmā and Viṣṇu by means of holy sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.84.96 \|\|

*ahaṃ tenomayā sārdhaṃ dīkṣāṃ saṃprāpya śāṃbhavīm \|*  
*arcitaḥ pratyahaṃ yena pūjitā ṇikarṇikā \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. If Maṇikarṇikā is worshipped by anyone, it is as though I have been daily worshipped along with Umā after the Śāṃbhavī Dīkṣā (Initiation in the adoration of Śaṃbhu).

## \|\| 2.84.97 \|\|

*tapāṃsi tena taptāni śīrṇaparṇādinā ciram \|*  
*sevitā śraddhayā yena śrīmatī maṇikarṇikā \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. If the glorious Maṇikarṇikā has been faithfully served by anyone, it is as though austerities have been performed by him for a long time with withered leaves etc. (for diet).

## \|\| 2.84.98-99 \|\|

*dattvā dānāni bhūrīṇi makhāniṣṭvā tu bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*ciraṃ taptvāpyaraṇyeṣu svargaiśvaryānmahīṃ punaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*vipuletra mahīpṛṣṭhe paṃcakrośyāṃ manoharā \|*  
*saṃśritā maṇikarṇīyaiste yātāścānivartakāḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. One may very well make plenty of gifts, one may perform many sacrifices and one may perform austerities in the forests for a long time. Still after enjoying heavenly opulence one has to return to the earth. But if Maṇikarṇikā, the charming Tīrtha in Pañcakrośī (the holy spot extending to five Krośas), in the extensive earth is resorted to, those devotees go away never to return (to Saṃsāra).

## \|\| 2.84.100 \|\|

*dānānāṃ ca vratānāṃ ca kratūnāṃ tapasāmapi \|*  
*idameva phalaṃ manye yadāpyā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. I think that this alone is the benefit of gifts, Vratas, sacrifices and austerities that Maṇikarṇikā becomes accessible.

## \|\| 2.84.101 \|\|

*mokṣalakṣmīriyaṃ sākṣācchrīmatī maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*prāyosyā mahimānaṃ vai navedmyahamapi sphuṭam \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. This glorious Maṇikarṇikā is the Glory of Salvation itself directly. Even I do not know clearly the (entire) greatness of this Maṇikarṇikā practically.

## \|\| 2.84.102-105 \|\|

*avācyāṃ maṇikarṇyāśca tīrthaṃ pāśupataṃ param \|*  
*tīrthaṃ tu rudravāsākhyaṃ viśvatīrthamataḥ param \|\| 102 \|\|*

*muktitīrthaṃ tato ramyamavimuktamathottamam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ ca tārakaṃ skāṃdaṃ ḍhuṃḍhestīrthaṃ tatopi ca \|\| 103 \|\|*

*bhavāneyamathaiśānaṃ jñānatīrthamathottamam \|*  
*naṃditīrthaṃ viṣṇutīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ paitāmahaṃ tataḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*nābhitīrthamidaṃ caiva brahmanālamataḥ param \|*  
*tato bhāgīrathaṃ tīrthaṃ yattavāgre purākathi \|\| 105 \|\|*

102-105. To the south of Maṇikarṇikā is the great Pāśupata Tīrtha; beyond it is the Tīrtha called Rudrāvāsa and thereafter is the great Viśva Tīrtha. Thereafter is the beautiful Mukti Tīrtha; then the excellent Avimukta, Tāraka Tīrtha and Skanda Tīrtha. Beyond it is the Tīrtha of Dhuṇḍhi. Then there are the Tīrthas of Bhavānī, Īśāna, the excellent Jñāna Tīrtha, Nandī Tīrtha, Viṣṇu Tīrtha and the Tīrtha of Pitāmaha. This is the Nābhi Tīrtha and beyond it is Brahmanāla. Then the Bhagīratha Tīrtha which has already been recounted to you.

## \|\| 2.84.106 \|\|

*tīrthātyuttaravāhinyāṃ svardhunyāṃ kāśisannidhau \|*  
*saṃtyanekāni puṇyāni mayoktānyalpaśaḥ punaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. On the north-flowing celestial river there are many meritorious Tīrthas near Kāśī but only a few have been mentioned by me.

## \|\| 2.84.107 \|\|

*tatrāpi nitarāṃ śreṣṭhā paṃcatīrthī nṛpāṃgaja \|*  
*yasyāṃ stātvā naro bhūyo garbhavāsaṃ na saṃsmaret \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. O Prince, among them Pañcatīrthī (set of five Tīrthas) is exceedingly excellent. By the holy ablution therein a man can well forget further stay in a womb.

## \|\| 2.84.108-110 \|\|

*prathamaṃ cāsisaṃbhedaṃ tīrthānāṃ pravaraṃ param \|*  
*tato daśāśvamedhākhyaṃ sarvatīrthaniṣevitam \|\| 108 \|\|*

*tataḥ pādodakaṃ tīrthamādikeśavasannidhau \|*  
*tataḥ paṃcanadaṃ puṇyaṃ snānamātrādaghaughahṛt \|\| 109 \|\|*

*eteṣāmapi tīrthānāṃ caturṇāmapi sattama \|*  
*paṃcamaṃ maṇikarṇyākhyaṃ manāveyavaśuddhidam \|\| 110 \|\|*

108-110. The first one is the confluence of Asi (with Gaṅgā), the greatest and the most excellent one among the Tīrthas. Thereafter is the Tīrtha called Daśāśvamedha which is resorted to by all the Tīrthas. There is the Pādodaka Tīrtha in the vicinity of Ādikeśava; then is the meritorious Pañcanada which removes mass of sins merely by the ablution. O highly excellent one, apart from these four Tīrthas the fifth one named Maṇikarṇikā accords the purity of the mind and the limbs.

## \|\| 2.84.111 \|\|

*ahaṃ snāmyatra satatamumayā saha parvasu \|*  
*brahmaṇā viṣṇunā sārdhaṃ saheṃdrādisurarṣibhiḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. I take bath here always in the company of Umā during Parvan days (religious festivals) and also with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra and other Suras and sages.

## \|\| 2.84.112-113 \|\|

*ataevātra gīyeta gātheyaṃ śrutisaṃmatā \|*  
*nāgalokakṛtāvāsaiḥ svargaukobhiśca saṃtatam \|\| 112 \|\|*

*satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyaṃ satyapūrvamidaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*maṇikarṇī samaṃ tīrthaṃ nāsti brahmāṃḍagolake \|\| 113 \|\|*

112-113. That is why this Gāthā (verse current among the folks) in accordance with the Vedas, is being sung always by those who reside in Nāgaloka and also by the heaven-dwellers: ‘It is the truth. It is the truth. (I repeat) Again it is the truth. This is the truthful statement. There is no Tīrtha on a par with Maṇikarṇikā anywhere in the Cosmic Egg.’

## \|\| 2.84.114 \|\|

*paṃcatīrthyāṃ naraḥ snātvā na dehaṃ pāṃcabhautikam \|*  
*gṛhṇāti jātucitkāśyāṃ paṃcāsyovātha jāyate \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. By taking the holy bath in Pañcatīrthī a man ceases to take up the body consisting of five elements. Or he becomes Pañcāsya (the five-countenanced Lord Viśveśvara himself).”

## \|\| 2.84.115 \|\|

*iti dattvā varāndevo vīrasyāṃtardadhe haraḥ \|*  
*sa ca vīropi vīreśaṃ prārcya prāptaḥ samīhitam \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. After granting to Vīra these boons, Lord Hara vanished. That Vīra adored Vīreśa and attained his desire.

## \|\| 2.84.116 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*tīrthādhyāyamimaṃ puṇyamagaste yo niśāmayet \|*  
*tasyāghasaṃkṣayaṃ yāyādapi janmaśatārjitam \|\| 116 \|\|*

Skanda said:

116\. O Agastya, if anyone listens to this meritorious chapter on Tīrthas, his sins become reduced even if they have been acquired in the course of hundreds of births.

## \|\| 2.84.117 \|\|

*iti vīreśvarākhyānaṃ tīrthākhyānaprasaṃgataḥ \|*  
*kathitaṃ te purāgaste kāmeśaṃ kathayāmyataḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. This narrative of Vīreśvara has already been told to you in the context of Tīrthas. Hereafter I shall describe Kāmeśa.

## Chapter 85 - Granting of Boons to Durvāsas

## \|\| 2.85.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*jagajjananyāḥ pārvatyāḥ purogaste purāriṇā \|*  
*yathākhyāyi kathā puṇyā tathā te kathayāmyaham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. I shall narrate unto you, O Agastya, the meritorious story in the manner recounted by Purārī (Śiva) to Pārvatī, the mother of the universe.

## \|\| 2.85.2-3 \|\|

*purā mahīmimāṃ sarvāṃ sasamudrādrikānanām \|*  
*sasaritkāṃ sārṇavāṃ ca sagrāmapurapattanām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*paribhramya mahātejā mahāmarṣo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*durvāsāḥ saṃpariprāptaḥ śaṃbhorānaṃdakānanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Formerly Durvāsas, a great ascetic, excessively refulgent and irascible, wandered over this earth consisting of oceans, mountains, forests, rivers, big lakes, villages, towns and cities. Ultimately he reached Ānandakānana of Śaṃbhu.

## \|\| 2.85.4 \|\|

*vilokyākrīḍamakhilaṃ bahuprāsādamaṃḍitam \|*  
*bahukuṃḍataḍāgaṃ ca śaṃbhostoṣamupāgamat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing the whole of the pleasure-grove of Śaṃbhu beautified with many palaces and consisting of many ponds and lakes, he became delighted.

## \|\| 2.85.5 \|\|

*padepade munīnāṃ ca jitakāla mahābhiyām \|*  
*dṛṣṭoṭajāni ramyāṇi durvāsā vismitobhavat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On seeing at every step the beautiful huts of the sages who had conquered the excessive fear of the god of Death, Durvāsas became surprised.

## \|\| 2.85.6 \|\|

*sarvartukusumānvṛkṣānsucchāyasnigdhapallavān \|*  
*saphalānsulatāśliṣṭāndṛṣṭvā prītimagānmuniḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing the trees with blossoms pertaining to all the seasons, having plenty of shade and glossy tender sprouts, yielding excellent fruits and entwined by excellent creepers, the sage became pleased.

## \|\| 2.85.7-11 \|\|

*durvāsāścātihṛṣṭobhū्ddṛṣṭvā pāśupatottamān \|*  
*bhūtibhūṣitasarvāṃgāñjaṭājaṭitamaulikān \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kaupīnamātra vasanānsmarāri dhyāna tatparān \|*  
*kakṣīkṛtamahālābūnhuḍutkārajitāṃbudān \|\| 8 \|\|*

*karaṃḍadaṃḍapānīya pātramātraparigrahān \|*  
*kvacittridaṃḍino dṛṣṭvā niḥsaṃgā niṣparigrahān \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kālādapi nirātaṃkānviśveśaśaraṇaṃ gatān \|*  
*kvacidvedarahasyajñānābālyabrahmacāriṇaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nityaṃ bhāgīrathīsnānaparipiṃgalamūrdhajān \|*  
*vilokya kāśyāṃ durvāsā brāhmaṇānmumudetarām \|\| 11 \|\|*

7-11. Durvāsas was exceedingly delighted on seeing the excellent Pāśupata devotees whose limbs were all embellished with holy ash. Their heads were covered with matted hairs. A loin cloth alone constituted the robe of everyone of them. They were engrossed in meditating on Smarāri (Śiva). Big bottle gourds were tucked in their armpits. The Huḍutkāra (Huḍ-like bellowing sound) produced by them was louder than the rumble of clouds. Their sole possessions were a Karaṇḍa (cane-vessel for holding the Liṅga), a staff and a drinking pot. In certain places, he saw the Tridaṇḍins (Sannyāsins having three staffs) devoid of possessions and contacts, not afraid of even Kāla because they had sought refuge in Viśveśa. In certain places he saw life-long celibates conversant with the mystic doctrines of the Vedas. On seeing the Brāhmaṇas in Kāśī with hairs turned tawny because of their daily bath in Gaṅgā, Durvāsas rejoiced all the more.

## \|\| 2.85.12 \|\|

*paśuṣvapi ca yā tuṣṭirmṛgeṣvapi ca yā dyutiḥ \|*  
*tiryakṣvapi ca yā hṛṣṭiḥ kāśyāṃ nānyatra sā sphuṭam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “In Kāśī there is a unique sense of satisfaction in the domesticated animals, a special lustre in the animals of the forest such as the deer etc. and an excessive joy seen in birds and other creatures not so very manifest elsewhere.

## \|\| 2.85.13 \|\|

*idaṃ suśreyaso vyuṣṭiḥ kvāmareṣu triviṣṭape \|*  
*yatratyeṣvapi tiryakṣu paramānaṃdavardhinī \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. This spot is the abode of excellent welfare. Where is such a spot available to the immortal ones in heaven? In the creatures of this place too, it increases the greatest pleasure.

## \|\| 2.85.14 \|\|

*varametepi paśava ānaṃdavanacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*sadānaṃdāḥ punardevānanaṃdanavanāśritāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Far superior are these animals that wander in Ānandavana with permanent bliss, and not the Devas who resort to Nandanavana.

## \|\| 2.85.15 \|\|

*varaṃ kāśīpurīvāsī mlecchopi hi śubhāyatiḥ \|*  
*nānyatratyo dīkṣitopi sa hi mukterabhājanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Better to be a Mleccha (Barbarian) resident of Kāśī with an auspicious future, than a Dīkṣita (initiated Vedic Brāhmaṇa) elsewhere, who does not merit salvation.

## \|\| 2.85.16 \|\|

*vaiśveśvarī purī caiṣā yathā me cittahāriṇī \|*  
*sarvāpi na tathā kṣoṇī na svargo naiva nāgabhūḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The entire earth, the heavenly world and the world of serpents, do not attract my mind in the same way as this city of Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 2.85.17 \|\|

*sthairyaṃ babaṃdha na kvāpi bhramato me manogatiḥ \|*  
*sarvasminnapi bhūbhāge yathā sthairyamagādiha \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Though I have been wandering all over the earth nowhere else did my mind gain steadfastness as it has here.

## \|\| 2.85.18 \|\|

*ramyā purī bhavedeṣā brahmāṃḍādakhilādapi \|*  
*pariṣṭutyeti durvāsāścetovṛttimavāpa ha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the entire Cosmic Egg, this must necessarily be the most beautiful city.” After eulogizing thus, Durvāsas attained some steadiness of the mind.

## \|\| 2.85.19 \|\|

*tapyamānopi hi tapaḥ suciraṃ sa mahātapāḥ \|*  
*yadā nāpa phalaṃ kiṃciccukopa ca tadā bhṛśam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Though that sage of excessive penance performed the austerities for a long time, he did not attain any fruit thereof. Then he got excessively angry.

## \|\| 2.85.20 \|\|

*dhikca māṃ tāpasaṃ duṣṭaṃ dhikca me duścaraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*dhikca kṣetramidaṃ śaṃbhoḥ sarveṣāṃ ca pratārakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “Fie upon me, a defiled ascetic! Fie upon my penance which is difficult to be performed! Fie upon this holy spot of Saṃbhu that deceives all!

## \|\| 2.85.21 \|\|

*yathā na muktiratra syātkasyāpi karavai tathā \|*  
*iti śaptuṃ yadodyuktaḥ saṃjahāsa tadā śivaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I shall do something to bring about such a state as no one gains salvation here.” Saying thus he was about to curse. Then Śiva laughed loudly.

## \|\| 2.85.22 \|\|

*tatra liṃgamabhūdekaṃ khyātaṃ prahasiteśvaram \|*  
*talliṃgadarśanātpuṃsāmānaṃdaḥ syātpadepade \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A Liṅga appeared there and it became well-known as Prahasiteśvara (‘Lord of boisterous laugh’). On visiting this Liṅga, men will attain delight at every step.

## \|\| 2.85.23 \|\|

*uvāca vismayāviṣṭo manasyeva maheśitā \|*  
*īdṛśebhyastapasvibhyo namostviti punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The surprised Maheśitā (Śiva) said in his mind: ‘I offer obeisance to ascetics like this again and again.

## \|\| 2.85.24 \|\|

*yatraiva hi tapasyaṃti yatraiva vihitāśramāḥ \|*  
*labdhapratiṣṭhā yatraiva tatraivāmarṣiṇo dvijāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. These Brāhmaṇas became unduly indignant with the place where they perform penance, where they have built their hermitages for penance and where they have been established.

## \|\| 2.85.25 \|\|

*manākciṃtitamātraṃ tu cellabhaṃte na tāpasāḥ \|*  
*krudhā tadaiva jīyaṃte hāriṇyā tapasāṃ śriyaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. If they do not get the least of what they have only just thought of, they are overwhelmed with anger that deprives them of the glory of austerities.

## \|\| 2.85.26 \|\|

*tathāpi tāpasā mānyāḥ svaśreyovṛddhikāṃkṣibhiḥ \|*  
*akrodhanāḥ krodhanā vā kā ciṃtā hi tapasvinām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Still ascetics should be honoured by those who desire their own welfare. Why mind this in regard to the ascetics whether they are hot-tempered or otherwise?’

## \|\| 2.85.27 \|\|

*iti yāvanmaheśāno manasyeva viciṃtayet \|*  
*tāvattatkrodhajo vahnirvyānaśe vyomamaṃḍalam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Even as Maheśāna thought within himself thus, the fire due to the anger of the (sage) pervaded the entire firmament.

## \|\| 2.85.28 \|\|

*tatkodhānaladhūmoghairvyāpitaṃ yannabhoṃgaṇam \|*  
*taddadhāti nabhodyāpi nīlimānaṃ mahattaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Since the entire expanse of the sky was permeated by the masses of columns of smoke arising from the fire of his anger, the sky retains its great bluish colour even today.

## \|\| 2.85.29 \|\|

*tato gaṇāḥ parikṣubdhāḥ pralayārṇava nīravat \|*  
*āḥ kimetatkimetadvai bhāṣamāṇāḥ parasparam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then the attendants (of Śiva) became agitated like the waters of the ocean at the time of the ultimate annihilation. They asked one another, “What! What is this!!”

## \|\| 2.85.30 \|\|

*garjaṃtastarjayaṃtaśca prodyatā yudhapāṇayaḥ \|*  
*pramathāḥ paritasthuste parito dhāma śāṃbhavam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Roaring and making gestures of threat and lifting their weapons in their hands, the Pramathas stood in readiness allround the abode of Śaṃbhu.

## \|\| 2.85.31 \|\|

*ko yamaḥ kothavā kālaḥ ko mṛtyuḥ kastathāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*ko vā vidhātā ke lekhāḥ kuddheṣvasmāsu kaḥ paraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “Who is Yama? Who is Kāla? Who is Mṛtyu (Death)? Who is the Antaka (destroyer)? Who is Vidhātā (creator)? Who are these Devas (like Indra)? When we are angry, who can be our enemy?

## \|\| 2.85.32 \|\|

*agniṃ pibāmo jalavaccūrṇīkurmokhilāngirīn \|*  
*saptāpi cārṇavāṃstūrṇaṃ karavāma marusthalīm \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. We shall drink fire like water. We shall turn all the mountains into powder. We shall convert all the seven oceans into desert region.

## \|\| 2.85.33 \|\|

*pātālaṃ cānayāmordhvamadho dadhmothavā divam \|*  
*ekameva hi vā grāsaṃ gaganaṃ karavāmahe \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. We shall pull up Pātāla or pull down heaven. We shall make a mouthful of the entire sky.

## \|\| 2.85.34 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍabhāṃḍamathavā sphoṭayāmaḥ kṣaṇena hi \|*  
*āsphālayāmo vānyonyaṃ kālaṃ mṛtyuṃ ca tālavat \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. We shall shatter the entire cosmos into pieces. We shall hurl Kāla and Mṛtyu against each other like palm fruits.

## \|\| 2.85.35 \|\|

*grasāmo vātha bhuvanaṃ muktvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*yatra muktā bhavaṃtyeva mṛtamātreṇa jaṃtavaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Or we shall be swallowing the universe excluding the city of Vārāṇasī where the creatures become liberated soon after death.

## \|\| 2.85.36 \|\|

*kuto'yaṃ dhūmasaṃbhāro jvālāvalyaḥ kutastvamūḥ \|*  
*ko vā mṛtyuṃjayaṃ rudraṃ no vidyānmadamohitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Whence is this mass of smoke? Whence is this mass of flames? Who is deluded by arrogance and conceit and does not know Rudra, the conqueror of the god of Death?”

## \|\| 2.85.37 \|\|

*iti pāriṣadāḥ śaṃbhormahābhaya bhayapradāḥ \|\| jalpaṃtaḥ kalpayāmāsuḥ prākāraṃ gaganaspṛśam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Prattling and boasting thus, the attendants of Saṃbhu, the strikers of fear into even great terror, built a rampart that touched the sky.

## \|\| 2.85.38-46 \|\|

*śakalīkṛtya bahuśaḥ śilāvatpralayānalam \|*  
*naṃdī ca naṃdiṣeṇaśca somanaṃdī mahodaraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*mahāhanurmahāgrīvo mahākālo jitāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*mṛtyuprakaṃpano bhīmo ghaṃṭākarṇo mahābalaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kṣobhaṇo drāvaṇo jṛṃbhī pacāsyaḥ paṃcalocanaḥ \|*  
*dviśirāstriśirāḥ somaḥ paṃcahasto daśānanaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*caṃḍo bhṛṃgiriṭistuṃḍī pracaṃḍastāṃḍavapriyaḥ \|*  
*piciṃḍilaḥ sthūlaśirāḥ sthūlakeśo gabhastimān \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kṣemakaḥ kṣemadhanvā ca vīrabhadro raṇapriyaḥ \|*  
*caṃḍapāṇiḥ śūlapāṇiḥ pāśapāṇiḥ karodaraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*dīrghagrīvotha piṃgākṣaḥ piṃgalaḥ piṃgamūrdhajaḥ \|*  
*bahunetro laṃbakarṇaḥ kharvaḥ parvatavigrahaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*gokarṇo gajakarṇaśca kokilākhyo gajānanaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ vai naigameyaśca vikaṭāsyoṭṭahāsakaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sīrapāṇiḥ śivārāvo vaiṇiko veṇuvādanaḥ \|*  
*durādharṣo duḥsahaśca garjano riputarjanaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*ityādayo gaṇeśānāḥ śatakoṭi durāsadāḥ \|*  
*kāśyāṃ nivārayāmāsurapi prābhaṃjanīṃ gatim \|\| 46 \|\|*

38-46. They split the fire of Pralaya (arising from the anger of Durvāsas) into many pieces as though they were rocky boulders. The following Gaṇeśānas unassailable to others like thunderbolt, checked even the movement of the wind in Kāśī. They were: Nandin, Nandiṣeṇa, Somanandin, Mahodara, Mahāhanu, Mahāgrīva, Mahākāla, Jitāntaka, Mṛtyuprakaṃpana, Bhīma, Ghaṇṭākarṇa, Mahābala, Kṣobhaṇa, Drāvaṇa, Jṛṃbhin, Pañcāsya, Pañcalocana, Dviśiras, Triśiras, Soma, Pañcahasta, Daśānana, Caṇḍa, Bhṛṅgiriṭi, Tundin, Pracaṇḍa, Tāṇḍavapriya, Piciṇḍila, Sthūlaśiras, Sthūlakeśa, Gabhastimān, Kṣemaka, Kṣemadhanvan, Vīrabhadra, Raṇapriya, Caṇḍapāṇi, Śūlapāṇi, Pāśapāṇi, Kṛśodara, Dīrghagrīva, Piṅgākṣa, Piṅgala, Piṅgamūrdhaja, Bahunetra, Laṃbakarṇa, Kharva, Parvatavigraha, Gokarṇa, Gajakarṇa, Kokilākhya, Gajānana, I (i.e. Skanda), Naigameya, Vikaṭāsya, Aṭṭahāsaka, Sīrapāṇi, Śivārāva, Vaiṇika, Veṇuvādana, Durādharṣa, Duḥsaha, Garjana and Riputarjana.

## \|\| 2.85.47 \|\|

*kṣubdheṣu teṣu vīreṣu cakaṃpe bhuvanatrayam \|*  
*durvāsasaśca kopāgni jvālābhirvyākulīkṛtam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. When those warriors were agitated, all the three worlds shook and became bewildered by the flames of the anger of Durvāsas.

## \|\| 2.85.48 \|\|

*tadā viviśatuḥ kāśyāṃ sūryācaṃdramasāvapi \|*  
*na gaṇairakṛtānujñau tattejaḥ śamitaprabhau \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The Sun and the Moon had their lustre dimmed by the refulgence of the Gaṇas and so (out of pity) were permitted by them to enter Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.85.49 \|\|

*nivārya pramathānīkamatikṣubdhamumādhavaḥ \|*  
*madaṃśa eva hi munīrānasūye ya eṣa vai \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Umādhava (Śiva) checked the army of Pramathas, which was highly perturbed (saying), “This sage, the son of Anasūya, is a part of mine.”

## \|\| 2.85.50 \|\|

*atho durvāsase liṃgādāvirāsītkṛpānidhiḥ \|*  
*mahātejomayaḥ śaṃbhurmuniśāpātpurīmavan \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thereafter Śaṃbhu of great refulgence, the storehouse of compassion, came out of the Liṅga of Durvāsas thereby saving the city from the curse of the sage.

## \|\| 2.85.51 \|\|

*mābhūcchāpo muneḥ kāśyāṃ nirvāṇapratibaṃdhakaḥ \|*  
*ityanukrośato devastasya pratyakṣatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. “Let not the curse of the sage be an obstacle to the people’s salvation at Kāśi.” Pitying thus the Lord became directly visible to him.

## \|\| 2.85.52 \|\|

*uvāca ca prasannosmi mahākrodhana tāpasa \|*  
*varayasva varaḥ kaste mayā deyo viśaṃkitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He said: “I am pleased, O sage of excessive wrath; unhesitatingly choose what boon is to be given to you by me?"

## \|\| 2.85.53-58 \|\|

*tato vilajjitogastya śāpodyatakaro muniḥ \|*  
*aparāddhaṃ bahu mayā krodhāṃdheneti durdhiyā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*uvāca ceti bahuśo dhiṅmāṃ krodhavaśaṃgatam \|*  
*trailokyābhayadāṃ kāśīṃ śaptumudyatacetasam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*duḥkhārṇava nimagnānāṃ yātāyāteti khedinām \|*  
*karmapāśitakaṃṭhānāṃ kāśyekā muktisādhanam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ jaṃtujātānāṃ jananyekaikkāśikā \|*  
*mahāmṛtastanyadātrī netrī ca paramaṃ padam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*jananyā saha no kāśī labhedupamitiṃ kvacit \|*  
*dhārayejjananī garbhe kāśī garbhādvimocayet \|\| 57 \|\|*

*evaṃbhūtāṃ tu yaḥ kāśīmanyopi hi śapiṣyati \|*  
*tasyaiva śāpo bhavitā na tu kāśyāḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 58 \|\|*

53-58. Thereupon, O Agastya, the sage who had raised his hand for cursing became ashamed. He said, “Becoming blind with anger, I of an evil intellect, have committed a serious crime.” He repeatedly said, “Fie upon me who have been over-povered by anger! Fie upon me who attempted mentally to curse Kāśī that bestows freedom from fear on all the three worlds!

Kāśī alone is the means of salvation to all those who are immersed in the ocean of misery, who are extremely distressed due to the frequent coming and going (i.e. transmigration) and whose necks have been fettered by Karrnas.

To all the creatures, Kāśī alone is the mother who accords the milk of great nectar and who leads them to the highest position. There can be no comparison between Kāśī and a mother. The mother conceives one in the womb and Kāśī releases one from the womb.

If anyone also curses Kāśī of such excellence, he himself will get cursed; but Kāśī will never.”

## \|\| 2.85.59 \|\|

*iti durvāsaso vākyaṃ śrutvā devastrilocanaḥ \|*  
*atīva tuṣito jātaḥ kāśīstavana labdhamut \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. On hearing these words of Durvāsas, the Three-eyed Lord became exceedingly delighted with the added pleasure due to his praise of Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.85.60 \|\|

*yaḥ kāśīṃ stauti medhāvī yaḥ kāśīṃ hṛdi dhārayet \|*  
*tena taptaṃ tapastīvraṃ teneṣṭaṃ kratukoṭibhiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The intelligent one who eulogizes Kāśī, he who keeps Kāśī in his heart (is blessed, for) a fierce penance has been performed by him, a crore of sacrifices have been performed by him (by such a person).

## \|\| 2.85.61 \|\|

*jihvāgre vartate yasya kāśītyakṣarayugmakam \|*  
*na tasya garbhavāsaḥ syātkvacideva sumedhasaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. If the two syllables “Kā-śī” find a place at the tip of the tongue of anyone, he is of highly gifted intellect. He will never be conceived in a womb.

## \|\| 2.85.62 \|\|

*yo maṃtraṃ japati prātaḥ kāśī varṇadvayātmakam \|*  
*sa tu lokadvayaṃ jitvā lokātītaṃ vrajetpadam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. One who utters the two-syllabled Mantra, namely Kāśī, in the morning, conquers both the worlds and attains the position beyond all the worlds.

## \|\| 2.85.63 \|\|

*ānusūyeya te jñānaṃ kāśīstavana puṇyataḥ \|*  
*yathedānīṃ samutpannaṃ tathā na tapasaḥ purā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O son of Anasūyā, what knowledge you have gained due to the merit of eulogizing Kāśī now has not been acquired before (by you) by means of penance.

## \|\| 2.85.64 \|\|

*mune na me priyastadvaddīkṣito mama pūjakaḥ \|*  
*yādṛkpriyataraḥ satyaṃ kāśīstavana lālasaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O sage, a Dīkṣita who eulogizes and adores me is not as dearly loved (by me) as one who is fond of eulogizing Kāśī. This is the truth.

## \|\| 2.85.65 \|\|

*tādṛktuṣṭirna me dānaistādṛktuṣṭirna me makhaiḥ \|*  
*na tuṣṭistapasā tādṛgyādṛśī kāśisaṃstavaiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Through the eulogy of Kāśī I derive a pleasure the like of which I never get through religious gifts, sacrifices or penance (performed by devotees).

## \|\| 2.85.66 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānanaṃ yena stutametatsucetasā \|*  
*tenāhaṃ saṃstutaḥ samyaksarvaiḥ sūktaiḥ śrutīritaiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. If Ānandakānana is eulogized with genuinely sincere mind by anyone, it is as though I have been perfectly eulogized with all the Sūktas occurring in the Śrutis.

## \|\| 2.85.67 \|\|

*tava kāmāḥ samṛddhāḥ syurānusūyeya tāpasa \|*  
*jñānaṃ te paramaṃ bhāvi mahāmohavināśanam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O ascetic, O son of Anasūyā, all your desires shall be fulfilled; you will have the greatest knowledge that is destructive of the great delusion (Saṃsāra).

## \|\| 2.85.68 \|\|

*aparaṃ ca varaṃ brūhi kiṃ dātavyaṃ tavānagha \|*  
*tvādṛśā eva munayaḥ ślāghanīyā yataḥ satām \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Mention, O sinless one, what other boon is to be granted to you, because sages like you alone are worthy of the praise of good men.

## \|\| 2.85.69 \|\|

*yasyāstveva hi sāmarthyaṃ tapasaḥ kruddhyatīhasaḥ \|*  
*kupitopyasamarthastu kiṃ kartā kṣīṇavṛttivat \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. It is only one who is competent and capable by the performance of penance who can become angry. What can one who is incompetent do, even when he is angry? He is like one who is (destitute, and) bereft of means of sustenance.”

## \|\| 2.85.70 \|\|

*iti śrutvā pariṣṭutya durvāsāḥ kṛttivāsasam \|*  
*varaṃ ca prārthayāmāsa parihṛṣṭa tanūruhaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. On hearing this, Durvāsas eulogized the Lord clad in elephant hide. He experienced horripilation due to excess of delight and prayed for a boon.

## \|\| 2.85.71-73 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*devadeva jagannātha karuṇākara śaṃkara \|*  
*mahāparādhavidhvaṃsinnaṃdhakāre smarāṃtaka \|\| 71 \|\|*

*mṛtyuṃjayograbhūteśa mṛḍānīśa trilocana \|*  
*yadi prasanno me nātha yadi deyo varo mama \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tadidaṃ kāmadaṃ nāma ligamastviha dhūrjaṭe \|*  
*idaṃ ca palvalaṃ metra kāmakuṃḍākhyamastu vai \|\| 73 \|\|*

Durvāsas said:

71-73. O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the universe, O Śaṅkara, the merciful, O destroyer of great sins and crimes, O enemy of Andhaka, O destroyer of Smara, O Mṛtyuñjaya (‘conqueror of death’), O Ugra, O Lord of goblins, O Lord of Mṛḍānī, O three-eyed Lord, if the Lord is pleased with me, if a boon is to be granted to me, let this Liṅga be called Kāmada here. O Dhūrjaṭi, let this pond of mine be called Kāmakuṇḍa.

## \|\| 2.85.74-78 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*evamastu mahātejo mune paramakopana \|*  
*yattvayā sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ durvāseśvarasaṃjñitam \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tadeva kāmakṛnnṛṇāṃ kāmeśvaramihāstviti \|*  
*yaḥ pradoṣe trayodaśyāṃ śanivāsarasaṃyuji \|\| 75 \|\|*

*saṃsnāsyati naro dhīmānkāmakuṃḍe tvadāspade \|*  
*tvatsthāpitaṃ ca kāmeśaṃ liṃgaṃ drakṣyati mānavaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*sa vai kāmakṛtāddoṣādyāmīṃ nāpsyati yātanām \|*  
*bahavopi hi pāpmāno bahubhirjanmabhiḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*kāmatīrthāṃbu saṃsnānādyāsyaṃti vilayaṃ kṣaṇāt \|*  
*kāmāḥ samṛddhimāpsyaṃti kāmeśvara niṣevaṇāt \|\| 78 \|\|*

Devadeva (Śiva) said:

74-78. Let it be so, O sage of great splendour, O excessively irascible one; this Liṅga named Durvāseśvara installed by you will be Kāmeśvara (by name) bestowing desired things on men. An intelligent man who takes his holy bath in Kāmakuṇḍa that has been your resort, at Pradoṣa (dusk) when Trayodaśī (thirteenth day) coincides with Saturday and visits Kāmeśa Liṅga installed by you, will never be subjected to the tortures of Yama due to the fault effected by lust. Many sins committed in the course of many births become destroyed instantly, due to the holy dip in the waters of Kāma Tīrtha. By resorting to Kāmeśvara desires will become fulfilled.

## \|\| 2.85.79-81 \|\|

*iti dattvā varāñśaṃbhustalliṃge layamāyayau \|*  
*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*talliṃgārādhanātkāmāḥ prāptā durvāsasā bhṛśam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kāśyāṃ kāmeśvaraḥ sadā \|*  
*pūjanīyaḥ prayatnena mahākāmābhilāṣukaiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*kāmakuṃḍakṛtasnānairmahāpātakaśāṃtaye \|*  
*idaṃ kāmeśvarākhyānaṃ yaḥ paṭhiṣyati puṇyavān \|*  
*yaḥ śroṣyati ca medhāvī tau niṣpāpau bhaviṣyataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

79-81. After granting these boons, Śaṃbhu merged into that Liṅga.

## Chapter 86 - Manifestation of Viśvakarmeśa

## \|\| 2.86.1 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*viśvakarmeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ yatkāśyāṃ prathitaṃ param \|*  
*tasya liṃgasya kathaya devadeva samudbhavam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:

1\. The Viśvakarmeśvara Liṅga in Kāśī is very well-known. O Lord of Devas, narrate to me the origin of that Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.86.2 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi kathāṃ pātakanāśinīm \|*  
*viśvakarmeśa liṃgasya prādurbhāvaṃ manoharam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Devadeva said:

2\. Listen, O goddess, I shall narrate the story that destroys sins, the charming story of how Viśvakarmeśa Liṅga manifested itself.

## \|\| 2.86.3 \|\|

*viśvakarmābhavatpūrvaṃ brahmaṇastvaparā tanuḥ \|*  
*tvaṣṭuḥ prajāpateḥ putro nipuṇaḥ sarvakarmasu \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly there was Viśvakarman who was another physical form of Brahmā (the Creator). He was the son of Patriarch Tvaṣṭṛ. He was (indeed) clever in all arts and crafts.

## \|\| 2.86.4 \|\|

*kṛtopanayanaḥ sotha bālo gurukule vasan \|*  
*cakāra guruśuśrūṣāṃ bhikṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After being invested with the sacred thread, the boy was living in the abode of his preceptor (for education). He had his daily meal out of the alms of cooked rice he got. He served his preceptor duly.

## \|\| 2.86.5-7 \|\|

*ekadā tadguruḥ prāha prāvṛṭkāle samāgate \|*  
*kurūṭajaṃ madarthaṃ tvaṃ yathā prāvṛṇna bādhate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yatkadācinna bhajyeta na purātanatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*gurupatnyātvabhihito re tvāṣṭra kuru kaṃcukam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mamāṃgayogyaṃ no gāḍhaṃ na ślathaṃ ca prayatnataḥ \|*  
*vinaiva vāsasā cāru vālkalaṃ ca sadojjvalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Once, at the advent of rainy season, his preceptor said to him; “Make a hut for me where the shower of rain will not torment us. It should never collapse nor should it become old and dilapidated.” He was addressed thus by the wife of the preceptor: “O son of Tvaṣṭṛ, make a bodice for me befitting my limbs. It should neither be too tight nor too loose. It should be made of bark and not of cotton. Make it carefully so that it will always remain bright.”

## \|\| 2.86.8-9 \|\|

*guruputreṇa cājñapto mamārthaṃ pāduke kuru \|*  
*yadārūḍhasya me pādau na paṃkaḥ saṃspṛśetkvacit \|\| 8 \|\|*

*carmādibaṃdhanirmukte dhāvato me sukhaprade \|*  
*yābhyāṃ ca saṃcare vāri sthala bhūmāviva drutam \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. He was commanded by the son of the preceptor: “Make a pair of sandals for me, on wearing which my feet can avert contamination with mud. It should net have any leather strapping. Even when I run it should be comfortable. With the sandals on, I should be able to wade through water as quickly as on dry ground.”

## \|\| 2.86.10-15 \|\|

*gurukanyāpi taṃ prāha tvāṣṭra me śravaṇocite \|*  
*bhūṣaṇe svena hastena kuru kāṃcananirmite \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kumārī krīḍanīyāni kautukāni ca dehi me \|*  
*daṃtidaṃtamayānyeva svahastaracitāni ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*gṛhopakaraṇaṃ dravyaṃ musalolūkhalādikam \|*  
*tathā ghaṭaya medhāvinyathā truṭyati na kvacit \|\| 12 \|\|*

*akṣālitānyapi yathā nityaṃ pīṭhāni sattama \|*  
*ujjvalāni bhavaṃtyeva sthālikāśca tathā kuru \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sūpakarmaṇyapi ca māṃ praśādhi tvaṣṭranaṃdana \|*  
*yathāṃgulyo na dahyaṃte pākaḥ syācca yathā śubhaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ekastaṃbhamayaṃ gehamekadāruvinirmitam \|*  
*tathā kuru varaṃ tvāṣṭra yatrecchā tatra dhāraye \|\| 15 \|\|*

10-15. The daughter of the preceptor told him: “O son of Tvaṣṭṛ, you will, with your own hands, make a pair of gold earrings for me. Give me fanciful toys worthy of girls. These also should be made by you yourself out of ivory. O intelligent one, make domestic instruments too such as mortar and pestle; make them unbreakable. O excellent one, make foot-stools which will always be bright even without being washed. Also cooking pans and pots. O son of Tvaṣṭṛ, instruct me in the art of cooking too, so that the fingers do not get burned but the dishes get cooked properly. Also make a single-pillared house, out of a single piece of wood, O son of Tvaṣṭṛ, which I can hold (like an umbrella) wherever I wish.”

## \|\| 2.86.16 \|\|

*ye sahādhyāyinopyasya vayojyeṣṭhāśca tepi hi \|*  
*sarvesarve samīhaṃte karma tatkṛtameva hi \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Those who studied along with him, those who were senior to him, all desired that something should be made by him.

## \|\| 2.86.17 \|\|

*tatheti sa pratijñāya sarveṣāṃ puratodrije \|*  
*madhye vanaṃ prāviśacca mahāciṃtābhayārditaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O Daughter of the Mountain, he promised everyone: “Let it be so” but, afraid and worried, he fled and entered into the middle of a forest.

## \|\| 2.86.18 \|\|

*kiṃcitkartuṃ na jānāti pratijñātaṃ ca tena vai \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ purataḥ sarvaṃ kariṣyāmīti niścitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He did not know how to make any of the things which had been promised by him. He had decisively committed himself by assuring everyone that he would do everything.

## \|\| 2.86.19-25 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi ko me sāhāyyamarpayet \|*  
*buddherapi vanasthasya śaraṇaṃ kaṃ vrajāmi ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*aṃgīkṛtya gurorvākyaṃ gurupatnyā guroḥ śiśoḥ \|*  
*yo na niṣpādayenmūḍhaḥ sa bhavennirayī naraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*guruśuśrūṣaṇaṃ dharma eko hi brahmacāriṇām \|*  
*aniṣpādya tu tadvākyaṃ kathaṃ me niṣkṛtirbhavet \|\| 21 \|\|*

*gurūṇāṃ vākyakaraṇātsarva eva manorathāḥ \|*  
*siddhyaṃtītarathā naiva tasmātkāryaṃ hi tadvacaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kathaṃ tadvacasaḥ siddhiṃ prāpsyāmyatra vane sthitaḥ \|*  
*kaśca metra sahāyī syāddhiṣaṇādurbalasya vai \|\| 23 \|\|*

*āstāṃ gurukathā dūraṃ yo'nyasyāpi laghorapi \|*  
*omityuktvā na kurute kāryaṃ sotha vrajatyadhaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kathametāni karmāṇi kariṣye'jño'sahāyavān \|*  
*aṃgīkṛtāni tadbhītyā namaste bhavitavyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

19-25. That son of Tvaṣṭṛ cogitated thus: ‘What shall I do? Where shall I go? I am in the middle of the forest. Who will help me and guide my intellect? Whom shall I seek refuge in? The foolish fellow who undertakes to do something at the instance of the preceptor, his wife or his child but does not fulfil the same certainly falls into hell. The sole duty of a religious student is the ministration of service to the preceptor. How can I discharge my duty without carrying out his behest? By fulfilling the tasks entrusted by preceptors and elders, one can realize all one’s desires, not otherwise. Hence his (Preceptor’s) behest should be fulfilled. Staying here in this forest, how can I hope to carry out their instructions? Who will help me here? I am weak and deficient in intellect. Leave aside the case of the preceptor. Even in the case of another of inferior status, if one assents to something but does not carry it out, he incurs downfall. Ignorant and having none to assist, how am I going to do all these things undertaken out of fear for them? Obeisance to you, O inevitable fate!’

## \|\| 2.86.26 \|\|

*yāvaditthaṃ ciṃtayati sa tvāṣṭro vanamadhyagaḥ \|*  
*tāvattadeva saṃprāptastenaiko'darśi tāpasaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. While that son of Tvaṣṭṭ, held up in the middle of the forest, was thinking thus, a sage was seen by him who had come there then only.

## \|\| 2.86.27-31 \|\|

*atha natvā sa taṃ prāha vane dṛṣṭaṃ tapasvinam \|*  
*ko bhavānmānasaṃ me yo nitarāṃ sukhayatyaho \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tvaddarśanena me gātraṃ ciṃtāsaṃtāpatāpitam \|*  
*himānī gāhaneneva śītalaṃ bhavati kṣaṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*kiṃ tvaṃ me prāktanaṃ karma prāptaṃ tāpasarūpadhṛk \|*  
*athavā karuṇāvārdhirāvirbhūtaḥ śivo bhavān \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yosi sosi namastubhyamupadeśena yuṃkṣva mām \|*  
*gurūktaṃ gurupatnyuktaṃ gurvapatyoktameva ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kathaṃ kartumahaṃ śaktaḥ karma tatra diśādbhutam \|*  
*kuru me buddhisāhāyyaṃ nirjane baṃdhutāṃ gataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

27-31. After bowing down to the ascetic seen in the forest, he said to him: “O esteemed Sir, who may you be? You have excessively pleased my mind. My body has been scorched due to feverish anxiety; but at your sight, it has become instantly cool as though it has dived through a mass of snowflakes. Has my previous Karma assumed your form of an ascetic and come here? Or are you Śiva himself, the ocean of compassion manifested before me? Whoever you may be, I offer obeisance to you. Instruct me as to how I shall be competent to carry out the task entrusted by the preceptor, his wife and his children? Tell me the procedure thereof. Give me intellectual assistance. You have come as a kinsman in this isolated place.”

## \|\| 2.86.32 \|\|

*ityuktastena sa vane tāpaso brahmacāriṇā \|*  
*kāruṇyapūrṇahṛdayo yathoktamupadiṣṭavān \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On being requested thus in the forest by the religious student, the ascetic with his heart full of compassion advised him accordingly.

## \|\| 2.86.33 \|\|

*ya āptatvena saṃpṛṣṭo durbuddhiṃ saṃprayacchati \|*  
*sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. If a person approached as an authority on being asked for guidance misguides one, he is sure to fall into a terrible hell, to stay there till all the living beings are annihilated.

## \|\| 2.86.34 \|\|

*tāpasa uvāca \|*  
*brahmacāriñśṛṇu brūyāṃ kimadbhutataraṃ tvidam \|*  
*viśveśānugrahādbrahmāpyabhavatsṛṣṭikovidaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

The Ascetic said:

34\. O Brahmacārī, I shall tell you. Listen. Is this any mysterious thing? Due to the blessings of Viśveśa, even Brahmā has become clever in the act of creation.

## \|\| 2.86.35 \|\|

*yadi tvaṃ tvāṣṭra sarvajñaṃ kāśyāmārādhayiṣyasi \|*  
*tataste viśvakarmeti nāma satyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. If you, O son of Tvaṣṭṛ, propitiate the omniscient Lord Śiva at Kāśī, your name Viśvakarman (‘one who performs all tasks’) shall be truly meaningful.

## \|\| 2.86.36 \|\|

*viśveśānugrahātkāśyāmabhilāṣā na durlabhāḥ \|*  
*sulabho durlabho vai yadyatra mokṣastanutyajām \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. With the blessings of Viśveśa in Kāśī, no desire shall be unattainable, even if it be for salvation; it is easily obtained. Mokṣa too difffīcult to achieve, is easy to people casting off their bodies here.

## \|\| 2.86.37 \|\|

*sṛṣṭeḥkaraṇa sāmarthyaṃ sṛṣṭirakṣāpravīṇatā \|*  
*vidhinā viṣṇunā prāpi viśveśānugrahātparāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It is due to the great favour of Viśveśa that the ability to create things was obtained by Brahmā and the capacity to protect the creation by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.86.38 \|\|

*yāhi vaiśveśvaraṃ sadma padmayā samadhiṣṭhitam \|*  
*nirvāṇasaṃjñayā bālā yadīccheḥ svānmanorathān \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If you desire the realization of your wishes, O boy, go to the abode of Viśveśvara presided over by the glory of ultimate salvation.

## \|\| 2.86.39 \|\|

*sa hi sarvapradaḥ śaṃbhuryācitaścopamanyunā \|*  
*payomātraṃ dadau tasmai sarvaṃ kṣīrābdhimeva ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Indeed Śaṃbhu is the bestower of everything. On being requested for milk only by Upamanyu he granted him the entire ocean of milk.

## \|\| 2.86.40 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānane śaṃbhoḥ kiṃ kiṃ kena na labhyate \|*  
*yatra vāsakṛtāṃ puṃsāṃ dharmarāśiḥ padepade \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. To a person staying in Ānandavana, mass of piety is attainable at every step. In fact, what is it that cannot be obtained in Saṃbhu’s Ānandakānana and who is it by whom it is not obtained?

## \|\| 2.86.41 \|\|

*svardhunī sparśamātreṇa mahāpātakasaṃtatiḥ \|*  
*yatra saṃkṣayati kṣipraṃ tāṃ kāśīṃ ko na saṃśrayet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Who will not resort to that Kāśī where masses of great sins become reduced merely by the touch of the celestial river.

## \|\| 2.86.42 \|\|

*na tādṛgdharmasaṃbhāro labhyate kratukoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*yādṛgvārāṇasī vīthī saṃcāreṇa padepade \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Even through crores of sacrifices such a mass of piety is not obtained, as is obtained at every step, while walking through the streets of Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.86.43 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ yadyatrāsti manorathaḥ \|*  
*tadā vārāṇasīṃ yāhi yāhi trailokyapāvanīm \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. If there is any desire for piety, wealth, love and salvation, go then to Vārāṇasī, go then to the sanctifier of all the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.86.44 \|\|

*sarvakāmaphalaprāptistadaiva syāddhruvaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*yadaiva sarvadaḥ sarvaḥ kāśyāṃ viśveśvaraḥ śritaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Certainly men will attain the fruits of all desires, when Śarva, Viśveśvara, the bestower of everything, is resorted to in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.86.45 \|\|

*sa tāpasoktamākarṇya tvāṣṭra itthaṃ suhṛṣṭavān \|*  
*kāśīsaṃprātyupāyaṃ ca tameva samapṛcchata \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On hearing the utterance of the ascetic thus, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ became highly pleased. He asked the ascetic himself the means of reaching Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.86.46 \|\|

*tvāṣṭra uvāca \|*  
*tadānaṃdavanaṃ śaṃbhoḥ kvāsti tāpasasattama \|*  
*yatra no durlabhaṃ kiṃcitsādhakānāṃ trayīsthitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

Tvaṣṭṛ said:

46\. O excellent one among ascetics, where is that Ānandavana of Śaṃbhu where nothing existing in all the three worlds becomes difficult to get for Sādhakas (Aspirants)?

## \|\| 2.86.47 \|\|

*svarge vā martyaloke vā balisadmani vā mune \|*  
*kva tadānaṃdagahanaṃ yatrānaṃdapayobdhijā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O sage, is it in heaven, or in the mortal world or in the abode of Bali? Where is that Ānandavana where there exist the Glory of Bliss?

## \|\| 2.86.48 \|\|

*yatra viśveśvaro devo viśveṣāṃ karṇadhārakaḥ \|*  
*vyācaṣṭe tārakaṃ jñānaṃ yena tanmayatāṃ yayuḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. It is the place where Lord Viśveśvara, the helmsman of all the worlds, imparts the Tārakajñāna (knowledge) whereby the devotees become identical with him.

## \|\| 2.86.49 \|\|

*sulabhā yatra niyatamānaṃdavanacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*api naiḥśreyasī lakṣmīḥ kimanyelpa manorathāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. It is the place where the Glory of Salvation is invariably easy of access to a person traversing Ānandavana. What to speak of lesser desires!

## \|\| 2.86.50-54 \|\|

*kastāṃ māṃ prāpayecchaṃbhoḥ kathaṃ yāmi tathā vada \|*  
*sa tapasvīti tadvākyamākarṇya śraddhayānvitam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*prāhāgaccha nayāmi tvāṃ yiyāsurahamapyaho \|*  
*durlabhaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ yadi kāśī na sevitā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*punaḥkva nṛtvaṃ śreyobhūḥ kva kāśīkarmabaṃdhahṛt \|*  
*vṛthāgate hi mānuṣye kāśīprāptivivarjanāt \|\| 52 \|\|*

*āyuṣyaṃ ca bhaviṣyaṃ ca sarvameva vṛthāgatam \|*  
*atohaṃ saphalīkartuṃ mānuṣyaṃ cāticaṃcalam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*yāsyāmi kāśīmāyāhi māyāṃ hitvā tvamapyaho \|*  
*iti tena saha tvāṣṭro muninātikṛpālunā \|\| 54 \|\|*

50-54. Kindly tell me, who will take me there to the city of Śaṃbhu? How should I go?

## \|\| 2.86.55-59 \|\|

*purīṃ vaiśveśvarīṃ prāpto manaḥsvāsthyamavāpa ca \|*  
*tataḥ prāpayya tāṃ kāśīṃ tāpasaḥ kvāpyatarkitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*jagāma kuṃbhasaṃbhūta sa tvāṣṭropītyamanyata \|*  
*avaśyaṃ sa hi viśveśaḥ sarveṣāṃ ciṃtitapradaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*satpathasthiravṛtīnāṃ dūrasthopi samīpagaḥ \|*  
*yasminprasannadṛktryakṣastaṃ daviṣṭhamapi dhruvam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*sunediṣṭhaṃ karotyeva svayaṃvartmopadeśayan \|*  
*kvāhaṃ tatra vane bālaściṃtākulitamānasaḥ \|*  
*kva tāpasaḥ sa yo māṃ vai sūdiśyeha cānayat \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kheloyamasya tryakṣasya yasya bhaktasya kutracit \|*  
*na durlabhataraṃ kiṃcidaho kvāhaṃ kva kāśikā \|\| 59 \|\|*

On hearing these words full of faith, that ascetic said: “Come. I shall take you. I too am desirous of going there. After obtaining human birth, if Kāśī is not resorted to, where is human birth once again? Where is Kāśī, the cause of welfare, the destroyer of the bondage of Karmas? If the human life is wasted by being bereft of the access to Kāśī, the future and the whole span of life, everything is gone waste. Hence in order to make this highly fickle human life fruitful, I will go to Kāśī. Come on, after setting aside Māyā (Delusion).” On hearing this, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ reached the city of Viśveśvara accompanied by that highly sympathetic sage. He regained the satisfaction of mind.

55-59. After taking him as far as Kāśī, O Pot-born One, the ascetic went somewhere unexpectedly. Then the son of Tvaṣṭṛ thought thus, ‘Indeed it is Viśveśa himself, the bestower of anything thought of on everyone. Though he is far off, he is present in the vicinity of those who steadily persist in the path of the good. If the Three-eyed Lord casts the benign glance on anyone, he is drawn very near to himself despite his being far off and he himself imparts instruction regarding the right path. Where was I, a lonely boy in the forest with mind bewildered due to anxiety? Where was that ascetic who advised me properly and brought me here? (A great disparity, indeed!) This is the playful pastime of this Three-eyed Lord whose devotee has nothing difficult to get. Where am I? Where is Kāśikā? (What a great difference between us!)

## \|\| 2.86.60 \|\|

*nārādhito mayā śaṃbhuḥ prāktane janmani kvacit \|*  
*śarīritvānumānena jñātametadasaṃśayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Śaṃbhu has not been propitiated by me anywhere in the previous birth. This is definitely known as an inference from (my being) an embodied being.

## \|\| 2.86.61 \|\|

*asmiñjanmani bālatvānna caivārādhitaḥ sphuṭam \|*  
*pratyakṣameva me vaitatkutonugrahadhīrmayi \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. In this birth too, it is obvious that he has not been propitiated because I am only a boy. This is directly observed. How does he have the inclination to bless?

## \|\| 2.86.62 \|\|

*ājñātaṃ gurubhaktirme hetuḥ śaṃbhuprasādane \|*  
*yayehānugṛhītosmi viśveśena kṛpālunā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Yes, it is known! my devotion to the preceptor is the cause of propitiation of Saṃbhu; it is due to that that I have been blessed by the compassionate Viśveśa.

## \|\| 2.86.63 \|\|

*athavā kāraṇāpekṣastryakṣastvitaradevavat \|*  
*raṃkamapyanugṛhṇāti kevalaṃ kāraṇaṃ kṛpā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Or the Three-eyed Lord does not depend upon a specific cause like other gods. He blesses even the poorest man and the cause thereof is compassion alone.

## \|\| 2.86.64 \|\|

*yadi no mayyanukrośaḥ kathaṃ tāpasasaṃgatiḥ \|*  
*tadrūpeṇa svayaṃ śaṃbhurānināyeha māṃ dhruvam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If he has no pity on me, what accounts for my contact with the ascetic? In the form (of that ascetic) Śaṃbhu himself has certainly brought me here.

## \|\| 2.86.65 \|\|

*na dānāni na vai yajñā na tapāṃsi vratāni ca \|\| \|*  
*śaṃbhoḥ prasādahetūni kāraṇaṃ tatkṛpaiva hi \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Neither charity nor performance of sacrifices, neither austerities nor Vratas can be the cause of Śaṃbhu’s pleasure. The cause thereof is his grace alone.

## \|\| 2.86.66 \|\|

*dayāmapi tadā kuryādasau viśveśvaraḥ parām \|*  
*yadāśrutyuktamadhvānaṃ sadbhiḥ kṣuṇṇaṃ na saṃtyajet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. When one does not leave off the path ordained in the Śrutis and traversed by the good, this Lord Viśveśvara does have the greatest pity.’

## \|\| 2.86.67 \|\|

*anukrośaṃ samarthyeti sa tvāṣṭraḥ rśābhavaṃ śuciḥ \|*  
*saṃsthāpya liṃgamīśasyārādhayatsvasthamānasaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. After invoking the sympathy of Śaṃbhu, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, with real purity, installed the Liṅga of Īśa and adored it with a steady mind.

## \|\| 2.86.68 \|\|

*ānīya puṣpasaṃbhāramārtavaṃ kānanādbahu \|*  
*snātvābhyarcayatīśānaṃ kaṃdamūlaphalāśanaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He used to take bath everyday and worship Īśāna after bringing from the forest a huge collection of flowers blossoming in the changing seasons. He sustained himself by eating bulbous roots, roots and fruits alone.

## \|\| 2.86.69 \|\|

*itthaṃ tvaṣṭṛtanūjasya liṃgārādhanacetasaḥ \|*  
*trihāyanātprasannobhūttasyeśaḥ karuṇānidhiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. When the son of Tvaṣṭṛ spent three years thus with the mind directed towards the propitiation of the Liṅga, the Lord, the storehouse of mercy, became pleased with him.

## \|\| 2.86.70-72 \|\|

*tasmādeva hi liṃgācca prādurbhūya bhavo'bravīt \|*  
*varaṃ varaya re tvāṣṭra dṛḍhabhaktyānayā tava \|\| 70 \|\|*

*prasannosmi bhṛśaṃ bāla gurvarthakṛtacetasaḥ \|*  
*guruṇā gurupatnyā ca gurvapatyadvayena ca \|\| 71 \|\|*

*yathārthitaṃ tathā kartuṃ te sāmarthyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 72 \|\|*

70-72. Coining out of that Liṅga itself, Bhava said: “O son of Tvaṣṭṛ, choose a boon, O boy who have determined in mind to work for the sake of the preceptor. I am pleased with your steady devotion. You will have the capacity to make the things in accordance with the request made by the preceptor, his wife and the two children of his.

## \|\| 2.86.73 \|\|

*anyānvarāṃśca te dadyāṃ tvāṣṭra tuṣṭastvadarcayā \|*  
*tāñśṛṇuṣva mahābhāga liṃgasyāsyādbhutaśriyaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O son of Tvaṣṭṛ, I shall grant you other boons too. I am satisfied with your adoration. O highly blessed one, listen to them. (It is due to the power) of this Liṅga of wonderful glory.

## \|\| 2.86.74-78 \|\|

*tvaṃ suvarṇādidhātūnāṃ dārūṇāṃ dṛṣadāmapi \|*  
*maṇīnāmapiratnānāṃ puṣpāṇāmapi vāsasām \|\| 74 \|\|*

*karpūrādisugaṃdhīnāṃ dravyāṇāmapyapāmapi \|*  
*kaṃdamūlaphalānāṃ ca dravyāṇāmapi ca tvacām \|\| 75 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ vastujātānāṃ kartuṃ karma pravetsyasi \|*  
*yasya yasya ruciryatra sadma devālayādiṣu \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tasya tasyeha tuṣṭyai tvaṃ tathā kartuṃ pravetsyasi \|*  
*sarvanepathyaracanāḥ sarvāḥ sūpasya saṃskṛtīḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*sarvāṇi śilpakāryāṇi tauryatrikamathāpi ca \|*  
*sarvaṃ jñāsyasi kartuṃ tvaṃ dvitīya iva padmabhūḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

74-78. Like another Brahmā (the Creator) you will know how to make things out of gold and other metals, wood, stones, gems, jewels, flowers, clothes, camphor and other scented things, water, bulbous roots, fruits, skins and peels of things—nay of all things. Whatever people may be interested in, houses, temples etc. and whatever may be the mode of liking, you will be able to carry out the task to their full satisfaction. You will know how to create things, the mode of making the dresses of all kinds, varieties of dishes from lentils, all types of fine arts, the triple symphony etc.

## \|\| 2.86.79-80 \|\|

*nānāvidhāni yaṃtrāṇi nānāyudhavidhānakam \|*  
*jalāśayānāṃ racanāḥ sudurgaracanāstathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*tādṛkkartuṃ purā vetsi yādṛṅnānyo'dhiyāsyati \|*  
*kalājātaṃ hi sarvaṃ tvamavayāsyasi me varāt \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. Different kinds of machines and musical instruments, different types of weaponry, arrangement of artificial ponds and reservoirs of water, building of forts—you will know how to create all these in such a manner as to excel others. Due to my boon, you will master all the arts.

## \|\| 2.86.81-83 \|\|

*sarveṃdrajālikī vidyā tvadadhīnā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*sarvakarmasu kauśalyaṃ sarvabuddhivariṣṭhatām \|\| 81 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ ca manovṛttiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi varānmama \|*  
*kiṃ bahūktena yatsvarge yatpātāle yadatra ca \|\| 82 \|\|*

*atilokottaraṃ karma tatsarvaṃ vetsyasi svayam \|\| 83 \|\|*

81-83. All (tricks of) jugglery and magical arts will be known to you. You will be clever in all tasks. Your intellect will be the most excellent one. Due to my boon, you will understand the mental predilections of everyone. Why say more? Whether in heaven or in Pātāla or here, you will know everything supernatural and superb.

## \|\| 2.86.84 \|\|

*viśveṣāṃ viśvakarmāṇi viśveṣu bhuvaneṣu ca \|*  
*yato jñāsyasi tannāma viśvakarmeti te'nagha \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. O sinless one, your name shall be Viśvakarman because you will be knowing all the activities of all the worlds and of everyone.

## \|\| 2.86.85 \|\|

*aparaḥ ko varo deyastava taṃ prārthayāśvaho \|*  
*tavādeyaṃ na me kiṃcilliṃgārcanaratasya hi \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. What other boon should be given to you? Request for it quickly. There is nothing that cannot be given to you since you have been engaged in the adoration of the Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.86.86 \|\|

*anyatrāpi hi yo liṃgaṃ samarcayati sanmatiḥ \|*  
*tasyāpi vāṃchitaṃ deyaṃ kiṃpunaryovikāśikam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Desired things should be granted even to that devotee of excellent mind who worships the Liṅga elsewhere. All the more so in the case of one who worships the Liṅga especially in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.86.87 \|\|

*yena kāśyāṃ samabhyarci yena kāśyāṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*yena kāśyāṃ stutaṃ liṃgaṃ sa me rūpāya darpaṇaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. He by whom a Liṅga has been installed in Kāśī, has been adored in Kāśī and has been eulogized in Kāśī, is a mirror unto my form.

## \|\| 2.86.88 \|\|

*tattvaṃ svacchosi mukuro mama netratrayasya hi \|*  
*kāśyāṃ liṃgārcanāttvāṣṭra varaṃ varaya suvrata \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. You are the bright and clear mirror of my three-eyed form, because you have adored the Liṅga in Kāśī. O son of Tvaṣṭṛ, O performer of religious vows, choose the boon.

## \|\| 2.86.89 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ yo rājadhānyāṃ me hitvā māmanyamarcayet \|*  
*sa varākolpadhīrmuṣṭo'lpatuṣṭirmuktivarjitaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. He who setting me aside worships another deity in Kāśī, my capital city, is a poor wretch, deficient in intellect, deprived of (good things) and devoid of salvation. He has to be satisfied with lesser things.

## \|\| 2.86.90 \|\|

*tadānaṃdavanehyatra samarcyohaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ \|*  
*druhiṇopeṃdracaṃdreṃdrairihānyo na samarcyate \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Hence here in Ānandavana, I am to be worshipped by those who desire salvation, by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Moon and Indra. No one else is adored here.

## \|\| 2.86.91 \|\|

*yathānaṃdavanaṃ prāpya tvaṃ māmarcitavānasi \|*  
*tathānye puṇyakarmāṇo māmabhyarcyaiva māmitāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Just as you have come to Ānandavana and have worshipped me, so also other persons of meritorious deeds have worshipped and attained me.

## \|\| 2.86.92 \|\|

*anugrāhyo'si nitarāṃ tato varaya durlabham \|*  
*śrāṇitaṃ tadavaihi tvaṃ vada mā cirayasva bhoḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. You are to be blessed completely. Hence choose a boon that is rare and know that it is already granted. Oh, speak out; do not delay.”

## \|\| 2.86.93 \|\|

*viśvakarmovāca \|*  
*idaṃ yatsthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ mayājñenāpi śaṃkara \|*  
*talliṃgamanyepyārādhya saṃtu samṛddhibhājanam \|\| 93 \|\|*

Viśvakarman said:

93\. O Śaṅkara, though this Liṅga has been installed by me, ignorant that I am, yet let others also be the recipients of excellent knowledge by propitiating it.

## \|\| 2.86.94 \|\|

*anyacca nātha prārthyosi tacca viśrāṇayiṣyasi \|*  
*mayā vinirmāpayitā svaṃ prāsādaṃ kadā bhavān \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. O Lord, you have to be requested for another thing too and you will grant it. When will Your Revered Lordship make me build your palace?

## \|\| 2.86.95 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*evamastu yaduktaṃ te tava liṃgasamarcakāḥ \|*  
*samṛddhibhājanaṃ vai syuḥ syuśca nirvāṇadīkṣitāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

Devadeva said:

95\. Let what you said be so. Those who worship your Liṅga shall become the recipients of excellent knowledge and well-initiated in the process of salvation.

## \|\| 2.86.96 \|\|

*yadā ca rājā bhavitā divodāso vidhervarāt \|*  
*tadā me vacanāttāta prāsādaṃ me vidhāsyati \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. When Divodāsa becomes the king due to the boon of Vidhi, then at my instance he will make you build my palace.

## \|\| 2.86.97-98 \|\|

*navīkṛtya punaḥ kāśī nirviṣṭā tena bhūbhujā \|*  
*gaṇeśamāyayā rājyātparinirviṇṇacetasā \|\| 97 \|\|*

*viṣṇoḥ sadupadeśācca māmeva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*nirvāṇalakṣmīḥ prāpteha hitvā rājyaśriyaṃ calām \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. Kāśī has been renovated and colonized by that king. Due to Gaṇeśa’s Māyā, he will become disgusted with kingdom. At the advice of Viṣṇu, he will seek refuge in me. Abandoning the glory of royal bliss, which is fickle, he has attained (will attain) the glory of salvation here.

## \|\| 2.86.99 \|\|

*viśvakarmanvraja guroḥ śāsanāya yatasva ca \|*  
*gurubhaktikṛto yasmānmadbhaktā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O Viśvakarman, go ahead. Endeavour to fulfil the command of the preceptor, since those who devoutly serve their preceptors are my devotees. Thee is no doubt in it.

## \|\| 2.86.100 \|\|

*ye guruṃ cāvamanyaṃte tevamānyā mayāpyaho \|*  
*tasmādgurūpadiṣṭaṃ hi kuru śiṣyasamīhitam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Those who dishonour their preceptor, are worthy of being dishonoured by me. Hence do what is advised by the preceptor. That should be your desire.

## \|\| 2.86.101 \|\|

*tata āgatya me pārśvaṃ yāvannirvāṇameṣyasi \|*  
*tāvatsthāsyasi śuddhātmā devānāṃ hitamācaran \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Thereafter you will come to slay with me—(you) a sanctified soul carrying out what is beneficial to the Devas till you finally attain salvation.

## \|\| 2.86.102 \|\|

*tavātra liṃge satataṃ sthāsyāmyahamabhīṣṭadaḥ \|*  
*asya liṃgasya bhaktānāṃ nirvāṇaśrīradūrataḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Here, in your Liṅga, I shall abide forever as the bestower of their desire. The Glory of Salvation is not far from the devotees of this Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.86.103 \|\|

*aṃgāreśādudīcyāṃ ye tvalliṃgasyasamarcakāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ manorathāvāptirbhaviṣyati padepade \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Those who adore your Liṅga which is to the north of Aṅgāreśa, will attain at every step the fulfilment of their desires.

## \|\| 2.86.104 \|\|

*ityuktvāṃtardadhe devastvāṣṭropi gurumāptavān \|*  
*guroḥ samīhitaṃ bhūri vidhāya sa gṛhānyayau \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. After saying thus the Lord vanished. The son of Tvaṣṭṛ went back to his preceptor. After carrying out many things desired by the preceptor, he returned to his house.

## \|\| 2.86.105 \|\|

*gṛhepi mātāpitarau saṃtoṣya nijakarmaṇā \|*  
*taduktājñāṃ samādhāya punaḥ kāśīṃ samāyayau \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. At his home too, he made his parents contented through his activity. After fulfilling properly their behests as declared by them, he came back to Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.86.106 \|\|

*svaliṃgārādhanāsakto nādyāpi tvaṣṭṛnaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*kāśīṃ tyajati medhāvī sarvadeva priyaṃ caran \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The son of Tvaṣṭṛ is eagerly attached to the propitiation of his own Liṅga. That sensible devotee does not leave off Kāśī till today. He is continuing the activities pleasing to all the Devas.

## \|\| 2.86.107 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*pṛṣṭāni yāni rligāni tvayā devi girīṃdraje \|*  
*kāśī muktau samarthāni tānyuktāni mayā tava \|\| 107 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

107\. O goddess, O daughter of the Lord of Mountains, all those Liṅgas in Kāśī efficacious in causing salvation and specifically asked by you, have been described by me to you.

## \|\| 2.86.108-110 \|\|

*liṃgamoṃkārasaṃjñaṃ ca tathā devaṃ triviṣṭapam \|*  
*mahādevaḥ kṛttivāsā ratneśaścaṃdrasaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

*kedāraścāpi dharmeśastathā vīreśvarābhidhaḥ \|*  
*kāmeśaviśvakarmeśau maṇikarṇīśvarastathā \|\| 109 \|\|*

*mamārcyamavimuktākhyaṃ tato devi mamā khyakam \|*  
*viśvanātheti viśvasminprathitaṃ viśvasaukhyadam \|\| 110 \|\|*

108-110. They are: the Liṅga named Oṃkāra, Lord Triviṣṭapa, Mahādeva, Kṛttivāsas, Ratneśa, Candra, Kedāra, Dharmeśa, Vīreśvara, Kāmeśa, Viśvakarmeśa and Maṇikarṇīśvara, that which is worthy of my adoration named Avimukta, then O goddess, that which has my name i.e. Viśvanātha which is well -known in the universe and which accords happiness to the whole universe.

## \|\| 2.86.111 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ samāsādya yena viśveśvarorcitaḥ \|*  
*na tasyāsti punarjanma kalpakoṭiśateṣvapi \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. If after reaching Avimukta, Viśveśvara is worshipped by anyone, he does not take birth again in the course of hundreds of crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 2.86.112 \|\|

*aṣṭau māsānvihāraḥ syādyatīnāṃ saṃyatātmanām \|*  
*ekatra caturomāsānabdaṃ nāvāsa iṣyate \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Yatis (mendicants) of well-controlled souls are allowed free movement for eight months. It is not desirable for them to stay in a place for a whole year, but only four months are enjoined.

## \|\| 2.86.113 \|\|

*avimukte praviṣṭānāṃ vihāro naiva yujyate \|*  
*mokṣopyasaṃśayaścātra tasmāttyājyā na kāśikā \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. In the case of those who have entered Avimukta free movement is not proper. Salvation is undoubted here. Hence, Kāśikā should not be abandoned.

## \|\| 2.86.114 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānanaṃ hitvā nānyadgacchettapovanam \|*  
*tapoyogaśca mokṣaśca yatotraiva madāśrayāt \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. One should not abandon Ānandavana and go to a penance-grove elsewhere, since, with my support, penance, Yoga and salvation—all belong to this place only.

## \|\| 2.86.115 \|\|

*kṛpayā sarvajaṃtūnāṃ kṣetrametanmayā kṛtam \|*  
*avaśyameva siddhyaṃti kṣetresminsiddhikāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Out of compassion for all creatures, this holy spot has been created by me. In this holy spot, all those who are desirous of Siddhi, do accomplish it.

## \|\| 2.86.116 \|\|

*atītaṃ vartamānaṃ ca jānato'jñānataḥ kṛtam \|*  
*yadenastallayaṃ yāyādānaṃdavanavīkṣaṇāt \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. On merely seeing Ānandavana all the sins of the past and present committed knowingly or unwittingly become destroyed.

## \|\| 2.86.117-118 \|\|

*atyugraiśca tapobhiryanmahādānairmahāvrataiḥ \|*  
*niyamaiśca yamaiḥ samyaktvayogena mahāmakhaiḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*
