46-47. All the verses beginning with the above indicating his assertion, Vyāsa recited with the left hand raised. Thereupon Śailādi made the hand paralysed playfully. There was also stupefaction of the power of speech of the excellent sage Vyāsa.

## \|\| 2.95.48 \|\|

*tato guptaṃ samāgamya viṣṇurvyāsamabhāṣata \|*  
*aparāddhaṃ mahaccātra bhavatā vyāsa niścitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thereupon Viṣṇu came there secretly and spoke to Vyāsa: “O Vyāsa, a great offence has certainly been committed by you.

## \|\| 2.95.49 \|\|

*tavaitadaparādhena bhītirmepi mahattarā \|*  
*eka eva hi viśveśo dvitīyo nāsti kaścana \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Even I am greatly afraid due to this offence of yours. There is only one Lord of the universe, and he is Viśveśa. There is no one else.

## \|\| 2.95.50 \|\|

*tatprasādādahaṃ cakrī lakṣmīśastatprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*trailokyarakṣāsāmarthyaṃ dattaṃ tenaiva śaṃbhunā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. I am the discus-bearer, due to his favour. I am the Lord of Lakṣmī due to his power. It was by Śaṃbhu himself that the capacity to sustain the three worlds was granted to me.

## \|\| 2.95.51 \|\|

*tadbhaktyā paramaiśvaryaṃ mayā labdhaṃ varāttataḥ \|*  
*idānīṃ stuhi taṃ śaṃbhuṃ yadi me śubhamicchasi \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Due to the devotion to him the greatest Aiśvarya (prosperity, lordship) was obtained by me as a boon from him. If you desire my welfare, eulogize Śaṃbhu.

## \|\| 2.95.52 \|\|

*anyadāpi na vai kāryā bhavatā śemuṣīdṛśī \|*  
*pārāśarya iti śrutvā saṃjñayā vyājahāra ha \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Do not entertain a thought like this to eulogize me on any other occasion, O son of Parāśara.” On hearing this, Vyāsa expressed by means of gestures:

## \|\| 2.95.53-54 \|\|

*bhujastaṃbhaḥ kṛtastena naṃdinā dṛṣṭimātrataḥ \|*  
*vākstaṃbhastadbhayājjātaḥ spṛśa me kaṃṭhakaṃdalīm \|\| 53 \|\|*

*yathā stotuṃ bhavānīśa prabhavābhi bhavāṃtakama \|*  
*saṃspṛśya viṣṇustatkaṃṭhaṃ guptameva jagāma ha \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. “The paralysis of the arm has been brought about by that Nandin by his mere eyes. The stunning of the speech has been caused by my fear of him. Touch the root of my throat so that I shall be able to eulogize Bhavānīśa, the destroyer of worldly existence.” After touching his throat, Viṣṇu secretly went away.

## \|\| 2.95.55 \|\|

*tataḥ satyavatīsūnustathā staṃbhitadorlataḥ \|*  
*prārabdhavānmaheśānaṃ parituṣṭotumudāradhīḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thereupon the son of Satyavatī whose arm had been paralysed in that manner, began to eulogize Maheśāna liberal-mindedly.

## \|\| 2.95.56 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*eko rudro na dvitīyo yatastadbrahmaivaikaṃ neha nānāsti kiṃcit \|*  
*yadyapyanyaḥ kopi vā kutracidvā vyācaṣṭāṃ tadyasya śaktirmadagre \|\| 56 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

\[Vyāsa’s Prayer; vv 56-63\]

56\. Brahman alone is one. There are not many entities here. Hence Rudra is only one. There is none second to him. If there be anyone else anywhere, let him who has the capacity to do so, explain it to me.

## \|\| 2.95.57 \|\|

*yaḥ kṣīrābdhermaṃdarāghātajāto jvālāmālī kālakūṭoti bhīmaḥ \|*  
*taṃ soḍhuṃ vā ko paro'bhūnmaheśādyatkīlābhiḥ kṛṣṇatāmāpa viṣṇuḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Highly terrible poison Kālakūṭa with flaming sparks around was born of the Milk Ocean, due to the churning with Manḍara. No one other than Maheśa could endure it. On account of its flames, Viṣṇu turned back.

## \|\| 2.95.58 \|\|

*yadvāṇobhūcchrīpatiryasya yaṃtā lokeśo yatsyaṃdanaṃ bhūḥ samastā \|*  
*vāhā vedā yasya yeneṣupātāddagdhā grāmāstraipurāstatsamaḥ kaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Śrīpati (Viṣṇu) was his arrow. The entire earth was his chariot. Brahmā, the Lord of the world, was his charioteer. The horses were the Vedas. Who is on a par with Rudra by whom the group of three Puras was burned by the discharge of the arrow?

## \|\| 2.95.59 \|\|

*yaṃ kadarpo vīkṣamāṇaḥ samānaṃ devairanyairbhasmajātaḥ svayaṃ hi \|*  
*pauṣpairbāṇaiḥ sarvaviśvaikajetā ko vā stutyaḥ kāmajetustatonyaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Kandarpa who was the sole conqueror of the universe through his flowery arrows, viewed Rudra as of the same level as the other Devas. He himself was reduced to ashes. Who is worthy of eulogy other than that conqueror of Kāma?

## \|\| 2.95.60 \|\|

*yaṃ vai vedo veda no naiva viṣṇurnovā vedhā no mano naiva vāṇī \|*  
*taṃ deveśaṃ mādṛśaḥ kolpamedhā yāthātmyādvai vettyaho viśvanātham \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Which man of meagre intellect like me (can) understand Viśvanātha in his true self, because the Veda does not know him? Neither Viṣṇu nor Brahmā, neither mind nor speech know that Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 2.95.61 \|\|

*yasminsarvaṃ yastu sarvatra sarvo yo vai kartā yo'vitā yo'pahartā \|*  
*no yasyādiryaḥ samastādireko no yasyāṃto yoṃtakṛttaṃ natosmi \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. I bow down to him wherein everything is stationed, who is everywhere, who is all, who is the maker, who is the protector, who is the destroyer, who has no beginning, who is the beginning (cause) of everything, who is the sole one, who has no end and who causes the end of everything.

## \|\| 2.95.62 \|\|

*yasyaikākhyā vājimedhena tulyā yasyā na tyā caikayālpeṃdralakṣmīḥ \|*  
*yasya stutyā labhyate satyaloko yasyārcāto mokṣalakṣmīradūrā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. (He is that Lord) the utterance of whose one name is on a par with a horse-sacrifice; by a single bowing down to whom Lakṣmī (glory) was attained by the insignificant Indra; by whose eulogy Satyaloka is obtained and by whose adoration the glory of salvation is not far off.

## \|\| 2.95.63 \|\|

*nānyaṃ devaṃ vedmyahaṃ śrīmaheśānnānyaṃ devaṃ staumi śaṃbhorṛte'ham \|*  
*nānyaṃ devaṃ vā namāmi trinetrātsatyaṃ satyaṃ satyametanmṛṣā na \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. I do not know any other Lord than Śrīmaheśa; I do not eulogize another Lord except Śaṃbhu; I do not bow down to a Lord other than the Three-eyed One. This is the truth, the truth, the truth, not a lie.”

## \|\| 2.95.64 \|\|

*itthaṃ yāvatstauti śaṃbhuṃ maharṣistāvannaṃdī śāṃbhavāddṛkprasādāt \|*  
*taddoḥ staṃbhaṃ tyaktavāṃścābabhāṣe smāyaṃsmāyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo namo vaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. When the great sage eulogized Śaṃbhu thus, there was a favourable glance from Śaṃbhu whereby Nandin undid the paralysis of his arm and smilingly said, “Obeisance to all of you Brāhmaṇas.”

## \|\| 2.95.65 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*idaṃ stavaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ vyāsa te parikīrtitam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhiṣyati medhāvī tasya tuṣyati śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

65\. O Vyāsa, this prayer proclaimed by you is highly meritorious. Śaṅkara becomes pleased with the wise one who will read and recite this.

## \|\| 2.95.66 \|\|

*vyāsāṣṭakamidaṃ prātaḥ paṭhitavyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*duḥsvapnapāpaśamanaṃ śivasānnidhyakārakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. This Vyāsāṣṭaka (‘Eulogy in Eight Verses by Vyāsa’) is to be read and recited in the morning with concentration. It makes evil dreams and sins subside. It gives the devotee (salvation in the form of) vicinity to Śiva.

## \|\| 2.95.67 \|\|

*mātṛhā pitṛhā vāpi goghno bālaghra eva vā \|*  
*surāpī svarṇahṛdvāpi niṣpāpo syāḥ stuterjapāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. By repeated utterance of this prayer, all the sinners become rid of their sins, such as a slayer of mother, a slayer of father, a killer of cows, a killer of boys, an imbiber of liquor, a stealer of gold etc.

## \|\| 2.95.68-69 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*pārāśaryastadārabhya śaṃbhubhaktiparobhavat \|*  
*liṃgaṃ vyāseśvaraṃ sthāpya ghaṃṭākarṇa hradāgrataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*vibhūtibhūṣaṇo nityaṃ nityarudrākṣabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*rudrasūktaparo nityaṃ nityaṃ liṃgārcakobhavat \|\| 69 \|\|*

Skanda said:

68-69. Ever since then the son of Parāśara became devoted to Śaṃbhu. Beyond Ghaṇṭākarṇahrada, he installed the Liṅga called Vyāseśvara. He always embellished himself with holy ash. He adorned himself with Rudrākṣas always. He became forever a worshipper of the Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.95.70 \|\|

*sa kṛtvā kṣetrasaṃnyāsaṃ tyajennādyāpi kāśikām \|*  
*tattvaṃ kṣetrasya vijñāya nirvāṇapadadāyinaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He renounced (all other) holy spots. After knowing the reality of this holy spot that bestows salvation, he does not leave off Kāśikā till today.

## \|\| 2.95.71 \|\|

*ghaṃṭākarṇahrade snātvā dṛṣṭvā vyāseśvaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*yatrakutra mṛto vāpi vārāṇasyāṃ mṛto bhavet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. A man should take his bath in Ghaṇṭākarṇahrada and visit Vyāseśvara. Wherever he happens to die, he will be on a par with one who dies in Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.95.72 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ vyāseśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ pūjayitvā narottamaḥ \|*  
*na jñānādbhraśyate kvāpi pātakairnābhibhūyate \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. After adoring Vyāseśvara Liṅga in Kāśī an excellent man does not suffer from loss of knowledge at any time. He is never assailed (affected) by sins.

## \|\| 2.95.73 \|\|

*vyāseśvarasya ye bhaktā na teṣāṃ kalikālataḥ \|*  
*na pāpato bhayaṃ kvāpi na ca kṣetropasargataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. To the devotees of Vyāseśvara there is no fear from Kali and Kāla; there is neither the fear of sins nor of obstacles to the holy spot.

## \|\| 2.95.74 \|\|

*vyāseśvaraḥ prayatnena draṣṭavyaḥ kāśivāsibhiḥ \|*  
*ghaṃṭākarṇakṛtasnānaiḥ kṣetrapātakabhīrubhiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Vyāseśvara should be visited with effort by the residents of Kāśī who are afraid of sins. They take their holy ablution in Ghaṇṭākarṇa(hrada).

## Chapter 96 - Vyāsa Released from the Curse

## \|\| 2.96.1-2 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*kṛpṇadvaipāyanaḥ skaṃda śaṃbhubhaktiparo yadi \|*  
*yadi kṣetrarahasyajñaḥ kṣetrasaṃnyāsakṛdyadi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathā dṛṣṭaprabhāvaścettathā cejjñānināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ śreṣṭhāṃ kathaṃ kila śapiṣyati \|\| 2 \|\|*

Agastya enquired:

1-2. O Skanda, how will he curse the city of Vārāṇasī if Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana is an ardent devotee of Śaṃbhu, if he knows the secret of the holy place and has known (by personal experience) the efficacy of the holy spot (Vārāṇasī) and if he was the most excellent among the knowers (of spiritual wisdom)?

Skanda replied:

## \|\| 2.96.3 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*satyametattvayā pṛcchi kathayāmi mune śṛṇu \|*  
*tasya vyāsasya caritaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ tvayi pṛcchati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O sage, it is the truth that has been enquired about by you. I shall narrate it; listen. On your having enquired, I shall recount the future story of Vyāsa.

## \|\| 2.96.4 \|\|

*yadārabhya munestasya naṃdī staṃbhitavānbhujam \|*  
*tadārabhya maheśānaṃ saṃstauti paramādṛtaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Ever since Nandin paralysed the arm of that sage, he began to eulogize Maheśāna with great reverence.

## \|\| 2.96.5-6 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ tīrthānyanekāni kāśyāṃ ligānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi sevyo viśveśaḥ snātavyā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*liṃgeṣveko hi viśveśastīrtheṣu maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*iti saṃvyāharanvyāsastaddvayaṃ bahu manyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. “There are many Tīrthas in Kāśī. There are many Liṅgas in Kāśī. Still Viśveśa is to be resorted to and Maṇikarṇikā should be used for the holy ablution. Among Liṅgas the only (important one) is Viśveśa and among Tīrthas it is Maṇikarṇikā.” Saying thus Vyāsa honoured both of them.

## \|\| 2.96.7 \|\|

*tyaktvā sa bahu vāgjālaṃ prātaḥ snātvā dinedine \|*  
*nirvāṇamaṃḍape vakti mahimānaṃ maheśituḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Discarding much of verbose talk, everyday he bathed in the morning and began to extol the greatness of Maheśitā in the Pavilion of Salvation.

## \|\| 2.96.8 \|\|

*śiṣyāṇāṃ purato nityaṃ kṣetrasya mahimā mahān \|*  
*vyākhyāyate mudā tena vyāsena paramarṣiṇā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Everyday, in front of his disciples, the greatness of the holy spot was joyously described by Vyāsa, the great sage.

## \|\| 2.96.9 \|\|

*atra yatkriyate kṣetre śubhaṃ vā'śubhameva vā \|*  
*saṃvartepi na tasyāṃtastasmācchreyaḥ samācaret \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Whatever is done here, in this holy spot, auspicious or otherwise, does not perish even in Saṃvarta (final annihilation). Hence one should regularly practise what is conducive to welfare.

## \|\| 2.96.10 \|\|

*kṣetrasiddhiṃ samīhaṃte ye cātra kṛtino janāḥ \|*  
*yāvajjīvaṃ na taistyājyā sudhībhirmaṇikarṇikā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Maṇikarṇikā should never be abandoned by the wise as long as they live, if they, highly intelligent persons who have completed their work (duties), desire to attain Siddhi of this holy place.

## \|\| 2.96.11 \|\|

*cakrapuṣkariṇī tīrthe snātavyaṃ prativāsaram \|*  
*puṣpaiḥ patraiḥ phalaistoyairarcyo viśveśvaraḥ sadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Ablution should be performed everyday in the Cakrapuṣkariṇī Tīrtha (Maṇikarṇikā). Viśveśvara should always be adored with flowers (and Bilva) leaves, fruits and water.

## \|\| 2.96.12 \|\|

*svavarṇāśramadharmaśca tyaktavyo na manāgapi \|*  
*pratyahaṃ kṣetramahimā śrotavyaḥ śraddhayā sakṛt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The duty pertaining to one’s own Varṇa and Āśrama should not be discarded even in the least. The greatness of the holy spot should be incessantly listened to everyday with faith.

## \|\| 2.96.13 \|\|

*yathāśakti ca deyāni dānānyatra suguptavat \|*  
*annānyapi ca deyāni vighnānparijihīrṣuṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Religious gifts are to be made here very secretly and in accordance with one’s capacity. Cooked food also should be given by one who wants to avoid obstacles.

## \|\| 2.96.14 \|\|

*paropakaraṇaṃ cātra kartavyaṃ sudhiyā sadā \|*  
*parvasvapi viśeṣeṇa snānadānādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Extending help to others should be carried out always by a sensible man. So also the rites of ablution, making gifts etc. especially on festive occasions.

## \|\| 2.96.15 \|\|

*viśeṣapūjā kartavyā sumahotsavapūrvakama \|*  
*kāryāstathādhikā yātrāḥ samarcyāḥ kṣetradevatāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Special worship should be conducted with elaborate celebrations. So also worshipful processions should be taken out. The deities of the holy spot should be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.96.16 \|\|

*atra marma na vaktavyaṃ sudhiyāṃ kasyacitkvacit \|*  
*paradāra paradravya parāpakaraṇaṃ tyajet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. No weak and vulnerable points of anyone should be mentioned anywhere here by the wise. One should (refrain from) other men’s wives, other people’s possessions and injury to others.

## \|\| 2.96.17 \|\|

*parāpavādo no vācyaḥ parerṣyāṃ na ca kārayet \|*  
*asatyaṃ naiva vaktavyaṃ prāṇaiḥ kaṃṭhagatairapi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Scandalous words about others should not be uttered. Jealousy should not be evinced in regard to others. Untruth should not be uttered even when the vital airs are choked in the throat.

## \|\| 2.96.18-19 \|\|

*atratya jaṃturakṣārthamasatyamapi bhāṣayet \|*  
*yenakenaprakāreṇa śubhenāpyaśubhena vā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*atratyaḥ prāṇimātropi rakṣaṇīyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*ekasminrakṣite jaṃtāvatra kāśyāṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*trailokyarakṣaṇātpuṇyaṃ yatsyāttatsyānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. One can utter untruth in order to save a creature living here. All living beings of this place should be assiduously protected by any means whatsoever, auspicious or inauspicious. If one creature is assiduously saved here in Kāśī, there is no doubt about this that one will attain that merit which one is likely to get by protecting the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.96.20 \|\|

*ye vasaṃti sadā kāśyāṃ kṣetrasaṃnyāsakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*ta eva rudrā maṃtavyā jīvanmuktā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Those who stay in Kāśī always, those who establish the installations within the precincts of the holy spot, should be considered Rudras. They are undoubtedly living liberated souls.

## \|\| 2.96.21 \|\|

*te pūjyāste namaskāryāste saṃtoṣyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*teṣu vai parituṣṭeṣu tuṣyedviśveśvaraḥ svayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. They should be adored. They should be bowed to. They should be made happy. If they are happy Viśveśvara himself will be happy.

## \|\| 2.96.22 \|\|

*kāśyāṃ vasaṃti ye martyā dūrasthairapi sannaraiḥ \|*  
*yogakṣemo vidhātavyasteṣāṃ viśveśiturmude \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. For the joy of Viśveśa, everything possible for acquiring and preserving the good of the people who stay in Kāśī should be done by even those good men who are far off.

## \|\| 2.96.23 \|\|

*prasarastviṃdriyāṇāṃ ca nivāryotra nivāsibhiḥ \|*  
*manasopi hi cāṃcalyamiha vāryaṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Free play of passions should be curbed by those who stay here. The fickleness of the mind too should be assiduously avoided here.

## \|\| 2.96.24 \|\|

*maraṇaṃ nābhikāṃkṣeddhi kāṃkṣyo mokṣo'pino punaḥ \|*  
*śarīraśoṣaṇopāyaḥ kartavyaḥ sudhiyā nahi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Death should not be directly desired here. Salvation too should not be wished for ardently. Means for drying up the body should not be undertaken by a sensible man.

## \|\| 2.96.25 \|\|

*śarīrasauṣṭhavaṃ kāṃkṣyaṃ vratasnānādisiddhaye \|*  
*āyurbahvatra vai ciṃtyaṃ mahāphalasamṛddhaye \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Perfection in functioning of the body should be desired for the fulfilment of the Vratas, ablution etc. Ample longevity should be thought of here for the flourishing growth of the great benefit.

## \|\| 2.96.26 \|\|

*ātmarakṣātra kartavyā mahāśreyobhivṛddhaye \|*  
*atrātma tyajanopāyaṃ manasāpi na ciṃtayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Self-protection should be done here for the increase of the good. One should not even mentally think of abandoning one’s body.

## \|\| 2.96.27 \|\|

*ekasminnapi yaccāhni kāśyāṃ śreyobhilabhyate \|*  
*na tu varṣaśatenāpi tadanyatrāpyate kvacit \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The good that is obtained in Kāśī in the course of a single day is not obtained in the course of even a hundred years anywhere else.

## \|\| 2.96.28 \|\|

*anyatra yogābhyasanādyāvajjanma yadarjyate \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ tadekena prāṇāyāmena labhyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. What is obtained elsewhere by means of Yogic practice throughout the life, is attained in Vārāṇasī by means of a singly Prāṇāyāma.

## \|\| 2.96.29 \|\|

*sarvatīrthāvagāhācca yāvajjanma yadarjyate \|*  
*tadānaṃdavane prāpyaṃ maṇikarṇyekamajjanāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. What is obtained by taking bath in all the Tīrthas throughout the life, can be obtained in Ānandavana by bathing in Maṇikarṇikā alone.

## \|\| 2.96.30 \|\|

*sarvaliṃgārcanātpuṇyaṃ yāvajjanma yadarjyate \|*  
*sakṛdviśveśamabhyarcya śraddhayā tadavāpyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. What is obtained as merit by worshipping all the Liṅgas throughout the life, is obtained by worshipping Viśveśa (only) once with faith.

## \|\| 2.96.31 \|\|

*yajjanmanāṃ sahasreṇa nirmalaṃ puṇyamarjitam \|*  
*tatpuṇyaparivartena bhavedviśveśadarśanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Obtaining a sight of Viśveśa may be possible by exchanging that faultless merit which has been acquired in the course of a thousand births.

## \|\| 2.96.32 \|\|

*gavāṃ koṭi pradānena samyagdattena yatphalama \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samyagāpyeta viśveśvara vilokanāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. By having a sight of Viśveśvara that merit is perfectly obtained that is acquired by duly making the gift of a crore of cows.

## \|\| 2.96.33 \|\|

*yatṣoḍaśamahādānaiḥ puṇyaṃ proktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*tatpuṇyaṃ jāyate puṃsāṃ viśveśe puṣpadānataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The merit said by the great sages to be obtained by making sixteen great religious gifts, comes to men by offering flowers unto Viśveśa.

## \|\| 2.96.34 \|\|

*aśvamedhādibhiryajñairyatphalaṃ prāpyatekhilaiḥ \|*  
*paṃcāmṛtānāṃ snapanādviśveśe tadavāpyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Whatever merit is obtained by everyone through horse-sacrifice and other Yajñas is acquired by bathing Viśveśa with Pañcāmṛta.

## \|\| 2.96.35 \|\|

*vājapeyasahasreṇa samyagiṣṭena yatphalam \|*  
*sakṛnmahārhairnaivedyairviśveśe tacchatādhikam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A hundred times of the merit acquired by a faultless performance of a thousand Vājapeyas, is obtained by offering valuable Naivedyas unto Viśveśa once (only).

## \|\| 2.96.36 \|\|

*dhvajātapatraṃ camaraṃ viśveśe yaḥ samarpayet \|*  
*ekacchatraṃ sa vai rājyaṃ prāpnuyādvasudhātale \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He who dedicates unto Viśveśa a banner, an umbrella and chowries shall obtain the rulership of the entire earth under his single Royal Umbrella.

## \|\| 2.96.37 \|\|

*mahāpūjopakaraṇaṃ yorpayedviśvabhartari \|*  
*na taṃ saṃpattisaṃbhārā vimuṃcaṃtīha kutracit \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Affluent collection of all requisite things will never leave a person who offers to the Lord of the universe all the ingredients of the great worship.

## \|\| 2.96.38 \|\|

*sarvartukusumāḍhyāṃ ca yaḥ kuryātpuṣpavāṭikām \|*  
*tadaṃgaṇe kalpavṛkṣāśchāyāṃ kurvaṃti śītalām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Wish-yielding celestial trees will spread cool shade in the courtyard of the devotee who makes a flower-garden with all the flowers of all the seasons.

## \|\| 2.96.39 \|\|

*yaḥ kṣīrasnapanārthaṃ vai viśveśe dhenumarpayet \|*  
*kṣīrārṇavataṭe tasya nivaseyuḥ pitāmahāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If a devotee offers unto Viśveśa a cow for the purpose of milk intended for bathing the Lord, his grandfathers will reside on the shores of the Milk Ocean.

## \|\| 2.96.40 \|\|

*viśveśarājasadane yaḥ sudhāṃ citrameva vā \|*  
*kārayettasya bhavanaṃ kailāsacitritaṃ bhavet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If a devotee gets the coating with lime done in the palatial abodes of Viśveśa or gets paintings done (on the wall), his own abode will be painted in Kailāsa.

## \|\| 2.96.41-43 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānyatino vāpi tathaiva śivayoginaḥ \|*  
*bhojayedyotra vai kāśyāmekaika gaṇanā kramāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

*koṭibhojyaphalaṃ tasya śraddhayā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tapastvatra prakartavyaṃ dānamatra pradāpayet \|\| 42 \|\|*

*viśveśastoṣaṇīyotra snānahomajapādibhiḥ \|*  
*anyatra koṭijapyena yatphalaṃ prāpyate naraiḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottaraśataṃ japtvā tadatra samavāpyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. If a devotee feeds Brāhmaṇas, ascetics or Śivayogins here in Kāśī, there is no doubt about this that he will get the benefit of feeding a crore of persons with faith for each of such persons.

Penance should be performed here; gifts must be made here; Viśveśa should be propitiated here by means of baths, Homas, Japas etc. What is obtained elsewhere by men by making a crore of Japas is obtained here by a hundred and eight Japas only.

## \|\| 2.96.44 \|\|

*koṭihomena yatproktaṃ phalamanyatra sūribhiḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottarāhutiśatāttadatrānaṃdakānane \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. What is said to be the merit acquired through a crore of Homas elsewhere by learned sages, can be acquired here in Ānandakānana through a hundred and eight Āhutis.

## \|\| 2.96.45 \|\|

*yo japedrudrasūktāni kāśyāṃ viśveśasannidhau \|*  
*pārāyaṇena vedānāṃ sarveṣāṃ phalamāpyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. If Rudrasūktas are recited in Kāśī in the vicinity of Viśveśa, the merit of the recitation of all the Vedas is obtained.

## \|\| 2.96.46 \|\|

*tasya puṇyaṃ na jānāmi ciṃtite cākṣare pare \|*  
*kāśyāṃ nityaṃ pravastavyaṃ sevyottaravahā sadā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I do not know (adequately) the merit of one who meditates on the great immutable, Absolute. Residence should always be made in Kāśī. The north-flowing (river) should always be resorted to.

## \|\| 2.96.47 \|\|

*āpadyapi hi ghorāyāṃ kāśī tyājyā na kutracit \|*  
*yataḥ sarvāpadāṃhartā trātā viśvapatiḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Even at the time of terrible disaster Kāśī should never be abandoned, because Lord Viśvapati is the protector (of devotees) and the remover of their adversities.

## \|\| 2.96.48 \|\|

*avaṃdhyaṃ divasaṃ kuryātsnānadānajapādibhiḥ \|*  
*yataḥ kāśyāṃ kṛtaṃ karma mahattvāya prakalpate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Through holy baths, gifts, Japas etc., the day should be made fruitful, because the rite performed in Kāśī is conducive to greatness.

## \|\| 2.96.49 \|\|

*kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇādīni kartavyāni prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tatheṃdriyavikārāśca na bādhaṃtetra karhicit \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Kṛcchracāndrāyaṇa and other (expiatory) rites should be assiduously performed so that the aberrations of the sense-organs do not at all harass one here.

## \|\| 2.96.50 \|\|

*yadīṃdriyāṇi kurvaṃti vikriyāmiha dehinām \|*  
*tadātravāsasaṃ siddhirvighnebhyo naiva labhyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. If the sense-organs corrupt the embodied ones inordinately the desire of obtaining a residence here is not fulfilled on account of obstacles.

## \|\| 2.96.51 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*kṛcchra cāṃdrāyaṇādīni vyāso vakṣyati yāni vai \|*  
*teṣāṃ svarūpamākhyāhi skaṃdeṃdriya viśuddhaye \|\| 51 \|\|*

Agastya said:

51\. O Skanda, narrate the characteristic features of those rites of Kṛcchracāndrāyaṇa etc., which Vyāsa will be expounding for purifying- the sense-organs.

## \|\| 2.96.52 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*kathayāmi mahābuddhe kṛcchrādīni tavāgrataḥ \|*  
*yāni kṛtvātra manujo dehaśuddhiṃ labhetparām \|\| 52 \|\|*

Skanda said:

52\. O highly intelligent one, I shall describe to you Kṛcchra etc., through the performance of which a man obtains great purity of the body.

## \|\| 2.96.53 \|\|

*ekabhaktena naktena tathaivāyācitena ca \|*  
*upavāsena caikena pādakṛcchraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Pādakṛcchra has been explained thus: the devotee takes only a single meal at night of what is obtained without requesting for it or he fasts a single day.

## \|\| 2.96.54 \|\|

*vaṭoduṃbararājīva bilvapatrakuśodakam \|*  
*pratyekaṃ pratyahaṃ pītaṃ parṇakṛcchraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Parṇakṛcchra is described as that expiation in which the water wherein leaves of banyan, Udumbara, lotus, Bilva (are boiled separately on each day (in succession) is drunk (with Kuśa dipped therein) everyday.

## \|\| 2.96.55 \|\|

*piṇyākaghṛtatakrāṃbu saktūnāṃ prativāsaram \|*  
*ekaikamupavāsaśca kṛcchraḥ saumyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Saumyakṛcchra has been explained thus: Each of the following is separately eaten each day: oil cake, ghee, buttermilk, wheat flour and water and fast is observed (cf. Yājñavalkya Smṛti III.321).

## \|\| 2.96.56-57 \|\|

*haviṣā prātaraśnīta haviṣā sāyameva ca \|*  
*haviṣā yācitaṃ trīṃstu sopavāsastrayahaṃ vaset \|\| 56 \|\|*

*ekaikagrāsamaśnīyādahāni trīṇi pūrvavat \|*  
*tryahaṃ copavasedaṃtyamatikṛcchraṃ carandvijaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. A Brāhmaṇa observing Atikṛcchra does as follows: He eats Havis in the morning for three days; Havis in the evening for three days obtained without request; Havis for three days and then observes fast for three days or as before takes in a morsel of food and observes fast for three days.

## \|\| 2.96.58 \|\|

*kṛcchrātikṛcchraṃ payasā divasānekaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*dvādaśāhopavāsena parākaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Kṛcchrātikṛcchra rite consists of taking in milk for twenty-one days. Parāka rite is explained as a rite in which a devotee observes fast for twelve days.

## \|\| 2.96.59 \|\|

*tryahaṃ prātastrayahaṃ sāyaṃ tryahamadyādayācitam \|*  
*tryahaṃ copavasedaṃtyaṃ prājāpatyaṃ carandvijaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A Brāhmaṇa performing the Antyaprājāpatya rite does as follows: He takes food in the morning for three days, then in the evening for three days, and then takes in food not begged for three days, and then observes fast for three days.

## \|\| 2.96.60 \|\|

*gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhisarpiḥ kuśodakam \|*  
*ekarātropavāsaśca kṛcchraḥ sāṃtapanaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. This (following) rite is known as Sāntapanakṛcchra. Cow’s urine, cowdung, milk, curds, ghee and Kuśa water—all these are mixed together and consumed. Fast is observed for a night.

## \|\| 2.96.61 \|\|

*pṛthaksāṃtapanadravyaiḥ ṣaḍahaḥ sopavāsakaḥ \|*  
*saptāhena tu kṛcchroyaṃ mahāsāṃtapanaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. This rite is known as Mahāsāntapanakṛcchra: In it the articles prescribed for Sāntapana are taken severally for six days and fast is observed on the seventh.

## \|\| 2.96.62-64 \|\|

*taptakṛcchraṃ caranvipro jalakṣīraghṛtānilān \|*  
*etāṃstryahaṃ pibeduṣṇānsakṛtsnāyī samāhitaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tryahamuṣṇāḥ pibedāpastryahamuṣṇaṃ payaḥ pibet \|*  
*tryahamuṣṇaghṛtaṃ prāśya vāyubhakṣo dinatrayam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*palamekaṃ payaḥ pītvā sarpiṣaśca paladvayam \|*  
*palamekaṃ tu toyasya taptakṛcchra udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. A Brāhmaṇa performing Taptakṛcchra expiation takes bath once. With great concentration and purity he drinks for three days hot water, milk, ghee and wind. For three days he drinks hot water, then he drinks hot milk for three days and then he drinks hot ghee for three days and for three days he takes in only air (i.e. observes fast). If it is milk or water, he drinks one Pala thereof and in the case of ghee it is two Palas. I have explained Taptakṛcchra.

## \|\| 2.96.65 \|\|

*gomūtreṇa samāyuktaṃ yāvakaṃ yaḥ prayojayet \|*  
*kṛcchramekāhnkiṃ proktaṃ śarīrasya viśodhanam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Ekāhnikakṛcchra is described as follows: The devotee takes in cooked barley mixed with cow’s urine. It purifies the body.

## \|\| 2.96.66 \|\|

*hastāvuttānataḥ kṛtvā divasaṃ mārutāśanaḥ \|*  
*rātrau jale sthito vyuṣṭaḥ prājāpatyena tatsamam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. This is on a par with Prājāpatya rite. The hands are kept stretched out the whole day. Only air is inhaled. The devotee stands in water throughout the night till dawn.

## \|\| 2.96.67 \|\|

*ekaikaṃ hrāsayedgrāsaṃ kṛṣṇe śukle ca vardhayet \|*  
*upaspṛśaṃ striṣavaṇametaccāṃdrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The following rite is known as Cāndrāyaṇa: During the dark half of the month, the devotee reduces the number of morsels by one everyday and during the bright half increases it by one everyday and drinks water three times everyday (The maximum number of morsels is fifteen on full-moon day).

## \|\| 2.96.68 \|\|

*ekaikaṃ vardhayedgrāsaṃ śukle kṛṣṇe ca hrāsayet \|*  
*bhuṃjīta darśe no kiṃcideṣa cāṃdrāyaṇo vidhiḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. This is the injunction regarding Cāndrāyaṇa: In the bright half the number of morsels is increased by one everyday and is reduced by one in the dark half. Nothing is eaten on the new-moon day.

## \|\| 2.96.69 \|\|

*caturaḥ prātaraśnīyātpiṃḍānvipraḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*caturostamite sūrye śiśucāṃdrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. A Brāhmaṇa with mental concentration and purity shall eat four lumps of rice in the morning and four lumps after sunset. This is known as Śiśu Cāndrāyaṇa.

## \|\| 2.96.70 \|\|

*aṣṭāvaṣṭau samaśnīyātpiṃḍānmadhyaṃdine sthite \|*  
*niyatātmā haviṣyasya yaticāṃdrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. A devotee with controlled self eats eight riceballs of sacrificial food at midday regularly. This is known as Yaticāndrāyaṇa.

## \|\| 2.96.71 \|\|

*yathākathaṃcitpiṃḍānāṃ tisrośītīḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*māsenāśnanhaviṣyasya caṃdrasyaiti salokatām \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. With concentration and mental purity the devotee on the whole eats three times eighty (i.e. 240) Haviṣya lumps in the course of a month (i.e. eight morsels per day), He goes to the world of Candra (Moon).

## \|\| 2.96.72 \|\|

*adbhirgātrāṇi śudhyaṃti manaḥ satyena śuddhyati \|*  
*vidyā tapobhyāṃ bhūtātmā buddhirjñānena śuddhyati \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Limbs become pure with water, mind with truth, ego (Bhūtātmā) through learning and austerities and intellect becomes pure with knowledge.

## \|\| 2.96.73 \|\|

*tacca jñānaṃ bhavetpuṃsāṃ samyakkāśīniṣevaṇāt \|*  
*kāśīniṣevaṇena syādviśveśakaruṇodayaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. That knowledge comes to men by serving or residing in Kāśī. The rise of compassion of Viśveśa also occurs by serving (resorting) to Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.96.74-80 \|\|

*tato mahodayāvāptiḥ karmanirmūlanakṣamā \|*  
*ataḥ kāśyāṃ prayatnena snāna dāna tapo japaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*vrataṃ purāṇaśravaṇaṃ smṛtyuktādhva niṣevaṇam \|*  
*pratikṣaṇe pratidinaṃ viśveśa padaciṃtanam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*liṃgārcanaṃ trikālaṃ ca liṃgasyāpi pratiṣṭhitiḥ \|*  
*sādhubhiḥ saha saṃlāpo jalpaḥ śivaśiveti ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

*atitheścāpi satkāro maitrītīrthanivāsibhiḥ \|*  
*āstikyabuddhirvinayo mānāmāna samānadhīḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*akāmitā tvanauddhatyamarāgitvamahiṃsanam \|*  
*apratigrahavṛttiśca matiścānugrahātmikā \|\| 78 \|\|*

*adaṃbhitātvamātsaryamaprārthitadhanāgamaḥ \|*  
*alobhitvamanālasyamapāruṣyamadīnatā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*ityādi satpravṛttiśca kartavyā kṣetravāsinā \|*  
*pratyahaṃ ceti śiṣyebhyaḥ sadharmamupadekṣyati \|\| 80 \|\|*

74-80. Then (is) the attainment of Mahodaya (‘great rise’ i.e. salvation) capable of eradicating Karmas. Hence one shall duly observe and practise assiduously holy bath, make gifts, penance, Japa, Vrata, listen to the Purāṇas, resort to the path indicated by Smṛtis, think of the feet of Viśveśa every moment, everyday, do worship of the Liṅgas three times, install Liṅgas, converse with good men, repeat the name Śiva, Śiva, give hospitable reception to a guest, make friendship with the other residents of the holy spot, to have faith in God, practice humility, remain unmoved by honour and insult, be free from lust, give up arrogance, practice non-attachment, abstain from violence, maintain (oneself) without receiving monetary gifts, be inclined to favour others, be free from hypocrisy, jealousy and spirit of competitiveness, acquire wealth without craving for it, practice non-covetousness, absence of lassitude, want of harshness and wretchedness. All these activities of a good man should be pursued by a resident of the holy spot. Thus he will impart instruction in piety to his disciples everyday.

## \|\| 2.96.81 \|\|

*nityaṃ triṣavaṇasnāyī nityaṃ bhikṣākṛtāśanaḥ \|*  
*liṃgapūjārcako nityamitthaṃ vyāso vasetpurā \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Vyāsa will be staying thus: taking bath thrice everyday, partaking of the alms received everyday and worshipping the Liṅgas everyday.

## \|\| 2.96.82-88 \|\|

*ekadā tasya jijñāsāṃ kartuṃ devīṃ harovadat \|*  
*adya bhikṣāṭanaṃ prāpte vyāse paramadhārmike \|\| 82 \|\|*

*api sarvagate kvāpi bhikṣāṃ mā yaccha suṃdari \|*  
*tathetyuktā bhavānī sā bhavaṃ bhavanivāraṇam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*namaskṛtya pratigṛhaṃ tasya bhikṣāṃ nyaṣedhayat \|*  
*sa muniḥ sahitaḥ śiṣyairbhikṣāmaprāpya dūnavat \|\| 84 \|\|*

*velātikramamālokya punarbabhrāma tāṃ purīm \|*  
*gṛhegṛhe pariprāptā bhikṣānyaiḥ sarvabhikṣukaiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tadahninālabhadbhikṣāṃ saśiṣyaḥ sa muniḥ kvacit \|*  
*atha sāyaṃtanaṃ karma kṛtvā chātraiḥ samanvitaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*upoṣaṇaparo bhūtvā tathaivāsīdaharniśam \|*  
*athānyedyurmunirvyāsaḥ kṛtvā mādhyāhnikaṃ vidhim \|\| 87 \|\|*

*yayau bhikṣāṭanaṃ kartuṃ saśiṣyaḥ paritaḥ purīm \|*  
*sarvatra sa paribhrāṃtaḥ pratisaudhaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

82-88. Once Hara was desirous of testing him. He spoke to the Goddess: “When Vyāsa, the extremely pious one, comes for alms today, O fair lady, do not give him alms anywhere.” Saying “So it shall be” to Bhava, the eradicator of worldly existence, Bhavānī went round every house. She bowed down to all and forbade giving alms to him (and his disciples). Unable to get the alms the sage and his disciples became dejected. Seeing that the time had elapsed, he wandered in the city again. Alms were duly received by all the other mendicants at every house but that sage and his disciples did not receive the alms anywhere. Accompanied by his disciples, he concluded the evening rites and remained without food thus for the whole day and night. The next day the sage performed the midday rites and went round the city begging for alms along with his disciples. He wandered everywhere visiting every house again and again.

## \|\| 2.96.89 \|\|

*na kvāpi labdhavānbhikṣāṃ bhāgyahīno dhanaṃ yathā \|*  
*atha ciṃtitavānvyāsaḥ pariśrāṃtaḥ paribhraman \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. He did not get alms anywhere like an unlucky fellow unable to get money. Then Vyāsa, utterly weary after his wandering thought:

## \|\| 2.96.90 \|\|

*ko heturyanna labhyeta bhikṣā yatnena rakṣitā \|*  
*aṃtevāsina āhūya vyāsaḥ papraccha cākhilān \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. ‘What may be the reason that alms cannot be obtained though assiduously sought after?’ He summoned his disciples. Vyāsa asked everyone:

## \|\| 2.96.91-95 \|\|

*bhavadbhirapi no bhikṣā pariprāpteti gamyate \|*  
*kimatra puri saṃvṛttaṃ dvitrā yāta mamājñayā \|\| 91 \|\|*

*dvitīyehnyapi yadbhikṣā na labhyetātiyatnataḥ \|*  
*aniṣṭaṃ kiṃcidatrāsīnmahāgurunipātajam \|\| 92 \|\|*

*annakṣayo vā sarvasyāṃ nagaryāmabhavatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*rājadaṃḍotha yugapajjātaḥ sarvapuraukasām \|\| 93 \|\|*

*athavā vāritā bhikṣā kenāpyasmāsu cerṣyayā \|*  
*puraukasobhavandusthāstūpasargeṇa kenacit \|\| 94 \|\|*

*kimetadakhilamajñātvā samāgacchata satvaram \|*  
*dvitrāḥ pavitracaraṇātprāpyānujñāṃ guroratha \|*  
*samācakhyuḥ samāgamya dṛṣṭvarddhi tatpuraukasām \|\| 95 \|\|*

91-95. “It seems that all of you too did not get alms. What has happened in this city? At my behest two or three of you go out. If alms cannot be got even on the second day despite best efforts, it is certain that some calamity has befallen arising out of great disaster. Instantly there has broken out a great famine for food in the entire city. Or a royal punishment has been meted out to all the citizens. Otherwise alms have been forbidden by someone out of malice towards us. Have the citizens become wretched by some mysterious portent foreboding evil. Go and find out all these things and return quickly.” Getting the permission from the holy preceptor two or three disciples noticed the opulence of the citizens and after returning said thus:

## \|\| 2.96.96-97 \|\|

*śiṣyā ūcuḥ \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃtvārādhyacaraṇā nopasargotra kaścana \|*  
*nānnakṣayo vā sarvasyāṃ nagaryāmiha kutracit \|\| 96 \|\|*

*yatra viśveśvaraḥ sākṣādyatrā'maradhunī svayam \|*  
*tvādṛśā yatra munayaḥ kva bhīstatropasargajā \|\| 97 \|\|*

The Disciples said:

96-97. May the worthy Sir listen. There is no great disaster here. There is no dearth of cooked food anywhere in the entire city. How can there be the fear of any mysterious portent where sages like you are present and where Viśveśvara is directly stationed and the celestial river also flows?

## \|\| 2.96.98 \|\|

*samṛddhiryā gṛhasthānāmiha viśveśituḥ puri \|*  
*na sarddhirasti vaikuṃṭhe svalpāstā alakādayaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Even in Vaikuṇṭha there is no such affluence as that of the householders here in the city of Viśveśa. (Cities like) Alakā etc. are extremely insignificant.

## \|\| 2.96.99 \|\|

*ratnākareṣu ratnāni na tāvaṃti mahāmune \|*  
*yāvaṃti saṃti viśveśanirmālyopabhujāṃ gṛhe \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O great sage, there are not as many jewels in oceans as there are in the houses of these people, who partake of the remnants of the worship of Viśveśa.

## \|\| 2.96.100 \|\|

*gṛhegṛhetra dhānyānāṃ rāśayo yādṛśaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*na tādṛśaḥ kalpavṛkṣadattā aiṃdre pure kvacit \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. There are heaps of grain in every house. Such heaps are not present anywhere in the city of Indra bequeathed by the celestial trees.

## \|\| 2.96.101 \|\|

*yatra sākṣādviśālākṣī suvistāraphalapradā \|*  
*na tatra puri sarvasyāṃ naro vai nirdhanaḥ kvacit \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. There is no poor man anywhere is that entire city where Viśālākṣī herself bestows extensive benefits.

## \|\| 2.96.102 \|\|

*nirvāṇalakṣmyāḥ sadane tvasminnānaṃdakānane \|*  
*mokṣopi yatra sulabhaḥ kimanyattatra durlabham \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. This Ānandakānana is the abode of the glory of salvation where salvation is easily accessible. How can anything else be rare there?

## \|\| 2.96.103 \|\|

*sīmaṃtinyaḥ striyaḥ sarvāḥ pativrataparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*sarvā bhavānī rūpiṇyo viśveśārpitasatkriyāḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. All the women are chaste and have their husbands alive. All of them have the form of Bhavānī. They have dedicated their righteous activities to Viśveśa.

## \|\| 2.96.104 \|\|

*yāvaṃtaḥ puruṣāḥ kāśyāṃ sarva eva gaṇādhipāḥ \|*  
*sarva eva kumārā vai sarve tārakadṛṣṭayaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The entire menfolk in Kāśī are the leaders of Gaṇas. All of them are Kumāras (Lord Kārttikeya). All have Tārakadṛṣṭi (vision of redemption).

## \|\| 2.96.105-107 \|\|

*tripuṃḍrāṃkitabhālā ye te sarve caṃdramaulayaḥ \|*  
*upasargasahasraiśca pīḍyamānā apīha ye \|\| 105 \|\|*

*na tyajaṃti sadā kāśīṃ sarvajñā eva tekhilāḥ \|*  
*gṛhegṛhepi vaṭavo brahmavādavivādinaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*svardhunī dhūtakaluṣāḥ saṃtīha caturānanāḥ \|*  
*nirvāṇalakṣmīpatayaḥ kṣetrasaṃnyāsakāriṇaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

105-107. Those whose foreheads are marked with Tripuṇḍra (three parallel lines of holy ash) have become moon-crested ones. Even those afflicted with thousands of calamities, do not leave Kāśī. All of them are Sarvajñas (identical with omniscient Lord Siva). In every house there are students expounding and discussing the topic of Brahman. All their sins have been washed off by the heavenly river. They have become the four-faced lord Brahmā (They are very clever and eloquent.) They are the lords of the glory of liberation. They stay permanently at the holy spot.

## \|\| 2.96.108 \|\|

*sarva eva hṛṣīkeśāḥ sarve vai puruṣottamāḥ \|*  
*acyutā eva vijñeyā etatkṣetraparigrahāḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Those who have resorted to this holy spot are Hṛṣīkeśas, Puruṣottamas, and should be known as Acyutas.

## \|\| 2.96.109 \|\|

*striyo vā puruṣā vāpi sarva eva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sarva eva trinayanāḥ sarva eva caturbhujāḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Whether women or men, all of them are entirely perfect, identical with the Three-eyed Lord and the Four-armed Lord.

## \|\| 2.96.110 \|\|

*śrīkaṃṭhāḥ sarva evātra sarve mṛtyuṃjayā dhruvam \|*  
*mokṣaśrī śritavarṣmāṇastvardhanārīśvarāyataḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. All of them are Srīkaṇṭhas here. All have certainly conquered death. Since they are Ardhanārīśvaras, they have their persons resorted to by the glory of salvation.

## \|\| 2.96.111 \|\|

*dharmarāśiḥ paraścātra mahāṃto'trārtharāśayaḥ \|*  
*sarve kāmāḥ phalaṃtyatra kaivalyaṃ cātra nirmalam \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. The mass of piety here is great. There are many great heaps of wealth. All desires bear fruit here. Kaivalya (Salvation) is free from impurity here.

## \|\| 2.96.112 \|\|

*na garbhavāsasaṃsargaḥ kāśīsaṃsthitikāriṇām \|*  
*na kaliścātra bādheta kālo naiva prabādhate \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Those who die in Kāśī do not have any contact with a womb thereafter. Neither Kali nor Kāla torment this holy spot.

## \|\| 2.96.113-114 \|\|

*enāṃsi nātra bādhaṃte viśveśaśaraṇārthinaḥ \|*  
*yatra viśveśvaraḥ sākṣānnādabiṃdukalātmakaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

*dhvanirūpī hi tatrāsti praṇavo maṃtravigrahaḥ \|*  
*ato vigrahavaṃtotra saṃti vedā viniścitam \|\| 114 \|\|*

113-114. Sins do not torment those who seek refuge in Viśveśa in this place. Where Viśveśvara is directly present in the form of Nāda, Bindu and Kalā, Praṇava with Mantras for its physical form is present in the form of Dhvani (sound). Hence it is certain that the Vedas in their physical form are here (they are present in personified forms).

## \|\| 2.96.115-121 \|\|

*sarasvatī saridrūpā hyataḥ śāstraniketanam \|*  
*ānaṃdakānanaṃ sarvaṃ dharmaśāstrakṛtālayam \|\| 115 \|\|*

*yāvaṃto divi vai devāstāvaṃtotra mṛṣā na hi \|*  
*nīrājayaṃti viśveśaṃ rātrau rātrau sadā'hayaḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

*svaphaṇāmaṇidīpaiśca prāpya kāśīṃ rasātalāt \|*  
*samudrāḥ sarva evātra kāmadhenuvrajānvitāḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

*paṃcapīyūṣadhārābhirviśveśaṃ snapayaṃti hi \|*  
*maṃdāraḥ pārijātaśca saṃtāno haricaṃdanaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*kalpadrumaśca paṃcaite tarubhiḥ saha sarvadā \|\| 119 \|\|*

*sarve suranikāyāśca sarva eva maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*yoginaḥ sarva evātra kāśīnāthamupāsate \|\| 120 \|\|*

*vidyānāṃ sadanaṃ kāśī kāśī lakṣmyāḥ parālayaḥ \|*  
*muktikṣetramidaṃ kāśī kāśī sarvā trayīmayī \|\| 121 \|\|*

115-121. Sarasvatī is in the form of a river. Therefore, the whole of Ānandakānana is an abode of scriptures; the Dharmaśāstras have their abode here. It is not false that all the Devas in heaven are entirely present here. Serpents come here from Rasātala and perform the rite of Nīrājana (‘waving of lights’) to Viśveśa every night by means of the lights of the jewels in their hoods. All the oceans along with the herds of Kāmadhenus bathe Viśveśvara with the flow of Pañcāmṛta. The five celestial trees, Mandāra, Pārijāta, Santāna, Haricandana and Kalpadruma, are always present here along with the other trees. All the groups of Suras, all the great sages and all the Yogins attend upon the Lord of Kāśī. Kāśī is the abode of lores. Kāśī is the great home of Lakṣmī. Kāśī is the holy spot of salvation. The entire city of Kāśī is in the form of the three Vedas.

## \|\| 2.96.122 \|\|

*iti śrutvā munivaraḥ pārāśaryo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ babhāṣe tāñśiṣyānpunaḥślokaṃ paṭhaṃtvamum \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. On hearing this, the son of Parāśara of great austere penance spoke thus to his disciples: “Repeat this Śloka.”

## \|\| 2.96.123 \|\|

*śiṣyā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vidyānāṃ cāśrayaḥ kāśī kāśī lakṣmyāḥ parālayaḥ \|*  
*muktikṣetramidaṃ kāśī kāśī sarvā trayīmayī \|\| 123 \|\|*

The Disciples said:

123\. Kāśī is the support of all lores. Kāśī is the great home of Lakṣmī. Kāśī is the holy spot of salvation. Kāśī is the entire extent of the three Vedas.

## \|\| 2.96.124 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*niśamyeti tadā vyāsaḥ krodhāṃdhīkṛtalocanaḥ \|*  
*kṣutkṛśānujvalanmūrtiḥ kāśīṃ śapsyati kuṃbhaja \|\| 124 \|\|*

Skanda said:

124\. On hearing this, Vyāsa shall become blinded with anger. His whole body will be burning with the fire of hunger. O Pot-born One, he will curse Kāśī.

Vyāsa said (i.e. will say):

## \|\| 2.96.125 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*mā bhūttraipūruṣīvidyā mā bhūttraipūruṣaṃ dhanam \|*  
*mā bhūttraipṛruṣī muktiḥ kāśīṃ vyāsaḥ śapanniti \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. May not scholarship continue for three generations! May not wealth continue for three generations! May salvation not be continuous for three generations!

Thus Vyāsa curses Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.96.126 \|\|

*garvaḥ parotra vidyānāṃ dhanagarvotra vai mahān \|*  
*muktigarveṇa no bhikṣāṃ prayacchaṃtyatra vāsinaḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. ‘Here arrogance of scholarship is excessive. The arrogance of wealth is also excessive here. The residents of this place do not give alms due to the arrogance of certainty of salvation.’

## \|\| 2.96.127 \|\|

*iti kṛtvā matiṃ vyāsaḥ kāśyāṃ śāpamadāttadā \|*  
*dattvāpi śāpaṃ sa munirbhikṣituṃ krodhavānyayau \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Thinking thus Vyāsa cursed Kāśī then. Even after cursing, the angry sage went for alms.

## \|\| 2.96.128 \|\|

*pratigehaṃ tvarāyuktaḥ praviśanvyomadattadṛk \|*  
*babhrāma nagarīṃ sarvāṃ kvāpi bhaikṣaṃ na labdhavān \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. He entered every house hurriedly with his eyes directed to the sky. He wandered all over the city, but did not get alms anywhere.

## \|\| 2.96.129 \|\|

*aṃśumālinamāvīkṣya manāglohitamaṃḍalam \|*  
*bhikṣāpātraṃ parikṣipya niryayāvāśramaṃ prati \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Seeing the Sun slightly reddish in its disc (in the evening), he threw the begging bowl down and went towards his hermitage.

## \|\| 2.96.130 \|\|

*atha gacchanmahādevyā gṛhadvāri niṣaṇṇayā \|*  
*prākṛtastrīsvarūpiṇyā bhikṣāyai prārthitotithiḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. While he was going on, he was requested to be the guest receiving alms by Mahādevī (Pārvatī) who had assumed the form of a laywoman and was seated at the portals of her house.

## \|\| 2.96.131 \|\|

*gṛhiṇyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavanbhikṣukāstāvadadya dṛṣṭā na kutracit \|*  
*asatkṛtyātithiṃ nātho na me bhokṣyati karhicit \|\| 131 \|\|*

The Housewife said:

131\. O holy Sir, mendicants were not seen anywhere today. My lord will never take food without extending hospitality to a guest.

## \|\| 2.96.132 \|\|

*vaiśvadevādikaṃ karma kṛtvā gṛhapatirmama \|*  
*pratīkṣetātithipathaṃ tasmāttvamatithirbhava \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. The lord of my house has concluded the rites of Vaiśvadeva etc. He is waiting for the arrival of a guest. Hence do you be the guest.

## \|\| 2.96.133-134 \|\|

*vinātithi gṛhasthoyastvannameko niṣevate \|*  
*niṣevate'ghaṃ sa paraṃ sahitaḥ svapitāmahaiḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaritamāyāhi kuru me patyurīhitam \|*  
*gārhasthyaṃ saphalaṃ kartumicchato'tithipūjanāt \|\| 134 \|\|*

133-134. A householder who eats food alone without a guest, actually partakes of a great sin along with his grandfathers. Hence do come quickly. Fulfil the desire of my husband who wishes to make the life of a householder fruitful by honouring a guest.

## \|\| 2.96.135-137 \|\|

*iti śrutvā gatāmarṣo vyāsastāmāha vismitaḥ \|*  
*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*bhadre kā tvaṃ kutaḥ prāptā pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭā na kutracit \|\| 135 \|\|*

*manye dharmamayī mūrtiḥ kāpi tvaṃ śucimānasā \|*  
*tvaddarśanātparāṃ prītiṃ saṃprāptānīṃdriyāṇi me \|\| 136 \|\|*

*tvaṃ sudhaiva bhaveḥ prāyaḥ sarvāvayavasuṃdari \|*  
*maṃdarāghātasaṃtrāsātyaktakṣīrārṇavasthitiḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

135-137. On hearing this, Vyāsa was not angry any more. He was surprised. He said to her:

## \|\| 2.96.138 \|\|

*kalāsudhākarasyātha kuhū rāhubhayārditā \|*  
*sīmaṃtinī svarūpeṇa tiṣṭheḥ kāśyāmanirbhayā \|\| 138 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

O fair lady, who are you? Whence have you come? You have not been seen before anywhere. I think, you are piety personified uniquely. You are pure-minded. All my senses have become delighted on seeing you. O Lady who are beautiful in every limb, you are sure to be the heavenly nectar itself. Due to the fear of being struck by Mandara mountain, you avoided staying behind in the Milk Ocean.

138\. Or (you are) the digit of the Moon who being of the New-Moon day and afraid of Rāhu is standing in the form of a lady fearlessly in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.96.139 \|\|

*athavā kamalāsi tvaṃ vihāya kamalālayam \|*  
*niśi saṃkocinaṃ kāśyāṃ vikāśinyāṃ vaseḥ sadā \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Or you are Kamalā (Goddess Lakṣmī) who have forsaken your residence in the lotus that closes at night and taken up permanent residence in Kāśī that (always) shines extensively.

## \|\| 2.96.140 \|\|

*kiṃvā nu karuṇāmūrtiriha kāśinivāsinām \|*  
*sarvaduḥkhaughahariṇī parānaṃdapradāyinī \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Or are you the embodiment of compassion, removing all the masses of misery of the residents of Kāśī and bestowing the greatest bliss?

## \|\| 2.96.141 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāḥ kimathavā'dhiṣṭhātrī devatā tvamu \|*  
*kiṃ vā nirvāṇalakṣmīstvaṃ yā kāśyāṃ parigīyate \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. Or are you the presiding deity of Vārāṇasī? Or are you the glorious salvation well-sung about in Kāśī?

## \|\| 2.96.142 \|\|

*śvapākaṃ yāyajūkaṃ vā prāṃte'laṃkurvatī samam \|*  
*madbhāgyaṃ vā pariṇatametadyoṣitsvarūpataḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. Has my good fortune transformed itself into this female form? (Are you the deity) that treats impartially a Cāṇḍāla and a person performing sacrifices?

## \|\| 2.96.143 \|\|

*athavā sā bhavennūnaṃ yā kṣetre parigīyate \|*  
*bhaktapotapradā bhaktyā bhavānī bhavanāśinī \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. Or you may be Bhavānī, the destroyer of worldly misery and the bestower of a raft (to cross the ocean of Saṃsāra) on the devotee, as a fruit of his devotion. She is certainly sung about in the holy spot.

## \|\| 2.96.144 \|\|

*sarvathaiva na nārī tvaṃ nāsurī naiva kinnarī \|*  
*vidyādharā na no nāgī no gaṃdharvī na yakṣiṇī \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. In every respect you are neither a mortal woman, nor an Asura woman, neither a Kinnarī nor a Vidyādharī or a lady of Nāga, Gandharva and Yakṣa tribes.

## \|\| 2.96.145 \|\|

*tvamiṣṭadevataivāsi kācinme mohahāriṇī \|*  
*keyaṃ ciṃtāthavāmetra kācittvaṃ bhava suṃdari \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. You are certainly the desired deity, someone who eradicates my delusion. O fair lady, whatever you may be, why should I be anxious about it?

## \|\| 2.96.146 \|\|

*paravānasmyahaṃ jātastavadarśanato'dhunā \|*  
*avaśyamevakartāsmi tavādeśyaṃ tadādiśa \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. I have become a dependent (of yours) on seeing you. I shall certainly carry out your behest. Do command me.

## \|\| 2.96.147 \|\|

*ekaṃ tapovyayaṃ hitvā kārayiṣyasi yatpunaḥ \|*  
*tadevāhaṃ kariṣyāmi vidheyaḥ śubhalocane \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. With the only exception of wasting (the power of my penance), I shall do, whatever you command me to do. I am at your disposal, O lady of splendid eyes.

## \|\| 2.96.148 \|\|

*na vacastvādṛśīnāṃhi mahattvaṃ hāpayetsatām \|*  
*paraṃ tvaṃ kāsi subhage satyaṃ brūhi mamāgrataḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. The words of noble ladies like you cannot belittle the greatness of good men. But anyhow tell me the truth, O auspicious lady. Who are you?

## \|\| 2.96.149 \|\|

*athavā tava dehesminkvā satyaṃ nirmalekṣaṇe \|*  
*iti pṛṣṭāha muninā sā viśvāyurghaṭodbhava \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. O lady of vision free from impurities, how can there be untruth in this body of yours?

## \|\| 2.96.150 \|\|

*atratyasyaiva hi mune gṛhiṇī gṛhamedhinaḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ vīkṣe caraṃtaṃ tvāṃ bhikṣāṃ śiṣyagaṇairvṛtam \|\| 150 \|\|*

On being asked thus by the sage, O Pot-born One, she, the very vital life of the universe, said:

150\. “O sage, I am the lady of the house of a householder staying here itself. I see you everyday seeking alms surrounded by the group of your disciples.

## \|\| 2.96.151-152 \|\|

*tvameva māṃ no jānīṣe jāne tvāmahameva hi \|*  
*tapasvinkiṃ bahūktena yāvannāstaṃ vrajedraviḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

*prāṇanāthasya me tāvadātithyaṃ saphalīkuru \|*  
*tacchutvā sa muniḥ prāha vinayānatakaṃdharaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

151-152. You alone do not know me. I know you very well. Of what avail is too much of a talk? O sage, before the sun sets, make the hospitality of my dear lord fruitful.”

On hearing it the sage said bowing down with humility:

## \|\| 2.96.153 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*asti me niyamaḥ kaścitsa siddhiṃ cedvrajecchubhe \|*  
*ekabhikṣāṃ tadāhaṃ tu kariṣye nānyathā punaḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

153\. O splendid lady, I abide by a certain rule. If that is duly observed, I shall receive the alms once. None on another occasion.

## \|\| 2.96.154-155 \|\|

*tapasvyudīritaṃ śrutvā sā provāca vacastataḥ \|*  
*aviśaṃka vada mune kastesti niyamaḥ sudhīḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

*mama bhartuḥ prasādena kiṃcinnyūnaṃ yato'tra na \|*  
*iti śrutvā prahṛṣṭātmā sa tāmāha tapodhanaḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

154-155a. On hearing the utterance of the sage she said thus: “O sage, speak out unhesitatingly. O learned one of excellent intellect, what is your rule? By the grace of my husband there is no shortage of anything here.”

155b. On hearing this that ascetic became pleased within himself and said:

## \|\| 2.96.156 \|\|

*ayutaṃ mama śiṣyā ye taiḥ sapaktimahaṃ vṛṇe \|*  
*astaṃ yāvanna yātyarkastāvadbhokṣyenyathā nahi \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. “I have ten thousand disciples. I request for cooked food for all of them. Before the sun sets I must take my food. Otherwise not.”

## \|\| 2.96.157 \|\|

*niśamyeti prahṛṣṭāsyā sā provāca muniṃtataḥ \|*  
*kiṃ vilaṃbena tadyāhi sarvāñśiṣyānsamāhvaya \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. On hearing this she too was delighted and said to the sage: “Why delay? Go and fetch all your disciples.”

## \|\| 2.96.158 \|\|

*punaḥ prāha sa tāṃ sādhvi tvetāvatsiddhirasti te \|*  
*yena tṛptiṃ gamiṣyaṃti macchiṣyāḥ sarva eva te \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. Again he asked her: “O good lady, have you such a power as to make all my disciples satisfied?”

## \|\| 2.96.159-166 \|\|

*smitvātha sābravīttaṃ tu mune bharturanugrahāt \|*  
*siddhameva sadaivāste sarvaṃ tāvanmamālaye \|\| 159 \|\|*

*yāvatārthijanastṛptimeti sarvopi sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ na tādṛṅmahilā bhartṛsaṃdehakārikāḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

*āyātorthī yadā gehe siddhaṃ kāryaṃ tadaiva hi \|*  
*paripūrṇā diśaḥ sarvāḥ paripūrṇāmanorathāḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*paripūrṇagṛhaṃ sarvaṃ patyuḥpāda prasādataḥ \|*  
*yāhi tūrṇaṃ samāyāhi yāvadannārthibhiḥ saha \|\| 162 \|\|*

*patirme bahukālīnaḥ kālaṃ na sahate ciram \|*  
*priyātithiḥ priyatamastadātithyasamṛddhaye \|\| 163 \|\|*

*āśu gatvā samāgaccha yāvannāstamito raviḥ \|*  
*iti prahṛṣṭastvaritaḥ śiṣyānāhūya sarvataḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

*āgatyatāṃ punaḥ prāha dṛṣṭvā tanmārgalocanām \|*  
*mātaḥ sarve samāyātāstvaritaṃ dehi bhojanam \|\| 165 \|\|*

*astācalaṃ hi samayā samiyādeṣa bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā maṃdirasyāṃtarviviśuste tapodhanāḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

159-166a. Smilingly she said to him: “Due to my husband’s grace, O sage, everything is kept ready in my abode so that everyone of the suppliants is satisfied in every respect. We are not one of those women who begin to doubt (the power of) their husbands. As soon as a guest or seeker of food comes at the house, the rite (of hospitality) is fulfilled. All the quarters are full. All the desires are perfectly fulfilled. Due to the grace of the feet of the Lord, the entire household is full. Go quickly and return along with as many of the seekers of hospitality as are there. My husband is one of those of olden times. He does not brook delay. My loving husband is fond of guests. Hence for the sake of perfect hospitality go hurriedly and return before sunset.”

On (hearing this) he was delighted. Hurriedly be called together all the disciples from everywhere. After coming back he saw her with her eyes waiting for his return. He said, “Mother, all have come. Give us food quickly. The sun has come very near the mountain of sunset.”

166b. After saying this the ascetics entered the temple.

## \|\| 2.96.167-168 \|\|

*tanmaṃḍapamaṇijyotistatyāhitadinaśriyaḥ \|*  
*yāvadgacchatitatsaudhamadhyamāśu tapasvinaḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

*pādauprakṣālya tāvatte kaiścitkaiścitsamarcya ca \|*  
*katicitpariviṣṭānnā bhoktumevopaveśitāḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

167-168. As the sages reached the middle of that palace they became resplendent like daylight due to the radiance of the jewels in the pavilion thereof. They were immediately received and the feet were washed by some and others were duly honoured. By a few they were seated and served with food.

## \|\| 2.96.169 \|\|

*taddivyapākasaṃbhārāndṛṣṭavā taddṛṣṭayaḥ kṣaṇāt \|*  
*parātṛptimupāgacchanghrāṇanyāmodarājibhiḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. On seeing the collection of foodstuffs cooked in divine manner their eyes attained the greatest satisfaction and their noses were delighted through the odour.

## \|\| 2.96.170 \|\|

*atitṛptiṃ samāpannāste tadannaniṣevaṇāt \|*  
*ācāṃtāścaṃdanaiḥ sragbhiraṃbaraiḥ paribhūṣitāḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. By taking in the cooked foodstuffs, they became extremely satisfied. After the washing of the mouths, they were adorned with garlands, garments and sandal-paste.

## \|\| 2.96.171-174 \|\|

*atha sāṃdhyaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā propaviśya tadagrataḥ \|*  
*abhinaṃdya mahāśīrbhiryāvadgaṃtuṃ pracakramuḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

*tāvadvṛddhagṛhasthena gṛhiṇī sā kaṭākṣitā \|*  
*papraccha tīrthe vasatāṃ ko dharmo mukhya eva hi \|\| 172 \|\|*

*tathā tadanusāreṇa tīrthe vartāmahe vayam \|*  
*sarvadharmavidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ śrutvā tadgṛhiṇī vacaḥ \|\| 173 \|\|*

*tadādarasudhāklinna mahānnasvādatarpitaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca munirvyāsaḥ smitvā tāṃ sarvavittamām \|\| 174 \|\|*

171-174. After concluding the evening rites the sage and others sat for a while in front of the householder. They showered him with blessings and got ready to leave.

Then the hint of a glance was directed at the lady by the old householder. She asked: “What is the main pious duty of those who reside in holy spots? We shall regulate our life in the holy spot in accordance with it,”

On hearing the words of the housewife Sage Vyāsa, the most excellent one among those who know all about pious duties and who were propitiated by the taste of dainty delicacies drenched with the nectar of her esteem, smilingly replied to the lady, the greatest among all-knowers.

## \|\| 2.96.175-180 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*svacchāṃtaḥkaraṇemātarmahāmiṣṭānnamānade \|*  
*sa eṣa dharmo nānyosti yattvayā paricaryate \|\| 175 \|\|*

*tvameva dharmaṃ jānāsi patiśuśrūṣaṇe ratā \|*  
*yadi pṛcchasi māṃ satyaṃ tadā kiṃcana vacmi te \|\| 176 \|\|*

*vaktavyameva pṛṣṭena manāgapi vijānatā \|*  
*sa eva dharmaḥ subhage nānyo dharmosti kaścana \|\| 177 \|\|*

*yenaiṣa toṣamāyāti tava bhartā ciraṃtanaḥ \|*  
*gṛhiṇyuvāca \|*  
*ayaṃ dharmo bhavennūnaṃ kriyate ca svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 178 \|\|*

*sādhāraṇāni dharmāṇi saṃpṛcche tāni me vada \|*  
*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ parotkarṣasahiṣṇutā \|\| 179 \|\|*

*vicārya kāritā nityaṃ svadhiṣṇyodaya ciṃtanam \|*  
*gṛhastha uvāca \|*  
*eṣu dharmeṣu bho vidvaṃstvayi kostīha tadvada \|\| 180 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

175-180. O mother of pure inner feelings, O bestower of honour along with dainty food, that alone is the main pious duty that is being practised by you and nothing else.

You alone who are engrossed in serving your husband are aware of the righteous duty. If you ask me still, I shall mention some truism to you.

On being asked, something should be said by one even if one knows but very little. O auspicious lady, that alone is Dharma whereby your aged husband becomes pleased. Nothing else.

## \|\| 2.96.181 \|\|

*tataḥ sthagitavadvyāsastasthau kiṃcinna coktavān \|*  
*tataḥ punargṛhasthena sa hi proktastapodhanaḥ \|\| 181 \|\|*

The housewife said: “Well, may this be Dharma. Certainly it is being practised in accordance with my capacity. But I am asking you about the general acts of piety, something common to all.”

Vyāsa replied:

Words that do not cause disgust and distress, ability to bear with the ascendancy of others, doing the duty after careful consideration, concern for the prosperity of one’s own abode.

The householder asked: “O learned one, tell me, which one of these Dharmas do you have (performed)?”

181\. Thereupon Vyāsa stood stunned as one cornered. He did not say anything. So the ascetic was further addressed by the householder:

## \|\| 2.96.182 \|\|

*yadyeta eva vai dharmāstvayā ye pratipāditāḥ \|*  
*taddāṃtatā tavaivaikṣi dānaṃ śāpasya cottamam \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. “If these alone that you have enumerated are Dharmas, then asceticism was seen among them by you alone. Pronouncing curses was seen excellent by you.

## \|\| 2.96.183 \|\|

*tvayyeva hi dayā samyagdhairyaṃ tvayyeva cottamam \|*  
*tvayi saṃbhāvanāstyeva kāmakrodhavinigrahe \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. Compassion is perfect in you alone. Fortitude is excellent in you. There is the possibility of curbing lust and wrath in you.

## \|\| 2.96.184 \|\|

*tvameva samyagjānīṣe vaktuṃ codvegavarjitam \|*  
*tvayyeva samyagdṛśyeta parotkarṣa sahiṣṇutā \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. You alone know very well how to speak words that do not cause disgust and distress. Ability to bear with the ascendancy of others is seen perfectly in you alone.

## \|\| 2.96.185 \|\|

*vicārya kāritāyāśca tvameva nilayomahān \|*  
*svasyadhiṣṇyasya ca bhavāṃściṃtayedudayaṃ dhruvam \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. You alone are the greatest abode of doing the duty after careful consideration. Certainly you show great concern for the prosperity of your own abode.

## \|\| 2.96.186 \|\|

*mamaikaṃ brūhi bho vidvañchāpaṃ dadyācca yaḥ krudhā \|*  
*alabhansvārthasaṃsiddhimabhāgyāttasya kasya saḥ \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. Tell me one thing, O learned one. If a person does not attain his selfish interest due to absence of fortune and if he curses angrily, on whom does that curse fall?”

## \|\| 2.96.187 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*yaḥ svārthasiddhimalabhannabhāgyācchapati krudhā \|*  
*sa śāpaḥ pratyuta bhavecchapturevāvivekinaḥ \|\| 187 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

187\. If a person does not attain his selfish interest due to absence of fortune and he curses angrily, that curse, on the contrary, falls on the person who has cursed because he has been thoughtless.

## \|\| 2.96.188 \|\|

*gṛhastha uvāca \|*  
*bhavatā bhramatā vipra nāptābhikṣā yadāpyaho \|*  
*tadāparāddhaṃ kimiha varākaiḥ kṣetravāsibhiḥ \|\| 188 \|\|*

The Householder said:

188\. O Brāhmaṇa if, Alas, alms are not received by you even after wandering, what is the crime committed by the poor residents of the holy spot?

## \|\| 2.96.189 \|\|

*tapasviñśṛṇu me vākyaṃ rājadhānyāṃ mameha yaḥ \|*  
*ṛddhiṃ draṣṭuṃ na śaknoti pariśaptaḥ sa eva hi \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. O ascetic, listen to my words. If a person is unable to bear seeing the opulence in this capital city of mine, he alone is one cursed.

## \|\| 2.96.190 \|\|

*adya prabhṛti na kṣetre madīye śāpavarjite \|*  
*āvasa krodhana mune na vāse yogyatātra te \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. O wrathful sage, from now onwards do not stay in my holy spot unaffected (by your) curse. You are not worthy enough to stay here.

## \|\| 2.96.191-192 \|\|

*idānīmeva nirgaccha bahiḥ kṣetrādito bhava \|*  
*tvadvidhānāṃ na yogyaṃ me kṣetraṃ mokṣaikasādhanam \|\| 191 \|\|*

*atrālpamapi yaddauṣṭyaṃ kṛtaṃ matkṣetravāsinām \|*  
*taddauṣṭyasya parīpāko rudrapaiśācyameva hi \|\| 192 \|\|*

191-192. The state of being a Rudrapiśāca will be the result of the wickedness, even if it be very little, perpetrated towards the residents of this holy spot. Get out now itself. Be outside this holy spot. My holy spot is the sole cause of salvation. It is not suitable to persons like you.

## \|\| 2.96.193 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vepamānaḥ sa pariśuṣkauṣṭhatālukaḥ \|*  
*jagāma śaraṇaṃ gaurīṃ luṭhaṃstaccaraṇāgrataḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. On hearing this his (Vyāsa’s) lips and palate became dry. He began to tremble. Rolling in front of the feet of Gaurī he sought refuge in her.

## \|\| 2.96.194 \|\|

*uvāca ca vaco mātastrāhi trāhi bhṛśaṃ rudan \|*  
*anāthastvatsanāthohaṃ bāliśastava bālakaḥ \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. Crying bitterly he spoke these words: “Mother, save me, save me. I am helpless. I shall be saved if you help me. I am puerile. I am your son.

## \|\| 2.96.195 \|\|

*śaraṇāgataṃ ca saṃtrāhi rakṣa māṃ śaraṇāgatam \|*  
*bahūnāmāgasāṃ gehamasmākaṃ duṣṭamānasam \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. Save me who have sought refuge in you. Protect me who seek refuge in you. Our defiled mind is the abode of many sins.

## \|\| 2.96.196-197 \|\|

*śaṃbhuśāpo'nyathākartuṃ bhavatyāpi na śakyate \|*  
*ahaṃ ca śaraṇāyātastadekaṃ kriyatāṃ śive \|\| 196 \|\|*

*pratyaṣṭami sadā kṣetre pratibhūtaṃ ca pārvati \|*  
*diśa praveśanādeśaṃ neśastvadvākyalaṃghakaḥ \|\| 197 \|\|*

196-197. The imprecation of Śaṃbhu cannot be altered even by your holiness. I too have sought refuge in you. Hence, O Śivā, let this be done. Grant me the permission to enter this holy spot on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days. The Lord will not go against your words.”

## \|\| 2.96.198 \|\|

*ityuktā tena muninā bhavānī karuṇājaniḥ \|*  
*mukhaṃ maheśiturvīkṣya tathetyāha tadājñayā \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. On being requested thus by the sage, Bhavānī the source of compassion, looked at the face of Maheśitā and at his bidding said, “So it will be.”

## \|\| 2.96.199 \|\|

*athāṃtarhitavaṃtau tau śivau kṣetraśivaṃkarau \|*  
*vyāsopi niryayau kṣetrātsvāparādhavaśaṃ vadan \|\| 199 \|\|*

199\. Then both of them Śiva and Śivā who bring about the happiness to the holy spot vanished. Vyāsa too confessing his own fault went out of the holy spot.

## \|\| 2.96.200 \|\|

*ahorātraṃ sa paśyanvai kṣetraṃ dṛṣṭeradūragam \|*  
*prāpyāṣṭamīṃ ca bhūtāṃ ca madhye kṣetraṃ sadā viśet \|\| 200 \|\|*

200\. Day and night he used to look at the holy spot not far from his vision. On the eighth and fourteenth lunar days he used to enter the holy spot.

## \|\| 2.96.201 \|\|

*lolārkādagnidigbhāge svardhunīṃ pūrvarodhasi \|*  
*sthito hyadyāpi paśyetsa kāśīprāsādarājikām \|\| 201 \|\|*

201\. Even today he looks at the row of palaces in Kāśī, being stationed on the eastern bank of the celestial river in the south-east of Lolārka.

## \|\| 2.96.202 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ kuṃbhaja sa vyāsaḥ kṣetre śāpaṃ pradāsyati \|*  
*kṣetraśāpapradānācca bahiryāsyati tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 202 \|\|*

Skanda said:

202\. Thus, O Pot-born One, Vyāsa will pronounce his imprecation on the holy spot. After giving his curse he will go out instantly.

## \|\| 2.96.203 \|\|

*ataevāvimuktasya kṣetrasya śubhaśaṃsinaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati śubhaṃ nityamanyathā tvanyathaiva hi \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. That is why everything will be auspicious to one praising the splendour and auspiciousness of the holy spot. Otherwise everything will be otherwise.

## \|\| 2.96.204 \|\|

*śrutvādhyāyamimaṃ puṇyaṃ vyāsaśāpa vimokṣaṇam \|*  
*mahādurgopasargebhyo bhayaṃ tasya na kutracit \|\| 204 \|\|*

204\. If one listens to this meritorious chapter entitled “Vyāsaśāpavimokṣaṇam"; (‘Release of Vyāsa from a curse’) one will never have the fear from great impassable difficulties and portents.

## Chapter 97 - Holy Spots in Vārāṇasī

## \|\| 2.97.1 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*etadbhaviṣyaṃ śrutvāhaṃ vyāsasya śivanaṃdana \|*  
*āścaryabhājanaṃ jātastīrthāni kathayādhunā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The locations of most of these holy spots have been noted in previous chapters.

Agastya said:

1\. O Son of Śiva, after listening to the future of Vyāsa, I am greatly surprised. Now, do narrate the details of the holy spots.

## \|\| 2.97.2 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānane yāni yatra saṃti ṣaḍānana \|*  
*tāni liṃgasvarūpāṇi samācakṣva mamāgrataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Six-faced One, recount to me all those holy shrines that are located in Ānandakānana in the form of Liṅgas.

## \|\| 2.97.3 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*ayameva hi vai praśno devyai devena bhostadā \|*  
*yādṛśaḥ kathito vacmi tādṛśaṃ śṛṇu kuṃbhaja \|\| 3 \|\|*

Skanda said:

3\. O Pot-born One, I shall tell you how this very question was clarified unto the Goddess then by the Lord. Listen.

## \|\| 2.97.4 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yāni yāni hi tīrthāni yatrayatra maheśvara \|*  
*tāni tānīha me kāśyāṃ tatratatra vada prabho \|\| 4 \|\|*

The Goddess said:

4\. O Lord Maheśvara, do describe to me all those holy shrines and (the places) where they are located in Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.97.5 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi viśālākṣi tīrthaṃ liṃgamudāhṛtam \|*  
*jalāśayepi tīrthākhyā jātā mūrti parigrahāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

The Lord of Devas said:

5\. Listen, O Large-eyed Goddess, Liṅga is called Tīrtha. A reservoir of water also is called Tīrtha because of its association with an idol.

## \|\| 2.97.6 \|\|

*mūrtayo brahmaviṣṇvarkaśivavighneśvarādikāḥ \|*  
*liṃgaṃ śaivamiti khyātaṃ yatraitattīrthameva tat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The idols are (of) Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Arka (the Sun), Śiva, Vighneśvara etc. Where there is a Liṅga of Siva, that is indeed a Tīrtha.

## \|\| 2.97.7 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ mahādevaḥ prathamaṃ tīrthamucyate \|*  
*taduttare mahākūpaḥ sārasvatapadapradaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Mahādeva in Vārāṇasī is mentioned as the first Tīrtha. To the north thereof the great well bestows Sārasvatapada (the position of a devotee of Goddess Sarasvatī).

## \|\| 2.97.8 \|\|

*kṣetrapūrvottarebhāge taddṛṣṭaṃ paśupāśahṛt \|*  
*tatpaścādvigrahavatī pūjyā vārāṇasī naraiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Seen in the north-east of the holy spot, it dispels the bondage of a Paśu (individual soul). Behind it, Vārāṇasī in embodied form should be worshipped by men.

## \|\| 2.97.9 \|\|

*sā pūjitā prayatnena sukhavastipradā sadā \|*  
*mahādevasya pūrveṇa goprekṣaṃ liṃgamuttamam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Assiduously worshipped, it always bestows comfortable residence (habitation). To the east of Mahādeva is the excellent Liṅga called Goprekṣa.

## \|\| 2.97.10-11 \|\|

*taddarśanādbhavetsamyaggodānajanitaṃ phalam \|*  
*golokātpreṣitā gāvaḥ pūrvaṃ yacchaṃbhunā svayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vārāṇasīṃ samāyātā goprekṣaṃ tattataḥ snṛtam \|*  
*goprekṣāddakṣiṇebhāge dadhīcīśvarasaṃjñitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. On visiting it, one acquires an excellent gift of cows as a fruit thereof It is known as Goprekṣa because, formerly cows were sent by Śaṃbhu himself from the World of Cows (Goloka) and they came to Vārāṇasī. To the south of Goprekṣa is (the Tīrtha) called Dadhīcīśvara.

## \|\| 2.97.12-13 \|\|

*taddarśanādbhavetpuṃsāṃ phalaṃ yajñasamudbhavam \|*  
*atrīśvaraṃ tu tatprācyāṃ madhukaiṭabhapūjitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvā prayatnena vaiṣṇavaṃ padamṛcchati \|*  
*goprekṣātpūrvadigbhāge liṃgaṃ vai vijvaraṃ smṛtam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. As a fruit of visiting it, men will derive the benefit resulting from the performance of Yajñas. The Tīrtha (Liṅga) Atrīśvara worshipped by Madhu and Kaiṭabha is to the east thereof. By visiting that Liṅga assiduously, one attains the region of Viṣṇu. The Liṅga (named) Vijvara is known as situated to the east of Goprekṣa.

## \|\| 2.97.14 \|\|

*tasya saṃpūjanānmartyo vijvaro jāyate kṣaṇāt \|*  
*prācyāṃ vedeśvarastasya caturvedaphalapradaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. By worshipping it a man becomes free from fever instantly. To the east thereof is Vedeśvara, the bestower of the merit of reciting the four Vedas.

## \|\| 2.97.15 \|\|

*vedeśvarādudīcyāṃ tu kṣetrajñaścādikeśavaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭaṃ tribhuvanaṃ sarvaṃ tasya saṃdarśanāddhruvam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. To the north of Vedeśvara are Kṣetrajña (Īśvara) and Ādikeśava. By visiting it, the three worlds are certainly seen.

## \|\| 2.97.16-17 \|\|

*saṃgameśvaramālokya tatprācyāma jāyatenaghaḥ \|*  
*caturmukhena vidhinā tatpūrveṇa caturmukham \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prayāgasaṃjñakama liṃgamarcitama brahmalokadam \|*  
*tatra śāṃtikarī gaurī pūjitā śāṃtikṛdbhavet \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. By visiting Saṅgameśvara to the east thereof, one becomes sinless. The four-faced Liṅga named Prayāga installed by Brahmā, the four-faced Lord, bestows the world of Brahmā when worshipped. If Gaurī, the begetter of Śānti (peace) is worshipped there, she brings about peace.

## \|\| 2.97.18 \|\|

*varaṇāyāstaṭe pūrve pūjyaṃ kuṃtīśvaraṃ nṛbhiḥ \|*  
*tatpūjanātprajāyaṃte putrā nijakulojjvalāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. To the east (the Liṅga named) Kuntīśvara should be worshipped by men on the banks of Varaṇā. As a result of the worship thereof, sons illuminating one’s own family are born.

## \|\| 2.97.19-21 \|\|

*kuṃtīśvarāduttaratastīrthaṃ vai kāpilo hradaḥ \|*  
*tatra vai snānamātreṇa vṛṣabhadhvajapūjanāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

*rājasūyasya yajñasya phalaṃ tvavikalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*roravādiṣu ye kecitpitaraḥ koṭisaṃmitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tatra śrāddhe kṛte putraiḥ pitṛlokaṃ prayāṃti te \|*  
*ānusūyeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ goprekṣāduttare mune \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. The Tīrtha to the north of Kuntīśvara is the eddy named Kāpila Hrada. Merely by taking bath there and worshipping the Bull-emblemed Lord, one shall derive the full benefit of a Rājasūyayajṅa. If a Śrāddha is performed by the sons there, the Manes numbering crores and crores residing in hells beginning with Raurava pass on to the region of Pitṛs.

O sage, the Liṅga named Ānusūyeśvara is to the north of Goprekṣa.

## \|\| 2.97.22-24 \|\|

*taddarśanādbhavetstrīṇāṃ pātivratya phalaṃ sphuṭam \|*  
*talliṃgapūrvadigbhāge pūjyaḥ siddhivināyakaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*yāṃ siddhiṃ yaḥ samīheta sa tāmāpnoti tannateḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśiporliṃgaṃ gaṇeśātpaścime tataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakūpastatrāsti hiraṇyāśvasamṛddhikṛt \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. By visiting it, women shall clearly attain the benefit of chastity.

To the east of that Liṅga is Siddhivināyaka who should be worshipped. One obtains that Siddhi (spiritual power) which one desires, as a result of making obeisance unto him.

The Liṅga of Hiraṇyakaśipu is to the west of Gaṇeśa. The well Hiraṇyakūpa is beyond that and it brings about abundance of gold and horses and wealth.

## \|\| 2.97.25 \|\|

*muṃḍāsureśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tatpratīcyāṃ ca siddhidam \|*  
*abhīṣṭadaṃ tu nairṛtyāṃ goprekṣādvṛṣabheśvaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Muṇḍāsureśvara Liṅga to the west thereof is also the bestower of spiritual power.

Vṛṣabheśvara to the south-west of Goprekṣa yields the desired fruit.

## \|\| 2.97.26 \|\|

*mune skaṃdeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ mahādevasya paścime \|*  
*talliṃgapūjanānnṛṇāṃ bhavenmama salokatā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O sage, the Skandeśvara Liṅga is to the west of Mahādeva. By worshipping that Liṅga, men shall attain the state of living in the same world as I.

## \|\| 2.97.27-29 \|\|

*tatpārśvato hi śākheśo viśākheśaśca tatra vai \|*  
*naigameyeśvarastatra yenye naṃdyādayo gaṇāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*teṣāmapi hi liṃgāni tatra saṃti sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*taddarśanādbhavetpuṃsāṃ tattadgaṇasalokatā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*naṃdīśvarātpratīcyāṃ ca śilādeśaḥ kudhīharaḥ \|*  
*mahābalapradastatra hiraṇyākṣeśvaraḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. Verily by the side thereof are Śākheśa, Viśākheśa, Naigameyeśvara as well as other Gaṇas beginning with Nandin. Thousands of Liṅgas are installed by them. By visiting them, men shall attain the state of being in the same world as those Gaṇas. Śilādeśa, the destroyer of corrupt intellect, is to the west of Nandīśvara. There Hiraṇyākṣeśvara bestows great strength. He is auspicious and splendid.

## \|\| 2.97.30 \|\|

*taddakṣiṇeṭṭahāsākhyaṃ liṃgaṃ sarvasukhapradam \|*  
*prasannavadaneśākhyaṃ liṃgaṃ tasyottare śubham \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. To the south thereof is the Liṅga named Aṭṭahāsa that bestows all happiness (happiness unto all). To the north thereof, is the auspicious Liṅga named Prasannavadaneśa.

## \|\| 2.97.31 \|\|

*prasannavadanastiṣṭhedbhaktastaddarśanācchubhāt \|*  
*taduttare prasannodaṃ kuṃḍaṃ nairmalyadaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. As a result of the auspicious vision thereof, a devotee stands with face beaming with pleasure. To the north of this is the holy pit (named) Prasannoda that bestows freedom from impurities on men.

## \|\| 2.97.32 \|\|

*pratīcyāmaṭṭahāsasya mitrāvaruṇanāmanī \|*  
*liṃge tallokade pūjye mahāpātakahāriṇī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. To the west of Aṭṭahāsa are the Liṅgas named after Mitra and Varuṇa. They dispel great sins and bestow their worlds. They are to be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.97.33 \|\|

*nairṛtyāṃ cāṭṭahāsasya vṛddhavāsiṣṭhasaṃjñakam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ tatpūjanātpuṃsāṃ jñānamutpadyate mahat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. To the south-west of Aṭṭahāsa is the Liṅga named Vṛddhavaśiṣṭha. By worshipping it men get great knowledge.

## \|\| 2.97.34 \|\|

*vasiṣṭheśa samīpasthaḥ kṛṣṇeśo viṣṇulokadaḥ \|*  
*tadyāmyāṃ yājñavalkyeśo brahmatejovivadharnaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Kṛṣṇeśa installed in the vicinity of Vaśiṣṭheśa bestows the world of Viṣṇu. Yājñavalkyeśa to the south thereof increases spiritual energy.

## \|\| 2.97.35-36 \|\|

*prahlādeśvaramabhyarcya tatpaścādbhaktivardhanam \|*  
*svayaṃlīnaḥ śivo yatra bhaktānugrahakāmyayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ataḥ svalīnaṃ tatpūrve liṃgaṃ pūjyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*sadaiva jñānaniṣṭhānāṃ paramānaṃdamicchatām \|*  
*yā gatirvihitā teṣāṃ svalīne sā tanutyajām \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Thereafter, one should worship Prahlādeśvara that increases devotional fervour and assiduously worship Svalīna Liṅga to the east thereof. With a desire to bless his devotees Śiva himself has merged therein. The goal of those who cast off their bodies in Svalīna is the same as has been laid down as the goal of those who wish for the greatest bliss and who always abide by spiritual knowledge.

## \|\| 2.97.37 \|\|

*vairocaneśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ svalīnātpurataḥ sthitam \|*  
*taduttare balīśaṃ ca mahābalavivardhanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Vairocaneśvara Liṅga is stationed in front of Svalīna. To the north thereof is Balīśa that causes great strength.

## \|\| 2.97.38-39 \|\|

*tatraiva liṃgaṃ bāṇeśaṃ pūjitaṃ sarvakāmadam \|*  
*caṃdreśvarasya pūrveṇa liṃgaṃ vidyeśvarābhidham \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sarvāvidyāḥ prasannāḥ syustasya liṃgasya sevanāt \|*  
*taddakṣiṇe tu vīreśo mahāsiddhi vidhāyakaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Bāṇeśa Liṅga (which is there itself, if) worshipped bestows all desires. To the east of Candreśvara is the Liṅga named Vidyeśvara. By resorting to that Liṅga, all the goddesses of learning become propitiated. Vīreśa to the south thereof is the deity that confers great Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.97.40 \|\|

*tatraiva vikaṭā devī sarvaduḥkhaughamocanī \|*  
*paṃcamudraṃ mahāpīṭhaṃ tajjñeyaṃ sarvasiddhidam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. There itself is the Goddess Vikaṭā that redeems (the devotees) from all miseries. That Mahāpīṭha named Pañcamudra should be known as one that yields all Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.97.41 \|\|

*tatra japtā mahāmaṃtrāḥ kṣipraṃ sidhyaṃti nānyathā \|*  
*tatpīṭhe vāyukoṇe tu saṃpūjyaḥ sagareśvaraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Great Mantras repeatedly recited there become fruitful quickly. Not otherwise. Sāgareśvara should be worshipped in the north-west corner of that Pīṭha.

## \|\| 2.97.42 \|\|

*tadarcanādaśvamedhaphalaṃ tvavikalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tadīśāne ca vālīśastiryagyoni nivārakaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Complete benefit of a horse-sacrifice will be derived by worshipping Sāgareśvara. Vālīśa to the north-east thereof is the preventer of birth in animal species.

## \|\| 2.97.43 \|\|

*mahāpāpaughavidhvaṃsī sugrīveśastaduttare \|*  
*hanūmadīśvarastatra brahmacaryaphalapradaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. To the north thereof is Sugrīveśa who destroys masses of great sins. Hanūmadīśvara there is the bestower of the merit of taking to celibacy.

## \|\| 2.97.44 \|\|

*mahābuddhipradastatra pūjyo jāṃbavatīśvaraḥ \|*  
*āśvine yeśvarau pūjyau gaṃgāyāḥ paścime taṭe \|\| 44 \|\|*
