*saṃtoṣya sarvānprathamaṃ munīṃdrānsvaisvairhṛdisthaiśca cirābhilāṣaiḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇamābhāṣya śivotha viṣṇuṃ jagāda sarvāmaravṛṃdavaṃdyaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. At the outset Śiva, worthy of being saluted by all the groups of the immortal ones, propitiated all the leading sages by means of the fulfilment of their life-long desires cherished within the hearts. After addressing Brahmā he spoke to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.98.25 \|\|

*ito niṣīdeti samānapūrvaṃ tvaṃ me samastaprabhutaikahetuḥ \|*  
*dūrepi tiṣṭhannikaṭastvameva tvatto na kaścinmama kāryakartā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With great honour (he made him sit near) saying, “Sit here. You are the sole cause of all my lordship. Even though you may be standing far off you are very near to me. There is no one other than you who can carry out my task.

## \|\| 2.98.26 \|\|

*tvayā divodāsa nareṃdravaryaḥ sadūpadeśaiśca tathopadiṣṭaḥ \|*  
*yathā sa siddhiṃ paramāmavāpa samīhitaṃ me nikhilaṃ ca siddham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The excellent king Divodāsa was given good advice so that he attained the greatest Siddhi and my (his) desire was completely achieved.

## \|\| 2.98.27 \|\|

*viṣṇo varaṃ brūhi ya īpsitaste nādeyamatrāsti kimapyaho te \|*  
*idaṃ mayā'naṃdavanaṃ yadāptaṃ hetustu tatratvamasau gaṇeśaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O Viṣṇu, ask for a boon. You will have whatever you desire. There is nothing here that cannot be given to you. It is due to you and this Gaṇeśa, that Ānandavana was obtained by me.

## \|\| 2.98.28 \|\|

*na me priyaṃ kiṃcana viṣṭapatraye tathā yatheyaṃ parasaukhyabhūmiḥ \|*  
*vārāṇasī brahmarasāyanasya khanirjaniryatra na dīrghaśāyinām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In all the three worlds, there is nothing else so lovable to me as this Vārāṇasī, the origin of the greatest happiness. It is the mine of Brahmarasāyana (Elixir of realization of Brahman). People who take the long sleep there (i.e. those who die there) do not have further birth.”

## \|\| 2.98.29 \|\|

*śrutveti vākyaṃ jagadīśituśca provāca viṣṇurvaradaṃ maheśam \|*  
*yadi prasannosi pinākapāṇe tadā padāddūramahaṃ na te syām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On hearing these words of the Lord of the universe, Viṣṇu spoke to Maheśa, the bestower of boons: “If, O Pināka-bearing Lord, you are pleased, then let me not be far removed from your feet.”

## \|\| 2.98.30 \|\|

*śrutveti vākyaṃ madhusūdanasya jagāda tuṣṭo nitarāṃ purāriḥ \|*  
*sadā murāre mama sannidhau tvaṃ tiṣṭhasva nirvāṇaramāśrayetra \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On hearing this speech of the Slayer of Madhu, Purāri was delighted and said thus: “O Enemy of Mura, stay forever near me here, in this resort of the Glory of Salvation.

## \|\| 2.98.31 \|\|

*ādāvanārādhya bhavaṃtamatra yo māṃ bhajiṣyatyapi bhaktiyuktaḥ \|*  
*samīhitaṃ tasya na setsyati dhruvaṃ parātparānmeṃbuja cakrapāṇe \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Someone may be devoted to me; but if he resorts to me without propitiating you at the outset, his desire will definitely not be realized through me, the deity greater than the greatest, O Lord having the lotus and the discus in the hands.

## \|\| 2.98.32 \|\|

*sarvatra saukhyaṃ mama muktimaṃḍape saṃtiṣṭhamānasya bhavedihācyuta \|*  
*na tattu kailāsagirau sunirmale na bhaktacetasyapi niścalaśriyi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O Acyuta, there is all happiness to one who abides here in this Pavilion of Salvation. That cannot be had even in Kailāsa mountain utterly free from impurities, nor even in the mind of a devotee with permanent glory.

## \|\| 2.98.33 \|\|

*nimeṣamātraṃ sthiracittavṛttayastiṣṭhaṃti ye dakṣiṇamaṃḍapetra me \|*  
*ananyabhāvā api gāḍhamānasā na te punargarbhadaśāmupāsate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. If the devotees stay even for a moment here in this southern pavilion of mine, with steady mind, without thinking about anything else and having perfect concentration of mind, they will never be reborn in a womb.

## \|\| 2.98.34 \|\|

*saṃsnāya ye cakrasarasyagādhe samastatīrthaika śirovibhūṣaṇe \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ viśaṃtīha nirīhamānasā nirenasaste mama pārṣadā hi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Those who duly bathe in the deep Cakrasaras lake, the crest-jewel of all the Tīrthas, and enter this (pavilion) for a short while without any wish in the mind, become free from sins. They are verily my attendants.

## \|\| 2.98.35 \|\|

*smaraṃti ye māmapavargamaṃḍape kiṃcidyathāśakti dadatyapi svam \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃti puṇyāśca kathāḥ kṣaṇaṃ sthirāste koṭigodānaphalaṃ bhajaṃti \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Those who remember me in the pavilion of salvation, and make gift of some money according to their capacity, those who listen to meritorious narratives even for a moment with steadiness, earn the merit of the gift of ten million cows.

## \|\| 2.98.36 \|\|

*upeṃdrataptāni tapāṃsi taiściraṃ snātā hi te cākhilatīrthasārthakaiḥ \|*  
*snātveha ye vai maṇikarṇikā hrade samāsate muktijanāśrayekṣaṇam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Upendra, if the devotees bathe in the Maṇikarṇikā Hrada and sit for a short while in the pavilion of those desirous of salvation, it is as fruitful as though penances have been performed by them for a long time and they have had their holy plunge in all the reputed Tīrthas.

## \|\| 2.98.37 \|\|

*tīrthāni saṃtīha padepade hare tulā kva teṣāṃ maṇikarṇikāyāḥ \|*  
*katīhano saṃti śubhāśca maṃḍapāḥ paraṃparomuktiramāśrayoyam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Hari, there are holy Tīrthas here at every step, but can they be compared to Maṇikarṇikā? Are there not many auspicious pavilions here? But this is the greatest resort of the glory of salvation.

## \|\| 2.98.38 \|\|

*kaivalyamaṃḍapasyāsya bhaviṣye dvāpare hare \|*  
*loke khyātirbhavitrīyameṣa kukkuṭamaṃḍapaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In the coming Dvāpara Age, O Hari, this Kaivalyamaṇḍapa (Pavilion of Salvation) will become reputed in the world as Kukkuṭamaṇḍapa.”

## \|\| 2.98.39 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*bhālanetrasamākhyāhi kathaṃ nirvāṇamaṃḍapaḥ \|*  
*tathā khyātimasau gaṃtā yathā devena bhāṣitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

Hari said:

39\. O Lord with an eye in the forehead, do recount to me. How is it that this Pavilion of Salvation will become reputed as said by the Lord?

## \|\| 2.98.40 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*mahānaṃdo dvijo nāma bhaviṣyotra caturbhuja \|*  
*agravedīsamācārastyaktatīrthapratigrahaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Devadeva said:

40\. O Four-armed Lord, a Brāhmaṇa will be born here by the name Mahānanda practising the rituals of Ṛgveda. He will be one abstaining from acceptance of monetary gifts in the holy spots.

## \|\| 2.98.41-43 \|\|

*adāṃbhiko'krūramanāḥ sadaivātithivallabhaḥ \|*  
*atha yauvanamāsādya pitaryuparate sa hi \|\| 41 \|\|*

*viṣameṣu śaraistīvraiḥ kāritastvapade padam \|*  
*jahāra kasyacidbhāryā maitrīṃ kṛtvā tu tena vai \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tayā ca prerito'peyaṃ papau cāpi vimohitaḥ \|*  
*abhakṣyabhakṣaṇarucirabhūnmadanamohitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. He will be devoid of hypocrisy. He will not be cruel-minded. He will always be the favourite of guests. But when his father passed away, he, in his prime of youth, was led astray by the fierce arrows of the Lord of Love. He became friendly with someone and abducted his wife. Urged by her and deluded utterly, he drank what should not be drunk. Fascinated by the god of Love, he contracted a taste for prohibited foodstuffs.

## \|\| 2.98.44 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavāndhanino dṛṣṭvā kṣaṇaṃ vaiṣṇavaveṣabhṛt \|*  
*śaivānniṃdati mūḍhātmā narakatrāṇakāraṇam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On seeing the devotees of Viṣṇu of great wealth, he immediately adopted the guise of a Vaiṣṇava. The deluded soul then begins to censure devotees of Śiva, the giver of salvation from hell.

## \|\| 2.98.45 \|\|

*śivabhaktānsamālokya kiṃcicca pariditsukān \|*  
*garhayedvaiṣṇavānsarvāñśaivaliṃgopajīvakaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On seeing the devotees of Śiva ready to give something, he may despise Vaiṣṇavas entirely and sustain himself through (what was offered to) the Śiva Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.98.46 \|\|

*iti pākhaṃḍadharmajñaḥ saṃdhyāsnānaparāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*viśālatilakaḥ sragvī śuddhadhautāṃbarojvalaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thus he became fully conversant with the practice of heresy. He was averse to the routine baths and prayers at dawn and dusk. He used to put big Tilaka marks (on the forehead), wear garlands and pure bright-washed clothes.

## \|\| 2.98.47 \|\|

*śikhī copagrahakaraḥ sarvebhyo'satpratigrahī \|*  
*tasyāpatyadvayaṃ jātamunmattapathavartinaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He flaunted the tuft of hairs (on the head). His hands were ready to receive anything and everything. He used to receive illegitimate gifts from everyone. He followed the path of the insane. A pair of sons was born to him.

## \|\| 2.98.48 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya pravṛttasya kaścitparvatadeśataḥ \|*  
*samāgamiṣyati dhanī tīrthayātrārthasiddhaye \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Even as he behaved thus, a certain rich man would be arriving there for the purpose of pilgrimage.

## \|\| 2.98.49-51 \|\|

*snātvā sa cakrasarasi kathayiṣyati ceti vai \|*  
*ahamasti dhanoditsurjātyā cāṃḍālasattamaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*asti kaścitpratigrāhī yasmai dadyāmahaṃ dhanam \|*  
*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā kaiściccāṃgulisaṃjñayā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*uddiṣṭa upaviṣṭosau yo japeddhyānamudrayā \|*  
*eṣa pratigrahaṃ tvatto grahīṣyati na cetaraḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-50a. After taking bath in the Cakrasaras lake, he would be saying thus: “I am a man with ready cash willing to donate. By birth I am the best among Cāṇḍalas. Is there anyone ready to accept gifts, so that I can offer this wealth.”

50b-51. On hearing his words, this fellow who was seated there was pointed out with a gesture of the fingers by some people: “Only he who utters prayers and adopts the postures of meditation, will take the gift. None else.”

## \|\| 2.98.52 \|\|

*iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā sa gatvā tatsamīpataḥ \|*  
*daṃḍavatpraṇipatyātha taṃ babhāṣe tadāṃtyajaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On hearing these words of those people, the low-caste fellow goes near him, prostrates before him and speaks thus:

## \|\| 2.98.53 \|\|

*māmuddhara mahāvipra tīrthaṃ me saphalīkuru \|*  
*kiṃcidvastvasti me tattvaṃ gṛhāṇānugrahaṃ kuru \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “O great Brāhmaṇa, redeem me. Make my pilgrimage fruitful. I have something which you do take and bless me.”

## \|\| 2.98.54 \|\|

*athākṣamālikāṃ karṇe kṛtvā dhyānaṃ visṛjya ca \|*  
*kiyaddhanaṃ tavāstīha papraccha karasaṃjñayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thereupon he placed the rosary on the ear and ceased to meditate. With a gesture of his hands he asked, “How much wealth do you have?”

## \|\| 2.98.55 \|\|

*tasya saṃjñāṃ sa vai buddhvā provācāti prahṛṣṭavat \|*  
*saṃtṛptiryāvatā te syāttāvaddāsyāmi nānyathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He took the hint and spoke as though extremely delighted, “I shall give you as much as will satisfy you. Not less.”

## \|\| 2.98.56-58 \|\|

*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tyaktvā maunamuvāca ha \|*  
*sānaṃdaḥ sa mahānaṃdo niḥspṛhosmi pratigrahe \|\| 56 \|\|*

*paraṃ te'nugrahārthaṃ tu kariṣyāmi pratigraham \|*  
*kiṃca me vacanaṃ tvaṃ cetkariṣyasyuttamottama \|\| 57 \|\|*

*yāvadastyakhilaṃ vittaṃ tanmadhye nyasya kasyacit \|*  
*na stokamapi dātavyaṃ tadā'dāsyāmi nānyathā \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. On hearing his words, that Mahānanda who was highly delighted broke silence and said thus: “I am not keen in accepting the gift. But I shall accept in order to bless you. O most excellent one among all excellent people, if you carry out my behest I shall do so. Whatever you have, from it, not even a bit should be given to anyone else. Then alone I shall accept and not otherwise.”

## \|\| 2.98.59-61 \|\|

*cāṃḍāla uvāca \|*  
*yāvadasti mayānītaṃ viśveśaprītaye vasu \|*  
*tāvattubhyaṃ pradāsyāmi viśveśastvaṃ yato mama \|\| 59 \|\|*

*ye vasaṃtīha viśveśa rājadhānyāṃ dvijottama \|*  
*kṣudrākṣudrā jaṃtumātrā viśveśāṃ śāsta eva hi \|\| 60 \|\|*

*paroddharaṇaśīlā ye ye parecchāprapūrakāḥ \|*  
*paropakṛtiśīlā ye viśveśāṃ śāsta eva hi \|\| 61 \|\|*

The Cāṇḍāla said:

59-61. Whatever money has been brought by me for the propitiation of Viśveśa, I shall give unto you, because, to me you are Viśveśa himself. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, those who stay in the royal capital of Viśveśa, be they important or insignificant creatures, all of them form part of Viśveśa. Those who habitually uplift and redeem others, those who fulfil the desires of others, those who regularly render help to others, are part of Viśveśa.

## \|\| 2.98.62 \|\|

*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prahṛṣṭeṃdriyamānasaḥ \|*  
*uvāca pārvatīyaṃ taṃ so'grajanmāṃtyajaṃ tadā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On hearing these words, he became highly delighted in his mind and all sense-organs. The Brāhmaṇa spoke to the low-caste man from a hilly tract:

## \|\| 2.98.63 \|\|

*āyāhi darbhānādehi kurūtsargaṃ tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*tatheti sa cakārāśu pārvatīyo mahāmanāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “Come on. Take the Darbha grass. Perform the rite of Utsarga (giving up) quickly.” The magnanimous man from the hilly tract did accordingly.

## \|\| 2.98.64-66 \|\|

*viśveśaḥ prīyatāṃ ceti procya yāto yathāgataḥ \|*  
*sa ca dvijo dvijairanyairdhikkṛtopi vasanniha \|\| 64 \|\|*

*bahirnirgatamātrastu bahubhiḥ paribhūyate \|*  
*cāṃḍālabrāhmaṇaścaiṣa cāṃḍālātta dhanastvasau \|\| 65 \|\|*

*asāveva hi cāṃḍālaḥ sarvalokabahiṣkṛtaḥ \|*  
*itthaṃ tamanudhāvaṃti thūtkurvaṃtaḥ parito hare \|\| 66 \|\|*

64-66. He uttered, “May Viśveśa be pleased.” He then went away. That Brāhmaṇa continued to stay there though despised and abused by the other Brāhmaṇas. The moment he came out he was assailed by many of them. “Here is a Cāṇḍāla Brāhmaṇa who has taken money from a Cāṇḍāla. He is verily a Cāṇḍāla, excommunicated by the entire world.” Saying thus they chased him, O Hari, producing Thutkāra (sound of spitting out).

## \|\| 2.98.67 \|\|

*sa ca tadbhayato gehātkākabhītadivāṃdhavat \|*  
*na niḥsaretkvacidapi lajjākṛti natāsyakaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Afraid of them, he never stirred out for some time like an owl afraid of crows. He dropped down his head due to shame.

## \|\| 2.98.68 \|\|

*sa ekadā saṃpradhārya gṛhiṇyā lokadūṣitaḥ \|*  
*jagāma kīkaṭāndeśāṃstyaktvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Once that fellow censured by the people consulted his wife and went to Kīkaṭa land abandoning the city of Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.98.69 \|\|

*madhye mārgaṃ sa gacchanvai lakṣitastu sakāṃcanaḥ \|*  
*api kārpaṭikāṃtasthaḥ sa ruddho mārgarodhibhiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. On the way of his destination, he was observed travelling with gold on his person. Though he was in the middle of the caravan of pilgrims, he was waylaid by highwaymen.

## \|\| 2.98.70-71 \|\|

*nītvā te tamaraṇyānīṃ taskarāḥ saparicchadam \|*  
*ulluṃṭhya dhanamādāya samālocya parasparam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*procurbhūridhanaṃ caitajjīryatyasminna jīvati \|*  
*asau dhanī prayatnena vadhyaḥ saparicārakaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. They took him to a dense forest along with all his possessions. They seized his wealth and consulted one another saying: “This vast wealth can be fully used up by us only if he ceases to live. He should be killed along with his servants.”

## \|\| 2.98.72 \|\|

*saṃpradhāryeti teprāhuḥ smartavyaṃ smara pāṃthika \|*  
*tvāṃ vayaṃ ghātayiṣyāmo niścitaṃ saparicchadam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. After deciding thus they said, “O traveller, remember what should be remembered. We are surely going to kill you along with your retinue.”

## \|\| 2.98.73-75 \|\|

*niśamyeti manasyeva kathayāmāsa sa dvijaḥ \|*  
*aho pratigṛhītaṃ me yadarthaṃ vasu bhūriśaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*kuṭuṃbamapi tannaṣṭaṃ naṣṭaścāpi pratigrahaḥ \|*  
*jīvitaṃ cāpi me naṣṭaṃ naṣṭā kāśīpurīsthitiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*yugapatsarvamevāśu naṣṭaṃ durbuddhiceṣṭayā \|*  
*na kāśyāṃ maraṇaṃ prāptaṃ tasmādduṣṭapratigrahāt \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-75. On hearing this, that Brāhmaṇa thought thus within his mind, ‘Alas! My family for the sake of which much wealth was taken by me as gift has become ruined. The wealth received as gift has also been lost. My life is lost and the residence in the city of Kāśī has also ceased. Everything has been ruined simultaneously owing to the activity of my evil intellect. Due to that defiled gift of money, I could not even die in Kāśī.’

## \|\| 2.98.76 \|\|

*prāṃte kuṭuṃbasmaraṇāttathākāśīsmṛterapi \|*  
*corairhatopi sa tadā kīkaṭe kukkuṭo'bhavat \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Since he remembered his family during the last moment of his life as well as Kāśī, he was reborn as a cock in the Kīkaṭa land, though he was killed by the thieves.

## \|\| 2.98.77 \|\|

*sā kukkuṭī sutau tau tu tāmracūḍatvamāpatuḥ \|*  
*prāṃte kāśīsmaraṇato jātā jātismṛtiḥ parā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The woman became a hen and both the sons also became cocks. Due to the recollection of Kāśī, he was able to recollect the previous birth.

## \|\| 2.98.78 \|\|

*itthaṃ bahutithekāle gate kārpaṭikottamāḥ \|*  
*tasminnevādhvani prāptāścatvāro yatra kukkuṭāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. After many years had passed by, four excellent pilgrims came to that wayside place where the cocks were living.

## \|\| 2.98.79-87 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāḥ kathāṃ proccaiḥ kurvaṃto'nyonyameva hi \|*  
*kāśīkathāṃ samākarṇya tadā te caraṇāyudhāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*jātismṛtiprabhāveṇa tatsaṃgena tu nirgatāḥ \|*  
*taiśca kārpaṭikaśreṣṭheḥ pathi dṛṣṭvā kṛpālubhiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*taṃdulādiparikṣepaiḥ prāpitāḥ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*te tu kṣetraṃ samāsādya catvāraścaraṇāyudhāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*cariṣyaṃto'tra parito muktimaṃḍapamuttamam \|*  
*jitāhārānsaniyamānkāmakrodhaparāṅmukhān \|\| 82 \|\|*

*prahāsānmatkathālāpāṃllābhamohavivarjitān \|*  
*svardhunīsnānasaṃklinna sunirmalaśiroruhān \|\| 83 \|\|*

*mannāmoccāraṇaparānmatkathārpitasuśrutīn \|*  
*maddattacittasadvṛttīndṛṣṭvā kṣetranivāsinaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*mānayāmāsuratha tānkukkuṭānsādhuvartmanaḥ \|*  
*prāktanāṃ vāsanāyogātsaṃpradhārya parasparam \|*  
*krameṇāhāramākuṃcya prāṇāṃstyakṣyaṃti cātra vai \|\| 85 \|\|*

*paśyatāṃ sarvalokānāṃ viṣṇo te madanugrahāt \|*  
*vimānamadhiruhyāśu kailāsaṃ prāpya matpadam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*nirviśya suciraṃ kālaṃ divyānbhogānanuttamān \|*  
*tato'tra jñānino bhūtvā muktiṃ prāpsyaṃti śāśvatīm \|\| 87 \|\|*

79-87. They were speaking the tales (topics) of Vārāṇasī to one another loudly. On hearing the story of Kāśī, those cocks also set off in their company, thanks to the power of their memory of the previous birth. The kind-hearted pilgrims saw them on the way, cast rice-grains etc. (for them to eat) and brought them to the excellent holy spot. Having reached the holy spot, those cocks would be moving round the excellent Pavilion of Salvation. The residents of the holy place saw them following certain set of rules. They had conquered (the desire) to eat. They performed religious observances. They were averse to anger. They were highly delighted to hear the talks and stories about me. They were devoid of greed and delusion. Their heads were wet, due to the plunge within the celestial river. They were engrossed in repeating my names. They paid due attention to my stories. Their mental activities were directed towards me. The residents of the holy place honoured those cocks as beings treading the paths of the good. Due to the impressions of the previous activities, they consulted one another and reduced their intake of food. Thus they would be casting off their lives. O Viṣṇu, by my grace, they will get into an aerial chariot even as all the people watched and will reach Kailāsa, my abode. For a long time they will enjoy excellent divine pleasures. Then they will become endowed with knowledge and attain eternal salvation.

## \|\| 2.98.88 \|\|

*tato lokāstadadārabhya kathayiṣyaṃti sarvataḥ \|*  
*muktimaṃḍapanāmaitadeṣa kukkuṭamaṃḍapaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. After this incident the people will begin to call this Pavilion of Salvation the Pavilion of Cocks.

## \|\| 2.98.89 \|\|

*caritramapi vai teṣāṃ ye smariṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*muktimaṃḍapamāsādya śreyaḥ prāpsyaṃti tepi hi \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Those men who come to the Muktimaṇḍapa and remember their story will certainly attain the good (i.e. Mokṣa).

## \|\| 2.98.90 \|\|

*iti yāvatkathāṃ śaṃbhurbhaviṣyāmagrato hareḥ \|*  
*akarottumulo nādo ghaṃṭānāṃ tāvadudgataḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Even as Śaṃbhu narrated this future story to Hari, a tumultuous sound of ringing bells arose there.

## \|\| 2.98.91 \|\|

*athanaṃdinamāhūya devadeva umādhavaḥ \|*  
*provāca naṃdinvijñāyāgatya brūhi kuto ravaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Thereupon the Lord of Devas, the Consort of Umā, called Nandin and said, “Nandin, go and find out whence (comes) this sound.”

## \|\| 2.98.92 \|\|

*atha naṃdī samāgatya provāca vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*namaskṛtya prahṛṣṭāsyaḥ prabaddhakarasaṃpuṭaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Then Nandin returned and spoke to the Bull-emblemed Lord after bowing down to him with palms joined in reverence, and face beaming with pleasure.

## \|\| 2.98.93 \|\|

*naṃdyuvāca \|*  
*devadeva trinayana kimapūrvaṃ bravīmi te \|*  
*mokṣalakṣmīvilāso'tra kaiścitkaiścitsamarcyate \|\| 93 \|\|*

Nandin said:

93\. O Lord of Devas, O Three-eyed Lord, what new thing can I say to you. The graceful charms of the Glory of Salvation are being adored by some here.

## \|\| 2.98.94-95 \|\|

*atha smitvābravīcchaṃbhuḥ siddhaṃ nastu samīhitam \|*  
*utthāya devadeveśaḥ saha devyā sumaṃgalaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*brahmaṇā hariṇā sārdhaṃ tato'gādraṃgamaṃḍapam \|*  
*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*śrutvādhyāyamimaṃ puṇyaṃ paramānaṃdakāraṇam \|*  
*naraḥ parāṃ mudaṃ prāpya kailāsaṃ prāpsyati dhruvam \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. Then Śaṃbhu said smiling, “Our desire has been fulfilled.” The Lord of the chiefs of Devas, in auspicious guise, got up. Accompanied by the Goddess, Brahmā and Hari, he went to the Raṅga Maṇḍapa.

## Chapter 99 - The Greatness of Śrī Viśveśvara

## \|\| 2.99.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu sūta yathā proktaṃ kuṃbhaje śarajanmanā \|*  
*devadevasya caritaṃ viśveśasya parātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1\. Listen, O Sūta, to the (activities of the) life of the Lord of Devas, of Viśveśa, the great Ātman, in the manner narrated to the Pot-born One by the Śaravana-born Lord (Kārttikeya).

## \|\| 2.99.2 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*senānīḥ kathaya tvaṃ me tato nirvāṇamaṃḍapāt \|*  
*nirgatya devo deveṃdraiḥ sahitaḥ kiṃ cakāra ha \|\| 2 \|\|*

Agastya said:

2\. O Senānī (Commander-in-chief i.e. Kārttikeya), do narrate to me what the Lord did after coming out of the Nirvāṇa Maṇḍapa accompanied by the Devas and Indra.

## \|\| 2.99.3 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*muktimaṃḍapataḥ śaṃbhurbrahmaviṣṇupurogamaḥ \|*  
*śṛṃgāramaṃḍapaṃ prāpya yaccakāra vadāmi tat \|\| 3 \|\|*

Skanda said:

3\. I shall describe what Śaṃbhu did after reaching Śṛṅgāra-Maṇḍapa from Mukti-Maṇḍapa, keeping Brahmā and Viṣṇu as forerunners.

## \|\| 2.99.4-7 \|\|

*prāṅmukhastūpaviśyeśaḥ sahāsmābhiḥ saheśayā \|*  
*brahmaṇādhiṣṭhitaḥ savye vāmapārśvetha śārṅgiṇā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vījyamāno maheṃdreṇa ṛṣibhiḥ parito vṛtaḥ \|*  
*gaṇaiḥ pṛṣṭhapradeśasthairjoṣaṃ tiṣṭhadbhirādarāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

*udāyudhaiḥ sevyamānaścāvasanmānabhūribhiḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇe viṣṇave śaṃbhuḥ pāṇimutkṣipya dakṣiṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*darśayāmāsa deveśo liṃgaṃ paśyata paśyata \|*  
*idameva paraṃ jyotiridameva parātparam \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. The Lord sat facing the East along with us and the Goddess. Brahmā sat on his right and Śārṅgin (Viṣṇu) sat on his left side. He was fanned by Mahendra and surrounded by the sages. He was silently served by the Gaṇas with arms lifted up. They were standing at the sides with respectful veneration to the utmost. Śaṃbhu raised his right hand and showed the Liṅga to Brahmā and Viṣṇu saying: “Look. This is the greatest splendour. This alone is greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 2.99.8-14 \|\|

*idameva hi me rūpaṃ sthāvaraṃ cāti siddhidam \|*  
*ete pāśupatā siddhā ābāla brahmacāriṇaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*jiteṃdriyāstaponiṣṭhāḥ paṃcārthajñānanirmalāḥ \|*  
*bhasmakūṭaśayā dātāḥ suśīlā ūrdhvaretasaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*liṃgārcanaratā nityamananyeṃdriyamānasāḥ \|*  
*sadaiva vāruṇāgneya snānadvaya sunirmalāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kaṃdamūlaphalāhārāḥ paratattvārpitekṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*satyavaṃto jitakrodhā nirmohā niṣparigrahāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nirīhā niṣprapaṃcāśca nirātaṃkā nirāmayāḥ \|*  
*nirbhagā nirupāyāśca niḥsaṃgā nirmalāśayāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nistīrṇodagrasaṃsārā nirvikalpā nirenasaḥ \|*  
*nirdvaṃdvā niścitārthāśca nirahaṃkāravṛttayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sadaiva me mahāprītā matputrā matsvarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*ete pūjyā namasyāśca madbuddhyāmatparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

8-14.\[1\] This alone is my immobile form that accords the highest Siddhi. These are Pāśupata devotees, Siddhas observing celibacy ever since childhood. They have conquered their sense-organs. They are fully engrossed in their penance. They are free from impurities due to their knowledge of the five topics (entities) (or the four Vedas, Itihāsas and Purāṇas). They lie down on a heap of holy ash. They have mental restraint. They are well-behaved. They are Ūrdhvaretas (They have sublimated their sexual energies). They are always engaged in the adoration of the Liṅga. Their sense-organs and minds do not turn towards anyone else. They are always pure on account of Vāruṇa (shower) and Āgneya (ash) baths. Their food consists of bulbous roots, roots and fruits. Their eyes are dedicated to the Supreme Being. They are truthful. They have conquered anger. They are devoid of delusion. They do not possess anything. They do not desire anything. They have no sense of identity with the body etc. They have no sorrow. They are free from ailments. The are Nirbhagas (i.e. have abandoned riches), Nirupāyas (do not employ means of expendiency); they have no contact with others; their hearts are free from impurities. They have crossed the terrible ocean of the worldly existence. They have no doubts. They are free from sins. They are free from opposing pairs (e.g. pleasure-pain). They have certain firm views. Their activities are uncontaminated by egotism. They are always my great favourites. They are my sons in my own form. These are to be adored and bowed to, thinking them to be I myself, by those who solely worship me.

## \|\| 2.99.15 \|\|

*arciteṣveṣvahaṃ prīto bhaviṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*asminvaiśveśvare kṣetre saṃbhojyāḥ śivayoginaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If they are adored, I become pleased undoubtedly. In this holy spot of Viśveśvara, Śivayogins should be duly fed.

## \|\| 2.99.16-19 \|\|

*koṭibhojyaphalaṃ samyagekaika parisaṃkhyayā \|*  
*ayaṃ viśveśvaraḥ sākṣātsthāvarātmā jagatprabhuḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ sarvasiddhīnāṃ kartā bhaktijuṣāmiha \|*  
*ahaṃ kadāciddṛśyaḥ syāmadṛśyaḥ syāṃ kadācana \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ānaṃdakānane cātra svairaṃ tiṣṭhāmi devatāḥ \|*  
*anugrahāya sarveṣāṃ bhaktānāmiha sarvadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sthāsyāmi liṃgarūpeṇa ciṃtitārthaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃbhūnyasvayaṃbhūni yāni liṃgāni sarvataḥ \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi cāyāṃti draṣṭuṃ liṃgamidaṃ sadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. If each one is perfectly fed, it has the merit of feeding ten million persons. This Viśveśvara is Lord of the universe himself in the form of a stationary being.

He brings about all the Siddhis of all persons who are devoted to him. I may be manifest sometimes and sometimes unmanifest.

O Devas, I stay in this Ānandakānana as I please, independently for the purpose of blessing all devotees here for ever.

I shall be staying in the form of a Liṅga, bestowing the object thought of. All the Liṅgas (whether) they are self-born or not, always come to see this Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.99.20 \|\|

*ahaṃ sarveṣu liṃgeṣu tiṣṭhā्myeva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ tviyaṃ parāmūrtirmama liṃgasvarūpiṇī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. There is no doubt about this that I stay in all the Liṅgas. But this is the greatest of my forms as a Liṅga.

## \|\| 2.99.21 \|\|

*yena liṃgamidaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śraddhayā śuddhacakṣuṣā \|*  
*sākṣātkāreṇa tenāhaṃ dṛṣṭa eva divaukasaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O heaven-dwellers, it is as good as I have been seen directly by the person by whom this Liṅga was seen faithfully with a pure vision.

## \|\| 2.99.22 \|\|

*śravaṇādasya liṃgasya pātakaṃ janmasaṃcitam \|*  
*kṣaṇātkṣayati śṛṇvaṃtu devā ṛṣigaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. May the Devas listen along with the sages. If one hears about this Liṅga, all his sins accumulated in the course of a birth perish in an instant.

## \|\| 2.99.23 \|\|

*smaraṇādasya liṃgasya pāpaṃ janmadvayārjitam \|*  
*avaśyaṃ naśyati kṣipraṃ mama vākyānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In one remembers this Liṅga, all the sins accumulated in the course of two births necessarily perish immediately at my behest. There should be no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.99.24 \|\|

*etalliṃgaṃ samuddiśya gṛhānniṣkramaṇakṣaṇāt \|*  
*vilīyate mahāpāpamapi janmatrayārjitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. With this Liṅga in view, if one sets out from his house, all the sins accumulated in the course of three births perish instantly.

## \|\| 2.99.25 \|\|

*darśanādasya liṃgasya hayamedhaśatodbhavam \|*  
*puṇyaṃ labheta niyataṃ mamānugrahatomarāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O immortal ones, by seeing this Liṅga, one gets the merit arising from a hundred horse-sacrifices invariably, due to my blessings.

## \|\| 2.99.26 \|\|

*svayaṃbhuvosya liṃgasya mama viśveśituḥ surāḥ \|*  
*rājasūyasahasrasya phalaṃ syātsparśamātrataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Suras, the merit of a thousand Rājasūya sacrifices accrues merely by the touch of this self-born Liṅga of myself, of Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 2.99.27 \|\|

*puṣpamātra pradānācca culukodakapūvarkam \|*  
*śatasauvarṇikaṃ puṇyaṃ labhate bhaktiyogataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Merely by offering flowers along with a palmful of water with devout feelings, one attains the merit of (offering) a hundred Suvarṇas (gold pieces).

## \|\| 2.99.28 \|\|

*pūjāmātraṃ vidhāyāsya liṃgarājasya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sahasrahemakamalapūjāphalamavāpyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. By performing the worship alone with great devotion of this king of Liṅgas, the merit of adoration with a thousand golden lotuses is obtained.

## \|\| 2.99.29 \|\|

*vidhāya mahatī pūjāṃ paṃcāmṛtapuraḥsarām \|*  
*asya liṃgasya labhate puruṣārthacatuṣṭayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By performing the great adoration of this Liṅga with Pañcāmṛta as the main constituent, one obtains all the four aims of life.

## \|\| 2.99.30 \|\|

*vastrapūtajalairliṃgaṃ snāpayitvā mamāmarāḥ \|*  
*lakṣāśvamedhajanitaṃ puṇyamāpnoti sattamaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O immortal ones, if an excellent devotee bathes the Liṅga of mine with the waters filtered and purified through a cloth, he obtains the merit arising from a hundred thousand horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.99.31 \|\|

*sugaṃdhacaṃdanarasairliṃgamālipya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*ālipyate surastrībhiḥ sugaṃdhairyakṣakardamaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. If anyone devoutly smears the Liṅga with sweet-smelling sandal juice, he will be smeared (in heaven) with scented Yakṣakardama (mixture of camphor, agallochum, musk and Kaṅkola) by celestial damsels.

## \|\| 2.99.32 \|\|

*sāmoda dhūpadānaiśca divyagaṃdhāśrayo bhavet \|*  
*ghṛtadīpaprabodhaiśca jyotīrūpa vimānagaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. By offering sweet-smelling incense (a devotee) becomes the receptacle of divine scent. By lighting lamps of clarified butter, he moves about in an aerial chariot in the form of a radiant splendour.

## \|\| 2.99.33 \|\|

*karpūravartidīpena sakṛddattena bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*karpūradehagauraśrīrbhavedbhālavilocanaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. By offering a lamp with camphor-wick once, a devotee attains white splendour of the body like camphor and becomes three-eyed with an eye in forehead.

## \|\| 2.99.34 \|\|

*dattvā naivedyamātraṃ tu sikthesikthe yugaṃyugam \|*  
*kailāsādrau vaseddhīmānmahābhogasamanvitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. By offering Naivedya alone, an intelligent devotee will enjoy great pleasures and reside on the Kailāsa Mountain at the rate of a Yuga for each particle of boiled rice.

## \|\| 2.99.35 \|\|

*viśveśe paramānnaṃ yo dadyātsājya saśarkaram \|*  
*trailokyaṃ tarpitaṃ tena sadevapitṛmānavam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. If anyone offers rice pudding with ghee and sugar unto Viśveśa, it is as though all the three worlds including Devas, Pitṛs and human beings have been propitiated by him.

## \|\| 2.99.36 \|\|

*mukhavāsaṃ tu yo dadyāddarpaṇaṃ cārucāmaram \|*  
*ullocaṃ sukhaparyaṃkaṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ mahat \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Great indeed is the merit of one who offers Mukhavāsa (perfume to make the breath fragrant), mirror, beautiful chowries, awning and comfortable couch.

## \|\| 2.99.37 \|\|

*saṃkhyā sāgararatnānāṃ kathaṃcitkartumiṣyate \|*  
*mukhavāsādidānasya kaḥ saṃkhyāmatra kārayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It is somehow possible to calculate the number of the jewels in an ocean; but who can calculate the merit of the offerings of Mukhavāsa etc.?

## \|\| 2.99.38 \|\|

*pūjopakaraṇadravyaṃ yo ghaṃṭā gaḍukādikam \|*  
*bhaktyā me bhavane dadyātsa vasedatra meṃtike \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He who devoutly offers the means and materials of worship like beīī, water-pot etc. in any abode (temple) shall stay here near me.

## \|\| 2.99.39 \|\|

*yo gītavādyanṛtyānāmekaṃ matprītaye vyadhāt \|*  
*tasyāgrato divārātraṃ bhavettauryatrikaṃ mahat \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If a devotee makes arrangement for either vocal, instrumental music or dance for propitiating me, in front of him there shall be great triple symphony.

## \|\| 2.99.40 \|\|

*citralekhanakarmādi prāsāde me'tra kārayet \|*  
*yaḥ sacitrānmahābhogānbhuṃkte matpurataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. One who makes arrangement for pictures and paintings in my mansion, shall enjoy great pleasures of diverse kinds staying before me.

## \|\| 2.99.41 \|\|

*sakṛdviśveśvaraṃ natvā madhye janmasudhīrnaraḥ \|*  
*trailokyavaṃditapado jāyate vasudhāpatiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. By bowing to Viśveśvara once in the course of life, a wise man becomes the lord of the earth with his feet bowed down to by all the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.99.42 \|\|

*yastu viśvevaraṃ dṛṣṭvā hyanyatrāpi vipadyate \|*  
*tasya janmāṃtare mokṣo bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If a devotee visits Viśveśvara but dies elsewhere, he will undoubtedly become liberated in the next birth.

## \|\| 2.99.43 \|\|

*viśveśākhyā tu jihvāgre viśvanāthakathāśrutau \|*  
*viśveśaśīlanaṃ citte yasya tasya janiḥ kutaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. How can there be rebirth if the name of Viśveśvara is at the tip of the tongue, the story of Viśvanātha in the ear and the regular meditation of Viśveśa in the mind?

## \|\| 2.99.44 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ me viśvanāthasya dṛṣṭvā yaścānumodate \|*  
*sa me gaṇeṣu gaṇyeta mahāpuṇyabalāśritaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After seeing Viśvanātha’s (my) Liṅga if one rejoices, he will be counted as one among my Gaṇas, because he has the strength of the merit.

## \|\| 2.99.45 \|\|

*nityaṃ viśveśa viśveśa viśvanātheti yo japet \|*  
*trisaṃdhyaṃ taṃ sukṛtinaṃ japāmyahamapi dhruvam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. If one repeats during the three Sandhyās (morning, midday and evening) everyday Viśveśa, Viśveśa and Viśvanātha I too shall utter the name of that meritorious devotee.

## \|\| 2.99.46 \|\|

*mamāpīdaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ sadā pūjyatamaṃ surāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjyaṃ devarṣi mānavaiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Suras, this great Liṅga is worthy of being worshipped even by me for ever. Hence it should be assiduously worshipped by Devas, sages and human beings.

## \|\| 2.99.47 \|\|

*yairna viśveśvaro dṛṣṭo yairna viśveśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kṛtāṃtadūtaiste dṛṣṭāstaiḥ smṛtā garbhavedanā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. If Viśveśvara is not seen and if Viśveśvara is not remembered, they are seen by the messengers of the god of Death and they have to recollect (experience) the sufferings of the womb.

## \|\| 2.99.48 \|\|

*yairidaṃ praṇataṃ liṃgaṃ praṇatāste surāsuraiḥ \|*  
*yasyai kena praṇāmena dikpālapadamalpakam \|*  
*dikpālapadataḥ pātaḥ pātaḥ śivanaternahi \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. If this Liṅga is bowed to, they will be bowed to by Suras and Asuras. When considered against a single bow to the Liṅga, the position of the Guardian of a Quarter is worthless. There is downfall from the position of a Guardian of a Quarter, (but) there is no downfall from the obeisance to Śiva.

## \|\| 2.99.49 \|\|

*śṛṇvaṃtu devarṣigaṇāḥ samastāstathyaṃ bruve tacca paropakṛtyai \|*  
*na bhūrbhuvaḥ svargamaharjanāṃtarviśveśatulyaṃ kvacidasti liṃgam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. May all the groups of Devas, sages and Gaṇas listen. I shall speak the truth and that too for helping others. Nowhere within the worlds of Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svarga, Mahaḥ and Jana, is there a Liṅga equal to Viśveśa.

## \|\| 2.99.50 \|\|

*na satyaloke na tapasyaho surā vaikuṃṭhakailāsarasātaleṣu \|*  
*tīrthaṃ kvacidvai maṇikarṇikāsamaṃ liṃgaṃ ca viśveśvaratulyamanyataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Neither in Satyaloka, nor in Tapoloka nor in Vaikuṇṭha, Kailāsa and Rasātala is a Tīrtha anywhere on a par with Maṇikarṇikā, or a Liṅga like Viśveśa.

## \|\| 2.99.51 \|\|

*na viśvanāthasya samaṃ hi liṃgaṃ na tīrthamanyanmaṇikarṇikātaḥ \|*  
*tapovanaṃ kutracidasti nānyacchubhaṃ mamānaṃdavanena tulyam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. There is no Liṅga equal to that of Viśvanātha. There is no Tīrtha other than Maṇikarṇikā. There is no splendid penance grove anywhere else on a par with my Ānandavana.

## \|\| 2.99.52 \|\|

*vārāṇasī tīrthamayī samastā yasyāstunāmāpi hi tīrthatīrtham \|*  
*tatrāpi kācinmama saukhyabhūmirmahāpavitrā maṇikarṇikāsau \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The whole of Vārāṇasī is full of Tīrthas. Its very name is ‘Tīrtha of all Tīrthas’. There itself is the highly sacred Maṇikarṇikā, the very ground of my happiness.

## \|\| 2.99.53 \|\|

*sthānādamuṣmānmamarājasaudhātprācyāṃ manāgīśasamāśritāyām \|*  
*savyepasavye ca karāḥ krameṇa śatatrayī yāpi śatadvayī ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. From the site which is my royal palace, the city extends in between the north and the east; to the left it is three hundred hands (up to Hariścandreśvara) and to the right it is two hundred hands (up to Gaṅgā Keśava—Comm.).

## \|\| 2.99.54 \|\|

*hastāḥ śataṃ paṃca surāpagāyāmudīcyavācyormaṇikarṇikeyam \|*  
*sārastrilokyāḥ parakośabhūmiryaiḥ sevitā te mama hṛcchayā hi \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In Gaṅgā, Maṇikarṇikā extends to five hundred hands north to south. It is the very essence of the three worlds. It is the basic support of the great soul. Those who resort to it lie in my heart (They are of the form of Sat—Comm.).

## \|\| 2.99.55 \|\|

*asminmamānaṃdavane yadetalliṃgaṃ sudhādhāma sudhāmadhāma \|*  
*āsapta pātālatalātsvayaṃbhu samutthitaṃ bhaktakṛpāvaśena \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In this Ānandakānana of mine, this Liṅga which is the abode of nectar (of Salvation) and from which the radiance of the Self originates has come out by itself from the bottom of the seven Pātālas out of compassion for the devotees.

## \|\| 2.99.56 \|\|

*yesmiñjanāḥ kṛtrimabhāvabuddhyā liṃgaṃ bhajiṣyaṃti ca hetuvādaiḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ hi daṃḍaḥ para eṣa eva nagarbhavāsādviramaṃti te dhruvam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The greatest punishment for those people who resort to this Liṅga after indulging in reasoning alone is this that they will never cease to be born and reborn in the womb.

## \|\| 2.99.57 \|\|

*yadyaddhitaṃ svasya sadaiva tattalliṃgetra deyaṃ mama bhaktimadbhiḥ \|*  
*ihāpyamutrāpi na tasya saṃkṣayo yatheha pāpasya kṛtasya pāpibhiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Whatever is beneficial (or desirable) to oneself should be offered to this Liṅga by people who are devoted to me. Neither here nor elsewhere does the sin committed by sinners perish as it perishes here.

## \|\| 2.99.58 \|\|

*dūrasthitairapyadhibuddhibhiryairliṃgaṃ samārādhi mamedamatra \|*  
*mayaiva dattaiḥ śubhavastujātairniḥśreyasaḥ śrīrvasaṃ yetsatastān \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. If any Liṅga here is worshipped by highly intelligent ones stationed far away, the Glory of Salvation shall abide in them along with auspicious things given by me alone.

## \|\| 2.99.59 \|\|

*śṛṇuṣva viṣṇo śṛṇu sṛṣṭikartaḥ śṛṇvaṃtu devarṣigaṇāḥ samastāḥ \|*  
*idaṃ hi liṃgaṃ parasiddhidaṃ satāṃ bhedo manāgatra na matsakāśataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O Viṣṇu, listen, O Creator (Brahmā) listen; may all the Devas, sages and the Gaṇas listen. This Liṅga gives the greatest Siddhi unto the good, due to being in my vicinity. There is not the slightest change in this regard.

## \|\| 2.99.60 \|\|

*asminhi liṃge'khilasiddhisādhane samarpitaṃ yaiḥ sukṛtārjitaṃ vasu \|*  
*tebhyotimātrākhilasaukhyasādhanaṃ dadāmi nirvāṇapadaṃ sunirbhayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. If the wealth earned by means of good merit is offered to this Liṅga that is the means of the achievement of all Siddhis. I accord to them the Nirvāṇapada (Position of Salvation) that is the means of obtaining every happiness beyond measure and which affords freedom from fear.

## \|\| 2.99.61 \|\|

*utkṣipya bāhuṃ tvasakṛdbravīmi trayīmaye'smiṃstrayameva sāram \|*  
*viśveśa liṃgaṃ maṇikarṇikāṃbu kāśīpurī satyamidaṃ trisatyam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Lifting up the hand, I assert again and again that, in this world having the three Vedas, only three things are essential: Viśveśa Liṅga, Maṇikarṇikā water and the city of Kāśī. This is the truth, threefold truth.”

## \|\| 2.99.62 \|\|

*utthāya devotha sa śaktirīśastasminhi liṃge kṛtacārupūjaḥ \|*  
*yayau layaṃ te ca surā jayeti jayeti coktvā nunuvustamīśam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Then the Lord got up along with Śakti, performed the excellent worship and merged into the same Liṅga. The Suras uttered, “Be victorious, be victorious” and eulogized the Lord.

## \|\| 2.99.63-64 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*kṣetrasya maitrāvaruṇe vimuktasya mahāmate \|*  
*prabhāvasyaikadeśoyaṃ kathitaḥ kalmaṣāpahaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tavāgre tu yathābuddhi kāśīviśleṣatāpi naḥ \|*  
*acireṇaiva kālena kāśīṃ prāpsyasyanuttamām \|\| 64 \|\|*

Skanda said:

63-64. O son of Mitra and Varuṇa, O highly intelligent one, only a part of the great efficacy of the holy spot Avimukta has been narrated. It dispels sins. I have narrated it to you in accordance with my understanding because you are being distressed due to separation from Kāśī. Ere long you will reach the excellent Kāśī.

## \|\| 2.99.65 \|\|

*astācalasya śikharaṃ prāptavāneṣa bhānumān \|*  
*tavāpi hi mamāpyeṣa maunasya samayo'bhavat \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The Sun has come to the peak of the mountain of setting. To you as well as to me, this is the time for silence.

## \|\| 2.99.66 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*śrutveti sa muniḥ sūta saṃdhyopāstyai vinirgataḥ \|*  
*praṇamyau meyamasakṛllopāmudrā samanvitaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

66\. On hearing this, O Sūta, the sage along with Lopāmudrā bowed down to the Son of Umā repeatedly and set out for the Sandhyā prayers.

## \|\| 2.99.67 \|\|

*rahasyaṃ parivijñāya kṣetrasya śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*agastyo niścitamanāḥ śivadhyānaparobhavat \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. After learning well the secret of the holy spot of the Moon-crested Lord, Agastya with a firm mind became engrossed in the meditation of Siva.

## \|\| 2.99.68 \|\|

*ānaṃdakānanasyeha mahimānaṃ mahattaram \|*  
*kotra varṇayituṃ śaktaḥ sūta varṣaśatairapi \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O Sūta, who is capable of adequately describing the exalted greatness of Ānandakānana even in a hundred years.

## \|\| 2.99.69 \|\|

*yathā devyai samākhyāyi śivena paramātmanā \|*  
*tathā skaṃdena kathitaṃ māhātmyaṃ kuṃbhasaṃbhave \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The greatness has been recounted to the Pot-born One by Skanda in the same manner as it was narrated to the Goddess by the noble Lord.

## \|\| 2.99.70 \|\|

*tavāgre ca samākhyātaṃ śukādīnāṃ ca sattama \|*  
*idānīṃ praṣṭukāmosi kiṃ tatpṛccha vadāmi te \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. O excellent one, it has been narrated to you as well as Śuka and others. Now tell me what you have been desirous of asking me. I shall narrate it to you.

## \|\| 2.99.71 \|\|

*śrutvādhyāyamimaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam \|*  
*samastaciṃtitaphalapradaṃ martyo bhavetkṛtī \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. On hearing this meritorious chapter that is destructive of all sins and that accords all the benefits desired, a man will become contented.

## Chapter 100 - Index to Kāśīkhanda

## \|\| 2.100.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*idaṃ skāṃdamahaṃ śrutvā kāśīkhaṃḍamanuttamam \|*  
*nitarāṃ paritṛptosmi hṛdi cāpi vidhāritam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Suta said:

1\. I am exceedingly satisfied on hearing this excellent Kāśīkhaṇḍa of the Skanda-Purāṇa. It has been retained in the heart.

## \|\| 2.100.2 \|\|

*anukramaṇikādhyāyaṃ tathā māhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*pārāśarya samācakṣva yathāpūrvamidaṃ bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Son of Parāśara, narrate the chapter covering the Anukramaṇikā as well as the excellent Māhātmya (greatness of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa) in order to make this like the previous one.

## \|\| 2.100.3 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*sūtāvadhehi dharmātmañjātūkarṇya niśāmaya \|*  
*śukavaiśaṃpāyanādyāḥ śṛṇvaṃtvapi ca bālakāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

3\. O righteous-souled Sūta, O Son of Jātukarṇi, listen. May the Sons Śuka, Vaiśaṃpāyana and others also listen.

## \|\| 2.100.4 \|\|

*anukramaṇikādhyāyaṃ māhātmyaṃ cāpi khaṃḍajam \|*  
*pravakṣyāmyaghanāśāya mahāpuṇyapravardhanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I shall narrate the chapter of Index and contents as well as the Māhātmya of this Khaṇḍa for the purpose of dispelling sins. It enhances the merit.

## \|\| 2.100.5 \|\|

*viṃdhyanāradasaṃvādaḥ prathame parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*satyalokaprabhāvaśca dvitīyaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The conversation of Vindhya and Nārada has been mentioned in the first (chapter). The power and greatness of Satyaloka has been cited in the second (chapter).

## \|\| 2.100.6 \|\|

*agasterāśramapade devānāmāgamastataḥ \|*  
*pativratā caritraṃ ca prasthānaṃ kuṃbhasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The arrival of the Devas to the penance-grove of Agastya (chapter third), the conduct of chaste women (chapter 4) and the departure of the Pot-born One (chapter 5).

## \|\| 2.100.7 \|\|

*tīrthapraśaṃsā ca tataḥ saptapuryastataḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*saṃyaminyāḥ svarūpaṃ ca bradhnalokastataḥ param \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The praise of the Tīrtha (chapter 6), then the seven cities are remembered (chapter 7); the nature of Saṃyaminī (chapter 8), and thereafter the world of Bradhna (Sun-god) (chapter 9).

## \|\| 2.100.8 \|\|

*iṃdrāgnyorlokasaṃprāptistataśca śivaśarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*agneḥ samudbhavastasmāt kravyādvaruṇasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then Śivaśarman’s arrival at the worlds of Indra and Agni (chapter 10). Then the origin of Agni (chapter 11). Thereafter the origin of Kravyāt (i.e. Nirṛti) and Varuṇa (chapter 12).

## \|\| 2.100.9 \|\|

*gaṃdhavatyalakāpuryorīśayostu samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*caṃdralokapariprāptiḥ śivaśarmadvijanmanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The origin of the lords of Gandhavatī (Capital of Vāyu) and Alakā (Capital of Kubera) (chapter 13), and the arrival of the Brāhmaṇa Śivaśarman in Candraloka (chapter 14).

## \|\| 2.100.10 \|\|

*uḍuloka kathā tasmāttataḥ śukrasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*māheya gurusaurīṇāṃ lokānāṃ varṇanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then the tale of the stellar world (chapter 15). Then the origin of Śukra (Venus) (chapter 16). Then the description of the worlds of Māheya (Mars), Guru (Jupiter) and Sauri (Saturn) (chapter 17).

## \|\| 2.100.11 \|\|

*saptarṣīṇāṃ tato lokā dhruvasya ca tapastataḥ \|*  
*tato dhruvapadaprāptirdhruvaloka sthitistataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The world of the Seven Sages (chapter 18), the penance of Dhruva (chapter 19), the arrival of Viṣṇu (chapter 20) and the arrival at the world of Dhruva (chapter 21).

## \|\| 2.100.12 \|\|

*darśanaṃ satyalokasya tasya vai śivaśarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*caturbhujābhiṣekaśca nirvāṇaṃ śivaśarmaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Sivaśarman’s vision of Satyaloka (chapter 22), the coronation of the Four-armed Lord (chapter 23), Śivaśarman’s Salvation (chapter 24).

## \|\| 2.100.13 \|\|

*skaṃdāgastyośca saṃvādo maṇikarṇyāḥ samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*tatastu gaṃgāmāhātmyaṃ tato daśaharāstavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The conversation between Skanda and Agastya begins (chapter 25); the origin of Maṇikarṇikā (chapter 26). Then the greatness of Gaṅgā and the hymn of Daśaharā (chapter 27).

## \|\| 2.100.14 \|\|

*prabhāvaścāpi gaṃgāyā gaṃgānāmasahasrakam \|*  
*vārāṇasyāḥ praśaṃsātha bhairavāvirbhavastataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The efficacy of Gaṅgā (chapter 28), the thousand names of Gaṅgā (chapter 29). Eulogy of Vārāṇasī (chapter 30). The manifestation of Bhairava (chapter 31).

## \|\| 2.100.15 \|\|

*daṃḍapāṇeḥ samudbhūtirjñānavāpyudbhavastataḥ \|*  
*ākhyānaṃ ca kalāvatyāḥ sadācārastataḥ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The origin of Daṇḍapāṇi (chapter 32), the origin of Jñānavāpī (chapter 33). The anecdote of Kalāvatī (chapter 34), then (rules of) good conduct (chapter 35).

## \|\| 2.100.16 \|\|

*brahmacāri prakaraṇaṃ tataḥ strīlakṣaṇāni ca \|*  
*kṛtyākṛtyaprakaraṇamavimukteśavarṇanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Brahmacāriprakaraṇa (Duties of celibate students) (chapter 36), the salient characteristics of women (chapter 37). Prescriptions and prohibitions (chapter 38). Description of Avimukteśa (chapter 39).

## \|\| 2.100.17 \|\|

*tato gṛhasthadharmāśca tato yoganirūpaṇam \|*  
*kālajñānaṃ tataḥ proktaṃ divodāsasya varṇanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then the duties of a householder (chapter 40). Review of Yoga (chapter 41). Kālajṅāna (chapter 42). The story of Divodāsa (chapter 43).

## \|\| 2.100.18 \|\|

*kāśyāśca varṇanaṃ tasmādyoginīvarṇanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*lolārkasya samākhyānamuttarārkakathā tataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Description of Kāśī (chapter 44). Description of Yoginīs (chapter 45). Narration (legend) of Lolārka (chapter 46). The story of Uttarārka (chapter 47).

## \|\| 2.100.19 \|\|

*sāṃbādityasya mahimā drupadāditya śaṃsanam \|*  
*tatastu garuḍākhyānamaruṇārkādayastataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The greatness of Sāṃbāditya (chapter 48); the eulogy of Drupadāditya (chapter 49) as well as Mayūkhāditya. The story of Garuḍa (chapter 50), Aruṇārka etc. (chapter 57) including the Sun-gods, viz. Vṛddha Keśava, Vimala Gaṅgādityas.

## \|\| 2.100.20 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhikaṃ tīrthaṃ maṃdarācca gaṇāgamaḥ \|*  
*piśācamocanākhyānaṃ gaṇeśapreṣaṇaṃ tataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The Tīrtha of Daśāśvamedha (chapter 52). The arrival of the Gaṇas from Mandara (chapter 53). Legend of Piśācamocana (chapter 54) and deputation of Gaṇeśa (chapter 55).

## \|\| 2.100.21 \|\|

*māyāgaṇapateścātha ḍhuṃḍhiprādurbhavastataḥ \|*  
*viṣṇumāyāprapaṃcotha divodāsavisarjanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Māyāgaṇapati described (chapter 56). The manifestation of Ḍhuṇḍhi (chapter 57). The series of Viṣṇu’s Māyā and Divodāsa being sent to Kailāsa (chapter 58).

## \|\| 2.100.22 \|\|

*tataḥ paṃcanadotpattirbiṃdumādhavasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*tato vaiṣṇavatīrthānāṃ māhātmyaparivarṇanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The origin of Pañcanada (chapter 59); the origin of Bindumādhava (chapter 60). Then the greatness of Vaiṣṇava Tīrthas (chapter 61).

## \|\| 2.100.23 \|\|

*prayāṇaṃ maṃdarātkāśīṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaśūlinaḥ \|*  
*jaigīṣavyena saṃvādo jyeṣṭhasthāne maheśituḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Departure of the bull-emblemed, trident-bearing Lord of Kāśī from Mandara (chapter 62). The dialogue of Jaigīṣavya and Maheśa at the Jyeṣṭha Sthāna (chapter 63).

## \|\| 2.100.24 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣetrarahasyasya kathanaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*athātaḥ kaṃdukeśasya vyāghreśasya samudbhavaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the narration of the secret of the holy spot which destroys sins (chapter 64). The origin of Kandukeśa and Vyāghreśa (chapter 65).

## \|\| 2.100.25 \|\|

*tataḥ śaileśvarakathā ratneśasya ca darśanam \|*  
*kṛttivāsaḥ samutpattistataścāyatanāgamaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then is the story of Śaileśvara (chapter 66); the vision of Ratneśa (chapter 67); the origin of Kṛttivāsas (chapter 69).

## \|\| 2.100.26 \|\|

*devatānāmadhiṣṭhānaṃ durgāsuraparākramaḥ \|*  
*durgāyā vijayaścātha tata oṃkāravarṇanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The Adhiṣṭhāna of the deities (chapter 70); the exploits of Durga (Demon) (chapter 71); Victory of Durgā (Goddess) (chapter 72). Then the description of Oṃkāra (chapter 73).

## \|\| 2.100.27 \|\|

*punaroṃkāramāhātmyaṃ trilocanasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*trilocanaprabhāvotha kedārākhyānameva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Further description of the greatness of Oṃkāra (chapter 74). The origin of Trilocana (chapter 75). The power of Trilocana (chapter 76). Narration of Kedāra (chapter 77).

## \|\| 2.100.28 \|\|

*tato dharmeśamahimā tataḥ pakṣikathā śubhā \|*  
*tato viśvabhujākhyānaṃ durdamasya kathā tataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The greatness of Dharmeśa (chapter 78). The story of the birds (chapter 79). The narration of Viśvabhuja (chapter 80). Then the story of Durdama (chapter 81).

## \|\| 2.100.29 \|\|

*tato vīreśvarākhyānaṃ vīreśa mahimā punaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgātīrthaiśca saṃyuktā kāmeśa mahimā tataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then the narration of Vīreśvara (chapter 82). Further greatness of Vīreśa (chapter 83). Gaṅgā in combination with the Tīrthas (chapter 84). Then the greatness of Kāmeśa (chapter 85).

## \|\| 2.100.30 \|\|

*viśvakarmeśa mahimā dakṣayajñasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*satyā dehavisargaśca tato dakṣeśvarodbhavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The greatness of Viśvakarmeśa (chapter 86); the beginning of the Yajña of Dakṣa (chapter 87); Satī casts off her body (chapter 88); then the origin of Dakṣeśvara (chapter 89).

## \|\| 2.100.31 \|\|

*tato vai pārvatīśasya mahimnaḥ parikīrtanam \|*  
*gaṃgeśasyātha mahimā narmadeśasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then the glorification of Pārvatīśa (chapter 90); then the greatness of Gaṅgeśa (chapter 91); the origin of Narmadeśa (chapter 92).

## \|\| 2.100.32 \|\|

*satīśvarasamutpattiramṛteśādi vaṇarnam \|*  
*vyāsasya hi bhujastaṃbho vyāsaśāpavimokṣaṇam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The origin of Satīśvara (chapter 93); the description of Amṛteśa etc. (chapter 94), Vyāsa’s arm benumbed (chapter 95). Redemption of Vyāsa’s curse (chapter 96).

## \|\| 2.100.33 \|\|

*kṣetratīrthakadaṃbaṃ ca muktimaṃḍapa saṃkathā \|*  
*viśveśāvirbhavaścātha tato yātrāparikramaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The groups of holy spots and Tīrthas (chapter 97). A detailed narration of Muktimaṇḍapa (chapter 98). The manifestation of Viśveśa (chapter. 99). Then the Yātrā Parikrama (order in the pilgrimage) (chapter 100).

## \|\| 2.100.34 \|\|

*etadākhyānaśatakaṃ krameṇa parikīrtitam \|*  
*yasya śravaṇamātreṇa sarvakhaṃḍa śruteḥ phalam \|*  
*anukramaṇikādhyāyepyasti yātrāparikramaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thus the hundred narrations have been enumerated in due order. On hearing this alone the benefit of the entire Khaṇḍa is acquired. In this chapter covering the contents, there is Yātrā Parikrama.

## \|\| 2.100.35 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yātrā parikramaṃ brūhi janānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|*  
*yathāvatsiddhikāmānāṃ satyavatyāḥ sutottama \|\| 35 \|\|*

Sūta said:

35\. Narrate the Yātrāparikrama, O excellent son of Satyavatī, with a desire for the welfare of the people desirous of the respective Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.100.36-40 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*niśāmaya mahāprājña lomaharṣaṇa vacmi te \|*  
*yathā prathamato yātrā kartavyā yātrikairmudā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sacailamādau saṃsnāya cakrapuṣkariṇījale \|*  
*saṃtarpyadevāsapitṝnbrāhmaṇāṃśca tathārthinaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ādityaṃ draupadīṃ viṣṇuṃ daṃḍapāṇiṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*namaskṛtya tato gaccheddraṣṭuṃ ḍhuṃḍhivināyakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*jñānavāpīmupaspṛśya naṃdikeśaṃ tatorcayet \|*  
*tārakeśaṃ tatobhyarcya mahākāleśvaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tataḥ punardaṃḍapāṇimityeṣā paṃcatīrthikā \|\| 40 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

36-40. Listen, O highly intelligent Lomaharṣaṇa. I shall tell you how the pilgrimage is to be joyously performed first by Pilgrims.

\[I. Pañca-Tīrthikā Yātrā\]

\[II. Vaiśveśvarī Yātrā\]

\[III. Aṣṭāyatana Yātrā\]

\[IV. Bath and Darśana of 14 Liṅgas\]

\[V. Ekādaśāyatanī Yātrā\]

\[VI. Gaurī Yātrā\]

\[Pilgrimages of Gaṇeśas, Bhairava etc.\]

\[Antargṛha Yātrā\]

## \|\| 2.100.100 \|\|

*śraddhāpūrvamimā yātrā kartavyāḥ kṣetravāsibhiḥ \|*  
*parvasvapi viśeṣeṇa kāryā yātrāśca sarvataḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. These Yātrās should be performed by the residents of the holy spot with great faith. During the days of great festivals especially, the Yātrās should be performed.

## \|\| 2.100.101 \|\|

*na vaṃdhyaṃ divasaṃ kuryādvināyātrāṃ kvacitkṛtī \|*  
*yātrādvayaṃ prayatnena kartavyaṃ prativāsaram \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The Kṛtin (one who wishes to be blessed) should never make the day deficient in Yātrās. Two Yātrās should be assiduously performed everyday.

## \|\| 2.100.102-104 \|\|

*ādau svargataraṃgiṇyāstato viśveśiturdhruvam \|*  
*yasya vaṃdhyaṃ dinaṃ yātaṃ kāśyāṃ nivasataḥ sataḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

*nirāśāḥ pitarastasya tasminneva dine'bhavan \|*  
*sa daṣṭaḥ kālasarpeṇa sa dṛṣṭo mṛtyunā sphuṭam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*sa muṣṭastatra divase viśveśo yatra nekṣitaḥ \|*  
*sarvatīrtheṣu sasnau sa sarvayātrāṃ vyadhātsa ca \|*  
*maṇikarṇyāṃ tu yaḥ snāto yo viśveśaṃ niraikṣata \|\| 104 \|\|*

102-104. Certainly it is bath in the celestial river at the outset and then (visit to) Viśveśa. If while staying in Kāśī, the day has been spent in vain, the Pitṛs become disappointed on the very same day. He is indeed bitten by the serpent of Kāla (death, time). He is seen by death to be sure. He is robbed, if he does not visit Viśveśa on that day. He who bathes in Maṇikarṇikā and visits Viśveśa, has bathed in all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 2.100.105 \|\|

*satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*dṛśyo viśveśvaro nityaṃ snātavyā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Truth! Truth! Again it is the truth, truth, truth again and again! Viśveśvara should be seen everyday and Maṇikarṇikā should be bathed in.

\[Phalaśruti (Fruit of hearing etc.) of the Kāśī Khaṇḍa\]

## Chapter 100 - Yātrā Parikrama (pilgrimages) (1): Pañca-tīrthikā Yātrā

## \|\| 2.100.41 \|\|

*dainaṃdinī vidhātavyā mahāphalamabhīpsubhiḥ \|*  
*tato vaiśveśvarī yātrā kāryā sarvārtha siddhidā \|\| 41 \|\|*

The following pilgrimage is called Pañcatīrthikā (Yātrā of the group of five Tīrthas): At the outset a devotee should take bath, along with the cloth worn, in the waters of Cakrapuṣkariṇī. He then duly offers libation to the Devas along with the Pitṛs. Then he propitiates the Brāhmaṇa suppliants. He then makes obeisance to Āditya, Draupadī, Viṣṇu, Daṇḍapāṇi and Maheśvara. Then he goes to visit Ḍhuṇḍhi Vināyaka. He performs ablution in Jñānavāpī and adores Nandikeśa. Thereafter he worships Tārakeśa and Mahākāleśvara thereafter. Then he adores Daṇḍapāṇi once again. This is Pañcatīrthikā.

41\. This should be done everyday by those who wish for great benefits.

## Chapter 100 - Yātrā Parikrama (pilgrimages) (2): Vaiśveśvarī Yātrā

## \|\| 2.100.42 \|\|

*dvisaptāyatanānāṃ ca kāryā yātrā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃ pratipadaṃ prāpya bhūtāvadhi yathāvidhi \|\| 42 \|\|*

Thereafter Vaiśveśvarī Yātrā (Pilgrimage to Viśveśvara) should be performed. This bestows the achievement of all objectives.

42\. Then the pilgrimage to the fourteen Āyatanas should be duly performed beginning with the first lunar day in the dark half and ending with the fourteenth.

## \|\| 2.100.43-47 \|\|

*athavā pratibhūtaṃ ca kṣetrasiddhimabhīpsubhiḥ \|*  
*tattattīrthakṛtasnānastattalliṃgakṛtārcanaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*maunena yātrāṃ kurvāṇaḥ phalaṃ prāpnoti yātrikaḥ \|*  
*oṃkāraṃ prathamaṃ paśyenmatsyodaryāṃ kṛtodakaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*triviṣṭapaṃ mahādevaṃ tato vai kṛttivāsasam \|*  
*ratneśaṃ cātha caṃdreśaṃ kedāraṃ ca tato vrajet \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dharmeśvaraṃ ca vīreśaṃ gacchetkāmeśvaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*viśvakarmeśvaraṃ cātha maṇikarṇīśvaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*avimukteśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā tato viśveśamarcayet \|*  
*eṣā yātrā prayatnena kartavyā kṣetravāsinā \|\| 47 \|\|*

43-47. Or the pilgrimage can be performed on every fourteenth lunar day by the people who desire the mastery of the holy spot. A pilgrim obtains the benefit if he takes bath in the different Tīrthas, worships the different Liṅgas and observes silence while travelling. He will visit (1) Oṃkāra at the outset after performing aquatic rites in Matsyodarī. Then he should go to (2) Triviṣṭapa, (3) Mahādeva, then (4) Kṛttivāsas, (5) Ratneśa, (6) then Candreśa and then (7) Kedāra, then he should go to (8) Dharmeśvara, (9) Vīreśa, and (10) Kāmeśvara. Then (11) Viśvakarmeśvara, then (12) Maṇikarṇīśvara. After seeing (13) Avimukteśvara he will worship Viśveśa (14) This pilgrimage should be assiduously performed by a resident of the holy spot.

## \|\| 2.100.48 \|\|

*yastu kṣetramuṣitvā tu naitāṃ yātrāṃ samācaret \|*  
*vighnāstasyopatiṣṭhaṃte kṣetroccāṭanasūcakāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. If someone stays in the holy spot but does not perform this pilgrimage, he will be beset with obstacles indicating expulsion from the holy spot.

## Chapter 100 - Yātrā Parikrama (pilgrimages) (3): Aṣṭāyatana Yātrā

## \|\| 2.100.49-50 \|\|

*aṣṭāyatana yātrānyā kartavyā vighraśāṃtaye \|*  
*dakṣeśaḥ pārvatīśaśca tathā paśupatīśvaraḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*gaṃgeśo narmadeśaśca gabhastīśaḥ satīśvaraḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamastārakeśaśca pratyaṣṭami viśeṣataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Another pilgrimage of eight Āyatanas should be performed for the purpose of subduing obstacles, especially on every eighth lunar day. They are: Dakṣeśa, Pārvatīśa, Paśupatīśvara, Gaṇeśa, Narmadeśa, Gabhastīśa, Satīśvara and the eighth one Tārakeśa.

## \|\| 2.100.51-62 \|\|

*dṛśyānyetāni liṃgāni mahāpāpopaśāṃtaye \|*  
*aparāpi śubhā yātrā yogakṣemakarī sadā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*sarvavighropahaṃtrī ca kartavyā kṣetravāsibhiḥ \|*  
*śaileśaṃ prathamaṃ vīkṣya varaṇāsnānapūrvakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*snānaṃ tu saṃgame kṛtvā draṣṭavyaḥ saṃgameśvaraḥ \|*  
*svalīna tīrthe susnātaḥ paśyetsvalīnamīśvaram \|\| 53 \|\|*

*snātvā maṃdākinī tīrthe draṣṭavyo madhyameśvaraḥ \|*  
*paśyeddhiraṇyagarbheśaṃ tatra tīrthe kṛtodakaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*maṇikarṇyāṃ tataḥ snātvā paśyedīśānamīśvaram \|*  
*tataḥ kūpamupaspṛśya goprekṣamavalokayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

*kāpileya hrade snātvā vīkṣeta vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*upaśāṃtaśivaṃ paśyettatkūpavihitodakaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*paṃcacūḍāhrade snātvā jyeṣṭhasthānaṃ tatorcayet \|*  
*catuḥsamudrakūpe tu snātvā devaṃ samarcayet \|\| 57 \|\|*

*devasyāgre tu yā vāpī tatropasparśane kṛte \|*  
*śukreśvaraṃ tataḥ paśyettatkūpavihitodakaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*daṃḍakhāte tataḥ snātvā vyāghreśaṃ pūjayettataḥ \|*  
*śaunakeśvarakuṃḍe tu snānaṃ kṛtvā tatorcayet \|\| 59 \|\|*

*jaṃbukeśaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ kṛtvā yātrāmimāṃ naraḥ \|*  
*kvacinna jāyate bhūyaḥ saṃsāre duḥkhasāgare \|\| 60 \|\|*

*samārabhya pratipadaṃ yāvatkṛṣṇā caturdaśī \|*  
*etatkrameṇa kartavyānye tadāyatanāni vai \|\| 61 \|\|*

*imāṃ yātrāṃ naraḥ kṛtvā na bhūyopyabhijāyate \|*  
*anyā yātrā prakartavyaikā daśāyatanodbhavā \|\| 62 \|\|*

51-62. All these Liṅgas should be visited for suppressing great obstacles.

## Chapter 100 - Yātrā Parikrama (pilgrimages) (4): Bath and Darśana of 14 Liṅgas

## Chapter 100 - Yātrā Parikrama (pilgrimages) (5): Ekādaśāyatanī Yātrā

## \|\| 2.100.63-66 \|\|

*āgnīdhra kuṃḍe susnātaḥ paśyedāgnīdhramīśvaram \|*  
*urvaśīśaṃ tato gacchettatastu nakulīśvaram \|\| 63 \|\|*

*āṣāḍhīśaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā bhārabhūteśvaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*lāṃgalīśamathālokya tatastu tripurāṃtakam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tato manaḥprakāmeśaṃ prītikeśamatho vrajet \|*  
*madālaseśvaraṃ tasmāttilaparṇeśvaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*yātraikādaśaliṃgānāmeṣā kāryā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*imāṃ yātrāṃ prakurvāṇo rudratvaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

There is another pilgrimage consisting of eleven Āyatanas. It should be performed.

63-66. Having bathed duly as per prescriptions in Agnīdhra-kuṇḍa, the devotee should visit Lord Agnīdhra. Then he should proceed to Urvaśīśa and thereafter to Nakulīśvara. After visiting Āṣāḍhīśa and Bhārabhūteśvara thereafter, after visiting Lāṅgalīśa and Tripurāntaka thereafter, and then Manaḥprakāmeśvara he should proceed to Prītikeśa. Thereafter he should visit Madālaseśvara and then Tilaparṇeśvara. This pilgrimage of eleven Liṅgas should be assiduously performed. A man performing this pilgrimage shall attain Rudra’s status.

## Chapter 100 - Yātrā Parikrama (pilgrimages) (6): Gaurī Yātrā

## \|\| 2.100.67-73 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi gārī yātrāmanuttamām \|*  
*śuklapakṣe tṛtīyāyāṃ yā yātrā viṣvagṛddhidā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*goprekṣatīrthe susnāya mukhanirmālikāṃ vrajet \|*  
*jyeṣṭhāvāpyāṃ naraḥ snātvā jyeṣṭhāgaurīṃ samarcayet \|\| 68 \|\|*

*saubhāgyagaurī saṃpūjyā jñānavāpyāṃ kṛtodakaiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ śṛṃgāragaurīṃ ca tatraiva ca kṛtodakaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*snātvā viśālagaṃgāyāṃ viśālākṣīṃ tato vrajet \|*  
*susnāto lalitātīrthe lalitāmarcayettataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*snātvā bhavānītīrthetha bhavānīṃ paripūjayet \|*  
*maṃgalā ca tatobhyarcyā biṃdutīrthakṛtodakaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tato gacchenmahālakṣmīṃ sthiralakṣmīsamṛddhaye \|*  
*imāṃ yātrāṃ naraḥ kṛtvā kṣetresminmuktijanmani \|\| 72 \|\|*

*na duḥkhairabhibhūyeta ihāmutrāpi kutracit \|*  
*kuryātpraticaturthīha yātrāṃ vighneśituḥ sadā \|\| 73 \|\|*

67-73. Hereafter I shall narrate the excellent Gaurī Yātrā that should be performed on the third lunar day of the bright half. It bestows all riches. Having bathed perfectly in Goprekṣa a devotee shall go to Mukhanirmālikā. After taking the bath in the Jyeṣṭhāvāpī tank, the man should worship Jyeṣṭhāgaurī. Saubhāgyagaurī should be worshipped by those who have performed aquatic rites in the Jñānavāpī tank. Then after performing the same rite there itself, he should worship Śṛṅgāragaurī. After bathing in Viśālagaṅgā he should proceed to Viśālākṣī. After a bath as per prescription in the Lalitā Tīrtha, the devotee should worship Lalitā. After bathing in the Bhavānī Tīrtha, he should adore Bhavānī. Then Maṅgalā should be worshipped by the devotees who have performed aquatic rites with the waters of Bindu Tīrtha. Thereafter, for the purpose of steady increase in the prosperity, he should go to Mahālakṣmī. By performing this pilgrimage in this holy spot that causes salvation no man will be assailed by miseries anywhere here or hereafter.

## Chapter 100 - Pilgrimages of Gaṇeśas, Bhairava etc.

## \|\| 2.100.74 \|\|

*brāhmaṇebhyastaduddeśāddeyā vai modakā mude \|*  
*bhaume bhairavayātrā ca kāryā pātakahāriṇī \|\| 74 \|\|*

One shall always perform the pilgrimage of Vighnarāja on every Caturthī day (fourth lunar day).

74\. With him (Gaṇeśa) in view Modakas (ball-shaped sweetmeat) should be given to Brāhmaṇas for their happiness. During Tuesdays Bhairava Yātrā that removes sins should be performed.

## \|\| 2.100.75 \|\|

*ravivāre raveryātrā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vāravisaṃyuji \|*  
*tathaiva ravisaptamyāṃ sarvavighnopaśāṃtaye \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The pilgrimage unto Ravi (Sun-god) should be performed on Sundays, on the sixth lunar day when it coincides with a Sunday and also on Ravisaptamī day, for the purpose of subduing all obstacles.

## \|\| 2.100.76 \|\|

*navamyāmathavāṣṭamyāṃ caṃḍīyātrā śubhā matā \|*  
*aṃtargṛhasya vai yātrā kartavyā prativāsaram \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Caṇḍī Yātrā is considered auspicious when performed on the eighth or ninth lunar day. Everyday the pilgrimage of the inner apartment (Sanctum) should be performed,

## Chapter 100 - Antargṛha Yātrā

## \|\| 2.100.77 \|\|

*prātaḥsnānaṃ vidhāyādau natvā paṃcavināyakān \|*  
*namaskṛtvātha viśveśaṃ sthitvā nirvāṇamaṃḍape \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. At the outset, the early morning bath is taken. Then the five Vināyakas are bowed to. A devotee then makes obeisance to Viśveśa standing in the Nirvāṇamaṇḍapa.

## \|\| 2.100.78 \|\|

*aṃtargṛhasya yātrā vai kariṣye ghaughaśāṃtaye \|*  
*gṛhītvā niyamaṃ ceti gatvātha maṇikarṇikām \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The devotee resolves thus: ‘I shall perform the Yātrā of the inner Sanctum for subḍueing the mass of sins.’ After taking up the vow thus, he goes to Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 2.100.79 \|\|

*snātvā maunena cāgatya maṇikarṇīśamarcayet \|*  
*kaṃbalāśvatarau natvā vāsukīśaṃ praṇamya ca \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. After the bath he will return silently and worship Maṇikarṇīkā. Then he bows to Kambala and Aśvatara and offers obeisance to Vāsukīśa.

## \|\| 2.100.80 \|\|

*parvateśaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā gaṃgākeśavamapyatha \|*  
*tatastu lalitāṃ dṛṣṭvā jarāsaṃdheśvaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Then he visits in order Parvateśa, Gaṅgākeśava, Lalitā and Jarāsandheśvara.

## \|\| 2.100.81 \|\|

*tato vai somanāthaṃ ca vārāhaṃ ca tato vrajet \|*  
*brahmeśvaraṃ tato natvā natvāgastīśvaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Then after seeing Somanātha, he goes to Varāha. Then bows to Brahmeśvara and Agastīśvara.

## \|\| 2.100.82 \|\|

*kaśyapeśaṃ namaskṛtya harikeśavanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*vaidyanāthaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā dhruveśamatha vīkṣya ca \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. He should pay obeisance to Kaśyapeśa and Harikeśavana. After visiting Vaidyanātha he should visit Dhruveśa.

## \|\| 2.100.83-86 \|\|

*gokarṇeśvaramabhyarcya hāṭakeśamatho vrajet \|*  
*asthikṣepa taḍāge ca dṛṣṭvā vai kīkaseśvaram \|\| 83 \|\|*

*bhārabhūtaṃ tato natvā citregupteśvaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*citraghaṃṭāṃ praṇamyātha tataḥ paśupatīśvaram \|\| 84 \|\|*

*pitāmaheśvaraṃ gatvā tatastu kalaśeśvaram \|*  
*caṃdreśastvatha vīreśo vidyeśognīśa eva ca \|\| 85 \|\|*

*nāgeśvaro hariścaṃdraściṃtāmaṇivināyakaḥ \|*  
*senāvināyakaścātha draṣṭavyaḥ sarvavighnahṛt \|\| 86 \|\|*

83-86. The following are to be visited, worshipped and bowed to: Gokarṇeśvara, Hāṭakeśvara, Kīkaseśvara in the lake where bones are cast (Asthikṣepa), Bhārabhūta, Citragupteśvara, Citraghaṇṭā, Paśupatīśvara, Pitāmaheśvara, Kalaśeśvara, Candreśa, Vīreśa, Vidyeśa, Agnīśa, Nāgeśvara, Hariścandra, Cintāmaṇivināyaka and Senāvināyaka, the remover of all obstacles.

## \|\| 2.100.87 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhavāmadevau ca mūrtirūpadharāvubhau \|*  
*draṣṭavyau yatnataḥ kāśyāṃ mahāvighnavināśinau \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Vaśiṣṭha and Vāmadeva in the form of idols should be deliberately seen in Kāśī. They are destroyers of great obstacles.

## \|\| 2.100.88-90 \|\|

*sīmāvināyakaṃ cātha karuṇeśaṃ tato vrajet \|*  
*trisaṃdhyeśo viśālākṣī dharmeśo viśvabāhukā \|*  
*āśāvināyakaścātha vṛddhādityastataḥ punaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*caturvaktreśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ brāhmīśastu tataḥ paraḥ \|*  
*tato manaḥprakāmeśa īśāneśastataḥ param \|\| 89 \|\|*

*caṃḍīcaṃḍīśvarau dṛśyau bhavānīśaṃkarau tataḥ \|*  
*ḍhuṃḍhiṃ praṇamya ca tato rājarājeśamarcayet \|\| 90 \|\|*

88-90. The following are then visited and bowed to: Sīmāvināyaka, Karuṇeśa, Trisandhyeśa, Viśālākṣī, Dharmeśa, Viśvabāhukā, Āśāvināyaka, Vṛddhāditya, Caturvaktreśvara Liṅga, then Brāhmīśa, Manaḥprakāmeśa, Īśāneśa, Caṇḍī and Caṇḍīśvara, Bhavānī and Saṅkara. Ḍhuṇḍhi should be worshipped. The devotee then should adore Rājarājeśa.

## \|\| 2.100.91-95 \|\|

*lāṃgalīśastatobhyarcyastatastu nakulīśvaraḥ \|*  
*parānneśamatho natvā paradravyeśvaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*pratigraheśvaraṃ vāpi niṣkalaṃkeśameva ca \|*  
*mārkaṃḍeyeśamabhyarcya tataścāpsaraseśvaram \|\| 92 \|\|*

*gaṃgeśorcyastato jñānavāpyāṃ snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*naṃdikeśaṃ tārakeśaṃ mahākāleśvaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*daṃḍapāṇiṃ maheśaṃ ca mokṣeśaṃ praṇamettataḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadreśvaraṃ natvā avimukteśvaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*vināyakāṃstataḥ paṃca viśvanāthaṃ tato vrajet \|*  
*tato maunaṃ visṛjyātha maṃtrametamudīrayet \|\| 95 \|\|*

91-95. Lāṅgalīśa should be worshipped then. Then Nakulīśvara. After bowing to Parānneśa the devotee bows to Paradravyeśvara, Pratigraheśvara or Niṣkalaṅkeśa. After worshipping Mārkaṇḍeyeśa he should bow to Apsaraseśvara. Then Gaṅgeśa is to be worshipped; then he should take his bath in Jñānavāpī tank. Then he should bow down to Nandikeśa, Tārakeśa, Mahākāleśvara, Daṇḍapāṇi, Maheśa and Mokṣeśa. After bowing down to Vīrabhadreśvara and Avimukteśvara, the five Vināyakas, he should go to Viśvanātha. Then he will break silence and utter this Mantra.

## \|\| 2.100.96 \|\|

*aṃtargṛhasya yātreyaṃ yathāvadyā mayā kṛtā \|*  
*nyūnātiriktayā śaṃbhuḥ prīyatāmanayā vibhuḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. “May Lord Śaṃbhu be pleased with this pilgrimage of the Antargṛha (Inner Sanctum), which has been duly performed by me, even if it be deficient or superfluous in any respect.”

## \|\| 2.100.97 \|\|

*iti maṃtraṃ samuccārya kṣaṇaṃ vai muktimaṃḍape \|*  
*viśramya yāyādbhavanaṃ niṣpāpaḥ puṇyavānnaraḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. After uttering this Mantra, the devotee rests for a short while in the Muktimaṇḍapa, He should then go home. The man is rid of his sins. He is meritorious.

## \|\| 2.100.98 \|\|

*saṃprāpya vāsaraṃ viṣṇorviṣṇutīrtheṣu sarvataḥ \|*  
*kāryā yātrā prayatnena mahāpuṇya samṛddhaye \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. On the day of Viṣṇu (i.e. Lunar eleventh) the pilgrimage to all the Viṣṇu Tīrthas should be assiduously performed for enhancing one’s great merit.

## \|\| 2.100.99 \|\|

*nabhasya paṃcadaśyāṃ ca kulastaṃbhaṃ samarcayet \|*  
*duḥkhaṃ rudrapiśācatvaṃ na bhavedyasya pūjanāt \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. On the fifteenth day in the month of Bhādrapada (August-Sept.) the devotee should worship Kulastaṃbha. The worship thereof will remove misery and Rudrapiśāca state.

## Chapter 100 - Phalaśruti (Fruit of hearing etc.) of the Kāśī Khaṇḍa

## \|\| 2.100.106 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*sūta skāṃdamidaṃ śrutvā kāśīmāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*naro na nirayaṃ yāti kṛtvāpyaghasahasrakam \|\| 106 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

106\. O Sūta, on hearing this excellent greatness of Kāśī as described in the Skanda Purāṇa, no man falls into hell even if he commits a thousand sins.

## \|\| 2.100.107 \|\|

*snātvā sarvāṇi tīrthāni yacchreyaḥ samupārjyate \|*  
*kāśīkhaṃḍasya śravaṇāttatsyātsūta na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. By listening to Kāśīkhaṇḍa, O Sūta, one undoubtedly attains that merit which is acquired after bathing in all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 2.100.108 \|\|

*dattvā dānāni sarvāṇi kṛtvā yajñānanekaśaḥ \|*  
*tatpuṇyaṃ labhate martyastadā tacchravaṇāddhruvam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Certainly then the man gets by thus listening that merit which is acquired by making all kinds of gifts and performing many Yajñas.

## \|\| 2.100.109-110 \|\|

*taptvā tapāṃsi cogrāṇi prāpyate yanmahatphalam \|*  
*śravaṇādasya khaṃḍasya labhate tanna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*adhītya caturo vedānsāṃgānyatphalamāpyate \|*  
*kāśīkhaṃḍaṃ samākarṇya tatphalaṃ labhyate naraiḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. By listening to Kāśīkhaṇḍa, that great merit is acquired which is usually acquired after performing severe penances and also by learning all the four Vedas along with their ancillaries.

## \|\| 2.100.111 \|\|

*gayayāṃ śrāddhadānācca yathā tṛpyaṃti pūrvajāḥ \|*  
*tathaitacchravaṇānnṛṇāṃ tṛpnuvaṃti pitāmahāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Grandfathers become satisfied by listening to this in the same manner as the ancestors are satisfied after gifts are made in Gayā.

## \|\| 2.100.112 \|\|

*taiśca sarvapurāṇāni śrutāni sthirabuddhibhiḥ \|*  
*kāśīkhaṃḍaṃ śrutaṃ yaiśca sarveṣāṃ śreyasāṃ padam \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. If Kāśīkhaṇḍa which is the cause of all welfare is heard by persons of steady intellect, then all the Purāṇas have been heard.

## \|\| 2.100.113 \|\|

*śrutāśca sarvadharmāstairmahāpuṇyekarāśibhiḥ \|*  
*śrutaṃ yaiḥ sthiracetobhiḥ kāśīmāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. If the excellent greatness of Kāśī is listened to by men of steady minds, they acquire great heaps of merits and all the Dharmas have been paid heed to by them.

## \|\| 2.100.114 \|\|

*idameva hi devejyā paramā parikīrtitā \|*  
*japettatkhaṃḍamakhilaṃ śrotavyaṃ śraddhayā dvijāḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. If the whole Khaṇḍa is recited (silently), that alone is the worship of the Lord. It is glorified as the greatest adoration. The entire Khaṇḍa should be listened to with faith, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.100.115 \|\|

*śṛṇuyādekamapi ya ākhyānaṃ kāśikhaṃḍajam \|*  
*śrutāni tena sarvāṇi dharmaśāstrāṇyasaṃśayam \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. If anyone listens to even one story of Kāśīkhaṇḍa, undoubtedly all the Dharmaśāstras have been heard by him.

## \|\| 2.100.116 \|\|

*mahādharmaikajananaṃ mahārthapratipādakam \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ sarvakāmāpteḥ kāśīkhaṃḍamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. This Kāśīkhaṇḍa is known as the sole cause of great Dharmas, the expounder of great truths and the cause of the acquisition of all desires.

## \|\| 2.100.117 \|\|

*etacchravaṇataḥ puṃsāṃ kaivalyaṃ naiva dūrataḥ \|*  
*tuṣyaṃti sarve pitaraḥ śrutvaitatkhaṃḍamuttamam \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. By listening to this, Kaivalya (Salvation) ceases to be far off in the case of men. All the Pitṛs become pleased on hearing this excellent Khaṇḍa.

## \|\| 2.100.118-119 \|\|

*prīṇaṃtyamartyāḥ sarvepi brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ \|*  
*munayaḥ parimodaṃte mādyaṃti sanakādayaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*hṛṣṭaḥ sarvo bhavedeva bhūtagrāmaścaturvidhaḥ \|*  
*mahimaśravaṇādasmādvārāṇasyā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

118-119. All the immortal beings beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva become pleased. The sages rejoice. Sanaka and others become elated. All shall certainly be delighted; all the four types of living beings become pleased by listening to this greatness of Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 2.100.120-121 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śrāvayedvidvānsamastaṃ tvardhameva vā \|*  
*pādamātraṃ tadardhaṃ vā tvekaṃ vyākhyānamuttamam \|\| 120 \|\|*

*sa namasyaḥ prayatnena saṃpūjyastviṣṭadevavat \|*  
*tasmai deyaṃ prayatnena viśveśa prītaye sadā \|\| 121 \|\|*

120-121. If a learned man expounds this excellent narrative entirely, or even half, or even a quarter or half of that or one excellent episode, he should be assiduously bowed to, he should be worshipped like a favourite deity. In order to please Viśveśa much should be given to him.

## \|\| 2.100.122-132 \|\|

*tasmiṃstuṣṭe hi saṃtuṣṭo viśveśo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yatraitatpaṭhyate khaṃḍaṃ parānaṃdasamāśrayam \|\| 122 \|\|*

*na tatra prabhavetkaścidamaṃgalasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyādvidvānyaścedaṃ śrāvayetsudhīḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

*yaḥ paṭhedapi puṇyātmā te sarve rudramūrtayaḥ \|*  
*ya etatpustakaṃ ramyaṃ lekhayitvā samarpayet \|\| 124 \|\|*

*akhilāni purāṇāni tena dattāni nānyathā \|*  
*atrākhyānāni yāvaṃti ślokā yāvaṃta eva hi \|\| 125 \|\|*

*tathā padāni yāvaṃti varṇā yāvaṃta eva hi \|*  
*yāvaṃtyapi ca mātrāṇi yāvaṃtyaḥ padapaṃktayaḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

*guṇe sūtrāṇi yāvaṃti yāvaṃtaḥ paṭataṃtavaḥ \|*  
*citrarūpāṇi yāvaṃti ramyapustakasaṃcake \|\| 127 \|\|*

*tāvadyugasahasrāṇi dātā svarge mahīyate \|*  
*etaddvādaśakṛtvo yaḥ śṛṇuyātkhaṃḍamuttamam \|\| 128 \|\|*

*brahmahatyāpi tasyāśu naśyecchaṃbhoranugrahāt \|*  
*aputraḥ śṛṇuyādyastu susnātaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

*tasya putro bhavatyeva śaṃbhorājñā prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*kiṃ bahūktena sūteha yasya yasya manorathaḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

*yo yastaṃ taṃ sa sasadā śrutvaitatprāpnuyātkṛtī \|*  
*śṛṇuyāddūradeśepi yaḥ kāśīkhaṃḍamuttamam \|\| 131 \|\|*

*sa kāśīvāsapuṇyasya bhājanaṃ syācchivājñayā \|*  
*etacchravaṇataḥ puṃsāṃ sarvatra vijayo bhavet \|*  
*saubhāgyaṃ cāpi sarvatra prāpnuyānnirmalāśayaḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

122-132. If he is satisfied, Viśveśa too is undoubtedly satisfied. There cannot be any powerful inauspicious thing in the place where this Khaṇḍa, the cause of the greatest bliss, is being read. The learned man who listens to this, the sensible scholar who expounds this and the meritorious-souled man who reads this, all these are forms of Rudra.

If anyone copies this and offers this beautiful book to anyone else, it is as though all the Purāṇas have been given by him, not otherwise.

A giver of the manuscript is honoured in heaven as many thousands of Yugas as there are episodes in this, as there are verses in this, as there are words, as there are syllables in this, as many Mātrās (Syllabic instants) there are here, as many rows of words are here, as there are threads in the string, as many threads in the cloth, as many pictures there are in the beautiful book.

He who listens to this excellent Khaṇḍa twelve times, will be rid of the sin of even Brāhmaṇa-slaughter immediately, with the favour of Śaṃbhu.

If a man without a son listens to this after due bath with great faith, he will surely have a son by the power of the command of Śaṃbhu.

Of what avail is speaking much, O Sūta? Whatever may be one’s wish one shall be blessed by listening to this and obtain the same.

Even if a man listens to this excellent Kāśīkhaṇḍa from a far-off land, he will have the merit of residing in Kāśī at the behest of Śiva.

By listening to this a man will be victorious everywhere. He will be of pure heart and he will enjoy bliss everywhere.

## \|\| 2.100.133 \|\|

*yasya viśveśvarastuṣṭastasyaitacchravaṇe matiḥ \|*  
*jāyate puṇyayuktasya mahānirmalacetasaḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. One shall have interest in listening to this, only if Viśveśa is pleased with one. He is meritorious. His mind is free from impurities.

## \|\| 2.100.134 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ maṃgalānāṃ ca mahāmaṃgalamuttamam \|*  
*gṛhepi likhitaṃ pūjyaṃ sarvamaṃgalasiddhaye \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. This book is the most excellent one of great auspiciousness among all auspicious things. It must be copied in writing and should be worshipped for the attainment of all auspiciousness.

:: End of Kāśīkhaṇḍa Uttarārdha ::

:: End of Kāśīkhanda ::
